# VibeSpace — engineering log

This file is the engineers' record of every release: the lanes, the verification rounds and what they found, the gate reds and their causes, measurements, the choices made and why. Below its own `# Changelog` title it holds the changelog as it stood before 2026-09-29, verbatim (2.369.198 and older).

`CHANGELOG.md` (with `CHANGELOG.zh.md` and `CHANGELOG.ja.md`) is the user's: what changed for the person using VibeSpace, one plain line per change, in the interface's language — the rules are in docs/changelog-style.md. From 2.369.199 on, every release also writes its section here, under the same `## <version> — <date>` heading as its user entry and in the same commit, newest first above the verbatim record.

### claude-steer-inject r4 — a Stop window closes on the CLI's words, a copy is claimed by its witness, riding is not landed, the hold chord keeps the composer's law at idle (acceptance r2's verdict: 11 reviewers on 7df30f96)
- **Why:** r2's 2 s clock started at the interrupted result, but the CLI runs its UserPromptSubmit hook BEFORE the follow-up's init, and the product's own hook (data/bin/vibespace-hook.mjs) waits on the hub up to 3 s. With a ~2.9 s hook the clock closed the window first: MARK-B was answered after Stop. In the owed-turn shape it drained an Alt+Enter-held frame into the turn the CLI was starting. r2 had measured with VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS=1.
- **Measured on 2.1.312** (measure/probe-r4.mjs raw, probe-r4w.mjs through each tree's own wrapper; the product's hooks registered by data/bin/vibespace-hook-register.mjs into a scratch HOME; a loopback hub and mock):
  - The CLI's hook timeout is the registered `timeout: 10` (600 s when a hook names none: `Hf = 600000`).
  - `CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_USER_PROMPT_SUBMIT_HOOK_EVENTS` makes the CLI say `hook_started` ~10 ms after the interrupted result and `hook_response` when the hook ends.
  - An interrupt INSIDE the hook cancels it and DROPS the held frame from the conversation: no user record, and the next request lacks it. So the init stays the interrupt point.
  - A person's frame's `uuid` becomes the CLI's user-record uuid, and the `source_uuid` of a queued_command attachment.
- **Built:**
  - The adapter sets the hook-events switch (chat only).
  - The wrapper consumes the UserPromptSubmit hook lines (never teed) and arms no clock while a hook runs. Its backstop is 30 s where the CLI owes a turn and 2 s where it owes nothing.
  - Stop keeps a `riding` frame, and a window that closes with no follow-up settles it as `landed`.
  - The wrapper stamps a `uuid` on each person's mid-turn frame. The copy names it (`cliUuid`), and an edit rewrites the copy.
  - The normalizer claims a copy by witness only, and a record with a block kind the copy lacks gives the bubble its blocks.
  - Alt+Enter is `_altEnter`: it holds during a turn and is the composer's own Enter at idle (unstamped).
  - The stream consumer draws the running line at a CLI-started turn's init.
  - The heavy suite runs its teardown on signals.
- **RED controls (7df30f96 vs this commit, the real 2.1.312 + the product's hooks):**
  - hook-stop (~2.9 s hook): answered after Stop vs 0 requests.
  - hook-owed: C rode B's tool result vs C ran as its own turn.
  - A 400 KB screenshot held / handed-own / kept, then restarted: 0 images vs 1 image each.
  - edit, restarted: 2 bubbles vs 1.
  - A 61-call turn, restarted: 2 bubbles vs 1.
  - The riding race (in-process): landed + answered vs kept + interrupted in the same tick.
  - The 1.5 s hook and the no-hook cases are green on both trees.
- **Accepted limit:** the init-tick interrupt races the CLI's first request. The reviewers saw 2/9 on 2.1.308 with a bare `sleep` hook; with the product's own 1.5 s hook it was 0/10 on 2.1.308 and 0/20 (+0/9 raw) on 2.1.312.
- **Tests:**
  - test-claude-steer 66 (base 54/8).
  - test-claude-steer-chrome 79 (base 66/11; new legs ⑮–⑱ and §A ⑤–⑦, the δ legs judged by signal).
  - test-stdout-registry 269 (base 267/2).

## 2.369.360 — 2026-10-27

### ci358-reds (items 7 + 8 and round 2 — c083607d → 5bdb59fb; the .358 mirror's two fast-tier races)
- **CI .358 — every chat wrapper rewrote its sidecar IN PLACE, and the hub read it empty (ci358-reds item 7; the mirror 91bf7e18's fast job, test-peer-delivery «✗ agy-peer-wake ④: RED COPY … `{"ok":false,"reason":"no live inbox for this conversation on any reachable machine","notRunning":true}`», green on the runner's two other runs):** the copy's sidecar sits at its expected path (item 5's /proc branch is never reached) and carries its caps from its first write; every later write was `fs.writeFileSync(metaFile, …)` — TRUNCATED, then written — and the ladder's `liveWithoutLane` read it in between: `JSON.parse('')` ⇒ wrapperCaps `no-sidecar` ⇒ «no live inbox … any reachable machine» + notRunning about a LIVE session — a second cause of the same words, found by the runner (the owner's 2026-10-24 report had its own, deterministic cause: the stash-only row + the peerMessage:false advert, fixed in .353 by agy-peer-wake); findRpcPeer skips a live peerMessage:true wrapper the same way. Traced here: ④ asks 110–155 ms after the copy's boot write, and its next (debounced) write is due at 200 ms — on the slower runner the two met. FIX (product): chat-wrapper / codex-chat-wrapper / acp-wrapper / agy-wrapper `persistMeta` write a temp file beside the sidecar and rename it over — a reader sees the old record or the new, whole. SUITE: the sidecars are awaited by their CONTENT (caps read), not their existence; ④ asks INSIDE a held write (`scripts/fixtures/sidecar-write-hold.cjs`: armed, a queue-resync makes the write, held between its truncate and its bytes) — the runner's order, every run; NEGATIVE CONTROL: a copy with the pre-.358 in-place write under the same hold reads 0 bytes and says the runner's line; a pin: every chat wrapper replaces its sidecar. dae9d4c0's suite with the copy's write held prints the runner's «2 FAILED (104 passed)».
- **CI .358 — test-remoteapp-token-sinks §8 judged the cert-changed REASON after waiting for the STATE (ci358-reds item 8; the fast re-run of 91bf7e18, «✗ the machine shows ANOTHER certificate ⇒ … the card's view says refused» with `refused: null`):** `fail()` flips the record's state at the app's exit, `rdp.ended` lands only after `rdpEndOf`'s async read of app.log; `endedS` (the state alone) returned between the two and the card's view was read with no reason yet — the ✗ printed the live record, its reason filled in by then. The .290 mirror fixed this race in §1's legs (`endedWhy`); §8's sealed-keeper leg kept `endedS`. FIX: the leg waits with `endedWhy` (≤ 10 s; a timeout names the wait and the record) and judges a copy taken at the wait. RED CONTROL: the same launch with app.log's read held 600 ms — `endedS` returns with no reason and the view says refused null (asserted — the runner's ✗), `endedWhy` waits through the hold and the view says refused; the same hold under dae9d4c0's suite prints the runner's line and «1 FAILED (76 passed)». Test-only.
- **CI .358 round 2 (ci358-reds, the acceptance of c083607d) — a sidecar temp a killed wrapper leaves is the age sweep's; the boot write is replaced too:** a wrapper killed between `persistMeta`'s temp write and its rename leaves `<id>.json.<pid>.tmp`, which the boot's age sweep (`^(.+)\.(buf|json)$`) never reaped and no kill path can unlink (persistMeta is synchronous, so only a SIGKILL / OOM / power loss lands between the two). The sweep moved out of server.js's boot into `src/server/wrapper-files.js` `sweepAgedWrapperFiles` (the same law: untouched 7 days + not live; server.js calls it) and reaps that temp too; a write or rename that throws already unlinked its own temp (now pinned). chat-wrapper's boot write — an in-place `writeFileSync(metaFile)` of a fresh id's file — goes through persistMeta; the pin covers each wrapper's whole file, and the exit record (`overwriteIfPresent`: r+, never truncated, padded, never recreates a sidecar the hub removed) is the one in-place write left. GATE: test-peer-delivery's age-sweep leg (an aged temp reaped beside the old law's .buf/.json; a young temp, a live session's temp and a stranger left; the wiring) — c083607d's sweep block, lifted verbatim, prints «2 FAILED (114 passed)», c083607d's chat-wrapper «1 FAILED (115 passed)»; this commit ALL PASS (116).

### phone-back-reload, acceptance rounds 5 to 8 — the late watch holds; a tap ends on the page, in both phases and across a hop (the chain's fifth to eighth commits, on the .358 pick 67dbe31d)
- **Acceptance round 5 (主开发, one reviewer + skeptics, three reproduced in Chrome 154; the fifth commit on 67dbe31d, for 2.369.359).** Measured first on Chrome 154 with the back/forward cache off and on (a pending cross-document traversal after the stay's new sentinel, the page entry below it): a step DOWN onto the page's own entry — `navigation.traverseTo(key)`, `navigation.back()`, here `history.go(-1)` too — ABORTS the pending traversal and lands there; a #fragment link's navigation (a click, `location.hash`) is a push — `currententrychange` says `push` right before its popstate, a traversal's says `traverse` — and aborts nothing; the document a late commit landed on, after its own push and a back, lists a stale COPY of its own entry right above it (index -1, its key): `navigation.forward()` or a `traverseTo` onto it commits at once, moves nothing and aborts nothing, while a step onto the first real entry above, or onto its page entry by key, aborts. (1) MAJOR: a tap AFTER the stay aborted nothing — round 4's late watch only dropped the intent, and the 6 s commit yanked the person to the older document while they used the page. A late tap now aborts the suspended go() by the step down onto the page's own entry (`abortGo(home)`), then a new sentinel (`rearm why input-late`); the step's popstate is the page's own (`ownStep`), never a back press; a key that IS the browser's own back or forward (Alt+← / →, ⌘ held, BrowserBack / BrowserForward) is no tap — its keydown reaches the page first, and read as one the step down ran ahead of the browser's back and the two went back past the page (measured: the first run of test-exit-slow-chrome ⑦ loaded the older document). (2) MINOR: a chain of slow pages (the late landing hops, its own go() slow too, so it stays at its bound and boots) filed «a slow exit»; PURE `slowExit` takes the document's own rows (`mine`) and never files for one that went on (a hop row of its own). (3) MINOR: a #fragment link's popstate ended the late watch though it aborts nothing — no slow row, no re-key, the older document booted silently; only a traversal's popstate (`currententrychange` navigationType `traverse`; without the API the URL rule) ends it now. (4) MINOR: on such a landing document `abortGo`'s `forward()` went onto the stale copy (it «committed» and aborted nothing: the intent dropped, the exit went on); the step now goes by key onto the entry above past a copy of the page's own, else onto `home`, and «landed» means the page stands there — a step refused, moving nothing or with none to take is NOT aborted: the page re-arms (`rearm why input abort 0`, said once) and the intent is kept for the landing document's rule (round 4 dropped it when no entry stood above). The `rearm` row carries `abort` (1 | 0; the census declares it). NEW heavy test-exit-late-chrome (Chrome twice: ⑨ a tap after the stay, ⑩ a chain of slow pages, ⑪ a #fragment link during the late watch — each on round 4's rules RED, then shipped); test-exit-slow-chrome's and test-exit-hop-chrome's swaps follow the moved lines.
- **Acceptance round 6 (主开发, one reviewer + two skeptics; the sixth commit on 36df506a).** (1) MAJOR, confirmed: a MOUSE's back button during the late watch was read as a tap — round 5's `navKey` told only the key forms, and the late watch heard `pointerdown`. Measured first on Chrome 154 with the back/forward cache off and on (lane probe h12: CDP `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` button `back` 4 s into a pending traversal, after the stay's push; CDP's Input commands are answered while a traversal is pending, only `Runtime.evaluate` waits for the commit): the page gets `pointerdown` + `mousedown` with button 3, then `mouseup` / `auxclick`, and the browser goes back at the release; left alone, that back aborts the pending go() and lands on the page's entry (no load); after a step down onto the page's entry at the pointerdown (round 5's rule, on the probe page), the back at the release went from there onto the older document — a load at +6 s. In the app (test-exit-late-chrome ⑫ on round 5's rules, both cache modes) the step down ran (rearm why input-late) but no load followed: the re-arm's new sentinel stood before the button's release 60 ms later, so the browser's back went onto the page's entry — the yank needs the release first (a quick click, a busy page: the fake world's quick leg loads), not reproduced in Chrome. A pan on round 5's rules cancelled the exit (⑬: the page stays); the shipped rules let it go on. The fix: ONE predicate `navInput(e)` (a keydown with Alt / ⌘ / BrowserBack / BrowserForward; any other event with button 3 / 4), so the key and the button forms cannot drift. (1b) Flagged by the lane and ruled by 主开发: in the late watch a tap is a pointerdown that ENDS in a pointerup — a `pointercancel` (a pan, a gesture the browser or the system took) never steps. Measured: headless Chrome gives a touch it pans `pointerdown`, then `pointercancel` 70–90 ms in, never a `pointerup`; headless Chrome has no edge-swipe back of its own (the swipe navigated nothing). NOT measured (no Android device here, reasoned only): Android's own back — the gesture, the bar's button — gives the page no input event at all; round 5's «a phone's back gesture sends no keydown» was such reasoning too. Chrome's own edge-swipe arrow, where a build has one, would begin as a touch the page sees; the pointerup rule keeps such a swipe from being a tap. The pending phase's listener is unchanged: there the step goes UP onto the sentinel, and the browser's back after it lands on the page's own entry (measured: a mouse back — its back onto the page's entry; Alt+← — no back at all), never past the page. (2) MINOR: kb-design-lessons §18 gets the routing row «A BACK PRESS on a phone / the exit plan» (the PURE verdicts, the ORCH, the diary, the gates). (3) MINOR: round 5's engineering bullet had landed inside .358's block, which shipped without round 5 — it moves here, beside this round's; the .358 blocks are byte-identical with 67dbe31d again, and the user files get a `## 2.369.359` entry. test-changelog-style ④ is RED on this chain alone: its package.json is still 2.369.357 (a lane changes no version file) and ④ lets the newest heading be at most the next patch — on int359's base (2.369.358) it is the next patch; shown green on a scratch copy with package.json at 2.369.358. - **Acceptance round 7 (主开发, one reviewer + two skeptics; the seventh commit on cb8c0a86).** (1) MINOR, confirmed: the PENDING phase — the exit's go() in its first 3 s, before the stay — still tapped at the first `pointerdown` or `keydown`, any button, any key (`onInput`, byte-identical since 36df506a: not round 6's regression), so a scroll 1 s into a slow exit CANCELLED it (the step up onto the sentinel: leave why input, rearm why input, the intent dropped) while the same scroll 4 s in let it go on — and the user changelog's «scrolling while you wait no longer counts as a tap» was false for those 3 s. The fix, as ruled: ONE tap in both phases — `tapOf(downs, e)` in mobile-back.js (a key at its keydown; a pointer at its pointerup after its pointerdown; a `pointercancel` ends the press untold; `navInput` never), asked by the pending go()'s new `onPendingInput` and by the late watch's `onLateInput`, over ONE list of events (`TAPS`; round 5's `INPUTS` is gone) and ONE `downs` (a press that began while the go() was pending and ends after the stay is the late watch's tap); `onInput` — what a tap does while pending, the step UP onto the sentinel — is unchanged. Measured in Chrome 154, cache off and on (test-exit-slow-chrome, CDP input 1.1 s into the pending go(), the older document's HTML held 6 s): ⑨ a pan (`pointerdown`, then `pointercancel`) — on round 6's rules the exit cancelled, the page stays; shipped, the stay at 3 s, the commit at 6 s, the older document goes on, the tab outside, nothing filed. ⑩ a mouse's back button (`pointerdown` / `pointerup`, button 3) — on round 6's rules the step up ran (the exit cancelled); shipped, no step: the browser's own back at the release aborts the pending traversal and takes the tab onto the page before VibeSpace, the older document never loads, nothing filed (the exit's unspent intent is dropped by the next VibeSpace load in the tab: a hop drop row). Not measured in the app: the browser's back by key while pending (no tap by the same predicate — the fake world's leg; lane probe h12 measured, on its own page, that such a back left alone counts from the pending entry and goes on back); Android's own back gives the page no event at all (reasoned, no device here), so it took that road in every round. ### desktop-doors-table — ONE table of desktop doors for the taskbar's preview tile, its compact list and the phone sheet; the phone can reorder (BUILD on bbca26b4 = int358, the 2.369.358 tree; the audit 2026-10-26 — the owner's registry law: a family is one PURE row per member + a census)
- **The drift (the audit's skeptic, verified on bbca26b4):** the desktop doors were enumerated by hand in five places — `_deskItems` (the preview tile's right-click; a compact-list row's right-click / ⋯, + Move up / Move down), the phone sheet's long press (desktop-switch-sheet.js: Rename · Delete), the phone window switcher's tab long press (mobile-nav.js: Rename · Delete), and three «+» labels (the preview strip's untranslated `'Add desktop'` title, the compact list's «+ Add desktop», the sheet's «New desktop», the tab strip's «Add desktop»). The phone offered no order door and has no drag: a phone could not reorder desktops at all. Its label read «Rename» where the desk said «Rename…»; its Delete ran outside the manager's done/after cancel guard. The pins were single-surface (test-desktop-switch ⑥ the sheet's two verbs, test-mobile-gaps #7 the tab's, test-duo-layout ⑧ the sheet's) — they pinned the gap as correct.
- **The table (PURE src/desktop-switch.js):** `DOORS` (switch · rename · delete · move-up · move-down · new, ONE t() key each — 『Rename…』 everywhere: the desk's ellipsis rule holds on the phone) + `DOOR_WHY` (gone «“{name}” is no longer there», only «Your only desktop — it cannot be deleted», first «Already the first desktop», last «Already the last desktop»); `desktopDoors({desk, desktops, order, tier})` → EVERY door, always, in one order, `enabled` by its rule (delete needs ≥ 2 desktops, move up not the first, move down not the last, a gone desktop shuts all but new), `why`, and `draw` — the ONLY thing the tier changes: 'row' (the tile / row tap; the list's «+»), 'item' (the doors menu), 'drag' (the preview's order — `order` false; a phone has no drag, its order doors are always items), 'off' (a shut door in a DESK menu is left out — the compact row's menu unchanged; the phone draws it greyed WITH its why). `doorItems(doors, {t})` = the menu's shape (ONE separator before the order doors); `sheetItems(rows, {t})` = the sheet's rows (each desktop's switch door + rowWords, then the 'new' door) — the sheet's DOM is drawn from it.
- **Every surface renders the table:** `DesktopManager._deskItems(desk, {order, after, tier})` is the ONE builder (doorItems over desktopDoors on the manager's own `_startRename` / `deleteDesktop` / `reorderDesktop`, each through `done` — a cancelled Rename… brings nothing back on either tier); the sheet's and the tab's long press call it with `tier: 'phone'` (`extraClass: 'mdesk-doors'`: 44 px rows, a shut door's why on a second line); after an act the sheet comes back on its new state (a delete re-shows the desktop on show, as before), the tabs re-draw. `_doorLabel(id, deskId)` gives every «+» (preview strip, compact list, tab strip; the sheet via sheetItems) the 'new' door's words and every switching row (preview tile, compact row, tab, sheet row) the switch door's as its title. No surface keeps a door literal.
- **Not folded in (judged):** taskbar.js `Move to Desktop` (a WINDOW's destinations — getDesktopMenuItems, with the Stage's refusal row) and the ⧉ list's «Other desktops (N)» (other desktops' WINDOWS — PURE otherDesktopWindows) list desktops as targets of a window, not a desktop's doors; each already reads one source. mobile-nav's «+» tab (the brief's mobile-nav.js:336) reads the table.
- **Gates:** fast test-desktop-switch ⑧ (the table: one order, each rule, the tier draws never decides, doorItems / sheetItems, zh + ja) + ⑨ THE SURFACE CENSUS (`_deskItems` run on its own source text for the preview / a compact row / the sheet / the tab over the first / a middle / the last / the only desktop: exactly the table's doors, its labels, a shut one greyed with its why; the acts on the manager's handlers through the guard; the builder's call sites named; no door word left in a surface file; every «+» and switching row on the table; RED CONTROL the base's sheet long press fails on every desktop — no Move up / Move down, «Rename» for 「Rename…」); heavy test-duo-layout ⑧ (951: the long press = the table's doors, Desk B last ⇒ Move down greyed with its why; 375×812: a middle desktop's four doors open, the first's Move up / the last's Move down greyed WITH its why inside 44 px rows, the last's Move up FROM THE PHONE reorders, the sheet comes back in the new order, a reload keeps it), test-mobile-gaps #7 (the tab's long press = the table's doors); test-desktop-small-chrome ⑬ / ⑱ unchanged and green (the 951 compact row's menu: Rename… · Delete · Move down).
- **Round 2 (主开发's acceptance of 8c680dcf — a chain on it, no squash; each fixup with a RED control run on 8c680dcf):** ① a gone desktop's doors on the DESK tier were an EMPTY popover (`draw` 'off' for every shut item ⇒ `doorItems` `[]`, showContextMenu has no empty guard) — the table now leaves a shut door out of a desk menu only while its desktop is HERE (`i >= 0`), a gone one draws every door greyed with its why on every tier; ### vault-totp-add — THE VAULT KIND REGISTRY + its census, then 添加… ▸ 两步验证… (the q-047 L2 the owner found missing 2026-10-26: 「我似乎不能添加两步验证在vault里」; amendment 1, the owner: 「你需要更系统化地方案管理代码中的各种细节，这种不是应该有个统一的注册表之类的吗」) (BUILD lane on bbca26b4 = int358)
- **The gap:** L1 (vault-totp) shipped the store, `POST /api/vault/totp` with its preview, the row extras and the rail category; L2 (the add dialog) was never built, and nothing kept the seven places that list a vault kind in agreement (the rail's PURPOSES, purposeOf, the registerVaultAdd doors, the row extras modules, vibespace-vault's verbs, the routes, the kb-features lines).

### chat-needs-you-card — what a conversation asks of you is a card in its chat, answerable where it appears (the owner 2026-10-26: «这个界面里是不是应该有个地方能让我看到需要approve？» — a channel watch's approval sat only in the tray)

- **The cause:** a For-you item reached its conversation's window only as the title-bar mini inbox badge (2.369.169 — cut in a maximized / tabbed title bar) and the top-bar tray; the chat drew S1's helper asks and the permission card, nothing else. A channel watch / access request is filed under the group key 'channels' — nothing on the item named the asking conversation, so not even the mini inbox counted it.
- **THE FOR-YOU ACTION REGISTRY — PURE src/foryou-actions.js (amendment 1, 主开发 07:5xZ — the owner's registry law «这种不是应该有个统一的注册表之类的吗»; imports nothing; test-architecture's PURE set):** ONE row per action type (24) — `{type, identity, producer (+ builtIn), waits, answer: card | buttons | reply, card: row | inbox-window | none, handled, chat (+ owner), kind, cli: {bin, verb, line: filed | wait | own}, scope}`; DERIVED from it: `ACTION_IDENTITY` (src/user-todos.js — its literal table is gone), `WAIT_ACTIONS` (src/attention-model.js), `CARD_ACTION_TYPES` + `ANSWER_ACTION_TYPES` (src/inbox-reply.js) — byte-identical sets but the audit's fix: `vault-rotate` merges by its `entry` (two keys' same-worded suggestions were ONE item, the second replacing the first's action); `vault-use-failed` is a row (in no table before; it merges by its text on purpose — head + cause). The rest of the module is the brief's row 1 (folded in from src/conversation-needs.js): `needsOf(items, keys)` / `recordsOf` — sessionKey OR the new `about` ∈ keys, a row's `chat` decides (S1's `helper-ask`, the permission card's `main-ask`, the proposal / API / wall cards keep their own chat card — never drawn twice); `placementOf(item, transcript)` — named (the tool card whose RESULT names the item or its request id) › tool (the row's CLI ≤ 15 min before the filing, 2 s skew) › turn (the record at the filing) › end (an open card is never hidden in history not loaded; a resolved one there is not drawn); `chipWords` · `settledWords` · `filedLine`.
- **scripts/id-branch-census.mjs gains the `foryou` family** (its ids ARE the registry's types, the registry its owner) as a RATCHET: 96 branch lines in 18 files measured today (`--seed-family foryou`, a new option that seeds a family the baseline lacks and refuses one it has); test-architecture §78 lets them only fall. test-approval-census's door regex reads a CONSTANT type too (src/main-ask.js, src/browser-takeover-request.js) and its MERGE-CELL pins read the registry rows.

### desktop-small — the desktop tier at a small mouse viewport: a release never buries a window, the taskbar overflows visibly and its desktops fold, menus stay inside the screen (BUILD on cc7d4e5f = 2.369.356; the owner: «桌面档应该测试屏幕尺寸比较小的时候什么地方不可用来修复一下», «userW有一大堆桌面，屏幕尺寸小了之后桌面就堆积在一起了»)
- **The evidence:** /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/desktop-small-usability/report.md — a naive-user walk + an independent verifier at 951×585 / 1024×600 / 1100×700 / 1280×640 (mouse, sidebar open): P2-1…P2-6, P3-1…P3-3, four unverified claims, twelve suggested fences. Every finding was re-measured first on the base with a lane probe (a scratch hub + stub chat claude + headless Chrome at the four viewports): all six P2 and three P3 reproduced at all four sizes; of the unverified claims the cascade reproduced (three Files windows on an empty desk opened on ONE spot at ≤ 1100 px, 30 px apart on one top at 1280 — 0–4 % of the earlier title bars visible), the toast-over-menu claim reproduced in a milder form (the desktop toast — anchored beside the tray's For-you button, z 100000 over every menu — stood over the desktop menu's lower rows and on the bottom-right composer; its body passes presses through, so «Delete» still took the click here, but its ✕ / action buttons would not), the model dropdown in a lower Quad cell did NOT (bounded by --dd-room and scrolling since phone-refusal-wrap P2-17 — 15 rows in a 157–215 px panel, the first row hittable), and Files at 320×195 keeps its 24 px head buttons (a squeezed path box, not a defect).
- **P2-1 a window buried under the taskbar.** `_snapToGrid` snapped only to the cell UNDER the pointer; over the taskbar there is none, so the free drag's place stood (1024×600 Quad: y 553 of a 556 px workspace, 2 px of the bar left); the tile minimized it, a second click restored it to the same place, the window list only raised it. PURE (src/lib/drag-end.js — the ONE door): `releasePoint` (a grid release outside every cell is judged just inside the workspace ⇒ the nearest cell), `releaseBox` (EVERY release keeps RELEASE_KEEP 80×32 of the title bar inside — window.js `_keepReachable` at the end of the title-bar drag's last drop branch and the tab tear-off's, plus every `_reflowWindows` as this client's fit, never captured; `_barKeep` adds the window's own border so it is 80×32 of the BAR), `reachable` / `insideBox` (THE RECOVERY: `revealWindow` — every door that names a window: its tile, its window-list row, the palette, a card — brings an unreachable window WHOLLY inside, witnessed as the user's act, its grid bounds captured; the focused window's tile minimizes only while `wm.isReachable(id)`). ### passkey-sink — P2 of the custom browser kernel: on a kernel with `webauthn` the passkey ceremony sinks to VibeSpace — the kernel transports (`VibeSpace.webauthnRequest` / `webauthnAnswer`), VibeSpace signs with the sealed key; UV = the owner decided THIS ceremony; no OS / GPM authenticator ever (BUILD lane on 1cdf214b = browser-surfaces, int356 pick 3; docs/design-custom-browser-plugin.zh.md §3 rewritten as built)
- **The switch (src/server/browser-dialogs.js):** `features` lists `webauthn` ⇒ `armPasskey` returns at once (no hook, no virtual authenticator — both stay for standard Chrome and a surfaces-only kernel); the tab is armed when `VibeSpace.enable` is taken (`none`, never `unknown`); `onDesktop` false. ONE record: `VibeSpace.webauthnRequest` → PURE `PK.kernelEvent` → the same `applyEvent` start (+ `kernel`: ids, `op` over `kind`, the hash, challenge, clientDataJSON, key types, UV asked, exclude, user.id); the webauthn SURFACE is the held card only (P1's row gains its answerer `sink: 'webauthn'`, PURE `SF.sinkOf`): in `w.surf`, never `w.open`, never a browser-surface card; its close ends a pending record; an orphan surface (no request — a reconnect) is cancelled after `passkeyOrphanMs`.
- **The gate:** PURE `WA.requestVerdict` first (rpMatches injected; the clientDataJSON, when handed, must hash to the hash we sign and name this type / origin / challenge ⇒ `webauthn_rp_mismatch`; no ES256 ⇒ `webauthn_alg_unsupported`), then `PS.gateVerdict` unchanged, then `PS.kernelFlags` (UV only for the card's once / always, the one-use grant, a takeover; policy yes ⇒ UV 0; UV required on an automatic release ⇒ the card; BE / BS never).
- **The signer (NEW PURE src/webauthn-sign.js, node crypto handed in):** authenticatorData, ES256 assertion (DER, P-256 only), makeCredential (32 random id bytes, COSE key, attestation `none`), a canonical CBOR encoder (uint / negative / bytes / text / array / map), the re-check. Get: `PS.signOrder` → unseal ONE key → bump + reconcile WRITTEN before the answer (`pkWrite` answers whether it reached the disk; no write ⇒ no signature). Create: the pair made on the server, SEALED before the answer (a lock ⇒ `webauthn_key_locked`, never a key we cannot keep); a page gone by then ⇒ the row dropped again.
- **The use law:** every signature / new key = `vaultUse('passkeys', {by, door: 'passkey', conv}, {purpose})` — the wiring hands `vault.noteUse` (the ONE writer); the receipt stays on the record. Cancel = `VibeSpace.cancelSurface` ⇒ the page sees NotAllowedError (Q4, the peer's answer); `PK.cancelText({kernel})` says so. REASONS + `webauthn_alg_unsupported` · `webauthn_rp_mismatch` · `webauthn_key_locked` (its sentence in the vault rule's words — the user was told, a person unlocks it on this instance's page, never ask them).
- **The fake kernel (scripts/fixtures/fake-kernel.mjs, extended):** `triggerWebAuthn` (the peer stub's field names) → `{request, answerPromise}`, `webauthnAnswer` (`no_such_request`), cancel / any surface answer ⇒ NotAllowedError, `abortWebAuthn`, `mode.features`.
- **Gates:** NEW test-webauthn-sign 37 (fast, 28 ms) · test-browser-passkey 151 (⑧ +43: the kernel road over the fake kernel; 1.4 s) · test-browser-passkey-store 38 (⑦) · test-browser-surfaces 133 (the answerer row) · test-vault-law 73 (⑪: a REAL vault + the engine's noteUse; the locked vault ⇒ webauthn_key_locked) · test-key-file-law 121 (RANDOM32 row: the credential id) · test-vault-words 11 (the locked sentence's row) · test-architecture 853 · i18n-check 9746 / 9746 · the whole fast tier · heavy test-browser-passkey-chrome 46 (K1–K5 + three mutant controls RED: UV always true · the count not advanced · the request not re-checked; 1 SKIP = the installed agent-browser is 0.38.2, as on the base) · test-browser-mediation-chrome 125 (unchanged).
- **Open:** `excludeCredentials` matching a kept row ⇒ the spec's InvalidStateError (kept in `req.exclude`, a new key is still made today); the peer's own stub not run (VIBESPACE_CUSTOM_BROWSER_PLUGIN unset).

### browser-login — P3 of the custom browser kernel: on a kernel with `credentials` the password manager is VibeSpace's vault — the kernel reports a page's login forms and fills what the vault holds (the agent never sees a value); an account the agent registers goes THROUGH the vault and is saved automatically with its provenance; a password the agent typed itself is saved too, marked `agent-typed` (BUILD lane on 6dcf2b5e = passkey-sink, int358 pick 6; the owner's D3 yes / D5 reversed; docs/design-custom-browser-plugin.zh.md §4 rewritten as built)
- **The entry (NEW PURE src/browser-login.js):** a vault ENTRY `web-login:<origin>#<user>` (never a STORE_KEYS row; the engine's SECRET_RE gains the same shape as a second anchored alternative), the sealed record `{v:1, origin, username, password, totpName?, createdAt, by, source: owner|vault-minted|agent-typed, strength: generated|unknown, createdIn?, submittedAt, pending?, previous?, lastUsedAt}`; THE ONE WRITER = NEW ORCH src/server/browser-logins.js (`writeEntry` → secretPut, the provenance word as the box's `kind`); every fill a use through the engine's `noteUse` (door `browser-login`, purpose «sign in at <origin>», a receipt; a refused grant a line too).
- **The grant:** src/grant-model.js DOORS + `browser-login`, resource `<origin>#<user>` · `<origin>#*` · `*` (NEW `RESOURCE_SHAPES` — another shape is `bad_resource` at the write, `unknown_shape` at the read); the three scopes' rows ADD through `GM.admits`; the owner's 「用于…」 in the Vault window → `grants.set / remove` (§97 (a) reader + (c) writer rows).
- **Detect / fill (src/server/browser-dialogs.js, the login road):** `VibeSpace.credentialFormDetected` → PURE `formOf` (fieldId kernel-private — Q5; each password field's `constraints` — Q5b; labels / names / rects never kept) → the tab's `e.forms` (≤ 8, a new document clears them). `vibespace-browser login [<origin>] [--user <u>] [--submit]` (OURS_PAGE; passes a held dialog) → `POST /api/agent/browser/login` → `fillLogin` → `planFill` → PURE `fillVerdict` (form · THE PHISHING RULE: the page's own origin, its frame's equal, https / localhost http, entries of that exact origin only · one entry, else `login_ambiguous` · the grant · the vault) → `VibeSpace.fillCredential {surfaceId, values, expectedOrigin, submit}` (the kernel's stale_origin ⇒ `login_phishing`) → the values dropped → `{ok, mode, origin, user, filled, submitted, receipt, text}` through the belt (`loginText(` — the peer-text census's new door). D3: a paired `totp:` entry's code is filled (`vault-totp.codeForLogin`, no second grant). A held http-auth surface is answered the same way (its credential answer). P1's credential row: `sink: 'credentials'` (its line names the verb); webauthn's sink is matched by name.
- **Register / save (D5 reversed):** `login --new-user <u> --generate` ⇒ PURE `generatePassword(constraints, rng)` (20, every class, the site's min / max and pattern — the charset ladder; a cap under 12 or a pattern none satisfies ⇒ `password_rules_unsupported`) → the entry SEALED (`vault-minted`, `pending: register`) BEFORE the kernel gets a byte → filled; `--generate` on a change-password form = a change (the old value in `previous`). `VibeSpace.credentialSubmitted` → PURE `saveVerdict` (new · same · update · agent-typed · owner-card · none) → the ONE writer → ONE For-you notice (`kind: notice`, i18n en / zh / ja); a person's own sign-in in a takeover ⇒ the save-login card (`POST /api/browser/logins/cards/:id/approve|reject`, its password held only until answered); a locked vault holds a submission until the next unlock; the flood guard saves ≤ 6 new agent-typed logins a site in 10 minutes (a page inventing submissions never floods the vault).
- **The Vault window:** PURPOSES + `web-logins`「网站登录」; the row `<user> · <site>` with its provenance (by you · agent 铸造 · agent 见过明文 + rotate); 显示 = the password; 删除; 添加 → 网站登录…; 用于… (src/lib/vault-login-row.js; `GET|POST /api/vault/web-logins`, `DELETE …/:name`, `POST …/grants|ungrant`). The output belt masks a web login's PASSWORD (not its JSON).

### phone-back-reload — a back on the phone never costs a load: the boot rebuilds the sentinel a discarded / history-loaded tab stands on, the 「再返回一次退出」 exit leaves past VibeSpace's older entries in ONE go(-n), the tab's navigation diary (+ an automatic incident when a back still costs a load), the stale-tab notice (FIX on 2.369.357 fbaf6988; the owner on an Android phone, Chrome, the hub over the tailnet, 96 open For-you items: the back button reloads VibeSpace — the loading screen, then home)
- **Why the first probe saw nothing:** it pressed `history.back()`. Chrome's back-button logic (NavigationController::GoBack with the history-manipulation intervention's skip) runs only for the BROWSER's back; the lane measured with CDP Alt+Left — the path Android's back takes (lane mobile-back-guard's finding). Chrome 154, headless and headed on Xvfb, phone emulation 382×580, a throwaway server from a scratch copy, each document numbered by an init script.
- **H1 cross-document traversal — REPRODUCED, three roads.** (a) A tab DISCARDED (chrome://discards' Urgent Discard, a debug page — Local State `internal_only_uis_enabled`; DevTools must be off the tab, and the tab comes back as a NEW target) and shown again: the restored document reports `document.wasDiscarded` true, navigation type `back_forward`, `history.state` {vs:1}, `navigation.entries()` both entries `sameDocument: true` — and the FIRST back (closing a window) was a cross-document load: bootStep had KEPT the sentinel over the dead document's page entry. (b) A renderer KILLED (Page.crash — Android's low-memory kill) and reloaded: navigation type `reload`, `history.state` null, `history.length` +1 (the boot pushed a second sentinel), the old page entry correctly `sameDocument: false`; the window back stayed same-document, the 「再返回一次退出」 exit LOADED the older entry (bfcache on or off). (c) A second load of the app in the tab (`location.href = '/?session=…'` over an earlier document): the exit landed on the older document — a full load with bfcache off, its cache restore with it on. A tab-start variant (the app the tab's first entry) needs the named load (below).
- **NOT the cause (measured):** `location.reload()` (the stale-tab path), the browser's reload, two reloads — entries `S*S`, the next back a same-document popstate; a cross-site previous entry — the exit lands on the other site. H2 dropped go(1): go(1) lands in 2–3 ms (8 of 8 window backs); with a patched history.go that drops it, the 500 ms belt pushes (511 ms) and the next back with no tap since stays same-document — on this Chrome; the diary now records every go1 (ms, or landed 0 + the push) so an Android export answers it there. H3 stale-tab reload: a scratch server at a version the bundle never matches ⇒ ONE reload (the per-tab sessionStorage stamp), then two reconnects SILENT; the back after it same-document ⇒ bounded already, only the silence was wrong.
- **H4 Chrome's documented behaviour (read, not guessed):** the Chromium history-manipulation-intervention doc — only the browser's back/forward buttons skip entries, never `history.back()`; an entry becomes skippable when its document creates another entry without a user activation, an activation un-skips it, all same-document entries share one state; all entries skippable ⇒ CanGoBack false (Android: back closes the tab). The Page Lifecycle doc — the browser freezes and discards hidden tabs at its discretion, a discarded page must be reloaded to be used, NO event fires at a discard, `document.wasDiscarded` says it at load. Close watchers (blink-dev intent to ship: Android's back closes a `<dialog>` / popover / CloseWatcher first, user-activation gated) — VibeSpace has none (no showModal / popover / CloseWatcher in src/lib), so nothing there applies. Predictive back: no Chrome documentation on same-document entries found; not measured.
- **The fix (PURE src/lib/back-guard.js + src/lib/mobile-back.js):** `bootStep` 'rebuild' — standing on a sentinel when wasDiscarded, the type is back_forward, or the Navigation API says the entry below is another document: `history.replaceState(null, '')` (the entry becomes this document's page entry) then the sentinel `push()`; a reload with the entry below same-document keeps. `exitPlan({ current, block, length })` over `navigation.entries()` — the contiguous same-origin block (主开发's rule: the browser exposes no other entry, so the page's index IS how many older entries stand below): null ⇒ the arm stays on the page's entry as before; else the arm re-arms AT ONCE and the next back inside 2 s (a popstate now) leaves with ONE `history.go(-(current + 1))`; the whole tab VibeSpace's (`history.length === block`) ⇒ `go(-current)` to the first entry — ONE load the diary names (`leave load 1`), no incident (主开发's rule); a go(-n) that did nothing (an entry outside the block was a FORWARD one) ⇒ 700 ms later the same named load. `backCostLoad` at boot — back_forward right after the previous document's rows (< 5 s), none a 'leave' ⇒ `app.autoCaptureIncident('a back press cost a page load', …, { toastKey })`, once per tab per 30 min. The rebuild's push without a tap was kept (never skipped) on every road measured.
- **The diary (NEW src/lib/nav-log.js):** 60 rows in sessionStorage `vibespace.navLog` — per tab, surviving every load in it; rows boot / pop / go1 / leave / hide / show / stale / cost / capture with a per-document id; never a URL (test-incident-recorder ⑥'s navNote census); every incident snapshot carries it (`navLog`). The stale-tab step (PURE `staleTabStep` in boot-ladder.js): ONE reload per server version per tab, then ONE notice («This tab still runs VibeSpace {old} after its one reload for {new} …», a warn toast), never a loop.
- **Census fallout:** test-record-clear-census H1 — the client's history writes are now exactly `history.pushState({ vs: 1 }, '')` + `history.replaceState(null, '')` (its control extended), storage rows `nav-log.js NAV_LOG_KEY` (telemetry) and `app.js noticeKey` (marker); test-boot-phase's stale-tab wait pin follows the line's new shape; test-back-guard §4 pins the ONE replaceState.
- **Chrome suite notes (test-mobile-back-chrome G/H):** ONE Chrome with `--disable-features=BackForwardCache`, `--window-size=382,580` (a discarded tab's restored page boots before any emulation reaches the new target — the window makes it a phone) and Local State for chrome://discards; attaching DevTools to a discarded, unloaded tab never finishes its handshake — show it first, attach after; the RED bundle = esbuild of the scratch tree with mobile-back.js's two anchors replaced (the base rule), served by swapping public/bundle.js (the index stamps `?v=<mtime>` per request); a capture's toast can be gone from the screen — judged from the toast history; a target created at about:blank keeps that entry (the tab-start leg creates it at the app's URL). Run by hand the suite needs VIBESPACE_SUITE_BUDGET_MS (the default 300 s budget fires before G ends); under the gate its row's 900 s holds the 480 s cap.
- **Not touched:** the phone home's boot rule (foryou-honest's lane).
- **Acceptance round 2 (主开发, two reviewers + two skeptics per finding; the second commit on 8449a450).** (1) MAJOR, reproduced: `history.go()` moves by JOINT-history steps and one iframe link followed inside an older VibeSpace document adds a step `navigation.entries()` never shows — tab [prev, V-old page, V-old sentinel, +1 iframe step, V-page, V-sentinel]: entries current 2 ⇒ go(-3) landed on V-old's page (a load; the probe's own CDP history list). Fix: the exit writes an INTENT (sessionStorage `vibespace.exitIntent`: time, hop, 8 chars of the left entry's random key, «below») before each go(); src/client.js calls `continueExit()` first — PURE `exitHop` answers hop when the load is back_forward, under 10 s, and `navigation.activation.from` names that entry (measured: the landed document's from key = V-page's page entry); the document never builds the App and goes on with ONE go(-(current + 1)), each a diary `hop` row; no `beforeunload` 700 ms later ⇒ once more, to 3 hops, then it stays (a `hop stay` row, the App boots — ONE named load); a person's tap or key, a boot without back_forward, or another way in drops the intent. Measured on the way: a go() onto a page whose response takes 3 s fires `beforeunload` 4 ms after the call and `pagehide` 3012 ms after — round 1's fallback judged by pagehide and would have fired a second go() in the middle of a real exit; now `beforeunload` judges (out of range, neither fires), listened to only around the go() — a first cut that held it for the page's life made the suite's reload leg read the OLD page's `app` (a page with a beforeunload listener makes each reload wait for it). The cross-document `navigate` event does not fire for such a traversal (measured), so it cannot judge. (2) MINOR: `backCostLoad` filed for a FORWARD press after the stay arm's exit (measured: one incident). It now takes `came` from `navigation.activation` (from.index > entry.index = back; no from = another site's page — measured null after a forward from the data: page; the discarded tab's first back: from = its sentinel, a back with no `pop` row, so «require a pop row» alone would have silenced the owner's own road) and cuts a back to 'other' when `from`'s key is not the previous document's last pagehide `ek`; without the API a non-stay-arm `pop` must be there. (3) MINOR: the stale-tab stamp is written as the reload fires; `staleTabStep` gains `pending` (`this._staleReloadAt`) — test-boot-phase replays the app's own method over fake timers: two reconnects 300 ms apart ⇒ `reload@1 RELOAD@1 notice@2` (round 1: the notice on the OLD page before its reload). (4) ACCEPTED COST, documented: the rebuild drops the tab's forward entries. (5) The chrome suite run bare assumes its ci.mjs row's budget (900 s, said at start) with its own 720 s ceiling. (6) The report's isolated-run row now names the subset run from the scratch copy. Correction: round 1's report gave test-incident-recorder as 40 — it is 39 (the same count on 8449a450's own tree).
- **Acceptance round 3 (主开发, two reviewers + skeptics, one in real Chrome 154; the third commit on 87331d62).** (1) MAJOR, reproduced with the back/forward cache off and on: a hop's go() that `beforeunload` announced and that is then CANCELLED (the previous entry answers 204, the load is stopped) fires neither pagehide nor pageshow — round 2's hop document waited on `leaving` for ever: the splash, no App, its beforeunload listener held, the intent kept, a tap ignored. Every exit go() now goes through `watchedGo(n, { nothing, cancelled, input })`: beforeunload starts a 3 s bound (`GONE_WAIT_MS`) and with no pagehide by then the page STAYS (`hop stay why cancelled`, the App boots — measured 3.0–3.1 s after the hop's go()); any tap or key before the page is gone stays at once; pagehide and each outcome remove every listener it added; the exit's own cancelled go() drops the intent (`leave why cancelled`); a page slower than 3 s still leaves. (2) MAJOR: NO KEY, NO HOP — `exitHop` clears unless `navigation.activation.from`'s key IS the intent's (undefined / '' fail closed) and without the API the exit writes no intent (round 1's one named load at most); reproduced in Chrome 154 with activation removed: round 2 hopped a forward press back out. (3) SHOULD: a persisted pageshow asks the intent as a load would (`shownStep` — measured: a cache restore updates activation, type traverse) and goes on when it is the exit's; Chrome 154 LOADED the hop road's older document in all four builds of the road (cross-site / srcdoc iframe × the newer page by script / browser-side; the cache names ConflictingBrowsingInstance), so the gate is test-back-guard's fake world, RED from round 2. (4) SHOULD: `backCostLoad` without activation is round 1's rule as shipped again (no leave / hop row) — round 2's pop-row rule silenced the discard road (it has no pop row) and the stay arm's back that loads an older document; a forward press files there too, the accepted cost. (5) SHOULD: test-incident-recorder ⑥'s privacy census PARSES (acorn) every navNote( / exitIntentWrite( under src/ — both rows of a ternary, shorthand keys, spreads, aliases, each value read for a url / title / text / location; seven planted shapes red, round 2's regex passes two of them. NEW heavy test-exit-hop-chrome: Chrome twice (the cache off, then on), ① a 204 ② a stopped load ③ no activation, each on round 2's rules (RED) then the shipped ones, ④ the cache-on note.
- **Acceptance round 4 (主开发, one reviewer + skeptics; the fourth commit on 6786bf26).** Measured first on Chrome 154 with the back/forward cache off and on (a pending cross-document traversal from a page entry with the sentinel above it): a same-document traversal ABORTS a pending one — `navigation.forward()` aborts it and lands on the sentinel; `history.go(1)` aborts it too, but Chrome counts it from the PENDING entry, so it lands nowhere —; a `pushState` aborts nothing, and the document the late commit lands on names the pushed entry as its `navigation.activation.from`; `window.stop()` aborts no traversal (it commits as if nothing happened). (1) MAJOR: the 3 s bound dropped the intent while the traversal was only SLOW (the older document's HTML at 3.5 s) — that document then booted with no intent and filed nothing, the owner's silent load. A stay now SUSPENDS the go() (`linger`): the intent kept — dropped only at a tap or key on the stayed page or when its 10 s window ends —, the late commit's pagehide writes `leave slow <ms>` / `hop n slow <ms>` and keys the intent to the entry the page leaves from, so the landing document goes on; one that lands past the window boots and files ONE incident «a slow exit» (NEW PURE `slowExit`; the cost row `why slow`). (2) MAJOR: a stay re-arms with a NEW sentinel (`push()` — never a traversal, which would abort a go() that may still be pending), diary `rearm why cancelled`: the next back is the 「再返回一次退出」 toast, not the browser's own back onto the older document. (3) MINOR: a tap while the go() is pending aborts it by the step onto the same-document entry above (`abortGo` = `navigation.forward()`; on the exit's page that step IS the re-arm, `rearm why input`); window.stop() is not called (measured useless); when the commit wins the race (`leave why input`, then `leave slow`) the kept intent makes the landing document go on. (4) MINOR: the late commit is told by its pagehide (`leave slow <ms>` after the stay's own `leave why cancelled`). Measured on the way (the first suite run red on it, the cache off and on): the document a traversal commits onto after a pushState made while it was pending gets a Navigation API that lost its own place — `currentEntry.index` -1 (its `entries()` end with a copy of it where the pushed entry stands) and both of `navigation.activation`'s indexes -1 —, so its hop found no entries (hop stay why api) and its arrival read as another site's page (no incident); the wiring finds its entry by key (`indexIn`) and reads both indexes -1 as a way in that cannot be told (`came` ''). NEW heavy test-exit-slow-chrome (Chrome twice; the Fetch domain holds the older document's HTML; ⑤ 3.5 s, ⑥ 12 s, ⑦ a 204 then a back, ⑧ a tap while pending — each on round 3's rules RED, then shipped); test-exit-hop-chrome's round-2 swaps follow the moved lines and its ①② judge the intent kept.
- **CI .358 — the renderer-kill road HUNG on the runner's Chrome 156 (ci358-reds; test-mobile-back-chrome WATCHDOG at 720 s in G, both tries, «waiting on: CDP Runtime.evaluate (552 s)»):** on Chrome 156 `Page.crash` kills the renderer LATE — Inspector.targetCrashed 6.2–7.0 s after it (measured on Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.47; 154: well inside the road's 1.5 s sleep) — so the road's `Page.reload` started a load the crash then killed: never answered, the tab left dead, and the next unbounded Runtime.evaluate waited for ever. The road now reloads once Inspector.targetCrashed has arrived (bounded 30 s — a renderer that never dies is a named ✗ with what the page said) and EVERY CDP call is bounded (45 s, the method named). Two Chrome-156 facts in G: a discard KEEPS the tab's document (chrome://discards' row «loaded», 154 «unloaded»), so the pre-fix back loads nothing there — G1 RED says which discard it saw and judges that; and the untouched RELOADED page's window back was skipped by Chrome's back-button intervention once in two runs (the shipped wiring's back loaded the older VibeSpace entry: back_forward, came back, a cost row) — the road now touches the reloaded page like every other road (B1 keeps the untouched case). The product's roads are proven on 156: the renderer kill (reload, push, state null), the exit in ONE traversal; `VS_CPU_THROTTLE`.

### engine-distribution — P4 of the custom browser kernel: a plugin installed from a PRIVATE git repository with the `plugin-git` credential (files only, shredded); the kernel downloaded by VibeSpace into `kernelPath(id)` with a receipt; its version MEASURED once; the fleet's plugin installed at boot at its pinned sha and pre-trusted (D2) (BUILD lane on 77800e7d = browser-login, int358 pick 8; docs/design-custom-browser-plugin.zh.md §5 rewritten as built)
- **The credential row:** `plugin-git` in src/integration-registry.js — host · username (optional, empty = x-access-token) · token (secret) · deployKey (secret, `multiline` ⇒ the card's textarea). Validators gitHost / sshPrivateKey (a passphrase-protected key refused by name). clusterEnv + the presets' integrations.json. Test reachability = git ls-remote (the loader registers the runner over a repository it knows on that host). Consumer src/server/plugin-install.js (no `wiredIn`: it lands with its consumer). `groupOf`: the installer's rows are Plugins rows (`PLUGIN_INSTALL_CONSUMER`).
- **The git road (src/server/plugin-install.js):**
  - `gitSpecOf` (a tag / branch / full sha ref; `#ref` still read) and `credentialFor(spec, null | 'plugin-git' | 'auto')` through the store's `resolveIntegration` — refused `plugin_git_credential` when unset, the vault locked, for another host, or the wrong kind.
  - `credentialFiles`: a 0700 `.cred-*` folder; https = 0600 token + user + a 0700 askpass that cats them; ssh = a 0600 key named by `GIT_SSH_COMMAND -i … IdentitiesOnly BatchMode StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new`.
  - `gitRun` is one child per step (init · `fetch --depth 1 -c credential.helper= -- <url> <ref|HEAD>` · checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD · rev-parse): serviceEnv(egress) + named switches, its timeout. §94 FIXED row.
  - `shredFile` (src/secret-file.js) on every way out. `GIT_CODES` by name; `plugin_tree_rejected` for every manifest / tree refusal; `testCredential` (ls-remote).
- **The loader (src/server/plugin-loader.js):**
  - `install({ref, credential, by})` records `{ref, sha, credential, by}`; a ref change is a source change.
  - D2: a fleet install of the id fleet.json names, at a FULL sha the clone arrived at, gets `trust {by:'fleet', sha, contentHash}` + enabled. `fleetTrustHolds` lets it hold only while all three still hold — a tag is never the anchor (主开发's pin, 2026-10-25: v0.1.2 = 7085e75f…).
  - `trustedBy` / `install.{ref, sha, by}` in `list()`, `installRecord(id)`, `fleet` on GET manifests; the route takes `ref` and `credential` (`plugin-git` only).
- **The kernel (PURE src/engine-kernel.js + ORCH src/server/engine-distribution.js):**
  - Inputs: kernel.json's verdict (the platform layout merged over the top one; the fleet's url + sha256 win), design 004's two hard rows factored into `downloadHardRows` (buildCompatVerdict asks it too, words unchanged).
  - Steps: https fetch with every hop https → sha256 → a LIST pass over node's zlib zstd + a streaming tar reader (ustar / GNU long names / pax) with every entry and the shape judged before a byte is written → the unpacked total vs the disk → extract → requiredFiles → `install-receipt.json {sha256 (the archive's), bytes (chrome's size), verifiedAt, version, archiveBytes, binarySha256}` → ONE rename.
  - `measure` = `--version` once (5 s, serviceEnv, §94 FIXED row) keyed by the receipt, on `data/browser-engines.json`.

- **Measured / declared:**
  - PURE `engineAnswerVerdict` takes the kernel side's optional `declaredVersion` / `integrity`; `engineChoiceVerdict` reads measured › reported › declared.
  - The keeper measures before the first launch, so the record's `browserChoice.version` is the measured one.

It installs when the record has no such id or a different source / ref, never a re-pull. `preinstall` ⇒ the kernel right away. Helm `customBrowser.preinstall` → fleet.json `browserEngine.preinstall` (parseBrowserEngineFact), the values documenting the ref as a FULL sha and the plugin-git integrations entry.

Measured on Node 24.12: `end(cb)` answers at 'finish' with no error, and a close-time failure comes after it as 'error' then 'close' — so round 2's writer landed a file whose close failed (the owner's data/ is an NFS bind; close-to-open reports ENOSPC / EIO at close). After the close it compares the size on disk with the bytes written. Injected through the stream's `fs` option: a close-time ENOSPC on an entry or on `.part` ⇒ `disk`, nothing landed; a close that cuts the file to 699 of 700 bytes ⇒ refused by name. The copy that settles at 'finish' lands both.

A put-back that fails leaves the record with NO kernel (`engine_kernel_aside`; the old record kept as `aside` and restored with it), ONE For-you notice, the card's own line. So does a landing whose final rename and put-back both fail. An empty place (ENOENT) seen by measure drops the record's kernel. RED: a boot without the put-back, and the round-2 landing record — both say «installed» over an empty place.

Fast: real git under the child's env reads no HOME sslCAInfo, and the hub's GIT_SSL_CAINFO reaches every child. Heavy, real TLS: a CA named only in HOME is refused on the certificate; through the door the clone works, and the copy whose door lacks the names fails. The gitBin shim is gone; the suite uses the door. Recorded in design §5.1.

### browser-display-holders — a browser the agents hold is «held» for its display window too: ✕ closes only the view, a person's Stop is never healed, the toast tells the truth (FIX, the owner 2026-10-25 «可以»)
- **The report:** ✕ on «W8N3 · Screeps live - Google Chrome» (profile personal-life's display, two conversations attached) said «Asked … to close — press ✕ again within 5 s to stop it»; Chrome's own «close N tabs?» sheet (invisible) kept it; the second ✕ stopped it; the journal: `[desktop] da-… stopped (user)` → 4 s later `its Chrome exited under a holder (seen by the tick) — started again on the attach road`, twice. Two notions of held never met: the window's `lease` (lane E's app lease) null ⇒ PURE `outerCloseVerdict` took A2's ask-then-Stop road; `healAttach` judged a holder + the budget, never who stopped it. .354's wording pick (e31e45ef, «no agent is using it…») was false for this case — its line is untouched here: the verdict now reaches that toast only with no holder and no lease.
- **Holders on the record (src/server/desktop-app-keeper.js — the ONE writer):** `view(rec)` lays `{profileId, holders, userStopped?}` over a `display-for-browser` record only (an app's view byte-identical) from the browser keeper's `displayHoldersOf(profileId, displayId)` (PURE `B.attachedHolders(leasesOn(id))` — one per conversation, never the person's Browse-yourself row; read through `leasesOn`, no new `reg.leases` site); `browserHoldersMoved()` (called from the browser keeper's `notify()`, i.e. every registry commit: attach / detach / drop / re-judge / the stamp) broadcasts ONE `desktop-apps-updated` when a `holders|stamp` digest moved — the seen-digest changes only there, so a GET in between never swallows a move.

A user-held app keeps A2 unchanged.
- **A person's stop is a fact (src/server/browser-keeper.js):** the desktop keeper's `stop(id, {why: 'user'})` of a live browser display calls `onBrowserDisplayStop` listeners BEFORE `machine.stop` (measured: the machine writes `stoppedBy` only after its teardown; Chrome dies with its X — a tick in between read a crash). `userStoppedDisplay` stamps `rec.userStopped = {at, by: 'user', displayId}`, emits ONE `browser-user-stopped` lease event `{profileId, label, holders}`; `healAttach` refuses while it stands (journal «NOT started again (user-stopped, never a heal)», before the budget), `healBrowser` too unless a verb's force; `markDaemonGone` writes `stoppedBy: 'user'`, `lastError: null`, «you stopped its display window — the next browser command starts it again». The Desktop list (src/lib/desktop-picker.js) keeps PURE `userStoppedHeld` rows: «You stopped it · N conversations start it again when they next use it» (zh/ja; disabled, no Open / Close).

### draft-focus-guard — a draft another client saved never replaces what you are typing (FIX, B-b0fa — the naive-user walk 2026-10-25, report §P1-2, re-run by an independent verifier)
- **The case:** two clients on one conversation; B's 300 ms autosave landed in A's FOCUSED box mid-sentence («oko好，退款那条也改成同样的策略\nk» was sent); a×8 / b×8 interleaved left one «a» in both boxes; B's own pending autosave then saved the overwritten value back (the typing lost on both sides). `_draftSyncHandler` ended with `this._textarea.value = value || ''`, the autosave saved the box when it fired.
- **One verdict, the same family:** PURE `landDraft` joins src/queue-putback.js next to `landDraftPrepend` (which stays the put-back's arithmetic and is landDraft's first row): putback · superseded · same · focused ⇒ hold · typing ⇒ hold · typed-here ⇒ hold · free ⇒ replace (`DRAFT_LANDING_TABLE`). chat-input.js only applies it (`_landDraft`); the held value waits in `_heldDraft` — the store already has it, so holding sends nothing and no frame type is new.
- **Re-judge points:** the box's own autosave (supersedes — its timer now nulls itself, so `dirty = _draftTimer !== null` is honest; `_send` nulls it too), `_send` after the box empties (the pin supersedes; a send without text lets it land), and the textarea's blur via `afterPress`: a press on Send blurs the box BEFORE its click sends, so the judge waits until no pointer is down, then one task (one pair of window capture listeners per page; 10 s cap for a release the page never saw). Measured: judged AT the blur, a real press on Send sent the held «hello world» instead of the typed «hello» (test-draft-focus-chrome ③ RED).
- **Focus = `document.hasFocus()` and the box active:** a background window's box got its blur and is not «focused» — a phone's draft still lands on an idle desktop window, as before. `_draftTaken` (what the box last took from the store) adds `typed-here`: a held value never deletes words typed since unless it keeps every character of them (another device continued the text), so leaving the box after two devices typed at once does not throw away your words.
- **Belts:** a replace clears any pending autosave (no autosave writes back what it replaced); `storeBefore` is `null` while a draft is held (the pinless deferred clear must not take another client's draft).
- **Gates:** test-queue-putback 156 (§0 the landing block + the autosave callback cut verbatim; §8 the rows, a 1536-combination grid, two composers on the real StateSync world — RED = the 2.369.354 composer: «x» lost on both sides, 8 and 15 of 16 lost); NEW heavy test-draft-focus-chrome 16 (two pages in two windows on one Antigravity conversation; RED = the overwrite sends «okok策略», loses 8 / 15 of 16; a judge at the blur sends «hello world»); test-queue-steer 897 (its storeBefore pin re-pinned); test-phone-composer-chrome 39.
- **Residual:** one register per conversation — two devices typing at once each keep their own words and the store keeps the last save; words superseded that way live only in their box until it closes.

### close-toast-wording — the «asked to close» toast names why the second ✕ stops the app (主开发, owner 2026-10-25)

The A2 verdict (src/desktop-fit.js outerCloseVerdict) is unchanged: a leased (agent-held) app closes the view only; a user-held app gets the app's own close, then Stop on a second press. kb-file-structure A2 paragraph carries the rule.

### claude-wrapper-queue — Claude's mid-turn queue is the WRAPPER's: a message sent during a turn is held by data/bin/chat-wrapper.js, Stop drops it and puts it back, nothing runs after Stop (BUILD, the owner 2026-10-25 «可以 按照你推荐来» — open question ① of stop-refills-composer)
- **Why:** stop-refills-composer (.353) MEASURED on Claude Code 2.1.308 with a local mock of `POST /v1/messages` that the CLI RUNS a frame it queued itself mid-turn right after `control_request {subtype:'interrupt'}` (dequeued AT the interrupt, a new turn +27 ms) — VibeSpace never held that message, so Stop could neither stop it nor put it back, and the 2026-09-07 law («Stop means stop») did not hold on claude. Re-measured here: +22 / +25 ms.
- **The wrapper (data/bin/chat-wrapper.js):** `promptQueue` items `{id, ts, line (the WHOLE stdin frame — images included), msgId, origin, text, preview, attachments, buffered}`; `publishQueue()` → top-level `queue_changed {items:[{id, msgId, preview, text?, ts, kind, from}], turn_id:null, verbs}` + sidecar `meta.queue`; `queued_input {msg_id}` per hold; the advert `caps {frameFile, inputQueue:true, queueVerbs:['remove','reorder','edit'], queueResync:true}` + a BASELINE empty publication at boot; `queue-op` (remove / reorder with afterId null = the front + anchor-gone / edit BY EXCLUSION — the first text block takes the words, an image stays; steer ⇒ not-steerable, run-* ⇒ not-startable, an unknown id ⇒ gone) and `queue-resync`, neither ever forwarded; the drain = ONE held frame per turn end, in the strip's order; Stop (`control_request interrupt` on stdin) = per-item `queue_op_result {reason:'stopped'}` → ONE `queue_dropped` (the person's rows — a frame with `webui_origin` is dropped, never put back; the BYTE-IDENTICAL droppedRecordFor twin, the fourth) → the emptied `queue_changed` → THEN the interrupt line goes on to the CLI as before (the server's 2 s SIGINT fallback unchanged). A frame-file body joins the history buffer when it reaches the CLI, never at the hold.
- **THE TURN GATE — the brief's predicate was MEASURED wrong, and so was this lane's first one:** the brief named `meta.streaming` («flips on the child's user record») — but in stream-json the CLI never echoes a prompt on stdout (2.1.308: the only user records are tool results and «[Request interrupted…]»), so a text-only turn never set it. The lane's first gate ended a turn at `session_state_changed idle` — MEASURED wrong too: a BACKGROUND AGENT keeps the session 'running' past the turn's `result` (no idle until the agent ends, ~12 s in the probe) while the CLI takes a new prompt at once (+114 ms) — waiting for idle would keep the person behind background work (test-claude-wrapper-queue ⑥'s control: held 7.9 s). The FINAL gate (`turnBusy`): OPENED by the wrapper itself the moment it writes a user frame (no echo to race: a frame written in the same tick is held) and by the CLI's own turn start — a top-level `system/init` said WHILE the CLI's last state word is running / requires_action (every turn has an init; the turn the CLI starts itself for a background task's notification has ONLY an init — no state change). A STATE word alone opens nothing: after the turn's result a background helper's permission ask says `requires_action` (and its work `running`) while no turn runs and the CLI takes a new prompt — test-helper-ask-ui's bridge probe caught a version that opened on it. An init said while idle or before any state opens nothing either: the real CLI says nothing before its first input (fresh or `--resume`, measured), but older suite stubs say an init at startup and wedged a version that opened on any init (test-chat-send-landing / -hygiene-ui / -scroll / channel-jump / inbox-window-ui / inbox-reply-ui / chat-proposal-card red until fixed; test-queue-putback §6 pins it with an any-init CONTROL); CLOSED by the turn's top-level `result` or `idle`; an `idle` that arrives after we wrote a frame and before that frame's turn started (`awaitingStart`) belongs to the turn before it and is ignored (the drain writes on a result, that turn's idle follows 1–2 ms later). A background Bash does not hold the session (idle follows the result). Measured: EVERY user frame starts with init and ends in `result`, local slash commands included (/context, /cost, an unknown /command, an empty or blank text, an empty array); a frame whose `message.content` is neither a string nor an array is IGNORED by the CLI without a word (no running, no result) — such a frame never opens the gate. `{type:'user'}` with no message makes the CLI exit 1 (unchanged; never sent by VibeSpace).
- **The frame names its message (src/adapters/claude-code.js):** `formatChatInput(text, msgId, {origin})` puts `webui_msg_id` (+ `webui_origin` for auto-resume / dispatch — server.js auto-resume and src/server/user-input.js pass it) at the frame's TOP LEVEL; a client-built frame (an image paste) is SPLICED (`{"webui_msg_id":…,` in front of its first key — never re-encoded). MEASURED: the CLI accepts unknown top-level keys and strips them (the transcript never holds them), so a pre-.354 wrapper that forwards the frame verbatim loses nothing — no caps gate needed on the send path. `formatQueueOp` real (the acp frame vocabulary), `formatQueueResync`.
- **The caps row + the rest:** src/backend-caps.js claude `inputModes.queueVerbs: ['remove','reorder','edit']` (+ the client mirror in src/lib/agent-meta.js; `deriveInputModes` does the rest — queueOps true, steer false); the ws `queue-op` case unchanged (its `no-queue-ops` refusal was already by the CAP; an old claude wrapper now gets the `wrapper-no-queue` sentence «predates the input-queue update … Terminate + Resume»); the ws attach asks `queue-resync` of a claude wrapper that adverts it. server.js `CLAUDE_STREAM_TYPES` learns `queued_input` / `queue_changed` / `queue_op_result` / `queue_dropped` (same line — the 1907-line budget). src/server/stdout/claude-stream-json.js passes them to the normalizer untouched (it spells none of them — test-queue-putback §5 pins that the put-back door sits at the gate). src/message-manager.js: `userMessageIds` + `webuiMsgId` stamped on a bubble from a `_fromWebui` record's msgId, `_stampQueueChip` / `_processQueuedInput` / `_processQueueChanged` / `_processQueueOpResult` (+ `queueOpFailureText`), `queue_dropped` → the base `_processQueueDropped`. Client: nothing new — the strip, the chips, the hint («Enter queues», no Alt+Enter), Session Properties' «Sending during a turn» row and the .353 put-back/toast all follow the caps row.
- **Spend:** a drained frame is the PERSON's turn (or VibeSpace's own already-authorized machine turn) deferred to the turn end — the same frame through the same typed door; no new SITE (test-spend-paths 366 green; this lane adds no producer to its census).
- **Measurements (real CLI 2.1.308, the wrapper over a local mock, no vendor traffic; base b214278b's wrapper = the RED control):** ① Stop — lane: B never reaches the mock, no queue-operation for it in the transcript, `queue_dropped {B}`, no turn after Stop; base: B requested +22–25 ms after the interrupt (enqueued at send, dequeued AT the interrupt). ② drain — lane: B's request +16 ms after A's `idle`, its enqueue only at the drain, a plain user record; base: the CLI enqueued B at send and ran it inside A's own running…idle span. ③ same-tick burst — lane: held at +2 ms, before the CLI's first record at +4 ms; base: the CLI enqueued B 5 ms after A. ④ a background Agent (`run_in_background`) — raw CLI: the turn's result at +127 ms, NO idle until the agent ended (+12.2 s), a prompt sent at +2.2 s requested +114 ms later; a background Bash: idle right after the result. Through the lane wrapper: B reached the CLI 116 ms after send while the agent worked; the idle-only gate (control) held it 7.9 s. Probes and run summaries: the lane dir's measure/ (probe-raw.mjs, probe-wrapper.mjs, runs/).
- **Gates:** test-queue-putback 91 (+ the fourth twin, the claude normalizer leg, the chat-wrapper order law + person-only pins, §6 LIVE: the real wrapper over the stand-in CLI → the real door → a real drafts store, + the hold-off CONTROL that runs the frame after the interrupt) · test-harness-contract 673 (claude now in the queue branch: resync ask + served + advertised + queue_dropped through the twin) · test-chat-frame-guard 60 (the «verbatim» pin now the spliced form; its bash stand-in ends each turn with a `result`, as the CLI does) · test-queue-steer 895 heavy (the seven claude pins flipped; ⑯ the real wrapper over the stand-in: every verb, the refusals, resync, the drain order, an image held whole, a dispatch row never editable / never put back, Stop's order law) · NEW heavy test-claude-wrapper-queue 25 (§A the real CLI + mock ①–⑥ with the hold-off CONTROL and the idle-only CONTROL; §B a worktree server + a claude session on the stand-in + headless chrome: the strip row with ✎/✕ and the queued chip, Stop empties it, the words back in the composer, ONE toast, chip removed). NEW fixture scripts/fixtures/claude-stand-in-cli.cjs (the measured turn shape, a background helper included — test-queue-steer ⑯ pins that a message typed while it works is not held). The shard-timing row for the new suite (scripts/fixtures/ci-shard-timings.json, an estimate: 30 s — §A SKIPs on the hosted runner) keeps test-ci-gate-shards' 90 % coverage.
- **A latent pin bug the queue UI exposed (src/lib/chat-view.js `_setRunOpen`):** with claude's queue on, the composer shows «Enter queues» while a turn streams — the message list is 11 px shorter (304 vs 315 in test-chat-scroll ⑪), and a run-header press while streaming then UNPINNED the view (`scrolledAway`: the browser's scroll anchoring moved scrollTop before the pinned follow ran). Base passed by geometry (twice on b214278b); the lane with ONLY the client caps mirror reverted passed too — the hint was the trigger, the bug the pin logic's. Fix: a person's toggle while pinned puts the view back at the live bottom in the same task (`if (this._pinned) this._scrollToBottom();`). test-chat-scroll 61 / test-fold-ux 120 / test-run-collapse-fold green with it; the same leg red without it. Codex and opencode had the hint all along (the leg runs claude only).
