- **Open:** a `/goal` set MID-TURN still goes straight to the CLI (its own queue) — rare, documented; a held message dies with the CLI process if the CLI exits mid-turn (the acp / agy rule — no put-back on exit); claude's CLI-inbox peer deliveries (rung 1) are still queued by the CLI itself and still run after Stop — they are not the person's words (their own ladder), but the law «nothing runs after Stop» does not yet cover them.

### codex-interrupted-putback — a Codex message the app-server had just started when Stop landed comes back into the composer too, and the note says so (BUILD, the owner 2026-10-25 «可以 按照你推荐来» on .353's open question ②)
- **The case:** Stop's sweep lists the queue, then deletes row by row. The app-server can DRAIN a row in between (the running turn ended on its own): `thread/queue/delete` answers `{deleted:false}`, the row opens its own turn, and Stop's `turn/interrupt` then cuts THAT turn off. .353 reported it `gone` («That message is no longer queued — it already ran.»), outside the `queue_dropped` record — the person re-typed a message that got zero useful tokens. The owner: put it back too, and say it (a duplicate send is cheaper than a lost message).
- **The witness, not a clock:** the app-server's own `userMessage` item (`clientId` = the submission's clientUserMessageId, the notification's `turnId`) is noted per cid in the item dispatch (`noteCidTurn` → `cidTurns`, bounded 200). The sweep HOLDS a drained row (its result deferred) and after the loop — latch still held — waits ≤ `STOP_DRAIN_WITNESS_MS` 1000 (inside the 6 s budget) for any unnamed person row, captures `stopTurn = meta.activeTurnId` ONCE (the record's `turnId`) and asks PURE `drainedWasStopped({turnId, stopTurnId, ended: completedTurns.has(turnId)})` (src/queue-putback.js; the wrapper carries a BYTE-IDENTICAL twin pinned by test-queue-putback). Same turn, not ended ⇒ `queue_op_result {op:'remove', ok:false, reason:'gone', started:true, detail:'it had started and was stopped — put back'}` and the row is spliced into `putBack` at its queue position with `started: true`; its turn ended / another turn / no witness ⇒ plain `gone`. A drained peer row stays `gone` and is never re-stashed (it was delivered). `attachmentDescriptors` folds the two row builders' attachment map into one helper.
- **Why `gone` + `started`, not a new reason:** the client's `if (op.ok === false && op.reason === 'gone') this._dropQueueRow(op.id);` is pinned verbatim by test-queue-steer (a regex and a mutant anchor) and is exactly right for this row (it is no longer queued) — the codex normalizer's `queueOpFailureText` words the `started` branch instead: «That message had already started — Stop stopped it and put it back into the input box.»
- **PURE / shape:** the record's rows carry `started: true` only when true (absent otherwise — the older shape unchanged); all three `droppedRecordFor` twins (acp / agy / codex) updated byte-identically; `queueDroppedOf` keeps it; `putbackNotice` adds `started` (⊆ n, the meta op carries it). record-shape judges `codex:rollout:event/queue_dropped` by TOP-LEVEL keys (`sh` has no `nested` spec for `items`), so no row change — confirmed by test-queue-putback §6 (zero unknown cards for `started` on the result and inside the items).
- **Client:** the toast's first part gains «, {n} had already started and was stopped — put back too» when `started > 0`; the base normalizer stamps a started row's bubble `stopped` (new chip state: «Started, then stopped», ↩ icon, title «It had already started when Stop cut it off — its words are back in the input box») — `Removed` would be false, it reached the agent. Three new t() keys, zh + ja.
- **Residual:** the caller re-reads the running turn after the closing refresh (≤ 2.5 s budget); if the judged turn ended on its own in that window, a row put back as started had finished (a duplicate send — the owner's chosen side). A wrapper spawned before this release still says `gone` (Terminate + Resume). No witness within 1 s ⇒ `gone`, as before.

### agy-harness-fixes-2 — five linked Antigravity harness bugs: the permission mode survives the journal ring and a Resume, the mode chip opens, no «agy skipped required», no false soft-deny card after a nudge turn, no stale «Antigravity: interrupted» after Steer / Stop (FIX, the owner 2026-10-25; diagnosed inside the owner's own Antigravity conversation, which this lane never read — every fixture is the stub agy)
- **Claims checked on b214278b before any fix:** 2–5 hold as reported. **1 holds only in part.** The reported reader line (`st.permissionMode || meta?.modes?.currentModeId || 'default'`) is not the code: `chatStatus()` already fell back to `meta.agentMode` (since 2.369.29), so a cut ring kept the mode LABEL. What it lost was the mode LIST (the sidecar had `configOptions: []`, `modes: null`) — the `[]` that bug 2 turned into an empty menu. And the Resume never read the ring: a sidecar `<wid>.json` belongs to ONE session (the hub's teardown deletes it, src/server/session-stdout.js cleanupOnExit — though heavy ⑤ measured an agy one back on disk after the restart: the wrapper's own finalize writes it 500 ms after SIGTERM), a Resume is a NEW session that never reads it, and its create carries the client's per-conversation pick (`savedCfg.permission`) or the instance default — a pick in the chip writes neither (model / effort picks call `_onConfigChange`; the permission branch of `_onClick` does not). So the sidecar the brief named cannot be a Resume's source; the durable fact is keyed by the CONVERSATION (主开发 agreed 11:31Z: agy-only, the client gap reported as open).
- **(1) The mode is a sidecar fact.** agy-wrapper `noteModes()` keeps `meta.agentMode` + `meta.modes {availableModes, currentModeId}` at boot and at every set-mode; `recordConversationMode()` writes `<buffers>/agy-conversation-modes/<conversation>.json {mode, at}` (0700 / 0600, tmp + rename, id `[\w-]{1,128}` only) at adoptConversation and every set-mode. Boot adopts it when the wrapper RESUMES (`AGY_WEBUI_RESUME_ID`) with `AGY_WEBUI_MODE` '' — on a continuation '' and «no pick» are the same bytes (src/lib/session-lifecycle.js:89) — and journals ONE info notice `mode-resumed`; a stated mode wins and becomes the fact; the retry's one-turn bypass is never recorded. `chatStatus()`: `permissionMode` ← journal, else `meta.agentMode`, else `meta.modes.currentModeId`; `permissionModes` ← journal when it names one, else `sidecarModes()` (configOptions' mode select, else `meta.modes.availableModes`). Residue: with a NON-empty `antigravity.defaultPermissionMode` the client still sends it on a Resume (stated ⇒ it wins over the conversation's own) — the owner gate named in session-lifecycle.js; unchanged.
- **(1b) The resumed WINDOW is told (found by heavy ⑤, not in the brief):** agy ran «Never ask» after the Resume but the creator's chip said «default». Two causes, both measured with a server-side trace: dtach's attaching client gets a clear-screen burst in front of the wrapper's first line — the Resume's `session` record read `\e[H\e[J{"ts"…"kind":"session"…}` — and src/server/stdout/acp-events.js, unlike claude-stream-json (DTACH_CLEAR_PREAMBLE) and codex-events (stripAnsi), never stripped it, so EVERY ACP / agy session's first record failed JSON.parse (a new agy chat's lost line is its spawn `config` record); and the Resume's own status fetch (`GET /api/session-messages?withStatus=1` → transcript-service) builds the reader by conversation id, so `wrapperMeta()` never found the session's sidecar. Fixes: acp-events strips the same preamble; `noteMode()` there turns a `session` / `config` record's mode into `session._permissionMode` + session-meta + `permission-mode-ack {ok:true, mode}` (the claude road's message — the creator window gets no init card: feedLive drops records before the normalizer exists); `AcpSessionMessages.wrapperMeta()` falls back to the live session's `_webuiId`.
- **(2)** src/lib/chat-status-bar.js: `status.permissionModes?.length` at `applyStatus`, `this._permissionModes?.length` at the click — the declared seed stays when a status names no modes.
- **(3)** `toolOfDeny`: `/required the [“"'`]([\w.:-]+)[”"'`] permission/i` first; the fallback `(?:tool|command)\s+(?!required\b)…`. The card and the Allow-once retry now say `command`.
- **(4)** `handleStderr`: jetski's `no output produced` line (its GUESS after any text-less turn) raises no card when nothing could be skipped — `state.mode === 'bypassPermissions' || childRetryBypass`, or `lastTurn` was the stop-check nudge and every tool step it reported completed (DONE without error). `lastTurn` = the last DISPATCHED prompt + its step → completed map, kept past its result because stderr lags stdout (nudgeTurnActive is already false by then). A step left open outside bypass still raises the card; the `SOFT_DENY_RE` line ④'s RED copy pins is unchanged.
- **(5)** every child stdout / stderr line carries its process (`mine`); `stoppedChild(from)` = `from !== child || restarting`. A stopped process's `result` is log-only («the stopped agy's result ignored (it was asked to stop): ERROR — interrupted») and its stderr says nothing to the chat. ### task-group-fanout — the Task Group fan-out stops being heavy, and the model learns exactly what it learns today (BUILD, 主开发's brief 2026-10-24 on 49b84f28, B-1eab's read-only measurements)
- **Measured on the owner's instance (the brief):** every store write — an Activity line, a Backlog op, a bind — called `onChange(this.list())`: every group's whole `_view` (500 Activity entries WITH detail, every Backlog item, `sessions[]` = 749 keys in the lanes group) = 1.57 MB of JSON to EVERY WebSocket client, 267 times a day, and every client repainted the board + every open Task Group window; `session-status-updated` = all 500 records (106 KB) per `vibespace-status`; the hook's `contextSignature` walked every told Context folder synchronously on the main thread (`fresh: true` readdirSync + statSync, ≤ 401 files, depth 4) — 92–185 ms a turn over the owner's NFS rows (not a storage mount: the .350 SafeFs road never covered them); `sessions[]` never pruned on archive (752).
- **tasks-updated = a DELTA (PURE src/task-delta.js + ORCH src/server/task-fanout.js):** the store's `_notify(ids)` names the groups a write touched (`onChange({ ids })`, null = every group); server.js's ONE broadcaster `taskFanout.note(ids)` coalesces a burst over 400 ms (a throttle: a steady stream still flushes every 400 ms; the store write stays synchronous, the exit-proxy / browser-keeper re-judges stay synchronous) and sends `{ type, epoch (this boot), base, seq, changed: [{ id, updatedAt, contentUpdatedAt, counts: {open, backlog, progress, sessions}, patch }], removed }` — the patch carries only what moved against what was SENT (a field by its value, `unset`; `progress` the entries added, `progressSet` the ones changed in place — a clear, `progressDropped` the ids that left the live 500, `progressAll` when the order itself moved; `backlog` added / changed by id, `backlogRemoved`, `backlogOrder`; `sessions` added, `sessionsRemoved`). A group no write named is compared field by field only (its derived ctxRes / folders / visibility still travel; its logs are never stringified). Over 256 KB ⇒ `{ refetch: true, changed: [{id}] }`. GET /api/tasks flushes first and answers `{ tasks, epoch, seq }` (`taskFanout.mark()` + `tasks.list()`, spelled through the store so the record-clear route census still sees it).
- **The client mirrors (src/lib/sidebar-tasks.js):** THE ORDER RULE `mirrorVerdict` — not loaded ⇒ hold (≤ 50, replayed after the fetch) · seq ≤ mine ⇒ drop · base = mine ⇒ apply · a gap / another boot / a refetch frame ⇒ fetch again (held meanwhile) — never a stale mirror; a GET's answer replaces unless a NEWER frame is already in (`fetchVerdict`: the R4 verify r1 `_tasksGen` rule kept, in the hub's order; a fetch-replace bumps the generation too). A fetched list is announced to the windows as a local `{type:'tasks-updated', local, refetch}`. `_upsertTaskLocal` MERGES (the API answers the stored record; a replaced entry would lose the derived wire fields for good under deltas). The consumers repaint only for what concerns them: task-log `touches(msg, taskId)`; task-detail `touches || metaChanged` (a reference row / the members); the board, session-props, principal-picker, browser-trace-view `metaChanged` (anything but the Activity log / Backlog / clocks); session-props skips another conversation's status frame (no history refetch).
- **session-status-updated = the touched keys:** `_notify(keys, extra)` → `{ statuses: {key: record}, removed, epoch, base, seq }` (+ the history clear's `cleared`, unchanged); the 500-record bound's pruned keys ride the next frame as `removed`; GET /api/session-status adds `syncMark()`; the sidebar's change guard compares the frame's own keys (a whole-map frame without `seq`, a suite's synthetic one, still works as before).
- **Archive unbinds:** THE ONE unbind writer `unbindKeys(keys, {ids, exact, dryRun})` (rule PURE task-membership `membersWithout`: a `<backend>:<id>` key itself, a bare archived id any key with that id) — `unbind` and `noteArchived` (the user-state write hook in server.js: only keys NEW to the archive list, so a conversation bound again after its archive stays; one still RUNNING — server.js `isLiveKey` over activeSessions — keeps its groups until it ends, its next turn still needs their context, and leaves at the first user-state write after). Migration `2026-10-task-group-archived-members`: the archive list's keys, archived first to data/archive/task-group-archived-members.json, then pruned through the live store (else the file); a key merely not discovered (a machine offline at boot) is never pruned — «no longer exists» is read as «archived»: the product has no conversation delete.
- **contextSignature off the loop (the owner's constraint — what the MODEL is told must not change):** the hook routes (prompt-context, task-context, task?full=1) first call `tasks.readSignatures(groups, {stale})` (SafeFs `contextFiles` per told folder — the same walk as `_listContextFiles`, test-sync-fs-census ④ — and `stat` per told file; one read per group key in flight; the walks seed the render's cache) and re-enter the route once it settled (≤ 1 s, inside the hook's 3 s abort; nothing above the call consumes anything; a WeakSet marks the re-entry — a `req._x` field reads as a session field to test-session-schema). `signatureFact` = the 4 s TTL it always had; no reader (a suite, a CLI) = the old synchronous walk, byte for byte. A read past the bound ⇒ `stale`: the group is DEFERRED whole that turn (nothing told, no seen mark moved; `s._sigStale[gid]` = the landing count) and the next turn re-reads — only a read that LANDED after the mark answers, so a root slower than the bound every time is still told, one turn late, never dropped. SessionStart with a stale group tells no group (the first prompt tells them whole). `--full` lists a folder still being read as last read and says so in its note.
- **Measured here (synthetic owner shape: 6 groups, 500 entries with detail, 750 members; test-task-group-fanout §4, test-hook-loop-hold):** bytes per Activity line 1716.1 KB → 2.1 KB (0.6 KB without a detail); per vibespace-status over 500 records 165.9 KB → 0.4 KB; open surfaces repainting per Activity line 8 → 2 (its own group's window + log); the hook path over a slow root (17 calls × 25 ms asleep in the call): base holds the main loop 447 ms per prompt, the off-thread road 0 ms (the answer when the read landed, 431 ms, byte-identical); a root past the bound: the answer at 1001 ms, the group deferred, told next turn.
- **Gates:** test-seen-marks §6 (NEW: 10 turns over 7 folder / store edits, the off-thread road byte-identical to the old synchronous walk — the control walked the fixture 30× on the main thread, the road 0×; the stale path: nothing new at N, the control's turn-N delivery byte for byte at N+1, nothing twice at N+2; SessionStart deferred), test-task-group-fanout (NEW fast: the PURE delta, a seeded walk of 240 writes of every writer where a mirror taking only the frames equals tasks.list() at every check, burst / mark / missed frame / byte cap / removal, the status walk of 400 writes, the measurement), test-hook-loop-hold (NEW heavy: the 3-number judge of test-boot-loop-hold, RED control the old road), test-migrations (+ the archived-members leg), census pins moved: test-record-clear(-census, -stores), test-browser-identity-census ⑦, test-fork-groups, test-task-groups, test-sync-fs-census (migrations 23 → 29), mount-reader-census (39 → 42), test-architecture (PURE src/task-delta.js).
- **Open:** the render's file reads (`_readText` at 内容 / 关键文件 levels) and the row roots' `_kindOf` stats stay synchronous on a home / network root (a delivery turn only, cached 4 s — the brief named the signature walk and the `_walk` readers); the board itself still re-renders whole when a member / title moves (rare now); an unarchived conversation does not rejoin a group it was bound to by hand (a folder row still includes it by cwd).

### agy-peer-wake — a live Antigravity conversation can be WOKEN (`vibespace-msg --wake` / an @mention), like codex (FIX on 368a790c; fixtures synthetic, no real conversation read)
- **The owner's report (2026-10-24):** `vibespace-msg send … --wake` to a running agy conversation → «woke 0 agents · 1 wake refused — … no live inbox for this conversation on any reachable machine». Cause: the ladder's rung 1.5 (`findRpcPeer`) needs `capsOf(backend).peerDelivery === 'rpc-queue'` AND the wrapper sidecar's `caps.peerMessage`; the antigravity row said 'stash-only' and data/bin/agy-wrapper.js adverted `peerMessage:false`, though its `case 'peer-message'` served the frame. acp-events consumed only `peer_result ok:false`, so the rung would never have settled.
- **Row + advert:** src/backend-caps.js antigravity `peerDelivery: 'rpc-queue'` + declared `inputModes.steerJoinsTurn: false` (deriveInputModes carries the key only where declared — every other row's shape byte-identical; notificationDelivery ⇒ 'queue' for it); src/lib/agent-meta.js mirrors both. The wrapper adverts `peerMessage: true, notificationSteer: false`; src/server/wrapper-files.js wrapperCaps takes a BOOLEAN `caps.notificationSteer` over the verb list's derived value (no field = the old rule; no codex advert changes).
- **WHY the declaration (the brief's «steer honesty», measured):** agy-harness-fixes' 'steer' (QUEUE_VERBS) is a stop + a restart + a NEW billed turn. With rpc-queue + a list naming steer, notificationDelivery derived 'steer' = «folded into the running turn, free»: the ladder would have written a busy agy's notification UNCHARGED (steerLane) — or, with only the brief's option (a), refused it 'wrapper-no-steer' with «predates notification steering — restart» (no restart cures it) — and stash-handover's billedFor («joins the running turn»), Session Properties («Steered into the running turn») and the strip's notifSteerMissing hint would all have lied. Declared on the row, the lane is 'queue' everywhere (charged at the write, its own turn after); (a) stays as the process's own statement and (b) as the wire's (`steer:'unsupported'` + the acp-events lane line). RED control in test-peer-delivery ②: the same verb list without the declaration derives 'steer'.
- **The wrapper's answers (data/bin/agy-wrapper.js):** `runPrompt` returns {mode:'turn'|'queued'} or {mode:null, reason}; the frame answers `peer_result {ok:true, mode}` (+ steer:'unsupported' for a waiting notification) or `{ok:false, mode:'undelivered', reason, text, fromName, peerKind}` (a mode: it is about the frame just written, so the settle consumes its entry). ONE mode-less `peerBack(q, reason)` for frames the wrapper took and will not run (Stop, remove, a failed dispatch from the queue, an undispatched peer turn when agy exits, the queue at finalizeExit). Base defects found on the way (RED on the base in ⑭): not signed in ⇒ NO answer (the words lost), the queue at exit ⇒ lost, a frame during a restart ⇒ 'turn' for what was queued. **Deviation from the brief, measured:** «a frame while the child is restarting → ok:false» — the frame is queued and the NEW process runs it (⑭: answered before the second start, the line after it, on the new model), so the honest answer is ok:true 'queued'; ok:false would re-stash AND run it (twice).
- **acp-events (src/server/stdout/acp-events.js):** `peer_result` gets codex-events' three twins — ok:false + text ⇒ re-stash (hand-over restore first, unchanged), ok:true + steer:'unsupported' ⇒ «[deliver] rpc-queue: no steer into the running turn on <backend> — the notification took the '<mode>' lane instead», EVERY answer ⇒ `deliverRef?.settleRpcDelivery?.(cid, {ok: msg.ok !== false, mode: msg.mode || null})` (property access on the lazy ref).
- **Addressing (brief item 5):** `addressableId(s)` for an agy chat session = its backendSessionId, adopted by acp-events from the wrapper's own `session` record (claudeSessionId null; agy has no fork ⇒ the verify-r6 rule never hides it) = the conversation id vibespace-msg resolves (conversation-index keys plain ids; no `antigravity:` prefix exists). Proven in the round trip; no predicate change.
- **Wording (brief item 6, the ONE place = conversation-deliver's last miss):** `liveWithoutLane(cid)` — a conversation RUNNING here with no live lane says «this conversation is running, but its agent takes no message mid-session» (stash-only / a terminal session of an rpc-queue harness) or «… its agent's process predates live messages — restart the session to receive them at once» (an rpc-queue wrapper whose own sidecar adverts no peerMessage — the owner's live agy conversation after the update, until it restarts); typed running (no notRunning; job-model's /no live inbox|not running/ classifier untouched ⇒ 'not-reachable'). «no live inbox for this conversation on any reachable machine» + notRunning stays for a conversation running nowhere. The rpc rung's noWake refusal while a turn runs says «this message would not join the running turn» (was «no turn is running to join»).
- **Gates:** test-peer-delivery agy-peer-wake ①–④ (the REAL ladder → the REAL agy wrapper + its sidecar → the fake agy → peer_result → the REAL acp-events consumer → settleRpcDelivery; idle round trip 51 ms; RED copy peerMessage:false ⇒ findRpcPeer skips it) · test-agy-harness ⑭ (idle / busy / empty / restarting / not signed in / at exit + the advert + the emitter census; its four wrappers start before ② and run beside the other sections — the suite measured 10.6 s on the base AND the lane, same box) · test-spend-paths §5b (the acp settle wiring + antigravity never on the predicted-free lane).

### lane backend-icons — OpenCode and Antigravity CLI drew no mark anywhere: each SVG opened with a comment holding a double hyphen, and Chrome refuses the whole file (the owner 2026-10-23 21:4x PT, the sidebar's 后端 filter: Claude and Codex with their marks, «Antigravity CLI» with none — 「图标补一下」; base c1dfc1af = 2.369.348)

After: both load (256 px), the popover paints OpenCode 81 / Antigravity 71 px at 1× (248 / 233 at 2×); the session cards draw both marks. The New Session backend row (.348) is a text-only segment switch — it draws no brand file, nothing to fix there.
- **Gates:** NEW scripts/test-brand-svg.mjs (fast, 133 ms, PURE in-process) — the census over the UNION of every SVG under public/, every BACKEND_META iconSrc and every `/brand/<name>.svg` the code spells in src/** + public/index.html + public/*.css (a template path resolves through `TEMPLATES` — channel-chrome's `url(/brand/${mark}.svg)` reads icons.js's `vendor-*` glyphs — or is RED): the file exists and passes a strict in-test XML checker (no `--` in a comment, one root `<svg>` with the SVG xmlns, balanced tags, no stray `&` / undefined entity, quoted unique attributes, no DTD). RED CONTROLS: the shipped c1dfc1af antigravity.svg (git cat-file when the clone holds it, else the embedded first line) is refused for its comment; 18 fixtures, one per rule; an absent path; an unresolved template. Measured against Chrome (an `<img>` of each fixture): 21/22 agree — the DOCTYPE rule is policy, stricter than Chrome, and says so. ### Lane session-props-scroll — the Session Properties window scrolls and keeps its margins again (on c1dfc1af = 2.369.348; the owner 2026-10-23 21:4x PT: 「这个界面目前也不能滚动了，而且 margin 很奇怪，优化一下」)
- **Cause:** int346 (lane task-group-context, 0e4d6c90) re-shaped the shared `.task-detail` container — the root class of BOTH the Task Group window (task-detail.js) and Session Properties (session-props.js) — into a bare flex column and moved `padding: 10px 12px; gap: 10px; overflow-y: auto` into a new `.task-detail-body` it built under the Task Group window's tabs. Session Properties appended its sections to the bare root, so it lost padding, section gap and scroll in one stroke. No rule widened the label column: it computes 72 px on .345, .348 and the fix; the owner's «values ~160 px in» is 80 CSS px (72 + the 8 px gap, flush against the edge) on a 2× screen.
- **Fix (src/lib/session-props.js + public/style.css):** the window builds the Task Group window's shape — root `.task-detail session-props` → ONE `.task-detail-body` (built once, never a `.session-props` fork of its rules) → every section; a re-render (every broadcast, ≤ 1 per 300 ms) clears and refills the BODY, puts its scroll offset back, and the status history / agent steps lists hold their previous height until their refetch paints. Measured on .345: a status change could leave the reader 160 px off (ja: 400 → 560) — the history list shrank to «Loading history…» for a frame and scroll anchoring kept the shifted view; the fix holds 400 → 400 on a content-identical re-render (a new history row above the view moves it by that row, 17 px, which is anchoring keeping the same content in view). The label column is ONE declared width, `flex: 0 0 72px` (the sidebar card's `min-width: 42px` no longer participates); a longer label wraps and the row aligns on its first baseline (was `center`, which floated a one-line value between a wrapped label's two lines).
- **The label decision:** keep 72 px and wrap. The owner's zh window has exactly ONE label longer than it («同时运行的浏览器数», 90 px); en has four (≤ 100 px), ja two (≤ 120 px). A column fitting every language (120 px) takes 48 px from every value at 440 px, where the working directory, the ID and the browser line already ellipsize; a zh-only 90 px column still wraps en / ja and takes 18 px. Known wart: zh breaks it as «同时运行的浏览 / 器数» (CJK breaks anywhere); a shorter zh word is a copy decision left to the owner.
- **Measured (lane harness, real Chrome 1100×900 desk, light theme, the owner's shape: 4 Task Groups bound, config overrides, a browser block, a 6-entry history; window 440 × 620, content 438 × 586):** .348 — header (0, 0), section gaps 0, «更改…» 0 px from the right edge, checkboxes at 0, content 1268 px, scrollTop stuck at 0. .345 — header (12, 10), gaps 10, values at 92, «更改…» 27 px in (12 padding + the 15 px scrollbar), checkboxes at 12. Fix — identical numbers in zh / en / ja. Pixel compare .345 ↔ fix (440 × 620, scrollTop 0): zh 0.70 %, en 0.28 %, ja 0.37 % of pixels differ — run-specific text (the scratch path / pid, start time, history clock) and the two select rows' baseline (each ~2 px taller, so content below them sits 4 px lower: 390 × 800 phone 2.48 %); .345 ↔ .348: 10.9 / 12.4 / 11.6 %. A re-render whose history answers 700 ms late: .345 moves the view 97 / 161 / 160 px (zh / en / ja; the list collapses 117–180 → 20 px), the fix 0 (held). The body follows a window resize (client 386 at 420 px, 786 at 820 px); phone 390 × 800: padding 12 / 10, scrolls (.348: 0 / 0, no scroll).
- **Tests:** NEW fast `test-task-detail-body` (PURE census, ~70 ms): every `className = 'task-detail…'` ROOT in src/lib appends a `.task-detail-body`, keeps its `.task-detail-section`s in it and never rebuilds the root; the CSS keeps `.task-detail` the bare column and `.task-detail-body` the flex 1 · min-height 0 · overflow-y auto · padding · gap, no window forking either. ### lane design-focus-whole — an artboard opened enlarged is shown WHOLE with a ring, like the canvas preview; only a tall page keeps fit-width + its inner scroll (the owner, 2026-10-23 22:3x PT, on the iPhone Duo POC: 「那个缺了一圈是预览和演示（放大）图周边差了一圈」; base c1dfc1af = 2.369.348)
- **Measured first.** A probe (the published page's runtime = the SAME createDesignCanvas + focusView as the window, built from the base tree, the Duo folder bundled by design-model.js `bundleCanvas`, headless Chrome) at the owner's pane — ≈ 1706×891, derived from their 1.76× and the missing ≈ 97 px: 176 %, the frame cut to 487 of 585 px, the composer row gone. **The brief's 1000×700 example does not reproduce**: 951×585 is width-bound there (z 1.018, 595 px tall in 668), so the base already showed it whole; the cut needs a pane wider than ≈ 1.63 × its height. The tests use the owner's pane (pure) and a 1238×569 window pane (heavy, with a PRECONDITION row proving the .348 rule cuts there).
- **The cause.** design-canvas-model.js `focusView` was fit-WIDTH only and cut the frame to the pane (`frameH = min(h, floor((ph − 2·pad)/z))`) — «its document then scrolls inside»; a screen artboard (html/body `overflow:hidden`, a fixed box) cannot scroll. Fit (`fitView`) and Present (`presentView`) contain; the focused view was the one road of three that could not show a board whole.
- **The fix (PURE + one call).** `focusFit(rect, declared)` → 'screen' | 'page'; a SCREEN = `fitView(rect, pane, {pad: FOCUS_PAD, maxZ: 2})` (contain, centred both ways, one ring on four sides), `frameH` = its own height; a TALL PAGE (h/w > `PAGE_RATIO` 2.4) = the old fit-width + cut + inner scroll; `declaredPrint(manifest, file)` reads the manifest ROW's own `print` (the hub's frame rows default every print to 'fixed' — silence and a declaration look alike there): a declared "fixed" is a screen at any height; "flow" alone makes nothing a page. design-canvas.js `refocus` = ONE `focusView(f, paneSize(), {declared: declaredPrint(st.manifest, f.file)})`. `PRESENT_PAD = 0` joins `FIT_PAD` 40 / `FOCUS_PAD` 16 — each view's ring is ONE constant. FOCUS_PAD stays 16, chosen by looking at 16 vs 40 side by side: 40 costs a 390-wide phone 20 % of the board's width for nothing; the canvas's 40 is room for the name strips the focused view hides.
- **The census (the line is data, not taste).** Every design.json on the hub, READ-ONLY (data/designs.json's registered folders + the lane dirs; ~/.vibespace and the production data/ hold none): 63 artboards in 11 designs. Screens: 951×585 … 1920×1240 (wide), 669×867 / 385×571 / 382×580 (Duo portrait), 390×844 ×7 and 375×812 (h/w 2.164–2.165, the tallest). Pages: 390×960 (2.462, the shortest) … 390×2500 (6.41) — all flow-declared phone documents whose body scrolls. 2.4 sits in the gap and keeps a 20:9 / 21:9 phone (2.22 / 2.33) a screen; a foldable's cover screen (≈ 2.5) declares "fixed". The table is in the lane report.
- **Behaviour changes to know.** A screen whose contained size is width-bound is now centred vertically (it sat at the top pad). The PHONE uses the same rule: a 390×844 screen on a 390-wide phone (pane 390×787) is now whole at 89 % (fit-width cut its bottom 22 px); a landscape board was already width-bound there (unchanged). A flow-declared document under the line (the manual's 1280×1600 example) is now shown whole — zoom in to read it; if 主开发 prefers «flow ⇒ page», it is one line in `focusFit`. Not changed: panning a board zoomed in so far that it covers the whole pane needs the ring (the frame takes its own pointer and wheel) — pre-existing.
- **Docs.** kb-features «Design window» (the three views' fit rules, the pads, the line with its census), kb-file-structure (the model's INDEX line + essay, the core's focus sentence, the viewer, the gate), design 003 (`print` is no longer «print CSS only»; en + zh), the agent manual's `print` row (a taller SCREEN says `"print": "fixed"`; test-design-canvas pins the manual and kb-features to the model's own number), kb-bugfix INDEX + essay.
- **Gates.** test-design-canvas (fast): the new focusView table (the owner's pane, a width-bound pane, the tall page, the declared fixed, a phone on a phone, the census line, declaredPrint, the three pads) + 5 new controls — RED CONTROL = the .348 rule (screens at fit-width: the Duo frame 487 of 585), the fixed declaration ignored, no line, the declaration read as the default, one ring per branch — + the refocus wiring pin. test-design-window (heavy) A⑪: `vibespace-design new duo`, a 951×585 fixed board with html/body overflow hidden and a 44 px rgb(255,0,170) row at the very bottom, focused by a REAL double-click in a 1238×569 pane: z = min of both ratios, a 16 px ring top and bottom (equal left/right), the frame's own viewport 585 with the row ending there, the row's pixel seen in a screenshot, zoom in keeps the frame at 585, back out = whole, Fit = contain exactly; the window closes and unwatches before B③ counts watches. A⑩ Present unchanged and green.
- **Not changed:** the version files (the user entry heads 2.369.350 on a scratch copy for test-changelog-style).

### lane chat-mermaid — a ```mermaid fence draws as a diagram through ONE self-hosted, sanitizing door (the owner 2026-10-23 22:3x PT, about an Antigravity reply that carried a flowchart: 「能不能展示 flowchart？」; base c1dfc1af = 2.369.348)
- **Why:** the chat drew a ```mermaid fence as a plain code block — no diagram path existed (src/lib/chat-renderers.js builds the code toolbar over highlight.js). The only mermaid code in the tree was the editor's Markdown preview (src/lib/code-editor.js), which loaded `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/dist/mermaid.min.js` by a `<script>` tag «to avoid 3MB bundle increase».
- **The CSP finding, MEASURED (it corrects the brief's «refused since the app CSP landed»):** the app page's policy is REPORT-ONLY (src/app-csp.js; nothing sends the enforcing header in this release), so the CDN script was never refused. On a scratch .348 hub (Chrome 154, the CDN request answered by a CDP `Fetch` stub — no outbound call) the stub RAN, i.e. the preview drew when the CDN was reachable, and EVERY preview filed `script-src-elem https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/dist/…` (disposition report) — an app-page report, a For-you CSP notice; with the CDN unreachable (a firewalled network: the same failure the self-hosted fonts fixed in 2.137.0) the preview showed the source as an unformatted `.mermaid` div plus an uncaught promise rejection. The enforce switch would have killed it outright: a third-party origin the policy names nowhere. Now no script comes from anywhere but this origin.
- **One renderer, self-hosted:** `mermaid` ^11.17.2 is a dependency (110 packages in the lock, all new — no existing version moved). `src/mermaid-entry.js` → `public/mermaid.js` (esbuild, ESM, minified, gitignored — the fourth client entry beside doc-editor.js; the build line sits after it): **3,451,024 B raw · 957,227 B gzip -9** (the hub sent 907,397 B); main bundle unchanged but for the door (+≈10 KB). index.html names it `<link rel="vs-lazy-bundle" href="/mermaid.js">` — an unknown rel fetches nothing — which the index route's own regex stamps `?v=<mtime>` like bundle.js; `ensureMermaid()` imports that stamped address ONCE, on the first diagram (a failed import is retried on the next). **First render, measured** (the chrome leg, a reply in a conversation's history): 251 ms from opening the conversation to the drawn card — mermaid.js fetched in 57 ms, initialize + render 47 ms; a later diagram ≈ 10–50 ms.
- **ONE door — src/lib/mermaid-render.js (+ PURE src/lib/mermaid-model.js):** `mountDiagrams(root, {app})` turns every ```mermaid / ~~~mermaid fence (any case) into a `.chat-diagram` card: 「图 | 源码」 (the source one click away), 「复制」 (the source), 「放大」 (`app.openDiagram` → `FileViewer.openDiagram`: a `viewer` window over the picture as an `<img>` of the sanitized SVG — it runs nothing, fetches nothing — with the image viewer's Fit / − / + / 1:1, wheel zoom and drag pan; openSpec `{action:'openDiagram', code}` via `registerOpenAction`, so a reload or another client re-draws it through the same door). Renders are SERIAL (mermaid's config is global: initialize + render are one queued task) and CACHED by (theme, font, source), ≤ 60; each mount re-scopes the cached picture to a fresh id. A failure shows the SOURCE by itself, 「渲染失败 · 第 N 行」 + mermaid's own words, line N marked (`suppressErrorRendering`: never mermaid's bomb). The theme is the live `--bg-window`'s luminance (dark / dracula / nord / solarized / monokai ⇒ mermaid dark, light ⇒ default — the deleted CDN code had called solarized light); `theme-colors-changed` re-draws every drawn card (one cache miss each) and an open zoom window. A tall diagram is capped at min(70vh, 720 px) in the card (aspect kept) — 放大 shows it whole.
- **Every door uses it:** the chat — `addWrapToggles` (message create, replace, gap render) draws first and a card's source gets no second toolbar; the streaming frame (`_renderStreamingText`) draws too: `renderMarkdown` marks a fence still OPEN `data-fence-open` off marked's own tokens (`diagramFences(marked.lexer(text))` matched to the drawn `<pre>`s in order; a count that disagrees keeps them all code), so mid-stream the fence is a code block and the frame its closing fence arrives in draws it (every later frame paints from the cache); an edit re-draws. The editor's preview (the CDN block and its `_mermaid` global deleted), the file viewer's markdown (by URL), a job panel's md block, a For-you item. Census (test-mermaid-render §7): every markdown parse in src/lib draws through `mountDiagrams` or is listed with its reason — doc-window.js / doc-window-model.js (the Doc window's reading render: Export HTML / Copy as HTML / Print leave the app). **Not covered: the Doc window itself** (the default door for a .md file) edits a fence as a Tiptap code block — a follow-up.
- **Security, proven:** mermaid runs `securityLevel: 'strict'`, HTML labels off everywhere and every key a diagram's own `%%{init: …}%%` / front-matter `config:` could re-open made `secure` (htmlLabels, securityLevel, theme / themeCSS / themeVariables / fontFamily / altFontFamily / darkMode, dompurifyConfig, the size caps) — measured: without them the probe's directive turns HTML labels on (3 foreignObjects, an `<img>` among them). Its SVG reaches the page only through src/lib/safe-html.js `sanitizeDiagramSvg` — the ONE sanitizer module, a SECOND dedicated DOMPurify (approval census §2: DOMPurify lives only there): SVG + filters only; no foreignObject / a (label kept) / image / feImage / use / animate* / set / script, no data-*, no tabindex; ids (`actor0`, `node-1` of sequence / sankey / architecture), in-picture references and classes (`mmd-`) under a RANDOM per-render scope; the theme `<style>` re-read by the browser's own CSS parser (`CSSStyleSheet`) keeping only style rules whose every selector starts at `#scope` with no sibling combinator and no at-rule; no url() off the picture, no image-set(), no backslash escape. The figure is `contain: paint`; a press inside it never reaches a delegated handler of the view. A diagram naming a picture off itself (`A@{ img: "https://…" }`) is refused BEFORE mermaid sees it — measured: mermaid fetches a node picture while it draws, before any sanitizer.
- **Gates:** see the commit; test-mermaid-render (fast, PURE), test-chat-mermaid-chrome (heavy, outbound blocked by `--host-resolver-rules`, every request logged, zero CSP reports).
- **Not changed:** the version files; the app page's CSP (`script-src 'self' 'report-sample'` — a new origin is NOT the fix).

### lane ci-351-reds — three test-side reds of the 6e1cd389 master CI (two of them the product's) and a control that could not open (主开发's brief; base 6e1cd389 = 2.369.350; a .351 pick)

FIX (the suite only): the leg waits — a poll of the witness against the clock, never a sleep — until no recorded call ends at or after now, asserts that quiescence, then judges on the witness's own facts (nothing recorded DURING the block; the probe's `blockedBy` = the CPU words) beside the line. A deterministic CONTROL reproduces the straddle without the race (a window opening in the read's recorded end keeps it). After: 0 / 20 alone, 0 / 20 beside the fast tier (load 3.6–6.9, the before run's 3.6–6.5), 0 / 60 in the tight loop. The base canary's RED CONTROL (names nothing) unchanged. ### lane hub-fuse-sync-guard — the main thread never waits on a storage mount, and a held loop names its call (主开发's brief after the 6.5-min hold of 2026-10-23 21:56 PT; base c1dfc1af = 2.369.348; a .350 pick)
- **The incident.** 21:56:10 → 22:02:40 PT the production hub answered nothing (curl 000 for 20 s, journal silent 6.5 min, 14 connections waiting); its MAIN thread sat in `request_wait_answer`, utime/stime frozen; /sys/fs/fuse/connections 73 (the NAS row, rclone over SMB) held 21–24 waiting requests, 144 (OneDrive) 4–6. The only other waiters: three orphaned `bfs … /` walks of an agent (2–3 h old, reparented to the user systemd); killing them drained both queues and the hub answered. The canary said at 21:54:59 «no sync fs call over 20 ms in that window» and nothing after the hold. The journal's loop gaps that day: 212 s (20:03), 216 s (21:00), 194 s (21:12), 143 s (21:25), 325 s (21:50), 313 s (22:01) — and at 21:44:27 loop-blame had named the class: `statSync …/vibespace-mounts/OneDrive/Courses/AIContext 1209 ms ← src/task-groups.js:606 TaskGroupManager._kindOf` (the OneDrive Task Group's Context row, stat'd on every member prompt).
- **Why nothing named it.** loop-blame wrapped 18 sync functions by hand (not accessSync / readlinkSync / opendirSync / realpathSync.native / fs.watch's inotify_add_watch / Dir#readSync …); its blame needed a canary probe in flight across the hold (the probe is sent every 10 s and answers in ms — none was); a call that THREW was never timed; nothing had a post-mortem.
- **THE WITNESS (src/server/sync-fs-witness.js + sync-fs-witness-worker.js).** loop-blame's ONE wrapper now covers `Object.keys(fs)` `*Sync` (44 on Node 24) + fs.watch + Dir#readSync + realpathSync.native, times a throwing call, and carries ONE hook. The witness keeps the in-flight slot (one: sync calls cannot interleave) mirrored into a SharedArrayBuffer — a watchdog THREAD names a call still in flight past 10 s, with the main thread's `/proc/self/task/<pid>/wchan` + `syscall` («[sync-fs] the main thread has waited 11 s in readFileSync(…) — the kernel: request_wait_answer in openat»), and a loop held outside any sync call is said so (CPU, a child, a native call); and a ring of the last 32 calls over 50 ms (the hub frames of the stack only for a mount path). A call ≥ 1 s hands itself to the canary at its return (`held()`: «[canary] the main loop was held N ms — the sync fs call that returned as it resumed: fn(path) ms, under storage mount «…» / not under a mount ← src/…:line fn», once per call; a late probe asks `heldIn` for the same call); ≥ 5 s on a mount path ⇒ mount-health `onHeld` files ONE For-you item per mount (origin server: «VibeSpace's server waited N s on the folder … — fn on path from file:line», the call's frames, who presses the mount, why it ran).
- **THE GUARD.** Before the syscall, a call whose path (path-resolve rules — never realpath) is under a STORAGE root is refused: `EVSMOUNTSYNC` {path, mount}, «[mount-guard] fn(path) from src/…:line refused — use SafeFs/async; the mount «…»» once per call site, telemetry `srv-mount-guard-refused` (⚙ Diagnostics). An uncaught refusal unwinds its callback and the hub keeps serving (server.js's uncaughtException handler: the call never reached the mount — exiting would trade one refused call for a whole-hub restart). Not armed before the first loop turn (a throw in the main-module evaluation would stop every boot). `mounts.mainThreadSyncGuard` (NEW, default on) = log only («… ran on the mount … — mounts.mainThreadSyncGuard is off (log only)»).
- **THE ROOTS (PURE src/mount-path-class.js + SHARED src/storage-path.js).** Every fuse / fuse.* / nfs* / cifs / smb* / sshfs / davfs* mount of /proc/self/mountinfo (fusectl and fuseblk are not) ∪ the product's filesystem storage rows (MountManager.storageRoots(), mounted or not), re-read every 30 s and on every `mounts-updated`. Kinds: storage (a product row; any FUSE / SMB / WebDAV mount — refused), home (the mount holding rootDir / dataDir — on the owner's box the workspace bindfs over NFS — witnessed, never refused), network (another kernel NFS mount — witnessed). The instance's own rootDir / dataDir subtree is local even on a network mount. storage-path.js is the one answer every module asks; a process nobody set (the device daemon, a child) answers null — its old road.
- **THE CENSUS (scripts/test-sync-fs-census.mjs + scripts/sync-fs-census.mjs).** acorn over server.js, src/*.js, src/server/*.js, src/routes/*.js: 2097 `fs.<x>Sync(` sites — 419 constant (a literal / the checkout / data / os.homedir() / /proc, or a file constant built only of those: a fixpoint over the file's declarations), 207 descriptor (judged at their open), 1471 rowed in 335 rows keyed by the enclosing scope (Class.method / function / route:VERB path; a `match` over «fn(paths)» where one scope mixes proofs; one '*' row per file at most): local-only 1280 · via-safefs 111 (each file named by its launcher) · guarded 80. Exact counts; RED controls (a new file's site, one more site in a covered scope, a new scope); ④ runs the conversions: a Task Group whose rows sit on a storage root makes ZERO main-thread sync calls there (the loop-blame hook counts; CONTROL without the root: 3), and the SafeFs ops answer exactly what task-groups' own walk / read answer. The 1471 sites were classified by six read-only agents over the base and reconciled by signature against the converted tree.
- **THE CONVERSIONS (before → after).** task-groups `_kindOf` / `_stat` / `_listContextFiles` / `_readText` (sync per prompt → a storage row answers from SafeFs facts, src/storage-facts.js: the last off-thread answer, re-read in the background past 4 s; never read yet = `reading`, worded on the row; new worker ops contextFiles / textHead), `groupsForSession` realpath (→ skipped on a storage cwd) · routes/sessions `realCwdOf` (every /api/sessions rebuild → skipped) · session-store `recoverCwdFromProjDir` (an existsSync walk into the cwd → a mount point is taken as there, nothing below probed) · ctx-sync (60 s timer + every member prompt → async fs; one per host:group in flight) · /dav (21 sync calls per request over the share → async fs, containedReal async) · files `localDuBytes` (a statSync every 1.2 s for a whole copy → async, one at a time) · browser-env `effectiveConfig` (a read of <cwd>/agent-browser.json at every spawn → reported not read on a storage cwd) · ws-handler pending editor (existsSync at attach → best-effort like remote) · device-mount (mkdirSync of a stale FUSE mount point → async) · desktop-serve catalog (existsSync of an app's program per GET → `execHere`). Cold doors stay sync and are refused by name on a storage mount; `importFromFile` and `publish` now say the refusal instead of «cannot read» / «file not found».
- **Measured (scripts/test-sync-fs-guard-server.mjs, a REAL `rclone mount :local:` with its daemon SIGSTOPped, server.js on a scratch worktree).** Guard on: POST /api/tasks/import of a file on the hung mount answers the refusal in 5 ms; GET /api/boot during it 7 ms. CONTROL guard off: GET /api/boot gets no answer in 2 s; the watchdog line at 11 s («request_wait_answer in openat»); at SIGCONT the canary's line «held 10715 ms … readFileSync(<mnt>/task.md) 10715 ms, under storage mount «<mnt>» ← src/task-groups.js:2178 TaskGroupManager.importFromFile» and the For-you item.
- **The cost.** Every main-thread sync call now passes the hook: a statSync of the instance's own tree 0.48 µs bare → 0.63 µs with the (old) wrapper → 0.98 µs with the witness (one `startsWith` on the own tree, the slot's three stores + the path's bytes); elsewhere ~0.6 µs more (the classifier's first-segment bucket of roots, cached per roots array; 54 roots on the owner's box). Against a store read of µs–ms and ~1 000 main-thread sync calls a second, under 0.1 % of a core.
- **A second hold the same night (22:43–22:48 PT, read-only check while this lane ran):** the hub's main thread in request_wait_answer again in bursts (journal 22:43:31 «longest loop gap 178s»), connection 144 (OneDrive) 3–4 waiting, the only other waiter pid localsearch-3 (GNOME's file indexer) crawling the OneDrive mount; reported to 主开发, no signal sent.
- **Seams moved.** mount-reader-census (§86) counts: safe-fs-worker 39→43, session-store 29→27, webdav 16→11, desktop-serve 15→14, + rows for the witness (mountinfo) and its thread (/proc/self/task); test-memory-census: the witness's Worker site + script (trackWorker, the memory skip, answerMemory first); test-user-todos-layout 68→69 declared sites (the hold item, origin server); test-fs-canary §7: realpathSync.native is now witnessed (kept = present and answering, identity relaxed); test-architecture PURE + mount-path-class.js, SHARED + storage-path.js; the mounts-updated refresh rides the mounts wiring (server.js keeps its pinned `onMountsUpdated` line and its 1906 lines); docs/settings.md regenerated.

### lane chat-proposal-card — a proposal is seen where it was made: the approval card at the chat's call row that filed it (the owner, 2026-10-23 18:2x PT, reading his work agent's chat: «最下面那个是 outbox 请求吗？我视觉上完全看不出来啊»; base ffc8b1ff = 2.369.347)
- **Measured.** The agent ran four `vibespace-channels read gmail/…` calls and `vibespace-channels reply …` (a reply-all), then wrote «Channels 里放了一条 reply-all 提案…». Nothing in the chat was the proposal: the card had TWO places (channel-outbox.js «ONE RECORD, TWO PLACES» — the conversation window's inline section, the Outbox window). The production session meta (read-only) holds the §26 witness's `reply` touch WITH the proposal id, 300 ms after the read on the same thread — the call row that filed it was already known; nothing drew the proposal there. The proposal was approved later elsewhere (`sent`).
- **Where the card goes (the brief: «below the row or as the row's expanded body — pick the one the browser-proposal card uses and say why»).** The browser-proposal card is a separate system notice the normalizer places by time (`placeProposalCard`), because a keeper claim / a passkey card is no call of the chat. A channel proposal is ALWAYS filed by a call the witness binds (the touch carries `proposalId`), and its sibling — the raw-API proposal card (B-2198 part 2, `chatApiCards`) — already sits as the call row's expanded body, kept on screen by the run fold's compact exemption. So: the row's expanded body, the API card's place — no server card source, no copy of the record in the message stream, the same fold rules.
- **The fix.** ① PURE `src/channel-touch.js` `FILED_OPS` (reply / compose / react / recall) + `filedProposals(touches)` — each id once, in the order filed, with its row's key. ② `src/lib/channel-outbox.js` `chatProposalCards(app, cardEl, filed, {onCount})` — ONE keyed `.chat-chan-props` box after the row's conversation rows (and its API cards); `keyedCard` + `placeArmed` (the Outbox's own card, arming and `shown` digest); awaiting = the whole card, decided = its ONE line (`line: true`, the conversation window's rule); a chip `.cct-prop` on the conversation's row (`proposalChipText`: «Proposal · <who> · <state>» — the first To by name + «+N», a chat reply by its room, a new message / reaction / recall; the outcome «sent · HH:MM» / «you rejected it» / expired). A shared record store: `GET /api/channels/outbox?ids=…` batched, re-read on `channel-outbox-updated` naming one of the ids (or none — an account-wide change) and on every attach (`refreshChatProposals`). ③ `channel-touch-view.js` renderBox / clearBox hand each row's filed proposals over; a moved count calls `view._updateRuns()`. ④ the server: `outboxView({ids})` keeps a proposal only while `drafterSees(p)` (the receipt's rule) — the route's `?ids=`. ⑤ the run fold: `runSummaryLabel({proposals})` — each box's `data-n` / `data-awaiting` («· 1 条提案待批准» / «· 1 条提案»). ⑥ CSS: the box is exempt from the compact hide; a chip row drops its words in the compact line (the state was the part cut at 1400 px — measured on the first screenshot). ⑦ `data/bin/vibespace-channels`: every waiting reply / react / recall / compose (and the webhook fan-out) prints «  the card is in this chat and in Channels › Outbox» under its verdict.
- **Traps met.** A bare `const CARD_WHERE` printed by the CLI is a row of test-peer-text-census (a bare local) — the sentence is a literal at each site. The brief's real names (the recipient) would red test-architecture's public-repo hygiene — the comments say «Ada». A trailing `// …` after a one-line `{ …; }` swallowed its brace (node --check caught it). test-channel-outbox's `prime()` grants by `setReach` — revoke with `setReach(…, level: null)`, an account `setGrain` alone leaves the reach.

### lane browser-takeover-queue — a request for a person is a RECORD seen in ONE place for all of them (the Agent browser window's «等你接管», the same For-you item), resolved by the handback (a fleet power user on Lark, 2026-10-23 23:35Z, relayed by the owner; base ffc8b1ff = 2.369.347)
- **Why:** 「我觉得可以在 browser 这个里面加一个像 Chatbot 的 outbox 一样的功能。经常会有很多时候它会需要我这边 take over 操作嘛，那所有等待我 take over 的都在这里集中一下，然后这样我多个 task 并行的时候都可以在这集中处理这些需要 take over 的东西」. Measured on the base: an agent that needs a person in its browser has no verb — it writes it in chat or files a `vibespace-ask` (a For-you item after a minute); the person finds the conversation, opens its live view and presses Take over; nothing lists «who waits for me in a browser».
- **THE RECORD (PURE src/browser-takeover-request.js):** `{id tr-<8 hex>, browserKey, profileId (null = the conversation's own browser), conversationKey, sessionId, names, text ≤ 300 code points (one line, hidden / reordering characters dropped — src/hidden-chars.js), url, title, at, askedAt, asks, state, takenAt, takenBy, doneAt, how, parked, itemId}`. ONE request per LEASE: a second ask re-asserts it (same id, new words, asks + 1). THE STATE FOLLOWS THE LEASE'S INPUT SIDE: a takeover ⇒ taken; an EXPLICIT handback (the live view's Hand back, the queue's Done / Hand back, «hand back and continue») ⇒ done; a handback nobody chose (idle, the view closed, a stop, a detach) ⇒ WAITING again (nobody said it is done — it stays listed); the person's Done without a takeover ⇒ done; the agent's withdraw / its lease ending ⇒ withdrawn. A closed record never moves (refused `closed`). Who may see it = the live view's rule: the owner while the conversation holds that browser; an agent its own; nobody else.
- **ONE WRITER (src/server/browser-keeper.js):** `requestTakeover` / `resolveTakeoverRequest` and the lease's own events (`emitInput` ⇒ `requestOnInput`, `dropInputsFor` ⇒ `endLeaseRequest`); persisted data/browser-takeovers.json (writeJsonAtomic; open ones all + a tail of 100 closed); broadcast `browser-takeovers-updated` with the change; a restart is a handback by construction (taken ⇒ waiting at load). `resolveFor` answers a page verb `human_asked` (409) while a request WAITS and carries the request on `browser_paused` while it is taken; the conversation's own browser is never idle-released under an open request (idleReleaseVerdict's `takenOver`). The tab: the dialog watch's own tabs (`ownTabs` + its title now), else the lease's last url.
- **THE VERB:** `vibespace-browser ask-human "<words>"` (`--withdraw`, `--status`, `--profile`) — OURS in the verb table; the CLI prints the server's line (it ships without src/). A page verb that meets `human_asked` / `browser_paused` + a request WAITS for the handback in long-polls (`GET /api/agent/browser/takeover-request?id&wait`, ≤ 20 s each) bounded at 90 s (under the harness's 2-min tool cap; the keeper's `askWaitMs` seam is the gate's 3 s), then asks /resolve again ONCE — still waiting ⇒ `[human_asked]`, nothing ran, «end your turn»; a reply through the item wakes the wait and says so. A job is refused (its route `takeover-request` on JOB_ROUTES_REFUSED). The ROUTE is `/api/agent/browser/takeover-request` (the verb stays `ask-human`): test-browser-human's census reserves «human» / «browse» in an agent route for the person's OWN browsing (Browse yourself) — no agent route may name it. A `vibespace-ask` whose words name a browser is NOT converted — two roads, kept apart.
- **ONE FOR-YOU ITEM (src/server/browser-handback.js, the announcer):** filed at the ask (urgent ⇒ band 1; action `browser-takeover` with ACTION_IDENTITY requestId; a stable dedupe text, the words in i18n params), resolved when the request ends (resolvedBy handed-back / user / agent / conversation-gone). Its doors: a DISMISSAL (or a batch «Mark all seen») parks the request — the SAME item re-filed at normal = band 4, still listed, never resolved by it; a REPLY (the ONE reply road) reopens the item and stamps `repliedAt` (the CLI's wait wakes); the ✓ is the person's Done (a taken one is handed back). The explicit handback's ONE delivery appends «This answers your request tr-… ("…") — it is done.»; a Done without a takeover is told once through the same ladder site (`browser-handback` reason).
- **THE SCREENS:** the Agent browser window grows «等你接管 · Waiting for you» ABOVE Profiles (src/lib/browser-takeover-queue.js — keyed rows patched in place: conversation (click = its window) · its browser · «在等你 · …» / «你正在操作 · 自 …» · «agent 请你：…» · the page · 接管 / 已完成 / 回复, or 打开实时视图 / 交还控制; the quiet empty line «没有等你接管的浏览器»); its title says «Agent 浏览器 · N 等你接管»; the rail's Browser icon carries the count (PURE `takeoverBadge`, channelsBadge's sibling: the waiting requests the attention list puts in bands 1–4 — a parked one counts, a band 1 switched off does not). Take over opens the session's live view with the input side TAKEN (`openBrowserLive` `takeOnOpen`, never persisted: a replay comes back watching); the For-you item's button opens it OFFERED. Every live view of that lease shows «agent 请你：<words>» under its bar while the request is open (not only one opened from the queue — the person who opened it from the chip needs the words as much); Hand back resolves it.

### lane browser-x-in-window — the one-browser model's B2, THE PICTURE SWITCH: on the attach road the live view shows the browser's OWN WINDOW and a takeover drives it (design q-026 r1 §2.1 / §3 row B2; the owner 2026-10-23 18:3x PT 「目前 chrome 还是没有被放进 browser 窗口里面」; base ffc8b1ff 2.369.347)
- **Why:** B1 (.290) put the keeper's Google Chrome on a `display-for-browser` xpra session nobody looked at: the live view still drew the CDP screencast (the page compositor's frames — M0: never a bubble, a passkey panel, not even the tab-modal dim) and a takeover drove the page through CDP.
- **MEASURED first (Chrome 154.0.8037.57 + xpra 6.5.4 + agent-browser 0.38.2, private xpra :2741; the lane's tools/probe-auth.sh, probe-auth2.sh, probe-windows.sh, probe-resize.sh):** the HTTP Basic sheet is drawn INSIDE Chrome's one X top-level (xpra lists ONE window; the brief's «xpra's window list» cannot see it — M0's F7 holds for it too); the watch's Fetch hook answering `Default` makes Chrome draw its own sheet over a commit of `chrome-error://chromewebdata/`, an answer is a NEW navigation (right password ⇒ the page commits; wrong ⇒ authRequired again; Cancel ⇒ the 401's own body commits); a GTK file chooser IS its own X window (class `chrome`/`Chrome`, DIALOG, modal, transient-for the browser window); menus are override-redirect, nameless, classless; xpra's wid = the server's X id; CDP window bounds = the X geometry; a CDP `setWindowBounds` moves Chrome's window but NOT xpra's corral, which then went back to the window's first geometry (2033×2284 — the picture drawn at 0.35).
- **THE SOURCE (PURE src/browser-picture.js `pictureSourceOf`):** 'x' for the attach road's live record with its display session, else 'screencast' with why (`no-display` / `remote` / `driver` / `no-display-session` / `not-running`) and the bar's words («the browser's own window» / «the page's picture — this machine has no display» …) in the mode badge's tooltip. A record's `host` names the machine that LAUNCHED it (this one) — only `hostId` is another machine.
- **THE PICTURE:** the live view mounts the desktop app window's own view (xpra-view.js — its fit ladder, its DPR rule; `workerUrlFor` is THE worker asset's one spelling) on the display session through the ONE desktop bridge; the socket names itself with a TICKET the live-view relay mints for that viewer (`x-ticket`; never for an agent's token) and the keeper names the holder's X window (`xWindowFor`: the lease's own window's CDP bounds matched against the desktop keeper's `windows(id)` rows — two twins ⇒ its window moved one pixel); the client draws ONLY that window, its dialogs and its menus (xpra-client `admit`: a refused window is never mapped, focused or made main, its draws acked unpainted). The bar is unchanged.
- **THE INPUT SIDE + THE FIT — SEATS:** a new stream source `browser-display` (stream-sources.js) seats a display-for-browser socket by the relay's ticket: `active` = the viewer holding the browser's takeover (input + geometry), `size` = the ruling pane while nobody drives (xpra's OWN configure-window + display size, never input — a new sieve mode, `releaseGeometry` on the way in), `watch` = everyone else. The relay says each viewer its seat (`x-seat`); a takeover sends the window's X focus (an input packet, cut while sizing) and a resize asks one `buffer-refresh`. Pointer / keys / wheel / paste / IME go to X through the view's own field; the agent's verbs stay CDP; the handback is unchanged.
- **THE AGENT IS TOLD:** on the X road the watch answers an HTTP sign-in `Default` (Chrome's own sheet; no credential ever passes through VibeSpace there) and keeps a NATIVE prompt until a main-frame commit of another url; /resolve carries `native` (that sheet, else Chrome's dialog WINDOWS over this conversation's window — `nativeDialogsFor`, the topmost browser window holding a dialog's centre); the CLI answers a page verb `[dialog_open]` by the title («Chrome's own sign-in sheet ("Sign in", "<origin>", realm …)» / «A window of Chrome's own, "Open File", …») while the page-busy ways out run; `dialog accept|dismiss` ⇒ `[native_dialog]`.
- **FOUND ON THE WAY (both fixed, both red-controlled):** (1) src/browser-fact.js let `stuck` through only for dialog / unresponsive / loop / blind — the live view's sign-in bar (`stuck.state === 'prompt'`, lane browser-ui-prompts) never reached a real page; 'prompt' is carried now and its id + native flag move the digest. (`passkey` is dropped the same way — NOT fixed here, reported.) (2) desktop-stream's `seatState` read any seat it did not know as 'free', which fell to the window engine's no-lease relay: a SIZING pane typed (the heavy suite's RED control — keys a watcher forced down its socket — caught it); 'size' is known now and the wiring's input policy relays a seated source's input for its driver only.
- **NOT CHANGED (scope):** Chrome's argv (B1's — the «unsupported flag» infobar is the desk's); the file chooser interception for a page's file input (the agent uploads — a person's GTK chooser would browse the hub's disk); a paired machine's profile and a conversation's own temporary browser keep the screencast (said in the tooltip); BROWSE YOURSELF keeps the page's picture (his window is built on it — its own address row, tab row, picture-geometry input: test-browser-human-ui; on the X road it is a follow-up); B3 / B4 / B5.
- **Gates:** NEW test-browser-picture (fast, 75: the verdict table, the measured rows + RED controls, the words census, the fact's prompt + its pre-lane control, the SIZE sieve + its watch control, the sources + seats, the REAL live-view bridge's ticket/seat lifecycle, wiring pins); NEW test-browser-x-picture (heavy, 32, real Chrome 154 on a private xpra display + the real agent-browser + the real bundle in a viewer Chrome: X pixel = CDP pixel; the sheet VISIBLE in X — 3 102–3 549 px of its blue button — and 0 in a CDP screenshot of the same scene (RED control); `open` / the next verb `[dialog_open]` by name; takeover keys sign in through X; forced watcher keys cut; X input latency median 9–11 ms; Hand back resumes, told once; ⑤ the SAME scene on the screencast road (a headless driver launch): the badge says the page's picture, the product's form under the bar, 0 sheet px in the screencast FRAME itself, CDP input latency median 8 ms); test-browser-prompts ③x (the native road over a fake CDP + the screencast control); test-browser-keeper ⑥ (the three doors over a fake CDP + fake rows); test-xpra-client §X (`admit` + a RED control) and the one worker-asset spelling; test-browser-live ① + ③ (the verdict; the screencast leg unchanged); test-desktop-apps + test-desktop-app-keeper (the allowlist pin re-anchored on the `sizing` clause); test-takeover-keyboard (the yield's getter sink / picture, 22 guarded focusSink sites, its four keyboard-yield controls re-anchored on `sinkEl()`); test-browser-fit (the pane = the X picture's while it shows); test-desktop-viewers (the seat line: the source's seat first); test-architecture (the PURE set; no new spawn site — the rows are the desktop keeper's own `windows(id)`).

### lane channel-row-notices — a standing state is one line that can be put away; a suggestion names its gain (the owner, 2026-10-23 19:2x PT, on his Channels window: 「这个提示最好不要常驻了，很丑陋；然后为啥我这里提示需要重新授权，重新授权干啥？」 + ADDENDUM 1/2; base c1dfc1af = 2.369.348)
- **Measured (his data/channels/adapters.json, shapes only).** The paragraph = the Lark record's `push.state 'unavailable'`, `lastStateCode 'sdk-not-installed'` ⇒ `pushLaneText` ⇒ the live lane's whole UNAVAILABLE_WORDS sentence (npm command, console steps, scope, "polled") as a WARN line on every open. The «需要重新授权» line = the same record's `auth.morePending: 248` (Lark's paged consent, lark.js consentPage: 177 held, 248 of the app's enabled scopes left) ⇒ grantsView `{what:'more', n:248}` ⇒ «重新授权一次即可开启：应用已开通的另外 248 项权限» + 重新授权. Nothing was broken: every DECLARED grant held (send/reactions/feed/people/files/minutes), lastPass ok, renews with 167 h left (no countdown). The pending NAMES were never stored (a count only). Slack's row also carries a stale English `lastAuthError` (a re-authorize with another account ~12 days ago) — not this lane's, reported.
- **The words (PURE src/channel-caps.js).** `pushLaneNotice(push, lane, {t, now, steps})` → null for a healthy / off / unstarted lane, else `{sig, line, details, verb}`: ONE line «实时推送未开启 — 消息靠轮询（30 秒–15 分钟）» (a demotion: «实时推送已退回为游标提醒…» + Re-declare), `sig` = `unavailable:<code>` / `demoted:<at>` (a restart parking the same code is no change), `details` = the lane's CAUSE (new per-lane `UNAVAILABLE_CAUSES`, no command) + «不会漏消息» + where the steps are. `reauthWhyText(kind, reason, facts)` over `REAUTH_WHYS` {read-only: send-scope-not-granted · more-pending: paged-consent · expiring: expires / renewals-stopped / overdue} → `{text, warn, fold}`; an unknown case/reason says '' (never bare). The paged consent in the owner's words: «继续授权以获取应用下一组权限（next 个），总计剩余 n 个权限» + the next page's feature families («— 下一组：云文档、日历…», or «— 授权后 agent 可通过 API 使用…» when an agent holds the account's raw API — the only shipped road that uses a scope beyond the floor; the floor always carries every declared grant) + «；现在的收发消息不受影响»; LED (shown) only with the raw API granted AND the families known, else under ⓘ; `chain: true` (lane lark-consent-chain) switches to «继续授权一次补齐剩余 n 项权限（共 K 页，逐页同意）». grantsText: «再授权一次可开启：… — 现在不做也能照常收发»; beside a feature the paged rest is «应用的下一组权限（剩余 n 个中的 next 个）», never «另外 n 项». Countdowns warn only once overdue.
- **The data.** lark.js `scopeFamily` (namespace → calendar/docs/contacts/mail/approval/attendance/tasks/meetings/minutes/messages/okr/hr/search/other; `SCOPE_FAMILY_OF`) + `PUSH_SETUP` steps (install command, long-connection events, im:message.group_msg, the bot) + `UNAVAILABLE_CAUSES`, each validated by the registry (a cause must name a declared code). The consent writes `morePendingScopes` (≤ 600 names, app order), `nextPageCount` and `morePendingPages` by the SAME `consentPage` the next consent runs (pageBytes) — engine + the three channels-auth writes keep them; grantsView 'more' = {n, next, pages, families (of the NEXT page), api}; adapterView auth gains morePending + nextPageCount; kinds digest gains `pushSetup`; pushView gains `unavailableCauses`. The owner's record has no names until his next consent (the fold says «具体是哪些，授权时才知道»); how many of the 248 a shipped feature needs is not knowable without a vendor read — by construction none of the declared grants (they are the floor).

The conversation window's read-only footer: «可读，回复需要再授权一次（缺 <scope> 权限）».
- **Traps met.** `pushNotice(` is a DOOR name of test-peer-text-census (session-status's notice queue) — renamed `pushLaneNotice`. `.chan-sec-more` is the account head's ⋯ button — the fold is `.chan-sec-details`. The panel's redraw keeps a section's OLD nodes and moves the new children into them: a handler closing over its own element acts on a detached copy — the ack / ⓘ resolve the line and fold through the DOM (`ev.target.closest`, `sec.querySelector`). test-bundle-globals counts «push (» inside an i18n KEY string as a bare call (incident-recorder has a top-level `function push`) — the heading key is «Real-time push — optional». A vendor id in channel-caps reds §78 + §83 (scopeWord reads a URL's last part instead). A new user-state key / module Set = test-record-clear-census H1b / H4 rows; a new lark export = a test-peer-parsers row.

### lane lark-consent-chain — ONE press of Re-authorize walks every Lark consent page in the same tab; the narrowing row only where Lark can refuse (the owner 2026-10-23 19:3x PT, on the row's «重新授权一次即可开启：应用已开通的另外 248 项权限»: 「不能一次性打开所有吗？」 + ADDENDUM 1 19:4x: 「lark 授权窗口那个什么 11 项权限的提示没用了吧？」; base c1dfc1af = 2.369.348)
- **Why it stays pages (measured, lane lark-minutes-scopes):** Lark's doc caps ONE consent at 200 scopes (CONSENT_SCOPES_MAX) and 主开发 measured a 200-scope authorize URL (5.6 KB) answered HTTP 431 by accounts.larksuite.com with the owner's cookies on the request (~8 KB header limit; 115 scopes = 3.3 KB passed) ⇒ CONSENT_URL_MAX_BYTES 3000; the owner's app has 425 enabled user scopes. Grants ACCUMULATE («最新生成的 user_access_token 将包含用户历史上已授予的所有权限»), so pages can be CHAINED: «一次性» = one press, not one page.
- **The chain:** src/channels/lark.js `begin({…, chain})` cuts the whole plan (`consentPlan` = consentPage repeated) and gives its flow `chain: {page, total}` (total = pages done + pages to go, ≤ src/consent-road.js `CHAIN_PAGES_MAX` 5 — an app needing more is said once in the journal and the row counts the rest); the ROUTE / RELAY state signs the place (`c: [page, total]` in the clear part; `stateVerdict` → `parts.chain`, malformed = bad-shape, tampered = bad-hmac; a chain-less state is byte-identical to before). src/oauth-loopback.js reports a code that landed IN A TAB with `tab: true` (the loopback listener, the route's `finishByState`; a paste-back is never chained) and returns what `onDone` answered; the engine (src/server/channels-auth.js `chainNext`) begins the next page over the SAME road and answers `{next: {url, page, total}}`; the landing (consent-road `landingHtml`, `nextOf`) draws «page k/N granted — Page k+1/N comes next — continuing…» with a 1 s `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` + a link (no script — the route's CSP stands; never the close script), the last page closes the tab as before. The loopback listener answers a chain page AFTER its exchange, with `Connection: close` (a kept-alive connection carried page 2's landing to page 1's closed listener — «state mismatch», caught by the smoke).
- **Every road, every door:** a record's Re-authorize (onAuthDone), a switched-client rebind (applyRebind now answers the record), and a CONNECT before the account exists — later pages run on the pending's own adapter (`chainPending`); Connect pressed meanwhile takes the pending's newest token in the same serialized step and marks `p.connectedId`, so a later page's token goes through THE ACCOUNT's token door (identity, cancel, stop judged there); a later page must name the same person as the first. Cancel / Disconnect / Remove / a newer Re-authorize end a Connect's later pages too.
- **Abortable, never repeated:** a later page that does not land (tab closed, declined, its 10 min) is no failed sign-in — no `lastAuthError`, no dead-sign-in item; the earlier pages' grants stay, the row's «另外 N 项» line returns. A declined later page's landing says «what you granted on the earlier pages stays» (`chain-stopped`, route and loopback), never «nothing was connected». The next page is cut from what the held token lacks; a page that granted none of its permissions ends the chain by name (`more < last`).
- **Rule 4 — features first:** when the plan has more than one page, `chainOrder` puts the namespaces a shipped feature reaches (im, contact, calendar, docx, docs, wiki, sheets, drive, bitable, minutes, approval — a MINIMAL map: lane channel-row-notices' families had not landed) on page 1; a single-page consent keeps the app's order byte for byte (lark-shape's ladder pin).
- **A page over the bound is refused by name:** `buildConsentUrl` throws «this consent page's authorize URL is N bytes — over the 3000 Lark's sign-in host takes (it answers 431); the page is not sent» — Lark never answers a 431 in the middle of a chain. A chain's later page reuses the app list its first page read (CHAIN_APP_READ_REUSE_MS 10 min — no vendor call in the landing's wait).
- **The row:** adapterView `consentChain` {page, total} (the running page — the record's flow or a Connect's later page) → channel-caps `consentChainText` «正在授权 第 2/3 页…（在打开的那个标签页里）» + 取消 under the CONNECTED health line (a working account no longer reads «Signing in…» while its page 2 waits); the «N more» grant line waits for the chain's end.
- **ADDENDUM 1 — the narrowing row:** the flow carries `scopesFrom: 'app' | 'floor'` (+ `scopesWhy`, `lacking` = the floor's scopes the app's list lacks); PURE channel-caps `narrowRowVerdict(flow, scopes)` draws «Sign in without …» only on the floor road (with the read's answer: «应用的权限列表没读到（<why>），这次按内置清单请求；若 Lark 拒绝（错误 20027），可去掉这 N 项重试») or when the app's own list lacks a scope this press drops (the no-妙记 app — lark-shape's 20027 legs); on the owner's app road nothing is drawn. NOTE: the addendum said 20027 cannot happen on the app road; it still can when the FLOOR names a scope the app's list lacks — that case keeps its row.
- **Gates:** test-channels-lark-shape ⑪c (the real engine + consent machine + a fake Lark on the loopback road: 248 enabled later ⇒ ONE press, 3 pages, 3 exchanges, each URL ≤ 3000, no extra asked twice, the feature scopes on page 1, the row's words in 3 languages; abort after page 1 + Cancel keeps page 1 and brings the «165 more» line back; the next press asks only the rest; a declined page 2; a page granting nothing stops the chain; RED CONTROLS: a copy paging without the byte bound is refused by name before Lark sees a byte, an engine that never chains holds page 1 only) · test-consent-road ⑫ (the signed place, 7 malformed shapes, the chain page × 3 languages, a javascript: next refused, chain-stopped, the relay page as shipped forwards a chained state verbatim; the REAL routes on the route road and through the admin's relay: 4 pages each under the unchanged CSP) · NEW heavy test-lark-consent-chain (chrome: the row's chain line + Cancel, the «N more» line hidden while it walks and gone after; the dialog's narrowing row absent on the app road, present with its why on the floor road; the real landing route's meta refresh followed by Chrome under its CSP; CONTROLS: the panel without the chain line, the dialog without the verdict) · test-peer-parsers (consentPlan / chainOrder rows) · test-architecture.

## 2.369.348 — 2026-10-23
