### lane channel-reauth-visible — a dead sign-in is ONE standing urgent item, said where the person looks until the account works again; Lark 20064 is a dead grant at its first answer (the owner 2026-10-23 14:2x PT: 「对于需要 reauth 的 channel 应该需要更明显的提示，在 inbox 或者 sidebar 高亮出来这里需要处理，然后进来之后账号行下方显示登录失效需要 reauth」; userW inc-mvl9qdru-dlew; B-f1bb; base ffc8b1ff = 2.369.347)
- **Why:** userW (inc-mvl9qdru-dlew, 2026-10-23): every Gmail account's refresh was refused from 07:14 PT; the engine filed «3 consecutive failures (auth-expired)» items, the pod log then says twice per account `gmail:<id>: superseded — retracted the inbox item (auth-expired)`, and he saw no standing sign — «我 channel 里所有的 email 的链接全都失效了, 且重新 connect 会报错说这个没有授权什么的»; his 11:00 PT re-connect ended «not finished in time» and nothing was raised again. The hub's Lark: its refresh token was revoked at 06:46 PT (20064 — another sign-in of the same user + app) and the record kept a LOW-read «3 consecutive failed passes (vendor-error)» item for 7 h while 30 passes failed.
- **What the code did (read in the tree, not on userW's pod):** the only item was the failure ladder's — filed at EXACTLY the 3rd failure of ONE live entry (`e.failures === FAILURES_BEFORE_LOUD`; a rebuilt entry — a restart, a settings change, a consent — counts again from 0), each re-file first retracting the standing one as `superseded`; `rec.failureItem` is nulled BEFORE the re-file, so a re-file that throws (the 'channels' key's open cap of 20 is shared by every account's items) leaves the item done and the record holding nothing — one way an item retracted as superseded never comes back; `applyRebind` retracted it when a consent LANDED, before any pass proved the sign-in. Lark: `refreshAccessToken` stamped `invalidGrantAt` only for an `auth-expired` refusal and CODE_AUTH has no 20064, so 20064 was `vendor-error` — the dead grant re-POSTed every pass, the ladder's item `normal`.
- **THE FIX ① — the dead sign-in on the record (src/server/channels-engine.js `speakSignin` / `retractSignin`, PURE src/channel-caps.js `signinDeadOf` / `signinCauseOf` / `signinView` / `signinCauseText` / `signinLineText`):** the FIRST pass whose vendor failure is `auth-expired` on a record that HOLDS a sign-in (`auth.tokenEnc`; never `tokenDropped` — the disconnect race; never `vault-locked`; a Connect never finished or a disconnected account keeps the base's 3-strike line) writes `rec.signinDead = {cause, since, item: {id, text}, at}` and files ONE item per account: origin channels, kind action, urgency **urgent** (band 1 — the attention model's one band-1 fact; `high` with its button would sit in band 4), text «<login> (<the account's label>): sign-in expired — re-authorize», i18n keys with the cause as a nested key, action `{type: 'channel-reauth', adapterId, signin: 'expired'}`, openCap bounded by the account count. A failing pass with nothing new writes nothing (the person's own dismissal stands); a NEW cause or `reassert` (a consent that ended unfinished — channels-auth `onAuthDone` / `applyRebind` failure and refusal) re-files the SAME text ⇒ the same id, words updated, reopened. The ladder's item is never filed for `auth-expired` and never beside a dead sign-in (speakFailure returns while `signinDead`); a ladder item standing when the sign-in dies is retracted («the dead sign-in item took over»). Retracted ONLY by the first pass that goes through with an adapter that no longer answers needs-reauth / needs-credentials, by the account's removal, or by the owner's own disconnect (a choice: «not connected» is the owner's act and has its own line). A successful consent retracts nothing — the forced pass after it does.
- **THE FIX ② — Lark's dead refresh (src/channels/lark.js `refreshFailure`):** a token-refresh failure whose code is in REFRESH_DEAD (20037 token-expired, **20064 revoked-elsewhere**, 20073 refresh-refused) or whose words say «refresh_token … revoked / refused / expired / invalid / used», or that CODE_AUTH already typed, is `auth-expired` with `detail.cause` at the FIRST answer; the stamp keeps `invalidGrantCause`, so the later «refresh token was refused» throws keep the cause and no second POST is sent. Rate refusals, 5xx, network failures and the pace / disconnect races are untouched. Gmail names its causes the same way (invalid_grant ⇒ refresh-refused, no refresh token ⇒ token-expired; invalid_client was already `clientRefused`).
- **THE FIX ③ — where the person looks:** the account view carries `authState` ('expired' | 'pending' — a consent in flight | 'ok'), `authCause`, `authSince` on every broadcast and the totals scope carries `signin` (the rail's first probe). The rail: PURE src/channel-focus.js `signinRowOf` (a band-1 row per dead account, through the SAME `needsMe` — the owner's band-1 switch moves it like any row) + `signinAccounts`; sidebar-rail `_railSigninFrom` ⇒ the Channels badge becomes red `⚠N` with the accounts named in its tip. The For-you row draws «Reconnect» in words on its own line (`.ut-reconnect` — the producer-action click, the account's Re-authorize dialog); the For-you window's verb says Reconnect. The Channels window: `signinLine` — the FIRST line under the account's head, «Sign-in expired — re-authorize · <cause> · since <HH:MM>» + Reconnect (the same reauthorize road, the record kept), «Re-authorizing… (in the tab that opened)» + Cancel while a consent runs; its own class so a FOLDED section still shows it; the section's red inset left edge; the head's dot red; the old «Couldn't connect» line is not drawn beside it. ### lane oauth-landing-words — the consent landing shows the address as typed, speaks one language, and names its verdict (the owner 2026-10-23 14:3x PT: 「这个提示里为啥把 email 打码了」 + B-24d8; base ffc8b1ff = 2.369.347)
- **The mask (not ours):** the hub's domain is served through Cloudflare, whose Email Address Obfuscation rewrites any address in an HTML body into `<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection">[email protected]</a>` + an inline decode script — and the landing's CSP (`script-src 'sha256-<CLOSE_SCRIPT>'` only) blocks that script, so the person read «[email protected]» where `LANDING.ok` printed `{user}`.
- **The fix, the address:** PURE `landingUser(address)` (src/consent-road.js) — escaped as text, `@` as `&#64;`, between Cloudflare's documented `<!--email_off-->` … `<!--/email_off-->` markers (belt and braces against any proxy); `fill` now escapes the template FIRST and inserts escaped pieces through function replacements (a name holding `$'` / `$&` no longer expands a replacement pattern).
- **The fix, the language (B-24d8 ①):** `landingLang(acceptLanguage)` — the browser's first language (highest q, earliest on a tie, q=0 refused, `*` none, the header read to 512 chars) through the app's own rule (src/lib/i18n.js `resolveLang` over navigator.language: zh* → zh, ja* → ja, else en); `landingHtml(r, {name, lang})` draws ONE paragraph and `<html lang>`; `LANDING` / `LANDING_WHY` are `{en, zh, ja}` rows, so a zh page no longer carries an English `{why}`. The route (src/routes/channels.js) hands every page `page(r, {lang})` through a wrapper (the pinned `.send(page(r))` stays), adds `Vary: Accept-Language`; the Lark / Gmail landing rows forward the options. Slack's and Dropline's pages take the argument and ignore it — still en + zh + ja (left as found; a follow-up if wanted).
- **The «(expired)» catch-all (B-24d8 ②), measured on the base:** NOT `LANDING_WHY` (bad-hmac read «not started by this VibeSpace, or it restarted since» — in English inside all three lines); it was src/oauth-loopback.js `finishByState`, which answered `why: 'expired'` for EVERY ended flow — a Re-authorize the person cancelled, one replaced by a second press, the cap, the flow's own 10-minute limit (≠ the state's 30 minutes). Now `ENDED_WHY`: timeout → `timed-out`, the engine's sweep → `expired`, `superseded`, `over-limit`, anything else (Cancel, Disconnect, shutdown) → `cancelled`; each has its sentence per language (bad-hmac ⇒ «started before VibeSpace restarted — start it again», expired ⇒ «longer than 30 minutes» = STATE_TTL_MS); an unknown why reads «refused». Slack's `LANDING_WHY` gained the four new words (its page would otherwise have fallen to «refused»).
- **Gates:** test-consent-road ⑪ (PURE: a 27-row language table + PARITY with the shipped i18n.js `resolveLang` row for row (24 rows); every page × language = one paragraph, never the other two; the address in all three languages: both markers, `&#64;`, no bare `@`, nothing `[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.-]+` matches; a 39-page verdict × language matrix — each its own sentence and none of the others'; the state's real verdicts through the page; RED CONTROLS = the bare-address print (the base: the pattern matches), the every-refusal-reads-expired page (red for 10 verdicts), a language-deaf page. The REAL engine + routes: Google from a ja browser (Japanese only, the mailbox marked, close script, Vary), Lark from zh, a CANCELLED Re-authorize (zh), the first of TWO presses (ja, superseded), no language (en), a state from before a RESTART (a new engine behind the same route, en)) 115/115; test-oauth-loopback (timed-out + the five ends by cause) 113/113. The new legs on a base tree (ffc8b1ff): the PURE block crashes (`landingLang` missing), the route legs red — the cancelled and the replaced Re-authorize both print «(expired)» ×3 languages, the Google page prints `ada.road@example.test` bare ×3.

### lane chat-live-tail-pin — a chat started in this window keeps a defined live tail; the pin changes only by intent and every change is traced (the owner's incident inc-mvl02dkn-gop0, 2026-10-23 13:22Z: «为啥没办法把这个对话pin to bottom»; base c8aa8820 = 2.369.344)
- **The capture.** The chat (sess-1-1792756830157) was a LIVE claude chat, 1.4 h old, `streaming:true`, **`historyLoaded:false`** on the server; the page had loaded 88 s before the server logged `[session] created` for it — this window CREATED the chat. Its trace geom: `st:0 sh:818 ch:818 kids:37 ws:null we:null total:null pin:0`. In the 300-event tail: 122 `pageDown` and 46 `wheelBottom carry:818` with `we:null total:null`; two ↓ presses (`userNav jumpToBottom` → `gapReset` → `fsb` to the bottom, then the content collapsed to one screen, `sh 818`); 34 `pageUp` in 0.4 s at `ws:null`; a `runLand {pin:0}` after a run-bar press; wheel-ups at `st:0` carrying 100 … 818 px; and **no `unpin` anywhere** — the snapshot said `pin:0`.
- **Root, client.** `_windowStart` / `_windowEnd` / `_total` were assigned only by a history load (loadHistory, the jumps, the extends). The CREATOR of a chat never gets one: it receives `created`, never `attached` (2.368.4), and for a new conversation (no resumeId) session-lifecycle fetches nothing. The bounds stayed `undefined`, the first live create's `this._total++` made them `NaN` (JSON: null) for good, and every comparison went false: `_atLiveTail` (`NaN >= NaN`) was never true again, so no scroll to the end ever re-pinned and every run-bar landing unpinned; ↓ called `jumpToBottom`, `Math.max(0, NaN − 50)` = NaN, `/api/session-messages?offset=NaN&limit=NaN` — `parseInt` → 0 / 50: the conversation's FIRST fifty messages, rendered as the tail and «pinned» (the one-screen `sh 818`); a wheel-up at the top then took the wheel-top branch (`windowStart > 0` false → `_maybeSeekEarlier`, a no-op without a gap) after `this._pinned = false` — the silent unpin (chat-view.js:706, untraced). The pageDown / wheelBottom storms were the same NaN: nothing later, traced every frame.
- **Root, server.** `_historyLoaded` ("this normalizer holds the whole conversation") was set ONLY by the first WS attach's `rebuildHistory` (ws-handler.js:1176–1195) — neither deferred while streaming nor failing on a session with helpers: never asked. The creator never attaches, so a chat stayed "not loaded" for its whole life unless another tab or a reload attached: in the bundle **every one of the 11 sessions created since that server started** was `historyLoaded:false` (the 主开发's lane chats included), every restored-and-attached one `true`. Consequences beyond the incident: every history page of such a chat re-read and re-converted the whole transcript in `transcripts.view()` under a throwaway `api:` id space (the live stream's ids are `sess-…:`), and the browser / proposal / group report cards were never written live (`feedBrowserCard` / `feedProposalCard` / `feedGroupCard` wait for "the first attach's rebuild").
- **The fix, server (src/ws-create.js).** A NEW conversation (no `resume`+`resumeId`, no `fork`, no adopted `keeperSid`) is born with `_historyLoaded = true` — its normalizer sees record zero, nothing on disk precedes it. A resume / fork / keeper adoption still loads at its first attach (unchanged: a create-time rebuild for a resume would queue the creator's first page behind `rebuildChain` during a restart's attach storm, where today the HTTP read converts at once; the creator of a RESUMED chat keeps reading its history over HTTP under `api:` ids — the remaining sibling, reported). session-schema's note says both writers.
- **The fix, client (src/lib/chat-view.js, chat-view-seek.js, session-lifecycle.js).** ① The window is defined at birth: `0 / 0 / 0` — the live tail IS the window until a history load says otherwise. ② ONE setter `_setPinned(v, why, extra)` for all fifteen sites (constructor, ↓, wheel-up, scroll-handler repin/unpin, send, resume re-tail, load-lock lift, trimBottom, jumpToIndex, jumpToBottom, jumpToAsk, runLand, teleport): traces `pin` / `unpin` {why}; pinning zeroes the new-message count and hides ↓, unpinning re-decides ↓ (`_syncScrollBtn`: shown when off the live tail or the list can scroll down — hidden on a one-screen chat at the tail; re-decided once per frame after a live append to an unpinned view). ③ `_hasEarlier()` (the window starts past 0, a teleport, or a huge session's sentinel short of line 0): with nothing earlier a wheel-up at the top keeps the pin, carries nothing and says «No earlier messages» ONCE per arrival at the top (`_noEarlier`; re-armed when the view leaves the top; quiet while a resumed creator's first page is in flight — `noteHistoryInFlight`); the scroll handler's pageUp asks it too. Nothing LATER (not teleported, `we ≥ total`) ⇒ the wheel-down branch carries nothing and the pageDown trace/fire is skipped (the 122 empty pageDowns that crowded the ring). ④ ↓ on a window that already ENDS at the live tail pins and scrolls — the live branch used to refetch the tail (a full DOM rebuild that re-folded the run the owner had just opened); a paged-out window still refetches. ⑤ `jumpToBottom` lands on the SERVER's tail: when the answer's `total` runs past the slab (our count fell short — a create that rendered no card is never counted) it fetches the slab that ends there (`tailRefetch` trace).
- **Not changed.** The scroll handler's geometric unpin (`!atBottom`, traced, gated by `_resumeDisplacement` in the resume horizon) stays the one displacement-sensitive site — a general positive-evidence gate there would also refuse the product's own programmatic reveals; no site that changes the pin without a user act remains (trimBottom is reached only unpinned — `trimSkipPinned`; the teleport / jumpToIndex / jumpToAsk / runLand callers are all the reader's navigation).
- **Gates.** test-chat-scroll ⑪ (heavy): the census (no bare `_pinned =` in src/lib outside the setter, terminal.js named; a CONTROL re-inserting the base's wheel-top line) + a chat created by the page's own `createSession` (the creator road) behind the stub claude: defined window 0 … the live count, one screen ⇒ pinned + ↓ hidden, six real wheel-ups at the top keep the pin with no pageUp / wheelTop / carry and ONE «No earlier messages»; a busy turn (~240 records/min, Read/Grep/Bash runs, results as live edits): the pin holds, a run header pressed open and closed never unpins, a real wheel up unpins (`scrolledAway`), wheeling back re-pins (`tail`), ↓ pins (`scrollBtn`), hides, lands on the newest card with an unbroken window and no refetch, keeps following; the created chat's history page is served by its live normalizer (`sess-…:` ids, the view's total). Fix 61/61; the base tree (`--tree`) 17 red (its geom: `ws undefined · we null · total null`, history ids `api`; after ↓ its window ran TICK-0 … with a hole — the first slab and the live stream below it). test-chat-trim-guard (fast): the bundle's geom as a unit over the shipped wheel handler (window 0 … 37, one screen, six notches: no page, no carry, pin kept, one noEarlier; a huge session at line 0 the same; CONTROL ws 4 unpins `wheelUp` and pages; at the tail a wheel-down carries nothing) — 5 of them red on base; three verbatim pins follow the new text.
- **Two older controls, re-anchored (not weakened).** test-chat-send-landing's ctl-hold (B-172e ①: without the tail hold the echo of a send from a paged-out window is lost) went GREEN on the fix — the server-tail refetch ALSO keeps that echo (it arrived during the fetch, so the answer's total ran past the slab). ctl-hold now reverts the hold AND the refetch (a `tail` marker in FIXES, asserted in the built bundle) and must still lose the echo; a new variant belt-tail reverts the hold ONLY and must stay GREEN — the refetch's own proof on the real road. test-chat-paging §4d's pre-fix control lost one of its 8 exact anchors (`&& (roomDown < 10 || px > roomDown)) {` — the wheel-down condition now continues on a second line); the anchor follows the new text, the control's patch is the same edge-only carry.
- **Heavy, run directly (no session bus; `ci.mjs --list-affected` = 205 of 342 — the i18n tables + the chat-view hub):** test-chat-scroll, test-attach-ack, test-init-frame, test-incident, test-chat-hygiene-ui, test-cwd-recreate, test-parked-ask-ui, test-group-report-card, test-peer-card-fold-ui, test-browser-propose-chrome, test-artifacts-handover-ui, test-artifacts-chrome (the other creator-road suite), test-inbox-reply-ui, test-codex-effort-meta, test-antigravity-session, test-agy-subagent-chrome, test-collab-live-counter, test-fold-ux, test-browser-resume-ui, test-helper-ask-ui, test-queue-steer, test-restore-liveness, test-reattach-stagger-ui, test-desktop-resume-paging green; test-worktree-userchan-ui red only on its stale-bundle guard (src touched after the build — rebuilt, re-run), test-chat-send-landing / test-chat-paging red on the two controls above (fixed, re-run).

### lane browser-shared-profile-freeze — one stuck page never holds a shared profile's other conversations; a silent page is answered by name; an Update leaves no browser nobody can reach (base c8aa8820 2.369.344; fleet feedback fb-8727ee62fb + fb-0898d92d0a, userW's instance, 2026-10-19 / 10-20)
- **Why:** fb-8727ee62fb: «Shared named browser profile (jarvis-work) repeatedly freezes for every session at once … three more freezes mid page-action (heavy banking pages): Runtime.evaluate / Page.navigate / tab new all time out while status and tab list still answer; `vibespace-browser restart` replies browser_answering and refuses because the daemon answers». fb-0898d92d0a (Chrome 155): «a session's own ephemeral browser and the named profile … run the same /usr/bin/google-chrome with the same flags … yet behave differently on the same heavy site: the ephemeral one reads one workspace's scheduled-payments page, then on switching workspace every CDP Runtime.evaluate times out and it cannot switch back». The daemon-orphan half of fb-8727ee62fb shipped in .332 (lane browser-daemon-survives-update; the restart judges the pages' answers) — Ⓓ below proves it holds on the new road.
- **MEASURED (scripts/measure-shared-profile-freeze.mjs — the REAL keeper + routes + dialog watch + `vibespace-browser`, agent-browser 0.38.2, Chrome 154, the hidden-window rung = the fleet's Xvfb shape; four conversations A/B/D/E on ONE named profile + C on its own ephemeral browser; a CDP TAP per conversation recording every call its driver sent, the target its session rode, the answer's ms):** a page holding its main thread 20 s ALREADY attached held nobody else (B/D/E/C ~110 ms; no renderer shared: 16 renderer processes, the raw client's own evaluate on every other tab 0–2 ms) — it held its OWN conversation (A's `eval` 19.8 s, A's `tab new` 19.6 s behind it: the server's tab list runs `tab list --json` through A's driver). THE FREEZE: every driver attached to the browser's RAW endpoint runs `Target.setDiscoverTargets`, attaches each NEW page target and holds its next command until that target answers `runIfWaitingForDebugger` + `Page.enable` — 30 s per try, tried twice (`waitingForDebugger` false: no resume cascade). One new tab born holding its main thread (8–20 s) held B, D and E's own-tab `eval 1+1` 19.8 s each, ALL AT ONCE; one born with a confirm() 59.8 s each; a tab born on a never-settling load / a light page: ~125 ms. `/json/list`, the tab list and `session info` answered throughout = the report's «status and the tab list still answer». The ephemeral C (its own Chrome, one driver) was never held by the others. CONTROL — the same births on the MEDIATED road (sharing instance: each lease shown only its own targets): 103–117 ms. Upstream agent-browser 0.39.0–0.39.2 does not change it (0.39.0 only lets `close` through the state lock).
- **fb-0898d92d0a (ephemeral vs named) — NOT a difference of the two:** a popup the conversation's OWN page opened born with a confirm() made every later `eval` time out (60 s, 30 s, 30 s) and `tab list` fail tabs_unreadable on the ephemeral browser AND on the named profile alike (a same-site popup shares its opener's renderer; the dialog blocks both); closing that popup freed the opener at once (raw closeTarget 11 ms, `eval` 0.2 s). Both run the same driver and the same flags; what differed on the report's site was its own timing. On production's shape (the managed ephemeral, the wiring's tab source) the dialog watch SEES such a popup's dialog (`dialog_open` in 92–115 ms, even one written synchronously into an about:blank popup on Chrome 154) — the remaining shape is a page holding its main thread, now answered page_busy.
- **THE FIX ① — THE SCOPE ROAD (src/browser-mediation.js PURE + src/server/cdp-mediator.js + the keeper):** an AGENT's lease of a local named profile shared cooperatively (`owner`, the default) is handed a url of ITS OWN through the in-process proxy: grant mode `scope` (`leaseRoadVerdict` — mediated stays mediated; no proxy / ephemeral / remote / the user's own Browse-yourself key ⇒ the raw url, as before). `judgeScope` passes EVERY call as written (no census class, no takeover fence, no interrupt, no window rewrite — the cooperative road keeps its own rules: /resolve's pause, the keeper's windows); what the connection DISCOVERS is the lease's own (the existing `filterEvent` / `admitReply` scope: its tabs, the tabs they open, its creates replayed); an attach BY ID admits that target (`admitReply {explicit}` — the keeper's bind, `tab <targetId>`); revoking a scope grant closes its connections, never its tabs (a detached conversation's page stays). The keeper: `leaseUrlFor` (only on the road the verdict names, only for a lease that STANDS — the identity census's new KNOWN row), the attach answer's env + `cdpUrl`, `leaseCliOpts` (the keeper's own calls in that session carry the SAME value — another spelling re-opens the driver's connection), `attachOpts` on the attach road (`--cdp` = the lease's url), the keeper's own raw reads stay on the raw endpoint (`rawCdpOf`), the scope admits the keeper's own tab for the lease (openOwnTab, reopen), and the server's `tab <target id>` looks the id up in the browser's own list too (the driver's list now holds only the conversation's tabs — another holder's tab is refused not_your_tab by the fence, never no_such_tab: test-browser-human-ui). MEASURED after: the same births ⇒ B/D/E 143–300 ms; B during A's never-settling load 185 ms (was 28.4 s).
- **THE FIX ② — A SILENT PAGE IS ANSWERED BY NAME (src/browser-stuck.js PURE + the dialog watch + routes + CLI):** /resolve asks the tab(s) the verb acts on FIRST — one `Runtime.evaluate` on the dialog watch's OWN session per tab (`pageAnswers`), bounded by PAGE_ANSWER_MS (5 s, the restart verdict's bound), the lease's pinned tab when the keeper knows it, else the conversation's own tabs where only the ones its agent WORKED in (navigated) are judged (measured: the keeper's bound about:blank in the holder's window answered beside the agent's silent page); the ask settles at the FIRST answer (a silent sibling never costs a healthy page's verb the bound); every judged tab silent ⇒ `pageBusyVerdict` ⇒ the CLI answers `[page_busy]` naming the tab, that nothing ran, that other conversations are not affected, and the way out that does not wait on it, and NEVER hands the verb to the driver (so its queue holds nothing). The ways out pass (`PAGE_BUSY_PASS_VERBS`: tab, close, dialog, stop, site-reset and a navigation — MEASURED on a page holding its main thread 15 s: `open` of another site 108 ms; `screenshot` 30 s timeout, `back` 15.6 s, `reload` 14.7 s, `tab new` 9.7 s and a bare `tab close` wait on the page — refused / not offered). A held popup of the silent tab is named with `tab close <its id>`, closed DIRECT through the watch's socket (the driver's own close reads the tab list through the held page) and said closed only once it is GONE — `close_pending` when Chrome accepted the close and kept a busy page (measured: closeTarget answers success at once). MEASURED after: A's next verb `page_busy` in 5.08 s (was 19.9 s), its `open` elsewhere 103 ms, B 89 ms.
- **Gates:** test-browser-mediation ⑧ (PURE judge / road verdict / explicit admission with CONTROLS = the mediated judge; the real proxy in mode scope over the fake browser — another holder's new tab never reaches the scoped connection, CONTROL the raw one is told; an attach by id passes; no census refusal; no interrupt; a revoke keeps the tabs; the real keeper hands two owner-profile leases a url each, in their env AND in the keeper's own calls) + its NEGATIVE CONTROL row re-pinned (an owner profile is unmediated and now scoped); test-browser-stuck ①p (the verdict and words) + ③p (the REAL routes + CLI + watch over the fake browser: page_busy by name in 492 ms at a 400 ms bound, the browser CLI never spawned, the ways out run, `--json`, a held popup closed by id through the watch, close_pending, CONTROL a CLI copy without the door spawns the browser CLI); test-browser-live ⑩ (the REAL driver, `BROWSER_LIVE_ONLY=freeze`: B 97 / 101 ms while a tab is born busy / with a confirm(), RED CONTROLS a driver on the RAW url 7.7 s / held at 12 s; A's own page page_busy in 5.09 s, B 89 ms, `open` elsewhere 103 ms; on the base tree 4 of 8 red: 0 scope grants, B 7.7 s, B 59.8 s, no page_busy); test-browser-daemon Ⓓ (an Update on the scope road: the daemon and Chrome outlive the old url, the boot RE-OWNS them, the next command's NEW url reaches the same daemon, browser and tab; RED CONTROL the old url reaches nothing); test-browser-identity-census (`leaseUrlFor`'s fence row) + test-browser-human's HOLDER census (`leaseUrlFor` conversation-only); test-browser-ephemeral (the attach anchor re-spelled `leaseUrl`); test-browser-human-ui (the agent's `tab <his tab>` still refused not_your_tab on the scope road). ⑩ c MEASURES its precondition (the page silent to a raw ask, its hold started from the raw client — a page-armed timer is clamped to ≥ 1 s in a tab not in front, which made an earlier draft of the leg flaky).
- **Left as found:** the server's `tab` verbs read the tab list through the conversation's own driver, so `tab new` / a bare `tab close` still wait on a page that holds its main thread (until it lets go or the driver's timeout) — page_busy offers the navigation that does not; a mediated lease's grant is unchanged; a takeover still pauses the cooperative road at /resolve only (no interrupt of a scope grant's calls in flight — the mediated road's ruling, not extended here).

### lane hub-dies-dead-ssh-host r2 — the dead-machine RED control is deterministic (test-only; on 35af2b64)
- **Why:** 主开发, the .346 stack's release chain: test-restore-liveness §7's RED CONTROL («the same hub with a feedStdin that does not listen DIES of the first stdin road») read red once (1 of 86; the re-run and the runner passed) — a control that depends on timing.
- **What made it timing-bound (measured here):** a child's stdin is a socketpair, not a 64 KiB pipe — ~108 KiB flushes into it before a write blocks (wmem_default 212992); the leg's ~610 KB tools tar met EPIPE 40/40 alone, but three things were still loose: (1) the hub had 45 s to print `Ready.` — under a loaded chain a late boot read as «survived» (the steps got NO ANSWER, `exited` null); (2) only `write EPIPE` counted, while a reader that leaves unread bytes resets the socket (`ECONNRESET`) — the same death, read as no death; (3) the death was judged after all five steps, not at the road that kills.
- **The control now:** the tools tar is padded to ~6 MB (one tracked tool, `data/bin/vibespace-docs`, in the throwaway worktree — under installAgentTools' 8 MB tar bound, far past any socket buffer); the stub ssh closes its stdin first (`exec 0<&-`); the boot gets 120 s and «did not boot» is its own red; the hub must EXIT (code 1) within 15 s of the tools install, with `write EPIPE` / `write ECONNRESET` / `ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED` in its journal and the next request refused. The fixed hub meets the same ~6 MB tar and must stay alive with no stream write error. test-dir-complete ⑦'s in-process control counts EPIPE / ECONNRESET / ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED (its payloads were already 1–3 MB) and its stub closes stdin too.
- **Runs (on this tree, 2026-10-23):** test-restore-liveness 5× (two at a time, staggered) with test-new-session-dialog and test-agentd-dial looping beside them (19 load runs, all green; load 6.3–9.3): **5/5 ALL PASS (87)** — every control hub booted in ~0.5 s and EXITED (code 1) right after the tools install with `write EPIPE` in its journal, the next request refused; every fixed hub alive with no stream write error. test-dir-complete 10× under the same load: 10/10 46/46.

### lane cli-call-timeouts — every agent CLI bounds its wait and names it; logging progress answers after the store write (hub feedback fb-8ae9289552; base c8aa8820 2.369.344)
- **Why:** hub feedback fb-8ae9289552 (2026-10-23, the lane group, 2.369.342): «vibespace-task progress hung for 30+ min once … while the hub answered http in 1 ms and load was 5; the same line re-issued 3 min later landed in 2 s. A CLI call must bound its wait and say what it waits on (the shared folder on NFS?), never hang.»
- **What the record shows (read-only journal 03:55–04:50 PT):** no line names the 04:1x hang. The same window had the OneDrive FUSE mount going `slow` → `wedged` (04:24, a context folder of ANOTHER group on it, its TASK.md skipped by the B-afc4 door) and a 616 MB search-index backfill. Two facts frame the fix: (1) the CLI's bare global fetch (undici) caps each phase at 300 s, so a 30-min wait was never ONE stalled response — the agent saw no bounded, named end; (2) the store's `_save()` wrote EVERY group's `.vibespace/TASK.md` synchronously on the caller's turn (mkdir + read + write + rename on the context folder — NFS / a FUSE mount), so a progress answer waited on every folder the store mirrors. Both are fixed structurally; the exact 04:1x stall is not reproduced.
- **THE ONE CALL (NEW src/cli-call.js, SHARED: PURE timing + words, the one node http/https transport):** `BUDGETS` read 15 s / write 30 s / wake 60 s; `classOf` (a GET reads, the rest write, a site names `wake`); `budgetOf` (`--timeout` › a site's base `ms` › the class; a long-poll's own wait `extraMs` always added); `takeTimeout` / `cliStart` (the flag out of argv IN PLACE, stops at `--`, a bad value refused exit 2); `phaseOf` connect → answer → step → body; `expiryLine` = ONE line: «the hub at <host> did not take the connection in N s — nothing was sent» / «the hub did not answer in N s» / «the hub answered the request but <step> did not return in N s» / «the hub answered (HTTP n) but the rest of its answer did not arrive in N s»; a write / wake adds «it may still take effect: look before you repeat it»; exit 124. `call()` is fetch-shaped (a real Response; a network error REJECTS with node's own error), buffers the answer under the budget, `stream` (attachments), a piped node stream body (exit push), `signal` (the browser dialog long-poll), `onExpiry: 'throw'` (a poll that must not end the process).
- **THE SERVER-SIDE STEP:** `stepAhead(res, key)` sends a **103 Early Hints** carrying `X-VibeSpace-Step: <key>` before a route waits on a slow step of its own — the final status stays free (a refusal after it is still a 403), fetch skips 1xx (old CLIs unaffected). Node sends a 103 only with a Link header, so `</api/agent/docs>; rel=preconnect` rides along. Keys are a closed table (`STEP_WORDS`: folder-write / folder-read / compact / approval / vendor / command); the hub sends the KEY, the CLI words it. Wired on `POST /api/agent/msg/dispatch` (`compact`).
- **THE MIRROR (src/task-groups.js):** `_syncTaskMd` keeps its shadowed / blocked skips (in-memory) and renders, then `_queueMirror` — per group, newest content wins, one write in flight; `_runMirror` writes mkdir / read / write tmp / rename through `mirrorFs()` (server.js: `app.locals.safeFs`, a worker with a deadline and the blocked-mount door; `fs.promises` when none), each op bounded by `MIRROR_BOUND_MS` 10 s; a miss keeps the copy for ONE retry timer (30 s, unref'd) or runs a newer queued copy at once. `mirrorStateOf(id)` → null | `{behind, pending, since, why}` (behind once a write outlived its bound or failed); `mirrorIdle()` for suites. The progress route answers `mirror: {behind: true, since, why}` only when behind; `vibespace-task progress` prints ONE fixed line under the receipt.
- **THE CLIs (16 tracked + the generated vibespace-status):** each loads `src/cli-call.js` in a checkout / `./cli-call.js` beside it (boot copy `createCliCallCopy`, gitignored, AGENT_TOOLS), refuses by name without it (exit 2, nothing sent), and calls `CC.cliStart` first. `--timeout` + `--call-timeout` on task / status / ask / msg / feedback / docs / design / page / remote; `--call-timeout` only where `--timeout` already means something (job run/ask, vault run, channels api wait) or a verb forwards argv (api, app, browser, window, exit). Site budgets: msg dispatch 240 s (COMPACT_WAIT_MS 180 s + the wake), send --wake / job run / api conversations.open / channels refresh + raw-API writes / browser + window + page writes = wake; job wait + app proposal wait = read + their `wait`; browser dialog long-poll = +20 s, throw; channels attachment = stream 120 s; exit use 90 s / run 105 s / pull + push 6 h (a transfer scales with its size; test-exit-run verify r2 holds a pull past any shorter client deadline); vault run 690 s. vibespace-exit's and vibespace-vault's own unbounded `http.request` postLong (written to dodge fetch's 300 s cap) now go through the one call with those bounds.
- **CENSUS (test-architecture §99):** every tracked data/bin/vibespace-* (git ls-files, §96) has no bare `fetch(` / `http(s).request|get(` / `require('http').request(` outside `EXEMPT97` (vibespace-hook.mjs: own 2.5 / 3 s aborts + 8 s exit; vibespace-opencode-op: the opencode server's own port, per-request timeoutMs); every `CC.call` caller loads the one call by its literal names and runs `CC.cliStart`; the brief's 16 CLIs call through it; no dead exemption; the generated vibespace-status template too; the ship path (copy + AGENT_TOOLS + .gitignore). CONTROLS: a bare fetch planted in vibespace-task and the pre-lane postLong shape are RED, CC.call and a comment are not. `src/cli-call.js` joins SHARED.
- **TESTS:** NEW scripts/test-cli-call.mjs (fast, 41, ~6 s): ① PURE budgets / flag / words; ② the transport over loopback hubs (silent → answer, a 103 → step, half an answer → body, 10.255.255.1 → connect, a real Response, 4xx, a beacon then a 403, FormData, a piped stream, stream mode, abort, ECONNREFUSED); ③ the real vibespace-task / -msg / -feedback / -job exit 124 with ONE line, a bad value exit 2 — CONTROL: the helper with its expiry cut is still waiting at 3× its budget; ④ the REAL progress route (express + agent-routes + the store, the folder write held by a fake slow mirror fs): exit 0 in ~80 ms, the entry kept, behind after the bound, said by the next answer, the copy lands once the folder answers — CONTROL: the base c8aa8820 store (a mutant-copy, a stalled 1.2 s TASK.md write) expires the same CLI, exit 124 (SKIP by name on a depth-1 checkout). Census moves: test-peer-text-census walks src/cli-call.js (its print rows judged, `cliStart(` a print helper), test-cli-registry EXCLUDED `cli-call.js`, test-msg-cli-groups the shipped-module set, mount-reader-census agent-tool-generators 23 → 25; host-layout copies gain cli-call.js (test-cli-one-text, test-backlog-no-truncation, test-channels-agent-cli, test-webhook-cli); TASK.md readers await `mirrorIdle()` (test-backlog-priority, test-mount-stranded, test-record-clear-stores).

### lane open-task-binds — a conversation opened INTO a Task Group is a MEMBER of it (one bind writer), and a group's folder includes itself (base c8aa8820 2.369.344)
- **Why:** the owner 2026-10-23 05:4x: «你最近建立的车道都不在 VibeSpace 车道 这个组里». `vibespace-api conversations open … --task T-…` recorded only the BIRTH group (ws-create `_initialGroupId` → meta `taskId`): the agent's `groupsForSession` counted it, the group's `sessions` (the panel, its counts, its activity log) did not — two truths. The New Session window's Task bound through the client's per-tab pending queue only (a reload before the id lost it); an automation has no tab at all.
- **The folder half (measured on the production store, read-only):** the group's folder is stored as `{path: '/var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/**', recursive: true}` — the agent context prints a recursive folder as `<path>/**` (task-groups.js renderTaskMd), and that print was written back as the path. `c === f.path || c.startsWith(f.path + '/')` then matched NO conversation, not even one started exactly at `/var/tmp/vibespace-lanes` (every lane's cwd). The equality half already existed server-side; app.js `_taskCwdSuggestions` had only the strict prefix.
- **THE FIX:** PURE `src/task-membership.js` — `folderOf` (a glob tail `/**` · `/*` is the recursive switch, never part of the path; `_sanitizeFolders` uses it, so every reader — `list()` for the panel, `groupsForSession`, TASK.md — sees the stored glob normalized with no migration), `insideFolder` (a folder includes itself; a recursive one every path under it on a whole segment) used by `groupsForSession`, sidebar-tasks `_folderRec` / `_sessionFolderMatch` and app.js `_taskCwdSuggestions`; `birthBindVerdict`. ws-create marks `_birthBind = {groupId, by}` from the create's `taskId` (the same id shape as `_initialGroupId`; the meta keeps `taskId`, no new key); conversation-ops `settleBirthGroups()` binds every marked live conversation through `bindConversation` (the owner's bind route's writer) once it has its OWN id (a fork waits past its source's), then drops the mark; server.js `broadcastActiveSessions` (the session list's ONE notify point — every id adoption broadcasts) asks it, and the open verb asks it once more after its id wait. An automation's open writes conversations.bind's own activity line (`boundNote` — ONE spelling); a window's open writes none, as the owner's route. `conversations.open --task` into a group the CALLER is not in ⇒ `not_granted` (conversations.bind's rule: the open now writes what a bind writes). The client's pending queue is unchanged (an idempotent second caller of the same writer; it still carries a fork's extra groups).
- **Gates:** NEW fast test-task-groups (30; on the base tree 24 RED — the glob folder matched nothing, nothing bound the opened conversation): the PURE tables, the real store over the owner's stored shape, conversations.open --task end to end over the real conversation-ops + the real store (pending ⇒ nothing; id + notify ⇒ in `sessions`, `groupsForSession` agrees without the birth note, ONE activity line; a fork; a window's open; a deleted group dropped; not_granted), the panel's own resolver evaluated from sidebar-tasks.js, the wiring pins and the folder-rule census (no hand-rolled `startsWith(<folder>.path + '/')` in a Task Group folder file) + its controls. test-conversation-ops' mutant tree copies the new PURE module; server.js stays at its line ratchet (the call rides the function's first line, after test-exit-rejudge's pinned re-judge order).
- **Left as found:** the birth group still counts in `groupsForSession` after the owner UNBINDS the conversation (the pre-id window needs it, and a persisted «bound» fact would be a new meta key — lane new-session-form owns that key's name); the conversations opened with --task BEFORE this fix stay outside `sessions` until bound once (`conversations bind` or the panel's tag).

- **Finding 1 (BROKEN): For you's «Granted access» granted nothing.** The agent asked `vibespace-ask "Share 'Lark (company login)' with me…" --options "Granted access|Send it myself"`; an option chip's press posts its label as the reply (design-user-inbox-reply D3a), so «Granted access» typed two words and the profile stayed invisible (`access: none`). Nothing let an ask carry a grant.
- **THE ASKER'S ROAD:** `vibespace-ask … --grant browser:<label|id>` → the agent route (src/agent-routes/status.js) resolves the profile from the keeper's own `list().profiles` through NEW PURE src/ask-grant.js (`parseGrantSpec`, `browserGrantTarget`: id exact, else label case-insensitive; unknown 404 / ambiguous 409 / a temporary browser 409 / no keeper 503, nothing filed; `channel:` / `machine:` refused 400 with their road — `vibespace-channels request`, the machine row's «Who can use it») and files `action: {type:'browser-grant', profileId, label}` (`grantItemFields`); ACTION_IDENTITY `browser-grant → profileId`. vibespace-ask's usage and vibespace-browser's not_owner way-out name the flag.

The model's `grantBrowser` (src/lib/user-todos-actions.js): the asker's live webui id → a FRESH `GET /api/browser/profiles/:id/use` → PURE `grantUseBody` (All agents / already listed ⇒ nothing to write; else the whole list as the dialog's wire rows + `{kind:'session', session}`) → the owner's whole-list PATCH with the `base` it read (409 list-changed ⇒ read again once) → ONLY THEN `postReply` with `grantReplyText` («Granted — … Attach it with `vibespace-browser use <id>`.» / «Already allowed — …»), its toast the grant's words. A refusal is toasted by «Who can use it»'s own words; nothing reaches the agent before the write landed.
- **A REPLY READS AS A REPLY:** every option chip, tray and window, reads «Reply: <label>» (`optionWords`; 回复：… / 返信：…); the reply sent is still exactly the label.

The tester's real complaint was jargon: both confirms now say what happens in plain words (a free check per account, the same as /usage, at most once a minute; still owner-pressed, §ban-safety unchanged; «Check now»); the four old keys left zh/ja.

The fast tier found three more: test-live-bar-layout's worded-button census (the grant button rides the 24 px `.ut-act` icon box ⇒ `.ut-action-grant { width: auto }` + the phone's 36 px, beside the exit / proposal rules), test-record-clear-census (a profile's `label` read into a refusal sentence ⇒ the temporary-browser refusal names the id), test-channel-names' control anchor on ACTION_IDENTITY's tail (the `browser-grant` row sits before `open-channel`).

### lane gmail-draft-not-a-message — a Gmail DRAFT is never a message of its thread: the record's kind is read off the vendor's labels (base c8aa8820 2.369.344; fleet feedback fb-9aa1d3bd1e, userW's instance, 2026-10-22)
- **Why:** the filing agent: «Channels 的 Gmail 会话视图把一封从未发出的草稿（labels DRAFT，今天已移 Trash）当成线程里的正式消息显示在顶部（带日期 Oct 8、To/Cc），用户误以为已发出». `threads.get` lists the account's unsent DRAFT among a thread's messages; `toRecord` made it an ordinary record — dated by its save (the TOP of the thread when saved early), its To / Cc drawn as the envelope of a sent mail, `isSelf` false (no SENT label), so it was also an unread mail from the owner's own address, a rule match, the row's last line when saved last.
- **THE FIX:** `src/channel-record.js` — `RECORD_KINDS` gains `draft` (+ `draftState` saved | trashed, CLOSED: TRASH / SPAM ⇒ trashed); `asDraftRecord` re-judges a stored record off `raw.labelIds` at read (`store.patched`, no migration — the reported record is served as a draft); PURE `draftsOf(records)` = the ONE rule the window and the agent's read ask: the messages in order, the standing drafts AFTER them, the binned only counted, a saved draft a LATER draft or a later own SENT mail in the same thread stands for is `replaced` (Gmail replaces a draft's message on every save and deletes it on send — the stored copy is a version Gmail no longer holds; never drawn as «not sent» over a sent mail). Gmail `toRecord` sets the kind; the thread's title-cache instant (`lastMailAt`) skips drafts. Every door a system notice is kept out of now keeps a draft out too: the filter (no rule, no wake, no For-you, no judge — `matchRecord` / `ruleHits` / `sentHit` / `placeHit` / `inferCandidate` / the estimate), `FO.systemRead` (never unread, never moves the read line, never news, never a watch hit — the engine's judge context lines included), the store's row line + instant. The window draws the drafts in a slot after the last message (before the Outbox): ONE dashed «Draft · not sent / 草稿 · 未发送 / 下書き · 未送信» row (saved time, its words, no avatar / head / facts / message bar), «1 deleted draft» for the binned; the around sheet too. The agent's read (`readFor` / `readAroundFor`) serves the drafts after the messages with `draftsTrashed`; the CLI prints `[draft · not sent] <words>` (no author, id or To / Cc), counts them apart in the header and says the binned count. Search: a stored draft hit carries `kind: 'draft'` (`searchFor`), the CLI marks it `[draft · not sent]` and the owner's Search dialog says «Draft · not sent» where the author would stand.
- **Gates:** test-channel-record ⑨ (the kinds, the re-judge, `draftsOf`'s table; CONTROL a copy without the draft kind serves the stored draft as the thread's FIRST message), test-channels-gmail-shape ㉓ (labels → kind ×7; the REAL engine over a fake vendor: kinds stored, anchor = the newest mail, the row's last line + instant = the last MAIL; CONTROL a copy whose toRecord drops the kind ⇒ the draft is the row's last line), test-channel-window-render ⑬c (zh: the mails only as rows, ONE draft row after the last, no To / Cc, «1 条草稿已删除», a newer save by broadcast replaces it in place; the ja words), test-channel-filter ⑱ (RULE_KINDS × a draft carrying the peer twin's words / mention / place: no hit, no sent / place / infer candidate, never in the estimate; CONTROL a copy without the two draft guards ⇒ keyword / mention / time-window hit it), test-channels-focus (a draft adds 0, never moves the line), test-channels-agent-cli (the read's and the search's draft lines), census rows: test-peer-text-census (`drafts` / `m.kind` / `r.draftsTrashed` + the draft-line pin), test-peer-parsers (4 exports), test-architecture §79 (channels-access requires channel-record).
- **Left as found:** a draft stored BEFORE it was binned or discarded stays drawn as «not sent» until a later draft or send of the thread replaces it — the history walk reads `messageAdded` only (a label change or a delete of a stored message is never learned; learning it is a `labelAdded` / `messageDeleted` walk + a side line, a lane of its own). A trashed MAIL (not a draft) stays the mail it was.

### lane oauth-setup-instructions — before the first attempt, the setup card says which client to create and the exact redirect addresses THIS instance needs; Gmail gains a fixed loopback for a Google Web client (base c8aa8820 2.369.344)
- **Why:** the owner 2026-10-23: «web application 的话，在集群外部署你是不是应该提供一下 redirect uri 有关的 instruction，不然用户会懵逼吧». A self-hoster with their own Google / Lark / Slack app met the redirect URIs only in a fold AFTER a refusal — and the refusal (Google «Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch», Lark 20029) happens on the vendor's OWN page, which the product never sees. Measured: the fleet's Google client is a Desktop app client (any 127.0.0.1 port, never an https address), so every relay / route road refuses at Google; a Web application client takes https AND `http://127.0.0.1:<fixed port>` but only addresses registered EXACTLY, so Gmail's ephemeral port could never serve one.
- **THE CARD (NEW PURE src/oauth-setup.js, imports consent-road only):** `setupCard({kind, redirect, base, relayPages, preset, origin, clientType})` → which client to create (`create`: Google = a Web application client whenever this instance has an https address or a relay page, a Desktop app client only for a hub whose browser is on the same machine with no relay — with the reason and the other kind as `alt`; every other vendor its one app; a company preset nothing; Dropline nothing — it registers its own client), the exact addresses (`rows`, each with when it is used: a person's own app's three ways back — ① the project's public relay page, ② their own copy of docs/slack-relay, ③ this instance's own https route — the fleet's page standing for ①② on a pod; the kind's FIXED loopback; Drive's rclone address; a company preset only its relay page or this instance's own address, NEVER the public page), the row the sign-in from THIS page uses now (consentRoad's own verdict), the console path + links, where the ID / secret go, the vendor's refusal words. `WORDS` = one i18nKey table; `docSection()` renders deploy/README.md's block from the same model.
- **ONE SOURCE (the registry rows' NEW `redirect` block, checkRow-validated, closed keys):** `console {path, links}`, `refusal`, `create`, `clientTypes` (Google), `loopback` (Lark's = its setup.callbackUrl — one spelling; Gmail's NEW `GMAIL_LOOPBACK_URL` = 127.0.0.1:17866/gmail/cb), `also [{uri, for:'drive'}]`, `selfRegisters + vendor` (Dropline). NEW scripts/gen-oauth-setup-doc.mjs writes deploy/README.md's «Register the redirect URIs» block between markers (`--check`); test-integration-registry holds the file equal and the README's addresses equal to the card's, in order.
- **GMAIL'S CLIENT KIND:** the Gmail row gains a non-secret field `clientType` (web | desktop; a gdrive-clients entry's `"clientType"` passes through preset-layers + the store's delegate values) read as a preset FACT (`delegate.facts: ['clientType']`, checkRow: a delegating row's non-secret fields only); the Gmail adapter gains the account OPTION `clientType` ('' | web | desktop — the preset's fact is its default for a new account) and its consent row `mode: ['ephemeral','fixed','public']` + `callbackUrl`. `consentRoad({clientType})`: 'desktop' ⇒ the loopback BEFORE the relay (`desktop-client` — a Desktop client takes no https address), 'web' ⇒ relay › route › the FIXED loopback (`fixed: true`; the adapter binds its registered callback, a busy port = the existing named refusal + paste-back), '' ⇒ as before. No port setting: channel-settings option roles are a closed string/enum set — 17866 is a documented constant.
- **WHERE IT IS SHOWN:** the Connect / Re-authorize / Duplicate dialogs draw the card FOLDED (label-less node rows, `setupFolds`) above the sign-in block for Custom / a borrowed storage client and per company preset — before any attempt; ⚙ → Integrations draws a Communication group FIRST with one setup card per OAuth type (from `GET /api/channels?scope=accounts` — the kinds digest's NEW `oauthSetup {base, relayPages, presets[{key, relayPage, clientType}]}`; not `integ-card`s, so the window's census is unchanged) and the Dropline card's «registers its own client» line; the refusal fold (`askAdmin.notes`, also for a FIXED loopback consent) carries the card's lines: the vendor's error words, the console path, and for an https address the Desktop-client case. NEW src/lib/oauth-setup-card.js draws all three.
- **ADDENDUM (主开发 12:24Z, the owner: is the relay generic?):** the card's road section and the README say it exactly — the public page is static, holds nothing, the BROWSER redirects, so an instance needs only be reachable from the approving browser (same machine, LAN, Tailscale, .local/.lan/.home, ::1/fc00::/7); it redirects only to such private addresses (a public https hostname is shown the code — never an open redirect); ① register it, ② host your own copy (data-allow), ③ register your own https route directly; the paste-back fold is the last resort; the public page's address is pinned (test-consent-road ⑨); presets never show ①.
- **GATES:** `npm run build` green (test-architecture: §78 dead exports, §81 literal loopback ports); a keep-going sweep of every fast suite 486/486 green after two census rows (test-takeover-census 27: the two new `<details>` folds; test-peer-parsers 323: `clientTypeOf` placed) and a re-run of the 37 `git ls-files` censuses on the staged tree; test-changelog-style 40/40 on a scratch copy at .346 (in place it reds by design — the heading is two patches ahead of 2.369.344); test-consent-road 92 (was 71: ⑨ the client kind, the real engine with a Web company client, the card's addresses per instance shape, RED = c8aa8820's verdict sends a Desktop client through the https relay page), test-integration-registry 312 (was 301: (f) the redirect blocks, checkRow controls, the Gmail loopback's one definition, deploy/README.md held equal + a hand-edited-address control), test-channels-gmail-shape 305 (the option list pin). Heavy: test-integrations-ui 242 (was 220: ⑬ the three surfaces, Copy, 375 px, the fold before the first attempt, «Desktop app» ⇒ 127.0.0.1:<any port> with not-said / Web as the control; ⑪ the refusal fold's console lines), test-channels-i18n 176 (zh / ja: the console link labels translated, 'slack' an allowed brand), test-channels-engine 818, test-channels-accounts 190, test-channels-aggregate 443, test-record-clear-walk 164, test-voice-teach-chrome 60, test-mounts-dialog-extract 61 (the storage dialogs unchanged), test-channel-jump 53, test-oauth-field-parity 271; test-vendor-whitelist 317 = base.
