### lane vault-paste-request — an agent ASKS for a secret, the owner PASTES it into a masked box in For you, the agent is told where it went (never the value); the Vault window's 添加… gains 「其他密钥或密码…」 (base c8aa8820 2.369.344)
- **Why:** the owner, 2026-10-23 05:1x: 「应该允许你给我弹一个保险库输入框让我直接 paste 进去，省得我还得手动去保险库搞」 — an agent could only say «please put X in the vault» and the owner walked to the Vault window; ADDENDUM ⑥ the same morning (the owner in the Vault window's 「＋ 添加…」): 「我压根没法添加啊」 — there was no way to add a plain secret the registry lists no row for.
- **THE VERB (one verb, two shapes):** `vibespace-vault request "<what>" --purpose "<why>" [--into <row>.<field> | --kind api-key|password|secret] [--name <label>]` — the first argument being words (not a `vault://` reference) selects the paste shape; `request <vault://…> --for "<purpose>"` (lane vault-manual-and-lock's grant ask) is unchanged. DEVIATION from the brief's `--for <row>.<field>`: in the grant shape `--for` already IS the purpose — one flag with two meanings would be an agent's silent mismatch — so the place is `--into`, and `--for` in the paste shape exits 2 naming `--purpose` / `--into`. No `vibespace-ask --secret` (one spelling). `uses` lists the paste boxes still waiting (`pastes`).
- **PURE src/vault-paste.js:** the ask's verdict (words / purpose one line each, bounded, a hidden or direction character refused `hidden_chars`, a secret shape «redacted»), the place (`targetOf`: a CARD row's `secret: true` field — an account-bound / per-machine row, a non-secret field, an unknown row / field each refused by name; else a FREE entry with its kind + label), the card's lines (i18nKey-declared, the row / field / kind labels as `{key}` WORDS params), the agent's receipt (`receiptText`: STORED where + for what / REFUSED with the cause and the 10-minute quiet / WITHDRAWN by a lock — every piece through peer-text `toAgentText` kind line), a free entry's facts, the value rule (trimmed like the registry, ≤ 8192).
- **ORCH src/server/vault-paste-door.js:** THE ITEM IS THE REQUEST — ONE For-you action item (origin vault, high) whose action carries ids and the place only (`{type: 'secret-request', requestId, into, kind, conv, scope}`); the agent's words / purpose / a new entry's label are the item's own i18n lines (`wordsOfItem` reads them back), so "Clear content…" takes them and a restart keeps the request (the index is rebuilt from the store). The owner's answer: a field ⇒ integration-store `setIntegration` (THE writer — trimmed, the field's own `validate`, sealed, the masked view broadcast; `invalid-values` ⇒ 400 invalid_value with the rule, never the value); a free entry ⇒ `vault.secretPut('secret:<10 hex>', v, {prov: 'owner', actor, label, kind, note})` and THE PASTE IS THE GRANT — the run door's new `grantPasted` lets the asking conversation use THAT new entry in runs for 8 h (no 验证是你: the entry did not exist before the paste, so a forged press grants only the value it supplied). Then `noteUse` (door `paste`, the purpose, a receipt), the audit lines `vault-secret-request` / `-stored` / `-refused` / `-added` / `-deleted` (names, never a value), the item resolved «stored», the receipt via `deliver.stashFor` (the asker's next turn — free, never a wake). ONE STATE: the item leaving open by ✓ / ✕ is a refusal the agent is told; a reopen of an answered one goes back to done. Bounds: 4 open per conversation, 64 hub-wide, the same place while open ⇒ its id (`already: 'open'`), quiet 10 min after a refusal.
- **A LOCK ACT WITHDRAWS EVERY OPEN REQUEST** (design q-043 decision ③ — test-vault-engine's census asks every vault-ask producer to end its asks on a lock): item done `vault_locked`, receipt WITHDRAWN («ask again once it is unlocked», no quiet). A request filed while locked or kept over a restart (a boot is no lock act) WAITS: its box says `vault_locked` by name with 解锁… inline (THE unlock dialog) — the brief's locked state.
- **ROUTES (src/routes/vault.js `registerPasteRoutes`):** agent `POST /api/agent/vault/secret-request` (the vsst_'s conversation by `addressableId`; a job token ⇒ job_no_use by its prefix — no jobs-stash reach; a `value` on the request ⇒ value_in_request, dropped) · person `POST /api/vault/secret-requests/:id/answer` {answer: store | deny, value} (renamed with `/answer` so the approval census sees the door) · person `POST /api/vault/secrets` {label, kind, note, value} (⑥) · person `DELETE /api/vault/secrets/:id`. `person()` now also takes `value` off the body on every refusal / failure path. `GET /api/agent/vault/uses` adds `pastes`.
- **THE ENGINE / INVENTORY / RUN DOOR:** `SECRET_RE` += `secret`; `secretPut` keeps `label` / `note` / `kind` beside the box and `secretNames` lists them; a refusal's words say «a stored password or key». vault-inventory: a `secret:` row (label, kind, note as detail, provenance «By you», revealable), purpose NEW `keys` «Passwords & keys» (between automation and agents), its delete door `DELETE /api/vault/secrets/<id>`, band doors `paste` + `deny` for a paste request. vault-run.js `isFreeEntry` + run-door `classOf` make a free entry runnable (the row's switch, a grant) — `vault://secrets/secret:<id>/secret`.
- **THE CLIENT:** NEW src/lib/vault-paste-box.js — THE masked field (`secretInput`: password, autocomplete off, no spell-check, password-manager ignore attributes, Enter = done), THE box (the field + 存入保险库 / 拒绝 + its state line: locked ⇒ vault_locked + 解锁…, not set up + a new entry ⇒ 设置第二密码…, a refusal's words), `submitSecretBox` (the value rides the model's ONE verb and leaves the field the moment it is stored or refused; kept on a refusal so the owner can unlock and press again), the same box as a dialog (`showSecretPasteDialog` — the For-you window's 「粘贴存入…」, the Vault band's door), ⑥ `showSecretAddDialog`. user-todos-row draws the request's words whole above the box and appends the box as DOM nodes; `patchRow` KEEPS the box while the request is open (a broadcast never takes the pasted value or the focus — the reply box's rule), drops it when the row resolves; resolvedBy `stored` = «saved to the vault». The panel's presses (clicks + Enter in replyKeys, the popup / phone home / mini inbox alike), `onVaultFacts` re-says every box live. inbox-reply ANSWER_ACTION_TYPES += secret-request (no typed reply — a reply goes INTO THE CHAT); user-todos ACTION_IDENTITY `secret-request: requestId`; inbox-window verbatim words + 粘贴存入… / 拒绝; vault-window 添加… gains 「其他密钥或密码…」 (order 50) and the band's 粘贴存入…; style.css (phone: a 16 px field, ≥ 36 px targets); 34 zh + ja keys.
- **Gates:** NEW test-vault-paste (fast, 77 — the agent door, people only, both writers, validate, refuse / dismiss / reopen, a lock withdraws, locked filing, ⑥ add / delete, a restart answers, bounds, THE SWEEP over every answer / frame / log / file / receipt with a positive control, the peer-text belt on the receipt, 4 MUTANTS red); NEW test-vault-paste-chrome (heavy, 43 — the CLI ask, the tray's masked box, a repaint keeps the pasted value + focus, paste ⇒ stored ⇒ the receipt at the next turn (prompt-context) ⇒ `uses`, the value in no DOM / WS frame / server log, Refuse, the PHONE over a restart that boots locked (vault_locked + 解锁… inline, a 16 px field), a mutant door as the RED control); test-vault-window-chrome ②d (⑥ add / reveal behind 验证是你 / a bearer refused / delete through the confirm) + the rail's 10 purposes; test-record-clear-walk §7 (the paste road: no probe / broadcast / file / journal / stdin holds the value; a clear takes the request's words); test-vault-law (the secret-kind census — a kind without a row is RED, its control a planted `note:`; the paste route swept × 6 bearers; the free entry a sentinel; the door set + use-law row); test-vault-engine Q (the free entry by kind) + the lock subscriber row; test-integration-registry (every field of every row judged as a target; validate decides); test-user-todos-layout (the box under a small DOM: locked / unlocked / not set up / refused / stored / deny, the row's words above it, producer row, 66 → 67 sites); censuses: approval (the new row + ACTION_IDENTITY), peer-text (the receipt's stash door), record-clear (3 routes, 3 receivers), inbox-reply (6 → 7), vault-inventory (10 purposes), architecture (PURE row, ci rows).
- **Not done / said:** a pasted free entry is granted to its asker for runs (8 h); any other conversation still needs the row's switch or its own request. The fleet's presets (cluster Secrets) are NOT reachable from a hub's vault — a hub entry never changes a pod; a paste into a registry field sets the hub's OWN value, which outranks a cluster default on that hub only.

### lane fleet-feedback-marks — the maintainers mark a fleet instance's agent feedback from the cluster side, and the filer is told (base c8aa8820 2.369.344; the owner's option B, 2026-10-21)
- **The gap.** A fleet instance keeps its own data/feedback.json; the triage job reads it per pod, but a record could be MARKED only through that pod's owner cookie or a key its owner granted — the maintainers had neither (one instance: 8 open records for 85 h, four of them shipped in 2.369.332).
- **THE MAINTAINER KEY** (PURE src/automation-keys.js `maintainerVerdict`; engine `useMaintainer`; the verb door src/routes/automation.js): an instance started with env `VIBESPACE_MAINTAINER_KEY_SHA` (the chart's `maintainerKeySha`) accepts the `vsmk_` key whose sha256 that is for EXACTLY `feedback.list` and `feedback.handled`, reach instance. The key is judged FIRST (`maintainer_key_unknown` 401 — an unknown bearer learns nothing of the table), then the closed list (`maintainer_key_scope` 403 — every other verb, and the conversation's GET doors). No record, no grant, no first-use card, no vault entry: the value never lives on the instance (test: no file under the data dir holds the value or the sha), and the vault's lock does not stop it (an instance whose owner never set a vault up is marked all the same). The compare is pairing-token's `tokenMatches` (constant time). ONE audit line a use, subject `maintainer`, key null — a mark's note «marked handled by the maintainer key · 2.369.NNN», never the note's text; an unknown key is not audited (the agent door's own rule).
- **The mark** is the same store call as the owner's PATCH and a granted conversation's (`store.setStatus`); `handledBy` = feedback-model `MAINTAINER_BY` («the maintainer key»), which the sheet words «the maintainers» / 「维护者」 / 「メンテナー」: «handled in 2.369.NNN by the maintainers, <when>» + the note, like a hub record.
- **THE CLI** (data/bin/vibespace-feedback): with env `VIBESPACE_MAINTAINER_KEY` and no session (the pod user's shell) `list --open` prints every open report with its id (feedback.list — other agents' words, belted by the instance) and `handled fb-… --version <v> [--note "…"]` marks one; the API is the instance's own port (`PORT`, else 3456) when no session named it. Without the key `handled` is refused by name (exit 2); in a session `list --open` = the agent's own open reports.
- **THE FILER IS TOLD** (主开发's plan B — the brief's «the line the hub gives» did not exist: the hub's only road was `vibespace-feedback list`): a mark that NAMES A RELEASE — the hub's feedback.handled, an instance's maintainer key, the forward's mark-back — queues ONE free next-turn notice for the conversation that filed the report: session-status kind `feedback-handled`, the sentence PURE feedback-model `handledSentence` («Your feedback report fb-… (about …) was handled in 2.369.NNN: <note>») — it never names who marked it, so the three roads say the byte-same words (test-feedback-forward ⑫; CONTROL: a sentence naming who ⇒ the roads disagree). The note is belted by the store before it is queued; the key is the running session's own (`filerKey`: by its conversation or webui id) else `<harness>:<conversation id>`; a forwarded or a job's report, the owner's click (no release) and a reopen tell nothing; the same report marked again replaces its notice. `vibespace-feedback list` stays the record.
- **The chart**: `maintainerKeySha` → env `VIBESPACE_MAINTAINER_KEY_SHA` (a plain value — a digest, not in the release Secret); anything but 64 lowercase hex REFUSES the render (the key itself pasted by mistake never reaches a pod). Default empty ⇒ no env, the Deployment byte-identical.
- **Censuses moved**: test-peer-text-census (the renderer row, the `feedback-handled` store row with its belt pins, NOTICE_ROWS 11 → 12, the CLI's declared row), test-automation-keys ⑮b's anchor (the verb's `by` line). vault.js SECRETS_AT_REST gains the maintainer key's row (`holds`: its sha256 only, in env).
- **Gates**: test-automation-keys ⑲ (PURE table + a generated property over the whole verb table, MUTANT without the closed list ⇒ the key reaches conversations.open; the engine over a real feedback store with the vault not set up; the doors; the real CLI), test-feedback-forward ⑫ (three roads, one sentence; 2 RED controls), test-feedback-ui ⑦ (HEAVY: the fake pod — a scratch instance started with the sha — the real CLI on its shell, the sheet in en + zh, the filer's real prompt-context carries the sentence once), test-helm-render M (+ CONTROL: no refusal ⇒ the key in the pod's env).

### lane grants-unify — every "who may use this" is ONE row shape, ONE reader, ONE writer (the owner, 2026-10-23: 「权限系统要 unify 一下，不想引入太多复杂度」; the only concepts are 给谁 `to` and 除了 `except`)
- **The model — PURE src/grant-model.js** (imports nothing): a row `{door, resource, to:[principal], except:[principal]}`; a principal is `{kind:'everyone'}` | `{kind:'group', id}` | `{kind:'conversation', key}` with ONE conversation-key spelling: the bare conversation id (`webui:<id>` before it has one) — exit / window `<backend>:<cid>` and automation `session:<cid>` map to it (`keyFromSessionKey` / `keyFromSubject`), a browser key that no binding names stands for itself. `admits(rows, facts)`: rows ADD; an exception subtracts only ITS row; everyone needs a caller with a key; the most specific entry is named; refusals by name in the order groups_unreadable › unknown_shape › excepted › fork_pending › not_granted. A malformed `to` entry is DROPPED (narrowing), a malformed `except` VOIDS the row (widening is never a guess). Write verdict: unknown_door / bad_resource / bad_row / too_many / bad_principal / bad_except / except_conflicts. Door entry fields (ENTRY_FIELDS): channel-reach authority + level, channel-api tier + perDay, window origin, group-visibility level. Legacy mappers for every census shape (pre-list singles, `allowExit:true`, instance+who, legacy, ephemeral) + `GM.LEGACY` (the pre-unify admissions, kept for the migration's check).
- **The store — ORCH src/server/grants-store.js**: data/grants.json (writeJsonAtomic, 0600), ONE writer `set(door, resource, {to, except}, by)` + `setMany` (all or nothing) + `remove` + `seed` (absent rows only); a line per landed write in data/grants-audit.jsonl (principal KEYS added / removed, no names; rotated at 4 MiB); the server-owned StateSync mirror `grants` (clientWrites:false; flushed with the other stores); `onChange` after a landed write; an unreadable file ⇒ every row refused `unknown_shape` and every write `store_unreadable` (never overwritten); a write that cannot land ⇒ `not_written`, memory unchanged. THE READ API (stable — the permissions window, lane 2, builds on it): `rowsFor(door, resource)`, `rowsOfDoor(door)`, `rowsForPrincipal(facts)` (every row that admits OR excepts — «what may conversation X reach»), `whoMayUse(door, resource)` («who may use Y»), `health()`. Doors: browser-profile, automation-key-use, automation-key-reach, channel-reach, channel-watch, channel-api, exit, window, group-visibility.
- **The doors** read rows and judge with `admits` (their own refusal words + `excepted`, naming where the owner lifts it); each writer calls the ONE writer. exit (exit-reach / exit-proxy / exit-routes / the dialog; config export/import carries the rows; `run`'s «ask each time» is the record's own `exit.ask`); window (window-reach / window-targets-engine; PUT …/reach/except); browser profile (`grantUse` = the keeper's in-memory mirror of the row; the PATCH / create / adopt / pick write the row; the caller's keys include its browser key); automation key use + reach (`use` / `reachRow` hydrated; 授权给… is now THE picker — it was a hand-made checkbox list — POST /api/automation/grants/:id/except); Task Group visibility (msg-acl + the Task Group dialog's «除了» row); channels — new ORCH src/server/channels-grants.js: `account:<id>` / `rule:<id>` / `conversation:<key>` (a grain's access, `authority`), `conversation:<key>#user` / `#request` (the owner's rows, approvals, `level`), `account:<id>#user` (pre-unify only), channel-watch per grain (who a notification may wake), channel-api per credential (`tier`); an exception rides only a Task Group / All agents entry. channel-acl `principalApplies` and channel-filter `rowNames` / `memberVia` / `memberStill` / the fan-out ask `admits`; the wake path (wakeEffOf, the group round-robin, the scope digest) asks `wakeAdmitOf` — the watch row's exception AND, when a reach row of that conversation leaves anybody out, the member's reach (a member left out of a group's ACCESS is never woken with words it may not read); with no exception anywhere the wake path is the base's (no extra work). The channel dialogs (Grant access…, Notify…, the API dialog) carry «除了» and stamp it (`grainStamp` adds a line per exception only when there are some — an old tab's stamp still matches).
- **The picker**: a folded «除了（可选）» row once a Task Group or All agents is ticked (THE same searchable list over that group's members; under All every conversation), chips «除了：…×», a member with its own row greyed «有自己的授权» (`except_conflicts` otherwise). Doors that draw it: exit access, window share, Agent browser «Who can use it» (+ New profile), Channels Grant access… / Notify… / API, the Vault window's 授权给…, the Task Group dialog's outside visibility. Not drawn: Reach & policy's «Grant reach to…» (a compact one-principal grant, not a who-list).
- **The migration 2026-10-grants-unify** (src/server/grants-migration.js, run by migrations.js): the seven sources become rows by the model's own mappers (the channel index by `rowsOfChannelIndex`); per resource the OLD reader (GM.LEGACY) must equal the NEW one (admits through the door's reader) for every principal the old rows name (each conversation in both spellings, a member of each named group, an outsider, every live session handed in); a resource that differs is NOT written (closed) and named, the run fails by name (retried next boot) — everything that agreed is written; a row the store already holds is kept and not judged again. Dry run over the owner's stores (read-only): 31 rows (exit 4, browser-profile 9, automation use 2 + reach 1, window 1, channel-reach 7, channel-watch 4, channel-api 3), 0 refused, 0 unknown, 294 ms (one-time). The 2026-09 channels pass judges its raw records itself (`legacyEffectiveFor`); a pre-split record's WATCHER settings are still read until it lifts them (never its access).
- **FOLLOW-UP (next release)**: the old fields stay on disk this release, UNREAD — hosts.json `exit.use` / `exit.run` (+ `run.ask`), browser-profiles.json `owner.who` lists, automation-keys.json grants' `subject` / `reach`, channels/index.json grain `access`, `reachEntries`, `accountGrants`, `apiGrants`, window-reach.json `rows`, task-groups.json `externalVisibility`. A migration in the next release strips them (archive first); §97 (b) names every place allowed to read them meanwhile.
- **test-architecture §97** (fast, grep-derived, each census with a planted control): (a) the 7 PURE readers import the model and call `admits`, and 16 reader / engine files hold no hand-written membership test; (b) 4 old fields read only where a row allows it (the migration, the legacy mappers, the 2026-09 passes, a served view); (c) 16 door write sites call the ONE writer and nothing else writes data/grants.json. Also: grant-model joins the PURE set; §66a allows the two legacy mappers; §86 rows for the store and the migration (own-tree).
- **Heavy-suite finds, fixed in-lane**: ① test-exit-access-ui — the served exit view spelled an unset hub `{mode:'default'}` and `accessOfView` read it back as unknown («网络 — 无法读取» on every row and toast); the view now omits an unset hub and the VIEW reader (`normHubView`) accepts `default` — a stored record keeps the old rule (test-exit-reach pins the round-trip on every shape). ② test-browser-who-ui — `decideAttach` judged by the browser key alone, so a list naming the conversation by its id refused its own holder; the keeper hands it the caller's conversation keys, and the agent routes' facts carry them too (`sessionFacts` / `jobFactsOf` → `conversationKeys`). ③ An agent's own `watch` where the owner left it out of a group's notification is refused `excepted` (never lifts the owner's exception).
- **The verify round's fixes (lane grants-verify on 42a53478 — no HIGH)**: ① test-exit-run's fake host manager kept the two lists on the record and built the manager without a store (58 reds) — its worlds now write the lists as rows through their own grants store (test-only). ② THE ROLLBACK ROAD: data/grants.json deleted with the ledger stamped answered `already` and closed every door in silence — `grantsStoreBoot` (migrations.js) re-runs the migration when an old list is still on disk (`rearmed`, the same rows byte-identical — on a copy of the owner's stores 33 → 33) and otherwise says `grants_store_missing` in the log, ⚙ Diagnostics and a notice, every boot; the first run leaves an empty store on disk (`ensureFile`) so a fresh instance is never mistaken for a deleted one. ③ §97 judges FUNCTION BODIES: (b) any `.exit` read outside its allow rows (an alias `const e = h.exit; … e.use` passed the old `.exit.use` regex; the files where `.exit` is no machine say so), (a) acorn over each reader function that asks GM.admits — groups / taskIds / groupIds only in its parameters and the facts it hands the model; the verify's two aliased plants are RED controls. ④ A stored hub the OLD reader refused (`{mode:'default'}` spelled out) made the whole access unknown: `GM.LEGACY.exit` now judges the RECORD, the mapper says unknown, the migration carries no grant and names it (`unread`); the stored reader keeps the old rule, only the served view's reader accepts `default`. ⑤ The key doors' own legs (test-automation-keys ⑳): an exception, an unknown kind, a malformed exception on use AND reach, RED under the verify's widening mutants A / B / D of the model. ⑥ ONE spelling of a pre-list browser key — `GM.browserKeyResolver` (a helper's key is its parent's, then its bound conversation, else itself): the migration, `rowForCreate` (a key no conversation answered for read as EVERYONE before) and the suites' fixture mapper all call it.
- **Suites**: test-grant-model (new, fast, 80 — every legacy mapper DIFFERENTIAL, two patched-copy controls), test-grants-store (new, fast, 41 — every door honours an exception incl. the REAL channel engine's round-robin / All agents fan-out / access-left-out; RED control: THE admits swapped for a copy ignoring `except` ⇒ all ten doors let the member in), test-migrations (+15: every source carried, the RED equivalence fixture, a kept row, an unreadable store, a no-judge control). Every door's existing suite adjusted to read rows (fixtures seed the store the way the migration would: scripts/grant-fixtures.mjs).

### lane path-field — ONE path field at every door: the candidates come from the person's own groups, folders and history, computed for the machine in question; a typed value takes effect on blur or says why not (L1 of the New Session train; base c8aa8820 2.369.344)
- **Why:** the owner accepted POC v2.2 (area-first-new-conversation, 2026-10-23 05:3x 「没啥问题」); its `rankCandidates` and the field's behaviour in poc/designs/area-first-poc/Main.html are the spec, now product code. Before: `setupDirAutocomplete` at seven doors — a parent listing + prefix filter, a task's folders floated on top, Enter-only, no relative paths, no remote recommendations beyond a host's recent cwds, the day-one chips PRESELECTED ~/vibespace on a fresh pod (study round 4: the product's own checkout holds the most files).
- **THE RULE (NEW PURE src/path-candidates.js, imports nothing):** `resolveRelative(input, bases, listing, {files})` (the bases in order — the selected groups' folders in selection order → the field's own context → home; every base that has it is a resolution, the first used; a link to a folder resolves to its target; an exact hit beats a completion), `rankCandidates(query, {bases, groups, recent, listing, name, machine, files, self})` (the POC's function byte-for-byte in its scoring: ① the groups' folders, one absent on the machine greyed with the create road · ② 由名字 one `<group folder>/<name>` per SELECTED group in selection order + `~/<name>`, a bare word plays the name when it is empty, −3000 so it never beats a real hit · ③ recent with counts · ④ the listing under the typed prefix / the whole-path fuzzy: segment prefix > subsequence > token, CJK plain · ⑤ mounts), `missingVerdict` (parent there ⇒ create; missing ⇒ said), `groupOn` (a group as seen from one machine: probed / declared `host::/abs` / absent), `isExcludedPath` (the ADDENDUM: the instance checkout, its data dir, dot-folders — never offered unasked, typed explicitly they resolve; a group folder or a recent one the person made stays theirs), `sliceListing` / `mergeListing` / `sliceAsk` (the hub's raw facts ⇄ the field's per-machine memory), `fuzzyFilter`, `recentCounts`, `legacySuggestions`. Words never live there: chips / whys / lines are `{ key, params }`, the field says them through t().
- **THE SERVER:** `GET /api/dir-complete` takes `bases` / `q` / `probe` / `kind` and answers the listing slice + `self` + `took` (+ `partial`) BESIDE the old `suggestions` (a caller sending none of the new params gets the old shape). NEW src/server/dir-slice.js: two NEW SafeFs ops (`dirSlice` — each asked folder listed once with its facts, `known` mtime ⇒ `same`; `dirIndex` — the folder index, 4 levels, ≤ 6000, dot / dependency folders, the checkout + data dir and every mount skipped, a budget inside the worker), a listing cache per folder with mtime invalidation (reused < 2 s, else re-stated), the index kept 30 s and refreshed BEHIND an answer, the whole answer raced against the 450 ms budget (a SafeFs deadline is never shortened — a timeout terminates the worker). `GET /api/home-folders` drops the excluded folders (day one starts in work/, not ~/vibespace).
- **THE HOST RUNG (the owner's note ④ «为啥在 mac 选项下就没有默认路径推荐了？»):** `hosts.dirSlice` runs ONE sh script there (NEW PURE src/dir-slice-script.js: list / probe / index / mounts / the Mac's display names via mdls) over the device link's runCmd first, the ssh rung otherwise, and the SAME sliceListing builds the answer; the index kept 60 s per machine (refreshed behind), the display names 10 min. `/api/hosts/:id/dir-complete` takes the same params; `/api/hosts/:id/recent-cwds` answers `recent: [{path, count, last}]` beside `cwds`. The brief said the rung «already knows» the Mac's display names — it did not (no code read them); the script asks mdls kMDItemDisplayName.
- **THE COMPONENT (NEW src/lib/path-field.js; its contract is frozen for the train's other lanes, new-session-form and task-group-context):** `pathField(input, {bases, groupsOf, host, kind, onCommit, name, onState, create, createWhen, picker, chips, id})` → `{el, input, value, verdict, commit, set, refresh, open, close, ensure, destroy}`; `appGroups(selectedIds)` (every door's default groupsOf: the person's groups) and `pathSuggest(text)` (the palette). The list floats in a body-level layer (inline on the phone), never pops by itself (a press, typing, ↓ or a Tab INTO the field), closes through utils.js onOutsidePress (§59); BLUR COMMITS deferred past pointer-up; 「未生效：…」 with 「用第一名」; the «不存在 — 创建？» tick (a 新建 row picked IS the consent), `ensure()` makes it; THE PICKER (createModalShell over the dialog: pinned groups with badges, the tree without the excluded folders, a preview with files / sizes / dates, «新建文件夹» inline, «选这个文件夹», the last node per `id` in localStorage, opening on a search).
- **THE DOORS:** New Session (app.js — the Create button awaits `commit()` + `ensure()`, the dialog's Enter skips while the field prevented it; the day-one chips row `_fillCwdRecent` kept as it was, its chips fill through the field — L2 owns the form), the storage / machine-mount dialogs (mounts-dialog.js — what takes effect is written back absolute, a mount point may be made once ticked, Submit commits each path field first; sftp's key path declares `pathKind: 'file'`), the app launcher's working directory, the Task Group panel's three (Link folder — Enter OR leaving links it; Context folder; Export / Import file — L3 re-wires these to the Context table on this field), the Files path bar (no folder button: the window IS the browser; the line under it only shows what did not take), the tour's first chat, the session palette's /path (pathSuggest). src/lib/autocomplete.js DELETED; its CSS replaced by the path field's.
- **CENSUS:** test-architecture §98 (NEW) — setupDirAutocomplete gone, every door row names its live call, every path-shaped input (markup id / class / placeholder, a `.placeholder = t('…folder…')`, a file-path-input) covered or exempt with a reason; planted controls. PURE set + 2; §86 reader counts moved (safe-fs-worker 24 → 39: the two new ops; files.js 42 → 43: the slice's SafeFs door); §59 the list's closer is onOutsidePress; §78 the package name is a constant (`SELF_PACKAGE`).
- **TESTS:** NEW test-path-candidates (fast, PURE, 57: the POC rank-test ported with its fixture and its 13 cases — scores identical to the POC's log — + the exclusion with a RED CONTROL), NEW test-dir-complete (fast, 39, ~2.3 s: the real files router over a temp HOME, the budget, the mtime cache, the host rung with a FAKE Mac — the real HostManager, its ssh rung run here), NEW test-path-field-chrome (heavy, 42: the component in real Chrome in zh against the real routes). test-mounts-dialog-extract draws both variants' path inputs as one canonical box before its pixel compare (the field is the ONE deliberate change; both count the same rows); test-slack-landing-nologin stubs path-field.js where it stubbed autocomplete.js.

### lane new-session-form — the New Session form in two columns (L2 of the New Session train; the owner accepted POC v2.2)
- **The shape (the POC's Main / Phone boards, report-v2.2 §«Product changes» items 1–4, 6–7):** LEFT «where and how it runs» = the harness's own flags (machine and folder — the name ABOVE the folder; backend as a segmented switch, model + effort, permission, 可用工具), RIGHT «what it may use» = VibeSpace's own stores (built-in locked on; Sessions + the Task Group chips; Channels; Browser; vault / automation keys / outside · notifications as read-only facts with doors; Accounts · as you; MCP). Two columns from 1100 px; the phone stacks LEFT then RIGHT and the kind switch is a full-width row. Every control keeps its id; `#input-backend` / `#input-mode` stay the values the switches set (hidden), so every suite that drives a select through `change` keeps driving `applyBackend`. New: src/lib/new-session-form.js (CLIENT mixin), src/lib/new-session-model.js (PURE), src/new-session-spec.js (PURE, both tiers).
- **The fold (the fleet census):** machine · account · additional arguments · git worktree fold under «More options»; each unfolds by itself from the person's own data — a paired machine used in the last 30 days, ≥ 2 accounts for the harness, a git folder (probed `/api/file/info?path=<cwd>/.git`, host-aware) — and says why («Opened by itself: …»). The open state is per device (`vs.newSession.moreOpen`, a record-clear STORAGE pref row). The footer carries the run's values as chips (a folded row's chip dashed; a chip opens its row); when Create cannot run it says why in words instead («Cannot create yet: Choose a folder first» — the path field's verdict; an EMPTY folder is refused now, where it used to start in the home folder — the brief's refusal, L1's `empty` verdict).
- **The Mode row is the header's Agent | Terminal switch** (a plain shell: Terminal only). No «Browser» kind: there is no New-Session road to a browser-only session today, so the switch does not offer one. The census's «terminal used in the last 30 days» unfold rule therefore unfolds nothing — the switch is always shown.
- **taskIds (item 1):** `spawnGroupIds(data)` (selection order, the old id shape, de-duplicated, ≤ 16; an older page's `taskId` = a list of one) → ws-create `_initialGroupIds` beside `_initialGroupId` (= the first; its pinned line in test-fork-groups re-pinned) → meta `taskId` + `taskIds` → boot-restore's two spawn-group paths → `groupsForSession({initialGroupIds})` at EVERY call site (agent-routes 6, mounts-plugins-wiring 4, server.js 5, browser-key 1 — a census in test-new-session-form with a planted control) and the browser ladder's Task-Group rung in selection order (mounts-plugins-wiring taskGroupDefault / taskGroupCap). The page binds the session to every picked group once its id exists (`bindIds`). The brief's test-task-groups does not exist on c8aa8820 (lane open-task-binds is creating it): the list legs live in the new fast test-new-session-form (the REAL TaskGroupManager) + test-fork-groups.
- **可用工具 (item 2):** a NEW caps row `toolAllowlist` (backend-caps; claude `{kind:'tools', allow:'--allowedTools', deny:'--disallowedTools', tools:[9], keep:['Bash']}`, codex `{kind:'sandbox', sandbox, approval, flags}`, null for shell / opencode / antigravity), mirrored in agent-meta (test-harness-contract re-derives it per descriptor: shape, the descriptor's caps, the client mirror, and that the adapter CONSUMES a pick exactly when the row exists — driven through buildSessionArgs). PURE `toolAllowlistArgs` judges every pick against the closed vocabularies; the claude adapter pushes the flags right after `--permission-mode` (a dash always ends the variadic lists); **a ✗ on Bash never reaches argv** — deny beats allow in Claude Code, so it would also block the `Bash(vibespace-…:*)` allow rules every reporting CLI rides: the chip cannot take ✗ (its lock + title say why) and the rule drops a forged one. Codex: the pick replaces the mode's sandbox / approval half (terminal argv; chat `CODEX_WEBUI_TOOLS_PICK`, read by the wrapper's `withToolsPick`); a machine without codex-linux-sandbox keeps its forced danger-full-access. The judged pick is `_toolPick` (session-schema row, config key `tools`) → meta `toolPick` → the `created` reply → the page latches it into the conversation's config (sidebar-state keeps it by shape) → resumeSession and inbox-reopen (REOPEN_CFG_KEYS) re-pass it.
- **The admitted-profile filter (item 3):** the Browser row lists ONLY the profiles the picked groups admit — the keeper's `admitsAtCreate` / `mayAttachAtCreate` (= `B.mayAttach` with no key) behind `GET /api/browser/admits` (boot-sentinel smoke row); until it answers, the profiles every conversation may use. ws-create judges the form's explicit pick (it sends `taskIds`) by the same verdict before the pin is written: a pick its groups do not admit starts without it — the «picking adds this conversation to Who can use it» road (owner ruling A) is the Agent browser panel's alone now (the open question the POC flagged, answered by the brief).

### lane ci-cjk-fonts — the heavy shards' CJK fonts came from apt in 3 s or in 21 min; every setup step of the Actions mirror now has a bound (base be837364 2.369.345)
- **Measured (2026-10-23, branch run 39959721371 and the .345 master mirror 39965870622, every job's step times + the logs).** «Install CJK fonts» (`apt install fonts-noto-cjk`, 61.2 MB) took 3–6 s on a shard the azure mirror served and 673 / 693 / 939 / 1253 s on the four it did not on the branch run (≈ 59 runner-minutes); on the mirror heavy 6/6 spent 1281 s and heavy 4/6 21 min in ONE fetch (two `Ign` stalls, then 58.6 MB at 45.8 kB/s), leaving 22 of its 45 min for 25 min of suites — cancelled with test-chat-paging running. The same mirror once took 55 s for dtach's 17 kB; nothing in the job bounded either wait.
- **The bytes and the HOMEs (measured here).** The runner's noble .deb (1:20230817+repack1-3, fetched and unpacked) carries notofonts/noto-cjk's four TTCs at tag Serif2.002 byte for byte — every sha256 and git blob equal; the Sans pair is the Sans2.004 build, the same bytes as this box's 1:20240730 package, whose Serif pair (2.003) differs. The Serif pair stays: a mail frame sets no font, so zh / ja mail is drawn in the default serif. A `~/.local/share/fonts` dir is its own HOME's only (another HOME saw 0 of its faces), and the chrome suites' servers run under scratch HOMEs — apt's fonts were every HOME's.
- **The fix.** scripts/ci-fonts.sh is the ONE fonts road: the four TTCs at the pinned tag, a sha256 each checked before install (a mismatch is a red naming the file), curl bounded (5 retries, 15 s to connect, 120 s a try), into ~/.local/share/fonts/noto-cjk behind an actions/cache keyed on the script (a stalled restore is a miss after 2 min); `--system` adds a /etc/fonts/conf.d `<dir>` + the system cache, so every HOME sees the same 30 faces (fontconfig de-duplicates the dir under the owner's HOME); NO apt fallback. Every ci.yml setup step carries timeout-minutes (a few times its measured worst; the suite steps keep their job's), and ci-apt.sh gives up a stalled connection at 30 s and an apt call at 80 s by name. test-ci-gate §2h holds all of it (20 mutant copies of ci.yml / ci-fonts.sh, each red for its own reason, + the road over a file:// fixture serving the wrong bytes); §2f runs the apt bound over a stub that never answers. Here: a cache miss 2.8 s, a hit 2.1 s; test-channel-threads-ui (107) and test-channels-e2e (213) run ALL PASS under apt's fonts (the noble .deb, unpacked) and under the road's (each a runner-shaped FONTCONFIG_FILE, DBus unset) with every px reading equal (28/28 and 63/63 lines, 26 of them zh / ja text); the only other differences are a clock in a fixture sentence and a hover-wash pixel count that is 68897 or 68896 on apt's fonts alone.

### lane hub-dies-dead-ssh-host — a paired ssh machine that cannot be reached never stops the hub (the .346 verify round's CONFIRMED HIGH; base 3180045d 2.369.346)
- **Why:** lane new-session-verify (report claim 3): a hosts.json record for an unreachable ssh machine, picked in the New Session host row ⇒ the hub's last journal line `Error: write EPIPE at WriteWrap.onWriteComplete`, every later request refused — 2 of 4 runs on the int tree. Mechanism: src/hosts.js fed ssh children on stdin with NO `'error'` listener (`child.stdin.end(tar)` ×2, `.end(script)`, `.end(JSON op)`, `.write(bootstrapScript())`); ssh to a machine it cannot reach exits at once (BatchMode), the bytes meet a closed pipe, the stream error is uncaught and server.js's uncaughtException handler exits the hub. Same shape in src/remote-fs.js `write` and src/machine-mounts.js `_run`.
- **Measured before (base 3180045d, this lane's probes/walk w3x-roads.mjs: a scratch hub, the dead record, a stub `ssh` exiting 255 first on PATH — never a real machine):** «install tools» on the dead machine ⇒ the hub DIES 2/2 (`write EPIPE`, every later request «fetch failed»). The verify round's exact New Session walk (w3c-sshdead.mjs, fake-Mac rung + real harvest) survived 4/4 on this box today — it reaches no stdin road at this box's timing (only `_run`'s `printf $HOME` and the git probe, no stdin); the crash is timing-bound there (a pipe smaller than the payload), deterministic on any payload bigger than a pipe holds (the tools tar is MBs). In-process, the base's HostManager over the five roads: 2 uncaught EPIPEs, 9 ssh spawns, errors without a name.
- **THE ONE FEED (src/hosts.js `feedStdin(child, bytes)`):** attaches the stdin `'error'` listener BEFORE the first write, keeps the error as `fed.error` (never a throw); `sshRefusal(h, err, stderr, fed)` names the failure — `host-unreachable` (ssh's own exit 255 / no answer in the bound) or `ssh-exited-early` (EPIPE / ECONNRESET / ERR_STREAM_DESTROYED with another exit) — with the machine's id + name + ssh's last stderr line; a remote command's own failure keeps the caller's words. All five hosts.js feeds + remote-fs `write` + machine-mounts `_run` go through it (machine-mounts' result carries `refusal`); `bootstrap` also listens on the child's `'error'` (no ssh binary) and its `done` event carries `refusal`. Exported: `feedStdin`, `sshRefusal`, `unreachableError`, `refusalBody`.
- **THE HOST RUNG REFUSES BY NAME BEFORE ANY SPAWN:** `hosts.reachable(id)` — a live device link ⇒ yes, a fresh `_hostDownUntil` memo ⇒ no (no spawn either way), else ONE `ssh -o ConnectTimeout=3 … true` over `_ssh` (BatchMode, the shared ControlMaster — a yes warms it; a test's patched `_ssh` answers it too), single-flight per machine, verdict kept 60 s; `refuseUnreachable(id)` throws `unreachableError` (code `host-unreachable`). Called first by `dirComplete` / `dirSlice` (ssh machines; a dial device answers through its link as before), `GET /api/hosts/:id/recent-cwds`, RemoteFs `home` (`/api/home?host=` ⇒ 400 `code: host-unreachable`, FS_REFUSALS). ### lane door-day-one-landing — day one asks one thing and lands in a chat on the person's files (base d3ab5db5 2.369.342)
- **Why:** two naive-user studies on real fleet pods (2.369.342, seven testers: study 1 D5–D8, D10, D11; study 2 C4–C9, C14, M3; lane 3's folder table). The welcome pitched «Your workspace for coding agents», «Sessions that never die», «raw terminal TUI» and showed 6 themes × 4 languages on screen one. Two non-technical testers asked "is this even for me?". Tour step 3 said «SSO is already configured, so no password is needed» right after a password sign-in. «Set a second password … there is no recovery» came at Start Chat Session and again at every sign-in, because «Later» was a sessionStorage snooze. The first-session box showed a grey `/home/<user>`, and every LATER New Session dialog kept the PREVIOUS area's folder in the field: testers typed the path 5/5 and 3/3 times, and lane 3's T3 had the typed folder appended to the pre-filled one. The sign-in terminal and the claude it ran showed as two ACTIVE sessions nobody made, and the first chat was «Session 3». The rail was unlabelled, so the way to Agents and Remote was found by hovering every icon. Git had no identity on a fresh pod.
- **MEASURED (code, base):**
  - the welcome's step 0 = `src/lib/setup-flows.js:228`; the SSO branch = `:324`; the guided login's ws create sends `name` and `ephemeral`, and **the server reads neither** (`src/ws-create.js` reads `sessionName`), so it became an ordinary live «Session N».
  - Manage Agents' Log in types bare `claude` into a login shell in `$HOME`. The claude REPL writes `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`, discovery lists it with no name, and the ladder falls to the cwd folder, so it reads as the account name (the home folder's name).
  - the window title's ladder put `webuiName` («Session {server seq}», a counter that includes the sign-in shells) before discovery's first-message `name`. The sidebar card already had the first message.
  - the dialog's cwd field was never cleared, so `if (cwd) …value = cwd` left the previous open's value in place.
- **THE FIX — PURE `src/day-one.js` (imports nothing; test-architecture PURE set):**
  - `tourSteps`: `protect` only where nothing protects the workspace. SSO or a sign-in password already set means the step and its SSO sentence leave.
  - `folderChips`: a Task Group's folders, then the home's folders WITH files (most first, ≤ 4), then «the last one you used», then the home's other folders, then the other recents (≤ 8). `firstFilesFolder` picks the folder the tour's chat starts in.
  - `vaultSetupAsk`: asks only `not_set_up && facts.secretWaiting && !snoozed`. `vaultLaterUntil` = 3 days.
  - `railLabels` / `railUsed`: the first week, or until every door was used once.
  - `gitIdentityPlan`: never over git's own identity, never mixing two people.
  - `SIGN_IN` / `isSignInRow`.
- **The wiring:**
  - **The tour (setup-flows.js):** step 0 is one sentence + three asks; the theme and language chips are gone (⚙ keeps both). The empty desktop's welcome (public/index.html) says the same sentence instead of «Multi-session terminal manager with tiling window support». Step 2 is skipped when the plan has no protect, and its SSO branch is deleted. Step 3 = the home's folders as chips with the files folder CHOSEN and the field filled, ONE primary «Start the chat», and the terminal as a link. The guided login sends `purpose: 'sign-in'`.
  - **The New Session dialog (app.js):** the field is `cwd || ''` on every open, with words for a placeholder. `_fillCwdRecent` paints `folderChips` through the new `src/lib/folder-chips.js` (loadHomeFolders / recentLocalCwds / chipWords / paintFolderChips; words chips read LTR).
  - **`GET /api/home-folders`** (src/routes/files.js, local only, cached 10 s): runs the new SafeFs op `folderCensus` (src/safe-fs-worker.js; deadline 15 s). It lists the home's non-hidden folders, each with a BOUNDED recursive count of files (cap 2000 entries, depth 4; `.`-names, node_modules, `__pycache__` and `snap` skipped). A mount point (in /proc/self/mountinfo, or on another st_dev) is named and never walked.
  - **The vault (src/server/vault-engine.js):** facts gain `secretWaiting` (not set up only). It is TRUE when:
    - a store's key file is minted in the legacy branch (a store's FIRST secret; stores mint only on encrypt);
    - a key file or a `data/agentd/host-*.token` exists beside the data (read lazily by `facts()`, at most every 5 s);
    - or secretPut / agentMint / agentPut refused for want of a vault.

    The moment it turns true is announced. NO new engine key: test-vault-law (a) classifies every exported key, and the file is untouched (64).
  - **The vault ask (vault-unlock.js):** `maybeNagVault` asks `vaultSetupAsk`. `onVaultState` asks at the BROADCAST whose `secretWaiting` turns true. «Later» = localStorage `vs-vault-later` = now + 3 days (it was a per-tab sessionStorage flag), and the setup dialog says why now.
  - **The sign-in terminal:**
    - ws-create keeps `_purpose: 'sign-in'` (persisted in meta, restored by boot-restore), and the live list carries `purpose`.
    - the sidebar skips such a live row.
    - routes/sessions.js drops a discovered row whose pid is under a sign-in terminal (its shell, two levels of children).
    - `openSignInTerminal` is used by the guided login, Manage Agents' Log in and the 8 add-account login terminals.
  - **The title (app.js syncSessionIdentity):** `given || match.name || match.webuiName`, so the first message names the window and the taskbar.
  - **Git (`src/server/git-identity.js`, ORCH):** at a local spawn, at most once a minute until settled. It reads `~/.claude.json` `oauthAccount` (emailAddress, displayName) and asks `git config --get user.name/user.email` from `/`. Where unset, it writes `git config --global user.*` (execFile, serviceEnv, 3 s bound). The log names fields, never values.
  - **The rail (sidebar-rail.js):** every door gets a `.rail-label`. The rail is `rail-labelled` (68 px, the collapsed strip too) while `railLabels` says so. A press records the door. The record is localStorage `vs-rail-labels`. `scripts/scratch.mjs` PRESET_KEYS sets it `done`, so every chrome suite keeps its 44 px pins.
- **Owner's ruling kept:** the Claude sign-in stays per person and is never skipped. The connect step (step 1) is untouched; lane door-signin-card reshapes it.
- **Gates:**
  - test-day-one is NEW (fast, 90, 120 ms). It covers every PURE row, with two RED CONTROLS (the base's recents-only chip rule; the base's not-set-up vault rule); the real vault engine (mint → true + broadcast, boot over a key file / a device token, a refused store, set up → false, no new key); folderCensus over a temp home (/proc as another device); git identity with real git over a temp HOME; wiring pins; and i18n.
  - test-day-one-chrome is NEW (heavy, 43, ~38 s, `--password-store=basic`). It runs a pod-shaped hub with a sign-in password and HOME/work holding 23 files. RED CONTROL: a bundle rebuilt from THIS source with the base's vault rule and prefill brings back the day-one ask and the carried folder.
  - test-new-session-dialog 103: A1 now asserts the field reopens EMPTY, and A1b covers the chips.
  - test-record-clear-census 242: the vault-later row moved to localStorage, plus a vs-rail-labels row.
  - mount-reader-census §86: counts moved, plus a git-identity row.
  - test-architecture: PURE set and §78; 13 orphaned i18n keys deleted (the old pitch, the old start step, the SSO sentence, the empty desktop's terminal-manager line).
  - test-vault-law 64 untouched; vault-engine 175; vault-secrets 159.

### lane door-signin-card — the humane Claude sign-in: a card, not a terminal TUI (base d3ab5db5 = 2.369.342)
- **Why:** two naive-user fleet studies (naive-cluster-1 D1–D4/D9, naive-cluster-2 B1/C2/C3/M1) — 7 testers on fresh 2.369.342 pods — ALL stopped at the Claude sign-in within the first minute. It is Claude Code's terminal TUI behind an unlabelled rail icon: a colour-theme picker with a code sample, "Select login method 1/2/3" (subscription / Console API / Bedrock-Vertex), a sign-in link cut at the window edge, "Paste code here if prompted >", then "Security notes" and "Do you trust this folder?" defaulting to "No, exit". The chat's own remedy was a DEAD END — a first task answered "Not logged in · Please run /login", and typing /login answered "/login isn't available in this environment" (Claude Code's print-mode text passed straight through). A silent user with no colleague to drive it never gets past it (the silent cohort: 9 of 17 fleet users signed in once by a colleague, or never started). The owner's ruling: the sign-in STAYS per person, made humane.
- **The fix (ONE commit, NO version bump; targets .344 because .343 is being integrated now):** the product drives `claude auth login --claudeai` ITSELF, in a hub-owned PTY, over the account's own pre-seeded config dir — so the person meets ONE card wherever the wall is (the chat's «Not logged in» card, the tour's connect step, Manage agents), never a terminal, a theme picker or a trust prompt.
  - **PURE src/signin-model.js** — `signinStep` reads the login screen off the PTY (steps: url / code-prompt / connected / error), reusing the OAT mint's proven reader (src/oat-mint-model.js: `cleanPty` strips OSC/CSI, `findUrl` rejoins a URL wrapped across a narrow PTY — we spawn 400 cols so it never wraps — `codeVerdict`) so a harness's login screen is read in ONE place. `signinCardView` maps the flow to the card's five states (no-login / url-shown / waiting-code / connected / failed+why). `publicSignin` is a whitelist — the OAuth login prints no token, and the credential bytes are the helper's, read in-process at finalize. Added to the test-architecture PURE set (with oat-mint-model, which it reuses, PURE → PURE).
  - **ORCH src/server/claude-signin.js** — runs VibeSpace's existing subscription-login helper (data/bin/vibespace-claude-subscription-login.mjs → `claude auth login --claudeai`) in a node-pty IT owns, in a 0700 scratch HOME with a no-op $BROWSER opener (a headless pod launches no browser; the person opens the URL in their own tab), CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = the account's OWN seeded dir (where the helper lands the credential). The env is the oat mint's allowlist (`mintEnvOf` over `agentEnv` — no hub secret rides along; §94 clean). It feeds the pasted code to the PTY and NOWHERE else. It does NOT re-implement finalize: on `connected` (the helper's "subscription credentials saved." line, or exit 0 + its success status file) the CLIENT calls the EXISTING /api/accounts/subscription/:id/finalize route — so the duplicate-identity merge, the login-expiry sweep and the pool wake are unchanged (signing in again folds into the existing account by e-mail). Routes POST/GET/DELETE /api/accounts/:id/signin (+ /signin/code) are human-only (an agent session/job bearer is refused by name); live phases ride a WS `claude-signin` broadcast. Wired in src/server/account-usage-routes.js beside the oat mint (no server.js change — the deps were already handed in). A hub killed mid-run leaves a scratch dir swept by age at boot.
  - **CLIENT src/lib/signin-card.js** — the shared card (escHtml / theme vars / SVG icons / i18n zh+ja / NO native dialog): «Sign in with Claude — your company uses a Claude subscription» + an «Open the sign-in page» link (a real anchor, target=_blank rel=noopener) + a paste-the-code box; `signinShowVerdict` drops a stale/older-run snapshot (the oat-mint HTTP-vs-WS flake class). Mounted at all three walls. The account dir is pre-seeded (`hasCompletedOnboarding`/`hasTrustDialogAccepted`, src/harnesses/claude.js seedDir shape), and `--claudeai` preselects the subscription, so no method menu / theme / trust prompt ever appears.
  - **The chat (src/lib/chat-view.js):** the `not_logged_in` exit branch mounts the sign-in card instead of the «run /login» bar; the waiting user message (the last user turn) is remembered so «Send my message again» re-sends it in ONE press — `resumeSession` now forwards `createSession`'s `initialMessage` (src/lib/session-lifecycle.js). The old dead-end system line and login bar are gone.
  - **The tour (src/lib/setup-flows.js):** the «Connect your agents» step shows the card inline and CANNOT be skipped silently — Continue, when nothing is signed in (`_obReady` from /api/backend-status, `_obSignedIn` from the card), warns once («You are not signed in yet — you won't be able to start a chat. Continue anyway?») and relabels to «Continue anyway» before it advances; the terminal/Codex login road folds under «Advanced».
  - **The terminal (src/lib/terminal.js):** the WebLinksAddon gets a handler — an http(s) link opens in a NEW TAB via `window.open(uri,'_blank','noopener,noreferrer')`, never xterm's default native «WARNING: This link could potentially be dangerous» confirm that scared 3 of 7 testers off the sign-in link (D3 / C2); non-http(s) is ignored.
- **Scoped out (said here):** remote-host subscription sign-in keeps the terminal road (the card drives the LOCAL hub's account dir); Codex sign-in is unchanged (the card is Claude-subscription-specific — the brief's humane card). The REAL 2.1.30x `claude auth login --claudeai` screen is OWNER-RUN: the shapes are modeled on the measured 2.1.296 capture (oat-mint-model header) + the helper's success line, and every test uses a FAKE claude.
- **Tests:** test-signin-model (fast, PURE: the recorded 2.1.30x login-screen fixture fed in chunks split mid-URL — url/code-prompt/connected — the no-half-URL rule, an error screen, the five card states, codeVerdict, the publicSignin whitelist, signinShowVerdict), test-claude-signin (fast, a FAKE claude in a stub PTY: url→code-prompt→connected, the pasted code reaches ONLY the PTY spied over every broadcast, the allowlist child env, scratch wiped on connected, the error + exit-code backstop, one-per-account, cancel, routes refuse an agent bearer), test-signin-card-ui (fast, the REAL card esbuild-bundled over a lean DOM: the five states, begin → create+signin, the code POST rides only /signin/code, connected → finalize, «Send my message again» → onResend, an older-rev snapshot ignored), test-setup-flows (fast, the tour step's non-silent Continue + the card mount + the Advanced fold), the terminal link-handler leg in test-terminal-zoom-select (heavy chrome: terminal.js's REAL handler with the REAL @xterm/addon-web-links — http opens via window.open with no confirm, non-http ignored), test-architecture (PURE set += signin-model + oat-mint-model; §86 reader-census +1 own-tree row). test-harness-contract untouched.
- **Gates:** build GREEN (test-architecture 797, i18n balanced 9146/9146, agentd unsigned). Fast GREEN on a scratch .343 bump (the `## 2.369.344` user heading is one ahead of the .343 cut 主开发 is integrating — test-changelog-style's ④ wants package.json's version or the next patch; no bump is committed). The full `--affected` heavy tier is for 主开发 on a quiet box.
- **Owner-run (never run here):** confirm the real `claude auth login --claudeai` 2.1.30x screen matches signin-model's reader (the printed URL + "Paste code here" + the helper's success line), and that the seed suppresses the method menu / theme / trust on a fresh pod.

### verify round — lane door-signin-fixes: the five findings of door-signin-verify on the humane Claude sign-in (base 959d583e = door-signin-card on 2.369.342)
- **Why:** the verify lane (door-signin-verify) cleared claims 1/3/6/7 with controls and found no HIGH, but five things on the card: (claim 5, MED-LOW) what «Send my message again» re-sends, (claim 8, PLAUSIBLE) the Claude card on a Codex / remote-host death, (claim 4, LOW) closing the card never cancels the run, (claim 2, LOW) the pasted code rides a failed run's error, and the debris of a never-logged-in «Subscription» row per failed attempt. ONE commit on 959d583e, no bump; int344 takes the pair. Each verify repro (scratch t2/t3/t4/t5) is PROMOTED into the lane's own suites as a leg that is RED on 959d583e.
- **1 · claim 5 — the re-send.** RED on base: chat-view's `_lastUserText` (read off the source, run over `_messages`) answered 'deploy to prod' for `[user, assistant 'Deployed.']` (an answered history), skipped an image-only waiting turn for an OLDER turn's text, re-armed the card's button on a later push. FIX: PURE `waitingTurnOf(messages)` (src/signin-model.js), taken AT THE WALL (`_showSignInCard` → `_waitingTurnText()`): walking back, an answer (assistant / tool, not the CLI's own login refusal — `<synthetic>` with no spent usage, or the classifier's "Not logged in" line) ⇒ nothing waiting; a record the person did not type (originKind / synthetic / imageAttachment / typed:false) is passed over; the first typed turn is it, its words (an image-attached turn's included; images alone ⇒ ''). Nothing waiting ⇒ «Connected», no button. The chat consumes `_waitingText` on its press and the card's `_resent` keeps a later re-render from re-arming it. NOTE: the verify's t5 ③ modelled "a turn with an image" with the `imageAttachment` flag — that flag marks the CLI's page images (message-manager.js), and a composer image turn (image block + text block) kept its text on base; the real base red for images is the image-ONLY waiting turn (an older text re-sent), which the leg pins.
- **2 · claim 8 — the wall.** RED on base: the exited branch (read off chat-view.js, run over a stub view) mounted the card for a Codex and a remote-host death. FIX: PURE `signinWallOf({oauthSubscription, host})` — the card only for a LOCAL conversation of the harness whose subscriptions it signs in, read off the declared caps row `capsOf(backend).oauthUsage` (a first cut on `backend === 'claude'` went RED on test-architecture §78 — no file branches on a member id; the subscription account the card creates and finalizes IS an `oauthUsageAccount`); any other death keeps the base's `_showLoginBar` and words verbatim (3 i18n keys restored, zh + ja). test-harness-contract untouched (no descriptor row, no verb — the one §7 EXEMPT line stays as door-signin-card left it).
- **3 · claim 4 — a run dies with the card that started it.** RED on base: `destroy()` sent no DELETE; the ORCH had no owner. FIX: `SignInCard.destroy()` and `pagehide` send `DELETE …/signin` (keepalive) for a live run — also when the close lands while the start is in flight; the card HOLDS its run over its socket (WS `claude-signin-hold {accountId, id}` → src/ws-handler.js → `socketHold`; again after every reconnect, then a GET to learn what it missed) and the socket's `close` calls `socketClosed` → the ORCH cancels a run whose last holder left and nobody re-held within `SIGNIN_ORPHAN_MS`. CHOICE: 3 min, not 0 — a reconnect or a phone that switched to the mail app for the sign-in link drops the socket while the person is mid-sign-in; an explicit close (card / modal / tour step / page) is immediate. Real node-pty legs (the REAL helper + a `sh` fake claude, /proc): close (the DELETE route) → helper + grandchild gone in ~26 ms, scratch removed; the holder's socket closing (orphanMs 0) → ~25 ms, scratch removed.
- **4 · claim 2 — the code never rides a failure.** RED on base: an echoing stub PTY + a silent exit 1 after the code → `error: "Paste code here if prompted > zq7Lk9#stateXYZ"` in the broadcast and the GET answer; the same on a REAL tty (the line discipline echoes what `read` takes); and in the heavy walk's new §6 over a real server: `"error":"Paste code here if prompted > SNTL-si1c#walkstate"` (base: 2 RED of 164). FIX: `sendCode` marks `codeSent`; the exit backstop then says ENDED_AFTER_CODE («the sign-in ended before Claude confirmed it — try again»), never the screen; `signinStep`'s lastLine is cut at PROMPT_RE (a bare prompt line is never a «why» either); oat-mint-model `redact` masks what stands after a code prompt (defense in depth — the OAT mint's sibling backstop publishes its lastLine the same way). test-record-clear-walk §6: a stub `claude auth login` reads the code on its tty and dies silently ⇒ no route answer, broadcast, file or journal line holds the typed word.
- **5 · debris — a row per failed attempt.** RED on base: three attempts in one card → three `POST /api/accounts/subscription`. ### gate red — the 2.369.342 master mirror (Actions run 39767737849, sha d3ab5db5) went red on heavy shard 5 while the branch run of the SAME sha was green: the runner image moved to Chrome 156.0.8078.47 between the two runs (lane chrome-156-drift; base d3ab5db5 = 2.369.342, test + census + the CSP collector, no user-visible change)
- **The drift:** nothing in the tree changed between the two runs; the runner's Chrome did. Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.47 (the runner's build, unpacked in the lane's own dir) reproduced both reds on the base exactly; the box's Chrome 154 reproduces neither.
- **Red 1 — test-browser-mediation-chrome ⑥, 11 methods without a census row.** 155 → 156 (`cdp-protocol-fetch.mjs --diff`, both sides recorded): +11 −1 methods, a new domain (FindInPage), two parameter changes that move no class (`Animation.seekAnimations` currentTime → currentTime? + currentTimes?, still page-mutation; `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` +textLayoutMode?, still view), one event added (`Storage.privateVerificationTokensUpdated`). The fixture `scripts/fixtures/cdp-protocol-156.0.8078.47/` was written by the fetch script from the real 156.
  - **FindInPage.findFirst / findNext / findPrev / stop — view**, not read. Measured on 156 (a data: page with a focused text field and two matches far below the fold): `findFirst` SCROLLS the page to its match (0 → 2414 px), highlights it and BLURS the field the user had focused; `findNext` / `findPrev` scroll on (2414 ⇄ 5037 px); `stop` from ANOTHER connection that never started a find ended this session's find and the picture changed — so none of them only reads the page, and each is refused while the user drives.

A stock 156 answers each `-32000 'Private Verification Tokens service is not available'`.
  - **`Storage.getRelatedWebsiteSets` left the protocol** — its row stays, marked `until` 156.
  - `CENSUS_CHROMES` = 153 + 154 + 155 + 156: 682 rows (664 / 661 / 664 / 674 listed, 0 unclassified, stale or misdated on each) — view 111, harmless 149, read 183, page-mutation 197.
- **Red 2 — the CSP teardown: «script-src-attr inline, line 1 column 101, source ""» on the app page** (test-record-clear-ui and test-channel-jump, every attempt). THE ELEMENT is no product element: it is the suites' own NEGATIVE CONTROL. Each parses its hostile `<img src=x onerror=…>` in `document.implementation.createHTMLDocument('')` from code evaluated over CDP. Column 101 is the `=` of `d.innerHTML =` in that one-line expression, and no source means a script with no URL (Runtime.evaluate). Measured on 156 against 154 (a loopback page served with the app's policy, report-uri + the CDP Audits issue):
  - **Chrome 156 reports an inline handler when its attribute is SET**, an inert document's too — createHTMLDocument, DOMParser, a `<template>`'s content, `Document.parseHTMLUnsafe`, a plain `setAttribute('onclick', …)`. It reports as the page that ran the code, at the statement's position. No handler runs (`window.__xss` stays unset); the violating node is not in the page's document (`DOM.resolveNode`: «does not belong to the document»).
  - **Chrome 154 reports none of those.** It reports a handler only when it compiles (a live detached `<img>` whose load fails).
  - **The same rule reaches suites that did not run on a 156 runner yet.** Found by running every chrome suite that carries `on*=` markup under 156, with the collector naming each line's code:
    - test-channel-window-render ④'s control: the same inert-document parse.
    - test-inbox-reply-ui ⑦ and test-docx-viewer: each planted live handler now reports TWICE against their `=== 1` — once when its attribute is set (source "", at the statement) and once when it compiles (the page, at 1:1), with the same sample.
    - test-channel-window-render ⑭: the hostile .md attachment `<img src=x onerror="window.__pwned=14">` reaches the viewer's sanitizer. DOMPurify's inert parse SETS the handler before it drops it: `bundle.js 127564:35` is `new DOMParser().parseFromString(…)`, sample «window.__pwned=14». Nothing ran.
- **The fix:**
  - The three controls run in a BLANK TAB: `scripts/scratch.mjs evalInBlankTab(cdpPort, expr)` opens a fresh about:blank tab of the suite's own Chrome, which has no policy, evaluates the expression there and closes the tab. The same parser reads the same markup and nothing reports.
  - **Takes match the suite's own code.** inbox-reply-ui ⑦ and docx-viewer take their planted handler by its SAMPLE and accept 1–2 reports (≤ 155 one, 156 two). channel-window-render ⑭ takes the report of its own attachment's sanitizer parse by sample AND by the bundle as its source (0 on ≤ 155, ≤ 1 on 156). A product report with other code, or this handler compiled on the page, is never taken: the sample in a suite's line key closes the position-only take's hazard (lane mirror-331-reds-chrome).
  - **The collector names the code:** the app policy's `script-src` gains `'report-sample'`, which allows nothing; a report then carries the first 40 characters of the handler it names. A chrome suite's sink (handed the suite's file) keeps that sample; a hub's own data/csp-reports.jsonl never does (`reportsOf(text, { sample })`, the never-a-value law kept). The teardown prints beside every line WHAT was reported (`cspWhat`): the sample, the code's source or «code with NO URL — a script this SUITE evaluated over CDP», and for an inline handler the Chrome 156 set-time rule. The runner's line now reads «script-src-attr inline — «window.__xss=1», set by code with NO URL at 1:101 …».
- **Measured:**
  - **The base under 156** (Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.47 in place of /usr/bin/google-chrome, through a scratch copy that changes only the `CHROME` line): test-record-clear-ui and test-channel-jump end with exactly the runner's line.

  - **The fix under 154:** test-channel-window-render 197, test-docx-viewer 95 and test-inbox-reply-ui, ALL PASS.
  - **The sweep** — 21 chrome suites carrying `on*=` markup under 156: every other one green with no CSP line.

The list is the only child that may shrink (`flex: 1; min-height: 0`), the API section had no flex rule (`min-height: auto` — it never shrinks below its 20 rows), so the list — which held the waiting message — was squeezed to its 20 px of padding and the API rows ran past the window's bottom, clipped, with nothing to scroll. The status listeners hear a batch.

Every press is THE model's `readNotices` (user-todos-actions.js): ONE POST, then a 5 s Undo toast posting exactly `changed` back.
- **Read on sight (the window):** the selected notice is marked done — THE status write, Mark done's own (kept for the keyboard) — after NOTICE_READ_MS on screen = the page visible, focus INSIDE the window, the pane showing (split, or the one-pane item view), re-checked when the clock ends; ‹ back marks it at once. A mail's HTML reaches the frame's DOMPurify only through mail-frame step 1, the allowlist re-serializer, which drops every handler: `<img onerror>`, `onclick`, `ONMOUSEOVER` and `<svg onload>` — none survive. No report comes from a mail; test-csp-report ③d pins it.

The new `scripts/symbolicate.mjs lookupMany` does it in one pass that keeps only the asked lines (`decodeMappings` holds ~2 M arrays); it equals `lookup` on 4000 random positions.
    - `purifyParseSites` returns exactly DOMPurify's call (purify.ts:1078) on both builds. MUTANT: the signature cut to the bare call ⇒ 3 sites, RED.

### lane agy-card-details — an Antigravity conversation's cards carry their details: the file a Read names, the command a run names, every subagent of one step, and a killed subagent said as killed (base d3ab5db5 2.369.342)
- **Why:** the owner, in an Antigravity conversation with two screenshots (2026-10-22): «你 review 一下 agy 支持，我发现很多卡片都缺少细节». The screenshots and the owner's store (read-only, shapes only) showed five gaps: a Read card with no path and «✓ 1 行»; the store road handing QUOTED paths to the sub view and the artifacts reader; a Bash card that is agy's own truncation notice with no command; two invoke_subagent calls of one planner step drawing one card; and a KILLED subagent whose window showed its reads «运行中» for ever while its card said «已停止 · 它没有发回答复».
- **MEASURED (the owner's parent conversation + its two subs, a store COPY + the parent's live ACP journal of 1292 records, production read-only; the owner's ids / text out of the tests):** agy's tool args reach a card by TWO roads — the LIVE stream (tool_info.parameters, CLEAN: `{Path, StartLine, EndLine}`, `{CommandLine}`) and the STORE (the db step args / transcript `tool_calls[].args`, every value a JSON-ENCODED STRING: `"Path":"\"/home/…\""`, `"StartLine":"1"`, `"CommandLine":"\"…\""`, `"Content":"\"…\""` — all 32 read_file calls carried a \"-wrapped Path). A read_file's stream output is a ONE-LINE summary («113 lines, 24215 bytes»), never the file's text; the text is in the store (transcript_full / the DB). The two subagents spawned in ONE planner step each got their OWN stream step index (:24 / :25) and a distinct «Created the following subagent: {id}» at that transcript step; the sub rows' `spawnStepIndex` was 27 for BOTH (not the link). The killed sub's last planner step issued 12 view_file calls and was killed (manage_subagents kill_all) before any result.
- **The normalizer (new PURE src/agy-tool-args.js, in the test-architecture PURE set):** ONE pass both roads take — `decodeScalar` (a value that is a JSON-encoded SCALAR becomes that scalar; a clean path / command / number stays itself — an object/array arg keeps its string), then agy's keys get the card's canonical aliases (Path/AbsolutePath/TargetFile→file_path, CommandLine→command, Cwd→cwd, StartLine→offset, EndLine→limit, toolAction→title, toolSummary→summary) while the raw keys (decoded) stay for the card's 技术细节 fold. The invariant: a harness's tool arguments are normalized ONCE. The wrapper's live tool_call and the store's stepRecords both emit `normalizeAgyToolArgs(args)`; pathArg + artifactRecordsOf decode (the artifacts reader's `agyFilePath` shares it) so a write's path and content are never \"-wrapped.
- **Link by ID, not by a counter (gap 4):** `subIdForStep(read, parent, step)` reads the parent transcript's own «Created the following subagent: {conversationId}» at the step — unique per call, and the stream-vs-transcript index drift cannot break it (spawnStepIndex 27 was shared; the step number was not the link). snapshotOf and the wrapper's linkSpawns try it FIRST, the message-step scan stays the fallback. Two invoke_subagent rows of one planner step keep distinct stream steps, so each becomes a spawn and each gets a card (never folded into one).
- **A process that ended is never «running» (gap 5):** a TERMINATED sub (killed / stopped-with-parent / failed — not an answered sub, which agy leaves ALIVE) closes its still-open tool cards: `closePendingRecords` turns each into a `tool_call_update` status 'failed' carrying the SUB_TERMINATED sentinel, which the renderer (src/helper-ask.js isSubTerminated) draws as the localized «terminated with the subagent» — never the token, never a spinner. The parent card (src/lib/subagent-card.js) says «被父代理终止» with the sub's «最后进展» (its last planner prose, else its last tool's own words), not «它没有发回答复».
- **The cards (src/lib/chat-renderers.js):** the Read card shows the normalized path and, for agy's «N lines, M bytes» summary, «N 行 · size» as its status (not «1 行»); the run card carries agy's toolSummary in its head (toolSummaryChipHtml — only agy sets input.summary, so claude / codex are unchanged); the truncation notice's `file:` path is already clickable (lane agy-links-file-url, in this base).
- **Scoped out, said here:** the Read card does NOT yet inline the file's text from the store (transcript_full / the DB). The «1 行» confusion is resolved by the summary-as-status + the clickable path (the file is one click away); inlining the text per read is a bounded helper-door read with marginal value over the path, and this lane is ONE commit — left for a follow-up.
- **Tests:** test-agy-store ⑫ (+9: decodeScalar / normalizeAgyToolArgs / artifactRecordsOf decode, subIdForStep by-id, a KILLED sub's cards closed + lastText, two-in-one-step → two cards, a made-up store — owner ids out), test-search-card-title (+5 render under the DOM shim: the Read «N 行 · size», the run card's toolSummary chip, the terminated sentinel → localized, the KILLED parent card's «被父代理终止» + «最后进展», a non-agy tool unchanged), test-agy-harness / test-antigravity-session / test-artifacts / test-path-linkify / test-page-link-ui / test-harness-contract / test-architecture (green; the gap-5 close is gated so an answered sub's dangling card keeps the base). +5 i18n keys (zh + ja).
- **Owner-run (real agy, never run here):** whether a NEW run's live stream carries the invoke_subagent output (the owner's journal, from a pre-cards wrapper, had none — the by-id link reads the store either way); whether the store text is worth inlining in the Read card.
