### lane agy-status-bar-facts — an Antigravity conversation's status bar shows what agy reports; what a bar shows is a descriptor row (base 72056f53 2.369.340)
- **Why:** the owner, on an Antigravity conversation (2026-10-21): «agy 的 chatview 缺少很多信息啊 什么 context 啊，cache rate，产物啊啥的下面都没有了». agy's stream carries `usage` on its result, but data/bin/agy-wrapper.js kept it in the sidecar only (`usage keys seen: {}` over the owner's 429 journal frames), so the bar — which reads the stream's usage — had nothing; the Artifacts reader was the ACP one, which reads `diff` contents agy never sends.
- **MEASURED (the owner's two agy conversations, production read-only, shapes only; the login file never opened):** `result.usage` = the CONVERSATION's RUNNING TOTAL. It equals, to the token, the sum over every model call of every turn in agy's own transcript (`<HOME>/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<conversation>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl`, one JSON row per step, a MODEL row carrying input_tokens / cache_read_tokens / output_tokens): 1 turn of 90 calls = 545 062 / 172 175 / 6 556 922; 5 turns = 577 850 / 58 173 / 4 065 912 (the binary names the computation `steps.CalculateTokenSums`). total_tokens = input + output; input EXCLUDES cache reads. So the live context is the turn's LAST call (90 228 tokens = 9 % of 1 048 576); the brief's «the last turn's input + cache_read» on the per-turn sum would read 677 %. step_update `usage` is NOT used: no capture of it exists (what it counts is unmeasured); the sidecar keeps its copy.
- **The record:** at each result the wrapper reads the tail (≤ 4 MiB) of THIS conversation's transcript through ONE gate (a uuid id, the realpath inside the store root, O_NOFOLLOW, a regular file; nothing else in agy's store is opened) and journals ONE `{type:'acp', kind:'usage', total, turn, last, model, modelFrom, durationSeconds}` (PURE src/agy-turn-usage.js). The ACP normalizer's `_processUsage` turns it into the ONE usage meta every bar reads: `last` = context + cache (claude's last-message reading; no transcript ⇒ nothing overwritten — a sum is never a context), `total` = the odometer in codex's totals shape, the turn's spend + time beside; a slug agy NAMED (init.model) is the served model, the one it was only started with is not. chatStatus replays it on attach — and for a conversation whose wrapper predates the record (dtach keeps the old wrapper across an update) the sidecar's own running total (meta.usage) is the odometer until it restarts. No new stdout consumer (acp-events.js unchanged; the side-effects road untouched).
- **THE ROW (PURE src/status-bar-facts.js):** `ui.statusBar` {context 'reported'|'table'|null, cache, odometer, model, duration, windows} on every chat descriptor + the client META (test-harness-contract deep-compares): claude reported/cache/model; codex + odometer; opencode reported/model only (ACP usage_update has no cache field — its bar used to draw ⚡0%); antigravity everything with a WINDOW TABLE; shell / a register()ed harness without a row = nothing reported. The bar gates context / ⚡ / Σ / the turn time on the row and draws ONE «not reported» chip naming what a harness lacks (claude: token total, turn time).
- **The window table (antigravity descriptor, DOCUMENTED not measured):** Google's Gemini API model pages read 2026-10-21 — gemini-4-argon «Context window (unified input and output token limit) 1,048,576» (page of 2026-10-14); input token limit 1,048,576 for gemini-3.8-flash (2026-09-02), gemini-3.7-flash (2026-10-12, deprecated), gemini-3.6-flash (2026-07-30), gemini-3.1-pro-preview (2026-10-09). agy slugs are `<code>-<level>` ⇒ prefix rows; an unknown slug ⇒ «window unknown» with the token count.
- **Artifacts:** `artifactsOf` = agy's own reader (src/harnesses/artifacts-of.js `antigravity`): the stream names its writes write_file / edit_file with an absolute `Path` (measured), init.tools the model-facing write_to_file / replace_file_content / multi_replace_file_content — both read; a file: URI percent-decoded, a relative path the cwd's. src/artifacts.js: agy's brain/<conversation>/ is its own artifacts dir (a report there + .metadata.json), so it is no longer «agent config» (the owner's report there was code, no card).
- **Todos:** left out — agy's CHECKPOINT steps are context checkpoints and manage_task names background command tasks; neither is a list of named steps with states.
- **Tests:** test-status-bar-facts (new, fast, 34: PURE + the normalizer (+ the sidecar odometer of a wrapper that predates the record) + the REAL bar per harness under a fake DOM; mutants: the cache gate cut ⇒ opencode ⚡0%, the context from the sum ⇒ 677 %), test-harness-contract (+24: every chat harness's row, RED rows, a register()ed harness), test-artifacts (+10: the owner's shapes, names replaced; a diff-carrying call still reads as ACP's; the base ACP reader produces nothing), test-agy-harness ⑬ (+9: one record per turn from the fake agy, the gate refuses a brain dir linked out of the store + its RED copy), test-antigravity-session ⑤ (+5, heavy: two turns through the real create path on a named account), test-agy-status-bar-chrome (new, heavy, 15: the agy bar's five facts + the Artifacts chip, a reload, a claude chat's «not reported»). The fake agy (scripts/fixtures/antigravity-agy) now speaks the measured semantics (running sums, agy's transcript under $HOME with AGY_STUB_TRANSCRIPT=1, write/edit steps).
- **Owner-run (real agy, never run here):** the step_update `usage` semantics; whether a real agy flushes the transcript row before its result (else `last` is the call before); whether init names the served model.

### lane device-node-version — the installer provisions Node 22.23.4 and replaces its OWN older node; the Machines card says which Node each agent runs, 「运行时过旧」 below the floor (the Node.js security releases of 2026-10-21; base 72056f53 2.369.340)
- **Why:** the Node.js 2026-10-21 security releases — 4 HIGH: CVE-2026-111497 (the Brotli decoder's out-of-bounds write), CVE-2026-105482 (dns.resolve NUL truncation), CVE-2026-105483 + CVE-2026-106069 (TLS hostname-check bypasses); fixed in 22.23.4 / 24.22.1 / 26.12.1. A paired machine's agent runs the node its installer provisioned (`<root>/node`, the pin v22.22.0) or found (a system node ≥ 18); the hub kept none of it, so no card could say «this agent runs an old Node».
- **The base, measured:** the hello-ack has carried `nodeVersion` since M0 — the hub's client read it and dropped it (no field on the record, none on the row). The installer's `find_node` takes `$ROOT/node/bin/node` second (after `--node`) whenever it runs ≥ 18, so a moved pin never reached an install that already had its own node — test-node-bootstrap ⑨'s RED CONTROL runs the 2.369.340 installer over the same fake mirror: the pin moved to v22.23.4 and its own node stayed v22.22.0, nothing fetched. The ps1 (by reading — no pwsh here) does the same, and `$nodeExe = $null` wiped `-NodeExe` (PowerShell names are case-blind: the parameter and the variable are one), so a `-NodeExe` was never tried.
- **The installer (sh + ps1):** the pin is v22.23.4 (the comment names the advisory and the hub's table). THE PIN MOVED: an install whose OWN node is older than the pin gets the pinned one in its place through the same road as a first provisioning (the mirror or the hub's `/vibespace-node/` fallback, SHASUMS256.txt verified, a smoke run, a rename inside the root); a second run downloads nothing, an older pin never downgrades, a failed download keeps the one it had (said, exit 0). A node the machine HAD (PATH / nvm / /usr/… / `--node`) is never touched. The sh replaces before the take-over (a POSIX rename leaves the running agent its inode); the ps1 after it (Windows will not move a folder whose node.exe runs) and moves the old folder aside first so a refused move changes nothing. The ps1 keeps `-NodeExe` in `$nodeArg` before the variable is reused.
- **The hello + the record:** the daemon's hello-ack adds `openssl` (process.versions.openssl) and `nodeOwn` (its execPath under realpath(`<root>/node`)). The hub's client (src/agentd/client.js) hands `{node, openssl, own, platform}` (PURE src/device-runtime.js `runtimeOf`, bounded) to a new `onRuntime` door — hosts.js (ssh) and dial-pairing.js (dial, the card repainted) → `hosts.noteRuntime` → the record's `deviceRuntime {node, openssl, own, platform, at}`, written only when it moved. Kept on the HOST record beside `devicePolicy` / `deviceElevated` (the hello-ack's other facts), not on `dial.lastAccept` (the dial upgrade's headers, rewritten at every accept before the hello and absent on an ssh machine).
- **The floor table:** src/device-runtime.js (NEW, PURE, imports nothing): `NODE_FLOORS` {22: 22.23.4, 24: 24.22.1, 26: 26.12.1} each naming `ADVISORIES['nodejs-2026-10-21']` (date + the 4 CVE ids); `runtimeVerdict` → old (below its line's floor) / ok / unlisted (a major the table has no floor for — no chip) / unknown (not said — no chip), `fix` = reinstall (its own node, or not said) | system; `upgradeLineOf` (brew / apt · dnf · apk / winget); `runtimeRow` = the `/api/hosts` row's `runtime`. A future advisory lands in this table — never a vendor call.
- **The card:** src/lib/machine-runtime-line.js (NEW, CLIENT): every machine's summary gets `Node v… · OpenSSL …` («Node：未知» when not said) + 「运行时过旧」 below the floor (title: the floor, the advisory's date, its ids); the open card's recipe — own node: run the pairing command again, the installer replaces it; a system node: its upgrade line, then the pairing command so the agent restarts on it; a dial device gets the 「重新安装…」 door (the existing `Install again…` key) = that device's pairing sheet. Theme vars, zh + ja.
- **What the owner does per machine:** the card says it. An agent on its installer's own node (every machine the installer provisioned): open its pairing sheet (「重新安装…」), generate the command and run it ON the machine — the installer replaces the node, then restarts the agent on it. An agent on the machine's own node: upgrade that node (the card's line), then the same. The agent's self-upgrade (landBundle) only lands a bundle — it never changes node; the «send the new command over its link» box hands a token, it runs no installer. This box's own node (v24.12.0) is below 24.22.1: its REAL daemon in test-host-stale-dialer-ui already wears the chip.
- **Tests:** test-node-bootstrap 19 → 30 (heavy, 474 ms; ⑨ the pin in sh + ps1 ≥ the table's floor, the own node replaced / not again / never downgraded / kept on a failed download, a system node and a `--node` untouched; RED = the 2.369.340 installer). test-dial-health 52 → 85 (fast, 186 ms; the 16-row floor table, the advisory's facts, the bounded statement, the row over the REAL HostManager across a restart, an old daemon ⇒ unknown, the wiring, the words zh + ja, CSS on theme vars, 2 patched-copy controls). test-agentd-session 36 → 43 (heavy, 7.9 s; the real daemon's hello: node = process.version, openssl, own false; a daemon started from `<root>/node/bin/node` says own = true; a bundle without the three fields ⇒ unknown). test-host-stale-dialer-ui 19 → 35 (heavy, 32 s; ③ three REAL paired devices — own node v22.22.0 / system v24.12.0 (a `--require` preload pins process.version) / never dialed: the rows, the card zh + en, the chip's title, the recipes, 「重新安装…」 opens that device's pairing sheet; CONTROL = a bundle without the line's paint). test-architecture 783 → 784 (device-runtime.js PURE). THE REDS (the new tests over the 2.369.340 product, the PURE module overlaid): test-dial-health stops at `hm.noteRuntime is not a function`; test-node-bootstrap 7 ✗ (the pin, the replacement and what follows from it); test-agentd-session 5 ✗ (no onRuntime, no fields); test-host-stale-dialer-ui 5 ✗ (no `runtime` on a row, no line on the card).
- **Gate reds met in the lane (fixed in the commit):** test-live-bar-layout §4c THE RATCHET (52 > 51 dead tokens — the upgrade line's `var(--text-primary)`; the theme's token is `--text`; test-dial-health W-RT2 now refuses a var the theme does not define); test-press-select §4 (the upgrade line's `user-select: all` — the page defaults to none; a census row with its reason: a command the person copies); test-agentd-dial B9's broadcast ceiling 4 → 5 (A's FIRST hello states its node once — the record's runtime moves, the card repaints; a re-dial of the same node moves nothing; the flap control still bites: 9 accepts / 8 closes).
- **Not measured:** the ps1 runs nowhere here (no pwsh) — its legs are read, not run; a real Windows re-pair should confirm the post-take-over swap. The real installer on a real machine is not run (NEVER touch a real paired machine): the fake mirror serves stub tarballs.

### lane runtime-floor — VibeSpace OWNS its Node runtime: ONE floor table + ONE provisioner; a Node security release = one commit that moves the table + the product's own update, never an image rebuild or a pod rollout (the owner 2026-10-22: «每次有漏洞都要更新 pod 也太麻烦了吧 有没有更好的解决方案？»; base 724baa52 = lane device-node-version on 72056f53)
- **What was true (measured 2026-10-21/22):** the hub = an nvm node BAKED into the systemd unit by scripts/install-service.sh (v24.12.0 — moved to v24.22.1 by hand); fleet pods = the image's /usr/local/bin/node (22.23.1; the image moves only with a rollout, and a pod restart kills every user's dtach session); device agents = the installer's pin (lane device-node-version moves it to v22.23.4).
- **THE TABLE:** PURE src/runtime-floor.js — NODE_FLOORS {22: 22.23.4, 24: 24.22.1, 26: 26.12.1} + ADVISORIES {nodejs-2026-10-21: date, url, 4 CVEs}, `verdict(process.version)` ok / below-floor {wanted} / unknown-major / unknown, `compare`. Lane device-node-version wrote the table first (src/device-runtime.js); it is MOVED here and re-exported there (the same objects, `===`) — the Machines card's chip, the hub's boot line, the updater and the provisioner read ONE file.
- **THE PROVISIONER:** src/node-runtime.js (SHARED) `provision(wanted, {root, mirror})` — SHASUMS256.txt first (an archive it does not list is never downloaded), the archive's sha256 must match BEFORE `tar` unpacks it, the unpacked binary must answer `wanted`, then `<root>/runtime/current` flips (a relative symlink renamed into place; win32: current.txt); writes ONLY under `<root>/runtime` (a link there ⇒ `not-own`, nothing written through it), so a system node is never touched; KEEP 2 versions; bounded (≤ 160 MiB archive, ≤ 256 KiB sums, ≤ 10 min) and never holding the loop (streams + child processes). `fetchFile` = THE ONE downloader of a node release file — the hub's device mirror route /vibespace-node now fetches through it (the same name list). **Pinned key: none** — the trust anchor is the mirror's HTTPS + its SHASUMS256.txt, the device installer's own rule; the release team's `.sig` is not checked (said, not hidden). nodejs.org is the default mirror (`VIBESPACE_NODE_MIRROR` overrides, the installer's name).
- **THE SAFETY ADDENDA (主开发's acceptance condition, 2026-10-22):** (1) THE HASH LIVES IN THIS REPO — src/runtime-floor.js `ARCHIVES` carries, per floor version, the six archives' SHASUMS256.txt lines (linux / darwin × x64 / arm64 tar.gz, win x64 / arm64 zip): 22.23.4 + 24.22.1 = the lines 主开发 fetched from nodejs.org and cross-checked against the hub's verified download (byte-for-byte equal), 26.12.1 fetched once over HTTPS by the lane (06:39Z). The provisioner checks the archive against the TABLE first (`archiveSha`), the mirror's SHASUMS256.txt second (`sums-disagree` before the download, `sha-mismatch` after it); a version / platform with no line is NEVER provisioned (`no-table-row`, not one request) — VIBESPACE_NODE_MIRROR can serve only the bytes this repo names; a musl archive has no line ⇒ Alpine is never provisioned. A security release now adds the six lines with the moved floor (test-update-road's release commit does). (2) THE SWITCH RE-VERIFIES WHAT IT EXECS — provision writes `<runtime>/node-v<ver>/.vibespace-runtime.json` {version, platform, sha256 of bin/node, archive + its sha256, provisionedAt}; `reexecOnOwnRuntime` hashes bin/node (1 MiB chunks, ~0.2 s) against it before the execve: `tampered` / `unverified` ⇒ no switch, one log line, the base node runs (a planted or corrupted binary never runs; the device agent's switch is the same function). Pinned key: still none — the release team's GPG `.sig` is the known gap.
- **THE ROADS — no unit, no image change:** server.js's FIRST line (src/server/runtime-boot.js `boot`) runs `reexecOnOwnRuntime`: when `data/runtime/current` is a NEWER node of the SAME major line (a native addon such as node-pty is built for one major's ABI — the provisioner only ever installs the running major's fixed release) that answers its version, the process REPLACES itself with it (process.execve — the same pid: the unit's baked node, run.sh and a pod's image entrypoint start the base node and keep supervising; once per start, `VIBESPACE_RUNTIME_REEXEC` dropped before any child; `VIBESPACE_RUNTIME_SWITCH=0` off; a node without execve / win32 stays). Then the `[runtime]` verdict line, and the boot pull's check 20 s in (`node scripts/runtime-check.mjs --provision` as a child; never in a throwaway root or with NO_AUTO_UPDATE). scripts/update.sh (hub + pods; ⚙ Update runs it) runs the same check after the pull + build, before the restart — it never fails the update. GET /api/runtime + ⚙ Diagnostics report «Node runtime» (zh + ja). server.js stays at its 1907-line ratchet (ONE line).
- **DEVICES:** an agent on its OWN node (`nodeOwn` = <root>/node or <root>/runtime) below the floor provisions for itself 90 s after its start (nodejs.org, then its hub's /vibespace-node; never in a scratch root) and switches at its next start — the same `reexecOnOwnRuntime` (a self-upgrade's successor, started on the same node, switches the same way; the launch site census of test-agentd-hidden-start / -spawn-hide unchanged). POSIX only: Windows has no execve, so a Windows agent never provisions and its road stays the installer's re-provision (the card's 「重新安装…」). A node the machine had is only said (the chip). The installers are untouched by this lane (device-node-version owns the pin lines). node-runtime's children carry windowsHide (the daemon's closure — test-agentd-spawn-hide). agent-env DAEMON_ENV_KEEP + VIBESPACE_NODE_MIRROR / VIBESPACE_RUNTIME_SWITCH / VIBESPACE_RUNTIME_REEXEC.
- **THE BELT (cheap, independent of the runtime):** MEASURED on node v24.12.0 — the built-in fetch asks `gzip, deflate` yet DECODES a `content-encoding: br` answer it never asked for. src/safe-fetch.js (SHARED) is fetch over http / https: asks gzip, unpacks gzip, REFUSES any other encoding before a decoder; bounded, redirects ≤ 5 (auth dropped across origins). The census (scripts/test-fetch-encoding.mjs) over src/server: vendor-fixed 5 files (browser-builds-keeper, decision-engine, dropline-client, ops-routes, text-model-client), own 2 (agent-tool-generators, plugin-loader — this instance's API), operator 1 (feedback-forward), client 1 (published-pages' service-worker text); UNTRUSTED 2 now on safeFetch: plugin-install (a GitHub release a person names + its asset, wherever it redirects) and provider-models (a base URL a person typed). The node release download asks identity and refuses an encoded answer (and is sha-checked).
- **Censuses moved:** test-vendor-whitelist (REQUESTY counts safeFetch; nodejs.org asserted NOT a vendor host — a public, sha-gated download), test-channels-egress (PRIMITIVE counts safeFetch; the nodejs.org row moved from the mirror route to src/node-runtime.js), test-architecture (runtime-floor PURE; node-runtime + safe-fetch SHARED; §86 row node-runtime 7), ci.mjs rows for the four new suites.
- **Tests:** test-runtime-floor (NEW, fast, 27 — + a lexical-compare RED copy; ②b every floor's six archive lines), test-node-runtime (NEW, fast, 34 — the FIXTURE table rows: no line ⇒ refused before any request + a no-table-check RED copy, sums that disagree, other bytes; the record; a planted binary ⇒ tampered / no record ⇒ unverified + a no-re-check RED copy; the fake loopback mirror: provisioned + flipped, again ⇒ nothing downloaded, wrong sha / unlisted / a lying binary / bounded bytes + time ⇒ refused and nothing flipped, a system node byte for byte, a linked runtime dir refused, KEEP 2, the loop never held, the switch's states, a REAL process.execve keeping the pid, a no-newer-check RED copy, the device decisions), test-update-road (NEW, fast, 8 — scripts/update.sh in a scratch checkout pulls ONE commit moving the table ⇒ provisions ⇒ server.js's real first line switches with the same pid; a missing release / a wrong sha never fail the update), test-fetch-encoding (NEW, fast, 14 + the planted-raw-fetch RED); test-dial-health 85, test-agentd-session, test-provider-models 28, test-architecture 787.
- **The owner's FIRST adoption** (the report's recipe): nothing to roll out — each instance's next update (⚙ Update, the boot pull, or `scripts/update.sh` by hand) provisions and the restart switches; pods with NO_AUTO_UPDATE need the one update by hand.

### lane auto-cli-oat-unprobeable — an account the quota probe cannot prove is never sent; a failed probe names its reason where the owner looks (the owner 2026-10-22 02:1xZ: «为什么现在开始出现很多长时间没刷新过用量信息的账户 因为一直没用到过吗？»; base 72056f53 = 2.369.340)
- **Measured on the owner's hub (read-only: data/auto-cli-state.json, data/accounts.json key names, data/usage-probe-log.ndjson outcomes, the journal; no token read):** six accounts with 11–36 consecutive `fails` were exactly the six with `oatEnc` whose login had ended (loginState `oat-only`, the row's 「仅长期 token」); the two others with `fails: 1` were transient. Their last probe-log rows are `written` on 10-19/10-20 (the logins were alive then) and NONE after: since the login died, refreshViaCliPanel's oat-only door (2026-10-13) refuses them with no spawn, no log row, `false` — and the loop booked every refusal as a failed probe (`attempts` + `fails` + the 5 min × 2^min(f,6) backoff), journaling `failed (stale-idle; …)` with no reason. So the brief's «the probe is `claude -p /usage` under that account's CLI dir» was the base's design, not what ran: the cost was phantom failures and a re-ask every ≤ 5.3 h for ever, not vendor calls. The owner's guess was right: those rows refresh only when a session bills on them.
- **The ADDENDUM (主开发 2026-10-22 02:49Z, measured on the hub — the brief's premise was wrong):** the six tokens are NOT profile-less: every oat-only row's `oatShape.scopes` is `user:file_upload, user:inference, user:mcp_servers, user:plugins, user:profile, user:sessions:claude_code` (re-read here, key names + scopes only); `claude -p /usage` works on the token MATERIALIZED in the row's folder (a mint-time probe succeeded 10-20; OAT-in-file is measured PASS per version — the fixture's `oat-file-scopes` FAIL is a file WITHOUT the row's real scopes). So an oat-only row is PROBEABLE through the same door and the same spawn (CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR = its folder) when its facts allow, and named when they do not. On the hub today the CLI is 2.1.308 (journal: «not measured (fixture: 2.1.296, 2.1.306)»), so the six read `unprobeable:cli-unmeasured` until a measurement adds 2.1.308 — said on the row and once a day in the journal.
- **The verdict (PURE src/auto-cli-model.js, imports only secret-shapes):** `probeEligibility(row)` reads the row's OWN facts, in this order: an oat-only row (checked FIRST — an expired login and our token file still parse loggedIn) is `unprobeable:oat-no-profile` when `oatScopes` lacks `user:profile`, `unprobeable:cli-unmeasured` when `oatCli.measured` is not true (oatFileCaps: the hub's CLI is not one oatInFile measured — the folder never gets the token), `unprobeable:oat-not-in-folder` when the folder does not hold the token (`loginState.oatFile` + `oatFile.state === 'written'`; a refusal the token chip names), else `probeable`; a row with no login is `unprobeable:no-login`; any login is `probeable` (an `expired` login without a token too — its own probe says why it fails). null = not a subject (not a subscription, a pool, a harness whose rung is not `cli-usage`). `accounts.list()` puts the facts on an oat row (`oatScopes` from the recorded shape — no secret; `oatCli: {cli, measured}` from oatFileCaps) and the verdict beside them; the loop, the probe door (before its spawn) and the row read the same verdict. The `oat-not-in-folder` kind is beyond the addendum's two: «measured» alone does not put the token there (a write that failed, a vault-locked key, a sweep not yet run), and probing then would spend a spawn on the expired login — so it is named, not sent.
- **The loop (src/server/auto-cli-loop.js):** an unprobeable account costs NO attempt, NO failure, NO backoff; `[auto-cli] quota refresh <id>: not probed — <the fact that failed>; refreshes when a session uses it` (e.g. `long-lived token only, and claude 2.1.308 is not measured with it in the account's folder`) ONCE a day per kind (`said`, `<id>|<kind>`, a new key in data/auto-cli-state.json beside the attempt clock, clamped like it — a restart says nothing again; a changed reason is said). The FIRST tick that sees one clears what the base booked against it (its `fails` and its `attempts` stamp) and says so on that line: `(36 failed attempts booked before this cleared)`. The cadence and the wandering threshold are untouched; no new vendor call (test-vendor-whitelist 316 = base).
- **A failed probe names its reason:** the door (src/usage-routes.js) now gives its two silent failures a verdict — `exit` (the CLI exited ≠ 0: `exit N: <its first line>`) and `parse` (exit 0, no quota line: `no quota lines in its answer: <its first line>` — the measured 152-row shape on the owner's hub). The first line skips a `Warning:` line (the CLI's stdin warning rides every probe, the successful ones too), stderr before stdout. Every verdict of the door goes through ONE function `panelSays`, which keeps the last failed one on the account RECORD (`probe: {at, ok: false, why}`, accounts.noteProbe through the one atomic writer, broadcast by `_notify`) and drops it on the next WRITTEN answer; an oat-only refusal (code `login`) is not a failed probe. The loop's failed line ends `— <why> [<class>]`. The ⟳ route's ladder is unchanged: it stops on `login` / `identity` / `write` only, so `exit` / `parse` fall through to the token rungs as before.
- **THE ONE scrub:** `probeWhyText` — control characters out (ANSI too), secret-shapes `redactSecrets` with `runs: true` (R1–R8 incl. unnamed key-material runs), THEN the 200-character bound (a cut after the redaction can only shorten). The raw probe ring (data/usage-probe-log.ndjson, 2.369.109 — the owner's verbatim debugger log) is unchanged and keeps the CLI's bytes; it is never a row, a journal line or a broadcast.

### gate red — the 2.369.341 release chain: three reds under load (box load 18–25 while other lanes' gates ran), each green alone on a rerun — all FIXTURE races, the product correct (lane gate-flakes-341, test-only)
- RED 1 test-desktop-webrtc-chrome ⑳ (heavy; lane speaker-passthrough-v1's sound leg): «the second press ⇒ muted, the machine's capture ENDED (its helper's stdin closed), no more packets (6)». MEASURED with a copy of the leg that samples Chrome's own inbound-rtp every 20 ms around the OFF press, against the agent's `[sound] <sid> off` log instant: the machine stops 4–8 ms after the click (the page mutes IN the click; `stream-audio off` → src/desktop-sound.js `stop` closes the encoder's socket BEFORE the helper's stdin and the packet handler is gated on `closed`), its `audio.sent` stands still from then on and equals Chrome's final count; Chrome receives 0 packets after the stop alone and 3–4 beside two heavy chrome suites (packets already on the wire, landed ≤ 16 ms later). THE LEG was the cause: `pk1` was `stats().audio.packets`, the strip's ONCE-A-SECOND getStats read (src/lib/stream-view.js readStats, STREAM_LIMITS.statsMs 1000), up to a second old at the stop, so `pk2 − pk1 ≤ 5` counted packets of that second that came BEFORE the stop — it held only while the press landed ≤ 100 ms after a stats tick (alone it reads 3–5; the measuring copy, its press 300 ms later in the tick: 18–19 with 0 packets after the stop). Fix (the leg, never a fixed count): Chrome's count read FRESH (`pc.getStats()`); THE TAIL waits until Chrome heard nothing for 300 ms by its own clock (report timestamp − lastPacketReceivedTimestamp; bounded 5 s), then NONE for 1.5 s; the machine's own `audio.sent` is the same at its «off» push and a later one, and ≥ Chrome's count. RED CONTROL in the leg: an OFF that never reaches the machine (the page's `setSound(false)` swallowed) — Chrome never goes quiet in 5 s and the machine's count keeps rising. The sibling row «「麦克风」 + 「声音」 together … keeps arriving» read the same snapshot ⇒ Chrome's fresh count too. Proof: the old row read 3 / 3 / 3 alone (⑳ only) and 5 (the full suite), 4 / 4 / 4 / 3 / 3 under load (box 8–41) — green, the count phase-locked to the stats tick; the press moved 300 / 600 ms later in the tick reads 19 / 34 — RED, with 0 packets after the stop; the new row at the same shifts: green, 0 new. The final suite: 3/3 alone and 5/5 beside two heavy chrome suites, ALL PASS (143).
- RED 2 (the same suite, a third run of the .341 chain, box busy with other gates): ⑳ «「麦克风」 + 「声音」 together … the viewer's voice reaches the machine (a render started)» ✗ with `{"voice":false,"packets":[547,597]}` — no render on the machine within 10 s, the machine's sound kept arriving; the row printed nothing about WHICH step stopped. MEASURED with a copy that times each step from the press: the toggle live 105–129 ms, Chrome sending at once, the agent's `[mic] … live` 41–92 ms, the render 51–179 ms — 8 runs at load 2–10, 3 confined to 4 CPUs beside 6 busy loops, 3 on 2 CPUs beside 4; NOT reproduced in 14. That shape (no render, the sound unaffected) is exactly a press Chrome refuses: a copy without the row's `Browser.grantPermissions` reads `voice:false` with the sound arriving and the button titled 「浏览器拒绝了麦克风」 — and the row never read the grant's own answer (the page's `cdp()` has no error check). No product race found (the receiver starts on the first packet; facts are memoised, `runMs` 20 s). Fix (the leg, ⑳ as a family): the grant's answer is read; each step waits for ITS effect, bounded 15 s — the toggle live, Chrome's outbound-rtp audio `packetsSent > 0`, the machine's `mic.packets > 0` (its stats push), the render — and «keeps arriving» is Chrome's fresh count rising by 30 (bounded 10 s), never a 1.2 s sleep; a red now says `STUCK AT: <the step>` with the toggle's class/title and the machine's mic numbers (checked: the copy without the grant reds «STUCK AT: the toggle never went live»). ### lane browser-uppercase-keys — capitals and symbols in an xpra window arrive as the viewer's machine typed them (a fleet user on a Mac, 2.369.340: inc-mvj6nj3e-av0w «在 Chrome 浏览器里无法输入大写，导致输入密码的时候无法输入大写» + inc-mvj6ysm7-kmhw; base a4b07508 = the 2.369.341 cut)
- THE REPORT, AS THE RINGS TELL IT: the Agent browser was an XPRA app window (div.xpra-win in picture-shell, the keys in textarea.xpra-ime); his Mac's Caps Lock switches the input method (a CJK IME); the captured attempt: Shift down → the letter's keydown OWNED by the input method + a composition on the same tick → Shift up 80 ms later → the commit 1.4 s later → Enter. His pod: xpra 6.5.4-r0, the version measured here.
- THE TWO ROADS, MEASURED (probes in the lane dir: the DOM keystrokes as a Linux and a Mac Chrome fire them, a text box and a password box):
  - CDP (the live view: browser-live-window onDocKey → keyRoute / macChord → keyRecord → the bridge → the driver's stream → Input.dispatchKeyEvent): CLEAN on base — 32 of 32 through the real driver 0.38.2, launched, headed and ATTACHED to a Chrome already running with the attach argv (the fleet's one-browser shape). The record's `text` IS the DOM key, so Shift, Caps Lock and the layout arrive as the viewer's machine applied them.
  - XPRA (xpra-view keyInputOf → xpra-client keyDown / typeText → xpra-proto keyActionFor / ImeKeymap.plan → key-action): xpra 6.5.4's OWN server keyboard code (KeyboardConfig parse + set_keymap + get_keycode + make_keymask_match + the XTest press, in do_process_keyboard_event's order) programmed with our keymap, a real Chrome on the display, the browser started before the keymap (the fleet's order). The brief's two candidates do not hold: the published keymap HAS the shift level for letters ([a, A]; every SHIFTED_TABLE symbol on its base key) and `shift` rides every packet — Shift+a, Shift+1, Caps Lock + a, Shift held over letters and typeText('Ab1!') (with Shift held, and released before the commit) all type right. RED on base: 14 of 36 — every keystroke whose FLAGS disagree with its CHARACTER. keyActionFor names the lower-case keysym and leaves the level to the `shift` / `lock` flags, and X applies the US map's Linux rule (Shift undoes Lock on a letter; Lock alone capitalises): the Caps Lock FLAG over small letters (a Mac whose Caps Lock switches the input source) typed a ⇒ "A" and Shift+b ⇒ "b"; a Mac's Caps Lock + Shift + a ("A" on the Mac) ⇒ "a"; a French layout's Shift+& ("1") ⇒ "!" and & ⇒ "7". (Shift+1 under a Caps Lock flag stays "!" — a two-level key ignores Lock.)
  - HIS CAPTURED SHAPE (the composition road) was right on base too, on the real rung with Chrome's own IME machinery (Shift down → imeSetComposition → Shift up → insertText commits): the committed capital typed "A", a committed "Ab1!" typed "Ab1!" — ImeKeymap.plan presses by the character. So his exact trigger is not proven: what this lane closes is the class his keys can hit on the keydown road; a CJK method's own full-width symbols (Shift+1 ⇒ ！ in Chinese mode) are what his Mac typed.
- THE FIX (src/lib/xpra-proto.js, PURE `typedModifiers`): for a character on a two-level key of the published map `shift` = "the character sits on the shifted level" (an upper-case letter, a SHIFTED_TABLE name — ImeKeymap.plan's own rule for a composed character); `lock` is never sent and the Caps Lock key is not forwarded (keyActionFor ⇒ null), so X never applies a Caps Lock of its own on top of the machine's (a Mac fires Caps Lock's keyup only when it turns off); a chord (control / mod1 / mod4 / mod5) and a one-level key (Space, Enter, the keypad, F-keys) keep the flags as held (Shift+Space, Shift+←). Fixed tree: 36 of 36 (48 of 48 with the IME rows).

The check judges the patch below it through runtime-check's own seam, `VIBESPACE_RUNTIME_BASE=v22.23.3`, against a mirror serving other bytes. Expected: refused (sums-disagree) before the download (ONE request, its SHASUMS256.txt), nothing flipped, the update ends 0.

The helper's end `device_lost` (the default speaker went away / changed) ⇒ a fresh run, twice a minute at most; else the capture ends by name and the stats say `failed`.

A live switch the helper refuses ⇒ the same capture started again IN PLACE with `--audio` (the picture freezes a moment); a GONE restart asks `audio on` again. Measured twice: the node harness (a sanitizer stub keeping hrefs exactly where DOMPurify's own rule does) and the real sanitizer in chrome.

And the code-span relative rule's first character was `[\w@%+=.\-]` — JS `\w` is ASCII, so `标书研究/方案.md` stayed plain.

### lane agy-slash-guard-paths — an Antigravity message that starts with a path is sent; only agy's own closed list of slash commands is refused (the owner 2026-10-21 23:0xZ; base 72056f53 2.369.340)
- **Why:** in an Antigravity chat the owner attached a zip and typed a line; the chat answered «Error: /home was not sent: Antigravity answers its slash commands itself …». data/bin/agy-wrapper.js `slashRefused` refused every line matching `/^\/[A-Za-z]/` and named `t.match(/^\/[\w:-]+/)`; the composer's upload (`_insertUploadedPaths`) writes the file's absolute path first, so EVERY message with an attachment was refused, and so was any line that starts with a path or a "/"-word that is not agy's.
- **The base, measured** (the base wrapper over pipes, the fake agy; lane probe.mjs): `/model`, `/usage opus`, `/help` refused (right); `/home/u/x.zip 这里是…` refused as «/home» and `/tmp/a.txt` as «/tmp» (the owner's error); `/notacommand hello` refused as «/notacommand»; `~/x`, `./run.sh`, `/ 2`, `/2026` passed the guard — and the base FAKE ended its stream on `/ 2` (exit 2), because it modelled agy as "any line starting with /".
- **The closed list:** scripts/fixtures/antigravity-cli-1.4.3.json `slashInPrint.answeredWithoutATurn` — /usage /quota /credits /model /effort /skills /permissions /hooks /help /changelog /config (provenance 'changelog', the binary's own `agy changelog`); `stream.inputErrors` says such a command in the stream ends the session (exit 2).
- **The fix:** src/harnesses/antigravity-slash.js (NEW, PURE — no require, no import): `AGY_SLASH_COMMANDS` (frozen, the fixture's spelling) + `agySlashCommand(text)` = the first word up to whitespace, lower-cased, when it is on the list, else null. ONE definition: the wrapper requires it beside src/ (`require(path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'src', 'harnesses', 'antigravity-slash.js'))`, the claude-transport.js precedent — no wrapper is on HostManager.AGENT_TOOLS), src/harnesses/antigravity.js re-exports the same array. `slashRefused` asks it; its sentence is unchanged and names the command in the list's spelling. Not in src/adapters/agy.js and not the descriptor file itself: the wrapper would pull the ACP adapter / normalizer / accounts helpers into its process.

### lane layout-stale-record-sync — 工作's windows vanished from the owner's desktop after the phone woke, and 恢复布局 did not hold: a NAMELESS record the phone saved before its attaches answered, a desktop restore that built none of it, an 'unbuilt' drop the belt took (the owner 2026-10-22 00:18Z «我的工作桌面里的窗口怎么突然都没了», «我刚才点了恢复布局也没正确恢复»; URGENT, data-loss class; base 72056f53 2.369.340)
- **The evidence (read-only: data/layout-history shapes, telemetry events, the server journal — no window title quoted).** A point holds the state BEFORE the write that made it. 23:32:38Z 工作 = 5 windows, desktop-stamped, every chat with serverSessionId + backendSessionId. 23:37:09 the phone wrote 工作 with the SAME five ids but NAMELESS (no serverSessionId / backend / backendSessionId / claudeSessionId / cwd, `openSpec.backendSessionId` null; 研究 / 个人 written at 23:37:14 / :32 kept theirs) — the phone's page-load at 23:37:08 (after an 11 453 s ws outage), then `ws-lagged 5 MB` and sixteen `ws-reply-timeout:attach`, the first five exactly 工作's sessions. 00:16:52 the journal: the Mac dialed in (woke); the Mac page reloaded at 00:16:47 (page-session-end 38 475 s), open-windows 0 at 00:17:17, 研究's eight built at 00:17:29; 00:17:31.509 the write 工作 5 → 0. 00:18:04 the restore of the 00:17:31 point (the nameless five); the Windows page booted at 00:18:05; 00:19:05 6 → 1 (its first save after opening a chat). 00:23:04 the phone's write, identities back — why reopening on the phone fixed it. No `[layout-sync] REFUSED` line all evening.
- **Not a stale record.** The 23:37:09 record was the newest when written; nothing older replaced anything newer. The brief's staleness gate ships as the belt it asked for (below); the three roads are:
- **Road 1 — the write (the phone, 23:37:09):** a chat window has no `app.sessions` entry until its attach answers ('attached'), and `restoreState`'s alive branch called `attachSession(alive.id, …)` WITHOUT the conversation id (`openSpec.backendSessionId: null`), so `captureWin` (src/lib/layout.js) wrote neither id; `mergeDesktopRecord` takes a page's capture WHOLE in the record's place — the save the phone made 1 s after its reload replaced five named entries with nameless ones.
- **Road 2 — the read (the woken desktop, 00:16:52):** `restoreState` matched a chat by backendSessionId (window or openSpec) or serverSessionId only; a nameless entry matched nothing and NO branch built it (its `openSpec.serverId` — a live session — was never read). desktop-manager.js `loadFromServer` then noted the five as build attempts.
- **Road 3 — the belt (00:17:31, 00:19:05):** 20 s later (`BUILD_GRACE_MS`) `recordFor` dropped them as 'unbuilt' evidence; the owner's switch to 研究 sent 工作 = [] and `shrinkVerdict` counted 'unbuilt' as an explanation although every session was alive. 恢复布局 restored the newest pre-loss point — the nameless one — and the Windows page that booted on it repeated roads 2 and 3 (6 → 1: only the window that was named stayed).
- **The fix (ONE commit):** (1) IDENTITY IS NEVER FORGOTTEN — PURE `keepIdentity` / `keepIdentities` / `sessionOf` (src/lib/desktop-record.js) in `mergeDesktopRecord` and in ws-handler's write (in place: the relay carries it); `restoreState` passes the conversation id to the attach (chat + terminal). (2) A NAMELESS ENTRY IS FOUND by the session its openSpec attaches to (`restoreState`). (3) A PAGE'S FAILURE IS NOT THE TRUTH — `shrinkVerdict`: 'unbuilt' explains no window whose session is alive unless another entry shows that session; refused at any count (`live`), the journal says «N LIVE (the sender could not build them)»; the refusal hands the record back, the page forgets the failed attempts and builds them. (4) THE STALENESS GATE (§6b guard 11) — every layout-sync names `base` (desktop-manager `stampOf`: the boot read, a relay, the ack, a refusal's record); ws-handler refuses `stale` a write whose base is older than the newest record ANOTHER writer stored (PURE `staleVerdict` / `foreignStamp` over a per-desktop write memory, so a writer's own unacked write never counts), before the shrink belt; the ack and the relay carry `updatedAt`; layout.js never applies a record older than the newest applied for its desktop (`behindStamp`, layout-model.js; `_appliedStamps` survives reconnects). (5) A RESTORE OUTRANKS EVERY LIVE CLIENT — routes/persistence.js stamps every restored record max(now, replaced + 1). (6) THE RING NAMES WHAT IT SAW — `writeLayouts.note` (a property: the ws ctx contract is untouched) gives the next point `writer` {desktop, viewport, evidence by reason, base} and `refused` [stale / shrink / cross-layer].
- **Pins moved (each because its line changed):** test-desktop-record §6 the two `_doAutoSave` sends + the ack (`base` / `updatedAt`), the rollback-point pin (`snapshotLayout(…, { writer, refused })`, `change, ...seen`), §7 belt-blind's find and switch-no-evidence's find; test-layout-model ⑥ the import line. Unchanged on purpose: ws-handler's `autoSave = { ...data.state, updatedAt: Date.now() }`, `state: data.state,`, the belt call, `writeLayouts(layoutData);` before the broadcast, the first desktop-record require line (a second require line carries the new names).
- **Measured:** see the lane report (/var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/layout-stale-record-sync/report.md) for every count; RED controls — the 2.369.340 belt ('unbuilt' explains a live window) takes the woken desktop's 工作 to 0 through real pages; the 2.369.340 merge and write keep the nameless capture; no stale gate lets the slept phone's old copy land over the restore (in-process and on two chromes); the 2.369.340 `restoreState` builds none of a nameless five and attaches without the conversation id; a page that applies older records lands 3000 over 5000.
- **Left by name:** loadPreset's matching (named presets) still reads backendSessionId / serverSessionId only — not on the incident's road; a nameless entry whose session is GONE and that has no conversation id cannot be rebuilt by any page (the ring kept the named point at 23:32 — a restore of it would). No new UI words.

### gate red — the 2.369.340 master mirror run (Actions run 39684300709) red on ONE fast suite: test-channel-api ⑨ «CONTROL (the base)» (lane channel-api-control-race; base 72056f53 = 2.369.340)
- **The red:** `✗ CONTROL (the base): the command printed the outcome AND a receipt message for it was filed — {"out": … "outcome": "pending" …, "receipts": 0}` — 185 passed, 35.9 s (≈ 6 s green), fast lane 2 at load 4.4. Green on this box and on every other .338–.340 run; nothing in .340 touched the road (`git diff fd843910 72056f53` over the CLI, the cards, the orchestrator, the agent routes, the policy, the suite and its helpers = empty).
- **The shape (a clock in the leg; the product is right):** `approveSoon(300)` approved «whatever is pending 300 ms after the spawn». On the loaded runner the base copy of the CLI had not filed its proposal by then ⇒ nothing was approved ⇒ it waited out its `--timeout 30` and printed `pending` with no receipt (the 35.9 s IS that wait). Reproduced here byte for byte with a one-shot 600 ms start stall of the channels CLI only (`NODE_OPTIONS=--require` a stall, matched on the CLI's path): the same line + leg A red too (3 ✗, 37.4 s). A second, latent race in leg C: «the user decided inside the 1 s window» was a wall-clock bet from the CLI's last poll to the approve — a 1.2 s stall at the CLI's exit ⇒ `heldNow: 1` (1 ✗).
- **The fix (scripts/test-channel-api.mjs ⑨ only — no product change):** the user approves once the command is WAITING (`approveWhenWaiting`: its first poll arrived; bounded 15 s, and a run-out prints what it saw — posts, polls, the proposals); the receipts are judged after the cards' own serialized `sync()` (the three fixed 150 ms `settle`s are gone — `approve()` resolves after the run is stored and its sync is queued); leg C holds the cards' clock (the product's `now` seam) at the CLI's last poll while the decision lands, then waits for the fallback's receipt as an effect (bounded) instead of a fixed 1 300 ms. Under every stall (start 0.6 / 3 s, exit 1.2 / 3 s, both 3 s): green. The control keeps its purpose — with the inline road reverted in a scratch copy (the CLI's two collect points dropped) legs A/B/C go RED (7 ✗) and the control still shows the base road's receipt.
- **Measured:** 10× alone: 186 each (6.1–6.2 s); 5× beside test-desktop-webrtc-chrome (127) + test-channels-aggregate-ui (223) looping, load 4.1–4.5: 186 each; 5× confined to 2 CPUs shared with 4 busy loops (taskset): 186 each (7.3–8.1 s). None of this box's load shapes turned the BASE red (base ×5 in the 2-CPU shape: green, 8.3–8.9 s) — the one-shot stalls are what reproduce the runner, and the fix stays green under each of them.
- **Left by name (order-free, not races):** ⑤'s refresh row: the stub vendor's `/token` answers after 30 ms, holding one refresh in flight for five concurrent calls (a refreshed token is cached, so a late caller never refreshes again); ④ `api wait` is approved at 300 ms on a proposal that exists before the wait starts — an approval before or after its first poll prints the same outcome.

### lane cli-2-1-306-records — the record oracle is pinned to claude 2.1.306: the records that build added are known, and the permission sentence it moved is read again (backlog B-42ed; base c1aba74c 2.369.337)
- **Why:** npm's latest claude CLI is 2.1.306 (measured 2026-10-21) while the oracle was pinned up to 2.1.296. Every instance whose CLI auto-updated showed the red "New fields on a known record" card for records the oracle had not seen, and the Actions mirror's §4d went informational (B-42ed: «new sentence Pz, moved name Dx (Gd)»). The hub's CLI stays 2.1.296.
- **The dump, STATIC:** `npm install --prefix <lane>/npm @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.306 --no-save --ignore-scripts` (the registry download is the lane's only network; never on PATH, never run as a session). The binary is `<prefix>/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64/claude` (the native ELF; `claude-code/bin/claude.exe` is a 500-byte launcher). `node scripts/claude-cli-dump.mjs <it> scripts/fixtures/claude-cli/2.1.296.json` → scripts/fixtures/claude-cli/2.1.306.json: union 177 shapes (2.1.296: 175), helpers u/A, 63 system subtypes and 35 stream record types, the 2.1.296 sets exactly.
- **The zod diff 2.1.296 → 2.1.306:**
  - No new subtype and no new stream record type, so no SHAPE_SINCE row and no list decision.
  - **21 new fields on eight declared shapes:** user 1, assistant 2, result 12 (result/success carries 11 of them, the error branch interrupted_by_shutdown), system/init 2, informational 1, turn_handoff_available 1, ui_invalidate 1, command_lifecycle 1.
  - **Two new zod keys,** workflow_agent and workflow_phase.
  - **Five non-record keys changed and are not judged:** the first-spelled `http` is now the HTTP hook config; sdk / sse / stdio are MCP server configs; parts is the Read tool's PDF parts.
  - **The permission sentences:** the same 14, under new names (anchor ep, list wp, set Ur).
- **FIELDS_306 (src/record-shape.js):** all 21 are `ignored`, each with the dump's own `.describe()` sense. A grep of src/, server.js and data/bin found no reader.
  - The nine `process_*` fields are memory / CPU telemetry sent only by a worker Anthropic hosts.
  - api_error_origin (assistant + result) is first_party only from Anthropic's own API.
  - interrupted_by_shutdown is a multi-tenant worker host's shutdown; handoff_intake_phases_ms is cloud handoff latency.
  - text_not_typed means a server or an app composed the user message.
  - assistant.refused_message_id (2.1.296 put it on the user re-ask).
  - init.original_cwd / additional_directories: the server reads init.cwd only.
  - informational.prompt_submit_outcome: a hook-ended prompt; the dim card shows the line's own content.
  - shared_message_id (handoff staging), ui_invalidate.prompts_screened (the plugin UI host, no UI surface channel attached), command_lifecycle.ran_ahead (the VS Code panel only).
- **WORKFLOW_PROGRESS_ITEMS:** the two new keys are the entries of task_progress.workflow_progress (CORPUS_KNOWN, the live Workflow card), which 2.1.306 now PARSES through a `type`-discriminated union. 2.1.296 built the same items with no schema. They have no uuid / session_id, so they are not stream records. Both are `known`: message-manager normalizeWorkflowProgress and routes/sessions normalizeWorkflowSnapshot read them, and every field the two read is declared by the literal.
- **THE MOVED NAME (scripts/claude-cli-dump.mjs):** the Dx row's sentence ("…To tell you how to proceed, the user said:") is 2.1.306's `D0`, still on the tool_result list.
  - **What changed in the bundle:** the members before it moved to another chunk, so its template literal now OPENS its line, and its own newline ends it. Its closing backtick and the next member (`n2=`) begin the next line.
  - **Why the extractor missed it:** it resolved a name only on a strings line that declares another member. D0's line declares none, so D0 went unresolved and the Dx row read as a GHOST.
  - **The fix:** a template still open at its line's end is judged on its whole declaration, through the line its closing backtick is on (≤ 4 KB on). Its VALUE still ends at its line, because the rows are prefixes.

  - PERMISSION_OUTCOME_CLI_VERSION → 2.1.306, no `until`.
  - B-42ed's «new sentence Pz» was on the mirror's own build (not kept); 2.1.306 has no unclassified sentence.

### lane oat-in-file-2-1-306 — the long-lived token in a pool member's file is granted on 2.1.306 too: the fixture holds ONE record per measured version, and a new measurement ADDS its record and never drops one
- **Why.** `cliCaps.oatInFile(version, fixture)` grants the token in a member's credential file only on the EXACT CLI version the fixture measured, and scripts/fixtures/oat-in-file.json held one record (2.1.296, 2026-10-14). So on a 2.1.306 CLI every oat-only pool member was escaped as unmeasured: no token written to its folder, no new placement on it, the spawn on the env road. That is a follow-up named by lane cli-2-1-306-records.
- **The measurement (主开发's rung, 2026-10-21 17:55–18:02Z).** `scripts/measure-claude-cred-read.mjs --variant oat --write-fixture` ran inside the loopback-only namespace with the strace watchdog, against the 2.1.306 linux-x64 ELF that lane downloaded (sha256 520bc6c1f40af466…). The verdicts are IDENTICAL to 2.1.296's: oat-file PASS, oat-env FAIL, oat-file-401 PASS, oat-file-near PASS, oat-file-switch PASS, oat-file-scopes FAIL. The notes say the same too. This lane ran no measurement, no real claude, no namespace and no sudo.
- **The shape: `{versions: {'<exact version>': <record>}}`.** Each record is exactly the one-version file's object (cliVersion, measuredAt, script, netns, variants), keyed by its own cliVersion.
  - **Why one file rather than one per version:** the store keeps reading ONE file (accounts.js `_oatFixture`, its read census unchanged), and the writer keeps one path.
  - The 2.1.296 record is the old file's object, unchanged. test-cli-caps ⑥ pins the sha256 of its JSON.
  - The committed file was produced with the writer's own rule, `withMeasured(the old file, the 2.1.306 record)`.
- **src/cli-caps.js (PURE).**
  - `oatInFile` reads the record keyed by the exact version. A key whose record names another version, a key in `--version` words, an inherited entry, or a versions value that is not a map grants nothing.
  - A bare record still reads as the fixture of its one version: an older `--fixture` scratch file, and the suites' own fixtures.
  - `measuredVersions(fixture)` lists the versions, oldest first. The store's `oatFileCaps().measured` is now `'2.1.296, 2.1.306'`, the words oat-file-sync's log says beside an unmeasured CLI.
  - `withMeasured(fixture, record)` is THE WRITER'S ONE RULE. It adds the record under its exact version and keeps every other entry as it was (even one that is not a full record, and other top-level keys). Re-measuring a version replaces only that version's record. The map is written oldest first and the input is never touched.
  - `withMeasured` throws on a record naming no exact version, and on a fixture that is neither shape: rewriting it could drop what it holds.
- **The writer changed.** In scripts/measure-claude-cred-read.mjs, `--write-fixture` wrote this run's record ALONE, which would have dropped 2.1.296. It now:
  - checks `withMeasured` over the file BEFORE the run and refuses (exit 2, no variant run) when it could not add;
  - re-reads the file at write time;
  - writes `withMeasured(the file now, this run's record)`;
  - logs `it holds 2.1.296, 2.1.306, …`.
- **The readers.** Every one goes through `accounts.oatFileCaps()`, so 2.1.306 now behaves as 2.1.296 everywhere:
  - `_placeable` (no escape);
  - the pool's `oat-cli-unmeasured` refusal;
  - `_syncOatFileNow`, which writes or takes back the file;
  - `resolveForSpawn`, which reads the file, not CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN;
  - the row's door (`written · CLI 2.1.306`);
  - oat-file-sync.
  - The client's words take `{cli}`. data/bin has no reader. Nothing else changes.
- **Tests.**
  - **test-cli-caps: 84** (base 52).
    - ② The map legs: each version true, 2.1.300 / 2.1.307 / 2.1.306-dev.1 false, a FAIL in one record leaks nothing into the other, the key-vs-record, inherited and array cases.
    - ②b The writer's rule: from no file, from the bare file, add-never-drop, the order, untouched input, re-measure, the refusals, `measuredVersions`. RED CONTROL: the base writer (this run's record alone) drops 2.1.296.
    - ③ RED CONTROL: the one-version reader (the base) grants the two-version file nothing; plus the own-entry mutant.
    - ④ The writer ADDS through `withMeasured` and refuses before the run.
    - ⑥ The committed file: the two versions, the pinned 2.1.296 record, the 2.1.306 verdicts equal to 2.1.296's, 2.1.300 false, no path / machine / person.
  - **test-oat-measure-fake (heavy, strace, the FAKE claude only): 20** (base 17).
    - The fresh file is `{versions: {'9.9.9': …}}`.
    - Over a COPY of the committed fixture, 9.9.9 is ADDED and 2.1.296 + 2.1.306 are kept byte-for-byte.
    - A junk `--fixture` is REFUSED before the run and left as it was.
  - **test-oat-materialize: 178** (base 176). The hub on 2.1.306 gets the archive, the file, the door `written · CLI 2.1.306` and the spawn from the file. RED CONTROL: over the base's one-version file, the same 2.1.306 is `cli-unmeasured`.
  - **test-account-pool: 87** (base 84). Back from 2.1.300 to 2.1.306, the oat-only member is a pool candidate again and the pool dir resolves through to its token file. RED CONTROL: the base's one-version fixture escapes it.
  - **Unchanged:** test-oat-identity 305 (it stubs the caps).
- **What the owner gains.** Updating the hub's claude to 2.1.306 no longer takes the token files back from oat-only pool members. The pool keeps placing on them as on 2.1.296. The hub's CLI stays 2.1.296; this lane is only the measurement's record.

### lane incident-paint-gap — a paint gap on an idle desktop is not a freeze: a gap is jank only with a busy main thread or a person there; an unpainted gap is a `paint-gap-s` metric, never an auto incident
- **The report (2026-10-21).** The auto incident recorder filed two «jank storm» incidents on the owner's Windows desktop that were no jank: inc-mvi50qdh-ygmh (13:18Z «9.1 s») and inc-mvi5ggqh-1tz8 (13:30Z «620.8 s — worst frame 620 780 ms»), 2.369.336 client, Windows Chrome.
- **The bundles (measured).** longTasks: two, 690 ms / 306 ms, both minutes before the storms. frameGaps: 9 144 ms, 71 266 ms, 620 780 ms and smaller. compStalls: 9.9 / 3.1 / 6.7 / 6.7 / 71.7 / 6.4 s — the SAME gaps, seen by the compositor-stall arm. screenEvents empty; visibility 'visible'; ws connected; the action ring's last input 13:16:55Z (a pointer on the chat input), nothing during the gaps.
- **The cause.** The main thread was never blocked (no long task near 9 s, let alone 620 s; the 1 s timer kept ticking — that is how the "storm" was measured). rAF stopped because the window was not PAINTING — an idle Windows desktop (monitor off / lock screen / an occluded window; Chrome keeps `visibilityState` 'visible' on a lock screen, so neither the hidden gate nor the tab-return filter caught it). `jankStormVerdict` summed the one 620 s paint gap as «slow frames», `onRendererFreeze` (≥ 5 s) filed the incident, and the compositor-stall arm pushed a stall for the same gap.
- **The fix (src/lib/telemetry-client.js).** New PURE `paintGapKind({t, gap}, {longTasks, inputs})` → `jank` (a long task overlaps ≥ half the gap, or a pointer/key during it or within 1 s after) | `unpainted`. `jankStormVerdict` counts only `jank` gaps. The compositor-stall arm files its «compositor stall» incident only for a `jank` gap (person present — the GPU/RTX-5090 case it was built for, RED control kept) and otherwise writes a `paint-gap-s` metric + a `paint-gap` event — never an incident. `installInputStamp` (pointerdown/keydown) is the "a person was there" stamp ring (`recentInputs`); `installScreenWatch` now also records window `focus`/`blur`, Page-Lifecycle `freeze`/`resume` and the Idle Detection verdict when the permission is already held (never a new prompt), stamped into `screenEvents`. incident-recorder.js is unchanged — its snapshot already carries `screenEvents`.
- **The two incidents re-judged.** Both `unpainted` (620 s / 9 s gaps, the long tasks 690/306 ms minutes away, no input) ⇒ no storm, no auto incident — a `paint-gap-s` metric and a ring line instead. A 9 s gap with a 9 s long task ⇒ `jank`; a 6 s gap with a key 300 ms after ⇒ `jank`; a 71 s compositor stall with no input ⇒ `unpainted`.
- **Gate.** test-freeze-probe (PURE + wiring, 48 legs — the base verdict that counts every slow frame files both incidents as the RED control). No new i18n (telemetry-client has no UI strings). CHANGELOG ×3 + docs/kb-bugfix-invariants.md (index + essay) + docs/kb-features.md + docs/kb-file-structure.md, same commit. No version bump — integrated, signed and cut by 主开发.

### lane vault-chip-zone-errors — two uncaught client errors at every start, found and fixed at their causes; the console ring keeps the stack and an offline tool names the line (incidents inc-mvi50qdh-ygmh / inc-mvi5ggqh-1tz8, 2.369.336 client, Windows Chrome, 2026-10-21 13:12–13:13Z)
- **What the bundles said.** The page loaded at 13:12:54Z. Its console ring then held `unhandled: Failed to execute 'insertBefore' on 'Node': The node before which the new node is to be inserted is not a child of this node.` twice (at load and at +5 s), then `uncaught: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` twice, 4 ms apart, from `bundle.js?v=…:1`. The minified bundle is one line, so `:1` named nothing.
- **Error 1 — the lock chip, `src/lib/vault-unlock.js:76` on the base.** `drawChip` did `host.insertBefore(chip, document.getElementById(beforeId) || null)` with host `#taskbar-tray` and the For-you button found document-wide.
  - The owner's synced `chrome.arrangement` (read-only, chrome keys only) has For-you in `toolbar-row2` between springs, and `taskbar-tray: []`. The bundle agrees: the For-you press was at y = 67 of a 1100 px viewport, the second toolbar row.
  - So the reference was not a child of the host, and the insert threw at every apply of the vault's facts. The two `unhandled` entries are `maybeNagVault` (the onboarding check) and `initVault`'s boot read, each reaching `applyVaultFacts`. A scratch hub with the owner's shape reproduced both, with these frames.
  - The throw stopped `drawLockStrip`, `drawGearMark`, the facts listeners and `onVaultState`'s `showUnlock`. So on the owner's desktop a locked vault showed NOTHING at start: no dialog, no strip, no ⚙ mark, no chip. The owner reached the dialog through the For-you item 12 s later.
- **Error 2 — the incident recorder, `src/lib/chat-enter-keys.js:76` on the base** (called from `src/lib/incident-recorder.js:55`). `actionKeyWords(e)` read `e.key.length`.
  - Chrome's autofill and saved passwords dispatch a bare `Event('keydown')` with no `key` on each field they fill, then input, change and a bare keyup. Measured through CDP `Autofill.trigger` on a card form: one keyless keydown per filled field.
  - The action ring fits this. It shows `C-Control`/`S-Shift`-shaped words, a modifier up and a fourth key, and no «typing» marker at all, so no character was typed into the dialog. Two fields were filled at once: two throws, 4 ms apart.
  - Right after the unlock, the owner triple-clicked the sidebar's session filter and pressed one key. That reads as clearing a user name the password manager put there (formless inputs are one synthetic form for it). This is inferred, not shipped: see the report.
  - The brief's suspect, «a renderer reading a missing list after the unlock broadcast», was not it: the throws came 0.7 s BEFORE the Unlock press.
- **The fix.**
  - `customize-mode.js` `slotBeside(id, fallback)`: the slot beside a movable chrome element is its OWN parent (the zone applyArrangement put it in) before it, else the fallback's end. The reference is always a child. `drawChip` uses it for both pairs (the taskbar and the phone nav), and app.js re-seats the chip after every arrangement (`placeVaultChip`), so it follows For-you when Customize moves it.
  - `applyVaultFacts` draws each lock sign under its own try (a `[vault]` console.error), so one sign's throw never takes the others or the dialog.
  - `actionKeyWords` answers a keydown with no string `key` as `{ key: '(fill)' }` (FILL_KEY) — the ring says a fill happened, never what (`keyMatches` already had this guard).
- **The ring keeps the stack.**
  - `src/lib/incident-stack.js` (PURE) `stackHead(err, origin)`: the first 3 `at` frames, the origin cut, the bundle's `line:column` kept, whole frames only, ≤ 400 chars. A frame too long for the room keeps its location and loses its name.
  - The recorder spreads it onto `uncaught` (`e.error`) and `unhandled` (`e.reason`) entries.
  - A full console ring of worst-case entries is 224 KB in bundle.json (+79 KB for the stacks), against the hub's 50 MB body cap (`express.json`). Measured by test-incident-recorder ③.
- **The map, served to nobody.**
  - `src/server/static-public.js`: express.static for every path but `*.map`, judged decoded (`%2E` is a dot). Such a path falls through to the later routes and ends in a 404. WebDAV and proxy `.map` paths are untouched. server.js keeps one line, at the bootstrap-size cap.
  - `scripts/symbolicate.mjs <bundle.json>` maps the ring's frames OFFLINE. The map is NEVER a file (主开发's ruling: the product keeps no map on disk; the build line is unchanged). It is rebuilt in memory (0.3–0.8 s) with the client esbuild step's flags PARSED off package.json's build script at run time — never a copied list; test-incident-recorder's census pins parsed == the script's — and refused unless the JS equals public/bundle.js byte for byte. A frame whose `?v=` is another build is refused (`--any-build` maps it anyway).
  - The `source-map` package is not in node_modules, so a 40-line base64-VLQ decoder is in the script.
- **Tests.**
  - test-vault-chrome Z: the chip before For-you on a default chrome and on the owner's shape, at a load and live as Customize moves it (row 2 → the right zone → the default). The dialog, strip and ⚙ mark show at that load, and the phone pair is placed the same way. A two-field bare-Event fill and the REAL `Autofill.trigger` path throw nothing; the captured ring says `(fill)`; the unlock + 6 s throws nothing. Every page exception is captured with CDP `Runtime.exceptionThrown`.
  - test-vault-chrome Z-RED: a patched bundle with the pre-fix chip and key words throws both errors. The ring keeps both stacks, and symbolicate names `src/lib/vault-unlock.js` (the insert) and `src/lib/chat-enter-keys.js` (the `.length`) from the real capture.
  - test-chat-enter-ime §2c (+ control).
  - test-incident-recorder (new, fast).
  - test-csp-report ⑨: the map in public/ answers 404 on every spelling; MUTANT: the guard cut serves it.

### lane job-wrapper-proto1-retire — the job wrapper's protocol-1 compat is removed as scheduled: a ≤ .330 server's spec on the command line is never read again (the expiry test-job-model set at .333 — lane job-wrapper-update-window, agent feedback fb-7f7be1e24e; base 609993e2 = int340 on the 2.369.339 cut)
- **What was due.** .333 kept a second door in data/bin/job-wrapper.js. A ≤ .330 server put the job's spec — argv, cwd and env, the job's secrets — on the wrapper's command line as base64 JSON (protocol 1), and the wrapper READ it, loudly, for an update's window (`COMPAT_PROTO_1` + `argvSpec()` + a warning line). Its expiry was 2.369.340: test-job-model went RED there while the flag was live, which int340's scratch .340 bump showed.
- **Why retire rather than move the date.** Every hub of the fleet is ≥ .331 (主开发's reading for this lane; the owner's 18 instances were measured ≥ .318 on 2026-10-15 and update through the product). A ≤ .330 server spawning a .340 wrapper is a hub that skipped nine releases in the middle of an update.
- **The wrapper.** COMPAT_PROTO_1, argvSpec and the warning line are gone.
  - An argument that is no file of the ctl dir, with no `--proto=`, is judged by its SHAPE only: base64 of a JSON object (`eyJ…`, a length that is a multiple of 4) = a ≤ .330 caller.
  - That run ends «[job-wrapper] not started: the server spoke protocol 1 (a server older than 2.369.331) — this wrapper speaks 2; an update in flight, or a server not restarted after one»: exit 75, exit.json reason update_window with proto {server 1, wrapper 2}. That is the road a protocol-3 spec takes.
  - The argument is never decoded, never echoed and never written; the ctl dir holds only the run's pid.json, exit.json and current.log.
  - Any other shape keeps «the spec path names no file of the ctl dir» (exit 2).
- **Who judges that end — measured with the REAL 2.369.330 engine (a scratch worktree at the .330 release) over this wrapper.**
  - Its 5 s sweep usually runs before its restart in a 45 s window. That engine predates update_window: it reads exit 75 as an error and files the run failed — «failed exit=75 error» to the agent, «Task …: failed (error)» to For you. That is fb-7f7be1e24e's false failure, now worded «not started … an update in flight» in the job's log. A cron child's next fire runs it.
  - When the restart comes first, this tree's engine judges the exit.json at boot: update_window (the run started before its boot), interrupted, no failure notice, and the one-shot task runs again (update-rerun → done, exit 0).
  - The .333 essay listed this residual («its old server says failed (once)»). An old server cannot be taught; the false failure stays possible only on a hub that skipped nine releases, and the fleet has none.
- **Tests.**
  - test-job-model: the expiry row is now the PIN of the removal — the wrapper's code holds no COMPAT_PROTO_1, no argvSpec, no base64 decode and no atob (its header records the removal in words). CONTROL: the ≤ .339 compat patched back whole, the flag alone, and one decode in the branch are each RED.
  - test-jobs-engine §12: the .330 call on the REAL wrapper, with a canary in the spec's env, gets exit 75, update_window (1 → 2). Its stderr and log are exactly the named line. No byte of the spec (the canary, its name, any 16 chars of the argument) is on stderr or in the ctl dir. NEGATIVE CONTROL: the read patched back in runs the job with the canary.
  - test-jobs-engine §12 M1 (the spec on argv again) now ends «not started» too. Its cmdline rows read the wrapper's own /proc/self through the front script, because the wrapper is gone by then.
  - test-agent-output-sinks §3: the .330 call is not run, and no word of the job reaches the log.
  - The new tests over the base wrapper are RED at each of those rows.
- Gates: the fast gate on a scratch copy bumped to .340 (never committed: package.json, package-lock.json, src/agentd/version.js and release/agentd/manifest.json stay .339) + test-job-model ×3, test-jobs-engine, test-agent-output-sinks, test-jobs-browser, test-record-clear-census and test-architecture (the lane report has the counts). No version bump — integrated, signed and cut by 主开发.

## 2.369.339 — 2026-10-21

### lane werift-lite-multihomed — a desktop stream stayed black once the viewer's browser was allowed the microphone on a multi-homed computer: werift wrote a=ice-lite where no browser reads it, and kept its FIRST nomination for good (backlog B-c7d7, found by lane stream-mic-road 2026-10-21; base c1aba74c = 2.369.337)
- THE MEASUREMENT (the base, this box — 6 adapters: two LAN addresses, two docker bridges, the tailnet v4/v6; headless Chrome, the real bundle): granted `audioCapture` (CDP `Browser.grantPermissions` — a person who pressed 「麦克风」 once), Chrome offered 6 host addresses (+ 6 TCP) instead of ONE mDNS name. ICE reached `connected`, DTLS stayed `connecting`, the selected pair changed 10× in 30 s, no picture (the view's ICE restarts at 15 s and 30 s changed nothing). A probe hooked into a bundle copy logged werift's checks: the FIRST check it received already carried USE-CANDIDATE — Chrome's docker-bridge candidate → werift's LAN-candidate socket — and werift took it as THE pair (`checkComplete` sets `nominated` only while none is). werift's sockets are wildcard-bound: its answer to that peer leaves with the source address the route picks (the bridge's, not the LAN address Chrome checked), so Chrome never matched it — the pair never validated on Chrome's side — and werift's DTLS went there for ever. Chrome's selected pair (bridge ↔ bridge) sent ClientHello retransmits (1463 B) and received 0 B.
- THE ROOT CAUSE: werift 0.25.0 writes `a=ice-lite` only inside each MEDIA section (its session never writes it). RFC 8839 §5.3 makes it a SESSION-level attribute and Chrome reads it only there — its own copy of the offer (`pc.remoteDescription.sdp`) has no a=ice-lite at all. Taking the agent for a FULL agent, Chrome nominates semi-aggressively (USE-CANDIDATE on its first checks, before any pair is valid). With one mDNS socket the first nominated pair happened to be the working one; with six adapters it was a cross-interface pair. A page-side experiment that ONLY moved the line to the session level played in 526 ms (3 of 3). The mic lane's hub-side filter of the browser's host candidates could not help: werift learns the same addresses as peer-reflexive from the checks.
- THE LATENT SECOND HALF (measured with the attribute fixed): Chrome then nominates only its selected, VALIDATED pair — and ~0.4 s later RENOMINATES another as more pairs pass; werift ignored it. It played only because Chrome still accepts packets on the old connection (504 KB arrived on the abandoned pair, 0 B on the selected one).
- THE FIX (the device; kind (a) for the pairs — werift's own option — plus the attribute where RFC 8839 puts it): `liteSessionSdp` (src/stream-model.js, PURE) = the offer's SDP with ONE `a=ice-lite` before the first m= (the media copies dropped), on the first offer and every ICE-restart offer. `followChoice` (src/agentd/stream-host.js) on werift's `iceFilterStunResponse` hook (asked before werift answers a check — always true, every check is answered): a USE-CANDIDATE check under THIS generation's ufrag moves the sending pair (`connection.nominated`) to the pair werift just took, a microtask later; the agent's log says «the browser moved its pair: …». No werift patch file: the tree has no patch mechanism and package.json is not this lane's to change; the hook is werift's public option. No hub-side candidate filter, no pinned address.
- THE STRIP — NEVER SILENT before a picture (src/lib/machine-desktop.js): when the view's connect budget (STREAM_LIMITS.connectMs, 15 s) runs out and it asks an ICE restart (streamStep code `timeout`), the strip says leg ⑥'s words 「串流中断：没能及时连上——正在重新连接…」 until a picture plays (one stream; a ② pane through its own `said`). Before: 「串流 · 连接中…」 for the whole restart budget, 45 s, then the VNC picture. No new words: with the fix there is no multi-homed failure left to name, so no 「多网卡：…」 line.
- THE NUMBERS (this box, 10 runs each, open → playing): the default origin (one mDNS name) 527 ms median (523–530) on the base, 426 ms (424–535) fixed; the microphone allowed: never on the base (0 of 3 within 10 s, 0 of 2 within 30 s), 527 ms (524–528, 10 of 10) fixed.
- THE GATES: test-desktop-webrtc-chrome ⑲ (the lane's ⑰ — renumbered at int339, lane stream-mic-road's ⑰ / ⑱ came first) — the real grant: 6 host addresses, it plays, the browser's copy of the offer says a=ice-lite at the session level, the picture arrives on the browser's selected pair; RED CONTROL = the bundle copy as werift alone runs it ⇒ black for 8 s, DTLS connecting (judged where the browser offers ≥ 2 addresses — a one-address runner says so); the mDNS road plays both ways; an agent that answers no check ⇒ the strip's words at 15 s, RED CONTROL = the pre-lane window silent. test-desktop-webrtc §15 (fast, deterministic on any box): two raw sockets nominate in turn against the REAL host + werift — its DTLS retransmits follow to the second, RED CONTROL the werift-alone copy keeps the first; a nomination of an older ICE generation moves nothing, RED CONTROL without the guard.

### lane stream-mic-road — the viewer's microphone reaches a paired machine's apps through a virtual microphone (backlog B-7af0; the product step after lane stream-mic-wheel-probe; base c1aba74c = 2.369.337)
- THE PREMISE, MEASURED FIRST: the brief named «the existing audio m-line» and «beside 「声音」». On c1aba74c the desktop stream had neither — src/agentd/stream-host.js offered ONE video transceiver (sendonly) + the `input` data channel, src/lib/stream-view.js answered video only, B-aec9 (speaker passthrough) is still parked, and the intercom (the voice on the machine's speakers) existed only in the probe's rig (mic-road.mjs offered its own sendrecv m-line). 主开发 confirmed the reading (16:12Z): the m-line is built HERE, offered only on the page's ask; 「麦克风」 is the strip's first audio control; the speakers road is built here as the same renderer; separate helpers per OS.
