### lane reply-infer-owner-between — the judged plain-reply road is TOLD what the chat's owner wrote between the send and the reply (agent feedback fb-377439b167 from a fleet instance on .334; base c1aba74c = 2.369.337)
- THE INCIDENT (the agent's own words, 2026-10-21): a peer's plain two-word message at 09:04Z was judged (0.90) an answer to the agent's send of 01:43Z. But the person who owns the chat had sent a voice note ([audio], untranscribed) at 09:01Z, between the two, and the peer was answering THAT. The agent was woken for nothing.
- WHY: `PLANS['reply-infer']` gave the judge only `sent`, `reply` and `gap` («never another message of the conversation — cost»). The fact that decided it, the owner's voice note 3 min before, sat in the engine's own thread index for free and was never passed.
- PURE (src/channel-filter.js):
  - `inferBetween(record, sent, ctx)` reads `ctx.turnsBetween(sentAt, at)` and returns `between {own, ownLast {kind, minBefore}, others, capped}`, now carried on `inferCandidate`'s answer. It keeps only turns strictly between the two instants, at most the newest `INFER.between` = 5. No reader, or a reader that cannot read, gives `null`, and the judge works as before.
  - `turnKindOf`: a voice note (an audio attachment or the vendor's `[audio]` token), else words, else a picture, else a file.
  - `inferBetweenLine` words the fact in FIXED words: counts, a kind and minutes, never anybody's words. «Nobody else wrote between sent and reply.» when the list is empty; «In the last 5 messages before the reply, …» when capped.
- THE JUDGE (src/decision-model.js):
  - `PART('between', 300, { kind: 'line' })`, last in the record.
  - `recordCeiling` 700 → **804** (+104 = estTokens of «between: » + 300 characters + the newline = 310 ASCII / 3). Every part at its cap now fits whole; at 700 the same record would be cut.
  - `REPLY_INFER_VERSION` 2: the question reads `between`, and a reply that follows the owner's own message more closely «is more likely an answer to THAT message: score it low unless its words clearly answer the agent's message».
  - The version is in the memo key, so a v1 answer judged blind (the incident's 0.90) is never reused.
- THE ENGINE (src/server/channels-engine.js):
  - `placeCtx` gains `turnsBetween`, over the thread index the place rules already read: the newest THREAD_IX_RECORDS of the stored log plus the batch, sorted once per batch and only when asked. No vendor call.
  - Each turn is `{at, self, kind}`. `self` = `FO.selfRead` AND not any agent's send from here: an agent writes from the owner's account, so its echo is not the owner's turn.
  - The asking principal's own sends (the send, its parts, its echo 0.8 s later) are not «between» at all. Vendor notices are nobody's.
  - `preInfer` passes `between: F.inferBetweenLine(c.between)`. The judge stays the ONE caller.
- THE AGENT:
  - A judged hit after the owner's own message has why `INFER_WHY_BETWEEN` «judged an answer to your message of <time>; the user also wrote in between». «The user» is the agent manual's word for the owner; the brief said «the person».
  - `sent.between {own, ownLast}` rides the hit, and the hand-over line prints it beside the score: «judged 0.90; the user also wrote in between — a voice note, 3 min before this».
  - The CLI's `watch` / `--show` print rules, not hits, so the words live where the score is printed, in the wake / next-turn block.
  - channel-words reads the new why before the plain one, in zh + ja.
- NOT IN THIS LANE: transcribing voice notes (a billed ASR call per note; the owner decides). No vendor call was added.
- THE GATES:
  - test-channel-filter ⑳: 21 new checks (363). They cover the incident, the brief's line word for word, nothing between, no reader, others only, the K bound, strictly-between, the line ≤ 300, the kinds table, the thread / no-send / before-the-send exclusions (reader never asked), the why + the hand-over, zh + ja + the reader order, and 2 patched-copy controls (no fact = the base; no K bound).
  - test-decision-model ㉑ (260): the part, the ceiling 804 = 700 + 104, the cap fits whole, v2 ≠ the v1 memo key, the line rides last.
  - test-channel-agent-watch ⑪ (94): the real decision engine's input ends «between: Nobody else wrote between sent and reply.».
  - test-channels-engine ㉗ (heavy, 817 = 810 + 7): THE INCIDENT over the real ingest loop, with a judge STUB recording its parts. Inputs: the agent's send at T, its echo from the owner's account, the owner's `[audio]` at T+7h18m, the peer's «Sounds good» 3 min later. The between line names the voice note; the echo is not counted.
    - A RESTARTED engine reads the turns from the stored log alone.
    - The wake says it.
    - RED CONTROL: the base's engine, a patched copy without the part, hands sent / reply / gap only.
  - Unchanged: test-vendor-whitelist 316 = base; test-spend-paths 364; test-peer-text-census 405; test-record-clear-census 242; test-channels-agent-cli 167; test-channel-revisions 63; test-decision-budget 28.

### lane mac-repair-retires-stale — a re-pair retires the older installs of the SAME hub; the «second agent with an old token» notice names the live install and its stop words stop the agent itself (backlog B-06e9 — the owner's Macbook 2026-10-18: four installs, three re-dialing with old tokens)
- THE GAP: each pairing installs a root keyed by the dial ADDRESS (`~/.vibespace/device@<host>`; its launchd job / user unit / scheduled task keyed by that root). A re-pair through another address (the LAN name, the Tailscale name, the relay) left the older roots running, each re-dialing with its retired token every 30 s for ever; the take-over block stops only THIS root's daemon. dial.json held `{url, token}` — no hub identity — so nothing on the machine could tell an older pairing of THIS hub from another hub's install (installs of different hubs coexist by design). The hub's stop words were generic (`launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/<label>`), and bootout alone does not stop the agent: the launchd job is a supervisor that exits 3 («already running») while the agent runs detached (ppid 1) holding `<root>/state/agentd.lock`.
- THE HUB'S ID: `src/server/dial-pairing.js` `hubId()` mints `vh-` + 16 hex ONCE into data/agentd/hub-id (O_EXCL, 0600; the PURE rule `hubIdOf` in src/dial-facts.js). A device hears it only after it proved its pairing: the --dial-check probe's 200 (`hub`) and, on a dialed link, the hub's `hello` (`hub`, a DeviceManager option — a field an older daemon ignores). `--dial-check` prints `hub id: vh-…` under its ok line; both installers keep it in dial.json; the daemon writes it at an ACCEPTED dial (after the host token matched, never over a dial.json rewritten for another address), so an older install learns it when it next dials in.
- THE RETIRE (install.sh `retire_siblings`, the ps1 twin): only when the dial check ran and passed AND the new daemon dialed in (its own state/dial-status.json `connectedAt` ≥ this run's start; ≤ 20 s, else «→ older installs on this machine were NOT retired: this install has not dialed in yet …»). Every other `~/.vibespace/device@*` root: the same `hub` ⇒ retire; another ⇒ kept («→ kept: … (another VibeSpace's install on this machine)»); a hub on one side only ⇒ unknown; no hub on either side ⇒ the same device id (the dial URL's `device=`) retires, another is unknown. Retire = the supervisor first (launchctl bootout / systemctl --user disable --now / Export-ScheduledTask + Unregister-ScheduledTask), its plist / unit / task XML MOVED to ~/.vibespace/disabled-launchagents/ (a name already there gets a `.<epoch>` suffix — never overwritten), then the agent holding the sibling's lock, ONLY when its command line names vibespace-device (TERM, ≤ 5 s, KILL if still alive). The root and its state stay. Said once: «→ retired N older installs of this hub: … (kept under ~/.vibespace; their launch items moved to ~/.vibespace/disabled-launchagents/)»; an unknown one is LISTED with its exact stop command and never touched.
- THE HUB'S WORDS (PURE src/dial-health.js): `liveInstallOf(dial.mintedBase)` = the installer's own root rule (the suite runs the installer's sed + tr in bash on each base); `dialHealthRow` adds `live`; `stopRecipeOf(platform, {liveKey})` = list the installs (with liveKey the live one is left out), stop the supervisor, AND kill the agent by its lock pid — per platform. The row (sidebar-mounts.js) and the For-you item (dial-health-watch.js itemOf) add «The live install on that machine is {live}; stop the others — …» (when the record names a base) and the door «Re-pairing this machine from its Machines card retires the older installs of this hub for you (an install too old to know this hub is listed with its stop command)», zh + ja. Copy copies the recipe.
- WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: the owner's three stale installs predate the hub id and are never accepted (retired tokens), so they never learn it — a re-pair LISTS them with their commands and does not retire them (the brief's rule: an unknown install is never touched). One way to attribute them, not taken: probe each sibling's own address with its own token and let the refusal name the hub — an unauthenticated answer (spoofable) and a network call per sibling.
- Pins moved: test-agentd-upgrade-signature (the dial link's `serveConnection` gains `onAuthed`), test-writer-sweep (+ the new `ps -p "$SP"` argv read, with its reason), mount-reader-census (dial-pairing.js 1 → 2: data/agentd/hub-id). test-device-install-check's control (n) follows the dial.json writer's new `"$HUB_ID"` argument.
- Tests: test-device-install-check +16 (R-1…R-16, controls (p) (q)): a scratch HOME with five siblings (two plists + a unit of this hub, one lock naming an innocent `sleep`, another hub's, a pre-change one), stub launchctl / systemctl recording ms-stamped calls; the REAL installer against the REAL dial gate retires the three, stops the two fake agents (not the innocent pid), keeps the other hub's, lists the unknown one; the first retire call comes after the new daemon's `connectedAt`; a daemon learns the hub at its next accepted dial through the hub's real device client (CONTROL (p): without `onAuthed` it never does); CONTROL (q) the installer without the retire step leaves all five; a link the hub drops ⇒ «NOT retired»; the classifier's table; the ps1 road pinned (no PowerShell here). test-dial-health ROW-1…7 (ROW-7 runs the copied recipe in bash: the listing names only the others, the kill line stops that agent, never the live one), W-0, H-2b, CONTROLS (e) no kill line (f) no live install. test-host-stale-dialer-ui: the REAL daemon learns the worktree server's hub id; the row names device@127.0.0.1 and the door (zh + en); Copy copies the recipe.

## 2.369.338 — 2026-10-21

### lane effort-menu-per-harness — the effort menu is the harness's own: `/api/session-options?backend=<id>` answers each harness its declared levels + its OWN extras; a level the CLI lacks is refused by name, never dropped
- **The owner's report (2026-10-21 13:4xZ).** On an Antigravity conversation (gemini-4-argon-high, 推理强度: ?) the effort menu offered 默认(重置) / low / medium / high / xhigh / max / ultracode: «antigravity 也是这几个档位吗？». `agy --help`: `--effort … (low|medium|high|xhigh|max)`, five levels and no ultracode, which is Claude Code's own (`--effort xhigh` + the ultracode settings key).
- **The cause.**
  - server.js answered `{ effortLevels: EFFORT_LEVELS, effortExtras: EFFORT_EXTRAS }` (cli-env: the claude CLI's parse + `effortExtrasFor(harnessOf('claude')…)`) to every asker.
  - The bar fetched it with no backend; its `extras ?? uiRow(backend).effortExtras` never fell back, because claude's `[ultracode]` was always there.
  - agyFlags / AGY_WEBUI_EFFORT passed `--effort` only for agy's five, so a carried ultracode spawned agy with none, without a word.
  - Mid-session, ws set-effort persisted `session._effort = 'ultracode'` before agy-wrapper's own "not applied" notice.
  - opencode (no levels) had the same chip and claude's ladder.
  - The client-only `caps.effort: false` hid the New Session dialog's effort row for Antigravity.
- **Measured «?».** The owner's session meta (production, read-only): `effort: null, effortOrigin: 'chosen'`, so nothing was asked (the dialog had no row). The «?» was honest. What was missing was a way to ask, and a title saying what the chip shows.
- **The fix.**
  - PURE src/harness-efforts.js (`effortLevelsOf` / `effortAnswerFor` / `sessionOptionsAnswer` + `effortExtrasFor`, moved from cli-env): the route answers `?backend=` from the descriptor's `ui.effortLevels`:
    - antigravity = AGY_EFFORTS (the adapter's one array);
    - claude = 'cli-help';
    - codex = 'model-catalog';
    - opencode = null.
    `ui.effortExtras` is that harness's own or `[]`. EFFORT_EXTRAS is gone.
  - Client:
    - `hasEffortMenu` (the declared row) replaces `caps.effort` (dropped from META and from test-harness-contract's CLIENT_ONLY_OK) for the bar's chip, the dialog's row and Session Properties' row;
    - the bar asks with its backend and falls back to `effortSeedLevels(backend)`;

### lane feedback-forward-404 — a forward target with NO feedback door pauses the outbox: said once, re-probed daily, caught up when the door appears (backlog B-9bcc; the owner 2026-10-21: fleet feedback is read from the cluster side — the forward stays for a target that IS a hub)
- THE RED (measured on loopback — a fake collector, never the real one): the fleet's forward target is the cluster's telemetry COLLECTOR (`/api/telemetry/ingest`, no feedback door). Every .333+ pod POSTed each report to `<target>/api/feedback/forward`, got 404, and `sendVerdict` said `retry`: the backoff 1 min … 1 h, then hourly for ever, never said. The base verdict sends 29 requests in a day for ONE report.
- PURE src/feedback-forward-model.js: `sendVerdict` gains `no-door` (404 / 405 / 501; 5xx, 403, 408, 429 and no answer keep the backoff). `pauseHolds(pause, {door, version}, now)` — the same door, the same answered version, the day not over. `pauseWords` — the log line and the For-you words (i18nKey, zh + ja). `outboxPush` answers the dropped ids (`gone`). `LIMITS.reprobeMs` 24 h; `VERSION_HEADER` `X-VibeSpace-Version`.
- ORCH src/server/feedback-forward.js — THE PAUSE: a no-door answer from the forward door OR the marks door persists `pause` {door, target, version, status, reason: no-door, since, pausedUntil, probes, todoId} in data/feedback-outbox.json; no backoff. While it holds, the pump and the 6-hourly pull send nothing (the pump's one timer is armed at pausedUntil). At pausedUntil ONE request re-probes — claimed before it is sent, so the pump and the pull never both probe: no door again ⇒ one more day, said nothing; any answer ⇒ the pause ends and the queue catches up oldest first; no answer ⇒ the pause stands. A new target URL ends the pause at once; a new release the target answers (its doors' answers, and the TELEMETRY forward's own answers: src/telemetry.js `onForwardAnswer` → `noteAnswer`) lets the re-probe through at once. Past 200 the oldest report goes, logged BY ID and kept in `lost`.
- SAID ONCE: «feedback forward paused: <target> has no feedback door (404) — re-probed daily; N records waiting» once per pause (and one «resumed» line); ONE low For-you notice (origin server, key feedback-forward) only when `telemetry.forwardUrl` is the instance's SETTING (`personSet`; a cluster-env target is the fleet admin's — the line only), resolved when the door answers. `GET /api/agent/feedback/mine` rows carry `forward: paused | waiting | dropped` (`forwardOf`); `vibespace-feedback list` prints «forward paused: the target has no door …» beside them.
- THE HUB: the forward doors and the telemetry ingest answer `X-VibeSpace-Version` after the collector's token, never to a bad one — how a paused origin learns its hub was updated.
- GATES: test-feedback-forward 84 ✓ (was 58: ⑨ the verdict table with no-door + pauseHolds; ⑪ 25 — the pause and its file, 23 h of hourly passes and pulls with NO request, the restart, the daily re-probe, the version note, the catch-up, the person-set notice and its resolve, the URL change, the marks door, the bound by id, the hub's header, the wiring; RED CONTROL the base verdict: 29 requests in the day vs 1) · test-user-todos-layout 329 (PRODUCERS row, 65 sites) · test-record-clear-census 242 (the `w` words receiver) · test-feedback-ui 31 (heavy) · test-architecture 779 · unchanged: test-vendor-whitelist 316 (our own hub, no vendor), test-spend-paths 364 (no wake), test-peer-text-census 405.

### lane inline-receipts-compose-api — the two siblings of .335's inline-receipt road (B-5ebc): a NEW mail (`compose`) and a raw API call (`api`) answer with their outcome; no second receipt message waits in the agent's queue
- THE RULE (the owner, .335): a command that performs an action answers with the action's outcome; a message carries only what the actor could not have learned from its own command. .335 (lane channel-direct-send-sync) shipped it for `reply` and left two doors on the old road.
- COMPOSE (measured on the base b21fafbc): `vibespace-channels compose` sent no `collect`, the route passed none and the engine's `compose` never set `receiptCollect`, so a direct new mail's `receipt()` took the message road — the CLI printed «sent directly (policy: direct)» and the SAME outcome came again as «[Channels · Outbox] Channel receipt …» on the next turn (test-channel-outbox's control on the base compose queues it). Now the route threads `collect` exactly as reply's (`compose`, and `compose --caller` → composeEach → propose), the engine's compose marks it through the SAME pair as propose (`markCollect` / `inlineReceiptOf`, one helper pair in src/server/channels-outbound.js), and the CLI prints the receipt inline and confirms the read through the collect door (GET status?id&collect=1); the timeout road falls back to the message as reply's does.
- API (measured): a DIRECT api write (write-auto / write-all / an always-allowed shape) RUNS inline and files NO proposal and NO receipt message — it already answered with its outcome (unchanged; `bytes` now rides its JSON). The duplicate was a GATED proposal the CLI waited on: `api … --wait` / `api wait <id>` printed the outcome, and src/server/channel-api-cards.js `receiptFor` ALSO filed «[Channels · API] …» for the next turn. Now `api … --wait` sends `collect` and every poll is a collect door (`GET /api/agent/channels/api/proposals/:id?collect=1`); the cards HOLD a decided proposal's receipt while its CLI waits — a lease each poll renews (`COLLECT_WINDOW_MS`, 20 s), judged by the outbox's own `receiptRoad({draftedBy: principal, kind: 'api'}, {collecting})` (no second verdict) — and a decided poll marks it read (`receipt.how: 'inline'`) and answers the card's words (`receiptText(p, {inline: true})`). A CLI that stops polling before the decision: the hold lapses and the receipt messages (a one-shot fallback timer at the window's end); an approval-gated proposal no CLI waits on keeps its card AND its receipt message.
- `api wait` on a FAILED run: the base already printed the error + code (stderr, exit 1 — the spread result's `error`); what it lacked were the card's words (which call; approved but NOT run; a fate — an expiry or a withdrawal read as plain `rejected`). Now the answer carries `receipt` (stdout JSON), or prints it before the code (stderr).
- A held send's CLI wait follows the hub's window (`collectWindowMs` rides `receiptPending`), not a hard-coded 20 s — the CLI's «the receipt will come as a message» and the engine's fallback agree.
- THE CENSUS (test-channel-outbox §C, grep-derived): the doors that send (an agent route or a helper it calls reaching eng.propose / compose / composeEach or api.call) each read `b.collect === true`; every CLI POST to those routes carries `collect` (reply · compose · compose --caller · api). Controls: the base compose, a planted send verb, a door that drops it — each RED by name.
- TESTS: test-channel-outbox 473 → 498 (§C the road rows for compose / api, the real-engine compose legs inline / timeout / job / review, RED CONTROL = the base compose queues a message, the census + 3 controls) · test-channel-api 176 → 186 (⑨ the real orchestrator + the real cards behind the route's two lines, the real CLI: --wait reads it inline and no message is filed, no --wait keeps the message, --timeout ⇒ the fallback; RED CONTROL = the base CLI's wait files the message) · test-channel-api-cards 33 → 43 (④ fake-clock legs, the fallback's own timer, RED CONTROL = no hold) · test-channels-agent-cli 154 → 165 (compose / --caller inline words, the held send's window, api inline outcome / a failed run's words / --timeout; RED CONTROL = the base compose CLI) · test-peer-text-census rows `x`, `r.collectWindowMs`, `windowMs`, `r.receipt`. test-spend-paths 364 unchanged (the inline roads file no wake).
- GATES: the fast gate on a scratch snapshot whose version files say 2.369.337 (so this heading is the next patch) — build + test-architecture + test-changelog-style (40) + the fast tier ALL GREEN; at-risk heavies (`ci.mjs --heavy --only=…`) ALL PASS: test-record-clear-walk 159 (the agent-route answers) · test-channel-api-chrome 68 · test-channels-e2e 213 · test-channels-groups-e2e 129 · test-channels-aggregate 443 · test-channels-engine 810 · test-webhook-routes 22 · test-webhook-pair-e2e 14 · test-webhook-ui-e2e 42. test-channel-api's ⑨ legs run side by side (real 2 s CLI polls) — the suite stays ~6.5 s.

## 2.369.337 — 2026-10-21

### lane dialog-unsaved-guard — a dialog closing with unsaved changes ASKS; ONE guard in createModalShell, every Save dialog wired, a census keeps it so (backlog B-bc31 — the owner 2026-10-21 ticked «也判断普通回复» in 通知…, closed it with ✕, and a colleague's reply went unjudged; base 3a4caf5d = 2.369.335)
- THE GAP (measured on origin/master): `showNotifyDialog`'s ticks and selects change rows in memory, and only 保存 writes. ✕ / Esc / the backdrop went straight to `close()`. An acorn census over every `createModalShell(` in src/lib counted 18 Save dialogs, and none guarded a change. The brief listed 16 files; five of them have no modal Save dialog (integrations-window / learn-card / settings-ui / task-log are inline window editors, doc-window-ui its save dot, channel-window a showInputDialog). Two were missing from the grep: sidebar-mounts' Edit "<mount>" (`tr('Save')`) and the account's Reach & policy… (grantAccessBody's Save, imported).
- THE GUARD (src/lib/utils.js): `createModalShell({ unsaved: { isDirty?, save, words?, discard?, saveLabel? } })`. ✕, the backdrop and both Escapes call `dismiss`. When dirty, an in-place sheet inside the dialog shows «有未保存的更改» · 继续编辑 / 放弃 / 保存, with 保存 focused and Esc on it meaning 继续编辑.
  - 保存 runs the dialog's own save: it landed if the dialog closed itself, is no longer dirty, or resolved `true`. Otherwise the sheet says «没有保存：<reason>»: what save threw or answered, else the error toast its own save showed meanwhile.
  - 放弃 runs `discard()` (a typed secret or name cleared), then closes.
  - The caller's `close()` never asks.
- THE WIRING (17 call sites + Reach & policy… = the census's 18; plus 铸造…): each dialog compares what it would write with what it drew (`drawn() !== base`). Notify… rows expose `sig()`. grantAccessBody returns `isDirty` / `save` for Access… and Reach & policy…, and its `setCaps` re-bases a clean list. A dialog whose state lands after an await registers `dirtyNow` / `saveNow` when drawn (no TDZ). The mount editor uses the shell's OWN flag (input / change in its form) with its submit as `save`. Its `unsaved` stays one short property: a first take broke test-record-clear-census, whose alias scope is a method's first 6000 characters, by pushing the Remove confirm's `name` 320 characters out of a 106-character margin.
- FOUND ON THE WAY:
  - API access…'s Save closed on a REFUSED write (`fetchJson` never throws; the `try` read every answer as success). It now says the error and stays.
  - Options… / Push lane… re-base on save, so the sheet's 保存 closes at once.
  - The OAT dialog's own Escape calls `dismiss('escape')`.
- THE GATES:
  - NEW scripts/test-dialog-unsaved-census.mjs (fast): 24 checks; the census prints 18 Save dialogs, 18 guarded, 0 declared false.
  - test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑫ (heavy): 223 = 204 + 19, the owner's exact tick on a 回复了它发过的消息 rule.
  - test-automation-keys-chrome UNSAVED (heavy): 94 = 87 + 7;
  - test-mounts-dialog-extract edit-unsaved (heavy, the shell's OWN flag): 61 = 60 + 1.
  - RED CONTROL = the base tree with the new legs: aggregate-ui ⑫ ✗ «ticked + ✕ ⇒ the dialog STAYS and asks» (the dialog closed and the tick was gone; the leg then threw on the closed dialog), automation-keys ✗ ×2 (u2: open false), mounts-dialog-extract ✗ edit-unsaved.
  - test-architecture 779 (build).
  - Fast gate on a scratch snapshot (package.json → .336 in the snapshot only): ALL GREEN (469 suites, 250 s) on the third run. Run 1 was red on test-record-clear-census: the mount editor's first take pushed the Remove confirm out of the alias pass's 6000-character window. Run 2 was red on test-account-policy-door: its pin on `setCaps`'s first two statements, so the clean-check moved below them.

### lane phone-tray-voice-done — on a phone, a dictation's stop closed the For-you tray under the reply it was filling: the ONE outside-press closer decided a touch at its LIFT by the element it went down on, and the recording capsule's 250-ms repaint had taken that element off the page — inside nothing, «outside» (the owner's incident inc-mvhzgiq8-bs3j, 2026-10-21 10:42Z, Android Chrome 448×850, 2.369.334: 「我刚才在手机上点开 Inbox，点回复、语音输入，然后点完成，Inbox 就被收起来了，我尝试了两次都这样。另外，这个"报告问题"的输入框也不能使用语音输入」; base 3a4caf5d = 2.369.335)
- THE BUNDLE (read-only): twice the same shape — `#mobile-nav-todos` (10:41:19Z) → Reply (31.8) → the mic (`rect<svg<button.voice-btn`, 33.2) → the mic again, on `span.voice-time` (35.6: the STOP, the owner's 「完成」) → the next press is on chat text BEHIND the tray (49.1); again at 50.1 / 53.3 / 54.5 / 56.9. No key, no outside press, no For-you write, no ws broadcast between the stop and the close. The hub's console holds NO `[voice] dictation` line for either reply (the composer's at 10:41:07 is there): the two reply dictations never reached the hub — the recorder had no word for what closed the tray.
- THE MEASURED CLOSER (a phone-emulated Chrome against the real built app at 448×850, DPR 3, the owner's UA, touch; the microphone, MediaRecorder and /api/voice/* stubbed in the page; every event traced, the stack of the `hidden` add captured): a stop tap held 60 ms passes; held 320 ms — across one capsule repaint (voice-input.js `paint()` rewrites `btn.innerHTML` every 250 ms while recording) — the order is `pointerdown span.voice-time` → (the repaint replaces the span) → `pointerup` → HIDE (stack: hidePopup ← onOutsidePress `judge` ← its document pointerup listener) → `blur textarea.ut-reply-input` → `click div#phone-home` (the page behind — the owner's chat text) → `rec.stop` from the recording's TICK (`!btn.isConnected` ⇒ `cancel()`) — and NO dictate request. utils.js `onOutsidePress` keeps a touch PENDING at pointerdown and judges it at pointerup with `within(roots, p.target)`: the span it went down on was detached by then, `popup.contains(span)` is false, the press was «outside». A finger rests 100–300 ms on a phone; the owner hit it 2 / 2.
- THE FIX (the ONE handler, src/lib/utils.js): the press's facts — inside / excluded / ignored / voice / nested — are measured WHERE AND WHEN it went down (`where(target, e)` at pointerdown; the tap at pointerup decides on them). A node redrawn away under the finger stays inside; an outside node that leaves the page still closes (the down-time facts, not «detached ⇒ keep»). The PURE table (src/lib/outside-press.js `pressCloses`) gains the `voice` fact: the voice UI that stands outside every box — src/voice-focus.js `VOICE_UI` = the follower's microphone host + a field's floating chip, both on document.body — is never an outside press of any surface (the chip's own stopPropagation never could stop a document CAPTURE closer: a tap on 「已插入 · 撤销」 closed the tray too — measured, the control below). voice-input.js `ours` is now the exported `voiceOwns` over the same selector (utils.js reads the selector: voice-input.js imports utils.js, so the predicate cannot be imported back).
- THE CAUSES IN THE RECORDER (user-todos-panel.js): `hidePopup(why)` — every closer of the tray leaves `{op:'popup-hide', panel:'for-you', why}` in the incident recorder's op ring: outside / frame (a press into an iframe, the window-blur path) / escape / back / jump / artifact / open-win / view / answer, and `button` (its own button again, togglePopup). Six suites pinned the closer lines verbatim and are re-pinned to them (record-clear-census H5 + CONTROL 13, back-guard, login-expiry, helper-ask, user-todos-layout, inbox-window-model).
- THE SECOND COMPLAINT («报告问题» had no dictation): on 2.369.334 it had none; the base (2.369.335) already carries lane voice-follows-focus, whose focus follower gives the Report a problem textarea (incident-recorder.js, a createModalShell box) a microphone — verified at the owner's 448×850 by touch in test-voice-follow-chrome ④b (≥ 40×40, outside the box, inside the screen, ON TOP of the modal — z 100001 over 99998; the words land; nothing captured). No code change for it.
- NOT TAKEN FROM THE BRIEF, with the reason: (a) `.voice-field` in the voice predicate — it wraps the BOX itself, so a press on another surface's reply box would never close a tray; a field's own microphone is inside its surface by containment, now judged at down time. (b) the tray's own exclude list — the ONE closer reads the voice fact for every surface (the tray, the title-bar mini inbox, every createPopover), so no per-site rule. (c) «the back guard's "a tap happened" accounting» — it has none: it re-arms by traversal (history.go(1)) precisely so no tap is counted (back-guard.js head).
- BEFORE → AFTER (test-tray-voice-phone, the held stop on 「0:02」 asserted to straddle a repaint): base closer — the tray CLOSES (op ring `why: 'outside'`), 0 requests, the words never land; a tap on the chip closes it · fix — the tray stays, 1 request, the words in the same focused box, no `popup-hide`; the chip's Undo works and the tray stays; the keyboard up (850 → 500) / folding mid-dictation changes nothing; Escape in the box folds it (draft kept), Escape / a real outside tap / the browser's back still close it with their causes; the draft is back on the next Reply.
- Gates: test-tray-voice-phone NEW heavy (19) · test-outside-press 68 → 74 (§1 four voice rows, §2 (n) the redrawn target + the chip / follower presses, §3 (f) the base closer as a patched copy: closes on both) · test-voice-follow-chrome 56 → 61 (④b the report box at 448×850; ③'s MUTANT now two layers: the guard removed keeps the popover — the closer's voice fact — and MUTANT 2, the guard AND the voice fact removed, closes it) · test-taskbar-group 82 (its sandbox evals onOutsidePress's text with the free names injected — `VOICE_UI` handed in; the first fast run was red on it) · test-architecture 779 · the fast gate ALL GREEN 250 s (a scratch snapshot at 2.369.336, changelog-style 40 on the .337 heading) · 17 at-risk heavies of the 217 `--list-affected` names (utils.js is in nearly every bundle) ALL PASS: tray-voice-phone 19, voice-follow 61, mobile-back 25, voice 36, voice-teach 55, phone-composer 39, popover-frame-close, mobile-gaps, inbox-reply-ui, record-clear-ui, record-clear-client 50, attention-policy-ui 28, taskbar-group-ui 68, inbox-window-ui, exit-access-ui 125, mobile-select 39, phone-chip-ui 25.

### lane judged-watch-state — a judged rule that cannot run says so to the one who set it and to the one who pays (B-f42e; the owner 2026-10-21 「做吧」 after one of the owner's agents read in the manual that judged rules «silently do not fire» when the plugin / its rules switch is off or the day's budget is spent)
- THE GAP (origin/master 3a4caf5d): the manual said «No key, the day's budget spent or the hour cap reached ⇒ that message is simply not a hit». The channels engine's pre-passes (`preJudge` / `preInfer`) refused by a log line once an hour; the judge's `quiet()` journalled once per 5 min; nothing reached the agent that armed the rule or the owner who pays — the agent learned it only by missing a message, and the skipped message was never judged again (fresh records are judged once).
- ONE PURE VERDICT (src/decision-model.js `judgedRoadState({pluginOn, rulesOn, keyPresent, budgetLeft, estUsd, budgetUsd, hourCapHit, rulePerHour, route})` → `{live, why ∈ ROAD_WHY, usedPct | perHour}`; order: the plugin, its switch (Routing for a route rule), the key, today's money — left < one judgment's price is a spent day —, the rule's hour). `budgetVerdict` now ASKS it for the switches, the key and the money (`ROAD_GATE_WHY` keeps the gate's words feature-off / daily-budget; the 1e-8 USD edge and the refusal order unchanged — test-decision-model ⑥ green as it was). The words: `judgedRoadLine`, `judgedSkipLine`, `roadWhyOf` (a judge refusal → the road's word). RED MUTANTS (㉒): the switch line dropped ⇒ the verdict AND the paid call's gate run a rule with rulesOn:false; the money line dropped ⇒ live on a spent day and the gate pays past the ceiling.
- THE ENGINE'S FACTS (src/server/decision-engine.js `roadFacts(use)`): the plugin row's switches, the key, the ceiling − settled − reserved, one judgment at `inputPlan(use).ceiling` × the row's rate. The channels pre-passes read them once a batch and ask the verdict per rule (+ its hour); the switch and the hour are refused at the door (journal words unchanged: plugin-off / feature-off / per-hour), the key and the money stay the judge's own refusal (its journal row, its server notice).
- THE AGENT IS TOLD AT THE DOOR: `agentWatch` (src/server/channels-access.js) answers `judged` (the line) + `road` for a row with a judged rule; the CLI prints it as the answer's LAST line (exit 0 — saved either way; a malformed rule is refused as today: exit 1 + the validator's [code] — the brief's «exit 2» is not today's code, kept); `watch --show` / `watches` print it under each judged row. A later switch flip makes the same row live (no new `watch`).
- THE SKIP'S THREE DOORS (channels-engine `noteSkips`, gated by `stillInEffect` — test-architecture §65 B): ① OWED — the skipped record kept in memory for the watchers it missed (≤ 50 a conversation, ≤ 200 conversations; a restart forgets them — said in the manual) and judged when the road returns (`owedPass`, a 60 s look while anything is owed; past `channels.replyInferHours` — the judged road's own window, default 24 h — dropped): an owed batch rides `onFresh` with `{owed}` (only the watchers that missed it, no msgs ledger); a watcher another rule already reached owes nothing; the memo keeps answers only, so a skip is never a «no». ② THE AGENT — ONE line a day per cause to the rule's agent through the next-turn stash (`Channels · judged rules`, kind notification — never a wake, no spend reason): «N messages matched nothing today because your judged rules could not run: <why> …»; later skips counted (the door's line says today's count). ③ THE OWNER — a skip of the day's budget calls `decisionEngine.notePaused(names)`: ONE For-you item a day (origin plugin, plugin llm, urgency low ⇒ the attention model's band-5 plugin row: no badge, no toast; door = the plugin's settings), a new name re-words it while open, a dismissed one is never repeated that day.
- THE NOTIFY… CHIP (src/lib/channel-filter-editor.js `judgedRoadOf` / `paintRoadChip`): beside each decision row and a ticked «Also judge plain replies» box — the SAME PURE verdict over the plugin row (`/api/plugins` decision status): «judged: live» · «paused: budget spent» · «off: rules switch» / routing / LLM plugin / no key; zh/ja words; `.chan-road-chip` on theme vars.
- TESTS: test-decision-model ㉒ (the table, the gate reading it, the words, 2 RED mutants); test-decision-engine L (roadFacts → verdict, notePaused over a REAL UserTodoManager — one low band-5 row, re-worded, dismissed never repeated, next day anew, 0 vendor calls + a RED control); test-decision-rule G (REAL channels + decision engines: switch off ⇒ 0 calls, ONE stash line, the door reads rules-off + 2; switch on ⇒ owedPass judges both and they wake; budget spent ⇒ ONE For-you item naming agent 3 + group B, one line, no wake; RED CONTROL = the base without the skip doors ⇒ silent, nothing re-judged), C (+ the hour cap's line), E / F (the chip: live, budget spent, rules switch off, zh plugin off); test-channels-agent-cli ㉒ (the REAL CLI over the REAL engine: the last line, --show, watches, the flip to live, budget spent, --infer, a keyword has none, malformed refused + RED base control). Census rows: test-user-todos-layout PRODUCERS (decision-engine.js · plugin, 64 → 65 sites), test-peer-text-census (r.judged / w.judged, the fromName), test-decision-budget's preJudge reserve pin moved to the road line (it had gone vacuous).

### lane new-session-account-follows-backend — the New Session dialog said Claude but offered Antigravity's accounts: the open filled the account row from the select's PREVIOUS value, then SET the select, and a programmatic set fires no `change` (the owner's incident inc-mvi2cv4b-hdwv, 2026-10-21 12:03Z, desktop 2195×1100, 2.369.334: 「创建过一次 Antigravity 对话后，再次创建对话的时候默认正确加载了 Claude 的信息，除了可选账号依然是 Antigravity 的」; base 3a4caf5d = 2.369.335)
- THE BUNDLE (read-only): the ring holds the second open only — the task board's + (`folder-add-btn`, `showNewSessionDialog({ cwd, taskId })`, no backend: no surface passes one, so every open starts on the designed default, Claude) → the cwd typed → two presses on the account select (the owner looking at Antigravity's list) → two on the backend select → the account select again → Create (a `create` frame goes out) → the report. No op, no console line: nothing in the recorder could say which backend the dialog had applied.
- THE CODE (app.js `showNewSessionDialog`): (1) the Task row filled the browser-profile row, (2) `updateAcctRow()` filled the account row, both reading `#input-backend.value` — still the previous open's `antigravity`; (3) only then `input-backend.value = b` + `_applySessionBackendOptions(b)` (model / permission / effort / worktree — the rows the owner saw right). The account row followed a backend only through the select's `change` listener, which a programmatic set never fires. The machine had the same hole: `#input-host` was set only when /api/hosts answered — after the rows — and that set fired no `change` either.
- MEASURED (test-new-session-dialog F / G, the base's open order rebuilt from a patched copy of today's app.js): after an Antigravity Create, the next open says Claude with the account row `['', 'subscription', 'agy-…']`, the Antigravity pick STILL SELECTED — and its Create sends `{ backend: 'claude', accountId: <the Antigravity account> }`: worse than the list the owner saw, a Claude session asked for on another harness's login. The inverse (Claude on a key, then an open on Antigravity) sends `{ backend: 'antigravity', accountId: <the Claude key> }`. An open on a machine keeps this machine's words after the list lands.
- THE FIX (ONE function): `applyBackend(b, { why })` sets the select AND refills every row derived from it — the session options with the backend's defaults, then `_refillNewSessionRows()`: the account row, the browser-profile row, the model menu (deferred, so it reads the account row this pass filled). The open decides the backend and the machine FIRST, sets the machine, then calls `applyBackend(b, { why: 'open' })`; the select's ONE `change` listener calls `applyBackend(value, { why: 'pick' })` (the second, account-only listener is gone); the boot fill goes through it too. The host list landing re-runs `_refillNewSessionRows()` when it changed the machine; a host pick runs the same. The rows derive from what the select HOLDS (what Create sends). Every apply leaves `{ op: 'ns-backend', backend, why }` in the incident recorder's op ring.
- NOT TAKEN: the PURE `newSessionDerived(backend, facts)` the brief offered for plain-data rows — the account row's inputs are not plain data (the host's verdicts and warm state, the settings, the i18n words, the previous pick and its toast), so ONE DOM function with a test that drives it. The remembered backend: the dialog does NOT remember the last backend (it never did — `backend || 'claude'`); kept, and said so in kb-features. The machine (G) is beyond the brief's backend rule, fixed because it is the same hole.
- BEFORE → AFTER (test-new-session-dialog): the second open after Antigravity — the account row Antigravity's with its pick selected, Create naming that account for Claude · Claude's row, the default selected, Claude's model menu and effort row, Create naming no account; an open on a machine — this machine's words · that machine's («CLI login @ lanebox (Pro/Max)»).
- ON THE WAY: test-new-session-dialog's teardown left its server's device daemon alive after EVERY run (title-rewritten, rooted by cwd / HOME only — `pkill -f <root>` never names it; the gate's reaper found it later). It now ends every process rooted in its scratch dirs (scratch.mjs endRootedProcesses) — off test-architecture §57b's ENDS_DEBT list.

### lane antigravity-spawn-argv — an Antigravity conversation starts: ONE session line for every harness (`node <wrapper> <buf> <meta> <ONE executable> …args`), the session's names ride the spawn's ENV, never argv (the owner 2026-10-21 11:4xZ: «Error: Antigravity exited (exit code 125) — see agy-wrapper.log. Resume the conversation to continue.», the create and the resume alike; base 23d3ce4d = the 2.369.336 cut)
- MEASURED (the owner's data/session-buffers/agy-wrapper.log, 11:35Z, read-only): `[antigravity] spawned /usr/bin/env --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --print-timeout 0 --model gemini-4-argon-high --dangerously-skip-permissions EDITOR=… CLAUDE_WEBUI_PORT=… CLAUDE_WEBUI_SESSION_ID=… VIBESPACE_API=… VIBESPACE_SESSION_CWD=… PATH=… VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN=vsst_… DISPLAY=… TERM=… COLORTERM=… AGY_WEBUI_*=… AGENT_BROWSER_*=… /home/<user>/.local/bin/agy` → env: `unexpected argument '--input-format'` → `session ended code=125` (env's usage exit).
- THE CAUSE: ws-create's local line was `[NODE_CMD, wrapper, buf, meta, ENV_CMD, EDITOR=…, …, spawnCmd, ...spawnArgs]`, so every wrapper's argv[4] was `/usr/bin/env`. chat-wrapper / codex-chat-wrapper / acp-wrapper / pty-wrapper spawn `argv[4] argv[5…]` and append their own flags AFTER, so `env K=V … <cli> <flags>` worked. agy-wrapper puts agy's flags FIRST (`spawn(cmd, ['--input-format', …, ...extraArgs])`), so they landed in front of the assignments.
- THE COMMIT THAT BROKE IT: not the .331 spawn-hygiene lanes (`git log 9408bc57..23d3ce4d -- src/ws-create.js` is empty, and no ENV_CMD change). The env prefix inside the wrapper argv dates from 85dcc966 (2026-04-12, the ws-handler extraction; moved verbatim by 61ee7f76). agy-wrapper.js arrived broken against it in 9408bc57 (int330, lane antigravity-harness → 2.369.330). Its suite drove the wrapper with argv[4] = the stub directly, never through ws-create, so no Antigravity chat ever started through the real path.
- THE SAME LINE PUT THE SESSION TOKEN ON argv for every local session. /proc/<pid>/cmdline of the dtach master and the wrapper is readable by every user of the machine for the session's whole life, and spawn logs that print the args wrote it to disk: the owner's hub holds codex-chat-wrapper.log 12 lines, agy-wrapper.log 2, chat-wrapper.log 134 (from 2026-07, when the token sat inside the 5 logged args). The values were not read; only counted.
- FIX:
  - src/spawn/line.js (PURE) `sessionSpawnLine({ node, wrapper, bufFile, metaFile, exe, args, env, pairs })` → `{ argv: [node, wrapper, buf, meta, exe, ...args], env: { ...env, ...pairs } }`. A later pair wins, as `env K=V` did, so the CLI's env is byte-for-byte what it was. `exeRefusal` throws on a launcher / an assignment / nothing at the executable's place.
  - ws-create builds `r6Pairs` (the old prefix minus the token, which r6Base already held) and `r6Base` (the old r6Env), then `r6Line = sessionSpawnLine(…)`. dtach and the R6 daemon pipe run `r6Argv` with `r6Env`.
  - boot-restore's remote re-adopt uses the same line, its two names on `readoptEnv`.
  - ENV_CMD is gone from server.js / ws-handler (WS_CTX_CONTRACT) / ws-create / boot-restore.
- THE WRAPPERS REFUSE BY NAME (`commandRefusal`, before any spawn, the ONE error line of the journal, exit 1):
  - agy-wrapper: argv[4] not an absolute executable ⇒ «agy-wrapper: the command is not an executable: <cmd> — the hub's Antigravity path is unresolved; reinstall agy or set ANTIGRAVITY_CMD»; `env` ⇒ «…a launcher, not agy — the hub put an env prefix where the executable goes …».
  - acp-wrapper (same contract): absolute, or a bare name the env's PATH resolves (the remote roads' `ssh`), else refused; `env` refused.
- THE CENSUS (scripts/spawn-env-census.mjs, test-architecture §94): THE ARGV PASS reads each site's argv words (arrays, spreads, branches, the variables they name). A secret-shaped NAME= word (TOKEN / SECRET / PASSWORD / CREDENTIAL / API_KEY …) is RED with no row possible; other NAME= words are counted (base 14, now 0). `pty` handed in by a context is node-pty, so ws-create's session spawn is a site now (it was invisible: 191 → 193 sites). §94 CONTROL: the token back on the line ⇒ RED.
- THE OWNER'S ISOLATED-HOME ACCOUNT reaches agy unchanged: `creds.spawnEnv(dir)` = { HOME, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS: 'disabled:' } rides spawnAccount.localEnv → r6Env → the wrapper → agy. Proven by the stub through the real path.
- TESTS:
  - NEW test-session-spawn-line (fast, 18): the builder per harness, the real ws-create to a stub pty for claude / codex / opencode / antigravity, and two ws-create mutants (the env prefix back; the names off the env), each RED on every harness.
  - NEW test-antigravity-session (heavy, 12): a stub agy through the real ws-create + node-pty + dtach + agy-wrapper on a named account in the real accounts store. Its argv = the wrapper's stream flags + agyFlags + the extra args; HOME = the account root, the bus disabled; the session's names in its env; agy's init became the journal's `session` record; no NAME= word and no token on the dtach master's / wrapper's / agy's command line; a bare `agy-not-installed` is refused by name.
  - test-agy-harness 79 → 85 (⑪ five refusals + a RED copy whose refusal is cut ⇒ «exit code 125»); test-acp-harness 135 → 139.
  - test-harness-spawn: «the adapter's env rides the spawn's env, no NAME= word on the line».
  - Pins re-pointed to the line: §60a, test-browser-profiles, test-cli-cmd-refresh, test-fork-flag.
  - test-integration-toggle (EXCLUDED debt) reads the dtach master's environ, not its argv.
- RED CONTROL = the base 23d3ce4d: test-antigravity-session 11 FAILED (1 passed). «agy-wrapper.log: spawned /usr/bin/env», «Antigravity exited (exit code 125) — see agy-wrapper.log», the stub never ran. The new census on the base: «SECRET ON ARGV src/ws-create.js:1359 VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN=…».

### lane channels-search-says-hidden — an agent's channel search says what it found: `--full` prints the SAVED hits first, several words match a message holding EVERY one of them anywhere, and a match where the agent cannot read is said to EXIST — never how many, where or what (a field miss 2026-10-21 08:2xZ on the owner's hub: an ops agent searched a vendor's mail it was told to find, read «found nothing you can see …» and reported the sync broken; the owner found the mail in one try; base aff72b10 = 2.369.334)
- THE CAUSE (主开发 measured it from the agent's raw re-run): (A) `search "<words>" --full` printed ONLY the full road's `results` — the vendor's ADDITIONS (the merge drops a hit the saved copy holds) — never the stored hits the plain search lists; every vendor hit was already saved, so it printed «the account's own search found nothing you can see that is not saved here» and the agent read «nothing». (B) a two-word query («Wren NID») found nothing while each word alone hit: `store.search` matched the whole query as ONE substring of a record's text / author / attachment names. The reach was not the cause (the agent's group held `visible` on both accounts) — but the same «nothing» was also what a match in a conversation it may NOT read produced, so «not there» and «there, hidden from you» read alike.
- (A) SAVED FIRST: data/bin/vibespace-channels `search … --full` runs the plain search FIRST (the same route, the same printing — the suite pins the two outputs byte-equal up to the --full hint), then the full road with `saved=<the rows it printed>`; the additions follow, each `(not saved here)`; no additions ⇒ «the account's own search added nothing beyond the N saved hits above» (N = the caller's own visible rows). A vendor refusal (floor / share) still prints the saved hits before it. The words after the rows are the server's (`said`) — an older server's answer falls back to the old lines.
- (B) EVERY WORD (src/channel-store.js `search`): the query's words (white space) match a record holding every one, each anywhere — its text, its author's name, an attachment's name, or its conversation's TITLE (the index's; a mail thread's subject); the raw-bytes pre-check asks only the words the title does not already hold. One word = the substring it always was (title beside it). The `match` predicate road (the Notify preview) is unchanged. The owner's Channels search box reads the same function (it gains the same match; its words are unchanged). The answer carries `match: 'every-word'` (PURE `SR.STORE_MATCH`); the CLI's trailer names it; its usage says «words (all must appear)».
- (C) EXISTENCE ONLY (the owner 08:5xZ: 「不要提示有 N 条在你看不到的对话里，应该只给存在与不存在的信息，数量本身也会泄漏信息」 — the first brief's count + account + title was withdrawn): `searchFor` also searches the conversations of each account the caller READS or may REQUEST something of (its `list --all` directory) that it may NOT read — reach asked FIRST, per conversation, in `searchFor` itself (test-architecture §65 reads it there; a msg-acl adapter — the built-in Agents adapter — never counts; an account it has no reach in at all stays total, §8) — ONE `store.search` (limit 1) for EXISTENCE, reach re-asked after the await (`stillSees`); the answer is a boolean `hiddenMatch` and the PURE words `SR.searchAnswer` → «nothing you can read matches "…"» + `HIDDEN_TEXT` («matches exist that you cannot read — ask the user to share them with you (Channels › the conversation's ⋯ or the account's ⋯ → Grant access…).» — the same bytes whatever matched); «nothing matches "…"» only when nothing matched where it looked (a byte-capped hidden part ⇒ no «nothing» claim). The `--full` road: a vendor hit in a STORED conversation it may not read — one the vendor answered, one the merge dropped as already stored (`vendorSearch` → `storedIn`), one Gmail's adapter dropped UNREAD by the `shows` hint (its page's `unshown`, threads only, carried in the memo page so a remembered answer says the same — `SR.unshownOf`) — is the same boolean; a hit in a conversation never stored here stays uncounted (no door shares it). The answer object carries no hidden row (the suite pins no title / sender / word / conversation or message id in its JSON). The brief's rule 2 verified, no change: `list --all` lists such a conversation among the titles it may REQUEST (lane channel-agent-watch W2).
- THE GATES: test-channel-search §S (+29: the PURE table — all visible / some hidden / all hidden / truly nothing / capped / no account / --full added nothing beyond N saved / found nothing either / vendor-found-but-hidden / additions + hidden / an older CLI; HIDDEN_TEXT has no digit and names the door; the memo's unshown round trip; the real engine — «Wren NID» across sender + text, a title word, a two-conversation miss; ALL HIDDEN = existence; NO LEAK over the whole answer; TRULY NOTHING; a requesting-only agent vs a no-reach one; --full's answered and already-stored hidden hits; CONTROLS: the one-substring store, the engine that never looks where the caller cannot read (the base's «nothing matches»), a MUTANT wording the count + account + title ⇒ NO LEAK red) · test-channels-agent-cli ㉒ (+10: the CLI against the REAL engine — two words, all hidden, no leak, truly nothing, --full saved FIRST then «added nothing beyond the 1 saved hit above», byte-equal to the plain search, a vendor addition after the saved hit, the existence line once; CONTROL: a CLI whose --full skips the plain search prints no saved hit) · test-channels-gmail-shape (+1: `unshown` names the dropped threads; CONTROL 1b's anchor re-taken) · test-peer-text-census (rows: `x.said`, `l`, `r.match`, `full`, `f.results`, `f.note`, `f.adds`, `f.remembered.ageSec`; the `said(` print helper). A focused element that the PURE predicate calls a target and that has no microphone of its own gets one: a fixed `.voice-follow` host holding the same `attachDictation` button (placement `follow`), ANCHORED to the field's box — re-placed on scroll (window capture), resize, the visual viewport, the field's own ResizeObserver and a 250-ms look (a field removed without a blur, a pane that moved); gone on blur (a recording finishes first and lands in ITS field — then the microphone follows the field that holds the focus) or when the field leaves the page (its recording cancelled). The field's DOM and layout never change. A box with its own microphone is marked through `Symbol.for('vibespace.voice.own')` ON THE ELEMENT — the lazy doc bundle (public/doc-editor.js) carries its own copy of the module and marks the box the main bundle's follower reads.
- THE PREDICATE (PURE src/voice-focus.js `dictationTarget(facts)` → `{ok, why}`, the ONE place): a textarea, an input of a text type (none, text, search, url, email, tel) or a [contenteditable] is a target, except — in this order — `secret` (type=password; autocomplete one-time-code / current-password / new-password: the vault's passwords, its second password included), `terminal` (xterm's helper textarea), `disabled`, `read-only`, `opted-out` (data-no-dictation on the field or an ancestor), `hidden` (< 4 px, opacity 0, outside the view: the copy helpers, the live view's / a desktop's keyboard proxies), `not-text` (checkbox, number, date, colour, file…). Never a list of places. type=number is `not-text` (no caret API; a number typed as text is a text input and a target).

The capsule widens away from the field (the `anchor` edge). 28 px desk, 40×40 phone.
- THE WORDS: `boxOf(el)` — a textarea / text input by its value and caret (type=email has no caret API in Chrome: its end), a contenteditable by a Range (focused: `insertText` at the restored selection; unfocused: a range edit). A focused box takes the words as a typed edit (its own Ctrl+Z); an unfocused followed one gets `input` + `change` (its own rules run as after typing). A ONE-LINE box takes a dictated line break as a space — a dictation never types the Enter that commits a box (chat-enter-keys.js, 2026-10-14: the Outbox reject box sent on a committing Enter). The context of a followed field (PURE `followFacts`): its label (aria-label / labelledby / <label> / placeholder / title) as the title, the dialog's title or the card's words around it as the text — ≤ 600 chars, no conversation; the chat composer keeps its richer facts.

### lane channel-direct-send-sync — a direct send's receipt is the command's own answer (the owner 2026-10-21: 「如果 agent 被允许通过 VibeSpace channel 自动发送消息的话，它那一次发送指令的返回结果应该告诉它已经发出去了，而不是再产生一条在队列中的消息等着我下一次发消息来处理」; base aff72b10 = 2.369.334)
- **The defect (measured on the hub 2026-10-21 02:00–05:30Z).** An agent whose replies to a Lark chat are policy «direct»: `vibespace-channels reply` answered «sent directly (policy: direct) — proposal p-…», and minutes later the SAME outcome arrived AGAIN as a message «[Channels · Outbox] Channel receipt — proposal p-…: SENT (vendor id om_…) …» — a billed «turn nobody typed», with a copy also sitting in the person's queue view. The receipt road exists for a proposal the person must decide (approve / reject / edit travel later); for a direct send it duplicated the command's own answer (propose → sendNow → receipt() stashed the receipt mid-turn, so it drained on the agent's next turn).
- **The rule.** A command that performs an action answers with the action's outcome; a message carries only what the actor could not have learned from its own command. `src/channel-policy.js` PURE `receiptRoad(proposal, event)` → inline | message | none: inline = the CLI read it (`receipt.road:'inline'`) or is still waiting in the collect window; message = an approval-gated proposal, a direct send no CLI waited on (a job / another door) or whose CLI timed out / died, a reaction / recall (one line, next turn), a later fate change; none = the user drafted it or the drafting agent withdrew it. A MUTANT that returns `message` for an inline-collected receipt reds.
- **The engine (`src/server/channels-outbound.js`).** `propose` records `receiptCollect` on a DIRECT send whose caller passed `collect`; `receipt()` consults `receiptRoad` and, for a collecting proposal, HOLDS the message road (no stash, no wake, no queue row) and arms a one-shot fallback timer (`armCollect`, the send window ≤ 20 s, overridable by `channels.collectWindowMs`). The CLI reads the receipt words from the reply response (or polls the collect door) and CONFIRMS the read (`collectReceipt` → `receipt.road:'inline'`, the timer disarmed). A CLI that never confirms (timed out / crashed) ⇒ the timer delivers the message after all (`collectExpire`). The receipt-wake census row (`channel-receipt`) is unchanged for the message road; the inline road files no wake. `stopCollect()` drops the timers on engine stop (a held receipt re-delivers at the next boot through the existing sweep).
- **The door + the CLI.** `GET /api/agent/channels/status?id=<p>&collect=1` → `collectReceipt`. `data/bin/vibespace-channels reply` (and the same shape for the `api` direct writes) prints the receipt INLINE — «SENT (vendor id om_…) · sent as user · the recipient sees: <the honesty line>» — then confirms the read; a held send polls the door, bounded, and on timeout prints «sending — the receipt will come as a message».
- **The stash heading (the owner: 「你所有的那个通知上面都写着说它 unreachable，这个有点不 make sense」).** A held batch drained at the next turn no longer heads «Messages that arrived while this conversation was unreachable» (the conversation is taking this very turn): PURE `stashHeading(why)` words the cause the hub already knew — busy («Messages that arrived during your previous turn», a turn was running / no free lane) or paced («Messages held until this turn (a delivery earlier would have cost a wake)», idle). «unreachable» is kept ONLY for a session that truly could not be reached (renderMsgStash's default, the hand-over of a gone session). The receipt stash carries the cause; `drainStashUnderCap` heads the batch by it.
- **Gates.** test-channel-outbox +34 (the PURE road + heading tables, the real engine inline / collect / timeout-fallback / approval-gated / job legs, a source-patch RED control patching the gate to `if (false)` ⇒ the base queues a message). No regression: test-channels-agent-cli, test-channels-engine, test-channel-groups, test-stash-strip, test-notify-retry, test-channel-record, test-spend-paths, test-architecture §79 (the outbound family's context fields grow by two: `collectReceipt`, `stopCollect`).

### lane cwr-10-rebuild-race — test-channel-window-render ⑩c was red under build-server load, green alone; test-only, base 0b8c3520 = 2.369.332
- THE RED (the .333 release chain on 976b5e3b, 2026-10-21 01:27Z / 18:27 PDT, load ≈ 20+ with ~16 heavy suites beside it; red twice, green alone 7 min later on the SAME tree — /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/hotfix-333/test-channel-window-render.log + cwr-rerun.log): ⑩c, the two base-fixture asserts around scripts/test-channel-window-render.mjs:820-830 — `{"scrollTop":1499,"tall":true,"before":24,"cleared":false,"topAfterClear":1475,"started":0,"older":0,"rows":24,"atBottom":true}`. NOT the 00:18-01:00 two-day-separator window lane channel-window-render-10h fixed in .326 — that clock pin is in this base (the CLOCK PIN leg is green here) and 18:27 is outside the window.
- THE CAUSE — a FIXTURE race; the product is right. The reconnect rebuild is `app.ws._notifyState(true)` → the window's `onState` (channel-window.js) → `render()` → `renderNow()`, and renderNow runs `const c = await renderBar(); if (!c) return;` — a server round-trip to `/api/channels/<adapter>/<conv>` — BEFORE it clears the list (`list.textContent = ''`) and re-reads (`loadPage` → the `?limit=` fetch the fixture's spy counts as `started`). Under build-server load the server's answer is seconds late, so the clear and the re-read start seconds late. The base fixture used FIXED-COUNT polls — `for (i<300) sleep(10)` (~3 s) for the clear, `for (i<400) sleep(25)` (~10 s) for started — and sampled the facts before the rebuild ran: `cleared:false`, `topAfterClear` still at the bottom, `started:0`. No page was ever read (`older:0`, no `?before=`) in any run — the product's `listReady` / `pageUpVerdict` guard held. So this is the fixture sampling before the effect, not a product miss.
- REPRODUCED deterministically, co-tenant-safe (no box load, no product edit): a one-shot wait on the reconnect's own renderBar round-trip (a client-side fetch wrapper inside the ⑩c fixture, 5 s), standing in for the loaded / frozen server (the box had a main-loop stall + hub outage 18:45-18:48 PDT that evening). base shape → RED (FAILED 194/1, `cleared:false topAfterClear:1499`, matching the chain's facts); a 20 s wait-for-effect probe → GREEN with tCleared 5029 ms / tStarted 5029 ms / tParsed 5437 ms (the rebuild is merely LATE); the fix → GREEN, three times. CPU throttling (Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate) was tried first and REJECTED as the lever: at ×40 it stretched the in-renderer re-render (tParsed → 15 s) rather than the server round-trip (tCleared only 3.58 s), so no throttle both reds a 3 s poll and greens a 10 s wait — the real differential is a slow round-trip, not slow renderer compute.
- THE FIX (scripts/test-channel-window-render.mjs only, the ⑩c block): a wall-clock `waitFor(pred, ms)` bounded at 10 s replaces the two fixed-count polls — wait for the list to empty (the clear), then wait for `started>=1 && parsed===started` — and on a timeout the ✗ words NAME it («the reconnect's rebuild never cleared the list within 10 s under load» / «the rebuild never started its re-read within 10 s under load»), so a real >10 s server freeze fails clearly instead of as a cryptic `cleared:false`. The three ⑩c asserts, their green messages and the leg count (195) are unchanged.
- NOT CHANGED: src/lib/channel-window.js, src/lib/ws.js, src/lib/reconnect-queue.js — the product rebuilds correctly and reads no page on a reconnect's own clear. No version bump; agentd not rebuilt.
- GATES: fast gate (VIBESPACE_CI_LANES=2 npm run ci) on a scratch 2.369.334 bump (throwaway branch, never committed) — GREEN; test-channel-window-render 3× quiet GREEN + 3× under the 5 s renderBar stall GREEN, the base shape under the same stall RED (the control); test-architecture GREEN (npm run build); the i18n check untouched (no chrome words changed).

### lane voice-dictionary-nag — Dropline's dictionary suggestion is «not now», never a nag: a dismissal CONSUMES the words' evidence (they come back only from a new dictation), ONE item at a time filed low, 「词典建议」 with every suggested word 加入 / 忽略, voice.suggestions.mode (a fleet user 2026-10-21; base 0b8c3520 = 2.369.332)
- THE INCIDENT (a fleet user 01:48Z: 「一天到晚有这个 Dropline 让我发信息的消息, 站在我的 inbox 里」; measured read-only on their 2.369.318 data/user-todos.json): 20 «Dropline suggests adding to your dictionary» items in 8 days (10 on one day, 4 that day), 18 dismissed; the same words back after each dismissal — «CLAUDE.md» 7×, «Claude» 5, «Lark» 4, «DocuSign» 3. Three causes: the candidate rule subtracted only the VENDOR's dictionary (`known`) and re-read a conversation's OLD messages at every later dictation; the engine heard only a chip reply and the ✓ — a × (dismissed) or 「全部标为已看」 was forgotten; and every conversation filed its own item (`lastProposal` is per conversation), pinned in band 2 under urgent (lane foryou-plugin-notices). The user, 02:04Z / 02:06Z: no «never again» and no timers either (「忽略过的永不再提也太极端了」 / 「你这逻辑也不太合理」) — 主开发's correction: a dismissal CONSUMES the evidence; the A/B/C answer is pending, so rule 1 is ONE swappable PURE function.
- RULE 1 — THE EVIDENCE LEDGER (PURE src/voice-model.js): `proposalCandidates` gives each candidate its occurrences `occ` [{key, byPerson}] (`messageKey` = FNV-1a of role + text: the same message read again is the SAME evidence); per instance, per word: `{term, evidence[], consumed[], suggestedAt[], dismissedAt[]}` — `ledgerSuggested` (shown ⇒ its occurrences become evidence), `ledgerDismissed` (the evidence is CONSUMED: those occurrences never count again, the count back to 0), `ledgerAdded` (加入 ⇒ out; `known` holds it), `evidenceOf`; bounded (2 000 words, the least recently touched out; ≤ 32 evidence / ≤ 64 consumed keys a word). THE ONE FUNCTION `evidenceRule(candidates, ledger)`: a word's weight (seen + byPerson ≥ 2, as before) is re-earned only from messages it was not dismissed on — a NEW dictation that says it brings it back; no quiet period, no retire count, no blacklist. THE PACE: `suggestionPace({open, ledger, now})` — an open item ⇒ `update` (merge in place); a dismissal on this instance < 24 h ago ⇒ `wait`; else `file`; no clock ⇒ `wait`; `mergeTerms` (deduped, ≤ 24). The clock is handed in — test-voice-model pins no Date.now / new Date in the block.
- THE ENGINE (src/server/voice-teach-engine.js): the ledger is the plugin's own store file `data/voice-suggestions.json` (`ledgerFile`, wired in mounts-plugins-wiring; read once, written whole through channel-store's writeJsonAtomic, 0600; §86 reader row own-tree). The proposals' preselected words wait in ONE For-you item (`state.item` {id, terms, lang}): a later batch while it is open is merged and the item RE-WORDED IN PLACE through the store's reshaping door (the same id, `judged` dropped, its door = the newest card); filed `urgency: 'low'`; the boot reshape unpins an open item an older engine filed normal. The answers: ✓ / the 加入 chip ⇒ `addItem` (ONE /v1/terms with exactly the item's words; they leave the ledger and join the cached dictionary at once); ×, the 忽略 chip, 「全部标为已看」 (a batch) by the person ⇒ `dismissItem` (the evidence consumed; nothing sent; the batch's cards leave the sheet); the sheet card's 加入所选 / 忽略 settles that card's words in the item (re-worded, or closed by the producer — never read back as the person's ✓); the card's 忽略 consumes too (its 30-day ignore kept). A dismissal < 24 h ago holds the ITEM only — the card still lands on the sheet. THE SETTINGS LIST: `view().candidates` (every word suggested now) and `answerWord(term, 'add' | 'ignore')` + `POST /api/voice/teach/word {term, verb}` (owner-only; 404 `no-candidate`, 400 `bad-request`; the word leaves the cards and the open item, re-worded in place).
- THE BAND (PURE src/attention-model.js `bandOfRow`): a plugin's reminder filed `low` ⇒ band 5 — no pin, no badge (bands 1–4), no toast (1–2); a normal / high one still heads band 2 (the owner's 10-19 pin). src/lib/user-todos-layout.js `trayBand`: a low reminder is no pin in the For-you window's session order either.
