## 2.369.333 — 2026-10-20

### gate red — the .333 branch run (ci/hotfix-333, 976b5e3b): test-webhook-routes ✗ «the global JSON parser skips /hook/ and the pairing route» — lane feedback-forward added the forward door (`api/feedback/forward$`) to server.js OWN_BODY_RE (right: the door reads its own raw bytes after its refusals, like /hook), and the suite pins that regex VERBATIM; neither the lane nor the local affected chain ran the suite. Fix = the pin (test-only, webhook-routes-pin). Lesson: a lane touching server.js OWN_BODY_RE / auth exemptions runs test-webhook-routes.

### lane feedback-forward — ONE inbox for the maintainer: an agent's feedback filed on any instance reaches the maintainer hub, and the maintainer's mark comes back (the owner 2026-10-20 「这个功能本来就是给你用的，你自己开发个处理流程」)
- THE GAP: `vibespace-feedback` filed into THAT instance's data/feedback.json, and the maintainer (a conversation on the owner's hub) read only the hub's own store. A fleet user's reports (userW's pod: six) were read with kubectl as the pod user, and a mark made on the hub never reached the instance whose agent filed the report.
- THE BASE: one commit on int332 07561196. Lane feedback-handled-verb's `feedback.list` / `feedback.handled` and `handledVersion` live there, not on .331. The commit rides .333 by cherry-pick onto 2.369.332.
- THE FORWARD (the origin, src/server/feedback-forward.js): an instance with a telemetry forward target (`Telemetry.forwardTarget()`: telemetry.forwardUrl / forwardToken, else VIBESPACE_TELEMETRY_FORWARD_URL / _TOKEN — the target the diagnostics batches use) puts every NEW report in data/feedback-outbox.json (feedback-store `onNew`; a repeat that only bumps a count is not new; tmp + rename, mode 600) and returns, so the filing agent never waits. The pump sends one report at a time to the hub's POST /api/feedback/forward. The doors come from the forward URL: …/api/telemetry/ingest names the hub, and a path prefix before it is kept. No target ⇒ nothing queued, no file, no request.
- THE ORIGIN KEY, not the token: the fleet shares ONE forward token (deploy/helm values: «ONE shared token as both the collector's ingestToken and every sender's forwardToken»), so the token cannot name an instance.
  - Each origin mints `fk_` + 32 random bytes once, kept in its outbox file, and sends it as `X-VibeSpace-Feedback-Origin`. The hub keeps only its sha256 (16 hex).
  - Dedupe is by (origin key, origin id). The marks door answers ONLY the reports that key forwarded.
  - A pod whose data is wiped mints a new key; its old reports stay on the hub under the old one.
  - AT REST the key is a named EXCEPTION in src/vault.js SECRETS_AT_REST (with its test-key-file-law RANDOM32 row): it is no store key, it opens only this instance's own marks, and the forward and its boot pull run before any unlock — the vault locks at every start, and a pod may have none.
- THE DOORS (the hub, src/routes/feedback.js):
  - The collector's ONE verdict comes first: `collectorVerdict` in src/telemetry.js, which the /api/telemetry/ingest door now asks too. 404 `collector disabled` while VIBESPACE_TELEMETRY_INGEST_TOKEN is unset, 403 `bad token`.
  - Then the origin key (400 `origin_key_missing`).
  - The forward body is read only AFTER the token: server.js OWN_BODY_RE skips the 50 MB global parser for it, and the route's own parser takes ≤ 64 KB (413 `too_large`).
  - auth.js exempts POST /api/feedback/forward and GET /api/feedback/forward/marks with the method exact; PATCH /api/feedback/:id stays the cookie's.
- THE BELT: a forwarded report is PEER text. `store.receive` stores the text, the about and the conversation, Task Group and instance names through src/peer-text.js toAgentText. The marks that come back (the hub's note, who marked) are belted at `applyMarks` on the origin. feedback.list belts again at read; the belt is idempotent.
- THE HUB'S STORE: forwarded records sit beside the own ones with `origin {instance, id, version, key}`.
  - `publicRow` carries `origin {instance, version}`, never the key's hash. The sheet draws an origin chip (tooltip 「转自 …」 / 「… から転送」), and feedback.list rows carry `origin`.
  - `isMine` never counts a forwarded record, so the hub's agents never list another instance's report.
  - A status change on a forwarded record (the owner's PATCH or feedback.handled — the same store call) stamps `markedAt`, strictly increasing. feedback.handled answers `markBack: <instance>`.
- THE MARK-BACK IS A PULL (the hub has no door into an origin): at boot + 1 min and every 6 h the origin asks GET /api/feedback/forward/marks?since=<cursor> with the same token and key.
  - Each mark `{id (the origin's), status, version, note, by, at}` is applied to the own record through the model's setStatus; a reopen goes back too.
  - The cursor persists in the outbox file. The filing agent's `vibespace-feedback list` then says «handled in 2.369.NNN».
- THE BOUNDS (the origin):
  - The outbox holds ≤ 200 unsent reports; the oldest is dropped, counted and logged.
  - One send at a time, oldest first; the first failure ends the pass and holds the outbox 1, 2, 4 … 32 min, then 1 h, after consecutive failed passes (any answer from the hub resets it) — one request per pass while the hub is down, never one per report. A send or a marks page times out at 10 s.
  - 400 / 413 / 422 mean the hub judged THIS report, so it is dropped (counted `refused`). Everything else is retried: a 403 while a token is fixed, a 404 from a hub before this door, 429, 5xx, no answer.
- THE BOUNDS (the hub):
  - The body is ≤ 64 KB.
  - A forwarded report passes the same validate as a local one (text ≤ 2000, about ≤ 60). A future `at` is filed now, the count is clamped, and a version that is no release number is kept as null.
  - At most 200 records per origin key (that origin's least recently reported goes), inside the 500 ring.
  - Marks: 200 a page, ≤ 10 pages a pull.
- THE BACKFILL: only NEW reports would leave the pods that already hold reports (userW's six). So the first time an instance has a target — at start, or at its first new report — it also queues, ONCE, the OPEN reports already on file (oldest first, inside the 200 bound; a handled one stays home). `backfilled: true` in the outbox file keeps it to once.
- A HUB WHOSE TARGET IS ITSELF: its own forward is answered `{self: true}` and dropped from the outbox, so the report is kept once.
- FLEET (deploy/):
  - No chart change was needed: main.yaml already sets VIBESPACE_TELEMETRY_FORWARD_URL / _TOKEN / VIBESPACE_TELEMETRY_INGEST_TOKEN from the values.
  - values.yaml's comment and deploy/README.md now SAY that the target also receives agents' feedback reports (their words); the diagnostics batches stay «never content».
  - The maintainer hub needs VIBESPACE_TELEMETRY_INGEST_TOKEN set to the fleet's forward token, and the pods' forwardUrl must name the hub.
  - Not measured here (never a fleet pod): what the live pods' forwardUrl names.
- TESTS AND CENSUSES:
  - scripts/test-feedback-forward.mjs (fast, 58 checks, 0.4 s), ①–⑩. CONTROLS: the receive without the belt stores a live frame; without the dedupe a retry is a second record; marks without the key filter hand one origin's marks to another.
  - test-auth: the DOORS row and the cross-site doors loop.
  - test-peer-text-census: the feedback store row names the forwarded producer and the returning mark, with 4 new pins.
  - scripts/mount-reader-census.mjs (§86): the outbox reader row (own-tree).
  - scripts/fixtures/boot-sentinel-gets.json: the marks GET in the smoke list (test-reach-model's census; a sentinel boot has no collector token, so it answers 404 JSON).
  - ci.mjs: the fast row.
  - test-record-clear-census needed no row: its stores are the five that Clear content empties, and feedback.json was never one; the outbox holds copies of its rows.
- Gates: the fast gate on a scratch copy with package.json at .332 (the .333 heading is the next patch there; never committed) + test-feedback-forward, test-auth, test-record-clear-census, test-peer-text-census, test-vendor-whitelist and test-architecture (the lane report has the counts).

### lane job-wrapper-update-window — a job started while VibeSpace updates itself is no longer a false failure (agent feedback fb-7f7be1e24e)
- **THE INCIDENT** (the owner's hub, read-only): cron jb-dfac2435's child jb-6f23c3de, run 1792532762683 (21:46:02.68Z).
  - The run: current.log 66 B «[job-wrapper] refused: the spec path names no file of the ctl dir», exit.json code 2, no spec.*.json. Its record says cause error, with a 'message' notice delivered at 21:46:05.0Z.
  - The window: data/bin/job-wrapper.js mtime 21:45:24Z (the pull), service stop 21:46:09Z, so 45 s.
  - Who spawned it: the run's ctl dir is 0775, the .330 server's mkdir (.331 chmods 0700). The OLD server spawned it and judged it, in its 5 s sweep, before the stop.
  - The 21:29Z run and the next fire at 22:04Z exited 0.
- **THE CAUSE:** scripts/update.sh runs pull → npm install → build → restart.
  - The tracked wrapper changes at the pull; the server restarts last.
  - The .330 server spawned `[wrapper, ctl, base64(spec)]`, and .331's wrapper (lane job-spec-off-argv) takes only a spec FILE of the ctl dir.
  - Measured by hand (measure/shapes.js): the base wrapper refuses the .330 call with exactly that line, exit 2.
- **THE WRAPPER:** a versioned protocol. PROTO = 2, and the server says `--proto=N`. An older server is known by its shape: a file of the ctl dir = 2 (.331/.332); base64 JSON with an argv = 1 (≤ .330).
  - Protocol 1 is READ once, loudly: the log opens with the warning line, and the exit is the child's.
  - An unknown protocol never starts the job: exit 75, exit.json reason update_window plus both protocols, and the spec file removed unread.
  - An unreadable `--proto` is refused by name, and the spec is removed unread too. The first cut left it behind; measured.
- **THE COMPAT'S EXPIRY:** COMPAT_PROTO_1 is due at 2.369.340. test-job-model's row goes RED there, and it is fast tier, so every gate sees it. Then: remove the branch, or re-decide with evidence and move the date.
  - Why an expiry: it is a second door that takes a job's secrets from argv, kept for hubs still updating from ≤ .330.
  - Only an old caller ever uses it. The §12 M1 control proves no server of this tree writes one.
- **THE SERVER:** `--proto=` + WRAPPER_PROTO; test-jobs-engine pins it equal to the wrapper's PROTO. _finalizeRun reads reason update_window.
  - It is a WINDOW when an older server generation started the run, or the wrapper changed on disk after this server's boot and less than 15 min ago (UPDATE_WINDOW_MS).
  - In a window:
    - cause update_window, run.exit null;
    - the task is INTERRUPTED, which is outside the failure badge;
    - no owner notice, no user inbox;
    - the boot replay runs a one-shot task again (trigger update-rerun);
    - a cron child waits for its next fire (measured: _fireCron reuses the child);
    - a service is DOWN, not a crash on the supervisor's count, and the boot replay starts it.
  - Outside a window: cause wrapper-mismatch, failed, and said: «it never started — data/bin/job-wrapper.js speaks another protocol than this server (restart VibeSpace to finish its update)».
- **THE ROADS:**
  - The in-app Update (update.sh, hub and pod alike) has the window.
  - The boot auto-update has none: server.js:67 pulls and builds before jobs-wiring creates the engine at server.js:1117.
  - A new image restarts both at once.
  - update.sh is unchanged. An old server cannot be taught to wait; the protocol makes the window harmless.
  - No other server-spawned helper changed its caller contract in .331 (pty-wrapper and vibespace-api: words only).
- **TESTS:**
  - test-jobs-engine §12 (+8): the wrapper by hand as each server generation calls it, the pair pin, and the no-compat CONTROL. The argv row names --proto. M1 = the .330 call against the REAL wrapper, which still runs it, and the cmdline rows are still RED.
  - test-jobs-engine §13 (+15): the real engine across a window (task, cron child, service), the two faults, and the ≤ .332 judgment MUTANT. Total 125 → 148.
  - test-job-model +2 (the expiry row + its control): 379 → 381.
  - §86 the reader census: src/jobs.js 23 → 24 (the wrapper's mtime stat, own tree).
- **CONTROLS** (scratch trees, logs/ctl-*): C1 the base's wrapper + engine under this lane's suites ⇒ 5 protocol rows RED (the .330 call refused exit 2 — the incident's line), then the no-compat mutant's anchor guard stops the suite; C2 no boot re-run ⇒ 2 RED; C3 a cron child re-run at boot ⇒ 2 RED; C4 every mismatch a window ⇒ the 2 fault rows RED; C5 no --proto ⇒ the argv row RED (then M1's anchor guard); C6 the window still writes the user inbox ⇒ 1 RED; C7 the window counted as a service crash ⇒ 1 RED (consecutiveFails 1); in-suite: the no-compat wrapper and the ≤ .332 judgment engine (failed exit=75 + a notice + the inbox).
- **THE SEAM WITH .332:** 2.369.332 carries lane mirror-331-reds-security's test-agent-output-sinks §3. Its CONTROL hands the wrapper the base64 call and expects a refusal; with this lane that call RUNS.

### lane conversations-archive-verb — the opener's lifecycle: ONE PURE reach rule, `conversations.archive`, the failure notice names verb · target · reason · door (the owner 2026-10-20 22:0xZ 「这些不用 archive 吗」; base 36190358 = 2.369.331)
- THE GAP, measured on the owner's hub (.331): 主开发's key (grant `always`) opened lane workers through conversations.open; `vibespace-api conversations end` on them answered not_granted («the key is not granted to that conversation (nor to one of its Task Groups)») while `rename` on the same targets had succeeded hours earlier. CAUSE: the opener's reach was a Map in memory (src/server/conversation-ops.js `openedBy`, webui id → key) — the hub's .331 restart emptied it; the engine's `reach` closure (grants only) then judged the key's own workers strangers. The verbs did not judge differently — the fact was lost between them.
- ONE RULE: PURE src/automation-keys.js `reachVerdict({keyId, caller, target: {conversationId, webuiId?, groups?}, grants, opened})` → (a) the key OPENED it (an `opened` row of the store — the engine writes one per successful open: the webui id at once, the conversation id when the CLI has reported it; a later reach by webui id fills it in), (b) a grant of the key names it (the conversation or one of its Task Groups), (c) it is the caller. Every verb that names another conversation (status / rename / bind / end / archive / invite) asks it through the engine's `reach(target)`; conversation-ops' `reached()` hands the live facts and carries the target's NAME on a refusal (the notice). data/automation-keys.json gained `opened` (≤ 2000 rows, FIFO; a row's key gone ⇒ the row drops at read). test-automation-keys ⑯: the 11-row table (self · opener by conversation id / by webui id before the id was known / after the END · a grant to the conversation / to its Task Group · a stranger · another key's open · another key's grant · an unopened webui id · nothing) + the MUTANT without (a) ⇒ RED (exactly the three opener rows); ⑰: a fresh engine over the same store (a restart) still reaches (status), ends and archives the worker; another key the coordinator holds does not reach it (the row is the opener's, not the caller's).
- THE VERB `conversations.archive` (act, billed false; args target · force? · resolveAsks? — yes/no fields, absent = not set): a live target ⇒ reach → the target's open For-you asks (`asksOf`: the store's open items under its key, by agent, not a notice — `asks_open` naming their ids unless resolveAsks dismisses them, resolvedBy `automation:<key>`) → the turn (src/server/turn-facts.js `turnOf`: running / waiting ⇒ `subject_busy` unless force — judged before the asks are dismissed, so a refusal changes nothing) → `endConversation` by the key → `archive(sessionKey)` = src/routes/persistence.js `archiveSession` (the sidebar's own archivedSessions write + the user-state-updated broadcast every client applies — never a second implementation; a bare legacy id counts as listed). An ENDED target (no live session) is resolved by the wiring's `deadOf`: `<backend>:<id>` as given, else the backend from the keys user-state's names / configs / modes or the Task Groups still carry, else claude; its Task Groups from tasks.groupsForSession; a dead `sess-…` names nothing durable ⇒ not_found. Already listed and nothing live to end ⇒ `already_archived` (409, like subject_busy / asks_open). ### lane key-instance-scope — a grant's REACH: 只有它开的会话 / 这些岗位的会话 / 整个 VibeSpace (the owner 2026-10-20 23:2xZ 「key 应该可以被授权在整个 vibe space 上工作」; base b8855d45 = lane conversations-archive-verb on 36190358 = .331; BUILD, ONE commit, no bump)
- THE ASK: after b8855d45 a key's reach over a target was the opener / a grant naming the target or its Task Group / the caller — the maintainer's key could not end or archive lane workers opened before the key existed or by another road (the owner's own create). The owner wants a grant that works on the WHOLE instance.
- THE REACH IS A GRANT FIELD (PURE src/automation-keys.js): `reach` on the grant row — `'opened'` (absent ⇒ this; the narrowest: nothing beyond the three doors above) | `{taskGroups: [ids]}` (their conversations too) | `'instance'` (every conversation of this instance, present and later). `reachOf` is the closed shape (a damaged value ⇒ the row is NO grant — fail closed, never read as wider nor quietly as narrower; `grant()` / `setReach()` refuse it `bad_args`); `reachVerdict({…, reach})` gains ONE row after self / opener / grant — instance ⇒ ok by 'instance', groups ∩ the target's ⇒ ok by 'groups', else not_granted whose `why` names the reach and the door and whose `reach` says the kind. `useVerdict` answers the reach a use rides: the WIDEST of the caller's always-grants (`widestReach`: instance › the groups' union › opened), else the once-grant's — a caller holding the key by two roads acts by the wider. MUTANT (test-automation-keys ⑯): `instance` let through for an `opened` grant ⇒ the four refused rows of the base table + the two opened rows of the reach table RED, nothing else moves.
- THE OWNER'S DOORS: the first-use card (src/server/automation-engine.js `ask`) carries `action.groups` = the caller's Task Group ids (space-joined — an action field is a scalar) and a second detail sentence saying what the reach is; the tray row (src/lib/user-todos-row.js) and the For-you window pane (src/lib/inbox-window.js) draw 作用范围 radios — 只有它开的会话 (checked) · 这些岗位的会话 (only when the caller is in one) · 整个 VibeSpace (red, title «this key may act on every conversation here, including yours») — ONE spelling in src/lib/automation-reach.js; the pressed answer carries `reach: opened | groups | instance` (`POST /api/automation/asks/:askId`; `engine.answer` turns groups into `{taskGroups: <the card's>}`, none ⇒ bad_args). The Vault window's key row: every 授权给 chip carries a REACH chip (vault-automation.js; 整个 VibeSpace red with that title) — a click opens the reach dialog (three rows + the Task Groups list) ⇒ `POST /api/automation/grants/:grantId/reach` ⇒ `engine.setReach` (the same store write, audited `key.reach` with the kind); 授权给… picks the reach of the grants it adds (`{subjects, reach}`). ### lane attention-policy-ui-red — the .332 blocker: test-attention-policy-ui's second ⚙ press toggled its OWN popover shut (the harness fires no pointerdown, so onOutsidePress never closed it on the view switch); test-only, base 07561196 = int332 on 2.369.331
- THE RED (runner Actions 39506174827 heavy shard 1/6, the only red of the run; and a plain box): test-attention-policy-ui died at scripts/test-attention-policy-ui.mjs:251 `flip(d, DIRECT)` with the page's `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'querySelector')` at `<anonymous>:1:190`. `flip` (:207) finds the DIRECT `.settings-row` in `[data-settings-block="attention"]` and clicks its toggle; the attention block was GONE, so `.find(…)` returned undefined and `r.querySelector('.settings-toggle input')` threw (col ~190 = `r.querySelector`, hence «undefined» not «null (reading 'click')»). The runner log carried no assertion line (ci.mjs's tail did not print the suite's stdout).
- THE CAUSE (ONE, deterministic — not a race): the .332-new createPopover ANCHOR-TOGGLE (lane menu-close-residue, B-5bd5 ②, src/lib/utils.js:580, detached return :594) closes a popover whose anchor is pressed while it is open. The suite opens the ⚙ attention door (channels-panel.js:2303 `createPopover(anchor, 'chan-attn-pop')`; door attnBtn :1190, data-attention-door :1191), flips a row (:238, succeeds — so the DIRECT label and the 12-row count are intact), switches the channel view 全部→需关注 (:245/:248), then presses the ⚙ AGAIN (:249) before flipping DIRECT back (:251). In the PRODUCT a real view-switch press (a trusted pointerdown) closes the popover first — onOutsidePress binds pointerdown (utils.js:492), never click — so the second ⚙ press REOPENS a closed door. But a synthetic element.click() fires NO pointerdown, so the popover stayed open and the second press TOGGLED it shut → no block → flip threw. On .331 createPopover had no toggle (it rebuilt), so the re-press rebuilt the block → the .331 mirrors passed on the runner.
- THE FIX (TEST ONLY — the product is correct and unchanged): :249 opens the door only if its popover is closed — `if (!((await d.ev(BLOCK)) || {}).inPop) await d.ev(…DOOR.click…)`. A door already open under the hand is not pressed again; where the view-switch press had closed it (the product) this reopens it. createPopover's universal toggle is untouched — it is guarded by test-outside-press.mjs (m)-legs (:418 detached return, :422 «the anchor pressed once more OPENS again (a toggle, not a lock)», :433 toggle:false = a programmatic rebuild only; a user re-press is not a programmatic rebuild, so toggle:false is NOT the right opt-out here).

### lane dm-reply-infers — a plain reply to an agent's message, judged ONCE by the decision API (backlog B-6b4b, userW's feedback; the owner 2026-10-20 「用 decision api 判定一次就行了，也不一定非得对方下一条就是回复，错误 trigger 还是挺贵的」)
- THE MISS: `reply-to-sent` (src/channel-filter.js `sentHit`) fires only on the vendor's reply MARKERS (a quote / reply id, a topic or Slack-thread root, a later record in a MAIL thread — lane channel-reply-real removed the old direct-chat clock clause after two unrelated messages woke an agent). userW answered an agent's 1:1 Lark message two hours later with a plain message and nobody was woken.
- THE RULE'S DOOR (one grammar, one validator, two doors): `reply-to-sent` gains an opt-in field `infer: true` — no new rule kind. `validateRule` keeps `infer: true`, stores `false` / absent as `{kind}` alone (the old row byte for byte), refuses a non-boolean `infer-flag` (worded by `filterProblemText`). The Notify… dialog: a «Also judge plain replies (LLM plugin)» box under the rule's row (`dialog-check-row` — `.dialog-body label`'s column flex would stack it), its note folded until ticked, the plugin off / no key / the Rules switch off SAID on the box with Open Plugins (`inferOffWhy` — the marker road works either way). The CLI: `vibespace-channels watch … --reply-to-sent --infer` (src/channel-watch-spec.js `BOOL_FLAGS` — the first value-less non-rule flag; `--infer` alone ⇒ `infer-without-reply-to-sent`). `ruleWhy` says «(plain messages judged)».
- THE SCOPE (PURE `F.inferCandidate(record, ctx)` → `{sent, key, gapMin}` | null): an UNMARKED peer message — no `replyTo`, no `root`, the classifier's kind `plain` with no quote / topic, on a thread-only channel (Slack) no foreign thread_ts; not a mail thread (marker (c) reads it); not one of the principal's own sends; a marker hit stays the marker road (never judged); and THIS principal (an agent, or a group member for its OWN sends — `ctx.sentByMe` per member, the reply-to-sent fan-out) SENT into the same conversation within `channels.replyInferHours` (the ONE setting: 1–168, default 24 — `F.INFER.hours`) BEFORE it. The newest such send is the one asked about; EVERY candidate is judged (never "the next message is the reply"). Outside the scope nothing is judged — no vendor call.
- THE JUDGMENT (ORCH, src/server/channels-engine.js `preInfer`, beside the decision rule's `preJudge`, BEFORE any filter runs): one `decisionEngine.judge('reply-infer', {sent, reply, gap}, {questions: [DM.REPLY_INFER_QUESTION], memo: {id: record id, sent: sent id}, accountNever})` per candidate (one per record × send however many watchers share it; a group's `rest` item never asks). The parts = the sent text (the outbox proposal's text, ≤ 2 000 — the sent entries now carry `id` = the send's first vendor id and `text`) + the candidate's text + the gap in minutes — NOTHING else of the conversation. The question (src/decision-model.js beside INBOX_QUESTION): a fixed predicate `answers_sent` — is the later message an answer to the agent's message (not a new topic, small talk, or for someone else); its probability is the score; yes = p ≥ `F.INFER.threshold` 0.80 (a wrong wake is expensive — above the decision rule's 0.70 default). The plan row `reply-infer`: wake path, batch 1, parts sent 1 000 / reply 1 000 / gap 60, record ceiling 700 tokens, memo `['use', 'id', 'sent', 'question']` (`question` = `v${REPLY_INFER_VERSION}`: a reworded question is a new key) — a record is judged ONCE against one send, for ever (no clock in the key; a re-pass, a restart, a second watcher answer from the memo). FEATURE_OF `reply-infer` → `rules` (the LLM plugin's Rules switch); then the key, the backoff and the day's budget (the owner's 1 USD) like every use; the journal line carries `p` (the decision ledger keeps the yes and the no). The readout names the use «Plain replies».
- THE CAPS: inside D1's daily budget, plus the conversation's own hour cap (`F.INFER.perHour` 20 — reserved with its check, given back when no call was made, the decision rule's `decisionHours` pattern; D1's `perHour` counts ONE engine-wide window across every use, so a per-use cap lives in the caller). A refusal (the budget, a backoff, the switch, no key, the hour cap) = no hit + the decision ledger's refused row + ONE channels journal line per reason per conversation an hour: `reply-infer — N plain message(s) not judged — <why> (no hit, no wake)`.
- THE OUTCOME: yes ⇒ the existing reply-to-sent hand-over to the sender (the same wake / next-turn / digest road, the same card, the same money door `channel-message`): the why = `judged an answer to your message of <HH:MM UTC>` (`F.INFER_WHY`, channel-words `wakeWhyText` + zh / ja), the hit's `sent` carries `score` (the pending row keeps it) and the hand-over line reads `Reply to your message (<when>, "<first words>", judged 0.86): …`. No ⇒ nothing; the memo remembers the no.
- THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW (read-only, before the commit) found no high finding; fixed: (M1) a judgment that cannot change the filter's answer is never bought — PURE `F.inferWorth(filter, record, ctx)`: `any` with another rule that already hits (the record notifies anyway), `every` with another rule that misses (it never can), matched with the batch's decisions / subjectOf / principal; (M2) the pre-pass ran its judgments one after another before the batch's other watchers — now ≤ 4 in flight (`INFER_PARALLEL`; the hour slot is still reserved in the check's synchronous step); (L3) one record the scope cannot read is skipped by name, never the pass; (L4) a message with no words is never a candidate; (L5) the question's version rides the memo key. SAID, not changed: only the newest send before a message is asked about (an answer to an older send after a newer one is missed — fails closed); the hour cap is checked before the memo, so a re-delivered record at the cap is not re-answered from the memo (records are fresh once); a group row with N members who each sent in the window costs up to N judgments a message (one per member's own send — the per-member law); a Lark `[image]` / `[sticker]` reply is judged on its placeholder (an image can be the answer — the judge says).
- GATES MOVED: test-channel-filter ⑮'s one-line control `const sent = ctx && ctx.sentByMe …` (the scope names its map `sends`); test-decision-model's judge-site census read the use names from a hand list without `reply-infer` (now `M.USES`, + a row: ONE `reply-infer` site, the channels engine); test-settings-view's advanced-tier bound 90 → 95 (the new row is the 91st); test-architecture 44d (docs/settings.md regenerated); heavy test-channels-aggregate ③g «every channels.* number setting is read by the engine with the schema's own default and bounds» — the first heavy run was RED twice (the pre-pass read the setting by hand): the engine now reads it through `setting()` with an ENGINE_BOUNDS row (24 / 1 / 168). ⑯'s words census (no «24 h» / «next message» beside a reply-to-sent word) holds: the window is named as «Settings › Channels», never as a number.
- NEW LEGS: test-channel-filter ⑲ (PURE — the RED control: the marker-only rule misses the 2 h plain answer; the scope's ten never-candidates; the span from the setting; two sends × three messages; worth-a-judgment both ways; per-member keys; yes / no / refused / absent; marker hit never reads a judgment; the hand-over; the validator + the CLI door; OFF = byte-identical over 15 fixtures against a copy without the judged road; MUTANTS RED: no span, no unmarked checks, no threshold, the marker-only copy); test-channel-agent-watch ⑪ (the REAL channels engine + D1's REAL engine over an in-process provider, zero vendor calls: a 2 h DM answer judged yes ⇒ ONE call, ONE wake; the parts carry nothing else; the ledger row with p; judged no ⇒ no wake, the same record again + a restart answer from the memo — MUTANT: an engine asking without the memo calls twice ⇒ RED; outside the scope / the owner's own ⇒ judge() never called; a quote ⇒ the marker wake, never judged; budget 0 ⇒ no call, the refused row + the journal line; `any` + a keyword that hits / `every` + one that misses ⇒ 0 judgments; 22 messages ⇒ 20 judgments, said once; a group judges each member against its own send; infer off ⇒ nothing judged, a quote still wakes); test-decision-model ㉑ (the row, the question, the memo key, the scrubbed input, the gates in the engine, the readout); test-vendor-whitelist (the allowlist keeps its 5 rows — no new vendor site: one `decisionEngine.judge('reply-infer'` line, no request primitive in the pre-pass); heavy test-decision-rule F (the box in Chrome: off by default, ticked ⇒ the note, Save ⇒ `{kind, infer: true}`, unticked ⇒ `{kind}` alone; phone 390 zh with the plugin off ⇒ the off line + Open Plugins).
- WHERE THE BRIEF'S SUITES ARE: test-channel-groups is the AGENT groups suite (vibespace-msg — no channels engine), so the engine rows went to test-channel-agent-watch, where reply-to-sent's own engine legs live; test-channels-groups-ui is the fast IM-panel suite, so the dialog's chrome leg went to heavy test-decision-rule (the Notify… dialog harness). ### lane automation-open-permission-resolve — two follow-ups of the automation keys: q-049 M2 (`default` is not a cap) + B-dbba (`open --name` ignored); base 07dbe6a1 = 2.369.329
- THE FINDING (design-desk/q-049-open-limits-verify.md rows 3 + «M2»): `conversations.open` without `--permission` passes NO flag to the harness (adapters/claude-code.js pushes `--permission-mode` only when a value is set), so the local claude's own three-layer config decided — a key whose `permissionModes` was `['default']` bounded nothing (bypassPermissions in a project's settings.json ran). The .325 follow-up had already reworded the label 「CLI 自己的设置」; this lane resolves it.
- THE RESOLUTION, three layers: (1) PURE `src/permission-rules.js claudeDefaultMode(record)` — over the typed record claudeRulesRecord already builds (its layers in the CLI's resolution order, user → project → local → [flag] → managed, a managed drop-in before its base), the LAST present layer that sets `permissions.defaultMode` wins; `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"` in any layer turns a resolved bypassPermissions back into the built-in default (both layers named); nothing set ⇒ `default` with no layer; an unavailable or non-claude record ⇒ `ok: false` (nothing resolved — never read `mode` as a fact). (2) ORCH `src/server/permission-rules.js resolveDefaultMode({backend, cwd, home})` — the caps row (`settings-files`, never a backend id) picks claude, ONE reader built on first use (`create({})` — nothing spawns) reads the hierarchy of THAT cwd off disk through the existing `readClaudeRules`, then the PURE resolution; codex / shell ⇒ `ok: false unsupported-harness`. (3) PURE `src/automation-keys.js permissionResolvedVerdict(limits, resolved)` — the RESOLVED mode must be in the key's list, else `permission_not_allowed` (403, the same code as a named mode outside the list) with the why «the CLI's own setting (project, /x/.claude/settings.json) is bypassPermissions; this key allows default, acceptEdits»; `resolved` null / not ok ⇒ the harness's own `default` stands (openLimitsVerdict already judged it).
- THE ENGINE (src/server/automation-engine.js `limitsJudge`, now async): the folder judge FIRST (openLimitsVerdict — a cwd outside the roots is refused before any config is read: the project layer follows the folder, and a folder the key does not reach is never read), then — only when the open names no permission mode — `openFacts.permissionDefault(realCwd, backend)` (the hub's wiring in mounts-plugins-wiring.js hands `resolveDefaultMode`; the PURE module requires nothing; no resolver wired = the old behaviour, the gates' fakes) and the resolved verdict; a read that THROWS refuses (fail closed, the failure named). Both judge sites (before the first-use card, after the grant) await it. The refusal carries `resolved {mode, layer}` beside the key's limits; the audit line keeps the code.
- THE PICKER (src/lib/vault-automation.js): the `default` row says 「CLI 自己的设置（现在是 X）」 — X the harness table's word for the resolved mode (内置默认 when no file sets one), the file as the row's title. GET /api/automation/keys (src/routes/automation.js, the same door) carries `permissionNow` per opening key (resolved for its first cwdRoot — 边界…) and `limitChoices.permissionNow` (the hub's own folder, `process.cwd()` — 铸造…, whose roots are not yet picked); null when the hub cannot say and the row then reads as before. i18n: zh / ja for the four new keys.
- B-dbba (observed 2026-10-20 on .323, the owner's first real use): `conversations open --name` was ignored — `src/conversation-spec.js wireOf` sent the name as `name`, while src/ws-create.js reads `data.sessionName` (the New session dialog sends `sessionName`; `name` is read only by the opencode-pty and tmux roads). The brief said "the ws create carries `customNames`" — it does not: the create path sets `session.name` + `_nameExplicit` + meta `nameExplicit` (the sidebar's own customNames store is the rename's). Fix: wireOf rides `sessionName`; the record is named at its create, the `created` answer / `conversations.status` / the audit line carry it; the first-use card of an open gains a first detail line «This call would open "<name>" in <cwd>.» (unnamed: «…a conversation in <cwd>.», i18n with params — the record-clear census needed no new row: the receiver is the call's own args, bounded).
- NOT DONE (named): a non-claude harness (codex, opencode) is not resolved — its `default` stays the harness's own, as before (no settings-files rung; the caps row says so); the mint dialog resolves for the hub's own folder, not for a root picked in the editor (the brief's "server cwd when none"); the resolved mode is NOT carried into the spawn as a flag (the CLI resolves the same files; a TOCTOU between the judge and the spawn is the folder's owner editing their own settings).

### lane browser-daemon-survives-update — the agent browser comes back after a server update: a restart judges the page's answers, a daemon whose browser ended is ended, a boot re-owns or ends every daemon it finds (backlog B-1574 — userW, profile jarvis-work, four freezes 10-05..10-18, each a working day's browser; 主开发's dispatch 14:51Z; base 2096f10f = 2.369.328)
- **Measured first** (agent-browser 0.38.2 + this box's Chrome 154 headless, a scratch HOME / XDG / socket dir; the lane's probes):
  - every renderer SIGSTOPped ⇒ `/json/version` and `/json/list` answer in 1 ms and `session info` answers active:true, while a direct `Runtime.evaluate` on the page is silent for 5 s (its `Page.getNavigationHistory` answers in 1 ms) and the agent's own `eval` fails "CDP command timed out: Runtime.evaluate" at 30 s. That is userW's freeze: the keeper's verdict (`/json/version`) never fired, so `restart` was refused browser_answering;
  - Chrome SIGKILLed ⇒ the daemon reaps it and lives on idle (1–3 CPU ticks a minute) with `session info` active:true for as long as anyone asks; only its next command relaunches Chrome, in place at about:blank, in 174–222 ms;
  - the whole Chrome SIGSTOPped ⇒ `session info` still answers; the daemon's own next command killed and relaunched Chrome after 38 s, the tabs lost;
  - the daemon SIGSTOPped ⇒ Chrome answers directly in 1 ms while the agent's commands and `session info` time out.
- **1. The restart verdict** (src/browser-stuck.js, PURE, beside `restartAdmission`): `pageAnswerVerdict` over ONE bounded ask of every page — src/server/browser-viewport.js `pageAnswers`: `/json/list`, then per page one socket with `Runtime.evaluate 1+1` (the renderer: `answered`) and `Page.getNavigationHistory` (the browser's side of the tab: `reached`), bounded by `PAGE_ANSWER_MS` 5 s (a healthy page answers in 1–5 ms, 16 busy tabs p95 25 ms — 5 s is 1000× that and a sixth of the agent's own 30 s command timeout). The admission, first match wins:
  - the user ⇒ ok; a person driving ⇒ take_over_first; the keeper's standing verdict ⇒ ok;
  - a page dialog / prompt / passkey on the conversation's tab (the dialog watch's fact) ⇒ browser_answering with its own door (held, not hung);
  - the page list unanswered, or no page answering ⇒ ok;
  - every page answering while the agent's last commands timed out through the driver (the watch's `unresponsive` by timeouts) ⇒ ok (`driver`: the page answers, its helper does not);
  - else browser_answering, NAMING what answered and what did not, with the `tab close` door.
  The keeper's `restartProfile` asks at the restart (`askPages`; seams `pageAsk`, `pageAnswerMs`) and its journal line says why. No `--force`: the design has no such word. The route and the CLI are unchanged (the CLI's usage line says the rule).
- **2. A daemon whose browser ended is ended** (src/browser-orphans.js, the other half of daemon-orphan-end): a daemon of ours that no LIVE record keeps (a stopped record, or none) whose Chrome has been gone — or whose DevTools endpoint has not answered (the census asks it, ≤ `ANSWER_ASK_MS`) — for `BROWSER_ENDED_MS` 60 s is ended by identity with its Chrome and its Xvfb, whoever leases it and however recent its last command.
  - The journal line, the row's note (`endedNote`) and `status` (`browserCell` now shows a stopped record's note) say it — never a silent exit.
  - A live record's daemon stays the tick's: healed in place while leased, closed by name, or judged unresponsive (keepers report a hang, they never kill one).
  - The daemon has no Chrome watch of its own (measured), so the check lives in the keeper's census, every 60 s: ended within 2 min of its browser's end. 60 s = twelve ticks; the tick heals a kept daemon's Chrome within one tick and a relaunch takes ~0.2 s.
  - `daemonsFromRows` reads a Chrome's endpoint off its own argv (`port`, `dir`; the main process's argv is NUL-separated, its children rewrite their titles — measured).
- **3. A server restart re-owns or ends** (PURE `reownVerdict`): at boot each daemon of THIS instance is judged by its own `session info` AND its pages.
  - Re-owned when a page is reached, or when nothing listens at its endpoint (its Chrome is gone; its next command relaunches in place).
  - Ended with its Chrome when its daemon does not answer, runs no browser, or its list / pages stay silent within the bound.
  - Two roads: `adoptAll` (a live record — it used to adopt on `session info` alone, so a wedged browser came back `ready`) and the boot census `bootReown` (a running daemon a stopped record names, or its launch mark names — what a pre-fix boot left behind).
  - The auto-update (scripts/update.sh → a systemd restart) is exactly this path. A box with no browser CLI to ask keeps the old reading (`cliAsked`).
- **4. ### lane menu-close-residue — a menu closes on a press INTO a frame, and its anchor toggles (B-5bd5; the owner 2026-09-26: the two residues lane M «lane-popover-close» aa4e7b9d left)
- THE RESIDUES: ① a press inside an `<iframe>` (a Web view window, a plugin window, the Channels mail frame, a Design artboard) is dispatched in the FRAME's document — the parent's capture-phase pointerdown (lane M's one closer, utils.js `onOutsidePress`) never fires, so an open menu stayed open over the frame; ② ⚙ pressed while its menu was open REBUILT the menu: the anchor is exempt from the closer (the popover was still open at the click), and `createPopover`'s dedup removed the open one for the handler to open a new one — every anchor that opens a popover under itself had the same residue.
- THE MEASUREMENT (the lane's probe: a two-origin page under headless Chrome, real CDP presses into a same-origin frame, a cross-origin frame — 127.0.0.1 vs localhost — and a sandboxed `srcdoc` frame; the report's §1): every frame kind alike — the parent sees NO pointerdown / mousedown, `focusout` on the previously focused element only when one was focused (relatedTarget null — no signal), and ALWAYS `window` blur with `document.activeElement` ALREADY the `<iframe>` element and `document.hasFocus()` still TRUE. A REAL blur to another top-level window (a second target brought to front): blur with activeElement unchanged (the menu row) and hasFocus() FALSE; with a frame holding the focus that blur never reaches the parent at all. The brief's simulation `window.dispatchEvent(new Event('blur'))` with the body active: active BODY, hasFocus() true. So the signal is `window` blur judged by the active element being a frame, hasFocus() as the belt; focusout is no signal.
- THE FIX ① (ONE closer extension, nothing per site): PURE `shouldCloseOnBlur({ active, el, excludes, pageFocused, ignored, connected })` in src/lib/outside-press.js (the table: gone > no-active > not-a-frame > page-unfocused > inside > excluded > ignored > frame; `FRAME_TAGS` = keyboard-yield.js's isFrame family IFRAME / FRAME / OBJECT / EMBED); `onOutsidePress` also listens to `window` blur under the same AbortController, `once` and `ignore` rule, reading document.activeElement + document.hasFocus() — every createPopover / showContextMenu / attachPopoverClose surface and the eight hand-built sites get it. Guarded by `typeof window` (test-taskbar-group re-evaluates the helper's source with injected free names and no window); its body says neither preventDefault nor stopPropagation (test-architecture §59c reads the helper's text).
- THE FIX ② (ONE place): `createPopover` stamps `pop._anchor`; its dedup, finding the open popover of the class hanging off the SAME anchor, CLOSES it and hands back a DETACHED element (`_closedByAnchor`) the caller fills unseen — so ⚙ (the toolbar button and the phone's), the session card's ⚙, the explorer's View / Upload, the minimap outline, Share…, the reaction chips' who-list and picker, the live browser's cap chip, the mini inbox, the attention door, the taskbar's window list, the task bind / folders / status popovers and the office offer now TOGGLE (pressed, or Enter on the focused button — the toggle is keyed on the anchor, not on a press); a CURSOR-placed popover is not an anchor's (the doc link bar / comment offer / note — their "anchor" is the whole pane, every press a new place; the usage dashboard's panel editor) and `opts.toggle === false` opts a programmatic rebuild out (the explorer's View menu `rebuild` removes first, so it never toggles). ALREADY TOGGLING before, unchanged: the sidebar's status / backend filter buttons (a class check in the handler), the principal picker (`isConnected`), the stream pill ⋯ (`had`), the stream details (`toggle()`), the taskbar group chooser (an existing one is pinned, never re-created); `showContextMenu` has no anchor.
- A FACT MET ON THE WAY: the Web view window HIDES a frame whose document it cannot read (its X-Frame-Options heuristic) and says the site blocked embedding — a Web view frame is only ever same-origin; the app's opaque-origin frames are its sandboxed ones (plugin windows, the mail frame, the Design artboards, the docx / file viewers), and the Design canvas SHIELDS its artboards (the pointer is the canvas's) until the focused view (a double-click) or Comment mode lifts the shield — only a live artboard takes a press.
- NOT A CHAT POPOVER: the brief's "a chat popover, focus into the artboard" — the chat message popover needs a running conversation; the hand-built `onOutsidePress` call it makes is the one the usage popup makes (once:false, hidden by class), exercised on the live artboard frame instead.
- GATES: test-outside-press ALL PASS 68 (was 40: the blur table, the window-blur path under a recording fake window, createPopover's anchor toggle under the fake DOM, two more patched copies — the helper without its blur listener stays open on a frame, createPopover without the toggle rebuilds ⚙'s menu) · test-popover-frame-close ALL PASS 49 ×3 alone (20.4 / 20.65 / 20.71 s wall at load ~9; the pre-fix bundle built in ~250 ms) · test-gear-menu ALL PASS · test-architecture ALL PASS 749 (inside npm run build it named two reds first: §57b the new suite without endRootedProcesses, §82 three INDEX rows over 300 chars — both fixed) · test-ci-gate-tiers 109 · test-ci-gate 68 · test-affected-model 66 · test-doc-comment-pop 41 · test-taskbar-group 82 · test-stream-stats 44 · test-changelog-style 40 (a scratch worktree at package 2.369.331) · test-design-docs 38 · test-codex-effort-meta 253 · the fast gate on a scratch worktree at HEAD with package.json 2.369.331: ALL GREEN — 450 suites in 254 s (test-outside-press 99 ms in lane 1; the snapshot worktree removed). Report with the measurement per frame kind, the anchors table and the logs: /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/menu-close-residue/report.md.

### lane statesync-last-arrival — StateSync's last-arrival class (B-cede; first seen 2.112.6, re-seen by lane stage-blank verify r4 Z3)
- THE BUG: the server answered no `state-set` and every remote `state-sync` op landed on arrival (`_applyOp`), so two clients setting one key within a round trip each took the OTHER's set last: each device ended on the other's (older-for-it) value while the server kept the later one — crossed until the next op or an enter(). Measured with the real client StateSync over the real SyncStore behind verify r4's two staged devices (the Z3 reproducer, copied into the lane dir): base crossed 4/15 reproducer rows (d=200 o=100; d=500 o=100/250/400 — the measured 4/15 shape) and 7/7 at the brief's offsets d ∈ {0,1,2,5,10,20,50} at a 100 ms hop; the fix 0/22.
- THE FRAMES (`src/sync-store.js`): `set(key, value, senderWs, basedOn)` / `delete(…)` answer the SENDER with `state-ack {type, store, key, version}` (the version its set produced; a delete of a key the store does not hold is answered with the store's version and broadcast to nobody, so no set waits) and stamp the op (broadcast + ring, so a resync replay carries them) with `from` (a per-socket id minted by the hub in a WeakMap, `c<n>` — never the client's text) and `basedOn` (the store version the sender had seen, a non-negative integer or omitted). A hub write (no socket) carries neither and is acked to nobody. `src/ws-handler.js`'s state-set case passes `data.basedOn`; the client's `state-set` sends it. The ws ctx contract (test-ws-contract) is untouched — it pins ctx dependencies, not frame fields; the frame list in kb-api.md and kb-design-lessons §13 gains `state-ack` deliberately.
- THE VERDICT (`src/sync-arrival.js`, PURE, test-architecture's PURE set): `arrivalVerdict({remote: {version, from}, own: {ackedVersion, pending}})` → no server version ⇒ apply (as before) · an own set of the key awaits its ack ⇒ queue · version ≤ the own acked set's ⇒ drop · else apply; `ARRIVAL_TABLE` = the five rows. The brief's `self` input is not taken: the sender learns its version from its own `state-ack`, so no client ever has to recognise its id in a broadcast — `from` rides for the receiver's record and the race's evidence.
- THE CLIENT (`src/lib/utils.js` StateSync): per store, per KEY — `pending` (own sets not acked, a count), `acked` (the last acked set's version), `held` (remote ops waiting). `set()` counts the pending set and sends `basedOn`; `_applyOp` advances `s.version` by max and asks the verdict at its ONE call site (queue ⇒ held, drop ⇒ nothing, apply ⇒ the op lands and the key's acked entry goes — every later op is newer still); `_applyAck` records the version, advances `s.version` and, at the key's last outstanding ack, releases its held ops back through `_applyOp`. A socket drop clears `pending` and releases every held op (judged without the lost ack; the resync then replays the own op if it landed). A full snapshot holds a pending key's value the same way (its value becomes an op at the snapshot's version, through `_applyOp` ⇒ held, dropped at the ack) — ④b measured this red before the hold: the snapshot replaced the own offline set and the client stayed on the older value while the server took the set. Per key, not per store as the brief worded it: another key's op is never the own set's business (the drafts store holds every chat's draft) — a per-store verdict loses it (§6 control).
- WHY THE ORDER IS SOUND: a socket is FIFO and the server writes in arrival order, so every op the server ordered before an own set reaches the sender before that set's ack; a queued op is therefore older than the ack that releases it, and after the ack every live op is newer. The clock is the store version only — never a wall clock.
- `s.version` now also advances with acks: a client that only ever wrote (one device) used to keep version 0, so its reconnect always took a full snapshot and the rollback defense never saw its own writes; now it resyncs by ops and a snapshot below its acked version is the rollback branch.
- GATE: scripts/test-sync-arrival.mjs (fast, in-process, deterministic — a discrete-event clock, FIFO links per direction, no timer): §1 the verdict table + its one caller; §2 THE RACE — 21 seeded rows (seed 5eedcede: per offset one symmetric 10/10 ms row + two seeded orders and latencies 1–30 ms), both clients on the server's value after quiescence and neither ever holding a value older than one it had acked (every frame recorded per client); 18/21 rows truly race (each basedOn < the other's version); §3 another key's op lands while an own set is pending; §4 a reconnect — the missed ops, the full snapshot (a ring gap), a set in flight when the socket drops (landed / lost); §5 the frames; §6 CONTROLS — the pre-fix client (the call answers 'apply') crosses 18/21 rows and holds older than acked in 18, takes the missed op and the snapshot over its own offline set; a per-store verdict never releases another key's op. test-doc-comments-sync and test-feedback-routes re-pinned (`store.set(data.key, data.value, ws, data.basedOn)`; the class cut gets `arrivalVerdict`).

- THE MEASUREMENT (lane browser-daemon-survives-update, Fix 4): the fleet image vibespace:3.7.0 (Chromium 154.0.8037.92, agent-browser 0.38.1), the shipped hidden-window args, `--network none`, 10 s per act, scripts/measure-hidden-window-cpu.mjs. Before, the default had two spellings: the schema row's `default: false` (what the Settings window and docs/settings.md show) and the keeper's read `setting('browser.idlePaintFreeze', false)`. `serverSetting()` returns only a stored value, so for an unset key the reader's own fallback IS the server's default. Both now take the module's constant: the schema imports it like its other PURE CJS tables, and `sweepIdlePaint` falls back to `BIdle.IDLE_PAINT_DEFAULT`. `idlePaintVerdict`'s ABSENT `enabled` stays off (the keeper always passes the value it read).
- NO MIGRATION: a default never rewrites a stored value. data/settings.json holds only what an owner set (sparse), so an explicit `false` stays off and an explicit `true` stays stored. Up to .331 a stored `false` could not come from the Settings window (a value equal to the default is dropped), so an owner who turned it on and back off has no stored value and gets ON. From .332, turning it off stores `false`.

### lane app-window-fit-topleft — a window whose app fixes its size, LARGER than the workspace, opens at the workspace's top-left (B-1f0b; base cd1fd652 = 2.369.330; the coordinator's decision on lane app-fit-fixed's «Larger than the workspace», 1aa55bb8)
- MEASURED first (heavy test-desktop-app-fixed's own harness: real xpra 6.5.4, headless Chrome 1920×963 at DPR 2, the sidebar at 470 ⇒ a 1450×878 workspace): the 1000×900 GTK fixture at 2× locks a 1002×965 window. Pre-lane (a tree with this lane's two calls pulled back) it stood at the CASCADE's x — 70 CSS px from the workspace's left — with its top already slid to the workspace's (setFixedSize's keepInside slides an overflowing axis to 0; the cascade survived only on the axis that fit), 86 CSS px of the picture past the bottom. A 1500×300 fixture (a 1502 px window, wider than the workspace) stood at x 0 but the cascade's y (100) and its title bar ran 1500 px: the ✕ 33 CSS px past the workspace's right edge, a click there hits nothing of ours — a window the person could not close.
- THE VERDICT: PURE src/lib/desktop-app-placement.js `fixedWindowPlacement({fixed, frame, workspace, phone})` → `{act, left, top, barMax, why}` (layout px): fits ⇒ `cascade` (its place, slid inside — unchanged); larger in EITHER dimension ⇒ `top-left` 0,0 of #workspace (below the toolbar, beside the sidebar — the workspace rect itself), `barMax` = the workspace's width when wider; the phone layout (the window IS the screen, the picture scales — app-fit-fixed's «named, not fixed»), not fixed, no frame, a workspace not laid out ⇒ `none`.
- THE WIRING: src/lib/window.js `_placeFixed(win, lock)` — the ONE caller of the verdict, called from exactly two sites: setFixedSize (the LOCK: before its keepInside, which it replaces for `top-left`; captured + announced with the lock) and `_reflowWindows` (the workspace ResizeObserver's rAF-coalesced reflow — a sidebar toggle, the browser window resized: a `top-left` window skips its grid-bounds placement). The re-judge's move is THIS client's — never captured into the shared grid bounds nor announced (the workspace-capped minimum's rule: another client's larger screen must not see the window jump), `onMoved` re-snaps the xpra surface, and a workspace that fits the window again gives back its stored place. `top-left` + wider ⇒ the title bar's inline `max-width` = barMax − the window's left border (`clientLeft`): the bar — and the ✕ at its end — stops at the workspace's right edge. No drag-time work: a person's drag moves the window as before; the next workspace resize judges again.
- AFTER (same harness, ours): BIG at 0.0,0.0 from the workspace, the title bar 1000×32 inside it, a click at the ✕'s centre hits the ✕; still 86 CSS px past the bottom (an 878 px workspace under a 965 px window — the top was already at 0, so the fix moves x, not y); Scale ▸ 1× (its row + the confirm) relaunches the app in the SAME window: 502×515, all four red edges on screen, 0 px past. WIDE at 0.0,0.0, the bar held to 1449 px (1450 − the 1 px border), the ✕ at x 1902 of a workspace ending at 1920, hit; 52 CSS px of the app past the right edge.
- NOT CHANGED: a fixed window that fits keeps the cascade; a snap / grid zone / stored bounds still MOVE a fixed window (app-fit-fixed's `_placeWindow` rule); the phone layout scales the picture. The app strip's ⋯ (its Scale ▸ rows) measured inside the workspace on BIG and WIDE alike, and Scale ▸ is the title bar's own menu row too.

### lane feedback-handled-verb — a conversation the owner granted marks an agent's feedback report handled, naming the release that shipped the fix (the owner 2026-10-20 17:4xZ 「你处理过的 agent 反馈你怎么不进行标记呢？」)
- THE GAP: a feedback record (data/feedback.json) left «open» only through `PATCH /api/feedback/:id` behind the owner's cookie. The maintainer conversation shipped the fixes (.326 / .330) but had no door, so six records whose fixes had shipped stayed open. The automation keys (design q-046) are the door for «a conversation the owner granted may do an owner act»: two rows in the CLOSED table, no new route.
- THE VERBS (src/automation-keys.js SCOPES): `feedback.handled {id: fb-<10 hex>, version: <n.n.n>, note?: ≤ 200}` (an act, not billed) · `feedback.list {}` (a read). Every argument is refused by name (`bad_args`). The audit keeps the id and the release, never the note (argsSummary). A store that could not write ⇒ 503 `write_failed`.
- THE SAME STORE CALL (src/server/feedback-store.js `automationVerbs`, wired beside conversation-ops' verbs over THE `feedback` instance the owner's routes use): `feedback.handled` = `store.setStatus(id, 'handled', {by: <the calling conversation's name>, version, note})`; the owner's PATCH is `store.setStatus(id, status)`. So the StateSync mirror (every open sheet), data/feedback.json and the live list move together. The record grows `handledVersion` / `handledNote` (PURE src/feedback-model.js setStatus: a malformed release ⇒ `version_bad`, a note over 200 characters ⇒ `note_too_long`; a reopen clears both; makeRecord carries both as null).
- THE GRANT is the engine's, unchanged: per key × conversation (or its Task Group). The first use files the existing first-use card ONCE; its Always grants the KEY, so the other feedback verb asks nothing. A key that lacks the verb, named with --key ⇒ 403 `verb_not_in_scope`; no key holding it ⇒ `not_granted`; locked ⇒ 423.
- PEER TEXT: `feedback.list` hands ANOTHER agent's words to the maintainer. The OPEN reports' text (a block), about, and the reporting conversation's and its Task Group's names (pieces) leave through src/peer-text.js toAgentText at the hub; the reporters list never leaves, and a handled note never rides it. test-peer-text-census: the vibespace-api declaration rewritten + a §6 store row «agent feedback reports» (5 pins, one negative: vibespace-feedback never prints the note).
- THE SHEET (src/lib/feedback-sheet.js): «handled in 2.369.NNN by <conversation>, <when>» + the note under it (text); the owner's own click keeps «handled <when>». zh「{who} 于 {when} 标为已处理（{version} 修复）」, ja「{who} が {when} に対応済み（{version} で修正）」. `vibespace-feedback list` tells the reporter `handled in <release>` (the number only).
- THE CLI (data/bin/vibespace-api): `call` is generic (the hub's table judges every verb); the usage names the two calls; `call` now prints the hub's answer as JSON under its ok line (feedback.list's reports). The CLI does NOT read the verb table: it ships alone to remote hosts (AGENT_TOOLS) and cannot require src/. Its usage text is hand-written; the hub's `keys` answer lists each key's verbs.
- RECORD-CLEAR: judged not owed. data/feedback.json is not one of the five content stores (the census's STORE_TOKENS; the feedback routes are `meta`), and the verbs ride the existing automation door; test-record-clear-census is green unchanged (242).
- GATES: test-automation-keys 148 → 179 (⑮: the table, 8 argument refusals, the audit summary, a key without the verb, the grant round trip over a REAL feedback store, a spy on THE store call, the belt on a planted frame, not_found, the lock, the CLI over a loopback door · ⑮b MUTANT: a verb that writes data/feedback.json directly ⇒ the live store and the mirror never move ⇒ RED); test-feedback-model 33 → 38; test-peer-text-census 404 → 405. ### lane antigravity-card-fixes — three owner-seen defects on the Antigravity card (主开发 measured 2026-10-20 17:4xZ: 「Antigravity CLI 未安装 [安装]」, 「Google 登录 未登录 ★」 over 「Personal Ultra 已登录 ☆」, no usage anywhere)
- **1 · A CLI INSTALLED AFTER BOOT STAYED «not installed».** The agent CLIs resolve once at boot (cli-env; `resolveCmd` answers the BARE name when nothing is found — the descriptor's «null when not installed» was never true); a spawn re-resolves a gone path (B-a18e) but a READ never spawns, and `/api/backend-status` handed antigravity's `machineStatus` the registry's boot answer. FIX = `cliCmds.check(backend, { force })` (src/server/cli-cmd.js), called by the status route for EVERY registered CLI: a resolved path re-validated (one `access` — an uninstall shows), an unresolved / gone one looked up again ≤ once per 30 s per CLI, or at once on a person's press (`?recheck=1`: Manage agents' first read after **Install**, a new **Re-check** beside Install, an account's ⋯ Re-check); a path found is adopted for spawns through forSpawn's single-flight lookup (one journal line). Who benefits: antigravity (its row now reads the CHECKED path), claude / codex (rows already re-ran `which` on a bare name; a MOVED absolute path is now re-found and adopted), opencode + every ACP agent (adopted at a read, so the next spawn is born right). Not changed, said: `harnessAvailability().installed` for an ACP/exe harness is `!!ACP_COMMANDS[id]` — true even for the bare name, so the New Session picker lists an uninstalled OpenCode/Antigravity as before.
- **2 · THE ★ NEVER MOVED.** The brief's diagnosis (the roster reading claude's field) was the claude roster, which is right; the antigravity roster read `accts[bill.defaultIdField]` and the server stored `defaultAntigravityAccountId` — the break was the CLIENT CACHE: src/lib/app.js built `_accounts` from `GET /api/accounts` and the `accounts-updated` push with two hand-picked fields (claude's, codex's). ### lane stream-leg-flap — the owner's Mac desktop went black: the stream relay's path election flipped udp leg ⇄ device link three times in 20 s (主开发's brief 18:03Z; base cd1fd652 = .330)
- MEASURED (the hub's journal, read only): «它的桌面», two displays = two sessions, offered 17:46:59Z with the leg up at once; BOTH flipped to «via the device link (the daemon spoke on the device link)» at 17:47:24Z and back to «via the daemon's udp leg (leg up)» 17:47:26/27Z, again 17:47:38/39Z → 17:47:39/41Z; both «stopped (closed)» 17:48:05Z — 24 s after the last flip, 66 s after the offer, no stream line after. Both sessions flip in the same second ⇒ ONE trigger shared by their two legs (the Mac's daemon, one path: its Tailscale address).
- THE RACE (base file:line): the hub forwarded on the path the daemon LAST spoke on — src/server/desktop-webrtc.js:155 (a PING flagged UP ⇒ udp; one not flagged ⇒ link), :159 (leg DATA ⇒ udp), :210 (ANY device-link frame ⇒ link). The daemon's half made the second signal: src/agentd/stream-host.js:215 took the leg DOWN when ONE PING went 2 s without its PONG (:202 at any socket error), so :438 sent the picture over the device link (two 4K pictures) until the re-probe 5 s after its last PING brought it UP — a device-link frame, then a PING flagged UP, every ~14 s. Each believed its path the better one; every flip lost pictures.
- THE RULE — ONE election per session with hysteresis (PURE src/stream-model.js legElect; the hub's one door `vote`): the leg is taken ONCE, when it comes up (a PING flagged UP, or its DATA); it is left only when MEASURED dead — no sign of life for legDeadMs 6 s while it carried the picture (= legMissMax 3 × legLiveMs 2 s: three of the daemon's own PING periods, the same bound as the daemon's verdict; a leg carrying the picture sends DATA continuously), legStaleMs 35 s idle (two 15 s keepalives + 5 s). The device link speaking (`relay.leg.held`) and a PING not flagged UP (`quiet`) are counted, never obeyed; the device link's frames always reach the browser; a flip never touches the session. THE DAEMON (SHARED stream-host.js createLeg): a PING unanswered 2 s is a MISS — re-asked at once, the picture stays on the leg, a late PONG still counts; three in a row ⇒ DOWN; a socket error is counted (`sendErrors` — a Mac's ENOBUFS under a burst), never a verdict. A dead leg: the daemon moves within 2 + 3 × 2 s, the hub 6 s after the leg's last sign.
- THE CLOSE: «closed» is the PAGE's word — src/lib/stream-view.js:261 `dispose(reason = 'closed')`, the window's × (or a ② pane folded / reshared); the hub's own stops say idle / viewer_gone / shutdown and the view's give-ups name their code (connect_timeout, ice_failed, restart_failed). Two sessions «closed» in one second with no re-offer = the window was closed, after the picture sat at «串流 · 2 个显示器 · 0 fps» with ICE still connected — nothing acted: fallbackVerdict (stream-view.js:171) reads only the connection state and no rule watched the frames.
- THE STALL (PURE stallStep; stream-view readStats): PLAYING, visible, no frame decoded for stallMs 12 s while the machine's sent count moved ⇒ ended `stalled` (the hub's record «stopped (stalled)») ⇒ the window's NEVER SILENT ladder offers it again with «串流中断：画面不再传过来——正在重新连接…»; ② panes now have that ladder too (machine-desktop paneEnd: a pane that played re-offers itself once, then 「重试」). 12 s is longer than the leg's own way back (≤ 8 s, then a key frame over the device link), so it never races the election; a still screen that sends nothing never stalls (a Mac's helper repeats its picture every 0.5 s anyway).
- CONTROLS: the flapping fake daemon (test-desktop-webrtc §14b — real loopback UDP + a stand-in device link, the hub on an injected clock): the .330 rule through the same hub flips 12× in 20 s; the election 0 (one election, all 78 browser datagrams on the leg); the leg dies ⇒ the device link at exactly 6 s, one change; it returns ⇒ taken once; 3 changes in 40 s. The daemon (§14c): a minute with every third PONG lost — the .330 rule (missMax 1) 8 DOWNs and 96 of 240 datagrams on the link; the hysteresis 0 and 240 on the leg. The viewer (test-desktop-display-modes-chrome ⑥): ② over a relay whose device-link half drops the machine's RTP ⇒ the owner's «串流 · 2 个显示器 · 0 fps», then both panes said and re-offered, playing again; the view without the rule sits at 0 fps.
- NOT MEASURED here (never a paired machine): which daemon trigger fired on the Mac — its agent log reads «relay leg down (no_echo)» or «(socket_error)» at 17:47:2xZ / 17:47:3xZ; the fix covers both. The daemon half reaches the Mac with the next SIGNED agentd; the hub half ships with the hub.

### lane ci-npm-retry — an INSTALL may be retried, a SUITE never: every workflow npm install goes through scripts/ci-npm.sh (B-fa5e; base 36190358 = 2.369.331)
- THE RED: the .330 mirror (Actions run 39462417012) lost heavy 6/6 in 27 s at `npm ci` — «npm error network read ECONNRESET … This is a problem related to network connectivity», exit 152. A registry blip read as a RED MIRROR and, by the release rule (a red mirror = census + fix the same day, never a retry), cost a census.
- WHAT NPM ITSELF RETRIES (read in npm 11.6.2's source, then measured on a loopback fake registry — 127.0.0.1, one 2 MB tarball, the server RSTing chosen requests): make-fetch-happen's `promiseRetry` wraps `fetch()` only until the response HEADERS (ECONNRESET is in its RETRY_ERRORS; `fetch-retries` default 2); a body that dies after them is retried by pacote's `tarballStream` once, and only on EINTEGRITY / Z_DATA_ERROR / ENOENT / EISDIR. Measured: a reset before the headers ×2 ⇒ green on the 3rd request; ×3 ⇒ red at the default 2 («request to … failed, reason: read ECONNRESET», exit 1), green with `--fetch-retries=5`; a reset MID-BODY ⇒ red on the FIRST request even at `--fetch-retries=5` — «npm error network read ECONNRESET», exit 152 (npm exits with the raw socket error's errno, −104), the runner's exact words and code. So the brief's «a reset mid-stream is retried by npm since v9» does not hold here: the step-level loop is what covers .330's blip. A second fresh `npm ci` after it ⇒ green. (The runner's npm is node 22's 10.x; 11.6.2 is the only npm on this box — no vendor calls.)
- THE DOOR: scripts/ci-npm.sh (`ci` | `install -g <package…>`, nothing else — exit 2 before npm runs), modelled on scripts/ci-apt.sh. npm's knobs take the request phase (`--fetch-retries=5 --fetch-retry-mintimeout=2000 --fetch-retry-maxtimeout=60000`), the loop the rest: 3 attempts, 20 s apart, each a FRESH `npm ci` (it removes node_modules first; never an `npm install` fallback — the lockfile stays the law), «install attempt N/3», every failed attempt a `::warning::` (a retried blip shows in the run's annotations, never silent), red only after the third with npm's own exit code. .github/workflows/ci.yml: the fast job and the 6 heavy shards install npm ci AND the claude CLI's `npm i -g` through it (the same registry, the same blip); secret-scan and mac-helper install nothing; the cache action: there is none in these workflows, so nothing changed there.
- WORST CASE, a registry that keeps resetting: ≤ 202 s of npm's own backoff per request (min(2000 × 10^k, 60000) ms, no randomize: 2 + 20 + 60 + 60 + 60 s) × 3 attempts + 40 s of pauses ≈ 11 min — under the fast job's 15-min timeout, so it ends RED with the door's ::error::, not CANCELLED. (A registry that HANGS waits npm's 5-min fetch-timeout per try; no loop shortens that.)
- THE GATE (test-ci-gate §2g, fast, 68 → 76): every npm install in every workflow goes through the door (4 steps), every job that runs scripts/ci.mjs installs through the door's `ci` form first, and a step naming scripts/ci.mjs is ONE plain `node scripts/ci.mjs …` line, once per job. The walk is line-based (this tree has no YAML parser); the `yaml` package of another install on this box read the same jobs / steps / run values from all three workflows. 11 MUTANT copies of ci.yml each go RED for their own reason: npm ci bare, the CLI bare, an `|| npm install` fallback, ci.mjs in a for loop, the heavy run `||`-doubled, an until loop in a run block, a retry action, a second `if: failure()` ci.mjs step, continue-on-error, ci.mjs handed to the door, the door after ci.mjs. The door itself runs over a stub npm + a stub sleep: 2 blips ⇒ 3 fresh `npm ci`, pauses 20,20, green; down ⇒ exactly 3, exit 152, no pause after the third; the CLI form; 6 refusals. CONTROLS on the tree: the base ci.yml ⇒ RED naming the 4 bare installs; a door with 1 attempt / no pause / an `npm install` fallback / exit 0 after the third ⇒ RED.
- docs/kb-design-lessons §18 «Release discipline» gains the sentence: an install blip is retried thrice, a suite never. Not covered here: scripts/ci-remote-provision.sh's `npm ci` on the self-hosted AIDev batch (not a workflow).

### lane agent-output-sinks — q-043 P0-b (design-vault-agent-access.zh.md D3 ②③ + §5 P0-b; credential class; base 9a5507aa = 2.369.326; a Fable verify follows the P0 set)

### lane app-page-csp — design q-043 D6 / §5 row P0-d: the app page's Content-Security-Policy, REPORT-ONLY, its report sink, and every chrome suite ending with zero reports (主开发's dispatch 13:13Z; base 9a5507aa = 2.369.326; the owner 2026-10-20 ③)
- **The header:** `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` on the app page (server.js's index route, `/` and `/index.html`) and on the sign-in page (src/auth.js `/login`: its one inline script carries a fresh per-response nonce; the Clerk frontend host joins script / connect / img / frame when SSO is on). The enforcing `Content-Security-Policy` is never sent: the switch belongs to a later half-day lane, after a week of reports.
- **The policy is measured** (src/app-csp.js, PURE). It started strict (default/script/connect/font/worker/frame 'self', img 'self' data:, object-src 'none', base-uri / form-action / frame-ancestors 'self'). A window walk and the brief's nine chrome suites then added only what they reported: img-src blob: https: (file bytes as pictures; a markdown file's remote pictures), connect-src blob: (reading back a blob: download), media-src blob: (a remote file's audio/video), frame-src blob: http: https: (a PDF's bytes; the Web view frames any site). style-src keeps 'unsafe-inline' (index.html's style attributes and <style>, the bundle's <style> elements). script-src stays 'self': no eval, no Worker, no inline handler in the page.
- **report-uri, not report-to (measured on Chrome):** report-uri posts each violation within ~0.4 s as `application/csp-report`, `Origin` = the page (or `null` from a sandboxed frame), no cookie. With report-to present, Chrome ignores report-uri, and its Reporting API sent nothing in 70 s, so a suite's teardown could never count on it.
- **The sink:** src/server/csp-reports.js, `POST /api/csp-report`, registered before the json body parser.
  - It is a door of src/auth.js (no cookie, no same-origin rule; test-auth DOORS row). The route judges for itself: report content types only (a page on another site cannot send one without a preflight), ≤ 32 KB read (413, never buffered past it), 60 posts a minute per address that would ADD a line (429, counted). A repeat is never paced. Measured: when every post was paced, test-channels-aggregate-ui's mail-frame bursts spent the budget and its teardown read 17 lines one run and 1 the next; with repeats unpaced it reads 27 every run.
  - A report becomes a line with no value (app-csp reportsOf): no sample, no query, no fragment, no user:pass, a URL cut to origin + 3 path segments, unknown directives dropped.
  - data/csp-reports.jsonl (0600, rotated to .1 past 1 MB) gets one line per (directive, blocked, source, line); the keys on disk are read back at boot.
  - ONE For-you notice (origin server, key csp-report) per NEW (directive, blocked) pair from an app-page document, ≤ 10 a day. A pair noticed at any boot never files again (its line carries `noticed: true`).
  - `GET /api/csp-reports` gives the count, app page apart from frames; the Diagnostics report shows it as a chip.
- **主开发's ruling 2, frames:** a report whose document is a frame the page made (`about` / `blob` / `data`, i.e. a srcdoc mail or design frame or a blob: page) is a line and a count, never a notice. A tracker in someone's mail is not something the owner can act on.
- **The teardown, one check in scripts/scratch.mjs:** a suite sets `VIBESPACE_CSP_REPORTS_FILE` at import, so every scratch hub it spawns (server.js hands it to the sink) writes its reports to that suite's one file, whatever its tree or cleanup order. At exit, before the scratch roots go, that file and any `<root>[/<dir>]/data/csp-reports.jsonl` still standing are read. A line ⇒ the reports are printed and the suite exits 1.
  - `takeCspReports(match)`: a suite that plants a violation on purpose takes its report. test-inbox-reply-ui ⑦ now also asserts that the policy reported its planted `<img onerror>`.
- **THE ONE EXCEPTION LIST (`CSP_EXCEPTIONS`, 主开发's rulings 13:33Z / 13:34Z):** measured, a srcdoc / blob: / data: frame INHERITS the app page's policy, report-only included. Each row is pinned by suite + directive + blocked + source + document; any other report fails the suite, and any app-page report always does. Never 'unsafe-inline' on the app page.
  - (1) test-design-window: the design's own inline scripts and handlers in the sandbox=allow-scripts artboard / print / present frames — script-src-elem / -attr `inline`, source and document `about`.
  - (2) test-channels-aggregate-ui, document `about`: 28 of its 29 reports are the hostile-mail corpus and the suite's probes, already blocked by the mail frame's OWN enforced meta CSP; 1 is the frame's nonce'd resizer.
  - Both rows are deleted by the frame-host lane (one static host document for design AND mail frames). The design frames are the enforce lane's first blocker.
- **Measured, round 0 (the strict start), the nine chrome suites:** 0 reports from test-vault-chrome, test-vault-window-chrome, test-automation-keys-chrome, test-browser-live, test-desktop-webrtc-chrome and test-gear-menu. test-design-window gave 6 (5 frame inline + 1 connect-src blob: from its download read-back); test-inbox-reply-ui 1 (its planted handler); test-channels-aggregate-ui 29 (the mail frame). After the fix: every suite ends with 0 unexcused.
- **The would-break list for the enforce lane** (the walk; none of these are in the gate): the code editor's HTML preview (a srcdoc frame with `allow-scripts allow-same-origin` running the file's scripts; it is also a same-origin XSS path); the chat's HTML Preview (a blob: page whose own inline scripts run same-origin; the Diagnostics report is a blob: page too, but it has no script and reports nothing); markdown preview's mermaid (loaded from cdn.jsdelivr.net, which is never allow-listed because jsdelivr serves any npm package).
- **Left out, with the reason:** the sandboxed pages already carry their own enforced policy (published pages, plugin windows, design pages, the Slack landing, apps, agent-routes' sandbox). The /proxy/ pages are third-party sites rewritten by unblocker (CSP stripped by design), not the app page. The xpra HTML5 client is the system package's own page and needs its own measurement. The oauth loopback "you can close this tab" pages are separate listeners serving one escaped line. User files (/api/file/raw, /api/file/serve) are the user's content; serving their HTML same-origin is a separate finding.
- **Census rows:** test-auth DOORS + the doors list; test-architecture PURE set + §86 reader row (csp-reports.js own-tree 2); test-user-todos-layout ⑪ 55 → 56 + PRODUCERS row (origin server); test-record-clear-census §I receiver `csp-reports.js|w` (the notice's own words); the boot sentinel's GET census (`/api/csp-reports` smoke); ci.mjs fast row. The route is written as a literal (test-auth's census reads the path).
