### lane design-frame-host — backlog B-8679, the first blocker of ENFORCING the app page's CSP: a frame the page makes navigates to the hub's frame host, its own policy as a real header (主开发's dispatch 15:53Z; base 1e3055c1 = lane app-page-csp on 2.369.326)
- **Why:** Chrome gives a srcdoc / blob: / data: frame its PARENT's policy, report-only too (lane app-page-csp §3). The Design window's artboards, Print and Print all and the channels' formatted mail were srcdoc frames, so they ran under the app page's `script-src 'self'`; two `CSP_EXCEPTIONS` rows excused them (test-design-window: 5 inline-script reports; test-channels-aggregate-ui: 27–29 `about` lines).
- **The host:** src/server/frame-host.js, `GET /frame-host?kind=design|mail` (one server.js line after the CSP sink; behind the sign-in gate like every read — measured: the sandboxed frame's navigation carries the cookie, `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`). ONE static document; its ONE inline script takes `{vsFrameDoc: 1, html}` from its PARENT only (never unframed), ONCE, and writes it with document.open / write / close. 404 for any other kind. Never in public/: express.static would serve it with no header, a same-origin writer.
- **Per-kind policy, a real header:** every kind starts with `sandbox` (opened top-level it is still an opaque origin — measured: origin 'null', cookie and localStorage throw), `frame-ancestors 'self'` (measured: another origin's frame of it is refused), no report-uri. design = `sandbox allow-scripts allow-modals; frame-ancestors 'self'`, a published page's rule (published-pages.js CSP: the sandbox only): inline scripts, handlers, eval and https:// assets run as when published. Not a hash list: the 25 real artboards on this box hold 2 inline scripts and 1 handler, so it would fit them, but every hash would be the agent's own script and it would break markup an artboard builds at run time; the wall is the opaque sandbox. mail = `sandbox allow-scripts; ` + mail-frame.js `cspFor({pictures, nonce, host})` + the ancestors: the per-document nonce rides in the address (`frameHostSrc`, URL-safe, ≤ 64), the host's script by sha256; the document keeps its `<meta>` (both enforce the same rules; the header adds the sandbox, the ancestors and the hash). Measured: a wrong nonce in the address ⇒ the resizer does not run.
- **The writer:** src/lib/frame-host.js `writeFrame(f, html, src)` keeps the document on the element (`__frameDoc`, what srcdoc held) and sets `src` (a fresh window per document); a capture listener takes the HOST's load, posts the document and stops it, so the caller's own load listener sees only the written document's (measured: Chrome fires the element's load again; an iframe inserted before its first write fires its about:blank load during the insertion). Users: design-window.js (the canvas's new `writeFrame` option, Print), design-present.js (Print all; its inner artboard frames are srcdoc frames of the host's document, so they inherit the design policy), channel-mail-frame.js (one nonce per document, in the meta and the address). The address lives in the two builders (design-canvas-model.js `FRAME_HOST`, mail-frame.js `frameHostSrc`) and the route. The published page passes no writer: srcdoc under its own sandbox policy.
- **Measured (probe, headless Chrome):** srcdoc artboard = 3 reports (script-src-elem, eval, script-src-attr); through the host = 0; canvas / print / print-all / mail all run; the nested print-all frames run; re-navigation gives a fresh global (a top-level `let` twice is fine); `contentWindow` is the same proxy across navigations.
- **Both exception rows DELETED** (scripts/scratch.mjs `CSP_EXCEPTIONS` is empty). test-design-window 174 checks (2 skipped) and test-channels-aggregate-ui 204 end with ZERO reports. The channels suite now asserts the product frames report nothing (the pictures mail, the hostile mail) and takes its OWN srcdoc probes' reports (the spoofer as a CONTROL that a srcdoc IS reported; the same-origin readers; the raw control); its sandbox probe runs on the host at the product frame's own address.
- **Gates:** test-csp-report ⑦ (+20: the route through server.js's own line and the real gate, each kind's header, the hash = the served script's, the handshake in a fake DOM with the browser's at-target order, the exception list empty, the address census; MUTANTS: the design sandbox cut, the host's source check cut, the writer's stopImmediatePropagation cut); test-design-canvas / test-mail-frame / test-channel-record / test-approval-census / test-peer-parsers pins moved off srcdoc (+ a negative control: the mail frame back on srcdoc is flagged).

### lane vault-scrub-forms — the desk's q-043 verify M1 (credential class; base = a local scaffold 03bf67e1 = vault-manual-and-lock 981c7223 + agent-output-sinks e54c08de, so the commit cherry-picks onto the .331 tree that carries both)
- THE RULE FIRST: the run scrubber is a BEST-EFFORT belt, never a guarantee — the design's premise is the owner reading the whole command on the card (+ the «once» / switch doors). The agent manual says it in one sentence («the output is scrubbed of the value's common spellings; a command that re-encodes it can still show it — the owner sees the whole command before it runs») and states the floor; the run card says it to the owner (the popup row and the For-you window, t() + zh / ja).
- THE FORMS, ONE LIST (src/vault-run.js, PURE): `FORMS` / `FORM_ROWS` — 12 rows, each naming a REAL tool that prints that spelling by itself. SPELLED (texts formsOf builds): raw, base64, percent, JSON, hex (as before) + UTF-16 LE / BE as the door's UTF-8 decoder reads those bytes (a WHATWG decoder written here — PowerShell 5's > / Out-File, reg export, Java writeChars), base32 (RFC 4648, padded or not, either case — oathtool -v, an otpauth secret). READ (`VIEWS` — a view undoes ONE family of escapes, looks for every spelled form in what it reads, masks the ORIGINAL span with its escapes): `qp` (=XX, soft breaks =\r\n anywhere — a mail body), `escape` (\xNN and octal as UTF-8 bytes, a non-UTF-8 byte as Latin-1; \uXXXX, \u{…}, \UXXXXXXXX; \\ \' \" \n \t \r — Python / Node / Rust reprs, git / bash quoting), `entity` (&#NN; &#xHH; and the five named — an HTML page, an XML config), `ansi` (SGR / EL CSI and ESC( — grep --color, git diff --color-words), `wrap` (line breaks — base64 at 64 / 76 columns).
- SKIPPED, with the reason (the header's ③ and the report): what an adversary invents — gzip / any compression (a compressed stream is not a spelling: its bytes depend on everything before them), encryption, a hash, a reversal, a case swap, spaced characters, a split with other output between the halves, two escape families on one value at once; THE FLOOR — a part of a value (its last four characters, a 7-byte fragment) is never masked; a value under MIN_MASK_BYTES (8) is never referenced.
- ONE WINDOW PER RUN (the desk's fix): `createRunMasker(secrets, streams)` — ONE masker per run fed by both pipes. It reads each pipe on its own AND, while both hold kept-back text, the two in arrival order; a find is masked on every pipe it covers (each pipe gets the placeholder) and is handed on whole or kept back whole on all of them; each pipe keeps back its last (longest spelled form − 1) characters as every view reads them + an unfinished token (a backslash run is read in pairs from its start, so only its last pair boundary is held — measured: holding the whole run kept 2 MiB of backslashes back until the end; a UTF-8 character still missing a byte). Reading only the merged text would have LOST a value written to one pipe in two pieces with the other pipe's chunk between them — measured, then fixed by reading each pipe too (the interleave leg + a seeded fuzz pin it). `createMasker` / `maskText` = the run masker on one stream; the output belt (agent-output-belt.js) masks whole texts through `maskText`, so it keeps no window of its own. Single stream: chunked at every split = the one-shot (pinned).
- THE DOOR (src/server/vault-run-door.js): `scrub = VR.createRunMasker(secrets, ['out', 'err'])` replaces the two per-stream maskers; every chunk reaches `parts` through ONE place (`handOn`); a cut still drops the held tail (never flushed). test-vault-law ④'s scrubbed-only census re-pinned on that shape (+ a second mutant: a raw chunk into handOn).
- GATES: test-vault-run-model ALL PASS 88 (was 73; 4.9 s — the 50 printings × 7 values at every split, ⑥b the producers' table: every printing × the 21-character value × start / middle / end × a cut at every point inside it; the floor row; two pipes; a 64 KiB backslash run handed on as it comes; 13 MUTANTS RED incl. each new form dropped ×7, a view's held tail ignored, a backslash run held whole) · test-vault-run ALL PASS 125 (was 117; 6.5 s — the printer emits 21 spellings on both pipes at once, an oracle reading every view, the split, two long forms across the 2 MiB cut, the card's sentence, the manual's sentence; MUTANTS RED: two scrubbers, a cut that flushes) · test-agent-output-sinks §2b + test-secret-shapes §3 (the belt: 10 more spellings, each stored exactly `<[vault:…]>`; RED on the old scrubber) · test-vault-law 53.
- SCOPE: no bump; package.json / package-lock.json / src/agentd/version.js untouched (the changelog heading runs on a scratch snapshot). Observed, not fixed (out of scope, said in the report): the For-you WINDOW renders a run card's detail as markdown (`mdInto`), not verbatim — the exit card's verify-r4 F4 trap; the popup row shows it as text.

### lane mount-password-off-argv — a storage mount's password is computed IN-PROCESS, never on argv (credential class, B-d752; dispatched by 主开发 2026-10-20; base eb9a6cb1 = lane spawn-env-debts on .327, lands after .331)
- THE FINDING (lane spawn-env-debts §Seams 3): src/mounts.js `_obscure(plain)` ran `execFileSync(this.rcloneBin(), ['obscure', String(plain)])` — a WebDAV / SFTP PASS-type mount password rode the child's ARGV, readable in /proc/<pid>/cmdline by every local user for that child's life, on a SYNC exec that blocked the hub's event loop (5 s timeout). THE LAW: a secret never rides argv; a public algorithm is computed in-process.
- THE FIX (option 1 — no child at all): rclone's `obscure` is a PUBLIC algorithm — AES-256-CTR under rclone's fixed 32-byte key (rclone fs/config/obscure/obscure.go `cryptKey`, unchanged since v1.39), a random 16-byte IV prefixed to the ciphertext, the whole base64url without padding. src/rclone-obscure.js (SHARED; node crypto only) is obscure()/reveal(); `_obscure(plain)` is now `rcloneObscure(String(plain))` — synchronous, no child, no argv, nothing blocks the loop. Its only two callers (src/mount-providers/webdav.js, sftp.js) are unchanged (a string in, a string out), so `_rcloneFor` stays synchronous — no async ripple through its five call sites.
- EQUIVALENCE PROVEN against the real binary on this box (by REVEAL, never by bytes — the IV differs): for empty / ascii / specials / unicode / 1 KB passwords, `rclone reveal <ours>` === plain AND our reveal(`rclone obscure`) === plain, on rclone v1.60.1-DEV (/usr/bin), v1.65.2 (the fleet image's pin) and v1.69.3 (the base's RCLONE_PIN). The key is version-stable; the binary's reveal is the standing proof (scripts/test-rclone-obscure.mjs §1–§2).
- TESTS: scripts/test-rclone-obscure.mjs (fast, ~200 ms; SKIPs the real-binary leg without rclone) — the PURE round trip + known rclone-produced samples, the real-binary reveal both ways, the real MountManager's webdav/sftp PASS obscured in-process (reveals to the secret, is NOT the plaintext, no env value carries the cleartext), and a runtime fake-rclone /proc cmdline control with the pre-fix argv MUTANT (the plaintext reappears on a child's /proc/<pid>/cmdline ⇒ RED). test-architecture §94: no child_process call hands a secret to `rclone obscure` on argv (a grep over tracked src + server.js + data/bin; the pre-fix spelling caught as a planted control). §93 (the spawn-ENV census) is untouched — the removed call was execFileSync, a SYNC form, never a §93 site.

### lane job-spec-off-argv — a Background Work job's spec rides a 0600 file, never argv; the wrapper's env is built (lane spawn-env-census report §Seams 2.1, 2026-10-20)
- THE FINDING: `_spawn` started each run as `spawn(node, [job-wrapper.js, ctlDir, base64(JSON.stringify(spec))], { detached, stdio: 'ignore' })` — the spec's env = jobEnv({ …cmd.env, …the job's secrets (envFrom → data/job-secrets.json), VIBESPACE_JOB_TOKEN (jbt_), … }) rode base64 on ARGV: /proc/<pid>/cmdline is readable by every local user (`ps -ef`), for the wrapper's whole life (it tees the job's log until the job ends). The same spawn passed NO env (the wrapper carried the server's whole env) and the wrapper fell back to it (`spec.env || process.env`).
- THE TRANSPORT: `<ctlDir>/spec.<runTs>.json`, opened O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL 0600 (never through a name already there — a planted file or link refuses the start), written whole, closed, then the spawn; a spawn that throws unlinks it. The ctl dir is made 0700 AND chmod'ed 0700 (mkdir's mode is umask-masked; the dir holds the spec and current.log, which sat 0664 in a 0775 dir). The wrapper's argv = [wrapper, ctlDir, specPath].
- THE UNLINK RULE: the wrapper reads the file ONCE and unlinks it — before its stamp, before the child. Nothing re-reads it, verified in src/jobs.js: `_adoptAndReplay` ADOPTS a live wrapper by its pid.json stamp (no spawn, no read); every other road to a run (the boot replay of a down service, restart-policy, a cron fire's child, create / start) goes through `_spawn`, which writes a FRESH file from the store (job.cmd + the secrets store + the in-memory token). Only a file of its own ctl dir is read or removed (a path elsewhere is refused and left alone). A leftover exists only if the wrapper dies before its first statement: 0600 in a 0700 dir, beside data/job-secrets.json (0600, the same secrets).
- THE REFUSAL: a spec with no env (or no argv, or unreadable) ⇒ `[job-wrapper] refused: the spec carries no env (a job never runs on the wrapper's own)` on stderr AND in current.log, exit.json {code: 2}, exit 2. The stamp is written first, so the engine's sweep ends the run (failed, that line its last line). A JSON parse error is named by its code / name, never its message (a parse message quotes the text).
- THE WRAPPER'S ENV: `wrapperEnv(jobId)` (src/jobs.js, exported with WRAPPER_ENV_KEEP) = PATH HOME LANG TMPDIR from the server's env + VIBESPACE_JOB_ID — an allowlist. Measured: the wrapper runs on an EMPTY env; `spawn` resolves a bare argv[0] through options.env.PATH (spec.env's). serviceEnv when it lands (lane spawn-env-census 1912531f, .331): the int331 integrator swaps it for `serviceEnv(process.env, { add: { VIBESPACE_JOB_ID: job.id } })` and deletes the §93 census's jobs.js `debt` row (the site then reads `named` / `builder`).
- GATES (the fast gate on a snapshot with package.json at 2.369.331 for the .332 heading): fast gate ALL GREEN 273 s (on 8c126284) (and a no-fail-fast pass of all 448 fast suites: its one red the expected .332 heading). test-jobs-engine §12 (heavy, +23 rows — base 117 s / 102 → 121 s / 125 on this box): a hub CHILD started from a planted shell (VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN / CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN, fakes built at runtime) runs a job with a secret (envFrom) whose child dumps its env as name → sha256; the wrapper's REAL /proc/<pid>/cmdline carries no byte of the secret and no jbt_ (raw or base64), its environ ⊆ the allowlist with no planted name or value; the job still sees its secret and ITS token (sha256 = the record's tokenHash); a front script at bin/job-wrapper.js stats the spec before the real wrapper reads it (0600, one link; the ctl dir 0700), gone after; the wrapper by hand: no env ⇒ exit 2 + the named line, the job never runs; a path outside the ctl dir is neither read nor removed; a planted link at the next run's spec path refuses the start. RED: M1 the spec on argv again (1404 base64 chars decoding to PROBE_SECRET + VIBESPACE_JOB_TOKEN; rows argv secret jbt mode gone), M2 the wrapper spawned with no env (the planted tokens in ITS environ; the job clean — jobEnv strips them), M3 the fallback restored (a spec without env RUNS and its job sees both planted tokens), M4 a plain 'w' open (the start writes the job token through the planted link). Moved: test-jobs-browser's verify-r1 ④ pin (`env: spec.env,` and no `process.env` in the wrapper); §86 src/jobs.js 22 → 23 (the O_EXCL open). The wrapper's comments never spell the jbt_ prefix (test-peer-text-census's AGENT_CLI_RE would class it an agent CLI). Also green: test-jobs-browser 121, test-job-notice 49, test-jobs-triage 98, test-job-model 361, test-artifacts-services 36, test-peer-text-census 404, test-record-clear-census 242, test-pid-identity 58, test-architecture 745, heavy test-jobs-panel (38 s), test-record-clear-walk 155 (a real server + a real job: the jbt_ self-read), test-artifacts-chrome 53; from a polluted shell (planted session tokens, a cloud key, a proxy) test-jobs-browser 121, test-job-notice 49, test-artifacts-services 36.

### lane quiet-box-flakes — two harness timing races that FAIL on a quiet / fast box and PASS loaded, the mirror of the usual flake (B-c820, found by lane xpra-title-election; base cb53ddc6 = 2.369.327). A flake is a race: the wait names the LAST EFFECT, never a sleep, a longer timeout, or a skip-by-speed. Test tooling only — no product change (the suites were right about the product; they raced their own reads).
- **test-desktop-xpra-window-open §S2** (the belt leg «a second top-level the app opened at +2000+1500 … lies in its slot of the root beside the main, and X agrees»): the race = the 'X agrees' sub-check read X against the client's OPTIMISTIC slot position, FROZEN at `own`, on a flat 6 s budget — but X reports a corral's place only AFTER the window's first paint (instrumented: right after `own` resolved X still had the second at an in-flight +678+482, moving to the slot +730+0 ~250 ms later). A quiet box reached the read before xpra repositioned, so §S2 went red while a loaded box (slower than xpra) passed. The wait now names the EFFECT: poll X until the corral lands where the client NOW has the window (re-read live each pass — a relayout moves it, never a frozen target), bounded by the configure round-trip XAGREE_DEADLINE_MS the §18 legs already use. RED control = the pre-fix §S2 read on a quiet box fails ≥ 1 / 10; 10× alone + 10× under race-sweep's 2-cpu sim green.
- **test-fs-canary §3** («a slow pool is still seen»): the race = the pool was made 'slow' by racing pbkdf2 jobs sized off a startup calibration (`saturate`), which on a quiet / turbo box drained before the canary's stat ever queued ⇒ fs < slowMs ⇒ red (loaded the box was slower than the jobs, so it passed). The wedge is now a MECHANISM: both libuv workers (UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE = 2) block on a read of an empty FIFO only the test writes to; the process-global pool's queue is FIFO and the canary's stat is submitted a cross-thread round-trip later, so it is always behind the two reads and waits exactly as long as the test holds the wedge — fast box as slow (P: held then released ⇒ fs ≈ the hold; W: held across three ticks ⇒ three deadline strikes + the wedged event). RED control (in-suite) = a FREE pool records nothing, the quiet box the old wedge raced; 10× alone + 10× loaded green.

### lane stream-sdr-ecoqos — Windows power throttling off for EVERY screen road while its stream runs, given back when it ends (backlog B-0485; the owner 2026-10-20 「SDR 路也关」; 主开发's dispatch 14:18Z; base cb53ddc6 = 2.369.327)
- **Why:** lane stream-hdr-passthrough measured that the agent and its ffmpegs are hidden background processes, so Windows runs them under EcoQoS. The SDR mapped road ran 3–6 fps at 4K; with throttling off on all three processes it ran 19–22. Only the HDR road opted out, and it never gave the agent's opt-out back.
- **The helper, reused:** src/stream-plan.js `unthrottlePs(pids, { restore })` is the HDR lane's script. The opt-out is byte for byte unchanged. `restore` is the same script with ONE character changed: ControlMask 1 → 0, so the system manages the process's throttling again, as before any stream. test-stream-hdr §6 pins the one-character difference. Neither script touches a display setting.
- **THE KEEPER** (src/agentd/stream-screen.js `createWindowsScreen`, every Windows road: direct, mapped, hdr):
  - Each ffmpeg is opted out once, as it starts; a restarted encoder or a re-asked capture gets its new pid.
  - The agent's opt-out is process-wide and outlives a stream, so it is HELD. The first stream that starts opts the agent out; the last one that ends gives it back.
  - The pids asked within 100 ms go in ONE PowerShell. Every script runs after the one before, so a give-back never overtakes the opt-out it undoes.
  - A pid whose ffmpeg ended before its batch went is dropped: a dead pid is never opted out, since pids are reused.
- **Tied to the stream's lifetime:** the source has ONE end, `close()`, which both `stop()` and an ending by name (`finish`: encoder_exited, capture_exited, display_gone, …) go through. Its `finally` gives the hold back, so an ffmpeg crash never leaves the agent opted out.
  - This includes the HDR road, which used to leave the agent opted out until the agent restarted.
- **The status word:** the source's numbers carry `ecoqos`:
  - `'off'`: the agent and every live ffmpeg answered ok;
  - `'on'`: still throttled, not yet answered, or refused;
  - `'n/a'`: not Windows (src/agentd/stream-mac.js says `'n/a'`).
  - `unthrottle {asked, ok}` stays as it was.
  - The stream details show it as the 「电源限制」 row (Power throttling · Off / On), after the encoder (src/stream-series.js detailRows `power`, src/lib/stream-stats.js). A Mac has no row.
- **No second switch:** the HDR lane's switch is 「HDR 直通」, which picks the road. It never governed the opt-out, so the opt-out has no switch on either road.
- **Tests:**
  - test-stream-op §8, through the real Windows-shaped daemon (74 → 88). The fake PowerShell now names each script's mode (off / restore), keeps the last one verbatim, and logs every script's kind:
    - the SDR mapped road: ONE opt-out script with three pids, the agent's own among them, byte for byte `unthrottlePs`, and ecoqos off; stopped ⇒ ONE give-back, the agent's pid alone;
    - the direct road: two pids, then the give-back;
    - an encoder CRASH (encoder_exited, no stop asked) ⇒ the give-back;
    - TWO streams at once: the agent opted out once; the first stopped gives nothing back; the last does;
    - every PowerShell around those streams is the facts read or the opt-out: no display-setting call.
    - The HDR lane's rows now read the new log: the HDR road gives the agent back too. Its H.264-browser row flipped from "the SDR road opts nothing out" to "opts out, in one script".
  - §9b, in-process:
    - Linux ⇒ not_windows, and nothing ran at all;
    - THE MODULE gives back after a stop and after a crash;
    - **MUTANT 1** (the keeper's give-back line cut) ⇒ both lifetime rows RED;
    - **MUTANT 2** (an ending by name skips `close()`'s give-back) ⇒ the crash row RED.
  - The same two mutants also run as whole trees (the bundle rebuilt from the mutated file, test-stream-op run against it): no-give-back 8 rows RED, crash-keeps-it 10 rows RED. On the crash-keeps-it tree, §8's earlier crash endings leak the hold, so the agent is never opted out again for the rest of the suite.
  - Other suites: test-stream-hdr 49 (+1), test-stream-stats 45 (+1, the power row's place), test-stream-mac 123 (+1, n/a).
  - The chrome stream suites stay green: test-desktop-webrtc-chrome 97, test-desktop-display-modes-chrome 42.
  - test-desktop-display-modes-chrome's fake PowerShell now answers the opt-out script. Before, an opt-out script there sat on the resident injector's stdin until the agent's 15 s child timeout.
- **Not run here:** nothing ran on a paired machine. The real leg is 主开发's: a read-only fps measurement before/after through vibespace-exit on the owner's box, after .328 lands there.

### lane frame-host-preview — backlog B-5b2c, security hygiene: the three frames the page made for FOREIGN HTML (the code editor's HTML preview, an .eml's body, a Word document's altChunk) move onto the frame host; `allow-same-origin` banned on them (主开发's dispatch 16:33Z; base ab99080c = lane design-frame-host)
- **Why:** the three were still srcdoc frames (the app page's policy), and the code editor's preview had `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin"` — an agent-written (or cloned-repo) HTML file previewed there ran AS THE APP: its cookie rode every request, the API answered it (measured in the new suite's CONTROL: the old shape's `fetch('/api/home')` = 200 with the owner's cookie, its origin the app's).
- **Measured first (probe, headless Chrome):** a subresource request from an opaque frame carries NO cookie (`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`, SameSite=Lax) — the old `<base href="/api/file/serve/<dir>/">` cannot work without `allow-same-origin`; after document.open / write the document keeps the HOST's URL, so relative URLs resolve against it; a scheme-ful path host-source (`http://<hub>/frame-host/f/<token>/`) in an opaque document's policy admits that folder and blocks the hub's `/api` (img + connect); a module script, a font and fetch() from the opaque frame are CORS requests (`Origin: null` — they fail without `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`); a per-response nonce on the host's line lets it run and blocks an inline script, a handler and a byte-exact copy of the line.
- **What a preview needs (measured):** the repo's own docs/**/*.html need their SIBLING files (split-ux `_base.css`, integrations `mockup.css`, the communication-panel's `frame.css` + a MODULE script `directions.js`, slack-relay `relay.js`); public/index.html asks only the hub (`/style.css`, `/bundle.js` …). Of the 450 .html files on the lane's box (60 days), 363 carry inline scripts, 210 load https:// scripts, 248 https:// stylesheets, 158 https:// pictures.
- **The kinds (src/server/frame-host.js):** `preview` = `sandbox allow-scripts; default-src 'none'`; its own inline scripts + eval, inline styles, data:/blob: pictures, https: (libraries, fonts, pictures, fetch) and ITS FOLDER by full address — never `'self'`, never http: (the hub reached over http is no source; over https it is reachable cookieless only, every private route refuses). `eml` / `docx` = the mail frame's own policy (`MF.cspFor`: no network, data: pictures; https: only `eml` + `pictures=1`) whose ONLY script source is a nonce made for that response (never the host's hash: a copied line would match it). Every header: `sandbox` first, `frame-ancestors 'self'`, no report-uri. The iframes carry `sandbox="allow-scripts"` for the host's line alone (a sandbox without it would stop the host taking the document — the brief's «sandbox without allow-scripts» is kept as «nothing of the document runs», measured).
- **The preview's folder:** `?kind=preview&base=<dir>` is judged on the SIGNED-IN navigation (absolute, the mount door, SafeFs realpath + stat — a new `realpath` op in src/safe-fs-worker.js) ⇒ a folder token (24 random characters, idle 30 min, ≤ 256, the same folder keeps its token) and a 302 to `/frame-host/f/<token>/` — the host at the folder's own address. `GET /frame-host/f/<token>/…` is a DOOR (src/auth.js, GET only — the token is the credential): a web file's extension only, no `.`/`..`/empty segment, no dot name (.env, .git), its REAL path inside the folder (a symlink out is a 404), answered with the preview policy (a sibling page the preview navigates to is sandboxed the same way), `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and no-store. A remote file's preview has no folder. `/api/file/serve/*` has no client caller any more (left in place — a follow-up may retire it).
- **The writer** stays src/lib/frame-host.js `writeFrame` (never a second); `hostAddress(kind, {base, pictures})` is the three viewers' address. code-editor.js (no `<base>` written into the page any more), file-viewer.js (the .eml body + a "Show pictures" button when the body has remote pictures — the mail frame's words), docx-viewer.js (the altChunk keeps its no-network meta as well).
- **test-docx-viewer was RED at the base** (5 reports, ab99080c, measured): its ⑤ innerHTML negative control and ⑪ library control (a same-origin srcdoc) — the suite's own, now taken with `takeCspReports` — and the viewer's EMBEDDED FONTS, registered from blob: URLs (the product): src/app-csp.js font-src gains `blob:` (test-csp-report ① pin moved). It ends with zero now (95 checks).
- **Gates:** test-csp-report ⑧ (+25 → 93): the three kinds' headers, the quiet nonce per response, the folder door through server.js's line and the real gate (.env / key.pem / a symlink out (file and folder) / encoded ../ / unknown token ⇒ 404; a malformed token and a POST ⇒ the gate), the token's life and cap, THE CENSUS over src/lib — `allow-same-origin` and srcdoc only where a reason row names the site (doc-window-ui.js's print frame: no scripts; design-canvas.js's published-viewer fallback; Print all's inner frames inside the host's design document) — MUTANTS: allow-same-origin back on the preview, srcdoc back on each of the three ⇒ RED; CONTROLS: a dead row, a new viewer's srcdoc, a comment. NEW heavy test-frame-host-viewers (39): the repo's pages previewed (folder files 200, the hub's blocked, opaque origin), public/index.html (nothing of the hub fetched), a hostile preview, the .eml (nothing runs, pictures after the press), the docx altChunk, the old-shape CONTROL; zero CSP reports. Census rows: §86 reader row (frame-host.js user-path 4, safe-fs-worker 18 → 19), test-raw-filename's byte-serving table (the folder's sendFile, declared), ci.mjs heavy row; the pre-push hook's `is_code_path` names docs/design-mockups/communication-panel (the new suite reads it — test-ci-gate-push said so; docs/mockups and docs/slack-relay were code paths already).

- MEASURED, not assumed: agy 1.4.3 (manifest of the Cloud Run auto-updater; cli_linux_x64.tar.gz sha512-verified; the installer READ, not run — it would also run `agy install`) run OFFLINE inside `bwrap --unshare-net` with a scratch HOME and NO D-Bus session bus, under strace; no sign-in, no prompt reaching anyone. scripts/fixtures/antigravity-cli-1.4.3.json records every fact with its provenance ('binary' / 'docs' / 'changelog' — the release notes the binary prints itself). Diffs vs the docs: `--effort low|medium|high|xhigh|max` (docs: three), `--mode accept-edits|auto|plan`, `--print-timeout` default 0 = wait until the turn completes (docs page: 5 m; the release notes: changed to unlimited — the wrapper PINS `--print-timeout 0` so a default that flips back cannot cut a long turn); an unauthenticated start on a PIPE refuses at once ("Error: authentication required. Run 'agy' to log in, then retry." + a result ERROR), while on a character-device stdin it prints the OAuth URL and WAITS 60 s for a pasted code; `agy models` needs a sign-in; `--version` / `--help` make no inet call, `models` / `agents` / a run look up DNS; everything lives under $HOME (`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli`, `~/.gemini/config`, `~/.config/antigravity`) and XDG_CONFIG_HOME is NOT honoured; with no D-Bus session bus the keyring is bypassed and the login is a FILE under HOME (the changelog's own words + `shouldBypassKeyring` in the binary); `-p "/usage"`, `/credits`, `/model` … answer WITHOUT a turn (changelog).
- THE CHAT WRAPPER (data/bin/agy-wrapper.js): agy is NOT ACP — ONE `agy --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json [--model] [--effort] [--mode | --dangerously-skip-permissions] [--conversation]` per conversation, translated into the SAME 'acp-events' journal acp-wrapper writes, so caps.streamProtocol 'acp-events', the ACP normalizer, the acp-events stdout consumer, the queue strip and the artifacts reader serve it unchanged (the journal is ours; the agent protocol is agy's). init → the `session` record (the conversation id adopted, how new/load); step_update agent_response → text chunks; tool → a tool card (tool_call with tool_info.parameters, then tool_call_update completed/failed with the output); subagent_info → a notice; result → prompt_end (SUCCESS end_turn, CANCELED/INTERRUPTED cancelled, else error with agy's words). THE SLASH REFUSAL: a chat line starting with "/" never reaches agy (its stream would end, exit 2). THE AUTH GATE: the first line waits until agy speaks or a 2 s grace passes with no sign-in request; agy's sign-in request on stderr (URL or refusal) kills it at once and says `auth-required` by name — a pasted-code wait would otherwise swallow our next line. SOFT-DENY → THE CARD 「agy skipped <tool>」: agy's stream never asks — a tool that needs approval is SKIPPED, the run carries on, a stderr notice names it — so that line becomes the harness-neutral permission card (`permission_request`, no new client) with **Allow and retry** / **Keep skipped**. Allow and retry restarts agy on the same conversation with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` for ONE turn (a run has no per-tool grant; the card's input says so) and sends a retry line naming the tool; the turn after is back on the conversation's mode. THE ONE-TURN BYPASS INVARIANT is checked at DISPATCH against the flag the live process was STARTED with (`childRetryBypass`), so a reorder / remove / Stop during the restart can never run a user turn with every tool approved (④b proves it by reordering a user line ahead of the retry during a slow restart; its RED copy, which checks only "the retry wants it", runs that user turn under always-proceed). A second answer to the same card is refused (stale). A restart now also drains what queued behind it, and a restart requested while one is in flight is folded into it (two children were possible before). `AGY_ERROR: {...}` → an error notice. NO cancel / switch verb in the stream ⇒ Stop and a model / effort / mode change RESTART agy on the same conversation (`--conversation`), said in the notice. Text only (another block type ends agy's stream) — an image is refused by name. THE VERSION LAW: `agy --version` per spawn → an `agent_version` record + agentInfo.version (agy self-updates; the fixture is per version).
- THE DESCRIPTOR (src/harnesses/antigravity.js, SHARED): kind chat, `exe: {command:'agy'}` (cli-env resolves it beside the ACP agents: `h.acp || h.exe`, ANTIGRAVITY_CMD overrides), AgyAdapter (src/adapters/agy.js: the AcpAdapter's stdin frames; chat = the wrapper + AGY_WEBUI_*, terminal = the TUI with `agyFlags`), the docs' model slugs as models(), settings table (model / effort / permission mode / extra args), creds null + ui.billing null (c2), NULL_QUOTA (c3) ⇒ autoResume derived never-armed, the 'prompt' resume verb declared, artifactsOf = the ACP reader (agy's tool records carry no diff: nothing is guessed until a signed-in capture shows write_to_file's parameters). backend-caps row `antigravity` (opencode's protocol rows; pool false). Client META row + New Session options + picker option + brand mark + CSS; permission words; the settings category «Antigravity CLI» (docs/settings.md regenerated). The job door strips GEMINI_API_KEY / AGY_ADC_AUTH / GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL (names in the binary); the agent door joins with c2's account row.

### lane antigravity-harness, commit 3 — the /usage reading: the judge (the STOP rule) + the capture kit; the parser waits for a signed-in capture
- WHAT IS KNOWN: agy's release notes say `-p "/usage"` (and /quota, /credits, /model, /effort, /skills) answers "without starting an agent turn, spending quota, or leaving a conversation behind" — one tab-separated record per line, or "a structured payload" under --output-format json / stream-json. WHAT IS NOT: that payload's SHAPE. The /usage docs page shows only the TUI panel (per-model limits, remaining requests/tokens); the binary holds the RPC names (RetrieveUserQuota, FetchQuotaStatus) and quota tags, but Go's string tables are deduplicated, so no print struct can be read off them; offline the CLI refuses before reading anything (measured: the json ERROR envelope, num_turns 0, every counter 0). A parser written now would be a guess, so there is none.
- src/harnesses/antigravity-usage.js (PURE): `USAGE_ARGV` (`-p /usage --output-format json`; stdin must be a closed PIPE — a character device makes an unauthenticated agy wait 60 s); `judgeUsageAnswer` → `turn-started` (THE BRIEF'S STOP RULE — any num_turns, a conversation_id or one token in the envelope, either output shape: the vendor's claim refuted, the reading door stays shut) · `auth-required` · `error` · `no-answer` · `unparsed` (a clean SUCCESS — kept for the capture, never guessed; `KNOWN_SHAPES` is empty until a signed-in capture pins one) · `reading`; `redactCapture` (e-mails, project ids, opaque tokens → placeholders).
- scripts/agy-usage-capture.mjs (a dev tool, run BY HAND once on a signed-in login): the exact command on the machine login or `--account <root>` (the spawn env — HOME root + bus disabled — and the three key names stripped), 30 s, judged; exit 0 written · 2 not signed in / error (nothing written) · 3 TURN-STARTED (the evidence written, marked); the redacted answer lands as scripts/fixtures/antigravity-usage-<version>.json. That capture is what the click-gated door (through the human-gated refresh route), the parser, the passive terminal capture and `pool: true` are built on — commit 3 deliberately ships none of them before it.
- GATES: test-agy-harness ⑩ (79, 7 s: the judge on the MEASURED unauthenticated answer, every turn sign alone, the empty shape table, a RED judge copy without the turn check calling a billed answer "unparsed"; the capture script against the fake agy — exit 2 / 0 / 3, redacted, the account env on the stub's own log, a non-root refused); test-agy-cli-probe (18, heavy): the capture script on the REAL agy offline (auth-required, exit 2, nothing written) AND commit 2's measurement as a leg — the account env on the real agy opens the ROOT's antigravity-oauth-token and, under strace, dials no bus and launches no dbus-launch even with a listening bus under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, with a RED control (a fresh root whose bus ADDRESS points at a planted socket IS dialed). Lesson kept in the suite: a listener in the test's own process needs agy run ASYNC — spawnSync blocked the event loop and a real dial sat uncounted in the backlog (the RED control caught it).

### lane vault-run-model — q-043 P0-e: a secret in a command, the PURE half of `vibespace-vault run` (主开发's dispatch 11:22Z; base 9a5507aa = 2.369.326; contract design q-043 §8 + §5 P0-e — the owner's five decisions as recommended; the door is P0-f)
- WHAT: src/vault-run.js (PURE; imports only vault-inventory + vault-blocked) — the reference grammar (`vault://<store>/<row>/<field>` = vault-inventory's `<store>:<entry>#<field>`, the row percent-encoded; `$VAULT{…}` in a template; `$VAULT_FILE{ref | NAME}` = a 0600 file's PATH), `parseRunArgs` (the CLI's words, spelled once), `planOf` (the request → env / files / templates / stdin, every refusal by name), `materialize` (the door's last step — the ONLY object that holds values), `shapeOf` / `shapeKeyOf`, `ownDoorOf`, `runVerdict`, `formsOf` / `createMasker` / `maskText`. Nothing reaches a user or an agent until P0-f.
- INJECTION: env → a 0600 file (a value, or `--file NAME=@template` rendered `op inject`-style) → stdin; a reference in argv ⇒ `argv_refused` (/proc/<pid>/cmdline); `--allow-argv` opens only a KNOWN tool marked argv-only — none is (all 19 known tools read env / a file / stdin). BEYOND THE BRIEF: the agent's PLAIN env may not name a library the tool loads, code a shell or interpreter runs first, a program the tool starts, a config pointer, a proxy or PATH (`env_refused`; a `--file` the hub renders may set a config pointer) — without it an «always» shape bends under `LD_PRELOAD` / `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` / `NODE_OPTIONS`; plain env NAMES are part of the shape.
- REFUSALS: 162 names in 7 classes — print / transform / pack (§8.2's 35 ⊂ them) + copy (cp / mv / dd / ln: a copied file never meets the scrubber) + trace (strace / gdb) ⇒ `tool_prints_secrets`; wrappers (sudo / timeout / xargs) ⇒ `tool_wraps_another`; VibeSpace's own CLIs + agent-browser ⇒ `tool_has_its_own_door`. argv[0] is the door's RESOLVED path (any directory, case, .exe, a version suffix). Shells and interpreters run: their whole line is the shape, never «always».
- SHAPE (decision ④): tool + flags (order-free) + hosts + entries + injection + plain env names + the templates' text + `--on`; positionals are CLASSES (<path> <word> <number> <url> <vaultfile>). A KNOWN tool's leading subcommand words belong to the tool (gh pr list ≠ gh repo delete) — beyond the letter of ④, a ruling for 主开发 if they should vary. Hosts: any URL, scp-like targets, the ssh target, psql's host, docker's registry, GH_HOST, a rendered kubeconfig's server; a known tool's defaults only when nothing names one. «always» only for a known tool that names a host.
- VERDICT: not set up / locked FIRST (THE words, src/vault-blocked.js) → the plan's refusal → an entry with its own door (accounts, integrations, channels, passkeys, automation keys, the hub's secrets; a store the table does not know fails closed — only mounts and app logins can be opened) / unknown / not opened / under 8 bytes → the grant → a live «always» → a cluster asks (once / always 8 h · 30 d · forever with re-auth / deny; 60 s), a local instance allows.
- SCRUBBER: the value + its forms — raw; base64 std / URL-safe ± padding AND the value's own characters at each of the three byte alignments inside a longer run (`Basic base64(user:pass)`, what `curl -v` prints); percent (upper / lower: encodeURIComponent, RFC 3986, a path, a WHATWG form, every byte; `+` for a space); JSON (`\/`, `\uXXXX` lower / upper incl. DEL as Python escapes it, HTML-safe); hex — longest first; a stream holds back (longest form − 1) characters. The header says it is a SIEVE (write-then-cat defeats it; same uid is not isolation; a tool can send the value out).
- GATES: test-vault-run-model (fast, 62 asserts, ~1.8 s) — the reference table, injectionOf's 30 cells, 18 plan refusals, the env table (37 names × 3 places), every refusal name, 16 shape pairs + 17 host rows + «always», the 4 608-cell verdict grid vs a reference, 7 values × 26 printings with Node's own encoders as the oracle, every split point + three chunkings, the sieve's named holes as controls; MUTANTS RED on patched copies (each patch asserted to hit once): no base64 (56 escapes), argv open by default (3), the print class unrefused (5), no window (663). test-architecture: src/vault-run.js AND src/vault-inventory.js join the PURE set (vault-inventory says PURE and imports nothing but was never listed — vault-run's import of it read as impure). test-record-clear-census: a receiver row `src/vault-run.js|x` (a refusal sentence names the `--file NAME` the agent typed — an env name, never a record's words). The class is spelled `<vaultfile>`: test-channel-record's frame census reads any `<a-b>` under src/ as a frame tag (its `git ls-files` walk could not see the file before it was tracked — the parallel sweep missed it, the gate did not). test-peer-text-census: `renderTemplate` classified in its renderer fence (a child's 0600 file, never text toward an agent).
- SEAMS for P0-f: an entry lane vault-mint-put mints (`agent:<conv>/<name>` in the `secrets` group, in flight) fails closed here (`ownDoorOf`: the hub's secrets are never referenced) — the lane that lands second adds its runnable row to OWN_DOORS / RUNNABLE_STORES; the words name `vibespace-vault list` (§8.2), `vibespace-vault request` (P0-c) and the Vault window's «Usable by agent runs» switch — P0-f ships them or rewords; the door realpaths argv[0] before the plan, reads templates inside the cwd fence, hands `entries` facts (`bytes` = the value's length) and the grant (P1 vault-use-reach; until then P0-f's call), decodes each stream with a StringDecoder before `push`, calls `end()` on exit / timeout / lock-kill, passes the audit's scrubbed text through secret-shapes, and names its plan `run` — test-architecture §69c owns the spelling `plan.argv` (the app-install slot's argv; this module's first draft tripped it). ### lane vault-run-door — q-043 P0-f: the DOOR of `vibespace-vault run` on the PURE module (主开发's dispatch 12:18Z; base 5470a4e1 = vault-run-model on 2.369.326; contract design q-043 §8 + §5 P0-f; the five decisions beyond P0-e's brief KEPT by 主开发's ruling)

- THE SWITCH (decision ⑤): off by default; ON needs this page's 验证是你 window (the route reads it; the client opens it FIRST, in the press's own task). Two tables say no: the model's ownDoorOf AND the door's own classOf (RUN_CLASS = storage + app logins; a `long-lived-oauth-token` / `session-token` kind never) — the suite proves the door refuses a login / channel / pairing token even with the model's table made to say yes and the store forced open. THE STORE data/vault-run.json (switches + the 30-day / for-ever «always») carries a MARK: HMAC under a key derived from the DEK (`vault.macOf`, new in the engine, null unless unlocked) — an agent shares the uid and can write the file, never a mark that verifies; a hand-edited store reads as EMPTY, audited `vault-run-store-refused`. An 8-hour «always» and the `seen` shapes live in memory only (a lock ends them).
- THE CARD (decisions ② ④): exit-proxy's ask shape — one per conversation × shape (a second run ⇒ `ask_pending`), 60 s ⇒ `ask_expired`, a full tray ⇒ `ask_unfiled`, the item and the ask ONE state (closed by another door ⇒ `ask_denied`), the caller's request closed ⇒ `caller_gone`, a lock ⇒ `vault_locked`; an allow re-checks the item's detail (`ask_changed`). Its detail is the WHOLE run (the command with its references, the secrets, how each is given, the hosts, the folder, the templates whole, what «this shape» means); a run whose card the store would cut ⇒ `card_too_long`; a hidden / direction character anywhere ⇒ `hidden_chars`. «此形状总是» needs the page's 验证是你 window (`reveal_needs_password` without), 30 days by default, never for a shell / an interpreter / an unknown destination (`always_not_offered`).
- MODEL CHANGE (the design's «shape seen?», §8.3 — P0-e had left it out): runVerdict takes `seen`; a CLUSTER asks every run without a live «always», a LOCAL instance asks a NEW shape and allows it after one 允许 (this unlock). The grid is 9 216 cells now; a new shape draws the card on both kinds (the brief's mutant). Also: the typed argv[0] is refused besides its resolved path (`vi` → vim.basic); the scrubber counts its UTF-8 bytes (`bytes`, the audit's count); the words no longer name `vibespace-vault request` (P0-c is not on this base — they say «ask the user in the chat»); `refusalOf` exported for the door.
- THE RUN: argv[0] on agentEnv()'s PATH (absolute entries only; a bare name never from the cwd) + realpath; the cwd, a tool path and a template inside the exit-transfer fence (project / temp / ~/Downloads, never .ssh / .git / data/) and asked of the mount door FIRST (`storage_blocked`); env = agentEnv() + the agent's plain env + the injected values; files 0600 (O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW) in a 0700 `vs-vault-run-<rand>` under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, shredded + unlinked when the child is gone (the design's «退出即 shred» — the brief's «unlinked after exec» read as the run's end: a tool may open its file late, git's credential file does); stdin = value + newline, closed at once; detached (its own group); 120 s default ≤ 600 s, SIGTERM then SIGKILL 5 s later; per stream StringDecoder → createMasker (≤ 2 MiB together, `truncated`), then secret-shapes in 64 KiB line-cut windows. A grandchild holding the pipes cannot hold the answer (2 s after the child's exit the pipes are cut). ≤ 4 runs per conversation, ≤ 16 at once.
- THE LOCK (decision ③): `vault.onLock` stops every running child by its group (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after the grace) — the agent gets `vault_locked` (+ `killed`), the conversation is noted on the owner's For-you list (the vault's one helper); every card settles; the seen shapes + the 8-hour «always» go. A locked vault refuses a run FIRST. Measured: a SIGTERM-deaf child gone in 402 ms with a 400 ms grace.
- THE AUDIT: one `vault-run` line in data/vault-audit.jsonl per run and per refusal past the parse — by {kind, key, name}, outcome, tool, entries, shapeId (sha256 of the key, 16 hex), hosts, injection, argvExposed, cwd, cmd (secret-shapes'd, ≤ 4 KiB), allowedBy, askId, exit, signal, ms, timedOut, truncated, scrubbed {hits, bytes, byForm}, redacted, stdout / stderr heads (scrubbed, ≤ 4 KiB) — never a value; + `vault-run-switch`, `vault-run-always`, `vault-run-store-refused`. record-clear never clears it (the audit exception).
- THE SECURITY REVIEW (an independent read-only reviewer over the door before the commit; no path found by which a value reaches the answer, the audit, the card, the logs or the store) — fixed here: ① A RUN ENDS WHOLE — a lock / timeout ended only the direct child (the SIGKILL backstop was cleared when it exited): now the child's group is SIGKILLed when the run ends (a backgrounded `cmd &` held the value) and so is every process carrying the run's MARK (`VS_RUN_MARK=<folder>` in its environ — a setsid / double-forked stray), found by a fresh /proc scan (pid-identity census: a `scan` row); a lock shreds the run files AT ONCE; ② UNBOUNDED INPUT — the URL scan's scheme was unbounded: a 32 KiB «a.a.a…» took 335 ms, a megabyte would stall the hub for minutes (quadratic) — now `{0,31}` (64 KiB: 4 ms); the request ≤ 64 KiB of words and a 4 KiB folder (`request_too_large`); ③ THE SHAPE KEY carried env NAMES only and a routing flag's value as a class — now `vr2`: plain env VALUES (`PGHOST=evil` is a new shape), keyed flag values (ssh -o / -J / -F / -W / -L / -R / -D / -S, curl -x / --proxy / --resolve / --connect-to / --socks*, git -c, rsync -e), PGHOST / PGHOSTADDR / MYSQL_HOST name hosts, HOME / XDG_*_HOME / any-case npm_config_userconfig refused as plain env, no «always» for npm / pip / docker (they run the project's code), a config file the card cannot show (curl -K, ssh -F, kubectl --kubeconfig) or a program an agent could have written; ④ THE CARD names the PROGRAM (its real path; «in a folder an agent can write» when the hub's uid can write it or its folder — no «always» then); ⑤ a non-hex store mark threw in timingSafeEqual on every call — now a 64-hex check inside the judging try; LOW: the store carries a GENERATION (an older copy restored = a replay, read as empty), switch-OFF drops the entry's «always» + seen shapes, the boot sweep shreds only a GONE hub's folders (`.owner` = src/proc-identity.js identity; another hub's live runs untouched) after ending their marked strays, the scrubber is built BEFORE any file holds a value, the 2 s pipe-cut path drops the held tail too, data/vault-run.json and templates are read through ONE O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK fd with fstat + a bound, the cwd passes the hidden-character door, `list` spells references through the model (`!'()*` used to drop an entry). ### lane vault-mint-put — design q-043 §9 (the owner 2026-10-19: 「保险库给 agent 一条『存放 + 随机密码』指令…agent 看不到密码也能完成任务」): the two agent verbs, their provenance, and the q-043 ① read law
- 主开发's dispatch; base 9a5507aa = 2.369.326 on origin/master. The Vault window v2 (lane vault-window-v2, 28f86535) is NOT on this base; the provenance rows are coded against src/vault-inventory.js as it stands here and the integrator wires v2's chip onto them (SEAM, below). ONE commit; agentd untouched.
- THE PRODUCT NEVER SHOWS A MINTED VALUE TO THE AGENT, AND AN AGENT CAN NEVER READ A STORED VALUE BACK. `vibespace-vault mint <name> [--length 24] [--charset ascii-printable|alnum|digits] [--for …]` — the HUB makes the random value (src/vault.js randomSecret, uniform rejection-sampling) and seals it; the agent gets only the entry name + its `vault://` reference. `vibespace-vault put <name> --from-file <0600 file> | --stdin` — the agent hands a value it already has; the value rides a 0600 file or stdin, NEVER argv (the CLI refuses a positional value; the route refuses a `value` in the URL query, `value_in_argv`). The owner reveals either in the Vault window behind 「验证是你」.
- The namespace is `agent:<conversation-or-group>/<name>`: the SCOPE is the authenticated principal's (a vsst_ session's conversation id, a jbt_ job's `job-<id>`) — derived server-side, never the agent's to choose; `<name>` holds no `/` and no `:`, so a name can never forge a scope (a namespace escape is refused `bad_name` before any entry is touched). An agent may CREATE in its own namespace without an owner card (no money, no leak) and may not READ (use = run / the browser fill, later lanes). Every mint/put is audited (`vault-agent-mint` / `vault-agent-put` {name, actor, by:agent} — never the value).
- Files: src/vault.js (PURE: agentEntryName, vaultRefOf, MINT_CHARSETS + mintVerdict + randomSecret); src/server/vault-engine.js (isSecretName now accepts `agent:<scope>/<name>`; agentMint/agentPut seal and NEVER return a value; secretNames carries prov/actor); src/routes/vault.js (POST /api/agent/vault/mint|put — scope from the session, the argv guard, trimmed agent errors that never leak the vault's facts); src/vault-inventory.js (secretRowOf's agent branch + AGENT_PROV {minted: never seen, stored: saw plaintext} + rowOf passes `provenance` through); data/bin/vibespace-vault (the mint/put verbs; put enforces a 0600 file).
- SEAM for the integrator / lane vault-window-v2: each agent entry's inventory row now carries `provenance = { by:'agent', prov:'minted'|'stored', sawPlaintext, actor }` and a `detail` meta line; v2's window `provenanceOf` chip reads `row.provenance`. The base window renders `detail` as a meta line via its existing 'secrets' path (no window code change this lane).
- SNAPSHOT: package.json is bumped to 2.369.328 so test-changelog-style accepts the `## 2.369.329` heading as NEXT_PATCH (the builder-branch convention). THE INTEGRATOR SETS THE REAL VERSION (.327/.328 presumably belong to sibling lanes merging first). src/agentd/version.js was regenerated to .328 by the build.
- Gates: fast gate (build = esbuild + test-architecture §78 + i18n-check); test-vault-engine 132 (PURE + engine mint/put + 2 MUTANTS: mint-echoes-value, namespace-escape); test-vault-routes 44 (scope-from-session, escape ⇒ bad_name, put value in the URL ⇒ value_in_argv, a bearer reads no value ⇒ q-043 ① law, locked ⇒ 423, + an argv-reading MUTANT); test-vault-inventory 95 (provenance rows + owner reveal + a rowOf-drops-provenance MUTANT); test-vault-law 32 (the agent-door census + mint/put answer no `value:`); test-record-clear-census 242 (mint/put are `meta` — they reach the jobs stash only to resolve a token to identity); the heavy test-vault-window-chrome 71 (regression — the inventory rows do not disturb the window).

### lane frp-spawn-env-allowlist — frpc's env BUILT, never the hub's inherited (主开发's finding in the .327 release chain, 2026-10-20 13:4xZ; base cb53ddc6 = .327)
- THE FINDING: test-frp-plugin's leg «frpc's env carries the instance token and the knock — never VIBESPACE_FRPS_TOKEN beside them» went RED when the suite ran from an agent conversation's shell — the fake frpc saw CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN and VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN: `start()` spawned frpc with `{ ...process.env, … }` minus two names, so frpc held whatever launched the hub. The lane env.sh (`env -i`) and systemd launch clean, hence the green lane run and mirror. Reproduced on the base from a PLANTED env (fake VIBESPACE_SESSION_TOKEN / CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN / CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY / HTTPS_PROXY): RED naming exactly the planted token names.
- MEASURED (a scratch copy of the box's frpc 0.70.0; loopback only — a fake frps and a fake proxy, both ours): frpc starts and dials frps on an EMPTY env (no PATH / HOME / LANG / TMPDIR), so HOME is not kept; of the proxy names it reads lowercase `http_proxy` ALONE (it sends `CONNECT <frps>` there) — HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY / all_proxy are ignored, and so is no_proxy (even for 127.0.0.1). No unit on this box and no chart value sets a proxy.
- FIX: PURE `relayEnv(base, { token, knock })` in src/relay-token.js with `RELAY_ENV_KEEP = ['PATH', 'LANG', 'TMPDIR', 'http_proxy']` and `KNOCK_ENV` (`VIBESPACE_FRP_AUTH_TOKEN`, moved from frp.js): the kept names from the hub's env + this instance's token + the knock during the grace only; an empty value is left out, a relay variable already in the hub's env is never taken. `src/plugins/frp.js` start(): `env = RT.relayEnv(process.env, { token, knock })` — its one long-lived child; frp.js copies process.env nowhere now. frpc.toml names `{{ .Envs.VIBESPACE_FRP_AUTH_TOKEN }}` only when the same start sends the knock, so the login never renders a missing name.
- DEVIATION from the brief: `http_proxy` is KEPT (the brief counted "a proxy" among the dropped). ### lane pool-provider-aware — the account pool knows each member's PROVIDER; a move to another provider is never silent (design q-053 r1 §2 + §6 row P0b; the owner 2026-10-20 「号池的部分要重新设计一下，区分不同 provider，切换账号本身也会影响 provider」 + decision ①: cross-provider auto-switch default NEVER — 「切到 X 需要你同意」)
- THE RULES (PURE src/account-pool-auto.js «THE PROVIDER»; every one OPTIONAL by input — `providerOf` absent ⇒ every verdict byte-identical, the readLogin rule): ① a candidate must SERVE the conversation's model — a member of the conversation's OWN provider serves it by construction (one provider, one list), another provider's must `resolveModel` it (the id, the id without `[1m]`, `aliases` → a LISTED id, a dated id by its undated prefix; `modelsSource:'none'` / no rows ⇒ null), else it is named in `modelBlocked`; ② a move across providers is COLD (`hotSwitchFor` ⇒ 'cold') and never voluntary — only off a current member that cannot serve at all (the hard wall), never for EDF / the spare lane / a soft band / a spawn; under the pool's `crossProvider:'never'` (the default) it is an OFFER (`crossOffer` on the blocked verdict), under `'allow'` the cold move (`cross` {from, to, model, toModel}, `switchMode:'cold'`); ③ the model is re-resolved against the new provider (`cross.toModel`). A provider without readings (`fallbackOnly: true`) is chosen only under 'allow', after every member with readings. An UNKNOWN provider (a deleted account) agrees with any (no claim).
- THE THREE DECISIONS: `decidePoolSwitch` (+ `providerOf`, `conversationModel`, `crossProvider`; a member of another provider is held APART from every ranking — `crossRows` — so the own provider always goes first), `rankPoolMembers` (+ `providerOf`, `fromProvider`: the device's sealed-orders snapshot is a HOT list — never another provider or a fallback-only member, whatever the setting), `soonestUsableMember` (parking: 'never' ⇒ own provider only; 'allow' ⇒ another that serves the model, after the own); `decidePinnedPlacement`: a pin of another provider is the owner's own (cold) move when it serves the model, else `pin-model-not-served` by name (the explicit pin route answers `model_not_served:<providerId>`). `poolBlockedNotice` says the offer («B (DeepSeek) can take it as deepseek-chat — a move to another provider restarts the conversation and waits for your OK in For you.») and the model wall by name.
- THE STORE (src/accounts.js): `memberProviderOf(id)` = the provider store's answer for the ACCOUNT (the lookup that store registers: `setProviderLookup(account → record)` — P0a's `providers.forAccount`), else its harness's FIRST-PARTY subscription read off the harness's own creds row (`loginLabel`: «Claude subscription», «ChatGPT subscription»; no harness-id table — test-architecture §78's id-branch ratchet) — never null for a known account; `poolMembers` rows carry `provider {id, kind, label}`; `poolCurrentFor(pool, sess, {withProvider:true})` ⇒ `{memberId, provider}` (the plain answer unchanged); the pool record's `crossProvider` ('never' | 'allow', absent = never; `updatePool` refuses anything else by name; PATCH /api/accounts/pool/:id passes it); `list()` carries `crossProvider` + `currentProvider`. SEAM (P0a, lane provider-record, cbbbe0e6 — landed while this lane ran, not in its base): wiring = ONE line `accounts.setProviderLookup((acct) => providers.forAccount(acct))`, and `resolveModel` delegates to src/model-providers.js's; this lane coded against design q-053 §1's record shape.
- THE ENGINE (src/server/usage-pool-engine.js «THE PROVIDER»): `providerIn(a, session)` into EVERY decision that can move a conversation — the spawn chooser (placing: never a cross move; a pin of another provider is not where a spawn starts — it applies through the cold switch), the per-session pass, the pool DEFAULT ('never', no card: the cards are per conversation), removal, the explicit pin route, auto-resume's alternative; the sealed orders, the auth-failure eviction and the default's parking keep to the member's own provider. THE DOORS THAT RE-POINT A LINK HOT never cross: a removal's verdict decides with 'never' and never follows a pin onto another provider; "Move every conversation here now" leaves a conversation of another provider where it is (`other-provider`, said as «stay where they are»); a member the store no longer knows (a deleted account) answers the pool's own first-party provider (`poolProviderOf`) — never «unknown», which agrees with any. `applyCrossMove` = THE cold move: the link → the member, ONE `pool-auto-switched` restart request carrying the re-resolved `model` (the client's `_poolColdRestart` resumes on it), a toast, and ONE line owed to the RESUMED conversation («Switched from A (Claude subscription) to B (DeepSeek) — model sonnet → deepseek-chat», fed by `feedPeerCard` at the next pass — the restart rebuilds the chat). NO connected client ⇒ nothing moves (a re-point the running CLI followed by itself would be the silent switch); it is asked again.

### lane pool-provider-latents — the two LATENT cross-provider moves closed: the device's sealed orders and account deletion (design q-055 verify M1 + M2, follows lane pool-provider-aware 59a2b451; money class) — must land before P0a's `accounts.setProviderLookup((acct) => providers.forAccount(acct))` line is wired (today every pool is one provider, so nothing moves on this tree)
- M1 — THE DEVICE'S SEALED ORDERS: the order named no provider, and the daemon's `_execute` took `ranked[0]` for ANY matched link — a conversation the owner had allowed onto another provider (a cold move or a pin) was re-pointed BACK, hot, by the device while the hub was away (no card, no restart; after Train 2's derived env, a credential read against the other vendor's endpoint). Now the order carries each ranked path's provider (`ranked[i].provider`), each per-session link's conversation provider (`links: [{path, provider}]`), the default's (`provider`) and a members table (`members: {id: provider}`); THE RULE is one PURE file both halves load — `src/sealed-orders.js` (imports nothing): `orderProviderFields` (the hub, usage-pool-engine `pushSealedOrders`) and `deviceFallback` (the device, agentd `sealedOrders._execute`): the conversation's provider = the member its link points at NOW (re-read at the banner); candidates = ranked rows of THAT provider only, under never AND allow (the reflex is a HOT re-point the running CLI follows by itself — another provider is the hub's cold move with a client and a line, or the owner's card; a device with no hub has neither); a link that now points at another provider than the order recorded ⇒ nothing (`moved-since`); a provider the order cannot name ⇒ nothing (`provider-unknown`, never a guess); an order with NO provider field (an older hub — every pool one provider) walks exactly as before; a missing field where others exist never widens. An OLDER DAEMON reads only `linkPaths` + `ranked`: `linkPaths` now holds only the links of the ranked list's provider, so an older daemon can never match — never re-point — a conversation of another provider (reduced coverage on skew, never a wrong move). A cold cross move (`applyCrossMove`) re-pushes the order AT ONCE (the moved link leaves `linkPaths` before a server-down window can open), and a default left UNPLACED (M2) keeps its own provider in the order (the reflex never re-creates it on another one). The daemon logs a refusal by name: «no usable fallback member of its own provider (no-same-provider: pv-…)».
- M2 — ACCOUNT DELETION (`accounts.remove` → `_healPoolsAfterRemoval`, a HOT re-point): the default went to the engine's pick else `alive[0]`, each link to the engine's pick else the POOL DEFAULT — whatever its provider; and the engine judged a deleted member as the pool's own first-party provider, so a deleted DeepSeek member's conversation could be "decided" onto a Claude member. Now the store reads the deleted account's provider BEFORE it splices it (`goneProviderOf` / `goneNameOf`: remembered in the process, carried by the mark across a restart; the engine's `poolProviderOf` asks it before the pool's own) and re-points only onto a member of THAT provider (the engine's pick only when it is one; else the default when it is; else that provider's first live member — they serve the conversation's model by construction). Nobody of that provider left ⇒ the link (or the default) is UNPLACED: unlinked + a persisted mark on the pool record (`unplaced: {default?, links: {sessKey: {member, name, provider, at, asked?}}}`, `unplacedOf` / `unplacedPools`), billing NOBODY — `poolCurrentFor` answers null for it (never "the default"), `hasOwnPoolLink` counts it (never a follower a default move restarts or carries), memberRemoved skips it. The engine decides it FROM the deleted member (`placeUnplaced`, every pass + at once from the DELETE route): a member of its own provider that can serve ⇒ the link written again (the removal's words; restarted when the pool is cold); its provider only walled ⇒ parked like 全B (`holdRemoved`); the pool's 'allow' + another provider serving its model ⇒ the cold move with its line; otherwise THE OWNER'S CARD 「账号已删，<对话> 需要你选一个 <provider> 账号」 ("Account deleted — "<title>" needs you to pick a <provider> account") — the exhausted case's card (`pool-cross-provider`: Allow once / Always for this pool / Deny, re-judged from the deleted member by `crossMoveNow`) when another provider's member could take it, the words alone when none can (filed ONCE — `noteUnplacedAsked` keeps it across a restart). Any placement (the owner's Allow, a pin, its own provider) clears the mark; the boot link sweep drops the mark of a conversation that is gone. THE DEFAULT: unplaced the same way; the pool tick decides FROM its deleted member (it never stops running for the pool's other conversations), and the spawn self-heal sets it again only onto a member of its provider — a new conversation with its own link starts without it, one that would read the default is refused by name (`default_unplaced`). A one-provider pool heals exactly as before.
- NOT A BILLED TURN: nothing here starts a turn — a re-placement is a link (+ a resume, `resumeSession` without a prompt, on a cold pool); a parked conversation's one continue is 全B's existing arm through auto-resume's authorizer. test-spend-paths 364 unchanged.

moved-since; provider-unknown; a row without a provider never widens), orderProviderFields, the real engine's pushed order (ranked + links + members + linkPaths without the other provider's link), a one-provider order unchanged, the cold move's immediate re-push, the unplaced default's provider in the order; **RED mutant: the device filter dropped ⇒ the DeepSeek conversation moved onto Claude**; M2 — the real store + engine through the DELETE route's own wiring: UNPLACED (bills nobody, never the Claude default), the deleted member's provider in the removal verdict, the card with the offer (Allow once ⇒ the cold move onto OpenRouter, deepseek-chat, the line naming the deleted member), the card without one (once, persisted), a DeepSeek account signed in later takes it, allow ⇒ the cold move itself, the unplaced default (the tick still runs; a new conversation still starts; a default reader refused by name); **RED mutant: the heal's provider filter dropped ⇒ the deleted DeepSeek member's conversation lands on the Claude default, hot, no card**. test-account-pool 84 (was 67): the store alone — the engine's other-provider pick refused, the remembered provider, UNPLACED + persisted + asked, a placement clears it, the default's mark, the boot sweep, a one-provider pool unchanged;
