### lane vault-totp — two-step codes in the vault (design q-047 L1; the owner 2026-10-19 「哦还有个 TOTP 也可以支持一下」, decisions ①–⑤ 2026-10-20 with ①'s amendment)
- THE MODEL: a two-step code is the vault's own secret entry `totp:<name>` (src/server/vault-engine.js SECRET_RE gains `totp`) — its value ONE JSON line `{v, seed (base32, canonical), digits 6–8, period 15–120, algorithm SHA1/256/512, issuer, account, addedAt, source}`, sealed whole (AAD = the entry name, as every entry). No new store, no new key file; SECRETS_AT_REST names it (src/vault.js).
- PURE src/totp.js (imports nothing; the HMAC injected — node:crypto on the hub): base32 (RFC 4648; spaces / dashes / case / padding forgiven, a length no encoder makes refused), hotp / totp (RFC 4226 / 6238), verify ±window (kept for a later sign-in door, wired to none), parseOtpauth (hotp refused by name; the issuer parameter over the label's), uriOf, valueOf / recordOf, nameOf (`github-owner`), grantOf + useVerdict. Refused by name, never trimmed.
- A PERSON (src/server/vault-totp.js behind src/routes/vault.js `person()`): `POST /api/vault/totp` adds (an otpauth link or the seed + settings — both taken OFF the body like a password; `preview: true` = the code it makes, nothing stored), `GET /api/vault/totp/:name` = 看码 — the CURRENT code with NO 「验证是你」 (decision ①: a code dies in 30 s, the seed is the secret), every view ONE audit line `vault-totp-view {who, ip, entry}`, paced 20 a minute per sign-in / 60 for the vault (its own buckets — a code never starves a reveal); `DELETE` drops its grants FIRST (an unwritable grants file refuses), then the entry (works locked).
- THE SEED (①'s amendment: viewable behind 「验证是你」, audited as a reveal, never in a list, never to an agent): the row is revealable through the window's own door — `POST /api/vault/reveal` `secrets:totp:<name>#seed` answers ONE value, the otpauth link (the seed + every setting, importable by any authenticator), audited `vault-reveal`; never the raw record. The inventory row carries the NAME only (kind `totp`, field `seed`, «Two-step code»): the issuer, account and settings are the value.
- THE AGENT DOOR (decision ②): `GET /api/agent/vault/totp/:name` (`vibespace-vault totp <name> [--json]`) → `{ok, name, code, secondsLeft, period}` — named fields only. Scoped by a person's grant (用于… — `POST /api/vault/totp/:name/grants {subjects}`, ✕ = `DELETE /api/vault/totp/grants/:id`; data/vault-grants.json 0600, tmp `wx` + fsync + rename): a conversation's grant holds THAT RUN — the digest of its session token (`runOfToken`), so a conversation that ended and came back is not covered (design §5 «会话结束失效»); a Task Group's covers its members. No grant / another conversation / a new run ⇒ 403 `not_granted`; a view ⇒ 409 `not_running`; a job or unknown token ⇒ 401; LOCKED ⇒ 423 first; paced 20 a minute per conversation; every answer ONE `vault-totp-use` line (ok / the refusal's code — never a code). The first-use For-you card (q-043 §6 / q-046's) is NOT in L1: the window's 用于… is the minimal form the design names (§4 #3).
- THE WINDOW (the L1 hunk kept small for L2's merge — src/lib/vault-window.js: one import, the delete confirm words, one line in rowFor, one in build, one in refresh; the rest in the new src/lib/vault-totp-row.js): 看码 → the code (3 + 3), its ring (`--p`) and seconds, asked again at the step's boundary only while the page is visible and at most 10 times; 复制 (30 s clear); 用于… (the automation picker's shape: running conversations + Task Groups, grant chips with ✕, an ended run's chip says so); 显示's help says it shows the seed and its settings (the owner's confusion note: a reveal's reason is the door's help, never a state). The ADD DIALOG is the mock's (totp-add-desktop, L2's drawing): L1 ships its door with `preview`.
- THE WIRING: `sessionCallerOf` / `conversationSubjects` lifted out of the automation routes' registration in src/server/mounts-plugins-wiring.js (one reading of a session token for both doors). `totpRunOf` finds the running session that carries the id AS ITS OWN — `addressableId(s) === cid` (a pending fork shares its parent's id and is never picked: test-msg-cli-groups §2c's addressing census stays at its 8 classified sites) — and reads its token on its own line (§71's raw-secret compare rule). A fork that CALLS with its parent's id presents its own token, so the parent's run-bound grant never covers it.
- FIXTURES: every seed / otpauth fixture is BUILT AT RUNTIME (`['JBSWY3DP','EHPK3PXP'].join('')`, `base32Encode(Buffer.from('12345678901234567890'))`, `base32Encode(randomBytes(20))`; even the product's alphabet constant is split) — the pre-push guard's generic-secret-assign flagged a literal `secret=<base32>` (主开发's ruling: concatenation, never an allow row).
- CENSUSES MOVED: scripts/fixtures/boot-sentinel-gets.json smoke + the three GETs (test-reach-model / the heavy boot sentinel); the `exists` refusal carries no record text (test-record-clear-census's sentence receivers); test-vault-law ④ (the agent doors = + the code door, whose answer is named fields only, no secretGet / reveal / unlock); mount-reader-census §86 (+ src/server/vault-totp.js, own-tree 2: the grants file); test-vault-secrets ⑧ (the seed in no file under data/ — raw / hex / base64 — and THE SEED'S READERS: every src/ caller of secretGet( named); kb-file-structure INDEX + 4 lines. test-claude-md-retire's latent middle-row pick (a new INDEX line moved `gone` / `live` onto a non-fixture row ⇒ a TypeError) — int325's own fix (47421d14) carried VERBATIM so the rebase merges an identical hunk.
- GATES (on 7fce2877, the fast gate on a snapshot with package.json at 2.369.327 for the .328 heading): fast gate ALL GREEN 313 s (and a no-fail-fast pass of all 444 fast suites, whose two reds — a bullet's word «verification» and a `totp.add(` read as a For-you add site — were fixed: the method is addEntry); test-totp 48 · test-vault-engine 88 · test-vault-law 32 · test-vault-inventory 93 · test-vault-routes 57 (7 mutants RED, the seed-answering agent door among them) · test-vault-secrets 133 · test-key-file-law 121 · test-record-clear-census 242 · test-user-todos-layout 314; heavy: test-vault-chrome 70 (④b in a real page, 54 s) · test-boot-sentinel 15 · test-vault-window-chrome 71 · test-automation-keys-chrome 41.

### lane vault-window-v2 — the Vault window grouped by what each secret is FOR (design q-047 §3 by the design desk; the owner 2026-10-19 「鉴于要支持的种类越来越复杂，建议重新设计一下 vault 界面的 UI」; decisions ④ group by the nine purposes, ⑤ this lane ∥ L1 vault-totp; the owner's confusion note 2026-10-20 07:3xZ, B-7edc)
- THE PURPOSES (PURE src/vault-inventory.js `PURPOSES` / `purposeOf` / `groupByPurpose`): two-step · accounts · integrations · machines · storage · app-logins · passkeys · automation · agents (+ other, drawn only when a row lands there). ONE row ⇒ ONE purpose, first rule wins: an `agent:` entry → agents (q-043 §9, before its store) · accounts → accounts · an integration's per-machine row (`<row>/<host>` — the same shape doorsOf already reads) and secrets `host:` / `frp:` → machines · other integrations + every channel → integrations · mounts → storage · app-secrets → app-logins · passkeys → passkeys · automation (`apikey:`) → automation · secrets `totp:` → two-step · anything else (a sealed file's key) → other. The window no longer groups by store (技术细节 still names store · entry · field). GROUPS / STORES unchanged — the collector and the routes still read the stores the same way.
- THE PROVENANCE (PURE `provenanceOf`, one chip, rules in order): `origin:'put'` → agent-put (agent 存入 · agent 见过明文) · an `agent:` entry → agent-mint · `origin` qr / paste → scan (扫码 · 我自己) · a `totp:` entry → me · `revealable:false` → system (系统 · 永不显示) · automation / `origin:'mint'` / secrets `apikey|frp|host|file:` → hub-mint · else me. The bar's filter has four choices over the six chips (me = me + scan; system = system + hub-mint). The row gained TWO named fields, copied closed by `rowOf`: `origin` ('mint' / 'put' / 'qr' / 'paste' / 'manual', else null — no store lists one yet; lane vault-totp's `source` and q-043 §9's put will) and `expiresAt` (src/accounts.js now lists the long-lived token's end = minted + OAT_TTL on its `oat` row ⇒ 「N 天后到期」 within 3 days, 「已过期」 after — PURE `stateChipsOf`, plus 「建议轮换」 for agent-put).
- THE VIEW (PURE `viewOf`): search (the English words + the page's OWN words for kind / purpose / provenance / label — `searchRows(rows, q, { wordsOf })`) → the provenance filter → 只看可显示 → the purpose picked; the rail's counts = the filtered rows per purpose (so a count IS the number of rows the list shows for it); `sortRows(rows, by, { byStore: false })` sorts inside a purpose (default 最近使用, design §3.2).
- THE WINDOW (src/lib/vault-window.js, rewritten; 980×680): rail · bar (search, 排序, 出处 chips, 只看可显示, 「添加…」 = `registerVaultAdd` doors — account / integration key / channel account / automation key; lane vault-totp registers 两步验证… there) · note (count, the countdown chip, 全部隐藏 while a value is open, 全部显示) · the list (purpose heads; 全部 draws only non-empty purposes, a picked one draws its head even empty — 自动化 key's 铸造… stays reachable). A row = name + meta · kind chip · provenance chip (its help = where it came from) · state chips · last use · the value and the doors BY KIND (a never-shown row has no 显示; a two-step row — kind `totp` / `doors.code`, lane vault-totp's — draws 「看码」 over `GET /api/vault/totp/:name`, the code + seconds only, never a seed) · 技术细节. KEYED: `build()` keeps a row's element while its facts' signature holds (an open value survives a refresh), `place()` MOVES nodes (`reconcile`), never rebuilds; icons are built node by node (createElementNS — the module still names no HTML sink, test-vault-inventory ①b).
- THE OWNER'S CONFUSION NOTE: the automation key's 「只为交给外界」 span beside the value (the `vw-ak-why` line, and the row detail that repeated it in the meta) is gone; every 「显示」 carries its reason as its title — the automation key's is the owner's own sentence 「显示密钥值——只在要交给外部系统时；内部 agent 按授权使用，不需要看到值」 (zh; en + ja beside it), any other value's says the 5-minute window; 隐藏 says hide.
- 「需要你」 = For you's OWN items (`inboxModel(app)` — the one client store; PURE `bandItemsOf`: origin `vault`, open, not cleared, urgent first then newest, ≤ 5, the total in the head; PURE `bandDoorsOf` per action type). Answers go through the model's verbs — `runAction` (the held automation call: 允许一次 · 一直 · 拒绝), `setStatus(id, 'done')` (知道了), the row's own 换新… / 打开行, `showUnlock` — so answered in the band it leaves the tray, answered in the tray it leaves the band (one item). In the tray a `vault-use-failed` / `vault-rotate` body opens the Vault window on its row (user-todos-actions `jump` → `replayOpenSpec({ action: 'openVault', focus })`).
- THE TWO NEW PRODUCERS (src/server/vault-hooks.js `createVaultAttention`, origin `vault`, kind notice, key `vault`, words as structure): 使用失败 `useFailed({ entry, name, code, who })` — PURE `useFailVerdict`: a cause the owner can act on (`vault_locked` → locked; `not_granted` / `verb_not_in_scope` / `once_spent` / `key_revoked` → not granted; `subject_ended` / `ask_expired` → expired; the owner's own `ask_denied` / `ask_quiet`, a caller gone, a bad call are NOT failures) — ONE card per entry per hour, its count updated while open, never re-filed inside the hour once answered (counted only), the next hour reopens it with a fresh count; wired at the automation engine's ONE audit exit (`done()` in `use()`: every refusal goes there — a locked refusal comes before a key is picked, so it files the automation door's card `apikey:*`). 建议轮换 `agentPut({ entry, name, who })` — one card per store act, nothing re-files it; its caller is q-043 §9's `put`, which does not exist in this tree yet, so in production it files nothing until that lands (the window's 「建议轮换」 chip reads `origin:'put'` off the row for the same reason). The token-expiry card the design lists stays the login-expiry watch's (origin login, the Agents area); the band is origin vault only, and the row's own 「N 天后到期」 chip carries the fact in the window.
- LOCKED (design §3.5): the rail lists the purposes with «—» (not pressable), the list holds one sentence + 「解锁…」 (beside the header's — the design puts it there), NO 「添加…」. The search/filter bar stays away while locked (lane vault-one-door's rule: nothing to search, no greyed control) — the mock draws it; this is the one place the window keeps the earlier law over the mock (the pixel numbers below include it).

### lane win-input-elevated — the device agent's elevated-input surround (owner 2026-10-20: 「Windows 上的管理员权限能不能成为默认」 — yes, by default; SURROUND ONLY)
- THE DECISION: the owner raises the elevation himself (the device-agent installer now registers the logon task at RunLevel Highest BY DEFAULT, asking the OS's own consent once). THE PRODUCT WRITES NO AUTO-ELEVATION AND NO CROSS-INTEGRITY INPUT CODE — when the daemon happens to run elevated, its SendInput reaches admin windows by the OS's own rules (UIPI is satisfied because the SENDER is elevated); the product just REPORTS it and FENCES it. The heading is .327 on a .325 package: the fast gate judged on a snapshot bumped to .326 (NEXT_PATCH), so test-changelog-style ④ accepts the entry; the integrator sets the real version.
- THE CAPABILITY (src/agentd/agentd.js): a new hello-ack field `elevated: true|false` — the daemon reads its OWN token (win32 only; IsInRole(Administrator) via psOnce, cached, read live each hello so it survives a self-upgrade; non-win32 / a failed probe ⇒ false). Recorded off the hello-ack onto the host record (client.js onElevated → dial-pairing/hosts noteElevated → h.deviceElevated, the onPolicy mirror) and surfaced on the desktop-access row. An old daemon that cannot report it ⇒ treated as not-elevated, never asked to inject into an admin window.
- THE FENCE (src/input-inject.js): PURE injectAllowed({windowClass, elevated, allow}) → {ok, why}. The UAC consent UI (Credential Dialog Xaml Host, Consent) and the secure desktop ($$$Secure UAP Background Dialog, UACBackgroundWindowClass) are refused BY CLASS ALWAYS — even elevated, even if an allow-list names them. An optional per-window allow-list (state/input-allow.json) narrows the rest; absent ⇒ every non-denied window. The resident PowerShell gained FrontClass/FrontTitle (GetClassName/GetWindowText) + an `E 0|1` flag so the unelevated UIPI short-circuit fires ONLY when the daemon is NOT elevated; inject(), when elevated, reads the foreground window once per batch, applies injectAllowed, and writes ONE audit line (state/input-audit.jsonl: at, actor, windowClass, windowTitle, keys, clicks, ok, why) — a denied batch sends not one press.
- THE INSTALLER (scripts/vibespace-agentd-install.ps1): RunLevel Highest by default via New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal — inline when already admin, else from an elevated child through ONE Start-Process -Verb RunAs (the child gets only the task name + the SECRET-FREE argument string + the user id; the task is argless, no token rides the command line). A declined consent (or -NoElevate) ⇒ the normal-rights fallback register + the machine card's 「Run as administrator…」 door. The daemon's self-heal (hidden-start.js taskWriteScript) stays normal-rights (a non-elevated daemon cannot set Highest; a self-upgrade only replaces current/, the task level persists).
- THE UI: the machine card (sidebar-mounts) wears an ADMIN badge when elevated, offers the 「Run as administrator…」 door (explain + a copyable admin recipe) when a Windows device is at normal rights; the pairing dialog says the agent runs as administrator by default with a 「以普通权限安装」 toggle (appends -NoElevate); manage-agents' Machines card names it. 10 new i18n keys (zh + ja).
- GATES: test-input-inject (new, fast) — injectAllowed over every shape + a MUTANT (a copy without the hard-deny ALLOWS the consent UI ⇒ RED) + the live fence over an in-memory resident child; test-agentd-hidden-start (+elevationUnit: Highest by default / RunAs consent / normal-rights fallback / -NoElevate / no token in the child); test-stream-op (+the hello-ack `elevated` assertion); test-desktop-webrtc (the INPUT_PS regex now pins the unelevated-only UIPI short-circuit + FrontClass). A portable-pwsh probe (win-input-elevated/probes/elevate-proof.mjs) proves the installer flow in a real PowerShell engine with stub cmdlets (the consent prompt never driven — a stub records that RunAs was requested).

### lane relay-token-per-instance — the frp relay token becomes PER INSTANCE, bound to its public names, revocable, NOT in the vault (the owner's decision 2026-10-20 07:4xZ, 「每实例独立 token、不进保险库」; contract = design q-051 r1, /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/design-desk/q-051-relay-token-per-instance.md §0–§7; owner Q1 grace 7 days ending early after 24 h of no `legacy` line, Q2 one cluster token + names by pod name, Q3 a revoke keeps the id; base 2ca1ffdd = 2.369.324)
- PURE `src/relay-token.js` (imports nothing, crypto handed in; test-architecture PURE set): the record `{v:1, instanceId 'vi-<12 hex>', label (shell-safe `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, it is pasted on the relay host), token 'vsrt_'+base64url(32 B) | null, mintedAt, rotatedAt, revokedAt, prefixes ['pf-','vibespace-instance'], subdomains ≤ 64}`, `parse` ⇒ null on any bad shape (revoked ⇔ no token), mint / rotate (same id) / revoke (id kept, token forgotten), `identityOf` (VIBESPACE_RELAY_CLUSTER_TOKEN + VIBESPACE_INSTANCE_NAME > the record > none; a pod named like an instance id has none), `registrationLine` (sha256 only — add / rotate / revoke), `frpcLines` (`user = "<id>"` + `metadatas.token = "{{ .Envs.VIBESPACE_RELAY_TOKEN }}"`), `nameVerdict` / `strippedName` (frps registers `<user>.<name>`), `refusalOf` / `loginOf` (the relay's words out of a proxy's start error / frpc.log — `knock_refused` = frps's own "token in login doesn't match…"), `alertOf` (ONE For-you item per name, i18n lines).
- `src/plugins/frp.js`: the record at `data/relay-token.json` via the new host-handle field `h.dataDir` (src/plugins.js), written by secret-file replaceShredding (0600, atomic, the old bytes overwritten). The first start of a relay configured the shared way MINTS (no outage: the plugin takes an unregistered id as the knock during the grace); `relayAdopt` at the boot replay / an unlock does the same for a frpc an OLDER build left running (it survives the hub upgrade detached — the owner's box restarts node only) and restarts it onto the identity once. frpc.toml: `user` + `metadatas.token` template, `auth.token` template only while the KNOCK is sent; the spawn env carries `VIBESPACE_FRP_AUTH_TOKEN` (the knock) + `VIBESPACE_RELAY_TOKEN` and drops VIBESPACE_FRPS_TOKEN / the cluster's name (each rides once). A LOCKED vault no longer stops an instance that holds its own token (status `knockLocked`, `vaultLocked` only for a shared-token-only instance — the old door). The knock is the old `tokenState` (the vault's `frp:token`, the plaintext override, the cluster's env) until `relayUpgradedAt` / `relayKnocklessAt`. `observe()` (publish, the vault's open hook, a 60 s unref'd watch while frpc runs): a login without the knock (frpc.log since this start, ≤ 16 KB) ⇒ `relayKnocklessAt`; the relay refusing the knock while an own token exists ⇒ one restart without it (≤ 1 / 10 min). Restarts wait for the old frpc to leave (`restartSoon`, async — the admin port). RETIREMENT (`RETIRE_ID 2026-10-relay-token-per-instance`, in the plugin's record; a boot migration cannot drop a vault entry — the vault is locked at boot — so the act sits in the open hook): only once the own token PUBLISHED (a proxy ran under it) AND a knockless login succeeded, `frp:token` is dropped (now when unlocked, else at the next unlock), `tokenSealed` / the plaintext override cleared; setting the shared token again re-arms the knock. The brief's literal "after the per-instance token published once" is necessary but not sufficient: published WITH the knock during the grace proves nothing about knockless logins (test-frp-plugin ① g mutant 3 — that rule drops the entry while the relay still asks it). Publish: the hub's name rule before the relay judges, `<user>.<name>` matched in frpc's status, `start error` read; `name_in_use:<holder>` / `name_not_yours` ⇒ ONE For-you item per name (`userTodos.add('frp', {origin:'plugin', plugin:'frp', kind:'notice', urgency:'high'})` through the new PluginManager option `forYou` — frp now `provides: ['relay','reminders']`) and the error says the holder. The card's doors = `config({ relay: 'mint'|'rotate'|'revoke'|'upgraded'|'knock' })` (no new route); a revoked identity refuses start / publish `relay_revoked` (never the shared token in its place); a pod's doors refuse `relay_cluster`. `status().relay` = kind, id, label, prefixes, subdomains, lines (hash only), login, knock on|locked|off|none, upgradedAt, publishedAt, retired — never a token.
- `tools/frps-login-plugin/` (Node ≥ 20, no deps): `plugin.js` (200 lines, ≤ 300) — Login / NewProxy / CloseProxy as designed; deviations from q-051 r1 §2, each measured in test-frps-plugin: (1) an id the table does not know is the KNOCK during the grace (r1 rejected it `bad_token` ⇒ every upgraded instance would have lost its relay between its upgrade and its registration), `unknown_instance` after; (2) names live in ONE top-level `names` map `{name: {owner}}` (owner = instance id or `<cluster>/<pod>`) instead of per-instance arrays — one lookup, the cluster's pods own names by pod name; (3) opt-in `--knock-file` VOUCH: frps runs its own auth check AFTER the plugin on the login the plugin hands back (frp server/service.go handleConnection → pluginManager.Login → RegisterControl → VerifyLogin, from the source as I know it — UNCONFIRMED on a real frps 0.70.0, the canary checks it), so a login accepted by the instance's own token is handed back with `privilege_key = md5(knock + timestamp)` — a registered instance then needs no shared token even during the grace (the restart-without-password property from the day of registration instead of after the grace). Off by default (`unchange`). (4) the table lives at /var/lib/frps-plugin/relay-instances.json (StateDirectory of a hardened unit — ProtectSystem=strict keeps /etc read-only, and the plugin writes its first claims). `relay-admin.js`: init / add / rotate / revoke / add-cluster / revoke-cluster / release / grace / list / owners / legacy / new-token / hash (stdin); `table.js`: the shapes, ONE lock file (O_EXCL, a 10 s stale lock taken over), atomic writes, constant-time hash compare. `frps-plugin.service` + README (install, ops table, vouching, ending the grace, rollback).

### lane xpra-title-election — a main window's title reaches the pane whichever packet came first (B-a566; race-sweep could not clear test-desktop-xpra-window-open §8's chromium title, red 3/10 under a 2-cpu load simulation, 0/10 alone)
- THE RACE, measured by a packet log on the real suite. The passing order is `new-window(wid, "Untitled - Google Chrome")` → `raise-window(wid)` → `window-metadata(wid, {title: "<page> - Google Chrome"})` — one wid, the metadata applied because the window exists, the title self-heals. Under load chromium's main X window is dropped and re-announced with the SAME wid while the fresh-title `window-metadata` lands in the lost → re-announce gap; `src/lib/xpra-client.js`'s handler dropped it at `if (!win) return`, and the re-announced `new-window` carried xpra's stale "Untitled" snapshot, so the bar kept it while X held the page title. The client's receive path is strictly ordered and synchronous (onmessage → onPacket, newWindow sets `windows` before any emit), so the only loss was that drop.
- THE FIX (no timers, no retries, no re-request): a bounded `pending` Map keyed by wid (FIFO, 64). A `window-metadata` for a wid not in `windows` is STASHED, not dropped; `newWindow` merges the stash onto the new record (`Object.assign(meta, held)` — the later fact wins over the new-window snapshot) BEFORE it computes the kind / title and makes its first emit; `lostWindow` clears a wid's stash.
- ONE ANNOUNCE DOOR: `setMain(win)` — the single place a window becomes the main (newWindow at creation, pickMain at a re-election). It sets mainWid, unslots a slot being adopted (mainWid FIRST, so its satellite hears 'adopted', not 'released'), emits 'main', then 'title' with the record's CURRENT title ('' allowed, never undefined), then the constraints. The window-metadata path is unchanged (it stores a title always, emits it only while the window is the main).
- Suites: test-xpra-client (fast) §T rows (a) a title that follows new-window; (b) a title that RACED AHEAD of new-window applied at creation; (c) THE RACE — a reused wid re-announced, the update in the gap kept; (d) a re-election announced through setMain with its stored title; (e) the pending map bounded; (f) RED CONTROL — a patched copy with the pre-fix `if (!win) return;` drops the raced title (the real B-a566 end state). test-desktop-xpra-window-open 10× alone + 10× loaded green; the pre-fix tree red under the load sim is the control.

### lane vault-locked-refusal-notice — a `vault_locked` refusal IS the signal: the hub tells the owner who was stopped and what; the agent is told the owner already knows (the owner 2026-10-20: 「为啥老是有 agent 和我说需要解锁 vault，这个不是应该系统检测到 agent 被阻拦了然后提醒我解锁吗」)
- THE CAUSE: the product made the AGENT the messenger. data/bin/vibespace-api's header ("tell the user; never ask for the password"), the vault and automation doors' `vault_locked` words, vibespace-vault's LOCKED line ("tell them") and docs/agent/vault-manual.md ("`vibespace-ask` is the way to ask them to unlock") all told the agent to relay it — and NO refusal path told the owner (the .325 boot item fired only at a restart; a lock act, or anyone stopped later, reached nobody's tray).
- PURE src/vault-blocked.js (imports nothing; PURE set): `createBlocked()` — `note({actor, verb, at, epoch})` keyed by the lock epoch (another epoch starts afresh), ≤ 50 actors × ≤ 8 verbs (the rest counts: `more`, `moreVerbs`), `fresh` only when what the owner reads changes (a new actor, a new verb, the first refusal past a bound — a door refusing every second refreshes nothing); `actorName` (an empty or id-shaped string — uuid, sess-/host-/dial-…, backend:id, a hex run — becomes a fallback name, never shown); `itemWords` (≤ 4 callers on the line, VibeSpace's own reads last, ≤ 11 detail lines + «…and N more», `N+` once some fell past the 50); `TOLD` / `AGENT_WORDS` / `agentWords(what)` — THE words toward an agent.
- ORCH src/server/vault-engine.js: `blocked(actor, verb)` = THE ONE HELPER (LOCKED only; a fresh note re-announces — `facts().blocked` = the strip's count — and runs `onBlocked(summary)`); the store-key road notes itself (`keyFor` / `secretGet` / `secretPut` refused while locked ⇒ «VibeSpace» with `the <store> store` / the secret's kind, never an id); the list is cleared at the setup, every unlock and every lock; the secret-box provider carries `blocked` (a door holding only the data dir reaches it through `SB.vaultForDir`).
- THE DOORS THAT NOTE: automation-engine `use()`'s one exit `done()` (the caller's NAME, `vibespace-api <verb>`); host-tokens `tokenFor` (the machine by `nameOf` — wired in server.js and mounts-plugins-wiring.js — `device link`; the link-token door passes the conversation's name: `its link to <machine>`; dial pairing rides it); channels-engine `tokensFor().read` (the account's label, `its sign-in`); frp `start` / `publish` / `config(token)` (`the relay`); sealed-json (the voice pair's sealed file); the store-key road (every store's key read). NOT noted, on purpose: desktop-access `rememberSignin` (people only — the person saw the refusal on their page), the spawn pre-check `lockedWhy` (a person's spawn), channels-auth's card facts (render-time; the store road notes the read).
- THE ONE FOR-YOU ITEM (src/server/vault-hooks.js `fileItem`, ONE add() site — test-user-todos-layout ⑪ stays 55): `VAULT_ITEM_TEXT` is the store's dedupe key (the same text ⇒ the same id; a later lock epoch REOPENS that row — one row, ever); the page words it from i18n: at boot `RELOCK_TEXT` + `NOTHING_YET`, once anyone is stopped `BLOCKED_TEXT {who}` + one `ROW_LINE` per caller (+ `MORE_LINE`); refreshed only on a fresh note; the owner's dismiss / done holds for that lock epoch (resolvedAt ≥ lockedSince); an older build's open restart item (its own text) is resolved at boot; `onUnlock` resolves it (unchanged).
- THE STRIP (src/lib/vault-unlock.js `drawLockStrip`): `facts.blocked` > 0 ⇒ 「The vault is locked — N waiting on it (For you names them).」, re-worded in place (`data-blocked`); 0 ⇒ the .325 sentence. 5 new keys (zh + ja).
- THE WORDS TOWARD AN AGENT, before → after: «the vault is locked — … (never ask for the password)» / «tell the user» / «tell them» → «the vault is locked — <what waits>; the user has already been told (their For you tray names what is waiting on it) — do not ask them to unlock it or for its password: wait, or do other work, and try again later» (routes/vault + routes/automation WORDS, channels `notConnectedError`, vibespace-vault's LOCKED line, vibespace-api's header + a usage line, vault-manual, automation-manual's row, the CLI registry's one line, the vibespace-vault rule row). The CODE is unchanged: `vault_locked` (423, exit 3; the attach's exit 7). Owner-facing / log words (key-file, secret-box, host-tokens, sealed-json, frp) keep their neutral sentences.
- THE LOCK LAW IS UNCHANGED: no note reads a key, mints one or unlocks (test-vault-law green; test-vault-engine M: still locked, no key file written).

### lane job-notice-dedupe — a published service's notice is a STATE CHANGE; its public-URL state is the relay's fact (agent feedback fb-4ff6e673ad, fb-a001be4917, fb-666f37fd38 — the owner: 「注意看一下 agent 给的 CLI 反馈」)
- THE CADENCE OF RECORD was the RESTARTS, not a timer: the four «public URL … is DOWN — publish failed: the vault is locked» notices of 2026-10-20 (00:50, 02:51, 04:19, 07:13Z, production `notifyLog` of jb-68c331d5 / jb-18ce4f26 / jb-1ade11b4 / jb-8917097b) each followed a release restart (data/boot-trace.json startedAt 07:12:59Z → notice 07:13:42Z). The vault locks at every restart by law; `_adoptAndReplay` re-ensures a published service at +8 s (src/jobs.js :1104 before); the relay refuses `vault_locked`; `_ensurePublish` (:998–1020 before) set `_publish = {state:'failed'}` and notified at EVERY failed attempt (:1019) — and `_publish` is runtime-only (`_`-prefixed keys never persist), so every boot was a "first" failure.
- PURE src/job-notice.js (new; test-architecture PURE set): `causeOf` = the failure's CLASS by name (vault_locked · relay_not_configured · port_in_use · subdomain_refused · forward_inactive · relay_unreachable; any other sentence is its own cause with digits folded — a port number is not a new cause); `noticeVerdict({prev, next, url, at})` over the job's down record — none→failed(X) ONE «DOWN» (only with a URL to be down), failed(X)→failed(X) nothing (`attempts`+1, `sinceAt` kept), failed(X)→failed(Y) ONE «DOWN» for Y, failed→published ONE «back UP» only when a DOWN was said in the episode (`said`, sticky across a cause change); a recovery to a NEW address says both URLs in that one notice. THE VAULT CLASS IS NEVER SAID PER JOB (the vault's For-you item carries it — lane vault-locked-refusal-notice notes the relay's refusal there); `whyOf` = its status words «waiting for the vault — … the owner has the unlock item, and this republishes by itself when it opens».
- src/jobs.js: `_publishOutcome` (:1036) = THE ONE landing place of a publish outcome — the record `job.publishDown {cause, error, sinceAt, downAt, lastAt, attempts, said}` is PERSISTED (the repeat came at every restart); `_ensurePublish`'s success and failure (:1027) both land there; a superseded attempt's failure counts nothing. `_teardownPublish` (:1120, a deliberate stop / park / refusal) ends the episode — a restart never does. `_adoptJobUrl(…, {quiet})`: a recovery to a new address is one notice, not «back UP» + «CHANGED».
- THE RELAY'S FACT (fb-666f37fd38): src/port-forward.js `_adoptPublish` (:134 — every relay success: the 30 s heal sweep's `_republish`, `restore`, `onMachineLinked`, the Ports panel's publish, `reprobe`, the job's own publish) calls `jobs.relayPublished(rec, url)` (:1052): the service on that forward (`_pfId`, else the local port) adopts the URL and clears its down record IN THE SAME TICK. `jobs.relayChanged(why)` (:1066) re-ensures every service still down; src/server/mounts-plugins-wiring.js `vault.onUnlock` (:70, above the first route registration — test-record-clear-census reads a route's span up to the next one, and a `getJobs` line inside the plugins route's span read as that route touching the jobs store) calls it with «the vault unlocked» — the unlock re-publishes at once instead of waiting for the Ports heal backoff (5 min) or the next restart. No separate relay "reconnect" event exists (frpc's own reconnect to frps keeps its proxies; the vault's unlock replays the relay through `sealSecrets` → `bootReplay`), so the unlock + the adopt point are the two doors.
- THE OWNER'S OWN FILTER (fb-a001be4917): `_notifyOwner`'s subscriber loop skips the owner's conversation and the owner lane never read a filter, so `subscribe --filter '^(?!.*vault is locked)'` on one's own job did nothing (production jb-18ce4f26 / jb-1ade11b4 carry exactly that row) and the only escape was `notify off`. ## 2.369.325 — 2026-10-20

### lane vault-relock-door — the vault's restart was silent on an open tab (the owner 2026-10-20: 「为啥我有的时候更新后需要重新输入二次密码有时候不用」; B-9674-class)
- THE SYMPTOM: the vault locks at EVERY restart by law (the DEK is zeroed on SIGTERM; no auto-unlock — unchanged). What differed was the ASK. The unlock dialog opened only at a page LOAD (`initVault`, src/lib/app.js) or after the stale-bundle reload an UPDATE triggers (`_checkBundleFreshness`). A restart that KEEPS the bundle (a crash, a same-build `systemctl restart`, the `Restart=always` respawn) reconnects the open tab WITHOUT a reload — and nothing re-read the vault state, so the tab sat on its stale `unlocked` UI while everything vault-gated (device links re-dialing, the relay, account switches) waited in silence until the owner noticed.
- THE FACTS NAME THE PROCESS: `facts()` (src/server/vault-engine.js) gained `startedAt` = the engine's construction time (the server's boot, ms), captured once at `create()` and unchanged by lock/unlock — a NEW process is the only new value. It is how a page tells a RESTART (a new startedAt) from a lock ACT (the same one). test-vault-engine §L pins it.
- THE OPEN TAB ASKS ON A RESTART: src/lib/vault-unlock.js `onVaultState(f)` applies the facts, then opens `showUnlock()` ONCE when `state === 'locked'` AND `startedAt` differs from the one this page last saw. The `vault-state` broadcast and a reconnect re-read both route through it; a lock ACT (`立即锁定` from another device, an agent's lock, the idle lock) carries the SAME startedAt — the chip and the strip only, no dialog (the RED CONTROL). On every ws reconnect AFTER the boot read (`vaultBooted`), the tab re-reads `/api/vault/state` so a bundle-preserving restart re-asks; the first connect is the page load itself, which the boot read handles. THE LOAD-TIME ask stays UNCONDITIONAL on locked — `maybeNagVault` (app.js) may pre-read the facts, so gating the boot on startedAt would wrongly suppress it (the gate caught this: ③/⑤ reds until the boot path was reverted to the original unconditional ask).
- THE PERSISTENT STRIP (owner decision 2026-10-20 「那需要一个常驻的警告提醒还没解锁」): `drawLockStrip()` draws `#vault-lock-strip` — the maintenance banner's shape, a flex child of #main-wrapper below `#maintenance-banner` when both show (public/style.css, a `--red` tone, SVG lock icon, zh+ja). It is drawn by `applyVaultFacts` (shown WHENEVER locked, incl. after a person's lock act; removed on unlock/not-set-up) and is NOT dismissable (no ×, no 稍后 — only the dialog's 稍后 closes the dialog). Its `解锁…` button fires `vs-vault-door`. The modal overlay (z 99998) sits above it, so the strip is reachable once the dialog is dismissed and never covers the dialog's button.
- THE FOR-YOU ITEM: src/server/vault-hooks.js `wireVaultHooks` now takes `userTodos` (wired in mounts-plugins-wiring.js) and, at boot when the vault is SET UP and LOCKED, files ONE tray notice (`userTodos.add('vault', {origin:'vault', kind:'notice', action:{type:'vault-unlock'}, i18n})`); its body-click door (src/lib/user-todos-actions.js) opens the unlock dialog via `vs-vault-door`. `onUnlock` resolves it (a person's unlock on any device clears it everywhere through the store's broadcast); a second boot while still locked re-files the SAME row (the store dedupes by sessionKey+text+action); a vault that is not set up files nothing. The item key: sessionKey `vault`, origin `vault`, action type `vault-unlock`. New English key extracted via `i18nKey(...)` in vault-hooks.js; zh+ja added.
- GATES: the unlock LAW is untouched — test-vault-law green. test-vault-engine (+§L startedAt, 83). test-vault-secrets (+⑨ the For-you filing: not-set-up files none, set-up+unlocked none, set-up+locked ONE, a second boot keeps one, unlock resolves — 130). test-user-todos-layout ② origin census: PRODUCERS gained `src/server/vault-hooks.js: vault`, the site count 54→55 (314). The heavy test-vault-chrome (56): the strip on ③/⑤/after 稍后/gone after ④; the new ③c (the OPEN tab re-asks on a bundle-preserving restart with NO navigate; a same-startedAt idle re-broadcast is the chip only — the RED CONTROL); and ③c-RED a patched worktree bundle (the reconnect re-read and the broadcast re-ask reverted) stays silent on a reconnect — the fix is load-bearing.

### lane channels-attachment-outside-archive — backlog B-5f20: a file on a message OUTSIDE the saved copy is fetched (the owner's agent, 2026-10-20: `vibespace-channels attachment` answered `not-found` for a Lark DM file it had found by `search --full` + `read --around`, while the raw `api` verb fetched it — 200, 206 KB; FIX, base 558de12a = 2.369.323; dispatched in 主开发's conversation with lane stream-mic-wheel-probe)
- **Before.** src/server/channels-engine.js `attachment()` found the carrier in the ARCHIVE only — the agent gate (`store.findRecord(msg)`) and `ownerRecordOf` (findRecord, then the newest 5000). An `around` read answers older messages from the vendor and stores nothing (F8), so the line `read --around` printed (`fetch: vibespace-channels attachment <conv> <msg> <id>`) always answered `no message in this conversation carries that attachment`, ZERO vendor calls (measured on the base engine loaded as a scratch copy over this lane's fixture).
- **After.** `aroundFor` (THE around read — the owner's sheet and the agent's `--around`) remembers each answered message that carries a file (non-body parts: id, name, mime) by (account, conversation, message): `noteShownOutside`, memory only, ≤ 2000 messages, newest kept. `attachment()` asks the archive FIRST, then that memory (`shownCarrier`); a hit rides the SAME leg — `Att.fetchVerdict` (capability, enabled, one flight, back-off, budget), the agents' share, `spendAs('agent'|'owner')` + `vendor()` → `e.adapter.fetchAttachment(convId, {messageId, attachmentId, mime, name})`, the message-scoped LRU cache — and the answer carries `source: 'vendor'` | `'archive'` (the agent route's `X-VibeSpace-Attachment` JSON gained `source`). Nothing is stored (the log's bytes identical); the archive window is unchanged.
- **Why the memory, not the ids the caller typed.** Lark's resource address (`im/v1/messages/:message_id/resources/:file_key`) names no chat: a fetch by whatever pair a caller typed would serve a file of ANOTHER conversation through the reach of this one. The vendor's own `around` answer for THIS conversation is what places a message in it. So a pair never shown here is refused before any call (`not-found`: "that message is not in the saved copy, and no read --around showed it in this conversation — find it first: …"), and a shown message the vendor no longer has answers "…not in the saved copy, and the vendor has no such message (or no such file on it) any more — nothing fetched" (remembered like any vendor refusal). The memory dies with the process: after a restart the agent reads `--around` again (its line is printed again).
- **Capability.** An account whose channel lists files but cannot fetch them (`caps.attachments !== 'fetch'`) answers `not-supported`, naming the account — the capability row, never an adapter id.

### lane design-window-placement — a Design an agent opens is PLACED beside its conversation, never popped to the front (backlog B-9674; owner 2026-10-20 「design 那个窗口会自动弹出到前台，而不是在开始 design 的对话的右侧分屏」; base 01672d8d = 2.369.322)
- THE RULE (lane agent-window-no-steal, already law for the agent browser): an agent's action may PLACE a window; only a person's action may FOCUS one. The Design window's `design-open` push (the agent's `vibespace-design new|open|add|sync`) now reads the SAME PURE verdict as the agent browser — `agentWindowPlacement` (src/lib/desktop-app-placement.js), extended for the `design-open` kind. `agentPlacedSession` tells the two agent pushes apart; a person's door (a chat card, the Designs home, the gear menu, a layout replay) calls `openDesign` directly and never rides the push.
- THE DOOR: `installDesignWindow` → `app.placeAgentWindow(msg, open)` (src/lib/app.js). A FRESH window is born quiet (createWindow's asked `quiet` — the active window and the DOM caret stay) and placed: beside a shown chat it is SNAPPED to the right half while the conversation snaps to the left (`wm.snapToHalf`), on another desktop it is created there (no switch), behind the active window when the chat is minimized; its taskbar entry pulses (`wm.markArrived`). An EXISTING design the agent re-opens or syncs is never raised — `markArrived` + `revealWindow(id, {raise:false})`. The front setting (`desktop.agentWindowsFront`, default OFF) restores the old front + focus for designs too; its description now names a Design (zh + ja).
- WHY SNAP, NOT `linkPlacement`'s tab-chain split (the agent browser's door): the Design canvas fits itself to its pane through a ResizeObserver; born hidden as a tab-chain split guest it never gets a non-zero size and never loads its artboards. A snapped free half window renders exactly as a full one, so the owner's picture (conversation left, Design right, same desktop) is delivered as two half windows and the agent browser's bindSplit door is untouched.
- TESTS: test-agent-window-placement — the PURE design-open rows (beside / desk / behind / minimize / badge / phone / front-on control + the malformed-push negatives) and the door pins (56 pass). test-design-window (heavy) — the composer keeps the caret and the active window, the fresh Design is the right split (conversation left, Design right, same desktop), its taskbar pulses, a second `open` does not raise it, the front setting brings it forward (control), a direct `openDesign` raises it (RED control) (173 pass). test-design-canvas (287) + i18n unaffected.

Refused (the password changed there) ⇒ nothing cleared, the hub remembers the refusal against THAT row (updatedAt) and never tries it again — a machine's lockout counts failures — and the dialog says 「上次记住的密码不对，请重输」 with the tick ON (the page reads GET …/signins fresh before the dialog). UNPAIR: src/hosts.js `onRemoved(fn)` (new) ⇒ desktop-access forgets the machine's desktop sign-in AND its RemoteApp sign-in (audited, why unpaired). - NOT CHANGED, SAID: the suite's two other clock legs (the line belt ≤ 40 × plain lines, measured 6.4; the engine ≤ 8 × two plain records, 1.1–1.6) keep it on FAST_SERIAL / CLOCK_JUDGES (rows reworded). ## 2.369.316 — 2026-10-19

### lane device-allow-flags — a paired device carries its OWN allow list, set only by the install command run on it; the hub cannot widen it; a cluster-paired device starts without socks / lan / input (design q-042 §3 D5, owner decision ③ 2026-10-19); base 42f694ab (device-act-audit, .313)
- THE FLAGS (PURE src/device-policy.js, imports only device-acts): `run` (commands, desktop apps, a browser, a Settings pane), `files` (write / move / remove / place / serve a file, the reverse tunnel — READS are never gated), `input`, `socks`, `lan` (a socket to ANOTHER host of its network; the device's own loopback stays a read), `sessions` (conversations, terminals, text posted into them, their pool orders — IMPLIES run + files: a conversation runs commands and writes its tools), `upgrade`. FLAG_OF maps every one of device-acts' 51 session / act / code rows to ONE flag, or ALWAYS (the handshake + the 9 stops — ending what is open never widens anything); an unknown action takes its family's flag, an unknown op needs every flag (fail closed). The census + a mutant row: scripts/test-device-policy.mjs ①.
- THE FILE: the installer's `--allow all|none|run,files,…` (`-Allow` on Windows) is judged by THE parser through the agent bundle's own `--write-policy` → <root>/state/policy.json (atomic, 0600) AFTER the dial check and BEFORE the host token / dial.json / the unit (an unknown flag ⇒ exit 2, nothing installed); without --allow a re-run keeps the file. agentd reads it ONCE at boot (no file = paired before the list: every flag, `legacy`; an unreadable file = reads only).
- THE DEVICE (src/agentd/agentd.js, after `authed`, before dispatch): `policyVerdict` — the file itself first (a place-secret / fs-op write / stream / mkdir onto policy.json, a removal / rename of it or a folder above it, a move / copy onto it ⇒ `policy_is_the_devices`, `files` on or not; lexical on the device's path module, `~` = its home, Windows case-insensitive), then the flag ⇒ `op-not-allowed {flag, remedy}`; the answer in the shape its caller waits for (`op-refused {id}`, `session-error {chan}`, `upgrade-failed`); acts.log gets the refused line whatever its layer. The hello-ack states the list (`policy`, read-only for the hub).
- THE HUB (src/agentd/client.js): `_request`, `_streamOp`, `tcpForward`, `openSession`, `openPipeSession` ask the same verdict over the stated list BEFORE anything is sent or a channel held — refused = an Error whose message names the op, the flag, what it allows and THE re-run (`re-run the pairing command on "<machine>" with --allow <the whole new list>`), ONE audit line `op-not-allowed` (head = the re-run); a version drift on a list without `upgrade` pushes nothing (said once per link + one line). `refusalOf(payload)` lets a chain ask before its first act: a dial session's setup (src/spawn/dial.js) asks `sessions` before it ships a tool, the session token or an account key / OAuth env. `onPolicy` keeps the stated list on the host record (`devicePolicy`, hosts.notePolicy, broadcast when it moved); `machine` names it in the sentence.
- THE DEFAULTS: POST /api/device/dial-pair answers `allowDefault` + `clusterInstance` (VIBESPACE_INSTANCE_NAME on the hub ⇒ run,files,sessions,upgrade; else all); an ssh graduation installs with it. ### lane stream-hdr-passthrough — 「HDR 直通」: a Windows HDR display streams as TRUE HDR (AV1 10-bit PQ) to a viewer that can show it (q-041 r3 P4 road B, owner 2026-10-19 「可以 按你推荐来」); base 2d7e2c64 (.313)

OFF by default, remembered per machine (`vibespace.streamHdr`, ≤ 32); a window that opens with it on waits for the decodingInfo answer before its first start (no SDR stream first); the media query's `change` (the window moved to another screen) restarts SDR / HDR. One-view modes (③ / ①); ②'s panes stay SDR.
- THE ROAD (src/stream-plan.js): planScreen(facts, {hdr: true}) ⇒ mode `hdr` = the mapped road's FP16 capture → THE PQ MAPPING (PASSTHROUGH: scRGB is absolute, 1.0 = 80 nits, and so is PQ — the machine's SDR white stays at its own nits (200 → code 571), no white level, no tone curve; linear BT.709 → BT.2020 (BT.2087 3×3) → ST 2084 → BT.2020-NCL Y'CbCr, 10-bit limited, P010) in the same worker (`pq` tables built there: FP16 → linear Float32 65 536, float32 bits >>> 13 → PQ 2^19; unrolled loop 65 ms a 4K frame on the owner's i9-12900K idle, NV12's 25) → av1_nvenc (`-preset p1 -tune ull -rc cbr -zerolatency 1 -delay 0 -rc-lookahead 0` — `-delay` defaults to INT_MAX frames; no `-profile`, not av1_nvenc's) with the frames TAGGED by setparams (bt2020 / smpte2084 / bt2020nc / tv — an output -color_* makes ffmpeg 8 insert a CPU conversion: the probe's trap) → IVF (length-framed) → src/stream-av1.js ivfReader (a key unit without its sequence header gets the last one in front) → temporal units. `sdr` = the mapped plan, field for field. The SDR roads' argvs are pinned byte for byte (test-stream-hdr §5).
- THE NEGOTIATION (src/stream-model.js streamCodecsOf; src/agentd/stream-host.js): `stream-offer {hdr: true}` to a source that `offersAv1` lists AV1 (fmtp level-idx=5;profile=0;tier=0) FIRST, then H.264; the page puts AV1 first in its answer (setCodecPreferences); werift sends the answer's first codec, and at `connected` — before the source starts — `source.useCodec(mime)` picks the hdr plan for AV1, else the SDR plan. Not asked ⇒ the offer is H.264 alone, unchanged. THE PACKETIZER: the P4 probe's measured aggregated-TU payloads (W = 0, Z / Y per packet, N on a new sequence; TD / tile lists / padding dropped) — byte for byte the probe's over THE fixtures at three MTUs.
- THE FALLBACK (hdrStallStep): while HDR is asked, a picture's bytes arrive and getStats' framesDecoded does not move for 2 s (5 s once frames were decoded — a lost key frame waits ≤ one 2 s GOP + its PLI) ⇒ the strip says 「HDR 直通已回退：浏览器无法解码」, the switch goes OFF (remembered), the stream restarts as the SDR picture (THE STILL covers it; `after` carries a hand-over; the stop's why `hdr_undecodable` reaches the machine's log). Exercised for real by headless Chrome's dav1d.
- MEASURED ON THE OWNER'S WINDOWS BOX (real legs hdr1–hdr4: this tree's stream host + screen source on the agent's node, a scratch hub + the real machine-desktop page in headless Chrome here, a mocked HDR viewer): ① WINDOWS POWER THROTTLING is the stream's real limit — the hidden agent and its ffmpegs run under EcoQoS: the SDR mapped road 3–6 fps (map 100 ms) and the HDR road 1–5 fps (map 250–700 ms, encode 0.7–1.4 s); with SetProcessInformation(ProcessPowerThrottling, EXECUTION_SPEED off) on the agent + both ffmpegs: SDR 19–22 fps (map 40, encode ~110 ms), HDR 13 fps (map 79, encode ~180 ms). ### lane tailscale-plugin-pod-dns — the Tailscale plugin never takes over a container's DNS (the owner's fleet pod 2026-10-19 12:3xZ: the plugin's tailscaled rewrote /etc/resolv.conf to 100.100.100.100 + the ts.net search domain; `getent hosts github.com` failed, scripts/update.sh could not fetch, the canary stalled on that pod alone while the canary instance — no plugin — updated); base 882c5e3e (.314)
- THE CAUSE: the pod has /dev/net/tun (chart `tun.enabled`) and the pod user is NOPASSWD: ALL, so mode `auto` picked KERNEL and ran `sudo -n tailscaled` — root. Nothing ever passed --accept-dns, so Tailscale's default (true) let its direct DNS manager overwrite resolv.conf (no systemd-resolved / resolvconf in a pod; header "# resolv.conf(5) file generated by tailscale", the original kept in /etc/resolv.pre-tailscale-backup.conf — both read off the 1.102.3 binary here). Userspace networking never configures the OS resolver.
- THE VERDICT (PURE src/tailscale-dns.js `dnsPolicy`, first match): a cluster pod (VIBESPACE_INSTANCE_NAME) ⇒ false `cluster`; resolv.conf OR Tailscale's backup beside it cluster-managed (a cluster.local / svc.* search domain, a 10.96.0.0/12 nameserver) ⇒ false `cluster-resolver`; no tun (userspace) ⇒ false `userspace`; a bare machine in kernel mode ⇒ false `not-asked` unless the new row `plugin.tailscale.magicDns` (boolean, default off) is on ⇒ true `asked`. `heal` = Tailscale's header present while the verdict is false.
- THE PLUGIN: `up` carries `--accept-dns=<v>` (a typed --accept-dns joins the OWNED upFlags, dropped); ONE `tailscale --socket=<ours> set --accept-dns=<v>` (sudo -n for a kernel-mode daemon, as setup's `up`; retried 20 × 500 ms while the socket comes up; one in flight) at every start (also when already running), after an install over a running daemon, and at boot for a daemon of ours that outlived the server — the plugin now owns its bootReplay (else the manager's default rule: enabled + desiredUp ⇒ start; the default skipped a running daemon, so an old install would never heal). tailscaled's direct manager restores its backup when the OS config empties. A heal logs ONE line `[tailscale] <why>: /etc/resolv.conf carried Tailscale's header — set --accept-dns=false (<why>); …`.
- THE NAMES: MagicDNS names never ride the system resolver. status() / lookup() keep a host table from OUR daemon's `status --json` (Self + Peer: DNSName → TailscaleIPs, IPv4 first, the bare label too); PluginManager.tunnelLookup(name) asks whichever plugin provides 'tunnel' (optional verb `lookup`); src/hosts.js `_tailnetOpts` adds `-o HostName=<ip> -o HostKeyAlias=<name>` to sshArgs and sshCmd (known_hosts stays keyed by the name); wired in mounts-plugins-wiring (`hosts.nameLookup`). Userspace mode's SOCKS5 already resolves tailnet names itself.
- THE ROW: a running tunnel row's fact line — 「DNS：集群解析器（Tailscale 名字经插件解析）」 / 「DNS：本机解析器（…）」 / 「DNS：Tailscale MagicDNS」 / a still-held rewrite (off and on restores it); status() carries `dns: {acceptDns, why, rewritten}`.
- NOT DONE HERE: the real pod leg (主开发's `tailscale set --accept-dns=false` on the owner's pod is the same call); other dialers of a tailnet name (rclone sftp / a dial device's http base) still use the system resolver — ssh hosts are the hub's host records.
- TESTS: test-tailscale-dns NEW (fast, 56, 5.6 s): ① 13 verdict rows + the reader + the lookup; ② a fake tailscale/tailscaled/pgrep/sudo through the REAL manager + plugin on a cluster-shaped box (start ⇒ ONE set --accept-dns=false, `up` carries it, a typed true dropped, the row's dns, tunnelLookup); ③ the boot self-heal (ONE set, ONE line, no restart; a clean file ⇒ the set, no line; bare kernel through the fake sudo: row on ⇒ true, off ⇒ false); ④ ssh argv + the rsync string + the wiring line; ⑤ zh/ja words; ⑥ MUTANTS: start without the apply, `up` without the flag, no own bootReplay ⇒ RED.

### lane win-device-boot-hidden — a Windows device's agent never shows a console window: not at logon, not after a reboot, not on an old install (owner 2026-10-19 after a reboot: a black Windows Terminal window titled 「vibespace-device」 on the desktop — 「这是啥 能关掉吗」); base 882c5e3e (.314)
- THE GAP: scripts/vibespace-agentd-install.ps1's AT-LOGON task ran `cmd.exe /c set VIBESPACE_DEVICE_ROOT=<root>&& set VIBESPACE_AGENTD_ROOT=<root>&& "<node>" "<root>\current\vibespace-device.js"`. A console program a task starts gets a console of its own; Windows 11 hands it to Windows Terminal; the daemon's `process.title` named the window. Closing it ended the agent until the next logon. The other launch sites were hidden already (the first launch `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden`, the re-exec `detached + windowsHide`, the --stdio bridge) — .310's census covered the daemon's CHILDREN only.
- THE TASK: Execute `powershell.exe`, Argument `-NoProfile -NonInteractive -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "$env:VIBESPACE_DEVICE_ROOT='<root>'; $env:VIBESPACE_AGENTD_ROOT='<root>'; Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden -FilePath '<node>' -ArgumentList ([char]34+'<root>\current\vibespace-device.js'+[char]34) -RedirectStandardOutput '<root>\state\agentd.out' -RedirectStandardError '<root>\state\agentd.err'"` = the installer's first launch (the shape the owner's box never showed) at every logon; the settings gain `-Hidden`; the name and `-Force` stay. Paths are PowerShell literals (`'`, ‘ ’ ‚ ‛ doubled), the script is quoted for node by `[char]34`, so the text holds no `"`. The env reaches node by inheritance (`-Environment` needs PS 7.3+). ONE text: the ps1 builds it (`Quote-Ps`, `$launch`, `$taskArgs`) and the daemon builds it (src/agentd/hidden-start.js `logonTaskArgs`) — a twin pin.
- WHY NOT `conhost.exe --headless`: undocumented, listed as an execution proxy (EDR rules alert on it), and not measurable here. The trade of the PowerShell form: the launcher PowerShell itself may show for about a second at logon (unmeasured); the daemon is never in it, and the launcher exits at once, so the task instance ends (the task's 72 h ExecutionTimeLimit never reaches the daemon either).
- SELF-HEAL, two halves. ① The console step (`consoleStep`, sync, inside the daemon body BEFORE the singleton): a win32 daemon not yet marked with a console handle on fd 0/1/2 (`tty.isatty`) runs ONE hidden PowerShell one-shot (Add-Type, FreeConsole + AttachConsole(pid) + GetConsoleWindow + IsWindowVisible of the window or its owner — Windows Terminal owns the pseudo-console window; the answer is the EXIT CODE 20 visible · 21 hidden · 22 no window · 23 none, 30 s bound). Visible ⇒ `startSuccessor(reExecArgv(argv[1]), {VIBESPACE_AGENTD_HIDDEN: '1'})` + exit 0 (cmd.exe ends, its window closes); the marked successor never looks again. Hidden / none / could not tell ⇒ stay (the last one logged once). ② The task step (`ensureLogonTask`, async 3 s after the start line, win32 only): read the task (`vs-task <b64 execute> <b64 args>`, UTF-8 base64 — a Chinese profile path survives the pipe's code page); absent ⇒ never created; foreign (our name, no vibespace-device.js / agentd.js) ⇒ left alone, logged; the hidden text already ⇒ nothing written; else (the old cmd.exe, a moved node) ⇒ the installer's own Register-ScheduledTask, ONE log line naming what it was.
- THE RE-EXEC IS ONE SITE: the self-upgrade's spawn moved into `startSuccessor(argv, env)` (detached, stdio ignore, windowsHide, `{...daemonEnv(process.env), ...env}`); each caller hands `reExecArgv(<script>)` at its own site — the upgrade with its version, the self-heal with the mark. The mark is ONE hop: read by the daemon, NOT in DAEMON_ENV_KEEP (daemonEnv drops it; test-agentd-session's derivation names it).
- ALSO FIXED (same launch site): the first launch's `-ArgumentList @("$current\vibespace-device.js")` — PS 5.1 joins -ArgumentList unquoted, so a profile path with a space split the script path and the installer said "the daemon exited immediately". Now `@("`"$current\vibespace-device.js`"")`.
- MEASURED in a real PowerShell engine (portable pwsh 7.4.6 on Linux; no Windows box may be touched): the ps1 persistence block run with stub ScheduledTasks cmdlets == `logonTaskArgs` for four profile paths (plain, `Jo O'Brien`, `张三 李`, a curly quote); the Argument through the Windows command-line rules ⇒ ONE -Command text ⇒ a stub Start-Process bound -FilePath, -ArgumentList `"…"` (quoted), -WindowStyle Hidden, both redirects, both env roots; the first launch's argument quoted; the three one-shots parse (0 errors), are ASCII, and run through -EncodedCommand with stub cmdlets (read old ⇒ rewrite, none ⇒ absent, hidden ⇒ same; write: powershell.exe + the exact Argument, -Hidden, -AtLogOn, -Force); `exit 20` is the process exit code; the probe off Windows exits 1 ⇒ unknown ⇒ stay (fails closed). NOT measured: a real Windows logon. The owner's box heals at the next release's self-upgrade (the task re-register); the console step is the backstop for a cold start under an old task.
- TESTS: test-agentd-hidden-start NEW (fast, 44): the rules + consoleStep over fakes (one re-exec, the loop guard, the silent hidden case, the said unknown), the ps1 task unit, THE TWIN ×4, the launch-site census (agentd AST: 2 daemon starts, both detached + ignore + windowsHide; ps1: 2 starts; 3 hub / POSIX rows) + 5 CONTROLS, MUTANTS (cmd.exe back in the ps1 ⇒ RED; logonTaskArgs back to cmd.exe ⇒ twin RED; no `same` row ⇒ 2 writes ⇒ RED), the wiring. test-agentd-spawn-hide (31): the re-exec row renamed, + the two one-shots, control (b) re-indented. test-agentd-session: the mark dropped. test-agentd-reexec-argv: the hand-over pin follows startSuccessor (the upgrade calls it inside handOver; ONE re-exec spawn; the self-heal's start precedes any listener). test-dial-facts: the first-launch pin quoted. test-architecture: hidden-start.js is DEVICE. ci.mjs: the new fast row.

### lane device-bundle-signing — a device re-execs nothing unsigned (SECURITY INCIDENT, design q-042 §3 D2 / §5 P0-a); base 07036579 (.312)
- BEFORE: a hub whose bundle version differed from a device's streamed its own data/bin/vibespace-agentd.js (client.js `_upgrade`) and the device landed it, repointed `current` and re-exec'd (agentd.js `beginUpgrade`) — no signature, no second source, and `version` (a hub-supplied string) was joined into a directory path unchecked. A compromised hub replaced every paired machine's code at its next hello.
- THE VERDICT (PURE src/agentd-signature.js, node crypto handed in): ed25519 over 'vibespace-agentd-bundle/v1' ‖ version ‖ sha256(bundle) ‖ keyId; `verify(trusted, bytes, version, record)` → ok | malformed / version-mismatch / unknown-key / bad-signature / unsigned. The digest is computed over the bytes handed in (the record's own sha256 is never trusted). A rotation ships as a KEY CHAIN inside every manifest (each successor signed by its predecessor, domain-separated); a link that claims a reachable signer but does not check is a forgery (refused, never skipped); a successor reached through the chain REPLACES the device's pin.
- THE DEVICE (src/agentd/agentd.js): the version must be version-shaped BEFORE a directory is made; after the last byte the bytes ON DISK are judged before the rename, the repoint and the re-exec (the only writer of `current` — test-architecture §92 + the suite's census); a refusal deletes the temp file (and the empty dir), logs one line and answers `upgrade-failed {code, keyId}`. TOFU: the first start of an install pins the release keys IN its bundle (<root>/state/trusted-keys.json, 0600, atomic); both installers delete the pin on a (re-)pair (a new trust-on-first-use = the lost-key recovery).
- THE HUB'S OWN MACHINE: every upgrade of the hub's OWN daemon (signed or not) carries a local proof — the hub writes 32 random bytes into the daemon's state dir (<root>/state/upgrade-proof, 0600) and sends them as `localProof`; on its own socket (never a dial link: `serveConnection(ws, { dialed: true })`) a matching proof is enough (sha256s compared in constant time, the file deleted on any read). Whoever writes that dir is already that machine's user; dev boxes and lane worktrees keep their local daemon current, and a hub's daemon that once ran an unsigned build (no baked key ⇒ no pin) never sticks on `unknown-key` at the next signed release — found in review, pinned by a real-daemon leg.
- THE HUB (src/agentd/client.js): `_releaseState()` = the manifest beside the bundle (data/bin/vibespace-agentd.manifest.json) names THESE bytes and this version (cached by mtime+size); otherwise `unsigned-local-build` — no upgrade to another machine (`_mayPush` at the hello, and `_upgrade` itself throws), said once per version (log + the door). A device refusal (SIG.REFUSALS) is never pushed again (the ledger gives up at once) and reaches hosts.onAgentUpgrade('refused') from all three construction sites (server.js local, dial-pairing, hosts.js ssh).
- THE DOOR (src/server/device-upgrade-watch.js `refused`): ONE URGENT For-you item per (device, version, code) — machine, from → to, the code, the key, who pushed (`hub` until P0-c brings the act's `by`); a refusal's item is never retracted (a later `matched` drops only the row). `unsigned-local-build` = the machine row's line only (`agentUpgrade.unsigned`), no item. Client words: exit-access-dialog `agentUpgradeText` + zh/ja.
- THE RELEASE ARTIFACT: release/agentd/manifest.json {v, version, sha256, keyId, sig, chain} — written by scripts/sign-agentd.mjs (npm run sign:agentd) on the release machine, COMMITTED with the release. The 5.3 MB bundle is NOT committed (history growth on every release; the sha256 is its identity): `npm run build:agentd` now builds with `--preserve-symlinks` and ends with scripts/agentd-release.mjs — the built bytes ARE the manifest's (and the signature verifies against src/agentd/release-keys.js) ⇒ the manifest is copied beside the bundle (gitignored), else UNSIGNED is printed and the copy removed; the build never fails on it.
- DETERMINISM, measured: the lane worktree (node_modules symlinked) built a bundle 2 670 bytes longer than production's — 891 `// ../node_modules/…` path comments; with `--preserve-symlinks` the worktree's bundle is byte-identical to the production checkout's at the same commit (sha256 78151ecd…). The fleet image (npm ci, real node_modules) prints the same paths.
- THE KEY: ed25519, `scripts/gen-release-key.mjs` → ~/.vibespace-release/agentd-ed25519.pem (0600 in 0700, never overwritten; `--encrypt` = passphrase from the terminal or stdin; `--rotate-from` prints the KEY_CHAIN link). sign-agentd refuses (exit 2, by name): CI set; a checkout with data/auth.json / agentd-tokens.json / server.pid; a key inside the repo, readable by others, not ed25519, or not in RELEASE_KEYS; a stale bundle. Neither script reads an environment variable but CI. src/agentd/release-keys.js ships EMPTY: until 主开发's first signed release no hub upgrades a paired machine (each says UNSIGNED at build and on the machine row).
- TESTS: scripts/test-agentd-upgrade-signature.mjs NEW (fast, 3.4 s, 98): the truth table (22 rows incl. two rotations out of order, a stranger's link, a forged link, a link replayed as a bundle signature), the hub over a fake daemon on the real Mux, REAL daemons from the built bundle (7 refusals with the temp file gone and the daemon still serving, a chain-signed landing + re-exec into a stub + the successor pinned, TOFU, the local proof end to end, a no-pin daemon refusing a signed release without the proof and landing it with it, a dial link ignoring a matching proof), a MUTANT bundle without the verdict lands a bad signature, the watch, the release scripts in a scratch repo (incl. a key handed in through the environment is never used), the census. test-architecture §92 (+ 2 controls), PURE set +2. test-device-upgrade-watch +REF-1–4 + control (47). test-key-file-law RANDOM32 +1 row (client.js: the local proof — a single-use nonce, never a key). test-dial-facts token-door EXEMPT +2 (the bundle digest, the proof compare — never a pairing token). test-user-todos-layout producer sites 49 → 50 (the refused-upgrade item). test-agentd-upgrade-loop and heavy test-agentd-dial C1/C3: the shipped fake bundle now carries its manifest (a throwaway key the device pins).
- NOT IN THIS LANE (the report's follow-ups): the fence is complete only with D5 — today `fs-op` write and `run-cmd` still let a hub write `<root>/<ver>/agentd.js`, `current` or trusted-keys.json directly (deny the agent root to both); a signed OLD release can be replayed (a rollback floor = a monotonic version pin); on the owner's box the hub runs as the same uid that can read ~/.vibespace-release (an encrypted key or the uid split closes it); the Mac screen helper's prebuilt (B-817d) follows the same shape later.
- VERIFY R1 → FIX R2 (lane device-bundle-signing-fix-r2, ONE commit on 9f73cf37). verify-r1 (refute by default) found no RED high, two RED mediums and three lows, all fixed here; the "rollback floor" follow-up above is one of them.
- RED-1, a validly signed OLDER release landed and re-exec'd (the replay of any past release). Fix: THE VERSION FLOOR. <state>/release-floor.json holds the newest version this install ever ran; it is raised at every start (0600, atomic), and `floorNow()` is never below the running VERSION. After the signature checks, `SIG.verify(…, {floor, honoured})` answers `downgrade` (+ `floor`) for a version below it. The device deletes the bytes and answers `upgrade-failed {code: 'downgrade', floor}`; the hub gives up at once (it is in SIG.REFUSALS); the watch files the same URGENT kind in its own words (「有人向 <machine> 推送了旧版本 X」, who pushed) plus the row's line. A deliberate rollback is a SIGNED statement: the record's `allowDowngradeTo` (= its own version; `sign-agentd --allow-downgrade-to <v>`, typed as a confirmation) is an optional line INSIDE the signed message, honoured ONCE per bundle (its sha256 lands in the floor file's `honoured`; the floor does not move). Never an env, never a hub-side flag. The hub's OWN daemon (the local proof) is exempt: whoever writes that state dir is that machine's user.
- RED-2, a device installed from a hub whose RELEASE_KEYS was empty pinned nothing, so every later signed release was `unknown-key` until a re-pair. Fix: TRUST ON FIRST USE at the first validly signed release. Every record now SIGNS the release's key set (`keys` = RELEASE_KEYS in sign-agentd; SIG.sign's default is the signer alone). A device with NO pin file and NO baked key (`trustsNoKey()`) passes `tofu: true`; the PURE verdict takes the record's own key set only when it is self-consistent (every row its key's id, the signer among them) and the signature over the bytes AND that set checks ⇒ pin `from: 'tofu'`, `upgrade-done {tofu: [ids]}` ⇒ client `_trusted` ⇒ hosts.onAgentUpgrade('trusted') ⇒ ONE URGENT item 「<machine> 首次信任发布钥 <fingerprint>」 (the undo: re-pair). A pin file that EXISTS (even unparsable) never re-TOFUs, and the PURE branch also needs an empty trusted set. The installers carry no key themselves — the bundle they fetch bakes RELEASE_KEYS; today's set is EMPTY, so a device paired before the first signed release now TOFUs that release instead of needing a re-pair.
- low ③, ssh hosts took the hub's unsigned bundle (installAgentd). Fix: THE SSH ROAD LANDS THROUGH THE SAME landBundle. The device's landing is ONE function, `landBundle` (verdict → rename → repointCurrent → the pin / the rollback record; test-architecture §92 counts exactly its two callers). Callers: `beginUpgrade` (the stream) and a new CLI mode `agentd.js --land-upgrade <staged> --version <v> --manifest <record>` (no lock, no socket, one stdout line, exit 0 / 3 / 4). installAgentd ships the bundle, plus its manifest when `DeviceManager.releaseOf` says these bytes ARE the signed release. The remote step (`installAgentdScript`) moves `current` only on these rungs: same bytes ⇒ nothing; nothing installed ⇒ lands as is (the owner's add-host act = the installer's TOFU); an install + an unsigned build ⇒ `unsigned-local-build` (row only); the installed agent knows --land-upgrade ⇒ IT judges (signature, floor, pin); a pre-signing agent there ⇒ the SIGNED release lands unverified once. Chosen over "a verify script shipped beside the bundle" (the hub's code judging the hub's bundle proves nothing) and "the daemon verifies itself at first boot" (the newcomer's bytes judging themselves): the agent ALREADY trusted on the host judges the newcomer, exactly as over a dial link. Refusals and first trusts reach the same door. Not a fence against a hub holding the host's ssh key (that is a shell — D6). The MANUAL real-host suites (test-agentd-switchover, test-host-mounts-tunnel) now need a signed build or a fresh host.
- low ④, `trustAfter` replaced the pin with the single successor. Fix: a successor ADDS. The pin after = pinned ∪ every key the chain reached − signed retirements (the signer first under the 16-key cap). A retirement is a KEY_CHAIN entry `{retire, sig}` signed by the RETIRING key ('vibespace-agentd-key-retire/v1'). It counts only for a reachable key; a bad one is `bad-signature`; a release signed by a key its own chain retires is `unknown-key`. `gen-release-key --retire <pem>` prints one; `--rotate-from` now says ADD the row (RELEASE_KEYS = every valid key).
- low ⑤, the `--encrypt` doc. gen-release-key's header now says when to use it (any machine that also runs a VibeSpace or agent sessions — they run as your uid and can read a plain PEM), how (≥ 12 characters; typed twice on a terminal, otherwise the FIRST stdin line with no confirmation), and that it is never stored. The release recipe in kb-design-lessons follows the verifier's corrected first-release order.
- TESTS: test-agentd-upgrade-signature 98 → 156 (5.2 s).
  - ① +22 rows: the floor; a rollback honoured once; forged and wrong-key rollbacks; TOFU incl. a slipped key, a signer outside its set and a pinned device given the flag; three pinned after a successor, two after a retirement; a forged retirement; a retired signer; an unknown retirement.
  - ② the hub's downgrade door (+ the floor, never re-pushed) and its first-trust door.
  - ③ +2 real daemons: TOFU on the first signed release over the stream (unsigned and a slipped key refused first); a signed rollback lands and is recorded. Daemon A refuses the replay, a forged rollback and a wrong-key rollback; its floor file is written at start.
  - ③b the ssh road over a fake ssh, eight fake hosts at once: fresh; unsigned onto an install; signed and verified; TOFU; pre-signing ×2; same bytes; a replay ⇒ downgrade; a junk pin never TOFUs; the rollback lands once, then is refused — except when re-landed onto a `current` that already holds those bytes (the standing agent catching up after --land-upgrade; found in review: it read as a second downgrade); a staged bad signature at the CLI.
  - ④ the two new items. ⑤ the signed key set, --allow-downgrade-to, --retire, --encrypt from stdin. ⑥ the census moved to landBundle + the --land-upgrade door.
  - Elsewhere: test-architecture §92 → landBundle and its two roads (+1 control); test-user-todos-layout producer sites 50 → 51 (the first-trust item).
- MUTANTS: 18 whole-tree copies (git-initialised; the suite unless noted), 18 RED: TOFU without the empty-set guard; TOFU on a pinned device (+ trustsNoKey always true — the brief's "unknown key through on a pinned device", 15 ✗); no floor check; a rollback honoured every time; allowDowngradeTo / the key set left out of the signed message; a successor replacing the pin; a retirement ignored; no floor in the daemon; the honoured digest never recorded; the ssh road landing by mv + ln; its unsigned rung dropped; a first trust never reaching the door; downgrade not a refusal; the watch reading downgrade as a bad signature; --land-upgrade as its own writer (test-architecture §92); the tofu ids never sent; the catch-up exemption dropped.

## 2.369.314 — 2026-10-19

### lane vault-e2e-password — every stored secret sealed under ONE vault key that only the owner's second password unwraps (owner 2026-10-19 09:3xZ after a leaked-credential incident: 「第一时间实现 e2e 加密的 vault 功能，直接使用 secondary password 而不是自动解锁」); base 07036579 (.312)
- THE FLAW REMOVED: the key-file law kept each store's key in a file beside its data (`.accounts-key` next to accounts.json …) — whoever held the disk held every secret. Now ONE random 32-byte DEK wraps every store key (data/vault.json `entries`, AES-256-GCM, AAD = the entry's name); the DEK is wrapped under KEK = scrypt(the second password) and lives IN THE HUB'S MEMORY ONLY, after a person's unlock.
- THE RECORD (src/vault.js — SHARED with zero fs: the PURE tier forbids even node:crypto): {v, kdf {scrypt N 2^17 · r 8 · p 2, salt}, check (HMAC under the KEK: a wrong password told apart BEFORE the unwrap, constant time), wrapped, verifier (HMAC under the DEK: the right password over a damaged wrap ⇒ `corrupt`, not `wrong_password`), entries, createdAt, rotatedAt, idleLockHours, sealing?}. p 2, not the brief's p 1: p 1 measured 223–235 ms on the hub (32 cores, load 16) — under the 250 ms floor; p 2 measured 393–472 ms (545 ms median under the gate's load), the same 128 MiB. Change password re-wraps the DEK only (a new salt); the entries stay byte-identical.
- THE ENGINE (src/server/vault-engine.js) registers in secret-box (`registerVault(dataDir, provider)`), so EVERY store key read — `lawfulKey`, `secretBox`, app-secrets' master, the passkey wiring — asks it first. LOCKED after every start. Locked ⇒ `key-unreadable:vault_locked` (KF.VAULT_LOCKED — the key-file law's own transient refusal family, so every store's refusals and rows already carry it; the words 「保险库已锁定——先解锁」); nothing read, nothing minted, no file touched (a counting fs spy: 0 calls). ### lane stream-mac-ax-respawn — a Mac's resident input child is REPLACED when its Accessibility grant changes (owner 2026-10-19 ~09:1xZ: vibespace-screen re-added under Accessibility, the stream's keys and clicks still did nothing, no error); base 07036579 (.312)
- THE CAUSE (measured on the owner's Mac): the injector keeps ONE resident `vibespace-screen --disclaim input` child per daemon — born 09:01Z, the Accessibility row deleted + re-added ~09:03Z. macOS judges event posting PER RUNNING PROCESS: the child kept the verdict it was born with and posted into the void, while a fresh child answered `ok` and `--disclaim facts` said granted. Killing the child fixed it on the spot.
- THE RULE (PURE `macRespawn(state, ev)` in src/input-inject.js): the child is replaced when ① its own answer flips ax_denied → ok, or a facts read says granted after it answered ax_denied (never for a child born BY a replacement — no loop); ② the facts' tcc.accessibility changes value, either way (unless the child was born under the new value); ③ the first facts read after the Accessibility door. Never on an ax_denied alone (however many), an `ok` with no denial before it, a value read again, an unknown value. Only M/D/U/W/K answers feed it (`P` / `C` answer ok without the helper's AX check).
- THE WIRING: src/agentd/stream-mac.js keeps the last tcc a facts read saw and tells ONE hook, `helper.onTcc(fn)` (the kept value at once; every read; the door); openSettings('accessibility') tells the door and, once `open` answers, re-reads the facts (forced). The injector subscribes when it takes the helper — agentd.js unchanged. A replacement logs `[input] replaced the Mac input child: accessibility <from> → <to>` once, answers the old child's lines in flight `err replaced` (refused by name: injector_replaced) and kills it through the one kill site; the next inject spawns the new child outside the 3-a-minute crash budget. A replaced or timed-out child's late stdout never answers the next child's lines. The Windows injector is untouched (the rule runs for `cgevent` only).
- GATES: test-stream-mac §5b (fast) — the rule table (PURE) + five legs over the fake helper and the REAL createMacScreen facts: the facts flip under an ax_denied child ⇒ a NEW pid lands ok; granted → denied ⇒ replaced; 50 injects (a `P` line before each, five more denied reads) ⇒ one child; the child's own flip ⇒ replaced once, the facts after it replace nothing; a line in flight ⇒ `err replaced` at once; the Accessibility door's re-read ⇒ replaced (value unchanged), the Screen Recording door nothing. MUTANTS M1–M7 all RED (respawn on every ax_denied · in-flight lines unanswered · no hook · no born guard · no origin guard · no door re-read · `P` answers counted). The stream-mac-stall door pin now expects ONE disclaimed facts re-read after the Accessibility pane. The fake helper (scripts/fixtures/stream/mac-fakes.mjs): cfg.inputLive (the child's own check flipping), cfg.inputDelayMs (lines in flight), the child's pid on each input line.
