### lane desktop-picker-instant — the machine rows answer at once from the hub's last known state; the probes refresh them in the background, timed in the log (owner 2026-10-19: 「这个界面的加载时间怎么越来越长了」 — the picker sat on 「正在查看机器…」 longer every time); base 07036579 (.312)
- THE CAUSE: GET /api/desktop/machines awaited, per paired machine in parallel, `handleIfConnected` (a bounded 3 s dial when the handle is not cached) and — a connected Windows / macOS machine — `probeDesktop` (the agent's tcp-forward to 5900 + up to 3 s for the RFB greeting). Nothing cached, nothing timed; the Desktop picker and the Apps dialog's 「运行于」 painted only after the slowest machine. Measured over the REAL access layer + route (scratch/measure.mjs, a Mac whose greeting takes 5 s, a Windows box with nothing on 5900, a Linux agent): base 07036579 5029 ms, again 5005 ms (every open waits); this lane 28 ms cold / 2 ms warm, the Mac's row landing 4996 ms later by the page's follow-up and the broadcast.
- THE ROWS (src/server/desktop-access.js `machinesNow`, PURE rules in the new src/desktop-machines-cache.js): the hub keeps each machine's LAST probed row `{row, at, ms}` in memory and in data/desktop-machines.json (channel-store `writeJsonAtomic`; read once at boot — a restart paints too). The route answers at once: each row from its entry + `probedAt`, `ageMs` (the hub's clock — never the browser's), `probeMs`, `stale` past 60 s; a machine never probed = `code: 'checking'` (that row only, never pressable; a handle that already said win32 / darwin makes it a desktop row). `refreshing: [hostId]` names the probes in flight; `?wait=1` answers after them; `?fresh=1[&host=]` = Check again (that machine, now, waited for). `machines()` keeps its meaning for callers (every machine probed now).
- THE REFRESH: every answer kicks `refreshHost` when MC.refreshDue says so — never while one is in flight (a second asker JOINS it: one probe per machine), no history / Check again / the daemon's hello always, a link the hub sees NOW that differs from the one the row was probed on at once (a dropped link is said without the floor), else 10 s after the last probe. The landed row is kept, written and BROADCAST — `desktop-machines-updated {hostId, machines}` (the cache-invalidation-must-NOTIFY law). The daemon's hello (the existing dial-in hook) re-probes that machine `helloListMs` later: after a restart each machine's row turns from the file's to the live one as it dials in.
- THE PAGES: `watchMachines(app, onRows)` (src/lib/desktop-picker.js) = the answer at once, then every broadcast, and ONE `?wait=1` follow-up when probes are in flight (a broadcast missed while the socket reconnects still lands); a row never goes back to an older probe (by `probedAt`; the socket and the follow-up may arrive in either order). The Desktop picker's nodes are KEYED (`r|group|hostId`, the group heads, the notes, the running apps) and re-used, put in order by `syncChildren` (only an out-of-place node moves) — a late probe patches its row and the focused row is never rebuilt or detached; the Apps dialog's machine buttons are keyed by hostId the same way. A row's title = 「上次检查 N 秒前 · 探测 M ms」 (machineProbeText); 「检查中…」 = the new row state `checking` (src/desktop-screens.js ROW_STATES, not pressable). Check again (the machine dialog's recheck) = `recheckMachines` (`?fresh=1&host=`).
- TIMED AND SAID: every probe logs ONE line `[desktop] <host> probed in <ms> ms → <code> (<why>)` — why: picker · recheck · hello · open (the window's gate) · install (TightVNC's after-probe); a probe over 2 s logs a second (warn) line naming its slowest step with every step timed (`dial` = reaching the agent, `forward` = its tcp-connect, `greeting` = the server's first bytes): `[desktop] mac probe slow: 5002 ms — the greeting took 4999 ms (dial 1 ms · forward 2 ms · greeting 4999 ms)`.
- THE INSTALLED APPS (brief item 3 — verified AWAITED): the machine dialog paints at once, but its installed list waited for `installedApps(why 'open')`, which re-lists a list older than 10 min ON the machine (391–446 apps in 5–20 s on the owner's Windows box) before answering — the old list never showed. ## 2.369.312 — 2026-10-19

### lane stream-audio-probe — the machine stream's SOUND: speaker passthrough and the microphone road, measured (owner 2026-10-19 「开始研究下透传麦克风和扬声器」; independence rule: no third-party host/driver); base 07036579 (.312)
- PROBE ONLY, nothing built: scripts/probes/stream-audio/ (win/ WASAPI helper + on-box Node legs, mac/ SCK-audio scratch helper + the AudioServerPlugIn and its no-install load test, hub/ werift ⇄ headless Chrome). Tones = 1 kHz, −20 dBFS, 200 ms. On Windows most legs ran on an idle virtual endpoint, so they were inaudible. Captured audio was never written to disk.
- WINDOWS SPEAKER (WASAPI loopback, in-box COM, csc):
  - 10 ms packets; event-driven capture works. AUTOCONVERTPCM gives 48 kHz float stereo from a 5.1 mix.
  - An app's sample reaches our capture 20 ms (virtual endpoint) / 31 ms (the owner's USB device) after the app writes it. Loopback stamps it with its PLAY time, so capture runs 20–35 ms AHEAD of the speaker. 0.5–2 % CPU.
  - A render endpoint that nothing plays to delivers NOTHING: 0 packets and no events in 3 s. The fix is a silent render stream of our own (zeros, 100 packets/s, the first after 10.6 ms).
- WINDOWS ENCODE (the agent's ffmpeg; libopus is present):
  - Raw `-f s16le` over a pipe (or UDP) comes out in ~90 ms clumps: the PCM demuxer reads ~4096 frames per packet, and no option changes that. A sample takes 62–100 ms to reach its RTP packet.
  - A streaming WAV header + `-f wav -max_size 1920 -ignore_length 1` gives a packet every 20 ms, 1–10 ms after the sample passes. App write → Opus RTP packet in the agent's hands: 21–30 ms.
  - ffmpeg ≈ 5 % of a core and ~0.9 s to its first packet. 10 ms frames add +29 kbps of headers.
- MAC SPEAKER (SCStreamConfiguration.capturesAudio, a scratch helper under the probe's granted launcher):
  - It rides the Screen Recording grant. tccd shows ScreenCapture (allowed) and only a coreaudiod Microphone PREFLIGHT (preflight_unknown: no prompt, no row). No System-Audio service was asked.
  - 48 kHz float32 stereo planar, 960-frame buffers, delivery p50 35 / p95 47 ms. Our tone is stamped +22 ms after its scheduled host time and is in hand at +58–73 ms. The level is exact.
  - Starting an output engine at capture start held SCK audio for ~1 s once.
- MAC OPUS IS IN-BOX: AudioToolbox (AVAudioConverter) encodes Opus in 0.28 ms per 20 ms packet; the packet exists ~1 ms after the buffer. It also decodes it (0.03 ms per packet, level intact). A Mac needs no ffmpeg for audio.
- THE WEBRTC ROAD (werift 0.25.0 → Chrome 154, hub):
  - Opus needs no packetizer: one Opus packet = one RTP payload, written with writeRtp on an audio track (werift rewrites SSRC / PT / seq).
  - One msid puts audio + video in ONE MediaStream, so the product's `<video>` can carry the sound.
  - Clean loopback: send → Chrome's audio graph 36–67 ms, → its output clock 73–103 ms (outputLatency 30–37 ms). NetEq 31–41 ms, 0 lost.
  - With 0–30 ms of jitter: NetEq 46–63 ms, output 88–122 ms, no gaps.
- THE DATA-CHANNEL FALLBACK (Opus on an unordered DC → WebCodecs AudioDecoder → an AudioWorklet): 22–39 ms to the graph, but 4–6 underruns per run with a 20 ms cushion. With a 60 ms cushion it costs the same as NetEq and still has no concealment. Not needed: V1 = the RTP track.
- THE MIC BACK (getUserMedia → the same audio m-line, sendrecv → werift receives Opus RTP): it arrives within ±13 ms of Chrome's own WebAudio stamp of the captured sample. ~7 kbps on the tone fixture (Chrome's encoder, DTX off).
- INTERCOM (no virtual mic; the viewer's voice plays on the machine's speakers): on Windows, PCM → our render stream reaches the mix in 31–36 ms; Ogg Opus → ffmpeg decode (< 1 ms) → render takes 57–60 ms. Both were measured on the virtual endpoint; the owner's device plays ~23 ms later than the virtual one.
- WINDOWS VIRTUAL MIC: there is no user-mode way to publish a capture endpoint.
  - Every virtual audio device on the owner's box (Steam Streaming Mic/Speakers, Voicemeeter VAIO, NVIDIA Broadcast, Dubbing) is a kernel .sys signed by "Microsoft Windows Hardware Compatibility Publisher" (attestation/WHQL).
  - Our own would be a SYSVAD/ACX-class driver + an EV certificate + a Partner Center account + an admin pnputil install. That is the same class as the parked virtual display (B-f6b3). Not built.
- MAC VIRTUAL MIC: our own AudioServerPlugIn (user space, no kernel) was BUILT on the owner's Mac (clang; 69 KB arm64 / 84 KB universal; ad-hoc signed).
  - It was load-tested WITHOUT installing: vsmic-host loads the CFPlugIn factory from the Info.plist, gets the driver interface, walks the HAL's 24 properties, then runs StartIO / zero time stamps at 48 kHz / WriteMix → ReadInput. 25/25 passed.
  - The tone written on the output side is read on the input side with 0 frames of added delay. A stopped feed reads as silence.
  - NOT measured: loading inside coreaudiod. That needs /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/HAL + admin + a coreaudiod restart; distribution needs Developer ID + notarization.
- SIDE FINDING (not audio): werift 0.25's ICE-lite keeps sending DTLS to the FIRST pair the browser nominated.
  - On the multi-homed hub, Chrome 154 nominated a tailnet pair and then moved to a LAN pair. werift answered the ClientHello on the tailnet pair, and the handshake never completed: both sides stayed "connecting" while Chrome retransmitted.
  - The probe pins werift to one address (iceInterfaceAddresses). A viewer that reaches a machine over BOTH a LAN and a tailnet may hit the same problem.
- NOT MEASURED:
  - a real viewer's output device (only headless Chrome's output clock);
  - the AudioServerPlugIn inside coreaudiod;
  - Windows' Steam Streaming Microphone as a loop (it would open a microphone endpoint on the owner's box — ask first);
  - bitrate on real program audio (the target is 64 kbps).

## 2.369.303 — 2026-10-18

### lane mobile-back-guard — the phone's back gesture closes the open panel first, and at home asks for a second back (the owner 2026-10-18: 「在手机版上能不能 block 一下那个返回手势啊？我有时候不小心返回返回着，就多返回了几下」); base 5342d803 (.300)
- WHY: the client had no history handling at all (no pushState / popstate under src/lib, no overscroll rule), so on a phone every edge swipe was the browser's history back and left the page.
- WHAT: PURE `src/lib/back-guard.js` (imports nothing): `backVerdict({ phone, enabled, target, lastBackAt, now, deepLinkFirst })` → `{ action: none | close | arm | leave, toast }`, `backTarget` (Esc's order: every `[data-popover]` → a dialog → the window switcher → a sheet → the window area (yields to the sidebar, the phone's home) → the sidebar's drill-down → null = home), `bootStep` (push / keep / none). The wiring is `src/lib/mobile-back.js` (phone code in its own module, kb-design-lessons §7a); app.js holds one import and one install line under `this.isMobile`. Each layer closes through its own closer: the floats are removed (Esc's rule), a modal shell through its ✕, the static overlay through `hideDialogs`, the For-you tray through its own `hidePopup` (new `vs-back-dismiss` event — drafts stashed), the drill-down through its ‹ row, the window area via `sidebar.toggle(true)` (the window stays open). At home: the toast `再返回一次退出` (showToast, 2 s; `noteOwnGesture()` — new in utils.js — so it is recorded seen, never an unread notification). Setting `mobile.backGuard` (new category Mobile, under Appearance & layout, default on, read live; off = the next back leaves). `@media (pointer: coarse) { html, body { overscroll-behavior: none } }`.
- MEASURED (Chrome 154, the browser's own back = the Alt+Left accelerator → NavigationController::GoBack, the same skip logic Android's back gesture runs; loopback two-page probe): re-arming with a fresh `pushState` in popstate is fragile — with backs 6 s apart (the tap's transient activation expired) the THIRD back skipped VibeSpace's entry and left; after one tap at boot, the SECOND back left; a push 1.5 s after load with no tap was skipped 4 of 4. Re-arming with `history.go(1)` onto the existing sentinel (a traversal adds no entry, marks nothing) held in every sequence (spaced backs, touch taps, no taps between backs). A tap un-skips an entry pushed before it. A reload or tab restore standing on the sentinel keeps the entry below same-document (back = popstate, no reload), so boot keeps the sentinel it stands on instead of pushing a second. A no-tap push at boot was skipped on some cold pages and kept on others (the app's own boot push: kept 4 of 4); either way an untouched page is never stranded. Hence: ONE pushState ever (plus a fallback if the forward entry vanished), re-arm by `go(1)`, and "arm" stands on the page's own entry for 2 s so the second back is the browser's and leaves even when VibeSpace is the tab's first page (a script `history.back()` there does nothing); a timer steps back onto the sentinel when the window lapses.
- SAME-DOCUMENT NAVIGATION: Chrome fires popstate on a `#fragment` navigation too. Every `href='#'` link and the chat's link handler preventDefault today, but rendered markdown elsewhere could navigate to a fragment; the wiring remembers the URL the sentinel stands above (`baseHref`) and reads a popstate onto ANOTHER URL as a navigation — nothing closes, a sentinel is pushed above the new entry (the click's own activation covers that push).
- DEEP LINK: the client reads no `?` link today; `location.search` non-empty marks the first back after boot `deepLinkFirst`: it closes no WINDOW (arms instead), a menu or dialog opened since still closes, then the same rule.
- OVERSCROLL: the rule stops Chrome for Android's own swipe-past-the-edge navigation and pull-to-refresh. Android's system back gesture and iOS Safari's edge swipe ignore it; they arrive as a history back, which the sentinel catches. Neither is reproducible in desktop Linux Chrome (synthetic touch/touchpad overscroll and pull-down: no navigation, no reload, with or without the rule), so the suite pins the computed style (none on a coarse pointer, auto on a fine one) and no phone browser was measured.
- NOT DONE: the optional web-app manifest — iOS standalone back-swipe behaviour could not be measured here (no iOS device or simulator) and the brief forbids guessing.
- TESTS: scripts/test-back-guard.mjs (fast, in-process · 125 ms, 65 ✓): the verdict table at the 2 s edges, backTarget order, bootStep, the REAL wiring esbuild-bundled over a fake history + clock (16 legs), RED controls (the edge `<=`, deepLinkFirst ignored, a pushState re-arm, no URL check). scripts/test-mobile-back-chrome.mjs (heavy, ~92 s, 20 ✓): 390×844 DPR 3 Android UA + 1280×800, the browser's own back and history.back(): switcher, "+" sheet, New Session dialog, For-you tray, window → sidebar, Task Groups drill-down, the seen toast, 2 s re-arm, the second back leaves to the previous page, untouched page, reload, a `#fragment` navigation, `?` link in zh, setting off, desktop untouched.

### lane stream-p2w-capture-probe — the Windows per-window capture facts (design q-041 r3 §3 P2w-0, the capture half): Windows.Graphics.Capture on windows the lane opened itself, on the owner's workstation; base 5342d803 (no src/ change, no bump)
- WHY: P2w makes one application window the stream's picture. Before a build lane, it needs the facts of a window's `GraphicsCaptureItem`: the colour model, the size, the border, the rate, what occlusion / minimize / a second display do, and whether the pipe can feed the mapped road. Two earlier workers stopped before any leg ran; this lane measures capture only (no input, no virtual display).
- THE HELPER: scripts/probes/stream-p2w/wgc-probe.cs, 300 lines of C# 5.
  - The in-box .NET Framework 4.8 csc builds it in 1.1 s. It references the 20 split WinMetadata `*.winmd` plus three Framework64 facades (System.Runtime, System.Runtime.WindowsRuntime, System.Runtime.InteropServices.WindowsRuntime). No SDK, no NuGet.
  - The chain: `IGraphicsCaptureItemInterop.CreateForWindow` → `Direct3D11CaptureFramePool.CreateFreeThreaded` → a staging copy → tight rows.
- COLOUR (the calibration window, 19 patches): exact in BOTH formats.
  - R16G16B16A16Float is scRGB exactly like DDA. Each patch has the P0 DDA capture's own bits (grey10 9884 … white 16640 = 2.5 at SDR white 200 nits). ÷ white/80 → sRGB OETF (`srgb8OfHalf`) reproduces all 19. The unmapped RED control gives DDA's 45 / 81 / 119 ….
  - B8G8R8A8 is the window's SDR picture, EXACT on an HDR display (all 19). DDA's 8-bit is clipped scRGB. Pixel by pixel, the mapped FP16 frame equals the BGRA frame on 99.974 % of channels; the rest are ±1, on scaled patch edges.
- SIZE: the frame is the DWM extended frame bounds, title bar included. It is neither GetWindowRect (which holds the invisible resize borders) nor the client.
  - A DPI-unaware window comes at its physical (scaled) size.
  - Windows 11's rounded corners and 1-px border carry alpha < 255.
- BORDER: an unpackaged exe gets `GraphicsCaptureAccess.RequestAccessAsync(Borderless)` = Allowed, and `IsBorderRequired = false` takes effect: no yellow border on screen.
  - Without it, the border is 3 px + a 1-px blend drawn INSIDE the window's edge on screen.
  - It is never in the frames: they are byte-identical either way.
  - `IsCursorCaptureEnabled` sets. Whether a pointer over the window gets drawn was not observable: the probe never moves the pointer.
- RATE (a 3480×1915 Edge window on a 120 Hz display):
  - The default MinUpdateInterval holds a window to ~52 fps (gaps 16.7 / 25 ms). At the source, `MinUpdateInterval` 1 ms gives 97.7 fps and 33 ms gives 26.8 fps.
  - Readback (staging copy + Map + rows) costs 8.4–8.9 ms per FP16 frame (~50 % of one core at 53 fps) and 4.3 ms per BGRA frame (~28 %). Without readback, 1–2 % of one core.
- OCCLUSION / MINIMIZE / ANOTHER DISPLAY:
  - Covered by a TopMost lane window: the live picture of the covered window (a GDI window kept ticking at its own 24 fps).
  - A covered CHROMIUM window stops painting (0 fps, Chromium's native occlusion tracking). With `--disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows` it paints at 49.8 fps.
  - Minimized: frames STOP. No black frame, no error, no size change; the session lives and resumes with the live picture on restore.
  - A session opened on a minimized window: the item is the minimized caption (459×67) and no frames come. On restore, the first frame lands in the small pool (clipped), then Recreate, then full frames.
  - Another display (both 4K at 175 %): a move during a session is seamless, with no gap and no resize. FP16 white is 2.5 there too.
- PIPE: the helper's `pipe` has the mapped road's ffmpeg #1 shape (W×H×8 tight rows on stdout).
  - Spawned by the agent's own node (a libuv pipe) with 64 KiB writes: near-4K FP16 holds 30 fps (1.6 GB/s; one 53 MB write gives 26 fps), near-4K BGRA 60 fps, 1920×1080 FP16 60 fps.
  - The same node reader takes 2.07 GB/s from ffmpeg (a synthetic source). So near-4K FP16 at 60 fps needs a smaller frame on the pipe (part C's NV12).
  - Into ffmpeg's h264_nvenc: BGRA holds 30 fps (NVENC 3 %); rgbaf16le reaches only 25 fps at ~4 cores (ffmpeg's float conversion, which also clamps).
- REFUSALS: `CreateForWindow` answers 0x80070057 "Could not capture the given window" for:
  - child windows (Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND, the UWP title bar);
  - invisible / IME windows, a never-shown window, a message-only window;
  - a bad handle.
- ACCEPTED: `CreateForWindow` gives an item for:
  - a UWP app by its ApplicationFrameWindow (frame bounds; its CoreWindow child gives a 0×0 item the pool refuses);
  - the taskbar;
  - Progman (both displays, 7680×2160);
  - GetDesktopWindow (0×0).
  - Elevated windows were not tried: the only one was the owner's.
- TRAPS:
  - Windows 11 Notepad restores the owner's previous tabs when it starts, so it is not a lane window. pad.ps1 stands in for it.
  - A process in the background cannot change another window's z-order: HWND_TOP, HWND_BOTTOM and minimize + restore were all ignored. Cover with a TopMost window.

### lane stream-hdr-probe — P4 probe: can the desktop stream's viewer show TRUE HDR (10-bit PQ), and can our chain carry it? (design q-041 r3 §1 HDR row + §3 P4; owner 2026-10-18 decision ⑤: probe only); base 5342d803 (.300)
- WHY: today an HDR desktop is mapped EXACTLY to SDR (FP16 scRGB ÷ white → sRGB OETF, 8-bit NV12 H.264 → werift → `<video>`); above SDR white clips. The owner asked whether real HDR could reach the viewer. Measured, nothing built: scripts/probes/stream-hdr/ (README.md = how to run), report /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/stream-hdr-probe/report.md.
- THE CLIP: one synthetic 10-bit PQ picture (100 / 203 / 1000-nit squares, a 0 → 1000-nit ramp; 10-bit codes 509 / 573 / 723 exact via geq) as HEVC Main10 (x265, HDR10 SEI), AV1 10-bit (SVT-AV1, PQ in the sequence header), VP9.2 (libvpx; VP9's bitstream has NO transfer field — only the container / config says PQ), + an 8-bit H.264 baseline with BT.2020 / PQ in its VUI. Every decode below read the codes back exact (723 / 573 / 281).
- BROWSER APIS (headless; hub Chrome 154 Linux · Windows Edge 155 on the RTX 5090 · Mac Chrome 155 on the M4 Pro):
  - WebCodecs: AV1 10-bit + VP9.2 decode everywhere (hub software only → I420P10, tagged PQ); HEVC Main10 PQ only with hardware (Windows, Mac). Hardware frames are opaque (format null).
  - `<video>` / MSE: AV1 10-bit + VP9.2 everywhere, HEVC on Windows / Mac; the presented frame is tagged PQ. mediaCapabilities says HDR yes / smooth / power-efficient for HEVC only (AV1 / VP9 rec2020 + pq: no, on all three).
  - 2D canvas `rec2100-pq` / `rec2100-hlg` / `srgb-linear`: REFUSED (TypeError, not a PredefinedColorSpace) on every stable browser; accepted only with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features (then a PQ frame keeps its code: 0.749 for 1000 nits). An sRGB canvas, float16 included, tone-maps a PQ frame to SDR: 1000 nits → 0.997, 203 nits → 0.734.
  - WebGPU `rgba16float` + `toneMapping: { mode: 'extended' }`: accepted and echoed everywhere (NVIDIA blackwell, Apple metal-3). Our PQ shader (10-bit planes → nits → BT.709 ÷ SDR white → extended sRGB) read back offscreen on BOTH real GPUs: 1000 nits 2.01 (maths 2.008), 203 nits 1.008 (1.007). Headless SwiftShader has no RGBA_F16 WebGPU swap chain: the first present loses the device ("A valid external Instance reference no longer exists").
  - WebRTC: receive AV1 (profile 0/1) + VP9 profile-id=2 everywhere; H.265 only Mac Chrome (receive + send); the color-space header extension and RTCRtpScriptTransform everywhere. matchMedia `(dynamic-range: high)` is false in every headless run (no HDR screen) — the owner's page answers that.
- OUR TRANSPORT (werift 0.25.0 → Chrome; scripts/probes/stream-hdr/webrtc-leg.mjs + the page's tile (e), a loopback whose sender transform swaps in the clip's frames):
  - H.264 8-bit with PQ in the VUI through the PRODUCT's packetizer (src/stream-h264.js): Chrome's WebRTC `<video>` frame is tagged bt2020 / PQ (hub, software) and Edge's too (Windows, hardware NV12). Today's codec carries PQ.
  - AV1 10-bit: hub Chrome decodes NOTHING — its log: `Dav1dDecoder::Decode unhandled bit depth: 10` (libwebrtc's software AV1 decoder is 8-bit only; the 8-bit control decodes and keeps PQ). Windows Edge decodes it in HARDWARE and keeps PQ (116 frames, opaque, bt2020 / pq). Through RTCRtpScriptTransform → WebCodecs the hub decodes it too (I420P10, PQ, exact codes).
  - VP9.2: 10 bits arrive (I420P10, exact codes) but the transfer is LOST (null) — with the color-space extension negotiated and sent on every frame's last packet too (bytes checked: `bede 0002 93 09100910`); drawn as SDR. Not an HDR road.
  - werift 0.25.0's own AV1 packetizer sends one OBU per packet with its size field and no Dependency Descriptor: Chrome then cuts each OBU into its own same-timestamp frame ("Failed to combine frames - invalid spatial index order") and decodes nothing. Aggregating the temporal unit (W=0, length-prefixed, Z / Y per PACKET) works — webrtc-leg.mjs `av1Payloads`.
  - A werift data channel into Chrome: 58–69 Mb/s on loopback (16 KiB messages).
- NVENC on the owner's Windows box (RTX 5090, driver 616.92, ffmpeg N-127564), 4K60 synthetic p010le / nv12 from memory, p1 / ull / cbr 20 Mb/s, 960 frames: hevc_nvenc main10 261–265 fps, av1_nvenc 10-bit 231–277 fps, h264_nvenc 8-bit 276–279 fps — 10 bits cost nothing. Both write BT.2020 / PQ / BT.2020-NCL into the BITSTREAM (raw HEVC VUI / AV1 sequence header). TRAPS: (1) output `-color_primaries / -color_trc / -colorspace` that differ from the frames' own tags make ffmpeg 8 insert a CPU swscale conversion (the same runs: 97–99 fps) — tag the frames (`setparams`), never the output; (2) 10-bit RGB input (x2bgr10le — the layout of a 10-bit desktop duplication) is converted by NVENC with BT.601 whatever is asked (full red → Y 323 / Cb 363 / Cr 954), and ffmpeg then writes matrix bt470bg, keeping primaries bt2020 + transfer PQ — consistent, so such a zero-copy chain stays colour-correct.
- THE MAPPER A PQ OUTPUT WOULD NEED (src/stream-plan.js; not implemented): scRGB is absolute (1.0 = 80 nits), so L = 80·v cd/m² (negative → 0; optionally × 203 / (0.08·W) to put the desktop's SDR white W at BT.2408 reference white); E = ((c1 + c2·Y^m1) / (1 + c3·Y^m1))^m2, Y = L / 10000, m1 = 0.1593017578125, m2 = 78.84375, c1 = 0.8359375, c2 = 18.8515625, c3 = 18.6875; 10-bit narrow D = round(64 + 876·E) per R'G'B', then BT.2020-NCL Y'CbCr (Y' = 0.2627R' + 0.6780G' + 0.0593B', Cb = (B' − Y') / 1.8814, Cr = (R' − Y') / 1.4746 → 64 + 876Y', 512 + 896C) into P010 (value << 6). THE TABLE: FP16 bits → E as Uint16Array(65 536) = 128 KiB — ONE table (absolute; one per white level only with the 203 anchor), the frame loop still three lookups per pixel; 8-bit variant D = round(16 + 219·E) in a Uint8Array(65 536) + NV12. Strict BT.2020 primaries need the 3×3 BT.709 → BT.2020 matrix on LINEAR values before PQ (channels mix ⇒ no per-channel table: a Float32Array(65 536) linear table, the matrix, then E by a float-indexed table, e.g. float32 bits >>> 13 → Uint16Array(2^19) = 1 MiB) — or keep BT.709 primaries in the VUI and clip wide-gamut negatives as today. P010 is 24.9 MB per 4K frame (NV12 12.4): twice today's pipe.
- VERDICT (data level; the screen-level answer is the owner's eye on hdr-probe.html, below): the viewer side CAN take PQ today without a new transport. Smallest chains, by size:
  - A · 8-bit PQ in today's H.264 (mapper table + VUI args + a per-viewer opt-in; ~40–60 lines): measured to arrive as PQ in Chrome and Edge. Cost: banding — 0–203 nits gets 127 codes (16–143) instead of SDR's 219; 203–1000 nits 38.
  - B · AV1 10-bit over the same werift RTP → `<video>` (av1_nvenc + P010 mapper + the aggregated-TU packetizer + codec negotiation with an H.264 fallback; ~150–200 lines): measured working on the owner's Windows Edge (hardware decode); a viewer without a hardware AV1 decoder (hub Chrome / Linux) decodes nothing.
  - C · RTCRtpScriptTransform (or a data channel) → WebCodecs → WebGPU extended canvas (B's sender + a ~150-line WebGPU renderer and a canvas in place of the `<video>`): works wherever WebCodecs decodes 10-bit (incl. software); the maths verified on both GPUs.
  - Not roads: a `rec2100-pq` 2D canvas (flag-only), VP9.2 over WebRTC (transfer lost), HEVC over WebRTC (Mac Chrome only).
  - RISKS for all: an SDR viewer tone-maps PQ (an sRGB canvas: 203 nits → 0.734, so the SDR desktop would look dim) ⇒ HDR only for a viewer that reports `(dynamic-range: high)`; how each browser places PQ 203 nits against its SDR white on a real HDR screen is unmeasured; the P010 pipe at 4K60 (≈1.5 GB/s) is unmeasured — the GPU (part C's helper) is the natural place for the mapping.

### lane stream-p3m-probe — P3m-0: the Mac screen + single-window capture, encode, input and TCC probe on the owner's Macbook (design q-041 r3 §3; probe sources only: scripts/probes/stream-p3m/, no src/ change, no bump); base 5342d803
- **THE MACHINE:**
  - MacBook Pro M4 Pro, macOS 26.5.2, lid shut, with two PG27UCDM 4K displays at 2× (EDR potential 10.15, now 1.0).
  - Command Line Tools 26.6, ffmpeg 8.0.1 with VideoToolbox.
  - The agent is a LaunchAgent running Homebrew's node; the detached daemon has ppid 1.
  - The session was LOCKED with the displays asleep until the owner came. The owner granted Screen Recording + Accessibility to the probe's launcher only.
- **TCC: TODAY'S SHAPE IS WRONG.** tccd's own log (`log show --predicate 'subsystem == "com.apple.TCC"'`, no root needed) shows the attribution.
  - It attributes every plain child of agentd to `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/25.8.2/bin/node`, BY PATH. A `brew upgrade node` orphans the grant, and granting node grants every node that LaunchAgent runs.
  - A background request gets NO prompt (`Service kTCCServiceScreenCapture does not allow prompting; returning denied`). It gets only a universalAccessAuthWarn alert and a disabled Settings row. Accessibility behaves the same ("returning Unknown").
  - The fix, measured: `posix_spawn` with `responsibility_spawnattrs_setdisclaim(attr, 1)` makes the helper its own client.
  - An ad-hoc client is keyed to path + cdhash. Measured: the same bytes at another path ⇒ refused; rebuilt in place ⇒ refused; the original restored ⇒ allowed.
- **CAPTURE (ScreenCaptureKit from a CLI helper):**
  - Display 4K native: 57 fps; capture latency displayTime → callback p50 −0.9 ms. CPU: helper 1.8 %, WindowServer +7 % and replayd +4 % of a core.
  - The default config is 1920×1080 POINTS 420v. Native size needs `contentRect × pointPixelScale`.
  - Every format runs at 4K: BGRA, 420v/f, x420, xf20, l10r, xf44, RGhA. The HDR stream presets give xf44 + DisplayP3_PQ; in that capture SDR white = 100 nits. The `captureHDRScreenshot*` presets segfault in `init(preset:)`.
  - **SDR greys are exact in every format: SCK does no tone-mapping, so the Mac needs no LUT stage.** But `colorSpaceName` nil hands the DISPLAY profile under a BT.709 tag (sRGB red → 208,74,34). `colorSpaceName = sRGB` makes it exact: BGRA 18/19 exact, 420v 19/19 within ±2.
  - A window filter in a CLI asserts `CGS_REQUIRE_INIT` unless `NSApplication.shared` comes first. The window frame includes the title bar (32 pt). Greys 19/19 exact at 57 fps.
- **BACKGROUND:** a covered window gives full frames. On a non-current Space (the probe's own full-screen window took the display's Space) the window has onScreen=false but still gives full frames at ~23 fps. **A minimized window gives `suspended` and no picture** — r3 §2's "never minimize" rule holds.
- **ENCODE (VTCompressionSession, H.264 Constrained Baseline, low-latency RC):**
  - `ForceKeyFrame` = an IDR on THAT frame (NAL 5 + SPS/PPS each time).
  - A live `AverageBitRate` change is followed without a restart. Never call `VTSessionSetProperty` from the output callback: that deadlocks.
  - Real frames:
    - 4K tops out at 37 fps (serial 29 ms per frame on the SCK queue, capture backed up to 130 ms).
    - **4K30 at 18.7 ms.**
    - **1440p60 (SCK-scaled) at 57 fps / 11.9 ms.**
  - The plain realtime session pipelines 80–150 ms and starves SCK at 4K. `MaxFrameDelayCount` is unsupported.
  - ffmpeg h264_videotoolbox over a pipe: NV12 or BGRA at 4K sustains 67 fps synthetic and 52 fps from SCK.
- **INPUT:**
  - `CGEventPostToPid` delivers into an app that is NOT frontmost, without activating it: TextEdit while Chrome was in front, a Chrome `data:` page while TextEdit was in front, and the probe's own window (keys + a click).
  - `CGEventPost(.cghidEventTap)` lands in the frontmost app.
  - Both need Accessibility. Without it, WindowServer's `kTCCServicePostEvent` check drops the events silently: the keyDown counter does not move and there is no prompt.
  - Read-back works through AX under the same grant, so Automation is never needed.
- **DISTRIBUTION:**
  - Building on the box requires the CLT: `/usr/bin/swiftc` is only xcrun's trampoline.
  - The on-box default target is minos 26.0. The helper needs `-target …-macos15.0`.
  - Universal build: arm64 + x86_64 → lipo → `codesign -s -`, 538 KB. The ad-hoc signature survives cp/ditto/tar/zip and a Linux round trip.
  - A file the agent lands has no quarantine and mode 0644: chmod +x and it runs (`spctl` says rejected, which does not matter).
  - The same file with a browser's quarantine BLOCKS in exec on a Gatekeeper prompt.
- REPORT: /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/stream-p3m-probe/report.md (a verdict and the build lines per r3 row, the greys table, the TCC map, PNGs).

Its version is persisted, so it only grows across restarts (a reconnecting client never takes the rollback branch). - MEASURED HERE FIRST (probe, loopback, the real daemon + the hub module + a werift stand-in, a padded fixture at 30 fps / 8 Mbps): the device-link relay is NOT slow by itself — stdio link, WS dial link, and the dial link through 10 / 50 ms emulated RTT all carried 30 fps with 0 RTP gaps. It tracks the LINK's capacity: a 6 / 4 / 2 Mbps link stand-in (token bucket + TCP backpressure) gave 21.5 / 14.4 / 7.2 fps, 0 gaps, and the picture's lag grew 7.5 s in 10 s at 2 Mbps (it queues in socket buffers; nothing drops). So the owner's 1.3 Mbps reads as a device link that carries ~1.3 Mbps; the UDP leg leaves that link out of the media path.
- THE LEG (PURE src/stream-model.js codec + verdicts, the mac handed in; hub src/server/desktop-webrtc.js; daemon src/agentd/stream-host.js createLeg): the relay socket is bound before the offer; `stream-offer` carries `relayLeg {port, key, hosts}` (a per-session 32-byte key over the device link only; the hub's IPv4s — the owner's browser on that machine reached them over UDP at 10 ms); the daemon adds its dial host and PINGs from its own socket: `VSR1`·type·flags·counter·nonce·HMAC-SHA256/16; an authenticated PING (counter strictly rising = the replay bound) teaches the hub the daemon's address and gets a PONG; DATA (`VSR1`·3·browser IPv4·port·datagram, no mac — the 5-tuple, as TURN ChannelData; DTLS / SRTP inside) both ways. ONE hub socket: the magic is never a STUN / DTLS / RTP first byte.
- THE LADDER: direct (host pairs, ICE priority) → the leg → the device link. The daemon goes UP at the first PONG (and flags UP at once), PINGs every 15 s idle / 2 s while it carries the picture, DOWN after 2 s without a PONG (re-asked 5 s after the last PING; a PONG brings it back — no new session, no ICE restart: the browser's 5-tuple and werift's shim peer never change). The hub forwards on the path the daemon LAST spoke on (leg DATA / PING UP ⇒ udp; device-link frames / PING without UP ⇒ link; silent 35 s ⇒ link). Chosen over two relay candidate sets (leg vs link by ICE priority): a leg dying mid-stream would need ICE consent to expire (30 s) and a restart; here the link takes over within 2 s + 2 s with the picture flowing.

### creds-merge-keep-rest — a merge keeps the survivor's other credentials, whoever wrote its file (B-5fc0, oat-census-closure's LEFT item 4; credential class, verify-gated)
- The hole: `accounts.mergeSubscription` kept and archived the survivor's other top-level keys (mcpOAuth, designOauth …) only when the survivor's `.credentials.json` was OUR long-lived-token file (pool-oat verify r2 F3). A survivor holding a real CLI login file — dead or alive, mcpOAuth beside it — was overwritten whole whenever the fold ran (`preferFromCreds`, the re-login merge; or no live login there, the auto-merge), and nothing was archived. Reproduced on base a03898f5 (the new suite copied into a tree with the base accounts.js swapped in): a re-login onto a dead login + mcpOAuth + designOauth ⇒ the file held claudeAiOauth alone, 0 archives; a survivor with mcpOAuth only (a logged-out CLI file) ⇒ the same; an unparseable survivor ⇒ overwritten, 0 archives; a fold side whose file did not parse, or was `{}`, was written over the survivor (its login and mcpOAuth gone).
- The fix: ONE PURE verdict in src/account-material.js, `credsMergeVerdict({ intoFile, intoOurs, fromFile, fromOurs, preferFrom, intoLogged, rest })` → `{ fold, write, archive, aside, keep, why }`. (a) OUR file on the merged-away side never travels — only its other keys; (b) a write over an EXISTING survivor file, ours or not, is `{ ...credsRestOf(survivor), ...folded }` and the old file is archived first; (c) a real login on the survivor wins unless preferFrom; (d) a survivor file that does not parse is archived as is and the fold goes on; two guard rows: a fold file that does not parse, or is an empty object, replaces nothing. `rest` is asked (login-expiry credsRestOf), not imported: account-material rides in the daemon bundle and stays free of login-expiry. The brief's `fromObj` became `fromFile` (bytes): an unparseable fold file must be told from an absent one, because the `.claude.json` copy rides on `fold` exactly as before.
- mergeSubscription reads each side's file ONCE (a Buffer), parses it, asks the verdict and acts. The archive is the existing `.dead-<ms>-m<6 hex>` writePrivateFile (0600; tmp `wx` + fsync + rename) — the one way, kept so test-oat-mint §8's write rows (`mergeSubscription writePrivateFile` ×2) and module edges stay as they were; not archiveCredentialFile (async, a rename, and the oat's acts have one caller). The archive holds the survivor's file AS READ, byte-for-byte (an unparseable file included), or, for OUR file, only its other keys. `intoLogged` is read off the same bytes (parseClaudeAuth's rule: an access token, and not our file); the separate readSubCreds parse is gone. The live guard and the Keychain refusal are untouched.
- A survivor holding ANOTHER row's token file (our mark naming a different account) is not ours for this survivor ⇒ archived whole, as materializeVerdict archives a foreign mark.
- Gates: test-creds-merge (new, fast, 49 legs, ≈ 90 ms): §1 the verdict, 14 rows + the no-rest refusal + an own `__proto__` key; §2 12 rows over the real AccountManager, each with a RED control on a scratch copy — the 4 rows this lane changed restore the pre-fix branch condition (`keeps = intoFile != null && intoOurs`) ⇒ the survivor's mcpOAuth (or its unparsed bytes) in no file and no archive; the others cut the row's own rule ⇒ red — plus the archive's name and mode, and the live guard; §3 the spies (console / stdout / stderr, 12 roster broadcasts, the merge's answer, archive names; our token in no file) with 4 planted leaks, each named. test-oat-materialize: its F3 RED control re-anchored onto the verdict (its accounts.js line is gone), same claim — 176/0. test-oat-mint 132/0 (§8's structure census unchanged), test-account-pool 59/0, test-claude-subscription-login green, test-hot-switch-incident 81/0, test-login-expiry 346/0, test-oat-identity 305/0. ### lane usage-fold-worker-exit-hook — a usage fold worker asleep in a read no longer holds the server's exit: src/server/exit-hook.js judges the fold workers at the join, gives them 2 s, then re-raises SIGTERM; usage-index and search-index re-raise through the same door (base rel282 6c9175d4, rides .284)
- Why: lane cache-bounds-stuck-worker-race (.283) measured it — process.exit() emits 'exit', then process.reallyExit() JOINS every worker thread, and one asleep in a read (storage that does not answer) is never joined: with one STUCK fold worker the real UsageHistory's exit was still running at 8 s (Node 22 + 24). A server whose ledger storage hangs could not restart by itself — a restart waited for an external SIGKILL. usage-index.js / search-index.js carried an exit hook for exactly this; the fold workers had none.
- Measured here (probe/exit-mech.mjs, Node 22.22.1 + 24.12.0): `new Worker()` starts its thread inside the constructor — a /proc/self/task diff around it names exactly that thread; a terminated BUSY worker leaves /proc/self/task within ms while the main thread stays blocked (no loop turn needed); one asleep in a fifo's open (wchan wait_for_partner) is still listed after any bound; a terminated worker asleep in a read keeps the loop alive (no natural exit). Plain process.exit(): the main thread in futex_do_wait at 8 s; a process.reallyExit wrap that re-raises: gone in ~0.1 s (rc 143) with every 'exit' listener run first.
- THE GAP A STUCK.size KEY LEAVES: STUCK fills only past the fold's own deadline (COLD_FOLD_DEADLINE_MS = 10 min) + the terminate deadline (5 s). A fold IN FLIGHT asleep in its read holds the exit the same way for those 10 minutes (base: alive at 8 s, both Nodes) — the very minutes a person restarts because the Usage window does not load. So the judge covers every LIVE fold worker; a merely busy one still ends normally.
- src/server/exit-hook.js (new, ORCH): `exitWithout(line, log)` = THE re-raise — say the line, remove every SIGTERM listener (the server's shutdown must not run again), SIGTERM with its default action, SIGKILL only if SIGTERM was ignored. `atJoin(name, judge)` wraps process.reallyExit once (main thread only): Node's own process.exit() calls it after 'exit' (its source: "an undocumented API that gets monkey-patched in the user land" — signal-exit wraps it the same way), so a judge runs AFTER every 'exit' listener, right before the join. `threadsNow` / `threadAdded` (the ONE thread a constructor added, else null — never a guess) / `threadsLeft(tids, boundMs)` (Atomics.wait naps over /proc/self/task: no loop turn comes at the join) and PURE `unjoinable(live, left)`. EXIT_BOUND_MS = 2000 — the class of the index owners' closeBoundMs.
- src/usage-history.js: LIVE = every fold worker not yet exited → its thread id (the diff around `new Worker`), dropped on its 'exit'. `foldJoinJudge` at the join: terminate the in-flight ones (the join's own first step), give all of them EXIT_BOUND_MS to leave; one still listed — or a STUCK one /proc never named — ⇒ `[usage] N stuck fold worker(s) cannot be joined — exiting without them` + the re-raise. Unchanged: the STUCK census row, the refusal, the terminate deadline, the one-worker queue. A merely busy fold leaves in ms ⇒ the join goes on, exit code 0.
- Unified: the re-raise is ONE door — usage-index.js and search-index.js call `exitWithout` from their own 'exit' listeners (search-index gains the SIGKILL fallback usage-index had); pid census §85: their 3 self rows → 2 in exit-hook.js; test-exit-forensics §6c KILL_DOORS: usage-index 2 + search-index 1 → exit-hook.js 2. NOT unified: the trigger. The index owners' workers are unref'd, so their process may end NATURALLY (the loop drained), which emits 'exit' and never calls reallyExit — their 'exit' listener stays. The fold workers are ref'd: a live one holds the loop, so process.exit() is their only way out and its join their only hang; and an 'exit' listener that ends the process skips every listener registered after it (the CONTROL below).
- No SIGTERM / SIGINT listener: one would change what SIGTERM does in every process that loads usage-history (a CLI with no handler of its own would stop dying on it). ### lane ci-hang-report — a suite the gate kills at its budget leaves Node's diagnostic report, asked for BEFORE the kill, and the ✗ row carries its digest (part of the CI ≤ 30 min goal; base rel280 915c4f016, rides .281; no user-facing change ⇒ no CHANGELOG line)

Blocked, nothing to read.
- THE FLAGS (scripts/hang-report.mjs `hangReportArgv`, from the running Node's own `process.allowedNodeEnvironmentFlags` — a suite runs on `process.execPath`): `--report-on-signal --report-signal=SIGUSR2 --report-directory=<the run's fail-log dir> --report-filename=<sha8>.<suite>.<try>.hang.json --report-exclude-env --report-exclude-network`. THE NODE FLOOR FACT: README / install.sh say Node 18+; `--report-exclude-env` exists from 22.13 / 23.3 (measured: 20.19.0 lacks it, 22.23.3 — the runner's setup-node 22 — and 24.12.0 — the hub — have it). Where it is missing the tier strips `environmentVariables` from the file once the suite is gone (the report's own AND each worker sub-report's copy — the first cut missed the workers', the Node-20 leg caught it) and cuts a file that does not parse before that key. The runner's env carries VIBESPACE_CI_OAT; no report keeps an environment.
- THE DEADLINE (scripts/ci.mjs `runSuiteAsync`, new option `hang: { dir, attempt }`; `askThenKill`): read the suite's threads + children from /proc FIRST (before the signal: a main thread later stuck writing the report is not what it says), remove a stale file of the same name, SIGUSR2, poll every 50 ms ≤ 2 s for a COMPLETE (parseable) file or the suite's exit, then SIGTERM, then SIGKILL 10 s on (new: a suite whose SIGTERM listener cannot run — a main thread blocked in the report's own wait for a worker — would otherwise hold its lane to the job timeout). Without `hang` the runner is the old one (SIGTERM, no flags). Wired: the fast tier (`<markers>/fail-logs` = data/ci-heavy/fail-logs, try 1), the heavy tier's try 1 and its in-row retry (try 2) into the run's own `<markers>/fail-logs` — hub, the hosted shards, and the AIDev batch (ci-remote copies `fail-logs/` back already). The digest rides INSIDE `lines[0]` (the ✗ entry): `lines[1]` / `lines[2]` stay the stdout tail / stderr the rerun ledger reads; the heavy fail log (`full`) starts with it.
- THE DIGEST (PURE `hangDigest(report | text, {root, snapshot})`, ≤ 12 lines): the top JS frames (≤ 8, `fn · file:line` under the run root, node:internal dropped and counted), the libuv handles that hold the loop (active AND referenced) by kind with the socket peer / pipe path / fd / child pid, cpu user/sys + maxRSS, and /proc's threads (`main S ep_poll · WorkerThread S wait_for_partner — +6 idle helpers`) + children. `parseReport` repairs a PARTIAL file: every whole top-level section, and the whole elements of the array it stopped in. The planted hang in test-ci-gate §11 (a read nobody answers on a unix socket + an interval + a worker in Atomics.wait), 3 s budget, Node 24.12:
  `✗ test-planted-hang FAILED (3062ms, ETIMEDOUT, SIGTERM) [lane 1] load 1.3→1.2 — hang report: <root>/fail-logs/abcdef01.test-planted-hang.1.hang.json`
  `  [hang] JS main: idle at the signal (no JS running — the loop waits on the handles below)`
  `  [hang] JS worker 1: at waitForever · scripts/test-planted-hang.mjs:6` (+ `at stuckFold · …:7`, `at <anonymous> · …:8  (+2 node:internal)`)
  `  [hang] handles holding the loop: timer ×1 · async ×1 · pipe ×3 (scripts/test-planted-hang.sock, → scripts/test-planted-hang.sock, scripts/test-planted-hang.sock) · workers ×1 — +12 unref'd / idle`
  `  [hang] cpu user 0.03 s · sys 0.01 s · maxRSS 109 MB` · `  [hang] threads at the deadline: main S ep_poll · WorkerThread S futex_do_wait — +6 idle helpers`
- WHAT A SIGNAL-ASKED REPORT CAN SEE (measured on 20.19 / 22.23 / 24.12; the reason the /proc line exists): Node's handler is a JS `process.on(SIGUSR2)` listener, so (1) an IDLE loop is reported in ~60 ms but its main-thread JS stack is EMPTY (`{"message": ""}` — no JS runs while the loop waits; the handles name the wait, and a worker's sub-report carries its frames: a busy worker and one in Atomics.wait both answer the interrupt); (2) a BUSY main thread (`for (;;) {}`) or one blocked synchronously (spawnSync, Atomics.wait, readFileSync of a FIFO) writes NOTHING — the row says `no hang report (asked with SIGUSR2, nothing written in 2000 ms)` and /proc shows `main R` or `main S <wchan>`; (3) a worker blocked in a SYSCALL (a FIFO open, spawnSync, a read off storage that does not answer — cache-bounds' "blocked in a read" shape) makes the main thread wait, unbounded, for that worker's sub-report (node_report.cc), so the file stops at its last 8 KB flush (16 386 bytes here, cut in "libuv") — the digest says PARTIAL and keeps the whole sections. Thread names: Node 24 names them (MainThread / WorkerThread / V8Worker …), 20 / 22 call nearly all `node` — the main thread is told by tid == pid, and threads parked on a futex or V8's named helpers are counted, not listed.

### lane fleet-helm-ephemeral — every fleet pod declares ephemeral-storage (request 2Gi + limit 20Gi) and the chart names a priority class, so a full node disk no longer evicts VibeSpace first (B-6911; owner 2026-10-15 做; base rel277 f174d5b88, rides .279)
- The incident: on 2026-10-12 one node evicted 14 instances (41 pods) before the one pod filling it (787 GiB in its writable layer, a 20Gi request, priority 1e6). The kubelet's full-disk order is usage OVER the ephemeral-storage request first, then lowest priority, then most over — all 20 fleet Deployments declared no request (= 0: over at 200 KiB) and 16 no priorityClassName.
- The chart: deploy/helm/vibespace-user/values.yaml `resources.requests.ephemeral-storage: "2Gi"` + `resources.limits.ephemeral-storage: "20Gi"`, documented beside them; templates/main.yaml unchanged (it renders `resources` through `toYaml`, so values.yaml is the one source and a private values file naming `resources` without the key keeps both — helm merges nested maps). `priorityClassName` keeps its empty default; its comment and deploy/README.md name the recommendation (a class above batch work with `preemptionPolicy: Never`, the YAML to create once) and the eviction rule.
- The numbers (kubelet stats/summary, measured by 主开发 2026-10-15T09:36Z, ns vibespace, 19 pods = 17 instances + admin + ceph-mint): median 0 MiB, p90 8 MiB, all but one ≤ 59 MiB; one instance at 8 496 MiB (rootfs 8 490 — browser profiles / tmp / caches). Request 2Gi = ≥ 34× every other instance; that one stays OVER it and still ranks first among the pods over theirs — the README says to give its release a larger request (e.g. 10Gi) and that the priority class orders that group. Limit 20Gi = 2.4× it, so no instance is evicted by its own limit at rollout; a runaway writer is evicted alone instead of filling the node.
- The rollout (docs only, the admin does it — deploy/README.md «Rolling it out to existing releases»): `helm upgrade u-<user> … --reuse-values --set resources.requests.ephemeral-storage=2Gi --set resources.limits.ephemeral-storage=20Gi [--set priorityClassName=<class>]`. `--set`, not a values file: `--reuse-values` replaces the new chart's values.yaml with the release's old coalesced values (helm reuseValues: `chart.Values = oldVals`), so the new defaults never arrive by themselves, and a values file over an older release brings every other default added since. Each upgrade recreates the pod (Recreate). Proven with real helm 3.21.3 and no cluster (HELM_DRIVER=memory + a HELM_MEMORY_DRIVER_DATA release record + a 4-answer fake discovery API, `--dry-run=client`) from releases on the 2.369.199 / .210 / .277 charts: `--reuse-values` alone renders no key; with the two `--set` both (the release's own memory override kept); `-f` of its own values and `--reset-then-reuse-values` pick the defaults up by themselves.
- Gates: test-helm-render 42 → 56 — J (8: the defaults on A / C / D; cpu / memory unchanged; a `--set` and a values file without the key render through; `=null` drops; fuse / tun device limits beside it; priorityClassName empty ⇒ no field; vs the f174d5b88 chart the two lines are the WHOLE diff over 6 shapes), K (4: the README's two `--set` equal the defaults; the modelled `--reuse-values` renders none alone, both with the recipe), 2 CONTROLS (the pre-lane values.yaml; a template that `omit`s the key from requests). The byte legs E / I now compare through `noEph` (the two lines aside). Held RED: the new suite on the f174d5b88 chart = 5 J reds.

### lane refresh-live-sessions — 「刷新所有活着的会话」: one note into every live conversation's next turn, free (userW's ask inc-mv8jk9wy-35s1; the owner 2026-10-15: manual only — automatic skill detection is "too intrusive, depends on Claude Code's implementation of the day"; base rel277 f174d5b88, rides .279)
- THE DOOR — where and why: the session list had NO list-wide menu (its header row is search · the unified filter · manage mode · sort; the only menus are per-folder right-click and the filter's own), and the ⚙ gear menu has no 会话 section either (Appearance / Manage agents / Tools / Communication / System / Update / All Settings / Help). So the list got its own ⋯ — `#session-list-menu` (UI_ICONS.more) beside sort in `#session-filter-row`, shown on both session tabs (hidden on Remote / the panels, like manage mode) — holding ONE entry 「刷新所有活着的会话…」 (UI_ICONS.refresh). There and not a new gear head: the action's scope IS the session list, the user's words name "会话列表的菜单", and a one-row gear head would sit two levels deep. Nowhere else.
- THE CONFIRM (src/lib/refresh-live.js, createModalShell; no native dialog): 「将提醒 N 个活着的会话（下一轮生效，不唤醒、不计费）」, plus 「打开着的 M 个已停止 / 只读的会话会跳过」 when M > 0; the note editable, pre-filled in the device's language (en / zh / ja), with the microphone (attachDictation — it is a message box), a live `n / 2000` count, an inline refusal (empty / over the bound ⇒ 确定 disabled), 取消 / 确定, Esc closes, Ctrl+Enter confirms (through `enterSubmits` — the IME owns its Enter). The toast: 「已排给 N 个，跳过 M 个已停止的」 (M = 0 ⇒ 「已排给 N 个活着的会话——下一轮生效」), a failed write named.
- THE PLAN (PURE src/refresh-note.js `refreshPlan(sessions, note)` → `{queue, replace, skipped, text, error}`): rows `{id, conversationId, state, queued}`; ONCE per conversation (live in any row ⇒ live — a read-only view of a running conversation never skips it); no conversation id ⇒ not in the plan (a session still starting reads its skills fresh); `queued` ⇒ `replace`; the text: CRLF / CR → LF, TAB → space, C0 / DEL / C1 out, trimmed; empty ⇒ `empty`, > 2 000 code points ⇒ `too-long`, and an erroring plan queues nothing. The client counts with it (live = the `active-sessions` rows; stopped = an open window whose session ended — ChatView `_readOnly`; read-only = an open history view); the server delivers with it.
- THE DELIVERY (src/server/stash-handover.js `refreshLive` + `POST /api/sessions/refresh-note`, cookie only — an agent's bearer is 403 `agent_forbidden`, like the hand-over): rows = this server's `activeSessions` (a tmux view skipped; cid = `addressableId`) + the pressing client's `others` (≤ 200; a client can only SKIP — its rows are stopped / read-only whatever it claims). The note takes THE belt (peer-text `toAgentText`, block, max 2 000) and is stashed per live conversation as `{source:'agent', kind:'notification', fromName:'VibeSpace refresh', ref:'refresh-note'}` — a NEW NOTIFICATION_SENDERS name, so the strip reads it as a VibeSpace notice and a wrapper's queue row as VibeSpace's. REPLACED, never doubled: the new entry is stored first, then the earlier one taken out by identity (`drainStash(cid, Set)`, apps-engine's take-back idiom) — a failed write (a ref'd entry throws) keeps the earlier note and is counted `failed`. No `deliverToConversation`, no `authorizeSpend`, no ledger row: test-spend-paths §44 gains nothing. Every client's strip follows through the existing `stash` fact broadcast. A closing server answers 503 `restarting`.
- WHAT THE AGENT READS (the drain, unchanged): `- [ts] VibeSpace (this workspace, not another agent) reports: [VibeSpace refresh] <note>` on its next injection, once, with no "reply to an agent" hint; the strip says 「有 1 条通知在等这个 agent 的下一轮: 一条 VibeSpace 通知」, Details = the note.

### lane boot-probes-unkillable — a probe that cannot be reaped is an ANSWER, never a wait; the restore never asks synchronously (B-92a4 HIGH, owner 2026-10-14 「怎么vibespace挂了好一会」; base rel274 9d0429d09)
- **The incident (production hub journal, 2026-10-14 17:14 PDT):** the new `node` printed `Password auth: ENABLED` and `[safe-fs] worker pool up`, then nothing for 96 s — no listener on :3456 — until a second restart; the next boot took 41 s, later boots 6–30 s. Production's data/ (data/sockets: 14 cw-* sockets) lives on NFS; the box runs ~3 700 processes.
- **The defect:** src/server/tls.js `runChild` resolved ONLY in execFile's callback — its timer merely TERMed the child. A child that cannot die on TERM (a `fuser` in D state on an NFS-backed fd walk; anything ignoring TERM) never fires the callback, so the promise never settles; boot-restore `probeSockets()` awaited those calls (fuser / pgrep per socket, the fd scan, four at a time) and server.js listens in `probeSockets().finally(…)` — one unsettled promise = no listener, for ever. The back door: `restoreSessions()` re-asked with `execFileSync` (sh fd scan 20 s, fuser 2 s, pgrep 2 s, the duplicate retire's pgrep) whatever the probes had not answered — execFileSync's timeout only signals too, so a sync child that cannot die holds the whole loop.
- **runChild answers at its own timer:** TERM at the bound; one turn later (the I/O a held loop runs after its timers) — unless the child has exited or closed its stdout, whose own answer then follows — it settles `{ code: 'TIMEOUT', out: <what it wrote>, err: 'timeout', ms }`; `KILL_AFTER_MS` (1 s) later a child still there gets KILL, its handle is unref'd and its pipes destroyed; a late callback is a no-op. One console line per (bin, basename of its path argument) per process. Measured over four child kinds (lane probe, bound 500 ms): answers in time — old code 0 · new code 0; obeys TERM — TIMEOUT at 502 · TIMEOUT at 503 ms (partial out kept); ignores TERM — **PENDING at 5 s, the child alive** · TIMEOUT at 501 ms, the child KILLed 1 s later; a grandchild holds stdout — **PENDING at 5 s** · TIMEOUT at 1 502 ms. The held-loop answer (700 ms hold over a 200 ms bound, tls-pass-retry's §1) stays the child's own, code 0, on both.
- **probeSockets is capped:** `PROBE_CAP_MS` 25 000 (env `VIBESPACE_PROBE_CAP_MS` for the gates) — a race with the four drains; what has no answer at the cap (a question in flight, one not asked) or ran out both bounds is `out.unanswered` (sockFile → `fuser` / `pgrep` / `not asked` / `fd-scan` for a duplicate the scan did not cover); past the cap no further question is asked (a chain stops at its next rung). `probeFacts(out)` rides the boot trace's restore-probes span: `restore-probes: N unanswered (fuser cw-…, …, +k)`.
- **restoreSessions never asks:** every `execFileSync` path is deleted (the import too). A socket with no answer — or the members of a duplicate set whose liveness has none (local: the fd scan; remote: a member's fuser) — is adopted ALIVE as `probe-pending`: never retired, never dedup-killed, never marked stopped on a non-answer (the keeper law); its card is an ordinary card. A missing tool (ENOENT) is no answer either; a pgrep "nobody" after a fuser timeout stays an answer (a dtach master's command line always names its socket).
- **The re-probe ladder:** after listen, off the loop: 10 s, then 30 / 60 / 120 / 120 s (≤ 5 tries), the same questions through runChild, four at a time; this server's own `dtach -a` attach clients are left out of the pgrep answer. alive ⇒ the mark clears; dead ⇒ `retireDeadSocket` and the adopted session leaves the list; a duplicate set answered ⇒ the same `dedupWebuiSockets`, its loser `retireDuplicate`'d; still unanswered after the fifth ⇒ kept alive, said once. The boot's two retire paths are one function each, called by both (the duplicate retire's pgrep is now a child).
- **Where it is said:** boot-trace `note(text)` (≤ 40 kept) — the restore's probe-pending line and each pass's verdict — answered live by GET /api/boot-trace (`notes`); ⚙ Diagnostics lists a span's note and the notes under the boot holds.
- **Census rows moved:** test-architecture's PID-question allowlist (four sync-rung rows gone, the `ownedP` needle moved, the duplicate retire's pgrep row); test-exit-forensics §6c `src/server/tls.js` 1 → 2 kill calls (TERM + KILL).
- **Gates:** NEW scripts/test-boot-probes.mjs (fast, 32, ~7 s): ① runChild over a TERM-ignoring child (TIMEOUT while it still runs, KILLed after the step, partial out, the held-loop answer, one line per key; CONTROL the old runChild in a scratch copy still PENDING at 5 s), ② the cap over twelve sockets with fake fuser + pgrep that never die (settles at the cap, 4 fuser + 8 not asked, the span note, nothing asked past it; CONTROL a copy without the race still PENDING at cap + 5 s), ③ restoreSessions over a scratch data dir (5 adopted, nothing retired or signalled, the duplicate pair undecided; the re-probe: alive / dead / duplicate loser SIGTERMed by its pgrep answer / still mute; five passes without an answer ⇒ kept, said once), ④ no execFileSync / spawnSync / execSync in boot-restore.js (three planted REDs). scripts/test-boot-loop-hold.mjs ⑤ / ⑥ (heavy): a real boot over the production-shaped stores with TERM-ignoring fake fuser + pgrep listens within cap + 5 s of the probes' start, every session restored probe-pending, none retired, the re-probe settles all alive once they answer; the pre-fix pair (old runChild, no cap) has no listener in 40 s. Measured (lane run, 18/18): the held boot listened 8 005 ms after the probes began (cap 8 000; 8 162 ms after the process started), `restore-probes: 13 unanswered (pgrep cw-…)`, 13/13 reconnected, `re-probe 1/5: 13 alive`; the pre-fix pair had no listener at 40 190 ms, its log ending past `[safe-fs] worker pool up` — the incident's last line. test-restore-liveness 80/80 (once).
- **Not in scope (said):** listening BEFORE the probes with a 正在恢复会话 page — a product decision (a client that connects mid-restore sees an empty sessions list) the owner has not taken. Residual seen on the way: wrapper-files' `resolveWrapperFiles` still walks /proc cmdlines synchronously in restoreSessions when a session's sidecar is missing.

### lane resume-account-door — a Resume whose pinned account cannot serve is said in the resume bar, with two doors (owner 2026-10-15 「无法 resume 一个对话」; base rel275 dd14db0bb)
- **Incident:** a stopped conversation pinned (per-session config `account`) to a subscription whose login was wiped three days earlier (journal `identity-cannot-serve: <name> cannot authorize a request right now (wiped)`). The Resume press ran the create, `resolveForSpawn` threw `subscription not logged in: <name>`, ws-create sent `Account error: <message>` ⇒ a red toast, the window back on the same Resume bar, no door named (Manage agents → log in; Session Properties → another account).
- **The verdict — PURE src/resume-account.js** (imports only login-expiry): `resumeAccountVerdict({ pinned, accounts, loginStates, poolAvailable, defaults })` reads the accounts list rows (`loginState` = login-expiry's reading, the long-lived token folded in), the usage route's `logins` (login-state's account-level state + `since`) and a host's evaluateOnHost verdicts — never a credentials file. Whys: wiped / never-logged-in / expired / oat-expired / missing-account / remote-cannot-ship / pool-no-target, each with the instant it stopped serving when one is known. Doors: `relogin` (via `login`, or `manage` for a pool / a host that cannot take the account) and `switch.to` = pools that can serve (this machine only) → the default account → the rest in the roster's order → the machine's CLI login. A pool serves while ANY member can (the create re-points a dead target); the CLI's own login, a stale default id and a host that has not answered are no claim. `resumeAccountWords` (zh / ja / en, the date) + `candidateLabel`.

## 2.369.275 — 2026-10-15

Hotfix by 主开发 (no lane; one PURE line + the test rows), 50 min after the first fleet instance updated to .274.

- **Incident:** userW's fleet pod booted 2.369.274 at 03:52:40Z; from 03:52:43Z its log showed `[auth] refused a cross-site WebSocket /ws — origin, origin "https://<his instance>" (own -)` (40 in 7 min: 35 /ws + 5 /api/browser/stream; no HTTP refusal). The page loaded, no conversation connected — "my instance is dead". Only he was on .274 (fleet census: 13 × .212, 1 × .227, 1 × .273, 1 × .96); a dead UI cannot self-update, so 主开发 updated his pod in place.
- **Cause:** `ownOriginOf` (src/write-origin.js, .274 pick 1 owner-write-origin) accepted only `http|https` in `X-Forwarded-Proto`. Traefik (the fleet's ingress) forwards a WebSocket upgrade with `X-Forwarded-Proto: wss` (a long-standing Traefik behaviour) ⇒ own '' ⇒ the Origin compare refused the instance's own page. The lane's deployment table (test-auth ③) had the ingress row for HTTP only; the handshake shape through the ingress was never a row. The hub (no proxy, or Caddy / Tailscale serve, which forward https) was never affected.
- **Fix:** `UPGRADE_PROTO = { ws: 'http', wss: 'https' }` applied to the forwarded scheme (one line, PURE); test-auth ③ gains the two ingress-upgrade rows (wss ⇒ https, ws ⇒ http) and the incident-shaped leg (a GET upgrade with Origin = the page, no Sec-Fetch-Site) with the CONTROL = the .274 reading (own '' ⇒ `origin … (own -)`, the exact log shape). 93/0.
- **Lesson (kb-bugfix-invariants):** a reverse proxy's forwarded headers on an UPGRADE are not the HTTP request's — every deployment row of an origin table needs its handshake twin.
