### lane owner-write-origin, commit 2 — every cookie write is same-origin or refused: ONE Fetch-Metadata gate at the auth layer, a census of the routes behind it (B-6b2b, rel249 verify #7; permission class)
- **The finding (rel249 verify #7, refuted for that lane and parked):** owner routes leaned on `SameSite=Lax` alone — a POST with the owner's cookie + `Origin: https://evil.example` + `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` answered 200. Lax keeps the cookie off a cross-SITE POST, but not off a same-SITE one (the fleet's pods share one registrable domain), and an instance nobody signs in to has no cookie to withhold at all: any page could POST to it, or open its `/ws` and drive its terminals (no Origin check existed on any upgrade).
- **The rule — PURE `src/write-origin.js` (imports nothing):** `crossSiteVerdict({method, headers}, own)` judges POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE and every WebSocket handshake (`Upgrade`); GET / HEAD / OPTIONS never. `Authorization: Bearer …` is not the cookie's authority (a browser never attaches one by itself; a cross-site script cannot without a CORS preflight this server never answers). `Sec-Fetch-Site` decides when present (same-origin / none allowed; same-site / cross-site refused) — so a proxy that forwards no proto never causes a false refusal on a modern browser; else `Origin` must equal the request's own origin (`null` never does); neither header = not a browser (curl, node, the CLIs) ⇒ allowed. `ownOriginOf(headers, {encrypted})` = the first `X-Forwarded-Proto` (else https on a TLS socket — the hub's own https — else http) + the first `X-Forwarded-Host` (else `Host`), normalized (case, default port), '' for a host that is no host. Basic auth is NOT exempt (a browser re-sends cached Basic credentials by itself); /dav keeps its own door.
- **ONE gate (src/auth.js):** the middleware lists the DOORS first (callers judged by their own credential: /api/agent/, /hook, the webhook pairing / replies, /dav, /svc, /p/, /otel/, telemetry ingest, the editor bridge, the device install files and dial) — unchanged lines, only moved above the rule; then `originVerdict(req)` refuses `403 {error:'cross-site', origin, own}` + ONE log line (`[auth] refused a cross-site POST /api/x/y — cross-site, origin "…" (own …)`, the route cut at 3 segments, ≤ 5 lines a minute, the rest counted); then the login flow (now with `/api/logout`, which revokes only what it presents) and the cookie. The rule runs with sign-in OFF too. `requestAuthed(req)` carries the same verdict, so every cookie door outside the middleware inherits it: the upgrade dispatcher's `/ws` + `/proxy/`, the desktop and browser streams, private `/svc` mounts (HTTP + upgrade), private `/p` pages.
- **server.js mounts the gate FIRST (no net lines):** `app.use(auth.middleware())` now precedes `auth.registerRoutes(app)` — login / logout / set-password stand behind the rule and set-password behind the cookie (a password change needs the session AND the current password; commit 1's by-state check stays as the route's own wall).
- **ONE own-origin implementation:** the dial-address list (mounts-plugins-wiring), published pages' `originOf`, the mount-push fallback (server.js), the Slack consent's return-address fallback (routes/channels.js — it used `req.protocol` + Host, i.e. http behind the https ingress) and the WebDAV link (`/api/mount-tokens` — the same http-behind-https link) all ask `ownOriginOf`; test-dial-facts' receiver row now declares `req.headers.origin` + ownOriginOf.
- **The agent-routes withdraw check is NOT replaced (deviation from the brief, with its reason):** `POST /api/agent/channels/proposals/:id/withdraw` refuses any BROWSER (cookie or Sec-Fetch-Site, no agent token) by name — the owner's own same-origin tab too (verify r2 LOW 6, pinned by test-channels-engine: `403 not-yours` "reject it from the card"). That is a ROLE rule (who may withdraw), not an origin rule; folding it into the gate would turn the pinned 403 into the token's 401. It stays, commented, and test-auth ⑥ declares it as the one non-origin reader of Sec-Fetch-Site / the Cookie header.
- **The UI:** VibeSpace's own page never meets the refusal (every call is same-origin — the fast tier's chrome suites and fastpar stay green); a page that ever does shows 「这次操作来自别的站点，已拒绝」 / "This action came from another site and was refused": `fetchJson` and `api()` (src/lib/utils.js) turn `{error:'cross-site'}` into the sentence, keeping `code`.
- **Gates — scripts/test-auth.mjs (fast, ~2.4 s; 11 → 88):** ① the hotfix legs re-read in the new order + the pre-fix-order control; ② the verdict table: 1 680 combinations (8 methods incl. a WebSocket handshake × 5 auth forms × 6 Sec-Fetch-Site × 7 Origin) against an oracle + 12 named rows; ③ the deployment table (Tailscale serve, the hub's own https, plain http on the same port, the fleet ingress + a sibling pod, a Host-rewriting ingress, a proxy chain, localhost / 127.0.0.1 / [::1], a relay with no forwarded proto) + "no file composes an origin by hand"; ④ the real middleware per mode (password / Clerk / none): cross-site / same-site / old-browser / null ⇒ 403 + one log line; our page / CLI / Bearer / reads ⇒ through; the nine doors reach their own judge; login / logout / set-password behind it; the log budget; RED = the gate cut; ⑤ real `ws` handshakes through a dispatcher shaped like server.js's: another site's refused with the cookie AND on an instance nobody signs in to, ours and a CLI's open; RED = requestAuthed without the verdict ⇒ a drive-by handshake opens; 9 pins that every upgrade / per-mount / per-page door asks auth.requestAuthed; no file but auth.js reads the Cookie header (the withdraw role check declared); ⑥ THE ROUTE CENSUS (acorn over server.js + src/**, every POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE / `.all` / prefix `.use`): 406 registrations in 40 files ⇒ 330 cookie-write routes refused cross-site by the real gate, 77 in declared doors, 0 outside; server.js mounts nothing between `express()` and the gate (AST walk); ONE express app; no second origin rule (3 declared readers); RED = a planted router before the gate, the pre-fix auth-routes order, the gate cut ⇒ all 330 outside.

### lane layout-layers-p0 — THE LAYER LAW: one layout document, every field owned by ONE layer, every read site through ONE PURE applyForViewport (design q-039 P0, the owner's 根治 ask 2026-10-14; base cfa05e571 = lane phone-sidebar-chrome)
- **Why:** the .264 (a phone's switcher tap restacked every desk), .268 (a phone record replaced a deferred desk record) and .273 (the desk's open sidebar popped the phone's) incidents were one class — "whose field is this?" answered by a per-field special case each time (ARRANGEMENT / VIEWPORT_CHROME lists on the write side, `membershipOnly` and `chromeToApply` on the read side).
- **The table (src/lib/desktop-record.js `LAYERS` + `layerOf`):** workspace (the windows, their identity and content, the tab chain as one unit, the document's desktops / presets / current) · arrangement — the desktop shard (z, box, maximize / minimize / snap + the legacy z / min / snap / snapBounds, the record's grid) · chrome (sidebarOpen, taskbarHeight, toolbarScale, toolbarHeight) · preference (theme, fonts, customGrids) · meta (viewport, updatedAt, seq, evidence). The phone shard (its window on show, its switcher order) stays local.
- **The read half (`applyForViewport(class, record, {source, writer})` → `{membership, arrangement, chrome, preference}`):** a phone takes the membership + a desktop's minimize only (§6b guard 5); a desktop takes a desktop-class record's arrangement + chrome live, a live phone record's membership only (guard 10), the boot's record whole (+ preference), a preset's membership + arrangement. `arrangementFor(layers, entry)` = one entry's subset. layout.js's five asks (the bars before the desktop gate, `_applyRemoteState`, `restoreState`, the boot bar heal in `loadAutoSave`, `loadPreset`) take their subsets BEFORE touching the page; the apply iterates the membership (no arrangement field in it). `membershipOnly`, `chromeToApply` and `TAKEN_WHOLE` are gone (layout-model.js imports nothing again).
- **Three design premises corrected by the code (each the least-change reading):** (1) a phone applied a desk record's whole arrangement before (`membershipOnly` was `phone writer && !isMobile`), and test-mobile-gaps #10 pins a desk's minimize as TRUTH on the phone — so the phone's subset carries the minimize (guard 5), nothing else; (2) the toolbar scale is applied LIVE from every record since 2.252.2 (before the desktop gate — a snap-back fix), not at the boot only — so toolbarScale / toolbarHeight sit in chrome beside taskbarHeight, not in preference; (3) the tab chain's active / layout / split stay in the workspace unit: a phone carries the split it cannot display by APPLYING it (its capture writes the chain it holds; captureForViewport carries top-level keys only) — moving them needs the write half first.
- **Behaviour changes (by the table):** a phone no longer takes a desk's box / z / maximize / snap, sidebar, bars, theme or fonts (its own localStorage theme and scale stand); a desk no longer takes a live phone record's toolbar scale; a loaded preset no longer changes the theme, the fonts or the sidebar.
- **Gates:** test-desktop-record §8 (the five rows; THE CENSUS of the production document's shape — every field in one layer, a planted window / record / chain field RED by name, no dead row; THE CAPTURE CENSUS — acorn over captureWin / captureChrome / captureState, a planted capture field RED; the truth table class × source × writer, 24 cells; key presence, legacy spellings, fail-closed source) + 8 patched-copy controls in §7; test-layout-model ⑧ (applyForViewport × writerClass, the old chromeToApply table) + ⑨ THE READ CENSUS (acorn: every layered read in layout.js off a subset / the page / one declared row, 5 READ_SITES, receivers, membershipOnly gone; 10 planted REDs + the blind-spot control); test-phone-desktop-sync ⑯ (+ D byte-identical across P's reloads / save / re-read; ⑯e the law on a desk + an iPhone, RED copy: every ask spelled 'desktop'). Verbatim pins moved: test-desktop-record §6 ×3, test-window-binding-model ×2, test-layout-model ⑥ ×2; test-record-clear-census drops layout.js's two font localStorage rows (the preset's font apply is gone; appearance-panel.js keeps its own).

### lane layout-layers-p1 — THE LAYER GATE: the server refuses a phone record that moves anything outside the workspace (design q-039 P1, the owner's 「同意了」 2026-10-14 21:28Z; base aaab7ac55 = lane layout-layers-p0 on cfa05e571)
- **Why:** P0 made every READ go by the layer table, but the server still stored whatever a phone sent. A phone tab running an older bundle (or a new client bug) could still write its own boxes, z, maximize, sidebar, bars or theme into the desk's record. No desk took them live (guard 10), but every desk's boot and every reconnect re-read takes the record whole.
- **PURE `layerGate(stamp, held, next)`** (src/lib/desktop-record.js, beside LAYERS): a `phone` stamp may change the workspace only. Every ARRANGEMENT field of each window the held record holds, and every RECORD field outside the workspace (`PHONE_KEEPS` = the grid + chrome + preference, derived from LAYERS), must equal the held record's. The comparison reads values the way the apply does:
  - legacy spellings count as their canonical (z/zIndex, min/isMinimized, snap/isSnapped, snapBounds/preSnapBounds);
  - an absent flag is false and an absent value is null;
  - a toolbar scale within 0.02 of 1 is the null the capture writes;
  - numbers within guard 4's 0.002 are equal.
- **Never judged:** a desktop stamp, no stamp (a pre-.264 sender, a desktop's as before), a first write, a window the held record lacks (phone-born, a move's arrival), and a field no layer names (§8's census reds it first). → `{ok:false, reason:'cross-layer', fields (table order), windows}`.
- **The handler** (src/ws-handler.js layout-sync) asks the gate right after the shrink belt (the belt's verdict and frame come first, unchanged) and before the stamp is stored. A refusal uses the belt's door: `layout-sync-refused {desktopId, reason:'cross-layer', fields, state: <the record kept>, sentAt}`, nothing written, nothing broadcast, a journal line `REFUSED a phone record of desktop "<name>" … it changes <fields> (window <ids>)`, and telemetry `layout-sync-refused` · `cross-layer <fields>`.
- **The write half had to move first:** P0's phone `recordFor` still wrote the page's own theme / fonts / taskbarHeight / toolbar scale (only VIEWPORT_CHROME = sidebarOpen + grid came from the held record), so the gate alone would have refused nearly every current phone save. `recordFor` / `presetState` now carry PHONE_KEEPS from the held record; VIEWPORT_CHROME is retired. The control `pre-p1-write-half` shows a current phone refused without the change.
- **Reconciliation** is the belt's protocol, with no new client branch: `onSyncRefused` makes the view = the record kept + what the page built (captureBuilt ⇒ the held arrangement on a phone), minus the held closes, then `rearmSave`. The re-send carries membership only, so a phone's close lands. A NEW phone is refused only when its held copy is staler than the server's; that case used to write the stale arrangement back, and now converges in one round trip.
- **An old phone tab** (a pre-.274 bundle writes its own theme / bars) is refused until it reloads. The stale-bundle check reloads it at its next reconnect, which a server update always forces.
- **Gates:**
  - test-desktop-record **369/0**:
    - §9 = the gate table on the real document shape (printed, 21 cells) + THE GATE CENSUS (each of the 19 arrangement / chrome / preference fields moved alone ⇒ refused by its own name);
    - §9b = the REAL registerWsHandler on a fake wss (the refusal frame's exact keys, nothing written or broadcast, journal + telemetry; desktop / unstamped / membership / first writes pass; the shrink belt unchanged and asked first);
    - §9c = a phone page (the real DesktopManager + LayoutManager) wired to the real handler. A current phone's close passes at once and keeps the desk's chrome. An OLD bundle's save with a close is refused, the page re-sends on its own, the close lands, and the desk is unchanged on disk;
    - 7 controls: no epsilon, no legacy, desktops judged, the chrome unjudged, new windows judged, the gate removed (a phone write moves a desk window), the P0 write half.
  - test-phone-desktop-sync: ⑥ is now the gate + belt 2 (the scrambled phone record is refused, D never hears it; the held one with a new window passes and D places it by its own default). New ⑰ runs on real pages: an old bundle's save after P's taps is refused, P re-sends membership only, the close lands, and D's disk / live / reload are unchanged. Its RED copy has the gate removed: the old save lands whole and D's reload takes the phone's arrangement.
  - ⑯d: a live phone-stamped record moving the sidebar is now refused by the server (cross-layer sidebarOpen) and D's sidebar stays open.
  - ⑥ and ⑮d forge their phone records from `GET /api/layouts` (the server's cache) instead of data/layouts.json. The file is flushed 500 ms after a write, so a record forged from it carried a stale z / box, and the gate rightly refused it (⑮d red in the first full run, even with ⑮d alone on a fresh server).

### lane ledger-rebuild-offloop — the usage ledger's cache REBUILD runs in the fold worker and swaps in whole (B-748f, the never-block law; memory-residency verify r3 #4; base 39c57b070 rel272, rides .274)
- **Measured:** every rebuild trigger — a shard rewritten (another inode, same size + a new mtime, bytes before its old end changed), shrunk or vanished, a walk that read a stale place, a reload after a repair, the re-attribution — dropped `_evCache`, and the NEXT reader (the pool tick, the estimator, a route) re-parsed the whole ledger inside its own call: 5 s at 497 MB, 69 s at 4.9 GB (verify r3). On a real-shape ledger (scripts/boot-shape.mjs `only: 'ledger'`) the base (git archive 39c57b070) held ONE loop turn for 367–372 ms of main-thread CPU at 60.1 MB and 547–550 ms at 79.1 MB / 164 515 rows (the gate's fixture is 79 MB: 60 MB read under the brief's 400 ms here); now the longest turn through the rebuild is 8–11 ms, the swap 0.000 ms, the reader served the previous cache, the result = the on-loop build.
- **Fix — ONE door, `_rebuildInWorker(why, c)` (src/usage-history.js):** every trigger asks it. A WHOLE cache (`c.whole`, set when a load pass ran to its end) is marked `stale` and KEEPS SERVING — stale but whole, never a blank; `_requestRebuild` runs one job at a time, an ask during it joins (`asks`); a failed job keeps the previous cache, says why in ONE line, and refuses a new try for 60 s doubling to 15 min (an out-of-memory or stuck worker would otherwise respawn on every reader's pass). No whole cache yet (the first load under way) ⇒ dropped, the pass starts over — the first load's own rule (B-1319). The `_loadSteps` rewrite / vanished rules `continue` past that shard, so the other shards' appends keep landing in the old cache.
- **The job:** usage-cold-worker.js op `rebuild` runs `_packWhole` on its own instance — the SAME `_loadSteps` pass + warm()'s settle + the hot rows' ts permutation — and posts the cache as transferable parts: the ColdSlab columns and hash indexes MOVED (cache-bounds `parts()` / `fromParts`), the hot rows / rids / mids v8-serialized in chunks of 2 048 inside ONE buffer. The loop `_stageBuilt`s one chunk per turn (~2 ms) where no reader looks, then `_swapCache` = ONE assignment + `ledgerGen++` (the cost memos) + `checkedAt = 0` (the appends since the worker read come in the next pass). One fold-worker job at a time across fold + rebuild (`_inWorker`); STUCK / the deadline / an exit / out-of-memory are the failure path. The rebuild has its own seams (`rebuildWorkerFile`, `rebuildWorkerHeapMb`): a fold stub knows no `rebuild` — test-cache-bounds §14's out-of-memory stub waited out the 10-min deadline until they were split.
- **Readers:** a sync reader is served the previous cache; `_aggregateWalk` over a `stale` cache awaits the rebuild and folds the new one (a stale cache's places only STALE); a walk's STALE and a vanished shard ask the door (r4's one rebuild per request kept — the r3ladder control still reds). The sync FULL-ROW readers (`aggregate()`, `rows()`: migrations and tests, no server caller) cannot wait for a worker: `_rebuildOnLoop()` is THE DECLARED on-loop rebuild, held to those two by the census.
- **Gates:** NEW test-ledger-rebuild (fast): ① acorn over usage-history.js — every `_evCache` drop / set is the door or one of 5 DECLARED rows, both `_loadSteps` restarts sit after the door, `_rebuildOnLoop` is asked by aggregate + _allRows only; the rest of the product (git ls-files src server.js data/bin) drops nothing and calls no sync full-row reader; 4 planted REDs (the base's rewrite rule, STALE rung, reload; a route asking the on-loop rebuild) + a planted tree RED. ② a rewrite: the reader gets the previous cache, ONE worker, a new generation, byte-identical to the on-loop build (sha256 over the hot window + cold columns + indexes, the cutoff pinned); after the swap an append, a cold id lookup and a route fold work. ③ three asks ⇒ one worker, one swap (control: no join ⇒ more). ④ a reader on every loop turn sees only the old or the new answer (control: staged into the live cache ⇒ half-built answers). ⑤ a failing worker: the cache kept, ONE line, a cold request told `REBUILD` in words, recovery after the wait (controls: no wait ⇒ ≥ 3 workers; a failure that drops the cache). ⑥ a walk over a stale cache folds the rebuilt one, once. ⑦ the 79 MB measurement with a loop meter of main-thread CPU per turn (process.threadCpuUsage between setImmediate turns — never a wall clock): base rule RED ≥ 400 ms vs ≤ 50 ms, swap ≤ 20 ms, no ledger line parsed on the loop, the hash = the on-loop build.

### lane gmail-anchor-churn — a Gmail thread's anchor is a message the vendor will keep; a lost anchor is said once and its re-read bounded (B-3081, a fleet pod 2026-10-12: «the stored anchor <id> of thread … is no longer in the thread — re-reading it» every ~60 s for the SAME thread, a new anchor each time; base rel272 39c57b070, rides .274)
- **The cause (measured, not guessed):** `history()` handed the engine the thread's NEWEST message id as its anchor — after the owner answered from the mail app that is a DRAFT (Gmail lists drafts among a thread's messages) whose id every save replaces, and history.list names each save as a `messagesAdded`. So every poll: the thread named ⇒ one `threads.get` (40 units) ⇒ the stored draft id gone ⇒ the warn + the whole thread re-emitted (the dedup absorbs all but the NEW draft — one more stored draft record per save) ⇒ the next draft id stored as the anchor. The base adapter (39c57b070's src/channels/gmail.js) through the real engine over a fake whose newest message is a draft re-saved each poll: 5 polls = 5 anchor replacements + 5 warns + 5 thread reads + 5 extra draft records.
- **THE ANCHOR RULE (PURE `anchorOf`, src/channels/gmail.js):** a DRAINED thread anchors on its newest message that is not `DRAFT` / `TRASH` (`TRANSIENT_LABELS`; a trashed message is expunged later); only transient messages ⇒ the previous anchor (or none). A page mid-walk still hands back its own last id (the same pass continues there; the engine stores an anchor only on a complete pass). A 12-shape table (draft / sent / trashed / normal × newest / older, unknown labels kept, only-drafts, empty).
- **A draft is no news (PURE `addIsNews`):** the history walk names a thread changed only for an add that is not transient — a draft saved in the mail app reads nothing; the reply, once sent, arrives as its own add (a new id, `SENT`). An add without labels is news, as before.
- **Said once, bounded:** per thread (in memory, ≤ `LOST_MAX` 1000) the vanished id last noted — the SAME id again (a pass that never completed kept it) is silent and not counted; a read that FINDS its stored anchor forgets the thread. `LOST_HOLD_AT` 3 distinct lost anchors within `LOST_WINDOW_MS` (1 h) ⇒ HELD: one line says so, the thread stays in `changed` but no `threads.get` on a mere mention until a delivered (`INBOX`) or sent (`SENT`) add joins it (PURE `addDelivered` lifts the hold in the walk), the hour passes, or a reseed owes it a walk. At most 2 lost-anchor lines + 1 hold line per thread until an anchor sticks.
- **Measured** (test-channels-gmail-shape ㉒, the REAL engine over an injected fake vendor, 61 s polls): the incident 5 polls — yours 1 anchor (the sent reply before the draft), 0 warns, 0 thread reads, 0 new draft records; CONTROL the pre-fix rules (a patched copy; the same harness over 39c57b070's file reads identically) 5 / 5 / 5 + 5 drafts. The rule alone (adds without labels read the thread every poll): anchor held, 0 warns; CONTROL the newest-id rule: 3 replacements then HELD. The walk alone: CONTROL draft-is-news = 5 reads. The bound (a `SCHEDULED`-labelled message replaced every poll, an `INBOX` reply at poll 7): reads `11100010` + 1 after the hour, 3 lines; CONTROL no hold `11111111`; pre-fix 8 reads + 8 warns. The note: the same id twice = 1 line (CONTROL 2).
- **Left as is (pre-existing, B-a085):** drafts in a read thread are still stored as the owner's records; a draft-only thread with no previous anchor stays anchor-less (read each due pass, as an empty thread always was).
- **Gates:** /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/gmail-anchor-churn/report.md.

### lane hook-seen-marks — the hook injection's seen marks survive a restart; the context-folder index is byte-budgeted (B-86d3 ① + ②; base 39c57b070 rel272)
- **The cost:** the per-session "already delivered" marks of the two hook routes (`_groupSeenAt` / `_ctxSig` / `_groupSnap` / `_preambleSeen` / `_toolsIntroSeen` / `_mgrIntroSeen` / `_jobsEventsSeenTs`) were in-memory only (session-schema `persisted: null`), so every VibeSpace restart made the first prompt of each live conversation re-send the preamble, the intros and the FULL context of every Task Group it belongs to (channel-jump verify r8: ≈ 108 KB ≈ 30–40k tokens over 13 sessions).
- **The marks' home (src/seen-marks.js, PURE):** `marksOf(s, version, key)` → the session meta's `seenMarks` {groups' content instants, each folder signature as a 53-bit DIGEST, a LITE diff snapshot per group, the preamble's hash, the build that taught each intro, the jobs cursor}. Written by `persistSeenMarks(s, key)` on the line before each hook route's `res.json` — when the injection is SENT, never while assembling — and only when the JSON differs (no write on a quiet turn). Restored by boot-restore's `sessionFromMeta` (`...restoreMarks(meta.seenMarks, BUILD_VERSION)`, the one meta→session spelling of all three restore paths). A meta without marks restores nothing: that session gets everything once, as before.
- **What a restart re-sends:** an unchanged group (content instant + folder digest) is not repeated — the first prompt names the unchanged groups in ONE `<vibespace-task-unchanged>` line, decided BEFORE the blocks so a re-delivery's cut never takes it; a moved group arrives as its DIFF over the lite snapshot; a folder that changed (digest mismatch — the file-level diff needs the old signature itself) is re-sent whole; the tools / manager intros are taught once again only under a NEW build; the preamble is keyed by its text's hash (the user's words; a build change does not change what the agent saw — a premise correction: the brief grouped it with the build-versioned intros). A SessionStart (resume / compact; the hook does not name its source) still carries the full context and clears the pointer.
- **The lite snapshot:** the store's `snapshotForDiff` carries every backlog item's text — 26–187 KB per real group — but `diffChanges` only ever speaks of items THIS session parked or claimed, so `liteSnap` keeps those (≤ 24 items, ≤ 8 KB; else none and that group is re-sent whole once — a session holding 51 items, measured). Without it (marks only) the busy group moving while down re-sent 121.3 KB of 121.4 (each session's changed group whole, its newest activity line cut by the 9600 B cap). Accepted edge: an item the session claimed AFTER its last delivery is not in its lite snapshot, so the diff names it `Backlog PARKED` instead of `CLAIMED` (the item still surfaces).
- **The index budget (task-groups `_indexRows`, setting `tasks.contextIndexBytes`, default 4096, 0 = the 100-file cap only):** one group's index lists the NEWEST files that fit, in path order, then `- … +M more (older) — \`vibespace-task [--group <id>] show --full\` lists every file`. The rules / tools part above it is byte-identical. `show --full` now really lists every file: `GET /api/agent/task?full=1` answers `contextIndex` (each path through the belt, `contextIndexAnswer` — a new door of test-peer-text-census) and data/bin/vibespace-task prints it.
- **Measured (scripts/test-seen-marks.mjs §5, 13 sessions × 3 groups in the production store's shape — counts and lengths, no contents):** first turn after a restart, nothing changed: 121.4 KB (base) → 3.8 KB; the lanes group moved: 121.4 KB → 10.9 KB. Index: lanes 78 files 6.4 KB → 47 rows + pointer 3.9 KB; personal 78 files 6.4 KB → 48 rows 4.0 KB; school 100 (of 158) files 10.2 KB → 38 rows 4.0 KB — its SessionStart was cut by the cap inside the index (9517 B with the trim pointer), now whole at 9213 B with the shared-folder teaching and the activity log.
- **Census moves:** session-schema rows (`persisted: 'session-meta seenMarks'`, two new in-memory rows `_marksRestored` / `_seenMarksKey`); test-peer-text-census `agentLine(base)` count 6 → 5 (the two index loops are one `_indexRows`), doors `contextIndexAnswer` + `renderUnchangedNote`, four CLI print rows; test-architecture PURE set + `src/seen-marks.js`; the settings reference regenerated.
- **Gates:** /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/hook-seen-marks/report.md.

### lane usage-pivots-on-demand — the Usage window asks for a session / project pivot only once its panel is on screen (B-f95d ②; base 39c57b070 rel272)
- **The cost (measured over a copy of this instance's ledger, 890k rows, read-only):** every load asked `pivot=session:origin,project:origin` beside the dashboard's own crosses (2026-09-10's `ORIGIN_PIVOTS`). All time that is 9.08 MB instead of 5.10 MB (+78 %; gzip 1027 KB vs 502 KB), 30 days 1.31 MB instead of 0.70 MB (+87 %). session×origin alone is 3.69 MB (one row per conversation EVER: 14,513 here) — and the default "Cost overview" draws it in its LAST panel, below the fold; project×origin (0.29 MB) is drawn only by the classic view's project hover.
- **Premise check:** the server already answered a pivot only when asked (`pivot=` → `aggregate({pivots})`, no `pivots` key otherwise) — the waste was the client's unconditional list. The route keeps `pivot=` and gains ONE flag: `only=pivots` answers `{pivots, asOf?, partial?}` alone (never the 5.1 MB of totals / groups the window already holds). No new route.
- **The rule (src/lib/usage-window.js):** a cross over an UNBOUNDED dimension (`unboundedPivot` = session or project on either side) is asked for by the panel that draws it, the first time that panel is ON SCREEN — `pivotHere(key, el)` draws the wait note and arms an IntersectionObserver (the window's scrolling body clips it; a minimized window never intersects); the dashboard's split panels, the classic session table and the classic "By project" section all go through it. A BOUNDED cross a dashboard panel draws (day×account: 203 KB All time) still rides the load — asking for it later would only cost a second fold (the accounts preset). One only=pivots ask at a time; an ask a load overtook (`state.gen`) is dropped (the load carries every held pivot); an asked key the server did not answer is filled empty, so nothing re-asks in a loop; a failed ask says so with Retry and arms nothing.
- **Held, then refreshed with the rest (the 2.309.0 law):** an asked pivot is HELD while a panel of the current view draws it — every later load (Refresh, a range / backend / account / device change, the harvest reload) carries it in the same answer; one nobody draws any more is let go at the end of the paint (so a custom dashboard never piles up past the route's cap of 8).
- **Found by the chrome leg, fixed in the lane:** the pivot's repaint rebuilt `.usage-body`, which threw the window back to the TOP — away from the panel the reader had just scrolled to. A repaint of the SAME view now keeps the body's scrollTop (a view switch still starts at the top); CONTROL bundle without it ⇒ the panel is off screen again.
- **Requests, the real window over the real route on the shaped ledger (base tree → this tree):** first paint 30 d = 1 request, 1,405,927 B (both crosses) → 1 request, 739,940 B (none); the session×origin panel scrolled into view = 0 → 1 request (only=pivots, 388,178 B; it drew from the first answer before); Refresh = 1 → 1 (1,405,927 → 1,128,117 B, the held cross only); All time = 1 → 1 (9,728,758 → 9,446,430 B with the panel held; 5,259,884 B for a window nobody scrolled); the classic "By project" on screen = 0 → 1 (only=pivots project×origin, 282,361 B). The trade: a panel's first look is a second fold on the server (one sample over the real-ledger copy: ~3 s at 30 days, ~6 s All time), shown as the panel's Loading… while the rest of the window is already drawn.
- **Fixture:** scripts/usage-shape-fixture.mjs writes a 40k-row ledger with this instance's DISTINCT counts (14,513 sessions — 11,383 with one row — 940 projects, 968 project×origin, 14,535 session×origin, 234 days, 24 models, 22 accounts, 4 hosts, 3 modes, 2 pools; mulberry32, never an LCG) — what sizes an answer is the distinct keys, not the rows (fixture All time 9.73 → 5.26 MB vs the real 9.08 → 5.10).
- **Gates:** test-usage-pivots (fast, 11: the shape, no pivot ⇒ none, only=pivots = the full answer's cross alone, the byte table, the window census + a planted RED control); test-usage-window-pivots (heavy, chrome, 18: the request census on the server side, the held ask's Loading… photographed on screen, Refresh / All time / classic / let-go legs, CONTROL bundles: the unconditional fetch planted back ⇒ the first paint asks for both; the kept scroll removed ⇒ back to the top; on the base tree 11 red). Pins moved: test-usage-origin (the `ORIGIN_PIVOTS` pin → its absence + the sections' asks; `renderSessions(d, state, { limit: 12, pivotHere })`; the cap check now `max(classic 2, widest preset)`), test-cache-bounds §32 (`FIXTURE_WRITERS` = boot-shape.mjs + usage-shape-fixture.mjs — fixture ledgers into a scratch tree), test-architecture §73 (the comparer still runs on the full answer in the same step; the send is `res.json(onlyPivots ? pivotsOnly(answer) : answer)`).

### lane browser-viewport-answer — an agent's own `set viewport` answers with the page's resulting size; a pin rules it; one trace row (B-6dae ①: the 2026-10-02 coordinator decision — no new read verb — and the 2026-10-14 ruling 「a pin RULES」; base rel272 39c57b070)
- **Premise fixed:** on rel272 an agent's raw `set viewport` BEAT a fixed size (`fitVerdict` letterboxes the agent's choice before `fixed`; launch-picture-size: "the latest explicit act wins"), and every page verb is refused `browser_paused` while the user drives, so neither a pin nor a holder could rule an agent's set. The ruling: a pin rules (the user's Pin size… or the agent's own `vibespace-browser size`); the latest act wins only among unpinned sets. Reason: the pin exists so that what the agent sees is that size.
- **The answer (src/browser-fit.js, PURE):** `agentSetAsked` (the words), `agentSetRuling` (a pin → who + the door), `agentSetAnswer` (ONE line): `viewport: 1280x720 (asked 1280x720)`; `… — the page did not take that size`; `viewport: 1920x1080 — pinned by the user, your 1280x720 did not apply; only the user unpins it (Pin size… → Auto …)`; `… pinned by you (vibespace-browser size) …; vibespace-browser size auto unpins it`; `… — the user drives this browser and their pane rules its size, …`; `viewport: unreadable (<why>) — …` (never a guessed number). The page-size note keeps `fixedBy` (`POST /api/browser/size` = the user, `POST /api/agent/browser/size` = the agent; a pin of unknown author is the user's).
- **The road:** the CLI says `viewportSet` on its /resolve (the verb, or a batch line); the answer carries `viewportRuling` while a pin holds ⇒ the binary never runs (exit 1 `[size_pinned]`; a batch carrying a set is refused whole). After a set that ran, the audit carries `viewport {argv, ran, handle}` ⇒ the bridge's `agentViewport` reads the page (`keeper.viewportFor` → `readViewport`, the tab the relay shows) and answers the line. A /resolve refused `browser_paused` for a set answers it too (`viewport` beside the refusal). `--json`: the line goes to stderr; a pinned set answers ONE JSON object.
- **ONE trace row (`agent-viewport`, kind viewport):** the bridge taps one command/result pair to the recorder's taps only (flat params: asked, gotWidth/gotHeight, ruled, by). The daemon's raw `viewport` mirror stays an untraced observation, so a set is one row; never a fit, never folded. The user's Pin size… keeps its own `viewer-fit` (fixed) row.
- **Gates:** test-browser-takeover ⑪ (PURE shapes; the real bridge over a stub keeper; END TO END the shipped CLI over the in-process routes + the real bridge + the real keeper, the page a fake CDP endpoint the fake browser CLI resizes); test-browser-trace ⑦ (the row census, the agent row through the real recorder, control (e)); test-browser-fit (the note's key pin gains `fixedBy`); test-browser-verbs (OURS unchanged). Report: /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/browser-viewport-answer/report.md.

### lane raw-api-redirect-judge — a Raw API call never follows a redirect the fence has not judged (B-fc37, channel-api verify r1 LOW; PERMISSION class; base 39c57b070 rel272)

The approved card: failed by name, nothing there; 重新提交 ⇒ a new pending card (sensitive `path`), a stale digest files nothing, a second press is refused, Approve on the new card sends the body there once.
- **The census (test-channel-api ⑦ 10, grep-derived):** the 4 files that require the fence (src/channel-api.js, src/server/channel-api.js, src/server/channel-api-cards.js, src/server/channels-wiring.js) hold ONE outbound fetch site — `fetchFn(` in `vendorFetch`, `redirect: 'manual'` after the init spread — and 2 `vendorFetch(` callers; any string-valued `redirect:` other than 'manual' is RED. ### channel-recall-ledger — ONE woken-for ledger door on every delivery road (B-70d2) + the recall note's leg on each road (B-e8e1)
- **The gap (B-70d2, left by channel-recall-engine-leg):** `stashHits` — the FREE next-turn stash, the delivery of a next-turn watch (the agent's own default) — wrote no woken-for row, so a recall of a message it handed told nobody, while a refused wake that was stashed did write one. **Fix:** `noteWoken` became `noteDelivered`, THE LEDGER DOOR: the ONE writer of `en.wokeFor`, called after the hand-over took by every road — `wakeNow` (billed, or refused and stashed), `stashHits` (new: its own `store.index.update` after the stash; a failed write is logged, never fails the delivery), `flushScopeNow` (one row per message on every conversation the digest carried, never a row for the digest). Row shape unchanged (`{vid, cid, at, msgAt, tk}`); .262/.270 rows read as before.
- **Keyed by the message's revision key:** `Rev.wokeKeyOf(vid)` (PURE, src/channel-revisions.js) — the vendor id the by-id recheck asks with, the same for every version, bounded at 512 — writes the row AND is the key `noteRecall` looks it up by (was: `String(vid)` on one side, a 512-cut on the other).
- **The bound is FAIR (`Rev.capWokeRows`):** the free stash makes the default agent watch write rows, so the newest-40 bound would let one chatty next-turn watch push another conversation's wake rows out (constructed: one wake of agent-1, then 45 handed to agent-2 ⇒ agent-1's row gone, its recall silent). Over 40 rows the conversation holding the most loses its oldest first.
- **Legs (scripts/test-channel-revisions.mjs, 36 → 58, in-process ~700 ms):** ⑦d a refused wake, stashed ⇒ row ⇒ ONE note; ⑦e the free stash ⇒ no billed turn, rows for both messages ⇒ ONE note, a re-check and a restart add none (CONTROL: the stash without the door = f57d1cbe9 ⇒ handed, recalled, 0 notes); ⑦f one message, two roads (agent-1 free stash, agent-2 billed wake) ⇒ one row and ONE note each, a recall nobody got ⇒ nothing; ⑦g the chatty watch beside a wake ⇒ 40 rows (1 + 39), the wake still noted (CONTROL: the newest-40 bound ⇒ 0 notes). Leg table: billed wake / scope digest / refused-stashed wake / free stash → 1 note each.
- **⑧ THE LEDGER DOOR CENSUS (acorn, grep-derived):** every `.stashFor(` / `.deliverToConversation(` call in channels-engine.js and every src/server/channel*.js beside it, by its enclosing named function, must call `noteDelivered(` after it — or sit in a NOT_A_ROAD row (`file › function` + why it carries no inbound message: reactionDigest, noteRecall, receiptNow, receiptFor — the census found the raw-API card receipt the brief did not name). RED controls: a planted road, the base free stash, a dead NOT_A_ROAD row, a second `wokeFor` writer. ⑨ PURE: the key, the fair cap (lone row kept, two conversations share 20/20) + the newest-N control.

The recall note still says "the channel message you were woken for" on a next-turn delivery (words unchanged by the brief).

### lane boot-flush-next-turn — a next-turn watch is never billed for what waited while nobody ran (MONEY; found by lane channel-recall-ledger; base f57d1cbe9 rel271)
- **Found (lane channel-recall-ledger's probe, copied):** a GROUP watch on the free next-turn road with no member live parks its hits as pending (`stashHits` → `keepPending`); the next boot's flush (`scheduleBootPending` → `flushPending` → `wakeNow`) delivered them as a BILLED wake, `spendReason: 'channel-message'`. On f57d1cbe9: `nobody live: billed 0 stashed 0 pending 1` → `after a restart with a member live: billed 1 [["member-1","channel-message"]]`. A whole-account next-turn watch stored with `notify: 'digest'` (the owner's grain verbs accept it; only the agent's CLI refuses `digest-is-a-wake`) went the other door: a boot SCOPE digest, billed too.
- **Cause:** a pending row did not say which road parked it; every leftover read as a held wake.
- **Fix (src/server/channels-engine.js, channels-access.js):** the row carries `road` — `keepPending(…, road = 'wake')`, `stashHits` parks with `'next-turn'`, wakeNow's own re-hold writes `'wake'`; `pendingOf` answers `roads`. `pendingRoadOf(watcher, pend)` = `'wake'` only when the watch's mode NOW (`F.deliveryModeOf`) is wake AND some carried row was parked on the wake road (a row with no road = an older version's, read by the current mode — never defaulted to a wake; a mix rides the wake that is billed anyway). `flushPending` sends a next-turn road to `stashPending` → `stashHits(…, {fromPending})` (nobody live ⇒ left pending as it is, never re-parked; taken ⇒ `clearCarried` + notify; the elided count rides the block). `flushScopeNow` skips a conversation whose stored hits are on the next-turn road; `scheduleBootPending` arms a scope digest only for the wake road (a next-turn one gets the conversation's flush ⇒ the stash). No new `stashFor` site: the flush reuses the next-turn door, so .272's ledger-door census (`noteDelivered` after every hand-over) holds after the combine.
- **The recall note's words (lane channel-recall-ledger's finding 2):** `Rev.recallNoteText` says "The channel message delivered to you at … was recalled by its sender" — never "woken for" (it is stashed after every road, the free one included). The note is the agent's line (English, through the belt); no zh / ja rendering exists, and no chrome suite pins it (test-channel-revisions ① moved).
- **Gates:** test-spend-paths §10c (+21 → 345, ~3 s): THE ROAD CENSUS over `engineSource` — every `pendingOf(` reader that STARTS a delivery (flushPending, flushScopeNow, scheduleBootPending) calls `pendingRoadOf(` after it in the same function; wakeNow's carry (a wake started by fresh hits) is the one named row; every `.pending.push(` names a road; both `keepPending` sites in stashHits pass `'next-turn'`; `stashPending` reaches no ladder. Six planted controls RED (each road check cut, a second door billing stored hits, a road-less row, the next-turn door parking on the default road). The probe as 8 legs over the REAL engine (a restart = a new engine over the same data dir; each boot window driven as its timer would): next-turn group ⇒ billed 0 / stashed 1 / pending 0; nobody live at boot ⇒ pending 1 unchanged; an old road-less row on a next-turn watch ⇒ stashed; POSITIVE: a wake watch's old row still wakes (billed 1); switched next-turn→wake and wake→next-turn ⇒ stashed; the whole-account next-turn digest ⇒ the conversation's flush, stashed. Two patched-copy controls BILL (no flush road ⇒ billed 1; no scheduler/scope road ⇒ a scope window, billed 1). On f57d1cbe9 the same file: 12 red (every next-turn leg billed 1). test-channel-revisions 36/0, test-channel-groups 448/0, test-channel-drain 421/0, test-channel-record 111/0, test-channel-agent-watch 81/0; fastpar see the lane report.
- **Found, not fixed (delivery, not money; same on f57d1cbe9):** a hit parked while nobody was live is handed over only by the next BOOT — a member coming live and a second hit stashes the second one alone (probe/live-later.mjs: `stashed 1 pending still 1`). `stashHits` could carry the watcher's next-turn pending the way `wakeNow` carries held hits; best done on top of .272's ledger door (it rewrites the same lines).

### lane stash-pending-live — a hit parked while nobody was live reaches the member when it COMES live, not at the next boot (found by lane boot-flush-next-turn; base a2009e1ce + d035f7cfa)
- **Found (lane boot-flush-next-turn's probe/live-later.mjs, copied):** a next-turn GROUP watch parks a hit while no member runs; a member comes live WITHOUT a restart and a second hit arrives ⇒ `stashed 1, pending still 1` — the second hit is stashed alone and the first waits for the next BOOT. A member that comes live with no new hit never gets it at all before a restart.
- **The carry (src/server/channels-engine.js `stashHits`):** the next hand-over to a live member carries what its watcher parked, the shape `wakeNow` carries held hits in — ONE block, the parked hits first, a fresh hit that is also parked once; the ledger door (`noteDelivered`) takes every carried message; the carried rows are cleared (`clearCarried`) and the panel repainted. Nobody live ⇒ the fresh hits park beside the parked ones (no duplicate); a refused stash (ENOSPC) re-parks only the fresh hits.
- **Read on the conversation's chain:** a fresh next-turn hit whose watcher holds parked hits goes onto the conversation's chain (`billedWake({conv})` — the boot flush and every wake read `pending` there), so two doors never hand one parked row over twice (measured: the boot flush + a fresh hit + the member's turn in one tick ⇒ once). The common hit (nothing parked) stays the synchronous free stash it was. A stop while it waited holds the fresh hits (the boot flush stashes them).
- **The one read:** `parkedNextTurn(en, w, pk)` = `pendingOf` + the ONE road judge `pendingRoadOf` — a wake road's held hits are never carried (they wait for their own wake). The road census (test-spend-paths §10c) now finds four readers that start a delivery from stored hits, each asking the road; a planted control without the carry's road check is RED.
- **A member's own turn (no new hit):** the hook injection points that drain the stash (src/agent-routes.js task-context = SessionStart, prompt-context) did not read the engine's pending at all; each now asks `carryParked(cid)` right before the drain (one line each, `carryParkedFor`). The engine walks `parkedKeys` (the conversations a pending row was written to — keepPending, a wake's re-hold, the boot scan; pruned when empty), and for every watcher that reaches `cid` (a live member of its group, the agent named) with parked next-turn hits queues the carry on that conversation's chain; a group prefers the member whose turn asked (`resolveTarget(…, prefer)`). Never a timer, never a wake: the carry lands in that member's stash within the chain step and rides its NEXT injection — at SessionStart that is the first prompt; codex (no SessionStart) asks at its first prompt and gets it at the second.
- **Gates:** test-spend-paths §10c 345 → 361 (~3.2 s): the probe as a leg (one block `PF`, pending 0 — `F` + pending 1 on d035f7cfa), the member's own turn, two asks in one tick, the boot flush + a hit + a turn in one tick (once), a non-member's turn, a member not live, two members (the asker gets it), a WAKE watch's held hit (never carried), ENOSPC (no duplicate), the REAL hook routes (claude: SessionStart asks, the first prompt carries it once; codex: the next prompt) + RED controls (no hit carry; the turn's carry off the chain ⇒ handed over twice; the routes without the ask ⇒ nothing). test-channel-revisions ⑦h 58 → 63: a carried message (by a hit, by a turn) is on the ledger once ⇒ its recall, ONE note; control without the carry ⇒ no row, no note. Nothing billed on any leg.

### oat-census-acorn — the ONE `.window-` writer's census, on the parser (oat-identity-verify-r4 F-V1 LOW: §9a's regex comment stripper blanked real code in 39 files and its two patterns missed 9 of 10 writer shapes)
- **The census (test-oat-identity §9a):** acorn parses every file `git ls-files` names in src/**, server.js, data/bin (the CLIs the engine ships and runs) and scripts/ (its tooling — not the suites / measure- / dbg- probes, which build fixtures on scratch dirs). A row is what the parser says: a `windowSidecarName` name (a call, an alias, an import, a computed key that folds to it), a string / template / regexp holding `.window-`, a construction that only folds to it (`'.win' + 'dow-'`, a join, a concat, a `const` bound to a constant string); path.join / fs.* / _writeAtomic / rename* over a row (or a variable it feeds, or a name its pattern filters) are the row's shape. Rows group by enclosing named function: window-stamp.js's ONE writer and ONE reader (the reader must not write); six NOT_A_WRITER rows, each with a why, its exact rows and whether it may write (the PURE name + its export, the owner's import, the shipped statusline's mirror of the name, its read, its refusal log `.window-refused.ndjson` — data/bin was outside the old census); every other group is RED by `file › function — shapes`; a dead or changed declaration and a file the parser cannot read are RED; a literal that IS a DOM query's selector argument is counted, not a row (18 today).
- **Today:** 13 rows in 8 functions over 825 files (760 src · server.js · 25 data/bin · 39 scripts) — 1 writer, 1 reader, 0 red, ~1.4 s.

### oat-identity-postcheck (B-3102 (a)(b)) — whose is a long-lived token AFTER the mint: the owner-confirmed anchor + the passive post-check
- **(a) The anchor** (src/server/oat-mint.js `confirm`): when the mint's ONE /usage probe stated a weekly window but proved nothing (no anchor yet / a shared window / matches no row) and the owner picked the row, that window (+ the probe's org, if any) becomes the row's TOKEN anchor — `oatAnchor` on the account record (accounts.setOatAnchor, the one atomic writer), journaled `anchor: owner-confirmed` in the probe log. A row whose established window or earlier anchor DISAGREES keeps it (`anchor: kept`). `panelVerdict` now reads every row's anchor as `{ ...oatAnchors, ...establishedWindows }` (the established `.window-` sidecar outranks), and a LATER probe that disagrees with the row's confirmed anchor is refused as the new reason `anchor_mismatch` (MINT_REASONS; 409 on confirm; the dialog says 「这把 token 的用量窗口和 {name} 已确认的不一致；没有保存…」) — never a silent overwrite; removing the token removes its anchor. The anchor is NOT written into the `.window-` sidecar the reading guard files by (主开发's premise ruling 12:41Z: a wrong pick there would re-file the row's own login readings) — the slot law and `guardReadingTarget` are unchanged.
- **(b) The passive post-check** — PURE `identityPostCheck(row, reading)` (NEW src/oat-identity-model.js, added to test-architecture's PURE set; imports reading-lag + record-lateness only) + ONE orchestrator (NEW src/server/oat-identity.js, built by the pool engine). Every token save ARMS `oatCheck = {state:'pending', since}` on the account record (setOat / moveOat; clearOat drops check + anchor). The real rate_limit_event producer (usage-pool-engine `recordRateLimitEventNow`) hands it the SLOT `readingSlotFor` chose + the record's window, READ-ONLY (one statement, its answer unused, before `guardReadingTarget`). Verdicts: `late` (> LATE_MS 2 min, or produced before the save) · `not-the-token` (the slot was not spending the token — judging reading = an env-token spawn of that row `_billingHow 'oat'` or a member folder holding OUR token file; premise ruling) · `no-evidence` (no weekly window — the 5 h reset names a time) · `no-anchor` (stays armed) · `confirmed` (the weekly phase agrees with the row's identity: its established window stamped at/before the save — a re-stamp from the slot's own API readings after it is not independent — else the oatAnchor; journaled ONCE) · `mismatch` (the phase differs, the org differs when both state one, or with no anchor another row's window). On mismatch: the token KEPT; `oatCheck.state = 'mismatch'` (the roster's red tag + the dialog: 「这枚长期 token 属于另一个账号——重新铸造或改绑」); `accounts._placeable` (the F5 door) refuses NEW placements ONLY where the pool would spend the token (member folder = our token file) — running links untouched, a member serving its own login keeps serving; an all-token pool refuses a new conversation as `oat-identity-mismatch`; ONE For-you notice (origin login, `webui:oat-identity`), resolved by the owner's act through the store's `_oatCheckHook` (a new token saved, the token removed, the token re-bound) — never an item the owner already handled. A confirmed check re-arms when the row's (independent) anchor changes; a mismatch waits for the owner.
- **The re-bind door (改绑)**: `POST /api/accounts/:id/oat/rebind {to}` (human-only, agent bearer 403) → engine `oatRebind` → `accounts.moveOat`: the SEALED blob moves (never decrypted) with its original mint time onto a Claude subscription row holding no live token (409 `target_has_token`), the target armed, the source's check / anchor / notice cleared, the moved token's host key copies swept (the DELETE route's sweep, now `sweepHostTokenCopies`). The token dialog shows the mismatch + a row picker (the matched row preselected via `oatIdentityOtherIds`) + Re-bind; re-mint and Remove token are the existing doors.

### lane cpu-ratio-controls — the last two clock-ratio controls are counts; the work meter reads a regex's backtracking; the wall-clock census reads THE RATIO
- **The reds (B-923c, B-e83c):** test-exit-run judged the secret-shape regexes by hrtime ratios — `best` / `bestRuns` at ×4 input ≤ ×8, `bestOf` at ×8 ≤ ×16, six quadratic controls ≥ ×12 — and read red 1 in 5 beside 32 spinners; test-channel-facts judged its decoder and V1 by CPU-time growth (scripts/cost-ratio.mjs) and its quadratic control read 17 × for 64 × beside a 12-wide fast tier (one red in 387). The base read that red again here, 1 run in 3 at load 5.
- **Why the work meter could not judge them:** a backtracking regex is ONE exec whose steps no charge saw (the meter's own comment: "V8 release builds expose no regexp step counter").
- **The backtrack charge (scripts/work-meter.mjs):** release V8 has no counter but has a LIMIT. `%NewRegExpWithBacktrackLimit(source, flags, n)` returns null from an exec past n backtracks. In a child started with `--allow-natives-syntax --no-regexp-optimization --no-regexp-tier-up`, every exec is charged its backtracks: the exec's twin (`(?:source)|()(?![\s\S])`, always matching unless over the limit) runs from the same lastIndex under limits 2^(k/16) until it answers. The caller gets the original exec's result.
  - `--no-regexp-optimization` is the point: V8's optimized greedy loop backs off a run uncounted (`/x*y/` on `'x' × n`: ×8 optimized at ×8 input, the clock ×68; ×64 unoptimized).
  - Deterministic: two children read the real keyRun leg 603125 → 4825309 steps both times. A process without the three flags is refused by name.
- **The meter's sticky miss:** it was charged the rest of the string. The split slow path's exec per position read every regex split quadratic by construction (`'aB1/' × n` ×16 at ×4 — R8's runWhole leg read red by the count until this). It is charged one place now.
- **test-exit-run:** 26 legs by the count at the old sizes — ×4.00–4.16 at 16 → 64 KiB (bound ×4.4), ×7.08–8.09 at 8 → 64 KiB (bound ×8.8). Its six backtracking copies (j k n q r s) read ×20–62 at 512 B → 4 KiB. At 64 KiB a copy's backtracks pass V8's 2^30 limit (~15 s each), so the controls run small. A control (j) without the charge reads ×8.03 (the meter alone is blind). 549/0, 16 s (15 s on the clock).
- **test-channel-facts:** V1 = `bounded` by the count (64 → 128 KB: 573 → 573 steps; CONTROL a copy whose addressList parses before its cut: ×2.00). The decoder = ×7.40 (the B-word, 2 → 16 KB, past its own 1000-character bound at both sizes) and ×8.00 (the Q-storm). CONTROL a copy whose payload run crosses `?` unbounded and must end at a blank (RFC 2047 read strictly): ×61. 119/0, 1.2 s, off FAST_SERIAL.
- **ci.mjs:** both suites leave CLOCK_JUDGES (test-architecture's census would read them STALE), test-channel-facts leaves FAST_SERIAL, test-exit-run leaves the heavy SERIAL lane (its reason was the clock).
- **The census reads THE RATIO (scripts/wall-clock-census.mjs):** one measurement at two input sizes compared through a factor is RATIO, RED always (no ratchet). The spans' producers are calls of one callee whose arguments differ only in numbers (`bestOf(f, mk, 8192)` / `bestOf(f, mk, 65536, 1)`, each resolved to its nearest declaration). Either spelling (`b / a <= 16`, `b < 16 * a`, a floor `Math.max(0.05, a)`), either polarity, a named ratio, an if-test, and cost-ratio's `growth(…).ratio` (CPU time).
  - A ratio of two DIFFERENT measurements (a fix against its control) stays control, as lane reconnect-storm-band ruled.
  - The fast tier holds 0 RATIO after this lane (5 in test-channel-facts before it).
- **test-ci-gate §2e:** 8 RATIO spellings and 4 look-alikes; a growth ratio planted in test-lazy's text is RED. THE FOURTH AND FIFTH: f57d1cbe9's test-exit-run, planted, reads RATIO on its 4 legs and 6 controls; its test-channel-facts on its 5 growth reads. Today's copies hold none.

### lane browser-probe-transient — one failed probe of the browser CLI's version never decides for ever (B-0b8c; base rel271 f57d1cbe9)
- **The incident:** the .268 boot (00:48:24 PDT) — the boot `--version` probe of the pinned binary (data/browser-tools, NFS) timed out ONCE under boot I/O ⇒ browser-env's toast 「Could not read the installed agent-browser version, so shared profiles stay off」; the 10-min memo had `floor.sharedProfiles` true again by 00:5x. THE LADDER (opt-in `retryMs`, the keeper's facts only): after each miss 5 s → 15 s → 45 s → 2 min → 10 min (`PROBE_RETRY_MS`), stopped by the first answer; a miss after the last rung = `exhausted`. Table (fake clock, 8 s per hung try): attempt 1 boot · miss → 5 s; 2 · miss → 15 s; 3 · miss → 45 s; 4 · miss → 2 min; 5 · miss → 10 min; 6 · miss → exhausted ⇒ 6 tries over 833 s ("14 minutes"). The brief's example said "5 tries over 13 minutes": its five delays are five RETRIES after the boot's miss, so the honest count is 6 and the span includes the 6 × 8 s timeouts.
- **Found + fixed on the way:** a synchronous execFile answer (every fake in the suites) left `inFlight` set to the settled promise for ever (`finish` cleared it inside the Promise executor, then the assignment re-set it) — every later probe past the memo answered the stale value. The flight is now cleared by ITS answer only and never set when the answer came synchronously.

Per-session isolation is on and working; `npm ls -g agent-browser` shows what is installed.» `floorNoticeDetail` (no CLI name — §52b) names the ladder, the wait per try, Check again, the withdrawal.
- **The keeper owns the notice:** its facts carry the ladder; `boot()` asks once (not awaited); `judgeFloor` (on every probe) files ONE For-you item (origin browser, kind notice, action `browser-floor-check`) only when exhausted, adopts an open one after a restart, and resolves it (`done` by agent) on the first non-unknown verdict; `checkFloorNow` = the door; `GET /api/browser/floor` → `{version, floor, lastProbe}`, `POST /api/browser/floor/check`; the digest carries `floor` + `lastProbe`; `shutdown()` stops the rung. browser-env's `checkFloor` no longer toasts (nor latches on) an unknown — its one-shot facts never settle; too-old unchanged. ### lane owner-write-origin, commit 1 — the hotfix: an anonymous POST /api/auth/set-password took a Clerk-only instance (found mid-lane, HIGH, credential; base 39c57b070 rel272, rides .273 alone — 主开发 ruling "split it")
- **Measured (in-process, the real src/auth.js mounted in server.js's order):** server.js:159 `auth.registerRoutes(app)` precedes :160 `app.use(auth.middleware())`, so the auth routes never met the cookie gate (the route's comment claimed "the request already passed the auth middleware"). The handler judged only `passwordEnabled`; on an SSO-only instance (Clerk on, no local password) that branch is skipped, so a cookie-less `POST /api/auth/set-password {newPassword}` answered 200, set the password (`userSet`), revoked EVERY session token and handed the caller a fresh `vs_token` cookie — a pre-auth takeover that also signs every real user out. Password instances were safe (the current password is required); auth-off instances are open by design.
- **Fix — the route judges its own caller, by the instance's state (src/auth.js, one line + the comment made true):** SSO and no password ⇒ a signed-in request only (`requestAuthed`, the session cookie), anonymous ⇒ 401 `unauthorized` before anything is read; a password configured ⇒ the current password (unchanged); neither configured ⇒ open (first-run onboarding: setup-flows.js `#ob-setpw` posts `{newPassword}` alone). No mount order moved; logout and login are untouched.
- **Gates:** new scripts/test-auth.mjs (fast, ~330 ms): ① the mount order READ from server.js; SSO-only — anonymous `{newPassword}` / `{remove:true}` / an unknown-token cookie ⇒ 401 with no password, no cookie, the signed-in session kept; the signed-in owner sets one (200 + a fresh cookie); a password instance — wrong current 401, right current 200 (as before); auth off — the onboarding POST sets the first password (200 + cookie) and the gate stands after it; RED CONTROL (a patched copy without the check) ⇒ the anonymous POST answers 200, sets a password, revokes the owner's session and hands out a cookie. There is no test-onboarding suite in the tree; the onboarding leg is ① here.

### stage-hero-key-race — the shared-hero publish law (rel271's Actions mirror: test-stage-overlap B2 + D red twice on a 2-vCPU runner; green on the hub and on the code-identical candidate runs 38606144701 / 38574037916)
- **The red, measured:** a Stage-born hero is materialized by its creation-tail focus BEFORE its session id lands (a new shell learns its id only in app.syncSessionIdentity — on the hub 18–30 ms after the materialize, the merges are event-driven); `_publishHero` returned on the null key ("publish next time") and the landing's publish (B-8194 `onIdentitySync`) was gated on `_active` and on a null `_heroKey`. The test's leave() ran inside that gap (the hub won it by 1 ms in the measured run); enter() saw a shared record and followed it: `{rec: born0, heroKey: null, hero: born1}` ⇒ born[0] borrowed onto the slot, born[1] parked — the runner's B2 + D. Reproduced on f57d1cbe9 every time with the landing HELD (the lane's probe, HOLD=1: B2 + D red; the released landing published nothing).
- **The publish law (stage-manager.js):** every hero publish is STAMPED `{key, openSpec, by: <this page's id>, seq}`; the page keeps `_heroWitness` = the raw record it last stood on (its own publish; the record a local pick superseded, taken at every `_materializeInner`; the record it followed or cleared). enter() follows the shared hero only when ANOTHER client wrote it since (`shared !== _heroWitness`, or no local hero); `_followRemoteHero` returns on the witnessed record (a reconnect snapshot's notify too). A pick with no key is OWED (`_heroOwed`); `onIdentitySync` — still app.syncSessionIdentity's per-merge hook — pays it on the Stage or off it (no `_active` gate), only while the record is still the witnessed one (a newer pick by another client is never overwritten), and records `ws:<landed key>` (`_scheduleRecord` staged, `_recordActiveWorkspace` off the Stage). A same key + openSpec publish writes nothing. No timers, no polls.
- **Tests:** test-stage-overlap 16 → 27: every "became hero" waits on the mechanism (the shared record names it, ≤ 20 s); F the race shape drawn by a HOLD seam over app.syncSessionIdentity (X published, Y picked unlanded, leave, enter ⇒ Y stays, X parked off the slot; released ⇒ the landing publishes Y); G an id landing after leave() publishes Z and the Stage comes back on Z; W the walk-over with a second page (another client): its pick adopted on enter and live; R the RED control — the pre-fix follow rebuilt into the scratch bundle ⇒ the race shape's B2 + D red. test-stage-visibility 197 → 211: §2 X21 (the stamp, the owed pick, the runner's red, the landing pays, an off-Stage landing + its ws record, the walk-over on enter, a landing never overwrites a newer remote pick + the live follow); §4 controls adopt-any-record (X21 RED) and landing-on-stage-only (the off-Stage leg RED); control (19) follow-blackout judges X20's publish leg only (its re-enter leg holds under the law); §5 the landing hook + the witness wiring.
- **Left:** a follow-REPLAYED hero (attachSession by serverId) carries no backendSessionId until a merge lands it (pre-existing): its `_heroKey` stays null meanwhile — the witness keeps it across a round trip, and its landing re-publishes the same key under this page's stamp, which no follower acts on.

### lane exit-close-cadence — an app's window closes at its exit, not ~3 s later (B-8778; base d419156bd rel269, rides .271)
- **Measured (hub, private env — scratch HOME / XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, no session bus; the real keeper in-process + xpra + GNOME Calculator 50 closed by `wmctrl -c`):** the app exited at +12 ms, the keeper's exit census answered at +32 ms, then the app-session teardown SIGTERMed its one member, `dbus-launch --autolaunch=<machine-id>`, which lived until the keeper's SIGKILL at STOP_GRACE_MS (+3 044 ms); the server/X session went in 10 ms; the commit that broadcasts `exited` landed at +3 171 ms. With a private session bus in the keeper's env: no such member, commit at +159 ms.
- **Cause:** with no DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS (and no `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus`) GLib autolaunches a bus over X11. dbus-launch's babysitter stays in the app's session and catches SIGTERM/SIGHUP (SigCgt 0x4003) by ending its bus and sleeping 3 s: a bare one dies 3 007 ms after a SIGTERM and 3 002 ms after its X server dies. onPartExit committed only after `teardown()`, so every client closed its window ≥ 3 s late. AIDev was green because ci-remote gives each run a private session bus; the hub's env.sh hands the suite the owner's bus, env-priv.sh none.
- **Fix (src/desktop-serve.js onPartExit):** the exit + its census are the verdict: `commit()` right after `windowsLeftAtExit`, then the teardown and its own commit. The in-memory record already read `exited` during the teardown; only the save + broadcast moved. A crash between the two commits leaves an exited record with live leftovers, which boot adoption's reapTerminalLeftovers already reaps (marker census + same-starttime parts). The file-changed signal still waits for the teardown (`fileChanged` is set by noteFileEnd). Not touched: Stop (its answer is its teardown's verdict, so an autolaunched bus still costs a Stop ~3 s), the display-gone branches, STOP_GRACE_MS.
- **Gates:** test-app-launch-once ⑦ (fast, 42 → 48 legs, 2.8 s): a sh app whose session keeps a TERM-proof member ⇒ the exited commit within EXIT_CENSUS_MS of the exit while the member runs, then the teardown reaps it (the keeper's clock moved past the grace), clean; RED CONTROL = an in-memory copy of desktop-serve in the pre-lane order (no commit 400 ms after the exit; the commit only past STOP_GRACE_MS). test-desktop-xpra-window §10 (1)(2) assert the EVENT chain (the app pid gone → the exited broadcast on each page ≤ EXIT_CENSUS_MS → the window gone one task later), never 2 s. On the -close part (.270, hub, env-priv): base 3 152 / 3 144 ms ✗✗; fixed 7–96 ms, 3/3 green at load 11–20. The .270 split deletes the giant: exit-close-cadence/post-merge.patch carries the same §10 hunk to test-desktop-xpra-window-close.mjs.

### Lane passkey-binding-isolated — the passkey hook's report binding moves to an isolated world (B-7c9a, security hygiene; closes the §2.8 residual lane passkey-prewrap-fix left open, on rel270 25cd69aef)
- The residual (docs/design-passkey-store.zh.md §2.8): on a live-document re-arm `Runtime.addBinding` left the new per-arm binding on the page's MAIN-world global for a few round trips until REARM took it; a page polling global names could grab it and call it to forge a passkey trace row / For-you card — no key, no cross-origin (the §2.8 ceiling). MEASURED on a real private Chrome 154 (scratch Xvfb, the real watch driving the real re-arm, passkey-binding-isolated/measure.mjs): a MessageChannel-speed poller saw the `vs`+24-hex binding and landed a forged `start` record in 16/16 live-document re-arms, window ~1.8–2.7 ms (out/measure-base.json).
- The fix: the binding is armed with `Runtime.addBinding({ name, executionContextName: <per-profile world> })`, so it lands only in the hook's ISOLATED WORLD and never on the page's main-world global (CDP-verified: with executionContextName the name is absent from the main world, present in the named world). The main-world hook (`installHook`) no longer holds any binding; it reports by dispatching a per-profile SECRET-named CustomEvent on `document` (dispatch + CustomEvent captured at document start, before any page script). The isolated-world reporter (`installReporter` — a second `addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` with `worldName` for new documents, `createIsolatedWorld` + `evaluate` for a live document on a re-arm) holds the binding and forwards the event's detail to it. `Runtime.bindingCalled` now arrives from the isolated-world context; the watch maps it back to the document's MAIN-world context by `frameId` (where `ctl` lives, so cancel / hold still reach it by identity). REARM hands the main-world `ctl` only the fresh key — the report path is the stable channel, so no binding is handed over (`REARM_FN` simplified; `dropExpression` removed — there is no main-world binding to drop).
- After: the same poller saw nothing and forged nothing in 16/16 re-arms (out/measure-fixed.json). The page can neither enter the isolated world nor guess the 128-bit channel, so it can no longer see the binding name nor forge trace / card events.
- Tests — the lane's heavy `test-browser-passkey-chrome`: S10 (across 8 live-document re-arms the page never saw the binding on its main-world global and never forged a record) GREEN; the control `"the arm bares the binding (no executionContextName)"` reopens the window and the forge lands, RED; a census that every `Runtime.addBinding` in the watch carries `executionContextName`. S0–S9 and the six prior controls unchanged — 36 pass, 1 skip (no real agent-browser 0.38.1 on this box). The PURE `test-browser-passkey` rewires its realm to the isolated-world reporter (one shared `document`, the secret channel) and the re-arm hands only the key — 122/0.
- Ceiling unchanged: no key theft, no cross-origin — Chrome's rpId↔origin check and the authenticator boundary still bound a forged event to trace/card noise.

### lane affected-static-reach — the affected heavy set narrows a BOOT dependency by static reach, and ONE boot sentinel is always in (q-036 P0; the owner: 「都按推荐来吧」; rides 2.369.270 — heads this section only because test-changelog-style caps the newest heading at the next patch)

- **The rule (scripts/reach-model.mjs, PURE; ci.mjs `reachContext` does the reads).** A heavy suite selected ONLY because it boots the product — the boot prefixes, or the graph behind a composition root it names — is selected by a changed product file iff its REACH meets the file's ATTRIBUTION. Every other dependency keeps the old rule: a suite that loads, names or declares the file keeps it, whatever its reach. The old rule stays the upper bound (`reach: false` is it).
  - REACH: the tokens of the suite's own code (its closure's scripts/ files minus the harness ≥ 60 heavy suites load, minus ci.mjs / affected-model / reach-model): `win:` (a registered window type's open action, `createWindow({ type })`, a hyphenated type literal; a bare `type: 'system'` is a transcript record), `api:<seg1>[/<seg2>]`, `mod:` (a src/ or data/bin/ path), `bin:` (a data/bin program by name), `cls:` (a selector's class). A route ≥ 60 booting suites spell is the boot's own probe (`api:home`) and nobody's reach.
  - ATTRIBUTION: a file's own tokens (its path, the windows it registers, every '/api/…' it spells, the classes a client module draws) + ONE HOP (each importer's path, windows, mounted routes). The composition roots add nothing: server.js, the bundle's entry (package.json's `--outfile=public/bundle.js`), and any module importing ≥ 60 src modules (src/lib/app.js 70; the next is 44). A class ≥ 4 client modules draw (`active`, `hidden`, `btn-create`) is nobody's key.
  - WHOLE CLASSES: a HUB (≥ 20 src/lib importers, derived: i18n utils icons window-types channel-chrome agent-meta contributions telemetry-client) and everything a hub imports (i18n-zh/ja), a page asset (public/…) and a shared TABLE affected-model models ⇒ every suite that drives a browser. A client module (src/lib/) never reaches a suite that drives no browser. server.js and a data/bin program a server module's CODE spawns (14: the wrappers, keepers, hooks — a comment naming one spawns nothing; rel269's src/agent-cli-text.js names vibespace-msg in one) keep every boot; an agent CLI no server module spawns (vibespace-msg, -channels, -task …) reaches the suites that run it and the routes it calls.
  - Composition roots are also LEAVES of a suite's own closure: a suite spelling 'server.js' walked the whole server graph as "loads" (152 suites "loaded" src/accounts.js), one pinning app.js's text walked the whole client.
- **The rows.** `reach: [...]` / `'all'` on a row is the author's assertion; undeclared = derived; derived empty = 'all'. The census (`ci.mjs --census`) pins declaration ⊇ the derived non-class tokens, `reach: []` only beside a `reads:` list, and no `reach:` on an always / non-booting row. The derivation left 9 booting suites empty (the design counted 16 with a quote-anchored `/api/` regex): test-helm-render (`[]`, its reads:), test-attach-ack, test-sidebar-scroll, test-desktop-drop, test-run-collapse-fold, test-stage-overlap, test-resume-breaker, test-update-dialog, test-toolbar-resize — each declares the modules / window it drives.
- **`--why`.** One ◇ line per changed product file (its attribution, how many booting suites it reaches alone), then ✓ per selected suite (`boots the product (…) — reach win:foo ∩ src/lib/foo-window.js`, `drives a browser ∩ public/style.css (a page asset …)`, `always (the boot sentinel …)`) and ✗ per suite the reach dropped (`reach {win:doc} ∌ src/lib/foo-window.js {…}`). Without `--why`: the old `·` lines + one line counting the drop.

### lane enter-recorder-keyup — the incident recorder's key ring tells a Shift chord from a Shift tap from a shifted character (inc-mv7mdv6b-emxq, the owner 2026-10-14 「又出现回车提前发送了」; no user line: nothing the user sees changes)
- **What the bundle showed, and what it could not:** the ring's tail was `ime end commit` → 196 ms → `S-Shift` → 554 ms → `Enter` (plain: no S-, no c:1) → the send 1 ms later. Five earlier sends that night had the same shape and their messages end in 「？」 (Shift+/); this one ends in 「）」 (Shift+0). The Enter came 750 ms after the commit with no Shift on it, so EnterGuard did what its rules say. Whether the Shift typed the 「）」 before a separate Enter, or was a Shift+Enter let go early, the ring could not say: a shifted printable key folded into the one-per-3-s "typing" marker, and a modifier's key-up was never recorded, so both read `S-Shift, Enter`.
- **The change (PURE in src/lib/chat-enter-keys.js, wired in src/lib/incident-recorder.js):** `actionKeyWords` writes `SHIFTED_CHAR` `'S-·'` for a character typed with Shift held and no Ctrl/Meta/Alt (c:1 when the IME owned it; never the character; C-/M-/A- chords still name the key, e.g. `C-S-A`). The new `actionKeyUpWords` returns `{ key, up: 1 }` for a Shift / Control / Alt / Meta key-up (null for every other key), and the recorder pushes it from a capture + passive `keyup` listener as `{ t, k: 'key', key, up: 1, el }`. Now the three shapes differ: a character then a send = `S-Shift S-· Shift↑ Enter`, a chord = `S-Shift S-Enter`, a tap then a send = `S-Shift Shift↑ Enter`; the up's time gives how long the Shift was held and how long before the Enter it was let go.
- **Not touched:** EnterGuard and its 50 ms window, the typing marker, the ime markers, the ws ring, CAP.action 500. The cost: a capital is three ring rows (down, S-·, up) where it was at most one burst marker. inc-mv7mdv6b-emxq's 500 rows covered 47.5 min with 31 modifier key-downs, so the window shrinks by roughly a tenth on that kind of typing.

### the judge's one-shot body (lane judge-one-shot-body — rule-learning-fix-r2's «Left» item 1)
- **What:** the Decision API judge (`judge()` in src/server/decision-engine.js) sent its decisions request with a STRING body. Node's fetch re-sends a body that has a source on an HTTP 421 (Misdirected Request) over a new connection — empty (`content-length: 0`) but with every header, the Authorization header included: a second keyed request no census saw (rule-learning-fix-r2's probe: 2 requests, the judge answered `backoff`). The body is now `Object.freeze`d where it is built, serialized ONCE into bytes and sent as a ONE-SHOT stream with its own `content-length` and `duplex: 'half'` (`redirect: 'error'` kept) ⇒ 1 request, `vendor-error` (status 421, costs 0).
- **ONE implementation:** PURE `oneShotBody(bytes)` in src/decision-model.js — a stream that hands the bytes over once and has no source; anything but a Uint8Array throws a TypeError (nothing is sent). The text client and the judge both send `body: M.oneShotBody(bytes)`; the client's inline stream is gone.
- **Measured (Node 24.12, loopback):** a string, a Uint8Array, a Buffer and a Blob body are each re-sent empty + keyed on a 421 (once, then `UND_ERR_REQ_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH`); a stream body = 1 request (without the length header it goes chunked — hence the explicit length). Followed redirects: a one-shot body cannot follow a 301 / 302 / 307 / 308 (the fetch fails, nothing reaches the other origin), but a 303 is still followed as a GET without the body — `redirect: 'error'` stays load-bearing.
- **The census (test-vendor-whitelist):** both ALLOW rows carry `oneShot: true`; for each, by token over the comment-stripped code: the ONE request primitive's call carries `body: M.oneShotBody(bytes), duplex: 'half',` and no other body key, `'content-length': String(bytes.length)` and `redirect: 'error'`; `const body = Object.freeze(`; ONE `const bytes = new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(body));` (`JSON.stringify(body)` once, `bytes` ×3, `body` ×2); no stream of the row's own — the helper is the only server-tier `new ReadableStream`, and a behaviour read shows it hands the bytes over once. CONTROLS 16/16 RED (8 plants × 2 rows: a string / bytes / a Buffer / a Blob body, a stream of its own, the length dropped, redirects followed, a second body key).
- **The wire, fast (test-decision-model ⑳):** the REAL judge over a loopback fake — 421 once / twice, a 303, a 307, a reset, a hang (250 ms) ⇒ each ONE request, the body byte-identical to the baseline with its own content-length (never chunked), no empty request carrying the key, the named why. ### lane pool-oat-materialize — a pooled member keeps its long-lived token: the oat is materialized as a CLI-shaped credentials file in the member's dir (design q-035 A, measured GO on CLI 2.1.296; B-b928; credential class, verify-gated)
- **Why:** a pooled session's CLI reads its member's `.credentials.json` through the per-session symlink, so a token living only in accounts.json (`oatEnc`) could never serve it — the pool escaped every oat-only member (「池用不了它的长期 token」, lane login-expiry-oat). The measurement (scripts/fixtures/oat-in-file.json — 主开发's loopback-only rung, fake tokens) found 2.1.296 spends a refresh-token-less file like a login (oat-file / oat-file-401 / oat-file-switch PASS), refuses one without scopes / subscriptionType ("Not logged in", oat-file-scopes) and defaults the model to sonnet on the env road (oat-env).
