### lane display-secret-fd — the app-secrets key never rides a display's bus environment: it is handed over once, in a file the service unlinks (B-6c6d, oat-verify F5 LOW, credential class)

- **The finding.** `secretServicePlan` laid `VS_APP_SECRETS_KEY` (the per-display key that unlocks the app's keyring) over `portalPlan`'s `env` in desktop-serve's bring-up (~931). That env is the environment dbus-daemon is STARTED with, and every service the bus activates inherits it. **MEASURED on the base tree (d5f352538, a real private bus + the libsecret probe + one Introspect of the portal and one org.a11y.Bus.GetAddress — /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/display-secret-fd/environ-census.mjs): the key sat in `/proc/<pid>/environ` of SEVEN live processes** — dbus-daemon, the secret service, xdg-desktop-portal, xdg-permission-store, xdg-document-portal, at-spi-bus-launcher and the a11y bus's own dbus-daemon — for the display's lifetime, readable by anything of the same uid (an agent's `cat /proc/*/environ`). **After: zero**, same seven-process session.
- **Why not a pipe.** The brief's first choice was an inherited fd. MEASURED (dbus 1.16.2, a `<type>session</type>` bus with the product's own bus.conf): a bus-activated service inherits the daemon's ENVIRONMENT (`VS_APP_SECRETS_KEY=…` arrived) but NOT its file descriptors — dbus's spawn closes every fd above stderr before exec, so the daemon's fd 3 (a pipe we held open) was gone in the child (`/proc/self/fd` = 0,1,2 only; a read of fd 3 is EBADF). A pipe cannot reach a service the BUS starts; it can and does reach the service's own child.
- **The handoff.** PURE `secretServicePlan` now answers `{ secrets, store, keyFile, files: [service file, key file] }` and NOTHING for an env (the `env` field is gone). The key file is `<app dir>/portal/run/secrets.key` — under the plan's private `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, written 0600 in a 0700 dir with the rest of `plan.files`, before dbus-daemon starts — and its path is the service's 5th Exec argument. `src/secret-service.py` reads it with `O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW` and UNLINKS it before it owns `org.freedesktop.secrets`; no key file ⇒ `[secrets] no per-display key: the key file is gone (secrets.key ENOENT) — it is handed over once, when the display starts` and exit 1 (libsecret is answered with Spawn.ChildExited in ms, never left hanging), as does an Exec line from an older tree (fewer than 5 argv). The sealer (`src/app-secrets-seal.js`) now takes the key off an inherited PIPE — `VS_APP_SECRETS_FD` is the fd NUMBER, `pass_fds` on the service's side — so even that short-lived child's environ carries no key. desktop-serve pushes `secrets.files` and assigns nothing into `plan.env`; its teardown unlinks the key file (an app that never asked for its keyring leaves it behind, and it must never sit at rest beside the sealed store).
- **The census (test-app-display-secrets ①c, printed).** `VS_APP_SECRETS_KEY` appears NOWHERE in src/ any more (RED control: the .267 line put back in a copy of desktop-apps.js ⇒ the census names it); every name of `plan.env` / `plan.appEnv` / the secrets plan is judged by shape — a secret-named key (KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASS|CRED) is allowed only when its value is an fd number (RED control: the key planted back over plan.env ⇒ `VS_APP_SECRETS_KEY`); and desktop-serve's bring-up is pinned to `plan.files.push(...secrets.files)` with no `Object.assign(plan.env, secrets…)`.
- **Gates.** test-app-display-secrets (fast) **49/0, 4.4 s** (was 40/0, 2.5 s): ①c the census above; ③ on the real bus — the ENVIRON CENSUS over `ps -s <bus pid>` (no process of the session carries the key or a secret-named env), the key file gone once the service ran, the RED control that re-lays the key over plan.env (the census then names dbus-daemon AND the service), and the no-key-file bus refusing by name in ≤ 3 s; the .267 legs (store / lookup / search / delete / Unlock / restart / Forget all / no secret in a log / the logging mutant) unchanged. test-app-display-secrets-chrome (heavy, the lane's one) **10/0, 9 s**: ①b scans EVERY readable `/proc/<pid>/environ` on the box (691 read) while a real Chrome 154 runs on the private bus with nine processes in the bus's session — only a planted control (`sleep` with the key in its env, the scan's positive control) holds it. test-app-display-session-census 25/0, test-architecture 690/0 (§86 row `src/app-secrets-seal.js` 2 → 3: the key read off the pipe fd), the whole fast tier 378/378.

### lane mediation-chrome-hub-red — test-browser-mediation-chrome r4 judges each refusal's code, not stderr's first line; ④ r3 M1 CONTROL reads Chrome's environ by the shape (B-a23c; no user line: a gate fix)

### lane browser-windows-rung-race — B-81c6: test-browser-windows ⑦ c31 raced in its HARNESS (two 40 ms sleeps), never in the keeper's plan read; the row is ordered by events now and the keeper journals its rung-2 lock queue (no user line: a test harness + one journal line)
- **The red (mirror-267 heavy 1/4, twice in a row; also twice on 2026-10-13):** row c31 got `aRung2Ran: true` beside A's correct `window_busy / user_driving`. c31 slept 40 ms for "B is inside its rung 2, holding the browser's lock", snapshotted the GLOBAL rung-2 count, started A, slept 40 ms for "A waits for the lock", then began the takeover.
- **Reproduced (the runner's shape: everything on cpus 0-3 with 8 CPU spinners, 2 node spawn loops and an fsync/tar IO loop):** base d5f352538 (a pristine `git archive` tree) red 10/10 (9 × the CI row, 1 × a third wrong ordering: B so slow that its own plan read came after the takeover began, so B refused itself); 4 spinners alone 0/2; quiet 0/1. A traced copy (each probe, rung-2 entry, lock queueing, plan read, takeover and release, timestamped) names the orderings. PASS: B enters rung 2 at ~15 ms, before the 40 ms snapshot; A probes, queues at the lock, the takeover begins, B is released, A's plan read refuses. FAIL ① (the CI row; reproduced with B's first probe held +30 ms): B's way to rung 2 outlasts the snapshot, so B's OWN rung 2 is counted as A's. FAIL ② (+60 ms): A overtakes B to the lock and reads its plan before the takeover began (A runs, B is refused). The keeper's verdict was right in all three: its plan read is synchronous with the lock grant (`await prev` → `fn()` → `planNow()` → the act, no await between), and a takeover or a live view registers synchronously (`inputs` / `watchers`).
- **Fix (the harness):** c31 waits on EVENTS: B's entry into rung 2 (the model's `rung2Entered`, called as B's rung 2 takes the hold) and A's place in the lock queue (the keeper's journal line, written before its wait). A rung 2 is A's only by A's own anchor (`rung2Log[].anchor`). New row c31v: a live view that opens during the lock wait ⇒ A's rung 2 runs without the cycle (⑦ rows 5 → 6).
- **Keeper (src/server/browser-keeper.js):** `rung2Serialized(profileId, fn, onWait)`: the map holds the queue's TAIL while any rung 2 of the browser is queued or in flight (r3 stored `prev.then(…)` but compared `cur`, so an entry never left the map); `onWait` runs synchronously when the lock is HELD, and the ladder journals `[browser] <holder> on <profile>: rung 2 waits for the browser's lock — another holder's rung 2 is in flight; the plan is read when the lock is granted`.
- **Controls:** (q) r5's slept harness with B's way to rung 2 +60 ms calls the PRODUCT keeper red, deterministically (B's rung 2 counted as A's, or A overtaking B); the event-ordered harness under the same delay is green. (r) A keeper copy that reads the plan after rung 1 but BEFORE the lock wait ⇒ c31 (A's rung 2 runs under the user's hands) and c31v (the cycle under the live view) red. (s) A keeper copy with r3's compare (`cur`) keeps the map entry, so a holder ALONE at the lock is journaled as waiting behind nobody (the rows' `bQueued: false` goes red).
- **Gates:** test-browser-windows 132/0 (127 before: + controls q, r, s and the setups of r and s); after the fix green 10/10 (each run the whole suite 132/0, on cpus 4-7 with the same noise beside the base's runs) under the same shape; fast tier 378/378 (every fast row of ci.mjs; the docs-reading suites again on the final text).

### lane oat-row-one-word — a row on its long-lived token says 「仅长期 token」 once (owner 2026-10-14, two screenshots: "这些提示有些多余，直接说仅长期 token 就行了" / "这里为啥没有仅长期 token 的提示了")
- **Cause:** an oat-only row said the token three ways — the ident's green 「仅长期 token」, the amber chip's sentence 「登录已过期 · 会话用长期 token；用量刷新需重新登录」 and the healthy green tag 「· 长期 token」. Row B (the login dir still there, its login expired, the token valid) lost the word: an expired login still parses `loggedIn`, so the ident chain took the e-mail · plan branch and the token-only fact lived only inside the chip's long sentence.
- **Fix (src/lib/manage-agents.js):** the oat-only chip's label is the word, `t('long-lived token only')` (last day: NEW key `long-lived token only · ends in {left}`, zh 「仅长期 token · {left} 后到期」, ja); the whole sentence stays in its title; colour, clock icon and the re-login door unchanged. `oatOnlyChipShown(a, { local })` (= the chip's own oat-only branch, local roster only) folds the rest: `subIdentHtml` (the roster's subscription ident, extracted) shows the e-mail or nothing for a token row under that chip (never 「not logged in」; loggedIn + oat-only keeps e-mail · plan — the chip carries the state); `oatTagHtml` (extracted) drops only the healthy green tag beside it — the amber ≤ 30 d countdown and the red expired tag stay. A host section (no chip there) and a token row with no login file at all (state unknown, no chip) keep the ident word as before. The two old chip-sentence keys (zh + ja) are deleted (no reader left; src/login-expiry.js's English SPEAK bucket label is its own literal).
- **Gates:** test-login-expiry §10 (329, real Chrome over the real manage-agents.js bundle + style.css): the chip's one word en/zh + colour + title + door; whole rows composed like the roster row — row A (no e-mail ⇒ line 2 empty, the word once, no green tag, never "not logged in"), row A with an e-mail, row B (e-mail · max, the chip, no green tag), the amber countdown kept, the host section and the chipless token row unchanged, zh rows; WIRING pin (the roster row calls the three helpers with `{ local: !selectedHost }` and holds no copy of the words) + a census of the word's doors (2 + the last-day key); RED control = this file with the fold off and the base sentence back — row A draws three hints, row B none of the word. i18n-check green.

### lane cli-one-text-arg — an agent CLI never silently drops words: a free-text command takes ONE text, refuses a stray word by name, takes long text from a file or stdin, and echoes the route's count

- **The incident (the owner, 2026-10-14).** An agent ran `vibespace-channels reply lark/<conv> "…若对照"有源码权限的人 vs 人员名单"会对不上。…" --to <id>`. The inner `"` closed the shell string, so the CLI got three words. `reply` sent `args[2]` and DROPPED the rest: the person read a message cut mid-sentence and nothing told the agent. The same shape was in `vibespace-msg send` (`args[2]`, the rest ignored) and in `vibespace-channels compose`, which took the LAST free word, so it sent only the tail. `vibespace-ask` (the default form) and `vibespace-task progress` / `backlog-add` JOINED every word, which lost the quotes and hid the mistake.
- **THE rule, once: PURE `src/agent-cli-text.js`** (imports nothing; the CLIs hand it `fs` as `io`). `takeDoors` (`--text "…"`, `--text -`, `--text-file <path>`, `--detail-file <path>`; `-` = stdin; one stdin per command), `textOf` (the argument OR its door, never both), `positionals` (the channels CLI finds flags by name: per-verb `valued` / `optional` / `bare` lists in `CH_TEXT_SPEC`), `strayRefusal` (the brief's sentence: count, first stray word quoted, cause, both doors; a stray FLAG or a word after an unknown flag is named as such), `oneText` (door error → stray → text), `sentLine` (`sent: N characters` from the route's `chars`; fewer than given ⇒ `the last K were CUT`; no `chars` ⇒ the CLI's own count), `chars` (code points). A file's text is its UTF-8 with ONE trailing newline trimmed. Stdin that is a char device (a terminal, `/dev/null`) is refused, never waited on.
- **How the CLIs reach it.** A checkout: `require('../../src/agent-cli-text.js')` (when `../../server.js` exists). A host: `require('./agent-cli-text.js')`, the boot-time copy (`createCliTextCopy` in agent-tool-generators, gitignored, `HostManager.AGENT_TOOLS` — §52a pins it). Both names are LITERAL, because test-peer-text-census refuses a computed require and walks a required module: the rule joined `PRINT_CLIS` (it prints nothing; every CLI print of its sentences is a row). A free-text verb REFUSES when the rule is missing (exit 2, it could not tell a stray word); other verbs work. `tty` is a stream builtin the census bans, so the stdin check is `fs.fstatSync(0).isCharacterDevice()`.
- **Per command (the census in test-cli-one-text, grep-derived from the four usage tables: 50 commands, each a verdict).** one-text (a stray word ⇒ exit 2, nothing sent; doors; echo): msg send, msg dispatch (`--file` kept), channels reply / compose / request, ask (the question; `--detail-file`), task progress / backlog-add (`--detail-file`). guard (a stray word ⇒ exit 2; no text of its own): channels react / unreact / withdraw (a `--why` that split), channels search (never a narrower search), task group-create / group-update (`--title` / `--objective`). text-flag: task backlog-edit (`--text` / `--text -` / `--text-file`; the ref stays a lookup). lookup (joined on purpose; a miss is named): ask resolve / show / clear, task progress-redact / backlog / backlog-claim / -unclaim / -done / -drop. members: msg group create / invite (a stray word is a member the server refuses). name: msg group rename (joined; the answer echoes it whole). no-text: the rest (`channels watch` rules are parsed by the server, which refuses an unexpected word).
- **The echo is the route's count.** `chars` (and `detailChars`) is the count of what the route KEPT: `msgSendAnswer` counts the stored message (so `dispatchAnswer` does too), `task-progress` the kept note (`addProgress` slices a note at 2000 and a detail at 6000 WITHOUT saying so — now the echo shows it), `task-backlog` the stored item, `user-todo` the stored question (cut at 500). Channels reply / compose (+ `--caller`) / request count the text they got.
- **Traps met.** (1) test-record-clear-census's alias pass scans at most 6000 characters of a block (`iSpan`). In the msg send handler, `deliverToConversation` sits right at that limit on the base, so ANY characters added above it pushed the call out of scan and the `req.body.text` row went dead. The count moved into `msgSendAnswer` (the handler is byte-identical above the call). (2) A call of the `chanAnswer` wrapper is a sentence sink, so `b.text` cannot sit in its arguments: the routes set `r.chars` before the call. (3) test-backlog-nudge finds the backlog-edit branch by the first `cmd === 'backlog-edit'` text, so the edit door is read inside that branch.
- **Gates.** test-cli-one-text (NEW, fast) 111/0: PURE rule; the census (+ a planted usage line caught); every one-text command — the incident's three pieces ⇒ exit 2, the sentence, ZERO calls on a counting fake route; the same words as ONE argument ⇒ sent whole + `sent: N characters`; `--text-file` / `--text -` byte for byte (quotes, newline, CJK, `$( )`, backticks, tab, emoji); `--detail-file`; given twice / missing file / nothing piped ⇒ refused; the cut echo; CONTROLS: msg send and channels reply without the scan send the FIRST piece and drop the rest, exit 0 (the incident), and ask's pre-fix join glues the pieces — each RED under the same judge; a host layout reads the copy beside it and REFUSES without it. Suites moved: test-peer-text-census (rows + the module walked + 2 print helpers), test-msg-cli-groups (dependency-free but for the rule), test-foryou-links (the loose question is refused), test-backlog-no-truncation (controls carry the rule beside them), mount-reader-census (agent-tool-generators 21 → 23), test-architecture (PURE row, §52a).
- **Docs.** The usage block of each CLI and `vibespace-docs msg|channels|ask|task` say: long or quoted text: `--text-file <path>` or `--text -` (stdin); the CLI refuses stray words. kb-api, kb-file-structure.

### lane peer-registry-identity — a conversation's CLI is found by its registration's PROCESS IDENTITY, never by a pid number (owner 2026-10-14 04:58Z: 「现在交给它」 → 「没有交出去 —— 联系不上这个 agent」 on 企业助手)
- **Cause (measured on the hub, read-only):** the host hard-froze at 10:26 and rebooted; the CLIs never cleaned ~/.claude/sessions, so 11 of 19 conversations held TWO registrations (30 records). Pids restart low after a reboot: 4 pre-freeze pids (15585 / 15598 / 15609 / 15622) now named kernel threads or another user's processes. `findPeer` took the FIRST record in readdir order (libuv sorts: "15622.json" < "17654.json") whose `kill(pid, 0)` held — EPERM counted alive — so the stale record won, its socket /run/user/1000/cc-socks/15622.sock did not exist, the post failed ENOENT and the ladder logged "the socket is not served: the conversation is not running"; 34 posts stashed (企业助手, 米哈游监控, Proxmox和Docker管理, Kaixu 学习). The other 7 twins' stale pids stayed free (dead ⇒ skipped).
- **Fix (src/peer-messaging.js, SHARED — the agentd bundle carries it):** PURE `registryIdentityOk(rec, probe)` — live iff the pid's /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 equals the record's `procStart` (the CLI writes it as a string; EPERM alone is never liveness there; no procStart / no /proc ⇒ pid-only, said in `identity`) AND `messagingSocketPath` is an existing socket (statSync isSocket; a Windows named pipe `\\.\pipe\…` — the CLI's own form there, matched by its own regex — has no inode to stat and is left to the post, else agentd on a Windows machine would find no peer). `lookupPeer` judges EVERY record of the session id, the newest passing `startedAt` wins, failing records are skipped (never cleaned); it answers `{peer, candidates, stale, why}` with `why` = "candidates: n, stale: m (pid-gone: g, pid-reused: k, socket-absent: j)". `findPeer` = its `peer` (all callers + agentd unchanged). The starttime comes from src/proc-identity.js `starttimeOf` (the pid+starttime law of Background Work).
- **The ladder's words (src/server/conversation-deliver.js rung 1):** stale registrations only ⇒ `[deliver] <cid>: no live inbox on this machine — stale registration(s) only — pid reused / socket absent (<why>)`; a final post refusal re-judges the registry — "the socket is not served: the conversation is not running" only when no record passes now, the stale words when only stale ones are left, and "the socket refused the post, though a registration still passes its identity check (pid, identity; why)" otherwise. A stub `peerMsg` with findPeer alone keeps working (no lookupPeer ⇒ the plain lookup).
- **Gates:** test-peer-messaging §4 (32: PURE verdicts over an injected probe — pid+start, pid-reused under EPERM, pid-gone, pid-only without procStart / without /proc, no socket path, a Windows named pipe never statted; the hub's shape with the stale record sorting first ⇒ the live record + its key + why `candidates: 2, stale: 1 (pid-reused: 1, socket-absent: 1)` + a real post; the mirror; two live records ⇒ newest `startedAt` either order; single stale ⇒ null + why; RED control = the pid-only first-record rule in a patched copy picks the stale record and its post fails ENOENT), test-peer-delivery (87: the ladder over the REAL lookup — the hub's shape delivers to the live socket, stale-only logs the new line and never "not running", no records ⇒ rung 1 silent, the three re-judged refusal verdicts, RED control through the ladder). test-notify-retry (307) and test-park-step (36) rigs now SERVE their stand-in sockets (a registration counts only while its socket exists). mount-reader-census: peer-messaging 3 → 4 (the socket stat). Fast suites reading the two files 20/20; the whole fast tier 379/0; test-architecture 690/0. Read-only proof over the hub's real registry (the .json records only, never a .key): the base rule picked the stale record for 4/11 twins, the new rule picks the live one for 11/11.

### lane decision-vendor-hygiene — a 402 / 400 stops the Decision API row like a 401; the owner's words in the questions pass the ONE scrub (B-2979 + B-d375)
- **Cause (B-2979, money):** `judge()` stopped the row only on 401 / 403 (`reconnect`: no call until a new key) and backed off on 429 / 5xx / 0. A 402 (the plan does not allow the model) and a 400 (the model refused the request shape — measured 2026-10-12: two models answered 400 to every call) fell to the `vendor-error` branch — unbilled, but one call and one journal line per record, every pass.
- **Fix (PURE, src/decision-model.js):** `rowStopOf(status)` → `reconnect` (401 / 403) | `plan` (402) | `shape` (400) | null, `ROW_STOPS`; WHY + `budgetVerdict({plan, shape})` after a refused key, before the walls and the money. **Engine (src/server/decision-engine.js):** ONE stop record `{sig, why, status, at}` — sig = sha256 of provider + model + key, so a new key, provider or model lifts it (the owner's Test still calls; its 200 lifts it too); `status().stop` {why, status, at} (`reconnect` kept for the card), the plugin row's `why`; `plan` / `shape` say ONE server notice per stop (`decision-stop:<why>:<sig12>`, i18n key = the chip title's sentence; said again at the next refusal only when no client received it); journal outcome `plan` / `shape`. The attention scan's STOP list takes the three row stops (its queue empties instead of re-asking a stopped row). **Client:** plugins-ui `DECISION_STOP_WORDS` (reconnect | plan | shape → the chip word, warn, + the title's sentence), zh + ja.
- **Measured (test-decision-engine I, the fake vendor, a pass of 5 records):** 402 — 5 calls before (the old classification, stubbed) → 1 after; 400 — 5 → 1; the same key + model with the vendor answering again: 0 calls, no second notice; a new model / a new key / the owner's Test: calls resume (5 of 5); a 422 stays one call a record. The attention scan runs ≤ 3 calls in flight, so up to 3 may land before the first answer stops the row.
- **Cause (B-d375, privacy, LOW):** a rule's condition, a routing rule's option descriptions and a webhook rule's condition ride `questions[]` (channel-filter `decisionQuestion` — the channels engine's ONE question site for rule / routing / webhook rules), which `buildInput` never sees ⇒ `buildRequest` sent them raw. `src/server/permission-rules.js` has no judge() site at this base.
- **Fix:** PURE `scrubQuestions(questions)` beside `cleanPart` — every string field of a question, its choices and its levels through `scrub` (the ONE table: secret-shapes `redactSecrets`, runs on), except the identifiers the answers are keyed by (type, name, choices[].value, levels[].label); a copy, nothing cut. The engine calls it once in `judge()`, right before its ONE `buildRequest`. The `[userBlock]` part already went through `cleanPart` (pinned now).
- **Gates:** test-decision-model 212/0 (the row-stop table + 5 budgetVerdict rows; the question scrub over the REAL channel-filter builders — 4 marks, identifiers kept, 30 product questions byte for byte, both dialects, the userBlock pin; census: ONE buildRequest caller in src (the engine) on the questions scrubQuestions returned, 5 judge() sites with their uses, the chip words ⊇ ROW_STOPS with zh + ja, the notice = the title's sentence; RED control: scrubQuestions = identity leaks 3 of 3 shapes), test-decision-engine 46/46 (I: the before / after counts with the old classification as the RED reference, notice once, status / plugin why, journal, the three lifting triggers, 401, 422; J: the fake vendor receives the condition + the option description redacted, RED control: scrubQuestions stubbed to identity sends the token; the card leg: desk «stopped — plan refused» warn, phone 390 zh 「已停 — 套餐不支持」).

### lane prepush-partner-patterns — the local push gate catches what GitHub push protection catches (B-89da; no user line: a gate change)
- **The incident:** 2.369.263's first cut (79cb1d60b) was refused by GitHub push protection (GH013 "Slack API Token") for the literal Slack-token fixture in decision-input-scrub's SIX (scripts/test-decision-engine.mjs:171, scripts/test-decision-model.mjs:246); it was re-cut as fb904524a with runtime-built fixtures.
- **Measured cause — the allowlist, applied per LINE (neither a path allowlist nor the regex):** both local scanners (repo-guard's scan.mjs in the global hook and scripts/secret-scan.mjs) MATCHED the token (slack-token, 43 chars) and then dropped it: the allow check was `allowed(line) || allowed(hit)`, and the SIX line also carried a PEM header that `.repo-guard-allow`'s `BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY` row matches, so one row silenced the Slack, Anthropic and GitHub shapes on that line. Reproduced over the refused range 69f2a59c1..79cb1d60b: with the repo allowlist both scanners rc 0; without it 8 findings, both Slack lines among them; the SIX line alone with ONLY that row rc 0, the same line with its PEM header cut rc 1. Hypothesis (a) holds but is not the cause (the pre-push gate never ran scripts/secret-scan.mjs, yet repo-guard's copy carries the same Slack rule); (c) refuted (38 characters after the prefix, the rule wants 10+); (d) refuted (the Actions workflow scans the tree after a push, and under the same allowlist it passed the two files too).
- **THE ONE TABLE:** scripts/secret-scan.mjs `RULES` — 21 partner rows (slack-token, slack-config-token, slack-app-token, slack-webhook, github-token 36, github-pat 82, gitlab-token, anthropic-key, openai-key, google-api-key 35, google-oauth-secret 28, google-oauth-token, aws-akid, aws-secret, stripe-key, twilio-api-key, sendgrid-key, npm-token 36, pypi-token, huggingface-token 34, private-key-block) + 9 generic rows. A partner row never consults the allowlist (GitHub never reads it); a generic row is silenced only by an allow row that overlaps its hit; every match on a line is judged. New modes: `--range=<a>..<b>|<b>` (every commit's added lines + the combined diff + the touched files' full text; a never-fetched base falls back to what no remote-tracking ref has; an unknown tip exits 2) and `--tree` (every tracked text file in one process, ~1.8 s).
- **Three callers, one file:** scripts/git-hooks/pre-push runs `--range` per pushed ref BEFORE `VIBESPACE_SKIP_CI` (that line moved below the scan), the heavy verdict and the fast tier; scripts/ci.mjs's fast tier runs `--tree` right after the build (absent at an old sha ⇒ not judged); .github/workflows/secret-scan.yml runs `--tree` (its per-file loop retired).
- **The tree under the table:** 22 findings on 2dd2f322a, all fixed. Partner literals are now built at runtime: test-exit-run (four GitHub tokens, an OPENSSH block, the AWS example key id, an OpenAI project key, the JWT-glued Slack / GitLab / Google shapes), test-cluster-presets (8 Google OAuth secrets), test-integrations-store (2), test-mounts-oauth (4). Three partner rows left .repo-guard-allow (each one allowed itself); two value rows were added for the second token of a fixture line that the line-wide allow used to cover (dbg-comm-surfaces' expired refresh token, lark-shape's echoed bearer).
- **Gates:** NEW test-secret-scan (fast, 113, ~0.7 s): every row RED at runtime plus two near-misses each; the rel263 shape through the REAL hook (refused before any tier with file:line and the fixture rule, also under VIBESPACE_SKIP_CI and as a new branch; a fix in a later commit is still refused; the squash goes through); controls: the hook without its block, the line-wide scanner and the base scanner each pass it; the allowlist cannot allow itself (rows for the literal, the path and `.*` stay RED, and the literal row is a finding of its own); the --range legs; the three-callers census. Also test-ci-gate 358 (its §4 stub repo carries the scanner), test-exit-run 547 (heavy, run alone), test-cluster-presets 231, test-integrations-store 29, test-mounts-oauth 17, test-channels-slack-send 73, test-channels-lark-shape 428.

### lane boot-loop-hold — the boot holds the main loop for nobody (B-1319)
- **Measured** on a production-shaped worktree instance (625 MB of synthetic stores at production's sizes — ledger 395 MB / 815 k rows, OTel stash 163 MB, anchors 34 MB, channels index 2 032 conversations, todos 1 000, task groups, session status — + 13 restored dtach sessions; base 2dd2f322a vs the lane, /tmp trees, one shape): base = main evaluation 648 ms and the listen tick 1.7 s in ONE gap of 2 328 ms (`fuser` per socket 1.2–1.35 s, the groups' ended-sweep rebuilding the archived set per member 123 ms, the identity repair's anchors 122 ms), then the ledger warm 3 946 ms in one tick at +8.4 s; lane = main evaluation 571 ms, listen tick 154 ms, nothing else ≥ 110 ms (monitorEventLoopDelay max 3 947 → 154 ms). The suspected stores cost 1–7 ms each (channels index 1.7 + 5.0, todos 0.9, session status 0.4 + 6.6, task groups 2.3 + 2.9 ms).
- **Moved:** the ledger warm → `warmStepped` (usage-history: the load pass is a generator; 1 MiB slices, the slide 16 384 rows a step, the cold columns settled a set per tick; a reader mid-warm finishes the pass) — 2.6 s → max step 36 ms; the restore's probes → `probeSockets()` children before listen (fuser / pgrep / the fd scan, four at a time, `runChild`'s own timer), `restoreSessions()` reads the answers; the OTel stash replay → an async read + 20 000 lines a tick, the rewrite only when the trim changes the file (it rewrote 163 MB at every boot) and off the loop; the identity repair → anchors prefetched (`prefetchAnchorRows`, size + mtime checked), boot and hourly; the groups' liveness → the archived set rebuilt only when the user state is.
- **Door:** src/server/boot-trace.js — the always-on boot clock (10 ms ticks for 90 s from server.js line 3; holds ≥ 100 ms named by step / span; the main evaluation said apart; data/boot-trace.json; GET /api/boot-trace; ⚙ → Diagnostics report "Server start — the longest holds", top 5). VIBESPACE_BOOT_TRACE=1 = the sync-op tracer (each hold's sites); VIBESPACE_BOOT_TRACE_SYNC=1 = the RED control (the old one-tick warm).
- **Gate:** test-boot-loop-hold (heavy, ~34 s) — its own preload clock (main thread only: a Worker inherits `-r`), law < 250 ms from the first loop turn to the warm's end: measured max 165 ms; RED control 3 580 ms, named usage-ledger-warm with its src/usage-history.js sites. Not the brief's literal measure: monitorEventLoopDelay never records its first interval (ELD max 54 ms over a 3.4 s boot hold, measured), "listen + 5 s" ends before the warm (the 7.45 s incident starts 8 s after listen), and a 1 MB parse takes ~2 ms here (a 2.8 MB channels index parses in 5 ms) — so the control is the real regression, not a synthetic parse.
- **Fast:** test-cache-bounds §31 (stepped warm = warm(), field for field; a mid-warm reader; a non-widening slice = RED); test-otel-truth's B-1319 legs (no read in create, the replay fills by itself, no rewrite without a trim, the trim's rewrite lands). Censuses moved: §86 reader counts (reading-repair +4, boot-restore +1, otel-ingest +1, usage-history +1), the PID-question row for probeSockets' fuser / pgrep line, the private-method census reads `*_x(` as a definition, §32 exempts scripts/boot-shape.mjs (a fixture writer).
- **Unchanged:** the restart path (`systemctl --user restart vibespace`, scripts/update.sh); the auto-update `git pull` stays synchronous in the main evaluation (nothing exists yet to wait on it; the port is not open).

### lane doc-table-native — a standard table holding a bare `<absent>` is a TABLE, never a raw block; the raw chip says what it is (owner 2026-10-14 「这下面不是标准的表格吗 为啥显示说是源码？」)
- **Cause (bisected on the shape, scripts/fixtures/doc-wheel/32-table-placeholder-cells.md):** an agent's adjudication report — a paragraph whose code span held `…/golden_imports/<case>/paper.txt`, then a 10-column GFM table — drew the table as a raw block (chip 「Markdown · 原样保留，点此改源码」). Hypotheses on base 2dd2f322a: (a) the `<case>` in the code span before — REFUTED (marked consumes a code span whole; paragraph + table with or without a blank line); (b) underscores in a cell's code span, (c) `"` `§` `(` `…` `$`, (d) 10 columns / no trailing pipe, (e) alignment rows `:--` `:-:` `--:`, (f) a short row — all tables on base (controls); (g) a BARE `<absent>` in a cell — RAW (the trigger: CommonMark inline raw HTML ⇒ `hasHtml` ⇒ the block raw, by design since .241, while the reading already showed the tag as text). Minimal failing `| 1 | <absent> |`, minimal passing ``| 1 | `<absent>` |``.
- **Fix (the rule):** ONE predicate doc-window-model `literalTag(src)` — a placeholder (no HTML element: `<absent>` `</sha>` `<id/>`) or an unpaired open tag (unpairedOpenTag; a `</name>` inside a code span closes nothing, `CODE_SPANS`) — asked by the reading's LITERAL_TAG AND the editor's inline tokenizer (doc-markdown `htmlInlineToken` ⇒ an `htmlLiteral` token ⇒ a text node, `HtmlLiteral`; `INLINE_START` = any `<letter`). Choice: the editor carries every tag the reading shows as text, so the r2 ruling's raw block (fixture 31's bare `STEP-<code>-nn` table) retires too, and a `/p/<id>` paragraph is a paragraph. Still raw: a paired / attributed real tag outside the marks, an HTML block, excess cells (GFM drops them).
- **The chip:** `t(RAW_KIND_WORD[kind])` + "· shown as its content · edit source" / "· cannot be shown, source below · edit" (zh 「Markdown 块 · 已按内容显示 · 点此编辑源码」 / 「… · 无法显示，给出源码 · 点此编辑」, ja likewise); the retired keys ("kept as written", "cannot be rendered", lower-case "front matter") are gone from both dictionaries.
- **The tall rows (confirmed, not a fault):** at 1400 px the R003 row is 181 px = its 168 px quote cell + padding; the code-span cell holds one 25 px line — the "tall blank" is the row's long text columns.
- **Tests:** test-doc-wheel 53/0 (the literal table 6 shapes × paragraph / item / cell / heading; the bisection (a)–(g) printed + excess-cells / attributed-tag raw controls; the minimal pair; fixture 32: native, an edit after `<absent>` saves one line; RED controls: the literal rule stubbed ⇒ (g) + fixture 32 raw, a close inside a code span counted ⇒ red); test-doc-window-width 65/0 (literalTag PURE table, reading legs, the chip pins, RED control: CODE_SPANS dropped); test-doc-window §17 (chrome, 1400 zh: native 5×10 table, no chip, both `<absent>` editable text, the tall row measured, Ⓧ after `<absent>` + Ctrl+S ⇒ that row only, the new chip words; before/after PNGs) + §12 / §13 pins moved to the new behaviour and words.

### lane pool-oat-measure — design q-035's six measurements (a long-lived token as a pool member's credential file) as variants of the creds-read measurement; a PURE reader of their fixture (no user line: a measurement + a reader nothing calls yet)
- **The question (design-pool-oat §2 A):** may a pool member whose only credential is its long-lived token hold it as a CLI-shaped `.credentials.json` (`claudeAiOauth.accessToken = <oat>`, `expiresAt` = mint + OAT_TTL, the standard scopes, NO refreshToken) and be spent like a login? scripts/measure-claude-cred-read.mjs gains six variants on member O (that file) beside member A (a login): `oat-file` (every request's bearer is the oat; no refresh; no write), `oat-env` (the same token as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, the hub's oat-only spawn today; its request heads diffed field by field against oat-file's, anthropic-beta flag by flag, plus the calls each made), `oat-file-401` (the mock 401s msg2: does the CLI rewrite, blank or delete the file? msg3 after it clears), `oat-file-near` (expiresAt +30 s: msg1 inside the refresh window, msg2 past it), `oat-file-switch` (link A → O → A, each + utimes), `oat-file-scopes` (no scopes / subscriptionType / rateLimitTier). Each prints PASS / FAIL + a note. The record holds every request head (the credential as a label), both files' sha / inode / mtime / shape before and after, and every strace write on them, one by one.
- **Fixture + reader:** `--write-fixture` (all six in one run) writes scripts/fixtures/oat-in-file.json `{cliVersion, measuredAt, script, netns, variants: {name: {verdict, note}}}`. PURE src/cli-caps.js `oatInFile(version, fixture)` is true only for the exact version the fixture names with oat-file, oat-file-401 and oat-file-switch PASS (design §5 gate 5); `OAT_VARIANTS` is the one spelling of the six (the script imports it). No fixture is committed: 主开发's namespace rung writes it, and until then oatInFile is false for every CLI. Nothing reads oatInFile yet (A's materialization is a later lane).
- **Isolation (主开发's ruling in this lane):** a lane creates no namespace or sandbox of any kind and never runs the real CLI. `--no-netns` refuses any `--claude` that is not a `#!` script or that lives under …/claude/versions/, before it runs. The lane's self-test is a FAKE claude (scripts/fixtures/oat-measure/fake-claude.mjs: good / rewrite401 / stale; it statx()es the creds file every turn and re-reads it on an mtime change, the 2.1.281-measured mechanism). The oat variants set HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY = the mock in both rungs (each CONNECT recorded and answered 403). A strace watchdog rides both rungs: the first non-loopback connect() SIGKILLs the CLI's process group and the run exits 3 (a belt; the namespace is the isolation). Tokens are built at runtime (no token-shaped literal in the tree); outputs carry labels, never bytes.
- **Gates:** test-cli-caps (fast, in-process, 41 legs, 130 ms): the two lists; the reader's truth table (RED control: 2.1.297 / 2.1.295 / 2.1.29 / 2.1.2960 / 2.1.296.1 ⇒ false); 4 patched readers, each turning its leg RED; a census (the script imports the list, writes the fixture path and holds no token literal; the reader imports nothing); `--no-netns` refusing an ELF and a script under …/claude/versions/ before either runs; the committed fixture's shape once it exists. test-oat-measure-fake (heavy — the measurement runs strace, which THE TIER RULE keeps out of fast; 9 legs, 7 s): the measurement over the fake — good ⇒ six PASS and a fixture oatInFile reads true for 9.9.9 only, the oat as a Bearer label, the file's bytes + inode kept, no token bytes in the outputs, nothing off loopback; rewrite401 ⇒ oat-file-401 FAIL with the tmp + rename named; stale ⇒ oat-file-switch FAIL. The hot-switch variants ran over the fake through the refactored spawn (baseline / symlink / hardlink-same / refresh read as 2.1.281 measured). test-claude-hot-switch (heavy, sudo) is 主开发's to run.
- **Fix (lane pool-oat-measure-fix, HOT):** 主开发's first namespace rung (claude 2.1.296, 2026-10-14 01:03Z) died at oat-file on `read ECONNRESET`, an unhandled 'error' on a Socket. Cause, by elimination and then reproduced: Node hands a CONNECT socket to the 'connect' handler without its own 'error' listener (the only server socket left bare; an Upgrade is destroyed when nobody listens), the oat variants send every proxied call there, and the CLI reset one the mock still read (after the 403 + FIN, before its own FIN). Every error path of the inner process now lands in `events` (the variant's evidence, and `· N events survived (where code ×n)` on its verdict line), never a crash: server clientError (a TLS ClientHello named `tls-hello-on-plain-port`, no request bytes kept) + error, each socket via 'connection' (CONNECT ones labelled), request / response / SSE, a throwing route (answered 500), the CLI's spawn + stdin/stdout/stderr, process uncaughtException / unhandledRejection. Two side fixes the handlers made necessary: a rejected main() exits 1 (the process handler would have swallowed it to exit 0), and a CLI that exits mid-turn ends that turn as EXITED, not a 90 s TIMEOUT. The fake gains five misbehaviours (reset, tls-hello, keepalive-drop, connect-reset = the crash's own shape, connect-rst-early). test-oat-measure-fake 9 → 17 legs, 12 s: each misbehaviour ⇒ exit 0, oat-file PASS, its event recorded; a census of the 12 handlers; RED control = a copy with them stubbed ⇒ connect-reset dies with the crash's stack (`read ECONNRESET`, no record); belt = only the process handlers kept ⇒ survives as `process uncaughtException ECONNRESET`. On the base, reset / tls-hello / keepalive-drop never crashed (Node's default clientError) but left no trace; connect-reset and connect-rst-early killed it.

### lane settings-multiline-row — a Settings row never squeezes its words: a textarea row STACKS, a too-wide control wraps under them (owner 2026-10-14 「这个地方布局有点问题」)
- **Cause:** `.settings-row` is a flex row whose `.settings-row-control` never shrinks (`flex-shrink: 0`) and whose words take what is left (`flex: 1; min-width: 0`). The multi-line row's control (`.settings-multiline`: the textarea + 「从我最近的判定草拟」 inline) is as wide as its max-content — measured 317 px in headless Chrome at every window width — so the words get the rest: 85 of 418 px at a 600 px window (label 2 lines), 245 of 578 px at 760, 25 of 358 px on a 390 px phone (label 6 lines, one glyph a line). The owner's ~80 px at ~750 px is the same rule with that machine's wider monospace / scrollbar / Save + ↺ in the control.
- **Fix (the rule):** settings-ui `_renderSetting` stamps `settings-row-stack` off the CONTROL it drew (`control.tagName === 'TEXTAREA' || control.querySelector('textarea')` — the json and the multi-line branches, and any later one); style.css's block "SETTINGS ROWS NEVER SQUEEZE THEIR WORDS" makes a stacked row a column (words on top across the row, the box `width: 100%; min-width: 0; min-height: 4.5em; resize: vertical` under them, its buttons on one line under the box, right-aligned). Theme vars only; the block sits after every rule it overrides.
- **The rail (brief item 2) — flex-wrap, not a container query:** `.settings-row { flex-wrap: wrap }` + `.settings-row-info { min-width: 40% }` + `.settings-row-control { margin-left: auto }`. A container query can only test the ROW's width, never the control's natural one (a select is as wide as its longest option); with wrap the words' hypothetical size is 40 % and the control's its own width, so a control wider than 60 % − gap goes to its own line, at the right — and a row with room lays out exactly as before (the words' flex-grow still eats the free space, the auto margin gets 0). Measured: it wraps 3 shipped rows at 600 px (accounts.onDemandQuotaRefresh 35.2 %, browser.noDisplayMode 39.96 %, the 中继令牌 link row 39.2 %), 7 on the phone, none at 760 / 1200. The multi-select rows' own wrap keeps its 16 px row gap (a global `row-gap` moved them 10 px — caught by the 2 px leg, dropped); the stack has its own 8 px.
- **Measured (scripts/test-settings-row-layout.mjs, HEAVY chrome · ~5 s, zh, advanced rows shown, 235 rows):** 我在乎什么 at 600 / 760 / 1200 / phone 390: words 418 / 578 / 1018 / 358 px = 100 % of the row, the box 100 %, label 1 line, the draft button under the box at the right; all 6 textarea rows (chrome.arrangement / zoneAlign / springs, usage.dashboard, decision.attentionBlock, plugin.voice-input.autoProjects) stacked; every other row (toggle / number / select / combobox / text / radio / multi / link / the Spending producer row) keeps its row-relative rects within 2 px of the pre-fix page at every width except the rail's wraps, each of which had < 40 %. CONTROLS: the pre-fix page (the CSS block cut, the renderer line cut through an esbuild plugin) — the box beside the words at its own 317 px at all three widths, 20 % at 600 and 7 % on the phone; a fixture select with one long option wraps at 600 (words 100 %) and stays beside at 1200 (59 %), pre-fix 0 %.
- **Tests:** test-settings-row-layout 28/0 (new heavy row in ci.mjs); test-settings-view §11 (fast, 8 pins: the renderer line, the two textarea branches, the stack / box / buttons / rail rules, the block after the rules it overrides, no literal colour) 103/0. PNGs (600 / 760 before–after, the rail fixture, the phone) are in the lane report.

### lane attention-rule-at-you — the first screen's 8th rule 「有人 @ 了我、我还没读的」 (owner on the .264 需关注 block: "怎么没有 at 我的这个选项")
- **Cause:** the 7 rules read no mention at all — records carried `mentions` (resolved) since design 012, but only the internal fold's `atYou` (agent groups) ever asked about the owner being named; a channel conversation that @-ed the owner landed on the first screen only by luck of another rule.
- **Fix (PURE, src/channel-focus.js):** `mentionsSelf` (a PERSON mention of the resolved self — never a broadcast / user group / own / system record, never a guess without a self), `keepAtYou` (bounded 50), `atYouOf` = THE @-you predicate (statusTag's new tag `at-you` after awaiting / unknown and before assigned, candidateOf's pre-filter clause, needsOwner). Rule `at-you` joins ATTENTION_RULES (2nd row, default on, the presets set it).
- **Engine:** the instants of the records that @ the owner are kept on the index entry (`atYouAts` + the newest one's words `atYouLast`) at countFresh (poll / walk / landed) and the push batch; rowView ships the ones past `readAt` (+ `atYouText` / `atYouWho`) — the panel's preview quotes the mentioning message for an at-you row. No new store read, no O(rows) pass.
- **Adapters:** `caps.mentions` (CLOSED: people / none / not-applicable): Slack people, Lark people (already filled on both lanes — the poll's open_id, the push event's object id; `@_all` now maps to a broadcast `!all`), Gmail not-applicable (a To / Cc is the direct address).
- **Tests:** test-channels-focus ⑭ (tag, rank, the exclusive 24 h edge, self-mention, read-up-to, switch off ⇒ next rule / All, presets, judge never sees it, RED control = a copy without the clause), test-channel-rows (at-you rows at the window edge in the candidateOf ⊇ statusTag property), test-settings-view (the 8th row, search 「@」), test-channels-lark-shape / -slack-shape (mentions census + caps.mentions closed), test-attention-policy-ui (12 rows, the @ row's chip + quoted preview; PNGs).

### lane decision-attention-facts — the channel judge gets FACTS, not more text (owner 2026-10-13: 「decision api给的优先级评估都不怎么样，你要不仔细在我本机上检查一下？」; findings /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/decision-quality/findings.zh.md §一)
- **Cause:** of the 16 rows the judge listed as 需要你 on the owner's hub about 4 were right, and a row that @-ed him by name scored 0.15. The record never said who the reader is (`to_me` guessed, `asks_me` became "is there a question"); `matters` was asked against an EMPTY block (140 of 145 answers 0.4–0.5); facts the product holds never reached the model (an @ of the owner, DM vs a 300-member group, when he last spoke, unread since his read line, one mail in 3 inboxes, a bulk sender); long groups showed the last 8, not what he had not read; mail bodies were mostly quotes and footers; the rubric rode twice (state + every question).
- **Fix (PURE, src/decision-model.js):** `attentionFacts(view, ctx)` = the record's FIRST line `facts:` — addressed (@-mentioned the reader / a direct message / a reply to the reader's message / no mention) · kind (a direct message / a group of N / a group / an email thread) · the reader last spoke here 2 h ago / has not spoken here lately · N messages since the reader last read, M h ago · the same message reached K of the reader's inboxes · an automated or bulk sender (level) — counts, kinds and ages, never a name. `attentionRecord(view, tail, facts, {since, unread, mail})`: the body = the messages past the read line NEWEST FIRST, at most 12 WHOLE messages inside the record ceiling, then "(N earlier unread messages omitted)" (N from the row's own count); the read line unknown ⇒ the last 8. `trimMailBody` (gmail records only): the quoted "On … wrote:" / "在 … 写道：" block (one or two lines), `>` lines, the `-- ` signature, an unsubscribe / "You have received this" / "You are receiving this" / © footer that starts past 40 %. RUBRIC v2: `to_me` reads the facts line; `matters` only with a non-empty block (`rubricClauses` / `rubricQuestions({hasBlock})` / the verdict's clauses); the [rubric] part is one line. `implicitLabel`, `addExample` (an implicit example never replaces the person's own; over 200 the oldest implicit goes first), `examplesForInput` (own labels first, implicit ones fill, marked `(inferred)`). `inboxKey` / `inboxCount`. JOURNAL_FIELDS + `p`.
- **ORCH:** src/server/channels-attention.js — the engine's `facts()` built ONCE per scan (at the drain's first call, dropped when the queue is empty and nothing flies; `status().scans`), `tailOf(v, {since, limit})`, `learn()` (the switch `decision.implicitLabels`, at most once an hour: the examples hash is memo material, so a batch re-judges the candidates once; `rowState(key)` = readAt / selfAt; a verdict keeps `at`). src/server/channels-engine.js — `attentionScanFacts` (the duplicate-inbox map over the live index, O(rows); mail accounts = `caps.glyph === 'mail'`, no vendor word), `attentionTail` (ONE bounded read ≤ 50; per record `atYou` = `FO.mentionsSelf` — the at-you rule's predicate, `toSelf` = a reply to an own record in the read, `automated` = the record's fact). src/server/decision-engine.js journals `p` (attention, one record). src/plugin-settings.js row `decision.implicitLabels` 「从我的行为学习」 (off) + docs/settings.md.
- **Choices:** the duplicate window is 60 min, not the brief's 15 — the owner's 3 Workspace copies span 22.1 min (15 min reads 2 / 2 / 1, 60 min 3 / 3 / 3; on his 1 204 mail rows no other pair up to 24 h). "has not spoken here lately" instead of "never" — `selfAt` 0 means none since stamping / in the last 200 records (healSelfAt), not a proof. ### lane decision-inbox-rank — the For-you judge gets facts, a three-way answer, an order and a decay (owner 2026-10-13: 「decision api给的优先级评估都不怎么样」)
- **Cause (decision-quality findings §二, measured on the owner's hub):** 25 of 34 judged items in 现在要你 — a 14-day-old 「会议室 hub 按哪种形态配」 at p 1.0, a 10-day-old one at 0.98, a 15-day-old one at 0.70. v1's level words defined `now` as "an agent waits on your decision", which every For-you item is; the judge saw neither the item's age, nor whether the agent was stuck or went on with a default, nor a date in the text; one item a call cannot rank items against each other.
- **Fix (PURE, src/decision-model.js INBOX v2 — only the use ④ block + the `inbox` plan row):** `inboxFacts(item, {now, board, tzOffsetMin})` → `{state: blocked | continued | finished | unknown, dated, due, reasks, askedAt}` (blocked = the board says blocked / needs-input for THIS ask: set before it, ≤ 10 min after it, or its reason / detail names the item; continued = an agent status or a progress note after the ask; finished = done since it); `datePhraseOf(text, base, tz)` — a conservative table (ISO, 10/13 but never 1/2, 22:00 / 5pm, 今晚 明天 后天 周五 下周一 月底 截止, tonight / tomorrow / EOD / by Friday / deadline; never 上周五, a version, a path or a timestamp), the phrase ≤ 40 characters of the text's own, `due` resolved in the hub's zone; `inboxFactsLine` = ONE English line first in the record (`facts` part, 240, through cleanPart): counts, kinds, ages and the quoted phrase — never an id or a name. The question is a `choice` (`inbox_need`: blocked / dated / whenever); `inboxVerdict` → `{group, why, p}`. `inboxPlace` = the declaration first (urgent / high / decisions ⇒ now, low / answered ⇒ later), then (a) THE DECAY `inboxStale` (48 h since the last ask, no progress after it, no live date — a stale blocked status too) ⇒ later `stale`, (b) a blocked FACT ⇒ now `blocked` with no call, then the judge (a v1 verdict keeps its group until re-scored). `inboxRank(items, now)` = urgent › high › blocked (oldest ask first) › decisions › dated (nearest first, unknown after) › the judge's p; 待判断 / 可以等 newest first. No clock inside: `now` is handed in.
- **Engine (`inboxPass`) / store / wiring:** the pass reads the BOARD once (mounts-plugins-wiring `inboxBoard`: SessionStatusManager `get` + `history` and the newest TaskGroups progress note per sessionKey — the stores' own readers) and writes every sortable item's facts (`store.setFacts([[id, facts]…])` — only what changed, ONE broadcast; a `{group: null, v: 0}` stand-in before any verdict); a blocked-fact or stale item is `placed` (no call); an item is judged again when its facts' signature (state | date phrase | re-asks — never the age) moves; the memo digest carries the signature. `setJudged` keeps `{group, why, p, at, v, facts, sig}`. A pass a refusal stopped is SAID: one log line when the reason changes + `status().inbox {at, judged, placed, stopped}` (the plugin's status spreads it); a thrown pass logs instead of `catch(() => {})`. `add()` counts a RE-ASK — the same agent filing the same words (and the same or no detail) of an OPEN item (`reasks`, `reaskedAt`; a server producer's re-file is not one; a re-file of a resolved item starts at 0). record-clear SHAPES todo drops `judged` (it holds a quoted date phrase of the words).
- **Client:** user-todos-layout `inboxSectionOf` / `inboxChip` read `inboxPlace`; `inboxSections(rows, {prev, now})` numbers every row by `inboxRank` at the first draw of an open and orders the rows and the groups of each section by those numbers (held: a row first seen while open goes last — the slot law). user-todos-row `judgedChipHtml` says why in OUR words: 卡住等你 / 有期限 · <the item's date phrase> / 随时 / 48 小时无人再问 (title: its agent / the judge + p / the clock; the row's meta already shows the age, so the chip does not repeat it); a v1 verdict keeps 现在 / 可等.
- **Cost:** `INBOX.version` 2 re-scores every open item the rules do not place — ≤ 34 calls on the owner's hub ≈ $0.002 (fewer: stale and blocked items cost none).
- **Gates:** test-decision-inbox ①–⑤ moved to v2 + ⑥ (the date table 19 fixtures, the board → state 12 fixtures, the facts line + census, the decay on two clocks, the order fixture, the five owner-measured SHAPES end to end through the REAL engine + store, a facts change judged again, the v1 → v2 re-score, re-asks in the store, a stopped pass said; RED: the model without the decay ⇒ the 14-day-old ask back in 现在要你, without the blocked fact ⇒ 待判断), test-user-todos-layout ㉑ (v2 order, slot law, zh chip words, no em-dash).

### lane voice-everywhere — the microphone on EVERY message box; on the phone it never opens the keyboard (owner 2026-10-13, phone, three messages)
- **Owner:** 「每个输入框都做一下那个 Dropline？我在手机上想要回一下 inbox 里的东西，发现没有」 + 「点麦克风那个图标会和展开输入框的图标重叠…误触了就会弹出键盘」 + should a mic tap fold the keyboard?
- **Root cause of the mis-tap (measured, base 79743b74b):** chat-input's phone `tall()` (⤢ shown) read `scrollHeight > 72` on `input` only. A multi-line SEND clears the value and resets the height with no input event, so the field went back to one line (44 px) with ⤢ still shown at its top-right — ON the 32-px mic: base geometry after a 4-line send = mic {290,115,324,147}, ⤢ {296,113,318,135}, `elementFromPoint(mic centre)` = ⤢. Deleting lines did the same (scrollHeight is read before the rAF autosize shrinks the box). While typing (3 lines) the two were 26 px apart, which is why it looked random.
- **Fix (phone composer, chat.css phone block + chat-input.js):** ⤢ shows only while the BOX is ≥ 92 px (two 40×40 hit areas + 8 px), judged on `offsetHeight` by a ResizeObserver (every height change: send, deletes, expand). The mic = 40×40 at the trailing bottom (right/bottom 2), ⤢ = 40×40 at the top-right corner; the field's padding-right 46.
- **ONE attach point (src/lib/voice-input.js):** `attachDictation(textarea, {getFacts, getCwd, openPlugins, placement})` → `{btn, chip, destroy}`; `createVoiceInput` is its chat flavour (placement 'chat' — chat-input.js still places btn + chip, its pinned rows unchanged); `voiceField(ta, d)` wraps the box + mic (`.voice-field`, the mic inside the trailing edge). 'field' chips float (fixed, in body, only while shown; a press on one stops propagation so a popover's outside-press never closes over it). 16 boxes attached (census below); showInputDialog got a `decorate` hook so utils.js imports nothing of voice.
- **The mic never focuses (the owner's question, decided):** a mic tap NEVER focuses the box (no keyboard appears); a keyboard already up stays and the words land at its caret; nothing is blurred. pointerdown + mousedown cancelled, tabIndex −1 at ≤ 768 px, no `.focus()` left in voice-input.js (the old insert() and the chip's Undo both focused). Unfocused box ⇒ setRangeText (+ input event) and an own Undo snapshot; focused ⇒ execCommand('insertText') (native Ctrl+Z). A box never focused takes the words at its end.
- **Absent when off:** `html.voice-absent` (one class) from /api/voice/status at the first attach (≤ 1 per 30 s; again on visibilitychange), the plugins-updated broadcast (`noteVoicePlugins`, app.js — the voice-input row's `enabled` = rec.enabled && keyed) and the plugin card's read (`noteVoiceStatus`). The old no-key press words stay for a stale page (test-voice-chrome ① leg unchanged).
- **Lifecycle:** an idle mic holds no document listener (Esc bound in start(), unbound in release()); the visibilitychange listener is ONE per page; a box that leaves the page while recording cancels (the 250-ms tick checks `btn.isConnected`). For-you rows are patched in place; the reply box is never replaced, so no capsule leaks.
- **Census (test-voice-boxes, fast, 22):** all 43 textarea sites under src/lib — 16 attached, 27 left out with a reason (settings / form fields, key / config pastes, stored record fields, off-screen copy helpers, keyboard / IME proxies, a doc block's raw source, the incident note); a new box / a dead row / a lost attach call is RED (4 planted controls + a planted focus()).
- **Placement CSS lives in style.css** (app-wide chrome; test-channel-edit-autosize loads style.css alone and caught an unstyled mic under the box taking the drag's pointerup). A RESIZABLE box keeps its drag grip: `voiceField` reads `resize` once laid out and `.voice-field-grip` steps the mic 16 px left of the corner (test-voice-chrome ⑥b + a RED run without the rule).
- **Gates:** test-voice-chrome 36 (new ④–⑦ + ⑥b: 1-line / 3-line / expanded / after-send geometry with real touch taps, never-focus, For-you phone, absent + live broadcast) — the same suite on a base copy: 13 RED. test-phone-composer-chrome 39 (mic 40 px + availability wait), test-voice-teach-chrome 20 (availability wait). user-todos-panel's Send reads `.ut-reply textarea` (the box moved into its field). test-inbox-window-ui's no-markup census skips `.chat-voice-btn` (our constant SVG icon counted as `svg`).

The stats row names the path.
- Cause ②: TightVNC captures an HDR desktop without tone mapping; `display-facts` carried no HDR fact. Fix ②: the Windows script reads DisplayConfig advanced-colour info per active path (HDR = enabled ∧ ¬wideColorEnforced) → `hdr` per screen; the switch bar shows 「HDR 已开 · 画面会偏白」 with the remedy. Probe compiled with portable pwsh 7.4.6 (user32 absent ⇒ caught ⇒ unknown); not measured on a real HDR machine.

### lane login-expiry-oat — A ROW WITH A LIVE LONG-LIVED TOKEN WAS CALLED DEAD (owner: "都绑定长期token了，怎么还提示过期")
- Mechanism: `loginState` read the OAuth credentials only, so a row whose refresh deadline passed read `expired` (red chip "every session on this account fails", For-you urgent) although the account held a valid long-lived token. Worse, resolveForSpawn only used the token when the dir login was WIPED: an `expired` login still parses `loggedIn`, so the row's own sessions spawned on the dead login.
- Fix: PURE `withOat` (src/login-expiry.js) — dead login + valid token ⇒ `oat-only` (msLeft = the token's; rank 1; WARN_STAGES gains the LOW `oat-only` rung; `ledgerExp` keys the token's ledger). `accounts.loginStateOf` folds the token for the ROW; `{ slot: true }` = the file alone, passed by every pool reader (a pooled CLI reads the member's file through its symlink and can never be handed the token — the design's 2026-09-07 law). resolveForSpawn / authFor: a dead dir login + valid token ⇒ `oatOnly`. Chip: warning colour + the two-fact words; the pool row keeps the slot truth and adds 「池用不了它的长期 token」. `refreshViaCliPanel` refuses an oat-only row (code `login`, route `loginNeeded`) before any probe spawn. Watch: one LOW notice, the login's urgent item retracted, then the token's 24h / 1h / expired.
- Brief deviation: the brief asked the pool engine not to escape an oat-only member. Not done — the slot cannot carry the token, so keeping the member would fail every pooled turn on it (the pre-2026-09-07 outage). The pool still escapes; its words now say why.

- **Measured first (the brief's premise corrected):** a stopped session does NOT keep its data/session-meta file — session-stdout.js onExit does `activeSessions.delete(id)` then `deleteSessionMeta(sockName)` (unlink + tombstone); the registry's rows live on the live session (`_artifacts`, persisted in that same meta). So after a stop NOTHING on the server named the window's `from` session or the document's registry owner, and `ownerOf` answered `no_owner`.
- **Fix (src/server/doc-engine.js `ownerMemo`):** every owner `ownerOf` resolves while live is remembered — the window's `from` session → its conversation, a registry-owned document (`host\u0001path`) → its conversation + session — in data/doc-owners.json (tmp+rename, written only when a mapping is new or moves, ≤ 500 per map, oldest out; ids and paths only). `ownerOf` = live registry → live `from` → the memo (`via: 'stopped'`, the document's registry owner first, the live order). A stopped owner then takes the existing door: `sendUserInput` answers `no_session` ⇒ ONE stash entry per message under the conversation, `delivered:'stashed'` with count/messages as today. A save from the window: `artifacts.noteEdit` takes `conversationId` when no live session (ONE `doc-edit` note in the stash). `no_owner` now only when no conversation was ever seen; words "No conversation goes with this document — open it from a chat to comment" (zh 这份文档没有对应的对话——从聊天里打开它再批注), engine + the window's owner line.
- **The drain needed nothing:** agent-routes `drainStashUnderCap(deliver, cid, …)` reads the stash by conversation id with no liveness filter, and no exit path drains or drops it — proven over the REAL conversation-deliver + drain (resumed under a new session id, stopped again, restarted, then a turn: every message in order).
- **Gates:** NEW scripts/test-doc-stopped-owner.mjs (fast, 19: ① stopped ⇒ stashed in order · ② the memo survives a restart · ③ no_owner words · ④ live without a pty unchanged · ⑤ a registry-owned document · ⑥ the edit note · ⑦ the drain · ⑧ two RED controls — the stopped rung removed ⇒ no_owner, the memo kept off disk ⇒ forgotten across a restart); test-doc-model unchanged (154); heavy test-doc-window §16 (a chat opens STOP.md, ws kill ⇒ GET owner via stopped, Send all ⇒ "…next turn" toast, nothing typed; resumed with the same id ⇒ its `stash` fact, and its hook's REAL prompt-context carries the message, notes in order, once — the stub now honours `--resume <id>` and a command's `sid`, and a stub started later never replays earlier command files — the resumed stub had replayed §5's prompt-context and drained its own stash). The hand-over route answered `unreachable` there: the stub has no peer inbox (a harness limit, not the product).

### lane split-ux-leftovers — a phone opens a split on its active window; the ⫿ words follow a rename (B-9cd4, found by lane split-keeps-sides)
- **Measured first:** a 390×844 phone booted on a [A, B | C] split record with the guest C active had `activeWindowId` = C AND the `.window-active` mark on C's element — the boot focused C standalone, then `restoreTabChain` moved C's content into the frame A and hid C's element; the frame never got the mark, and ≤ 768 px only the marked window displays ⇒ blank until a pick (`wm.focusWindow`). The ⫿ button's words were written at render / tab switch only; `setTitle` re-wrote the tab label, never the button.

- **Gates:** test-chain-layout ⑰ +4 (the phone row, a focus elsewhere ⇒ null, the pre-fix control, a wiring pin); test-window-binding-model ⑨ +3 (rename ⇒ title + aria-label, the neutered-relabel RED control, a split restored around the focused guest); test-split-ux §14 +2 heavy legs (③ rename ⇒ the title attribute + tooltip.png; ④ the phone's first paint before any pick + phone.png), both RED on the base 2baa66aaf.

### lane app-display-notify-sink — an app on its own display gets a notifications sink; THE RED CENSUS of its session bus (B-4a59 piece 2, owner path 1 "an app's display is a complete private session")
- **Measured first (a scratch Xvfb + the .256 plan's private bus, nobody owning org.freedesktop.Notifications):** libnotify / a GApplication got `ServiceUnknown` — the notification silently dropped behind one GLib warning; the portal's `Notification.AddNotification` answered `()` and xdg-desktop-portal-gtk dropped it ("Unable to send notifications"); Ubuntu's `notify-send` CLI failed "Could not connect: Permission denied" in 8 ms — its AppArmor profile (`/etc/apparmor.d/notify-send`, abstractions/dbus-session-strict) connects only to `/run/user/<uid>/bus` and `/tmp/dbus-*`, so it is refused on ANY private path socket even with the sink (an app calling libnotify in-process is not confined; the plan's socket path is unchanged — flatpak reads a single `unix:path=` address).
- **The D-Bus server:** python3 + GObject introspection (Gio = GDBus) — on this box (GLib 2.88, python 3.14); node has no D-Bus. `src/notify-sink.py` (~90 lines) owns the name, answers GetServerInformation (VibeSpace, spec 1.2), GetCapabilities (`body` — no actions, no icons in P0), Notify (an id; `replaces_id` kept) and CloseNotification (+ NotificationClosed(id, 3)); it appends ONE JSON line per call (one `write`, O_APPEND) to `$VS_NOTIFY_JOURNAL` in the app's own 0700 portal dir — no network, no token, nothing on argv. A machine without python3 / python3-gi / the file ⇒ `notify: 'unavailable: <why>'` on the record, the app launches as before (`D.notifySinkFacts`, the gi probe once per interpreter).
- **The plan (PURE, src/desktop-apps.js):** `portalPlan({ …, notify })` adds `services/org.freedesktop.Notifications.service` (`Exec=<python3> <sink>`) + `VS_NOTIFY_JOURNAL` on the BUS env (never the app's), and says `notify: 'on' | 'off' | 'unavailable: …'`; `notifyRecord` (bounds 80/200/1000, control chars dropped), `notifyVerdict` (always a toast; For you when critical OR no pane shows the window), `SESSION_BUS_NAMES` + `sessionBusCensus`. Setting `desktop.appNotifications` on|off (default on).
- **The door:** desktop-serve drains the journal (an `fs.watch` on the portal dir + every tick; a restart reads the tail into the ring without re-announcing), keeps the last 50 per app and calls the hub's new `hooks.onNotify`; the hub keeper broadcasts `desktop-app-notify` and files ONE For-you item per app (`desktop-app-notify` action → Show window) while one is open; `POST /api/desktop/apps/:id/notifications/seen` (the window's press, the For-you action) or the app's teardown resolves it. `GET …/notifications` = the ring (device #0's apps; a paired device's daemon has no sink file ⇒ unavailable, said).
- **The window:** a toast INSIDE the app window (top-right of the picture: the bell SVG, the app's name, summary, body; 6 s; a click raises the window — a §62 door, the row moved 2 → 3), ⋯ ▸ Notifications (the ring, newest first).
- **THE CENSUS (scripts/test-app-display-session-census, fast, 23):** universe printed = the brief's 11 names ∪ the table (13): 5 PROVIDED (the bus's ListActivatableNames), 8 ABSENT-AND-SAID (a11y → piece 3, secrets → piece 4, ScreenSaver / PowerManagement.Inhibit / gvfs / polkit agent → never, StatusNotifierWatcher / dconf → not planned); RED controls: a table without the Notifications row, the .256 bus without the sink, an unknown asked name. Plus the sink over a scratch dbus-run-session (`notify-send -u critical` ⇒ ONE record; capabilities; close; without the sink notify-send fails in 11 ms).
- **Heavy (scripts/test-desktop-app-notify, 10, ~45 s):** a fake app (scripts/fixtures/notify-app.py: xmessage + Notify on its bus) on the vnc-display rung under `desktop.appPortal = all` in a worktree server with no owner bus: the toast in the window (PNG), no For-you for a normal one in front, a minimized window + two criticals ⇒ ONE item, raised + pressed ⇒ resolved, the ring, the ⋯ row. ### desktop-v2-entry — Desktop v2 P0 (Opus): the Desktop picker, one display at a time, the stats strip (design q-030)
- **The UNCONFIRMEDs, settled in the bundled noVNC 1.7.0 first:** (1) clip and scale ARE exclusive — `_updateClip` sets `newClip = false` whenever `_scaleViewport`, and the Display's `viewportChangeSize` falls back to the whole fb when not clipping ⇒ a ≤ 20-line BUILD-TIME patch (src/novnc-patch.js, 15 added lines: `vsCrop` keeps clip + autoscale together); (2) `_handleExtendedDesktopSize` keeps only screen 0's id/flags and `rQskipBytes(16)` over every other rect ⇒ the same patch dispatches the 4 + 16·n payload as `vsscreens` (PURE `rfbScreens`); (3) `new RFB(target, urlOrChannel)` takes a channel object (Websock.attach checks its props) ⇒ the machine window hands noVNC its own WebSocket and times the FramebufferUpdateRequests it sends (no hub skimmer, no `/api/desktop/<id>/screens` route).
- **Choices (simpler answers):** the fake two-screen server is a NEW stub on test-machine-app-chrome's harness shape (test-desktop-vnc-fit runs a real Xvnc, there is no fake server to grow); browser ⇄ hub = the page's timing of `GET …/link` minus the hub's `took` (a browser cannot send a WS ping); the `?netem` bench is xpra-only (stream-relay-rfb has none), so ⑥ delays the stub's updates by 200 ms instead (read: 201 ms at 5 fps); the Apps dialog's link still opens the window at once (inc-mv51w0ow-crw3, pinned by test-mac-ard-signin-chrome) and makes it the picker's recent row; Wayland seat = the hub's own WAYLAND_DISPLAY / XDG_SESSION_TYPE. Not built: "frame it once" for an unknown layout, the ⌨ capture button (keyboard lock is P1), TightVNC's share-one-monitor op, display chips fetched live (the picker shows what each window mapped last).
- **Tests:** test-screen-map (30, fast), test-desktop-picker (13, fast), test-desktop-v2-chrome (18, heavy: ③ every canvas pixel = screen 2's pattern, ④ the press lands at (1920, 400), ⑤ one session through 2 · 1 · 全部, ⑪ the unpatched mutant reds the crop predicate). test-mac-ard-signin-chrome presses the renamed link.
- User line: The Desktop button now offers your recent, local and paired-machine desktops; a Mac or Windows machine with several displays can be shown one display at a time

### desktop-v2-latency — Desktop v2 P1 (Opus): the quality ladder, paste to the machine, full-screen shortcuts, the comparison row, the D4 probe (design q-030 §4)
- **The ladder:** PURE `qualityPlan` (src/desktop-quality.js) through vnc-view `ladder`: input (a key, a press / drag / wheel — never a bare hover) or a moving picture (≥ 2 answers to incremental requests, ≥ 24 KB, in the last second) ⇒ 3 / 1; still ≥ 500 ms ⇒ 8 / 2 + ONE non-incremental request for the shown display (a still screen sends nothing — the fluid parts would stay blurry); a slow link (median of the last 5 updates ≥ 32 KB from their first byte < 2000 kbps, normal at ≥ 3000) one rung down (6 / 4 still, 1 / 6 moving, 慢链路). ONE SetEncodings per rung: `_compressionLevel` written before the public `qualityLevel` (each public write sends one).
- **Measured traps:** (1) judging inside our channel send = inside noVNC's flush(): the quality write appended SetEncodings to the queue being sent and the input's bytes went out TWICE (test-desktop-v2-latency over noVNC's own Websock) ⇒ the judge runs in a microtask after the send; (2) our own refresh re-read the last second's changes and flipped back to fluid once ⇒ only a request that CLOSED a change counts the picture as moving (`updateTimer().request` answers it); (3) a byte-weighted rate is drowned by one 8 MB fast frame ⇒ the median.
- **Paste:** Ctrl/⌘+V is kept from noVNC (its keydown preventDefault kills the browser's `paste` — measured in Chrome 154 on a focused canvas); the paste event's text/plain → `clipboardPasteFrom` (ClientCutText, CRLF → LF), then `sendKey(v)`. **Full screen:** the window's content; `navigator.keyboard.lock()` behind PURE `keyboardLockGate` (secure page, the API, full screen, ⌨ on); http says the https words. headless Chrome never leaves full screen on Esc (locked or not), so the heavy leg asserts the lock / unlock calls and Esc as a key on the machine.
- **D4 probe (report only):** /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/desktop-v2-latency/d4-probe.md — xpra 6.5.4's pipewire / portal shadow cannot load here (`codecs/gstreamer/capture.py` imports `CSC_ALIAS`, absent from xpra-common's `codecs/constants.py`); the portal asks GNOME's share dialog on the physical screen at every start (no restore token). No rung.
- **Tests:** test-quality-plan (24, fast, 2 RED mutants), test-desktop-v2-latency (23, fast: the REAL vnc-view over noVNC's own setters / `_sendEncodings` / `clipboardPasteFrom` / `sendKey`; RED: public setters = 2 SetEncodings), test-desktop-v2-latency-chrome (18, heavy: a holding / animating / paced stub, the hub on the box's LAN address for the http leg; ladder / fullscreen / phone .png). test-desktop-v2-chrome ② reads the strip's new parts.
- User line: A paired machine's desktop stays fluid while you move and turns sharp when you stop; fullscreen captures your shortcuts; paste reaches the machine

### lane tls-pass-retry (Opus) — the https boot pass said "no-tailscale" on a box where Tailscale ran, and waited an hour (owner on .260)

- **Measured cause:** production journal 2026-10-13 — `hub.start()` at 02:58:32.6 (the "running at" line), the `[tls] https off — no-tailscale` verdict 23.6 s later, and between them `[canary] the main loop held the probe's answer 7450ms` (+ `[port-forward] frpc reload … aborted due to timeout`). execFile's own `timeout` kill DESTROYS the unread stdout before signalling: a bound that fires late on a held loop turns an answer the child gave in ms into `code 0, out '', err ''` (reproduced: a 4 ms stub + a 700 ms hold over a 200 ms bound) ⇒ "tailscale status answered nothing" ⇒ no-tailscale. So the timeout was not tailscale being slow — STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS stays 10 s.
- **Fix:** `runChild` keeps its own timer (an answer given before the kill is kept; `TIMEOUT` only when our kill ended it); a failed status/cert call logs one raw `[tls]` warn (code, ms, stdout bytes, first stderr line — never contents); timeout / no JSON / half a JSON = `status-unreadable`; a boot miss re-runs at 60 s → 5 min → hourly (PURE `nextPassMs`; a miss after a served pass stays hourly); `POST /api/tls/recheck` (people only) + Settings Check again + "Last check: …".
- **Gates:** test-tls-plan 54/54 (§7b RED control), test-tls-pass 18/18 (§1 base runChild RED), test-tls-demux 32/32, test-architecture, test-https-hub-chrome 25/25 (⑥ Check again flips the row in the same process; PNGs).

### lane channel-record-revisions — a stored channel message learns its recall and its edits (owner 2026-10-13, userW's recall)
- **Premise measured on 4d8f5bf5f:** the record already declared `edited` (time) / `recalled` (flag) facts and Lark's `toRecord` emitted them, but the change feed is a SEARCH (new messages only) — a stored message was never re-read, so a recall minutes later never arrived; Slack's history simply drops a deleted message.
- **The row + the method (src/channels/index.js):** `caps.revisions = {recall, edit, how: byid|absent|none}` (validated by name; a missing row = none); `revisionOf(convId, {messageId, threadKey})` declared by it, the wrapper closes the states (recalled / edited / same / unknown), a finite `editedAt` or no edit, the body bounded. Lark byid (GET im/v1/messages/:id; 230011 / 230110 / `deleted:true` = recalled — the catch re-throws a rate refusal first), Slack absent (history or replies at oldest = latest = ts, inclusive; absent or a tombstone = recalled), Gmail / webhook / agents `how: none`; the fake's NAMED seam `VIBESPACE_CHANNELS_FAKE_REVISIONS=<file>`.
- **The record:** side kind `rv` = one version `{editedAt, text, blocks?}` (≤ 8 KiB: the tree drops first, then the text cuts, `truncated`), key `rv:<msg>:<editedAt>`; a recall = the `fx` flag. src/channel-revisions.js (PURE): `foldVersions` (the record is the ORIGINAL, never overwritten), `recalledAtOf`, `planRecheck` (24 h fresh / 7 d woken-for, ≤ 1/message/hour, ≤ 12 a pass, ≤ 240 an account-hour; the owner's Refresh re-asks after 5 s), the trim keeps 20 versions. **Found on the way:** channel-store's `SIDE_HEAD_RE` named only rx|th|pl|fx — an `rv` line was appended and never read back (the chrome leg caught it).
- **The engine:** `revisionsPass` after every good pass (never fails the pass; `affordable` first); `withView` folds `recalledAt` + `versions` + the current body (window) / `revisionText` (agent); a `revised` broadcast carries each changed row's read shape (applied in place); `en.lastRecalled` ⇒ the list row's `lastRecalled`; the woken-for ledger `en.wokeFor` (≤ 40, 7 d) on each delivered wake ⇒ ONE stashed note per (message, conversation) on its recall (reach first, fromName `Channels · recalls`).
- **The window / CLI:** a recalled row folds to one line with ▸ 展开 (the kept copy dimmed under 撤回于 …); an edited row shows the newest body + 已编辑 · {time} ▸ 查看 N 个版本; the list preview says 撤回了一条消息; `vibespace-channels read` prints the server's revision line, `--versions` every version.
- **Gates:** test-channel-revisions (new fast, 22), lark-shape 425 / slack-shape 223 (revisionOf legs), peer-text census rows (m.revisionText → agentRevisionLine door, m.versions / v.*, REV_NOTE_FROM), record-clear reader row, store allow-list, test-channel-revisions-ui (new heavy, 17: two desk tabs + phone 390; PNGs). Not covered by an engine leg: the woken-for note (its census rows are in).

- **Cause:** doc-window-ui's click handler opened a link ONLY on Ctrl/⌘+click and `preventDefault`ed every plain click (nothing happened, nothing said why); `editLink()` with the caret on a link ran `extendMarkRange('link').unsetLink()` — the toolbar's Link REMOVED it, and no door changed an href. SafeLink had `autolink: false`.
