The caret on a link (or a 300 ms hover) shows ONE bar keyed to the link: address + Open / Edit / Copy / Remove (a phone: a bottom row with words). Edit = a two-field dialog (address + text) prefilled; the toolbar's Link and Ctrl/⌘+K are the same door. Read-only (`view.editable` false) ⇒ a plain click opens. SafeLink: `autolink` on, but `shouldAutoLink` only for `https?://` / `mailto:` / `www.` + safeHref; links stay non-inclusive.
- **Measured on the way:** the house Ctrl+K (session-palette.js) is a CAPTURE listener that `preventDefault`s, so ProseMirror's keymap never saw the chord (`eventBelongsToView` drops defaultPrevented events) ⇒ the palette skips `[data-own-mod-k]` (set by the editor) as it skips `.xterm`. linkify alone links `README.md` as http://README.md ⇒ the AUTO_LINK rule. Tiptap's autolink appendTransaction links the first textblock's last word on ANY multi-block change ⇒ the disk repaint, a raw block's commit and a column alignment carry `preventAutolink` (else a repaint would dirty the file). The doc window has no read-only open today (the editor is always editable): the rule keys on `view.editable` and the heavy leg drives `setEditable(false)`.
- **Gates:** fast ci ALL GREEN 299 s with the package at .257 and int257's seam 97a69593f applied UNCOMMITTED (c7c44837b alone reds test-changelog-style — the .258 heading — and test-press-select — the raw-block opt-in, classified at int257). test-doc-window-width ⑧ (the link table 23 rows + the pre-lane door as a RED control + window / palette / SafeLink pins + shouldAutoLink 8 rows). test-doc-window §14 `VS_DOC_WINDOW_ONLY=link` 32/32 (click ⇒ bar; Open ⇒ a new page target; Copy ⇒ clipboard + toast; Edit address / text ⇒ the markdown on disk; javascript: refused; the toolbar's Link on a link ⇒ Edit — RED on c7c44837b: no dialog, the link gone; Remove; Ctrl+K ⇒ the dialog, not the palette; paste; autolink; hover; read-only click opens; phone 390 bottom row); the full suite 174/174. ### lane heavy-flake-thresholds — two heavy suites red on master, neither a regression (B-1542, Opus)
- **test-browser-hidden-paint leg a ("stopped drawing ≥ 29 s after the last verb"; int257 measured 28.4–28.7 s on base AND head):** its clock started at `tIdle`, taken AFTER the 5 s GPU sample that follows the last verb — 5.1 s late — so the stop (the 30 s window + up to one 5 s keeper sweep) cleared 29 s only when the sweep phase landed late. Now judged on the clocks the freeze runs on: from the dialog watch's own `lastVerbAt` (the verdict's input), the freeze must come at the FIRST keeper sweep past `IDLE_PAINT_MS` with the sweep before it inside the window (every sweep seen through a pass-through spy on `idlePaintVerdict`, which the keeper reads off the module object at each sweep); the message decomposes the stop: window + time to the first sweep past it + the sweep gap measured in the run (beside `TICK_MS`) + the freeze's own work. New leg a2 = the RED control: the window shortened to 2 × `TICK_MS` ⇒ the stop moves with it, and the old literal bound is red on the same numbers.
- **test-window-drag-ui C / C2 controls (red 2/3 under the heavy tier's load, green alone):** recorded with Chrome's own `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` 6 — the C2 red pressed at (0, 0): `tabPt` read B's tab before the merged strip was laid out (a fixed 300 ms), the press missed, no drag began and the control read "ended"; int257's C web tab red released on the torn-off window's own content (`div.media-content`) — its rAF-coalesced follow not yet drawn after a fixed 150 ms. Every gesture's premise is now waited for on the page's own frames (`frames()` / `premise()` / `pressPt()`: the press point hit-tests on its target, the follow is drawn, the release point is off the dragged window — its own row in the drop and tab legs), never a wall-clock guess at the frame rate under load.
- **Evidence:** hidden-paint ×3 alone (12/12, 197 s each; leg a stop 34.2 / 34.2 / 34.2 s = 30 s + 4.2 s to the first sweep + 7–8 ms; a2 13.4–13.5 s) and ×2 beside a window-drag-ui run (34.3 / 34.2 s; a2 13.4 s); window-drag-ui ×3 alone and ×2 beside hidden-paint, 112/112 each (~130 s); its C + C2 legs under `setCPUThrottlingRate` 6 — before: 2 red of 5 runs, after: 4/4 green (64/64). The box sat at load 4–12 during these runs (int257's reds were at 25–37): the CPU throttle is the load proof for the drag controls; leg a's verdict reads the sweep gap it measured, whatever the load.

### lane picture-path-nodelay (Opus), one commit on 2baa66aaf (2.369.259)
- **Measured first (test-picture-path-nagle, a REAL agentd from the built bundle under a scratch HOME, the REAL bridge + hub forward, an RFB stand-in on the device that answers a key's RELEASE only — a real VNC server answers input with nothing):** a key press (down + up back to back) came back in **42.0 ms median, p95 43.0** — the press's ACK has no reply to ride, the release sits behind Nagle until the peer's 40 ms delayed-ACK timer. After: **0.70 ms median, p95 1.14**. A stand-in that answered every KeyEvent showed nothing (0.7 ms both ways): the reply carries the ACK — that is why the first probe must not echo.
- **The hops (grep):** stream-relay-rfb.js's connect to the forward, desktop-access.js forwardPort's accept, agentd.js's `tcp-connect` socket — none set noDelay; ws sets it on its own sockets, so the WebSocket hops (browser → bridge, the xpra relay's client, the dial link) were already fine. Also set: browser-access.js's CDP forward accept (the browser view's screencast + input — the desktop forward's twin). Marked `// nagle: ok — <reason>`: the daemon's reverse tunnel accept, the exit-SOCKS accept + its egress connect, its unix socket. Mount / WebDAV forwards untouched, but they ride `tcp-connect` too, so their device-side socket is noDelay now. No keep-alive added: every hop is loopback; the long-lived link keeps its own pings.
- **A daemon that predates the change:** no capability moved; behind today's hub a press+release comes back in 0.56 ms — the hub hop held the release, and once the hub sends it the two writes reach the device together. A pointer stream spaced under 40 ms can still wait at an old daemon's hop until it updates.
- **Gates:** test-architecture §90 (every `net.connect(` / `createConnection(` / `net.createServer(` in the desktop / device / stream-relay / browser-access server files and the whole daemon is followed by `.setNoDelay(true)` or says `// nagle: ok — <reason>`; controls: a planted bare connect, a bare accept, a reason-less ok RED); test-picture-nodelay (fast: a spy on both ends of the hub hop + a desktop-access copy without its call); test-picture-path-nagle (heavy: AFTER's median under half of BEFORE's from the same run, the bundle has exactly one `tsock.setNoDelay(true)`).

### lane slack-search (Opus) — the Channels search box searches Slack too (owner 2026-10-12: 「话说slack不支持搜索吗？」)
- **Cause:** design 010's third reading row is declared per ADAPTER (src/channels/index.js: an adapter without `caps.search` is local-only — `search` / `around` answer `not-supported`); Lark and Gmail declared it, src/channels/slack.js never did, although every workspace app asks `search:read` (slack-manifest USER_SCOPES) and the raw API row already allowed `/api/search.*`. So the search dialog's section two said "This channel offers no search of its own" for Slack.
- **Change (src/channels/slack.js + slack-limits.js):** `caps.search = {via:'query', scope:'search:read', pageSize:20, pagesPerPress:2, perMin:10, cost:1, snippet:true, context:'around', match:'tokens', adds:'unsaved'}`. `search({query, pageToken})` = ONE `search.messages` (the person's words as Slack's `query` VERBATIM — the engine passes no conversation scope today (the dialog's `conv` only shapes the memo's reads), so no `in:` is ever added; the person's own `in:` / `from:` / `before:` ride as typed; `sort=timestamp desc`, `count` 20, the continuation = Slack's page NUMBER ≤ 100, a malformed token refused by name with no request); the envelope judged (no `messages` object / `matches` not a list = not a page); per match `{convId: channel.id, vendorId: ts, at, fromId: user, threadKey: thread_ts | the permalink's ?thread_ts= (the documented match carries no thread field), snippet: the text through `Text.mrkdwnText` (the same reader as a saved record's text) + the name door, cut to SR.SNIPPET_READ_MAX first, ≤ SR.SNIPPET_MAX}`; a channel / ts that is not an id counts malformed. `search.messages` has its OWN per-method bucket (Tier 2, 20/min; the row asks ≤ 10 a sliding minute); a 429 rides `api()`'s existing hold (Retry-After) and reaches the engine as `rate-limited` → its back-off — never a retry loop. `around(convId, {vendorId, at})` (≤ 3 requests, ≤ SR.AROUND_MAX, read-only): `conversations.history` `latest`=ts inclusive (25) — the hit + before; then `oldest`=ts exclusive … ts + max(600 s, half the span the first page covered) (25) — kept ONLY when it has no more (Slack answers a window NEWEST first: a fuller window is not the hit's neighbours, so that side is left out, never drawn with a gap); a hit the channel listing does not hold = a thread reply ⇒ `conversations.replies` named by the reply's own ts (the vendor's documented door: a parent or any message of the thread), root first; a longer thread is read again from the hit (`oldest` inclusive) under its root; `thread_not_found` (a deleted reply) leaves the channel page, `target:false`. Row `context: 'around'` (the engine reads only "declared"; the per-hit choice channel / thread is the adapter's).
- **Words (src/channel-search.js + i18n zh/ja):** the `adds: 'unsaved'` status words said "Asked {vendor}'s whole mailbox: …" — written for Gmail, wrong for any other vendor declaring `unsaved`; now "Asked {vendor}'s whole history: N not saved here — may be related" (zh 全部历史 / ja 全履歴; Gmail's line changes with it — a row's words fit every vendor that declares the row). Slack declares `unsaved` (a hit adds what the copy never saved: a public channel never joined, a thread reply, history before the first read) — never "older".
- **Fixtures:** scripts/fixtures/slack/search.json — `search.messages` pages in Slack's DOCUMENTED shape (docs.slack.dev, read 2026-10-12: matches[] {channel{id,…}, iid, permalink, team, text, ts, type, user, username}, `paging` + `pagination`) — a match with thread_ts, one whose permalink names its thread, one without, a next page, an empty page, odd matches — plus an `archive` (history the first read never reaches: served only to a `latest`-bounded read) and a thread in C0LAUNCH01 (a public channel never joined). slack-vendor.cjs answers `search.messages`, `inclusive: 'true'`, `conversations.replies` named by any message of its thread + `limit`; channels-vendor-stub.cjs steers the Slack fake's scopes header / 429s from mode.json (`slackScopes`, `slack429`).

The stream ran 268 s: 280 B down (greeting + types + 260 B of DH params), 13 B up (version + type) — the credentials never left: the page is `http://<hostname>:3456`, not a secure context, `crypto.subtle` undefined, noVNC's `_negotiateARDAuthAsync` threw in `AESECBCipher._importKey` (unhandled), and vnc-view.js had set no status after `sendCredentials` (连接中… throughout). NEW scripts/test-mac-ard-signin-chrome.mjs (heavy, 24): a real agentd as a Mac + a fixture ARD server (DH 1024 + AES-128-ECB decrypt) behind the real bridge, the page on the box's non-loopback IPv4 (`isSecureContext === false` asserted first) — dialogs closed, 正在登录… ⇒ 已连接 + frame, the exact name/password decrypted, the named status at 20.1 s, phone 390; RED control: e2a303c61's vnc-view.js on the same origin = 连接中… + nothing sent + noVNC's `reading 'importKey'` rejection; CONTROL: on 127.0.0.1 the base page connects.

### lane doc-comments-synced (Opus), one commit on e2a303c61 (2.369.257)
- **The cause (owner 2026-10-12: his 18 comments "disappeared" after updating; "确实是因为不同步 我remote到原来的电脑就有了"):** the Doc window's comment strip lived ONLY in the browser's localStorage (`vs-doc-comments:<host>\u0001<path>`, src/lib/doc-window-ui.js) — per browser profile, so another computer's strip was empty. Chat drafts were already server-side (`drafts` SyncStore, data/drafts.json).
- **The fix:** the strip's record = the `drafts` SyncStore row `doc:<host>\u0001<path>` through the composer's own door (`saveDraft('doc', …)` / `loadDraft` / the StateSync listener, handed in via the door's `deps` — the lazy bundle's own utils copy has no StateSync). PURE `commentRows` (≤ 200 rows, each as commentItem bounds it) + `mergeComments(server, local)` in src/doc-model.js. Writes coalesce 300 ms (a send's emptying at once; flushed on pagehide / close); another client's change patches the keyed rows in place (a pending write of ours wins; an open note box is its own popover, untouched). ONE-TIME MIGRATION per browser per document (`adoptRecord`): after the store's load, the old local rows merge in (server first, local-only ids appended — a stale copy can only add) and the key is removed (rows past the cap stay for room). Send all drops the rows IT sent, by id (a row another client added meanwhile stays). `StateSync.init` now returns its one load (true once the snapshot is in) — a second caller used to get an EMPTY store at once. The strip's add cap moved 20 → 200 (= `LIMITS.sendItems`, what one Send all carries since 2.369.257).
- **Gates:** test-doc-model §3b (the merge table + 2 RED controls), NEW scripts/test-doc-comments-sync.mjs (fast, in-process: the real SyncStore behind the cut-verbatim state-set / state-resync cases + two real client StateSyncs; a `doc:` key round-trips, broadcasts, survives the flush; one init load; a reconnect; RED controls: a chat:-only state-set, the old init), test-record-clear-census (H1 row `oldKey`; H1c drafts writers now chat-input + doc-window-ui + utils), test-doc-window §15 heavy (two pages on one instance: live add / remove both ways, a reload reads the server, the old-key upload, the stale-copy merge, Send all empties the other page, the phone sheet; PNGs desk-a / desk-b / phone).
- **Seen, not fixed (not this lane):** a background tab brought to the front adopts the desktop's shared layout and its own Doc window closes with it (§15 re-opens the document on page B after the switch).

### lane split-keeps-sides (Opus) — the strip's split button keeps every tab on its side (owner 2026-10-12, inc-mv4q1u6b-ksyh), on 5b55012b4
- **The incident:** "这个分屏的逻辑非常诡异，为啥在右侧的标签页分屏后跑到左侧了" — `splitActive` bound "the ACTIVE tab on the left, the partner on the right", so an active tab on the RIGHT of the strip landed in the LEFT pane; with a far partner `enterSplit`'s guest-alone creation also moved the tabs between ([A, B, C], C active, B partner ⇒ [B | A, C]).
- **The rule (design-split-ux.zh.md §8 v3):** a split never moves a tab across the strip. PURE `splitSideFor(chain, anchorId, guestId)` → `{ side, pair }` from `visualTabOrder`; `enterSplit` from tabs cuts the strip when the guest already sits on `side`; a verb that names the other side still moves the guest alone. Wired into `splitActive` (⫿ / `v` / the merge toast), F3's merge-drop split and the button's tooltip (new key "Show side by side — {name} on the left, this tab on the right", zh / ja).
- **Gates:** test-chain-layout ⑰ (2 728 composed splits; controls side-always-right / guest-always-alone red); test-split-ux §14 (heavy, desk 1100 + phone 390, the pre-fix door as control; `SPLIT_UX_ONLY=sides`, `SPLIT_UX_PNG_DIR`) and its legs 4 / 5 / 10 / 11① / L7b rewritten from the old rule (L7b's control is now the pre-fix F3 side).

### lane doc-comment-raw-block (Opus) — a document's raw block is commentable (owner 2026-10-12, a blog draft's `<!-- [CONFIRM-BLOCK …] -->` source box: "这个html部分无法批注")
- **Cause:** the comment popover keyed only to the editor's TEXT selection. A raw block is an atom: a click makes a NodeSelection whose `textBetween` is empty (offerComment returned null), and a mouse selection inside its body is a DOM selection the editor never reads (the node view's `ignoreMutation` swallows it).
- **Change (src/lib/doc-window-model.js + doc-window-ui.js):** PURE `rawCommentAnchor` — a NodeSelection ⇒ the quote `HTML block: <source>` (Front matter / Markdown block; ≤ 200 code points), a DOM selection inside one block ⇒ the selected text (line = the block's + the source lines before it when the box shows source); a paragraph + the block, or two blocks ⇒ refused `text` (THE TEXT RULE WINS — the editor's own selection quotes the paragraph); the source box open ⇒ refused `editing`. `rawCommentTarget` re-finds the block for the strip (its quote nearest the saved line, else the saved pos / line, else gone ⇒ said). The window: `selNow` reads the raw selection first (a `selectionchange` listener scoped to this editor), the same `commentOffer` / `noteBox` / strip; the stored comment gains ONE field `raw {pos, line, kind, offset?}` (`commentItem` drops it — the chat message is unchanged). The strip shows `L9 · HTML block` as a raw comment's context line; a press selects + scrolls to the block. A selection in the open source box ⇒ a toast "Press Finish first …".
- **Measured on the way:** Chrome started NO selection inside the contenteditable=false island (a real CDP drag: mousedown not prevented, no selectstart, no selectionchange) — the block's body now says `user-select:text`. `sourceLine(loaded, doc, pos)` at a block's START answers the block before (a front-matter doc gave L7 for an L9 block) ⇒ the raw block's line reads `pos + 1`.

## 2.369.257 — 2026-10-12

### hot fix hotfix-doc-comments (Opus), one commit on b4659213b (2.369.256)
- **The cause (measured on b4659213b):** the Doc window's Send all spelled EVERY strip item into ONE message (`commentsVerdict` → `commentsText`) and refused `too_long` past `LIMITS.messageBytes` (4096 B UTF-8) with "the comments are longer than 4 KB — send some of them first" — a per-MESSAGE bound applied per SEND, and the strip has no way to send some (only ✕ per comment). CJK is 3 bytes a character: the owner's 18 comments with 200-char quotes are ~10 KB.
- **The fix:** `src/doc-model.js` PURE `commentsBatches(path, items)` (replaces `commentsVerdict`, whose only importers were the engine and test-doc-model) packs the items in order, greedily, into the fewest messages each ≤ `LIMITS.items` (20) rows and ≤ 4096 B measured on the SPELLED text (with the widest `(k/n)` heading the send can have); more than one ⇒ heading `[Doc comments] <path> (k/n)`, the circled numbering continues (`commentsText(path, items, start, of)`); one item bigger than a message of its own gets its note clipped with "…" (counted in `clipped`); the packer asserts its own bound; `too_many` = a per-send sanity cap `LIMITS.sendItems` 200. `src/server/doc-engine.js` `comments()` sends the batches in order through the same door (THE typing sender, sync — one call per message; else one `stashFor` per message — the stash is an array pushed in order and drained in order), answers `{ok, delivered, count, messages, sent, clipped}` or `fail(code, why, {sent})` part-way; `too_long` left STATUS. `src/routes/doc.js` passes `sent` on a failure. `src/lib/doc-window-ui.js`: ok ⇒ "Sent {n} comments" / "Sent {n} comments in {m} messages"; part-way ⇒ the first `sent` leave the strip, "Sent {sent} of {n} — the rest are still here" (zh + ja).
- **Gates:** test-doc-model (rows: 18 CJK ⇒ 4 messages ≤ 4096 B, (k/n), ①…⑱ continuous; 21 ⇒ 20 + 1; a giant note clipped; the 200 cap; the hub: 18 ⇒ n typed calls in order / n stash rows in order / message 2 refused ⇒ `sent` = message 1's count; RED controls: the packer's fit removed ⇒ its assert throws, the numbering restarting ⇒ red), test-doc-comment-pop, test-architecture, test-spend-paths, build + i18n-check, heavy test-doc-window, the fast gate.

### lane browser-tmpdir-socket-length (Opus) — HOT FIX: every new agent browser on the owner's hub died FATAL "Socket path too long"
- **Measured (production, read-only):** session 44a6501f's CLI answer `FATAL:chrome/browser/process_singleton_posix.cc:313] Socket path too long: <the hub's data dir, 51 bytes>/browser-env/tmp/org.chromium.Chromium.2QgDc3/SingletonSocket` (the owner's home path elided), three relaunches then `[launch_failed]`. TMPDIR (lane browser-resource-care, B-afeb) = 67 bytes + Chrome's `/org.chromium.Chromium.XXXXXX/SingletonSocket` (45) = 112; Chrome refuses `>= sizeof(sun_path)` = 108, so TMPDIR has 62. Pods' data dirs are short (no gate saw it); an adopted daemon kept its Chrome, so only a fresh launch showed it.
- **Fix:** PURE `browserTmpDir` (browser-profiles.js) — the data path only while it fits, else `/var/tmp/vibespace-<uid>/browser-tmp` (disk-backed; a tmpfs/ramfs `/var/tmp` read off /proc/self/mountinfo ⇒ the same shape under `os.tmpdir()` with a warn), the why logged once. `F.makeBrowserTmpDir` makes it 0700 and refuses a per-uid name that is not this uid's own directory (lstat; a planted symlink ⇒ null + a warn, the CLI keeps its own TMPDIR) — the ONE maker for the keeper's runtime and browser-env's `tmpDir()` (the `/resolve` answer → the CLI's `childEnv` ⑧; the Xvfb auth file rides the same TMPDIR). `launchFatalOf` names a known launch FATAL (`socket_path_too_long`, `tmp_dir_unwritable`; never a profile lock) in `launch_failed` on both launch sites, so `vibespace-browser` prints the reason and the fix.
- **Measured against the OS (test-browser-tmpdir ②):** Linux binds a 108-byte sun_path (no NUL) and refuses 109 (EINVAL) — Chrome's `>=` check is one byte stricter, so the verdict moves at a 63-byte TMPDIR. CONTROL: the .255 rule's 112-byte socket path is refused by the kernel; the verdict's dir binds.
- **Gates:** test-browser-tmpdir (new, fast: PURE table, the OS bind control + boundary, the classifier, the maker incl. the planted-symlink refusal and the RAM fallback warn, the REAL browser-env wiring + the keeper's one maker).

### cache-bounds-stall-control — test-cache-bounds' timing bounds judged against a same-run control (Opus), on d8a709566 (2.369.254)
- **Red:** GitHub run 38184698598 (fast shard) and its --failed rerun: §13 `stall < 100` failed at 111 / 101 ms on the 4-core runner, while the fold witness `_allRows ×0` held both times.
- **Cause (measured):** the probe started BEFORE the test's own `sync0 = t.aggregate(q)`. That is a sync fold of the fixture (28 ms idle here, 33–40 ms at load 10–12) and it is the reference, not the product's walk. With the probe after it, the walk stalls 0–8 ms.
- **Change (suite only):** §13 judges the witness (`_allRows ×0`). The stall is judged by `stall <= control + fold/2`, where control = the same hook work driven directly on a copy of the fixture and fold = a sync fold of the same query (median of 3), both measured in the same run. Neither of the brief's rules bites on this fixture: the r2rung mutant's fold on the loop adds 23–50 ms (+50 ms passes it; ×3.1 sits on a 3× line). The r2rung control now also asserts that the rule FAILS. §14 `took14 < 3000` becomes a witness, code ≠ DEADLINE, plus a mutant deaf to its worker's death (DEADLINE ⇒ RED). §26 `took2 < 200` becomes its witness (`_coldWalks` +1; r3stuck ×2 ⇒ RED). Each bound prints one line: measured / control / rule.

### agent-window-no-steal — an agent's new window never takes the person's focus, on c05302462
- **Owner (2026-10-11):** his flight-research conversation started six agent-browser Chromes in a day (four in five minutes, 18:35–18:40Z); every one opened its pane in front of his work. **Measured road:** window-targets-engine `desktop-app-opened` → app.js `agentBrowserPlacement` → `openDesktopApp(…)` → createWindow's trailing `focusWindow` (a split guest: `bindSplit` focus `guest`) raised the chat's frame over the active window and took `activeWindowId`; the xpra view's `connected` then focused its IME box (the caret left the person's text box even for a window behind); a fresh satellite (`onSatellite`) `revealWindow` + `handle.focus()`; the live view's auto-bind (`autoBindLiveViews`) the same split focus.
- **The rule (kb-patterns):** an agent's action may PLACE a window; only a person's action may FOCUS one. PURE `agentWindowPlacement` (src/lib/desktop-app-placement.js, extends D3's verdict): chat shown on this desk ⇒ `beside` (its chain, createWindow's asked `quiet`), chat on another desk ⇒ `desk` (created, `moveWindowToDesktop` — hidden there, no switch), chat minimized ⇒ `own` behind the active window (minimized while a drag/resize or a text box is live), no chat here ⇒ nothing (D3), phone ⇒ its own window never shown; `focus:false`, `deskSwitch:false` always unless the new setting `desktop.agentWindowsFront` (default OFF) — then exactly D3's old answer with focus. `satelliteFocus` (rule 3): a fresh satellite of an agent-opened record is placed behind + pulses unless its main pane is the active window. New WM doors: `placeBehind(id)` (restack only) + `markArrived(id)` (`window-arrived` ⇒ `.taskbar-item.arrived` / `#mobile-nav-title.arrived` pulse + accent until focusWindow clears it). xpra-view `mayFocus` (the pane focuses its IME on connect only while it is the active window). A relaunch successor (`retarget`) never revealed — unchanged.
- **Not changed:** the person's own launches (Apps dialog, Browse yourself, whole desktop, a vibespace-window request he pressed) keep front + focus; the phone live-view auto-open (lane S4, the owner asked for it: it opens only when that chat is the shown window) keeps its focus + "Back to the chat" toast.

### machine-app-crop — one app of a paired Windows / macOS machine as its own window over the existing VNC path (owner 2026-10-11 "都做吧" — route ② of B-bb0b; Opus; on 82859e6f5)
- **Measured first:** "Run on its desktop…" answered `{ok, hostId, platform, shown}` — no process at all (Windows: `Start-Process %ComSpec% /d /s /c "<line>"`, so the app is a CHILD of that cmd.exe; macOS: `nohup sh -lc "$1" &`, and `open -a` hands the launch to launchd — no lineage). The run now takes `window: true` ⇒ the plan prints `vibespace-launched <pid> <the machine's epoch ms>` (Windows `-PassThru`; macOS `$!` + `date +%s`) and the answer carries `launched`; the plain "Run…" plan is byte for byte the old one.
- **Device ops `window-track` / `window-pin`** (three touches each: agentd handlers + hello-ack capabilities + `DeviceManager.windowTrack / windowUntrack / windowPin` gated; replies in the id-keyed set; the push `window-rect` has its own branch BEFORE prevControl; a watch belongs to its link — the link's death stops it and the client re-arms it by its window, re-pinned): PURE src/machine-window.js — Windows ONE `-EncodedCommand` PowerShell with user32 (EnumWindows + GetWindowThreadProcessId + IsWindowVisible + GetWindowRect, DwmGetWindowAttribute EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS, DPI-aware; the process table only while finding), macOS ONE osascript JXA over CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo + NSRunningApplication.launchDate. Which window: lineage of the launched pid ⇒ started after the run (2 s slack) ⇒ new since the first look; the largest of equals. Find ≤ 20 s at 250 ms; follow at 100 ms, pushes ≥ 100 ms apart (the latest never dropped); `gone` ends it. Pin = HWND_TOPMOST after a restore / HWND_NOTOPMOST; a Mac ACTIVATES the app (no topmost) — before the person's input too (≥ 3 s apart). A watch that ends (untrack, link, window) undoes its own pin.
- **Hub:** src/server/machine-app.js (track / long-poll watch / on-top / untrack — routes `/api/desktop/machine-app/*`, human_only): ONE pinned window per machine (pinning one unpins the other; every pane hears which is on top); a page that stops polling for 30 s ends its watch; a pin the hub could not undo is REPORTED (`pinsLeft`, a journal line), never forced.
- **Page:** src/lib/machine-app.js — the `machine-app` window (not persisted): the same stream + sign-in as the whole desktop (`machineViewOpts`, now shared); the crop is LAYOUT (noVNC's screen moved into a stage sized + shifted by `cropLayout` inside a box the app's size), so noVNC's own pointer math lands every click on the app; captured drags leaving the box are held at its edge, presses / wheels outside dropped; gone ⇒ the words + "Open its whole desktop" / "Run again"; the dialog gains "Run as its own window…" (the default for `open -a …` / `start "" …`) and closes once the window opens.
- **Measured off-box:** the generated PowerShell (find / follow / gone / pin) ran under real PowerShell 7.4.6 with user32 swapped for a stub class: UTF-8 titles (CJK + quotes), the DWM rectangle, the process table, `gone`, `ok` — parsed by the PURE reader. Not run: real Windows / macOS (no paired machine may be touched) — the manual check for WIN-DESK1 is in the lane report.
- **Gates:** test-machine-window (fast, 71: parsers, picker, crop + pointer math, the runner over a fake spawn, the capability gate + RED controls, the hub's pins, the launch report); test-machine-app-chrome (heavy, 23: two REAL agentd copies + a stub RFB server, desk 1100 + phone 390, PNGs desk / phone / gone).
- **User line (for CHANGELOG*.md at integration — test-changelog-style ④ refuses a .252 entry on this .250 base):** en "An app you run on a paired Windows or Mac computer can be shown as its own window instead of the whole desktop — one app at a time." · zh "在已配对的 Windows 或 Mac 电脑上运行的应用，可以作为独立窗口显示，而不必打开整个桌面——一次一个应用。" · ja "ペアリングした Windows や Mac で実行したアプリを、デスクトップ全体ではなく単独のウィンドウとして表示できます——一度に一つのアプリ。"

### channels-fold-default — the Channels list starts folded (owner 2026-10-11)

**Lane channels-fold-default (the owner, 2026-10-11: "能不能让 channels 默认收缩，不然翻找起来很困难").** Every account section of the Channels panel opened EXPANDED with all its conversations (the owner's Lark: 81); only the built-in agents watcher folded by default. Now: channel-groups-view.js `accountFoldDefault` — a section starts FOLDED unless a row in it `needsYou` (statusTag awaiting / unknown / assigned / held / direct, or an @ of the person) or the account itself needs signing in (dot bad / warn / attn); the panel decides that default ONCE per page per account (`DEFAULT_FOLD`) and holds it — a row that comes to need the person later raises the folded head's "N need attention" (accent) + a dot, never opens the list. The person's open / close is user state in the SAME map (`channelsPanelFolds['acct:<id>']`, literal booleans, ≤ 64, pruned to live accounts at every write — `foldsToWrite`) and wins both ways (`accountFold`). A folded head says what is inside: count · N need attention · N unread (CSS-shown only while folded). A filter OPENS a section holding a match virtually (its matches only — its own rows + the server's search answer for it; never written; cleared ⇒ the fold is back). Accounts with no choice is `null` in `foldsFrom` and folds when every section in it does. Non-built-in sources (the webhook door) fold the same way; the agents watcher keeps its rule; the internal block is unchanged. The All tab stays the one newest-first list (design 008 paging); its internal band and the account sections below share the folds. Rows are keyed and kept: a fold toggles a class, nothing is rebuilt. Note: a user state that already holds `accounts: false` (any earlier fold write wrote the whole map) keeps Accounts open; the sections still fold.
**Gates:** test-channels-groups-ui (fast, +16: needsYou / default / choice both ways / virtual filter / map pruning + bound / wiring pins; 2 CONTROLS — a copy opening sections by default, a copy ignoring the remembered fold — red; `foldsFrom(null).accounts` pin now `null`; the copy rewrites every `./channel-focus.js` import); NEW test-channels-fold-default (heavy, chrome, the real panel over a stub server — 3 accounts / 60 conversations at 1100 + 390 px: first paint, a new attention row stays folded with count + dot, open / close survives a reload both ways, the filter finds a row in folded Gmail and restores; 2 CONTROL bundles red). PNGs: /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/channels-fold-default/{desk,phone,desk-filter}.png.

### lark-search-miss — the Lark search feed stops flapping and nagging (owner 2026-10-11, screenshot: "搜索漏掉了 200 条中的 7 条 (3.5%) — 已恢复为每个会话单独检查 · 话题：250 条搜索结果带话题 · 检查新话题 7872 次，发现 159 个" — "老有这个提示是咋回事 能根治吗？"; Opus; on 82859e6f5)
- **Measured first (the owner's instance, read-only: adapters.json's lark `feed` row + the stored records' metadata, never a body):** the 7 misses in the demoting window = **6 `system` records** (a member joined / left — Lark's message search does not index them; each fetched 66–232 s after it was written) + **1 `post`** the per-chat poll fetched 223 s in (the search had last looked ~90 s in; later posts of the same chat WERE found ⇒ the index lag). Lifetime `missedTypes`: system 51 · text 5 · image 1 · media 1 · post 1 — **51 of 59 = system**. No thread reply, no bot message, no chat type among them. The flap: promote at ≤ 2 % over 200 + one cold cycle, demote at > 2 % over ≥ 20 — the system bursts crossed the line both ways every cycle, and the demoted line was a warning re-worded with the live rate.
- **Fix at the root (src/channel-feed.js, PURE):** every miss is a NAMED memo row `{id, convId, chatType, msgType, createdAt, firstSeenAt, ageAtFirstSeen, searchWindow, inThread, fromBot, hadSearchHit, cls}` with ONE class (`classifyMiss`, first match): excluded-type / excluded-chat / bot / thread (the adapter's declared `caps.changeFeed.blind` — Lark: `msgTypes ['system']`, `threadReplies: true` = the topic check is the replies' declared source, `bots: false`: no app card was ever missed) — never counted, not even as a sample; gap (no window searched it) — the catch-up's; lag (the search last looked < 10 min after it was written) and unknown — COUNTED. The window's overlap is LEARNED: `lagMargin` = p95 of the lag rows' `ageAtFirstSeen` (newest 20, bounded 30 s – 10 min, persisted as `feed.lagMargin`), `overlapOf` = max(setting, margin) feeds every window AND the coverage judge. The memo: `<account>/feed-misses.json` (≤ 500 rows, 0600, written only when a miss is named, dropped with the account — channel-store `feedMiss*`).
- **Promotion rule:** `modeVerdict` also needs the last `PROMOTE_CYCLES` = 3 full polling cycles CLEAN (`cleanMs` = now − the newest counted miss) and holds a demotion `DEMOTE_HOLD_MS` = 6 h; demote unchanged. A feed row measured under the old rule starts over ONCE (`measureRev` 2 — measuring, samples cleared: the old counts included records the search cannot return).
- **The words:** ONE quiet line that changes only on a flip — "新消息：搜索每 {s} 秒 + 每会话核对（核实中）" / "…（搜索漏 {pct}%，{class}）" (the flip's own numbers, `lastFlip.cls`) / "新消息：搜索每 {s} 秒（已核实无漏）"; no warning style for a demotion; the facts (live numbers, the learned overlap, the classes not counted, the last 20 misses with class, the topic checks) are its tooltip (`feedFactsText`); the topic-check line left the row. The adapter view (`GET /api/channels/adapters/:id/view`, the digest) carries `misses` (last 20, classified), `missClasses`, `missUncounted`, `lagLearned`, `overlapSettingSec`.
- **Tests:** test-channel-feed ⑪ (fixtures lag / thread / bot / excluded type + chat / gap / unknown; the memo bound + disk read; lagMargin p95 + bounds; a stub search lagging 90 s found WHOLE after the overlap learns; 3 clean cycles + the 6 h hold; RED controls: an unclassified miss counted as 0, the window without the learned overlap, the promote rule with one clean cycle); test-channels-engine (I2) (the memo named + persisted + dropped on disconnect, hadSearchHit both ways, the learned overlap) + the census row `feedConvAt`; test-channel-caps (the 3 spellings, the old warning words ⇒ RED control, the tooltip, the panel pins); new heavy test-feed-miss-ui (real server + chrome, the owner's seeded state: one quiet line, the tooltip facts, the view's misses, carrying). Moved: the promote legs of test-channels-aggregate / -engine wait 3 cycles; the lark-shape declaration pin keeps its tail.
- **Deviation:** the brief's `GET /api/channels/adapters/:id` does not exist — the per-account read is `…/:id/view` (it carries the misses). The heavy leg is its own suite (the aggregate-ui world has no change feed and a 90 s real-time lag would take ~50 min to flip): the account card is a VENDOR account's, so the harness marks the fake's digest row as Lark (one field, CDP) — the feed facts are the server's own.

### bypass-no-prompts — a bypassPermissions conversation never shows a permission card (owner 2026-10-10: "claude code 那个动不动就弹 permission 的毛病能禁止吗？我都开了 bypassPermissions 了就是不要看到这个"; Opus; on 642984620)
- **Measured first (the real CLI 2.1.288, a scratch HOME + CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, `--permission-mode bypassPermissions --permission-prompt-tool stdio`, haiku, 4 short turns; probe /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/bypass-no-prompts/measure.mjs):** under bypass the Bash tool's own safety check still asks — `decision_reason_type: "safetyCheck"`, `classifier_approvable: false`, `suppress_always_allow_rule: true`, `permission_suggestions: []`, "This shell -c script runs rm and could not be checked" (circuitBreaker `dangerousRemoval` in the binary) — for a `-c` script its parser cannot read that runs rm: a function definition (`bash -c 'f() { rm -f "$1"; }; f x'`) and an ANSI-C string (`bash -c $'rm -f x\necho g'`) asked; a plain `bash -c "echo x; rm -f f"`, `/usr/bin/env bash -c`, a custom `wrap.sh bash -c "cd d && rm -f f2"`, a `for` loop, `eval` and `IFS=… read` did NOT (8 shapes). **A PreToolUse hook answering `permissionDecision: "allow"` does NOT suppress it**: the hook ran for all 4 calls and both asks still arrived (option (b) closed). Not measured this round: the WebFetch provenance re-ask (read in the 2.1.281 binary by lane S1) and MCP asks — both are `can_use_tool` and take the same door.
- **Shipped = (c) the protocol door, src/server/bypass-auto-allow.js:** in the claude stdout consumer, right before the live feed, a `can_use_tool` reaching a chat session whose `_permissionMode` is `bypassPermissions` (read per ask — the CLI's init / set_permission_mode facts; a switch away stops it at the next ask) is answered ALLOW with the exact input through THE one answer path (helper-asks `answerUnasked` → permission-answer.js) and never reaches the normalizer: no card, nothing pending, main-ask / the parked-turn machinery see nothing. Written down three ways: a `system`/`vs_auto_allow` record appended to the buffer after the allow (the normalizer's quiet line — the dim harness notice with `say: 'bypass-auto-allow'`; on a rebuild the replayed ask comes off its card), a `[bypass] auto-allow {op, tool, reasonType, head}` row in the server console ring the incident bundle carries (head through redactSecrets), and `session._autoAllowed` in the session list → Session Properties "Auto-allowed under bypass". A helper's ask and the provenance re-ask are allowed the same way; AskUserQuestion (a question, not a permission) never. No silent failure: no live process ⇒ the door steps aside and the card forms; an auto-allowed call whose result reads as a denial turns its line into a warning.
- **The switch:** `permissions.bypassAnswersAsks` (default ON; Chat category — Settings has no permission-mode row to sit beside), read server-side at every ask; OFF = the card as before. docs/settings.md regenerated.
- **Tests:** test-bypass-auto-allow (new, fast, 48: the measured ask ⇒ one allow frame with the exact input, no card, no pending ask, the line + head, the audit row, the count, the rebuild; refused ⇒ warning; no pty ⇒ card; switch OFF / every other mode / mid-session switch ⇒ card; helper + provenance allowed, AskUserQuestion not; RED controls = the door with the switch check / the mode check removed). Census moves: test-helper-ask ⑲ (the door reaches answerPermission through helper-asks), test-unknown-records (no new `msg.type ===` in the consumer; the renderer branch stays inside its 1600-char window — the words moved to `bypassLineWords`).
- **Heavy, by hand on the real CLI 2.1.288 (not a committed suite: it needs a pool member's access token; probe /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/bypass-no-prompts/door-probe.mjs — the worktree's REAL door + normalizer fed the way the stdout consumer feeds them):** switch ON — the CLI asked once (`safetyCheck`, the function-def shape), 0 cards, max pending asks 0, the tool ran (its file removed), 1 quiet line + 1 audit row, `_autoAllowed` 1, the turn ended `success`; switch OFF — the same ask formed the card (pending 1) and ran only after Allow (0.8 s later). One OFF run had the model skip the call (no ask, no run) — rerun.
- **Limits:** the quiet line and the count live in the server's buffer / session — a server restart rebuilds from the CLI's own stdout ring, which never held our record, so the line and the count of earlier auto-allows are gone after a restart (the console-ring rows went into any incident bundle taken before it). ### lane browser-stderr-pipe (Opus) — the agent browser can no longer freeze on a log pipe nobody reads
- **Incident userW inc-mv2qf3xs-7g87 (2026-10-10 18:32Z, 2.369.245)** + the fleet's weeks of "DevTools accepts, answers 0 bytes" (6 hangs / 26 h). MEASURED on 642984620 with the pinned driver 0.38.1 (scratch HOME, its own Xvfb): the daemon's fds 0/1/2 are /dev/null; Chrome's fd 2 is `pipe:[…]` whose only other end is the daemon's fd 14. Its source (cli/src/native/cdp/chrome.rs `try_launch_chrome`) spawns Chrome with `.stderr(Stdio::piped())` and reads it only when the launch FAILS (DevToolsActivePort is the success path) — on success nothing ever reads it.
- **Numbers:** idle on about:blank Chrome writes ≈ 3.7 KB at launch then ≈ 5 B/s ⇒ 64 KB in ≈ 3.4 h (the fleet's rate); with `--enable-logging=stderr` + a page logging every 5 ms the pipe held 63 502 B after 3 s, the main thread sat in `anon_pipe_write`, `/json/version` answered 0 bytes at 5.0–6.5 s (3 runs). The whole process group shares that fd 2.
- **Fix (owner ruling 19:02Z): the pin is 0.38.2** — agent-browser 0.38.2 (2026-10-01, #2003 "Fixed Chrome freezing after launch") drains Chrome's stderr for the browser's lifetime (`chrome-stderr-drain` thread). `AGENT_BROWSER_CLI.table` 0.38.1 → 0.38.2, `CLI_PIN_RECORD` re-measured (tarball 52 980 321 B, unpacked 117 855 861 B, sha1 3eeb49e7…), package.json's install line + deploy/docker/Dockerfile. Measured under the same spam: 0.38.1 froze at 6.0 s; 0.38.2 answered 30/30 asks over 30 s, its Chrome's fd 2 still a pipe — drained. **The 0.38.2 diff carries more than the pipe fix** (9 commits): /dev/shm < 256 MiB ⇒ the driver adds `--disable-dev-shm-usage` (#1890 — a 64 MiB pod mount now gets it), Browser Use Cloud V4 (#1879), auth-vault login control selection (#2014), chat mode allows webmcp/skills (#2015), Kernel profile object (#2004), eve 0.57 (#1945); `--help` gains lines (Browser Use env, chat, login), removes no verb or flag. No launch/CDP surface we pin changed.
- **Defence in depth (src/browser-stderr.js + the keeper):** the keeper's config gains `--disable-logging --log-level=3` for a record launched with them (`rec.quietLog`, the automationFlag precedent: a browser running at the update keeps its view until its next launch; a provider's own `AGENT_BROWSER_ARGS` gets them too; a user's own logging switch wins) — 98 B vs 11 276 B of Chrome's own stderr in 20 s on the same page; no spawn of ours leaves an unread pipe (census). A keeper-written launcher (fd 2 a file) was built and measured (held 30/30 on 0.38.1 with 1.1 MB in the file) and dropped with the bump: it changed every default/pinned-build launch view (test-browser-builds red) for a fault the pin removes.
- **The keeper names it** (a browser whose daemon still runs 0.38.1 — `rec.cli` keeps a running browser's version until its next start): at the unresponsive verdict it samples /proc twice (fd 2 a pipe + the main thread still in pipe_write) ⇒ `rec.unresponsive.cause = 'stderr-pipe-full'`, a journal line (the incident bundle) and the Browser panel row's words ("…a fault of the browser driver 0.38.1, fixed in 0.38.2 — Restart starts it again on the updated driver…"). Reports only — Restart stays the user's act or a gated agent's.
- **Tests:** test-browser-stderr-pipe (fast, 37): quiet-switch table + `--enable-logging` src census (planted RED), the stdio rule over src/server/browser-*.js + browser-facts (planted unread pipe / no-stdio spawn RED) + the rule in miniature (a 200 KB writer ends with a reader, blocks on an unread pipe), the verdict + controls (a reader drained it / fd 2 a file / answered), the pin ≥ 0.38.2 in all three spellings, the keeper wiring, the words en/zh/ja. test-browser-unresponsive ④ (heavy): the real keeper names the cause once per run + its journal line. test-browser-stderr-pipe-real (heavy, real Chrome): the 0.38.1 hang + the verdict over the real /proc (VIBESPACE_AB_BASE), the 0.38.2 pin held ≥ 3×, the quiet legs.

### webhook-l1-server — the webhook channel, server half (design v4 §2–§11; Opus)
- **What:** a built-in `webhook` adapter (a path = a conversation, callers = external peers with their own `vswh_` tokens, the owner the only identity) with the inbound door `POST /hook/<slug>` (src/webhook-auth.js ①–⑫, every refusal before the body; one 401 / 405 / 429 shape), the record mapping (src/webhook-record.js; facts `event` + `fields` added to FACT_SCHEMA), replies as the owner (`reply --to` ⇒ the record's caller, `ambiguous-caller` otherwise; `composeEach` = one proposal per caller), delivery none / reply-url (src/egress-fence.js: resolve once, pinned, no 3xx, 10 s, 64 KiB) / poll (a bounded per-caller queue + the caller's long-poll), the per-path `wakesPerHour` budget before `paceVerdict` (+ `all` ⇒ digest there), the `fact` rule, the `channel-webhook` record-clear kind (store door `rewriteRecords`), and the engine's `builtin` branches replaced by declared module facts (test-architecture §88).
- **Contract:** `PUSH_TRANSPORTS` closed (+ `http-inbound`, `long-poll`), caps `honestyLine` (`option`/`never`), `policyDefault` ∈ `policyModes`, `sendStartsTurn`, `kind`; module `removable` / `listed` / `seed` / `reach` validated; prepareSend passes `recipients`.
- **Census moves:** mount-reader-census channel-store 30 → 31 (`rewriteRecords`); test-record-clear-census `adapterFor` gate row (the adapter's `findRecord` dep reads its own indexed conversation); test-channel-filter census +3 webhook rows, RULE_KINDS 13; test-channel-placement + the webhook row; server.js held at 1907 lines (the JSON skip folded into the existing two lines).
- **Deviations from the brief / design (said, not hidden):** caps `budget` has no `settingKey` (webhook is no manifest vendor); the auth.js line exempts `/hook/<slug>` for ANY method (so a non-POST is the route's 405); a Bearer caller's replies are signed with `sha256(token)` (the record keeps only the hash); with sign-in ON an agent bearer alone is the cookie gate's 401 — the route's own 403 shows beside a cookie (heavy) and on an auth-off instance (fast); scope digests are not yet counted by the per-path budget; the path's `fromName` is the option `replyName` (the fromName census keeps that word for ladder deliveries).

### webhook-l3-cli-pair — the webhook channel's agent words, manuals and the interconnect skeleton (design v4 §7 / §9 / §12 L3; Opus; stacked on L1)
- **What:** `vibespace-channels compose webhook/<path> --caller <id>[,<id>]|all "…"` (agent route `POST /api/agent/channels/compose {conv, caller}` → the engine's `composeEach`, one proposal per caller); an ambiguous `reply` / a named refusal prints the callers as `c-… "name"` rows + the two ways on (exit 1); `read webhook/<path>` prints a `callers:` header (id, name, kind, delivery, last call, generation — the adapter's new `callersOf`, through a passthrough on the wrapper and `readFor`); the CLI's ANSWER DOOR (`answerOf`, every server answer parsed there) withholds any `vswh_` value; caller ids / names reach the agent through `agentId` (readFor, the outbound refusal rows) with peer-text-census rows; no verb makes a path or mints a token.
- **Interconnect phase 1:** PURE `src/webhook-pair.js` (the `vswp_` one-time code — 10 min, single use — the hook URL verdict, `completionVerdict` + `complete` = the verdict BEFORE the one write, the bounded pending memo, the canonical peer payload `{text, threadKey, inReplyTo, attachments, from}` + `X-VibeSpace-Peer-Version: 1`); routes `POST /api/channels/webhook/paths/:slug/pair-code` (owner, A) · `POST /api/channels/webhook/join` (owner, B — posts the completion frame through the egress fence and writes ONLY on A's 200) · `POST /api/channels/webhook/:slug/pair` (L1's 501 → the completion, refused before a byte unless a code is pending); callersStore `pair()` (a `peer` row with its own token + the peer's token sealed, re-pair rotates in place) / `outKeyOf` / `freshId`; a peer send = the canonical payload signed as our caller id on the peer's path over `/hook/<slug>`; `/hook` reads a peer's call with the fixed mapping (author = the registered name, `from.name` only a fact).
- **Docs:** `vibespace-docs channels` (Webhook paths section), the index-manual CLI line, kb-api, kb-features, kb-file-structure, docs/design-webhook.zh.md §16 as-built, docs/design-instance-pairing.md marked superseded (candidate 3 = webhook §12).
- **Deviations:** `vibespace-msg list` lists sessions, not channel conversations — the path shows as `webhook/<slug>` in `vibespace-channels list` (heavy leg); the pending half of a code lives in memory (a restart voids it); the pairing has owner ROUTES only (no owner CLI by design; the Channels-window paste box is L2 / a follow-up).

### lane belt-nested-opener (Opus) — the frame rule inerts to a FIXED POINT; a nested opener never leaves a live frame (B-2103)
- **Finding (lane lark-unknown-tags, 2026-10-09):** `inertFrames` folded in ONE pass, so `<system-reminder <system-reminder>>` became `<system-reminder [system-reminder]>` — the inner tag inerted, the outer opener re-assembled by the pass (its attribute run had stopped at the inner `<`), live by `carriesFrame`. Every door through the belt (Gmail, Slack, agent messages, job output, page dialogs, For-you quotes) took the single pass; only the Lark reader's fence looped.
- **Fix (src/channel-record.js `foldFrames`):** the fold repeats until the text stops changing, ≤ `FRAME_PASSES` = 4 (one level per pass; linear). Still live after that ⇒ `FRAME_WITHHELD` (`[peer text withheld: a nested frame could not be inerted]`). One function, three callers: `inertFrames` (so peerText / peerName / inertFrameLine / the record + block schema), the Lark fence `quoteTags` (its own loop and global pattern copy removed) and src/browser-stuck.js's byte-equal copy (`pageText`). src/peer-text.js `toAgentText` asserts `!carriesFrame` over the whole joined output, else the placeholder (cut to `max`).
- **Why 4, not the brief's "cut by the byte bound":** a 5-deep nest is ~90 chars, far under any bound — so the bound is the pass count itself, and a deeper nest is withheld whole rather than walked.
- **Tests:** test-peer-text-census §1 fixed point (1–4 deep, split, benign `<b>`, 5-deep withheld, idempotent), §3 V8 nested opener at every SITES door + engine read / thread / search (the judge RED on a belt-bypassing and a one-pass door), §4 controls (one pass + no assert ⇒ LIVE; the assert alone withholds; bound removed ⇒ placeholder never fires), §5 the copy's 12 lines + `foldFrames` byte-equal and THE FOLD HAS ONE SPELLING (a door with its own pass red by name); test-peer-parsers `foldFrames` row; re-aimed anchors in test-channel-blocks / test-channel-record (the fence) and test-browser-stuck 1.2.

### lane reaction-strip-anchor (Opus) — B-59ff: a late reaction strip above the view never moves the reader's row
- **Measured cause (chrome, 1280 + 390 px; the base by a sibling session, parts/measured-base.md, + test-channel-threads-ui (k)):** the trickle asks only rows ≥ 10 % in view (IntersectionObserver), so its strip always grows a VISIBLE row; the browser anchors on the first visible row, so every row BELOW the grown one moved 34 px with scrollTop unchanged (the r1 PICK_ROW symptom). A row wholly above the view the browser held (0 px); the row cut by the top edge it answered with scrollTop −36 (72 px). The brief's "row above the viewport" premise is not what ad7a18198 does.
- **Fix (r2 — the 主开发's ruling: opting the whole list out of the browser's anchoring left every other late writer unheld):** ONE ResizeObserver over every list row (channel-window.js, beside observeRows; its callback runs after layout, before paint): each changed row's place before the change = its place now less the growth of the changed rows above it; the reader's row = the row at the view's middle BEFORE the change; PURE `anchorDelta({rowTop, rowBottom, viewportTop, deltaH})` (channel-paging.js) moves scrollTop by the change of every row above it. `.chanwin-list { overflow-anchor: none }` = the ONE mechanism; `.chanmsg-rx { min-height: var(--reaction-strip-h) }` (24 / 28 px touch) reserves a known strip at first paint. A mutation landing inside a pass tears it: (a) the -wal answered old, the -shm new ⇒ the -shm alone refreshed beside a -wal size from before the commit — the runner's pair (:144 `[shm]`, then :148 reads that as the checkpoint's refresh); (b) x.db answered old, the truncate, -wal and -shm new ⇒ `[shm, wal]` without the db (:148 alone). A traced copy (each stat answer, each suite mutation, each invalidate, wall ms) caught (b) naturally: 1/3 alone, then 3/320 (8 parallel × 40 beside 24 busy node loops), every trace `stat x.db = 4096|a · SUITE truncate · stat -wal = 0|c · stat -shm · INVALIDATE shm,wal`. The base suite alone 0/10, beside 32 loops 0/10, under the 2 ms stall preload 0/10, pinned to 2 CPUs with 8 loops 0/10, 8 × 10 parallel 0/80: the window is one threadpool `readlink` (≈ 0.3 ms of a 30 ms tick), not timer lateness.
- **Cause — the product; the suite only met it:** on a real device each `statRemote` is a network round trip, and a writer commits (-wal frames, then the -shm index) or checkpoints (db, then -wal / -shm) between two of them. (a) is the very disk I/O error the outgrown gate exists for (the reader re-reads a -shm pointing past its -wal cap); (b) serves a -wal / -shm after a checkpoint over a db's pre-checkpoint pages for one tick.
- **Fix (src/device-mount.js heldRefresher):** a family (x.db + -wal / -shm held) with a file that moved in the pass gets a second look in the same pass — x.db, -shm, then -wal last — before the outgrown judgment: what moved in either look is refreshed together, and the -wal size judged is no older than any move that triggered the refresh. `cand` became a Map (abs → moved); a plain file never gets a second look (no extra device stat; the other sections' stat counts unchanged).
- **Legs + control:** §12b (scripts/test-pull-refresh.mjs; §12 and every other § unchanged) — the fake device lands the change right after a chosen answer, so the torn pass is at a fixed point: a commit right after the -wal's answer leaves the family alone; a checkpoint right after a pass's first answer refreshes all three in one invalidate. CONTROL = the same suite over a git-archive tree of ad7a18198's src: 10/10 red on both legs (`["t.db-shm"]` and `["t.db-shm","t.db-wal"]` — the runner's shapes).
- **Timings (fixed):** alone 10/10 green 3.28–3.40 s (box load 15–21 from the other lanes); beside 24 busy node loops 10/10 green 3.35–3.43 s; the traced twin 0/320 (old 3/320). It stays a fast parallel row. test-device-mount-rclone (heavy, the pinned rclone 1.69.3 copied into the worktree) ALL PASS 17 in 16.7 s; test-architecture ALL PASS (658); build rc 0.

### Lane daemon-orphan-end — a browser daemon (and its Xvfb) with no browser, no lease and no conversation is ended by the keeper, by identity

- **The fact (a fleet pod, 2026-10-07):** 13 `agent-browser` daemons + 7 `Xvfb -auth …/agent-browser-xauth-*` with no Chrome child, up to 2.6 d old, each from a conversation that had ended or a temporary browser recorded "stopped (idle)". The keeper ended a daemon only on Stop / Forget / a leased browser's idle ceiling.
- **The rule (PURE src/browser-orphans.js):** `daemonVerdict` ends a daemon the keeper started (its record's pid + starttime, or its env's `AGENT_BROWSER_CONFIG` = one of the keeper's `machine[-ephemeral]-<mark>.json`) after 10 min with no Chrome child, no lease, no verb / viewer, and its conversation gone or its record stopped-idle; a running conversation's stopped daemon is kept for the next verb up to 6 h idle. Its Xvfb (child, or the one whose `-auth` its env's XAUTHORITY names) goes with it. A daemon without the mark — incl. a lease session's `machine.json` daemon attached over CDP — is reported (once), never ended.
- **The keeper:** `orphanCensus` — one /proc walk (`browser-facts.daemonRows`, ≈50 ms for 944 processes) every 60 s from the tick and once at boot after adoption; SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 5 s, by pid + starttime; ONE journal line per ending; the row's note "stopped — the daemon was ended after N idle (restarts on the next command)". The tick's timer stays on while an unheld daemon waits out its grace.
- **Paired machines:** `browser-serve status` answers `daemon {pid, starttime, startedAt, chrome}`; new op `end-daemon {profileId, pid, starttime}` (only that profile's daemon, only with no Chrome), capability `browser-end-daemon` (an older agent is never asked; the row says it was reported). `lastVerbAt` is the hub's own profile stamp (the machine has none).

### pid-identity-census — a pid is never an identity (B-1cc6)

- **The fact.** This box's pid_max is 4 194 304 and its pids wrapped ≥ 3 times since the 09-17 boot; the lane's own scratch `sleep` drew pid 4 096 971. A pid recorded hours ago can name a stranger: `process.kill(pid)` kills it, `kill -0` reads a dead one (or a zombie) as alive.
- **One helper.** SHARED `src/proc-identity.js`: `identityOf` {pid, starttime, bootId} (`ps -o lstart=` with no /proc), `judge` (same / zombie / pid-recycled / gone / unknown-identity / unknown), `sameProcess`, `aliveIdentity` (null = unprovable, never alive), `signalIdentity` — the choke point, refusals said once ("a process this build cannot prove is ours — restart it to re-record"). Re-pointed: jobs.js (identical rule, moved; gained the zombie rung), browser-facts.js procStart/sameProcess (identical), agentd pidStartTime (verbatim) + `kill(sid)` behind `_childProven` (was weaker: an unverifiable child was assumed alive and signalled; a legacy meta passed on a cmdline substring).
- **The census.** test-architecture §85 over scripts/pid-identity-census.mjs: 77 signal/alive sites in 76 rows — 30 proven (3 identity, 11 starttime, 16 fresh scan), 37 exempt (7 handle, 4 self, 24 probe, 2 owner-named), 9 unknown-identity (the remote keeper's 5 cmdline-only kills, the opencode serve record, two shell sweeps of a remote meta's childPid, claude-code's in-memory `_childPid` SIGINT); + 10 persisted-pid records. Controls: a bare `process.kill(stamp.pid)` planted into jobs.js, agentd's kill without its proof, an unlisted shell `kill -0` — each RED; a comment stays quiet.
- **Gates.** New fast test-pid-identity (29: the verdict table over a fixture /proc incl. a comm holding ") ", report-once, a bare-pid MUTANT that turns the table red, a REAL scratch sleep whose wrong-starttime and starttime-less records are never signalled while the true one is).
- **Not done.** The 9 unknown rows stay EXEMPT with their reason (backlog in the lane report); desktop-display / the ci.mjs reaper / vnc keep their own identical (reaper: weaker) readers; the daemon ops (desktop-serve stop, browser-serve, exit-run) do not carry an identity across the wire yet.

### discovery-cursor-persist — a server restart never re-walks an account's whole listing; the discovery cursor is persisted beside the feed's (B-6638)

- **The fact (found by gmail-feed-gap):** discovery's walk state lived in memory ⇒ every restart re-listed every account (100 listing pages for a 10 000-conversation account, 0 reads) and a walk the restart cut started over from page 1.
- **PURE (src/channel-drain.js):** `listingVerdict({persisted, complete, refused, intent})` → `resume | rewalk | none`; `discoveryOf` (heal), `discoveryRecord` (write shape), `cursorRefused(err)` (the adapter's typed `detail.cursorRefused`, or `not-found` on a call that carried a cursor).
- **Engine:** `e.disc` is born from `rec.discovery` (`discFromRecord`); `discover()` writes it at every walk's end via `keepDisc` — `store.index.flush()` FIRST, then `saveAdapters()`; a refused kept cursor is caught inside the `vendor()` call ⇒ ONE walk from page 1, one journal line; `dropLive` clears it (every lifecycle verb re-lists as before).
- **Adapters:** Gmail (400 "Invalid pageToken"), Slack (`invalid_cursor`), Lark (a page_token refusal) type `cursorRefused` only on a call that carried a cursor; fake / agents list one page (nothing to resume). No vendor lacks stable page tokens.
- **Measured (test-channels-aggregate ㉓, one 10 000-row account):** restart +30 min ⇒ **0** listing pages (BEFORE: 100); a walk cut at page 40 ⇒ 60 pages after the restart, 0 unlisted; a refused cursor ⇒ 1 + 100 calls, said once. ㉒'s restart leg now asserts 0 listing pages.
- **Tests:** test-channels-aggregate ㉓ (CONTROL: the in-memory base ⇒ 100 / 100), test-channel-drain (verdict table, round-trip, heal, refusal typing), test-channel-adapter-contract (the listing cursor contract), test-channels-engine (its OWED BEFORE CURSOR crash leg went red until the index flush preceded the record write).

### lane browser-held-not-hung — a page that answers every command is never "not responding" (owner 2026-10-08, his 2.369.231 instance)

- **The rule:** "not responding" is a claim about the PAGE's answers, never about the dialog watch's ability to see in. PURE `stuckVerdict(recent, {n, tabHeld, now})`: a held tab is `unresponsive`/`tab-held` only when the conversation's outcomes hold no `ok` within `OK_RECENT_MS` = 60 s; a recent ok ⇒ ok (`held` carried); nothing asked ⇒ the new `blind` fact. `stuckWords` words `blind` as an info line (chip "dialog watch blind", no Restart, the tab's title in the tooltip) on every surface: the live view (a quiet line, never the yellow banner), the chip (never amber), the panel row (info tone, no Restart in its menu), the profile row.
- **The watch:** `factFor` returns `held` beside `stuck`; the hold is re-judged at every re-ask (an ok aging past 60 s moves the row ⇒ `stuck`, else `held-rejudged`); a closed held tab emits `held-cleared`; `noteOutcome` judges with the hold.
- **Measured** (scripts/measure-held-enable.mjs, NOT a test): a fresh socket's Page.enable on a running daemon with 16 busy tabs — p50 1 ms / p95 25 ms / max 25 ms (160 enables: 16 busy tabs × 5 rounds, idle and with the lease's own `open` loop); an alert's tab never answers in 30 s, answers the re-ask in 1 ms after `dialog accept`; the REAL watch on that browser: held after 5004 ms, the lease's `tab new` on another tab ok in 157 ms ⇒ the fact `blind`, the row `blind`. ENABLE_TIMEOUT_MS stays 5 s (load is not the hold).
- **Gates:** test-browser-stuck (hold verdict table 10 rows + 2 controls red; watch legs over the fake CDP: blind / ok / aged ok / scope / closed / re-judged / answered), test-browser-panel-model, test-browser-fact, test-browser-dialog-chrome (fast half), test-architecture, test-changelog-style, build. ### gmail-feed-gap — a gap in the change feed is ONE history walk from the saved cursor, never a whole-index pass (B-5134)

- **The fact (int226 on the .227 tree):** channel-feed-authority made Gmail's history.list the AUTHORITATIVE feed (`feed-only`: no per-row timer), but `feedState` judged it "behind" (not carrying) once its last good page was older than the fresh bound — a laptop asleep, a restart, an outage, a rate-limit park — and every row fell back to its tier: ONE whole-index pass. Reproduced here (test-channels-aggregate ㉒, the base rule as a patched copy): a 20-min clock jump over 10 000 rows ⇒ **10 000 rows due, 10 101 vendor calls in one pass** (1 feed + 10 000 reads + 100 listing pages) — the owner's number to the call.
- **PURE (src/channel-feed.js):** `gapVerdict({cursor, lastPageAt, now, coldTierSec, expired, freshBoundMs})` → `catch-up` (a cursor and a gap of any length, a boot included) | `rewalk` (expired / no cursor — the listing re-walk, as built) | `fresh`, with `overCold`; `addGap` (merged, ≤ GAPS_MAX 20) and `coverageOf` = `sample` with the declared gaps excluded (a record inside a gap is counted `excluded`, never judged a miss).
- **The carrying fact (src/channel-caps.js `feedState`):** an authoritative feed holding its cursor (`feed.carrying = {since}`, persisted on the adapter row, stamped by a good page, cleared only by a refusal) stays `carrying` through a silence (state `catching-up`, `gapSince`) and through a back-off (state `backoff`, parked by name) — `feed-only` holds, the tiers stay parked, the due index is not rebuilt. A measured (Lark) feed still reads `behind` (it has no cursor to resume). Words: "Catching up since {time} — the change feed resumes from where it stopped" / "… {vendor} asked the change feed to wait; it resumes from where it stopped at {until}" (zh / ja).
- **Engine (`historyFeed`):** the gap is judged before the call; a catch-up page returns `{due, pages, catchUp:true}` and writes ONE journal line per gap: "<account>: the change feed resumed after <n> min — <p> history pages, <m> conversations touched, 0 per-row reads"; a rate refusal logs the park once by name and keeps carrying; a refusal clears the fact. The measured feed's long-stop span (`window().gap`) is declared to the net (`f.gaps`); `feedSample` reads `coverageOf`.
- **Drain rule 21a:** a catch-up is ONE `feed` action with its pages (`pass.feed.walked`), done for the pass, its rows ahead like a page's.
- **Gmail adapter:** a history walk refused mid-way or longer than HISTORY_PAGES_PER_SYNC (20) keeps its page token (`mailbox.walk`) and the next sync RESUMES there; the cursor moves only after the walk's last page (it used to jump to the mailbox's newest id after page 20 — every change past page 20 was lost — and a refused page re-asked pages 1…n). `changes()` answers `pages`; the registry passes it (bounded).
- **Measured (test-channels-aggregate ㉒, 10 000 rows, scripted history fake, 10 changes a page):** 20-min jump ⇒ 0 due, **31 calls** (ONE walk of 3 pages + 30 named reads, 0 listing), still carrying, the since unchanged; restart +30 min on the same store ⇒ boots carrying (persisted since), the same ONE walk + 30 reads (+ discovery's boot listing, 100 pages, as before); 404 ⇒ the listing re-walk (100 pages), 0 reads, no catch-up line; rate-limit mid-walk ⇒ parked (backoff · rate-limited, carrying), 0 due / 0 reads, resumed ⇒ 30 reads.
- **Tests:** test-channel-feed ⑩ (the gap table, addGap, the net excludes a declared gap; CONTROL: a copy counting the silence as misses demotes a complete feed), test-channels-aggregate ㉒ (above; CONTROL: the base rule ⇒ 10 000 due / 10 000 reads), test-channel-caps (catching-up / park / measured / refused + words), test-channel-drain (rule 21a in the paced walk, exercised, never violated), test-channels-gmail-shape (a 429 on page 2 resumes from its token; 25 pages ⇒ none lost past page 20).

The engine persists it per account (`<account>/search-memo.json`, 0600, atomic, read at first use; dropped by dropLive's disconnect / removal, or when the file names another identity). - **Before:** `reply-to-mine` fired only for a message IN A TOPIC under one of "mine" (the owner's or this principal's sends, one `ctx.mine` set). A quote, a Gmail thread reply, a DM's next message — the ways people actually answer — woke no agent that had sent the message.
- **The rule (src/channel-filter.js, PURE):** RULE_KINDS + `reply-to-sent` (a PLACE rule). `sentHit(record, ctx)` judges five shapes against `ctx.sentByMe` only (Map vendorId → {at, words, subject}): (a) a quote / reply naming a sent id; (b) a topic reply / (d) a Slack thread reply under a sent parent / root / threadKey; (c) a record in a MAIL thread (`convKind 'thread'`) newer than a sent mail; (e) a DIRECT chat (`dm`): the peer's message within REPLY_WINDOW_MS (24 h) after the newest send. A fixed why per shape (SENT_WHYS, `{when}` = the answered message's UTC clock, `{subject}` = the mail's) — channel-words `wakeWhyText` words each in zh / ja. `matchRecord` returns `sent: {at, words}`; `renderWakeBlock` starts that hit's line "Reply to your message (<when>, "<first words>"): from …".
- **The ctx split (channels-engine onFresh `placeCtx`):** `ownerMine` (the log's isSelf ids), `sentIds` (the index ledger `sentBy`), `sentByMe` (the outbox's SENT proposals of this drafter on this conversation, the last 30 days, ≤ 500 per drafter — SENT_WINDOW_MS / SENT_MAX), `convKind` (the index row's kind). `reply-to-mine` / `in-thread-with-me` read all three (unchanged meaning); `reply-to-sent` reads `sentByMe` only — the owner's messages are never an agent's sends.
- **A group = each member (the owner's revision):** `fanOutWatchers(eff, live, {filterOf})` fans a GROUP row whose filter carries `reply-to-sent` out to its live members — one item each, keyed `group:<gid>><cid>` (principalKey / fanOfKey / fanTargetOf / fanWatcher grew the group shape; the ledger is the stored row's `stats.fan[cid]`, as All agents'), `split:'sent'` = only the sent half (`splitFilter`; a match-every filter whole), the row's other rules (match any) stay ONE round-robin group item (`split:'rest'`). `resolveTarget` names a member item's member; `storedWatcherFor` drops a member that left the group; `rowNames` names a member item for that member alone. All agents was already per conversation (its fan-out reads each target's own sends).
- **The dialog:** the kind "is a reply to a message this agent sent" for every principal, with the note "Set this on a group to cover each of its agents for their own sends — a reply notifies only the agent whose message it answers." (zh / ja).
- **Not built (the owner's revision 21:50Z):** the automatic per-send watcher and its `channels.autoReplyWatchDays` setting — a trigger the owner sets in Notify….
- **Gates:** test-channel-filter ⑮ 23 (every shape + why, ctx split, zh/ja words, the per-member fan-out; 3 patched-copy controls RED: DM next message ignored, the owner's messages counted as sent, the group as one round-robin item) — 254/0; test-channel-agent-watch ⑨ (a real engine: group of A + B and All agents — two replies to A's ⇒ A twice, B's ⇒ B, the owner's ⇒ nobody, nothing billed; the stash line begins "Reply to your message"; CONTROL: the engine without the per-member fan-out hands a reply to the wrong member) — 58/0; test-channels-engine 789/0.

### channel-feed-authority — a mailbox is not 89 000 chat rooms (Opus; base 189aadbb0)

- **Root cause (fleet pod, 4 Gmail accounts, 88 915 threads):** every conversation carried its own poll timer by activity tier (channel-caps `cadenceFor`), and `dueList` walked every row of the account each pass to find the due ones. Gmail's adapter already asked `history.list` once per pass, but declared no change feed, so the engine never let the feed REPLACE the per-row timers: cold threads came due by the thousand, each a 40-unit `threads.get` (the 2026-10-05 quota storms).
- **OWNER'S LAW (2026-10-06, "不能'获取更新'而不是'查询每条是否有更新'吗！"):** an adapter that can say what changed has no per-row question: no per-row timer, no per-row staleness check, no per-row vendor call beyond the rows the feed named, the window the user is looking at, and the owner's press.
- **Feed authority (PURE channel-caps + channels/index.js + channel-feed.js):** `changeFeed.authority` is `authoritative` (only `via: 'history'`, Gmail) or `measured` (Lark's search, unchanged). An authoritative feed is `carrying` from its first fresh good answer (not measured; positive evidence only — never run, behind, backing off or refused carries nothing), and `laneState` answers `pollCadence: 'feed-only'`: `cadenceFor` = 0 s for every row (never due by the clock), the hot cadence for a WATCHED row. Named rows, kicks, presses and owed marks are due through the engine, as before.
- **Gmail (`changes()`):** the pass's ONE history.list (forced; the per-thread `history()` reads after it reuse the 20 s memo) → `changed`. A changed thread the engine has not named is listed from the head page of the listing's own query (so the feed never births a thread outside it); one that page does not hold is dropped (the daily re-walk is its net). Expired cursor / CHANGED_CAP overflow / first connect = the RESEED WALK: `threads.list` answers each thread's `historyId`, judged against the LOST cursor (`walkFrom`, persisted as `gmailWalkFrom`): newer ⇒ named changed, else walked. No per-thread read rides the walk; it ends only on a walk from page 1 to the last page.
- **Engine:** `feedPage` → `historyFeed` for an authoritative row (ONE `changes()`, births through `admitListed` — discovery's per-row code moved out verbatim, a reseed ⇒ `discoverSoon`, refusals through `feedRefusal`); the named rows go ahead of the plain ones (drain rule 21, the drain module untouched). Under `feed-only` the listing re-walk is daily (`FEED_ONLY_REWALK_MS`), never every cold cycle (890 pages each 15 min at 88 915 threads).
- **The due index:** `dueList` reads per account a sorted (dueAt, key) array + a Map + the owed-mark set. Each row's key is a LOWER bound (a tier only relaxes as time passes); a head the clock did not make due is re-keyed to its true instant. Re-keyed at `store.index.onTouch` (every row write), `store.stamps.set` (wrapped) and a watch start. Rebuilt in ONE O(rows) pass at boot, on a whole-map touch, when the tier settings or the lane change, or when more than an eighth of the rows are dirty. The forced pass (`all`) still walks. `dueRow` is the one rule for both paths.
- **Measured (test-channels-aggregate ㉑):** a pass = 1 feed call + 20 named reads = 21 vendor calls at 1 000, 10 000 and 90 000 rows; dueList at 90 000 rows with 20 due is under 2 ms, linear in due rows rather than total rows. Four patched-copy controls: per-row timer restored, scan restored, measured feed treated as authoritative, watched refresh removed.
- **Follow-up (not built):** Gmail PUSH (`users.watch` → Pub/Sub) is the next rung; it needs a topic in the cluster's GCP project.

The port is read off the job's pid tree by NEW src/proc-listen.js (moved out of port-forward.js's detectLocal, which reads it too: /proc/net/tcp{,6} LISTEN ∩ the tree's socket inodes; fs.promises only, bounded, no exec) on the jobs engine's existing 5 s sweep, ≤ 1 read per job per 30 s (`_listenRead`; `job.listen` = {port, firstAt, at} persisted so a stopped job's row keeps its address). The engine's `_serviceDoor` (a signature per job, no I/O) calls jobs-wiring's `onService` → artifact-registry `noteService`: the card is born at the first listen and patched in place (port moved, stopped, up again). A stopped job's row stays 24 h greyed "stopped at …", then goes. Client: globe icon, the link as the path line, the chip's "Services" head after the docs, a click opens the Web view (`openBrowser`), ⋯ = copy URL / open in a new tab / show the job.

### mirror-green-222 — the 2.369.222 Actions mirror's fast red (test-browser-passkey ④, run 37419676410): the dialog watch said ready before the passkey hook was armed

- **The red:** ④ "the dialog watch over a fake CDP socket", right after the arm leg: `no ceremony ⇒ none`, `start ⇒ pending`, `after 3 s ⇒ passkey_open` (`{"state":"unknown"}`), the routes' fact, the verb in flight (`null`) — 59 passed, 5 failed; 64 / 0 here on c34711faa.
- **Cause (measured):** `arm()` resolved on the watch's ready (Page.enable answered on every tab) while the hook's three calls were in flight — `armPasskey` was fire-and-forget, `pk.armed` set on Runtime.enable's ANSWER; the suite waited until Runtime.enable was SENT (5 ms ticks). An event loop ≥ 5 ms late fires that tick in the same timers pass as the reply that sent it ⇒ asked before the answer ⇒ `unknown`. Not the clock (no Date.now on the path), not the keeper fake (`unknown` ⇔ answer not delivered, 233 / 233). The UNMODIFIED suite: a 2 ms / 1 ms event-loop stall preload 8 / 20 red, `taskset -c 0-3` + 8 burners 3 / 30, each the runner's 59 / 5 shape; idle 0 / 20, 3 burners 0 / 30. The MODULE_TYPELESS warning prints here too (② imports i18n-zh.js) — unrelated.
- **Fix (browser-dialogs):** the open step awaits each enabled tab's arming (`armPasskey` hands back its promise as `pk.arming`; the body is `armHook`) before `ready()` — `arm()` resolves after the hook is armed, still within its budget; readySeen / prune untouched.
- **Tests:** test-browser-passkey ④ reads at once after `arm` (the Runtime.enable-sent loop gone) + ⑤ CONTROL: a copy ready before the hook's last answer ⇒ `unknown` right after arm (every run). Fixed: stall 0 / 20, 8 burners 0 / 30, idle 0 / 10; the new suite on the base product: the arm leg + the runner's 5 legs red every run.

### lane gmail-quota-share — a mailbox polled from two instances stops tripping Gmail's shared bucket (owner 2026-10-05 "有没有可能避免触发限额")
- Measured (two fleet pods, read-only): one mailbox (10 040 threads) connected on TWO instances through the same cluster OAuth client = one Gmail bucket (6 000 units/min per project + user); each instance's default budget 3 000/min = the whole cap between them; the busier one logged "10 rate refusals in a row despite the pace" at 14:54 / 15:28 / 16:02Z (~50 min parked each), always on discovery's per-thread `threads.get?format=metadata`.
- A — NEW PURE `src/channel-budget.js` `budgetStep(state, event, facts)` over {refused, quiet-minute, setting-changed, boot}: a burst's FIRST rate strike halves the ceiling (floor 10 % of the setting, ≥ one read), later strikes only restart the quiet clock; every quiet minute +10 % of the setting; the refused ceiling is a WALL for 60 min (the creep stops one step under it — a pure +10 %/min creep returns to the tripping ceiling in 5 min and re-trips: control (e)). Engine: `budgetDecl().limit` = the learned ceiling (the setting = its cap), `paceDecl` scales `perSec` by the same ratio, `failPass` steps 'refused' (burstStart = rateStrikes === 1) inside the record write it already made, a good pass steps 'quiet-minute'; state persisted as `rec.budgetLearned` in adapters.json (never the index). Lark/Slack get it through the same door.
- B — `budgetView().learned` {ceiling, setting, refusedAt, fullAt}; channel-caps `learnedBudgetText` on the account card + the Channels panel row ("Polling at 1500 of 3000 quota units/min — Google refused this account's quota at 16:02; another instance may be polling the same account · back to 3000 by 17:03"); ONE For-you item per (account, day) at the day's 2nd halving (`speakSlowed`, §65 owner surface named), retracted at the setting. en/zh/ja.

The naming read names who STARTED the thread; the walk's thread read fills every author at the next listing. Gmail has no recent-roots recheck.
