### lane stash-any-turn — what waits for the next turn rides the next turn, whoever starts it (the owner 2026-10-05: "outbox 发的消息也是一个计费回合啊，也应该直接唤醒把")
- **Observation.** The owner approved a proposal in the Outbox; the agent's billed wake (the channel receipt) carried nothing of a group's parked next-turn report, and the strip kept "waiting for your next message" until he typed. Cause: `turnIsUserInitiated(s)` gated the report at both prompt-context sites (decide, push).
- **Fix.** Both gates gone: the report rides a turn of ANY origin. `turnIsUserInitiated` callers before → after: 2 gates (agent-routes.js prompt-context decide + push) → 1 word-picker (`reportsForTurn(cid, {budget, aside: !turnIsUserInitiated(s)})`). The echo guard is words: groups-engine `ASIDE_LINE` under the report head on a machine turn, measured inside the budget (WHOLE-or-nothing and the cut pointer unchanged). New: `wakesInFlight` — while a group's wake to a member is on its way, that group sits out the member's reports (the woken turn asks prompt-context before the post resolves; without it the woken message rode twice — patched-copy control red). The stash drains (`drainNotifsUnderCap` / `drainStashUnderCap`) and the stash hand-over were never keystroke-gated (verified: no stamp read on their path).
- **Strip.** "rides your next message" / "your first message after this turn ends" → "rides the next turn" / "the next turn, after this one ends" (11 keys, zh/ja); the Details list and "Hand over now" unchanged.
- **Gates.** test-channel-groups §4 drain table (owner / job notification / channel receipt / peer message / auto-resume continue: rides, once; aside words iff machine) + CONTROL gate-restored copy (the notification's turn carries nothing) + (g3) in-flight leg and its CONTROL; test-msg-cli-groups needle re-pointed; test-stash-strip / test-group-report-card words re-pointed.

### lane brand-marks — the Lark and Gmail monochrome marks redrawn by COLOUR ANALYSIS, verified by measurement (owner: "多色转单色 logo 要注意不同颜色的对比度")

- **The rule:** a multi-colour mark goes monochrome by keeping every boundary between strongly contrasting colours (ΔL* ≥ 20 or a hue jump ≥ 60° on ≥ 25 % of its length) as a NEGATIVE GAP; similar colours merge. `scripts/measure-brand-marks.mjs` (official marks by path, never committed) prints the boundary table and the proof; `scripts/test-brand-marks.mjs` (fast) pins the SVG contract and the gaps on the path data.
- **Lark** (official app icon, 3 colours): wing #00d6b9 ↔ head #133c9a HIGH (ΔL* 48, hue 116°), body #3370ff ↔ head HIGH (ΔL* 23) ⇒ three facets with two 1.3-unit gaps. **Gmail** (Google's current 192px.svg): flap ↔ left leg red-on-red low (merged), flap ↔ right leg red/yellow on green HIGH (hue 66°) ⇒ one uniform-stroke M (4.75 stroke, round caps) with a 1.4-unit gap under the flap on the right only.
- **Measured** (48 px dilated-edge IoU new / old, ≥ 0.6): Lark 0.78 / 0.60 and 0.76 / 0.31, Gmail 0.68 / 0.38; every gap is background at 14 px and the badge's 10 px in ≥ 1 of DPR 1 / 2. Slack unchanged (already the official mono shape).

### lane chat-enter-ime-r2 (Opus) — the Enter that commits an English word in a Chinese IME sent the message (inc-muukd9oq-qyc3, the owner's correction)

- **The correction** (the owner): "其实是中文输入法用回车上英文词的时候触发的 bug，而不是切换中英文". The ring re-read: Enter :09.651 and :10.802 composing (no `chat-input` frame), Shift :11.860, Enter :12.243 → `chat-input` at :12.244. The commit is the :12.243 Enter itself — Chrome 152/macOS delivered the commit's Enter as a PLAIN keydown (keyCode 13, isComposing false); the Shift was a capital letter inside the composition (the 2.369.207 recorder's one-per-3-s typing marker hides the letters after it), not its end. r1's 383 ms was Shift→Enter, not commit→send: the committing Enter follows compositionend within a millisecond or two, in either order.
- **The fix:** `EnterGuard` drops r1's exemption (`keydown` / `_lastKeyEnter`, the Safari 229 disarm, `isEnterKey`): EVERY compositionend arms `_imeEndedAt`; a plain Enter within `IME_COMMIT_BURST_MS` 50 ms ⇒ `'ime-swallow'` — ChatInput preventDefaults it (no newline, no send) and shows "Input method just ended — press Enter again to send" once; the next Enter sends. Cmd/Ctrl+Enter, Shift+Enter, `chat.enterSends` off and touch unchanged. The window is 50 ms, not r1's 600 (主开发's acceptance call): the commit's Enter lands 0–1 ms after the end, in the same event burst, while a human's two presses — Space commits, Enter sends, every Chinese sentence, often < 600 ms — are ≥ 80–100 ms apart; 600 ms would have swallowed a real send once per message, 50 ms never does.
- **Forensics:** the `k:'ime'` end marker carries `how: 'commit' | 'cancel'` (compositionend `data` non-empty / empty — the length only, never the text).
- **Gates:** test-chat-enter-ime (fast 58/58 — the owner's table: Enter(229) → compositionend → Enter(13) +1 ms ⇒ swallow; commit → +1/+30 ms ⇒ swallow, +120/+300/+700 ms ⇒ send; Space → Enter at 120/250 ms ⇒ send; Cmd+Enter ⇒ send; Safari order ⇒ no send, one hint; patched copies: r1's exemption restored ⇒ the owner's sequence SENDS, 600 ms back ⇒ Space → Enter swallowed) · test-chat-enter-ime-chrome (heavy 14/14 — the measured compositionend → keydown gap asserted < 50 ms; CDP imeSetComposition → a 229 Enter → insertText → a plain Enter 20 ms later ⇒ no send, no newline, the line; 150 ms ⇒ sent; mutant bundles r1-restored / window-removed ⇒ SENDS).

### artifacts-model — a conversation's deliverables are DERIVED from the harness's write record, never declared by the agent (owner 2026-10-05; docs/design-artifacts.zh.md + .md twin)

- **The model:** `src/file-type-table.js` = the ONE extension table (CJS, pure data; src/lib/file-types.js maps its icon keys; + rst / markdown). `src/artifacts.js` (PURE): the row `{key: host:path, kind, by, writes, edits, lastOp, lastId…}`, closed KINDS (agent-steering markdown — CLAUDE.md / SKILL.md / AGENTS.md / `.claude/` — is code), THE reducer (same path = one row, same call id = once, ≤ 500 rows, oldest code evicted first and returned), merge, view (doc › page › design › media › upload › other; code folded), cardBlock / cardFacts, autoOpenVerdict, and the PURE halves of the doc-window contract.
- **The hook:** every descriptor declares `artifactsOf(record)` (src/harnesses/artifacts-of.js: claude Write / Edit / MultiEdit / NotebookEdit; codex apply_patch envelope + live JSON `changes[]`; ACP diff + fs/write_text_file; shell `null`). test-harness-contract proves each (a reader answers a foreign record with `[]`, a null hook never produces on either path). §78 harness family 188 = baseline (no id branch added).
- **The registry:** src/server/artifact-registry.js = the ONE writer — `observe` from claude-stream-json's parse AND session-brain's claudeSideEffects (one call each; the call id keeps the row moving once), codex-events, acp-events; `session._artifacts` (session-schema rows `_artifacts` + `_artifactsTimer`) → session-meta `artifacts` (1.5 s debounce), restored at both boot-restore sites; GET /api/artifacts (the chip); ws `artifact-touch` (the user's save: by user, edits+1, one stash note). **Contract toward doc-window:** `ownerOf({host, path}) → {sessionId, row} | null`, `noteEdit({sessionId, host, path, summary})` = ONE "[Doc edit] <path>: <summary>" next-turn note through deliver.stashFor.
- **The replay:** normalizers.convertWithCards takes `opts.artifacts` (artifactDeriveOpts — normalizers never reach up to src/server) and folds each record before the next (no afterRecord); rebuildHistory merges the derived rows with the persisted ones (the user's saves) and settles every card; the view-only history read derives too. The card = `noticeKind: 'artifact'`, id `{view}:af:{key hash}`, patched in place (`edit` op, content only), held in the rebuild queue as `acard`.

### lane slack-landing-nologin — the Slack consent landing needs no VibeSpace login (userW)

- **Incident:** a fleet user on a Clerk-SSO pod pressed Allow on the cluster-preset Slack app in ANOTHER browser profile (their Slack identity lives apart from their SSO login); `src/auth.js middleware()` answered the cookie-less GET `/api/channels/oauth/cb/slack?code&state` with `302 /login` and the code was lost — design 018 assumed one browser profile.
- **Fix:** the ONE gate exempts exactly `GET /api/channels/oauth/cb/<kind>` (regex over the path, GET only); the route gets a per-address door limit (`landingAllowed`: fixed one-minute window, ≤ 30, bounded at 1000 addresses, 429 with `landingHtml({why:'too-many'})` before the state is judged); `LANDING.ok` (en/zh/ja) says "Done here — go back to the VibeSpace window where you pressed Connect", no sign-in words; the consent block's finish line names `st.user` (`connectedLine` in src/lib/mounts-dialog.js; the Duplicate dialog's `finishText` is a function of the identity, its watcher answers `row.auth.user`); a `public` flow's paste-back hint no longer promises a 127.0.0.1 address (`publicPasteHint`, per flow from `start`).
- **Gate:** scripts/test-slack-landing-nologin.mjs (fast, ~270 ms): a real `Auth` + the real channels router over express, password AND a stubbed Clerk — the no-cookie landing lands; `POST /oauth/callback`, `GET /oauth/status`, a POST to the landing path, `/oauth/cb`, `/oauth/cbx/slack`, `/oauth/cb/slack/extra` stay 401 / `302 /login`; forged / expired / used refused by name without a cookie; the 31st landing 429 with the engine stub asked 30 times; a DOM-free `connectedLine` render (en + the zh/ja tables); controls via scripts/mutant-copy.mjs — exemption removed ⇒ `302 /login`, limit removed ⇒ the 31st judged.
- **Verify r1 (adversarial, credential class):** the exemption's edge holds (trailing slash, `..`, `%2e%2e`, case, `//`, `sl%2fack`, HEAD / OPTIONS, a fragment: the landing or 302 / 401, never another handler — `p` is `req.path`, the gate is mounted once at the root); replay / 10 concurrent landings = ONE `oauth.v2.access`; a stolen state on a NEW account's flow ends it as the lander (the owner's dialog names them before Create & connect — no record without the owner's tab); both re-authorize doors (the record's own flow and the switched-client rebind) refuse another identity, token untouched. **MED fixed:** the now cookie-free page printed a refused re-authorize's sentence — the account's label and its HELD Slack identity — to whoever held the state; `oauthLanding` answers fixed words for an existing account's flow (the owner's window keeps the sentence). **LOW fixed:** a clock stepped back kept an address at 429 until it caught up (`t < h.at` opens a new window); the 429 page said "start again" — its own en / zh / ja words now say wait + reload. Behind an ingress every landing shares one `remoteAddress` (no `trust proxy` anywhere; X-Forwarded-For deliberately unread): 30 / min is the pod's one user, and a stranger flooding it only delays that user's landing (the paste-back stays open).

### lane mount-cache-scan (on 7fceb8a7)

- **mount-cache-scan: a mount still rebuilding its cache is STARTING — not failed, not writable** (lane mount-cache-scan, the owner's OneDrive, 2026-10-04): rclone `--vfs-cache-mode full` rebuilt its VFS cache index (164 788 cached files) for 4.5 min before mounting (spawned 16:52:33, first mount attempt 16:57:09); `_waitMounted(m, 5000)` called it failed, `unblockPath` freed the bare mount point, an outside writer dropped `WestcliffCourses/AIWorkspace/.restore` into it at 16:52:59 and rclone died `is not empty`. The three 16:52 "stale daemon … at mount time — killing it" lines were Connect clicks killing the scan before them. The 15:09:43 / 16:41:43 "daemon survived lazy unmount" lines came from `_healthSweep`'s hung branch (both on the 60 s watchdog's :43 phase; that branch logs nothing before the kill): a mounted OneDrive whose `ls` took over 6 s while its daemon was busy was lazily unmounted, then killed.
  **Build (src/mounts.js):** a live daemon with no fuse mount is `starting` (`_starting`; the `list()` row's `starting: {since, files, capped, maxMin}`). `_waitMounted(m, pid)` waits while the pid lives: `hung` = no utime+stime progress (≥ 30 ticks) for 60 s, `ceiling` = 15 min (≈ 3× the measured scan), both SIGKILL; the path stays blocked (`blockPath(mp, ceiling + 60 s)`) and shadowed until the mount exists. A connect while starting JOINS (`mount()` hands back the in-flight promise; `_mountInner` answers `'starting'`; a daemon found on the mount point with no mount — a restart mid-scan — is ADOPTED, never killed). A mount within 5 s answers the caller as before; past that the route answers `{success: true, starting: true}`. rclone dying "is not empty" → the connect-time stranded move (`<mp>.stranded-<ts>/`) + ONE retry; every connect-time stranded move is said on the row (`stranded`) beside the existing level-2 server-notice. NOT DONE: a For you item — the wiring file is the census's `browser` producer (test-user-todos-layout ⑪, exact site count) and test-record-clear-census must classify the new receiver; it needs its own producer row (proposed follow-up). The sweep skips a starting record, and its hung branch keeps a daemon that made CPU progress during the 6 s probe connected (path blocked 65 s, "storage busy" on the row); an idle daemon whose listing hangs is still torn down. The cache count is a child `find -printf .` stopped at 200 000 (never a walk on the event loop). UI (sidebar-mounts.js): the row says "Starting — rebuilding its cache index (N files), <elapsed> so far …" (keyed `mount-start:<id>`, elapsed patched in place every second); no Connect button or row click while starting.
  **Tests:** new suite test-mount-starting (24 checks, 14.9 s — a heavy "slow —" row at int213: over the fast tier's 10 s rule): a fake rclone (bash re-exec'd with argv[0] = …/rclone, as the /proc scan needs) drives the real MountManager through ① the starting row + count + blocked/shadowed path, ② a joined connect, ③ adoption by a restarted manager, ④ sweeps that never touch a starting or CPU-busy daemon (an idle one still goes), ⑤ a hung daemon killed, ⑥ "not empty" → stranded + one retry, said on the row; ⑦ patched-copy controls via mutantCopies: the 5 s verdict restored ⇒ the scanning daemon is killed (red); unblock before mount ⇒ the path is writable (red).

### lane chat-enter-ime (Opus) — an Enter meant for the input method sent the message (inc-muukd9oq-qyc3)

- **The incident** (the owner, Chrome 152 / macOS / a Chinese IME): two composing Enters swallowed, a Shift tap, Enter 383 ms later ⇒ sent mid-turn. Reading: the Shift tap ended the composition (a Chinese IME commits on Shift), so the Enter was plain; the recorder had no `shiftKey` / `isComposing` to prove it.
- **Forensics first:** the action ring's key record carries `S-` (Shift) and `c:1` (the IME owned the key), and `k:'ime'` `ph:start|end` markers for a textarea's compositions (no text) — `actionKeyWords` / `imeMarker` in the new PURE `src/lib/chat-enter-keys.js`.
- **The narrow guard:** `EnterGuard` — a compositionend whose last keydown was not the physical Enter (key, or code Enter/NumpadEnter: Chrome/Windows reports 'Process') arms `_imeEndedAt`; a plain Enter within 600 ms inserts the newline and shows "Input method just ended — press Enter again to send" for 2 s (zh/ja); once — the next Enter sends. Safari's compositionend-before-keydown order disarms on the 229 Enter. **Why 600 ms:** the incident's gap was 383 ms; a fast typist's Space-select → Enter lands at ~150–300 ms and loses nothing (the newline stays, the line explains, Enter again sends); a deliberate commit-then-send reads the committed text first, well past 600 ms (the 700 ms row sends).
- **The setting:** `chat.enterSends` (desktop, default on = today) — off ⇒ Enter newline, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends; `composerSendModes(caps, {enterSends})` adds a send segment (or names the key in the queue segment) so the mid-turn line says which key sends. Touch keeps `chat.touchEnterSends`. docs/settings.md regenerated.
- **Gates:** test-chat-enter-ime (fast, PURE — the sequence table incl. Chrome/Windows/Safari commit orders, the recorder words, 6 patched-copy controls: the window removed ⇒ the incident SENDS); test-chat-enter-ime-chrome (heavy — CDP `Input.imeSetComposition` → Shift keydown → `Input.insertText` → Enter on a real ChatInput: no send, newline, the line; 2 s later hidden; Enter ⇒ sent; 700 ms ⇒ sent; enterSends off; the mutant bundle ⇒ sends).

### mirror-green-212 — the 2.369.212 Actions mirror's red: a hub race, not a runner clock
- test-desktop-remote red twice on heavy 2/4 (`port … answered no VNC greeting within 3 s`). The fake VNC server had been listening all along, and the greeting was sent but DROPPED. `tcpForward` (src/agentd/client.js) handed back a handle with `onData` null until the caller's `await` resumed, and the agent's tcp-open and the greeting parsed in one read reached that null consumer. It hit about 1 probe in 10 on an idle box (driver: idle 36/40, 4 drops = 4 misses), latent since 0c280720; .212 touched only src/agentd/version.js near it. FIX = the handle keeps chunks (then the close) until onData / onClose are set and flushes them in order. That covers the 5900 probe and the user port forward (port-forward.js, SSH banners). New D014 leg: a server in another process, the hub stalled 150 ms between the ask and the resume, 40/40 greetings seen (40 arrived before the consumer). Its CONTROL is the pre-fix handle as a scratch copy: 10/10 lost, misses = early arrivals. The probe's 3 s is unchanged.

### app-system-harden — Layer 1 root paths made defensively robust, with tests (Opus; base 18000665)

- **Owner's choice (2026-10-04):** the Layer 1 code does what the design says even when files inside the app system or under HOME are not what the code expects; one structural guard per item, a test that shows the guarded case, a patched-copy control per test.
- **Helper:** `#!/bin/bash -p` + an `env -i` re-exec (same pid) before any external command — root code runs on a fixed PATH with LC_ALL=C, the allowlist reaches the app only as VS_KEEP_<name>, `--root` gets a fixed env; `inside` walks every bind target / root write level by level (a link refused by name, parents root's, mkdir one level at a time); passwd/group must be regular files; the lock is the userland's etc directory (no lock file).
- **SYS_SCRIPT:** `rdir` / `put` (dir canonical + root's via `cd` + `pwd -P`, then a relative install + `mv -T`), `stage` (user-side sources + keys copied O_NOFOLLOW into root's $T from a held cwd), `cpin` for Rebase copies, `rmchild` the only recursive removal (expected child of the canonical sysroot, root's real dir, `--one-file-system`). INSTALL_SCRIPT checks root's private copies against `HELPER_SHA256` / `SUDOERS_SHA256` before visudo / install (the pod's checkout is on the PVC).
- **Machine half:** `inRoot` + O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK fd reads for identity / entries / .desktop / sys icons; `existsIn` resolves Exec targets inside the rootfs the way the chroot will; `verifyRow` re-checks a sys row's shim at every catalog read (exact `shimText(target)` bytes, this user's, not group/other-writable) → `shim-not-ours` + one log line, and desktop-serve refuses to launch a blocked sys row; the gate is shut under systemd (`INVOCATION_ID`). `planDigest` binds `sysDigestPart` (layer + SYS_SCRIPT argv minus the nonce); a plan whose layer and argv disagree has no digest and installPackage refuses it.
- **r2 (the residual closed, coordinator's ask):** the drop-in carries `#<uid> ALL=(root) NOPASSWD:NOSETENV: <helper>` (INSTALL_SCRIPT writes the server user's uid for `#VS_UID`, visudo-checks, then requires that line); the file is now `/etc/sudoers.d/~vibespace-sysroot` so it is read after boot-root.sh's user-named drop-in (the last match wins; the user's ALL rule implies SETENV). sudo now refuses LD_PRELOAD / BASH_ENV / PATH… on the command line for the helper; ENV_KEEP (= what a command line may set) is pinned free of loader / shell / PATH knobs. Container proof with the user's drop-in named `zz-node` (sorts after `vibespace-sysroot`) + a control drop-in without the line. After r2: test-app-system 115/115, test-app-system-enter 45/45 in 81 s, build + the brief's gates green.
- **Gates:** test-app-system 112/112 (§5 census rules envClean / inside + staged / put / removal / digest, §6 controls, §8 in-process items 4 · 6 · 7 · 8 with controls); test-app-system-enter 44/44 in 81 s (the 7 hardening legs, each with its patched-copy control, in the disposable container; the first run hung silently — a walk that refused Debian's /etc/localtime link cascaded; found with a streamed container run); the census pins it touches stay green.

### lane exit-runs-dialog-fit (Opus) — the machine's Commands list fits its own width (the owner: 「这个界面展示不全」)

- **Cause:** `.exit-runs-body { min-width: min(640px, 92vw) }` inside the base `.dialog` (a fixed 440 px, `overflow: hidden`): on any viewport over 768 px the body was 640 wide in a 440 dialog — the intro line, every row's head, the decoded script and every stdout line ran 200 px past the dialog's right edge and were clipped (the pres wrapped, at 640). At ≤ 768 px the phone rule's `min-width: 0` hid it. A transfer row's `0.0 s` sat on a line of its own (a flex-wrap summary, the verdict `nowrap`).
- **Fix (CSS + the painter):** `.dialog.exit-runs-dialog { width: 960px; max-width: calc((100vw - 32px) / var(--ui-scale)) }`, the body `min-width: 0`, scrolling down only. The summary is a grid — time · who (`fit-content(14em)`) · ONE `minmax(0, 1fr)` column holding the head (two-line clamp; the whole command is the open row's body) over an outcome line (verdict · duration). Below 560 px (a container query on `.exit-runs-list`) time + who share a line, the command goes under. Script / stdout / stderr pres carry the chat's `chat-pre-wrapped` (the class the chat's machine cards draw their command with) and the chat's Wrap toggle (`chat-wrap-toggle`, 换行 / 不换行): off = `white-space: pre`, the pre scrolls sideways inside itself. Wrapped = pre-wrap + overflow-wrap:anywhere (`word-break: normal` over chat's break-all — no mid-word splits). The transfer's sha256 flags line wraps anywhere (it was 25 px past the body at 390). `durationText(ms)`: a duration that rounds to 0.0 reads `<0.1 s`.
- **Gates:** NEW heavy scripts/test-exit-runs-dialog-fit-ui.mjs (pairing-ui-harness bootWorld + the real painter behind a one-line opener hook in a scratch bundle, the GET stubbed in the page, private HOME / XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, no DISPLAY): 390 / 768 / 1280 × zh / en, the rect census (no element or text run past min(body, dialog) client width, the body inside the dialog, the dialog inside the viewport, the intro line whole), every pre wraps or scrolls itself (Wrap off: 1341 px inside 310–882), the grid stacking, the transfer outcome line, CONTROL = the 2.369.207 CSS swapped in (red: body outside the dialog, 61 boxes past, intro cut) · 39 checks, ~55 s. test-exit-runs-dialog §1b (DOM-free duration words + control f). test-architecture, test-changelog-style, `npm run build` green.

### job-publish-stable — a published service keeps its public URL across restarts, and the CLI prints it (Opus)

- **The incident (2026-10-04 04:43Z, before a demo):** a `--keep-up --port 8766 --publish` service's public URL answered 404 after a reboot + stop/start while 127.0.0.1:8766 answered 200 — the frpc proxy had become `type = "tcp"`, `publicSub` null. Two causes: `_ensurePublish` called `pf.publish` the instant the job spawned, `frpPublish` PROBED the not-yet-listening port, and `probeProto` read a refused connection as `tcp`; then the adopt line `rec.publicSub = r.subdomain || null` threw the name away (and the job stop path's `unforward` deleted the record outright).
- **Sticky name (src/port-forward.js):** `_adoptPublish` keeps `publicSub`/`publicPort` across mode changes; only an explicit `unpublish(id)` clears them; job stop/park = `unpublish`/`unforward(id, {keepName:true})` → `port-forwards.json` `names[id]`, restored by `forward()`.
- **No probe race:** `plugins.probeProto` throws `EUNREACHABLE` when no pass connected; `_decideProto` = override › fresh probe › LAST protocol (else http) + `protoPending`; `reprobe(id)` (heal sweep + the job's `_publishRecheck`) republishes under the same name when the answer differs. Jobs wait ≤ 60 s for the port before publishing. One log line per decision.
- **Said, never silent:** `lastPublicUrl` on the job; a different URL (or a failed publish of a job that had one) = one owner notice through `_notifyOwner`. CLI `show`/`poll` print `public URL:` (publishing… / the failure / the URL the next start brings back), `list` appends `↗ <url>`; manual §6 "How to find the URL".
- **Tests:** test-port-forward +20 (restart keeps the subdomain, late listener → http same name, undecided keeps the last protocol, TCP→http repair, explicit unpublish clears, keepName stop/start; controls: pre-fix adopt line loses the name, pre-fix probe publishes `tcp://`); test-jobs-engine §11 +14 (late-listening real service via the real PortForwardManager + fake frp, CLI show/list/poll against a stand-in API, stop/start same URL, change notice once; control: no wait ⇒ the publish runs on a silent port). test-peer-text-census: 8 judge rows for the new `public URL:` prints (all VibeSpace-minted: the relay URL, flags, an enum, ports, the publish error sentence) — red without them (38 ✗, the walk names each).
- **User line (for the integrator):** en "A published Background Work service keeps its public URL across restarts, and `vibespace-job show` prints it" · zh "已发布的后台服务重启后公网链接保持不变，`vibespace-job show` 会显示该链接" · ja "公開中のバックグラウンドサービスは再起動しても公開URLが変わらず、`vibespace-job show` で表示されます"

### lane win-run-codepage (Opus): a Windows device's `run` output arrives as readable text, not GBK mojibake

- **The case (2026-10-04):** on the owner's Chinese Windows box `vibespace-exit run WIN-DESK1 -- 'dir … 2>nul'` and PowerShell errors came back as mojibake — cmd.exe and console programs write in the console's OEM code page (936 = GBK) and agentd `run-cmd` returned `String(stdout)` (UTF-8). The stored heads, the card and the Commands list kept it.
- **The fix (device side):** PURE `XS.decodeRunOutput` in src/exit-shell.js — each stream judged alone: valid UTF-8 stays UTF-8, else the code page `chcp` names (registry OEMCP next; asked once per daemon, cached) → gbk / shift_jis / euc-kr / big5 / windows-1252 / utf-8, else latin1; decoded BEFORE the 1 MiB / 64 KiB cut (a stream cut by maxBuffer or a kill drops its torn last character); `cmd-result.encoding` names it, `utf-8-fallback` when this node lacks the label. POSIX unchanged (no `encoding` key, `String()` byte for byte).
- **Full ICU:** the Windows installer provisions node from nodejs.org/dist (official builds are full-icu since Node 13; an existing `Program Files\nodejs` is the same build); a small-ICU node falls back by name.
- **Found on the way:** GBK 系统 (cf b5 cd b3) and 路 (c2 b7) are VALID UTF-8 on their own — the judge must read the whole stream, and a fixture for it must not be one of them; a UTF-8 stream torn by maxBuffer must not be mis-judged as GBK (stream-mode decode).
- **Tests:** test-exit-run §9 — byte fixtures (GBK, Shift-JIS, UTF-8, chcp in zh / ja / en, reg's OEMCP line), the whole-stream judge, an invalid sequence, the cut, a no-ICU stand-in; a REAL daemon from this tree's bundle made a fake Windows box (`dir-missing` → 系统找不到指定的路径。 encoding gbk; UTF-8 stays; 2.2 MB of GBK past maxBuffer cut clean at 1 MiB; chcp asked once for three runs); POSIX byte-identical; controls (w1) a String() decoder (7 rows red), (w2) a daemon keeping String(stdout) (the production mojibake).

### lane win-upgrade-pipe (Opus, base b5eb3d29) — a Windows device's self-upgrade must not kill its agent

- **Incident (owner's Windows box, 2026-10-04 01:38Z):** `upgrade to 2.369.205 landed — re-exec` → `vibespace-device 2.369.205 starting` → `server error: listen EADDRINUSE … \\.\pipe\vibespace-agentd-ecce10a7eeb5`, then nothing until the owner reran the install command at 01:57Z. The re-exec unlinked SOCK, spawned the successor and exited; on Windows SOCK is a NAMED PIPE — no unlink frees it, it stays bound while any pipe handle of the old process is open. The successor reached `listen` first and its error handler exited; then the old one exited; no agent. The hub logged "upgrading (attempt 1/3)" and nothing spoke (`stuck` needs a device that answers).
- **Fix ① (src/agentd/reexec.js `handOver`, wired in agentd.js beginUpgrade):** the old daemon closes its listener, THEN unlinks the lock + spawns the successor + exits — bounded at 1.5 s (a lingering local connection keeps a Windows pipe bound until the process exits; the line says so and spawns anyway). Every platform.
- **Fix ② (`listenWithRetry`, agentd.js serve):** EADDRINUSE is retried every 250 ms for ≤ 15 s while the lock file names this pid (one line when it starts, one when it listens or gives up); any other error / a lock not ours ⇒ the old `server error` exit. This is what saves the .205 → .206 hop: the OLD (.205) code runs that re-exec and still spawns before it lets go.
- **Fix ③ (src/server/device-upgrade-watch.js `begun` / `answered` / `sweep`):** client.js reports every upgrade start (`onUpgradeBegin`) and every hello (`onAnswer`) through the same door (dial-pairing.js, hosts.js ssh); a device silent `GONE_AFTER_MS` = 5 min after its upgrade began gets ONE high For-you item per (machine, version) — "<machine> stopped answering after its upgrade to <v> began — rerun its install command (Remote → <machine> → Pairing command)" — retracted (`system`) when it dials in. The deadline is persisted (`gone` in data/device-upgrades.json): a hub restart inside the window still fires. 30 s unref'd tick.
- **Tests:** test-agentd-reexec-argv (e) — a win32 named-pipe model on a fake clock over THE functions: CAUSE (pre-fix shape dies EADDRINUSE), ① free at the spawn, ② the .205-code hop listens after retries, ①+② a lingering connection, the lock-not-ours refusal (no retry), the 15 s bound, a REAL net.Server re-listen after EADDRINUSE, wiring + bundle census, 3 patched-copy controls (no close / no retry / no lock gate). test-agentd-dial: a REAL POSIX re-exec through the real dial gate (old closes, then the successor starts and listens; door events answered → begun → answered → matched; a third daemon exits 3 "already running"). test-device-upgrade-watch GONE-1..10 + 3 controls (no retract / no (machine, version) rule / the pre-fix door without `begun`).
- **Not done (listed):** item 4 — `run` output on a Chinese Windows arrives as mojibake (console code page 936); decoding stdout/stderr with the console's code page on win32 (TextDecoder gbk / shift_jis, UTF-8 first when valid) is a follow-up.

### slack-connect-easy — connecting Slack in two pastes, nothing to choose in Slack (Opus build, design 017; base 9d448a44)

- **The ask:** the owner tried 2.369.204's Slack connect and ended on Slack's "Create new app" chooser and an empty User Token Scopes page (「不知道选啥」). Design 017's minimal set 1–5 is built: the Connect dialog's Slack type is three numbered steps — ① a one-time app configuration token (`xoxe.xoxp-…`) → VibeSpace makes the person's own app with ONE `apps.manifest.create`, ② the app's install page by id, ③ the `xoxp-` as before — and the 2.369.204 link stays folded as "Another way" with "Copy app setup".
- **The credential:** the setup token reaches slack.js `createApp` as the exchange's `code`, is the Bearer of one JSON POST and is dropped in the create branch's `finally`; the create's `credentials` / `oauth_authorize_url` are never read (http path). It is in no flow status, record, call record, log line, frame, answer, error or file of the data dir — slack-shape ⑧ and slack-send ⑧ census it with planted-leak controls (a copy that puts it in the step facts over an unfiltered loopback, a copy that words a refusal with it). `xoxe.` / `xoxe-` joined secret-shapes (PREFIX_RE, the whole token now redacted incl. its `xoxe.` head) and secret-scan (`slack-config-token`). Fact found: the base scanner already flagged `xoxe.xoxp-…` through its `xoxp-` rule; only the refresh token `xoxe-…` was unseen (slack-send ⑧ shows both on the base's scanner).
- **The flow machine:** oauth-loopback's `paste` mode accepts `{continue:true, step, facts}` — a step that landed keeps the flow running (`step`, `stepFacts` ≤ 8 short strings, carried by `status()` and the engine's `safeFlow`); a step that lands on a flow ended meanwhile is still recorded. Each paste names its box; slack-manifest.js `pasteAction` (the closed table) refuses a wrong-box token by its shape before any call; refusals carry a closed `why` to the card (`detail.code`).
- **Rules the gates enforced:** test-oauth-field-parity §6 (the account dialogs build no form control) moved the stepper's DOM into mounts-dialog.js `wireStepPaste`; test-record-clear-census H1 classified the remembered-app key (`owner`: id, app name, workspace name — never a token).
- **Not built / to check:** the https variant (design step 6 — no https instance at hand). The workspace is named before step 2 only when the create's answer names one — the documented answer does not, and no second call is made for it. The JSON body shape, the answer's fields and the install link by app_id are built against the docs and a fake Slack; q-017-probe.md (the coordinator's live probe) had not landed when this lane closed.

### around-sheet-fix — the Channels search's "Around this message" sheet drew its rows cut and overlapping (Opus)

The owner (2026-10-03, zh, 2.369.203, a Lark full-history hit → 这条消息前后): 「这啥玩意啊！」 — every row's left edge cut ("李天雨" showed "雨", "没事" showed "殳事"), the round avatar on the name and the first line, a horizontal scrollbar, and a picture row saying "图片 未找到 重试" for a message VibeSpace never stored.

- **Cause (measured on 3452dce3 by the new leg, not guessed):** the sheet put the window's `.chanmsg` rows in a bare `.chan-around-list`. The row's `padding-left: calc(6px + var(--chan-gutter))` is invalid where no list defines `--chan-gutter`, so it fell to 0 under the row's `margin: 0 -6px`: the name and first line started 6 px left of the box (179 < 185 at 1400 px), the absolute avatar covered both, `scrollWidth` 481 > `clientWidth` 475 (347 > 341 at 390 px), and `scrollIntoView` left the found row 21 px off centre. The picture asked our attachment route, which serves only an attachment of a record we STORED (`fetchVerdict` rule 3, the route is not a proxy) ⇒ `not-found` with a Retry that could never work.
- **Fix:** the list is `chanwin-list chan-around-list`, the outbox's way: one rule for the gutter, padding and scroll, and the sheet only caps its height. `renderAroundRows` draws `unsaved` rows. A file there is a named chip, "not saved — open the conversation to see it" (zh/ja), with no link and no Retry, and it asks nothing because the vendor read is not allowed for a record we never stored. The rows also get the window's day separators. The found row is centred by the list's own `scrollTop`, vertically only. `dayLabel` names another year's day with its year, because the sheet reaches years back.
- **Fixture:** the fake vendor's archive gains `<kind>-ops-old-pic` (author 李天雨, a Lark-shaped `[image]`). It never matches a search, so ⑪'s 20 hits and test-channel-search are unchanged.
- **Gates:** test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑪b (new, 30 rows: zh / en / ja × desktop + 390 px, each on a fresh page). It checks every row's avatar, name, first line and chip inside the list's box, the avatar on none of them, `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`, the found row centred with the page unscrolled, the chip's words with zero `/attachment/` asks, and the picture's separator carrying its year. It counts only asks that name the picture, because a fresh page restores the channel windows earlier legs opened, and their thumbnails are not the sheet's. It is red on 3452dce3 (all 24 judged rows; the six page and panel loads pass) and green after (the whole suite 171/171, run alone). ### desktop-vnc-native — a Windows / macOS machine's whole desktop (Opus build, design 014 D1; base ed1e0b83)

- **What shipped:** the `vnc-native` rung (src/desktop-display.js `VNC_NATIVE` + PURE `rfbGreeting`), the picker rows for darwin / win32 (`desktop_ready` / `no_vnc` / `offline`, Linux rows byte-identical — frozen from ed1e0b83's own machinePickRow), the access layer's probe / open / target / gone / runOnDesktop / UAC install, the bridge's `human_only` + `upstreamWhy`, the routes (`/api/desktop/machine-desktop/{open,run,last-close}`, `what: 'tightvnc'`), the page's dialog + window (src/lib/machine-desktop.js) and vnc-view's `credentials` / `resizeSession`. No new device op; no keeper row.
- **Design vs code (said in 车道群 before building; the coordinator chose option A):** the Windows agent runs UNELEVATED (scripts/vibespace-agentd-install.ps1: a logon task without `-RunLevel Highest`, "no admin"), and the xpra install door's runner is POSIX sh + setsid / flock / `tail --pid`, so "TightVNC through the same door, silently, the password typed in the hub's dialog" could not run. Option A: the same slot / plan / digest, but the agent's argv asks Windows for elevation on that machine's screen (UAC); the person there clicks Yes and types the VNC password into the elevated window — it never passes through VibeSpace. `run-cmd` is not detached (execFile, 30 s cap): the run plan detaches itself (nohup on macOS, Start-Process on Windows).
- **MSI facts (measured 2026-10-03):** tightvnc-2.8.85-gpl-setup-64bit.msi, 2,531,328 bytes, SHA-256 d8fbed7b…5f3e; every property in the flag table was read out of the MSI's own string pool (SET_/VALUE_OF_ LOOPBACKONLY, ALLOWLOOPBACK, ACCEPTHTTPCONNECTIONS, RFBPORT, USEVNCAUTHENTICATION, PASSWORD; SERVER_REGISTER_AS_SERVICE, SERVER_ADD_FIREWALL_EXCEPTION, SERVER_ALLOW_SAS; ADDLOCAL). TightVNC refuses loopback connections by default — ALLOWLOOPBACK=1 is what lets the agent's forward in. UNCONFIRMED until the owner's first use: which sign-in the owner's Mac's Screen Sharing offers noVNC (the probe names it; ARD-only and VNC-password both handled), whether `start "" blender` finds Blender on WIN-DESK1, and that LOOPBACKONLY binds 127.0.0.1 (the install script checks the listen addresses and fails by name otherwise).
- **Found while gating:** the picture forward's `allowHalfOpen` kept a closed window's connection to the machine open until the last viewer left (a Mac would keep showing a viewer) — fixed in desktop-access (close the agent channel on `end`), with a control.
- **Gates:** test-rfb-greeting (new, fast), test-desktop-apps, test-desktop-stream-keepalive, test-vnc-view, test-desktop-remote (heavy, a real agent), test-architecture, test-window-types, test-changelog-style, `npm run build` (i18n zh / ja). The verify rounds follow (2: the password never in a log / record / audit, loopback-only, ARD-only greeting, offline mid-view, two windows one forward, the run box's command as itself).
- **Verify r1 (Opus):** HIGH F2 — the elevated TightVNC script downloaded the MSI into the user's own %TEMP% and checked its SHA-256 BEFORE the password prompt, so any process of that user (an agent's `vibespace-exit run`) could swap the checked file and get an administrator install; now an admin-only directory (protected ACL) + the hash again right before msiexec. MEDIUM F1 — Run on its desktop spelled its own hidden-character list (242 code points of src/hidden-chars.js ran: the tag block, U+034F…) — it asks the one set, and the approval census names the door. MEDIUM F4 — a desktop run left no audit line — now one exit-audit line per run / refused line (the owner's Commands list). LOW F3 — a TightVNC listening beyond loopback after the install is stopped + disabled, not only reported. Open LOW: an unanswered UAC prompt past the 15-min deadline reads install_timeout with apt words.
- **Verify r2 (Opus):** re-attacked every r1 fix with new shapes; all held. F2 — the MSI lands in %SystemRoot%\Temp under a fresh-GUID directory whose protected ACL (SYSTEM + Administrators, inheritance off) inherits onto the file, and the SHA-256 is re-checked right before msiexec with nothing writable (no Invoke-WebRequest / Copy / Move / Out-File) between: a %TEMP% swap, a hard link, a space/unicode path, a different volume all shut out. ### lane usage-index-shadow — a shadow SQLite index of the usage ledger, and the cursor store's hygiene (design 011 lane 3: L0 + L1)

- **L1, the index as a SHADOW.** `~/.vibespace/db/<sha256 of data/'s real path, 16 hex>/usage.db` on LOCAL disk, survey §2.2's schema (`usage_event` keyed by rid, INSERT OR IGNORE in _loadEvents's order — the first row of a rid wins; `shard_mark`; the `attribution` table waits for lane 4's reader — a schema change is a version bump, a version bump is a rebuild). It feeds NOTHING: every `/api/usage-stats` aggregate is asked a second time of the index and compared (costs to 1e-9 relative, everything else exact); a difference is a telemetry event `usage-index-diff` carrying the query, never shown. Owner Q1 (SQLite for this index, assumed yes): a "no" drops L1 whole — the three new files, the push, the comparer line, §73 — and L0 stands alone. Owner Q2 (local disk, assumed yes): a "no" is `indexDirFor` in src/server/usage-index.js.
- **One thread owns the database.** PURE `src/usage-index-model.js`; `src/usage-index-worker.js` is the ONLY file naming `node:sqlite` and refuses the main thread (test-architecture §73, seven planted readers / openers as controls); ORCH `src/server/usage-index.js` starts it 30 s after boot (from account-usage-routes.js), keeps one FIFO, names every unavailability. EXCLUSIVE + WAL + NORMAL: no -shm; a second server on the same data/ gets SQLITE_BUSY, says so, never retries. user_version ≠ 1 / NOTADB / CORRUPT ⇒ delete and rebuild; SQLITE_FULL / IOERR / READONLY / ENOSPC ⇒ off by name. Owner Q3 (the 22.16 floor lands with lane 4): node:sqlite loads only inside the worker, so an older Node has the shadow off BY NAME and the server never notices.
- **Read-your-writes (design 011 §2).** Both commit points push the bytes they just appended (`_pushIndex`: shard, start offset, inode, text) in the same synchronous step, and the comparer posts its query in the same step as the memory answer — the FIFO answers over exactly the appends that answer saw. A push is taken only when it starts at the shard's mark with the marked inode; anything else (a dropped push, a torn tail before it, a rewrite in between, the first build having read past it) re-reads that shard from its mark. The commit point's order is unchanged: append (+ push), cursors, ack.
- **Recovery by shard marks** — (size, inode, sha1 of the first ≤ 4 KiB, bytes consumed) → append | rebuild (every repair's tmp + rename is a new inode; a shrink; a changed head) | gone | same; 16 MiB chunks, each committed with its mark (kill -9 loses at most the chunk in flight); `reloadEvents` and the re-bake ask for a re-check.
- **Measured: process.exit() joins worker threads.** With the worker blocked in a syscall (open() of a FIFO) the process never exits (`timeout 10` killed the probe). The owner's `exit` hook asks the worker to close and waits ≤ 2 s on a SharedArrayBuffer flag, then re-raises SIGTERM with the default action (systemd: a clean stop). A deadline answers 503 `unresponsive` and never terminates the worker.
- **The aggregate is ONE grouped pass**: session × the raw columns every dimension derives from × UTC day × local hour / weekday (JS `getHours` / `getDay` registered as SQL functions — the calls memory makes), folded in the worker, priced per (model, account) cell by the ledger's own `_cost`. 500 000 synthetic rows: ~1 s, against ~6 s for a GROUP BY per dimension and ~5.3 s through a temp table. Build: 160 000 rows in 1.2 s, 57 MB.
- **L0 — the cursor store.** `_cursors.json` is written only when its bytes change (`_cursorsJson` = the text on disk; JSON.stringify of production's parsed file gives the file back). The walker's unchanged-file path stamps `sid` into an entry once (parity-pinned with the shipped scanner), so the first idle walk after a scan still writes; an active machine still writes most walks — the size is what shrinks. Keys whose transcript is gone are dropped by the walk's writer at most hourly and only on proof (under a readable walk root, stat ENOENT); an unmounted projects dir drops nothing. Production, read once 2026-10-03: 37 024 keys, 25 817 dead (4.1 of 6.7 MB), every key under the two roots, 45 ms to stat them all.
- **Scratch sweep.** `scripts/ci.mjs` `sweepUsageIndexDirs` (after every suite, both runners) removes `~/.vibespace/db/<x>/` only when its owner.json names an absolute data/ that is gone.
- **Gates.** NEW test-usage-index-parity (fast, 2.3 s, 40 ✓ — L0; 14 query shapes over duplicate rids differing in account, rid-less rows, an empty shard, a torn line, a remote harvest into an old month, a push onto a torn line, a missed push, a repair rewrite; read-your-writes through both commit points with a tail-only CONTROL worker; a TZ=America/St_Johns child across a DST change). NEW test-usage-index-owner (fast, 7.4 s, 32 ✓ — kill -9 mid-build and mid-push-stream, deleted / newer / older / not-a-database rebuilt, a second opener, a deadline 503 keeping the worker, SIGTERM bounded with a wedged worker + CONTROL, SQLITE_FULL / no node:sqlite / a dead worker named, the sweep). test-architecture §73 + the PURE set.
- **Verify r1 (on a copy of the real 296 MB ledger: 613 710 rows, built in 4.3 s, a 343 MB index, parity on every Usage-window dimension and the 8 heaviest pivots).** Four fixes, each a test-usage-index-owner §8 leg with its pre-fix CONTROL: L0 drops a dead key only when the key's own directory answers and its root still holds a live key — an unmounted FUSE transcript root (an EMPTY mount point) dropped every live cursor, and one 1.1 GB transcript walked again appended 21 MB of duplicate rows; a full disk (SQLITE_FULL / ENOSPC / EDQUOT) deletes the disabled index's files (a stopped build left 146 MB on the full disk); the worker's V8 heap is capped (`heapMb` 128) and the aggregate streams its grouped rows (`iterate`) — uncapped, a first build left the server +262 MB RSS for good, now +109 MB, same build time; liveness runs on `performance.now()` (a wall-clock step back after a deadline kept the index "unresponsive" for the size of the step). Measured, no change: the wedged worker on a stopped bindfs mount ends SIGTERM, SIGINT and an uncaught exception in 2.0 s (a `systemctl --user stop` with KillMode=process: 2.0 s, the detached child lives); the comparer adds ~76 ms of main-thread work per all-time window read (1.90 → 2.05 s).

### lane channels-quiet-index — a poll that brings nothing writes nothing to the channels index (design 011 lane 2)

**on a server with tens of thousands of conversations the channels index is no longer rewritten every two seconds while nothing arrives**

#### Every poll rewrote the whole index (design 011 F4, the db survey)

Measured on userW's pod: `data/channels/index.json` 87 MB, rewritten whole about every 2.3 s (≈ 35–40 MB/s) with no message arriving — every pass stamped `lane.lastPollAt` / `lastScanAt` / `walkStartedAt` into the conversation's row (src/server/channels-engine.js: the ingest's index update, the refusal), so a row was dirty after every poll and each flush wrote every chunk (`writeBuffersAtomic`).

- The three stamps leave the persisted row for `data/channels/poll-stamps.json` (`{v, fields, stamps: {key: [lastPollAt, lastScanAt, walkStartedAt]}}`, one line per conversation): memory first, written at most every 120 s (`STAMPS_FLUSH_MS`) and at close (tmp + rename); a key whose row left the index leaves at the next write; a row born under a departed key starts unstamped; an unreadable file is set aside like every store family there.
- They still persist (a row is due at `lastPollAt + cadence`): a clean restart or a kill -9 keeps every due time (the journal, below); a kill while the journal cannot be written (said) re-polls at most the rows whose due time fell in the lost 120 s; a deleted side file is SAID at the start (with the count of rows now due) and that re-poll goes through the vendor's budget and pace.
- `store.stamps` = `set` (the ONE writer) / `lane(row)` (the ONE read: the row's lane with the stamps over it — the engine's `laneOf`: the due list, the scheduler census, the watch, the refresh answer, the change feed's by-id gate, the agent's `polledAt`; channel-caps' `freshnessClaim` is handed that merged view, no signature change) / `get` / `flush`.
- The row serializer omits the three keys (`INDEX_KEYS`); `serializeChunk` heals a row that still carries them (an index written before this lane, or a write past the door): the newer instant wins into the side map, and the side file is written BEFORE the index write that drops them. Read-compatible, no migration.
- `flush` skips equal bytes: a touched chunk is compared with its cached bytes, a whole rebuild with the previous layout (as one byte stream), the top-level tables as text; `updatedAt` moves only with a real write; `flushStats()` gains `writes` / `skipped`.
- MEASURED (test-channels-index-scale ⑩): a quiet minute at 50 276 rows (51.9 MB on disk) — the timer's 12 passes polled the account in 2 of them and brought nothing: 0 index writes (2 flushes skipped, the same file); CONTROL the stamp back in the row: the 51.9 MB index written 2 times, once per polling pass. Printed, not judged: discovery's own cycle (every coldSec = 900 s) stamps `listedAt` on every listed row — 1 index write(s) per cycle, a fourth stamp outside this lane's three.
- Gates: test-channel-store ⑭ (a pass that brings nothing writes 0 index bytes; restart; legacy read + heal + kill after the heal; a departed / re-born key; the deleted file said; the engine census; the journal — 12 controls), test-channels-index-scale ⑩ (heavy), test-channels-engine (after a restart none due early + control; the side file deleted: said, spent through the budget), test-channel-drain ②c (a restart's re-poll in the model: clean 0, kill -9 ≤ the lost interval's share, file gone = 873 paced inside the minute), test-channels-census-pace unchanged.
- verify r1: a FOREIGN-shaped `poll-stamps.json` (another `v`, its columns renamed or gone) was read as "no stamps" in silence — every conversation due at once, unsaid; it is now set aside and said like every family (`v === 1` and a `lastPollAt` column required), and a v1 entry that is not a list is counted in a start line (test-channel-store ⑭ + a patched-copy control)
- fix (the 2.369.203 heavy run's test-channels-e2e ⑰ — the integration reverted this lane; bisected red on 103238d2, green on cc20f5c6): a kill -9 lost every stamp set since the side file's last write (≤ 120 s; that run's server never lived 120 s, so it had none), the restored window's row read "never polled", and its open fetched it at once as the owner's — ahead of discovery (drain rule 12); the vendor refusing that first fetch (Retry-After 20 s) held the 40 new conversations back for the whole wait. Each `stamps.set` now appends ONE line to `data/channels/poll-stamps.log` (the key's whole triple — O(the change), never the index); the side file's write folds it (truncated after the rename), a start replays it in order (the last line per key wins), a line a kill cut short is counted and said and the next line starts on its own. Gates: test-channel-store ⑭ (a SIGKILLed child: 40 of 40 instants read back with no side file; a torn tail; controls: no journal → 0 of 40, no replay → 0 of 40, no fold, close() leaves it unfolded), test-channels-engine (a kill → 0 due early; control no journal → every row due), test-channel-drain ②c words, test-channels-index-scale ⑩ prints the journal's bytes in the quiet minute, heavy test-channels-e2e ALL PASS 205 (⑰ red on 103238d2 in the same run shape).

### slack-core — Slack as the fourth Channels adapter (design 012 lane S1, B-ff09; Opus, base ed1e0b83)

- **The adapter** (`src/channels/slack.js` + PURE `slack-text.js` / `slack-limits.js` / `slack-manifest.js` / `slack-words.js`): each person's OWN internal Slack app, made from Slack's share-a-manifest link (user scopes only, rotation off); the User OAuth Token (`xoxp-`) is PASTED — `oauth-loopback` gains a third mode, `paste` (no listener; the paste is the exchange's `code`; a refused paste keeps the flow open). ONE `auth.test` per paste: identity `userId = T…/U…` (D11), scopes from `x-oauth-scopes`. Poll only: `users.conversations` (all four kinds; an app's DM flagged `app`), `conversations.history` to the anchor (`oldest`), `conversations.replies`, `reactions.get` (answered from the last page while fresh — no request), `files.info` + the private URL on files.slack.com ONLY.
- **Per-method buckets inside the adapter** (D3, the contract unchanged): Tier 1–4 floors per method in a sliding minute, one message a second per conversation (a sub-second gap is waited once), a 429 holds that method for its `Retry-After` (≤ 15 min); a spent method is the typed `rate-limited` with `retryAfterSec`; a clock that steps back frees nothing.
- **Render** (D10, no schema change): mrkdwn / rich_text / Block Kit / legacy attachments / files onto the existing block kinds; strikethrough as text; lists as "• " paragraphs; an UNKNOWN block is a card titled with its type; `thread_broadcast` is ONE record; `ekm_access_denied` said in our words; a clip's transcript is words. Mentions carry a closed `kind` (person / broadcast / group — a broadcast or a group never equals a person).
- **Three new contract rows** (`src/channels/index.js`): `caps.policyModes` (Slack: review only — `channel-policy.policyMode(policy, caps)` clamps a stored `direct`, the engine refuses `setPolicy direct` by name, the picker hides it), `caps.prepareSend` (each `@Name` resolved to an id ONCE at propose — handle › display › full › first name tiers; two people ⇒ the proposal refused `mention-ambiguous`; stored on the proposal, shown on the card, sent verbatim), `caps.retention: 'purge-on-remove'` (removing the account deletes msgs/<id>/, attachments/<id>/ and its ended proposals — store `purgeAccount`). `convCaps.audience` (dm / private / public / external + the organizations) is the card's "Seen by" line.
- **Engine**: Slack in `REAL_ADAPTERS`; a `signin:'paste'` registry row has no client (every credential question answers `source: 'paste'`); the index / row carry `app` (never the Direct tag — `channel-focus`); the account view adds `policyModes`, `retention`, `setup {probes}` (the first real install's probe list, by name: `lastRead`, `sendMarker`, `userOnlyManifest`, `scopes`, `planLimited`, `historyTier`).
- **Client**: the Connect / Re-authorize / Duplicate dialogs show four steps instead of an OAuth client for a paste row, the paste box is a password field (`xoxp-…`); the Outbox card's "Seen by" / "Notifies" / "Not a member here" lines; the reach editor offers only the vendor's modes; the account card says where the copy lives and that agents' reads go to the model provider (owner Q2), the free plan's hidden history; the remove dialog says the local copy goes. zh / ja for every new word (45 keys).
- **Gates**: NEW test-channels-slack-shape (118) and test-channels-slack-send (40, the REAL engine over the fake Slack — the token in no file of the data dir by scripts/secret-scan.mjs + a positive control); legs + controls in adapter-contract (172), record (frame census over the fixtures, mention kinds), placement (the fixture = the declaration), identity (T2/U1 ≠ T1/U1), focus (app DM), oauth-loopback (paste mode), peer-parsers (10 Slack rows, linear + capped), integrations-ui heavy (the zh connect card + paste box, 168). The fixtures' instants are moved to an hour ago for engine legs (`tsShift`) — the store's retention trims anything older than its floor.
- **Cut from S1 (design §2/§3)**: custom emoji pictures (`reactions.custom: 'none'` — their host emoji.slack-edge.com is not in this lane's egress; drawn as `:name:`); the paste refusal's sentence is English inside a zh dialog (a server sentence — a code the client words is a follow-up).
- **verify r1** (Opus): (F1) the per-method buckets' skew guard pinned the newest instant ever seen — a clock that ran ahead once (an RTC read as UTC at boot) and was then corrected froze every Slack method, send gap and hold until the wall clock caught up; a step back now REBASES the stored instants by the step (a step back still frees nothing). (F2) an owner's edit at Approve skipped `prepareSend` — an added `@Alice` two people answer went out as plain words and the card's Notifies line kept the proposal's names; the edit is now decided like the proposal (a name it adds is resolved or refused by name, a decided name keeps its id) and stored. (F3) three fast suites were red on the lane head and green in its build run (their censuses walk `git ls-files`, and the new files were untracked then): test-channels-egress (slack-limits / slack-text / slack-words now declare an empty `EGRESS`), test-channel-record's tree census (six Slack name sites classified), test-approval-census Z2 (slack-manifest's invisible-character class spelled as escapes). Legs + patched-copy controls in slack-shape / slack-send.

### lane accept-fixes-jobs (Opus fix, base ed1e0b83) — the agent browser inside a Background Work job: F5, F6, F10, F11 of the owner's acceptance of 2.369.202

- **F5 — `status` inside a job lied** ("no profile attached / pin: none (ephemeral)" while the next `open` landed on office-devices): the route answered `statusFor(<the job's child handle>)` — an empty set, no pin. Now `/api/agent/browser/status` for a `jbt_` adds `job` (src/routes/browser.js `jobBindingOf`): the profile the next page verb lands on by the ONE verdict `resolveForJob` runs (`jobResolveVerdict` over the owner's set — read only, nothing attached or told), the owner's pin, the job's own lease (its window) once it has one; the CLI prints those three lines (or `job_no_profile` with its words).
- **F6 — a job could not save into its own directory**, and the refusal told it to restart a "session started before this version": the jobs engine never exported a directory. `_spawn` now exports `VIBESPACE_JOB_CWD` = the job's `cmd.cwd` when absolute (never the server's `process.cwd()` fallback); vibespace-browser's fence takes it as the root inside a job (job token, no session token — the shell's `cd` never counts); `writePathVerdict({job})` says "the job's working directory" and, with none, names the job's case ("a run started before this VibeSpace version, or a job created without a directory").
- **F10 — the browsers row read "帮手 1" for the job's window:** `browser-profiles.attachmentsFor` rebuilt the child list as `{handle, since}` and DROPPED the `job` tag the keeper's `childrenOf` carries, so `/api/browser/session/:id`'s `jobNames` loop never ran and the row fell to "Helper {n}". The tag is kept (one line); the strip's UI files are untouched (browser-live-window's `Job: {name}` already existed).
- **F11 — a stopped job's window stayed open** in the shared profile: `releaseJob` → `detach(by:'user')` keeps a conversation's page for its return (`noteLeftTab`) — a job never returns. `releaseJobHandle` now closes the job's own tabs over CDP (`jobWindowCloser`: the holders snapshotted before the detach, `TBS.tabOwners` over one target read — the ownership its `tab list` uses; the user's, another holder's and orphan tabs untouched) and keeps no left-tab record for it. Decision: CLOSE, not keep — a kept window would be nobody's (the handle is dropped; no holder could close it). Every end reaches it: exit / crash / stop / boot through `_finalizeRun` → `onRunEnded` → `releaseJob`, archive / missed finalize through the reconcile sweep.
- **Gates:** test-jobs-browser 98 → 111 (④ + F5 before/after the first verb + the REAL CLI's status words, F10 through the route → `browserListFor`, F11 window closed at finalize and at the sweep with the owner's window untouched; ⑥ NEW: a real JobManager runs the real CLI — screenshot into the job's cwd passes the fence with TMPDIR elsewhere, outside it / no cwd refused in the job's words; exit / crash / stop each call `onRunEnded` once). Base ed1e0b83 + the new suite: 10 red (all 9 new rows + the copy's git-status row). Patched-copy controls (fixed tree, one file back to base): routes ⇒ the 2 F5 rows, jobs.js ⇒ 2 F6 rows, browser-verbs.js ⇒ 2 F6 word rows, browser-profiles.js ⇒ F10, keeper ⇒ 3 F11 rows.
- **Authority:** the job token's routes and admission are unchanged (status adds read-only facts of the job's own binding; the write fence is the CLI's local guard) — no verify round.
- **User line:** en "A Background Work job that uses the agent browser now shows under its own name in the live view, can save screenshots and downloads in its own folder, and its browser window closes when the job ends." · zh "使用 agent 浏览器的后台工作：实时视图里以任务名显示，截图和下载可以存到它自己的文件夹，任务结束时它的浏览器窗口随之关闭。" · ja "エージェントブラウザを使うバックグラウンド作業は、ライブビューでジョブ名で表示され、スクリーンショットやダウンロードを自分のフォルダに保存でき、ジョブが終わるとそのブラウザウィンドウも閉じます。"

### lane app-fit-fixed (Opus, 2026-10-03) — a window whose app fixes its size: frame = picture, not resizable, never scaled

- **The owner (2.369.202, "2× · 自动"):** WeChat's login filled the top-left ~45 % of a blank window; Inkscape 1.4.3's welcome was cut at the bottom between two bands. Correction mid-lane (binding): the app's title area under our bar is expected (the bars auto-hide); a fixed-size window is FOLLOWED and resizing is disabled — no "scaled-down 75 %" rule.
- **Root cause, measured (real xpra 6.5.4, headless Chrome 1920×963 DPR 2, sidebar 470, xprop beside xpra's metadata):** both apps state min = max (WeChat 560×760, Inkscape 1420×1356 device px). WeChat: the fit honoured the maximum but the window learnt only a minimum ⇒ a 280×380 CSS picture in an 898×618 pane, 81 % blank. Inkscape: the welcome is a lone DIALOG (modal, no transient-for, the only window) ⇒ no main: never fitted or named, mapped at X's centre 188,0 (94 CSS px bands), 678 CSS px tall in a 555 px pane. A 1000×900 GTK fixture at 2× was scaled to fit (stage 0.903, badge).
- **Fix:** xpra-proto `fixedSizeOf`; xpra-client `fixedWindow` / `loneFixed` / `on.fixed` (a lone fixed dialog at 0,0, held by the belt, contained by the display); xpra-view `onFixedSize` + no scale while `fixedFollows()`; desktop-app-window → `WindowManager.setFixedSize` (min = max inline, uncapped, no handles / maximize button (style.css), no resize drag, no maximize, no snap/grid zone, `_placeWindow` moves only, `resizeWindowTo` refuses; null restores the pre-lock size). After: pane = picture to 0.0 CSS px for WeChat (282×382 window), Inkscape (712×743), both fixtures; stage 1.
- **Larger than the workspace (asked by the owner to report):** the window keeps the app's size, its top on the workspace, the rest past the bottom / right edge and clipped by #workspace (the 1000×900 fixture at 2× on an 878 px workspace: 86 CSS px); it cannot be dragged above the workspace top, so Scale ▸ 1× is how to see that strip. Phone layout: today's scale-to-fit kept.

The panel row (src/browser-trace.js `remoteOwned`) is no longer `not-ours` for a paired machine's profile whose provider owns its directory: Browse yourself, Delete…, Stop; housekeeping's `queueVerdict` still refuses it (this machine's sweep never judges another machine's folder).

### lane windows-device-fs — the Files view and every other hub→device shell call on a Windows machine

- **The report** (coordinator, 2026-10-03 02:50 PDT): GET /api/files?host=host-dial-WIN-DESK1 → 400 "command failed (127)" — src/remote-fs.js ran `sh -c` for every device file operation; a Windows machine has no `sh`.
- **Files**: a Windows agent's files go through its own fs ops (`fs-portable`: + `home` / `copy` / `move` / `du`, `~` expanded on the device, downloads over read-range); folder .zip and the archive verbs are refused by name; an agent without `fs-portable` gets "this machine's agent is X, too old to browse files on Windows — rerun the device's install command (Remote → <machine> → Pairing command)". POSIX machines unchanged.
- **The door**: src/agentd/client.js refuses a `sh` / `bash` argv or session spawn asked of a win32 agent by name (`windows_no_shell`) before sending; the census (36 sites) judges every hub→device shell site.
- **verify-r1 F1 (HIGH, fixed)**: keyed on the PLATFORM, the door refused a Windows machine WITH `sh` (Git for Windows / MSYS2 / Cygwin put sh.exe on PATH; node resolves `sh` to it) the 28 sites it ran before, and an old agent's Files view. Now the agent measures at its first hello which POSIX shells start there (`posixShells`); the door refuses only a shell that list leaves out; an agent too old to say is asked (once per link on the Files route) and a failed spawn is named (`windows_no_shell` / the outdated sentence), never a bare 127.
- **verify-r2**: the agent's shell probe is async, parallel and bounded (3 s, the child killed): a shell counts only if it RAN `echo vs-$((40+2))` and answered `vs-42` — a hung `sh` (WSL booting / a prompt), a broken one (exit ≠ 0), a non-POSIX one are absent (r1 counted all three present and blocked the agent 5 s per shell: first link 5.5 s → 3.0 s); every hello re-measures (a shell installed later is seen at the next link). An old agent's one-per-link `sh -c 'exit 0'` counts only an exit 0 (a broken `sh` ⇒ the outdated sentence). The Files routes send the refusal as a CODE + params (`fsErrorBody`), worded client-side in zh / ja (`fsErrorText`); du stopped at 10^6 entries reads "at least …"; a cross-drive move that fails says what is left where (no partial copy, no errno).
- **Gates**: test-windows-device-fs (new, fast, 134), test-exit-run, test-sysinfo-op, test-raw-filename, test-agentd-switchover, test-architecture, test-changelog-style, `npm run build`, every fast suite that reads a touched file.

## 2.369.203 — 2026-10-03

### prod-stall-202 — the 6–15 s production stalls (Opus): 2.369.202 stopped its event loop every one to two minutes

- **Diagnosed on the live process (read-only):** SIGUSR1 → V8 inspector on 127.0.0.1:9229, Profiler at 1 ms for 240 s (11:51:19–11:55:20Z), inspector closed (`process._debugEnd`, 9229 no longer listening). The profile's 16.9 s busy run (11:54:59→11:55:16Z = the journal's 04:55:20 "longest loop gap 11s") is 13.4 s `readFileUtf8`: the auto-cli `tick` (auto-cli-loop.js:121) → `projectionRereadFor` × 13 accounts → `sessionBillingMember` × 25 pooled conversations → `validateBillingSlot` → `accounts.poolMembers` → `parseClaudeAuth` × 13 members × 2 files ≈ 9 K synchronous reads a tick (10.1 s), plus `maybePoolAutoSwitchForPool` (2.9 s), the usage walker's per-line `resolveAccount` → `accounts.list()` (2.0 s), `loginStateOf` (1.2 s). The data dir is bindfs over NFS (100–180 µs per 2 KB read, worse under load 29). Not new code: the hot functions are identical in 2.369.201 (whose telemetry already shows 0.5–3.6 s max lag, one 9.2 s); the stall length follows the NFS latency. Profile + analysis scripts: /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/prod-stall-202/.
- **Fix:** `accounts.isPoolMember` (one login read, the same predicate as `poolMembers().some`), `projectionBillingIndex` (who-bills-where once per tick, dropped with the tick; `projectionRereadFor(member, now, index)`), `accounts.poolsWithMember` (memberPoolsOf's hot-pool answer read live, one login per pool), server.js `resolveAccount` from the record. 11 514 → 498 fs calls a tick at production's shape; 1.8 s → 82 ms synchronous at 150 µs per call.
- **Gate:** test-auto-cli-tick-reads (24) — decisions equal to a fix-reverted patched copy across login-file states, hot/held pools and mid-tick login changes; WORK linear in conversations and members; LOOP < 250 ms with the reverted copy > 1 s. test-auto-cli-refresh's four wiring pins follow the new signature. Hotfix-sized (5 files, no state format, no route): fit to ship on top of 2.369.203 alone.

### lane channels-followups — an agent's `list` bounded to the newest 200; Gmail's own search behind channel search (designs 008 S6, 010 S6)

**an agent's channel list names the newest 200 conversations it can see and says how many more (found with search); searching a Gmail account also asks Gmail's own search over the whole mailbox — each hit marked "not saved here", its thread a click away**

- design 008 S6: `engine.listFor` sorts the conversations the caller may see (reach asked of every row — the count needs it) by `lastAt` and builds only the newest `LIST_FOR_MAX` (200). The answer adds `more` (the rest of what it may see), `moreRequestable` (the same bound over `--all`'s directory titles) and `max`; a hidden conversation is in neither count. The CLI prints one line after the rows — `… N more conversations you can see — only the newest 200 are listed; use search: …` — and `… N more you may request` under the directory; the manual says the bound.
- design 010 S6: Gmail declares `caps.search {via:'query', scope:null, pageSize:10, pagesPerPress:2, perMin:6, cost:205, snippet:true, context:'thread', match:'tokens'}`. `search` = `messages.list?q=<words>&maxResults=10` with no label filter (all mail but spam and trash — also the threads outside the synced scope), the page judged (not an object, `messages` not a list, more than 10 ⇒ vendor-error); per id: not shown to the caller ⇒ dropped with no read at all (neither the vendor nor the local log); held locally ⇒ the hit at its stored instant, no read; else ONE `messages.get format=metadata&metadataHeaders=From` (internalDate, the From address, Gmail's `snippet` through `SR.snippetOf`); a message gone between the list and its read ⇒ malformed; a 429 re-throws (the engine backs the account's search off). `around` = ONE `threads.get format=full` (no memo, no title cache, no body held), ≤ 50 messages centred on the hit.
- Engine: `vendorSearch` hands the adapter two HINTS — `storedAt(convId, vendorId)` (an index row, then `store.findRecord`'s instant) and, for an agent's `--full`, `shows(convId)` (its visible set) — so a per-hit read is spent only on a hit the person is shown; Lark's one-request page ignores both. Floor, share, minute, budget, reach after the await, no page token for agents, nothing stored: Lark's leg unchanged.
- Units: the quota table (`unitsFor`, read 2026-09-26) charges `messages.get` 20 — the design's "5 units per hit" is `messages.list`'s price. A page costs ≤ 5 + 10 × 20 = 205 units (`cost`), paced at the account's 40 units/s (≈ 5 s for a page of ten new hits).
- Words: `match: 'tokens'` (Gmail matches words) ⇒ the dialog says "may be related". Gmail has no change feed, so the VS1–VS4 counters (`rec.feed.counters.fullSearch`) are Lark's alone.
- Words (verify r1 F2): a search row declares what its hits ADD — `caps.search.adds: 'older' | 'unsaved'`, required and refused by name in the registry (Lark and the fakes `older`, Gmail `unsaved`: mail outside the synced scope or a reply newer than its stored thread is not "older"). `SR.statusText` / `SR.sectionHead` and the agent's `--full` line read the row, never the adapter id: Gmail's dialog says "Not saved here — from Gmail's search" / "Asked Gmail's whole mailbox: N not saved here — may be related" (4 keys × zh / ja); Lark's words unchanged.
- Gates: test-channels-agent-cli ⑳ (the REAL engine behind the stub: 205 visible + 230 newer hidden ⇒ 200 rows + "5 more"; `--all` 200 + 200; CONTROLS: no bound ⇒ 205 rows, a whole-index count ⇒ "237 more"); test-channels-gmail-shape ⑳ (a fresh engine connected through the consent loopback: the press reads 4 metadata — never the held msg_ops_b; an agent that sees one thread reads 1; around = one threads.get, 50 of 60; nothing born or appended; a 429 ⇒ `backoff` and no call inside it; the adapter alone; the hints' order — `shows` before `storedAt`; CONTROLS: an engine copy without the hints reads the held and the hidden hits, an adapter copy asking `storedAt` first reads the hidden thread's ids, an adapter copy without the reader returns the 1 MB snippet); test-vendor-whitelist §FS-G (Gmail's words request and per-hit read live in `search` only, the thread read in `around` only; two planted controls); census rows in test-peer-text-census (the list's counts) and test-record-clear-census (`vendorSearch`'s `store.index.has(` gate).

### lane store-timing — measure the stores' sync writes and the mount, off the main thread (design 011 lane 1, step M)

The owner asked which parts are dragged down by file reads and writes and need a real database (2026-10-03). Design 011 answers "SQLite only as the usage ledger's index" and orders everything else by measurement — this lane is that measurement. It fixes nothing.
- **The clock.** NEW PURE `src/timed-sync.js`: `timedSync(name, fn)` with a CLOSED name table `STORES` (20 rows: session-meta, session-status, user-todos, task-groups, jobs, job-notifications, channels index, usage shards, usage cursors, otel-truth (read / boot rewrite / append), the telemetry summary read), a fixed-bucket histogram per name (≤1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500 ms, 1, 2, 5 s, slower), per-minute maxima for the last hour. OFF until server.js turns it on before any store is built (`VIBESPACE_STORE_TIMING=0` keeps it off); off = `if (!on) return fn();`, no clock read. The span is the write call as the store makes it today (a helper that stringifies inside the call counts its stringify). An unknown name runs untimed — a typo can never break a write.
- **The sites** (24 calls): writeSessionMeta + readSessionMeta (session-stdout.js), session-status / user-todos `_flush` + their boot reads, task-groups `_save` / `_load`, jobs `_save` (jobs.json and job-notifications.json apart) / `_saveNotifs` / `_load`, the channels index write (`writeIndex`, both the incremental and the fallback write) and its boot read, the usage commit point (shard appends in `_walkAndAppend` and `ingestRemoteEvents`, the cursor write) and the cursor read, otel-ingest's boot read + rewrite and its per-request append, telemetry `summary()`'s shard reads. The commit point's order (appends, then cursors) is unchanged — timedSync is synchronous.
- **Reported**: every 5 min one `srv-store-ms:<name>` metric per name with samples (value = the window's max, detail = n + the bucket counts) — the Diagnostics summary gives their percentiles; `/api/sysinfo` (this machine only) carries `storeWrites` = the three slowest writes of the last hour; the System window draws it as one line, "Slowest store writes (last hour): jobs 812 ms · channels/index 240 ms" (en/zh/ja).
- **The canary off the main thread.** The 2.108.6 canary moved from server.js into NEW `src/server/fs-canary.js` + `fs-canary-worker.js`: the stat runs and is timed in its own one-worker SafeFs (an ASYNC stat on purpose — it watches the shared libuv pool), and the main side measures only how long the answer waited. `srv-fs-canary-ms` (worker clock, the only fact that strikes; three timeouts → `srv-threadpool-wedged` + the mount health sweep, as before) and NEW `srv-loop-canary-ms` (a blocked loop) are logged and counted apart; a probe with no answer is `srv-fs-canary-lost`, never a strike. Before, a main-thread stall longer than 5 s struck as a wedged pool.
- **Gates.** NEW scripts/test-timed-sync.mjs (fast, 21): buckets, the closed names, zero clock reads when off, the hour window, the real stores' names in a scratch dir. NEW scripts/test-fs-canary.mjs (fast, 20): a 1.5 s and a past-the-deadline blocked loop read as the loop's fact only; a pool saturated from the main thread reads as the fs fact; three timeouts strike and kick the sweep; a lost probe; CONTROL — a copy that times the stat on the main thread again reads the same blocked loop as a 1500 ms stat. test-architecture §72: every sync write inside a write row's sites sits inside a timedSync of that file's rows (unwrapped ones printed), every call is a literal row in its own file, every row used; planted controls + the real jobs.js `_save` unwrapped. Both suites registered fast in scripts/ci.mjs.
