### lane chat-scroll — a send always lands on the sent message (B-172e); the paging gate's mirror flake (B-8c25)

- **B-172e (inc-mt1zrvj3-wsr4, owner on 2.361.6: after scrolling up, a sent message was not shown).** The incident bundle had aged out of data/incidents, so the cause was reproduced on b924041f with a new heavy suite (test-chat-send-landing: a live session behind the real chat-wrapper + a stub CLI over a 40 MB §1c transcript, real wheel + a typed Enter). Three mechanisms: ① `jumpToBottom` sized its slab by the total read before its fetch, and the user's own echo (fed live by the server in the same breath) arrived during that fetch on a view still in history — deferred, then replaced by a slab that ended before it; ② a teleported seek slab's stale accounting read "at the tail", so onSend pinned the slab; ③ an extend in flight across the send wrote its old slab into the new window (`window 776..377` on the base run). Fixes: `_tailHold` (live ops held across the tail fetch, replayed in order once the slab is the pinned view; window end = the slab's end), the slab branch in onSend, `_windowGen` + `_windowMoved` (a page answered after a full-window rebuild is dropped). Each fix has its own scratch-copy control that fails its own row.
- **B-8c25 (test-chat-paging ① red once on the 2.369.195 mirror).** Re-read from the job log: the red was `up-fast-3: landed at scrollTop 31 (inside the 100 px pageUp band) with 2472 messages and the gap still above`; the `runsRestore` ring the item cited is the §4d control's `up-mid-1` evidence, and its `by` is only the last writer (2.7 s earlier). Cause: a notch inside the 300 ms post-landing load lock scrolled into the pageUp band and nothing re-took the skipped decision (the lift re-checked `scrollTop < 10` only). Fix: `_lockSkippedPageUp` at the lift, on the scroll handler's own evidence (a real wheel-up ≤ 1200 ms, unpinned, history above). Gate: test-chat-paging §4g, constructed, with an instance-neutered control that parks.
- **Verify r1 (lane chat-scroll): a hung tail fetch held the whole view.** B-172e's hold was released by the last overlapping `jumpToBottom` to finish, so one tail fetch that never answered kept every live op held: the reader's ↓ landed a pinned tail slab without the sent message or its answer, and the next send did not show either, until the hung fetch answered and its older slab replaced the view. Fix: only the newest tail call (`_tailCall`) lands or fails for the view; an older call answered later drops its slab. Gate: test-chat-send-landing row `hang-return` + control `ctl-newest`.
- **Gates.** test-chat-trim-guard, test-hidden-view-suspend, test-text-window, test-fold-ux + test-run-collapse-fold (the brief's "test-chat-run-summary" does not exist; these two pin chat-run-summary.js and the fold pass), test-architecture, test-changelog-style, `npm run build`; heavy: test-chat-paging (with §4g), test-desktop-resume-paging, test-chat-send-landing (new, ci.mjs heavy). test-desktop-resume-paging's source-level control gained patch (6), the `_windowGen` layer stripped (old control, new layer): without it the control's ungated sentinel page was dropped as stale by the resume re-tail's rebuild and its `extendTop:done` check went red on the fix.

#### B-31d7 — a long backlog line is refused by name instead of stored clipped and answered "not stored"

- Root cause, measured on the store: B-4ffb (the reported item) is stored at exactly 500 characters — `TaskGroupManager.update()` clips an item's line to `CAPS.backlogItem` (500) and its detail to `CAPS.detail` (6000), and the route's identity echo compared that clipped text with the sent one ⇒ 500 "the item was not stored — nothing parked" for an item that was in the store. The report's "~330 characters" was an estimate; a 330-character CJK title stores and echoes fine on the base.
- POST /api/agent/task-backlog: `add` past either cap ⇒ 400 before the write ("the item's line is N characters — … at most 500; shorten it and put the rest in --detail (up to 6000 characters) — nothing parked"); `edit` with `--text` / `--detail` past the cap ⇒ 400 "… — nothing changed". The caps are `BACKLOG_CAPS` exported by src/task-groups.js (one source). The UI's own backlog edits still go through `update()` unchanged.

### lane page-link — a /p/<id> page link in chat opens the page (B-2dbc)

**a page link in an agent's message opens the page again (Cmd/Ctrl+click) and a click copies its full address; a web address in a code span or a tool's output is copied and opened whole**

- **The incident** (userW inc-murolahg-3rtv, 2.369.199; report /var/tmp/vibespace-lanes/userW-forensics-4/report.md): an agent wrote "私有页 /p/pg5vex1gylcn（文件 …）"; two clicks copied the bare "/p/pg5vex1gylcn", a Cmd+click flashed "Not found" and opened nothing. Unchanged in .200 / .201.
- **Cause.** `linkifySegment` runs URLs → `/p/<id>` pages → paths. The path pass split the HTML at tags and linkified EVERY text run — also the text inside the spans the earlier passes made: `/p/pg…` matches PATH_SRC, and so does the `//host/…` of a URL (the lookbehind stops at `:`). The click handler's `closest('.chat-link')` found the INNER path span: a click copied its data-path, Cmd+click asked /api/file/info → "Not found". The page pass ran over the raw HTML, so `https://x/a-/p/pg…` put a span inside the URL's `data-href`. Assistant prose hides the URL half (marked autolinks a prose URL to `<a>`, which linkify skips); code spans and tool output (`linkifyText`) do not. test-path-linkify's ORDER pin claimed the path pass "never sees them" — it read the call order, never ran the renderer.
- **Fix** (src/lib/chat-renderers.js): `_linkifyBareText(html, fn)` — one alternation that skips a whole `<span class="chat-link…">text</span>` and every tag; the page pass and the path pass both run through it. Our link spans hold escaped text only, so the skip is exact. `/p/<id>/raw` still links the page shell (unchanged).
- **Byte identity.** Every cell the pre-fix rule rendered without a nested link is unchanged (15 of 27: paths with :line:col, CJK punctuation, relative code spans, markdown links, prose URLs); only the nested inner span is gone from page links and from URLs in code / tool output.
- **Gates.** test-path-linkify 14 → 26 (now in-process, ~0.5 s: ④ the REAL renderer bundled by esbuild — the userW message as an assistant message and as tool output, a URL in code / tool output, the page-in-URL attribute, the CENSUS over 9 texts × 3 entries (no link inside a link, no markup inside an attribute, reach 19 cells); ⑤ a patched copy without the link-span skip reproduces `span.chat-link > span.chat-link-path data-path="/p/…"`, the census goes red on 12 cells, byte identity over the rest). test-page-link-ui (new, heavy, chrome, ~9 s, 16): a stub claude behind the real wrapper answers with the incident's message; a REAL click copies `<origin>/p/<id>`, a REAL Cmd+click opens a tab on it (no "Not found", no file probe), a URL in a code span copies whole; ⑤ the pre-fix rule re-installed on the live renderer copies the bare path and flashes "Not found". On the base tree the node legs are 8 red, the chrome leg (head tree with only chat-renderers.js reverted) 8 red.

### lane window-targets-residuals — window-target residuals (B-a38d, B-f18a)

#### B-a38d — after a restart, `type` with no ref under an `auto` share acts as the resolved mode instead of answering the machine

- **Reproduced on b924041f** (the runner's shape, four ways the tree is unreachable, through the real engine): attach resolved `auto` to pixels, `type "hi"` with no ref answered `no_injection_backend` (the pixel road; no xdotool there); a second engine over the same data dir (a restart: the share and the lease persist, `resolutions` live in memory) answered the SAME call `python3_missing` / `a11y_unavailable` / `helper_error` / `helper_missing` — `act()` saw no resolution, so `pixelShare` was false and it asked the tree for the focused node and passed the helper's code through. The residual was named (not changed) in the 2.369.181 mirror-red entry of kb-bugfix-invariants.
- **Fix** (src/server/window-targets-engine.js `act` → `type`): an `auto` share with no resolution in this process is resolved (`ensureResolved`, the attach probe) BEFORE a no-ref `type` picks its road, followed by a re-check (`held()`), the share re-read; the road then follows the resolved mode (pixels ⇒ keys, tree ⇒ the focused node). The focused-node read gets its own re-check too (a revoke during it answered `no_focused_node` / the helper's code to a revoked session). The old `held()` before `actOnNode` is now redundant by construction and annotated `// no-await-before`.
- **Why not "refuse `mode_pixels`"** (the backlog's one-line hint): pixel mode ALLOWS `type` without a ref (keys); a `mode_pixels` refusal would have told the agent to "act with … type" — the call it just made — and the same call before the restart typed keys. The manual's table says `auto` acts "as the resolved mode"; the 2.369.181 entry's residual named exactly this road ("resolving first would add a re-check site the §5 census must pin").
- **Gates:** test-window-targets §4r (each shape: before and after a restart ⇒ `no_injection_backend`, the re-resolution names the reason; THE LAW: one code across four shapes; NEGATIVE CONTROL = a patched copy without the pre-road probe answers `python3_missing` / `a11y_unavailable` / `helper_error` / `helper_missing`); §5 two race legs (a revoke during the pre-road probe on a display with no injection backend ⇒ `not_exposed`, never the backend verdict; a revoke during the focused-node read with nothing focused ⇒ `not_exposed`, never `no_focused_node`) — the per-site census neuters each new `held()` and a leg goes red.

#### B-f18a — the window-injection leftovers (lane E verify r4 O1–O4)

- **Reproduced on b924041f** (repro script, fake xdotool / `locale` binaries): ① a type whose xdotool got SIGTERM from outside answered `xdotool type failed (exit null): no message` and ran NO release pass (`runInject` read only `err.killed`, which is node's own kill); ② a `locale` with no C.UTF-8, an env naming no locale and `en_US.utf8` in `locale -a` ⇒ `no_utf8_locale`; ③ an xdotool whose stderr echoes its argv (a `set -x` wrapper) put the typed text in the refusal (`… -- my secret passphrase; Invalid multi-byte sequence encountered`); ④ a hanging `locale`: the first verdict took 6,010 ms (3 s per candidate), the second 0 ms — the 60 s NO memo was already on the base.
- **Fix.** ① `runInject` marks a signal death nobody here sent `outside` and `killed`; `afterKill` releases and says "killed part-way by SIGTERM (not by VibeSpace)" — key / click / scroll / type alike. ② `utf8LocaleEnv` (src/desktop-display.js) gains a third tier: `locale -a`'s UTF-8 locales (en_US first, at most 4, each verified with `locale charmap`), the list remembered 60 s. ③ `xdoStderr`: a refusal quotes only xdotool's measured lines (`Invalid multi-byte sequence encountered`, `xdo_enter_text_window reported an error`, `Failed creating new xdo instance`, `Error: Can't open display: (null)|:N`) and counts the rest as withheld. ④ the walk stops at the first `locale` timeout (6 s → 3 s; with the new tier it would have been 9 s), the NO memo kept.
- **Gates:** test-window-targets §2 — four legs, each with a patched copy of the pre-fix code as its control (① releases nothing; ② refused; ③ the text in the refusal; ④ three calls ≥ 750 ms on a time-scaled copy whose only change is the probe limit).

### lane pool-readings-truth — B-a4f1: the estimator's weekly roll waits the same landing minute as the pool's own reader

- **The premise was wrong; the switch was real.** B-a4f1 read the 2026-09-18 incident as "an empty-window reading (0 % with a sliding reset) on an exhausted member drew the pool onto it". The production record says otherwise. Journal 08:59:15 PDT (15:59:15Z): nine conversations moved onto Personal Max ("its fable quota was at 0%") and every continue was rejected; the vendor's wall named 16:00:00Z. The member's last reading before that was the isolated panel at 15:31:17Z (usage-probe-log): "Current week (Fable): 100% used · resets Sep 18, 8:59am", parsed as 15:59:00Z. That is a STATED reset, minute-precise and 15 s in the past, not an empty window. The 16:27Z write the item blamed came from the `control` rung (anchor stream, `source:'control'`), and it was TRUE: the week rolled at 16:00Z, the 16:04Z panel already read 0 %/0 %, and the 16:45Z panel read 5h 90 % after 410 requests. Its 5h reset 21:20Z was pinned (the window opened at 16:20Z), and `windowState` filed it as `empty` (425 s < 600 s jitter). That costs a deadline, never headroom.
- **Why 2.369.117 did not stop it.** That release named this very switch ("09:59:15Z … 45 s before", the PDT wall clock labelled Z) and put `RESET_GRACE_SEC` into `bucketRemaining`. But the engine reads members through `poolReadCache`, the estimator overlay. `estimateBuckets` re-based a weekly bucket on the bare stated instant (`resetSec * 1000 <= nowMs` → u 0, reset +7 d), and `overlayCache` replaced the raw dead bucket with that one, so the grace never saw it. The member's learned rates exist (rates.json `org:29c41b2c…`), so this was the live path. Reproduced on the base b924041f (`pool-readings-truth/repro/a4f1-replay.cjs`, the real writer, estimator and decidePoolSwitch): the raw path decides `null`, the overlay path decides `to:'pm' reason:'exhausted'`.
- **FIX.** `RESET_GRACE_SEC` moved into PURE src/quota-model.js (account-pool-auto imports and re-exports it). Inside the grace, `estimateBuckets` abstains on a weekly bucket, so the overlay keeps the raw reading and `bucketRemaining` rules it. One second past the grace it rolls exactly as before. The 5h roll is unchanged (it always abstained).
- **Not built:** "refuse placement whose only evidence is an empty window". No incident supports it, and quota-model's r4 measurement shows that refusing a stated 0 % regresses a fresh member to "no usage data".
- **Gates:** test-pool-auto (+4: the 15:59:15Z replay through the overlay, the grace edge, the roll one second past it, one constant), test-usage-estimator (+2). Pre-fix control: the same suites over `git archive b924041f`, where the 15 s, edge and constant legs are red.

### lane pool-readings-truth — B-9b40: the auto-cli /usage probe loads no MCP server

- **Measured, not assumed.** Production: under every member's probe cwd (`~/.cache/claude-cli-nodejs/…-probe-config-cwd/`) sit five `mcp-logs-claude-ai-*` dirs (Claude Docs, Gmail, Google Calendar, a writing assistant, Idiolect). There are ~515 files each for Personal Max, one per probe, the newest 2026-10-03T01:01:35Z, each starting "Initializing claude.ai proxy transport … Using claude.ai proxy at https://mcp-proxy…". In the claude 2.1.288 binary, `headlessSyncsClaudeAiConnectors` is `!vk() && !HYe() && !Hr()`, and `vk()` is `mcpProcessWiring.strictConfig()`, which `--strict-mcp-config` sets. So print mode lists the account's connectors (`/v1/mcp_servers`) and connects each through the mcp-proxy unless the MCP config is strict.
- **FIX.** One frozen `PANEL_PROBE_ARGS = ['-p', '/usage', '--strict-mcp-config']` in src/usage-routes.js, used by both the spawn and the probe log. With no `--mcp-config`, no MCP server is loaded, and the probe's one vendor call is the panel. §ban-safety: the change removes calls and adds none. I did not run the real CLI here (that would be a vendor call); the fake-CLI leg records the argv the binary received.
- **Gates:** test-vendor-whitelist §5b (+3: the flag present and no `--mcp-config`, /usage only, one spelling at the spawn), test-usage-probe-log §2 (+1: the fake `claude` records its argv, and the log names the same argv). Pre-fix control over `git archive b924041f`: all four are red.

### lane pool-readings-truth — B-ce1c: the machine login and the pool's copy of the same account are labelled as two sign-ins (the "reuse the machine login" half is a design question, not built)

- **The owner's misreading (2026-09-07).** `~/.claude/.credentials.json` held the owner's own address, alive to 09-10. The pool's copy `data/subs/sub-cac86a3ff4d1` (the same account) had expired on 09-02. Manage Agents' CLI-login row read `= “Personal Max”`, and the usage popup folded the CLI-login chip into Personal Max's ("also the CLI login on this machine"), so the live machine login was taken for Personal Max.
- **FIX (words only).** PURE `machineLoginLinkHint(name, vendor)` in src/lib/manage-agents.js. The row now reads `same account as “Personal Max” · a separate sign-in`, and its tooltip says: one Anthropic account, one quota, usage merged, but two sign-ins that each expire and renew on their own, and signing in one does not sign in the other. The codex twin (the machine ~/.codex login vs a ChatGPT account) uses the same helper. The usage popup's merged chip says "one quota, two separate sign-ins". Three new strings in zh/ja; the three superseded keys are removed.
- **Verified from the binary (claude 2.1.288):** the claude.ai OAuth refresh (`grant_type:"refresh_token"`) destructures `refresh_token: K = e` from the response and stores `K`, so the CLI keeps whatever rotated token the server returns. The repo already records server-side rotation ("token self-refresh ROTATES the refresh token out from under the CLI", kb-design-lessons; accounts.js: one credential copy per account so a rotating refresh token is never rotated out from under a sibling). So "reuse the machine login" cannot COPY ~/.claude/.credentials.json into the pool. Two files holding one refresh token lose one of them at the first refresh.
- **Not built, the one question for the owner:** when a pool copy has expired and this machine's CLI login is the same account and alive, should "reuse" MOVE the machine login into the pool (the machine's CLI is then signed out, one credential, rotation-safe), or should the pool keep its own device sign-in? A copy is not an option.
- **Gates:** test-roster-live-usage (+6: the pure words, the codex twin, both row wirings escaped, the popup chip wiring, zh/ja with {name}/{vendor}). Pre-fix control over `git archive b924041f`: all six are red.

### lane group-chat-ui — B-a354: a `mention` member hears ONLY what @mentions it (the owner's "at-style group")

The wake is unchanged (an @ wakes every mode but mute).

### lane gmail-reply-all — Gmail reply-all, in the thread (B-a085)

The owner (2026-10-02 18:15 PDT): "a new thread is unfriendly to humans — speed this up". `vibespace-channels reply <gmail conv> --all` = To: the sender (Reply-To, else From) + the anchor's To, Cc: its Cc, the account's own address and duplicates removed — resolved when proposed, stored on the proposal envelope, sent verbatim in the thread (threadId + In-Reply-To / References). The adapter echoes `all`; the engine refuses an answer without it. `--cc <addr>` adds people (the compose address rule; listed apart as `added`) — chosen over `compose --in-reply-to` because it reuses the whole reply path (stored anchor, reach, the two-phase draft in the thread, reconcile). The window composer of a mail conversation has a "Reply all" box; the approval card lists every recipient (To labelled reply-all, the whole Cc, the drafter's added Cc apart). The agent's view of the envelope passes the belt (`agentEnvelope`). A recipient header over 16 KB is refused, never clipped; on the wire a non-ASCII display name is encoded on its own (`encodeAddressHeader` — one encoded-word over the whole To hid every address). Refused by name on chat channels (`replyAll` / `cc`). Gates: test-channels-gmail-shape, test-channel-outbox (+ the echo control), test-channels-agent-cli, test-peer-text-census (door + rows), test-channel-window-render ⑩i. Essay: kb-bugfix-invariants.md (B-a085).

Verify r1 (Opus): F1 HIGH — an agent's `reply --cc` now needs compose's reach (the whole account; a conversation grant ⇒ `bad-proposal` / `cc`, nothing created) and gets compose's verdict (direct only when a composed message would be); before, a conversation-only agent with `send` on a direct conversation mailed any address with no card. F2 MEDIUM — Gmail's address grammar (`addressList` + `addressParts`): a comment never splits a list or names the address (`j@x (张 <evil@x>)` went to evil on the wire), a group's members are plain recipients (we were not filtered out of one), an address never sits inside an encoded-word. Gates: test-channel-outbox (F1 legs + CONTROL), test-channels-gmail-shape (F2 + reply-all anchor-gone legs + CONTROLs).

Verify r2 (Opus): F3 MEDIUM — Gmail lists the owner's unsent DRAFT among a thread's messages and the sync stores it (ours), so a reply answering it (named with `--to`, or simply the newest stored message) went to the draft's unsent To — and with `--all` its Cc — direct on a direct conversation: people the thread never wrote to. `replyEnvelope` now refuses a DRAFT anchor by name (`reply-anchor-draft`; the engine answers `bad-proposal` / `reply-anchor`, nothing created). Held: every `--cc` / `--all` / Reply-To path and 54 address-grammar rows (card ≡ MIME).

### lane runaway-daemon — the 16:23 OOM: a leaked scratch daemon's fs worker storm, the reaper's age, the daemon a suite leaves (B-442c)

The 45.7 GB process was test-restore-liveness's §4 self-upgraded daemon (lane stdin-liveness's run, 16:20–16:23): a kill by the pid file missed the re-exec child, `rm -rf` deleted its bundle, and its fs worker pool turned one death into a doubling respawn storm (a failed Worker's `'error'` + `'exit'` both ran `die()`). src/agentd/worker-pool.js is the pool, bounded: one death per worker, `live` ≤ size, crash backoff 500 ms → 60 s, said in agentd.log. Reproduced on the real bundle (94 MB → 4.2 GB, 978 threads in 10 s); the fixed bundle stays flat. The reaper aged processes by the /proc dir's mtime (re-instantiated at 16:23:10 by the OOM's dentry eviction: "young: 42 s" for hour-old orphans); it reads btime + starttime now (scratch-run.mjs `procBornMs`). scratch.mjs `endDaemonsOf` / `endRootedProcesses` find a daemon by its own root env; test-architecture §57b names the 80 server-booting suites that never call the end helper (shrink-only debt). install-service.sh writes `OOMPolicy=continue`. Gates: test-agentd-worker-pool 16 (new, fast), test-scratch-reaper 141, test-restore-liveness 80, test-fd-limit 53, test-architecture 409, test-changelog-style, `npm run build`.

Verify r1: a worker blocked IN A SYSCALL (a hung mount; a FIFO with no writer) outlives its terminate — two such reads held both slots and every later fs op on the device hung with no deadline and no log line (measured on a real self-upgraded daemon: each `stat /` timed out at the client's 30 s). The pool now abandons a terminated worker still alive 2 s later (its slot refilled, at most 8 times, each said), a queued op fails by name at its own deadline, and with every slot wedged an op fails by name instead of running inline. `process.exit` joins every worker thread, so the same wedge held SIGTERM and the self-upgrade's re-exec (the daemon logged "exiting" and stayed, serving nothing); both exit through `pool.exit`, which runs the exit handlers and ends by SIGKILL while a worker is stuck. A worker that exits on its own (a bundle that parses and serves nothing) is a crash with backoff, not a silent 500 ms respawn loop. test-agentd-worker-pool §5–§7 + controls.

### lane mac-pull-refresh — a pull mount shows a file rewritten in place (B-35e3; B-0de9 not built)

#### B-35e3 — a held reader of a pull mount sees a same-size rewrite within the poll interval

- Reproduced on b924041f with the real chain (local agentd serve-folder → bridge → the pinned rclone 1.69.3): after a same-size rewrite on the device, fresh opens read the new bytes, but a held fd and a kept-open sqlite connection read the old ones until another process opened the file, and the mount's mtime stayed the mount time. Variants measured: without `--no-modtime` the mtime moves and the held reader stays stale; `rclone mount2` the same; `--direct-io` makes held readers fresh but `mmap(MAP_SHARED)` fails with ENODEV (rejected).
- src/device-mount.js: `pullMountArgs` (no `--no-modtime`) + `heldRefresher` (a GET through the bridge ⇒ a /proc fd scan, ≥ 10 s apart; a 5 s tick asks the device for each held file's stat by a Depth-0 PROPFIND through the bridge; a moved stat ⇒ one open in a child, plus one more pass; a newly found file gets one pass; at most 64 held files). Cost: an idle mount 0; the /proc scan measured 20k fds ≈ 300 ms async / 90 ms sync on the lane box, hence GET-triggered, never a plain timer.
- Gates: test-device-mount-rclone B-35e3 leg (heavy, real agentd + rclone, 10 checks; the held fd fresh in 3.5–4 s) — CONTROL on b924041f: 3 red (held fd still the old bytes after 15 s, the sqlite row old, the mtime pinned). test-pull-refresh (new fast suite, 18 legs, 1.8 s) — 4 mutants red: `--no-modtime` back, no once-more pass, no rescan, the prefix without its '/'.

#### verify r1 (Opus) — five fixes in src/device-mount.js, test-pull-refresh §10–§13 (29 legs)

- Cost, measured on the owner-shaped box (load ~35, 20.5k fds, UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=32, 5 mounts × 10 held files, a 300 ms device stat): event-loop delay unchanged (p99 2.1 ms vs 2.2), idle mounts 0 work, but every mount ran its OWN /proc scan (5 mounts read nonstop = 18 % of a core, ELU 9 %). Fix: one /proc pass serves every refresher (reused only by a mount whose GET came before it started — a sequence number; a clock tie reused a scan begun in the same ms).
- Device offline: it asked every 5 s forever, silently (8 tcpForwards/min per held file). Fix: 3 unanswered passes are said once in the journal and slow the pass to a minute; the first answer is said and restores 5 s. statRemote tells `false` (answered, not a file) from `null` (no answer). rclone dead (ENOTCONN): it kept asking silently. Fix: rclone's exit stops the refresher and says so.
- SQLite WAL (real chain): a WAL rewritten within its size now reaches a kept-open connection (4 s; base stale), but a reader that connected on an EMPTY -wal got `disk I/O error` (base: stale rows): rclone caps a held fd at the size its file had at open (an appended file: fstat grows, reads past the old end are EOF). Fix: a -wal grown past its first-seen size leaves its family alone, said once. `realpathSync(mountpoint)` → `await fs.promises.realpath`.
- Controls: base 10 legs red; minus the shared scan 2, the WAL rule 3, the journal 6, the exit stop 1, async realpath 1. `--no-modtime` was only ever in the pull argv: `ls -l` of 60 files = 1 PROPFIND with and without it (modtime rides the listing).
- OPEN: a change made before the refresher's first look at a held file can stay unseen by that fd (rclone relists, the fd keeps the old inode, `(deleted)` like a rename-over) — reproduced on b2f4a01c too.

#### B-0de9 — not built: a different code path

- The heal's log text is produced by our own bridge when the device-side tcp-connect to the serve-folder port fails: `catch { sock.destroy() }` in deviceFolderMount drops the device's reason (reproduced with a failing tcpForward: the exact "couldn't list files: Propfind … connection reset by peer"). That is the heal / tunnel bring-up, not the freshness path. Next step for whoever takes it: carry the tcp-connect error into the mount failure, then read userW's log.

### lane desktop-wayland — a desktop app never reaches the machine's own Wayland desktop

The owner, 2026-10-02 21:36 PDT: Blender, started by the keeper on xpra :4, opened on the machine's physical screen while its VibeSpace window waited for ever. Read-only on the live process: no WAYLAND_DISPLAY in its env, fd 3 connected to /run/user/1000/wayland-0 — libwayland's default when the variable is unset.

- **Fix** (src/desktop-display.js): `x11Env` names `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=vibespace-x11-only` (`NO_WAYLAND_DISPLAY`) instead of deleting it, and sets `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=x11`. `startXServer` / `startX11vnc` / `startXpra` drop the variable (`withoutWayland`): x11vnc 0.9.17 exits on any value — re-measured with the new name — xpra reads any value as a Wayland session, and test-desktop-app-keeper §7's stand-in Xvnc (Xvfb + x11vnc inheriting its env) went red until the X server was in the set.
- **Callers**: desktop apps here and a paired machine's desktop-serve op share src/desktop-serve.js (app spawn, relaunch, `x11EnvFor` → window targets / tier 3). The agent browser's hidden-window rung (src/browser-display.js) does not use x11Env, runs only with no live Wayland socket, and keeps its measured `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=''`.
- **Gate**: test-desktop-display §9 — the env table, shim X parts, and the real libwayland pair (the pre-fix env connects to a scratch wayland-0, x11Env's env is refused, a wayland-0 control connects). test-desktop-display 201 ✓ 0 skip, test-desktop-apps 388, test-desktop-serve 210 (1 environmental skip: a directory owned by another uid), test-browser-display 117, test-architecture 425, test-changelog-style 40, test-browser-tier3 111, test-desktop-app-keeper 347 (heavy, 1 skip), `npm run build` green.

Why now: userW's pod could not load after 2.369.200 — data/channels/index.json is 67 MB and was rewritten whole about once per second during the Lark catch-up, each write + whole-index copy blocking the event loop (requests stalled up to 5.5 s).

### lane channel-index-copy — a conversation read never copies the channels index (B-f32b)

**opening Channel windows on an account with tens of thousands of conversations no longer queues the server: a window costs its own conversation, and index.json is rewritten only where it changed**

#### One window copied the whole index up to five times (B-f32b, userW inc-muro2wt1-e8lu, 2026-10-03)

userW's pod (49,977 Gmail threads + 207 Lark chats + 90 agent groups, index.json 45 MB): 19 windows opened in ~20 s, the 9th still titled "Channel" 55 s later. `known()` — on watch, refresh, messages, mark-read and the broadcast's re-read — read one key through `store.index.snapshot()` (a deep copy of the whole index, 0.51–0.55 s each); the index write stringified everything every 2 s while anything changed; every partial broadcast summed unread over all rows; mark-read broadcast a bare id (a scan of every key). Every broadcast also walked every row of every account for the card's census (`schedulerView`, ~90 ms at 50,274 rows). Reproduced first on a generated 50,274-row index: nine windows clicked over 4.4 s finished at 3.0 … 24.4 s (event-loop stall 14.1 s); after the fix each finishes ≤ 8 ms after its click (longest stall 30 ms), the write after one row changed takes 30 ms (was 579 ms).

- One-row reads: `store.index.has(key)` (no copy) / `peek(key)` (that row) / `table(name)`; whole scans read `live()`; the engine calls `snapshot()` nowhere.
- The incremental index write: cached chunks of 256 rows, byte-identical to the whole-file serialization; `entry()` marks its row, an update reaching `ix.conversations` or `live()` marks every row (the conservative default), `rows()` + `touch(key)` for a scan that marks only what it changes (discovery's unlisting — every steady pass now writes incrementally); close() writes the whole file; every tick sweeps two chunks and writes + says a row changed outside `update()`.
- The kept row facts (`index.onTouch`): per account, listed / unread / unlisted / paused / overridden / the first read, re-summed on a full digest, a whole-map touch or once a minute; the digest's unread total reads them. Mark-read broadcasts its key; discovery pages and change-feed births ask `has()`.
- r2, the paced census (the coordinator's ruling on the lane's question): the clock counts (hot / warm / cold / due) walked at most once per 5 s per account, ONE trailing walk + broadcast after the last change (the card settles exact); the user-moved numbers exact on every broadcast. Engine deps `censusEveryMs` / `censusTimer`; `schedulerExact` / `censusStats` for the gates.
- verify r1 (the incremental write attacked: SIGKILL at each of 28 write steps, ENOSPC at each step + a real /dev/full, two racing writer processes, the loader on 14 truncations — the old file or the new one every time, never torn; a proxy census over 33 channel suites saw no write through a read surface): three LATENT tracker gaps closed in the store — an update's rows are marked again at its END (a write inside an async fn's await cleared their marks; no async update fn exists today), the sweep's cycle end counts the map against the cached chunks (a row BORN outside `entry()` sat in no chunk until close()), and a re-born row or a touch of a row not in the map is a whole-map change (the file kept the old place: content equal, bytes not). test-channel-store ⑬ (+7, a control per rule).
- `scripts/work-meter.mjs` `measureAsync` (an awaited call measured).
- Gates: test-channels-census-pace (new, fast, 10 — a 21 s burst over 50,274 rows: 5 walks ≤ 6, user-moved numbers exact on all 47 broadcasts, the trailing census = the full walk; controls pace 0 and a timer that never fires). test-channels-index-scale (new, heavy, 39 — the whole open bounded at 50,286 vs 100,560 rows, 120,905 vs 120,807 work, 0 census walks inside it, the base 358 M → 716 M; the write bounded, 588 K vs the whole-file 117 M; byte identity; the sweep; the verify census's own control; the kept total; ⑧ every engine writer incremental; controls for each). VIBESPACE_CHANNELS_INDEX_VERIFY over 32 channel suites: 0 drift. test-channels-engine's markRead control and ⑲d control re-modelled for the new code.

## 2.369.200 — 2026-10-02

### lane fleet-image-2 — fleet image 3.6.0: a pid 1 that reaps, agent-browser baked, the fleet e2e's two product gaps, the suites' dev-box assumptions

The fleet e2e ran the browser and desktop suites on a pod of image 3.6.0-rc1 and found the image's pid 1 never reaped (thousands of zombies per pod; one suite hung on one), no agent-browser in the image, four suites calibrated on the dev box, and two product gaps. Image matters only — no user-visible change.

- **pid 1 = tini, both Dockerfiles.** The fleet image ran `runuser` as pid 1, the single-container image `node`; neither reaps, so every detached process whose parent died stayed a zombie until the pod restarted, and a zombie reads alive to `kill -0` and `tail --pid`. `ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/tini", "--", …]`. Measured on the built image: 100 orphans ⇒ 0 zombies (the previous image: 100, ppid 1). Shutdown unchanged (`docker stop` ≈ 2.1 s on both: runuser's own 2 s grace).
- **agent-browser 0.38.1 baked** (pinned = TABLE_VERSION; the build checks `--version`). A copy a user installed into /usr/local was wiped by every roll. With no `~/.agent-browser/browsers` it runs the Debian chromium 154 — headless, or headed on its own Xvfb (`Chrome/154`) — measured in the image with no network. **Tools:** x11vnc, xclip, ffmpeg, and python3-setproctitle (an xpra Recommends: with it xpra rewrites its environ — the shape the rung was measured on).
- **Product gap 1 — a screenshot without a picture never said the loop.** `vibespace-browser`'s direct `screenshot` of a looping tab that drew no frame in 4 s answered `[no_picture]` without the `[navigation_loop]` note its picture answer prints (met on a pod's chromium 154). Now both say it. Gate: test-browser-site-reset (the shotHang row: RED 106/1 on the pre-fix CLI, 107/107 after); test-browser-site-reset-chrome ③ already asserts it on a real page.
- **Product gap 2 — test-browser-propose-chrome ④b pressed a stale coordinate** (red 3 runs of 7 on a pod: the card moved ~22 px between the read and the press). ### lane trace-fits — the live view's page-size changes fold out of the agent's action list

The owner (2026-10-01): "浏览器每次resize窗口或者移动窗口你都会算作一次操作，导致我的操作列表里全是view fit操作，毫无信息量 … 但也不要完全不要这个信息". Production census (read-only, the busiest profile scope): 37 of 194 trace entries were `viewer-fit` rows ("live view: set viewport 1072 907 (fit)", kind `viewport`), each with a 3 KB before and a 33 KB after frame — every drag, resize, snap, split or desktop switch of the live-view window re-fits the page (lane S4 verify r1 F6 taps OUR resize as ONE `viewer-fit` pair, so the reflow between two agent actions is on the record) and wrote a row of its own; the Actions pane and the tool card counted page sizes as actions.

- **F1 — coalesced at the source** (src/server/browser-trace.js `finalize`, PURE src/browser-trace.js `fitCoalesceVerdict` / `coalesceFits`, `FIT_COALESCE_MS` = 10 s beside AFTER_SETTLE_MS). A fit landing within 10 s of the tap's last fit (measured from the run's `lastAt`, so a long drag is one row), with no other traced action between (`tp.lastCmd` / a pending record's `prevCmd`), REPLACES the run: the run keeps its id, its first `at`, its first before frame and its session; takes the last geometry / text / result and the last after frame as a NEW file `<id>-after-<n>.jpg` (a client may hold the old one cached under the same URL — the clients add `?v=<n>`); `n` counts, `lastAt` moves; the superseded after frame is unlinked at once, never left for the sweep. The index stays APPEND-ONLY as it was: the replacement is appended under the SAME id and `loadIndex` lets the later line supersede the earlier — no tombstone, the id is the key, the sweep's rewrite compacts the file. The stream `trace` record and `browser-trace-appended` carry `replaced: true` (+ `n`, `lastAt`) so the clients patch the row in place. A fit after a click, or 11 s after the last, starts a new run — the reflow between two agent actions stays its own row.
- **F2 — folded on every list** (PURE `foldFits` / `visibleEntries`). Consecutive fit entries are ONE dim row "Live view fitted ×N · 1072×907 (last)" (zh 实时视图已适配 ×N · {size}（最后一次）, ja ライブビューに合わせました ×N · {size}（最後）); the counts exclude fits everywhere — the tool card's "N action(s)" (`traceSummary.n`, the fits beside as "K page-size change(s)" through `countText`), the Actions pane's head and the window's "Actions (N)", the Agent browser panel's traced-actions column (`scopeDigest.n`), a session's `count` (`pairSessions`, the recorder's `bs.count`, the end marker — the end card's "N actions") with `fits` beside. ONE per-device toggle "Show page-size changes" (`vibespace.browserTrace.showFits`, localStorage, default OFF; a <label> wrapping its checkbox) in the Actions pane's head and under the replay's Actions head expands them wherever a list is drawn (an expanded coalesced fit says `×n`). The replay keeps a run as a thin tick (`.brp-tick`) between steps — never a step, never a frame of its own, unless the toggle is on. `GET /api/browser/actions` answers `summary` (`n` / `failed` / `fits`). The tool card's thumbnail strip draws one dim "×N" thumb per run.
- **F3 — retention.** `traceSizePlan` drops page-size frames FIRST (the plan's entries carry `fit`; oldest fit first across every session, `why` "page-size frames go first; its action list is kept"), then the old oldest-session rule; `kept[].fitFrameBytes`. `usageOf` → `{used, fitBytes, total, …}`: the panel's "{used} of {size}" is the agent actions' bytes with "page-size frames: 12 MB" (`.bprof-trace-fits`) under it, as the brief asked; `total` rides beside for the limit's own measure.
- **F4 — pinned, not rebuilt.** The bridge (src/server/browser-stream.js, lane S4) already bounds its own fit storm: `scheduleFit` re-arms ONE timer per relay (`FIT_DEBOUNCE_MS` 250), `runFit` parks a fit asked while one is in flight (`fitAgain`) and runs it once after, and the verdict reads the live `fits` map — the latest geometry wins. test-browser-trace ⑥ pins the three.
- **Measured** (test-browser-trace ③ — a synthetic trace in the census's shape through the REAL recorder: 157 agent actions + 37 fits in 10 storms 2.5 s apart): before, 194 entries, 37 fit rows, 388 frame files, 188 KB of fit frames; after, 167 entries, 10 fit rows (n = 4,3,5,3,4,3,5,4,3,3), 334 frame files, 29 KB of fit frames; the index 194 lines / 167 ids, folded at reload.
- **Gates.** test-browser-trace (fast, 67): the verdict table, the merge, the fold, the counts, the flood, the fit-first plan + usage / housekeeping, four patched-copy controls one per rule (a verdict blind to the action between, a fold that never folds, a plan without the fit-first pass, a recorder that leaves the superseded frame), the wiring pins (the three surfaces, the route's `summary`, the toggle's <label>, F4, zh + ja, ci.mjs). test-browser-replay-ui (heavy): ③ the replay's two ticks where the runs happened (after the 3rd and the 5th step), the toggle on (8 steps, "viewer-fit 1072×907 ×3") and off by a real mouse; ⑥ the Actions pane's two dim fold rows among nine agent rows, the count line "9 个操作 · 5 次页面尺寸变化 · 最新在最后", the toggle on / off. test-ax-paint 25, test-architecture 404, test-browser-housekeeping 190, test-browser-sessions 117, test-changelog-style 40; test-record-clear-census (237) gained the row classifying the toggle's localStorage key as a `pref` (the §H1 storage census went red on it in the fast tier, green with the row).
- **Where reality bent the brief.** The user line was 215 characters against the style gate's 160 — it is two Changed bullets; and the FIRST bullet had to stay under 139, because test-changelog-style's own patched-copy controls plant their banned word by appending 18–21 characters to the first bullet and expect only their rule to break (a legal 140–160-character first bullet turns those two controls red — a slack the gate assumes, left as found). The tool card's COUNT is proven by PURE `traceSummary` + `countText` + the wiring pin, not seen in chrome: the replay suite's stub claude emits no tool call and its rebuild carries no transcript, so no tool card exists there. The agent's own `viewport` verb was never traced (an untraced observation since lane S4) — "stays a full row" needed nothing; the fold reads `viewer-fit` only.

### lane group-pending — a group message says where it stands with each recipient

**The owner (2026-10-01, the pair window "生活方式助手 · VibeSpace 主开发"): "你这个最新回复应该还没有实际发出去，其实应该展示成pending的状态之类的防止confusion".** A message VibeSpace 主开发 sent to a next-turn pair was drawn exactly like a delivered one while it waited for the other member's next turn; nothing in the window said so. Every fact needed was already on the server — the record's instant, each member's report marker (`reportedUpTo`), its notify mode, the log's leave / kick records — but the marker was a private fact (not in the group view) and a hand-over moved it without any broadcast.

- **P1 — ONE rule, PURE.** `deliveryOf(group, rec, {log})` in src/channel-groups.js: one row `{member, name, state, at}` per recipient = every member but the author that was a member AT the record's instant (`joinedAt <= rec.at` — reportFor's floor is `joinedAt - 1`, pinned); the owner (observer) is never a row. `DELIVERY_STATES` = waiting | handed | muted | left. **THE PIN:** reportFor reads `r.at > marker`, so a marker EQUAL to the record's instant means the record was in that report ⇒ handed — the §1f table pins it against the real engine (the commit stamps the marker to exactly `rec.at`) and a `>` patched copy goes red. `left` reads the log: the member's earliest leave / kick after the record, with no invite of it in between (joined-after-then-left is no recipient; left-then-re-invited is `left`); a departed member the page does not witness is no row.
- **What reality forced (two things the brief assumed).** ① The marker is a RECORD instant, not a clock: `markReported` stores `rep.upTo` = the newest record the report covered, so "read at {time}" would have printed the message's own time. **The follow-up (the coordinator, same day): the hand-over CLOCK is its own field** — `markReported` stamps `members[].reportedAt = now()` beside a marker it moves (persisted with the group record through the same door, validated, in the view; a legacy row has none), `deliveryOf` carries it as the handed row's `at`, the window says "Read by beta · 12:41" (zh "beta 已在 12:41 读到", ja "beta が 12:41 に読みました"; the time drawn as the message head draws its own — local 24 h HH:MM) and the CLI " — read by beta 12:41Z" (UTC + Z like every other instant that CLI prints — the one deliberate deviation from the asked " — read by beta 12:41": an agent reads these lines on any machine). A row stamped before the clock existed still prints "Read by beta". Gates: test-channel-groups §1f (the clock rows, the on-disk persistence, the no-move control keeps the clock, an ENGINE patched copy that moves the marker without the clock ⇒ `at` null — red above), test-channels-groups-ui §2b (the clocked words en / zh / ja, the default formatter), test-msg-cli-groups (the clause with / without the clock, the real engine's stamp), test-channels-groups-e2e ④b (the title says WHEN in en / zh / ja). ② The engine keeps no wake receipt (a successful wake only stamps the marker; the `group-wake` audit line is not on the record or the member), and a mention is no proof (a refused wake rides the report), so `woken` folds into `handed` with no `via` — "已唤醒 {name}" is not printed anywhere.
- **The digest + the broadcast.** `view()` now carries `members[].reportedUpTo` (null before any report); `markReported` announces `channel-groups-updated` for the group when the marker MOVED (an unmoved marker sends nothing — the markRead lesson) — so the sender's window flips without a reload. No new broadcast kind, no new persistence.
- **P2 — the window.** Every message row (the owner's own too) carries `.chanmsg-dlv`: a CSS dot (hollow while anyone waits, filled once it reached everyone it could, dimmed when only muted / departed are left) + the words from `deliveryLineText` (src/lib/channel-words.js, `t`/`tc` injected): ONE recipient ⇒ "Waiting for beta's next turn" / "Read by beta" / "beta is muted and will not read it" / "beta left"; several ⇒ "1 waiting · 1 read · 1 muted · 1 left" with every sentence in the title. The counts are `tc('delivery', …)` keys — "{n} waiting" is also the stash strip's "{n} 条在等" (same spelling, another meaning). The line is keyed by its row and patched only when its signature (every recipient's state + name) moved; a broadcast carrying the group or landing a record re-judges every drawn line (`redrawDelivery`) — never a list rebuild. zh / ja entries for all eight strings; `chanmsg-dlv` is an i18n-census data path (it names a recipient).
- **P3 — the agent.** `GET /api/agent/msg/read` records carry `delivery` (the same rows, names through the belt; a system record `null`); `vibespace-msg read` ends each message line with one clause: " — waiting for beta's next turn" / " — read by beta" / " — beta is muted (never reads it)" / " — beta left", a group " — waiting: a, b · read: c". An older server's record (no rows) prints no clause. The manual's Groups section says it. `send`'s answer unchanged.
- **P4.** The recipient's card ring, the report injection, the wake path, the pacer, the spend guard: untouched.
- **Gates.** test-channel-groups 338 (§1f: the table, the engine pin, the announce + its no-move control, five patched-copy controls — `>`, no owner exclusion, no presence rule, no mute rule, no departure witness); test-channels-groups-ui 88 (§2b the words en / zh / ja from the dictionaries with width budgets in the words, the tone, the re-export; §4 pins on the window, the engine's view + announce, the CSS dot); test-msg-cli-groups 142 (the clause over the stub and over the REAL engine: waiting ⇒ handed after `commitReports`); test-channels-groups-e2e ④b (heavy: the owner's message reads "1 waiting · 1 read" with a hollow dot; one typed character into beta's session + its hook call hands the report over ⇒ the SAME node reads "2 read" with a filled dot, beta's stub recorded no frame; beta muted ⇒ "1 read · 1 muted", back to next-turn ⇒ "1 waiting · 1 read" in place; zh / ja pages: the line whole, the title in the language). The brief named test-channels-groups-ui as the heavy gate — it is the fast half; the chrome legs went to test-channels-groups-e2e, its heavy twin.

The owner (2026-10-01): "这个加表情的加号太丑了。做成 lark 官方那种鼠标指上去才会在消息的右侧出现，不改变上下布局关系。" + "把 reply in thread，quote 也都放在鼠标悬浮按钮里". ### lane exit-run-output — the shell is the device's fact; a spawn failure names itself; the output where the user looks

The owner (2026-10-01, a screenshot of a Windows box WINDOWS-PC): "这里执行了指令怎么看不到回复。侧边栏也看不到指令和结果历史". data/exit-audit.jsonl held four `run` lines from one conversation — `nvidia-smi …`, `cmd /d /c ver`, `hostname`, `echo NOMAD_READONLY_PING` — every one `code 1`, `ms 7–8`, `ok true`, no output; the chat showed four cards "ran `…` on WINDOWS-PC — exit 1 · 0.0 s"; the agent spent a turn guessing "远端缺少或无法启动 sh". Three layers: (R1) src/exit-proxy.js ran EVERY command as `dm.runCmd('sh', ['-lc', cmd])` — the HUB chose the shell, and a Windows daemon has no `sh` (execFile ENOENT in ~8 ms); (R2) the daemon's `run-cmd` folded a spawn failure into `code: Number.isInteger(err.code) ? err.code : 1` with empty streams and dropped `err.message`; (R3) the card printed head + exit + seconds, the audit line kept no output, nothing listed a machine's runs.

- **E1 THE SHELL IS THE DEVICE'S FACT.** PURE `src/exit-shell.js` (imports nothing; the daemon bundles it): `shellPlan(platform, line)` — win32 ⇒ `cmd.exe /d /s /c "<line>"` with `windowsVerbatimArguments: true` (THE QUOTING RULE, from cmd's own /? text: /S strips the first and last quote of the text after /C and runs the rest verbatim, so ONE pair of quotes around the line and node must not re-quote; a CR / LF line is refused `ESHELLLINE` before any spawn — cmd runs one line and would drop the rest in silence), every other platform ⇒ `sh -lc` as before. The `run-cmd` op accepts `{shell: <line>}` beside the argv form; `run-shell` joins the hello-ack capabilities; client.js `runShell` is capability-gated (`host_needs_daemon`); exit-proxy sends `{shell}` to a daemon that advertises it and `sh -lc` to an older one, and the reply + the audit line name the interpreter and the platform. The device's stated platform (the dial headers' F7 statement) is now on the machine row and the Machines card. No Windows box ran this lane: the cmd.exe branch is unit-level on the PURE builder (stated, pinned, never measured) — said in the manual and the gate.
- **E2 A SPAWN FAILURE NAMES ITSELF.** `spawnFailure(err)` (an errno string under a `spawn …` syscall — ENOENT / EACCES / …; never a non-zero exit, a kill at the cap or the maxBuffer overflow) ⇒ `cmd-result.spawnError {code, message}` beside `code` = the shell's own convention an older hub still reads (127 not found / 126 not executable / 1). The hub refuses `spawn_failed` (502) with ONE sentence (`could not start `hostname` on "WINDOWS-PC" — sh: not found on that machine (ENOENT); nothing ran. "WINDOWS-PC" runs Windows: commands there run under cmd.exe — its agent is older than this VibeSpace…`), the audit line / the row's last run / the card say why, the CLI exits by the shell's code. exit-reach's REFUSALS gains the row; the words census covers it.
- **E3 OUTPUT WHERE THE USER LOOKS.** `E.outputHeads` = the ONE bound + judge: each stream cut to 4096 BYTES (said), browser-trace's `withoutUrlSecrets`, then the peer-text belt per line (a frame in a command's output is never live) — stored on the audit line (`stdout`, `stderr`, `cut`), carried by the card as a structured block (`exitRun`, through `injectPeerCard` of the three normalizers) and drawn by chat-renderers: the first three lines of stderr (else stdout) in mono under the exit line + "Show output" holding both heads (an expander on the same card — never a second card, never re-created). test-peer-text-census gains the door `outputHeads(` with its rows and an attack-leg driver; the ONE audit writer now broadcasts `exit-audit`.
- **E4 COMMAND HISTORY.** `GET /api/hosts/:id/exit-runs` (cookie; any bearer 403 `human_only`) = the owner's last 50 runs on a machine with names, verdicts, durations and the heads; `GET /api/agent/exit/runs` (vsst_) = the caller's OWN runs (`vibespace-exit runs [<machine>] [--limit N]`). src/lib/exit-runs-dialog.js ("Recent commands…" in "Who can use it", "Commands…" on the Machines card): a fresh GET, keyed `<details>` rows patched in place off `exit-audit` (an opened row stays the same node, still open), 50 kept. test-architecture §65 (D) now also censuses data/bin/vibespace-exit's paths (agent routes only) with a control.
- **E5** docs/agent/exit-manual.md (`vibespace-docs exit`): the platform rule, the output bound, the history verb; the index row points at it.
- **Reality vs the brief:** the user line is three bullets (the changelog style gate caps a bullet at 160 characters); §65 is a channels-engine census, so the owner-route pin became a (D) row for the exit CLI + the 403 pin, not a roster row; the control daemon for the §6 leg is a rebased copy bundled by esbuild (mutant-copy's CJS re-binding cannot be bundled: esbuild renames a shadowed `require`).
- **Gates:** test-exit-run (fast, 106: PURE tables, node's REAL execFile errors, the real manager over fake daemons, the real routes + CLI, a REAL daemon built from this tree + a control daemon that never consults the judge), test-exit-reach (265: the spawn_failed card rows + control (l), the daemon pin re-spelled), test-peer-text-census (360), test-architecture (408), test-dial-facts / test-exit-proxy / test-exit-rejudge green; test-exit-access-ui ⑤ (heavy: the card's block + the expander in place, the list's keyed rows patched live, the platform on the row and the card, the real CLI's `runs`).

### lane exit-run-output — verify r1 (the peer-content class: 4 KiB heads now persisted / broadcast / carded; the authority class: the device's shell, the owner's history)

- **F1 HIGH — nine secret shapes stored verbatim.** `printenv`, `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, a kubeconfig, a `.netrc`, a bearer in a log line: `outputHeads` kept every one on the audit line (append-only), in the `exit-audit` broadcast, on the card, in both history reads and the CLI's `runs` — the URL rule and the belt redact none of them. FIX = PURE `src/secret-shapes.js` `redactSecrets` (R1 PEM block · R2 a secret-named `KEY=value` with the value's extent decided in code · R3 bearer / basic · R4 known prefixes incl. our own vsst_/vsmt_/jbt_ · R5 `password <x>`), bounded 64 KiB, linear, idempotent, called once in `outputHeads` after the URL rule and before the belt; `CREDENTIAL_WORDS` exported from browser-trace. The agent's API result keeps the whole stream. Gate: test-exit-run §2b (24 rows + idempotence + the bound + a 32→64 KiB clock ratio) + the §3 printenv leg (audit / broadcast / card / both lists redacted, the API whole) + control (e); the census pin2 re-spelled.
- **F2 MEDIUM — the audit grew without bound and the history read starved.** Append-only with 8 KiB of heads per `run` line: 10 000 runs = 79 MB on disk (measured), for ever; and `auditTail` read the LAST 2 MiB whole then filtered by host, so ~240 such lines filled the window — a quiet machine's only run read 0 of 1 in the owner's list AND the agent's `runs` behind another machine's storm. FIX = a ring of two files at the ONE writer (`exit-audit.jsonl` → `.1` at 8 MB, bytes counted; `auditMaxBytes` for suites) + a chunked backwards read (512 KiB) over the ring with the caller's predicate inside it and a raw-substring `hostId` check before any parse, stopped at `limit` matches. Gate: test-exit-run §3 (a 256 KiB ring under a 60-run storm: the quiet row found in both lists, the rotation seen, the limit honoured across the ring).

W6: every rule of secret-shapes.js removed on its own reddens the §2b table (R1 2 rows · R2 9 · R2b 2 · R3 1 · R4 5 · R5 2 · R6 1); the product parts' file-level reverts are in the verify report. ### lane hooks-create — VibeSpace creates ~/.claude/settings.json when the CLI never wrote one, and tells the conversations that predate it

**The incident (2026-10-01 21:50 PDT, read-only forensics on a fleet pod, VibeSpace 2.369.199).** Every boot logged `Hook registration (claude) skipped: /home/<user>/.claude/settings.json not found (start the CLI once to create it)`. The CLI does not write settings.json on its first run — only when somebody changes a setting — so a user who only chats never has one: ~/.claude with projects/, plugins/, skills/ and no settings.json since the pod's first day. VibeSpace never registered SessionStart / UserPromptSubmit / Stop there, so her agents never got the tools intro, task context or bookkeeping (0 `vibespace-reminder` in 11 transcripts); asked to "just use the browser", an agent spent four minutes probing DISPLAY, installing gcloud and listing MCP servers before it found `vibespace-browser` through an env var. Four more pods were in the same state.

- **H1 — the create rule, a closed set.** `createIfMissing` ∈ `false | 'dir-exists'` (src/harness-config.js `CREATE_RULES` / `createRule`): the FILE is created when its directory exists (the directory proves the CLI has run here), never the directory. The legacy `true` was the same rule (the writer has never created a directory) and is read as 'dir-exists'; codex's hooks.json + config.toml now declare it by name — **codex's rule did not change**, only the created file's mode (umask before, 0600 now). claude's SETTINGS_FILE moved `false` → 'dir-exists'. A created file is written to a tmp and LINKED into place exclusively — a settings.json the CLI wrote in that gap is never replaced (EEXIST ⇒ re-read + re-apply over the CLI's content) — mode 0600, chowned to its directory's owner when the writer runs as root. Both writers answer `'created'` (truthy: every `&&`/`!!` caller unchanged); the refusal for a missing file carries `e.missing` = `no-dir` ("<dir> not found — the CLI has not run on this machine; nothing is created") or `not-ours`; `readConfigPlan` names the kind in the receipt's `reason` (`will-create` | `no-dir` | `not-ours`) — the only free field a remote helper's CFG line carries, so the chip reads it on every machine. The plan carries the rule by name (an older helper reads `'dir-exists'` truthy = the same rule). The boot CLI-config plan (cleanupPeriodDays) follows the same rule and logs `[cli-config] created ~/.claude/settings.json (the CLI had never written one) (boot)`. `ensureAgentHooks` logs `created ~/.claude/settings.json (the CLI had never written one) and registered VibeSpace hooks` and calls `onHookFileCreated`; `agentHooksStatus` adds `dirExists` / `creatable`. `hookRegistrationSafe` is unchanged (a worktree / temp server never writes). The shipped register helper (it embeds harness-config.js) is regenerated, so remote hosts follow the rule at the next install / spawn.
- **H2 — the words.** A missing file says what is true now (src/lib/cli-config-chips.js `receiptLine`): `will-create` locally = "… will be created at the next start — or press Apply" with `apply: true` — the Settings window draws a working **Apply** beside it, the Machines card's primary button becomes **Apply** while a file will be created (both `POST /api/cli-config/apply`, human-triggered: the hook registration with `auto: true` — the master switch and a Remove opt-out still hold — plus the CLI-config plan; a temp server root answers 409 `unsafe_root`); on a remote host "… will be created at the next tool install or session start on that machine" (no button); `no-dir` (dim) "~/.claude not found — the CLI has not run on this machine, so nothing is written"; no reason (an older helper) "not found". The Machines card's hook state reads "{label}: will be created at the next start — or press Apply" / "{label}: the CLI has not run on this machine". "start the CLI once to create it" and "{label}: run the CLI once first" are retired from code, zh and ja (test-harness-settings §8's census over 470 files).
- **H3 — the conversations already running.** A CLI process keeps the hook configuration it started with (the brief's premise; the 2.1.281 binary carries a per-session hooks snapshot — not measured live, no CLI was run). src/server/hooks-late.js (ORCH) gets `onHookFileCreated`, HOLDS it until `ready()` (server.js calls it right after `restoreSessions()` — the boot registration runs before the restore), then queues ONE note per running LOCAL session of that harness that reads the file (ssh / dial sessions and a wrapper-injected codex chat excluded; once per webui id) through the existing queue (session-status kind `hooks-late`, `replaceKind`): "VibeSpace's hooks were registered after this conversation started — Terminate and Resume it to get the tools context" — never a billed turn. **What the brief did not foresee:** for claude that queue is drained ONLY by the UserPromptSubmit hook — the very hook such a session may lack. So the note carries the webui id it was queued for and agent-routes drops it unread in any OTHER process of the conversation (`hooksLateStale`, before the queue is peeked): a Terminate + Resume starts with the hooks and must never read "Terminate and Resume it". If the running CLI does pick the new hooks up, the note rides its next prompt; if it does not, the For-you line is the carrier. The owner gets ONE For-you line (origin agent, kind action) only when at least one session predates it: "{n} running Claude Code conversations started before VibeSpace registered its hooks — Terminate and Resume them to give their agents the VibeSpace tools" (zh "有 {n} 个正在运行的 {label} 对话早于 VibeSpace 注册 hook 启动——终止并恢复它们，它们的 agent 才能获得 VibeSpace 工具", ja "実行中の {label} の会話 {n} 件は VibeSpace が hook を登録する前に開始されました — 終了して再開すると、それぞれの agent が VibeSpace のツールを使えるようになります"; the singular too), the conversations by name in the detail. The user's typed text is never rewritten (the typing path's directive stands).
- **Gates.** The brief's test-harness-config / test-agent-hooks / test-cli-config-chips do not exist; their asserts went to the nearest suites (the coordinator's rule): **test-claude-retention 88** (§6 the rule table: no-dir refused + said + no directory, created 0600 + registered, the CAS path + mode kept, a symlink written through, not-ours, a no-op creates nothing, the create-gap race, the TOML writer, the receipt kinds + CFG round trip, the boot plan alone creates; CONTROLS: a patched copy whose create path makes the directory fails the no-dir leg, the pre-lane `false` on the incident's shape registers nothing; §7 ensureAgentHooks on a /tmp/vs-hkc-<pid> HOME with ~/.claude absent / present, the journal line, the callback once, the belt; §8 the notes per session kind, the exact sentence, ONE For-you line + its zh/ja structure, once per session, the stale drop for a resumed process, no line when nothing runs, never a billed turn, the Apply route's three answers; §9 wiring pins; the owner's real CLI config hashed before / after — byte- and mtime-identical), **test-harness-settings 198** (§8 the four missing kinds + the retired-sentence census; the plan pins), **test-harness-contract 374** (the identity pin holds; the rule ∈ the closed set), **test-user-todos-layout 235** (the producer census learns src/server/hooks-late.js — 20 sites), test-architecture 404, i18n-check.
- **Scope kept.** No change to what the hooks inject, no new hook event, nothing written when ~/.claude is absent, never a directory created. Not covered: a session restored LATER than `restoreSessions()` (an R6 pipe session re-opened asynchronously — the switch is off by default) is not counted.

### lane hooks-create H5 — on a machine with no desktop session, an unset window preference means a hidden window (the owner's decision, 2026-10-01 22:05 PDT)

**Why.** `browser.headed` unset ('' = inherit the CLI's own config) meant headless on a fleet pod (no desktop, no user config), and Google sign-in refuses headless Chrome (the same pod tonight, another user before). The hidden-window rung (the CLI's own invisible Xvfb, UA Chrome/154 — measured in lane headless-fallback) existed but only answered a window someone ASKED for.

- **The rule, PURE** (src/browser-display.js `resolveHeaded({setting, display, mode})`): an explicit yes / no wins; UNSET on a machine with NO desktop session (no live Wayland / X socket — a stale DISPLAY counts as none) where Xvfb is installed and `browser.noDisplayMode` is auto ⇒ a window is asked for ⇒ the hidden-window rung; with a desktop, without Xvfb, Xvfb unknown, or "Always headless" ⇒ today's meaning (inherit). `noDesktop(d)` exported beside it.
- **Where it is resolved — at the LAUNCH, never at the spawn.** The keeper's launch fact (`displays.factFor({…, preference})` — both local launch sites, the conversation's browser and a named profile) resolves the stored preference against the probe it just took; the fact records `wanted.byDefault: true`, and `planForFact` re-derives the same plan from it, so every later call (the agent's verbs through /resolve, the keeper's own cdp-url, the live view) names the same planned file — `headed: true`, x11 pinned — and nothing restarts. Rung D's spawn config (browser-env) keeps the preference AS STORED: it is composed at the spawn, and a config that baked "no desktop now" would open a VISIBLE window on a dev box whose desktop logged in later. **The deviation from the brief's wording:** the keeper's `headedSetting()` stays the STORED value (it composes base configs and is what a paired machine receives); the ONE resolution is `resolveHeaded`, called where the display is probed — the keeper's launch fact for a local browser, and the paired machine's own `browser-serve start` (src/browser-serve.js `planLaunch`) for its browser: the hub's display must not decide a remote machine's (a remote desktop would otherwise get a visible window). An older daemon receives the stored null and keeps today's meaning.
- **The words.** The `browser.headed` row: the unset option reads "Unset: a hidden window without a desktop, else ~/.agent-browser/config.json"; the description "… Unset (default): on a machine without a desktop, a hidden window when Xvfb is installed; otherwise whatever your own ~/.agent-browser/config.json says. … Applies to the next browser that starts — a browser already running is not restarted." Settings' fact line (GET /api/browser/display now answers `preference`): on such a machine with the setting unset "This machine has no desktop session now — with the window setting unset, an agent's browser runs in a hidden window (the live view can still take over)"; with Headless chosen "… the window setting says Headless, so an agent's browser runs headless". zh / ja for all four (the retired option label and description removed from both dictionaries).
- **Gates.** test-browser-display 116 (① THE TABLE — 13 rows: desktop × Xvfb × preference × mode, the stale-DISPLAY pod row exact, the fact's `byDefault` re-derived from a base that says nothing or false; CONTROL: a patched copy without the no-desktop branch — the old inherit — reads exactly the 3 no-desktop rows as inherit; ③ a fleet-pod keeper: no user config, Xvfb on the launch PATH, setting unset ⇒ launched HEADED on the CLI's own Xvfb, the launch config it names carries headed:true, `wanted.byDefault`, UA Chrome/154, no restart; 'no' ⇒ headless + the fact line says so; a live Wayland socket ⇒ inherit; a paired machine's `browser-serve start` with the preference unset resolves against ITS display — hidden window with Xvfb, headless without; the keeper control's anchor follows the launch line); test-browser-env 36 (②b rung D's spawn config keeps unset unset, the keeper's launch config from it = headed:true on a no-desktop + Xvfb machine, inherit with a desktop / no / headless / an older caller). **A suite that depended on the box:** test-browser-env ③'s keeper ran with `/usr/bin` on its PATH, so on a box with Xvfb and no desktop session in the suite's env an unset preference now planned the hidden window and the x11 pin landed after the keeper mark ("mark last" — a composition convention; the mark is read anywhere on the command line); its keeper now runs on a private PATH holding only `sleep` (test-browser-display's rule: the rung is chosen by what the suite puts on the PATH, never by what the box has installed).

### lane cluster-presets — company presets from ONE cluster Secret, mounted and watched; env is the fallback (B-53fe)

**The class (the owner, 2026-10-01 22:20 PDT: "这种环境问题怎么总是出现 以后能避免吗 每次下发环境变量都要给人家重启").** A company preset (the Google OAuth clients Drive / Gmail sign in with, a Lark app, a browser key) was an ENV VAR read at boot (`VIBESPACE_GDRIVE_CLIENTS`, the integrations JSON), written PER RELEASE (`gdrive.clients`, `integrations:` in each user's values). The boot read is sync and size-checked (1 MiB, the kubelet's tmpfs); live = `fs.watch` on the directory (the kubelet's atomic `..data` rename) + a 30 s stat-signature poll (ino/size/mtime + the `..data` target — a missed event, a plain directory's in-place `override/` edit), debounced, ONE single-flight re-read; only a DIFFERENT merged result replaces the snapshot, writes ONE journal line naming keys (`[presets] changed (<dir>): Google clients: added org2; rotated org1 · integrations: removed lark/other`) and runs the listeners; a file that cannot be read / parsed / is not an array / is too large keeps its previous presets, is said ONCE per transition (`describeJsonError` — the position, never a byte), and the summary carries it (`kept`). `src/preset-layers.js` (PURE, joins test-architecture's PURE set) holds the ONE parser of each shape (the env readers' rules moved verbatim — the store's env JSON and `MountManager._envDrivePresets` call it too), the PER-KEY merge (a release entry replaces the cluster entry with the same identity — integrations: row id + preset key; Google: the key — and adds the rest; both absent ⇒ `null` = the env fallback; a present `[]` is an answer), the value-free diff and the line's words. The integration store asks the file rung before the env for the keyed JSON (`clusterJsonEntries`; the single-field env form unchanged; `cluster:<k>` / `presetsFor` / `offeredCredentials` follow) and gained `presetsChanged()` (every CARD row's recomputed `publicView` broadcast as `integrations-updated` why `presets`; the listeners ONCE with id null — the channels engine re-asks every adapter's `auth.state()` and re-pushes its digest, whose account dialogs read `presetsFor`) + `presetItems()`. `MountManager.drivePresets()` asks the same instance first (Drive `_driveClient`, gmail-sync `_client`, the storage dialog's drive-defaults, the Gmail channel row through the injected reader — one instance, so a rotation reaches all of them at once; a live rclone mount takes a rotated secret at its next (re)mount). No preset env when the volume is on (only `VIBESPACE_PRESETS_DIR`); never a `subPath`. `presets.override {gdriveClients, integrations}` is the per-release block; empty = the legacy `gdrive.clients` / `integrations` blocks (Secret keys unchanged, so existing values keep working as overrides); the legacy single `gdrive.clientId/secret` becomes one override entry keyed `default`. The item list never depends on the values, so the Deployment renders identical with or without an override — changing one is a Secret-only upgrade (no roll; the kubelet re-projects it live). `presets.volume=false` renders byte-identical to the 2.369.199 chart (measured over three value shapes).

### lane design-kit-287 — Claude Code 2.1.287 ships no design kit; the kit comes from an older version on the machine, and says so

The owner (2026-10-02 03:45 PDT): "design相关功能又出问题了 设计工具包未就绪：design skill text not found in the CLI binary (neither template-literal nor zstd layout — layout changed again?)". Production's journal 03:23–03:32: `[design-kit] NOT ready: CLI 2.1.287` ×3 (2.1.287 installed Oct 1 23:33).

- **Measured, not assumed (the binaries read as bytes; no CLI turn).** The layout did not change — the kit LEFT the CLI. 2.1.287's `/design` router answers types → hub → consent; 2.1.281's answered types → **canvas** → hub → consent. Both remaining modes work through claude.ai (an Artifact of the published "Design" type; the claude.ai/design hub, whose instructions an MCP tool fetches live — a claude.ai/design project, not the canvas kit). The canvas module went with the mode: `loadDesignCanvasFiles` / `isDesignCanvasSkillEnabled` / `buildDesignCanvasPrompt` 0 (3 each in 2.1.280 and 2.1.281); the bunfs table lost `payload.template.html.asset` and `seed-canvas.mjs-<h>.txt.zst`; of 166 zstd frames decoded in each binary, 2.1.281 holds the skill (56 496 B), helper (40 699 B) and payload (2 488 483 B), 2.1.287 none. No runtime fetch exists (no loader left; the only design URL is the claude.ai/design tip link, same in both), so "run /design once in a terminal" cannot help either — brief case (b).
- **The ladder.** The running CLI's own pieces first (its extraction dir, then its binary), else another version on this machine in the PURE `donorOrder`: an installed binary (the running binary's own versions dir, then `~/.local/share/claude/versions`), then a kit this server stored earlier (sha256-checked against its kit.json). Rule: older than the running CLI only (a newer installed binary is an update landing or a version stepped back from), newest first, the binary before a stored copy at one version, one stored copy per donor. The stored rung is there because the CLI's updater keeps three versions — 2.1.274 was purged at 03:38 while this lane measured; production's data/design-kit still holds kits whose binaries are long gone — so without it the fix would die two updates later (a choice beyond the brief, named here).
