### lane dialog-keys — a dialog you opened takes the keys while you drive the agent's browser

- While you drive the agent's browser, a dialog you open yourself (Delete → confirm) now takes Enter and Escape; a dialog that pops up on its own still does not.

#### A dialog you opened takes the keys (lane dialog-keys, the owner's "ok" 2026-09-30 on takeover-keyboard r4's proposal)

Before, every app dialog that opened while you drove the agent's browser was taken back — its Enter and Escape went to the page (Delete → the confirm → Enter put a line break into the page's text box and the file was kept; a toast said "click the dialog's buttons"). Now every app modal says it opened (`announceModal` in createModalShell and app._showDialog), and the live view judges who opened it by the last act the browser itself marked trusted (a press — never one on the picture, which went to the page — or a key the app took, within 250 ms): yours ⇒ the dialog takes Enter / Escape / Tab / typing, the takeover goes on (the agent stays refused), the chip says "Keyboard is in the dialog — it goes back when you answer it", and when it closes (answered, dismissed, or removed by a script) the keys go back where they were — the page, the chat box you had been typing in, or the dialog under it; a dialog that opens by itself (a broadcast, a timer, a notification, a script's synthetic click) stays taken back and is said once — the password guard is unchanged. PURE `dialogOpener` / `dialogVerdict` / `dialogReturn` / `dialogReclaimCue` + keyboardOwnership's `dialog` state (src/browser-takeover.js), the hold / return stack in src/lib/keyboard-yield.js, one MutationObserver per live view armed only while a dialog holds. Gates: test-browser-takeover ⑦ (the tables + 10 patched-copy controls), test-takeover-keyboard (15 DOM-mini dialog scenarios, 8 controls, the announcement census, the census's dialog row), test-browser-live-input ⑦ (a real Delete → Enter confirms, the page gets no line break; a dialog a script opens is taken back and said; the pre-fix control puts the line break into the page). Verify r1 (the keyboard-authority class): while a dialog you opened holds the keys they never fall to nowhere — a confirm answered over a dialog whose button was re-rendered meanwhile, a dialog that popped up by itself over yours and was answered, the middle of three nested dialogs closed by a script: each used to leave the keyboard on the page body (typing went nowhere while the chip still said "in the dialog"); now the dialog that still holds gets its own field back (`dialogReturn` 'older' + `settleDialogs({active})`, three DOM-mini scenarios + a control). The K6 revert table (59 product parts, one per scratch copy) found three parts no gate reddened — the release re-stamp (a touch tap held past 250 ms), the held dialog's `keep` over a yield, the opener spent at a take — each has its scenario and control now; the modal-trigger census (K2/K3) is recorded in kb-bugfix-invariants.

### lane toolbar-fold — the toolbar's buttons fold into a menu on a narrow screen

- On a narrow screen the toolbar's buttons fold into a ⋯ menu instead of overlapping.

lane-toolbar-fold (owner 2026-09-30: the top-right cluster of green buttons "takes too much width on a low-resolution screen and overlaps other chrome"). Measured first, 60 states × 2 font sets: `.toolbar-right { min-width: 160px; justify-content: flex-end }` let the zone shrink to 160 px and its buttons overflow LEFTWARD — over the layout presets, over the "VibeSpace" title and, with the sidebar open, under the sidebar (⚙ / Presets / New Session hidden at 1024×768 and UI 125 %); 21 of 60 states overlapped, 1366×768 at UI 125 % in every language, ja 1280×720 at 100 %. Now the toolbar follows lane I's chrome-bar rule: the zones keep their content width, the title shrinks first (then hides), the buttons give up their words one at a time (the icon stays, the words become its tooltip and screen-reader name), and only then fold into ONE ⋯ by priority — Presets, Desktop, the layout presets, Apps, Web view, Files, Terminal, New Session last; ⚙, ☰ and the taskbar widgets moved up never fold. The ⋯ menu (registry menu `toolbar-overflow`) lists exactly the folded buttons in the arranged order, each row running the same command as its button (the layout presets as a submenu of their own buttons; Terminal's host picker is one implementation anchored at whichever control was pressed). Customize mode pauses the fold (every element full, the bar may wrap, its alignment chip below the whole bar) and Done re-folds. `barLayout` gains zones (`groups`, each its own gap) and `barLadder` (the icon step); `createBarFold` gains compact forms, live-measured items, an in-bar ruler and suspension. Gates: test-toolbar-fold (fast, 34: ladder / zone tables, the real table over the measured zh / ja / en / DejaVu widths — 256 states, 3000 seeded bars through an independent geometry walk, mutant-copy controls) and test-toolbar-fold-ui (heavy: the rect census at 4 widths × 3 languages × sidebar × UI scale + toolbar scales under this box's fonts AND the runner's DejaVu set, the ⋯ rows doing what the buttons did, Customize, the arranged order, the pre-fix toolbar RED as its control).

### lane billing-chip — the phone's billing chip follows the pool's current account

- On a phone, the billing chip now follows the pool's current account instead of keeping the one from when the conversation started.

lane billing-chip — a phone has no title bars, so its billing identity is the chat status bar's chip, and that chip skipped a repaint while its key was unchanged: the key named only the POOL while the chip prints the pool and the account serving the conversation (`⣿ <pool> → <account>`), so a per-session switch, a pin or "Move every conversation here now" changed the account and the chip never repainted. Both billing chips (the title bar's and the phone's) now repaint on ONE key (`billingAuthKey`, src/lib/pool-priority-model.js) that covers everything they print — the account by name and id, the machine, the "estimated" mark, an API key's tail, the placement (pinned / priority #n / automatic); a moved pool default, which no chip prints, repaints nothing. The phone chip's tooltip also names how the account was placed, as the title-bar chip does. The sidebar card prints no pool account, so its render gate is unchanged. Known, not changed: the phone chip's 90 px cap cuts a long `pool → account` at the account's end. Gates: test-billing-chip (fast, new — the real status bar and title-bar chip through a fake DOM, the pre-fix key as a patched-copy control) and a phone leg in test-mobile-gaps (heavy — a stub active-sessions frame at 390 px, the chip's text and a screenshot).

### lane lark-p2p — the Lark search feed read as the vendor answers it

- **Lark single chats now appear in Channels (the search feed read every hit as malformed).**

##### lane-lark-p2p — the Lark search feed, read as the vendor answers it

Since 2.369.197 the Lark "new-message search" was meant to find every new message — single chats included, which Lark's chat list never names. On a real account it found none: Lark answers each hit's time as an ISO 8601 text (`2026-03-21T16:15:30+08:00`), the adapter expected a number of milliseconds and dropped every hit as malformed (241 260 of them), so no single chat was ever born. The request also put its time window where Lark does not read it (the window belongs inside `filter`), so every page returned the whole searchable history and the search never finished a window — hidden, because no hit was readable. Now: the request carries its window and chat type in `filter`; the hits are read in the form the vendor sends (the fixture is the production probe's field list, verbatim); an account whose feed the old version wrote starts over at the update — a fresh search window plus the 7-day single-chat catch-up, the chats it finds born as read (no agent is woken for old messages). If a future answer again has a shape this version cannot read, the feed stops after one page and the account card says so with the field names ("Lark's search answers, but its hits have a shape this version does not read (missing or unreadable: …) — the single-chat feed is off until an update") instead of paging silently; when Lark's search times out, the card says how many times in a row and until when each chat is checked on its own ("Lark's search did not answer 3× in a row — each chat is checked on its own until 03:28"), and one answered page ends the count (a single 504 later waits 30 s, not 15 minutes). Nothing to do after the update — the search permission the account already holds is the one it uses; only if the account card says "One Re-authorize adds: … single chats" is the single-chat read permission missing (one Re-authorize, as that line says). Zero vendor calls in the lane: the shape comes from the production log line and Lark's own API doc. Verify r1: a search that never finishes a window (more pages for ever, with no total) is now stopped at the number of messages a window of that length can hold — 151 pages for a 90-second window — and the card says the time window was ignored, instead of searching at the feed's full rate for ever. Two odd search hits in a quiet minute no longer switch the single-chat feed off for a day (the "unreadable shape" verdict is judged per search window; a whole page of unreadable hits still stops it at once). When the search returns hits this version cannot read but the feed is still on, the account card says how many and which fields on a line of its own (it was a hover tooltip). A single missed search answer reads "is not answering — … until HH:MM", never "did not answer 1× in a row" — and while the search still delivered a page within the last two and a half minutes, one or two missed answers do not turn the card to "not answering" at all (a search that fails every other time was shown as down 98 % of the time while it found every new message). A search answer that is not a page — an empty reply, one without `has_more`, or one that says there is more but gives no way to ask for it — is now treated as a failed search (retried on the usual ladder, the cursor held); it used to be read as "nothing more in this window", and the messages the window still held were never asked for. The account card's "N search hits could not be read" line now counts the last hour and disappears when the hour holds none — it used to count since the account was connected and never went away (two odd hits in one minute stayed on the card for good). Verify r3: when Lark's search keeps answering something that is not a search page (a changed API, a proxy page, a captive portal), the account card now says so ("Lark's search answered 3× in a row with something that is not a search page — each chat is checked on its own until HH:MM") and the server journal names the missing field once — it used to read "failed N× in a row" with nothing in the journal at all. The "N search hits could not be read in the last hour" count is now exact however busy the search is (it was capped by a per-page memory of 200 pages and read a third of the truth on a busy account). A search whose pages loop (page A, page B, page A again, with fresh page tokens) is stopped at its third page and the card says the answer's shape is not one this version reads; it used to run 161 pages before a different limit stopped it and called it "ignored its time window".

### lane badge-stale — every per-session pool-link writer announces the move; a no-change title meta re-draws nothing

- The account name on a window's title bar follows the account the conversation actually uses after the pool moves it.

lane badge-stale — when the pool engine moved ONE conversation to another account (a per-session switch, a pin, a partial "Move every conversation here now", a removed member's eviction), the server re-pointed the conversation's credential link and told no page, so a window's title chip kept the old account until some unrelated update happened to go out — 30+ minutes on the owner's page while the conversation ran one long turn. The one writer of that link now announces the move (one session-list update per pool pass), exactly as a move of the pool's default always did. Also: every session-list update re-drew the tab strip of every grouped window (each tab's account chip made anew every 5 seconds, a hover or a click on a tab lost); an update that changes nothing now re-draws nothing. Gates: test-pool-link-notify and test-title-meta-guard (fast, new — the real account store and the real window manager, each with its pre-fix copy as a patched-copy control).

### lane fleet-image — the fleet image's display stack; mc pinned

- **The fleet image carries the display stack.** `deploy/docker/Dockerfile` adds xvfb + at-spi2-core + gir1.2-atspi-2.0 + python3-gi, so the agent browser's hidden-window rung (Xvfb) and the window-target tree / input rungs run on every pod. Found by a fleet user's Google sign-in refused as "this browser may not be secure": the image had no Xvfb, so the agent browser could only start headless (a HeadlessChrome user agent), and no at-spi / xdotool, so a shared window was pixels-only with no way to click. xpra 6 + xdotool + wmctrl were already in the Dockerfile but never built into the running 3.5.0 image; the 3.6.0 rebuild carries all of them.
- **The MinIO client is pinned to its last GitHub release** (tag + sha256) in both Dockerfiles: dl.min.io answers 410 Gone, and the 3.6.0 image build failed at step 10 on it.
- No user-visible change in the product itself (an image matter): no entry in the user changelog.

### lane browser-propose — a refused sign-in becomes ONE proposal with ONE Approve; the automation flag hidden by default

**when a site refuses the agent's browser, the agent proposes a switch and you approve it with one click; the agent's browser no longer announces itself as automated**

- When a site refuses the agent's browser, the agent proposes a switch and you approve it with one click (CloakBrowser is installed if needed).
- The agent's browser no longer announces itself as automated (one launch flag).

#### Details (lane browser-propose)

A fresh Google sign-in in an agent's browser on a pod with no desktop was refused ("This browser or app may not be secure"); the agent explained it in prose and suggested copying a session, and nothing on screen was a button. Now: the agent's Chromium starts with `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled` (Settings → Agent browser → "Do not announce the agent browser as automated", on by default; your own `~/.agent-browser/config.json` value wins; CloakBrowser is not affected) — measured on agent-browser 0.38.1, pages read `navigator.webdriver` as false instead of true, with or without a window. When a navigation lands on a known sign-in refusal page (Google's), the agent's command says so as a hint — never as a detection. When the agent files `vibespace-browser blocked … --tier 2`, ONE card appears in the chat where it happened (and one item in For you) saying in plain words what Approve does: install CloakBrowser if it is missing (about 217 MB, once, from its maker — its progress shows on the card), add only that page's site to the sites CloakBrowser may open, switch this conversation's browser to CloakBrowser (in place when that keeps your logins, else a new CloakBrowser profile for the conversation — a profile a newer Chromium wrote is never opened by an older one), and reopen the page. Approve runs exactly what the card shows; Reject is told to the agent the next time it opens that site; a second claim is the same card; a failure says which step and Approve tries again. The agent hears about your Approve for free — in its running turn when that costs nothing, else with your next message; it never wakes by itself. Only you can approve (an agent's token is refused), and what you read is what runs: the card prints the page address exactly as it will open, and a character that is not drawn or reorders a line never reaches the card's words. The agent's manual teaches it to file the claim at once and say one sentence instead of explaining workarounds.

Verify round 1: approving a sign-in on Google, Microsoft, GitHub or Apple also lets CloakBrowser open the sites that sign-in page loads its parts from (the card names them); any other site the page is refused is named to the agent, whose next claim asks you for exactly that site with one Approve. Approve runs only for the conversation that asked and only while the card is still true (no download it did not show, no switch of a browser more conversations share than it said); a loopback site is never offered; a failed or cut CloakBrowser download is removed so Approve again downloads it again, and a stalled one says so on the card. The chat card's Approve (and the For-you popup's, after it opens) waits until it has sat still under the pointer; an agent's cheap claims can no longer push another conversation's open proposal out.

### lane site-reset — the navigation loop named within seconds; site-reset <host> (on top of browser-propose)

**a page that keeps reloading is named at once, and one site's stored login can be cleared**

- When a page in the agent's browser keeps reloading or bouncing between two addresses, the agent is told at once — with the addresses — instead of waiting for a timeout.
- The agent can clear one site's stored login in its own browser; on a shared profile it proposes it and you approve with one click.
- On a shared browser profile, the tab an agent opened itself is treated as its own (it is told of a loop there at once, and can stop or close it) even when no live view is open.
- A tab a page opens (a popup, a link that opens a new tab) belongs to the conversation whose page opened it: an agent is never told of its loop, and cannot stop or close it, just because its own command happened to be running at the time.
- Which tab is an agent's own on a shared browser is remembered across a VibeSpace restart: after an update, a page that keeps reloading in the agent's tab is still reported to that agent, and its stop and close still work.
- A page that moves itself slowly — a new address every few seconds, twenty times without settling — is reported as a navigation loop too, instead of timing out every command for good.
- While you drive one agent's browser view, a page that keeps reloading in another agent's own tab is still reported to that agent, even before the view has named the tab you are on.
- A page that moves itself through twelve ever-new addresses without settling (a session id rewritten into every address) is reported as a navigation loop too.
- Stopping a page in the agent's browser no longer fails on a momentary "not attached to an active page" from Chrome (a page mid-switch): the stop is asked again for up to half a second.
- A page that reloads itself on a timer (a dashboard on a meta refresh) is still readable by the agent: `snapshot` and `get` answer with the reload noted beside the result, and the status chip says "page refreshes itself every N s" instead of "page keeps reloading" — before, every reading command was refused once the reloads had been counted as a loop.
- A page that keeps reloading in a tab of a shared browser that belongs to no conversation (one born while two agents' commands overlapped, the browser's own first tab) is now reported to every agent on that browser as "a tab that may be yours keeps reloading", and an agent's stop says by name that it cannot tell whose tab it is — before, an agent that already had tabs of its own heard nothing and its stop said "nothing of yours was loading".
- A tab an agent opens with `tab new` is its own even when another agent's command was running on the shared browser at that moment: a page that keeps reloading there is reported to that agent at once, and its stop and close work (before: the tab belonged to nobody and the agent heard nothing).

#### Details (lane site-reset)

On a fleet pod a bank's sign-in page kept bouncing to its app and back (most likely an expired login stored in the browser), and every browser command the agent ran timed out. VibeSpace now watches each tab's navigations: six or more page loads of its own within 30 seconds that keep coming back to the same addresses (two, three or a longer round trip through a sign-in service) is a navigation loop, and the command that ran into it returns at once with `[navigation_loop]`, the addresses (without their query) and the ways out — `vibespace-browser stop` (new: stops the page loading at once), `tab close`, a screenshot that no longer waits for a page that never draws, and `vibespace-browser site-reset <host>`. That clears the cookies the site receives and the data its pages stored — nothing of any other site — in the agent's own browser; on a profile other conversations or you use, it is one card in the chat and one For-you item ("The agent proposes clearing <host>'s login and stored data in the profile <name>. Every conversation using this profile (N) … will be signed out of <host>. Nothing else is touched."), and Approve runs exactly that. The chat chip says "page keeps reloading", the live view lists the addresses, and a cleared profile's live views say so in one line. Measured on agent-browser 0.38.1 with local test pages (never a real site); a command the loop cut short still keeps that browser session busy for up to 25 seconds, which the answers say.

### lane browser-resume — the conversation's browser kept (logins + tabs), Resume, Hand back and continue, whose tab it is

- **The agent's browser can be resumed after it closes — its logins and tabs are kept.** When a conversation's own browser closes (after its turn, when it idles out, when you stop it, when VibeSpace restarts), its logins and its open tabs are kept for that conversation until the conversation ends, and its next browser command starts it again with them. The Agent browser panel lists the kept browsers with their size, and Forget removes one. A conversation fenced to allowed domains keeps its tabs only.
- **A Resume button where the live view says the browser stopped.** When the agent's browser has stopped, its live view shows **Resume** in place of Reconnect (the chat's last browser card and the Agent browser panel's kept row have it too): the browser starts again with the same logins and its last tabs, on the tab that was showing, and the view follows it. **Hand back and continue…** hands a browser you drove back for the agent's NEXT turn with a one-line note — the agent reads your note and the tabs then (nothing is sent now) and its next command runs in the same browser; the agent can also run `vibespace-browser resume` itself.
- **You can see, switch and close the agent's browser tabs — and the agent only ever touches its own.** The live view has a row of the browser's tabs (each with its site's initial and whose tab it is). While you drive the agent's browser you can switch its tab or close one of its tabs from there (never its last one) and it is told what you did when you hand back; your own tabs (Browse yourself) you switch or close any time; another conversation's tab is never yours to touch from there. **Close all…** at the row's end quits the browser after asking by its name. On a browser several conversations share, the agent's `tab list` / `tab <id>` / `tab close` work on its own tabs only — your tab and other conversations' tabs are counted, never shown to it, switched or closed.

Details (lane browser-resume, chunk A — design §3.9): rung D's generated config names `data/browser-profiles/<browser key>` (0700); a new store `data/browser-kept.json` (0600) holds each conversation's kept tabs (web pages only, titles through the peer-text door), what stopped it and whether its next start reopens them (an automatic stop yes, the user's Stop / the agent's own close or detach no). A Terminate is not an end (Terminate → Resume finds the same key); the end is Forget, a conversation no binding names any more, an adopt, or the bound: `browser.keptBytesPerConversation` (512 MB — caches first, logins never) and `browser.keptBytesTotal` (4 GB — least recently used first), measured hourly with `du` off the event loop; a running browser is never trimmed or removed, nor is the kept browser of a conversation whose session still runs removed by the total bound (verify F2). New routes `GET /api/browser/kept`, `DELETE /api/browser/kept/:browserKey` (cookie only). An agent may not `new --adopt` another conversation's kept folder (`adopt_not_yours`) — judged on the folder's real path (a symlink or a `//` spelling gets no further), and every "is this folder a named profile's" check compares real paths, so a folder registered as a profile is never deleted by the kept store or the boot sweep (verify F1). A kept folder that disappeared out of band is read as "tabs only" at every read (never "its logins are kept" over nothing; verify r2). When the kept browsers pass the total only because their conversations run, the Agent browser panel says so and that Forget frees one. A profile on a paired machine never answers for a local folder of the same path. Gate: test-browser-kept (fast).

Details (lane browser-resume, chunk B — design §3.9, the owner's ruling 2): ONE `restore` record per kept entry (an automatic stop's, or the user's Resume / hand-back — sticky until the agent's next command is told, then consumed); a deliberate stop's tabs WAIT at the next start. The reopen (PURE `resumePlan`, measured on 0.38.1): the first page into the launch tab, the rest as `tab new` in order, then the tab on show switched back to by its CDP target id — on a running browser every page is a new tab; never a `tab close`; bounded (30 s for the agent's start, 90 s for the user's Resume), a page that failed named. The resolve answer carries `restored` / `kept` / `resumed` (the CLI prints one note each). New routes `POST /api/browser/session/:sessionId/resume`, `POST /api/browser/kept/:browserKey/resume` (the live session resolved server-side), `POST /api/browser/session/:sessionId/hand-back` (cookie only) and `POST /api/agent/browser/resume` (the 13th OURS verb). The hand-back ends a takeover with the new cause `continue`, files ONE stash entry (kind notification, "a browser handback" on the strip) + ONE display-only card, and delivers nothing (no turn, no notice — the spend census unchanged); the note is belted like peer text (one line, ≤ 500, frames inert); a stash that cannot take it puts the note on the agent's next command instead. Refusals by name: `not_kept`, `child_not_kept`, `resume_adopted`, `no_live_session`, `not_yours`, `stash_refused`. A hand-back pressed again with nothing new while the previous one still waits for the agent's next turn is refused `already_handed_back` — one frame per turn, never a copy (verify r2). The frame says whether you drove the browser (a takeover ended with the hand-back) or resumed it and handed it back. A helper's (sub-agent's) browser keeps nothing, and its first command now says so (`[browser_not_kept]`). Gates: test-browser-kept ⑧–⑪ (fast), test-browser-fact ⑧, test-spend-paths, the identity and human-route censuses; test-browser-resume-ui (heavy, chrome).

Details (lane browser-resume, chunk C — design §3.9, the owner's ruling 3): measured first on the real agent-browser 0.38.1 + Chrome — on a shared profile's one Chrome every session lists every page and `tab close <id>` closes any tab (another session's next command answers `tab_gone`), a session's first command binds a new tab of its own, a popup names the tab that opened it. PURE `src/browser-tabs.js` decides whose each tab is (a lease's ROOTS — the tab it was bound to, its `tab new`s, learned after its first command's audit and kept sticky — plus what they opened; a session's current tab only when nobody roots it; the user's own holder first) and every verdict: the agent's (its own tabs only; unreadable ⇒ refused) and the user's (his tabs always but never his last; the agent's only while THIS viewer holds the takeover, never its last, not on a "separate tabs" browser in this release; another conversation's never). New route `POST /api/agent/browser/tab` (after the belt; `resolveFor` first, one read, at most ONE act under the conversation's own session; `passthrough` where the browser holds only its tabs); the CLI routes a shared profile's `tab` verbs there and refuses a `tab` line inside a `batch` (`tab_in_batch`); a `tab_gone` names this tool's way out. The live-view bridge sends `tab-owners` after each `tabs` record and answers the row's `tab-act` with a typed `tab-ack`; a switch you make moves the takeover's anchor; closing the tab on show moves the agent to a neighbour of its own first; your acts ride the takeover cycle into the handback, its notice and the hand-back-and-continue frame (never a delivery of their own) — the takeover is re-asked right before each switch / close runs, and the act is recorded in that same instant, so a handback that lands meanwhile either stops it or tells the agent about it (verify F3). Whose-tab is decided in one pass over the browser's page list (a chain of thousands of popups no longer costs seconds per tab record), and a page-chosen title is cut before it is walked (verify r2). Every reader of page-chosen bytes in the two browser modules is a row of the peer-parser census now (test-peer-parsers: a proven cap and linearity, 221). Gates: test-browser-tabs (fast, new), test-browser-verbs, test-live-strip, the tab-release / holder / identity censuses; test-browser-resume-ui ⑥ and test-browser-human-ui (b2) on the REAL 0.38.1 (heavy).

### lane hot-switch — late records never move the pool; a refuted wall never demotes the pin; the hot-switch verdict measured; OTel org = a label

**a conversation whose output reaches VibeSpace hours late no longer moves every conversation onto a spent account; a limit that another account hit is no longer charged to the one a conversation is on; the usage screens stop calling readings "not corroborated"**

- **A late backlog is no longer taken as current.** When a conversation's output reached VibeSpace hours late (its connection had stalled; the first message you typed let it through), every limit and usage number in it was treated as current. A limit another account had hit hours earlier was charged to the account the conversation was on by then. The pool then moved every conversation onto an account whose 5-hour limit was spent, and each message you sent answered "session limit". Output that the agent wrote more than two minutes before it arrives is now shown in the chat but never changes an account's numbers, limits or placement. The log says how late it was and how much of it there was.
- **A limit that states another account's reset time is no longer charged to your account.** When a limit's own reset time shows it belongs to a different account than the one the conversation is linked to, the account is no longer marked spent. This now also holds for the "You've reached your … limit" message that comes with the limit. The account is not taken out of that conversation's choices either.
- **Moving a running conversation to another account of the pool is real, and now measured.** A running claude process uses the account its link points to from its next message on. This was checked on claude 2.1.281 with fake credentials. A gate re-checks it on every CLI update and fails if a new CLI stops following the link.
- **The usage screens no longer mark readings "not corroborated", and the log stops saying "observed on X while linked to Y".** Both came from a telemetry field that names one account for the whole machine, not the account a request was billed to.

#### Details

##### lane-hot-switch — the 2026-09-30 incident, measured

- **The measurement** (scripts/measure-claude-cred-read.mjs, record scripts/fixtures/claude-cred-read-2.1.281.json). The real claude 2.1.281 ran in a network namespace with only loopback, with fake credentials and a per-session link exactly like data/pool-links. A mock server recorded the Authorization header of every request, and strace watched the creds path. Every turn the CLI statx()es `$CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR/.credentials.json` through the link and re-reads the file when its mtime differs. These changes were followed on the next turn: a symlink re-point (with or without the utimes bump), an in-place overwrite, and a hard-link replacement with a new mtime. A replacement with an EQUAL mtime was not followed (the bump in repointPoolSymlink is load-bearing). There was no local gate after a 429. The OTel `organization.id` was the scratch `~/.claude.json` org for both tokens. Assistant records carry a `timestamp` stamped at emission.
- **The production evidence.** Every 5-hour "session limit · resets H:MM" in the incident conversation from 09-28 to 09-30 (47 of them) matches the identity-verified panel window of the member its link named at that moment, never the "birth member" the OTel rows named. Four different reset times fell inside 5 h on 09-29, which one account's window cannot produce. The OTel org was a single value for ~99 % of all local rows for four days. It is written machine-wide by whichever claude process last refetched its own profile (every 24 h).
- **What happened** (journal, read-only). The server crashed at 12:03 (EMFILE). One conversation's stdout bridge came back dead in both directions. At 15:05:14 the owner's first message since the crash tripped the broken-stdin detector, and the local re-attach released the three-hour backlog in three seconds. Stale readings were re-filed as current: the spent member's 5 h read 95 % again. A 12:15 Fable rejection (another member's week, per its own window) was archived at the record, but its window-less banner then marked the linked member's Fable. The turn end excluded that member from the conversation, and the pool moved ten conversations onto the spent member.
- **Fixes.** ① src/record-lateness.js + the engine's gateLiveFact: a record is judged by its own stamp; unstamped records inherit the stamp just before them or look ahead in the same chunk. Both feeds apply this. Late readings, walls, banners, turn ends and odometer entries are counted and journalled, never acted on. ② `_turnWallRefuted`: the banner, the turn-end fold, the session-wall exclusion and the two-walls ring all follow a refutation, the way they already followed a re-file. ③ `hotSwitchEvidence` on the claude caps row, test-architecture §67, and the heavy re-measuring gate test-claude-hot-switch. ④ The OTel label is retired as an identity everywhere: corroboration, the witness veto, the refresh skip, the observed-org wall rung and the "observed on" lines. The stash row writes `labelMatchesSlot` instead of `agreed`.
- **Repair.** Nothing persistent was left to undo. The false Fable marks on the two members were overwritten by live readings minutes later (15:06:59 and 15:27). The session-wall exclusions were in memory and expired. No ledger row was re-keyed.
- **Held.** A stdout bridge silent for three hours while the CLI was making API requests went unnoticed: a heal trigger needs a stdin probe that old wrappers cannot answer without a billed turn. The 12:03 EMFILE crash. Rows from no-pool sessions baked by the OTel `truthLookup` between 2.361.0 and 2026-09-07 were skipped by B-f69c ②'s backfill, whose premise ("a no-pool session's org is its slot") is refuted too. They were not quantified.
- Gates: test-hot-switch-incident (fast, new: §A late records, §B refuted walls, §C the load-bearing bump, §D the label census, 12 patched-copy controls), test-claude-hot-switch (heavy, new), test-architecture §67, plus updated test-otel-truth, test-auto-resume(-loop), test-readings-attribution, test-window-anchor-heal, test-rate-limit-capture, test-fable-cap-pool-storm, test-pool-auto, test-stdout-registry.

### lane dead-bridge — the 12:03 crash and the three-hour dead bridge (on top of hot-switch)

- **The server no longer stops when the disk it lives on briefly refuses to open files.** On 30 September the server stopped because the shared drive its folder lives on ran out of open files for a moment: saving a status file failed, and that one failed save ended the whole server. Now a failed save keeps its data and tries again, and a notice says which side ran out — VibeSpace itself, the shared drive, or the machine.
- **A message typed into a conversation whose output was stuck is no longer handed to the agent twice.** When a restart left a conversation's output stuck, the message that unstuck it was delivered once through the stuck connection and once more through the new one. It is re-sent now only when the first connection never worked at all.
- **A conversation whose output stopped reaching VibeSpace after a server restart is reconnected by itself within minutes, and what it missed is shown as caught up, never re-run.** After that crash one conversation kept working for three hours while nothing it did reached the screen, until you typed. A restart no longer leaves the old connection behind to block the new one, and a conversation that has sent nothing for 3 minutes while its agent is still working is reconnected; a note in the chat says when the output was lost and restored and how many records came in (Settings → Session → "Reconnect a silent conversation after", 0 turns it off).
##### lane-dead-bridge — the 12:03 crash and the three-hour dead bridge

- **Who ran out (measured).** node raises its own soft open-files limit to the hard one at startup, so the server ran at 524288, not the unit's 1024, and held ~75 handles. The EMFILE came from the workspace's `fuse.bindfs` daemon (soft 1024, 947 open — ~700 of them another group's mmapped venv); a FUSE daemon's refusal reaches the caller's open() as its own. The unit template now states `LimitNOFILE=524288` (65536 would have lowered the server's limit). The durable bindfs fix (a `[Mount] LimitNOFILE=` drop-in) is the machine owner's.
- **Why the bridge stayed dead (reproduced on raw dtach and a worktree server).** node-pty's pty masters have no close-on-exec, so every process the server spawned after an attach (mounts, a Background Work job, agent browsers, the next attach clients) held them; the crash path, unlike the clean shutdown, ended no attach client, so the old clients survived, stuck. dtach's master then never attaches a new client while the pty is busy (it re-enters its write loop before reading the attach packet); the new client's own clear-screen byte made the 09-09 attach probe read it as alive. The owner's message caused a second connect, which broke the loop once.
- **Fixes.** ① One attach-pty teardown for the clean shutdown and the crash path. ② The boot sweep ends orphaned attach clients of our sockets (a dtach with a terminal whose parent died — never a master, never a person's own attach) after the restore's attaches connected: attach first, then kill (dtach drops what it reads with no client attached — measured). ③ The dead-bridge watch: silent ≥ N minutes while the wrapper's buffer file or an OTel api_request shows the CLI working ⇒ re-attach through the one healer (≤ 3 an hour, an empty heal doubles the wait). ④ What a re-attach releases is counted through lane-hot-switch's late-record rule and one card says so. ⑤ session-status, user-todos and the channels index retry a failed save (a server held at a full table for a minute stays up — the channels index was the next timer to kill it) and name who ran out; an fd gauge (80 %, once an hour) and the boot log line say the real limit.
- **Production, not touched.** The 13 orphaned attach clients of the 09-29 20:49 server are still attached to the live sessions; the boot sweep ends them at the next update + restart (until then a restart during a busy turn can repeat this).
- **verify r1.** The broken-stdin detector's re-send DOUBLED the message in the stuck-master shape (a connected, never-attached client's queued input is read by the master after the client dies — reproduced on raw dtach, 2×): it re-sends only through a bridge that never spoke (`_ptyOpenedAt`); test-dead-bridge §1 ⑥ + test-bridge-liveness §F. The fd gauge's and the write-error blame's hourly notice was spent before asking whether any client received it — undelivered notices are tried again at the next sample (test-fd-limit §E). Three parts no gate pinned (user-todos' timer guard, the post-heal orphan sweep, the empty-heal doubling) are pinned now.
- Gates: test-dead-bridge (heavy, new), test-bridge-liveness + test-fd-limit (fast, new), test-restore-liveness ⑤ (the EMFILE-shaped restart, extended).

### lane codex-0159 — the reset-credit consume carries an idempotencyKey; the codex protocol drift gate

**using a codex reset credit works again with the current codex CLI**

#### Fixed

- Using a codex reset credit works again with the current codex CLI.

#### Details (lane codex-0159)

The codex CLI refused every reset-credit request VibeSpace sent ("Invalid request: missing field `idempotencyKey`"): the consume went out with no parameters. Measured on the CLI itself, the key is required on 0.153.4 as well as on 0.159.3 — the credit had been failing before the update, which only made it visible. Now the server mints one key per press (a UUID kept with that press's attempt) and hands it to the conversation's wrapper with the request; the wrapper sends it, makes up its own when an older server sends none, and retries once with the SAME key only when the CLI gave no answer — the CLI counts one key once, so a retry can never spend a second credit, and its answer `alreadyRedeemed` for that key is read as this press's own reset. A conversation whose wrapper is older than the key (refused before anything was spent) now says "Terminate + Resume the conversation to update its wrapper" instead of the CLI's raw words, and the CLI's `nothingToReset` / `noCredit` answers are said in words.

A new fast gate, scripts/test-codex-protocol-drift.mjs, judges every request the codex wrapper makes, and every notification it consumes, against tables measured from the CLI itself (scripts/fixtures/codex-app-server/0.153.4- and 0.159.3-methods.json, written by the maintainer tool scripts/measure-codex-protocol.mjs: the CLI's own JSON Schema, read without starting anything, plus each method's answer to an empty request from an app-server in an empty network namespace with an empty CODEX_HOME — no vendor call). An installed codex-cli that no table measured fails the gate by name, with the remedy. Between 0.153.4 and 0.159.3 the wrapper's methods changed only by new optional fields; the gate also drives the real wrapper against a stub that answers as the measured table says (the key once, the same-key retry, the pre-fix wrapper reproducing the incident's exact answer).

#### B-956d — the Desktop takes a free display when its preferred one is held

- The production Desktop singleton was pinned to `:7` (src/vnc.js) while desktop apps' X servers take the lowest free display with `-displayfd` — an app could hold :7 first and the Desktop never started. Now VIBESPACE_VNC_DISPLAY (else the historic :7) is the PREFERRED display: Xvnc starts on it with `-displayfd 3`; held ⇒ Xvnc again with `-displayfd` alone (the X server picks, race-free). The display it named is recorded in `data/vnc.json {display, port, pid, start}`; a restart that finds the port listening adopts THAT display (the desktop-singleton rung and the session run on it). A record for another port is ignored. MEASURED by hand (Xtigervnc, a scratch Xvfb on the preferred display): the held display exits code 1 in 17 ms; `-displayfd` alone answered `:5` in 165 ms, port listening. Note: the override now names the preferred display, not a hard pin — held, the Desktop goes elsewhere instead of failing.
- Gate: test-vnc-view (in-process, a stand-in X server keeping X's lock rule in a scratch dir — nothing real on any display): free ⇒ the preferred display taken + recorded; held ⇒ another display, recorded with port + pid, the singleton rung reads it; a restart adopts it with no second server; CONTROL = the same file without the fallback refuses to start (the report).

## 2.369.198 — a formatted mail that scrolls into view is drawn, never a blank box; on a busy server the agent's page on a phone keeps the phone's width; while you drive the agent's browser, a click on a text box's label gives that box the keyboard

A gate-fix release: 2.369.197's post-push gates were red on eight suites (four in the local heavy run, four on the Actions mirror) while the lanes' own runs were green — launch-environment and composition effects, and one product rule among them.

- **A formatted mail that scrolls into view is drawn.** In a Channels conversation of short formatted mails, a mail that came into view because a mail above it got shorter could stay an empty box until you scrolled. Now every applied height re-judges which mails are drawn.
- **The agent's page on a phone keeps the phone's width on a busy server.** The live view could re-fit a headless page at 500 px ("Page 500 px wide (its narrowest)") when a late frame of an earlier fit arrived; a frame is now judged only when it answers the fit it is compared with.
- **Typing while you drive the agent's browser, a fourth check.** A click on a text box's label gives that box the keyboard; a box the app re-creates under your click gets its one message; the chip no longer rewrites its unchanged words on every focus move.

### Integration / gate — the eight reds of 2.369.197 and their causes

- test-browser-display-chrome (local heavy): its launch-PATH farm linked the first `agent-browser` on PATH — the VibeSpace shim on the push shell ⇒ `binary_absent`; the farm now links resolved binaries.
- test-window-target (local heavy): the switch-less Chrome 154 control's wording followed the caller's `QT_ACCESSIBILITY` / `GTK_MODULES`; the child runs without them and the table keeps every reason seen per Chrome major.
- test-browser-live-input (local heavy): a control patch anchored on a whole line the .197 integration had extended; it anchors on the line's head.
- test-browser-live-fit (local heavy): the bridge judged an earlier fit's late frame as this fit's answer ⇒ the 500 px headed floor on a headless phone page (the product fix above).
- test-pool-auto (Actions fast): `git show <pre-fix sha>:` on the depth-1 checkout; the historical rung skips with evidence on a shallow clone, a ref-free sweep carries the leg.
- test-channel-threads-ui (Actions heavy): the ⑥ control's premise was a font fact (no CJK family on the runner); the control narrows the box by construction, and the heavy job installs `fonts-noto-cjk`.
- test-channels-aggregate-ui (Actions heavy): the product rule above (an applied height never re-judged the live set) + a judge that sampled at a fixed nap; it now waits on the frames' own settled evidence.
- test-browser-live (Actions heavy): the Chrome CDP port was picked free and held for up to a minute before Chrome bound it; Chrome now picks its own port (`--remote-debugging-port=0`, read from `DevToolsActivePort`).
- test-desktop-app-keeper (first run red, green on the gate's retry): not root-caused — held with the evidence: the fake picture server's close now fails by name with the connections it waits on.
- The composed tree (this integration): lane takeover-keyboard's r4 input-surface census met 2.369.197's BROWSE YOURSELF rows it had never seen — the address box's `inputmode` (a new census construct) and four `focusSink()` sites of the user's own acts (his address box's Enter / Escape while he drives, the touch Keyboard button, Continue here); both classified in test-takeover-keyboard, the pin moved 13 → 17.

### Details (the lanes' own words)

#### lane-heavy-197 — the local heavy run

The post-push heavy run on 2.369.197 was red on four suites and flaky on a fifth. Nothing here changes what a user sees in the product except where a bullet says so; the rest is the gate reading the machine it runs on instead of the code it judges.

- **test-browser-display-chrome (every leg red in 0.7 s).** The suite's launch-PATH farm linked "the first `agent-browser` on PATH" — on the push shell that is the VibeSpace shim — so the product it tested answered `binary_absent` while the suite had resolved the real CLI two lines earlier; `symlinkSync` also linked dangling names. The farm now links the resolver's REAL binary and every other name's first existing target, and prints what it linked. Red on the pre-fix file under the same PATH, 26/26 green after.
- **test-window-target (the negative control).** Chrome 154 launched without the accessibility switch reads "its accessibility tree is closed (4 nodes)" when the caller's shell carries `QT_ACCESSIBILITY=1` / `GTK_MODULES` (this box's, inherited by the push shell) and "no accessibility tree" under `env -i` (the integrator's runs) — the control's wording was the shell's, not the code's. The lane-E child now runs without those variables (the product's own switch is the only accessibility input a launch carries), the table keeps every reason observed per Chrome major, and the assertion says which one it saw. Red reproduced with the shell's variables on the pre-fix file, green with and without them after.
- **test-browser-live-input ⑦.** A control patch anchored on a whole line the 2.369.197 integration had extended (`expectWakes` on the Hand-back handler); the integrator merged that lane a second time after its full heavy run and this suite never ran on the final text. The anchor is the line's head up to the clause the patch removes. 163/163 after.
- **The live view of a phone no longer widens a headless page to 500 px on a slow machine (test-browser-live-fit ④, a PRODUCT fix).** The bridge judged every frame against its newest fit: on the loaded gate machine the frame of the pane's FIRST fit (390×700) arrived after the settled fit (390×737) had been asked — same width, a smaller height — which is exactly the shape of "a headed window that cannot be that narrow", so the page was re-fitted at 500 px and the phone showed a 500-wide page scaled down with its link drawn at 59 px (the run-1 red; run 2 hit the same shape on the desktop pane: a band under the page). What a user would have seen: on a busy server the agent's page on the phone suddenly too wide, the chip saying "Page 500 px wide (its narrowest)" about a headless browser. Now a frame is judged only when it is this fit's answer: a frame at a size we asked for in the last 10 s is that earlier fit's, late; a frame read before the daemon's echo of this set shows the page before it. The headed floor itself is unchanged (measured on 0.38.1) and still fires on a real headed browser. Deterministic proof in test-browser-fit (the late frame and the pre-echo frame, each with a control that floors at 500 without its fence); the suite prints the bridge's own fit lines when the phone leg fails.
- **test-desktop-app-keeper (failed once, passed on the gate's retry) — held with the evidence.** Its first run ended at 44.7 s with node's "unsettled top-level await" (exit 13) at the close of block (e)'s fake picture server: the close never called back while nothing kept the loop alive. The retry and every run since (alone and under a four-suite load, with a diagnostic printing the open connections) closed with none; the keeper's probes destroy their sockets on the banner. Not root-caused: the fake server now tracks what it accepted, and a close that does not answer in 3 s is failed BY NAME with those connections (peer port, reading, pending) and the suite goes on — a recurrence names itself instead of exiting silently.

#### lane-mirror-197 — the Actions mirror

The mirror run (36594877665) was red on `fast` (test-pool-auto, 6 of 456) and `heavy` (test-channel-threads-ui, test-channels-aggregate-ui, and test-browser-live once before its retry). None was a product bug the owner could meet except one; each was root-caused UNDER THE RUNNER'S OWN CONDITIONS (reproduced here with a depth-1 clone, a fontconfig that offers only DejaVu, `taskset -c 0-3` + `nice 15`) and fixed at the cause — no skips, no retries as acceptance.

- **test-pool-auto (fast job, 6 red / 450 green).** Three byte-identity sweeps compared the pool verdicts against the pre-fix source with `git show b970f16d:…`; the runner's checkout is `fetch-depth: 1` (the pushed commit alone), so the ref is absent there BY CONSTRUCTION — three `fatal: invalid object name` lines and three copies-census legs that counted the copy that was never made. Reproduced exactly in a local `git clone --depth 1`. Now `preFixCopy()` names the world: the ref present ⇒ the historical rung runs (full clones, the pre-push hook); absent on a SHALLOW clone ⇒ the rung SKIPS with evidence and the census keys on whether that control ran (the 2.369.164 r2 rule), while a ref-free sweep (the three membership shapes, null / [] / omitted priority, the no-pin path) carries the leg everywhere; absent on a FULL clone ⇒ a failure by name, never a skip (a control proves the helper tells the two worlds apart). Depth-1: 457 pass; full: 460 pass.
- **test-channel-threads-ui (heavy, both attempts).** The naive-user ⑥ control asserted "the pre-fix nowrap rule cuts this ja composer line at 360 px" — a fact about the FONT: the runner image has no CJK family and DejaVu's fallback boxes are narrower than the glyphs a Japanese user sees, so the one-line text FIT its box and nothing was cut (`cutNow:false`; reproduced here under a DejaVu-only fontconfig, byte for byte). The control now measures the one-line width and, where it fits, narrows the box BY CONSTRUCTION to 60 % of that width and judges the RULE there: the pre-fix rule cuts, the product rule wraps whole — under any font. And the heavy job installs `fonts-noto-cjk` (ci.yml, with the reason): users have CJK fonts; every zh / ja "drawn whole" census on the runner was blind under tofu.
- **test-channels-aggregate-ui (heavy, both attempts).** Attempt 1 — three hostile mails "dropped before the census": the judge saw each frame live, napped 300 ms, and read the row after a neighbour's late height had pushed it out of the keep zone and the lazy rule had dropped its frame. Attempt 2 — 7 short mails on screen, the 7th a blank box: a real product rule gap (below). The judge now waits on the frames' OWN evidence with a deadline — live, measured, and STILL (two reads 150 ms apart at the same y) — never a fixed sample; the same run under the runner's conditions here also caught the suite's spoof leg reading a frame's height before its content had loaded (24 px, then 327 px — a legitimate growth read as the spoof's), so that judge waits for the height to settle too.
- **test-browser-live (heavy, red once, green on the gate's retry — not acceptance).** The pre-fix-client control's record ended at `chrome: "<dbus noise>"`: Chrome's /json showed no page target within a fixed 30 s. Two orders were possible and neither was named: the leg picked its Chrome port with `freePort()` and held it FREE through a worktree copy, an esbuild rebuild, a server boot and a session create — 20–60 s in which the other lane's processes pick ports the same way — before Chrome bound it; and a fixed budget on a throttled 4-vCPU box. Now `launchChrome()` lets Chrome pick its own port (`--remote-debugging-port=0`) and reads it from Chrome's own `DevToolsActivePort` file — the port cannot be taken between pick and bind — with a deadline scaled to that machine's measured Chrome start and the leg's own rebuild time; the record carries the start time, the port, an early exit and the stderr TAIL. Server ports are picked right before their bind, at every site of the suite.
- **What you could see.** In a Channels conversation of short formatted mails, a mail that came INTO view because a mail above it got shorter (its frame had just measured itself, smaller than the placeholder it was born with) could stay an empty box until you scrolled. The live set was re-judged on a scroll or when a row crossed the observer's edge — an applied height moves the rows below without either. Now every applied height re-judges the live set, so a visible mail is never a blank box.

#### lane takeover-keyboard — verify r4 (typing into the chat while you drive the browser)

- Checked a fourth time (the rules of round 3 and the census behind them): clicking the LABEL of a text box (the word next to it) now gives the box the keyboard like clicking the box itself (before it was taken back with a message to click the box); a text box that the app re-creates under your click while it is being focused (a list row patched by an update) now gets its one message instead of none; the browser view's chip no longer re-writes its unchanged words on every focus move while you type elsewhere (it did four times per move, invisible but felt by screen readers); and the census of "every place that takes keys" now reads the app the way the browser runs it — text boxes and dropdowns built through helper functions, by a conditional, or in the page's own markup were missed before (the outbox editor, the For-you window's reply box, the New Session dialog's dropdowns, 31 places in all) even though each already followed its rule. Measured on real Chrome and left as designed: an open dropdown list takes the arrow keys, typing and Enter / Escape itself while you drive (nothing leaks to the page), the colour picker stays open, and a dialog you open while driving still sends Enter to the page after telling you so once — whether such a dialog should take the keyboard instead is a question for the owner.

## 2.369.197 — you can clear the text of an Activity entry, a For-you item, a status entry, a background job or a group message — the record keeps its place and time, every copy of the words goes with it, and a group message's card in another agent's chat says it was cleared; a Gmail mail with formatting is shown formatted (in a sealed frame, remote pictures only when you ask), Lark messages no longer show raw tags like `<p>`, Lark cards show their contents and a Lark bot is shown by its name; Channels show threads and emoji reactions — a reply says what it answers and where it will land, a thread opens beside the list, you add or remove a reaction with a click, and an agent proposes a reaction you approve like a reply; Lark finds every new message with one search, your single chats included, and checks each chat less often once the search is proven to miss nothing; pairing a device lets you pick the address it dials, replaces a command only when you ask and says why a device cannot connect; a paired machine is lent to agents only as you allow, network and commands separately; you can pin one conversation to one account of its pool and order a pool yourself, and an account taken out of a pool stops serving at once; you can open an agent-browser profile yourself and browse with its logins in your own tab of the same browser while the agents keep working in theirs; when a page in the agent's browser opens a dialog the agent is told at once what it asks, the live view shows it with its buttons, and a page that stops responding offers Restart; while you drive the agent's browser a click into the chat box or a terminal lets you type there; an agent's browser starts even when nobody is logged in to the machine's desktop (a hidden window, else headless — it says which); CloakBrowser can be installed and used, and it reaches only the sites you list; a group message sent to another agent shows in that agent's chat, and the notices waiting for an agent (and the ones a hand-over delivered) can be opened and read; a tab pulled out of its group on the Stage stays on screen, and a file saved from a preview keeps its own name instead of "raw"; a new conversation can never take over a stopped one's browser, and taking a conversation out of a Task Group takes a kept browser profile away at once; a Chrome window you share with an agent is readable by it again on Chrome 154, and a desktop app is drawn whole again after you minimize it and the sidebar moves it

### "Clear content…" (the owner's ask, 2026-09-28)

The owner: a peer agent pasted content from an unrelated mailbox into the 工作 Task Group's records, and there was no way to remove it — editing data/ by hand is not allowed (the running server owns those files, and the group message log is append-only).

- **Right-click (or long-press) a record → "Clear content…".** Offered on an entry in the Task Group log window (Activity tab — also a ⋯ on each row), an item in the For-you popup and the For-you window, an entry in Session Properties' status history, a job in the Background Work panel, and a message in an agent group's window. One confirm dialog names the record's time and its first words, says what will happen, and asks once.
- **Many at once.** In the Task Group log window the search box is now the "Find…" box on the Activity tab; "Select…" adds a checkbox to each row and a bar with "Select all shown (N)" and "Clear selected (N)" — so "every entry that mentions X" is: type X, Select…, Select all shown, Clear selected. Only the entries shown under the current Find text are cleared; the dialog lists them.
- **What a clear leaves.** The record keeps its id, time, author and position; its text becomes "[cleared at the user's request]" (shown as 已按用户要求清除 in Chinese and ユーザーの要請により消去済み in Japanese, dimmed). A detail, option chips, a reply, a job's context, its runs' last log lines and its delivery notes go with it. The file stores the English sentence and `clearedAt` / `clearedBy`, never a translation.
- **Every copy goes.** The Task Group's TASK.md in its context folder, the context injected into its agents (a clear is not announced to them as news), `vibespace-task show`, the For-you preview of a resolved item (and the full text a client kept), the current status line and a queued "the user changed your status" note, a job's archived copy, the event lines and held notifications its agents would read, the drained-notification files, the job's own For-you items, and an agent group's list line and the next-turn reports its members get.
- **Agents can clear their own words.** `vibespace-task progress-redact <P-id>` clears an Activity entry the agent's own session wrote (`progress` now prints the new entry's id; `show` prints the ids of your own entries); `vibespace-ask clear <id>` clears an item it filed itself. Another session's entry, a fork that has no conversation of its own yet, and a background job's token are refused with a plain reason. Only the user clears anything else.
- **Group messages are append-only.** Clearing one appends a replacement record to the group's log and marks it in the group's index; everyone reads the cleared text. The original line stays in the log file on disk — group logs are never rolled or trimmed, so there is nothing to compact on (said in the essay, not hidden).
- **An audit line with no words.** Each clear writes one journal line — which kind, which ids, how many, by whom — and a group message also gets a channels-audit row. The cleared words are never repeated there.
- **Under the hood.** PURE `src/record-clear.js` (the five kinds, which fields a clear replaces, who may clear, the log fold), `src/server/record-clear.js` (the one entry point: the rule asked for every record, one write and one broadcast per store, the journal line), `src/routes/records-clear.js` (owner-only `POST /api/records/clear` and `/clear-many`; an agent token is refused by name), each store's one door (`clearProgress`, `clearItems`, `clearHistory`, `clearJobs` — the archive written first — and `clearMessages`), `src/lib/record-clear-ui.js` (the dialog). Activity-log entries now carry a stable `P-` id (added once to existing entries when the server starts).
- **Verify r1 (four findings, each reproduced, fixed and pinned with a pre-fix copy as the control).** A `--notify` reminder's held notification kept the reminder's words after its job was cleared and injected them into the owner conversation's next turn — every held notification of a cleared job now reads the sentence. A status entry set with `--detail` and no reason left the current record's detail (the "Now" row's expander) untouched — the current record follows when its reason OR its detail repeats the entry. The channels panel's generic conversation reader (`GET /api/channels/<adapter>/<conversation>/messages`) served an agent group's ORIGINAL message line by path after a clear — it now answers 404 for a conversation the engine does not know (the group window reads its own folded route). The session status popover's Reason box had lost its "optional" placeholder to a mid-line comment — restored, and test-architecture §48b now refuses an assignment statement at the end of a mid-line comment in any product file.
- **Verify r2 (the UX pass; every finding reproduced first, fixed and pinned).** Every surface now shows a visible way in, not only a right-click: a "Clear content…" button at the end of the For-you window's item actions, a ⋯ on each status-history row in Session Properties, a "Clear content…" button in an expanded Background Work job, a ⋯ on a group message when the pointer rests on it (a long-press on a phone). In the Task Group log: an entry that Find matched only by its detail opens that detail, and the confirm dialog says "Found in the detail: “…”" under it; a cleared entry no longer shows a checkbox (or a ⋯) while selecting; clearing a selection ends Select mode; a selection of any size clears (it is sent in parts of 200 — before, "Select all shown" over a full 500-entry log was one request the server refused); the day and time cells use the device's language (they were in US English on a Chinese page). A refusal is now worded on the owner's own device ("Could not clear: no such record" / 找不到这条记录 / 該当する記録がありません …) instead of the server's English sentence. A cleared job's old run log is withheld and says so — `vibespace-job logs` prints "(log withheld — this job's content was cleared at the user's request)" and the panel "The log is hidden — this job's content was cleared", never "(no log)"; a run that starts after the clear logs normally. Chinese: "Already cleared" reads 已经清除过了, "Select none" 取消全选.
- **Verify r3 (the reader-census round — seven more copies found by a runtime walk and the census, each reproduced, fixed and pinned with a pre-fix copy as the control).** A background job's pending ask (the panel it was waiting on) kept its words after the job was cleared and was still served to the panel dialog — the ask is withdrawn with the clear (the job goes back to running, it may ask again; its For-you item is resolved and cleared). A job run that had started before the clear and was stopped by force afterwards re-published its log's last line into every job list — a covered run keeps no last line. A held notification whose text ran over several lines kept its later lines in the drained-notification file — the file writes one line per notification now, and old entries' continuation lines go with the entry. A job cleared once and cleared again after it announced more kept the new announce in the agents' update ring — a second clear takes it. A notification that was being delivered at the moment of the clear was held afterwards with the old words — it is held as the sentence. A notification (or a group wake) a codex conversation's wrapper could not queue is handed back to the delivery ladder's own queue (data/msg-stash.json), which no clear reached — both doors now rewrite it. A running published service's port forward kept `service: <the old name>` in the Ports panel — it is relabelled.
- **Forward-ported onto 2.369.196 (the merge).** 2.369.195's "Hand over now" keeps what it handed over — each notice's original entry and the message that carried them — for a day (`data/stash-handover.json`), so a message the agent's wrapper hands back can be put back as itself. That is one more copy of a job's or a group message's words: a clear now reaches it through the delivery ladder's door (the same rule as the ladder's own queue, plus the cleared jobs' ids), the kept entries read the sentence, and a hand-over that carried the words keeps only a fingerprint of its message — a returned message is still recognised and comes back cleared. The group message's ⋯ button paints the window background (its colour named two tokens no theme defines). Gates: test-record-clear-stores (f3) with two pre-fix copies as controls; the census names the new file's owner and pins the five statements.
- **Verify r3 on the merged tree (the closure round; each finding reproduced first, fixed and pinned with a pre-fix copy as the control).** Clearing a job or a group message while "Hand over now" was still delivering it left the message that carried the words in the hand-over's one-day memory on disk — the memory now keeps only a fingerprint of such a message, and a message the agent's wrapper hands back is still put back as the cleared notices. A hand-over the wrapper had already handed back, whose message carried a background job's own notification (the form the job engine writes, with the job id in parentheses), kept that job's name and words in the same memory after the clear — the memory now recognises the job id however it is written. An agent running as a Codex fork was told "this session is a fork that has no conversation of its own yet" on every `vibespace-task progress-redact` / `vibespace-ask clear`, for the life of the session (the fork flag is never cleared on Codex) — the verbs now ask the same fork question every other agent verb asks, so a fork that has its own thread clears its own entries. The reader census now derives the list of route files from the tree (it had been typed by hand and missed the "Hand over now" route, which reads both waiting-notice stores through helpers) and follows a handler into the same-file functions it calls: 79 routes classified, one more negative control.
- **Verify r4 (what lies outside the census — time and order at every write door; each finding reproduced first, fixed and pinned with a pre-fix copy as the control).** A notification or a group wake that was already queued inside a Codex conversation when the owner cleared its job or message came BACK with the old words when the conversation was stopped or the queued item removed — hours later, even after a VibeSpace restart — and was held again for the conversation's next turn (in data/msg-stash.json). Every entry the delivery ladder holds is now judged by the stores at the moment it is written: a message that names a cleared job, or repeats a cleared group message, is held as the cleared sentence (a job's later notifications, written after the clear, are held as themselves). Clearing a For-you item or a status entry now writes the cleared record to disk before anything says it is cleared — it used to wait up to half a second, so a crash in that half second brought the words back after the dialog had said the clear cannot be undone. The confirm dialog now also says what a clear cannot reach: an agent that already received the words keeps them in its own conversation — only VibeSpace's records change. A background job that keeps running after it was cleared (a recurring digest) and is cleared a second time no longer gets the second round of its words back through a notification that was waiting in a Codex conversation's queue or on its way at that moment. The For-you popup's Notifications tab no longer keeps an item's words in the browser after the item is cleared: the arrival notice is remembered by its heading and the item it points to, and shows the item's current text (the cleared sentence once cleared); entries an older version stored are trimmed the next time the page loads.
- **Verify r5 (the client side — what a page keeps after the clear; each finding reproduced in Chrome first, fixed and pinned with a pre-fix copy as the control).** A background job's "Job input" window (the phone's, a replayed window on every other device) kept the job's name in its title — and so in the taskbar, in the saved workspace layout and in an incident's snapshot — and the question the clear had withdrawn: it only listened for changes to its own job by id, and a clear announces the ids it cleared. It now redraws on its job's clear and shows the cleared sentence in the device's language. A session's card in the sidebar, opened on its status history, kept a cleared history entry's words for good when that entry was not the session's current status: the update the clear sends looked like "nothing changed" to the sidebar. The update now names what was cleared, and the card redraws. A Task Group's detail window on a device where one of its fields had the keyboard (the title, the objective) kept a cleared Activity entry's words — the window does not redraw while you type, and the redraw after it may never come; its Activity list is now redrawn on its own. The same for Session Properties while one of its drop-downs has the keyboard (the account for the next resume, the browser limit): its "Now" line and its status history are now redrawn from the latest status on every update. A For-you arrival notice still on screen (they stay up to the notice-duration setting, 60 s at most) shows the cleared sentence as soon as its item is cleared. The workspace layout the server saves (data/layouts.json, its rollback points, what one device sends the others) no longer keeps a job's name at all: the "Job input" window's title is stored as "Job input" — each device still shows the job's name in the window it draws. A layout file an older version wrote is corrected the first time the server reads it. Three click handlers no longer keep a whole record in the browser's memory after a clear — the For-you arrival notice (the item), the Task Groups view's colour bars and Session Properties' Task Group checkboxes (the group, its activity notes included): they keep the record's id and look the current record up when clicked. A list that was still loading when a clear landed can no longer draw the old words over it: an agent group's window (a page of messages), the Background Work window, and the For-you inbox's catch-up after a reconnect. The "Remove job" confirmation names a cleared job by the cleared sentence in the device's language (it showed the stored English text on a Chinese or Japanese device). A background job's question arriving in For you no longer leaves the job's name in the browser: the arrival notice was remembered with its heading and the item's label, and for a background job that label is the job's name — it is now remembered by its heading alone, and the Notifications tab shows the item's current label and text (older entries are cut back to their heading). A client-side census now stands guard over all of this: a fast check over the page's code (every browser storage key it writes, every window title that shows a record's words, every place a surface reads a record's text, the caches it keeps, the updates each surface redraws on — four deliberately broken copies must fail it), and a Chrome run with two devices that plants a unique word in each of the five kinds of record, opens every surface, clears them, and then looks for the word everywhere the page could keep it: the screen, the browser's storage, the page's memory, the saved layout and an incident report.
- **Verify r6 (census adequacy, the closure: every r5 fix reverted on a copy, one part at a time, and the gate that turns red named).** The fast census's repaint rows now check everything their labels name: the Task Group detail window's repaint while a field is being typed in, Session Properties' repaint while a select has the focus, and the live For-you arrival toast's re-wording — one of them was written so that it passed on half of its claim, the others checked only that the window listened. Each is reverted on a copy in the census itself and turns exactly its own row red. Two more places could bring cleared words back when the browser reconnected at the moment of a clear (reproduced by dropping the connection for real and holding the page's older answers until after the clear): a session's card in the sidebar showed a cleared current status again (and kept it until some other status changed), and the Channels panel showed a cleared group message again as the group's last line. Both now ignore an answer that is older than an update they already received. An agent group's window opened (or restored on another device) at the moment a message was cleared showed the message's words: it ignored the clear until its first page had arrived, and that page had been read before the clear. It now keeps the clear from the moment it opens. The class these three belong to — an answer read before a clear, shown after it — now has its own gates: the fast census lists every place the page fetches one of the five stores and requires the check that drops an older answer (a new place is refused until it says which), and the browser census clears with such answers deliberately in flight (the connection dropped for real, the windows mid-refresh) — the one r5 fix that no test noticed when it was taken out (Session Properties' history painting whichever answer came last) is now caught by both. The status box you open from a session's state chip or Session Properties ("Change…") no longer brings back a reason that was cleared while it was open: pressing Apply to change only the state used to save the old words again as your own status; an untouched Reason box now follows the current record. Folding a group of Background Work jobs saved the jobs' NAME in your account's saved preferences on the server (every device, a configuration export), and clearing the job did not reach it: the fold is now remembered by a fingerprint of the name, and an older saved entry is dropped (that group's fold goes back to its default once).
- **Verify r7 (the final closure, fresh eyes; each finding reproduced in Chrome first, fixed and pinned with a pre-fix copy as the control).** A layout you saved by name while a background job's "Job input" window was open — or the layout of a desktop you had switched away from — kept that job's name in the page's memory after the job was cleared (never shown, never sent; gone at the next reload): the page now records such a window under its generic title the moment it captures a layout, from the same table the server uses. Every other place your browser's state is saved on the server — drafts, settings, uploads, the stage, bookmarks, themes, every section of a config backup, diagnostics, incident captures, the ops log, each session's sidecar files — was exported and searched after a clear and holds none of the words; each is now listed in the census with what proves it, and the release gate's walk exports a backup with every section after the clear. The For-you popup, once closed (a click anywhere else closes it — including the right-click that opens "Clear content…" on another window), kept its rows in the page: a record cleared while it was closed stayed there unseen until the popup was opened again; the popup now empties itself when it closes (a reply you were typing is kept as a draft). Double-clicking a background job's Start answered "<job name> is already running", and that message stayed in the For-you Notifications tab after the job was cleared: Background Work now names the job by its id in such a message.
