- **Verify round 6 (H1): text written by an agent, a peer or a file can no longer change how the rest of the page looks.** Its styles and borrowed page styles are removed (and it cannot place buttons or forms), so an agent's message can no longer make the command shown above Allow — or an outgoing message awaiting your approval — read differently from what will run.
- **Verify round 6 (L1): an address only the device vouches for is never checked for you.** Round 5 worded it as the device's claim but still checked it — so pressing "Generate a new command" once made it the command's address, and from then on the sheet called it "the address this device connects through" as a fact. The claim now sits on its own row, unchecked ("VibeSpace did not offer it, so it is not checked: choose it only if it is yours"); the command's own address stays checked.
- **Verify round 6 (B1, B2): the agent browser's confirmation card shows what the action acts on, and Confirm runs only that; Hand back says how many conversations it wakes.** A confirmation card could be repainted by a later record (a forged "click" over a pending file upload, then Confirm confirmed the upload); it now names the file, URL or script, keeps the first version it showed, and a Confirm runs only for the card it was pressed on. The live view's Hand back button now reads "Hand back (wakes N)" when it also wakes other conversations sharing the browser (N billed turns), and it never wakes a different number than it showed.
- **Verify round 6 (K1–K5): a permission card shows everything Allow will run, and Allow runs exactly the agent's request.** A helper's card showed only the first line of its command (a second line piping a download into a shell was hidden); the plain-words summary of VibeSpace's own tools skipped extra commands that write files or read secrets; Always Allow did not say it would also change the permission mode or add folders; and the server took the command from the browser rather than from the agent's own request. Each is fixed: the whole command is shown (every line) above Allow, the summary names every extra command and the full line is always shown under it, Always Allow lists everything it changes, and hidden characters are drawn as marked codes with Allow then needing a second press.
- **Verify round 6 (O1–O5): an outgoing message you approve is the one that is sent.** An agent's Lark reply could name a message from ANOTHER chat and land there while the card showed this one — a reply now answers only a message of its own conversation, and the card shows which. Who a Gmail reply goes to is fixed (and shown) when the agent proposes it, not by mail that arrives later. The card shows To, Cc and Subject each on its own line, never cut off. A card that just appeared or moved can't be approved by a stray click for a moment, and approving sends only what the card showed. Invisible characters that reorder text are refused in recipients and subjects and shown as marks in the message.
- **Verify round 6 (V1): an Allow that just slid under your pointer does not count.** In the For-you list, answering one "Allow … to run a command?" request collapses its row and the next request's Allow moves up to where you just clicked; in the For-you window, Allow opens the next request with its Allow in the same place — a double-click allowed a command you never read. An Allow now answers only once it has stayed in place for a moment; an earlier press does nothing and says so.
- **Verify round 6 (R1): "Use a reset credit" spends it only on the limit the dialog showed.** A dialog left open past the limit's own reset used to spend the credit on the brand-new window (it had said nothing would be discarded). Now nothing is spent and the dialog says the limit has reset — open it again to see the account.
- **Verify round 6 (J1): a click on an expired or replaced Background Work panel can no longer answer the job's newer question.** Every panel after the first answered or expired one was numbered 1 again, so pressing "Yes" on an old panel ("Run the unit tests?") answered the new one ("Delete the production backup bucket?"). Panels now keep their own number, and an answer for another panel is refused ("nothing was recorded") while the form shows the panel the job waits on now.
- **Verify round 6 (W1): a request that changed after you saw it no longer says "you denied it".** When you pressed Allow on a run-a-command request whose command had changed, nothing ran — but the chat card said you denied it and the agent was told you had not allowed it. Both now say the request changed after it was shown, and the agent is told to ask again.
- **Verify round 6 (Z2): one rule for characters you cannot see, everywhere a request is approved.** The run-a-command request, outgoing messages, permission cards and the agent browser's confirmation card each had their own (different) list of invisible and direction-changing characters; they now share one list, so a character caught on one card is caught on all of them.
- **Verify round 6 (Z1): a command with characters you cannot see is refused, like one with direction marks.** A zero-width space inside a web address (so `example.com<invisible>.evil.io` reads as example.com), a soft hyphen, a byte-order mark or a carriage return made the command shown above Allow differ from the one that would run; the agent is now told to remove them before anything is asked.
- **Verify round 6 (P2, P3): "Pair a device" never replaces a pairing you were not shown.** If another window paired the name you typed, the button turned into "Replace its pairing" once a second — and a click that landed right after the change replaced it; such a press now stops with "… was paired a moment ago". And a pairing sheet whose device was removed meanwhile no longer quietly pairs it again ("… is no longer paired — nothing was created").
- **Verify round 6 (P1): "send the new command to the connected device over its link" either keeps the device or changes nothing.** If the device dropped (or something else dialed in under its name) after you opened its pairing sheet, pressing Generate with that box ticked used to fall back to an ordinary new command — cutting off the device you chose to keep. It now stops with "… is no longer connected — nothing was changed" (or "reconnected after this sheet opened — reopen it"), and nothing is replaced.
- **Verify round 6 (D1): "Stop" on the Public URLs / Tailscale plugin asks what it will stop.** Its confirmation was an empty "Confirm / OK" box — OK stopped every public link of this VibeSpace (or its tailnet) without a word. It now says "Stop Public URLs? — Public URLs from this instance will stop working until you start it again" on a red Stop button, and every confirmation in the app is checked to carry its words.
- **Verify round 6 (S1): Terminate / Force kill in the System panel acts on the machine the process is listed for.** It read the panel's machine only after you confirmed — if the panel switched back to "This machine" meanwhile, the same process number on a different machine received the signal.
- **Verify round 6 (I1): installing xpra or LibreOffice runs exactly the commands the dialog showed.** The dialog showed the commands it would run as root, then re-planned from the machine's current state when you pressed Install — a machine whose package sources changed in between got a different install (a new signing key and package source) that you never saw. If the plan changed, nothing runs now; the dialog shows the new commands and waits for you to press Install again.
- **Verify round 6 (E1): a file you delete in the Files window is the one you saw.** Delete, Overwrite?, Rename, Compress, Extract to Folder and New File / New Folder read the window's current folder and machine only AFTER you confirmed — and another browser tab moving the same window (the layout follows across your devices) while the dialog was open made "Delete build?" delete a "build" in another folder, or on another machine. Each now acts on the folder and machine shown when you started it. Gate: the new approval census (test-approval-census), whose first rule reads every confirm and name dialog in the client for a live read after it.
- PURE `src/dial-facts.js` (the address list, the custom-address verdict, the dial failure classifier, the row state), SHARED `src/sock-path.js` (the socket rung ladder + the witness `state/socket-path`), PURE `src/exit-reach.js` (the two lists, the verdict, the stamp / base, the ask, the words); `src/exit-proxy.js` judges at every call (Task Group membership read live, a pending fork never inherits its parent's grant), asks, audits and cards; the new `dial-status` device op (three-touch, capability-gated); `vibespace-device.js --dial-check`; the dial upgrade answers a refusal with `401` + `X-VibeSpace-Dial-Refusal` + a sentence and a probe with `200` (nothing registered); `cmd-result` carries `timedOut`.
- API: `GET /api/device/dial-addresses`; `POST /api/device/dial-pair {deviceId, base}` (the only minter); `GET /api/hosts/:id/dial-status`; `GET / PATCH /api/hosts/:id/exit-access` (with `base`, 409 on a stale one); `GET /api/exits/audit`, `GET /api/exits/asks`, `POST /api/exits/asks/:askId` (cookie only); `POST /api/hosts/:id/allow-exit` answers 410 (docs/kb-api.md "Exits + pairing").
- Gates: new fast test-dial-facts, test-sock-path (the census of every socket path the tree builds), test-exit-reach (the 84-cell table, the words census, the real manager and routes, seven patched-copy controls); test-exit-proxy re-tiered fast; test-migrations, test-user-todos-layout ⑪, test-peer-delivery, test-principal-picker, test-architecture §66 (no allowExit reader left, one minter, the run bound, row words from the state); new heavy test-device-install-check, test-pair-dialog-ui, test-exit-access-ui; test-agentd-dial gains the real dial gate legs and a 120-byte root.

### Pin a conversation to one account of its pool (the owner, 2026-09-28: "你可以加一个手动overwrite这个会话的池对象选择功能，变成池的子菜单，直接选池本身就是自动切换，如果在子菜单里选"自动"也是自动切换，但如果选择某个具体账号，那在这个账号耗尽之前就pin在这个账号下，刷新后也优先切到这个账号")

- Click the billing chip on a conversation's title bar (or the card's billing entry): the pool it runs on now opens a **submenu** — **Automatic** first, then every account of the pool with its usage and its state in words. Clicking the pool row itself, or Automatic, lets the pool decide as before.
- **Picking an account pins the conversation to it**: it moves there at once (in the middle of a turn too — you chose it), and nothing automatic moves it while that account can serve — not the pool's order, not the soonest-reset rule. When the account runs out (or its login dies, or it is taken out of the pool) the pool's own rules move the conversation elsewhere and say so — "UCI Max is out of quota — running on Martin Max until it resets (pin kept)" — and when the account can serve again the conversation goes back at its next stop ("back on UCI Max (pinned)"), never in the middle of a turn.
- An account that is out of quota is not greyed out: picking it pins now and the conversation moves there when it can. On a pool without hot switching (every ChatGPT pool) the pin applies at the conversation's next restart — it never restarts it by itself. A stopped conversation keeps the pin for when it resumes.
- The pin survives a server restart and a resume; a fork starts unpinned. The chip's tooltip says `(pinned)`; Session Properties says `Pinned to UCI Max (automatic otherwise)`. "Move every conversation here now" leaves pinned conversations where they are.
- **The pool row now names the account THIS conversation runs on** — the same one the title-bar chip shows (before, the menu showed the pool's default account while the chip showed the conversation's own, e.g. "✓ 全部 → UCI Max" beside "全部 → Martin Max"). Where new conversations start is said separately, in words.
- One rule everywhere: **a pinned conversation > the pool's manual priority > automatic**.

### Manual priority replaces switching the whole pool by hand (the owner, 2026-09-28: "手动切换整个池其实比较confusing，我建议移除这个功能，或者做成'手动优先级'这样的概念")

- **What goes.** The pool's `Switch target ▸` menu and the `Auto-switch when nearly exhausted` toggle are gone. A pool you had set to manual keeps its account as #1 of a new order (nothing moves when you update).
- **What comes.** Manage Agents → the pool's ⋯ → **Members & placement…** → Placement: **Automatic** (the pool picks, as before) or **Manual priority** (your order). With Manual priority the top account that can serve takes the pool; when it runs out the next one takes over; when it can serve again the pool goes back to it at once for new conversations, and each running conversation goes back **at its next stop** — never in the middle of a turn (and, unlike the automatic mode, without waiting for its prompt cache to go cold).
- Each account in the list shows its place (`#1`, `#2` …) and what state it is in, in words — usable, out of quota until a time, login expired, not signed in — and nothing is greyed out. Reorder by dragging or with the row's ⋯ (Move to top / up / down).
- **Move every conversation here now** (on #1's ⋯) moves every running conversation of the pool to that account at once — even when it already is the pool's account. On a pool without hot switching it asks first and restarts them.
- The window's billing chip says which rule placed a conversation: `(priority #1)` or `(automatic)`; Session Properties says the same.

### Taking an account out of a pool (the owner, 2026-09-28: "如果用到一半把账号从池里排除，不会第一时间触发切走，比如现在我把martinmax排除池子了你却还在用")

- **What happened.** Removing a member (the pool's Members… dialog, or "Exclude from pool" on the account's own menu) only moved the pool's default — and to the first account in the list, not a chosen one. Every conversation already running on the removed account kept billing it until that account ran out: six conversations stayed on Martin Max after it was excluded.
- **Now.** The moment you save, every conversation still on the removed account moves — including one that is in the middle of a turn — to the member the pool would pick for it (the same rules it uses when an account runs out), and each one tells you: `Pool "全部": Martin Max was removed from the pool — conversation "B2B助手" moved to Fish Max.` (in your language). On a pool without hot switching the conversation is restarted to apply it. The pool's default moves by the same decision, not to the first account in the list.
- **If the server was down when you removed it**, the pool's next check (within 30 seconds) finds any conversation still pointed at an account the pool no longer lists and moves it the same way.
- **If no other member can take the conversations, they stop and wait (the owner's decision, 2026-09-28: "全B"): 移出账号后没有账号能接手的对话会停下等待，有账号可用时自动继续。** A conversation in the middle of a turn finishes that turn (it is never cut off mid-answer), then stops; the account you took out serves nothing after that — subscription or pay-per-use alike. It waits on the pool's account that frees up soonest, and the moment an account can serve it again it continues by itself — one continue, through the same spending limits as any automatic continue. A conversation that was idle simply waits: your next message goes out when an account can serve it. Each conversation tells you so (`Martin Max was removed from the pool and no other member can take over — conversation "B2B助手" stopped after its turn and continues automatically when a member can serve it.`), "For you" says it once, and a new conversation is never started on the account you took out (with no signed-in account left in the pool it is refused with the same sentence). The hourly "keeps running" notice is gone — nothing keeps running.
- Moving a conversation off a removed account never starts a turn by itself.

### An account that signs in (the owner, 2026-09-29: "好")

- **账号登录成功后，池会立刻重新决策一次并读一次用量。** When an account of a pool finishes its login (Add subscription, Re-login, or a ChatGPT device login), VibeSpace reads that account's usage once (the same `/usage` read the ⟳ button does, on the machine that holds the login) and the pool decides again right away — a conversation pinned to that account goes back to it, and a conversation waiting for an account to become usable continues. The journal says `member wake <account> (login)`.
- It happens once per login: the login dialog asks every few seconds while it waits, and a second login of the same account within 5 minutes reads nothing again. An account that is in no pool, or a login that did not finish, triggers nothing. If the usage read does not answer, the pool still decides once, and no conversation is continued because of that account.
- This was written on 2026-09-08 and never switched on: the login routes asked for it and the server never handed it to them. It is now wired, and a test fails if it is ever unwired again.

### Found by the verification round before release (none of it shipped)

- **A pin now survives a resume.** The pin was saved into the conversation's settings, and that store silently dropped it: a stopped conversation you pinned was never pinned (while the toast said "Pinned to … — applies when the conversation resumes"), and a running one lost its pin the next time it was resumed. A ChatGPT conversation on the default ChatGPT pool also lost it at the resume, the one moment its pin can apply. A pin belongs to the pool it was made on: switching the conversation to another pool does not carry it along.
- **A pinned conversation no longer bounces.** While its account's reading wobbled around "out of quota", a pinned conversation was moved away and back on every check (12 of 12) — each move re-sends the whole conversation. The return now waits the same 3 minutes every voluntary move waits. And when the account a pinned conversation is running on meanwhile runs out, it moves at once — in the middle of a turn too — like every other conversation (it used to wait for the turn to end, or, on a pool without hot switching, never moved).
- **"Move every conversation here now" checks the account first.** On an account that is out of quota it moved everything there and the pool moved everything back half a minute later. Now it says `UCI Max: out of quota until Tue 14:00 — nothing was moved`, moves only the conversations the account can serve, and its message says how many moved, how many stayed on their own pin and how many it could not take. On a pool without hot switching the question names how many conversations restart.
- **Taking an account out of a pool that restarts to switch** no longer restarts conversations it has nothing to do with: only the ones that were running on that account move. When no other account can take them they stop after their current turn and wait (see above; a ChatGPT conversation, which holds its account for life, is restarted onto the account that frees up soonest once its turn is over), and the message you get when you remove the account says so.
- The chip's tooltip says `pinned to Fish Max, running here for now` while a pinned conversation runs on another account (it said `→ UCI Max (pinned)`); a pin on a signed-out account says the account cannot sign in.
- **When you take an account out of a pool and no other account can take over,** new conversations now start on the pool's account that frees up soonest — never on the account you took out (that happened when the removal was picked up after a restart) and never simply on the first account in the list. The conversations already running on it stop after their current turn and wait (see above).
- **Deleting an account** moves each of its pool conversations to where the pool would place that conversation (a pinned one to its pin), instead of putting all of them on one account and moving them again half a minute later.
- **A pin survives a resume even while its account is out of the pool** — it waits, exactly as it does for a running conversation, and applies again when you add the account back.
- A pinned conversation is no longer told its account is "out of quota" when that account merely has not recovered enough yet ("Fish Max has not got enough quota back yet — running on UCI Max for now"), and never "Fish Max is out of quota — running on Fish Max" when the pool put it back on its pin ("is back on Fish Max (pinned)").

### Browse yourself (the owner, 2026-09-28: "我能自己打开一个浏览器profile用它浏览吗")

- **Where.** Every profile on this computer has **Browse yourself** as the first button of its row in the Agent browser panel. When the profile's browser is not running, the "which browser does my agent use" dialog also offers **Open it yourself** — the way to get past a site's check that blocks your agent.
- **What you get.** The profile's browser starts (or, when it runs, you join it) with its logins, and a window opens on **your own tab** with an address bar: Back, Forward, Reload and the address. Only web addresses are opened. Pages your tab opens (a login popup) are in the Tabs list; click one to go to it.
- **Your agents keep working.** Nothing is paused, interrupted or announced: each conversation stays on its own tab. Taking over an agent's tab from its live view still works as before (the agent is interrupted, told, and reminded when you hand back).
- **Recorded like an agent's.** Your clicks, keys, scrolls and typing (kept as a length, never the words) are recorded with before-and-after pictures, and your browsing appears in the Sessions list as "You · 14:02 · 4 min" with Replay. Turn off **Also record my own actions** on the profile's row to keep only when you started and stopped.
- **Two ways to finish.** **Close** closes your tab and window; the browser keeps running for your agents and closes by itself once nobody uses it. **Quit the whole browser** stops it for everyone — the confirmation names the conversations that lose their pages, and each one's next command opens the browser again with a new tab.
- **Walking away.** If you close the window without Close, or your connection drops, your tab is kept: 12 hours when you started the browser (Settings → Agent browser → "Keep your own browsing tab after its window closes"), 10 minutes when you joined a browser an agent started. The row then says **Open your browsing window**. A server restart ends it.
- **Several windows or devices.** A second window of yours (another tab, the phone) watches until you press **Continue here**. On a phone or tablet, a **Keyboard** button brings up the keyboard.
- **Not yet:** profiles saved on a paired machine, a conversation's own temporary browser, and browsers VibeSpace only connects to have no Browse yourself button.

### Fixed

- After a profile's browser was stopped (its Stop button, or Quit the whole browser), a conversation that used it answered "bound tab is gone" to its next browser command. The conversation's next command now opens a new tab first — on a "separate tabs" profile too.

### Checked before release (adversarial verify, round 1)

- **Your tabs are yours, theirs are theirs.** The Tabs list of your browsing window shows every tab of the browser; clicking a conversation's tab now says it is that conversation's (take over from its live view to use it) instead of moving your window onto it, and **Close** closes only your tab and the pages your tab opened — never a conversation's page.
- **A restart keeps your browsing.** A VibeSpace restart (an update) no longer stops the browser you were using: your tab is kept for the same 12 hours / 10 minutes, the row offers Continue, and your window picks it up again.
- **Delete… while you browse** a profile says so and asks you to Close (or Quit) first, instead of closing your page.
- **What is recorded:** a password inside an address (`https://name:password@…`) is never kept in the recorded actions, and characters you type with AltGr or Option are kept as a length like any other typing.
- **Your agents cannot see that you are browsing** (nothing in any answer to them changes while you browse) and an agent's token cannot open, drive, end or read your browsing.

### Checked before release (adversarial verify, round 2)

- **If the browser crashes while you browse it**, VibeSpace starts it again; your window now says your page went with it and offers Browse again (before, the window stayed on a page that no longer existed, every address you typed failed and Browse yourself only brought that window back).
- **What is recorded:** a sign-in code, token, key or signature in an address (`?code=`, `?token=`, `#access_token=`, a signed download link) is no longer kept in the recorded actions — the recorded address keeps its site and path and says `?«cut»` — for your browsing and your agents' alike.
- **A page a finished conversation left open is yours to use.** When no conversation is using the browser, clicking such a tab in your Tabs list switches to it (it becomes yours, and Close closes it); if that conversation comes back, it opens a new tab of its own.
- **A conversation's Stop can no longer close the browser you are browsing.** The Stop list in a conversation's browser window now says you are browsing it yourself; only Quit the whole browser (in your window) or Stop on its row in the Agent browser panel end it.
- **On a profile whose tabs your agents share, your browsing window tells you** in one line at its top: "Agents on this profile can also see and drive this tab". A "separate tabs" profile shows nothing.

### Checked before release (adversarial verify, round 3)

- **A page you took over stays yours when its conversation comes back.** If a conversation had detached from the browser (or a helper of it had finished) and you took the page it left open, that conversation's next command could land in your page when it came back; it now opens a new tab of its own (and if that tab cannot be opened, its command is refused instead of running in your page).
- **After a browser you started crashes and restarts**, Browse again keeps your page for the same 12 hours while you are away (it had dropped to 10 minutes, as for a browser an agent started).
- **What is recorded:** a sign-in link carried inside another address (an email's tracked link, a sign-in page's "continue to" address) is cut from the recorded actions like one typed directly; the page you open is unchanged.

### Checked before release (adversarial verify, round 4)

- **The same holds after many conversations used the browser.** VibeSpace remembers the pages up to 64 conversations left open on one browser; the 65th used to make it forget the oldest silently, and that conversation could come back into a page you had taken. A forgotten conversation now opens a new tab of its own when it comes back.
- **Taking a page at the moment its conversation comes back.** If you clicked a page a conversation had left open in the same instant that conversation sent its next command, the command could run in the page you were taking; the conversation now opens a new tab of its own.

### A page dialog is a fact the agent is told (userW: "jarvis-work 卡死"; the owner: "让agent知道这个对话框的存在和交互能力")

- **What went wrong.** A page with unsaved input (a mail draft) answers a navigation with the browser's "Leave site? Changes you made may not be saved." dialog. Until now the agent's command waited 30 seconds and failed with no word of the dialog, every command after it did the same, the live view froze, and nothing offered the two answers that fix it. Measured on agent-browser 0.38.1: in the configuration VibeSpace used, that dialog was usually accepted silently instead — the draft was lost without a word.
- **Now.** A command that runs into a dialog ends at once with `[dialog_open]` and its first line says what the page asks and how to answer: `vibespace-browser dialog accept [text]` or `vibespace-browser dialog dismiss` (for a "Leave site?" dialog, accept leaves the page and loses what was typed; dismiss stays). Every later command says the same until it is answered, and `snapshot` / `get url` lead with it. A plain alert is accepted for the agent and mentioned in its next result.
- **The live view** shows the dialog above the page with its own buttons (Leave page / Stay on page, OK / Cancel, a text box for a prompt); your answer is told to the agent on its next command.
- **A dialog that opens while the agent is idle** reaches it as one note with your next message — no extra turn is started for it.
- **A page that stops responding** (three commands in a row ran into the timeout, or the tab does not answer at all) shows "page not responding" on the browser chip and a Restart button in the live view. Restart is always your click, never automatic.
- **When it applies.** Dialogs are held for a decision from each browser's next start; a browser that is already running when you update keeps its old behaviour until it restarts (it is not restarted for you), the agent is told when such a browser accepted a "Leave site?" dialog by itself, and its row in the Agent browser panel says so and offers **Restart to hold dialogs**.
- **A slow or endlessly navigating page** is told to the agent as loading (how long, how many navigations started), never branded hung; after 2 minutes of it the timeouts count toward "page not responding".
- The dialog's words the agent reads are exactly what you see: characters that render as nothing (zero-width, direction controls, hidden "tag" text) are removed, VibeSpace's own markers are neutralised, and the text is quoted as the page's own words.
- Agent manual: a new "Page dialogs" section (`vibespace-docs browser`); the session's tools intro gains one line.

### Typing into the chat while you drive the browser (userW inc-mum339id-1zsb: "PC web端 takeover browser后无法在session窗口里输入")

- **What went wrong.** With the chat and its agent's browser side by side, after Take over every click into the chat's text box was undone at once: the keyboard went straight back to the browser, so what the user typed went into the web page instead of the chat, and nothing said why. The rule behind it (2.369.180) protects you while you type into the page: if the app moves the cursor into the chat box by itself — a window re-attaching, a reconnect, a message arriving — the keyboard is taken back, so a password you are typing never ends up in the chat, one Enter from being sent to the agent. It treated your own click on the chat box the same way.
- **Now.** A click (or a tap) of yours on a text box outside the browser view — the chat box, a terminal — gives the keyboard to that box. The takeover does not end: you still drive the browser, the agent's commands are still refused, and Enter sends your chat message as usual. A click on the browser picture (or anywhere in the browser view) gives the keyboard back to the page. The view's bar says "Keyboard is in the chat box — click the picture to keep using the page" (键盘在对话框 — 点画面继续操作网页), and a line above the chat box says "You are typing to the agent (you still drive the browser)" (你在给 agent 打字（浏览器仍由你接管）).
- **The password protection stays.** Only your own click on that very box counts — a cursor the app moves by itself, a click elsewhere followed by the app focusing the chat box, or a click that is not a real one is still taken back to the page, without a message (the old message told you to Hand back, which you no longer need to).
- Two browsers driven at once: one click in the chat box gives it the keyboard from both; a click on either picture gives the keys to that browser.
- Checked adversarially before release: a click on the browser's own tab, title bar or taskbar button also takes the keyboard back to the page (before, the next keys still went into the chat box); a key you were holding in the page when you clicked the chat box is let go in the page (it stayed held down there); clicking a chat box that already shows the cursor gives it the keyboard too; the bar's "Keyboard is in the chat box" note is readable on the light theme.
- Checked again (round 2): with the browser window minimized (or on another desktop, or its stream reconnecting), a click in the chat box now gives it the keyboard too — when the browser comes back your typing stays in the chat box and both sides say so at once; if the app itself had put the cursor in the chat box meanwhile, the browser takes the cursor back the moment it returns (before, it took only the keys, silently, and what you typed next for the chat went into the page). If the chat box you clicked is on another desktop, coming back to the browser's desktop gives the keyboard back to the page (before, your typing went nowhere while the bar still said the keyboard was in the chat box). A key you are holding down when the browser window is minimized, or when you press Hand back, is now let go in the page (it stayed held down there). The same now holds for a desktop app and the Desktop: a click on its picture while you drive gives it your keyboard (before, what you typed there went into the agent's page). A button that puts the cursor in a text box (the chat box's expand button) still leaves your keys with the browser — so the app cannot hand them to the chat box by itself — but now says so once: "Typing still goes to the browser — click the text box itself to type there". A click into a page shown inside another window (a web view, a plugin) cannot take the keyboard from the browser you drive — the app cannot tell your click there from that page's own script — and now says so: "Typing still goes to the browser — to type in another page, hand back first". The live view's "You are driving" badge, its Hand back button and its keyboard chip are readable on every theme (on the light theme they were faint yellow on white).
- Checked a third time (every place in the app that takes keys, one by one): while you drive, a dropdown of the app (the editor's language, a setting, a dialog's choice) stays open under your click — before, it closed at once and could not be used. A click in the code editor, a channel's message box, the For-you reply box, a settings field or a dialog's text box gives it your keyboard like the chat box. "Copy Path" and the other copy commands no longer show a message about a text box. A dialog you open while you drive (Delete's "are you sure") now says your Enter still goes to the browser — click its buttons to answer it. After you click the chat's messages (not its text box) the browser view says your keys are in no text box, instead of "in the chat box". A list you click (the file explorer's, the For-you list) does not take the keyboard while you drive — its keys stay the browser's.

### A browser that asks for a window, on a machine with no desktop session (2026-09-28: the dev box sat at the login screen after a reboot, and every agent browser failed to start)

- **Why it failed.** Your `~/.agent-browser/config.json` asks for a visible window on Wayland (`headed: true`, `--ozone-platform=wayland`). After the reboot nobody was logged in, so there was no desktop for the window — Chrome stopped with "The platform failed to initialize", and every agent browser command answered "the browser did not start".
- **Now.** A window is a preference; whether the machine has a desktop is checked each time a browser starts, on the machine where it runs. With no desktop session the browser starts anyway, instead of failing:
  - **in a hidden window** when Xvfb is installed on that machine — a normal browser on an invisible screen, so sign-in pages see an ordinary Chrome (they often turn away a headless one);
  - **headless** (no screen at all) when it is not, or when you choose "Always headless" in Settings → Agent browser → "When this machine has no desktop session".
  Either way pages work the same, and you can watch it and take it over in its live view. Your config file is never changed; VibeSpace starts the browser with a copy that leaves out the window and the Wayland setting, and uses that copy for every command on that browser so it is never restarted back into the failure.
- **It says so.** The Agent browser panel's row, the "which browser" dialog and the live view say "This machine has no desktop session — the browser runs in a hidden window" (or "— runs headless") "(the live view can still take over)"; the agent's command that started it prints a one-line note; Settings → Agent browser shows, under "Show the agent browser window", what this machine has right now (a Wayland desktop, an X11 display, or none), what a browser will do there, and "Xvfb: installed / not installed".
- **When you log in again** the next browser that starts is a window again (no restart of VibeSpace needed), and its row says the desktop is back. A config that pins a display this machine does not have while it has another (Wayland asked, only X11 here) runs on the one it has.
- Measured on agent-browser 0.38.1 + Chrome 154: headless starts fine with the Wayland setting left in, but it is dropped anyway so the config never names a display that is not there. The hidden window needs two more adjustments, also measured: it is told to draw on X11 (a machine that says its sessions are Wayland would otherwise make Chrome look for Wayland), and a leftover DISPLAY from an old session is cleared for that launch (otherwise the invisible screen is never started).

### CloakBrowser, measured before it is offered (the owner: 「下载吧」)

- **What was measured.** CloakBrowser 0.5.10 (the free build, Chromium 146 for Linux) was downloaded once on the VibeSpace machine and every connection it made was recorded: the download itself, a second start, a start with a (fake) key present, and ten minutes of doing nothing.
- **What it connects to.** The one-time download (about 217 MB) comes from cloakbrowser.dev, which hands the file over from GitHub's download storage (github.com and release-assets.githubusercontent.com). The download is checked on your machine against a signature built into the installer, then against the file's checksum. **The browser itself connected to nothing on the internet** — not when it started, not with a key present, not after ten idle minutes. The installer would normally check GitHub every hour and quietly download newer versions; VibeSpace turns that off and keeps the exact version it tested.
- **What the free version needs.** No account, no sign-in, no key. A key only matters for the maker's newer version (Chromium 151), which you get by signing in with GitHub and which checks the key with the maker each time it starts — VibeSpace does not install that one, because it was not tested. The key card under Integrations now says this; it used to say CloakBrowser could only be used with a key.

### Installing it

- **Manage agents → CloakBrowser → Install…** (and "Download and install…" in a profile's browser dialog) now works. The confirmation says what happens: about 217 MB from cloakbrowser.dev, about 729 MB on disk, checked to be the exact copy VibeSpace tested, no account or key needed.
- The download can only reach those three download addresses — anything else it tries (such as the update check) is refused. After the download, VibeSpace checks the browser file is byte-for-byte the tested one; if it is not, it is not used and the install says so.
- VibeSpace only installs it on Linux computers (the only kind it was tested on); elsewhere the row says VibeSpace can't install it there.

### Using it

- In a profile's browser dialog you can switch between Chromium and CloakBrowser (and back). The profile keeps its saved logins; sites may ask you to sign in once more because the browser looks like a new device to them.
- **A CloakBrowser browser only reaches the sites you list** in Settings → Agent browser → "Sites CloakBrowser may open". With no site listed it opens nothing, and the dialog tells you so before you switch. A site that is not listed shows "egress refused: … is not in the egress allowlist" (http) or does not open (https); your agent is told to ask you to add the site rather than retry.
- Fixed along the way (found by trying the switch on the real browsers): right after a switch the browser was restarted without its settings, and after switching back every conversation using the profile lost its tab until it opened a new one. Both are fixed.

### 群里发给另一个 agent 的消息，现在在它的对话里能看到 (the owner, 2026-09-28: "怎么在那个对话里看不到你发了消息？")
- A message an agent sends into a group without `--wake` reaches the other members with their next turn. Until now the agent read it and nothing in its conversation showed it. Now, **before** that turn, the strip above the member's composer says it is waiting ("1 notice is waiting for this agent's next turn: a group message from alpha"; the sidebar card says "1 waiting"). A hand-over never carries a group message, so when group messages are all that is waiting there is no "Hand over now" button, only the sentence "they ride your next message".
- **When** the turn takes it, the conversation shows one card per message: "alpha → <group>", the message's words, right under your own message. A message the agent saw cut short says so, and a report that could not show every message says "… and N more (vibespace-msg read <group>)". Click the group's name to open the group. A message that woke the agent (`--wake`, an @mention) shows the same card. Each message is shown once, and the cards are still there after a restart.
- Fixed at the same time: when a message woke an agent, the agent's turn could also be handed that message a second time as part of its group report. The woken turn is now marked as not typed by you before the message is posted, not after.
- "Card kinds that collapse" gains **Group messages** (off by default).

### What waits for an agent, and what was handed over, can now be read (the owner, 2026-09-28: "现在是完全看不了这个细节了嘛？包括在聊天框里 queue 的时候也没法展开看细节")
- The strip above a conversation's composer ("2 notices are waiting for this agent's next turn") now has a **Details** button: one line per waiting notice — a channel receipt, a job result named by its job, a message from a named agent — with the first line of its text; at most 12 are listed and the rest is counted ("2 more are waiting, not previewed"). The list stays open while the facts change under it, and every line is text (a peer's markup stays words).
- The card VibeSpace posts after **Hand over now** used to say only "2 waiting notice(s) handed over". Its title is that sentence in your language, and the notices it delivered sit behind "Show the 2 notices".
- Under the hood: the `stash` session fact carries `previews` + `previewsHeld` (PURE src/stash-summary.js), the hand-over's card text opens with its own head line and `handoverFacts` reads it back for the card (`noticeCardView` honours a fact's body and expander label). Gates: test-stash-strip ①d + ④ (incl. a control without the facts), test-chat-hygiene.

### The window that disappeared (userW, 2026-09-28: "在 Dynamic Desktop 里面用这个Browser，Browser 拖不出来"; the owner: "他那个拖动出标签栏了，然后窗口就消失了")

- **What happened.** On the Stage the agent's browser sat in one tab group with its chat. He pulled the browser's tab out of the bar — and the window was gone. Its taskbar button was there; clicking it (he did, five times) showed nothing; only putting the browser back beside the chat from the window menu brought it back.
- **Why.** When the agent starts its browser while the Stage is not on screen, the live view opens inside the chat's tab group anyway. Leaving the Stage hides every Stage window, and coming back showed only the chat and the windows the Stage had recorded for it — not this tab, which the Stage had never recorded. A tab is drawn by its group's window, so the leftover "hidden" mark on the tab's own window did not matter — until the tab was pulled out and became a window of its own, still marked hidden.
- **Now.** Coming back to the Stage shows the chat's whole tab group; a window pulled out of a group takes on the group's visibility (never an old hidden mark); and on the Stage the pulled-out window joins that chat's workspace, so it comes back with the chat every time. Reproduced on 2.369.196 by replaying the report's own record (the tab pressed at (1246, 104), let go at (795, 455), on his screen size and UI scale); fixed in the same replay.

### Pulling a tab out of its group sideways

- **What happened.** On the Stage the agent's browser sat beside its chat in one tab group. Pulling the browser's tab toward the empty workspace did nothing: the tab stayed in the group. The report's own record shows the pull — from the tab (1246, 104) to the workspace (795, 455) — which is more sideways than downward.
- **Why.** Since split tabs v2 (2.369.182) a tab drag decided once, on its first 8 px, whether it was a reorder inside the strip (mostly sideways) or a pull out (mostly down), and a reorder stayed a reorder for the whole drag. So a diagonal pull out of the bar — the natural way to drag a tab to the middle of the screen — was a reorder, and the tab never left. It was not the Stage: the same pull on any desktop did the same (reproduced in both).
- **Now.** A sideways drag still reorders the tabs while the pointer stays near the tab bar; once the pointer is more than 30 px above or below the bar, the tab tears off and follows the pointer as its own window (the way browsers do it). A reorder that wobbles a little below the bar stays a reorder. On the Stage the torn-off window stays on the Stage, in the conversation's workspace, and stays apart through the workspace record, another device's update and a leave / re-enter of the Stage.

### A drop the Stage refuses is said (the owner's rule stays: windows never move between the Stage and a normal desktop)

- Dragging a Stage window by its title bar onto a desktop preview used to show nothing and the drop did nothing. Now the preview is outlined as refused, a short line beside the pointer says "Windows on the Stage stay on the Stage" (for the conversation: "The conversation stays on the Stage"), and the drop puts the window back where the drag began with a message saying what to do instead. The other way round — a desktop window dragged onto the Stage preview — says "Windows can't be moved onto the Stage".
- The window menu's "Move to Desktop ▸" on a Stage window holds one line saying why, instead of desktop names that did nothing. A taskbar button dropped on a preview and the command-mode keys say the same.

### Files saved from a preview are named (userW, 2026-09-28: "我从vibespace预览里下载文件，文件名都叫raw")

- **Before.** Right-click a picture in the file viewer or in the chat and choose "Save image as…", press the PDF viewer's own download button, save a video, or drag a picture out of the chat: the file was called `raw` (`raw.png`, `raw.pdf`). Only the Download button in the toolbar and Download in the file list's right-click menu gave the real name.
- **Now.** Each of those saves the file under its own name — `photo.png`, `截图 2026-09-28.png`, `季度报告 (终稿).pdf` — for a file on this machine and for one on a remote machine alike. A preview stays a preview: opening a PDF still shows it, it never starts a download.
- Nothing else about previews changed: a video still seeks and a missing file is still "not found".
- **Download and Download as Zip of a file or folder with a Chinese name on a remote machine now work.** Before, the download never started — the tab just kept loading. Both now save under the file's own name, like on this machine.
- **The code editor's Download button on a file from a remote machine downloads that file.** Before, it asked this machine for a file at the same path — usually "not found", or a different file that happened to be there.
- **A file that is missing on a remote machine now says "not found"** in the viewer and on Download, as it does on this machine. Before, the preview was blank and Download saved an empty file under the name. Stopping a remote video or download part-way also stops the transfer on that machine instead of leaving it hanging.
- **Files whose name starts with a dot** (`.env`, `.hidden.png`) can be previewed and downloaded; before, both said "not found".

### The agent browser's identity, a fourth time (identity round 4, 2026-09-28 — after 2.369.196's "Who can use it")

- **Leaving a Task Group takes the profile away at once** (identity round 4 — until then it took effect at the conversation's next browser command). A conversation that leaves the Task Group a profile is kept to loses it the moment the group changes: its tab in that browser closes, a mediated connection is cut, and its next command is refused (the refusal says so). Narrowing the list closes the tabs of every conversation it leaves out; if the Task Group list cannot be read at that moment, nobody is cut off and the command says to run it again.
- **Verified a fourth time (2026-09-28, identity round 4 — CLOSURE: what lies OUTSIDE round 3's census and belt — the chat cards and notices, the websocket, the CDP mediator, time and order, the belt's own edges).** (1) **One conversation could freeze every other conversation's — and the user's — new tab in a shared browser through the mediating proxy.** Measured on Chrome 153: a browser-level `Target.setAutoAttach {waitForDebuggerOnStart:true}` from one CDP client pauses ANOTHER client's new tab at its first navigation (`Runtime.evaluate` still answers; `Page.navigate` never returns) until the arming client resumes it — and the proxy DROPS that `attachedToTarget` for a target the lease does not own, so a lease that armed it could never resume what it froze; the census classed the method `session` (scoping only), and scoping does not see a side effect Chrome applies browser-wide. The judge now refuses the browser-level pause by name (`auto_attach_pause_refused`, the way out in its words); the page-level form — what the real 0.38.1 daemon sends, tapped through a logging proxy — and the no-pause form pass; `autoAttachRelated` with the pause needs its target in scope. Gate: test-browser-mediation ②r4 (the PURE table, the real proxy over the fake upstream — the browser never sees the call — and a control copy without the rule, which forwards it). (2) **A new conversation could BE a stopped one to the browser subsystem.** The browser key is `bk-` + 8 hex digits (32 bits) and every authority hangs on it — "Who can use it" rows, leases, pins, caps, the `told` memory, child handles, claims, the bindings, the trace, the env directory — yet it was the only id minted with no uniqueness check (the profile id, the grant token and the claim id each loop), and nothing ever retires a stopped conversation's list row while its binding is pruned past 4096. Reproduced: a conversation attached to a kept profile with an alias and a pin, then stopped; a new conversation minted with the same 8 digits answered `status` with the old one's attachments and alias and resolved `open` on the kept profile — its first bare command would have landed in the stranger's logged-in browser. Now ws-create's one mint goes through the fresh-key rule: a key the keeper's registry, the env's bindings / directory / session meta, or a live session still names is never minted again (a check that cannot read says so and mints unchecked; an exhausted loop is said by name, never a refused create). Gate: test-browser-identity-census ⑥ (each named place on both sides, the PURE loop, the one-mint-site census + controls (l) / (l′)). (3) **A conversation removed from a Task Group kept the profile's browser until IT chose to send a command.** "Leaving a Task Group takes effect at the next browser command" was the documented rule, and for the CLI rung it held; but a mediated lease's grant stood with the lease, and the mediated url is in the env the agent's daemon holds — a raw CDP client on it (reproduced on the real keeper + mediator over a fake browser) went on reading and driving the kept profile after the user took the conversation out of the group, for as long as the agent sent no verb. Now a Task Group change is judged like a narrowing of the list: the task store's one change hook re-judges every lease admitted through a Task Group at once — the tab closes, the grant is revoked (its connections close `lease_gone`), the next verb says `profile_changed`; a stopped member and an unreadable store stay undecided and kept, silently. Gate: test-browser-identity-census ⑦ (+ controls (m) server.js without the hook, (m′) a keeper copy that never walks a task-row list). (4, LOW, hardened) **The belt's own edges:** its key pattern had word boundaries and a case, so `trace_bk-…`, `xbk-…`, `bk-…f` and `BK-…` would have passed (no product spelling composes a key that way — the belt is the last line for a route written raw tomorrow); an object KEY was never judged; a string of 64 KiB or more was returned raw; a subtree deeper than 24 was returned raw. Now every key-shaped run is masked whatever surrounds it, object keys are judged (two masking alike are told apart), every string is judged whatever its length, and a too-deep subtree is dropped — and the census walk reads object keys too. **Judged and left (LOW / by design):** with sign-in OFF every `/api/browser/*` cookie route — the whole raw registry, every conversation's key, list, lease, pin and pid — is open to any process on the machine or the LAN, the agent's shell included, exactly like every other route of the product (the belt guards the agent-labelled routes; sign-in is the instance's one wall); an agent's own browser navigating to this instance's origin sees the sign-in page unless the user signed in inside that profile browser themselves (the CLI allows `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` by design; sign-in is by cookie only); a same-user process can read the registry, the bindings and the session meta off the disk and can find any profile browser's raw loopback CDP port (§6.1: "CDP is unauthenticated by design … binds loopback") — the design's stated trust level, not a product surface; co-admitted conversations on a shared profile share its cookies, download policy and permissions (a shared profile is shared state); `profile_locked` still names the pid of a Chrome holding a directory the asker is admitted to (round 3's LOW 5).

### Chrome 154 (lane cdp-154)

- Chrome 154.0.8037.57 reached this box: its four new CDP methods have census rows (the two browser-wide setters, `Browser.addMockCamera` / `Browser.setGlobalPrivacyControl`, refused while a lease holds the browser — measured with two browser contexts), the seven it dropped keep theirs marked `until`, and the census reads both Chromes; test-browser-mediation-chrome compares the launched Chrome at its own version. Gate: test-cdp-census (new, fast).

### Integration (2.369.197 — the lanes above composed onto 2.369.196)

- **One browser-key mint.** The fresh-key rule (a key any store still names is never minted again) lives in src/server/browser-key.js `mintKey`, so the spawn AND a live session's first browser use go through it (round 4 had put it in a ws-create-local mint the late key never used). Gates: test-browser-identity-census ⑥ (re-pinned + a runtime leg), test-browser-share-model ③e.
- **The channel reply path keeps both designs**: the stored reply anchor and envelope (pairing's "what you approve is what runs") AND the placement / reactions (threads) — at propose, approve, send and reconcile; the approval card shows the hidden-character marks and ONE quote of the answered message (the anchor row; the placement line says only where it lands), and its digest now covers the placement and a reaction.
- **The agent's copy of a channel record** passes the read-time view (a bot's name, markup read) and then the frame rule and the name door on the way out, and never carries a mail's formatted body; the app names, a mention's name inside a Lark card and a held body's file name pass the name door.
- **"Clear content…" reaches every new copy**: a group message's report card re-words, a cleared entry's preview in the waiting strip says it in the device's language, an error no longer quotes a For-you item's words, and the thread index and a reply's anchor read only a known conversation's log.
- **The browser lanes together**: one agent-token guard on the human browser routes; Restart refuses while you browse the profile yourself (`browsing_yourself`) and a dialog on your own tab is never told to an agent; the switch dialog shows both the CloakBrowser install card and "Open it yourself"; the belt masks your own browsing key like an agent's; the keeper launches with the provider's and the display's environment together.
- **The full heavy tier on the composed tree** (199 suites, 2 lanes, 5388 s; 14 red on the first run, every one root-caused, none "passed on retry"): eleven were suites that had not yet seen another lane's change — the placement words, the `direct` tag, a reaction's emoji as content, the name door on a file name, the threads migration and the reaction strip under every message, the pairing address, the installer tokens, the keyless CloakBrowser, the group card's head, the ephemeral launch line, the pool pin's payload key, a daemon install a control only got by accident; one was a real regression — the waiting strip took two lines on a phone once it wrapped for its Details list (the text now yields); and four came from this machine moving to Chrome 154 and xpra 6.5.4 on 2026-09-28 (the .196 tree fails the same way here): Chrome's caption layout and xpra's keymap handling are measured rows now, **Chrome 154 is readable by an agent only with an accessibility setting in its environment** (VibeSpace now gives it to the Chrome it starts), and **xpra 6.5.4 left an app unpainted after a minimize and a resize** (the desktop-app window now asks xpra to repaint, as xpra's own web client does).
- **The first push of this version was refused by its own gate**, and rightly: the socket-path census (test-sock-path, lane-pairing) walked `data/bin` on disk, and the production checkout's `data/bin` also holds what the server copies there at boot (`vibespace-browser-verbs.js`) and what a mount installed (`rclone`) — two "producers" no lane worktree ever had. The census now reads the tracked files (`git ls-files`), the tree git ships, never a directory walk; a census over the checkout is a census over one machine.
- **Numbering**: the design's §27 (rich messages), §28 (threads and reactions), §29 (the Lark search); test-architecture §64/§65 (reactions, the access gate), §66 (pairing).

## 2.369.196 — while you drive the agent's browser, pasted text and the Chinese input method now reach the page, a Mac's ⌘ keys work as the editing keys and text you copy in the page lands in your own clipboard; the "which browser does my agent use" dialog is rebuilt in plain words — it names the browser, offers a switch only when one is possible, and says each next step as one sentence and one button that works; a browser profile can be given to several conversations and Task Groups at once, picked from a searchable list; each run of an agent's browser shows where it started and ended — in the chat and in the live view — with a replay you can step through, and the browser's records are kept by size (1 GB per profile) instead of for 7 days

### Typing text into the agent's browser (the owner, 2026-09-27: "我似乎无法从外面复制文本进入那个浏览器", "中文输入法也不 work")

- **Why it failed.** The browser refuses a typed "character" event that carries four or more characters — measured on the Chromium the agent runs (151) and on Chrome 153 — and the agent-browser stream swallowed the refusal. Every paste of four characters or more, and every word of four or more characters from an input method (most Chinese phrases, two emoji), disappeared at the last step while the bar said the input was sent. Short pastes (up to three characters) and ordinary typing always worked, which is why it looked random.
- **Now.** A paste or an input-method commit is sent as one piece of text; the server cuts it into pieces the browser accepts and sends them in order with the keys and clicks around it, so a paste never lands before the click that chose the field. Line breaks and tabs are kept (the browser drops a piece that starts with a tab, and a line break sent alone — the cutting follows those measured rules). Up to 20 000 characters per paste, as before; a very long paste takes a few seconds. One receipt answers the whole paste; if the browser refuses part of it, the bar says how many characters got in. On a browser shared through the credit fence, the pieces are paced so none is dropped.
- **The key that ends an input-method word** (Enter or Space) no longer reaches the page as a stray key release; a key only releases on the page if it was pressed there.
- **After you click the bar or an empty area** of the live view, the keyboard goes back to the browser at once, so the input method starts with your first key.

### A Mac's keys on the agent's Linux browser

- ⌘A / ⌘C / ⌘X / ⌘V / ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z act as select all / copy / cut / paste / undo / redo. Before, the Linux browser TYPED the letter ("a", "c", "x", "z"). ⌘←/→ go to the start / end of the line, ⌥←/→ jump by word (instead of Back / Forward), ⌥⌫ deletes a word, and characters typed with ⌥ (™, é) are typed as characters. A Mac browser, and a Windows or Linux viewer, are unchanged.

### Copying out of the agent's browser

- Select text in the page (a drag and a double or triple click now select — before, the drag moved nothing and a double click was two single clicks) and press Ctrl+C / ⌘C (or cut): the text lands in YOUR clipboard. The page still gets the key, so a web terminal's Ctrl+C still interrupts. On a page served over plain http the copy happens within the key press itself; if the browser does not allow it, a "Copied in the page — click to copy" chip appears on the bar and one click copies. A page's own "Copy" button, clicked, shows that chip too. A password field is never read. Nothing selected, or text in an embedded frame from another site, is said on the bar instead of doing nothing.
- **Only your own copy key puts text on your clipboard (security verify).** Before this round, any text the page copied while you drove was written to your clipboard — on an https instance with nothing pressed at all, on plain http within five seconds of any click. A page's own script (or one the agent had planted with `eval` before you took over) could therefore put its text on your clipboard on a timer; reproduced on the real browser. Now a copy leaves the server only right after your own copy / cut key or your click in the page, once per key or click, and only a copy answering your key is written by itself — a copy after a click is offered as the chip. A copy nobody asked for is dropped.

### The live view's bar in plain words

- **"Sized for another window" is gone.** When the page is laid out for another window that is watching the same browser, the chip now says which: "Sized for your other window · Fit here" (another window on this page), "…your other tab…" (another tab or window of this browser), "…another device…"; its tooltip gives the page's size, says the picture here is shown smaller or larger because of it, and what the click does. Clicking it makes the page follow THIS window (the other one then shows the chip). While somebody else is driving, their window keeps the size and the click applies when they hand back. In Chinese: "网页大小跟随你的另一个标签页 · 点此适配本窗口".
- **The recording chip** says "Recording video" (since when), "Video off" (the click opens Agent browser, where video is switched on per profile — every action the agent takes is listed under Actions either way; nothing changed about the default), or "Video did not start" with what to do, instead of "recording refused" and a raw command line.
- The fit and copy chips stay visible longer when the bar is narrow (they fold after the viewers count and the recording chip).
- **The words, read again by a native reader (reality verify).** Chinese: the chip's tooltip says 照着…的大小调的 (not 排的), and "等那个窗口交还控制" instead of 对方 (the window that drives is usually your own other tab); Japanese likewise says そのウィンドウ, not 相手. Sentences are joined without the stray space after 。 and the agent's size reads "Agent 把这个网页设成了 1280×720。" instead of "… 1280×720. 这个窗口"; English says "the iPhone 15 size (390×844)" instead of "the size of a iPhone 15". "Page … · could not resize" no longer shows the browser's English error meant for the agent (it stays in the server log). The copy chip is drawn as a button ("已在网页里复制 — 点这里放进剪贴板") and the message beside it points at the button instead of quoting half of it; the recording chip says 未开录像. On a narrow bar the ⋯ menu keeps the fit chip's full words, so the reason the page looks small is still there.

### The page's size while you drive the agent's browser (reality verify; both were already so before this release)

- **A shared browser** (a profile shared with other conversations) cannot change its page size while someone drives it — the shared-browser fence refuses it like any agent act. The chip now says so plainly ("Page 1398×835 · resized after the handback"; "A shared browser cannot change its size while you drive it …") instead of the browser's error, the page is fitted to your window again right when you hand back (before, it stayed unfitted for 30 seconds), and a refused resize is never mistaken for one the agent made (the chip could say "Agent's size 1398×835" for a size the agent never set).
- **Taking over resizes the page at once** (it waited a quarter of a second, and a second tab closing could push it later — right under your first drag), and the page is never resized while you hold a mouse button: a drag or a text selection finishes in the layout it started in, and the resize follows your release.

### Recording and the server log

- Turning video on while the agent is working started the recorder twice; the second start failed and left "recording refused" beside a recording that was running. A recording now starts once; a second request waits for the first.
- The log line "already holds …" is written when a conversation takes or re-takes a browser, no longer on every agent command, and the handback line prints the page's address without its query string (order numbers, tokens).

### Browser sessions: seen in the chat and in the live view, each with a replay; records kept by size (the owner: "最关键是能在聊天界面和浏览器查看界面两个地方都能看到 session 的开始和结束，以及每个浏览器 session 的回放" / "记录不要按照 7 天上限，而是按照容量，每个浏览器 profile 最多保留 1GB 记录")

A browser session is one run of a conversation's browser: from the moment the agent can use it (the profile given to it, the browser started or joined) to the moment it is let go (taken away, stopped by you, switched to another browser, or the conversation ends). A browser that goes idle is not an end — the session goes on.

- **In the chat.** Two small VibeSpace cards per session, drawn like the takeover and handback cards (never as the agent's words, never a turn): "Browser session started · work · 14:02" and "Browser session ended · 12 min · 38 actions" with a **Replay** button. A temporary browser is named "a browser of its own". Both cards are still there after a reload and after a server restart, in the place they happened.
- **The replay window** ("Browser replay · <conversation>"): the sessions on the left, newest first (when, how long, how many actions), and under the chosen one its actions (time, what it did, a thumbnail). On the right, the action's after-screenshot at full width with the click point or element box drawn on it, a Before / After switch, and the action, its page and its time. ← and → step, Home and End jump, Space plays one action a second and stops at the last. On a phone the list sits above the picture and every button is at least 44 px. It says plainly when there is nothing to show: no sessions for this conversation, the action trace is off, or "Frames of this session were removed to stay under the 1 GB limit; the action list is kept".
- **In the live view.** The Actions pane starts with a Sessions list (each with Replay), and the actions carry a line where each session begins ("Session 3 · started 14:02"). When the browser is stopped, the live view opens straight onto that list instead of only saying the browser stopped.
- **Also:** Session properties has a "Browser sessions (n)" row with Replay; the Agent browser panel has **Replay…** on each profile that has records.
- **Kept by size, not by age.** Each profile keeps its records up to 1 GB (the new setting "Browser records kept per profile (MB)", at least 64 MB; the temporary browsers together count as one). Over it, the screenshots of the oldest sessions are removed first; the list of what the agent did is always kept, so a replay can still say what happened. Nothing is removed for being old. The Agent browser panel shows "{used} of {size}" per profile, and every sentence that said "kept 7 days or 200 MB" now says the size rule. Video recordings keep their own limit (7 days or 200 MB), unchanged.
- Under the hood: the recorder writes a `start` and an `end` line per session into `data/browser-trace/<profile|ephemeral>/sessions.ndjson` on the keeper's lease events, and every action carries its session id (`bs-…`); an action with no open session opens one, a restart re-opens a session whose lease came back and ends the rest ("restart") at their last action, and records from before this release form sessions of their own. The chat cards are system messages with the session's own id, fed live by the recorder and placed by time from those lines whenever a conversation's history is rebuilt or opened read-only. `GET /api/browser/sessions` (your login only; the agent's tools get nothing new). New window type `browser-replay`.
- Gates: test-browser-sessions (fast, in-process · 196 ms: the session pairing, the size plan with two patched copies that must fail — one that also removes by age, one whose sweep drops the action lists — the real recorder on the lease events and across a restart, the cards placed by time and fed once, the route, the replay keys, the words in zh and ja), test-browser-replay-ui (heavy, chrome: the cards live and after a real server restart, the replay from a card, from Session properties and from the panel, the click drawn within 3 px, the keys and the one-a-second play, the swept session, the stopped live view, the phone, zh / ja / en rect census); test-browser-housekeeping re-pointed to the size rule.

### The browser-switch dialog, rebuilt (the owner's zh screenshot of the old one)

The old dialog, opened from an agent browser's live view, read "浏览器 backend", "chromium 151", "tier 1 / tier 2", a red paragraph about "§7.2.1 egress measurement … binary_absent", a seat line, a source chip, a per-site memory form, and buttons stacked one character per line ("打开集成", "安装 CloakBrowser…", "取消", "切换", "记住") — in a dialog that could switch nothing on this build.

- **What it says now.** The title is "Browser for “shopping”". The first line says whose browser it is and what it is: "Your agent's browser: Chromium — VibeSpace's default browser (the open-source version of Chrome)." When there is another browser the profile can switch to, it is ONE card: its name, one line about it, what switching does ("Switching restarts the browser; open pages reopen by themselves and saved logins come along. You can switch back any time.", a warning when a few sites may ask to sign in again, how many conversations use it now), and one button that does what it says. When a step comes first, the card says it and offers it: a missing licence key ("Enter license key…" opens the key's card), a program that is not installed ("Download and install…", behind a confirmation that says about 200 MB is downloaded — nothing is requested before you confirm), a program that cannot be installed here ("Set location in Settings…" opens Settings on the CloakBrowser row), a failed install ("Install again…"), a licence whose browsers are all in use ("Open Agent browser…"), a browser you are driving by hand ("Go to live view"). A step with nothing to press says so in one sentence, and a row that changes by itself says "this updates by itself". No control is ever shown greyed out.
- **When there is nothing to switch to** (this build — CloakBrowser is not part of it): the dialog says "There's no other browser for “shopping” yet. If a site blocks your agent, take over in the live view and get past the check yourself." — and nothing offers to open it: the live view's bar names the browser as a plain label, the agent's "blocked" note shows the note and Dismiss only, and the profile picker has no switch row. A browser that is not VibeSpace's to switch (a connected browser, a cloud one, a desktop window) says why on its first line.
- **The agent's blocked note** reads "Your agent reports shop.example blocked it: “captcha”.", with the agent's evidence behind Details (readable on a phone, kept open while the dialog refreshes) and Dismiss (zh 知道了, ja 非表示 — never the same word as Close).
- **A switch that fails is undone.** A switch used to commit the new browser before starting it, so a start that failed left the profile on a browser that could not start. Now any failure puts the profile back where it was and starts the old browser again; the message says "CloakBrowser didn't start. “shopping” is back on Chromium." (or, when the old one did not start either, that it stays on Chromium and starts the next time your agent uses it). While a switch runs the dialog shows only "Switching to CloakBrowser… You can close this window; the switch goes on."
- **The same words everywhere.** The bar, the picker, Session Properties and the Actions pane say "Chromium" / "CloakBrowser" (no version, no plan); Manage Agents' CloakBrowser row says installed / installing / not installed with an "Install…" button behind the same confirmation (the path in its tooltip, no disabled button); Settings' row is "CloakBrowser program file"; the licence-key card says 授权码 in zh like the dialog. Every sentence has zh and ja entries (ja quotes 「」). An act that opens another window closes the dialog first, so the window it opened is not hidden behind it.
- **Worded buttons on the 24 px icon class** are found by a census now (test-live-bar-layout §4b): it flagged the live view's cap Stop / Use the default and the desktop app strip's Take over / Hand back, whose width only came from another file's rule; each carries its size on its own classes.
- Under the hood: the server sends each row's closed STATE (17, one precedence in src/browser-switch.js `rowState`) and its facts; the device's own words come from the PURE src/lib/browser-switcher-model.js; the dialog is a keyed patch (a broadcast never rebuilds the button under the pointer). The profile digest carries `backends[id] = {id, major, plan, choices}`; the install verdict carries `npm` and `state.failed`; a failed switch answers `restored`, `from`, `to`. Nothing the agent's CLI reads changed.
- Gates: test-browser-switcher-model (fast, in-process · 202 ms: every state's words and control verbatim over fixture views the REAL switch module builds, the closed set on both sides, every answer worded with the rollback facts first, the hidden rows, zh + ja, wiring pins, five patched-copy controls), test-browser-switcher-ui (heavy, ~35 s: 19 views × en / zh / ja × 1280 / 360 px under DejaVu Sans, measured from rendered rects and shot, the acts, two controls), test-browser-backend ③b (the states on the real keeper, the digest's choices, the rollback on `launch_failed` and on a stale-view `backend_no_key`, the route's body, the agent's `next`), test-browser-live-ui ②b (the entry points on this build and with another browser available) + its controls now strip the own-class size rules, test-browser-share-model (the picker row), test-live-bar-layout §4b.

### "Who can use it" becomes a list of conversations and Task Groups (the owner's report: a Chinese UI, the Agent browser panel)

The row's "谁能使用" was a plain dropdown of every running conversation: no Task Group in it, and only one choice. A profile is a browser with your logins; you want to give it to a few conversations, or to everything in a Task Group, and keep it from the rest.

- **The panel row shows the list.** "Who can use it" reads "All my conversations", or one small chip per conversation and Task Group (a conversation with its agent's icon, dimmed when it is not running; a Task Group with the people icon). More than four fold into "+2 more" (two on a phone). A **Change…** button opens the dialog. If the list can no longer let anyone in (the only Task Group was deleted), an amber line says "Nobody can use it now: the Task Group it was limited to was deleted" — never "everyone".
- **The dialog.** "Who can use work?" with two answers: "All my conversations" (the default) or "Only these". Under "Only these" is the same searchable picker the channel dialogs use: Task Groups first, conversations under their Task Group, the rest under Other, recent picks on top; type to filter, ↓ and Enter or the mouse to pick, the chip's × to remove. Picking a Task Group means every conversation in it — bound to it or started in its folders — now and later. Conversations on other machines are not listed (the Agent browser runs on this machine only), said in one line. If a conversation that uses the profile right now would lose it, the dialog says how many before you save ("1 conversation using it now will lose it when you save (their pages in it close)."). Saving with "Only these" and nobody picked is refused in place.
- **Nothing is overwritten by accident.** The dialog reads the list fresh from the server (never the panel's copy) and saves the whole list with a stamp of what it read; if another window or an agent changed it meanwhile, it says so, saves nothing, and re-opens on the list as it is now.
- **Picking a profile for a conversation adds it.** Choosing a profile kept to some conversations in New Session, Session properties or a session card's menu adds that conversation to the list (the toast says so), so the panel always shows everyone who can use it. A default the conversation got on its own (a resumed conversation's own pin, a fork's copy of its parent's, a Task Group's or the instance's default) adds nothing — a fork is another conversation.
- **Leaving a Task Group takes effect at the next browser command.** A conversation that leaves the Task Group a profile is kept to is refused at its next command, and its tab in that browser closes in the same step (the refusal says so). Narrowing the list closes the tabs of every conversation it leaves out; if the Task Group list cannot be read at that moment, nobody is cut off and the command says to run it again.
- **The agent is told only about itself.** `vibespace-browser profiles` says for each profile "used by: all your conversations", "chosen conversations — yours included" (or "…through its Task Group"), "…not yours (the user can add this conversation under "Who can use it" in the Agent browser panel)", or "…unknown for yours right now"; it never sees the list or another conversation. A refused command names the button: add this conversation under "Who can use it" (Change…), or switch it to "All my conversations".
- **Upgrading keeps every conversation that could use a profile.** A one-time migration turns a profile kept to one conversation or one Task Group into a one-row list, and adds every conversation whose own pin let it in until now.
