The memory is now on disk for a day, and a notification that does come back without it is delivered whole, not cut. (3) On a phone the "Hand over now" button hid its cost; and on a Codex agent mid-turn the strip said nothing about cost while a turn that could not take the message was billed unannounced. The button now always says "starts a turn" or "joins the running turn", on every width, and its tooltip says what happens if the running turn cannot take it. Also: the chat's copy of the channel-witness list is bounded like the server's (measured under 200 reads/s). Gates: test-stash-strip ②e + five patched-copy controls, test-channel-touch.
- **Verify round 5 (2026-09-27; one defect reproduced on the real hook routes, three small ones on the module).** (1) When a conversation resumed with a large Task Group context and a handed-back hand-over (now delivered whole rather than cut at 400 characters) was waiting, the two rode the same injection and the 9.6 KB inline cap cut the tail — the notices: one of six reached the agent, all six had already left their queue, the chat card showed all six, and the cut's own pointer named the task context, not the notices. Now a waiting notice is delivered only when it fits whole under the cap; otherwise it stays in its queue (the strip keeps counting it) and rides the very next prompt, whose head is small. The Background Work digest waits the same way. (2) The hand-over memory forgets spent records before live ones and says which live one it forgot; a corrupt memory file and an echo for a forgotten hand-over are logged instead of passing in silence; a memory record with a junk timestamp is dropped at load. Refuted through the real spend guard: every harness row's button word matches its ledger stamp, a refused fold bills exactly once, a second press finds nothing waiting; the queues stay bounded while a hand-over is in flight. Gates: test-stash-strip ②f + three patched-copy controls.
- **Verify round 6 (2026-09-27; one defect reproduced on the real hook routes with an 800-fill sweep, two small ones beside it).** Round 5 made a waiting notice ride only when it fit under the inline cap — measured against what came BEFORE it. Four things ride AFTER it on a prompt: a one-line rescue pointer the belt prepends past 8 KB, the "the user changed your status" reminders (taken from their queue at the same moment), the backlog cleanup nudge, and the Background Work update. When a large Task Group diff had left the notices just enough room, those followers pushed the payload over the cap and the cut fell on the tail: the nudge (harmless — it repeats), the status reminder (lost — its queue was already empty), the reply hint, and in a narrow window the newest notice itself (its card shown, its queue empty). Now everything that rides after the notices is rendered or reserved first and counted, so the cap is never crossed; the payload's order is unchanged. Also: a batch of notices that fit by their lines but not with the section's own header no longer waits whole — the oldest wait, the rest ride; and when a queue's 30-entry cap drops its oldest notice (the one the newest-first delivery keeps holding under a flood), the log now says which one and that it was never delivered. Refuted: the by-identity take (same-bytes notices are distinct; nothing between the peek and the take), the hook script (a 9 600-byte answer reaches the CLI byte for byte), the order (the tools intro always rides first and whole), the once-only card, the memory's spent-first bound (a forgotten record's second echo is a visible duplicate, by round 2's law). Judged: newest-first delivery holds the oldest notice under a steady flood — visibly (the agent's "held" line, the strip's count, three billed presses for eight 4 KiB blocks). Gates: test-stash-strip ②g + three patched-copy controls.
- **Verify round 7 (2026-09-27; four defects reproduced on the real hook routes, none in the money paths).** Rounds 5 and 6 made the waiting notices fit the inline cap or wait, measured against what came before and after them. What remained was the front of the payload itself. (1) After a restart the server forgets what a conversation has already been shown, so its first prompt re-sends the whole Task Group context — for two groups with a long backlog, or three groups, that alone is at the 9.6 KB cap — and the reminders queued behind it ("the user changed your status", "the user took over your browser — wait for the handback") and the Background Work update were taken from their queues and then cut off the end; the Group Manager teaching was marked delivered and cut mid-sentence on both hook calls; with standing instructions of 3 000 characters the tools introduction lost its tail on the first prompt and was marked delivered. Now every one of them rides only when it fits whole and is otherwise left where it was, untouched, for the next prompt (the reminders oldest first, as many as fit) — the log says which one waited and why. (2) A Codex conversation's SessionStart hook is run by the app-server and its answer is thrown away, and that answer used to carry every waiting notice — three channel messages and a job result left their queues into it, the chat showed them as delivered, and the first prompt (the one Codex does read) found nothing; the SessionStart answer for such a harness is now empty and touches nothing. (3) Codex also runs the per-prompt hook about 100 ms after the wrapper's own delivery and drops that answer too; a message, a reminder or a job event arriving in that window was lost the same way — the hook now names its event and a hook call on a Codex chat conversation is answered empty. (4) Nothing else: the payload's order is unchanged (byte-identical to round 5 where every producer fits), a helper that shares its parent's token drains the parent's queue by the product's rule (the bearer owns the call — judged, not changed), the stores are read before the server listens so a first prompt at boot drains once. Gates: test-stash-strip ②h (a source census of every producer with a control that adds an uncounted one; the restart's first prompt, three groups, the manager, the 3 000-char preamble; the two Codex doors; the real hook script's header; the order vs round 5; the boot) + five patched-copy controls; test-profile-blindness (consumeNotices by count).
- **Verify round 8 (2026-09-27; the three doors of round 7 attacked, one small defect reproduced and fixed, nothing in the money paths).** Every harness × chat/terminal × both hook calls × the caller was driven on the real routes (40 cells: exactly one path delivers for every harness that has one, none twice); a seeded walk of 25 000 calls with random messages, job results, reminders, group edits and server restarts found every item delivered whole exactly once; the hook script the server generates is byte-for-byte the shipped one and reaches every remote host at its next session start; the money checks of rounds 3–5 are unchanged. The defect: a reminder record written by a newer VibeSpace and read by an older one (after a rollback) sat at the head of the queue uncounted, so the reminder behind it that had room was delivered one prompt late and the unknown record vanished silently — now it counts as a position, is dropped by name in the log, and the reminders that fit ride the same prompt. Judged from the Codex source (0.154.0, the installed version): Codex now records both hooks' answers for every front end, so the round-7 doors are what keeps a Codex chat from receiving its context twice; Codex also runs a hook only after the user has trusted it in its own UI — on a machine where that never happened a Codex terminal session gets no VibeSpace context at all (a backlog item). The owner's own Task Groups: two of them render 12 KB and 20 KB for one group (the shared folder's 100-file index), so six of the thirteen live conversations get a trimmed context at every start and every restart — legal under the owner's rule, and a restart re-sends about 108 KB of context across all thirteen; a persisted seen-marker and a budgeted file index are proposed, not built. Gates: test-stash-strip ②i (the unrenderable record + its control) and ②j (the exactly-once walk + the consume-first control).

- Gates: test-stash-strip (fast), test-channel-jump ⑨ (heavy: a rejected draft's receipt on a real page), test-spend-paths (the new `stash-handover` reason and its one site), test-peer-delivery (its sender name).

### The Channels conversation window: raw → blocks → DOM (lane channel-render, design §25)

The owner (two screenshots): "可以优化下 channel 部分的界面。架构层面你可能需要设计一个不同 connector 的 raw message to HTML 的接口，比如邮件展示的时候就需要自动折叠 quote 内容，lark 展示的时候需要自动把 markdown 格式的一些链接之类的变成链接。这个当作 IM 用还是有必要把界面好好优化下至少保证人能看清楚必要的信息."

- **In a Lark conversation:** a message like `[https://….example](https://….example/)` is now a link that opens in a new tab, and so is a bare URL (the sentence's full stop stays outside it); `@name` is a small chip; a picture sits in the message itself — the "[image]" words above the thumbnail are gone (also for messages read before this release); a rich-text post keeps its links, mentions, pictures and code blocks; a card shows its title and lines; a system message says who did what ("Ada invited Brook, Cass to the group." instead of "{from_user} invited …"); stickers, shared chats and forwarded messages are one grey line in your language.
- **In a Gmail thread:** the window's title is the subject without the ticket banner or a `Re: RE:` chain ("RE: Quarterly numbers", not "====== Please reply above this line ====== …") — the conversation list shows the same, and its preview line is the message, not the banner; the banner itself is one dim line; the quoted history ("On … wrote:", "在 … 写道：", Outlook's From/Sent block, "-----Original Message-----", a forwarded message) is folded behind "显示引用内容（N 行）" with who wrote it beside the button — one click opens it, and it stays open when new messages arrive; a signature ("-- ", "Sent from my iPhone") folds the same way; a mail that is only a forward is shown open.
- **The footer is one short line:** "以你的身份直接发送" (Lark) / "以你的身份起草并发送" (Gmail, which drafts then sends), the policy sentence behind the ⓘ beside it. A Gmail account whose sign-in cannot reply yet (a token from before 2.369.191 holds `gmail.send`, which cannot create the reply's draft) says "只读 —— 这个账号需要重新授权才能回复" with a **重新授权** button right there that opens that account's own re-authorize dialog; only a Lark account that lacks a send scope adds one more line naming exactly the missing scope and the app-console step.
- **Easier to read:** body text 13 px; messages by one person within five minutes share one name line, and each later message shows its own time on hover; on a phone the fold button and Re-authorize are at least 36 px tall.
- **A new message no longer rebuilds the window** — it is appended under the last one, so an opened quote stays open, a reply you are typing is no longer wiped when a message arrives (the footer is rebuilt only when what it says changes, and then carries your text over), and you are not pulled to the bottom unless you were there. A window used to draw every message twice when the conversation's own "hot" broadcast arrived while it was still loading; opening, updates, reconnects and scrolling up now run one after another.
- **How it is built (the architecture the owner asked for):** each connector turns its raw message into a TYPED block tree — never HTML — at ingest (`record.blocks`): paragraphs of text / link / mention / code / bold runs, quote and signature (foldable, with attribution), banner, code, picture / file by attachment id, card, system line. The schema lives in src/channel-record.js (a closed set, bounds, every string frame-neutered, a link only for http(s)/mailto — anything else stays words), the rungs in PURE src/channel-blocks.js (generic, mail, Lark, stored-record, `cleanSubject`), and ONE renderer (src/lib/channel-blocks-view.js) builds the DOM with textContent only, re-checking every link at render time. Messages stored before this release get their tree when they are read (the adapter's declared `blocksOf`), with no migration. Agents are unaffected: they still read `text`, and their read route never carries the tree. Adapters declare it on their capability row (`render: 'blocks'`, `titleForm: 'subject'`, a `sendGrant` for the console step) — nothing in the window knows an adapter id.
- **A re-authorized account can reply everywhere at once (inc-muk9jj0j-rel3).** The owner: "已经重新授权过 但还是有个邮件提示没有发送权限" — after re-authorizing Gmail, a thread opened minutes later still said "sending needs the send permission". Each conversation remembered its own "can I send here" answer, and a re-authorization refreshed none of them: only the threads the next refresh happened to visit changed, every other thread stayed read-only for hours. Now the answer is worked out again for EVERY conversation of that account the moment its sign-in changes (Gmail and Lark can tell from the sign-in's permissions alone — no request to Google or Lark), the open windows switch from the read-only line to the composer by themselves, and a thread opened afterwards is writable at once — including threads judged before this release (the server re-checks them when it starts and whenever one is read).
- **"推送…" says what it is.** The account menu's Push… row and dialog now open with one line: push = the platform tells VibeSpace about a new message within seconds, off = polling every few minutes; Gmail needs a Google Cloud Pub/Sub topic + this instance's own pull subscription (one re-authorize adds the permission), Lark uses the app's long connection with no public address — plus what "exclusive" and "shared" mean. Words only.
- Gates: test-channel-blocks (fast, new — incl. eight patched-copy controls and the real engine in-process with zero vendor calls), test-channel-window-render (heavy, new — the two screenshots' points in chrome, zh, with an innerHTML negative control for a hostile record; ⑦ the re-authorization reaching open windows; ⑧ the Push… words); test-channels-engine ⑯ (the re-judge, with the skip-the-invalidation control); test-channel-record ④e (every string of the tree inert), test-channels-images ⑤, test-channels-aggregate-ui ②b and test-channels-e2e ⑥ follow the new window. 23 new zh + ja strings.
- **Verify round (adversarial, 2026-09-27) — three real defects, each reproduced, fixed, pinned, with a patched-copy control.** ① **The rungs were quadratic and walked the RAW body.** The e-mail linkifier's unbounded local part made the regex engine eat a whole word and backtrack at every position (a 64 KiB word: 2.3 s), `trimUrl` re-counted the brackets per trimmed character (a URL followed by 60 000 `)`: 11 s), the `-- ` signature test counted the rest of the body per line (16 K lines: 1 s) — and Gmail's / Lark's `toRecord` hand the rung the vendor body BEFORE the record's own 64 KiB cut, so one 1 MiB single-line mail would have held the server's event loop for minutes (every session, every client; the same walk ran in every browser at render). Now every part of the e-mail pattern is RFC-bounded, the bracket census is taken once, the signature test stops at its bound, every rung bounds its input first, and a rung NEVER THROWS (a system template of `{a}` × 100 000 over a 64 KiB part threw RangeError out of ingest, and Lark's history page has no per-item catch — one poison message parked the account). All fifteen pathological inputs now run in ≤ 73 ms; the linearity table is a gate. ② **A `mailto:` link carried a compose form.** `mailto:you@x?bcc=evil%40y` passed the one-@ regex (the mail client percent-decodes RFC 6068 hfields) and opened a compose window with a hidden recipient; a mailto is now ONE address (`MAILTO_RE`). ③ **A stored tree was served as written.** The log is append-only and its writer is not always `makeRecord`; a tree that fails the schema reached every client with the renderer as the only wall. The read now judges it: refused ⇒ dropped (the text is drawn), valid ⇒ served cleaned. Also: a Lark mention chip is named by the message's own mentions / the roster before the element's `user_name` claim, an emotion's type and a system template's parts are bounded, and a reply typed before a disconnect is HELD for the composer's return instead of silently dropped. Verified inert in chrome (test-channel-window-render ⑨): markup labels, `javascript:` / `data:` / `vbscript:` / `jav&#x61;script:` targets, a mailto with `?bcc=`, a 3 000-char URL, a unicode confusable (a bare one stays words — the bare-URL alphabet is ASCII; a markdown one links to its punycode target, said in the title), a rich-text post with hostile `a` / `md` / `at` / `code_block` / `emotion` / `img` elements, a card with a `url` action and a frame in its title, a system template over an injected name, a 100 KB body of an unknown type, an RTL-override file name, and two trees written past makeRecord — `window.__xss` never set, no `<script>`, no `on*` attribute, every `img` src our route; a mail whose only content is an attacker's own "On … wrote:" line or a `-- ` signature is SHOWN, never folded to nothing; a banner-only subject keeps the original title. ⑩: three broadcasts DURING an upward page draw 60 rows once, in order; a draft survives the burst, a message's arrival and a footer rebuild; an opened quote survives an append AND the whole-page redraw a late record forces. test-channels-engine ⑯ pins the converse: a disconnect flips every conversation of the account to read-only on read and on disk, and a send typed a moment earlier is refused `send-not-available · send-scope-not-granted`. LOW, left as is: an attacker's own "On … wrote:" line ABOVE text folds that text (as Gmail does — the attribution shows the line, the button the count); a `lines` count up to 1 000 000 reads on the fold button; a `stale`-marked verdict of an adapter without `sendCapsOf` is re-written at every boot; a label that is a confusable of the target's own host shows the confusable (the title carries the punycode).

### The look (lane channel-polish)

The owner: "界面美化别忘了做（channel 部分）… 这个当作 IM 用还是有必要把界面好好优化下至少保证人能看清楚必要的信息". The words, the rules and the safety of what a message shows are unchanged — this is what it looks like.

- **Everyone has a face.** Each person in a conversation gets a small round avatar with their initials ("Ada Example" → AE; a Chinese or Japanese name → its first character) in a colour that is always the same for that person, on every screen and after every refresh; your own is in the accent colour and your name too. The colours come from the theme and stay readable in all six themes (at least 4.5 : 1).
- **One person talking reads as one block.** Messages by the same person within five minutes share one avatar and one name line; each later message shows its own time in the avatar's column when you point at it (it used to be drawn over the end of the text). A "Cass added Brook to the group" line is now a quiet centred line — not a message from Cass — and the next message starts fresh.
- **The rest of the window:** the day ("Yesterday", "Today") is a small label on a thin line; the header is the conversation's avatar, its name and the access chip on one line with ⋯, and the members / state below (one line on a phone); a picture is a rounded card up to 280 px wide, its file name shown when you point at it; a file is a small card with its type icon, name and size; a Lark card has a border and a bold title; quoted mail history is a thin-barred block; the message box is one soft box with the send button inside.
- **The conversation list** shows each conversation's avatar (the same one its window shows; a mail thread gets the mail icon, an agent group the people icon), its name (bold while unread), the time (highlighted while unread), its one tag, the last message and the unread count. On the default-width sidebar the avatar sits small beside the name so the tag keeps its room; on a wider sidebar or a phone it spans both lines. Rows no longer wear a box each. An account shows its kind as a small coloured tile, and at the default width its name is no longer cut to "Lark / …".
- **Fixed on the narrowest sidebar (200 px):** the Outbox button no longer sits past the edge, the account's status line no longer runs off it (nothing scrolls sideways any more), and a tag such as "1 to approve" is always shown whole.
- **On a phone** every button in a conversation and in the list is at least 36 px (the ⋯, the access chip, a file, the ⓘ, the filter and its buttons were 16–28 px).
- **Picking an agent or a group no longer means scrolling a dropdown of every session.** The owner: "如果 session 特别多的话，你现在的那个选择 session/group 的 dropdown 交互会很不友好". Everywhere you choose who — Grant access…, Notify…, Reach & policy's "Grant reach to…", New group / Invite…, a desktop app's Share with agents and Ask an agent — is now ONE picker: a search box (it matches the name, the folder, the Task Group, the agent type or the start of the id; accents and case do not matter, Chinese and Japanese match anywhere in the name), a list under it with the Task Groups first and each session under its Task Group (then "Other"), each session showing its agent icon, name, folder, a live dot and its Task Group; the ones you picked recently on this device come first. ↑ ↓ Enter pick, Esc clears the search, Backspace removes the last pick; where several can be chosen they show as chips with ✕. The list updates in place when sessions come and go. What each dialog saves is exactly what it saved before.
- **The Notify… dialog asks three plain questions and says back what it will do.** The owner: "那个通知配置项目本身就有点 confusing". Each notification is now: *Who gets woken?* (the picker) · *On which messages?* — Every message / Only messages matching a rule… (the rule editor opens under it) / Only when a name is mentioned · *How often at most?* — Right away, every time / A digest every N minutes / At most N times a day (a number past its limit is still said under its field) — and one sentence at the bottom, rewritten as you change anything: "工作 will be woken right away for every message in this account, at most 40 times a day." The per-notification "wake the agent with each outbox receipt" switch is gone from this dialog (the receipt now rides the Approve ▾ button). **Grant access…** asks "Who may read and act here?" with the picker and, per agent or group, two plain answers — "May draft replies (you approve)" / "May reply directly" (only the first where direct sending is not offered, the reason said once). What both dialogs save is exactly what they saved before.
- Gates: test-channel-blocks ⑭ (fast — the initials, the colour per person, every avatar colour pair in all six themes computed from the stylesheet), test-principal-picker (fast, new — the search / order / sections / recent arithmetic and a census that no dropdown of the roster is left), test-channel-filter ⑫ (fast — the Notify sentence in en / zh / ja for five notifications), test-channel-window-render ⑪ (heavy — one avatar per run, the time beside it on hover, the system line, the same avatar and colour after a new message arrives) + ⑫ (40 sessions in 3 Task Groups: the box focused, 3 letters narrow to the right 12, Enter picks, the saved request unchanged), test-channels-i18n ④ (heavy — every surface in zh / ja / en, desktop and phone, under the runner's font: nothing overlaps, nothing is cut, nothing scrolls sideways, every phone target ≥ 36 px, every avatar readable). The screenshot driver (scripts/dbg-comm-surfaces.mjs) gains the IM pass the gate and the before / after shots use.
- **Verify round 2 (adversarial, 2026-09-27) — three real defects, each reproduced on the lane as delivered, fixed, pinned, with a control.** ① **A digest's daily limit could not be changed.** The Notify dialog offered "right away", "a digest every N minutes" and "at most N times a day" as three answers to one question, so with a digest chosen the daily limit was greyed out — a digest saved earlier with its own limit (every 1440 minutes, at most 1000 a day) showed the number and would not take a new one. The daily limit is now its own line under the two answers and can always be edited; what the dialog shows and what it saves are the same record in every combination. ② **Re-reading a conversation asked the platform for older history nobody scrolled for.** When a window re-read its messages (after a reconnect), emptying the list moved the scroll position to the top, and the window took that for you scrolling up: it read the page above and, in a short conversation, asked Lark / Gmail for older history — a request counted against the account's per-minute budget — and then would not ask again when you did scroll up. A window now ignores the scroll its own re-read causes, and several re-reads waiting in line are one. ③ **A long message naming many people was slow to draw.** A 64 KiB Lark message with 256 mentions took 1.6 s to prepare every time it was read (19 ms now). Also: a session / Task Group picker stops listening for roster changes the moment its dialog closes (it used to stop at the next change); measured with 500 sessions and 50 Task Groups the picker opens in 80 ms and a keystroke redraws it in 7 ms. Refuted, with a reproduction each: script or markup through any message field, link, mention, file name, avatar or picker row (every one is drawn as text; links only http(s) and a plain mail address); a hand-edited message log (judged when it is read); the five dialogs' saved data against 2.369.193 (identical). Gates: test-channel-blocks ⑬, test-channel-filter ⑫ (fast); test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑦b, test-channel-window-render ⑩b / ⑩c / ⑫b (heavy).
- **Verify round 6 (adversarial, 2026-09-27) — the money class closed by a census and a server belt, not by a sixth example.** ① **Loading older history is now bounded on the server, per conversation, whatever a window does.** Before, twenty simultaneous requests for the same page of one conversation reached Lark twenty times, and a conversation whose beginning had already been reached cost one vendor request per scroll to the top, for ever (the account's whole minute budget was the only limit). Now one request is in flight at a time (the others wait and get the same page), two requests are at least 1.5 s apart (the second is answered "Loading older messages is paused for a moment", once, and the window waits), and "nothing older" is remembered until a new message arrives, you press Refresh or sign in again. ② **A zoom wheel (Ctrl+wheel, a trackpad pinch) or a sideways Shift+wheel at the top no longer loads older history** — neither moves the list. ③ **Scrolling inside a long code block (or an edit box) no longer loads the conversation's older history** — a wheel, a finger or ArrowUp / PageUp inside a block that can still scroll up moves the block, not the list. ④ **A page that brought nothing pauses the window for a moment** instead of asking again on every scroll event. ⑤ **A click on an account's ⋯ or on its header lands even when a new message arrives during the press** (the header is updated in place, never rebuilt). Gates: test-channel-drain ⑥ (fast, the pure rule + four mutants), test-channels-engine ⑭ (fast, through the real route with three controls), test-channel-blocks ⑮ (fast, the census as 55 verdict rows + three tables + two controls), test-channels-aggregate ⑦ (heavy), test-channel-window-render ⑩h (heavy — 27 trusted-input legs, every non-gesture path 0, the seven real page-up gestures 7), test-channels-panel-redraw ⑤d + ⑧ CONTROL (heavy).
- **Verify round 7 (adversarial, 2026-09-28) — the belt attacked, one seam closed, the battery made a gate.** A message that arrives by push (Lark's live lane) now also lets "nothing older" be asked again — before, only a polled message, a Refresh or a sign-in did; the vendor is still asked at most once per 1.5 s per conversation. The upward-page battery now carries its own negative control (a build that pages on a window maximize goes red there), and the server's one vendor call site is pinned by a census with a bypass control. Round 6's one-in-nine red was the test's own bookkeeping (it counted the page's listeners instead of naming them, and a listener left over from the previous step made the count drift under CPU starvation — reproduced 2/2 on one core, fixed, 3/3 green there after); the product was never wrong. Gates: test-channels-engine ⑭ ⑧ + ⑨ (fast, two controls), test-channel-window-render ⑩h CONTROL (heavy).
- **Verify round 5 (adversarial, 2026-09-27) — round 4's mechanisms attacked with trusted input; every finding reproduced, fixed, pinned with a control.** ① **A window resize right after scrolling up in a short conversation still asked the vendor for older history** — round 4 refused the resize's own scroll reset only when the conversation got SHORTER than it was when you scrolled; in a conversation that fits its window, scrolling up loads the page above (correct), and a maximize inside 1.5 s makes it fit again — back to exactly as tall as before, which round 4 let through. Now a scroll event on a conversation that fits its window never loads history (your wheel, pull or key there asks directly). ② **Pressing ↑ or Home while typing a rejection reason (or editing a draft) in a proposal card loaded older history — and could ask the vendor** — the card sits inside the message list and the list took the key as scrolling. A key typed in a text box is typing. ③ **The Channels panel showed a stale "Access: …" line after you granted access to a second agent or group** — the row was redrawn only when its first principal changed; every fact the line prints now counts (a census in the gate). ④ **A click on an account's ⋯ menu or fold (or "Show all", a rule line) was lost when a digest arrived between the press and the release** — round 4 kept the rows in place but not the account head; a node redrawn the same is now kept too, and its menu opens under the button as before. ⑤ A held Enter in the agent picker no longer toggles the first row on and off at key-repeat speed. ⑥ After a save the server refused, the Grant access… / Notify… dialog gives the keyboard back to its Save button (Esc reachable again without the mouse). Refuted with reproductions: a wheel up during an arrival (one page, every row once), a shrink in the same frame as the wheel, the fence walk on 3 018 shapes byte-identical (13 107 quoted openers 488 ms → 1.4 ms), the picker's highlight by key across a rename.
- **Verify round 4 (adversarial, 2026-09-27) — round 3's mechanisms broken with trusted input and a regex census; every finding reproduced, fixed, pinned with a control.** ① **A wheel DOWN followed by a maximize inside 1.5 s still asked the vendor for older history** — round 3 counted every wheel as "the person's scroll", so the maximize's own scroll reset rode it. Now only a scroll toward older counts (a wheel up, a finger pulled down, ArrowUp / PageUp / Home, the scrollbar), and it remembers how tall the conversation was: a scroll event on a conversation that just got SHORTER (a maximize that lets it fit, a fold, a picture becoming a chip) is the browser's reset, never a scroll, whatever the clock says. ② **The keyboard never loaded older history**: PageUp / Home / ArrowUp scrolled the list but the list could not hear them (it was not focusable) — a click in the conversation now lets the keys reach it, and an up key at the top asks directly like a wheel. ③ **A message of many "```x" lines (a code fence never closed) took about a second to render** — each opener re-scanned the whole message for a closer; one scan now, the result identical (3 ms). Every other pattern over message bytes was measured at its bound (≤ 18 ms on its worst shape). ④ **The "who" picker no longer goes quiet:** when the list changed by itself and Enter could not safely pick, nothing happened and nothing said so — Enter now highlights the first row so you see what the next Enter will take; and a click on a row that coincided with a live-sessions update (every second on a busy instance) was dropped by the browser — rows are no longer rebuilt under the pointer. Saving Grant access… freezes the dialog until the write answers, so what you see is what is saved. ⑤ **The Channels panel with "Show all" open over hundreds of conversations redrew every row on every update** — about 100 ms of stall per update, a click on a row during one lost; it now repaints only what changed (2–4 ms). A heavy test that had been red on this branch since round 2 (a stale check of the Notify dialog's cap field) is green again.
- **Verify round 3 (adversarial, 2026-09-27) — four real defects, each reproduced on the lane as delivered, fixed, pinned, with a control; the rest refuted.** ① **Maximizing a short conversation window asked the vendor for older history.** When the window grew past its content the browser reset the scroll to the top and fired the same event a person's scroll fires; the window read the page above and sent a metered request to Lark / Gmail. The same happened on any resize (the sidebar opening, a phone rotation, another device's layout) and could on folding a quote. Now paging up needs the person's own input — a wheel, a touch, a keyboard scroll, a drag of the scrollbar — within 1.5 s; a wheel up (or a finger pulled down) while already at the top asks directly, so a conversation that fits its window can finally load older history too; and a resize keeps a reader who was at the newest there (it used to leave them at the oldest row). ② **Enter in the "who" picker could grant access to a session the person never saw.** Type "pag", see pager-01 first, pager-01's session ends, the list updates under the cursor, Enter — access went to pager-02. Enter now takes only the highlighted row or the first row the person's own typing put there; a list that changed by itself takes nothing until they type again, and a picked session that ended keeps its name on its chip. ③ **A message reading `<system-reminder` followed by a long run of spaces stalled the server about two seconds on every read of its page** (and every open window and every browser tab re-read it on every update) — a regex that backtracked over whitespace, fixed with identical matches; a label-less link's address now counts toward the message size bound. ④ **The Notify… dialog:** re-pointing a notification from one agent to another carried the first agent's hidden receipt flag along (billed wakes the second never opted into); a mention typed as `@@name` was stored as `@name` (matched nothing) and an unchanged save then widened it to `name`; a digest whose limit an older build stored as 0 previewed as "will not be woken" while it did wake once per window — the preview now says the truth and why it will not save; the refusal names the field the dialog draws; a rule's name survives a save; a notification whose rule is missing says so instead of blaming your input. Also: a link labelled `paypal.com` that points elsewhere now shows its real target. Refuted with reproductions: minimize / desktop switch / phone switch / an arrival on a short room (no request, position kept); every new text sink (avatars, day pills, cards, files, the composer line, the preview) is textContent — 84 hostile trees, 0 violations; the stored-tree judge is per page (24 ms per 50 at the limits); the mention alternation, cleanSubject and the avatar hash are linear; the 200 px rail census.

### The late browser key (B-f7ab — the owner hit it today)

A chat started on 2026-09-17, before per-session browsers, ran `vibespace-browser status` / `open` and every command answered "this session has no browser key (browser isolation is off, or it predates the feature) — it cannot hold a profile"; the agent tried the old CLI name, was refused by the shim, and parked itself waiting for a human. Nothing needed a human: the browser tool builds its environment from the server's answer, so a key given late works for the session that is already running.

- **Its first browser command gets it a browser.** A live session on this machine with no browser key now gets one the first time anything asks — `open`, `status`, a pin from Session properties, the live view's list. It is minted exactly as a new session's is (the same key, the same generated config, the same pin rules: its Task Group's or the instance's default profile), recorded for THAT conversation (so a later Terminate → Resume keeps the same browser), and the command says so once: `note: this session had no browser yet — VibeSpace gave it one now … [browser_key_minted]`. A second command mints nothing.
- **One conversation, one browser.** A conversation that already had a key gets that key back; if another running session of the same conversation holds it, the second one is told which session has it. A fork that has not announced its own conversation yet is refused (a key given then would belong to the conversation it was forked from).
- **Otherwise it says why and what to do.** `no_browser_key` names the reason: a session on another machine ("restart this session (Terminate → Resume) to get a browser key: it runs on another machine, where its browser is decided when the session starts"), per-session browsers or agent integration switched off (names the setting — no restart needed once it is on), a conversation not known yet. A session that is not running any more answers `session-gone`.
- **"No browser yet", not silence.** Session Properties' Agent browser row (and the live view) of such a session says "no browser yet — the agent's first browser command gets one"; the setting "Give each session its own agent browser" now says a running session without a browser gets one at its next browser command.
- Under the hood: ONE mint and ONE writer of a key's session fields (src/server/browser-key.js `mintKey` / `applyKey`) shared by the spawn and the late key; the rules as a PURE verdict (`lateKeyVerdict` in src/browser-profiles.js); the binding still written only at the session-meta choke point.
- **Verify r1 (2026-09-27):** the default profile a late key applies (the Task Group's or the instance's) is dated when the session STARTED, not when the key was minted — a profile the user kept to another conversation after that session started stays closed to it (the agent is told `not_owner`, by the button), exactly as if the session had had its key from the start; before, a session from before the narrowing walked into that profile (its logins) on its agent's first browser command. Every `vibespace-browser` verb now prints a refusal's `remedy:` line (only the page verbs did — `status` on a keyless session said what happened and not what to do). Gates: test-browser-share-model ③f (+ a control copy that dates the pin at the mint), test-browser-pin (the remedy line).
- **Verify r2 (2026-09-27):** a default the user set AFTER a session started no longer reaches it through its late key. Round 1 dated the pin at the start, but the late key still read the defaults at the mint — a profile narrowed to another conversation and then made the instance (or Task Group) default walked in, dated at the start; the spawn-keyed twin had landed on the default in force at its start. Now a session spawned while per-session browsers are off RECORDS what its pin ladder picked (`browserPinAtStart`: the profile, the origin, the date, a fork's parent row verbatim, the group cap in force) and the late key restores exactly that; a record from before this round gets the current default as a landing that never authorizes a narrowed profile (the agent is told `not_owner`, by the button). Also: the group cap is never read live at the mint; a profile picked in the New Session dialog while the switch was off is no longer lost; a key minted by a command that is then refused is still announced (`[browser_key_minted]` on the refusal too). Gates: test-browser-share-model ③f (r2) — the four reproduced scenes beside their spawn-keyed twins, the 8-row spawn ↔ late parity table, two control copies (the r1 engine admits; a live-cap copy stamps the later cap); test-browser-continuity ⑤ asserts the witness on a real server.
- **Verify r3 (2026-09-27, LOW):** a landing (the current default applied to a record from before round 2, dated 0) now authorizes nothing at all — before, `0 ≥ scopeAt` read true on a narrowed profile that carried no scope date (a shape only a hand-edited or restored-after-the-migration registry holds: every narrowing the product writes stamps the date), so the landing admitted the legacy session where a witnessed one is refused; and a witness on a record that states no start is dated 0 (never by its own claim — a future date in a damaged record was the keeper's clock). Neither shape is reachable through the product (this instance: every record has a start, every narrowed profile a date — counted, not read); the rules are made honest where they are stated. Round 3 otherwise REFUTED every attack on the witness: the write is synchronous with the spawn (no route can land between), it is byte-for-byte the keyed twin's pin row + cap stamp for a group pick / a dialog pick (+ the hint downgrade) / a fork of a keyed parent (the parent's row verbatim), a shell's witness is inert, it survives a restart unchanged and the first route at boot+27 ms restores it, a mint then a restart is identical, a keyless resume keeps its conversation's own row over a stale witness, a deleted / foreign / mis-typed witness pins nothing. Gates: test-browser-share-model ③f (r3) — 16 PURE rows, the real keeper over the constructed registry shape, a patched-copy control that admits both.
- Gates: test-browser-share-model ③ (fast: the verdict table and its words; the REAL routes + keeper + browser-env over the fake agent-browser — the first resolve mints, bindings.json names that conversation, a second resolve returns the same key, the conversation's old key comes back, a twin session is refused `held_elsewhere`, both fork record shapes refused, remote / unknown conversation / switches off / session gone refused by name; CONTROLS: an engine copy that mints a second key on the second call, and one without the fork rule — the old terminal fork gets its parent's key), test-browser-fact ⑦ (the keyless fact and its words), test-browser-share ⑦ (heavy: the real agent-browser + Chrome — a session stripped of its key after create runs `vibespace-browser open <local url>` from a shell with no browser variables and browses; the fact and the live view name its browser), test-browser-continuity ⑤ (heavy, a real worktree server: a session spawned with per-session browsers off is refused `isolation_off` by name, then — switched on — its first agent route mints through the real wiring and the real session-meta choke point, bound to its conversation, and its Terminate → Resume spawns on that same key), test-browser-pin (a router without the engine refuses by name).

### Integration — the seven lanes on one tree

- **A channel conversation window draws its list ONE way.** Two lanes had each fixed "messages shown two or three times" (2.369.194 with a render generation, the render lane with a queue); the window keeps the queue — every redraw, new-message patch and older page runs one after another — and the rule that the list's own redraw never counts as you scrolling up for older history.
- **A draft's receipt and the Hand over now press share one queue.** A notice being handed over is never the one the queue's 30-entry limit drops, so the card never says "Not delivered" for something the agent received; a hand-over that carried one of two receipts marks only that one handed; a hand-over that came back puts its receipt back to "waiting"; a queue that could not be saved to disk is restored exactly as it was.
- **Renumbered where two lanes chose the same number:** the design's chat-to-conversation witness is §26 (the render layer keeps §25); test-channels-engine ⑮ (a storage mount's client) and ⑯ (a re-authorization), test-channel-filter ⑫ (the Notify sentence). An agent's withdraw is exempt from the channel-witness census by name (it reads and drafts nothing).
- Gates: test-channel-outbox merge-a…e and test-stash-strip ②c (the merged queue, each with a patched copy of the ladder as its control); test-channels-aggregate-ui ⑨/⑨b with one control bundle that neuters the queue and the whole ready rule; test-architecture §63; the lanes' spelling pins re-pointed to the merged lines.
- **Three heavy reds on the merged tree, each root-caused (none a flake):** test-desktop-app-window shared a window with an agent that existed only in the page — since the channel-withdraw lane the Share dialog sends the agent's live session id and the server names its conversation, so the leg now shares with a stub agent the server actually runs (a dtach session restored at boot) and keeps a page-only ghost for the "not running any more" refusal; test-channel-jump still expected the phone strip to hide "starts a turn" (the lane's own r4 keeps the money word on the button); test-queue-steer's layout pin now reads the stash strip above the queue strip.

## 2.369.194 — the For-you inbox opens as a window that reads long messages at full width and handles them one after another; a Word document opens as paper pages with a fit-width toolbar; apps a user or their agent installs will survive a pod recreation (design, probes passed on a test pod); a Grant access / Notify save no longer overwrites a newer list

### The For-you window (docs/design-user-inbox-reply.md §9)

The owner: "有时候agent给我发好几条很长的消息，在这么小的面板很难review，给我做一个对长文本更友好的"展开详情"面板吧，可以打开一个独立窗口来查看和处理这个inbox里的消息。" — in the popup (and the title-bar mini inbox) a long item was cut after a few lines behind "▸ detail" in a ~400 px panel.

- **⤢ now opens a window.** Every row's ⤢ opens the For-you window ON that item; the popup's tab strip has a ⤢ for the whole inbox; the mini inbox's head has one for that session only; and ⚙ Communication ▸ For you… opens it too. The small read-only viewer the ⤢ used to open is gone — one place to read.
- **Left, the list; right, the item.** The list shows the same items in the same order as the popup (Actions | Notices, the same counts), with "All sessions | <this session>" and a filter box. The item is shown whole at the window's width: the title and the detail rendered (paragraphs, lists, code blocks), selectable, never cut — it scrolls inside the pane. Its session (click to go there, with its running dot and board state), urgency, age and producer sit above it; option chips, a multi-line reply box (Enter sends, Shift+Enter a new line; when the agent cannot take a reply the box says why), and Reply · Mark done · Dismiss · Reopen · Copy · the producer's own button (a reset credit) below.
- **Like a mail client.** After you mark an item done, dismiss it, or answer it, the next open item is selected; the handled one stays where it was, dimmed, until the window is opened again. Something handled elsewhere never moves what you are reading. Keys: ↑/↓ (or j/k) move through the list, Enter goes to the reply box, Esc comes back to the list.
- **Narrow windows and phones** show one side at a time: the list, then the item with a ‹ back; rows are finger-sized on touch.
- **Live and shared like every window**: new items appear as they are filed (a reply you are typing keeps its text and focus), the running dots and the reply box follow the agent, and the window comes back after a reload and on your other devices.
- **Safe with hostile text**: an item's title, detail, options and a session's name are shown as text — raw HTML in an agent's message is escaped by the markdown renderer before DOMPurify.
- **Under the hood**: what the popup and the window share (the store and its three broadcasts, the live facts, an item's words, go-to-session, done/dismiss/reopen, the reply, the producer's action, reply drafts) moved verbatim into ONE client model, src/lib/user-todos-actions.js; the popup subscribes to it and behaves as before. The popup's group order is PURE `sortGroups` and its keyed reconciler `reconcileKeyed`, both now shared with the window. The window's own rules are PURE src/lib/inbox-window-layout.js: `nextSelection` (the next open item below, else the one above, else none), `holdSelection`, `paneMode` (one threshold, 620 px), `scopeRows`, `rowPreview`, `itemView`. Named deviation: the second tab is Notices (the popup's "Notifications" page is the toast history, not items one handles). Not changed: an agent's detail is still stored up to 2 000 characters — the window shows all of it.
- Gates: test-inbox-window-model (fast, in-process · 71 ms: the six rules as tables, each beside a patched copy that breaks it, and the wiring pins — the window calls every rule, uses only the model's verbs, writes innerHTML twice (sanitized markdown, an icon), the four doors, the viewer retired, zh + ja), test-inbox-window-ui (heavy, chrome + a worktree server + a stub claude: the popup row's ⤢ shows the full 3 072-character item while the popup row stays cut, hostile strings as text with an innerHTML control, Mark done moves on and dims in place, a half-typed reply survives a broadcast and Enter delivers it quoted, the keys, the scoped mini-inbox door, the ⚙ row, a second page replays the window, 480 px and the phone). Existing pins follow the moved code (test-user-todos-layout, test-reset-credit-ui, test-helper-ask, test-login-expiry, test-window-types, test-contributions, test-architecture §62); test-inbox-reply-ui ⑪b now puts a layout-history modal over the popup (the viewer it used is retired).
- **Verify round (2026-09-27 — a fresh-eyes walk in chrome at 1280×800 / 1024×700 / 480 px / 390×844 over six open items across three sessions, two with 2 000-character markdown details, chips, notices and a resolved tail; then an adversarial read of the extraction).** Fixed: ① **the "Recently resolved" head was a dead control while one of its rows was selected** — every render re-opened the tail around the selection, so the click did nothing; closing it now moves the selection to the first open row. ② **Under a session scope the empty list said "Nothing needs you right now. Agents file items here…"** beside five open items of other sessions — it now says "No open items for this session." / "No notices for this session.". ③ **A window kept open never re-sorted**: the popup's append-only slots (right while a pointer rests on the list) were kept for the whole life of the window, so a row handled in the morning sat dimmed in its group all day and a new urgent item landed at the bottom of its group; a tab or scope switch and every door (⤢, the mini inbox's ⤢, ⚙ For you…) now re-sort the list like an open does — the slots hold BETWEEN navigations, where the pointer is. ④ With a Spending notice selected the scope button read "Spending" and scoped every account-level notice (Login expiry too) — no per-session scope is offered for an instance-level item. ⑤ Reply with an empty box did nothing — it now puts the cursor in the box. Measured and NOT findings: on the phone the window is on top after the sheet's ⤢ and revealing an already-open window yields the Sessions drawer (the first walk's phone screenshots had the desktop layout's `sidebarOpen` synced to the phone — pre-existing cross-device behaviour, and a JS click that bypassed the drawer); at 1024×700 a fresh open is 764 px wide ⇒ two panes (the one-pane window in the first walk was a 920 px window proportionally reflowed by a viewport shrink); the popup's regression legs (badge counts, folds, a half-typed reply across a broadcast, the in-place resolve, the reconnect resync, the mini inbox) are test-inbox-reply-ui's and stayed green.
- **Long text — the caps and the wire (the owner's complaint IS long messages).** Measured on the scratch server before the change: `vibespace-ask "…" --detail <5 000 chars>` exited 0, printed "added to the user's For you tray" and the store kept 2 000 characters — cut SILENTLY, the user read a context that stopped mid-sentence; a 404-character question kept 300, silently. Now a question holds up to 500 characters and a detail up to 8 000 (src/user-todos.js `TEXT_MAX` / `DETAIL_MAX`); past a cap the store cuts and NAMES it on the record it returns (`textCut` / `detailCut` — never stored) and the CLI prints `NOTE: your --detail was CUT at 8000 characters — the user's tray holds only that much and the rest never reached them. Put the whole content in your CHAT reply` (the agent manual says 8000 too). The wire does not grow with history: `user-todos-updated` and `GET /api/user-todos` carry an OPEN item whole and a RESOLVED one as its first 300 characters + `detailTruncated: true` (`previewOf` — 250 resolved × 8 000 would be 2 MB per broadcast); a new cookie-only `GET /api/user-todos/:id` serves one record whole (an agent token 403 `agent_forbidden`, an unknown id 404). The window loads a previewed item's rest the moment it shows it (`inboxModel.ensureDetail`: single-flight, ONE GET) and says under the text "Showing the first 300 characters — loading the rest…", or the load's failure by name; Copy loads it first. THE READER'S TEXT NEVER SHRINKS: the model remembers every whole detail it has seen (PURE `restoreDetails`, pruned to the ids the snapshot still lists), so when another client resolves the item being read, the row dims in place and the pane keeps the whole text with no fetch. Also pinned in chrome: `javascript:` / `data:` / `vbscript:` links in an item never survive (DOMPurify's URI rule), an https link opens beside the workspace with `noopener noreferrer`.
- Gates (the round): test-user-todos-layout ⑫ (223: the caps table with the cut named on the return, the snapshot shape — open whole / resolved previewed / the ledger whole —, `previewOf`, `restoreDetails` as a table, the read route's 200 / 403 / 404, wiring pins; four patched-copy controls: the old 2 000 cap, a silent cut, a whole-broadcast snapshot, a no-restore layout), test-inbox-window-model (126: itemView's `cut` sentence + a control; the six new wiring pins), test-inbox-window-ui ⑬–⑲ (21 s: the wire shape + the route, a resolved ~6 000-character item loaded whole through ONE GET, the reader's open text kept whole with NO fetch when resolved elsewhere, the tail head, the scoped hint and the notice's absent scope button, the link vectors, the REAL vibespace-ask cut at 8 000 / 500 and 7 999 whole). Left as LOW: a markdown image (`![](https://…)`) in an item loads its picture when rendered (the chat renderer does the same); a new URGENT group filed while the window is open still appends at the end until the next navigation; a session absent from the sidebar is named by its 8-character id (the popup's own fallback); the openSpec carries the first door's item/scope to a replay.

### Design — apps a user or their agent installs survive a pod recreation (docs only)

- **docs/design-app-persistence.zh.md (+ .md twin)** — the owner's question "users and their agents install apps; they must be there after a pod restart, with their data (SteamDeck-like? system/chroot separation?)" answered by a judge-panel review of four roads (persistent overlay / chroot app system / Nix on the PVC / manifest replay + .deb cache; three independent judges, every factual claim checked). Recommendation: ONE product-owned manifest + a local .deb cache + a one-click For-you gate as the spine on every pod (no image or chart change), plus a persistent **app system** (a same-release minbase userland on the PVC entered per launch through a private mount namespace + chroot) on pods that have the mount capability — zero replay at boot, untouched by image upgrades; capability-less pods degrade to an offline replay after listen. The overlay road is rejected as a source of truth (the only design that can make a pod fail to boot), Nix parked. Probes P0 (a day on a test pod) come before any code; owner decisions D1–D6 listed.

### Lane docx-viewer — the Word viewer (the owner: "能不能优化一下这个docx/word文档editor？目前渲染有点问题")

- **What you see when you open the same paper again.** The page is white paper with a soft shadow on the workspace's own background — in the light theme and in every dark one — and it is centred in the window: no grey band across the top, no page cut off on the left. A slim toolbar sits above it: **Fit width** (the default), **100%**, zoom out / zoom in, the zoom level, and **"1 / 4"** on the right, which follows you as you scroll. Ctrl (⌘ on a Mac) + mouse wheel zooms the pages, not the whole browser. The zoom you pick is remembered on this device. What was wrong, measured on the old viewer at your window's shape (817 CSS px wide at 175 % display scaling — the ~1430 px screenshot): the 816 px Letter page overhung the library's 648 px grey frame by 84 px on each side, so the frame's grey top strip was the "band narrower than the page" and the page's left 30 px sat behind the window edge where no scrolling could reach it.
- **The paper looks like Word's.** The running head now appears on page 2 onward (a paper whose body starts in a new section after the title page showed no running head at all — Word carries the previous section's header forward, the library did not); the header's page number sits at the right margin (the Header style's right-aligned tab stop was ignored — 181 px short; now within 13 px, the library's own rounding, the same at every UI scale); bulleted lists show their • (Word writes its default bullet as a Symbol-font code point a browser without that font cannot draw); headings, coloured text and the page colour are the document's own, never the theme's. Embedded fonts are used.
- **Refusals say what to do.** A legacy `.doc` now says "Legacy Word files (.doc) cannot be shown here. Open it in Word or LibreOffice and save it as .docx." before anything is downloaded (it used to end in "Error: Can't find end of central directory : is this a zip file ?"); a password-protected `.docx` and a file that is not a Word document get their own sentence.
- **A crafted .docx is harmless.** Measured on the old viewer: a document carrying an embedded HTML part ran its script inside VibeSpace the moment it was opened (the library shows those parts in a same-origin iframe with scripts on), a style's font name broke out of the stylesheet and restyled the whole workspace, and `javascript:` links stayed clickable. Now the document renders inside its own shadow root (its styles cannot reach the workspace, the workspace's cannot bend it), embedded HTML sits in a sandboxed iframe with no script and no network, `javascript:` / `data:` / file links lose their link (the text stays, the tooltip says why), web links open in a new tab, and in-document links scroll the document.
- **Big documents.** "Rendering…" appears at once; the 80-page fixture is ready in ~160 ms (parse ~60 ms, render ~6 ms) with no main-thread task of 50 ms or more.
- Out of scope: editing. The viewer is read-only; whether an editor is wanted (LibreOffice as a desktop app, or in-browser) is being asked separately.
- Gates: test-docx-viewer-model (fast, in-process, 73 ms: every rule tabled + a patched copy per rule), test-docx-viewer (heavy, chrome, ~55 s: the committed python-docx fixtures under scripts/fixtures/docx/, the text order checked against mammoth's extraction of the same file, the untouched library's own build loaded as the controls). i18n: 14 new strings in zh and ja.

### mirror-193 — the Actions mirror for 2.369.193 (heavy job: test-channels-aggregate-ui red on both attempts, test-exit-forensics flaky)

- **Grant access… could revoke an agent's access without anyone asking it to (product).** The dialogs for a whole account or a rule drew the Channels panel's own copy of the lists, which can be a moment behind the server (a grant through the route, another window, an agent's approved request). If that copy was stale, the dialog showed the wrong list — for an account with no access yet, it pre-filled the first live agent — and Save wrote that whole list over the newer one. On the mirror the agent Xi, granted a moment before, was replaced by `reader`. Now every dialog reads the account fresh before it draws (`GET /api/channels/adapters/:id/view`), and every Save carries a stamp of the list it drew: if the list changed in the meantime, the save is refused, nothing is written, a toast says so, and the dialog re-opens on the list as it is now (`409 grain-changed`; PURE `grainStamp` / `grainBaseVerdict` in src/channel-filter.js).
- **A conversation window could show every message two or three times (product).** Opening a window, the watch beat and the mark-read each ask the window to redraw; each redraw cleared the list, waited for its page and appended it, so on a slow machine or connection two or three redraws in flight all appended. A redraw of a window scrolled to its bottom could also ask for the newest page a second time and put it on top. Now only the newest redraw draws the list, and no older page is asked for while the list is being redrawn. Found by running the suite on a deliberately starved CPU (its picture checks failed 5 of 14 runs there: they found the stale copy's picture).
- **The two gate judges that read the runner's speed.** The toast check counted the toast stack before a save and cut it after — an older toast expiring during a slow save made the new one fall off the end (the mirror's `[]`); every save is now judged by the toast's arrival. test-exit-forensics sent SIGTERM and then unlinked the files, as the server does; on a busy CPU the woken processes ran their signal handler before the unlink, so the negative control wrote into a file that was then removed ("re-created nothing") and the real checks passed without testing anything. The kill is now built unlink-then-SIGTERM, a trial counts only when the handler itself logged that it ran after the unlink, and a padding trial only when the handler opened the inflated file.
- **A page error in that suite now names its line** (the expression's own line, and V8's parse for a syntax error), instead of a JSON record cut at 900 characters.
- Gates: test-channel-filter ⑪, test-channels-engine ⑬ (control: the engine without the check writes the mirror's exact `[reader, 工作]`), test-channels-aggregate-ui (the stale-panel order built on every machine by holding the page's broadcasts; ⑧ a grant landing while the dialog is open; ⑨/⑨b the window race built; one control bundle with the three fixes reverted: the stale list drawn, 27 messages for 9, 18 for 9), test-exit-forensics (10/10 on the starved CPU).

## 2.369.193 — the pre-push gate is short again: 162 suites in about 4 minutes, everything that boots a server or a browser runs after the push; the Actions fast job is back to a 15-minute limit

### The release gate's fast tier is defined by a rule (B-f4cb)

- **The pre-push gate is short again: 162 suites, about 4 minutes (235–249 s here, was 1051 s); everything that boots a server or a browser runs in the heavy tier after the push.** The fast tier had grown, one reasonable exception at a time, from the two-minute battery it was built as to 184 suites and 1051 s on the dev box and past 15 minutes on GitHub's runner — long enough that the check inside `git push` outlived the ssh connection (nothing was pushed, twice this week) and the mirror's fast job was cancelled at its time limit.
- **The rule, written above the tier table in scripts/ci.mjs:** a suite stays in the fast tier only if it is PURE or in-process (no scratch server, no browser, no git checkout, no real agent CLI / X server / dtach / agent-browser / strace), or the one named pin of a money, credential, kill or architecture law, AND it measured under 10 s. Every fast row now says which, with its measured time (`PURE · 40 ms`). There is one exception by owner decision: the real chat turn (test-chat-e2e).
- **23 suites moved to the heavy tier** (750 s of the old 1051): test-ci-heavy-launch (131 s), test-browser-ephemeral, test-browser-fit, test-window-targets, test-codex-effort-meta, test-exit-forensics, test-channels-aggregate, test-stdout-registry, test-desktop-display, test-discovery-interpret, test-desktop-serve, test-browser-continuity, test-desktop-viewers, test-fork-groups, test-channels-accounts (13 s since 2.369.192), test-browser-mediation, test-cli-cmd-refresh, test-agentd-session, test-restore-smoke (runs on every push, like the other boot smokes), test-browser-profiles, test-design-kit, test-harness-settings, test-codex-sandbox-net. Nothing is lost: the heavy tier runs after every push on the suites the push touched, in full once a day, blocks the next push when red, and runs in full on the Actions mirror.
- **A linked account's sign-in law stays on every push.** test-channels-accounts moved (13 s), but its identity judge — a sign-in is replaced only by a consent naming the same person — is now test-channels-accounts-model in the fast tier (the PURE table moved verbatim, plus pins that the engine's token door and rebind ask it and refuse on its answer).
- **The launcher's pin stays on every push.** test-ci-heavy-launch was fast because a broken detached launch fails silently; test-ci-gate §10 now launches the real `--heavy-launch` once in a stub repository (a separate child, a green marker naming the commit, its pid file and worktree removed) in under a second.
- **The rule is a test.** ci.mjs `FAST_DISQUALIFIERS` / `fastRuleFindings` judge every fast row from its source (the scratch-server passport `vncEnv`, a worktree add, the chrome passport or a headless launch, a real program by name or by `command -v`); test-ci-gate §2b fails a hit the row does not allow, an allowance nothing needs, a missing kind or time, a time ≥ 10 s — each with a negative control — and `node scripts/ci.mjs --census` prints the same findings.
- **test-ci-gate itself 29 s → 5.6 s:** the impact-scope import walk reads each shared file once per computation instead of once per suite (3.9 s → 0.18 s per call, the same answer on all 331 rows), and its `--dirty-ok` leg runs in a stub repository instead of building this checkout (and no longer leaves the real tree dirty while the child starts).
- **The Actions mirror:** the fast job's time limit is back to 15 minutes (2.369.192 raised it to 30 as a stopgap); the heavy job's goes 45 → 60 minutes, because it now carries the moved suites (~10 more minutes on the runner, on a job that measured 32–34).
- Five suites that pinned their own row's exact spelling (`{ name: 'x', tier: 'fast' }`) now accept the row with its `why` (test-ax-paint, test-browser-faces, test-channel-drain, test-status-bar-chips, test-workflow-disk).
- Gates: test-ci-gate (§2b THE TIER RULE with controls, §10 the launcher in a stub repository), `--census`, test-architecture §43 (every suite in exactly one tier).

## 2.369.192 — taking over the agent's browser interrupts everything it was doing there, tells it, and the handback says re-run; Gmail and Lark are read at a steady pace and a linked account's sign-in can no longer be overwritten, stolen by another user's consent or logged out by a concurrent refresh; the first click after the page loads lands

### Lane S2 — the agent's browser: a takeover INTERRUPTS, TELLS and REMINDS; one answer to "which browser is this conversation using" (B-7199; naive-user study 2, T4 / T5 / T7)

The second naive-user study (2.369.186): "Session properties says pinned 'work'; the status-bar chip says 'Agent browser · tester-b-scratch' then '(ephemeral) Second chat'; the live view tab says 'ephemeral (no profile)'" — "实况窗口一直显示旧画面，上面盖着红字 'Live view unavailable: this session is not attached to bp-56a75ced'，点 Reconnect 没反应" — "侧窗格、浮动窗口、键盘输入框三种方式，字全都没到页面里，也没有任何'没送到'的提示" — "永久删除后，'会话属性'仍写 PINNED PROFILE 'bp-17eb27c4'" — "新建对话框里的档案列表丢了"

- **Taking over the agent's browser now interrupts it, tells it, and the handback reminds it to re-run.** The owner: "关于接管浏览器的时候agent脚本，其实应该直接打断所有脚本和agent操作，告知agent发生了打断，交还时提醒它重新运行" (when you take over the agent's browser, interrupt all of its scripts and operations there, tell it so, and remind it to re-run when you hand back). Before, a takeover only refused the agent's NEXT command: whatever it was already doing ran on under your hands, and on a shared browser its scripts and page edits were still allowed while you drove. Now: on a shared (mediated) browser everything the agent had in flight is cut the moment you take over (a script it is running is stopped — measured on Chrome 153 + agent-browser 0.38.1: a 5-second loop stopped at once; a script waiting on a timer, or a `fill` whose single text insertion had already reached the page, cannot be recalled and finishes), and while you drive only reads go through; the command the agent was running ends with `browser_interrupted`; the conversation shows "VibeSpace browser — The user took over …; 2 operations were interrupted: fill, eval" (once per takeover, no billed turn) and the agent reads the same at its next turn; the live view's toast names them too. When you hand back, the message to the agent ends "Re-run what was interrupted: …" (only when something was interrupted or refused). The setting "Fence scripts and page edits while you drive a shared browser" (`browser.fenceScriptsWhileDriven`) is gone — scripts are always interrupted; a stored value is ignored. A handback that could not be delivered now reaches the agent once, not twice.
- **Verify r5 (the interrupt round: three fixes, and the terminate blast measured).** (1) A page verb the takeover cut short is now named on the handback's re-run list even when the agent's command reached the server a moment AFTER you took over: the command's own audit tells the server "I was interrupted" and its verb joins the cycle there, so the "Re-run what was interrupted: …" reminder no longer omits a verb the agent was told `[browser_interrupted]` for. (2) An agent's own words can no longer be spoken by VibeSpace: a command name that is not one of the browser tool's own verbs (a hand-crafted request) is never spelled inside VibeSpace's takeover card, the agent's re-run notice or your "For you" item — only the tool's real verbs (fill, eval, open, click…) are. (3) A takeover card shown before the conversation's chat window has ever opened is no longer lost when the window first loads (it was rebuilt from the transcript, where a display-only card is not written) — the card is held and replayed after the rebuild; the agent's own notice was, and remains, the durable half. Measured (real proxy + Chrome 153): the takeover's script-stop (`Runtime.terminateExecution`) is a page-context primitive, so if the agent's aborted call was only WAITING (nothing of the agent's running) and your own page's script happens to be executing at that instant, that one synchronous run is aborted (one `setInterval` tick, 6/6 forced-busy trials; the interval keeps firing, an in-flight navigation still lands, the page is left intact) — inherent to CDP, bounded and transient, recorded in docs/design-agent-browser-v2 §6.2.2. Gates: test-browser-takeover ⑧ + test-browser-mediation ⑦ (the audit verb joins the cycle, the re-run allow-list) unchanged and green; a new session field `_heldPeerCards` (test-session-schema); the cycle attacks (five calls across two tabs + one on another browser interrupted exactly, 20 cycles = 20 cards / 0 billed turns, the killed-session stash bounded) and the blast measurement left under /tmp/vibespace-lanes/s2-verify-r5*.
- **Taking over a shared browser takes it whole (verify r6).** When you take over a named profile's browser from any chat's live view, every other chat attached to that same browser is interrupted and paused with it — each gets its own card, each is reminded of its own commands at the handback, and a chat that attaches while you drive waits like the others; the agent's refusal now says when a cut command's text had already landed in the page ("check the page before running it again") and when the takeover came between its calls; the live view's toast says when a script running in the page was stopped with it; and a notification delivered to a chat before its window first opened is no longer shown twice when the window opens.
- **One browser, one holder — and one click never wakes every chat on it (verify r7).** With a shared browser open in two live views (two chats, or a phone and a desktop), the second view's Take over is now refused "another viewer took over" while the first is driving, instead of both views driving the same Chrome at once and one chat staying paused after the other view handed back; a view whose window is gone never blocks — the next Take over moves the whole browser. Handing back from one view now sends a billed message only to the chats whose agents had something interrupted or refused; the other chats on that browser get a free notice on their next turn. And when the takeover caught a command whose reply had not come back from the page yet, the agent's refusal says so ("whether it took effect is unknown: check the page") instead of calling it cut.
- **One answer everywhere.** The status-bar chip and its menu, the sidebar card, Session Properties, the live view's title and its strip, and the pin picker now print the same line for a conversation's browser, worked out once on the server: the browser in use ("work", or "no profile (temporary browser)" — the word "ephemeral" is gone from these surfaces), and when the pin says otherwise both names in one amber sentence ("pinned work · running nothing — work could not start — another browser has it open", "pinned work · running Personal — the agent is still on Personal"). Raw profile ids appear only in tooltips; the strip underlines the tab the conversation uses now (its tooltip says so) instead of a "(default)" suffix.
- **The live view follows the conversation's browser.** When a profile is recreated, adopted, detached or pinned, an open live view that was showing the conversation's browser moves to the new one by itself — no red "not attached" overlay left over the old picture; a view you pointed at another browser, a helper's view and a view you are driving stay put. Reconnect re-resolves a view whose browser is gone, and a stale error clears on the next picture or page change.
- **Typing while you drive has a receipt.** Every click and key sent from the live view is answered: if it does not reach the browser within 1.5 s (or the browser refuses it), the bar says "Input is not reaching the browser" and "not delivered — …" instead of "Typing goes to the browser". And typing into a browser shared with all conversations now reaches the page — the sharing proxy refused your own keys while you drove (measured on agent-browser 0.38.1: one input record is one browser call and the stream server reports nothing back; with the fix the real browser receives every key you type while you drive), so it now admits exactly the inputs the live view forwarded.
- **A deleted profile leaves no pin behind.** The Agent browser panel's Delete… (owner ruling A (6): every chat's lease released, the browser stopped, every pin cleared, the directory set aside) now leaves each chat that pinned it saying "work was deleted — its pin was cleared" instead of a raw id or silence, a pin left behind by an earlier delete is cleared at start-up, and the API refuses a set-aside or DELETE of a pinned profile without `unpin` ("N conversation(s) use this profile").
- **The New Session dialog lists every profile** the Agent browser panel lists (a separate-tabs one too — under owner ruling A the pick is the conversation's pin, opened through the keeper on its first browser command) and updates while the dialog is open; the first row reads "No profile (temporary browser)".
- **Session Properties' Agent browser section** updates the moment you pin, keeps the name on one line, uses the window's own buttons, and Esc closes the window.
- **Verify round (the sharing proxy's fence).** The first cut let the agent's own browser commands spend the credits your takeover minted: an `agent-browser click` racing your click landed on the shared browser while you were driving, your own key was refused, and the bar said "delivered". A credit is now bound to the exact click or key it was minted for (measured on agent-browser 0.38.1); nothing else passes the fence while you drive, and nothing of the agent's can burn your credits. **Verify r2:** the credit is also bound to the tab you are looking at — an agent's own connection to the shared browser, on one of its other tabs, could mirror the Enter you were about to press and land it there as if you had typed it (your own Enter refused, the bar saying delivered); now only a call on the tab you drive can spend your credit, and a mirror anywhere else burns nothing. **Verify r3:** while you drive, the agent could still move what you were looking at — its raw `tab` switch on the shared browser was not stopped by the fence, the picture followed and your next keys went to the tab it chose; a takeover is now anchored to the tab it began on: a switch you did not make is refused where it is seen (your keys answer "the browser moved to another tab while you were driving — hand back and take over again to drive it", nothing is forwarded), and the agent's `vibespace-browser tab` / `open` / `back` refusals say by name that they would move your view. Two more doors closed: a method that makes the page ignore every input (armed before your takeover, it swallowed your keys while the bar said delivered) is refused on every lease, and moving the focus to another field while you drive is refused. Receipts say what was seen — "it reached another tab than the one you are looking at and was refused there", "the browser has not answered it" — and over a browser that streams directly the bar says "Typing is sent to the browser" (VibeSpace sees its own write, not the page's answer).
- **Verify r4 (the fence is a census, and the grace is measured).** Three rounds each found the takeover fence one method short, because it was a hand-written list (Input.* + a navigation family, then + the deaf-page arm, then + a focus move). It is now a CENSUS: every one of the 664 methods the installed Chrome (153.0.8010.47) lists in its own protocol has a row in src/cdp-census.js, classed input (15) / view (106) / page-mutation (195) / read (176) / session (11) / harmless (147) / refused (14); while you drive a shared browser, input and view are refused, reads / session / harmless answer, and a method the census does not know (a newer Chrome's) is refused BY NAME until it gets a row — never a silent hole. The page-mutation class (script evaluation, DOM / CSS edits, cookies…) stays open by design (D6) behind ONE new setting, `browser.fenceScriptsWhileDriven`, default OFF (the owner has been asked); ON, that class is refused too and the refusal names the setting. The takeover anchor's 1 s grace (r3 F6: a whole second in which an agent's tab switch was followed) is now 62 ms = 3 × the measured p99 of the daemon's tabs-record latency (2 × 100 real switches on agent-browser 0.38.1 + Chrome 153.0.8010.47: p99 15.4 / 20.4 ms; scripts/measure-anchor-grace.mjs). Gates: test-browser-mediation ⑥ (the census over the pinned protocol fixture, every row's verdict on the anchor's tab and the lease's other tab, the unknown rule, the switch read live by the real proxy, three patched-copy controls), test-browser-mediation-chrome ⑥ (heavy: the launched Chrome's own /json/protocol — extras print and fail — and every class against a real paused lease with the raw endpoint as the oracle), test-browser-fact ③ r4 (the grace pinned to its measurement).
