**Under the hood.** Discovery walks the cursor to the end, resuming across passes when the budget cuts it; the engine peeks one entry per conversation instead of deep-cloning the index; broadcasts carry only the changed conversations (`partial`, merged in place by every client); the full conversation view (identity warnings, reach) is fetched on open (`GET /api/channels/:a/:c`). A latent single-flight bug (the pass's `finally` could run before its promise was stored, wedging the account's loop) is fixed. An attachment's bytes are written and evicted asynchronously (up to 100 MB; data/ may sit on a slow mount), each write through its own temp file. The row pill is the short form ("19s ago", "refresh paused") so it fits a 188 px panel in every language; the full sentence is its tooltip. Gmail keeps its mailbox cursor across restarts (it used to re-walk every thread) and its health line / Edit dialog show the scope it really reads.

**Verify round (lane R2, 2026-09-26) — six findings, each reproduced on the build's bytes first.**
- **An account- or rule-wide daily wake cap now holds under a burst.** One pass that brought news to 100 conversations under a whole-account assignment with a cap of 5 started 100 billed turns whenever delivering a wake took more than a couple of milliseconds (it always does): each conversation's wake read the shared ledger before delivering and wrote it after. The wakes of one account- or rule-wide assignment now run one at a time, so exactly 5 go out and the other 95 wait with "daily wake cap reached (5 of 5 in 24 h)".
- **`vibespace-channels refresh` and `read --fresh` never say "0 new" without fetching.** Twenty refreshes at once used to answer eighteen of them with another refresh's result — "refreshed: 0 new" on stale data. Each refresh now waits for any fetch in flight and then runs its own.
- **An agent cannot use up an account's minute.** Agent refreshes together may spend at most 25 % of an account's per-minute vendor budget (new setting `channels.agentBudgetSharePct`); past it the refusal says so with the wait. A spent budget's sentence now says how much of it agent refreshes took.
- **A vendor rate limit is said from the first failure.** The account line said "last sync 12 s ago" from a failed fetch and the failure line waited for the third failure; now "last sync" is the last good fetch, and a failure shows at once as "rate limited — retrying in 30 s".
- **A setting out of range is said.** Typing 1800 into "at most 900" stored 1800 while the channels engine silently used 900. The Settings number field now keeps the value inside the row's own bounds and says so in a toast ("kept at the maximum, 900"); the engine reads the same bounds and logs a clamp once.
- **The upgrade's boot line reports what it changed.** The migration's log line always said zeros (it was filled a moment after it was printed) and a channels store that refused writes was recorded as migrated; the counts are now the rows changed, they ride the migration ledger, and a refusing store fails the run so the next boot retries it.

**Verify round r3 (lane R2, 2026-09-26) — one major, reproduced on the r2 bytes first, and one minor of a known class; the rest of the round returned lows (recorded in docs/design-communication-panel §6.5's "Lane R2 verify lows").**
- **An agent's refresh no longer pokes a vendor that just rate-limited the account.** A 429 puts an account into a back-off (30 s, then 2, 5, 15 min); the timer honoured it, but the agent's `refresh` and a window's open ran through the same door as the owner's own Refresh press, which bypasses it on purpose. Forty agent refreshes across forty conversations inside a 30 s back-off made fifteen vendor calls in a second (only the agent share bounded them), every one refused again, and the failure count climbed from 1 to 16 — the account's back-off jumped to its 15-minute maximum and the OWNER's whole account stopped polling because an agent pressed refresh. Now an agent refresh (and `read --fresh`) during a back-off is refused by name with the wait — "the vendor refused this account's last fetch (rate-limited) — it is retried in 27 s; read what is there now" (`backoff`, 429 + Retry-After, exit 4) — and makes no call; a window opened during the back-off is hot but pokes nothing; the owner's own Refresh press keeps its bypass (a person pressed it) and a failed press counts as one more failure.
- **The Channels panel and a conversation window re-read on every reconnect.** A digest broadcast sent while the socket was down never arrives, and a pass broadcasts only the rows it changed — so a row's unread count, freshness pill or held-hits note missed during a network blip stayed stale until the next whole-account change. Both now re-read once the socket is back (the same rule the desktop-app launcher and the For-you inbox follow).
- **Concurrent refreshes of one conversation share one fetch (verify r4, major).** Twenty agent refreshes of the same conversation fired together made twenty vendor calls — the per-conversation floor is asked before the wait for a running pass, and after the wait every caller ran a pass of its own — three refreshes queued behind a timer pass that had just fetched their conversation added three more, and five windows opened on one stale conversation made five. A pass that ran while a refresh waited and fetched THAT conversation now answers it (a real fetch of the conversation, completed after the call began; the r2 rule stands — a pass with no entry for the conversation never does). One fetch, every answer honest, the agent share charged once. Also: the owner's Refresh press that fails into a back-off now answers the retry instant (Retry-After on the route, "rate limited — retrying in N s" in the toast) instead of a bare "the refresh failed" that invited the next press — each press inside a 429 is a real vendor refusal and a step of the account's back-off (30 s → 2 → 5 → 15 min), so three presses parked an account 15 minutes while the toast said only "failed".
- **A refresh is a request the account's own fetch loop judges — the seam three rounds patched is closed (verify r5, structural).** r2, r3 and r4 each found one money defect at the same place: the caller's refresh deciding a vendor call against the account's running fetch pass, with N callers deciding at once (an answer taken from somebody else's pass; the back-off door; a pass per waiter). Now the owner's Refresh press, a window's open and `vibespace-channels refresh` only file a request into the account's set; the fetch loop alone drains it — every gate (a vendor back-off, the agents' share of the minute, the vendor budget, the per-conversation floor) judged once per conversation at drain time, each conversation fetched at most once per pass however many asked, a fetch the timer was making anyway carrying its waiters, and every caller answered by the drain that judged its conversation with that conversation's own outcome: fetched with its count, refused by name with the wait, or the pass's own failure. A decision for this new shape, in plain words: **inside a vendor back-off your own Refresh press is honoured once per back-off window** (one real attempt — if the vendor refuses it again the wait grows one step and that press is spent); every further press in the same window is refused with "rate limited — retrying in N s" and makes no call; an agent's refresh, a window's open and the open window's heartbeat never call the vendor during a back-off. Also: at most 200 refreshes may wait per account (past it: `refresh-queue-full`, 429, try again in a moment); a refresh still unanswered after 30 s answers "still running" and the window updates when it lands (the panel's toast says so — never "Up to date"); an account changed or removed while a refresh waited answers `account-changed`; the toast now words a spent budget, the floor, the full queue, the changed account and a restarting server in your language; pending refreshes live in memory — a restart drops them and never turns them into a burst of fetches at boot. The closing check on this shape found and fixed two more: a steady stream of refreshes could keep an account busy so its own timed polling never ran, and a refresh asked for during a long poll of a big account waited for the whole poll — now the loop takes up pending refreshes between every two fetches and a busy account still does its timed polling on its next pass.
- **The independent closing verify (r6): an agent's storm can no longer crowd out your own Refresh, and a refused refresh is told so at once.** Two hundred refreshes filed by one agent while a fetch was in flight filled the account's waiting set and refused the owner's own Refresh press (and a window's open) with "too many refreshes waiting" — now an agent may fill at most 180 of the 200 slots, the last 20 are yours. And a refresh the loop REFUSED (the floor, the agents' share, a spent budget, a vendor back-off) in the first second of a long poll was only told at the poll's end — behind an 18 s poll `vibespace-channels refresh` printed "refresh started — still running" for a request that was never made; a refusal is now answered the moment it is judged (an `ok` still lands when the poll ends, which keeps a stream of refreshes from starving the account's own polling). A timed or forced poll asked of a busy account now runs after the one in flight instead of vanishing into it (a connect's first ingest asked of a busy account used to be silently skipped).
- **Verify r7 (the round after the closing verify): a true refresh answer no longer waits for the whole poll, a stream of refreshes can no longer push your own polling behind it, and repeated Re-authorize presses no longer pile up full ingests.** r6 answered a REFUSED refresh at once but still held a TRUE answer for the poll's end — behind a long poll `vibespace-channels refresh` and the panel's Refresh said "still running" for a fetch that had landed seconds earlier (measured: heard at 2.8 s of a 2.8 s poll; now at 0.12 s). Delivering it at its fetch is safe now because the poll takes the timer's turn at every fetch boundary and alternates one requested conversation with one due one — a burst of refreshes serves the account's own due conversations DURING the burst (35 of 35 inside a 2.5 s storm; 0 of 35 without the alternation) instead of after it, and a trickle of refreshes heavier than the vendor carries still leaves the due list half the fetches. Three Re-authorize presses (or option saves) while the account was busy used to run three full forced ingests one after another — now ONE runs after the poll in flight. `vibespace-channels refresh` exits 4 (a refusal with its sentence — retry) on `account-changed` and `stopped` instead of 1 (an error). Held under attack: the waiting set's reserve is per account and counts a window's open as yours (many windows opened at once on a stale account can spend your own 20 slots — the rule, low), a job token never reaches the channels routes, a refusal leaves the waiting set the instant it is answered, an agent and you asking for the same conversation at once is ONE fetch charged to you, the timer's ledger, settlement under an adapter failure, the words in zh/ja through textContent.
- **Verify r8 (the independent closing verify of r7): under a steady stream of refreshes the earliest request for each conversation no longer waits for the stream to stop, and your own Refresh press is served before an agent's.** r7's poll never ends while requests keep coming (it takes the timer's turn at every fetch boundary), and its drain put every boundary's new requests IN FRONT of the ones already waiting and never let a repeat request for a conversation fetched earlier in that poll join the one still queued — so the first waiter for each conversation was pushed back by every later boundary until the stream stopped (measured on r7: with four windows re-filing, the owner's one Refresh press said "still running" at 30 s; 85 of 398 requests waited past 2 s, up to 11.8 s; 395 vendor calls for 398 requests on five conversations — no coalescing), and the owner's press on a due conversation behind 180 agent requests was fetched 181st (r6's LIFO riders had put it first; r7's filing order put it last). Now the requested items at the front of a poll are served in filing order across boundaries, a repeat request rides the one still queued (one vendor call), and the owner's press / a window's open go before agents' (each class in filing order). Held under attack on r7's bytes (measured): an `ok` is durable and readable the instant it is heard (the log, the index, `readFor`); a poll that fails after an `ok` still broadcasts its conversation; a taken timer turn runs discovery once per poll; one queued poll per account with `force` sticky (30 option saves during one held poll = one forced ingest; a forced ask during the queued poll runs one more; a forced ask racing the poll's end is not lost); the owner's reserve; settlement under a throw, a remove mid-fetch and stop; the back-off window (one honoured press per window, the exponent stepped once, a second window after an outside failure); a restart. Recorded, not fixed: the panel's "N new" toast can precede the window's repaint by the poll's remainder (the broadcast lands at the poll's end); a request filed inside a fetch waits for a taken turn's discovery walk; a stopped engine's in-flight poll keeps fetching to its queue's end; an ingest in flight when its account is removed re-creates that conversation's index row (invisible in the digest); the CLI's refused-set census derives from the route's table only.
- **Verify r9 (the second structural closure): the refresh scheduler is now one small, separately tested decision — and four rough edges it had are gone.** Seven verify rounds each found one money-class ordering defect in how the account's fetch loop scheduled refreshes, every fix written into the same asynchronous loop that the next round then found a new ordering bug in. The whole decision — which conversation is fetched next, who is answered with what, when a refusal is said, when your own polling gets its turn — is now a pure step function (`src/channel-drain.js`, 17 numbered rules) that the engine only drives, checked by a seeded random walk of 36 × 3000 steps asserting every rule at every step, with a mutant per rule that must turn it red. Visible changes: when your Refresh press brings news, the window repaints at the same moment as the "N new" toast (before, a whole poll later); an agent's refreshes judged together can no longer overspend its share of the account's minute; a steady stream of refreshes no longer keeps one poll running forever (it ends after 25 request fetches in a row and the next starts at once, so a Re-authorize or option save queued behind it runs); discovery never runs ahead of your own waiting press; a stopped engine or a removed account makes no further vendor call (43 before); and inside a rate-limit back-off, if you leave (your press times out) before its fetch, an agent riding it is not fetched on your press. Nothing else changed: the 70-cell table, every r2–r8 shape, the routes, the CLI and the words hold unchanged.

**Gates.** New fast `test-channel-drain` (256 — r9: the PURE drain's seeded walk, 36 seeds × 3000 steps over three profiles against an independent oracle, every one of its 17 rules asserted at every step and exercised, exactly-once / honest ok / no lost answer / liveness; the 70-cell table and the r2–r8 repros in the model's terms; fairness (the i-th of 35 due rows within i request fetches, a lone request behind 873 due rows waits one due fetch, the bound 25); 22 mutants each turning its repro AND the walk red; the census). New fast `test-channels-aggregate` (278 — r9: every control re-pointed at the model / driver seams through a closed world, r7's drain as three per-rule copies, ⑥g(11b)'s press moment made deterministic, ⑥g(8b) the broadcast at the fetch + its control; 276 — r8: ⑥g(11) the front run — a one-key 15 ms stream heard within a round (max 61 ms, 41 calls for 99 requests), the owner's one press under a 4-lane stream heard at 181 ms, the owner's rider ahead of 40 agent riders at position 1 (+ r7's drain as the control: 2706 ms and 74 calls, 1559 ms, position 41); 271 — r7: ⑥g(8) an `ok` heard at ITS fetch behind a 1.8 s pass (+ r6's ok-for-the-end control: heard at its end), ⑥g(9) a 2.5 s saturating storm's 35 due rows served DURING it + a 25 ms trickle with a mid-way re-due (64/70 due fetches, 0 pending) (+ the no-interleave control: 0/35 during, 25/70), ⑥g(10) ONE pass queued per account, `force` sticky (+ r6's per-ask control: 3 forced passes, 80 fetches), ⑥f's at-start control (the RIGHT fetch answered at its start — caught by the instant alone, 3/3), ⑥g(6)'s one-over-budget control, ⑥g(1) counted during the storm AND after `idle()`; r6: ⑥f's judge reads the answer's own instant (`answeredAt`), ⑥g(3b) the owner's reserve, ⑥g(6) the budget cut mid-pass — the two budget lines ⑥f's `budget` state never reached, ⑥g(7) a refusal heard at the first boundary of a 2.7 s pass, each with a patched-copy control; ⑥f (r5): THE CONCURRENCY TABLE, 70 cells — {1, 5, 20} callers × {one key, N keys} × {idle, a timer pass inside the fetch of our key, a timer pass not fetching it, a vendor back-off, the budget spent, the agent share spent, the floor fresh} × {agent, owner} against a scripted adapter that answers after 20 ms — asserting the vendor calls per key (0 or 1 per pass; the owner's ONE honoured press per back-off window, a second round of presses making none), every `ok` a fetch of ITS key that ended after the call began with `appended` = the news, the agent share charged exactly the agent-caused fetches, every refusal named with its wait, no waiter left in the set; controls re-pointed at the drain: answer-everyone-from-the-first-fetch lies 19 of 20, the gate line removed calls 40× and escalates to 41, one-item-per-waiter calls 20 / 5 / 4, every-press-honoured makes 2 calls and climbs to 3; run 3× for flake; ⑥e: 20 concurrent agent refreshes of one conversation, 5 windows opened on one stale conversation and 3 refreshes queued behind a timer pass each make ONE vendor call, the share charged once (control: the copy running its own pass after every wait makes 20 / 5 / 4); ⑥d: 40 agent refreshes + a window open inside a scripted 429 back-off make zero calls and leave `consecutiveFailures` at 1, the owner's press runs and its failure answers the wait it escalated into, the back-off lifts; control: the copy without the gate calls 40× and escalates to 41; the route maps, the CLI's refusal list and the two reconnect re-reads pinned; incl. patched-copy controls: the old 5-page discovery bound, a scheduler that polls everything, the per-conversation-only wake (100 wakes past a cap of 5) and the foreign-pass refresh (18 of 20 lie) must go red; the agent share at 100 % starves the hot rows); new heavy `test-channels-aggregate-ui` (25, zh). Updated: test-channel-filter (95), -caps (80), -acl (65), -store (135), test-channels-engine (142), -push (70), -lane-parity (33), -gmail-shape (95), -lark-shape (84), -accounts (125), -agent-cli (38 — r7: the refused set DERIVED from the agent route's status table, the two reply-only retry-ables excepted by name and proven absent from the request-set region, one fixture per code driven to exit 4 with its sentence, `pending` exit 0, a channel-words case per code), -groups-ui (61), test-oauth-field-parity (245), test-migrations (197). Heavy, rewritten for the no-Track model: test-channels-e2e (130), -groups-e2e (39), test-integrations-ui (136), test-channels-i18n (41; the search and rule-grain dialogs are new census surfaces).

## 2.369.184 — the 2.369.183 mirror red was the pen leg reading Chrome's post-layout mouse re-target, not the pen; and a grouped taskbar button no longer grows a hover chooser under a pointer that did not move (a rebuild under a resting pointer after a click or an Esc)

- **A grouped taskbar button no longer grows a hover chooser under a pointer that did not arrive.** Click a grouped button (or dismiss its hover list with Esc) and leave the pointer there: when any window title changed — a terminal's or an agent's, which happens all the time — the taskbar re-rendered the button under the pointer and the list popped up 300 ms later, unasked (5 of 5 when constructed). The hover is now armed only by the pointer MOVING over the button, once per visit; a press spends the visit until the pointer leaves, and the visit belongs to the group, so a re-render keeps it. A pointer that moved away while the button was being re-rendered still gets its next hover (PURE `hoverStep`, src/lib/taskbar-group.js).
- **The pen leg's mirror red (2.369.183) was the test, not the pen.** test-taskbar-group-ui (l) read the LAST pointerenter's type after the chooser opened; one or two frames after the open Chrome re-computes hover and moves the MOUSE pointer onto the button where the pen rests, so a slow runner read `mouse` (master's leg, CPU ×20: 17/20 red; ×1: 0/20). The leg now attributes the open to the pen's own typed enter (scripts/pen-hover-judge.mjs), waits for Chrome's re-target so the race is in every record, and runs once more at CPU ×20. `--only l|o [--trials N] [--throttle R] [--trace]` runs one leg N times.
- Gates: test-taskbar-group §10 (the judge over 360 fake-clock interleavings) + §11 (hoverStep over 378 timed scripts), each with patched-copy controls; test-taskbar-group-ui (l2) + (o) + CONTROL 2 (o). Chrome pins: (l) and (o) 40/40 at CPU ×20; the whole heavy suite green ×3 on one core shared with 8 busy loops (master: (a) and (l) red there).

## 2.369.183 — one session, many browsers (lane P): the Agent browser window lists EVERY browser of its session (its own, its helpers', its profiles), a per-conversation browser limit, pop out / fold back, and two grouped chats whose browsers follow them (docs/design-browser-multiview.zh.md)

The owner: "确实 得考虑一个会话里可能有多个并行浏览器，怎么展示的问题，你来设计实现一下吧。另外也得考虑如果两个tabbed窗口每个都打开了各自的浏览器，怎么展示的问题" — and on the design: "这个上限应该是一个属于对话属性的东西，可以调整" / "如果我已经开了并排展示俩 agent 对话呢？变成四列？" / "那得考虑重新合并的操作逻辑".

- **One window, every browser.** The Agent browser window's tab strip now lists all of a session's browsers — its attached profiles, its own browser, and each helper's (sub-agent's) browser — with who is driving (`agent` / `you`) and a state dot (running a command / running / released — hollow, "the next command starts it again"). It appears with two or more browsers; one browser looks as before. A browser that starts later becomes a tab at the END of the strip and never changes the picture you are watching — not even while you have taken over.
- **Helpers' browsers are watchable.** Click a helper's tab to see its picture (its own browser, never the parent's). A claude helper is named after its task ("Helper: check prices") when exactly one helper opened a browser at a time and its own call's result names it; two at once, or a codex helper, read "Helper 1 / Helper 2" — never guessed.
- **The strip folds** by priority into `▾+N` on narrow windows: the tab you are looking at never folds, a browser running a command outlasts a quiet one.
- **A limit per conversation.** The `2/3` chip at the strip's end is this conversation's running browsers against ITS limit (default 3 — Settings → Agent browser → *Browsers one conversation may run at once*; a Task Group can set its own default for its new conversations; each conversation can change its own from the chip's − / + or in Session Properties → Browsers at once, and a resume keeps it). Red at the limit; clicking it lists only this conversation's running browsers (helpers' too), each with Stop (a profile another conversation also uses says "detach it instead"). The agent's next browser past the limit is refused and told where the limit is changed. The machine's own ceiling (six, shared with desktop apps) stays, and its refusal now names only the asking conversation's own browsers — everything else is a count, never another session's name or id.
- **Released after the turn.** A conversation's own browser (and its helpers') is let go 3 minutes after its turn ends (Settings → Agent browser → *Release a conversation's browser after its turn ends*, 0 = never); the tab stays, hollow; the next command starts it again. Never while you drive it or watch it in a live view, and a live view never starts it. Chat sessions only: a terminal session publishes no turn, so its browser is kept until the browser tool's own idle timeout.
- **Pop out and fold back.** Right-click a strip tab → *Open in new window* opens a second Agent browser window of the same session showing that browser (same strip, its own selection). Fold it back from its title-bar menu (*Fold back into the Agent browser window* — the main window selects that tab) or by dropping its icon on the other window / its group (the one drag exception folds back instead of grouping two views of one session). Closing the main window leaves the next one as the main one.
- **Two grouped chats, each with its browser.** Still two panes, never four columns: a chat's browser is born beside it only while the chat is not yet side by side; otherwise it arrives as a pulsing tab (on the browser side, else its chat's side) and nothing on screen moves. With chats on the left and their browsers on the right, switching the chat switches the right to its browser (and clicking a browser switches the chat) — the views are already connected, nothing reconnects. When the other side shows a chat you placed there, nothing follows. The phone shows one pane and never follows.
- **Verify fixes (lane P verify r1, 2026-09-26).** A live view never STARTS a browser of any kind: a click on a hollow (stopped) profile tab now says it is released instead of launching it, and a live view opened before the conversation's first browser command waits, hollow, "Not started yet — the next command starts it" — it no longer asks the browser tool a question that starts a background daemon. Folding back the window you are DRIVING keeps your control: it moves to the other window before this one closes (no hand-back to the agent, no notice); driving in both windows is refused in plain words. A helper is named after its task only when its own call's result names the browser it opened and no other helper was opening one at the same time — never by order. A Task Group's browser limit applies to its NEW conversations (a running one keeps the limit it started with). A released own browser beside an attached profile says "Released — used again only when no profile is attached".
- **Verify fixes (lane P verify r2, 2026-09-26).** A terminal-mode agent's browser is no longer released 3 minutes after its last browser command while it is still working — the release after the turn now applies only where the session reports its turn (chat); a terminal session's browser ends by the browser tool's own idle timeout, as before. A live view that picks up a browser while it is still starting waits for the start to finish (a start that fails is what the view shows — it never starts one itself). And a conversation's browser is started with the idle timeout the conversation was spawned with, so the agent's first command (or a live view) no longer replaces the browser VibeSpace just started when the idle setting changed since the spawn; the new setting applies from the conversation's next start (a resume). Gates: `test-browser-ephemeral` (fast, 188 — the wiring's own facts over a terminal and a chat session, the slow-launch call order for own / helper / attachment, the failed start, the launch's idle; four patched-copy controls), `test-architecture` (fast, 298 — §61), heavy `test-browser-live` (128, 1 skip — the REAL 0.38.1: a view mid-start then the agent's command, one daemon, the recorded pid, never restarted; the pre-fix launch as the control).
- Gates: `test-browser-handles` (fast, 152 — the list's truth table + a negative control, the child rung, the three naming outcomes, the bridge's helper relay), `test-live-strip` (new, fast, 36 — the fold at 1400 / 900 / 600, the chip, the conversation cap beside the machine ceiling, two patched-copy controls), `test-browser-ephemeral` (fast, 139 — the refusal never carries another session's name / lease id with a patched-copy control, the release timing table, the real keeper's cap + release), `test-chain-layout` (fast, 83 — partnerFor / followFor / livePlacement / foldBackTarget + two controls), `test-session-schema` (7), `test-contributions` (219), `test-browser-pin` (181); heavy `test-browser-live` (116 — a helper relay draws its picture, a four-tab strip, a new browser mid-takeover lands at the tail on the same socket, the phone strip folds) and `test-browser-multiview` (new, 29 — real clicks: the follow with zero reconnects, the quiet tab, two chats side by side, pop out + both fold-backs, reload, phone).
- **Integration (2.369.183 — lanes F / H / I / J / M / N were already in 2.369.180–.182).** ONE refusal code for "a browser a view will not start": lane H's `browser_stopped` for every kind (P's `browser_released` is retired for views; the Stop route keeps it for "not started") — a view that WAS showing the browser greys by name and keeps its last frame (H), a view just switched to it reads the tab's own hollow words (P), and either picks the browser up by itself. ONE `EPHEMERAL_REF`, H's `~ephemeral` (persisted in 2.369.180 layouts; P's `@ephemeral` retired). ONE relay key over both helper shapes (P's view by handle, H's `~child:` recorder tap). The launch passes the pairs' idle once (H r4 LOW 5 and P r2 F2 were the same finding; H's `pairsIdleMs` reads P's PURE one) and keeps H's launch mark; P's in-flight wait runs before H's process judge. A fold-back's `pass` is not a stale-approval moment for J's sweep. A strip tab's *Open in new window* passes `popOut` — since lane H's naive-study fix a plain open FOCUSES the session's one view, so the pop-out is the one deliberate second window. The strip is its own row above I's bar (its `▾+N` is `stripMoreBtn`; `state().stripFolded`), the bind row keeps I's unbound-only rule inside P's `registerLiveViewMenus`, the auto-bind keeps H's `EPHEMERAL_REF` target inside P's placement; P's popovers and menus close through M's outside-press closer (createPopover / showContextMenu); test-browser-multiview hands its server `vncEnv()` (N's §57); P's turnKnown pin is test-architecture §61; test-browser-ephemeral's P sections are ⑦ / ⑧; P's F2 control strips H's attachment wait too (layered guards).

## 2.369.182 — RELEASE NOTE: sessions started before this version have no VIBESPACE_SESSION_CWD, so the browser tool writes only under /tmp and ~/Downloads until the session is restarted (Terminate + Resume). Five lanes: the window-targets refusal codes no longer depend on the machine and a window screenshot never lands in the agent's directory (E3); split tabs v2 (F); a grouped taskbar button opens its group (K); floating menus close on a click into an app's picture (M); VibeSpace's own tools stop asking for permission every step, and the browser tool's file reads and writes stay in the session's frame (L)

**Release note.** Sessions started before this version have no VIBESPACE_SESSION_CWD, so the browser tool writes only under /tmp and ~/Downloads until the session is restarted (Terminate + Resume): lane L's write fence is the directory the SESSION was started in, exported as `VIBESPACE_SESSION_CWD` on every spawn path — a session spawned by an earlier version does not carry it, and the tool then fences writes to `/tmp` and `~/Downloads` only.

### Lane E3 — mirror red on .181: window-targets refusal order was environment-dependent

The Actions mirror of 2.369.181 (fast tier, ubuntu-latest) was red on test-window-targets — 259 passed, 2 failed, 3 skipped — while this box and the integration's own fast tier were 320/0. A mirror-only red names the machine-dependent gate first: here the product answered a different refusal CODE depending on which capability the machine lacked.

- **Reproduced here by constructing the runner's shape** (a PATH without python3 / the gi binding / xdotool / Xvfb, DISPLAY and the session bus unset): exactly 259 / 2 / 3. Before the fix, `click @e1` before any snapshot answered `mode_pixels` (the `auto` probe ran first and resolved pixels because no tree was reachable) where this box answered `ref_unknown`; an `auto` window's snapshot answered the helper's own code — `python3_missing` (no python3), `a11y_unavailable` (python3 without gi, the runner's case), `helper_error` (gi but no accessibility bus: libatspi aborts) — where this box answered `mode_pixels`.
- **Preconditions before probes.** `act` checks a `@ref` (no snapshot yet, or a ref the last snapshot never minted ⇒ `ref_unknown`) right after the share-mode check and BEFORE the `auto` probe starts anything: the same answer on every machine, no helper process spawned.
- **An unreachable tree is one verdict.** Under an `auto` share, a snapshot that cannot reach a tree for ANY reason — the new closed set `TREE_UNREACHABLE` in src/window-targets.js: helper_missing, python3_missing, helper_timeout, helper_error, a11y_unavailable — resolves the window to pixel mode and is refused `mode_pixels`; the reason it saw is named in the sentence ("the accessibility tree is unreachable here (a11y_unavailable: …) — pixel mode") and rides as `reason: {code, why}` on the agent route. Attach's resolution names the reason too. An explicit tree share and the user's own desktop still pass the helper's code through (no other road there); a caller's error (`bad-request`) is never folded.
- **A remembered probe answer belongs to its environment.** The accessibility / portal / ScreenCast probe memos were keyed by name alone, so a process asking from a second environment heard the first one's YES. They are keyed now by PATH, the session and accessibility buses, DISPLAY / WAYLAND_DISPLAY, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (and the interpreter + helper for the accessibility probe).
- **The suite is honest about the machine.** §4r builds the runner's shape on EVERY machine (PATH = an empty directory, DISPLAY and the buses unset) and makes the tree unreachable four ways, each proven by an evidence line; the two mirror legs answer one code in all four (`ref_unknown` with no probe spawned, `mode_pixels` with the reason varying), and a patched copy restoring the old order is the negative control (it answers the machine — the mirror's red). §2 pins the environment-keyed memo (control: the key without the environment) and derives `TREE_UNREACHABLE`'s coverage from the helper runner's own refusals + the helper's import refusal. §5's no-tree window now sits on a pid no machine can hand out, so its mode legs run everywhere (the `if (!real)` gate is gone). Every SKIP says what is missing (§3's reason reaches §4's and §5's skips; the xdotool half of a control is skipped by name instead of passing silently).
- Gates: test-window-targets 346 / 0 / 0 here (×3), 286 / 0 / 3 in three constructed runner shapes (no python3; python3 without gi on a bare Xvfb; gi without a bus); test-window-reach 98 (+3 pure legs: four reasons one resolution, the one-line clip, a tree share ignores the probe).
- **A window screenshot never lands in your current directory** (the owner's pixel-mode test: `vibespace-window screenshot <handle>` without `--out` wrote `window-<handle>-<ts>.png` into the agent's cwd — the production checkout). Without `--out` the PNG goes to `<temp dir>/vibespace-window/<handle>-<ts>.png` (a private 0700 directory) and the path is printed as before; a relative `--out` is resolved against the SESSION's directory (`VIBESPACE_SESSION_CWD`, when the spawn exported it) or else that temp directory — never the shell's cwd. An `--out` under `~/.ssh`, `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.vibespace`, a `.git` directory, any other `~/.<name>` entry or VibeSpace's own data directory is refused `write_path_refused` by name (judged after symbolic links, the browser CLI's credential-store rule copied into this single-file tool), a final-component link or a missing directory is `out_unusable`, and every refusal is decided before the request, so nothing is captured. The agent manual says where screenshots land and shows `--out`. Gates: test-window-targets 363 / 0 / 0 (×2; §6 = 17 new legs, red 13 on the pre-fix CLI, the old default in a patched copy writing into the cwd as the control), test-window-target (heavy) 146 / 0 / 0, build (test-architecture 309, ws-contract 5, session-schema 5).

### Lane F — split tabs v2 (lane F): a strip half per side, drag a tab to reorder or move it across, both sides switchable, paths from a chat open side by side, two new settings (inc-muhfb5al-jzk6, docs/design-split-ux.zh.md §8)

The owner (2.369.177, Report a problem): "这个UX非常奇怪啊，首先并排之后tab列表都在左侧，比较难看出来哪边是哪个tab。其次我没法拖动tab重排序，最后我只能调整右侧展示的tab而无法调整左侧的。建议加入tab拖动+直接两侧分开展示的功能。" Then: "另外以后从窗口打开文件路径/本地链接的时候默认side by side展示吧。然后拖动窗口后是直接side by side还是普通tabbed，以及打开文件路径/链接默认用并排还是独立窗口也都加入设置选项。"

- **A strip half per side.** In side-by-side mode every tab belongs to a side (`split.left` / `split.right` in PURE `chain-layout.js`), and the tab bar is two halves laid on the panes' own columns — the title bar is a CSS subgrid of the window's grid, so the halves follow the divider while you drag it (±1 px every frame, measured) with no script. The tab shown in each pane is highlighted and underlined in its colour; the glyph sits over the divider. Measured before: at ratio 0.5 the right pane's tab sat 282 px left of the right pane; at 0.7 every tab sat over the left pane.
- **Both sides switchable.** A tab of the left half shows on the left, of the right half on the right (D19 (a), which only ever replaced the non-anchor pane, is retired). A press inside a pane now focuses that pane, so the keyboard and the menus act on the tab under your hand.
- **Drag a tab sideways to reorder it** (a marker shows the slot, Esc cancels); the first 8 px decide — sideways = reorder, down = the old pull-out. Across the middle the tab MOVES to the other side (a tab you were looking at stays visible there; its old side shows its neighbour); the last tab out of a side ends side by side. No drag ever creates a split. `Ctrl+Shift+PageUp / PageDown` and command mode `{` / `}` move the active tab within its list (a regular browser tab may keep the chord for itself — `{` / `}` always work). A window dropped on a group lands at the slot under the pointer.
- **Paths from a chat open side by side** (Settings → Window → *Opening a file path or link from a window*: side by side — the default — / as a tab / in its own window): a path or local link opened from a chat is born beside THAT chat (never the active window; if the window is already side by side, on the side the chat is not on); the same path again shows its tab (a `:line` link moves the editor). A text file goes straight to the editor.
- **Merge drop → side by side** (Settings → Window → *Dropping a window onto another*: tabs — the default — / side by side at once): the dragged window lands on the right; the toast offers **Undo** (it goes back where it stood) and **Unsplit** (stay grouped as tabs).
- **Other clients** apply a reorder / move / switch / swap IN PLACE (no content re-parented); a window still being opened asynchronously on another client (a CSV viewer) keeps its group waiting for it instead of landing free — which used to break the group on that client's next save. Layouts carry `order` + the side lists; a record written before this restores by one repair rule (no migration).
- **Fixed on the way:** a tab group dragged by its title bar onto another window's icon orphaned its other tabs inside the hidden host — the group now just moves; closing a tab left of the active one no longer switches the group to the active tab's right-hand neighbour (the index slid; it is re-found by window id now).
- **Verify fixes (adversarial verifier r1, each reproduced red first):** (1) **a divider drag no longer snaps back when another client changes the group during it** — client 1 clicked a tab while client 2 dragged the divider 0.50 → 0.15; the record, held for client 2's pointerup, copied its 0.50 over the drag and the apply's anti-echo clear dropped client 2's save (0.50 on every client a second later). A user's divider act is now held locally until a save carries it (PURE `holdRatio` / `heldRatio`, ≤ 60 s); both in-place apply paths keep it and it is re-sent once at the drag's real time. Measured: 0.15 on both clients and on disk, exactly one send, no echo; an idle client never re-sends. (2) **no tab under the window controls on a narrow window** — a 640 px window dragged to 0.85 drew the right tab over □: the right column now keeps a floor (the controls + a tab's room), the tail is a margin, the ⫿ badge steps aside on a tight column. (3) with *Side by side at once*, the notification's **Unsplit** puts the dropped window back at the slot it was dropped on (it went last). (4) dropping a window onto a group that is **already** side by side now says so with **Undo** (window back where it was, the split back to how it was). (5) the docs now say it plainly: a press shows a tab, so a dragged tab always arrives shown. (6) after a reload the active window id followed the restore's re-keying (it named a window that no longer existed). Not fixed, recorded in design §8: the lane commit's trailer (history is not rewritten); two clients holding the same sessions under different window ids (pre-existing sync core).
- Gates: `scripts/test-chain-layout.mjs` (new, fast, 63 — a seeded 2 400-step walk of every verb + the held ratio + six patched-copy controls), `test-window-binding-model` ④⑤ (fast, 130), `test-contributions` (209), `test-split-ux` leg 12 (heavy, L1–L11 + L1b / L4a / L7b–L7d with runtime controls).

### Lane K — a grouped taskbar button opens its group on click; the chooser comes on hover or when the group is already in front (lane K)

The owner, on a taskbar button reading "VibeSpace 主开发 · 2 windows grouped": every click on it popped a two-row chooser instead of doing anything — "这个体验比较差". Now a grouped button behaves like a window button first:

- **Click = open the group.** The host window is restored if minimized, focused and raised, showing the tab that was already on show — the same activation a single window's button performs (`activateWindow`, one path for both).
- **Click when the group is already in front = the chooser** (the group's windows, the one on show marked), so a keyboard or a touch screen always reaches the list. A row switches straight to that tab; Esc, a click elsewhere or a row closes it.
- **Hover = the chooser**, after ~300 ms of hover intent, on a mouse or a pen — never on touch, never while a window / tab drag or a resize is in progress, never while another menu or popover is open. It never takes the focus; moving onto it keeps it open, hovering a row highlights it, and it closes 250 ms after the pointer leaves the button and the chooser. Crossing the button on the way to its neighbour opens nothing.
- **Keyboard:** the grouped button is focusable; Enter / Space = the click rule, ArrowUp = the chooser (focus on the active row, Arrow keys / Home / End / Enter / Esc inside).
- A single (ungrouped) button is unchanged (click focuses, click again minimizes, no hover). Right-click still opens the window menu. No new setting.
- On the way: the chooser was placed in viewport px under the UI scale (off its button at 125 %) — now layout px; the subtitle "N windows grouped" is translated (zh / ja); the native tooltip that listed the titles is gone from the grouped button (the hover chooser lists them, the tooltip sat over it — the button carries an `aria-label`).
- Gates: test-taskbar-group (new, fast: the PURE verdicts of src/lib/taskbar-group.js — click, hover, in-front, keys — with patched-copy controls: the old always-chooser click fails the 8 "behind" clicks, a hover that forgets touch fails its rows; wiring pins over the comment-stripped taskbar.js) and test-taskbar-group-ui (new, heavy: chrome with a real mouse — (a) click behind activates with no chooser, (b) click in front = the pinned chooser and a row switches the tab, (c) hover on the page clock / leave grace / a 150 ms cross-over, (d) a real title-bar drag over the button, (e) touch taps, (f) keys, (g) the single button unchanged, (h) right-click, (i) the 125 % UI scale; CONTROL = the scratch bundle rebuilt with the old click ⇒ (a) red).
- **Verify r1 (minor): the hover chooser left a document listener behind on every hover.** A popover's outside-click close (`attachPopoverClose`, utils.js) was removed only by an outside mousedown; the hover chooser opens and closes with no click at all, so 30 hovers grew the document's mousedown listeners 3 → 33, each holding its detached chooser. The close now OWNS its listener (`popover._closeCtl`, an AbortController, also returned as a disposer; a listener that finds its popover gone removes itself), and the chooser's one cleanup aborts it. Gates: test-taskbar-group-ui (j) — 30 hover cycles, listener counts unchanged — with CONTROL 2 (the abort reverted ⇒ +30); test-taskbar-group §7 + §9 (the real `attachPopoverClose` in node against a fake document, master's function as the control). The five lows from the same verify are fixed in the next bullet.
- **Verify r1, the five lows (fixed here, each a red→green leg with a control):** ① after a reload a restored tab group showed as separate single buttons until the first window event, so the first click landed on a single button — `restoreTabChain` now notifies like every other chain mutation and the group is ONE button at once; ② a taskbar rebuild while the chooser was open (a tab title change) orphaned it — the rebuilt button now takes it over: it says `aria-expanded="true"`, Esc hands the focus back to it (was: the page body), and a click on it keeps the same chooser (was: counted as a click elsewhere, closed and re-opened); ③ a pen now gets the hover chooser like a mouse (touch still never); ④ right-click on a chooser row opens THAT window's menu, as a window-list row does — the chooser stays pinned beneath it and re-lists after the action (Move closes it); ⑤ a dead `.taskbar-window-list` selector (a class nothing produces — the window list is `overlap-switcher`) is dropped from the taskbar's "another popover is open" check and from the autohide taskbar's conceal guard in app.js. Gates: test-taskbar-group-ui (k)–(n), each red on the previous commit's code, CONTROL 2 extended (the four fixes reverted ⇒ each red again); test-taskbar-group §7 pins, a PRODUCER CENSUS over the class names both guards query (their pre-fix spellings = its controls) and §9's live-exclusion case (the previous commit's `attachPopoverClose` = its control).

### Lane M — floating menus close when you click into an app's picture (lane M)

The owner, with Google Chrome open as a desktop app (inc-muhms5kt-0ejl, 2026-09-26): "vibespace中的悬浮菜单，不相应在app画面里的点击自动隐藏" — VibeSpace's floating menus stayed open when you clicked inside the app's picture, while a click anywhere else closed them. The incident's own record shows it: ⚙ pressed, two clicks into the Chrome picture, then ⚙ pressed again to get rid of the menu.

- **Why.** Every menu closed on a document `mousedown`. The app's picture cancels its `pointerdown` (so the app gets the press and the browser neither selects nor drags), and a cancelled `pointerdown` makes the browser send no `mousedown` at all — in any phase. Measured in Chrome and on the real xpra rung: a click into the picture reaches the page as pointerdown ×1 and click ×1, mousedown ×0. noVNC's canvas also stops its `mousedown`. So no menu ever saw a click into an app.
- **Fix: one closer for every floating surface.** `onOutsidePress` (src/lib/utils.js, decisions in the new PURE src/lib/outside-press.js) listens for `pointerdown` in the capture phase — the first thing a press dispatches, before the picture can cancel it — and never cancels or stops the press, so the app still gets the click. The ⚙ menu and its flyouts, every right-click / window menu, the ⋯ menu with Scale ▸ and Show window frame ▸, the taskbar window list, the For-you popup, the quota popup, the chat status-bar panels, the TODO list, the code-block language picker, the message-details popover, the phone's window list and customize mode's spring editor all close through it. Each keeps its own rules: its anchor / toggle button, a menu opened from it, the For-you popup's phone button and session inbox badges.
- **Touch.** A finger tap in the picture closes a menu. A scroll, a drag or a long-press does not (the phone's window list used to close the moment a finger touched outside it, even to scroll).
- **Fixed on the way.** The closer used to arm on a `setTimeout(0)` after the opening click. On a busy page Chrome runs input before timers, so a quick click could arrive before the closer existed (measured on the real rung: the window menu and the window list stayed open). It now arms at once and recognises the opening press by its timestamp.
- Not covered: a click into an embedded web page (an iframe: a Web view window or a plugin window) still never reaches VibeSpace's document.
- Gates: test-outside-press (new, fast: the PURE tables, the real helper under a browser dispatch model, the pre-lane closer and two mutant copies as controls), test-architecture §59 (census: no document `mousedown` / `click` closer anywhere in src/lib, every document `pointerdown` in the capture phase, planted controls), test-desktop-xpra-window §17 (heavy: a live GNOME Calculator — the ⚙ menu with its flyout, the window menu, ⋯ Scale ▸, the window list and the For-you popup each close on one click into the picture while the calculator takes the digit; a finger drag keeps the menu, a finger tap closes it; CONTROL = a mutant-copy server with the pre-lane bubble `mousedown` closer: every surface stays open, the digits still land).

### Lane L — VibeSpace's own tools no longer ask for permission every step; the New Session dialog starts clean (lane L)

The naive-user study 2 (three operators, twelve collaborative browser scenarios on 2.369.177): "想让助手填一张表 → 7 到 15 张「Permission: Bash」卡，Always Allow 不管用，偶尔要点两次" · "助手为了修自己的配置问题提议跑 `close --all`，操作员怕关掉别人的浏览器只好拒绝" · "新建会话对话框保留上一个会话的名字，打字变成「S11 chromeS12 first…」；开着下拉时按 Esc 关掉整个对话框".

- **VibeSpace's own tools run without a card per step.** New setting `claude.allowAgentTools` (Claude section, default ON): every claude spawn — chat and terminal, new and resumed, local and remote — carries allow rules for vibespace-browser, -status, -task, -ask, -docs, -msg, -window, -channels, -page and the `vibespace-job` verbs that do not run a command, in its inline `--settings` (the CLI's `flagSettings` layer; nothing is written to `~/.claude/settings.json`). Still asked: `vibespace-job run` / `start` (they run any shell command), `vibespace-job access`, `vibespace-exit`, and anything else in the same command line. Rule spelling measured on claude 2.1.281 (`Bash(<tool>:*)`, prefix = "equal, or followed by a blank"). Codex: nothing shipped — its only per-command allow is an execpolicy file in `CODEX_HOME`, and its default sandbox already runs these tools without asking.
- **"Always Allow" now sticks.** It reached the CLI as `permission_updates`, a key the CLI's permission-result schema strips — every Always Allow had been a plain Allow. It is sent as `updatedPermissions`, and on a card for one of our tools it allows the whole tool (the CLI suggested only the verb — `vibespace-browser click *` never covered the next `fill`). The button's tooltip names the rules.
- **"Some cards need two clicks"**: one real click always answered a card (measured on the pre-fix build); a HOVERED Allow turned into a dark button with dark words that read as disabled (`.chat-perm-btn:hover` outranked `.chat-perm-allow`). It stays green now.
- **A card for our tools says what it does.** A line that is only browser steps wears the agent browser's face — its icon, "Agent browser", "Open https://…", "Click @e1 · Read the page" — on the card and in the permission prompt. A line that also runs something else stays a Bash card, says what our part does and names the rest ("also runs: pgrep"); `close --all` carries "Closes only this conversation's browser — browsers of other sessions are not touched." The CLI's usage line says the same scope.
- **The New Session dialog starts clean.** The name field is empty on every open (the cwd and the other prefills stay); Escape closes the open cwd suggestion list or dropdown first and the dialog on the next press; the permission modes read as words with the protocol value as a hint ("Ask before acting · default", "Never ask (full access) · bypassPermissions", "Never ask — refuse what is not pre-approved · dontAsk"), zh + ja.
- **Round 2 (the adversarial verify's six findings, each reproduced first).** Publishing a page (`vibespace-page publish`) **keeps asking** (owner decision): only `list` / `kit` are allowed, and the spawn also carries `permissions.ask` for publish, so no allow rule — ours or the user's — pre-approves it. **Round 3 (integrator decision 2026-09-26): that ask rule follows the session's permission mode** — on 2.1.281 an ask rule outranks the mode, so shipping it everywhere made publish prompt in a full-access session that had never asked; our rules may only keep our own allow list from widening, never change what the chosen mode does. The rule now rides only a spawn in a mode that asks anyway (default, acceptEdits, plan); with full access (`bypassPermissions`, or `--dangerously-skip-permissions` in the session's own args) publish runs as it always did, in `dontAsk` it is refused as it always was, and `auto` / no mode flag decide for themselves. The allow list stays verb-listed (list, kit — never publish) in every mode; the mode is read off the spawn's own argv, and a mid-session mode switch rewrites no settings, so the rule follows the mode the session was started in. **Always Allow on a command that can run anything** (`vibespace-job run`, `vibespace-exit`) now remembers only that exact line instead of `vibespace-job run *`; where no exact line can be saved, or for publish, the card says why instead of offering the button. **The browser face is worn only by the bare tool name** — `./data/bin/vibespace-browser …` or `PATH=… vibespace-browser …` (which the CLI's rule does not trust, so it asks) stays a Bash card that names the file. **`vibespace-browser upload` refuses a file from `~/.claude`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.vibespace`, `~/.codex` or VibeSpace's account stores** by name (`upload_secret_refused`, a symlink into one included), and the setting states the trade-off: anything the agent can read it can type or upload into a page without asking. Effort **ultracode** beside a user's own `--settings <file>` is exactly one `--settings` flag (the user's; the mode stands down and the journal says so). The job cards say what `rm` / `stop` / `notify-cron` / `access` do (zh + ja).
- **Round 4 (the round-2 adversarial verify's surviving MAJOR — a SILENT arbitrary-path file WRITE).** Pre-approving `vibespace-browser` grants every path its writing verbs can reach, and none had a path guard — the write-direction twin of the round-2 upload READ guard. Measured on the real 0.38.1: `download <ref> <path>` wrote a clicked `data:` link's payload verbatim to an arbitrary absolute path, `pdf <path>` wrote a %PDF anywhere, and `open data:text/html,<a download>` is not refused (no external server needed) — so in default / acceptEdits / plan / auto (where the CLI's own Write tool would ASK to write out of cwd) a page or agent could silently overwrite `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` (an SSH backdoor) or `~/.claude/settings.json` hooks (RCE next session). **CONTAINMENT, not a name list:** every verb that writes a file — `download`, `pdf`, `screenshot`, `state save`, `record start/restart`, `trace stop`, `profiler stop`, `network har stop`, and the `-o`/`--output` (diff) and `--screenshot-dir` flags, censused from the CLI's help so a new writer cannot slip in unclassified — resolves its output path (a literal `~`, a relative path against the session's project cwd, `..`, symlinks via the realpath of the deepest existing ancestor, a trailing slash, the `--` valve, a batch line) and is ALLOWED only inside the session's project cwd subtree, the OS temp dir, or `~/Downloads`; anything else is refused BY NAME (`write_path_refused`) with the remedy "save under the project, /tmp or ~/Downloads", before `/resolve` and before the binary is even asked its version. Additionally and unconditionally, a resolved target under a dot-entry directly under a home (`~/.ssh`, `~/.claude`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config`, any `~/.x`) or under the account stores is refused by the store — even when the project cwd is `$HOME` itself. The invariant: **an allow rule on a tool is a grant on every path the tool can write; the tool confines its writes, or the rule cannot exist.** `open data:text/html,…` stays allowed (it is not the hole).
- **Round 5 (the round-3 adversarial verify: one CRITICAL, two MAJORs — each reproduced red on 33781ed1 first).** **A file lands where it was checked.** The browser's own daemon resolves a relative path against ITS working directory — whatever launched it (measured on the real 0.38.1: a daemon started in A wrote `pdf ./out.pdf` typed in B to A) — and VibeSpace launched every managed daemon from the SERVER's directory, the checkout, so `pdf ./data/bin/vibespace-hook.mjs` passed the round-4 check and overwrote a hook every session runs. Now the tool hands the browser the ABSOLUTE path it checked — in the command, in every batch line (a batch of arguments goes over in the browser's own JSON form), in every stdin element — for exactly the words the browser reads as paths (measured per verb: `download` saves the word after the selector and ignores a third, so "the last word" would have missed it; a lone `screenshot` word is a file only with a `/` or `.png`/`.jpg`/`.jpeg`/`.webp` — `screenshot .btn` stays an element; `record start` never touches its URL); and every browser daemon runs in a private `/tmp/vibespace-browser-cwd-<uid>` — the keeper's launches and the tool's own — never the checkout (refused by name even if asked). **`..` after a symbolic link follows the link** (with `l -> ~/.ssh`, `pdf l/../.ssh/authorized_keys` wrote a PDF into ~/.ssh; uploads had the same hole). **The fence is the session's directory**, exported to every session as `VIBESPACE_SESSION_CWD` (local sessions and all five remote transports) — never wherever the agent's shell has `cd`ed; outside a VibeSpace session only `/tmp` and `~/Downloads` are writable. `~/Downloads/x` now actually works (the browser does not expand `~`); `AGENT_BROWSER_SCREENSHOT_DIR` is no longer passed (it named a write directory nobody checked); a project in `~/.config/<proj>` can write inside itself; and `.ssh` / `.claude` / `.codex` / `.vibespace` / `.git` directories — a project's `.claude/settings.json` hooks and `.git/hooks` too — and VibeSpace's own data directory are refused wherever they stand. The invariant: **a path is judged and written in the SAME frame — the CLI hands the binary the absolute path it judged, and a daemon never runs in the checkout.**
- **Round 6 (the round-4 closing verify: one MAJOR, one MINOR — each reproduced red on bf7479d7 first).** **`wait --download <path>` is a write like every other.** The browser's `wait --download [path]` ("Wait for a download to complete (optionally save to path)", 0.38.1) was judged nowhere and handed relative — `wait --download /etc/cron.d/x` and `… ~/.ssh/zz` ran (today's browser keeps the bytes in its own Downloads folder, but a build that honours the name would have written there). It is now fenced like every writer and handed absolute. The census that should have caught it read only the help's COMMAND signatures; it now reads every OPTION too: the 0.38.1 help of every verb is checked in (one file per verb), and an option whose placeholder or description names a file, path, directory, save, write or output must be a write slot, a read slot, refused, or on an explicit list with its reason (`--json`, a cookie's `--path`, `record --contact-sheet` … — twelve rows, none dead). **A lone `screenshot` selector with a `/` inside stays a selector:** `screenshot '.x[href="/login"]'` was rewritten into a file path and a working element screenshot failed to save; a lone word starting with `#`, `@` or `.` (not `./` / `../`) and without an image extension is handed as typed, `[href="/login"]` / `shots/a.png` / `.shots/a.png` still as files.
- Gates: `test-agent-tool-rules` (fast, 134 — incl. a binary oracle re-reading the 2.1.281 strings; r2: 41 legs red on the pre-r2 tree, and each finding's pin proven red on a patched copy with that fix reverted; r3: 11 legs red on the r2 tree, the bypass leg red on a patched copy that always injects the ask rule) and `test-new-session-dialog` (heavy, 58 — chrome + a stub CLI asking like the CLI; 22 finding legs red on the pre-fix build, every control green); the upload and WRITE refusals in `test-browser-verbs` (fast, 535 — the r4 verb census over the help, the containment table, and a patched pre-r2 / pre-r4 CLI copy as the controls; r5: the measured path-slot table, the physical resolver, the session fence, a patched-copy control per round-3 finding, the runtime's daemon directory with the pre-r5 runtime as control; r6: the OPTION census over the checked-in 0.38.1 help, `wait --download` judged and handed absolute and the lone-selector table, controls = the table without `wait` and the r5 heuristic, pure and through the CLI); r5 also `test-remote-shell` (fast, 53 — a real `sh` sees the exported session directory), `test-architecture` §59 (every spawn path exports it; the CLI's fence never falls back to the shell's cwd; every daemon launch names a cwd), `test-browser-mediation-chrome` (heavy — the REAL daemon started in A: the tool's `pdf ./frame.pdf` from B lands in B, the round-4 hand-over lands in A) and `test-browser-live` (heavy, 106 — the keeper's and the real daemon's /proc cwd).

### Integration (the five lanes on one tree)

- **One outside-press closer, with lane K's ownership kept (K × M).** Lane M made `attachPopoverClose` one line over `onOutsidePress` (a capture-phase `pointerdown`); lane K had made it OWN its listener (`popover._closeCtl`, disposed by the hover chooser's one cleanup) with a LIVE exclusion list (`popover._closeExclude`, which the chooser's re-anchor pushes). The merged helper is M's closer plus K's two fields — `_closeExclude` is the very array the helper reads at every press, `_closeCtl` aborts it. test-taskbar-group §9 now reads both functions out of utils.js and runs the composed closer; test-architecture §59c accepts exactly that body.
- **A split's tabs keep their billing chips fitted (F × lane G of 2.369.179).** Split tabs v2 puts a split's tabs inside the two strip halves, and `_fitChipsOf` only walked the strip's direct children — every split tab's chip was never decided. It walks the strip's descendants now (test-title-chips pin + the -ui measurement follow).
- **Both floors hold on a split's right column (F × lane I of 2.369.180).** F's right-column floor (the window controls + a tab's room) and lane I's per-pane floor meet as `minmax(max(<pane floor>px, <controls' floor>), …fr)`; every write still passes the pair's pane floors.
- **The taskbar chooser lists a group in its strip order (F × K)** — `visualTabOrder`: a split's left half, then its right; the active row marked by window id.
- **The browser CLI hands the binary the in-frame argv AND keeps lane H's scoped `close --all` (L × lane H of 2.369.180):** `const argv = closeAllScoped ? framed.argv.filter((x) => x !== '--all') : [...framed.argv]`; test-architecture §60b and test-browser-verbs' r5 control follow the merged line. The usage text says both scopes (an attached profile closes only your session; the shared browser refuses).
- **One flag table (L × H):** lane H's measured 0.38.1 table refuses `--ca-cert` as a launch flag, so lane L's `PATH_OPTION_ALLOW` row for it is gone (the option census counts it `refused`); `a11y` — a page verb lane H added — gets its launch-free `--help` fixture for lane L's census.
- **No document `mousedown` outside lane M's census (L × M):** lane L's `<select>` picker tracker in app.js is a capture `pointerdown` (a tracker, never a closer).
- **Every new server a suite boots gets its own Desktop names (§57):** test-taskbar-group-ui (K) and test-new-session-dialog (L) pass `vncEnv()`.
- **The heavy suites follow the merged tree.** test-taskbar-group-ui (K) placed its three windows by the default cascade, which since 2.369.181 keeps a window inside the workspace — on its short page that lifted the lone window's title bar onto the group's tab strip, and leg (d)'s drag, released there, MERGED it; the window is now placed clear of that row through `_placeWindow`. Its (j) listener-leak leg and the leg's control count lane M's closer (`pointerdown` / `pointerup` / `pointercancel`; the control still grows by exactly 30). test-browser-live-ui's floor control (lane I) removed only the pane's own floor, but the right track now carries split tabs v2's controls floor too (≈143 px on a 320 px host — enough for the bar), so the control removes both. test-browser-pin's L6 control, test-browser-mediation-chrome's r5 control and test-browser-verbs' r5 control patch the merged hand-over line.
- Section numbers: lane M's census is test-architecture §59 and test-desktop-xpra-window §17; lane L's frame census is test-architecture §60.

## 2.369.181 — three lanes: a desktop app at 1.5× is a real 1.5×, its scale chip is a button, Chrome draws its own frame, every app has its own default scale, and a snapped window never hangs off the workspace (D + D2); agents see only the windows you share with them, in tree or pixel mode, and you can ask one to take control (E); a workflow window reads its run's own files and a stopped run says so (Q)

### Lane D + D2 — (A) after a Scale ▸ switch the app looks the same, only smaller or bigger; (B) the scale chip is a button; (C) Chrome drops our bars; (D) every app can have its own default scale, chosen on its card before it starts; (D2) a snapped, restored or un-maximized window never hangs past the workspace

The owner, 2026-09-25, two screenshots and two asks: "从2x切换到1.5x之后出现大量白边，你窗口尺寸计算不对（当然也可能是计算器本身的尺寸计算问题）", "Chrome的顶部标题栏似乎不会自动隐藏？", "那个1.5x 已选的提示直接可以点快速切换" and "最好加入可以在app启动前那个app选择界面调整每个app默认dpi的能力". docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.3 / §3.4 (the dated lane-D notes).

**(A) Geometry — a scale is a scale, and the window follows it.**
- **The white edges were the calculator's own background, and 1.5× was only ever half a scale.** Measured first on the real rung: our picture covered the window exactly at every switch. What changed was the app: "1.5×" used to mean "1× buttons with bigger text" (GTK cannot draw a fraction on X11), and GNOME Calculator keeps its content in a column of fixed width — so going 2× → 1.5× halved every button in a window that kept its size, and the calculator's own background filled the rest (25 % of the width → 62 %). Now a fractional scale is a real one: the app draws at the next whole scale and the picture is shown smaller (1.5× = drawn at 2×, shown at 75 %; 2.5× = drawn at 3×, shown at 83 %) — buttons and text both, a little softer than a whole scale. Google Chrome keeps its own crisp fractional scaling. The Scale ▸ rows, the card menu and Settings say a plain "1.5×" (no "text only"); the chip's tooltip says "Drawn at 2× and shown at 75 %".
- **The window follows the scale.** A Scale ▸ relaunch resizes the window so the app keeps its size in its own units: 2× → 1.5× makes the window 75 % as big, 1.5× → 2× brings it back exactly; capped at the workspace, left alone when maximized, in a tab group or on the phone. The app's own background stays the same share of the window at every step.
- **No bands of our own either.** A CSD app is mapped at its final size (its window used to be fitted with our bars still showing and re-fitted a moment later); an app whose minimum is bigger than the window is scaled to fit AND fills it (a DPR-1 screen at 2× showed 116 px of background either side); the app's own resize right after it opens no longer flashes a strip of background.
- Also fixed on the way: scrolling in any app (Chrome's settings page measured) left ghost rows until a full repaint — every scroll step now reads one snapshot of the picture; a transparent window is cleared under each draw.

**(B) The chip changes the scale.** The "1.5× · chosen" chip in a desktop-app window's status strip is now a control: a click (or Enter / Space — role=button, tabindex, aria-haspopup) opens the same Scale ▸ rows the ⋯ and the title-bar / taskbar menu carry, right at the chip; a pick asks and relaunches as before (and the window follows, (A)). Where the window cannot relaunch (still starting, a whole-display rung) the chip stays plain text and its tooltip says why. The tooltip's tail is now "Click to change the scale".

**(C) Chrome is seamless like the Calculator.** Measured: Chrome did not recognise xpra's window manager, so it drew no ─ □ ✕ of its own and asked for a frame — the "Chrome title bar" in the screenshot was ours, with the strip below it. The keeper now switches the Chrome profile to Chrome's own frame once (only if the user never chose — a later choice inside Chrome wins): both VibeSpace bars fold, the top-edge hover or Alt brings them back, dragging Chrome's tab strip moves our window by exactly the drag (Chrome reports its press 10,5 px off, so the drag starts at our own press now), and Chrome's ─ □ ✕ minimize, maximize and close our window. Still visible: not maximized, Chrome's own thin resize border and rounded top corners (xpra does not pass their size on).

**(D) A default scale per app.**
- On a machine whose rung scales apps (xpra), every catalog card in the launch dialog has a small control beside it — "Auto" or "1.5×" — whose menu (Auto (Settings → Desktop app scale) / 1× / 1.5× / 2× / 2.5× / 3×) stores the app's default scale WITHOUT launching it. It lives in user state `desktopAppScale[<app>]` (the key the frame choice uses: the catalog id, else `exec:<name>`), synced to every client — an open dialog on another client updates in place. Auto removes the entry: Settings → Desktop app scale decides again, as before.
- **Every launch carries it.** A card, a Recent row, a typed command: the launch POST sends the app's stored default as `scaleChoice`; the record runs at it with origin `app` and the chip says "1.5× · App default". The order is: a window's own Scale ▸ choice > the app's default > an explicit Settings value > auto (derived from the screen). The route refuses a bad value by name (400 `bad-request`) before a paired machine is asked; a paired machine gets it inside the launch op's `body` (the op is otherwise unchanged; an agent older than this drops the field and its record says what it did run at).
- **Scale ▸ in the window** marks the app's default row ("· App default"), says "1.5× is this app's default" when the window runs at it, offers "Make 2× the default for this app" when it runs at another explicit scale (no relaunch) and "Forget this app's default (1.5×)".
- **2.5× and 3× are offered** (window menu and card), each a real scale by (A)'s rule (2.5 = drawn at 3×, shown at 83 %; 3 = GDK_SCALE 3). The Settings enum stays 1 / 1.5 / 2.
- The per-app frame choice and the default scale share ONE user-state loader (`src/lib/desktop-app-prefs.js`, lane B's loader moved out of the window): read once per page and again on every reconnect, the broadcast keeps every client in step, a write is an edit of one app's entry — local first, then applied to the server's current map and PATCHed merge-only; a refused save rolls back and toasts.

**Gates.** test-desktop-apps §14 (the knob table, the relaunch arithmetic and its round trips, the Chrome preference, a floor-rule CONTROL copy) + §10/§13 pins; test-xpra-client §7 (the main named before its first fit with an old-order CONTROL, the picture scale, the kept backing, the scroll snapshot with an old-loop CONTROL, our own press); test-desktop-seamless §6 (Chrome's measured metadata ⇒ the verdict, CONTROL without the preference); test-desktop-app-scale (new, fast: the explicit set against the ceil and dpi rules, the launch field carried or refused, scalePick's precedence table with a no-app-default copy failing exactly its app rows, the client model with a stores-auto copy, the words + zh/ja, the route with a check-less copy letting a bad value through, the op body); heavy test-desktop-xpra-window §14 (real xpra + two pages: the card control stores 1.5× with nothing launched and the second client's open dialog hears it; the card launches xterm at 1.5× origin app — drawn at GDK_SCALE 2, shown at 75 %, measured in its display; the chip a trusted-click / Enter control opening the same rows; a pick relaunches the same window at 2× · chosen; Make 2× stores it; CONTROL a copy without the field and the control), §15 (GNOME Calculator at DPR 2 and 1, auto → 1 → 1.5 → 2 → auto → 1 plus a resize to 1200×800 and back: every edge ≤ 1 px, none of the pane's background, the window = the predicted size, the calculator's column proportional to its true scale) and §16 (real Chrome), with one CONTROL copy (2× → 1.5× halves the column in an unchanged window; Chrome keeps both bars); test-desktop-remote §7 (the real daemon runs the app default over the hub's explicit Settings value); test-desktop-app-window (no card control on the vnc-display rung); test-desktop-app-keeper §20 re-pinned. `scripts/ci.mjs` `budgetFor` reads a row's own `budgetMs` (test-desktop-xpra-window 1500 s — it measured 897 s against the old 900 s cap).

**Verify fixes (2026-09-25).**
- **A page that missed a broadcast no longer wipes another client's per-app choices.** Reproduced on a real server with two browser pages, the launch dialog open on both: B's connection dropped for a moment, A set xterm to 2×, B came back still showing "Auto" and set the Calculator to 1.5× — the stored map became `{"gnome-calculator":1.5}` and A's choice was gone without a word (B saving while still disconnected did the same; the Show window frame ▸ choices rode the same loader). Now the loader re-reads user state on every reconnect, and a save changes only its own app's entry of the map the server holds at that moment; saves from one page run one at a time; a save the server refuses is taken back off the screen and the toast says why. After, same recipe: B showed "2×" once reconnected and the server kept `{"xterm":2,"gnome-calculator":1.5}`; saving while disconnected kept `{"xterm":3,"gnome-calculator":2}`. Gate: test-desktop-app-scale §8 (two pages over a fake server that merges like the route; controls: no reconnect re-read, the old whole-map PATCH, a kept refused edit) + a §7 census that every save passes an edit + heavy test-desktop-xpra-window §14 (1b) (the same recipe on two real pages). The four remaining low findings are recorded, not fixed, in docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.4 ("Lane D verify lows").

**A snapped window no longer hangs off the screen (2026-09-26, inc-muhmqvzf-jodk — the owner: "chrome吸附在右侧，右侧有截断").** On a Mac at 1920×963 with the sidebar open and a 1×3 grid, Google Chrome dropped into the right-hand third had its right edge cut off — Chrome's own ⋮ and ✕ (and, on 2.369.177, our own title-bar ✕ and Paste too) were past the edge of the screen. Measured on the real rung: the picture inside the window was complete; the WINDOW was wider than its cell (Chrome needs about 512 px, the cell was 478), grew to the right from the cell's left edge, and the workspace cut off whatever hung past it — 58 device px of Chrome on this lane. The same happened to any window whose minimum is larger than its zone at the right or bottom edge: GNOME Calculator (618 px tall at 2×) dropped on the bottom half lost 360 device px of its keypad under the taskbar, a terminal in the last cell of a 1×6 grid, and at UI scale 125 % a new desktop-app window opened 4 px too low. Now these ways of putting a window into a place go through one placement rule: dropping it on a snap zone, a grid cell or a shift-drag range; command mode's halves and cell keys; a layout preset; the stored position a layout restore, a layout sync or a desktop switch applies; the workspace resizing under a visible window (the sidebar opening, the browser window resizing); un-maximizing on the workspace it was maximized on; and a new window's first position. A window bigger than its zone still overlaps its neighbour, but slides back inside the workspace instead of hanging past it (a window you left hanging off the edge yourself stays where you put it). Measured after with the reproducer's recipe — 103 states (Chrome and Calculator, DPR 1 and 2, UI 100 % and 125 %, the sidebar closed / at 426 / at 470, every snap, grid cell, maximize, restore and resize) — and the new gate's 80 (the same matrix at the owner's 470 px sidebar): 0 px hidden by the workspace in every one; the owner's case 58 → 0, Chrome's ⋮ and ✕ back on screen (found in the screenshot pixels). Gates: test-window-minsize §4 (the rule, the real window-manager paths on the owner's 1450 px workspace, a pre-fix copy as the control) and the new heavy test-desktop-app-snap (the whole matrix on the real rung, judged on screenshot pixels, with a pre-fix control server).

**Verify fixes (2026-09-26).** The adversarial verify found the first fix's list above claimed two everyday paths it did not cover, both a three-click flow on the owner's screen: minimize a window with the sidebar closed, open the sidebar, restore it — or maximize it, open the sidebar, un-maximize — and the window came back at its old position on the wider workspace, hanging 422 CSS px past the narrower one (Chrome in the right third: 842 device px of the picture off screen, two thirds of Chrome with its ⋮ and ✕). Worse, the hanging box was then saved as the window's position, so the next time the sidebar closed the window moved even further off (1090 device px). Both boxes are ones VibeSpace kept by itself, never a place you chose: a minimized window is now placed with the others whenever the workspace resizes (it just isn't told until you restore it), and un-maximizing after the workspace changed carries the window to the same share of the new workspace its visible twins keep, then slides it inside like any other placement. A position is never saved as zeros from a minimized window any more, a stored position lands on whole pixels (a phone-and-back round trip left up to one device pixel of the picture under the window's edge), and a second, smaller screen that has to squeeze an app's minimum keeps that compromise to itself instead of moving the window on everyone else's screen. After, the verifier's recipe on the real rung (Chrome, DPR 2, UI 100 %, the sidebar at 470): minimize → sidebar → restore 842 → 0 device px hidden, maximize → sidebar → un-maximize 842 → 0 (GNOME Calculator the same, 0 and 0), the sidebar closed and opened again afterwards 1090 → 0 and 842 → 0, the phone round trip's picture exactly 0 past its pane. Gates: test-window-minsize §4b (both flows, the cascade, the hidden capture, whole px and the local capped raise on the real window manager, with a pre-fix copy as the control) and test-desktop-app-snap's new flow lines (the same flows on the real rung at the owner's DPR / UI / sidebar, a pre-fix control server).
