Still not covered, named: dragging a maximized window off its title bar and the Move mode place the window where you drop it (your drop); the pixel judge's margin at UI 125 % (85–87 % found vs the 80 % floor on a half-pixel blur) is unchanged.


### Lane E — agents see only the windows you share with them, in tree or pixel mode — browsers included, several agents on several windows at once

The owner (2026-09-25): "浏览器窗口不是也应该能给agent操作吗？为啥你说不让？另外可能默认不要让agent能看到所有窗口，而是创建前和创建后能选择把窗口暴露给哪些agent或者group，或者直接从一个窗口能发起让某个特定agent控制的request。话说我们的设计下多个窗口是可以同时被多个agent操作的吧？" and at 19:05: "我理解任何窗口发送给agent的时候应该都要有个选项可以切换无障碍还是像素模式。像素模式是最接近用户本人操作的方案作为兜底。" Built as decided (D1–D7, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.6):

- **Hidden by default (D1).** A desktop-app window is invisible to every agent until you share it: `vibespace-window list` shows nothing else, and every verb on it answers `not_exposed` ("the user has not shared this window with you — ask them (they can share it from the window's ⋯ menu)"). One exception: a window an agent opened itself (`vibespace-window open`) is shared with that agent only.
- **Share with agents or Task Groups (D2)** — before launch (the Desktop apps dialog's new "Share with agents" row; each app remembers what you last launched it with) or after (the window's ⋯ and its title-bar / taskbar menu → "Share with agent…": every live agent and Task Group as a checkbox; a group reaches every session in it, now or later). Unchecking revokes at once — an agent holding the window loses it, and its next action answers `not_exposed`. The window shows a "Shared with 2 · Pixels" chip.
- **Ask an agent to take control (D3)** — from the window: pick one agent, add a line if you like. It gets a message naming the window, on its next turn, for free; tick "Wake it now" and it starts right away as a billed turn through the unattended-turn budget (a refusal says why and the message still rides its next turn). Asking also shares the window with that agent, and can end another agent's hold.
- **Your browser, shared, is a target like any app (D4).** A Chrome / Firefox you launched from Desktop apps now starts with its accessibility switch on, so an agent you shared it with reads the page itself — measured on Chrome 153: 237 nodes in ~50 ms, the page button's own `press` action clicked, text typed into a page field, the page scrolled; without the switch it shows 4 closed frames. Agents still cannot open your browser themselves (`browser_is_human`); their own web work stays `vibespace-browser`.
- **Tree or pixel mode, per window (D7).** Every share carries a mode — Auto (default), Accessibility tree, Pixels — switchable any time from the share dialog; it takes effect at the agent's next action. In pixel mode the agent works like you do by hand: `screenshot` (the window's own image, with its size and origin), `click --at x,y` on that image, `type`, `key`, and the new `scroll`; the tree verbs are refused by name. Auto picks the tree when the app has one and says why when it does not ("no accessibility tree — pixel mode").
- **The pixel road is honest now.** Screenshots grab the app's own windows (on the xpra rung the old whole-display grab was always black); a window nobody has open has no pixels, so pixel actions on it are refused `window_not_visible` instead of silently doing nothing; `--at` beyond the image or the screen is refused by name, never clamped; a wheel button on `click` is refused instead of becoming a left click; and two clicks (or keys) in a row on the same spot no longer hang the second one.
- **Several agents, several windows (D6)** — one holder per window, any number of windows held by different agents at once; measured concurrently (a calculator click and xterm typing, both landed).
- Routes (human-only — an agent token is refused `agent_forbidden`): `GET/POST/DELETE /api/desktop/apps/:id/reach`, `PUT …/reach/mode`, `POST …/reach/request`, and `share` on the launch; broadcast `window-reach-updated`. New spend reason `window-share-request` (the wake). A window on a paired machine cannot be shared (`share_local_only`).
- Gates: test-window-reach (new, fast — the reach table, the mode table, the pixel plan, three patched-copy controls), test-window-targets (hidden by default, the T6 browser legs now `not_exposed` until shared, the request over a stub ladder, the human routes), test-window-target (heavy — a calculator, xterm and Chrome on the real xpra rung under a private session bus: hidden, shared, pixels vs tree, a group joined later, a revoke mid-lease, two agents at once, the request with the real spend guard refusing the wake, Chrome's page tree with the no-switch control), test-desktop-app-window (heavy — the ⋯ / taskbar rows, the chip, the mode switch, a revoke, the launcher row remembered per app).
- **Verify fixes (2026-09-25, the adversarial verifier's two findings above low, each reproduced red first).** (1) The Desktop apps dialog no longer says "Hidden from agents" while the click shares the app with what it remembered: the row's words now come from the same rule the launch uses — untouched, it reads "Each app launches as you last shared it" whenever any app remembers a share, each app card that will launch shared carries a chip naming who and how ("Shared with Ops · Pixels"), and a launch that applied a remembered share says so in a toast ("Started shared with Ops · Pixels — change it from the window's ⋯"). The owner's D2 asks the next launch to PROPOSE the same share; a proposal is something you see before you click. (2) Taking a window back now stops an agent's action that was already on its way: a revoke, leaving the Task Group, a takeover or the real-desktop switch going off that lands while the agent's verb is waiting (a mode probe of up to 3 s, the helper reading the tree, the input probe, the screenshot grab) now stops it — nothing is clicked or typed, no tree or image is handed over, and an attach never answers "attached" with its lease already gone (the verb answers `not_exposed` / `window_paused`; the image is deleted). Reproduced with a delayed fake helper: a revoke 100 ms into a 400 ms wait let `click --at` inject, `click @ref` run its action, `snapshot` hand over the tree and `attach` say attached — all four now refused. Gates: test-window-reach §7b (the 50-cell "the words name the act" table + a control that says "hidden" when untouched), test-window-targets §5 (seven race legs + a patched engine copy without the re-check that lets the click through), test-desktop-app-window §E (the card chip and the row's words before the second launch, the toast after it). Five lows are recorded, not fixed, in docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.6 ("lane E verify lows").
- **Verify r2 fixes (2026-09-25, four findings, each reproduced red first).** (1) The launcher no longer names a share by an out-of-date memory: an app card and the launch toast now say "alpha (not running now)" for an agent that is gone and "Ops (not in the list now)" for a Task Group that was deleted or archived — the share picker's own words — and a renamed group shows its current name (before: "Shared with alpha, Ops (old name) · Auto" while the launch wrote rows nobody matched). The launch's audit line now counts those rows (`unmatched`). (2) If the Task Group store cannot be read, an agent's action on a window shared through a group is refused `reach_unreadable` ("the Task Group store could not be read — try again") and the agent keeps its hold; before, the fault looked like you taking the window away — the agent was told the window was not shared with it, lost its hold, and the audit said "exposure revoked by the user" (a revoke of somebody else during the fault dropped it too). `list` says how many windows it could not decide; `detach` still works. (3) Taking a window over now stops an action that is already running: typing, a chord, a click or a scroll the agent started stops the moment you press Take over or revoke the share — only that one program is stopped, by its own process handle — and the agent is told it was stopped part-way (`did.partial`; the CLI says to look again before continuing). Whatever key or button it was holding is let go first: measured on this box, stopping the typing program between a key's press and its release left the key held and the display repeated it ("qqqq…") into the window you had just taken over. Text typed as keys is now at most 1,500 characters a call, and its time limit grows with the text (a 4,000-character type could never finish inside the old fixed 20 s — it was cut off after about 1,600 characters). (4) Every one of the engine's "is this agent still allowed?" checks is now tested on its own: the suite removes each in turn and a test must fail (four could be removed before without any test noticing — the scroll, the typed keys, the app-window screenshot and the real-desktop screenshot). Gates: test-window-reach (§2b the unreadable store, the §7b roster leg through the real text builders + two new patched-copy controls), test-window-targets (§2b the cancel kills only its own child and releases what it held, §3 the same on the real fixture display with a no-release control, §5 deterministic race legs + the per-site census + the unreadable and cancel legs with their controls, the route and the CLI), test-desktop-app-window §E (the remembered group deleted before a third launch). Three lows are recorded, not fixed, in docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.6 ("lane E verify r2 lows").
- **Verify r3 fixes (2026-09-26, one minor + four lows, each reproduced red first).** (1) Taking a window over now stops the agent's typing even if the agent gave the window up and took it back while its action was starting (or you unshared and re-shared it and the agent re-attached): a running action now belongs to the WINDOW, not to the hold that started it — before, the takeover looked at the new hold, found nothing running, and the agent's text kept landing through your takeover (reproduced: `ok` after the whole 400 ms type, nothing stopped). (2) An action stopped by its own time limit now says it stopped part-way, like one you stopped: the agent's answer carries `did.partial` (and what was let go), the audit line says so, and the CLI prints "STOPPED PART-WAY" — before, only a cancel carried it. (3) Typing non-English text as keys (Chinese, accented letters) no longer depends on the server's language setting: measured on this box with no LANG, `type "ab中文é"` typed "ab" and then failed with a plain error; now the typing program runs under a UTF-8 locale (`LC_ALL=C.UTF-8`, the rule the window lister already used) and the whole text lands; on a machine where no UTF-8 locale exists at all the type is refused by name (`no_utf8_locale`, naming the first such character) before anything is typed. A type the typing program gives up on after it started now says part of it may have landed, and its error is the program's own message, never the command line holding the text. (4) `vibespace-window list` no longer shows a window whose share you removed while the list was being put together. (5) The launch's audit line no longer counts a Task Group as "nobody's" while the Task Group store cannot be read — it counts it `undecided` (the share view marks the row the same way). Gates: test-window-targets (§2b the locale rule over fake `locale` answers; §3 the real Xvfb with LANG stripped + a no-rule control; §5 two re-attach legs + the r2 object-keyed act as the control, the forced-timeout leg through the route and the CLI + a control, the `list` leg as the census's 15th site, the launch audit during a store fault + a control), test-window-reach (§2c the reached-state table + wiring pins + control (g)).


### Lane Q — a workflow window shows its run's details from the run's own files, and a run that stopped says so

The owner, on a View Workflow window whose chip read 运行中, "11 个 agent · 10 完成 · 运行中…", a note saying phase names and labels appear when the run finishes, and eleven rows reading "(agent)" under one phase with that same sentence as its title: "…这个workflow怎么没有细节". The run had stopped two days earlier (its newest file was two days old, one agent never returned) and the launching session's live progress tree was gone after seven server restarts. The labels and the phases were on disk the whole time.

- **The run dir is read for what it holds.** Since CLI 2.1.267 every `started` line of a run's `journal.jsonl` carries the agent's `label` and `phase`, and every `agent-<id>.meta.json` carries `description` (the label), `workflowPhase` and often `model` — measured over 495 local run dirs from 2.1.201 to 2.1.281. The new PURE `src/workflow-disk.js` `parseRunDir` builds the window's view from them: the labels (journal first, then meta), the phases in the order the run started them (it matched the finished snapshot's order in 136 of 137 runs), the model, and each agent's state from the journal exactly as before (done / retried / running) plus a `failed` record, which is now shown as an error instead of "running". An agent with no phase sits under one last "Other" phase; a run from an older CLI (no labels anywhere) still shows "(agent)" rows under "Agents".
- **A run that stopped is never "running".** With no live progress tree, no final snapshot and no file of the run written for 10 minutes, the run is **Stalled** (已中断): the chip says so (no pulse), the line under the title reads "最后活动 2 天前；1 个 agent 未完成", the agent that never returned is marked unfinished, and the note says the run most likely stopped with its session. A stalled window re-checks every 15 s, so a resume under the same run id brings it back to running. While the launching session's live tree is held by the server — and its newest progress record is under 10 minutes old — the run counts as running whatever its files say, and the tree still wins for states and the last tool; the disk fills in labels and phases the tree lacks.
- **The chat card says the same.** The status bar's existing workflow poll hands the verdict to the chat view, and a Workflow card whose chip still said ⟳ running shows **Stalled** with the same sentence as its tooltip (one wording function for both surfaces). The status bar's running-workflows chip does not show a stalled run (it keeps re-checking it every 15 s).
- **Remote runs too.** The one read-only probe a remote View Workflow uses now also ships each agent's meta file and the host's own clock, so a run on another machine gets the same labels, phases and verdict, judged against that machine's time.
- **The wrong sentence is gone.** No note or phase title claims labels only appear when the run finishes; the running note says the view comes from the run's files and that token totals arrive at the end.
- **Verification round (lane Q, six findings, all fixed).** *A run that stalled before a restart no longer reads running after it:* the chat session's replayed progress records used to count as proof of life for as long as they were kept; a progress record now carries the time it arrived, and the live tree counts only while its newest record is under 10 minutes old (a run whose agents and progress are both silent for 10 minutes reads Stalled until its next record — the same rule as its files). *A running workflow is no longer closed by its own second name:* the CLI's list of live background tasks names a workflow by its short task id, and the card was also known by its run id, which the list never names — so every such list closed the card (it read "finished") and, after a quiet stretch, the window read Stalled; a card is now kept open when any of its ids is named. *The chat card comes back:* a stalled run stays on the status bar's list and is re-checked every 15 s, so when it writes again the card returns to ⟳ running along with the window (measured 16 s). *The note agrees with the chip:* a stalled run that still carries the session's progress tree shows the stalled note, not "Live view". *Long labels are readable:* every agent label and phase title shows its full text on hover. *Remote runs judge like local ones:* the remote probe's newest-file time now covers the agents' meta files too, and an answer without the host's clock says "unknown" instead of judging the host's files by this machine's clock.
- Gates: `scripts/test-workflow-disk.mjs` (fast, 68 — the moved journal arithmetic against its pre-move reference, the parse table over synthetic fixtures in the real files' key shapes, the liveness table at its boundaries, the zh/ja words, the REAL route over a scratch home — stalled, running, live tree, snapshot untouched, resume, pre-2.1.267 — the REAL remote probe script run by `sh`, and two patched-copy controls that ignore the metas / drop the verdict and go red, and the fixture-isolation census: the suite re-homes its own process and proves the real `~/.claude/projects` gained nothing); `scripts/test-fold-ux.mjs` F5 (heavy, chrome — the window over a real stalled run dir in zh, the card's chip through the status bar's poll, a just-written run as the control, and the pre-fix server answer failing the same judge); `test-workflow-live-view` (the every-live-return census now names the one seam); `test-task-lifecycle` pin updated. Lane Q verify: `test-workflow-disk` 95 (+ the `treeAlive` / `liveNoteKind` tables, the REAL route under a REAL normalizer fed the wire's order + a level set and under a REAL `rebuildHistory` of 2-day-old / 1-minute-old records, the remote meta-only and no-clock legs, and patched-copy controls of the route, the normalizer and the probe — the level-set leg's two layers each proven alone), `test-workflow-live-view` 23 (the per-key control), `test-task-lifecycle` 61 (the stamp: live now, replay = arrival, history = none), `test-fold-ux` F5 97 (the stalled-with-tree note, the long-label title, the card coming back — control: the pre-fix drop on a twin run).

### Integration (the three lanes on one tree)

- **The desktop strip folds every new chip (lanes D + E met lane I's fold).** Lane E's "Shared with N · <mode>" chip joins the strip's fold table at priority 2 (key `share`, beside the holder chip) — a chip without a priority could never fold and the bar would overflow at a narrow width; lane D's scale chip, now a button, keeps its priority 3. The ⋯ is decided by the fold alone (never `style.display`): shown for the xpra rows, for a shareable app on every rung (lane E's Share with agent… / Ask an agent to take control…), and whenever something is folded. New census in test-live-bar-layout §5: every strip control but the never-fold set carries a priority (a control planted without one is named).
- **The launch dialog carries both rows.** One launch POST sends the app's default scale (`scaleChoice`, lane D) and the dialog's share (`share`, lane E); the route checks the scale first, then validates the share before anything starts. The launcher's wiring pin (test-xpra-client) accepts both.
- **The §57 census reads a server started through a launcher.** Lane D's new test-desktop-app-snap started its server as `dbus-run-session -- node server.js` — node an argument, not the command — which the census did not see, so that suite would have booted on the singleton Desktop's `:7` / 5901. The suite now passes `vncEnv()`, and the census (test-architecture §57) matches a launcher-wrapped spawn too, with the pre-fix shape as a new negative control.
- **The live-view UI gate shares before it attaches.** test-browser-live-ui (lane I, written before lane E) leased a desktop app to an agent without sharing it — refused since lane E. It now shares the app with the browsing session first, and its fold judge expects the ⋯ on every rung for a local app.


## 2.369.180 — four lanes: gate suites never claim the singleton Desktop's display or port (N); the agent's ephemeral browser shows itself, heals within a budget and is owned by its launch mark (H); the live view's bar never wraps and the window menu opens it (I); takeover clicks land where you click and the keyboard goes only to the page (J)

### Lane N — gate suites never claim the singleton Desktop's display :7 / port 5901; a throwaway server stops the Xvnc it started (the heavy RED on 69720f2b)

The heavy gate went red on 69720f2b: test-desktop-app-window's singleton Desktop leg read `null` twice (the status chip never settled), while the same tree passed in a lane's own run. The singleton Desktop (src/vnc.js) always takes X display `:7` and port 5901 unless told otherwise, and uses whatever already listens on that port. Since Xtigervnc was installed on this box (2026-09-21), every scratch server that opened the Desktop started, or took over, ONE Xtigervnc shared by every run on the machine and by the owner's own VibeSpace — and left it running after the suite ended, because nothing stopped it.

- **Seen live, three times in 20 minutes, from other lanes' runs:** a suite ends and its Xtigervnc `:7` stays alive in a deleted scratch directory; 40 s later another run's server connects to it and the leg prints "Connected" to somebody else's desktop (while its message said "this box has no Xvnc"). The gate's reaper never listed it: the process calls itself `Xtigervnc`, a name missing from its list.
- **Reproduced red:** `:7` is also in the range X's `-displayfd` hands out lowest-first to every desktop-app keeper's Xvfb (measured: picks 6 9 11 … around a live `:7`). With a keeper-style Xvfb holding `:7`, master's suite fails exactly like the heavy gate did (`null`).
- **Per-run names.** Every suite that starts a server now gives it its own display and port (`scripts/scratch.mjs` `vncEnv()`: a free port, and a display number from 1000 up with neither an X lock file nor a socket). 60 suites; test-architecture §57 checks every `server.js` spawn under `scripts/test-*.mjs` carries them (inline, through a variable, a spread or a function-built env), with the pre-fix shapes as negative controls.
- **A throwaway server stops the Xvnc it started.** On SIGINT/SIGTERM a server whose code lives under the temp directory stops the Xvnc THIS process spawned — matched by pid and process start time, never by the pid file, and never one it took over. An installed server is unchanged: its desktop outlives an app-only restart and the next boot takes it over (the design since 2.104.0 — stopping it at every restart would close the owner's desktop). `stop()` no longer signals whatever pid the pid file names (it outlives its writer; pids wrap daily here), and the Xvnc spawn has an `error` listener.
- **The reaper judges `Xtigervnc`.** Added to the names `scripts/ci.mjs` reaps under an abandoned scratch directory (Xvnc, Xvfb and x11vnc were already there).
- **The reaper reads a scratch directory off a process's arguments.** A test server's terminal sessions run under dtach with the real home directory, so their scratch directory appears only in their command line (`dtach -c /tmp/vs-…/data/sockets/…`); 140 of them from 20 test-browser-resources runs were still alive. Any argument that starts with (or, after `=`, names) a `/tmp/vs-…` scratch directory now counts; VibeSpace's own `/tmp/vs-ab-<uid>` never does.
- **A suite owns what its server started.** `scripts/scratch.mjs` `endRootedProcesses(root)` ends every process whose working directory, home or arguments lie in a scratch directory; test-browser-resources calls it when it stops its server (the dtach sessions went on running before) and checks nothing is left.
- Gates: test-desktop-app-window (heavy) — the chip must say what this box can produce (`Connected` with an Xvnc on PATH, the server's "no VNC server installed" without) and names which; the singleton runs on the run's own names; a SIGTERMed server leaves no Xvnc and nothing on its display; CONTROL = a patched server copy without the hook (scripts/mutant-copy.mjs) leaves its Xvnc running. test-vnc-view (fast) — what a shutdown may stop, over `sleep` stand-ins: nothing it did not start (even a live pid named by the pid file — the pre-fix `stop()` in a patched copy SIGTERMs it, the control), its own spawn by pid + start time, never a recycled pid, nothing at all on an installed server. test-ci-gate §9b — the incident's process over a fake /proc, the stale rule with the pre-fix name set as a patched-copy control, and a dry run on the real /proc; §9c — a leaked dtach + pty-wrapper with the real home and the root only in its arguments is listed, a young one under a present directory and a production Chrome under `/tmp/vs-ab-<uid>` are not (controls: ci.mjs without the argument roots misses the leak; without the exclusion it would reap the Chrome). test-browser-resources — nothing its server started outlives the teardown. test-architecture §57.

### Lane H — the agent's ephemeral browser shows itself: the live view opens beside the chat, its actions are recorded, agent-browser 0.38.1

The owner, watching an agent run `vibespace-browser open https://www.larksuite.com/` from a chat session (2026-09-25): "我在前端完全没看到浏览器出现啊 … 也没记录任何浏览器操作". The server had started the conversation's managed ephemeral browser (`ephemeral bp-a5c2e087 … started (first verb …)`), yet `/api/agent/browser/status` answered `leases: []`, no window opened and `data/browser-trace/` stayed empty. The ephemeral browser was a second-class holder: it was not a lease ROW anywhere a reader looked. The live view's auto-bind opens only on a NEW row of the digest's `leases`; the action-trace recorder arms only on lease events, and the keeper emitted none for an ephemeral (its boot arming skipped it on purpose, "armed by the live view's tap", which never came).

- **One representation: the holder rows.** PURE `browser-profiles.holderRows` = every named lease, plus a managed ephemeral browser's lease WHILE ITS BROWSER IS READY, marked `ephemeral: true` (`child` for a sub-agent's, `label` = its record's). The keeper's digest `leases`, the status route's `leases` (the owner's `leases: []`), `holdersFor`, `liveHoldingFor` and the recorder's arming all read it; `leasesOn` marks the lease `ephemeral`. An idle-out takes the row out of the digest, and the next verb brings it back. That return is the "it started" event.
- **The live view opens beside the chat.** When a session's ephemeral browser starts and its chat window is open on the desktop you are looking at, the auto-bind opens the live view INSIDE that chat's chain as a split, silently, like a profile lease. It opens on THAT browser (`EPHEMERAL_REF = '~ephemeral'`, a reserved ref no alias can spell), never on the session's default pane. A view of a stopped managed ephemeral is refused `browser_stopped` by name. It never asks the CLI, because `stream status` with no daemon STARTS one (measured on 0.32.0). The view greys, and when the next verb restarts the browser the same window reconnects.
- **Its actions are recorded with nobody watching.** The ephemeral's start is now a lease-seam `browser-ready` (with its conversation), a verb on a live one is a `verb` event and its stop is a `browser-stopped`. The recorder arms a tap on it with no viewer, under scope `ephemeral`. A listener's promise HOLDS the verb that caused the event for up to 3 s (`ARM_WAIT_MS`), so the first `open` runs on a tapped stream. A named attach waits the same way. A recorder that boots over an adopted ephemeral taps it too. A sub-agent's ephemeral is listed but never tapped, because its pairs are not its session's. The conversation → key binding is re-asked once per session through the meta choke point's own rule. (The production row was present, keyed by the conversation id `9f4cd444…`, not by `sess-4-…`.)
- **The chips.** The status-bar chip names the ephemeral as `Agent browser · (ephemeral) <session>` (was `ephemeral (no profile)`), and its tooltip says whether it is running. The session card gains an `Agent browser · …` chip while its agent holds a LIVE browser (the new live fact `browserLive`: '' / 'ephemeral' / a profile id, re-published on start/stop). Click opens the live view.
- **agent-browser 0.38.1** (was 0.32.0; `npm install -g agent-browser@0.38.1` done on this machine, so the "too old for shared profiles" notice no longer fires: floor 0.37.1). The router's tables were re-measured with the product's own method (`scripts/browser-flag-census.mjs`, `--help`, `skills get core --full` → `scripts/fixtures/browser-verbs/*-0.38.1.*`; 0.32.0's stay as r3's evidence), `TABLE_VERSION = '0.38.1'`. New global flags: VALUE `--ca-cert`, `--input-mode`; BOOLEAN `--no-ca-cert`, `--no-pin-tab`, `--no-webmcp`, `--pin-tab` (global now). Decisions: `--ca-cert` / `--no-ca-cert` / `--no-webmcp` → `launch_flag_refused` (which CAs the browser trusts is a launch decision); `--no-pin-tab` → `identity_flag_refused` (it drops the sticky tab binding, so on a shared profile the next command would fall back to another session's tab); `--pin-tab` / `--input-mode` pass. New verbs: `a11y [url]` is a page verb AND a navigation verb (a `file:` / `chrome:` url is refused like `open`'s); `webmcp` (page-declared tools, experimental) → `verb_not_offered`, because VibeSpace neither mediates nor traces it. The manual lists all of it.
- **Fixed on the way:** test-browser-live ④ had skipped on this box for a week with "Chrome exited early (exit code: 21)", recorded as environmental. It was the suite. It launched the real browser without the config it then streamed with, so the daemon relaunched onto the same profile directory, and Chrome's 21 is profile-in-use. It launches with that config now and runs: real frames through the real bridge, and a real `open` recorded (action `navigate`) on 0.38.1 and on 0.32.0. Its teardown also closed under the WRONG socket root, so every run leaked its daemon: 90 were alive on this box, the 7 from this lane's runs are killed, the others are not this lane's to end. It now closes under the same root. Once the launch worked, each leak would have held a Chrome.
- Gates: test-browser-profiles ㉒ (the PURE holder rows + EPHEMERAL_REF), test-browser-ephemeral ④ (the real keeper, routes and CLI: the row, the events, the verb held by a pending listener, `browser_stopped` without a CLI ask, the REAL recorder tapping with no viewer, the boot arming, the child skipped; CONTROL a keeper copy through scripts/mutant-copy.mjs whose holder rows drop the ephemeral ⇒ no row, no `browserLive`, no tap), test-browser-verbs (the 0.38.1 census + the new decisions), test-browser-live ③b (heavy: the SHIPPED CLI's first `open` ⇒ within 5 s a split live view born beside the chat, streaming the ephemeral; the navigation in data/browser-trace/ephemeral; the tool card's thumbnail; both chips; greys on stop, reconnects on the next verb. CONTROL: the same world on a server whose keeper copy drops the ephemeral ⇒ no window, no trace, no card chip) + ④ on the real 0.38.1 binary.
- **Verify r1 fixes (2026-09-25).**
  - **The cleaner now judges by evidence, not by a process's name.** The test-gate's scratch cleaner (the reaper in `scripts/ci.mjs` that ends what a finished suite left running) threw away every process whose program name it did not know BEFORE it looked at the evidence. So a leaked `agent-browser-linux-x64` daemon and a `headless_shell` Chrome under a DELETED scratch dir were invisible, and `--reap` said "no scratch orphans". That is the class that left 1045 daemons/Chromes (47 GB) on this box. The cleaner now reads the places such a process names its scratch dir: its working dir, HOME, the device roots, `AGENT_BROWSER_SOCKET_DIR` / `_PROFILE` / `_CONFIG`, and a Chrome's `--user-data-dir=`. When that dir is gone, it ends every process rooted there that nothing alive outside the group owns, whatever its name. A user's shell in a deleted dir, still parented by its terminal, is left alone. The name list only matters for a scratch dir that still exists. Measured on this box: 1 of 6 probe orphans listed before, 5 of 5 (plus the two field daemons from 3–4 days ago) after, with the owned shell spared. `node scripts/ci.mjs --reap` prints every process it ends (pid, parent, command, dir, rule) and a closing count. `--reap --dry-run` prints the same list and ends nothing.
  - **A dead ephemeral browser is seen by its process, not its record.** For up to 5 s after its daemon died, the record still said `ready`. A live view reconnecting in that window (the client retries after 1 s) asked the CLI for the stream port, and on 0.38.1, as on 0.32.0, that STARTS a daemon the keeper never holds (re-measured: `stream status` with no daemon started pid 2435523). The keeper now checks the pid before answering a view and refuses `browser_stopped` with no CLI ask. The bridge also tells the keeper when an ephemeral browser's stream closes, so its holder row leaves at once: 25 ms, where it used to wait for the tick.
  - **The arm wait belongs to the verb that started the browser.** While the recorder's tap was stuck connecting, EVERY verb waited the full 3 s (the verifier measured open 3150 ms, snapshot 3098 ms, click 3108 ms). Now only the verb that started the browser waits. Later verbs never wait on an arming they did not start (0–1 ms), and a failed arming is not retried by a verb for 30 s.
  - **Detach on an ephemeral says what it does.** `vibespace-browser detach` in a conversation whose only browser is its own ephemeral one used to print "its browser idles out unless re-attached". The next tick then stopped and deleted it silently, with events that named neither the ephemeral nor its session, so the recorder kept a stale tap that blocked the next one. Now the detach stops the browser and removes its record right away, and says so ("this conversation's own browser … is stopped now … the next browser command starts it again"). Its events carry the ephemeral and its session, and the next verb's browser is traced again.
  - **agent-browser 0.38.1's shared-profile gate re-run.** test-browser-resources (12 real Chromes) had never run on 0.38.1, yet the floor says 0.38.1 supports shared profiles. It ran with 31 GB free at the start and passed, 71/71 in 22 s (k=12: 199 processes, 17.6 GB RSS / 2.9 GB PSS). Two sessions on a host that names a profile each launch on their own per-key directory, and round 2's line still reproduces the SingletonLock collision as its control. That suite never puts two sessions on ONE named profile, though, and that is the shape the verifier saw collide on 0.38.1 (and the study's "bank"). It is fixed by the one-launcher rule below and pinned on the real binary (test-browser-mediation-chrome ④). The floor stands.
  - **A named profile ("bank") starts again.** In the naive-user study the owner-style "bank" profile never started: Chrome said "SingletonLock: File exists" on every command, and on Reconnect in the live view. The cause, measured on the real 0.38.1: VibeSpace started the profile's browser, then handed every conversation using it the profile's FOLDER, and each conversation's own browser process tried to start a second Chrome on that folder, which Chrome refuses. Now VibeSpace is the only thing that ever starts a profile's browser. Each conversation reaches that one browser through its debugging address and gets its own tab, and if the address is unknown the command is refused with a sentence that says so, never a second start. The same holds for the live view, confirmation answers, screen recording and the backend switch. On the way: VibeSpace's own follow-up call after starting a profile browser used slightly different settings, which on 0.38.1 silently restarts the browser (a new Chrome, and a recorded process id that is already dead). Every call now repeats the settings the browser was started with. Real 0.38.1 run: two conversations on one profile both work, each on its own tab, with exactly one Chrome on the folder; the old way reproduces the SingletonLock error.
  - **"Open live view" goes to the one view.** The status-bar chip's "Open live view" (and the session card, the phone switcher, Session Properties) opened a new window on every click. It now brings the session's existing live view forward (from another desktop, a tab or a minimized window), and only creates one when there is none.
  - **A stopped browser's view says it is stopped.** After the conversation's browser was stopped, its live view showed a blank page labelled "Agent is driving", as if a new browser had started. A live view now never starts a browser, neither the conversation's own nor a profile's (it used to restart a profile's browser just by reconnecting). A stopped view keeps the last picture, greyed, labelled "Browser stopped", with "the agent's next browser command starts it again", and it reconnects by itself when the browser runs again.
  - **Helpers' browsers are recorded.** The "Browser actions" rows under commands that drove a helper's (sub-agent's) browser said "no recorded actions in this call", because only browsers somebody was watching got recorded. A helper's browser is now recorded as well (never given a live view of its own), and its actions stay findable through the conversation after it ends.

- **Verify r2 fixes (2026-09-25).**
  - **A profile's browser starts again after its daemon dies.** Measured on the real 0.38.1: when the browser daemon is killed (a crash, an out-of-memory kill, or VibeSpace's own stop after its 3 s grace), its Chrome keeps running, still holding the profile folder's lock. The next start on that folder died with "Chrome exited early (exit code: 21)", the "bank never starts" symptom by a second path. A conversation's own browser was left running forever instead (19 such Chromes on this box, about 3 GB). VibeSpace now records which Chrome each start launched (its process and start time, from the daemon's children). When it sees the daemon gone (the 5 s check, a view asking for its port, a new start, a stop), it ends that Chrome (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL) and says so in the log. Before every start on a folder, it also checks who holds the lock. If the holder is its own leftover (the recorded Chrome, or one whose environment names the profile's VibeSpace namespace, with no live daemon above it), it is ended. Anything else, such as the user's own Chrome on that folder, is refused as `profile_locked`, naming the process id, and never signalled. The raw exit code no longer reaches anyone. Real 0.38.1 run: daemon killed, its Chrome survives, a relaunch dies with exit 21 (the control); VibeSpace's check ends it, and the next start comes up with a new DevTools port (33677 → 40379).
  - **The cleaner never lists VibeSpace's own browser folder.** VibeSpace's fallback socket folder for long home paths, `/tmp/vs-ab-<uid>`, has the same shape as a test scratch folder, so a production browser rooted there could be listed. Present or gone, that exact shape is now never scratch, and `scripts/scratch.mjs` refuses to create it.
  - **The cleaner sees real Chromes.** A Chrome that rewrote its process title has one space-joined command line, so its `--user-data-dir` was invisible. `/usr/bin/google-chrome` failed the name check. Both are read now: the joined command line in both spellings, and the process's own `comm` name.
  - **One sweep, not two.** A helper's Chrome whose parent daemon was itself being cleaned from another finished folder was spared until the next sweep. The cleaner now decides to a fixpoint.
  - **A recycled pid is not the browser.** A record whose process id now belongs to another process (alive, different start time) counts as stopped for "is it running", in the 5 s check, a view's port and a start. A view of it is refused `browser_stopped` without asking the CLI, which would start a daemon nobody holds. A record whose start time could never be read (no /proc) is still never guessed stopped, and stop() still signals only a proven process.
  - **"Not recorded" says why.** When the recorder cannot tap a conversation's browser, the next 30 s of its commands are not recorded. The empty "Browser actions" rows used to say nothing. The recorder now tells every client once per failure (`browser-trace-status` arm_failed, with the end of the gap and the reason), and those rows read "not recorded until 17:42:10: <why>" (zh/ja too). A later successful tap clears it.
  - **`close --all` on an attached profile closes only your own session.** The binary's `close --all` closes every session of the profile. With one holder, that killed the profile's own browser for everyone (measured: `{closed:2, sessions:[both]}`). On an attached profile, `vibespace-browser close --all` now runs your session's `close`, drops your lease and says so (`[close_all_scoped]`). The old refusal when others were attached is no longer needed. The manual is corrected.
  - **An agent cannot detach a browser the user has taken over.** An agent's `detach` while the user drives the browser is refused as `browser_paused`, by name, like any other command. Before, it ended the user's takeover, and on the conversation's own browser it stopped that browser under the user (the takeover key `<key>|ephemeral` was never even consulted). The user's own detach from the UI still ends it.

- **Verify r3 fixes (2026-09-25).**
  - **A profile's browser starts again even after its daemon relaunched Chrome.** Measured on the real 0.38.1: when the browser window is closed (or Chrome crashes), the daemon keeps running and the next command opens a new Chrome inside it. VibeSpace still remembered the first Chrome, so after the daemon was killed it never ended the new one, and every later start of that profile was refused with "profile_locked … it may be the user's own browser" — forever, on VibeSpace's own profile folder. The earlier fallback (the Chrome's environment naming VibeSpace's namespace) never worked on the real binary: it removes those variables from Chrome. Now VibeSpace re-reads which Chrome the daemon runs every time it looks at the browser (the 5 s check, a command, a view, a stop), from the folder's lock file, and the profile's CDP address follows the new Chrome. A leftover Chrome nobody recorded is still ended when it sits on a folder VibeSpace created itself and no live daemon owns it. A folder VibeSpace never created (an adopted one) is never touched: the start is refused by name, and only that message says it may be the user's own browser. A conversation's own browser no longer leaks the Chrome its daemon relaunched.
  - **A profile folder with a space in its path works.** The leftover-Chrome rule did nothing for a folder like `…/home with space/…` (the path was cut at the space), so the start died with "exit code: 21" again. Command lines are now read exactly, and the whole folder name is matched on Chrome's rewritten one. The test-folder cleaner reads command lines the same way.
  - **A record without a start time is not "running".** A browser record whose process start time could not be read when it was launched (the process was already gone) could keep a reused process id counted as a live browser forever. On a machine that reads start times such a launch now fails with a clear message, and such a record counts as stopped. With no /proc (macOS) nothing changes.
  - **The test-folder cleaner finishes in one sweep.** A chain of more than 8 leftover process groups took two sweeps; the limit now follows the number of candidates.
  - **A refused lease drop after `close` is said plainly.** If the user took over the browser while the agent's `close` ran, dropping the agent's lease is refused. The CLI now says "your `close` ran, but your lease on <profile> was NOT dropped" with the reason, and exits non-zero, instead of only printing the server's words about a detach the agent never typed.

  - **A profile's browser comes back after its window is closed.** Measured on the real 0.38.1: when the user closed a profile's browser window (or Chrome crashed), its daemon kept running with no browser, and nothing in VibeSpace ever started one again — agents reach a profile over its DevTools address and cannot launch it. The profile stayed "ready" on a dead address for the rest of the conversation: every command failed with "Connection refused" and the live view said "unavailable". VibeSpace now starts the browser again inside the same daemon (about 150 ms) — within seconds while a conversation holds the profile, or at the next command or live view. The agent's next command reaches the new browser; its old pages are gone, so the first one answers `tab_gone` and the agent opens a new tab (the manual says so). If the folder is meanwhile open in the user's own browser, VibeSpace does not start a second one on top of it and says so by name; if the restart fails, the command says `browser_closed` instead of handing out a dead address. A CloakBrowser profile is not restarted this way (its launch flags would be lost); it says so.
  - **VibeSpace never closes a browser you opened yourself on a profile's folder.** If you opened a profile's folder (`~/.agent-browser/vs-…`) in Chrome by hand — to look at what the agent logged into — the agent's next command closed your window, and so did the 5 s check after a daemon crash and an idle stop. VibeSpace used to count any Chrome on a folder it created as its own. Now every browser VibeSpace starts carries a marker on its command line (`--vibespace-keeper=<profile>`), and only a browser with that marker (or the browser VibeSpace recorded) is ever ended. Yours is left running and reported: the start answers "profile_locked … is open in a browser VibeSpace did not start (pid N) — it may be your own browser — close it first". Browsers started before this update are still recognised by the browser CLI's own launch shape.
  - **A conversation's browser that restarted into a new temporary folder is cleaned up.** If its daemon was killed in the few seconds after the browser restarted itself, that Chrome leaked; the marker now finds it wherever it runs.
  - **The right process is recorded when a wrapper sits between the daemon and Chrome.** VibeSpace now reads the browser from the profile folder's lock, so after a crash it ends the Chrome itself, not the wrapper.
  - **Changing the idle timeout no longer restarts every running conversation's browser.** A conversation's browser is launched with the idle timeout its session started with — the one its commands carry — not the setting's current value.
  - **A lock left by a renamed machine says what to do.** The message now names the lock file and says: close the browser on that machine, or, if this machine was renamed, remove `<folder>/SingletonLock`.

  - **A browser that keeps closing is no longer restarted forever.** Measured on the real 0.38.1: when a profile's browser died again right after every restart (a page that crashes it on load, a window the user keeps closing, too little memory), VibeSpace restarted it on every 5-second check for as long as a conversation held the profile — 12 restarts a minute, a new 165 MB Chrome each time, the profile still shown as running, nobody told. Now VibeSpace restarts a closed profile browser at most 3 times in 10 minutes. After that it stops, the profile says "keeps closing", every agent command on it answers `browser_unstable`, and you get one notice in For you ("Agent browser "Bank" keeps closing — VibeSpace stopped starting it again after 3 restarts in 10 min"). Press Stop on the profile in ⚙ → Tools → Agent browser… — the named profiles there now have a Stop button — and the next command starts it fresh.
  - **A browser that died right after its restart is no longer called started.** If the restarted browser died before VibeSpace could see it (or a profile's browser died right after it first started), VibeSpace recorded a success and forgot that the browser had closed: nothing restarted it again and every agent command got a dead address. Now that case is `browser_closed` by name; the agent's next command tries again at once, and the 5-second check tries again 30 seconds later.
  - **A live view no longer starts a browser nobody is using.** Opening (or reconnecting) the live view of a profile whose browser you had closed, while no conversation held it, started the browser again.   - **A browser you opened by hand is safe from the old-version rule.** A Chrome opened by hand on a profile's folder with `--remote-debugging-port=0` could still be closed by the rule kept for browsers started before the marker existed. That rule now applies only to profiles that were last started before the marker; a profile VibeSpace has started with the marker never uses it.
  - **The restart follows your close at once.** When your own browser held a profile's folder, VibeSpace waited up to 30 seconds after you closed it before restarting the profile's browser. Now the next check (within 5 seconds) restarts it; the 30-second wait applies only after a restart attempt that failed.

### Lane I — the agent browser's live view bar never wraps or overlaps, in every language and width; the window menu opens the live view

The owner, zh, a ~1400 px live view of an ephemeral browser: "观看" / "接管" stacked one character per line over "并排到 VibeSpace 主开发 旁" and the URL, the word "undefined" before the viewer count, "标签页 (1)" / "控制台 (0)" / "操作 (0)" squeezed into vertical stacks — and no "Agent browser — live view" on the chat window's own menu. "你这些UI都检查过吗？" The honest answer was no: the live view was gated for behaviour in English, never looked at in zh / ja at real widths. It is now.

- **Why it broke (audit I):** every text button in the bar is a `.file-tool-btn`, and viewers.css's `.file-tool-btn` — a 24×24 ICON box, loaded after style.css — won every same-specificity tie, so the bar's own `width: auto` never applied: each label was a 24 px box with its words stacked one glyph per line, painting over its neighbours. The web-view hand-off wrote `UI_ICONS.web` (a key only the file icons have), so its innerHTML printed "undefined" (since 2.369.134).
- **The bar now:** every item keeps its words on one line at its own width; the URL alone flexes (down to 120 px, ellipsised); what does not fit folds into ONE ⋯ menu by priority — Tabs / Console / Actions first, then the backend chip, then bind / viewers / recording, the URL, then the mode badge last (its sentence becomes the ⋯'s first row and the ⋯ takes its colour); the one mode toggle and Reconnect never fold. The ⋯ rows carry the live counts ("Tabs (3)", ✓ on the open pane) and do each item's own act. The badge speaks in short words ("Agent is driving" / "You are driving" / "Another viewer is driving"), the "— agent asked to pause" sentence is its tooltip; ONE toggle (Take over ↔ Hand back — the Watch button was a second Hand back); the bind button is an icon (its words carry the session's name). The globe hands the URL to a web view.
- **The window menu:** a chat (or terminal) window whose conversation has a browser — running, or used since the session started — offers "Agent browser — live view" on its title-bar / tab / taskbar menu; it opens the live view BOUND beside that window, or binds / brings forward the one already open (never a second viewer). A bound live pane's menu says Unsplit once (its own Unbind only while it is a free window). The sidebar card keeps its entry.
- **The desktop-app strip** follows the same rule: with an agent lease at 600 px the status collapsed to nothing, the chips to one-letter stubs and ⋯ / Paste painted outside the strip; now the status flexes, the agent / origin / fact chips and Keep running / Stop fold into its ⋯, and the window-live form has the same one toggle and short badge.
- **Fixed on the way (the same tie):** Stop was never red, the copy chip never accent, Hand back never yellow, Confirm never green, the Browser profiles panel's Set aside / Delete never coloured and its 2.369.145 nowrap fix never applied; the paste box's Send / Cancel were 24 px boxes.
- Measured (the new heavy gate: 72 live-view states, 18 with two profiles, 54 desktop-strip states): at 1400 and 900 nothing folds in any language (the bar needs 631 px in zh, 717 in ja, 702 in en); at 600 zh folds Console + Actions, ja and en fold Tabs + Console + Actions (ja Take over: Console + Actions); the desktop strip under an agent lease folds its fact chips + Stop at 600 (ja also Stop at 900); zero overlaps, zero wrapped labels, zero clipped buttons, zero stray words in every state.
- **Verifier r1 — a bound live view at the split divider's clamp:** dragging the divider as far as it goes left the live pane at 15 % of its window — 134 px beside a 900 px chat — while the badge + toggle that never folded needed 169–222 px: the toggle was cut and the ⋯, the only way to the folded URL / bind / Tabs / Console / Actions, was clipped out of the bar in every language (ja already at a 1400 px window). Now the badge folds too (last), so the bar degrades to [toggle][⋯] (71–99 px), and a split pane never renders narrower than its own bar's minimum: the view publishes it (`barLayout`'s new `floor` + the bar's padding) through `WindowManager.setPaneMinWidth`, the grid spells it as the pane track's minimum (`splitColumns(ratio, mins)`, capped at the window floor minus the divider) and the divider stops there — the ratio stays what you dragged. Measured at the clamp: 900 / 600 / 320 px windows ⇒ panes of 134 / 87–115 / 87–115 px, toggle and ⋯ inside the bar in all 18 states (zh / ja / en × Watch / Take over); the floor removed ⇒ 47 px panes, both outside again. Five lows recorded, not fixed (docs/design-agent-browser-v2.md §4.4).
- Gates: test-live-bar-layout (new, fast: the PURE fold rule over hand-computed tables + 3000 seeded bars, the cascade-tie census over every `.file-tool-btn` companion class, the wiring pins; mutant-copy controls), test-browser-live-ui (new, heavy: every state shot and measured at zh / ja / en × 600 / 900 / 1400 × dark / light × free / bound × Watch / Take over, the desktop strip under a real agent lease, the window menu; controls = patched copies of style.css without the bar rules go RED), test-architecture §58 (every `UI_ICONS` / `FILE_ICONS` name resolves), test-contributions (the window menu row), test-window-binding (the bind button's words from its aria-label). Verifier r1: test-browser-live-ui ⑥ (the split floor — the window menu's act binds the view, a real divider drag to the clamp on 900 / 600 / 320 px windows, zh / ja-light / en × Watch / Take over: the toggle and the ⋯ inside the bar, no overflow, the whole census, the pane at ≥ its floor, the folded badge riding the ⋯; CONTROL: the floor removed at runtime ⇒ outside again), test-live-bar-layout (the fits:false branch stated, `floor` rows + the property "a bar as wide as its floor always fits", the split-floor rows over the verifier's measured widths beside the pre-fix table, a floor-without-⋯ mutant), test-window-binding-model (a pane floor is its track's minimum, capped; every grid write carries the pair's floors).

### Lane J — takeover clicks land where you click; while you drive, your keystrokes go only to the page

The owner, taking over the agent's browser from the live view: "接管浏览器的时候鼠标操作位置不对" — the mouse landed in the wrong place. The live view mapped every pointer by the size the stream's frames CLAIM — agent-browser's configured 1280×720 (0.32.0 and 0.38.1 alike) — while the page is 1280×577 headless and, headed on a big screen, e.g. 1265×1277 squeezed into a 713×720 picture. Measured on the real rung before the fix: a click on a grid cell landed 71 px off headless and 132 px off (or nowhere) on the owner's headed shape; after: on the cell, at DPR 2 and 1, UI scale 100 % and 125 %, a wide and a tall window.

- **Two sizes, never one.** The picture is letterboxed by its own size; the pointer is scaled to the page's real viewport, which the server now reads from the page itself (CDP layout metrics of the active tab — on the first frame, when the picture changes size, when another tab becomes active, and at every Take over) and tells every open live view. The stream's claim is used only where it matches the picture; otherwise the picture 1:1.
- **The agent's cursor** in the live view is placed through the same measurement as your clicks (it drifted the same way).
- **The action trace's "where it clicked" dot** was scaled by the same claim (too high on every thumbnail); it now uses the page's size.
- **No more "ephemeral → ephemeral".** Choosing the already-ticked row of the browser profile menu (the live view's title opens it) no longer tells the agent "browser profile changed: ephemeral (no profile) → ephemeral (no profile) (by user)"; a pin that moves nothing says nothing.
- The raw CDP address the server uses for the viewport read never reaches a live view (the daemon's `cdp_url` echo is dropped from the stream).
- Gates: test-browser-takeover (a PURE table of 4 page shapes × 2 window shapes × 2 zooms, the pre-fix formula as control, the bridge's viewport record, the CDP reader, the trace), test-browser-handles (the no-op pin + a patched-copy control that produces the owner's exact sentence), test-browser-live ⑤ (heavy: the whole stack on a real agent browser — headless and headed on its own 2560×1440 Xvfb — clicked from chrome emulated as the owner's Mac; the pre-fix belief in a patched copy is the control, through the same socket). Leg ④ now resolves the real binary the way the server does (it skipped whenever run inside a VibeSpace session) and the suite reaps the agent-browser daemons it starts.

**Lane J r2 — while you drive the agent's browser, your keystrokes go only to the page.**

The second naive-user study (2026-09-25, three operators on master 2.369.177, twelve collaboration scenarios) found that **every scenario where the person had to type inside the assistant's browser failed**: "接管后想在页面里打字 → 字消失，或跑进聊天输入框「tomsmithtomsmith…」" — typed text vanished, or landed in the CHAT COMPOSER, one Enter from sending a username (and, next, a password) to the agent. The live view forwarded keys only while its own element had focus, and every chat attach / reconnect put the caret back in the composer. Three more findings of the same study, fixed with it: "接管前助手排的审批卡 → 交回后还挂着，点 Allow 会跑旧计划" (an approval queued before a takeover ran a stale step after the hand back), "点击画面有没有送达的反馈：没有，所以分不清「画面卡了」还是「点丢了」", and "并排看时画面上下各三分之一黑边".

- **A takeover owns the keyboard.** While you drive, every key, every paste and every IME composition goes to the page — whatever has focus in the app. Nothing reaches a chat box or a terminal: the chat's attach / reconnect focus stands down, and a text box elsewhere that takes focus anyway gives it straight back ("Typing goes to the agent's browser while you drive it — press Hand back to type here"). The bar says **Typing goes to the browser** and the picture wears a focus ring. Only two chords stay the app's: Ctrl+\ (command mode) and Ctrl+Alt+←/→ (desktop switch). Esc goes to the page (pages close their own dialogs with it); handing back is the button. A paste arrives as its text (never a Ctrl+V into a browser whose clipboard is not yours); an IME composes in the view and the committed text is sent. The keyboard is released the moment you hand back, the socket drops, or the view is hidden (a desktop switch, a background tab) — typing blind into a page you cannot see is not driving.
- **Every click shows where it went.** A ripple at the page point the click was sent to, an "input sent · n" echo in the bar (or "not sent — …" when the view is disconnected), and a small marker where the page has your pointer (the screencast draws no cursor).
- **Stale approvals are answered, not left armed.** When you take over, the conversation's pending approval cards for browser page commands aimed at that browser are answered with a deny that names `browser_paused` ("…it did NOT run … wait for the handback message, which names the page they left, then re-plan"); the card says "Not run — you took over the browser, so this step went stale. The agent re-plans after you hand back." A card the agent queued while you drove goes the same way at the hand back. `vibespace-browser status`, a mention in an `echo`, a command on another attached profile are left alone (the CLI's own verb table decides). A deny opens no turn.
- **The picture fills the pane's width, top-aligned.** The spare room sits below the page, never a band above and below; the pointer, the ripple and both cursors use the same placement.
- **Verified on the real rung, not changed:** saucedemo's "Add to cart" is NOT a trusted-events site — after the login, Chrome's Password Manager raises its tab-modal "Change your password — found in a data breach" dialog (the public demo password), which swallows every input to the tab, CLI and live view alike, and is invisible to the screencast; a fresh navigation clears it (both the CLI click and the live-view click then add to the cart). The reCAPTCHA demo's "I'm not a robot" answers one live-view click by opening its image challenge (the click lands; the widget wants a human for the rest).
- Gates: test-browser-takeover ⑦ (fast: the ownership / key-route / focus / owner tables, text records, the top-aligned mapping with a centred-maths control, the stale verdict over the CLI's verb table, the REAL normalizer + claude adapter + the one permission answer under the takeover and handback sweep — a restart keeps the reason — with a patched-copy control that leaves the card pending, the one-answer census, the wiring pin), test-browser-live ⑥ (heavy, the real rung: the queued approval denied on the fake CLI's stdin at the first takeover; the band above the picture measured in pixels, the pre-fix centred CSS as the control; a form input clicked — ripple, echo, marker; the chat window attached and its composer focused by hand, then "tomsmith", an IME commit and a paste typed into the client ⇒ the page holds them and the composer is empty; CONTROL = the client rebuilt with the keyboard owner neutered ⇒ "tomsmith" lands in the chat composer).

### Integration (the four lanes on one tree)

- **The reaper reads a scratch root off the arguments the way lane H reads `--user-data-dir`:** lane N's `argvScratchRoots` is called by lane H's `scratchRootsOf` after the cwd and environment roots; a NUL-separated command line is read element by element (a root where an element starts with `/tmp/vs-…` or is a `<flag>=/tmp/vs-…` element), so a path merely mentioned inside another argument (`sh -c '…'`) roots nothing, and only a title-rewritten command line is read word by word. One `PRODUCT_ROOT_RE`; `Xtigervnc` on lane H's name list. test-ci-gate's controls (c)/(f) drop the argv reading too.
- **The live view's bar carries all four lanes:** the short badge (I) names a stopped / closed / failing browser (H) instead of "driving"; the "Typing goes to the browser" chip and the "input sent · n" echo (J) fold into ⋯ like every other item (the chip with bind/viewers/recording, the echo first; test-browser-live-ui's split-floor states now fold it, and its pre-fix-stylesheet control in Take over goes red on the Hand back toggle by name — the chip displaces the other labels); the one mode toggle (I) claims the keyboard through the `mode` answer (J); a desktop app on a paired machine keeps its machine chip in the folding strip (C + I).
- **A live view that opens after the stream did now knows it is connected.** Lane H's action recorder starts a browser's stream before anybody watches, so the live view always joined an open stream and never heard it open; lane J's takeover then never took the keyboard (keys went to the chat box). The bridge now tells a late viewer the stream is open.
- Every server a new suite boots gets its own Desktop display and port (`vncEnv()`, test-architecture §57); lane I's icon census is test-architecture §58.
- Suites that were red on their own lane and are fixed here: test-attach-rebuild (lane J moved the permission answer's live-feed site into `src/server/permission-answer.js`; the census follows it) and test-fixture-isolation (lane H's ephemeral leg in test-browser-live minted a fixture-family session id without being a transcript writer; it now uses a random id like the suite's other legs). The desktop-app install button's rule moved to `(0,2,0)` for lane I's cascade-tie census.

## 2.369.179 — the billing badge yields to the window title (lane G)

The owner, on a tab strip whose titles read "V.." and a six-letter stub beside a billing chip "≋ 全部 → UCI Max" and an inbox chip "⌸ 1": "这个全部->UCI Max占据了绝大部分空间，都看不到窗口标题了，你有什么好的解决方案吗？" The title wins now.

- **Three forms, one rule.** A window's billing chip (on a tab, and on a standalone title bar when space is short) takes the widest form that leaves the title readable: **full** ("≋ 全部 → UCI Max") only when the whole title fits beside it; else **compact** — the pool's glyph + the member's short name ("≋ UCI Max", a long name cut at 8 characters: "Northwi…") — when at least 6 characters of the title still show; else **icon** (the glyph and its colour, so a pooled window stays recognisable). API chips shorten the same way; a subscription chip, which never had a glyph, shows a crown only as an icon.
- **Nothing is lost.** The tooltip leads with the full words ("全部 → UCI Max · Pooled account · Click to switch billing"), and a click still opens the billing switcher, whose pool row names the pool and its member.
- **It follows the room.** Re-decided in one frame when the window is resized (one ResizeObserver per title bar, released when the window closes), when the title or the pool's member changes, on a tab switch, and when the owner dots or the inbox chip appear or go. Measured in layout px, so the UI scale never enters; the decision never reads the form currently shown, so it cannot flicker between two.
- **The inbox chip keeps its number** at its minimal width (never wider than "99+"; tighter padding on a tab).
- The phone layout is unchanged (it has no title bars), and so is the sidebar card (it has room).
- Gates: `scripts/test-title-chips.mjs` (fast — the rule's table at its exact boundaries, three patched-copy controls, the real `_fitChip` over a fake box with a label-only-room control, the wiring pins) and `scripts/test-title-chips-ui.mjs` (heavy, chrome — a pooled 3-tab chain at 640 px keeps every title readable: ≥ 6 characters beside a compact chip, ≥ 5 beside an icon — measured 7 under this box's Noto Sans and 6 under DejaVu Sans, the Actions runner's `system-ui`, which legs 1–5 also run under, the labels proven drawn in it; a 2-tab chain resized 1240 → 400 → 1240 px goes compact → icon → compact, one window at 1240 px shows every word; the control bundles an always-full rule and every title drops to ≤ 3 characters).

## 2.369.178 — desktop apps on paired machines: launch, stop, relaunch and watch a desktop app on another of your machines, and install xpra there from the dialog (lane C, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.5; owner D5–D8 2026-09-25)

The owner, after testing the desktop apps: "以及你要思考下整个app功能对于remote host的适配程度，自动seamless setup能力等等。" — how well does the whole app feature fit remote hosts, and can the setup happen by itself. Until now a desktop app could only run on the machine VibeSpace itself runs on; every other machine was refused by name. Now it can run on any paired Linux machine that runs the VibeSpace agent (D5), and xpra can be installed there from the launch dialog (D6).

- **Run on another machine.** The launch dialog has a "Run on" row: this machine plus every paired machine. Pick one and you see that machine's own app list and what it can run; the app starts there and the window's title says which machine it is on. A machine that cannot run apps is shown greyed with the reason in words (offline, its agent needs an upgrade, no X11 on macOS / Windows) — never hidden. Stop, Keep running, Scale ▸ and the window list work through that machine's agent.
- **The picture comes through VibeSpace.** The app's xpra port on the other machine is forwarded over the agent's own connection; your browser still talks only to VibeSpace, and seats, typing, the clipboard and the one-active-viewer rule are unchanged. Measured on a real paired box (dial pairing through a scratch hub): paired in 0.8 s, launch → ready 1.8 s, xpra round trip 7–8 ms on a 6–9 ms link, a key to its drawn echo 11–18 ms.
- **The apps live on their machine** (D8). Each paired machine keeps its own record (`~/.vibespace/desktop-apps.json`), so an app outlives a VibeSpace restart; the hub keeps its copy in `data/desktop-apps-hosts.json` (never mixed into this machine's store) and picks every machine's apps back up at boot, in the background. A machine that stops answering keeps its windows ("machine not answering" — the window reconnects when it returns) instead of closing them.
- **"Install xpra on <machine>…"** shows exactly what will run first (the distro's own xpra when it is 5 or newer, else xpra.org's repository pinned to 6.x), then runs it with passwordless sudo and streams the log into the dialog; without passwordless sudo you get the commands to copy. The install runs detached on the machine: a VibeSpace restart, a lost link or the agent's own restart never kills apt halfway, a second click follows the running install instead of starting another, and a lock held by the install itself (the kernel releases it when the install ends) makes sure there is only ever one. The fleet image installs xpra 6.x from xpra.org's bookworm repository, pinned (D7), so every machine speaks one xpra version.
- **One implementation on every machine.** The half of the desktop-app keeper that happens on the machine — starting X, xpra and the app, knowing which processes are the app's, stopping them, fitting the window, listing windows, the resource sample, the record — moved verbatim into the shared `src/desktop-serve.js`, which the agent bundles and answers as the `desktop-serve` op (nine ops, every answer `{ok, code, error}`, never a throw across the wire). VibeSpace keeps the policy (idle stop, the resource report, the viewer seats). `src/server/desktop-access.js` is the one way to reach a machine: in-process here, the op on a paired device (an ssh host gets the agent installed over ssh, as Add machine already does), an agent too old for the op refused by name before it is asked. Migration `2026-09-desktop-apps-host-key` stamps existing records `hostId: 'local'`; nothing changes for apps on this machine.
- **Routes:** `GET/POST /api/desktop/apps` take `host`; new `GET /api/desktop/machines`, `GET /api/desktop/install-plan`, `POST /api/desktop/install-xpra` (the log as NDJSON).
- **Five adversarial verify rounds**, every finding reproduced red first and fixed with a control that shows the old behaviour:
  - C2 verify: a click on a paired machine whose link drops mid-request answers at once, not after a 60 s timeout; a viewer that half-closes during setup releases its forward; a long install is waited out and named (never "exited 1", never killed).
  - r2: a viewer whose connection resets while the forward opens no longer takes the whole VibeSpace server down (an uncaught socket error — the agent browser's CDP mediator had the same shape and is fixed too); a streaming command whose link died is never left paused on the machine; the install became detached with its own pidfile.
  - r3: the install never follows a stale pid after a pid wrap; an orphaned command is never left paused by a log it cannot write; a browser lease revoked while its client was still connecting refuses that client instead of wiring it to the old browser.
  - r4: two simultaneous "Install" clicks could still both start (1–4 in 150) — the lock became `flock`, held by the running install itself on local storage, never broken by hand (40 + 20 trials of five simultaneous starts: one install every time).
  - r5 (four lows): a start in the same second as an earlier install's end runs instead of answering that old result (the recorded end time is nanoseconds now); the lock's directory is named by the user id (`/run/user/<uid>`, else a private `/tmp/vibespace-<uid>`), never by an environment variable two starters may not share; an install runner that did not get the lock is reported in ~0.2 s instead of after 10 s; the docs say who holds the lock — the install's shell and apt-get, never dpkg (apt-get closes inherited descriptors for dpkg; a dpkg that outlives both is held off by dpkg's own lock).
- Gates: new test-desktop-serve (fast, 196, ~16 s — the op table, the install plan, the hub's registry of a paired machine over a stub device, the bridge's endpoint, the routes, the install launcher under simultaneous, killed and squatted starts) and test-desktop-remote (heavy, 70, ~53 s — a real agent daemon from the built bundle as the paired machine: a real xpra session through VibeSpace's bridge, typed keys landing in the app, offline ⇒ 404, the daemon killed mid-install, the install's lock held while it runs); test-desktop-xpra-window §13 (real Chrome driving an app on a paired scratch daemon); test-migrations (the new row); test-architecture (desktop-serve.js in the shared set; §56: capabilities pinned by content); test-browser-mediation ③c; test-desktop-app-keeper, -apps, -viewers, test-xpra-client, test-browser-providers, test-opencode-remote re-pinned where a wiring line moved.

## 2.369.177 — seamless desktop-app windows: an app that draws its own title bar gets none of ours, and its header bar moves our window (round 3 lane B, docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless §3.3; owner D3 2026-09-25)

The owner, trying GNOME Calculator on the xpra rung: "if the inner window has full window controls (a close button …), the outer window should not show anything, for a seamless effect." A desktop app whose main window says `decorations: 0` (a GTK header bar) now shows NO VibeSpace title bar and NO status strip — they fold to 0 height; the 1 px frame and the resize handles stay.

- **The app's header bar moves the window.** xpra is the display's window manager and hands the app's move request to the client (`initiate-moveresize`); the VibeSpace window enters its title bar's own drag from that press (snap, shake bypass, tab merge, desktop-preview drop — one implementation, `WindowManager.beginDragFromPointer`), edges resize through the handles' own path (`beginResizeFromPointer`), a CANCEL puts it back. The X window stays at 0,0. Measured: a 120×64 drag moves the window by exactly 120/64; GTK4 sends its CANCEL on the button release, after the drop (a no-op).
- **The app's own ─ □ buttons work.** Measured: GTK 4.22 under xpra 6.5.3 paints minimize, maximize and close; maximize / restore / minimize now act on our window (set semantics), and restoring ours re-maps the app.
- **The bars come back** on a 250 ms hover of the top edge or while Alt is held — over the app, never resizing it; they linger 1.5 s after the pointer goes back into the app and fold when it leaves the window.
- **Paused** (the bars show) while an agent drives the app, in a tab group, on a phone, and while the picture is not connected.
- **Escape hatches:** the taskbar item's menu (Show window frame ▸ Auto / On / Off — per app, synced to every client — plus Scale ▸, Keep running, Stop app), the same under the revealed ⋯, and Settings → Window → Seamless desktop app windows = Off.
- **With the strip folded** the plain-http copy chip floats at the pane's bottom-right (gone after 10 s) and the idle stop's last minute is a toast.
- **Verifier r1, three fixes:** (1) dragging a MAXIMIZED seamless window off — by the app's header bar or by our title bar — now tells the app it is no longer maximized (window.js's drag un-maximize calls `onResize` like every other un-maximize; before, the app kept its restore glyph and its next click did nothing); (2) the floating copy chip moved from the pane's top-right, where it sat over the app's own ─ □ ✕ for 10 s, to the bottom-right; (3) the revealed bars sit UNDER the resize handles (z-index 9 / 8 < 10), so a press on the top edge after the 250 ms reveal is a resize again, not a drag.
- **Fixed on the way:** a click into an app's picture never activated its VibeSpace window (the pane cancels its pointerdown, so the window's mousedown focus never fired).
- Gates: test-desktop-seamless (new, fast: the verdict's 192-row matrix vs the formula + a pause-less control, the reveal transitions, the WindowManager seams over a fake DOM), test-xpra-client §2d/§2e, test-desktop-xpra-window §12 (heavy: every leg above on the real rung, CONTROL = a copy with the verdict forced false; §10/§11 now reveal the folded bars the user's way before clicking the outer ✕ / the ⋯ of a seamless calculator; r1: §12 (3b) drag off a maximized window + a live muted-onResize control, §12 (4) the revealed hit test at the top edge + a live z-index-25 control, §12 (9) the chip clear of the header bar + a live top-placement control; test-desktop-seamless §4 (e) + a mutant-copy control of window.js, §5 CSS pins).

## 2.369.176 — a browser desktop app changes its scale from the ⋯ menu like any other app, keeping its profile (owner 2026-09-25 "你不让我在这里调我怎么调？")

The Scale ▸ rows of a browser app (Chrome as a desktop app) were greyed out with "stop it and launch it again": a relaunch mints a new session with a new profile dir, and a browser started on an empty profile loses its logins and tabs. Now the keeper relaunches a browser in a different ORDER: the successor is recorded first (every refusal — the cap, a vanished binary — happens before anything stops), the old record names it, the old browser is stopped and, once every part is verified gone (a browser locks its profile dir), its profile dir is MOVED onto the successor's path, then the successor starts on it at the chosen scale. The picture reconnects in the same window; logins and tabs come back with the profile.

- What a "live" scale change would need does not exist on X11: GDK_SCALE / Xft.dpi are read once at the app's start, so a true scale change is always a restart. The confirm dialog for a browser says the profile is kept.
- Gates: test-desktop-apps (the PURE verdict no longer refuses a browser row); test-desktop-app-keeper §18 (c3) on the real xpra rung with the fake browser — the file the old browser wrote is in the successor's profile, the old dir is gone by a move (never `profileRemovedAt`), the successor process was started on the carried path, the old record names its successor in the same broadcast that shows it exited; CONTROL: a keeper without the carry starts the successor empty.
