### perf 5 — the ledger scan stops stalling the loop: the walk yields every MiB, and nobody reads a half-walked ledger

- **What was wrong.** `UsageHistory.scan()` — the Usage window's route, the pool engine's 30 s odometer tick, the 3-min background rescan, the boot scan, the message popup's rid lookups — ran the ONE ledger walk (src/usage-walker.js, 2.297.0) synchronously on the server's event loop. Its cost is O(new transcript bytes): a catch-up after a restart, a day of workflow agents, or a freshly imported history held the loop for the whole walk, and every ws frame, heartbeat and attach waited behind it.
- **What changed.** `runUsageWalk({…, budgetBytes, onBudget})`: with an `onBudget` hook the walk YIELDS to it every `budgetBytes` of consumed bytes and answers a PROMISE of the same `{events, cursors, cursorFile, filesTouched}`; without one it is exactly the synchronous function it was (the daemon's `usage-scan` child and the shipped `data/bin/vibespace-usage-scan` keep that form — a child has no loop to block; the scanner is unchanged). ONE WALK: the body became a generator whose `yield`s are the budget points, driven straight through (sync) or across one `await onBudget()` per yield; a yield sits only after a whole line is in the cursor (one per whole budget, never splitting a line), so cursor semantics are untouched — byte offsets, the incomplete trailing line, size < offset ⇒ reset, zst plain-offset cursors, the parked `pendMid`, the device two-phase commit. A rejected hook rejects the walk and closes the file it was parked in. `UsageHistory.scan()` runs the budgeted form (1 MiB, `setImmediate`) and keeps the SYNC `{skipped}` answer when throttled (15 s) or in flight; otherwise it returns the walk's promise, also answered by the new `scanSettled()` (never rejects). NO HALF LEDGER: events are buffered and appended once, synchronously, beside the cursor write; GET /api/usage-stats, the pool odometer tick, the boot `warm()` and the (now async) `eventForRid`/`eventForMid` behind /api/usage-stats/rid-info all await `scanSettled()` first. A `reloadCursors()` that lands while a walk is parked drops that walk whole (writing the advanced old map back would resurrect what a repair purged — the 2.369.85 class). `srv-usage-scan-ms` is now the walk's wall time. No new op, no capability, the cursor file format unchanged; an old daemon or scanner walks whole files as before.
- **Measured** (NEW scripts/measure-usage-walk-yield.mjs: a 200.1 MB §1c-shaped ledger — 89,170 lines, 22,395 usage records, every record id minted from the fixtureSid family — in a scratch.mjs HOME, page cache warm, three runs each; the "before" is the same code with the hook removed, which is the pre-chunk synchronous walk): max loop gap during the walk **359.6 → 7.9 ms** (median; worst yielding run 18.5 ms, perf_hooks' histogram agrees), the ws-heartbeat-shaped 1 s pulse (armed to fall due 30 ms into the walk) late by **329 → 0 ms**; wall **358 → 352 ms** (−1.7 %, within the +10 % bound); the Usage route asked 104 ms into the walk answered at 446–447 ms, after the walk settled at 346–357 ms, and its totals equalled the post-walk totals (22,395 requests) on every run. On this box the synchronous 200 MB walk is a third of a second, not seconds: only lines containing `"usage"` are parsed. The route's own work over a finished ledger (the first shard parse + aggregate, ~90 ms on 22k events) is unchanged and is not the walk's.
- **Gates.** test-usage-walk-parity 53 → 82 (the routing table's parity gate for the walk): a 7.4 MiB four-kind fixture (main, subagent, workflow, codex rollout, a zst rollout when the runtime reads zstd, an incomplete trailing line) — the budgeted yielding walk ≡ the sync module walk ≡ the shipped scanner on events, cursors and filesTouched; ⌊consumed / 1 MiB⌋ yields (7); a hooked re-walk emits nothing and never yields; a rejected hook leaks no descriptor; a NEGATIVE CONTROL (scratch copy whose budget point swallows its line) fails the event parity while its sync spelling stays intact; a 10 MiB file truncated at the first yield resets on the next run exactly as the sync walk does; `UsageHistory.scan()` returns the walk's promise, a scan in flight answers the sync `{skipped}`, nothing is in the ledger while the walk is held at a budget point, the real usage-stats route (registered on a fake app) does not answer until `scanSettled()` and then answers the post-walk totals, the persisted cursor store equals the sync walk's, the throttle holds, the async rid lookups resolve — 8 legs red on the unfixed tree (the control's two included: its mutation has no budget point to target there). The existing callers of `scan()` in test-usage-scan-subagents / -usage-origin / -otel-truth / -remote-attribution now await it (the parity suite's two per-run `mkdtemp` leaks are gone too). Fast tier 151/151 besides test-record-shape (red on this branch only: the CLI auto-updated to 2.1.281, fixed on master by 2.369.161); test-usage-scan-op (real daemon, the sync child) 24, test-codex-zst 222, test-fixture-isolation 94, test-architecture 195.
- **Honest limits.** The budget bounds the walk's parse, not a single line: one enormous transcript line is still parsed in one piece (only lines containing `"usage"` are parsed at all). The directory sweep and the per-file `stat`s before the first byte are not budgeted (they were not the cost measured here). The measurement's transcript FILE is named with an ordinary id — the walk's own fixture guard refuses a fixtureSid file, so a fixtureSid-named file would measure a walk that reads nothing; isolation is the scratch HOME, and every id inside the file is from the fixtureSid family.

### perf r1 — the verifier's round: a slab goes only to a view that will paint it, the text window is bounded by what it adds, and the resume watermark means "applied"

- **What was wrong.** (1) **Major — perf 1 made every many-window shape slower.** The text window was bounded at 2 MiB for the WHOLE window, and on the 6 MB §1c fixture the walk to 24 text cards pulled a 513 KB pasted image in past the floor: 208 records / 1.55 MB per attach against tail(50)'s 637 KB — and every attach got one. The verifier's probe (19 live sessions, headless Chrome, 5 rounds, master 348aa226 vs the lane): a cold open of 19 windows 12.3 → 29.8 MB on the wire, first paint median 277 → 756 ms, all-19-painted 571 → 1,929 ms, server CPU 0.23 → 0.41 s, history render 8.5 → 21.1 ms per window; after a server restart the 14 HIDDEN windows paid for it too (29.8 MB, render 33.5 ms × 19 on the main thread for windows nobody looked at). (2) **Medium — a held resume could never heal an op that failed to apply.** `_onOp` stamped `_lastSeq` BEFORE the op ran and `_applyHeldResume` stamped the replay's `opSeq` even past a failed op, so a renderer exception on one create (the verifier's race probe: `msg_b_2_3` inside a 23-op held replay) left the view one card short for the life of the epoch — the next held resume replayed `[]`; the pre-lane catch-up could not heal it either (the live creates after the lost one moved `_windowEnd` past it). (3)/(4) **Medium — overstated numbers**: perf 1's ×1.5 frame / +40 % first paint came from one 48 MB single-window run; perf 4's "29 MB → 23.5 KB" compared against a control whose server still carried perf 1's slabs (both corrected in place above). (5) **Low — 60–145 ms client stalls on every same-epoch reconnect** (2–3 per drop) that master did not show.
- **What changed.** ① **The growth budget** (src/text-window.js): `TEXT_WINDOW.maxGrowthBytes` = 128 KiB of serialized records PAST the floor replaces the 2 MiB whole-window cap; a record that would cross it ends the walk (an image past the floor is never pulled in for the text around it); the floor itself is never measured; `reason` `maxGrowth`, `growth` returned. ② **The attach asks for its slab**: `attach {slab:'floor'|'text'}` — PURE `attachSlab({suspended, inFlight, burst = 1})` in src/lib/view-visibility.js: a SUSPENDED view (the derived hidden-reason flag — a hidden window's queued reconnect, a born-hidden view-only open) ⇒ `'floor'`; a displayed one while any other attach is in flight on the socket (`WsManager.attachesInFlight()`: sent/queued → `attached`|`error`, cleared on a drop, 15 s staleness) ⇒ `'floor'` — a burst gives the text window to its FIRST attach only; else `'text'`. The server maps the word through ONE function (`attachWindowOpts`: floor = tail(50) exactly) on both ws attach paths; absent (an older client) = the text window. Callers: session-lifecycle's live and view-only opens, ChatView `_attachSlabHint()` for the re-attach and the rescue. A floor view that is short for its viewport takes the short-view rescue's one page (the pre-lane path). ③ **The watermark means APPLIED**: `_onOp` advances `_lastSeq` only after the op ran; a throwing op sets `_seqPoisoned` (the watermark stays at the last fully-applied prefix; later ops still render); the held replay counts `failed` and never stamps `opSeq` while poisoned; `_reattach` then omits `sinceSeq`, and the same-epoch full rung of a poisoned view rebuilds from the payload's slab (`_fullViewReset`, trace `reattach:heal`) — the flag clears only when that rebuild ran through (no self-triggered retry loop). ④ The storm harness's control marker follows the guarded line, and its header says what the control is not (master).
- **Measured** (the verifier's probes, re-run on this machine the same session; 19 live sessions on 6 MB §1c fixtures, headless Chrome; "master" = 348aa226, "first cut" = the lane before this round, fc16dd35; cold-open medians over rounds 1–4 of 5): **cold open of 19 displayed windows** — first paint median master ~205 ms / first cut 526–658 / **now 194–234 (~212, +3 %)**; all 19 painted master ~457 ms / 1,339–1,396 / **now 424–529 (~473, +3.5 %)**; bytes on the wire master 11.99 MB / 29.06 / **now 12.12 MB (+1 %)**; server CPU master 0.13–0.20 s / 0.34–0.40 / **now 0.14–0.20**; render per window first cut 18.4–20.1 ms / **now 7.0–7.9**; client tick lags ≥ 20 ms per round first cut 8–11 / **now 0–2**. (A burst of 4 text windows was measured too: +22 % first paint, +13 % all-painted — hence 1; burst 0 = master within noise.) **Server restart under 19 windows (14 hidden / 5 visible)**, server CPU read over a FIXED 10 s window after the reconnect (the probe's until-painted window is 8× longer with the stagger and was charging idle server time to the fix): bytes master 11.99 MB / first cut 29.78 / **now 12.12 MB**; server CPU master 1.97 s / **now 1.75 s**; visible first paint p95 master 548–610 ms / **now 193–322**; server loop max master 540–589 ms / **now 189–213**; client tick-lag Σ master 22–94 ms / first cut 719 / **now 85–93**; render per window first cut 33.5 ms / **now 11.3–12.1**; all 19 painted master 0.56–0.63 s / **now 4.8 s** — the hidden windows at their perf-2 slots, by design (a window un-hidden early attaches at once). **Same-epoch drops ×5**: bytes per reconnect master 12,010 KB / **now 40.7 KB**; visible `attached` p95 master 75–142 ms / **now 5–53 ms**. **(5) attributed**: a profiler over every ChatView method and every ws frame handler (≥ 4 ms) on the FIRST-CUT tree found no JS in either stall — they sit ~65–83 ms after the close (19 views appending "Disconnected") and at `ws.onopen` (a 50–59 ms long task: 19 views appending "Reconnected"), i.e. style/layout over 19 views each holding a 208-record window; master shows 0 per drop, this round 0–1 per drop (≤ 48 ms). The held replay was not implicated (no rAF slicing added).
- **Gates.** test-text-window 35 → 45 (the growth table; an image-heavy list stops at `maxGrowth` with window = floor + growth and no image past the floor; the floor never measured; `attachWindowOpts`; the 6 MB and 48 MB §1c fixtures generated in a scratch dir, converted by the REAL normalizer, PRINTED, growth ≤ 128 KiB asserted; the ws-handler pins — red on the unfixed tree). test-hidden-view-suspend 83 → 102 (§7: the `attachSlab` table + the frames a displayed / suspended / burst view sends + the in-flight counter and the four call sites; §8: a live throw ⇒ no `sinceSeq`, a held-replay throw ⇒ 22/23 rendered + watermark not stamped + no `sinceSeq` + the full rung rebuilds via `_fullViewReset` not a catch-up + the heal restores resume-by-seq, a clean-replay control — 11 legs red on the unfixed tree). test-chat-paging §4f (the text leg: ≥ minText, or — stopped by the growth budget — more text than tail(50) for ≤ 128 KiB over the control's frame; on this cut 20 vs 16 text, +128 KB, 2.34 vs 1.77 viewports, no rescue) and its tail(50) control anchors; test-transcript-parity (the tool-heavy tail: 329 records / 21 text, 128 KB past the floor, still byte-identical in-process vs the REAL daemon); test-reconnect-storm (its control now ships master-sized slabs: 11,993 KB vs the fix's 23.5 KB).
- **Honest limits.** The text window now often stops short of 24 text cards on image- or output-heavy tails (20 on test-chat-paging's cut, 12 on the 6 MB fixture) — the first slab is still more text than tail(50) and ≥ 2 viewports on §1c, and the reader pages the rest. Only the first attach of a burst gets the text window, so after a page reload the FOCUSED window may be a floor one (the short-view rescue covers a short view). The probe numbers are one machine, one session; the verifier's master cold-open numbers (277 / 571 ms) ran ~30 % slower than this session's master, so compare within a row, never across.

### r1 — the Actions mirror's two reds (test-chat-paging, test-reconnect-storm on 3207e03b, both attempts): a wheel-up's own scroll re-pinned the view it had just unpinned, and a stall the harness never built

- **What was wrong.** (1) **Product, behind a font — §4b.** A window whose rendered height is within the 50 px pin band of its viewport is "at the live tail" at every scrollTop; the scroll a wheel-up produced reached the scroll handler during `_extendTop`'s first fetch and re-pinned the view the wheel handler had just unpinned, and the grow loop, reading the pin, stopped after ONE slab and re-tailed (`wheelTop repin(we 1539/1539) trimSkipPinned pinnedRetail`). The fold window's attach slab is 67 px taller than its list here (Noto Sans) and 48 px on the runner (DejaVu Sans): with DejaVu Sans forced on this box and the new gate neutered, the mirror's `481/1179 1087/629 1391/79 807/0` reproduces byte for byte. (2) **§4f** "≥ 2 viewports, no rescue" was this box's fonts on this box's fixture: the §1c generator counted real bytes and every record carries the suite's pid-bearing scratch cwd, so the tail differed by machine (runner 3,795 records, an image-free 68 KB tail(50), 1.58 viewports; here 3,785, a 571 KB image in it, 2.14). (3) **(j)** throttled the page's network — the runner's chrome does not throttle websocket reads, its page drained the 25.6 MB burst at 0 queue, and the fallback busy-wait began after the burst was over; here the leg was green by the page's natural lag (the unpaced burst is cut here with no stall at all, full CPU and `taskset -c 0`).
- **What changed.** `_repinVerdict(atTail)` (src/lib/chat-view.js): no re-pin while an upward page is in flight (`_extendingTop`, raised with `_loading` by `_extendTop`, dropped in its finally; traced `repinSkipPageUp`). test-chat-paging §4b constructs the band (list = rendered slab − 25 px, asserted) AND the order (each fetch held three frames on the instance, so the wheel's own scroll is decided while the first slab is in flight — a loopback fetch on an idle box can land first and hide the race the mirror lost), waits for each notch's own landing, and a same-band view with the gate neutered on the instance must re-pin (NEGATIVE CONTROL §4b); §4f asserts the rescue law (no rescue ⇔ the first paint filled its viewport) and text window ≥ tail(50) in height on both builds. scripts/huge-transcript-fixture.mjs counts every record as if its cwd were a fixed 29-byte path — the same records everywhere, byte-identical to this box's former fixture. test-reconnect-storm (j): the page is PAUSED (CDP `Debugger.pause`, confirmed by `Debugger.paused`) before a burst paced at one 400 KB frame per 0.15 s and stopped by the server's own cut line (≤ 160 frames); a CONTROL leg sends the same paced burst unfrozen and must never be cut (the page socket's own queue, a new preload column). `VS_PAGING_UI_FONT` / `VS_STORM_BIG_PACE=none` are debugging aids, never the gate.
- **Measured.** (j) three consecutive full runs + one under `taskset -c 0`: control 64 × 400 KB in 11.0–11.8 s, the page socket's queue 0 B, 0 ws-lagged; the freeze landed 8–20 ms after the request, the cut 3.1–3.2 s into the burst after 21 frames at 4,410,829 B (limit + one frame), exactly one lagged, the window equal to the server 861–917 ms after the resume (2,455 ms on one CPU). The old unpaced burst with no stall: cut here at full CPU and under `taskset -c 0` (the runner's page drained it at 0). test-chat-paging 3× (plain; `taskset -c 0,1`; `VS_PAGING_UI_FONT='DejaVu Sans'` + `taskset -c 0,1`): all green; §4b's control re-pins after one slab (`sh 481`/`501`) on every run, the fix grows 4 passes on the first notch.
- **Gates.** test-chat-trim-guard 199 → 205 (⑧: the `_repinVerdict` table, the source pins, the REAL `_extendTop` loop over a fake band list — 4 passes / 528 px; NEGATIVE CONTROL ⑧ neutered: 1 pass / 73 px, re-tailed); test-chat-paging §4b (+2 legs + a control) and §4f (the rescue law on both builds, the superset height); test-reconnect-storm (j) 3 → 5 legs.
- **Honest limits.** The pin band is gated only for `_extendTop`'s span; the gap-seek path (`_loadEarlierGap`, a window already at message 0 of a huge tail) is unchanged — its rendered window is the whole registered tail and never within 50 px of one viewport. The (j) pace is a rate every page measured so far drains (this box at one CPU, the runner at full speed); a machine whose page cannot paint 2.7 MB/s of tool results would make the control red — which is then a real signal about that page.

### r1b — the band-0 notch: a tall window's first wheel-up loaded history and went nowhere (the r1 verifier's reproduction; pre-existing, byte-identical on 3207e03b)

- **A carried notch is spent only by a landing that applies it.** In a list TALLER than its rendered window (no scroll range — a tall or maximized window over a fold-dominated session) the grow loop's first passes land clamped at scrollTop 0; `_applyWheelCarry` consumed the carry there anyway, the loop landed at the very bottom and the landing's own scroll re-pinned the view (`wheelTop{carry:120} extendTop:done{st:0,sh:565} … extendTop:grown repin`, no `wheelCarry`; unfixed `761/1327/565` pinned). Now a grow loop's pass (`_extendTop` and `_extendBottom`, `{ keepRest: true }`) keeps what it had no room for for its next pass and each loop's finally drops the rest (`_dropWheelCarry` → `wheelCarry:drop`); the gap slabs still consume either way. Fixed: `642/1327/565` unpinned, 34 + 86 = 120 px delivered; the verifier's maximized shape `855/1570` pinned → `735/1570`. The r1 sentence "the landing's carried notch moves the reader out of the band" is corrected in kb-bugfix-invariants and in `_repinVerdict`'s comment (a notch under the 50 px band still re-pins — the tail's hysteresis). Gates: test-chat-trim-guard 205 → 214 (⑨ the REAL loop + REAL accounting over a fake band-0 list and its keepRest-stripped control, 5 units, the loops' pins, the assignment census 3 → 4); test-chat-paging §4b BAND 0 (+4 legs + a control; red on the unfixed product: the 3 band-0 legs, the control green). Not fixed here: test-reconnect-storm (d)'s loop-delay leg compares the maxima of two sequential runs and flaked once in five under concurrent load (404 vs 227 ms) — a heavy-tier noise question, not the mirror's red.

## 2.369.166 — desktop apps: a browser as an app (your own window, its own profile; the agent browser stays separate); Round 3 Lane A: a copy in the app reaches the local clipboard with no click on plain http, the app's exit closes its window everywhere and ✕ asks the app first, the scale is derived from DPR × UI scale with a per-window Scale menu

B-bfe6, the owner: "应用里面也可以加入一下浏览器". docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.7 (+ the English twin).

- **What it is.** The launcher's catalog gains a **Browsers** section: Chromium (chromium → chromium-browser → google-chrome, the first on PATH — shown as "Google Chrome" when that is the one) and Firefox (firefox → firefox-esr). One sentence, in the section and in every browser card's tooltip, says what it is not: *This is your own browser window (an app); the Agent browser (Browser profiles) is separate.* It is a HUMAN'S window — a registry exec, never an agent's (§5) — on the xpra per-window rung like every app; the idle timeout, the runaway guard and the single active viewer (x5) apply unchanged.
- **Its own profile.** Every browser session gets `data/desktop-apps/<id>/profile`, created 0700 by the keeper and named in the argv (chromium `--user-data-dir=<dir> --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check --password-store=basic`, firefox `--new-instance -profile <dir>` + a `user.js` as its first-run switch). It is removed when the session ends — a stop, the browser exiting by itself, a failed start; boot finishes a removal a crash interrupted — unless "Keep the profile after it closes" was ticked, always ASYNC (a Chrome profile is thousands of files and data/ may be NFS), after re-proving the dir is the keeper's own, and left (said on the record) when a process survived the teardown. Never an agent-browser profile, never the user's real `~/.config/chromium` / `~/.mozilla` / snap / flatpak profile — refused by name (`profile-not-owned`, `profile-is-users`); a browser row may not carry a profile or automation flag (`automation-flag`: --remote-debugging-*, --enable-automation, --headless, marionette …).
- **Open URL.** An optional field in the Browsers section: http/https only, checked by the SAME pure `validateBrowserUrl` in the dialog and in the server (`bad-url` by name), passed as ONE argv item AFTER the profile flags. The window's title bar shows the page title xpra reports. `url` / `keepProfile` on a non-browser row or a typed command are refused (`not-a-browser`), never ignored.
- **Snaps.** Ubuntu's firefox / chromium-browser are snaps (measured here: `/usr/bin/firefox` is a 2,377-byte script → `/snap/bin/firefox`); a snap sees a private /tmp and no hidden folder of $HOME, so it would silently swap our profile for one of its own. `desktop-display.browserConfinement` states the fact; the row is offered only when this instance's data dir is inside $HOME outside a hidden folder, else dimmed with that reason and refused `snap-profile-unreachable` (409).
- **Measured** (a real google-chrome launched from the dialog on the xpra rung): the window mapped, our own http server served the GET of the URL argument, the title bar read `vs-bfe6 <pid> - Google Chrome` (X agrees), the running process carried the keeper's `--user-data-dir` and the URL with no automation flag, Chrome wrote its profile into the keeper's 0700 dir, Stop removed it; the runaway guard's sample read 133 MB over 2 processes and 487 MB over 9 in two runs (it lands during Chrome's start-up — a floor, not a steady state). Chrome ALSO creates `~/.config/google-chrome/Crash Reports` (its crashpad db) and opens `~/.local/share/pki/nssdb` whatever `--user-data-dir` says (strace) — neither holds a cookie, history or login; HOME is deliberately not redirected so downloads land in the real Downloads folder.
- **Open.** The 2 GiB runaway RSS limit counts the whole session set — heavy browsing can reach it (unchanged by decision); a kept profile is not yet re-launchable; Firefox's `user.js` and a non-snap Firefox are unmeasured on this box (the snap's window leg is SKIPPED with its reason).
- **Gates.** test-desktop-apps §11 (+30: the rows, the first-on-PATH pick over all 8 presence combinations, both argvs exact, the URL table, the profile-dir refusals incl. the snap rule, the launch request, wiring pins), test-desktop-display §7 (+7: the probe beside the rungs, the snap fact on a scratch PATH), test-desktop-app-keeper §18 (+20 on the real Xvfb+x11vnc rung: 0700, the argv the process got, stop removes / keep keeps / an app-exit removes, refusals + route codes, the boot belt, a no-retire keeper copy as the control), test-desktop-xpra-window §8 (a real browser from the dialog; a snap or absent browser SKIPPED with its reason); test-desktop-app-window's dimmed-card assert admits the snap verdict's sentence beside `not on PATH` / parked. Each new leg was run RED on 2.369.160 first.
- **Docs.** kb-file-structure (desktop-apps.js, desktop-display.js, desktop-app-keeper.js, routes/desktop-apps.js, desktop-app-launcher.js), kb-features, kb-api, design-desktop-apps §5 + §7.7 + §9-12 (zh + en), CLAUDE.md one index line.

### B-bfe6 r1 — desktop browser app: an agent cannot open the human's browser; the keep-profile checkbox and the dimmed snap card fixed

The verifier's three findings on B-bfe6, each reproduced first and pinned by a leg that was red before the fix.

- **An agent could launch the human's browser.** `POST /api/agent/window/open {appId:'chromium'}` (the route under `vibespace-window open chromium`) started a real Chrome with a fresh profile and silently dropped the agent's `url` / `keepProfile`; `snapshot` / `click` / `type` then drove it through the accessibility tree with none of the agent browser's mediation (no CDP judge, no action trace, no egress proxy, no takeover). The window-targets engine now refuses a registry row carrying `browser`, and any `url` / `keepProfile` in the agent body, BY NAME — `browser_is_human` (403), pointing at `vibespace-browser` — before the keeper is asked; `list` no longer offers browser rows; the CLI prints the remedy. A non-browser row still opens. Attaching to a browser window the human launched is unchanged (an owner question, design §7.7 open item (e)).
- **The keep-profile checkbox sat above its text** at every width: `.dialog-body label`'s column flex out-ranked `.desktop-launch-check`. The rule is now `.dialog-body label.desktop-launch-check` (one row, box left).
- **A dimmed snap browser card was unreadable**: its 204-character English sentence (with the data-dir path) was a 10 px nowrap sub-label cut to about 27 characters, tooltip-only on a phone. The keeper now also sends the verdict's `reasonCode`; the card says a short translated reason ("Snap: cannot reach the data folder", zh + ja), keeps the sentence as its tooltip, and a dimmed card's sub-label may take two lines.
- **Gates.** test-window-targets §4 (+7: the refusal, a custom-id browser row and the `app` spelling, url / keepProfile, the list without browser rows, a non-browser row still opens, 403, and a patched sibling copy without the refusal that DOES launch — the negative control); test-desktop-app-window §B (1200×800 and 375×667: the box left of its text on one row, a synthetic snap row injected into the catalog fetch says the short reason unclipped with the sentence in its tooltip, the zh key).

### The three browser faces — mockups A/B/C + rubric for the owner (B-d03a, documents only)

The owner: the product now has THREE things called a browser — the toolbar's iframe web view (`#btn-browser` → window type `browser`), the AGENT browser (rail entry, ⚙ Tools ▸ Browser profiles…, the status-bar chip, the live view; 2.369.134) and, with B-bfe6, a browser launched as a human's DESKTOP APP on the xpra rung — "可能会和其他几个功能产生 confusion"; ruling "先出渲染稿再改". This release is **documents only, no product code**: `docs/design-browser-faces.zh.md` (+ the English mirror) names the three faces in one table (what it is / who drives it / where it opens / when / what it is NOT), names seven confusions from the code (one globe glyph = `UI_ICONS.web` on the toolbar, `RAIL_ICONS.browser` on the rail, `UI_ICONS.globe` in the gear row, `FILE_ICONS.web` on the Apps card — three meanings; the Settings category "Browser" is agent-only while "Show Browser button" is the web view; the phone has no desktop-app entry), renders three directions as real standalone HTML under the product's own class names and theme variables in `docs/mockups/browser-faces/` (A: one Browser hub with three cards · B: rename — Web view / Agent browser / Browser app — and keep three entries · C: fold the iframe into the browser app as its no-backend fallback rung), scores them on six criteria (discoverability, naming honesty, phone parity, i18n length, migration cost, what breaks; measured: the toolbar entry 72/79/83 px zh/en/ja in A and C, B's "Web view" 83/86/105 px) and recommends **B now** with the per-file change list (labels and icons only — no window-type id, openSpec, settings key or rail id changes) and seven owner decisions (names, the Settings category rename, the rail glyph, whether C is the end state after B-bfe6, the phone sheet, which "two chips", who owns the Apps card's sub-label). Every mockup was shot in headless Chrome over CDP (desktop 1200×800 in zh/en/ja + a 390 px phone variant each = 12 PNGs, committed beside the HTML) and verified by PIXEL: every `[data-face]` entry's box must hold ≥ 30 light pixels and ≥ 4 colours, and the same check over an empty patch of the workspace must fail (built-in negative control) — `index.json` is the cited run. Reproduce: `node docs/mockups/browser-faces/build.mjs && node docs/mockups/browser-faces/shoot.mjs`.

### Round 3, Lane A — seamless copy, close and DPI (docs/design-desktop-apps-seamless.md, the owner's 2026-09-23 test of .156/.158)

- **A1 — a copy you make in the app reaches your clipboard with no click, even on plain http.** The owner: "why does a copy inside the app need a click to reach my clipboard — can't that be seamless?" On `http://<hostname>` the page is not a secure context and has no clipboard API, so every copy became the "Copied in the app — click to copy" chip. Measured in headless Chrome 153 on a hostname page (§2.1 M1): an asynchronous `execCommand('copy')` succeeds 0…4800 ms after a trusted Ctrl+C and fails from 5200 ms (Chrome's 5 s transient activation), and the app's clipboard token arrives about 30 ms after the Ctrl+C. The xpra view now stamps the user's OWN trusted copy chord (Ctrl/⌘+C or +X, forwarded to the app — never a synthetic event, an auto-repeat, a plain key or a view-only pane); the token that follows it inside the window is written through the hidden textarea with no click and a "Copied to your clipboard" toast. One chord allows at most one write: a copy nobody made on this page (an agent, an app on a timer, another client) still gets the chip. The browser's own `false` falls to the chip. The first time a device needs the chip on plain http, a one-time hint says **Enable HTTPS for seamless copy** and links the new docs section (docs/getting-started.md "HTTPS for seamless copy": the Chrome flag, `tailscale serve`, a Caddy reverse proxy — the product serves no TLS). Secure pages are unchanged (the API). The dead `clipboardDelivery` twin in xpra-proto.js is removed; the rule lives only in picture-shell.js.
  - **Measured on the real rung** (test-desktop-xpra-window §9, GNOME Calculator on xpra, a hostname page, read back from the secure loopback page): the user types 1234 and presses Ctrl+C ⇒ the token arrives ~30 ms later and the browser clipboard reads `1234` with no click and no chip; a token 5.5 s after a Ctrl+C ⇒ the chip, clipboard untouched; a copy 0.1 s after a plain digit key (the page has activation, no copy chord) ⇒ the chip, clipboard untouched; a second Ctrl+C writes `12345` and clears the pending chip.
  - **Not done in A1.** A copy made with a MOUSE (the app's Edit ▸ Copy menu) still gets the chip — the stamp is the copy chord only, so a click in the app never lets a later copy write behind the user's back; the RFB rung (noVNC owns its canvas's keys) keeps the chip; Firefox / Safari unmeasured (the chip is their fallback).
  - **Gates.** test-xpra-client 196 → 217: §1 (+5: the age table 0/23/300/4800/4999 ⇒ gesture, 5000/5200/7000/none/negative/NaN/∞/string ⇒ chip; the API keeps precedence; the xpra-proto twin gone; the hint predicate; the docs anchor exists) + §3c (+16 under the fake DOM: the no-click write, the stamp spent, the first chip's hint + storage, the SVG dismiss, 5.2 s late ⇒ chip, 4.8 s ⇒ write, a refused execCommand ⇒ chip, synthetic / repeat / letter never stamp, Ctrl+X and ⌘+C stamp, view-only never stamps, one hint per device, no hint on an https refusal) + the §4 WIRING PIN (the stamp and its age); test-desktop-xpra-window 129 → 138: §2 (+1, the first chip's hint) and §9 (+8, new). Red first on the pre-change tree: §1/§3c 9 red then a TypeError (no hint element); the heavy §2 hint leg red and §9 showed the chip after the user's own Ctrl+C.
  - **Docs.** kb-file-structure (picture-shell.js, xpra-view.js, xpra-proto.js), kb-features, design-desktop-apps §7.8 (zh + en), docs/getting-started.md (the HTTPS section), the seamless design (zh + en) now carried on this branch, CLAUDE.md index line.
- **A2 — the app's exit closes its window; the outer ✕ is the app's own close.** The owner: "after I close the inner window I have to close the outer one again." Measured before (M3c): the calculator's own ✕ ⇒ `lost-window` 23 ms ⇒ the record `exited` 61 ms ⇒ the VibeSpace window stayed as a dead picture. Now every client closes that window itself from its own `desktop-apps-updated` broadcast, with a toast ("Calculator exited" / "… stopped"). The decision is PURE (`exitCloseVerdict` in src/desktop-apps.js) and taken ONCE per window: `failed` keeps its red sentence, an agent lease keeps the window with its marker, any stop closes (Stop, the idle stop), and an app exit closes unless a window was LEFT on the display — the keeper now takes ONE window census at the exit, before the teardown, and records `windowsAtExit` (a forking launcher whose child still shows a window ⇒ 1, the window keeps its sentence). A window replayed from the layout whose record is already dead opens nothing — it is born `desktop-app-pending` (opacity 0) and closed before it paints; a record the keeper forgot says "This desktop app no longer exists". The title-bar ✕ — and every other USER close (a tab ✕, the taskbar menu's Close, Ctrl+\\ x, the phone's ✕) through the new `WindowManager.requestClose` veto point — on the ACTIVE xpra pane sends `close-window` to the app's MAIN window (`outerCloseVerdict`; the app may answer with its own "save?" dialog and nothing closes), with a toast naming the second ✕; a second ✕ within 5 s is the Stop. A blocked / Watch pane, an agent-held window, the RFB rung and a pane with no main window close the pane as before.
  - **Measured on the real rung** (test-desktop-xpra-window §10, GNOME Calculator 50 + a Tk stand-in on xpra 6.5.3, two headless Chrome clients, two runs): the calculator's own ✕ ⇒ the window gone on BOTH pages 1028–1033 ms after the click, each with "Calculator exited"; the outer ✕ ⇒ the calculator process gone 257–775 ms and both windows 231–750 ms after the click (an app exit, `windowsAtExit 0`, no `stoppedBy`); a Tk app answering WM_DELETE_WINDOW with its own "Save?" dialog keeps everything, its dialog closing is not the app exiting, the second ✕ 1.5–1.8 s later ⇒ Stop ⇒ both windows gone 416–738 ms later; a dead record replayed from the layout was created pending and never revealed. The keeper (test-desktop-app-keeper §19): an app exit's broadcast lands 153 ms (xpra) / 261 ms (Xvfb+x11vnc) after the state flip. Found on the way: xpra's Corral wrapper is mapped only while a client is connected, so the xpra census counts the windows' existence, not X's viewability.
  - **Not done in A2.** The layout is shared, so a blocked pane's ✕ still closes every client's copy (the app keeps running — as before); the RFB rung has no per-window protocol (its ✕ closes the pane only); a forking launcher still ends the whole session when the launcher exits (adopting the real app pid is a follow-up).
  - **Gates.** test-desktop-apps 335 → 342 (§12: the census table, 14 exit-verdict rows, 16 outer-✕ rows, wiring pins on the keeper, the window, WindowManager and every user close); test-xpra-client 217 → 223 (§2c `closeMain`: the main window only, never a dialog, never from Watch / view-only, nothing after the main is lost); heavy test-desktop-app-keeper 300 → 319 (§19 on the xpra AND the Xvfb+x11vnc rungs: exit ⇒ `windowsAtExit 0` + the broadcast, a forking launcher ⇒ 1, Stop ⇒ no census; CONTROL = a keeper copy without the census); heavy test-desktop-xpra-window 138 → 154 (§10, CONTROL = a copy whose window never closes itself: the dead picture stays; the old "Stop ⇒ Stopped" leg now asserts the window closes); heavy test-desktop-app-window's Stop leg likewise (107). The fast legs were red on the pre-change tree.

- **A3 — the app's scale follows VibeSpace's own scale, and each window can change it.** The owner: "the app's DPI should be adjustable — ideally derived from VibeSpace's own DPI — and there should still be a setting." Before (M4): a DPR-2 page at UI scale 125 % launched a 2× app beside 1.25× chrome — the pane is counter-zoomed to net zoom 1, so the UI scale never reached the app. Now every launch carries the launching client's `uiScale` beside its `dpr`, and `desktop.appScale: auto` derives from their product (PURE `scalePick` / `appScaleFor('auto', dpr, uiScale)`): the ratio-nearest integer (midpoints √2, 2√2) is GDK_SCALE, the fraction goes only UPWARD into the display's font dpi (`scaleKnobs`: GDK_SCALE = floor, dpi = 96 × scale / GDK_SCALE) — 1.25 ⇒ widgets 1× / text 120 dpi, 1.5 and 2 ⇒ 2× / 96, 2.5 ⇒ 2× / 120, 3 ⇒ 3× / 96; a screen of 1.5 or more never gets the text-only 1.5 (r2's rule kept). An explicit 1.5× stays what it was: text only in GTK (GDK_SCALE 1, 144 dpi). The record keeps `scaleOrigin` (auto | setting | chosen) and `scaleFrom` ({dpr, uiScale}); the chip prints "2.5× · auto" / "1.5× · chosen" / "2× · Settings" and its tooltip the numbers. A ⋯ button on the window's bar (and the title-bar / taskbar menu's `Scale` row) offers **Scale ▸ Auto (n×) / 1× / 1.5× / 2×** (PURE `scaleMenuModel`: auto = what THIS client would derive now; the running row is not offered again; disabled with the reason while an agent holds the app, while this pane is not the active viewer, for a browser app and on a whole-display rung). A pick asks first ("The app restarts at the new scale; unsaved work in it is lost."), then `POST /api/desktop/apps/:id/relaunch {scale, dpr, uiScale}`: the keeper starts the SAME app (catalog row by id, typed command as typed) at that scale FIRST (a refusal leaves the running app untouched; the one being replaced does not count against the cap), names it on the old record (`replacedBy`, committed before the old one's stop broadcasts) and stops the old one (`stoppedBy: 'relaunch'`). The asking window retargets from the answer at once; every other client's window follows the `replacedBy` in its broadcast; a layout replay of a replaced id follows the chain — same window, same place, the picture reconnects. The global setting stays the default for new launches.
  - **Measured on the real rung** (xpra 6.5.3, GNOME Calculator 50 and xterm, headless Chrome at DPR 2 with `vibespace.uiScale` 125; test-desktop-xpra-window §11 + test-desktop-app-keeper §20, two runs each): launched from the launcher's own catalog card ⇒ the record `2.5×, 120 dpi, auto, from {dpr 2, uiScale 1.25}`; inside the app's display GDK_SCALE=2 in the calculator's environ and `Xft.dpi: 120` in its resource database (xdpyinfo 120x120); the chip "2.5× · auto". The text half: the same 40×10 xterm is 1.23× larger at 2.5× (120 dpi) than at 2× (96 dpi) — 644×324 vs 524×264 device px, the fraction carried by the dpi. GNOME Calculator's minimum stays 720×1232 at 2.5× — it is button-bound (its 120-dpi text fits the 2× buttons). ⋯ → Scale ▸ 1.5× → Relaunch ⇒ the SAME VibeSpace window on BOTH pages names the successor 102–103 ms after the confirm, the successor is ready 1534–1549 ms after it (1349 ms keeper-side), runs at `1.5×, 144 dpi, chosen` (GDK_SCALE=1, Xft.dpi 144 measured; its minimum back to 360×616), the chip says "1.5× · chosen", the old session `exited` / `relaunch` / `replacedBy` with its calculator gone, one window per client. CONTROL = a keeper copy with the pre-A3 pick (the setting + dpr only): the same client gets 2× at Xft.dpi 96.
  - **Not done in A3.** The menu and the setting offer 1× / 1.5× / 2× (auto may still derive up to 3× — DPR 2 at UI 150 %); the seamless design's 2.5× / 3× rows are not offered explicitly. The relaunch is refused server-side for a non-ready / non-xpra / browser record, but an agent LEASE is gated on the client only (the keeper does not see window leases; the agent routes never reach `/relaunch`). Qt's fractional QT_SCALE_FACTOR and Electron's `--force-device-scale-factor` stay unmeasured (D9); the vnc-display rung is never scaled (a whole display at the browser's pixels).
  - **Gates.** test-desktop-apps 342 → 367 (§13: the design's derivation table row for row + the √2 / 2√2 boundaries, DPR 2 × 1.25 ⇒ GDK_SCALE 2 + 120 dpi, the explicit 1.5 stays text-only, the .158 answers unchanged with uiScale absent (the regression control), origins, the `uiScale` refusal by name, the relaunch request / verdict / body, the menu model, `exitCloseVerdict` → `relaunched`, wiring pins); test-xpra-client 223 → 224 (`launchUiScale` + the launch POST pin); heavy test-desktop-app-keeper 319 → 330 (§20 on the xpra rung: the derivation measured in the display, the xterm text ratio, the relaunch at 1.5× measured, the old record named before its stop broadcasts, refusals by name, the cap, the vnc-display rung, CONTROL = the pre-A3 pick); heavy test-desktop-xpra-window 154 → 173 (§11, the controls of §6/§7 re-spelled for the new levers).

**Chunk 2 — the channel side, server: the OAuth client lives on the account.** A channel account names its own client the way a storage mount does: an env preset by key (`cluster:<k>`, unchanged) or its OWN client (`custom` + `credential {appId, appSecretEnc}`, the secret sealed under `data/.channels-key`; adapters.json and integrations.json are now written 0600). Presets reach the account dialog as `{key,label}` from the one env reader both features share (Google: `drivePresets()`; Lark: `VIBESPACE_INTEGRATIONS`) — no new env name, the env-NAME and BUILDER censuses green. **Sign in before the account exists:** `POST /api/channels/oauth/start` `{kind, clientPreset | clientId + clientSecret | credentialKey | credential}`, `GET /api/channels/oauth/status`, `POST /api/channels/oauth/callback {url}` (the storage consent block's shapes; the adapter's own consent runs against an in-memory record whose token waits sealed), and `connect {flowId, name, options}` creates the record at that moment — a dialog closed half-way leaves nothing. **Re-authorize = the mount semantics:** naming another client is a re-authorization under it; the account keeps its old client and token until the new consent lands, then both are replaced in one write (a failed consent changes nothing); the old `credential-bound` refusal is gone. **Duplicate** (`POST /adapters/:id/duplicate {name?}`) copies exactly the declared `DUPLICATE_FIELDS` — type, client (a custom secret re-sealed), filters, push claim, sender line — and never the token, tracked conversations, assignments, reach grants or the log; the copy is unauthorized and signs in on its own. **Remove** (`DELETE /adapters/:id`) is refused `409 account-referenced` naming each reference — assignments, reach grants to the whole account, unsettled outbox proposals (agent groups never count); **Disconnect** only drops the token and now keeps EVERY account's record (the "a further account's disconnect removes it" special case is gone). Edit's in-place saves: `PUT /adapters/:id {label}` and `{credential}` (a custom client's secret, same id; another id ⇒ `409 client-change-needs-reauth`), and `GET /adapters/:id/config` (owner-only, D3 — the one answer that carries the custom secret, like the storage config route). **The Integrations window keeps only the six browser key rows:** lark / gmail / fake are `bindsPerAccount` rows with a `clientHint` each — `GET /api/integrations` leaves them out and every card verb on them answers `404 binds-per-account` by name; no Test verb on an account's client (D7). **Chunk 4a — D2: on the storage side too, switching the OAuth client IS a re-authorization.** In a Google Drive or Gmail connection's Edit dialog, changing the client the record resolves to (the `OAuth client` preset, or Drive's custom client id — a rotated secret of the same client is not a switch) used to save silently beside the old token, and the next refresh failed with `invalid_client`. ## 2.369.164 — small-fixes batch
- **r2 (mirror-only red, same version):** test-discovery-spawn §10 keyed its copy census on a constant (`minCopies: 1`) while its only copy-writing producer is a negative control gated on `git show <pre-fix ref>` — on the Actions mirror (a depth-1 checkout) every control skips, nothing is written, and the census went red while the full-history tree was green. The census now keys on whether any control ran (copies exist exactly when one did), reproduced and proven green in a local `git clone --depth 1` control; the rule (a census over copies counts the producers that ran, never a constant; any `git show <old ref>` producer is machine-dependent) is recorded in kb-bugfix-invariants.
- **r1 (integration follow-up, same version):** test-rate-limit-capture ⑥ now pins the same-source calibration rule where batch 8 moved it (`usage-estimator.sweepAnchorGroup`) and pins the engine to hold no inline copy of it; the pre-push fast gate caught the stale pin because the integration ran 44 suites by name instead of the fast tier as a whole — integrators run `node scripts/ci.mjs` (the fast tier) before the squash from now on.

- **batch 1 — B-0220: a suite's patched copies never live in the tree (`scripts/test-new-member-wake.mjs`, `scripts/test-auto-resume-loop.mjs`).** test-new-member-wake loaded its negative-control copies of `usage-pool-engine.js`, `account-usage-routes.js`, `usage-routes.js` and master's `auto-resume.js` as SIBLINGS inside `src/` (so their relative requires resolved; gitignored, so `git status` never showed them), and test-auto-resume-loop's §5 AUDIT — walk `src/`, classify every `noteRecovered` call site — counted the mutant engine as product code: 3 red in a 2026-09-22 integration that ran both at once, green alone. Now every copy goes through ONE helper, `loadCopy(origRel, src)`: written to this process's `scratch('wake-mut')` dir, its `require` re-bound on line 1 (line numbers unchanged) to `createRequire(<the real module's path>)`, so `./x` and `../x` reach the very files and require-cache entries a sibling would. The gitignore block for the old names is gone; a legacy sweep still removes copies a pre-fix run stranded (dead PID only). New legs, each RED on the pre-fix placement first: test-new-member-wake §10 reads `git status --porcelain --ignored --untracked-files=all -- src` while every copy still exists (after exit it would pass on the old code too) and checks the helper's own ledger is outside the checkout; test-auto-resume-loop now runs a HELD child of test-new-member-wake (`VS_WAKE_HOLD`: it stops after §10 with every copy on disk until released; a dead parent or 5 min releases it) and runs its whole self inside that window — pre-fix placement reproduces exactly the incident's 3 AUDIT reds. Counts: test-new-member-wake 119 → 121 (fast, ~5.7 s unchanged), test-auto-resume-loop 218 → 221 (heavy, ~8 s → ~14 s).
- **batch 2 — B-3ccf: `--heavy-launch` does not re-run a heavy tier already GREEN for that very sha (`scripts/ci.mjs`).** A hand-run `npm run ci:heavy` before the push leaves `data/ci-heavy/<sha>.green`, and the pre-push hook's `--heavy-launch <sha>` started the same tier for the same sha again — on 2.369.102 a 35-min re-run that held the machine lock for a verdict already on disk. The launcher now asks the markers first through PURE `heavyAlreadyGreen`: a GREEN for exactly that sha (short shas resolved), not partial, whose FILE mtime is newer than the sha's commit time, and whose scope covers this launch (FULL covers any launch; AFFECTED only an affected launch over the SAME range, never one the 24 h net made FULL) ⇒ `heavy already GREEN for <sha> (<age>), not relaunching`, exit 0, no child. A RED (or a red newer than the green), a PARTIAL, a STALE or a narrower green still relaunches; an unknown commit time never skips. Asked AFTER supersession, so an ancestor's in-flight run is still stopped. test-ci-heavy-launch §8 (fast): end to end in a stub repo with the real module — fresh full green ⇒ no pid file, no log, marker untouched; stale / red / partial ⇒ a child is launched and waited out — plus 13 pure arms; RED on the unfixed launcher first (3 asserts: the export, the message, the child). 109 → 129. `scripts/dbg-ci-mutations.mjs` carries the matching mutant.

Now the resolver lives in ONE module (the boot spelling + an async twin) and `cliCmds.forSpawn(backend, cmd)` runs once right before the ONE local argv (pty terminal, chat wrapper and daemon pipe all spawn it): a path still executable costs one `access`; a gone one is re-resolved ONCE, handed to the adapter (claude / codex / every ACP harness) so later spawns are born right, and ONE journal line names the old and the new path; if nothing is found the spawn fails exactly as before, with a line saying so. ## 2.369.163 — quota: a named cap alone may retire a cap; the ledger re-keyed to the credential slot by a crash-resumable migration; the projection buys one owner-approved read per bucket window, persisted and clamped; B-ff38 held for the owner

The quota lane: B-9f4b and the two open items of the limit-fix batch (B-f69c, owner decision ut-1c6c15a2db ②③), each finding reproduced red first, then three adversarial verify rounds. B-ff38 was deliberately NOT built.

- **B-9f4b — only a cap the parse can NAME carries the right to retire (`src/quota-model.js`, `src/harnesses/claude-quota.js`, `src/adapters/claude-code.js`).** A code-named scoped bucket (`nimbus_quill: {utilization: 0, resets_at: null}`, the 2026-08-09 live `get_usage` envelope without its `seven_day_sonnet`) could claim the parse had listed every model cap and ERASE a real, spent Fable cap — end to end through the real write path the pool read that account 0 → 100 % free. Each claude parser now states how many caps it NAMED as a model (`scopedNamedCount`: a `limits[]`/`model_scoped` display name, a `seven_day_<model>` key, a `Current week (<model>)` panel line) and `authoritativeScopesOf` needs at least one; the code-named bucket is still kept and still counts for the MIN; a `model_scoped` name without a number is a drop. Latent on this instance (every one of the 123 real scoped readings names Fable). **One limit is no longer drawn as two donuts:** on a set with no plan limit (`__global_codex__`: the Spark model limit + credits) `toLegacyView` projected the limit promoted into the plan slot a second time as a `scopedWeekly` row; it is skipped exactly when its window IS the `sevenDay` it fills. The pool's answer is identical either way; files self-heal on their next write (no migration).
- **B-f69c ② — the ledger rows the OTel org attributed are re-keyed to the credential slot (`src/ledger-slot-backfill.js`, migration `2026-09-backfill-ledger-by-slot` in `src/server/migrations.js`, `src/usage-history.js`).** From 2.361.0 until the 2026-09-07 attribution law the org the CLI cached at SPAWN chose a permanent ledger row's account twice over (the bake override by rid and the corrective attribution entries every later bake inherited). The one-shot migration touches only PROVABLE rows — billed through a pool AND demonstrably written by that path (the OTel stash names the rid, or a corrective entry governs it), the slot proven by the slot-transition ledger or the conversation's own walk, refused inside a re-point's lag shadow or on a slot whose login was already dead; a row whose slot names its own account is confirmed and left alone. Proven ⇒ re-keyed in place (tokens kept, `slotRekeyedBy`/`slotRekeyedFrom`, the original archived); unprovable ⇒ ARCHIVED with a per-row reason, never a guess; the corrective entries archived out of attribution.ndjson; every moved identity re-learned (one spelling per anchors file); the re-bake never re-derives a slot-proven row. On this instance's shape: 37,399 re-keyed / 5,337 archived / 84 corrective, 5 identities re-learned; idempotent (a byte-identical second run); crash-resumable with a pass marker — a pass killed at any point is resumed, never archived twice, a torn archive tail closed before appending, the whole repair's totals reported.
- **B-f69c ③ — the estimator's projection asks the owner-approved fast rung ONCE per bucket window, 8–10 min before the line (`src/account-pool-auto.js`, `src/usage-estimator.js`, `src/server/usage-pool-engine.js`, `src/server/auto-cli-loop.js`).** The burn (`burnRates`: learned rate × the trailing 10-min ledger + live cost) projects each member's buckets; a crossing of a live conversation's switch line before the next scheduled reading asks `claude -p /usage` now — the same `refreshViaCliPanel`, the same floor/backoff/one-per-tick, no new vendor path, never a cadence — only when the crossing is inside `PROJECTION_WINDOW_MS` (10 min), never on a reading younger than the 5-min floor (a passive reading IS the reading), and never again for that bucket before its window resets; a read of any rung inside the window buys the bucket. A COLD conversation decides on the view 5 min ahead and moves early, saying so; a projection alone never moves a WARM one. **The auto-cli loop now lives in `src/server/auto-cli-loop.js`** (out of server.js, 2099 → 2045 lines) with its attempt clock, backoff and bought buckets persisted to `data/auto-cli-state.json` — stamped BEFORE the spawn, stamps from a stepped-back clock clamped to now, an unreadable file said once, shared by every account id of one identity group.
- **The producer fix (`src/usage-routes.js`).** `refreshViaCliPanel` no longer answers `true` on a refused write — it had made the idle rung re-spawn every floor on a cache that never advanced; a refused write now takes the loop's failure backoff and the ⟳ route says "not recorded".
- **Three adversarial rounds.** r1 — 1 medium: the projection re-bought at the floor for the whole approach of a slow crossing (7 reads before one line) (+ a `from:null` re-point lost its lag shadow in the backfill). r2 — 4 medium: the instant-keyed memory was defeated by burn noise (Poisson arrivals: 3–4 reads per line, a 10-member fleet 42 in an hour), a fresh passive reading was re-bought, the in-memory pacing state was lost on every restart (a crash loop: 11–15 spawns in 40 min), a crashed backfill archived the same rows twice (32,837 duplicate lines) (+ the relearn's phantom spellings, the number-less `model_scoped` name). r3 — 2 medium: a future-stamped state file pinned every rung off (a 720 h clock step: 0 spawns in 4 h), the projection read was spent at the first tick the floor allowed, the farthest point from the line (+ the stamp-before-spawn order, the identity-shared memory, the producer's boolean, the torn archive tail, the finished-pass marker).
- **B-ff38 NOT shipped.** Production data contradicts the spec: the disabled-reason it keys on sits on healthy, serving members. The owner decides.
- **Integration (merged onto 2.369.162) — the heavy gate went RED on a network round trip, not on this lane.** The first heavy run of the merged tree (5c941bf0) failed test-incident twice (ECONNREFUSED on its first POST) and five suites once (test-chat-paging, test-ax-budget, test-toolbar-resize, test-attach-rescue: no `window.app`; test-permission-rules: ENOENT), all green on the same lane's heavy run seven hours earlier. ① Every suite's scratch server ran server.js's boot `git pull --ff-only` — a network fetch into the SHARED .git before `listen`: 0.5–0.9 s to the first `/api/home` with `NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`, 2.5–15.5 s without, past the 10 s window 18 scratch suites wait before falling through. A server whose code lives under the OS temp dir now never auto-updates and says so (`[auto-update] skipped: throwaway/temp server root`, the hookRegistrationSafe rule); test-incident pins it (that line and no `pull --ff-only`; a 60 s boot wait that fails loudly with the boot log; boot now ~790 ms), negative control = the same suite over 2.369.162's server.js fails the pin on its `pull --ff-only` line. ② test-permission-rules' mk()-ref sweep walked src/ while test-restore-liveness wrote and unlinked a gitignored pre-fix copy of session-stdout.js in a parallel lane; the sweep now reads the git listing (tracked + untracked-not-ignored), control = a planted gitignored copy carrying the retired `ref?.()` call turns the pre-fix suite red on exactly that line and leaves the fixed one green.
- **Gates.** test-quota-model 358 · test-pool-auto 197 · test-auto-cli-refresh 92 · test-migrations 157 · test-usage-estimator 94 · test-new-member-wake 123 · test-get-usage-parse 36 · test-fable-cap-pool-storm 358 · test-codex-quota 18 · test-auto-resume 231 · test-auto-resume-loop 218 · test-readings-attribution 513 · test-spend-paths 291 · test-vendor-whitelist 63 · test-architecture 195 · test-incident 36 · test-permission-rules 165 — every new leg red on the unfixed tree, each fix with a scratch-dir patched copy as its negative control; all stubs, zero vendor calls.
- **Docs.** kb-bugfix-invariants (the scratch-server boot `git pull` entry) + its CLAUDE.md index line, kb-file-structure server.js (the auto-update guard); kb-file-structure (quota-model.js, account-pool-auto.js projection essay, usage-estimator.js, usage-history.js, usage-routes.js, the new auto-cli-loop.js and ledger-slot-backfill.js entries, the migration entry), kb-design-lessons (§9 addenda B-9f4b / B-f69c ③, §18 rows), kb-bugfix-invariants (the r6 entry's and the 130-fire entry's follow-ups), CLAUDE.md (two index lines, gate counts).

## 2.369.162 — side by side: an explicit second step — no drag ever splits (the title-bar half drop zone is gone, the tab merge stays the one drag exception); the strip's ⫿ button (one pulse + a "Grouped as tabs → Show side by side" toast right after a merge), the window menu's "Show side by side ▸ Beside {name}" and command mode's v / V enter it — with the strip in the panes' visual order, the same button as the badge (Unsplit / Swap left and right) and every announced split undoable for 5 s

docs/design-split-ux.zh.md (+ the English mirror), lane-split: the design, then three chunks — (1) the model + the window-manager core, (2) the verbs and surfaces, (3) the owner-gesture chrome gate — and the verifier's round (r1), one release.

- **What the owner saw — three problems.** (1) a drag meant to move a window entered side by side by accident; (2) the window landed on the wrong side (dragged left, shown on the right); (3) in side by side the tabs were not in the panes' order and the split could not be told apart from plain tabs. In the owner's words: "我本来是想拖动窗口到左侧，结果莫名其妙进入了side by side模式 … side by side模式下标题栏的标签位置不符合直觉 … side by side模式和普通tabbed模式不太好区分 … 我往左拖却让窗口出现在了右侧" — and, as the binding second directive: "尽量不要搞太多拖动时候的复杂逻辑 … 保持tab逻辑是唯一正常拖动吸附机制的例外，然后tab合并后在增加切换成side by side的按钮". The screenshot: one title bar, two tabs ("Fi…", "Vi…"), two panes, nothing in the chrome saying "split".
- **The rule the owner set.** No drag ever splits; the tab merge (icon onto icon / onto a tab strip) stays the ONLY drag exception to move / snap / grid; side by side is an explicit SECOND step after the merge — a button, a menu verb or a key, never a drop zone.
- **Why (reproduced, `scripts/dbg-split-gesture.mjs`).** 80 % of a title bar was a split drop zone, and the split shadowed the snap band. `tab-group.js:_detectSplitDropTarget` ran on EVERY frame of a title-bar drag (`window.js:_setupDrag`) and a tab drag (`_setupTabDrag`) and armed a split on the left/right half of ANY other window's title bar outside the icon/tab/controls — no hover intent, no modifier, 80 % of a title bar (489 / 610 px); on release the split branch ran BEFORE the snap, so a window dragged to the screen edge over a snapped window's bar split while the snap indicator was showing. The side came from `chain-layout.dropSide` = which half of the TARGET's bar the pointer was on, never the drag direction (a pointer arriving from the right enters the right half first). `_renderTabBar` drew the chain order (host first) whatever the panes' order, and the only split mark was a 9 px `⫿ ` pseudo-glyph (a tofu box on common fonts) beside a divider the colour of the window border.
- **Research (design §3).** VS Code (the Split Editor button), JetBrains (tab menu Split Right / Split Down), Arc (Add Split View) and Chrome 145+ (tab menu; its one drag entry needs a dwell + an explicit label) are button-or-menu first; tmux (`prefix %`) and iTerm2 (`⌘D`) are keys only — none arms a split from half of a title bar, so VibeSpace takes a button, a menu verb and a command-mode key.
- **What changed.** (1) NO drag ever splits: `_detectSplitDropTarget` / `_markSplitDrop` / `.tab-split-drop-*` / both drop branches / `dropSide` deleted, no body zone added; a window drag is move / snap / grid, and the tab merge (icon stack / tab bar) is untouched and stays the only exception. (2) The explicit entries, all through `wm.bindSplit(anchor, guest, {side, announce:true})`: the strip's `.tab-split-btn` (the `columns` SVG) on any ≥ 2-tab chain = `splitActive` (the active tab LEFT beside the most recently active other tab, `chain.recent`, local); right after a USER merge (the three merge drops only — never a restore or a remote sync) it pulses once and a 5 s "Grouped as tabs" toast offers "Show side by side" in one click (`showToast` gains `action`); the window menu's "Show side by side ▸ Beside {name} (on the right)" (and Unsplit / Swap left and right in a split; a tab's right-click now opens THAT tab's own window menu); command mode `v` (toggle) / `V` (swap) + `chain.unsplit` / `chain.splitBeside`, a toast — never silence — without a group; the live view's "Snap beside" is announced (undoable), its auto-bind stays silent. (3) The strip in a split is drawn in VISUAL order (the design's variant A) (PURE `visualTabOrder`: the left pane's tab, an aria-hidden `.tab-split-glyph`, the right pane's tab, then the hidden tabs), each pane tab underlined in its owner colour. (4) The same button is the badge: `.on` + aria-pressed, click ⇒ Unsplit / Swap left and right (`swapSplit`, PURE `swappedPair`; the chainSyncKey carries the pair so other clients rebuild); the divider rests brighter than a border (accent 35 % mixed in), lights on hover and its right-click carries the same two verbs. (5) Undo: an announced split snapshots both windows and offers Undo for 5 s — a guest that was free comes back out at its own rect, a guest that was already a tab restores the chain's previous layout, and a stale undo SAYS "Nothing to undo any more — the group changed". The phone (≤ 768 px) is unchanged: one pane, no button / glyph, the split kept in the model and never flattened. zh + ja for every new string.
- **Measured.** Before (2.369.160, `scripts/dbg-split-gesture.mjs`, 1280×900, A snapped left, B free on the right): G1 B dragged Δx −409 px LEFT and released on the right half of A's bar ⇒ split with B on the RIGHT, snap indicator showing; G2 released at the workspace's left edge + 12 over A's bar ⇒ split pair [B,A] shadowing the left snap, strip [A,B]; 0 glyph / badge / button elements after a split; divider background == window border (rgba(255,255,255,.07)); 80 % of a title bar a split zone. After (`test-split-ux`, 73 green at chunk 3, 85 after r1): G1 (released on A's bar below the snap band) ⇒ no chain, B moved 409 px left to the pointer-carried rect ±8 px; the exact §1 path (inside the top band) ⇒ the top snap the indicator promised ±2 px; G2 ⇒ the left snap zone ±2 px, `_isSnapped`; a 1.5 s hold over A's body ⇒ no chain; the merge + one toast click ⇒ pair [B,A], strip [B,A], one glyph between, underlines = each session's owner colour (computed); swap / unsplit (host ±1 px), Undo (B back ±2 px), the stale-undo toast, the divider lit on hover (rgb(45,212,191) vs the border's rgba(255,255,255,.07)), a second desktop client following the split and a swap with no revert, the phone one pane, command mode v / v / V. The same suite against a checkout of 2.369.160: 10 failed / 15 passed (G1, the §1 path and G2 split; no button, no toast).
- **Split r1 (the verifier's three, each reproduced in headless Chrome first).** ① On a ≥ 3-tab group the strip button's tooltip named the partner from BEFORE a plain tab switch (`chain.recent` moves on every switch, the label was computed once at render) while the click split with `splitPartner` of the new `recent` — `_labelSplitBtn` now writes title/aria-label and `switchTab` re-runs it. ② After a split through the strip button the post-merge "Grouped as tabs" toast stayed up with a "Show side by side" action that did nothing — the toast is kept on the chain, every `bindSplit` of that chain withdraws it, and if its action still runs after the group changed it SAYS "Already shown side by side" / "The tab group changed — nothing to show side by side" (two new keys, zh + ja). ③ The window menu's "Beside {name} (on the right)" moved the focus to the NAMED partner (right-click A, type into C) while the strip button kept it on the clicked tab — the rule is now one: every user entry (button, menu, command mode's `chain.splitBeside`) passes `focus:'anchor'`; the default 'guest' stays for the programmatic `intoChain` bind and the live view's Snap beside. Gates: test-split-ux 73 → 85 (leg 11, a third session; red on the pre-r1 tree: 5 legs) · test-contributions 203 (the two bindSplit shape pins now carry `focus:'anchor'`; red against the pre-r1 taskbar/command-mode).
- **Honest limits / found, not fixed.** A drag gives no split at all any more — a "dragged" split is merge-then-click (two steps, the owner's accepted cost).
