## 2.369.161 — the record-shape oracle follows CLI 2.1.281 — the gate went red the moment the CLI auto-updated

The Claude Code CLI on the developer box auto-updated 2.1.280 → 2.1.281 and scripts/test-record-shape.mjs (fast tier, inside every push's pre-push gate) read `union 0 shapes · 0 system subtypes · 0 stream record types` from the new binary: five §4 legs red, every push blocked.

- **Why.** Nothing in the SDK record union changed shape. The minifier re-assigned its short names across the whole bundle (the zod object helper `u(` → `d(`, the lazy wrapper `p(` → `f(`, the boolean `H()` → `O()`, the enum `V(` → `z(`), and the extractor had `u(`/`R(` spelled into its regex.
- **What changed.** The extractor (`extractZodUnion`) reads the helper pair off an ANCHOR — the `system/compact_boundary` object (else `init` / `task_started`), which exists only in that union — and walks every object literal spelled with that pair. An identifier guard keeps a method call ending in the helper's letter out (2.1.281's MCP content blocks carry `QVt.extend({type:R("resource_link")})`, which a bare `d(` matched as a fake shape). A form it does not know fails a leg whose message NAMES the anchor, never a silent 0 / 0 / 0. New §4a pins the 2.1.280 and 2.1.281 spellings, a future rename, an unminified `z.object`/`z.literal` bundle and the no-anchor error.
- **The 2.1.281 census.** 155 shapes · 52 system subtypes · 35 stream record types (2.1.280: 154 · 51 · 35). New subtype `system/per_turn_effort_changed {per_turn_effort_active}` — sent when the server refused the per-turn effort message; from then on an effort switch rewrites the prompt cache — goes on `DECLARED_UPSTREAM_UNSEEN`, so the fall-back Unknown-event card shows it (a dim notice plus an effort-picker warning is proposed, not built). Six fields declared `ignored` with reasons: `system/init` +{per_turn_effort_active, view_mode}, `assistant` +{local_command_outcome}, `conversation_reset` +{trigger, user_message_uuid, timestamp}. No field or top-level type was removed. `SCHEMA_CLI_VERSION` = '2.1.281'.
- **Older CLIs still pass.** `SHAPE_SINCE` names the build that first declared a row. The reverse legs (dead list entry / ghost shape) excuse a newer row on an older installed CLI and print it by name; the forward legs stay strict. STRICT green against 2.1.273, 2.1.274, 2.1.280 and 2.1.281 (`VIBESPACE_ORACLE_BINARY` pins the file the oracle reads).
- **The drift alarm still fires.** A scratch dump of the 2.1.281 binary with one planted field on `system/task_started` fails the ⊆ leg naming `claude:stream:system/task_started.planted_drift_field`. The suite now carries the same control in memory on the real union.
- **Gates.** test-record-shape 76 (+15; 1 skip = the opt-in local census), test-unknown-records 61, test-architecture 195, test-fixture-isolation 86; `npm run build` green.
- **Docs.** docs/design-unknown-records.md §4 (the 2.1.281 census), kb-file-structure (record-shape.js, message-manager.js), CLAUDE.md index line.

## 2.369.160 — inc-mudv05ja-n5rv: the pinned chat windows flickered — fresh cards painted at their placeholder, swapped cards lost their fold, the pinned scroll chased both; the live workflow card and the detail window now update in place; a tab return is not a jank storm; the freeze keeps session-meta whole

The owner's report "不知道是不是workflow的问题，界面有点异常闪烁" (the UI flickers abnormally — maybe the workflow's doing) arrived 12 minutes after an incident that had filed itself ("jank storm — 13.3s"). Integration of two parallel lanes (fix-inc-mudv05ja: the side bugs and the root fixes; fix-inc-mudv05ja-card: the same card fix built independently — its agent-state words, its suite legs and its measurement harness were ported onto the first lane's patcher, its own patcher was not taken: two patchers would be one bug).

- **What the owner saw.** In five pinned compact chat windows (120 Hz) the whole window content jumped by up to 1.5 viewports and snapped back 1–3 frames later, on every tool completion, every workflow heartbeat and every live append: TEN identical +678 px pop/unpop pairs in 37 s on the workflow session's window, a 12-write ±678–836 px shake of the pinned scroll in 197 ms, a +940/−730 px jump on another window exactly at the 180 ms fold debounce. The live Workflow card blinked on every progress record (a Script the reader had opened snapped shut, the working agents' dots restarted), and the View Workflow window re-drew itself every 2.5 s.
- **Why.** ① A freshly created chat card enters `content-visibility:auto` LOCKED at its placeholder (80 px; 0 px in compact) until its first relevance check, and every tool completion, re-render, live append and live Workflow heartbeat created one — and dropping a reservation's override on screen re-locks the card for a frame (measured 197 → 0 → 197). ② A swapped card lost the four run-fold classes, and the fold pass ran before the next paint only for pure tail appends — a replaced folded card, or an append at the trim cap, painted unfolded until the 180 ms debounce. ③ The pinned scroll rewrote `scrollTop = scrollHeight` for ten frames whatever happened and so chased every one of those transients. ④ A running Workflow emits a `task_progress` per agent tool use (several a second) and each one re-rendered the WHOLE card through the swap point — label, View Workflow button, both `<details>`, the tree, every chip. ⑤ The CLI's words for a working agent are `start` / `progress` (8 production buffers: 161 progress, 26 start, 253 done, 56 error, zero `running`), so the chip's pulse and the tally's "N running" never showed in production at all. ⑥ The View Workflow window cleared and rebuilt itself on every 2.5 s poll. The owner's suspicion was partly right: the workflow card made its window the loudest, but the mechanism is generic.
- **What changed.** `_swapMessageEl` is geometry- and fold-neutral: the run classes ride the swap, every run record is re-pointed, and a rendered card — a swap or a live append — gets its real height reserved in its first frame, the override held until the card has left the screen (one IntersectionObserver per view) instead of released on screen. PURE `foldPassMode(records)` (chat-run-summary.js) folds tail appends, 1:1 replaces and trim-cap appends before the next paint. `_forceScrollToBottom` writes only when there is somewhere to go and stops once scrollHeight held still for two frames or swung A-B-A. A Workflow `taskInfo` edit patches the card IN PLACE (`_scheduleWorkflowPatch` → `_patchWorkflowCard`, one pass per frame and at most one per 150 ms): the status chip, the phases and the agent chips keyed by `data-agent-key` (the pulsing dot never re-created), the ✓ line — the `<details>` and the View Workflow button are never touched, and a card that draws nothing from taskInfo (a pending tool call, an error result: `drawsWorkflowCard`) is left alone. PURE `workflowAgentState` maps start / progress / running to `running` in ONE place, read by the chip and the tally. The View Workflow window renders only when the run's JSON changed, keeps its head and status chip node, keys its rows by agentId and keeps expander state; its state dots are `aria-hidden`.
- **Measured.** The card, in headless Chrome against a stub `claude` emitting task_progress at 3/s, before = 2.369.159, after = this tree (the parallel lane's harness, re-run on the shipped patcher; the lane's own numbers on its patcher were identical): whole-card replacements per 10 s **30 → 0**; agent-chip re-creations **120 → 0**; the steady running chip's pulse restarted **9 times in 3 s → 0** (monotonic 11.6 s → 14.5 s); the chip fed the real word `progress`: **no animation → pulses**; an opened Script: **shut within 3 s → stays open**; the tally with four agents working: **"0/4 · 1 running" → "0/4 · 4 running"**; the usage line still updates live (25k → 175k tokens). The window, in test-fold-ux's chrome legs on a live-shaped view (each with an in-page pre-fix control that reproduces the defect): a folded member's replacement unfolded in **6 of 6** sampled frames → display:none in all; a visible card's swap at the placeholder for **2 frames** (heights 0, 0, 197…) → **0**; 6 s of live appends rewrote scrollTop while already at the bottom **72 times → 0**, zero A-B-A frames; the reproduction's pinned list showed **83 A-B-A frames in 8 s** before the fix.
- **Honest limits.** A live card's reservation is held until the card leaves the screen instead of a two-frame release; paging slabs keep their tuned two-frame release, so a layout read in that frame can still see 0 px there. The owner's ±678/940 px amplitudes were not reproduced — the test scene's cards are shorter (jumps of about 200 px); the mechanisms were, each with a control. Not done: the judge's optional cheap items C (the status bar's tasks chip removed and re-added when the task set empties), D (`setTitleMeta` without a no-op guard on the 5 s sidebar merge) and F (the Agent card's status line rebuilt with its View Log button per subagent frame), E (the window-waiting blink after a turn — a product question, left alone on purpose), and recording the real rAF interval in the incident snapshot.
- **A tab return is not a jank storm (`src/lib/telemetry-client.js`).** The auto incident's whole evidence was ONE rAF interval of 13 288 ms, logged 1 ms after the tab came back from a 254 s hide: the loop pushed a frame gap when `!document.hidden`, which is already false at a return, and `jankStormVerdict` read it 3 s later as 13.3 s of slow frames — an auto incident and a whole scene freeze on every long tab hide. PURE `frameGapIsReturn` keeps such an interval out of the ring, and `jankStormVerdict(…, {visibleSince})` skips one that straddles the return; a genuine storm after the return still fires.
- **The freeze keeps session-meta whole (`src/incident.js`).** Session-meta and wrapper-meta were frozen through a 64 KiB byte cap that keeps the tail bytes; since 2.369.140 a meta carries `taskRecords` (the owner's own: 96 877 B), so both bundles held an unparseable fragment — for exactly the sessions with workflows. `copyJsonWhole`: the file whole up to 2 MiB; above that valid JSON trimmed as data (the largest array keeps its newest records; `_frozenTrimmed` names each field, its counts and the original size); an unparseable file freezes as `{_frozenTrimmed, rawTail}`.
- **Gates.** test-task-lifecycle 57 (+17: the real normalizer into the real ChatView, renderers and status bar over a parsing mini DOM — 30 progress edits leave the same element with 0 swaps; the steady chip and its dot are the same nodes and draw `running` from `progress`; the patched tree equals a fresh render byte for byte; 10 passes = 10 patches; a no-change update writes nothing to the document; an opened Script stays open; a terminal edit is applied in one pass and equals a fresh render; a pending card is left alone; the status-bar chips keep their nodes; XSS over both patch paths; the vocabulary table; the pre-fix negative control bundled from the same source gives 30 swaps, a re-created chip and dot and a shut Script — red first on the pre-port patcher: the vocabulary legs and the pending-card leg); test-fold-ux 89 (heavy; the chrome legs above + the `foldPassMode` table and its control + the F2 leg fed the real words — the dot pulses and the tally counts it, red on a pre-mapping copy); test-chat-trim-guard 184 (the pin chain's unit table + control); test-freeze-probe 26; test-incident 35; test-desktop-resume-paging 40 (its negative-control marker now follows `_reserveFreshHeights`'s new `{ live }` signature — the drifted marker had failed it loudly since r2). test-run-collapse-fold (heavy): its "synchronous tail-append path" pin read the minified bundle for the spelling `nextSibling===null`, which `foldPassMode` writes as `== null` — re-pinned on the classifier's behaviour (a tail append → raf, a mid-list insert → debounce) and on the observer's call. Unchanged and green on the merged tree, one at a time: test-chat-paging (all fixtures + its pre-fix controls), test-workflow-live-view 17, test-turn-truth-ui 80, test-hidden-view-suspend 42, test-worktree-userchan-ui 85, test-harness-contract 368, test-collab-live-counter 79, test-status-bar-chips 39, test-ax-paint 20, test-architecture 195, test-fixture-isolation 86, test-session-schema 5, test-server-globals 2, test-ws-contract 5; `npm run build` green. Heavy tier (the gate-computed scope b5715787..HEAD = the FULL tier, package files changed): **GREEN, 127 of 127** on a clean commit whose code is this one; the first run was RED on test-run-collapse-fold (the spelling pin above) and test-opencode-plugin (a 30 s server-boot timeout while four lanes saturated the box — green alone and in the second run). test-chat-paging failed its first attempt in both runs and passed each retry: once the harness error that 2.369.159 reproduces under the same Chrome contention, once a downward-gesture anchor loss that six further runs (four under load, two beside three Chrome suites) did not reproduce — named, not explained.
- **Docs.** kb-bugfix-invariants (ONE incident entry), kb-file-structure (chat-view.js, chat-renderers.js, workflow-detail.js, telemetry-client.js, incident.js), kb-design-lessons §11 (the first-frame lock), CLAUDE.md one index line.

**Also in 2.369.160 (r2):** scripts/test-transcript-parity.mjs no longer races its own daemon at teardown — it SIGTERMs the scratch agentd, waits for the pid to be gone (5 s, then SIGKILL) and removes the scratch home/data dirs with retries; the bare `rmSync` right after the kill hit ENOTEMPTY three times in the fast gate on 2026-09-23 with every assertion green, blocking a push each time.

## 2.369.159 — agent groups: the Communication panel is an IM whose first screen is the group list; a group exists only because somebody made one (`send <agent>` is the pair's two-member group), and each member's notify mode decides what reaches it when — a report on its next user turn is free, a wake is a billed turn through the one ladder, paced and counted before the act — four adversarial rounds

docs/design-communication-panel.zh.md §22 (+ the English twin's new §22), owner rulings D1/D2 + the §22.5 table. Squash of feat-comm-groups (the build g1–g4 and the verifier's rounds r1–r4).

- **What the owner asked for.** "我不太需要一个 agent 订阅另一个 agent 的消息作为信息源这种 feature … 我设想的是第一位看到的是'群列表' … 一个简易 IM" — the subscribe-to-an-agent shape becomes a secondary *Message watcher* and the panel opens on the groups. **D1:** "agent 主动拉群, agent 不再能'私聊', 或者说 agent 私聊本质上就是自动建立一个两人群。每个 Task Group 还是不要自动建群了, 感觉会有 spam 风险。" — groups are EXPLICIT: `vibespace-msg group create` or the panel's New group; `send <agent>` finds or creates the two-member group of that pair (symmetric, exactly one per pair, it takes no third member); no Task Group ever becomes a group by itself. **D2:** "每个群成员可以自行设置'通知模式', 默认是'下次用户发消息收报告'。" — every (group, member) carries `notify` ∈ `next-turn` (default) | `mention` | `always` | `mute`; a member sets its own, the owner anyone's. And "拉群要设计一下, 建群之后是不是还能拉人, 拉人的时候可以附加 context 消息? 我需要手动拉人能力" — invite after creation, with a context message, by hand from the panel too.
- **The first screen is the group list (the owner's clarification, beside D1/D2).** ONE list of every agent group and every TRACKED conversation of a connected account (Lark chats, Gmail threads), newest activity first: source glyph · name · time / a source chip (`Agents`, `Direct`, the account's label) · the last line · the owner's unread. Archived groups fold apart; the list repaints in place from the broadcasts (no fetch); the rail's Channels badge counts the groups' unread. **Accounts** and the **Message watcher** (the §7/§8/§9 filter / assign / reach / outbox machinery, unchanged) fold BELOW, the fold persisted in user state and followed across clients. A group opens in the same `channel` window: its log (system records worded by kind in the device's language, an invite's context under its record) and a detail pane (the owner first as *You (observer)*, a notify select per member, Remove, Invite…, Rename…, Archive). A store that was set aside (see data safety) is a warning line above the list.
- **What is free and what costs a turn.** FREE: a message under `next-turn` — appended to the group log and handed to each member as ONE report on that member's next USER-initiated turn (a turn a person started; a turn any ladder rung or auto-resume started gets no report, so agents cannot talk each other into an echo chamber on the owner's money); a `--quiet` invite; a plain `send`; `mute` (no wake, no report — `read` on purpose). BILLED: a WAKE — an @mention of a member (every mode but `mute`), an invite (unless `--quiet`; N invitees = N wakes), every message to an `always` member, `send --wake` — is the member's report delivered NOW down THE delivery ladder under `spendReason:'peer-message'`; a refused wake is journaled (`group-wake` in the channels audit) and never stashed (the message is in the log and rides the next report).
- **The owner's own words go out directly; agent drafts still propose.** In a group the composer sends as You (`@` autocompletes member names; a preview of who THIS text wakes, parity-tested against the engine's `wakeVerdict`, said before the click). On an external conversation that offers `sendAsUser` the owner's message goes out directly too (`POST /api/channels/:a/:c/send` = a user proposal with `direct:true`: no policy, no guard, still the outbox record + audit + the never-re-sent `unknown`); where only the bot identity is offered the composer keeps the proposal path and says why. An agent's `direct` is ignored — agent drafts keep the outbox cards.
- **What an agent can do.** `vibespace-msg group list` (= `groups`), `group create|invite|leave|kick|rename|archive|notify`, `read <group> [--before <ts>] [--limit n]`, `send <group|agent> "…" [--wake] [--yes]`. Every answer ECHOES the wakes as billed turns — `woke 2 agents = 2 billed turns: beta, gamma`, said at zero too, a refused or floored wake marked `(not billed)` with its reason. A refusal prints `refused [<code>] — <why>` + a remedy and exits 1 (2 outside a session, 3 server gone); a name several sessions or groups share — or a bare name that is both a group and a session — is refused `ambiguous` WITH the candidate ids, never guessed. A Background Work job (jbt_) speaks as its owner conversation — list / read / send only, never creates a group or changes membership (`job-token`, refused locally and by every group op). The manual (`vibespace-docs msg`) opens with `## Groups`; the Reporting-back teaching every Task-Group session gets carries ONE pointer line.
- **The money mechanics.** Every wake — whichever verb causes it — asks ONE pacer: at most one wake per sender → member conversation per 30 s and at most 8 wakes per sender per minute; a floored wake is said like an authorizer refusal (`rate floor`, not billed, the message still posted and in the member's next report). The count comes BEFORE the act: an agent's send / create / invite that would wake more than 5 is refused `confirm-wakes` (with the number, nothing written) until it says `--yes` / `yes:true`. The owner's routes carry the consent echo — the panel sends the count its preview said as `expectWakes`, the engine counts inside its door and refuses `409 wake-count-mismatch` on any other number (a missing echo is 0; the 409 carries the group view it counted against so the composer repaints) — including the Channels composer's `/send`, `/propose` and the outbox `/approve` into the built-in Agents adapter (the adapter module declares `sendStartsTurn`; test-architecture §49 censuses every owner route that can start a turn). With auth off the owner is paced exactly like an agent (with auth on, the cookie proved the owner). Every wake still goes through the spend authorizer. The pace is persisted (`data/channels/wake-pace.json`; a stamp more than 5 s in the future is ignored and pruned); a wake that did not go out refunds its pair slot while the attempt stays in the sender's minute, and a throw after the grant before anything reached the authorizer or the adapter (a blocked store's 503, an EACCES / ENOSPC outbox write) gives back the pair AND the sender's minute, so the retry is sent, not floored by a wake that never happened (once the adapter's send was called, the wake counts).
- **Data safety: the ONE channel-store loader.** Every JSON store under `data/channels/` loads through one reader: an unreadable file is set aside as `<name>.corrupt-<ts>` with its bytes kept (never unlinked), logged in one named line and reported as ONE "For you" item before the store starts empty (before, a corrupt `groups.json` read as empty and the first group verb overwrote every group). A failed rename BLOCKS that store's writes — every family's refusal is `code:'store-blocked'` / 503, the action refused and said (not answered ok and lost at restart), every refused flush logged, a blocked `wake-pace.json` never overwritten; a file that could not be set aside says so in its own words. The digest (GET /api/channels, every `channels-updated`) carries `quarantined`, drawn on the first screen.
- **The report budget.** A next-turn report is budgeted as its WHOLE text (three forms, fullest first, else `fits:false` and the group waits with its marker unmoved); news after the member's JOIN only, the invite context first, newest kept; a line longer than 400 characters is cut and followed by `(N message(s) above cut short — the whole text: vibespace-msg read <group> --before <ts> --limit <n>)`; prompt-context appends ONE `### Group messages since your last turn` section LAST from what the 9600 B cap left (≤ 4 KiB for all groups), taken back report by report until it fits, and moves its markers only when it fits uncut; a turn with no room still names up to three waiting groups.
- **The unread memo.** The owner's unread per group is memoised against the read mark and `lastAt` and moved by the one log-append door (a broadcast used to re-read every unread group's whole log — ~100 ms of main loop per agent post at 200 groups × 500 messages; now about 1–2 ms, and the lists read no log). The owner's mark `ownerRead` moves only by the owner's own act; a no-op mark broadcasts nothing.
- **The model and the engine.** PURE `src/channel-groups.js` (the record keyed by CONVERSATION id so a resume keeps the identity; the owner implicit, never stored; membership as pure transitions from a closed error set; `mentionsIn`, `wakeVerdict` = the D2 table, `reportFor`). ORCH `src/server/groups-engine.js`: `data/channels/groups.json` behind channel-store's serialized `groups.*` door, each group's log an append-only `msgs/groups/<id>.ndjson` with system records, invite reach = msg-acl `messageable` from the inviter (one uniform refusal), every change broadcasting `channel-groups-updated`, a member whose name or liveness moved re-announced through the session list's one notify point (`noteRoster`, nothing moved ⇒ nothing sent). Routes: the agent side `/api/agent/msg/groups`, `/read`, `/group`; the owner side `/api/channel-groups` (list / messages / roster / create / post / invite / kick / rename / archive / notify / read). The panel: PURE `src/lib/channel-groups-view.js` + `src/lib/channel-group-dialogs.js` (New group — LIVE sessions grouped by Task Group, nothing pre-selected, no whole-group checkbox, "Wake now" with its billed-turn echo); every name, context and message through textContent; zh + ja for every string. A terminal's focus / query answers and mouse reports no longer count as a person typing.
- **Four adversarial rounds, every finding reproduced first and fixed red-first.** r1 — 4 medium (+3 low): an @mention was an unpaced wake and the `--wake` floor was keyed by spelling; a report could exceed its budget and lose its lines to the cap; a group named like a session took `send <that session>`; a cid-less sender took the pre-groups direct lane. r2 — 5 medium among nine: one command could spend a slot's hour (per-sender pace + count-before-act `--yes`), the owner's routes were unfenced with auth off (the echo), a corrupt store was overwritten (the loader), cut lines vanished (the pointer), every broadcast re-read the logs (the memo). r3 — 2 medium among eight: the composer's `/send` / `/propose` and the outbox `/approve` were side doors around the wake gate, and a renamed member made every Send a 409. r4 — 2 low, one cause: a throw between the wake grant and the send kept the floor.
- **Not built this round:** the source reply-model axis (`reply: thread | quote | none`, design §22.1) — channel-caps has no such axis yet.
- **Gates (merged with master 2.369.158, run one at a time on the final tree, 2026-09-23):** `npm run build` green (i18n-check 4490/4490, bundle-globals 6, test-architecture 195, ws-contract 5, session-schema 5); test-channel-groups 251 (PURE legs, the store's one door with a read-modify-write control, the engine over the REAL store + ladder with a recording authorizer, the user-turn report gate through the REAL prompt-context route, the groups.json one-writer census with a planted writer), test-msg-cli-groups 95, test-channels-groups-ui 61 (wake-preview parity over 320 rows with a mute-blind control, the XSS census with a planted `innerHTML`), test-channel-store 134, test-channels-engine 142, test-channel-outbox 107, test-channel-acl 47 (§3 = invite reach through msg-acl), test-spend-paths 291 (the engine's one ladder forward allowlisted, a patched copy posting beside it UNWIRED), test-architecture 195 (§49), test-fixture-isolation 86, test-migrations 105, test-integration-registry 208; heavy test-channels-groups-e2e 39 (two stub-CLI dtach sessions, every wake through the REAL ladder, auth ON with the owner's cookie — 43 s → 14 s), test-channels-e2e 135 (⑩b the composer's direct send), test-channels-i18n 27; the heavy tier for this range (package files ⇒ the FULL tier) GREEN, 127 of 127 suites in 979 s.

## 2.369.158 — desktop apps on HiDPI screens: the xpra rung renders the app at the screen's resolution (device pixels end to end, the app's scale fixed at launch by `desktop.appScale`), the app's minimum size clamps the VibeSpace window (capped by the workspace), and a phone shows the whole app scaled to fit and still clickable — never cropped

docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.6 (+ the English mirror). Squash of fix-xpra-dpi-minsize (the build and the verifier's round r2, whose five findings were each reproduced on the real rung before the fix).

- **The owner's three findings (2026-09-23, GNOME Calculator on the xpra rung, a devicePixelRatio-2 screen).** ① The keypad's lower rows were cut off: "if the inner window has a minimum height, the OUTER window's resize must be limited to that height". ② "The DPI is way too low — nowhere to adjust?" ③ "This still looks like VNC."
- **Root causes, measured.** ① The hello's `metadata.supported` was xpra-html5 v21's list, which names `size-hints` (the pre-4 name). xpra 6.x calls them `size-constraints` and sends only the keys a client lists, so no window ever carried its minimum: the fit belt asked for a pane shorter than the calculator's 616 px, X clamped the window to its minimum and the pane cropped it. With the key the calculator says `{increment:[2,2], minimum-size:[360,616]}`. ② The pane's CSS px were used as X px: the app drew a 96-dpi bitmap and the 2× screen blew it up. ③ xpra IS a pixel stream per window (damage regions, png/webp/jpeg/h264), not vector or DOM rendering; what looked like VNC was that upscaled bitmap.
- **Device pixels end to end.** The client speaks DEVICE px (hello, display-configure, every fit; the increments kept) and sends the display's font dpi, never 96 × DPR (xpra rewrites Xft.dpi to a changed client dpi, measured 96 → 144). Canvases carry device pixels in a CSS box of device ÷ DPR (1:1); the pointer maps CSS → device through the stage's fit; a DPR change relayouts; the UI-scale counter-zoom holds (measured at 1.25 on a 2× page). Fractional screens (125 / 150 / 175 %) are 1:1 too: the device pane rounds DOWN (rounding to the nearest gave a 733.33 CSS box in a 733 pane, a 0.9995 zoom and a false "Scaled to fit" badge, 4.18 % of the pixels off), an overflow under one CSS px is not an overflow, each canvas backing is rounded up to the ratio's grid step (`gridStep`/`backingSize`: 2 ⇒ 2, 1.5 ⇒ 3, 1.25 ⇒ 5, 1.75 ⇒ 7) inside a whole-CSS-px box (Chrome snaps a canvas's paint box to whole CSS px, which had left even an odd-width xterm at DPR 2 18.6 % off), and the stage origin sits on the device-pixel grid (re-snapped on fit, pointer enter and the window's new `onMoved`). Measured: at DPR 2 the canvas equals the screen pixel for pixel (1 of 1.19 M off, vs 45.7 % before); at DPR 1.5, 9 / 12 / 229 of ~1.7 M stable pixels off.
- **The app's scale, fixed at launch: `desktop.appScale` (auto | 1 | 1.5 | 2, zh/ja).** `POST /api/desktop/apps` takes `dpr` (1..3, refused by name outside; the launcher sends `devicePixelRatio`). Auto = 2× when the launching screen's DPR is 1.5 or more, else 1×. The record carries `scale` + `dpi`, the status strip shows a `2×` chip, and a change takes effect at the next launch. The knobs, each measured on this box (xpra 6.5.3, gnome-calculator 50 / GTK 4.22, a GTK 3.24 probe, xterm), only the working ones kept: GDK_SCALE = the integer part (GTK3 and GTK4 exactly 2×: 360x616 → 720x1232, 195x53 → 390x106); `xpra start --dpi` = 96 × scale / GDK_SCALE (96 at 1× and 2×, 144 at 1.5×), because Xft.dpi MULTIPLIES with GDK_SCALE (192 + GDK_SCALE=2 = 4× text); GDK_DPI_SCALE not set (GTK4 ignores it, GTK3 would double-count); QT_ENABLE_HIGHDPI_SCALING=1 + QT_SCALE_FACTOR=<integer part> (unmeasured — no Qt app on this box); xterm's bitmap font ignores every dpi, so at a scale > 1 the keeper `xrdb -merge`s an Xft face into the app's own display. X11 GTK has no fractional scale, so 1.5× enlarges only the text (the calculator's minimum is 360×616 at 1× AND 1.5× — 0.67× keys on a 150 % screen): auto never picks it, and the option is labelled "text only in GTK apps" with the setting's description rewritten (zh/ja).
- **The Xft.dpi race, waited out.** xpra REPLACES the display's resource database about a second after the display is up (Xft.dpi appears at ~1.25 s, and the keeper's merged XTerm* lines vanish in the same sample). An app started before it got Xvfb's 100 dpi (a 1.5× xterm at 7×14) and lost its Xft face. The keeper now waits for `Xft.dpi` (`waitForXftDpi`, bounded, a miss is a warning) before it merges and starts the app. Measured: xterm cells 6×13 / 10×19 / 13×26 at 1× / 1.5× / 2×, ready time unchanged (1.52 s).
- **The app's minimum clamps the VibeSpace window, capped by the workspace.** `minPaneCss(the main window's size-constraints, DPR)` + the window's own chrome → `WindowManager.setMinSize`, the terminal's rule (the `.window` CSS min) per window, in the new PURE `src/lib/window-min-size.js`. Snap zones, grid cells, presets, maximize and layout restore keep the window at its minimum (overlapping a smaller cell honestly); the resize drag stops there with the opposite edge fixed (the old `Math.max(320, newW)` let a west drag slide the window); an open window below it is raised; the fit never asks below the minimum. A window's own minimum is capped at the workspace (never below 320×180): a 1× client taking over a 2× app used to get a 742×1299 window on an 815 px workspace with the keypad off-screen and no way to shrink it. Now the window slides onto the workspace, gets its full minimum back when the workspace grows, and the picture scales to fit with the badge (measured: 900×815, scale 0.607, the digits land). The minimum is re-measured when the window's chrome, its visibility or the UI scale changes (a ResizeObserver + the new `vs:ui-scale` event from `applyUiPrefs`; the bounded 20 s retry is gone). Measured on GNOME Calculator at 2× (`minimum-size [740,1232]`): a drag 700 px past the minimum stops at 372×683 layout px with the app whole, and two clicks on '7' copy "77"; the control's same drag leaves a 318×113 pane and a cropped calculator.
- **A phone shows the whole app, scaled and clickable.** On the ≤768 px layout the picture is scaled to fit and centred with "Scaled to fit — the app needs at least {w}×{h}" (zh/ja). The X display is at least the app's minimum: max(the pane, the main window's fit), one rule (`displayFor`), one sender (`syncDisplay`), grown before the configure/map. Before, the display was the pane (640×982) under a calculator fitted to 740×1232; X clamps the pointer at its screen's edge, so the lower rows and the right column were unclickable (`7894564564`). Now all ten digits and the bottom-right corner are reachable. An active pane scales only in the minimum case (the main window only, the badge's own condition), so an oversized dialog no longer zooms the picture.
- **Honest limits.** The picture is a pixel stream, not vector rendering: no frontend vector rendering exists for X apps, so crispness comes from rendering at the screen's resolution and showing it 1:1, and text can still pass a lossy encoding. The scale is fixed at launch; another client with a different DPR maps its own device pixels (crisp, the app sized by the launch scale). On a small 150 % screen a tall 2× app is scaled to fit (pick 1× there). The Qt knobs are unmeasured, and the vnc-display rung stays CSS px. GTK Broadway (GTK3's own HTML5 backend) is noted in §7.6 as a possible GTK-only future rung, not built.
- **Gates (merged with master 2.369.157, run one at a time on the final tree, 2026-09-23):** `npm run build` green (i18n-check 4387/4387, bundle-globals 6, test-architecture 191, ws-contract 5, session-schema 5) · test-xpra-client 196 (§6/§6b: the device-pixel hello and geometry maths, `minPaneCss` incl. rounding up and a 9-ratio × 4-minimum sweep, the `size-constraints` announcement, the view's device canvases / pointer / scaled-to-fit badge, the fractional-ratio sweeps, the 1.5 identity fit, the display grown before the map, the oversized dialog; controls = the old metadata list and patched copies with the ratio pinned to 1 or the r1 spelling) · test-window-minsize 35 (NEW, fast: the PURE rule + the real WindowManager drag / `setMinSize` over a fake DOM, the workspace cap, the re-measure pins; the pre-fix drag and the uncapped r1 spelling as patched-copy controls) · test-desktop-apps 305 (§10: the scale table incl. auto with the nearest-0.5 rule as the control, the knobs, the launch `dpr`, the wait < merge < start order pin) · test-desktop-display 172 (xpra's `--dpi`, a real xpra at dpi 144, the xrdb merge + its no-xrdb control) · test-vnc-view 70 · test-window-types 62 · test-desktop-viewers 93 · test-ax-paint 20 · test-harness-settings 201 · test-fixture-isolation 86 · test-desktop-stream-keepalive 23 · test-server-globals 2 · HEAVY: the gate's impact scope for e560ece7..HEAD is the whole tier (the version bump touches package-lock.json, a global input) — HEAVY GATE GREEN, 126 of 126 suites in 1020 s, among them test-desktop-xpra-window 115 ✓ / 0 skipped (§6 a deviceScaleFactor-2 page: X = pane × 2, the canvas backing 2× its CSS box, the pointer at 2×, the canvas equal to the screen pixel for pixel, GNOME Calculator's drag stopping at its minimum and two clicks copying "77", UI scale 1.25 on the 2× page, phones 390×844 unscaled / 320×568 scaled with the badge, the pre-fix control cropping the calculator; §7 DPR 1.5 pixel for pixel, the phone's ten digits + corner, a DPR-1 takeover, the 1.5× xterm cell, the control = this tree with the nine r2 levers pulled back), test-window-binding 63, test-desktop-app-window ✓, test-desktop-app-keeper 280 (1 skipped), test-desktop-xpra ✓, test-desktop-vnc-fit 32, test-restore-liveness 66.
- **Docs:** docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7.6 (+ docs/design-desktop-apps.md) records the findings, the measurements and the limits; kb-file-structure (window-min-size.js, window.js, xpra-proto / xpra-client / xpra-view, desktop-app-window, desktop-app-launcher, desktop-apps, desktop-display, the keeper, settings-schema, the suites), kb-features (HiDPI + the app's minimum), kb-api (`dpr` on the launch, `scale` + `dpi` on the record); the CLAUDE.md index line for window-min-size.js; the ci.mjs fast-tier row for test-window-minsize.

## 2.369.157 — reset credits on Codex: auto never by default, a Use… button and dialog where the interface exists, an advanced auto timed by the vendor's mechanics (OpenAI at the wall, Anthropic's ReLU knee), the escape ladder forked by warmth; and the codex pool session finally speaks as ONE member (held at spawn until a cold restart) for its credits, readings, walls, continues, ledger rows and badge — four adversarial rounds

docs/design-reset-credits.zh.md, P1 codex (§7 SHIPPED, progress §9–§15). Squash of feat-reset-credits-p1 (chunks p1–p3, verifier rounds r2, r3, the r3 re-check and r4).

- **Why: the owner's rulings (2026-09-22, design §8).** "reset 自动消费永远默认不进行" (auto-consumption is NEVER the default), so `off` stays the default and `auto` is an advanced opt-in. "有合适接口后界面里给按钮" (a button wherever an interface exists): codex has one (`account/rateLimitResetCredit/consume`); Claude Code offers only the interactive `/limit-reset`, so its button is disabled WITH that reason. The value model: OpenAI's re-opened window is a smooth DECREASING benefit (R−t)/P + (1−q), so use it at the wall at once, the only floor being the LAST credit at low value; Anthropic's in-place refill is a ReLU, full value while b·(R−t) ≥ one week's quota, so below the knee only when the grant would lapse or is re-granted. ② the `MIN_WAIT` threshold is "作废" (retired; the value model replaces it). ③ "无自有软链的“跟随者”是 legacy, 不做兼容" (a follower of the pool default with no link of its own gets no compatibility).
- **The verdict (`src/reset-credit.js`, PURE, imports nothing, CJS).** `resetCreditVerdict(facts) → {use, reason, valueFraction, windowFraction, waitSavedSec}`. It answers only at a wall the vendor stated (never proactively). OpenAI (a consumed credit re-opens the window): use it at the wall at once; the ONE refusal is the last credit with under a tenth of a window left (`CREDIT_FLOOR = 0.1`, compared against the window term (R−t)/P; at a wall q≈0, so the owner's (1−q) term is ≈1 for every wall, recorded in design §9). Anthropic (a refill in place): the ReLU, use while b·(R−t) ≥ W (the knee inclusive, decided on the unrounded ratio), or when the grant lapses within a day or is re-granted weekly. Every refusal names its reason from a closed set. `describeUse` gives the dialog / For-you / notice sentences as i18n lines; `offerOf` is the one sanitizer of a card's `{available, mode, accountKey}` offer; `dialogModel` / `refusalLine` word the manual use.
- **The ladder forks by warmth (owner B1).** The engine's `tryResetCredit` closure became `resetCreditRung`, run BEFORE the switch rung at both codex exhaustion sites. A warm conversation (in a turn, or its cache not yet cold) goes credit → switch → wait; a cold one goes switch → credit (only when no member can take it; a pay-per-use usage-credits member is not an alternative) → wait, and a cold wall whose switch moved nothing asks the verdict's `after-switch` rung. The pool alternative asks the switch rung's own decision with the current member treated as walled. The vendor comes from the harness quota source (`resetCreditVendor`); the mode is read through `harnessSetting(session.backend, …)`, gated on `capsOf(backend).resetCredit`, never on an id.
- **Three modes (`codex.limitResetCredit`).** `off` (default): a chat card at the wall names the credits once per limit event. `ask` (new): the same card plus ONE For-you decision per limit event (words as i18n structure, a `reset-credit` action payload for its button; the item expires at the wall's reset, is dismissed once no running conversation holds that login, and is re-seeded from the inbox after a server restart), then the switch/wait rungs as usual. `auto`: consumed through the unattended-spend ceiling (fail closed), the notice naming the account, the wait saved and the credits left. The claude table gets NO row: the table cannot express a disabled row, and the greyed button carries the reason.
- **The manual use (design §5).** ONE confirm dialog (`src/lib/reset-credit-dialog.js`, `openResetCreditDialog`) opened from three places: the **Manage Agents roster** (a ChatGPT row, and the machine's codex login, shows `· N reset credits` beside its name plus a compact **Use…** button, repainted from the usage poll; a Claude row's button is DISABLED with "Claude Code offers only the interactive /limit-reset — run it in a terminal session", shown only once a passive grant sample exists, and none is captured yet); the **chat wall card / auto-resume arm card** ("Use a reset credit"); and the **`ask` item** (Confirm ⇒ done, "Not now" ⇒ dismissed). The dialog says the account, what the credit does (a new window until t + one period, or the reset it replaces), the wait it saves (only at a wall; otherwise the share of the window it discards) and the credits left after. A refusal is shown BY NAME with Confirm disabled; a failed POST is a toast. The roster's count survives passive pushes and a live wrapper that never learned it (`toLegacyView` projects `extra.resetCredits`; the cache writer carries the dated count across a write that does not state it).
- **The route (`src/routes/reset-credit.js`).** `GET /api/accounts/:id/reset-credit` is the preview; `POST` writes ONE `codex-reset-credit` verb on a live chat session that HOLDS that login, through the SAME engine writer the auto rung uses (`writeResetCredit`: the spend ceiling under the held identity, reason `codex-reset-credit`, plus the 10-min floor) → `{ok, sessionId}` or `{error, code}`: `not_supported` (capability, never an id) · `no_live_session` · `no_credits` · `cooldown` · `spend_refused` · `agent_forbidden` (human-triggered only) · `restart_pending` (409: the only carrier's cold restart is in flight; the dialog names the member). A pool move with no restart request yet is allowed, and the dialog says the conversation keeps this login until a client restarts it. A person's FAILED attempt files one notice naming the vendor's answer and is never walked down the switch/wait ladder. The ws `codex-reset-credit` case (a second writer with no ceiling and no floor) is gone; test-reset-credit-ui §4 censuses writers, case labels and readers over every server-tier file.
- **No soft hold at the pool default (§8 ③, reversing 2.369.153 at that site).** A default follower has no link of its own and is legacy: the default site computes no `inTurn` and has no `warm-soft-defer` branch, so a SOFT-exhausted default moves at once and the in-turn warm follower moves with it. 2.369.149's PROACTIVE warm-cache hold at the 'edf' tier stays (key `poolId:default`); the per-session first-stop rule is untouched. test-fable-cap-pool-storm §18 (d) is inverted with the pre-ruling engine as the patched-copy control; (e) keeps the hard band's at-once move.
- **ONE credit per account wall.** The one-try floor is the IDENTITY's (`_resetCreditTries`, read by the rung and the manual preview). A sibling walled on the same account FOLLOWS the credit in flight and the leader's answer settles every follower (reset ⇒ recovered; failure ⇒ each walks its own switch/wait; no answer in 10 min counts as a failure). `alreadyRedeemed`, or a failure after a NEWER reading that shows the account open, is SUPERSEDED (re-read, never demoted or armed).
- **The attribution model, and why codex needs it.** Codex cannot hot-switch (`capsOf('codex').hotSwitch = impossible`: CODEX_HOME is canonicalized at startup and the token lives in memory, measured 2026-08-24). A pool move re-points the link, but a running codex process keeps spending the member it started on until it is restarted. Every consumer used to read the link, so after a switch the credit, the reading, the wall, the continue, the permanent-ledger row and the billing badge all named the pool's NEW member while the process spent the OLD one. A credit spent that way dodged A's own per-identity ceiling and its last-credit floor. The model: `ws-create` stamps `_heldPoolMember` for a local pool whose backend cannot hot-switch (caps row); it is persisted in the session-meta and restored on both restore paths. ONE rule, `accounts.poolMemberOfSession`, is read by the engine (`sessionBillingMember`, `codexQuotaKeyFor`, `quotaVerdictFor`), the ledger's `recordUsageAttribution` and `sessionAuth` (the badge). It resolves stamp → slot-transition ledger → `held-unknown`. The ledger step handles a process spawned before the stamp: it reads the pool's rows on both sides of the process's start (the last `to` before it, else the first move's `from`); a disagreement, or a restored session with no recorded start, is unknown. The answer is persisted with its origin (`heldPoolOrigin: 'ledger'`; the `no-start` marker is persisted at the first restore so a rename between two restarts cannot turn it into a confident answer). An unreadable ledger read is not memoized. The ledger keeps a row whose `from` contradicts the previous `to`. `held-unknown` spends nothing. A held session is judged DIRECTLY: its own cache and login, an empty held verdict fails closed, and the pre-fire gate continues it only on a positive answer. Its own wall demotes its member through `validateHeldSlot`. A held member the pool no longer lists (narrowed out, or its login file wiped; codex has no login reader) is never continued at its reset. That is the money-safe side, and the owner can revert it by deleting that one check. A held process reaches the pool's new member only by a **cold restart**: ONE sender, `sendColdRestart` (default switch, per-session switch, auth eviction, `requestHeldRestart`), which never re-names a conversation within 10 min or while its request may be in flight; the manual routes claim through `claimColdRestarts`.
- **The reset answer and its hold.** The wrapper emits the post-reset re-read BEFORE the `reset` answer, and reports a failed or empty re-read (`rate_limits_updated {error, onDemand, afterReset}`) instead of swallowing it. The engine holds pool decisions about that account: it probes the account at once and at 30 s. The hold ends only on a post-reset reading (the leader's own, or one that reads usable; a sibling's stale spent push is ignored) or a new wall with a DIFFERENT stated reset. Its 10-min ceiling lifts it without forcing a decision. A wall record RESTATING the re-opened event (same stated reset inside the 10-min floor; a conversation whose turn was in flight at the vendor when the credit landed) is decided before anything is written. It is journaled as `restated wall of the re-opened event` and writes nothing: it keeps the hold and walks no ladder. The rung's own same-event check reads the same strict predicate.
- **What four adversarial rounds found and closed.** Each finding was reproduced with the verifier's recipe on the real engine before its fix, and each is gated beside its pre-fix control in test-codex-pool §R8–§R20.
  - **Round r2 (five findings, §R8–§R13).** ① One account wall seen by two warm conversations spent TWO credits, and the second's `alreadyRedeemed` then demoted the account the first had just re-opened. Closed by the per-identity floor and followers. ② After a switch, the codex wrapper still on A spent A's credit, charged to and named as B. Closed by the `_heldPoolMember` stamp; the auto rung refuses a `moved` process by name. ③ The button went dead seconds after it appeared (`no_live_session`). Closed: the carrier is the session holding the login. ④ The roster chip vanished after any passive push. Closed: the count is carried and dated. ⑤ The ws `codex-reset-credit` case was a second writer. Removed and censused. Lows: a cold wall that moved nothing, and the anthropic knee firing up to 0.05 % early.
  - **Round r3 (three majors, one medium, three lows, §R14–§R20).** ① A process still holding walled A after its pool moved to B got a 45 s "switched to a usable account (B)" arm, and the real auto-resume delivered a billed continue into it, then again every quarantine window. Closed: the fire verdict is the held member's, and the cold restart is re-asked (`requestHeldRestart`). ② A `reset` answer arrived before the post-reset re-read, and a pool evaluation in that gap moved every conversation off the account just re-opened. Closed: re-read first, plus the hold. ③ The permanent ledger and the billing badge billed a held process's requests to the new member. Closed by `accounts.poolMemberOfSession`; the switch no longer re-attributes held followers. ④ A process spawned before the stamp kept the old misattribution. Closed by the slot-transition ledger step and `held-unknown`. Lows: the wall card names whose spend ceiling refused, and the count survives a wrapper that never learned it. test-restore-liveness §4 ④ proves a held stamp survives the end-to-end restore over the self-upgrading daemon, with the stamp-less meta as the control.
  - **The r3 re-check (one major, two mediums, four lows, §R14c/§R14d/§R15 r4/§R17b/§R19b/§R19c).** ① A held member the pool no longer lists made the held-only verdict answer "no members" (`usable:null`), and the pre-fire gate delivered a billed continue into the process still holding walled A. Closed: direct judgment, fail closed, continue only on a positive answer. ② A `reset` with no post-reset reading lifted the hold at 30 s and forced a decision on the wall's stale spent mark. Closed: probes, and a ceiling that lifts without deciding. ③ A process from a pool older than the ledger flipped from "holds A" to unknown at the pool's first recorded move. Closed: rows on both sides of the start, a persisted answer, no memoized unknown. Lows: ONE cold-restart sender, the dialog naming a carrier being restarted, and ask items swept after a server restart.
  - **Round r4 (one medium, four lows, §R15 r5/§R14c r5/§R17b r5/§R19c r5).** ① A wall restating the SAME limit event after a `reset` answer re-marked the re-opened account spent, ended the hold, and the next evaluation moved the pool off it and cold-restarted every conversation on it. Closed: freshness is decided before anything is written. ② A held member narrowed out of the pool read healthy at its reset and got one automatic continue. Closed: never continued. ③ The manual Use… through a carrier whose restart is in flight was warned, not refused. Closed: `restart_pending` (409). ④ The `no-start` origin was erased by the rename / thread-meta writers. Closed: the marker is persisted at the first restore.
- **Residuals, by name.** (a) A `held-unknown` process's readings and walls still land on the pool's current member until it restarts; nothing spends through it, but its numbers are attributed to the link. (b) The 10-min hold ceiling: if no post-reset reading arrives by then, the hold lifts and the next evaluation decides from the cache as it stands (verifier §2c). (c) The client cold-restart path (`_poolColdRestart`) and the dialog's new carrier sentences were not exercised in a browser. (d) test-chat-e2e (a real vendor turn) was not run; the heavy tier ran test-restore-liveness only.
