## 2.369.156 — desktop apps get the xpra seamless rung end to end: the app IS the picture (per-window xpra, the fit belt on both rungs, clipboard both ways), the ws bridge's per-packet fences for a watching viewer (lifecycle, keymap, display size, geometry; 16 MiB caps), the Xvfb reap by evidence, and ONE ACTIVE viewer per app window (others blocked behind Resume here; agent-held ⇒ everyone watches, scaled to fit) — docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md §7 P8-2 (x1–x5, the verifier's rounds r5–r8, §7.1–§7.5). Squash of feat-desktop-xpra-whole.

**The xpra rung, server half (x1; DA1 / DA5).** `src/desktop-display.js` gained the real `xpra-seamless` recipe: ONE `xpra start` per app session (`--daemon=no --displayfd=3 --use-display=no --html=on --bind-tcp=127.0.0.1:<port> --bind=none --resize-display=yes --clipboard-direction=both`, its own Xvfb capped at 4096x2304, every other feature off by name, session / socket / pid files under the app's own dir); xpra is the window manager and the app stays the keeper's own detached child. Four measured xpra 6.5.3 traps are pinned: a missing XAUTHORITY file makes xpra write the real `~/.Xauthority` (the recipe creates the file first), `--mmap=no` refuses every client, `--commands=no` kills `--start*`, and setproctitle blanks xpra's environ (so the boot belt also reaps by pid+starttime). The xpra row is WIRED: when xpra is installed every NEW session takes it, and an existing vnc-display record is adopted as born, never migrated. `desktop.backendPrefs` (new setting) reorders the ladder for the instance. The keeper asks the recipe's own READY probe (HTTP for xpra) and answers `windows(id)`. The ws bridge relays xpra ws↔ws with the same backpressure / keepalive / named close (the old 501 is gone). The routes host the upstream html5 client behind our auth at `/api/desktop/:id/xpra-ui/*` (nosniff, no listing). The xpra listener is 127.0.0.1-only: a raw TCP connect to the box's other address is refused, so the picture reaches a browser only through the cookie-authed relay. Measured: first window 0.7–0.9 s, keystroke echo 34 ms on loopback / 265 ms at rtt 200 ms + 1 Mbps.

**The xpra window, drawn by us (x2; D21 (c) (b), §4.4).** The npm `xpra-html5-client` was vetted and REFUSED (license contradiction MPL-2.0 vs Apache-2.0, frozen since 2022 at the xpra 4.x protocol, 2.37 MB ESM with its own window model). The transport is the upstream html5 v21 `Protocol.js` worker, served unmodified from the installed package behind our auth (docs/third-party-notices.md). Everything above the packets is ours: PURE `src/lib/xpra-proto.js` (the hello and every packet form read from Client.js on this box, the wheel as button clicks, the pane fit under size hints, the clipboard rule), the DOM-free `src/lib/xpra-client.js` (the first top-level mapped at 0,0 at the pane's fitted size and re-fitted on every pane resize, dialogs nudged inside, draws painted in order and every one acked), `src/lib/xpra-view.js` (a theme-colour pane — no root, no black — one canvas per window at net zoom 1, an IME textarea, the app's own title + icon to the title bar), all on `src/lib/picture-shell.js` (the bar / status / Paste / Reconnect / bounded ladder extracted from vnc-view.js — both views on ONE shell). THE KEYMAP IS NATIVE: xpra 6.5.3 only translates a keycodes-only client onto its `us` keymap, so `é` / `中` could not be typed; the client sends `x11_keycodes` + `query_struct` and publishes a keycode row per character outside the keymap before pressing it — `é中文` reached xterm. Measured: 898×550 of an 898×553 pane with ZERO black pixels outside the app window, the title equal to X's.

**The clipboard both ways, on EVERY rung (x2 follow-through; owner acceptance 2).** The clipboard chrome lives in the shared shell: master 2.369.136's paste box (moved with its exact words — a dead view refuses, a refused / empty / API-less clipboard opens a textarea whose native paste works on plain http) and the COPY CHIP (a copy inside the remote app goes to the browser clipboard on a secure page, and on plain http becomes "Copied in the app — click to copy", copying through the click). The RFB view's silent `writeText(...).catch(() => {})` is gone. Measured on the plain-http hostname page: real pastes reach the app through Ctrl+V and through the paste box; under UI scale 125 the canvas sits at net zoom 1 and pointers land on exactly the X coordinates.

**The fit belt on both rungs (x4, r5; owner: "就算是vnc也不能这样啊，完全无法做自动贴合，尺寸匹配吗？").** The vnc-display rung FITS too: Xvnc spells `-AcceptSetDesktopSize` (measured on Xtigervnc 1.15: a client's SetDesktopSize answered in 43 ms; `=0` is the one lever that refuses), and the keeper's APP-FIT step (PURE `appFitPlan` + one chained xdotool) moves the app's top-level to 0,0 at the framebuffer size after ready, after every SetDesktopSize the bridge reports, and on a belt; Xvfb+x11vnc keeps its fixed geometry, is still fitted, the browser scales, and the chip names the limit. Under a window manager (measured with the fleet image's own xfwm4 4.18) the fit resolves the CLIENT inside the frame (the old rule picked xfwm4's 5x5 helper) and maximises it through wmctrl. The belt stops forking on settled sessions (0 forks over 8 settled unwatched ticks; it was 3 per session per tick). On the xpra rung the client checks every server geometry packet against the fit and corrects an app that resizes or moves itself (GNOME Calculator's mode switch: 100 % of the pane, the pre-fix client 78 % then 41 %), bounded to three fights. The title bar names the app window's own title on both rungs; xwininfo lines are parsed from the right (a title with quotes or a COMPOUND_TEXT name used to drop the window from the fit).

**The ws bridge's per-packet fences for a watching viewer (r5–r8; three adversarial verify rounds).** The window-live input policy on the xpra kind is applied PER PACKET, so a Watch viewer still gets a picture (the old all-or-nothing rule dropped its hello). A refused viewer's packets pass only from an ALLOWLIST (`XPRA_WATCH_TYPES`: hello, pings, damage acks, map-window, buffer-refresh); input and every control packet are cut; `shutdown-server` / `exit-server` are cut from EVERY viewer (a crafted one used to end the session), and the xpra socket refuses the acting hello requests (`stop=no,exit=no,…`) with `XPRA_CLIENT_CAN_SHUTDOWN=0`. The KEYMAP (a Watch viewer's `keyboard-config` reprogrammed X's shared keymap), the DISPLAY SIZE (a Watch viewer's `display-configure 1x1` collapsed the holder's display) and the window GEOMETRY (`configure-window`) are fenced the same way — each cut and its last packet HELD, replayed at that viewer's takeover so the pane that takes over still gets its own fit; the rfb twin cuts a refused viewer's SetDesktopSize. CAPS: an xpra packet header may declare at most 16 MiB (xpra's own client limit), an incomplete packet may hold one largest packet, ClientCutText the same 16 MiB, one ws message one packet — past any of them THAT viewer is closed 1009 `packet-too-large` (measured: a 2 GiB-declared stream closed in its first chunk, +0 MiB arrayBuffers; the uncapped bridge held +97 MiB).

**The Xvfb reap by evidence (r5, x5).** xpra hands its Xvfb a sanitised env without the session marker but WITH the app's own XAUTHORITY path; the keeper's teardown, its leftover census and the boot belt ask both, so a crashed xpra's `Xvfb-for-Xpra-S<pid>` (100–190 MB) is reaped with the keeper up and after a keeper SIGKILL. The suites' exit sweeps reap by the same evidence (marker / XAUTHORITY path / a dead owner plus a gone scratch dir), never by a name.

**ONE ACTIVE viewer per app window (x5; the owner's ruling: "直接block掉非active客户端的app界面，因为多客户端同时操作鼠标感觉也会有问题" + "仿照terminal…可以手动take over").** The terminal's size-override made the default: among the HUMAN viewers of an app window exactly one is ACTIVE (the first to attach; its pane drives the app's geometry, only its input / clipboard reach the app). Every other client is BLOCKED: an overlay with the app's own title (as text), "Active on another client" and "Resume here", and NO picture — the bridge opens no upstream for it (0 packets either way). Resume here takes over at once (the pane flips before the answer; the previous active is cut, close 4001, and reconnects as a blocked viewer; measured on xpra: the app re-fits to the new pane in 648 ms). While an agent DRIVES the window every human is Watch — the picture scaled to fit, nothing sent that could change the app's geometry. PURE `src/desktop-viewers.js`, the keeper's election + the `desktop-app-viewers` broadcast (panes by their public key, never a socket's id), `GET/POST /api/desktop/apps/:id/viewers[/takeover]`, both rungs.

**The x5 close-out — the round-3 verify's four LOWs, and its two INFO items as the product's DEFAULTS (the owner can object).** Default (a), a **5 s grace**: when the active client's socket closes while others watch, its seat is HELD for its pane (the others stay blocked; the broadcast still names that pane); the same window reconnecting, or the reloaded page's new window in the same tab (`?prev=`, a hint only), takes it back; only then does the most recently active remaining client take over — a page reload or a network blip no longer hands the app to another device. Default (b), **Watch never upscales**: the xpra Watch stage scale is capped at 1 and centred (a pane larger than the app shows it crisp at 1:1; the vnc rung keeps noVNC's scaleViewport). LOW-1: every join logged a false "reconcile failed" warn — the refresh skips a socket not wired yet. LOW-2: on the xpra rung a blocked pane's overlay named the launch label — the keeper now reads the app's own title from X into the record while a blocked seat exists (a hostile title shows verbatim, as text). LOW-3: an anonymous stream socket (the hosted xpra-ui page) could take the active seat — only named panes are elected; an anonymous socket only watches. LOW-4: a silently dropped active socket blocked its own pane's reconnect for up to 29.8 s — the pane's newer socket takes the seat at once (11 ms through the bridge) and the old one is cut.

**Gates (run on the merged tree, 2026-09-22):** `npm run build` green (i18n 4342/4342, bundle-globals 6, test-architecture 191 incl. the §43 tier census, ws-contract 5, session-schema 5). FAST: test-desktop-viewers 93 (new: the PURE rule, the keeper's election, the bridge over fake xpra/rfb upstreams with the pre-x5 bridge as a patched-copy control, the grace / LOW-1..4 legs each with its control), test-desktop-apps 286, test-desktop-display 164, test-desktop-stream-keepalive 23, test-xpra-client 154 (new), test-vnc-view 70, test-window-targets 130, test-window-types 62, test-contributions 182, test-server-globals 2, test-architecture 191, test-ax-paint 20, test-status-bar-chips 39, test-hidden-view-suspend 42, test-model-echo 25, test-backlog-no-truncation 28. HEAVY: test-desktop-app-keeper 280 + 1 SKIP (no window manager on this box; the xfwm4 leg runs with `VIBESPACE_TEST_WM_DIR`), test-desktop-xpra 58 (new: a real server with password auth + the real xpra 6.5.3 from node — the binding check, relay auth, resize + clipboard at the protocol level, idle / keep-alive, adoption across a SIGKILL + reboot), test-desktop-xpra-window 79 (new, chrome: the seamless window pixel by pixel, the plain-http clipboard, net zoom 1 under the UI scale, the belt against the app's own resizes, x5 with two pages and a pre-x5 server copy as the control), test-desktop-vnc-fit 32 (new), test-desktop-app-window 97, test-window-target 103, test-window-binding 63, test-ax-budget 22, test-chat-paging green. Open, recorded in design §9: the fleet image's xpra 3.1.3 protocol forms, images on the clipboard, the window icon on the vnc rung, the WM path's maximise measured only against the image's xfwm4 from a scratch X. Docs: both design docs (§7 P8-2 row, §7.1–§7.5, §9), kb-file-structure / kb-api / kb-features / kb-bugfix-invariants / kb-design-lessons §18, docs/settings.md (`desktop.idleTimeoutMin`, `desktop.backendPrefs`), docs/third-party-notices.md (the upstream Protocol.js worker), CLAUDE.md index lines, ci.mjs rows, the Dockerfile's `xdotool wmctrl`.


**Also in 2.369.156 (r3) — a mirror-only red in test-desktop-display.** The 'display that does not answer' leg expected `xdpyinfo failed`, which presumes xdpyinfo is installed; the Actions runner has none, so the probe refused by name (`xdpyinfo not on PATH`) and the leg went red there while green here. The leg now judges on the evidence (which of the two named failures the box can produce) and prints which branch ran. The mirror's heavy job was green; only the fast job carried this. The same suite's `[::1]`-only listener leg also went red once INSIDE the push hook's fast gate (green standalone): under the gate's concurrency the kernel handed a v6 ephemeral port that another suite held on 127.0.0.1 — the leg now proves the precondition independently (a 127.0.0.1 bind on the same number must succeed) before asserting.
## 2.369.155 — Claude Code's own auto-continue at a usage limit is spawned OFF on every VibeSpace claude session — which changes nothing in chat and leaves terminal sessions stopped at a wall — and the two standing Actions-mirror reds were races in the suites

- **Why:** the owner's ruling (2026-09-22). Claude Code 2.1.280 has its own "wait for the usage limit to reset, then continue" — settings key `autoContinueAtUsageLimit`, ON by default when absent (behind the GrowthBook flag `tengu_marble_heron`, itself default-on when absent). When it fires it enqueues `"Your claude.ai usage limit has reset. Continue the task you were working on…"` — a billed turn nobody typed that bypasses VibeSpace's auto-resume gates (the arm/fire ladder, the loop breaker, the unattended-spend ceiling, the pool switch).
- **What it really changes, per mode (read from the binary by byte offset):** the CLI's continue only arms in an INTERACTIVE launch — `Zrn(argv)` is non-interactive whenever `!process.stdout.isTTY`. **Chat sessions never run it**: every chat transport (local chat-wrapper, the ssh keeper, the agentd pipe session) hands the CLI a pipe or a file for stdout, so there VibeSpace's own auto-resume was and stays the only automatic continue; the switch is belt and braces. **Terminal sessions did run it, and it was their only automatic continue** (VibeSpace's auto-resume delivers into chat sessions only). With the switch OFF a terminal session **stops at the wall**, the limit dialog offers the wait as a choice, and nothing continues it by itself. The owner's trade-off to revisit: keep it off (the CLI's continue has no spend ceiling), scope the default to chat only, or give terminal sessions a VibeSpace-side resume.
- **The mechanism, from the binary:** `autoContinueAtUsageLimit` is a real settings-schema key, read through `D7(key)` over `["policySettings","flagSettings","userSettings"]` — so the per-invocation `--settings` JSON (flagSettings) is honoured, project/local settings are not, and a managed policy value outranks it. No env var, no dedicated flag.
- **The switch:** new claude harness-settings row `claude.autoContinueAtUsageLimit` (Settings → Claude, boolean, default OFF, apply kind spawn); its description states the per-mode truth above. `src/adapters/claude-code.js` merges `autoContinueAtUsageLimit:false` into the ONE `--settings` flag on every claude spawn unless the row is ON (then nothing is passed and Claude Code's own setting governs); a missing settings bag counts as off. A user's own `--settings <file>` in extra args is never clobbered by this default, and an explicit key in the user's inline JSON is kept. Every transport carries it because it is in the spawn args. zh/ja strings added.
- **No detection.** A first cut journaled a `cli-auto-continue` spend event keyed on the CLI's `origin:{kind:"auto-continuation"}` — but 2.1.280 stamps that origin on ten kinds of enqueue (plan-mode approval, `/goal` approval, the ultraplan hand-off, dialog follow-ups, the reset credit), only one of them the usage-limit continue, so every plan approval would have been journaled as "continued by itself after a usage limit"; and the stream consumers only see chat sessions, where the CLI's continue cannot fire. It was removed before release. Seeing it in terminal sessions would need a transcript scan of their JSONL — an open gap.
- **Gates:** test-fallback-policy (§5 argv legs with the ON control, the file-clobber and inline-key legs; §5b pins the per-mode premise — chat-wrapper piped, pty-wrapper a pty, auto-resume chat-only, the row's wording — each with a snippet control), test-auto-resume, test-remote-shell (the remote line, the terminal spec, the single-builder + merge census with its control), test-harness-settings (the row, coerce, not cli-config), test-stdout-registry (a census: no source reads the generic `auto-continuation` origin, with the refuted rung as its control; plan/`/goal`/ultraplan records handed to no brain consumer, a live-recorder control), test-peer-command-card (the same three shapes through the turn-start transcript lookup: no card, nothing handed on — red on the first cut).
- **Not verified live:** no vendor turn was spent to watch the CLI's continue fire (§ban-safety); the per-mode behaviour is read from the 2.1.280 binary.

**Also in 2.369.155 — the two standing Actions-mirror reds were races in the suites on the slow runner, not in the product (suites only; product code untouched).** Both went red on the Actions `ci` heavy job (0c7f6af0 / 3a1b77ca / 89c33c29 / 694b52fb) and green on every developer box.

- **test-window-binding ③ "a real title-bar drag moved the host by (18, 20)":** ② puts the body zoom back after its own `captureState` stamped the host's gridBounds under the zoom, so the workspace ResizeObserver rescales the host one frame after the next layout (700×500 @ 70,70 → 883×642 @ 88,90). ③ probed the title bar and pressed at once; on the loaded runner the reflow landed between the probe and the press, the press hit bare `main` and nothing dragged — the (18, 20) is the reflow itself. Reproduced to the pixel locally with CDP `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate` ×8. Fix: `settledGeometry` after the zoom reset (the host rect stable over three double-rAF+task samples with no reflow pending, a named check that prints the reflow), the press's landing recorded in the page and asserted before the delta; `VS_CPU_THROTTLE=<n>` reproduces the runner. Negative control: settle removed at ×8 ⇒ "the press reached the host's title bar" red.
- **test-chat-paging NEGATIVE CONTROL ② "0 rows violate":** the pre-fix copy did re-pin in the middle of history on every mirror run, but inside a 4×700 px fling whose later notches and the count trim's landing unpinned it before the settle sample; locally the same fling happened to settle pinned. The mid-history pin is deterministic, its survival to the sample is not. Fix (rule + control): rule ② also reads the gesture's own trace ring — a `repin` with `we < total` during the gesture is the pin, whatever the sample shows (scripts/paging-gesture-rules.mjs, three judge rows in test-chat-trim-guard incl. an at-the-tail control); ② is judged on a CONSTRUCTED probe (`pinProbe`: leave the tail with three real up gestures, park the viewport 80 px above the DOM's bottom, re-park until it holds, wait out the 1.5 s input horizon, ONE notch; the precondition asserted and printed) that runs on the fix (green) and on the patched copy (red).
- **Still open on the mirror, by name (not this fix):** test-chat-paging ① on the fix legs ("up-fast-2: landed … inside the pageUp band"), test-channels-i18n zh/ja "ZERO visible Latin-only text nodes", test-codex-remote-wrapper "reconnected (fresh attach child)" once (green on retry).

## 2.369.154 — backlog priority + ownership: every push selects the right items, numbers mean the list you saw, the Backlog tab sets priority, and a session holding too many items is asked to clean up

- **Why:** the owner's ruling on the 2.369.150 cap incident — no store cap; with proper PRIORITY grading and OWNERSHIP, every push (the per-turn reminder, the listing) picks the right items. Ownership existed (`claimedBy`, the parker auto-claims); priority did not, and every reader walked the array oldest-first.
- **Priority + selection:** backlog items carry `priority: high|normal|low` (closed set; anything else, and every item stored before, reads as normal — no migration). New PURE src/backlog-select.js: `sortBacklog` = open by priority, newest first within one, then resolved by resolution time — every listing, TASK.md and the route's numbering use it; `selectReminders` = what one session is reminded of: its ≤ 5 highest-priority newest CLAIMED items, ONE `- unclaimed HIGH:` line naming the open high items no RUNNING session owns (a claimant no longer running reads `(claimant not running)`), everything else a count. TASK.md prints `!` (high) / `↓` (low) after the id; the repo task file round-trips the marker, declares `backlog_priority: markers` in its frontmatter and escapes a normal text that itself begins `! ` / `↓ ` with one backslash — a file without the key (every pre-priority file) is read verbatim. A priority change reaches the item's owners as a diff line.
- **Route + CLI, numbers mean the list you saw:** `POST /api/agent/task-backlog` accepts `priority` on `add` and `edit` (a value outside the set is a 400 naming it); GET task answers in `sortBacklog` order plus `you`. A 1-based number resolves against the list GET task last served THIS session in this group (another session's add no longer shifts it); an item resolved or deleted since is refused by name and nothing changes. `edit` / `claim` / `unclaim` / `done` / `drop` echo the item by id (`edit` used to assign an undeclared `actedIdx` and never echoed). `vibespace-task backlog-add … --priority high|normal|low`, `backlog-edit <id> --priority …`; `backlog` prints the markers and a `(you)` / `(claimed by N)` / `(unclaimed)` tail; `backlog-done` / `-drop` print `resolved [B-xxxx] <text>`; the usage and docs/agent/task-manual.md steer mutating verbs to ids. Against a server that predates priority (checkout updated, server not yet restarted) the CLI never claims a priority it did not see stored — it prints `note: the server did not record --priority <p> …`; the 2.369.151 exact-text fallback for a pre-2.369.150 answer is kept.
- **Backlog tab (src/lib/task-log.js):** rows in `sortBacklog` order (each keeps its store index, so every write still patches the right item); a non-normal item carries a High (accent) / Low (muted) chip after its id; priority is set from the row's right-click / long-press `Priority` submenu (current one ticked) or the ✎ editor's Priority select — one whole-backlog write through the existing group-update path, the store broadcast repaints every client. Copy as Markdown follows the same order with the markers. New strings in zh + ja; the chip CSS uses theme vars only.
- **The cleanup nudge:** a session "holds" every open item it claimed or parked (`addedBy` — unclaiming your own parked item does not hand the clutter to somebody else). When that reaches the new setting `tasks.backlogNudgeAt` (Settings → Integration, default 20, 0 = off; a stored value of the wrong type — a boolean, an object, a blank string — reads as the default), ONE English paragraph (≤ 500 B) names the count, how many are older than 14 days and the three oldest ids with their ages, and asks for `backlog-done` / `backlog-drop` / a merge with `backlog-edit <id> --detail`. The same words ride the route's answer to `add` / `edit` / `claim` (`nudge`, printed by the CLI as a `note:` line; never on `done` / `drop` / `unclaim` / `show`), the end of every full context injection's backlog note, and EVERY turn's `<vibespace-reminder>` (a group whose full context rides the same prompt is skipped, so a codex first prompt says it once). N groups over the threshold share ONE paragraph under ONE budget (`nudgeTextAll`).
- **Fixes found on the way (each reproduced first):** numbers resolved in STORE order while the listing printed newest first (`edit 1` rewrote the listing's #3); a normal repo-file item beginning `! ` turned into a high item; 2 groups × 25 CJK items put SessionStart at 10.8 KB, past the 10240-byte persisted-output wrap, and task-context had no inline cap at all (3 groups were 12.8 KB before the nudge) — task-context now passes the same 9600 B `capInline` prompt-context uses, the unclaimed-HIGH line spends a 600 B text budget and the claimed-item lines of a multi-group context one shared 1500 B budget (2 / 3 groups × 60 CJK items: 7.8 / 9.0 KB, untrimmed).
- **Gates:** test-backlog-priority 108 (new, fast: pure legs with an oldest-first control, store + repo-file round trip incl. marker-like text and a pre-priority file, the real route's numbering against the shown list with two sessions, the injection's budgets, the REAL CLI over loopback, wiring pins, the Backlog tab with cut-copy controls, zh + ja keys) · test-backlog-nudge 83 (new, fast: threshold normalization incl. the wrong-type leg, ownedOpen / backlogNudge / nudgeText / nudgeTextAll budgets, the real route's verbs, every turn through the REAL task-context + prompt-context, 1 / 2 / 3 / 5 groups × 60 CJK items ≤ 9600 B, the CLI's `note:` line, the setting row — each leg with a patched-copy control) · test-backlog-no-truncation 24 → 28 (the older-server `--priority` note on add and edit, with a no-check control). The pre-existing red of the EXCLUDED test-integration-toggle ("task-context delivers content while ON" answers an empty context) is identical on 2.369.152 — not caused here.


**Also in 2.369.154 — the collab live-counter gate pins the read-only stream line by what it guarantees, not by the spinner's spelling.** The heavy gate went red on every run since 2.369.150 on one leg of test-collab-live-counter: "the read-only stream line carries the same label element". The product was fine — the leg was a source regex that required the spinner's literal `<span class="chat-spinner"></span>`, and 2.369.150's accessibility pass rightly marked every spinner `aria-hidden="true"` (test-ax-paint ③ requires it). The label element and its one-text-write-per-tick path were untouched. The leg now pins what it is about: the spinner+label template of the read-only line and of the ChatInput line are extracted and must be EQUAL (a change to one twin alone is red; the spinner's own attributes stay test-ax-paint's), and a new behavioural leg (⑤b) drives the real `_showTyping` on the real read-only view — same label and spinner nodes across ticks, one mutation per changed label, none for an unchanged one; red on a patched copy that rebuilds the line. Gates: test-collab-live-counter 79 (×2) · test-ax-paint 20 · test-status-bar-chips 39 · test-fold-ux 70 · test-turn-truth-ui 80 · test-architecture 190.
## 2.369.153 — a soft-exhausted pool member lets a warm conversation finish its turn before moving it

- **The first-stop rule (owner: "软耗尽的话 热对话切走时机晚一点，普通10%，热对话的话就5%这样。如果一个对话到达了冷对话切走的标准但还热着，就在停下来的第一时间切走。"):** on a HOT pool, a member in the SOFT band (a bucket under its hot bar — 5h 10 %, weekly 5 % — but none under its hard bar — 5h 5 %, weekly 3 %) still moves a cold or idle conversation at once, but a conversation that is warm AND in a turn is no longer cut over mid-turn: `decidePoolSwitch` answers `none('warm-soft-defer')` naming the tripped bucket, its bars and where the move goes, and the move is made at the conversation's FIRST STOP, in the same call — at the turn-end boundary, or, under the CLI's authoritative turn state (whose `result` still reads 'running'), on its `session_state_changed idle` record. The cache being still warm at that instant is accepted. A bucket under the hard bar or a dead login moves every conversation at once, warm or not (every exhausted verdict names its `band`); the proactive EDF tier is unchanged.
- **In a turn** = `_isStreaming === true` or the harness's turn state is `running` / `requires_action` (a turn paused on the user is not over); a session with neither fact (terminal mode) is not in a turn and moves at once.
- **Every stop re-decides (verifier LOW-2):** a signalled stop of a conversation no longer in a turn — the turn-end boundary or the authoritative idle record — forces the pool's re-decision past the 10 s evaluation gate, owed or not. A turn the pool never evaluated while it ran (the gate closed by a default switch seconds earlier) had recorded nothing to owe, so its stop inside that window used to move nothing. The evaluation is cheap and the 180 s dwell belt still bounds it; nothing is recorded as owed any more — the stop decides from the facts.
- **The journal speaks, the user is not interrupted:** `[pool] defer <sid>: soft-exhausted (5h 7% < hot 10%) but mid-turn with a warm cache — moves at its first stop (to <member name>)`, once per (pool, conversation) per 10 min; a per-session re-point ends that conversation's deferral episode, so a new one inside the 10 minutes speaks at once (verifier LOW-3); the defer and warm-cache lines name the target member by name, the id only as a fallback (verifier INFO-a); the move itself posts the normal switch notice.
- **The pool default holds rather than pins — a recorded deviation, awaiting the owner's ratification:** a conversation following the pool default reads the pool's own credential link, fixed in its environment at spawn, so it cannot be pinned to the old member through a per-session link (the process would never read it, and the ledger would bill it to the wrong member). The default's soft move therefore waits for its warm mid-turn follower's first stop, and its other followers — cold ones included — wait and move with it then (at most one turn; the soft band is still usable). Hard-band and dead-login moves of the default are immediate. Every local conversation spawned since per-session links exist is decided on its own link. This departs from the letter of the rule for the default's cold co-followers and ships as is for the owner to ratify.
- **Gates:** test-pool-auto 170 (+32: the in-turn truth table, every band × warm × in-turn verdict, the `band` field, EDF unchanged, `wouldToName` on the warm-cache verdict, and wiring pins over both sites, the boundary, the ungated force, the ungated idle hook, the throttle reset, the name in both journal lines and server.js); test-fable-cap-pool-storm §18 +43 through the real engine and the real stdout pipeline (deferred then moved at the first stop with the gate closed, the cold sibling at once, the authoritative idle record, the hard band, the pool default held then moved, hard default at once, a never-evaluated turn moved at a stop inside the 10 s window at both stops, two deferral episodes ⇒ two lines) — each with a patched-copy control (the 2.369.149 engine, the stop without its force, the engine without the idle hook, a copy that defers the hard band too, the pre-fix owed-move engine, a re-point that keeps the throttle keys); test-auto-resume and test-stdout-registry pins follow the new boundary call and engine dep; the Pool/billing gate row carries the current counts (verifier INFO-b).

## 2.369.152 — spend notices die with the window they are about, and the stale ones already in the inbox are retired

- **Spend notices no longer live forever:** every "For you" item the spending ceiling files now carries the end of the window it talks about — the "this hour" warning expires 60 minutes after it is filed, the "today" warning after 24 hours, a refusal after 6 hours (its own re-file cadence) — and the inbox resolves it as `expired` then (checked at startup and every 5 minutes). The owner's inbox held 13 such warnings about windows that had closed 137–288 hours earlier.
- **The stale ones are retired on update:** a one-shot migration moves every Spending item filed before the Notices section existed (2.369.118) out of the action list (they coloured the red badge) into Notices, and gives each open one the end of the window it was about (read from the detail line the spending guard wrote: an hour warning 1 hour after it was filed, a refusal 6 hours, anything else 24 hours). One whose end has passed is resolved as `expired`, dated at that end rather than at the update, so the retirements sort as old history under "Recently resolved" instead of crowding out today's (kept in the store, never deleted); one still inside its window gets that end as its expiry. The inbox is written to disk before the migration is recorded as done. The migration's counts are recorded in `data/migrations.json`. On a copy of the owner's inbox: 13 retired, 2 fresh ones stamped, every other item byte-identical, a second run a no-op.
- **The inbox store:** items take an optional `expiresAt`; a re-file keeps the later end; an item without one never expires; reopening an expired item by hand makes it lasting. A notice row shows "expires in N min / N h"; a resolved row says "expired".
- **The migration runner** records a migration's returned counts beside its ledger timestamp (`reports[id]`).
- Gates: test-user-todos-expiry 38 (new, fast tier) · test-migrations 105 (the live path's file on disk when `run()` returns, the window-derived ends, and a patched-copy control without the live flush) · test-spend-paths 288 · test-user-todos-layout 22 · test-restore-smoke · test-ci-gate 224 · test-architecture 190.

## 2.369.150 — the accessibility tree stops growing with the transcript: the reader's band, paint-only structure out at the source, the minimap strip and the status bar's chips (design-accessibility-tree §8 lean set, chunks a0–a5 — the root fix under 2.369.144's lever)

**Also in 2.369.150 — a parked backlog item vanished at the 200-item cap.** A Task Group whose backlog held exactly 200 items (open + done + dropped) lost every `vibespace-task backlog-add` silently: the store sliced the array to `CAPS.backlogItems`, cutting the NEWEST item off, while the route and the CLI echoed the last surviving item by position — "parked as [B-a5b0]" for an item that was never stored (reported by a peer session on the owner's instance). Owner ruling: no cap at all — a bound belongs to a READ (what an injection selects, by ownership and priority), never to a WRITE. The store now keeps every item; the route acknowledges an add only after finding the stored item by identity (addedAt + addedBy + text) and refuses by name otherwise; claim/unclaim echo by id, never by position; the CLI prints the server's item and exits 1 when there is none. Gate: scripts/test-backlog-no-truncation.mjs (fast, 20). Priority grading + ownership-aware injection selection is the follow-up lane.

- **Why:** 2.369.144 found the owner's Windows freeze in Chrome's accessibility tree (HandleAXEvents 39.5 s on the browser UI thread; 50,150 nodes). The census (design §1) put 52–68 % of those nodes in four visible transcripts whose rendered cards were 82–85 % OFF-SCREEN and every one in the tree (`.chat-msg { content-visibility:auto }` keeps an off-screen subtree in the tree, §0), 16–18 nodes of pure paint per closed tool-card shell, one minimap marker per user turn of the WHOLE conversation per window, and a 20 % stale share from the status bar rebuilding itself by innerHTML on every tick. The .144 lever kept transcripts out entirely; this release makes exposure a function of the VIEWPORT, never of the rendered window.
- **The reader's band (a1, src/lib/chat-view.js `_syncAxExposure`, design §3 row 1):** every rendered card (gap cards too) farther than `AX_BAND_VIEWPORTS` = 2 viewports from the viewport is `aria-hidden`; cards inside the band, the card holding the focus, the last jump target and the last search reveal's card (ChatSearch `onReveal`) are exposed — the exemption lapses once the reader scrolls away (the rule `_setStableHeights` already uses). A focus that lands inside a band-hidden card (Tab / Shift+Tab / `.focus()`) exposes that card in the focus event's OWN task — a `focusin` on the list, no layout read — instead of on the next pass ≥ 150 ms later (verifier finding: Shift+Tab from the composer after three page-ups landed on a fork button whose card was still aria-hidden, and Chrome 153 had to repair our markup itself — "Blocked aria-hidden on an element because its descendant retained focus"; a `.focus()` without a scroll never ran a pass at all). ONE derivation with ONE layout read (`_cardPositions`), run at the END of every landing the paging machinery makes (extendTop / extendBottom / trim / gap slab up + down / gap trim / teleport / the fold pass — never inside an anchored section), 150 ms after the last scroll event (programmatic scrolls too — a jump moves the band with it), on resume from any hidden reason, on the setting's flip, plus ONE settle pass 1.2 s later (heights keep resolving after a landing); never mid-gesture (a pass whose wheel/touch input is younger than the debounce re-arms); a suspended view skips; teardown removes nothing; `_axBand` records every pass's why / counts / geometry for incident bundles. `aria-hidden` and not `content-visibility:hidden`: a0 measured the former layout-neutral (sh 767 → 767) and the latter moving the layout (767 → 658) — every 2.369.142 paging invariant stands. `accessibility.exposeChat` stays boolean (design §8, no three-valued form): on = the band, off = the whole list `aria-hidden` as in 2.369.144; `applyAxExposure` re-derives every live view's band on the flip. Description + zh/ja + docs/settings.md say both halves.
- **Paint-only structure out at the source (a2, design §3 rows 2 + 3 lean):** `src/lib/icons.js` `_s()` — the ONE helper every UI/file icon goes through — emits `aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"` on the `<svg>` (the `python` / `alert` raw strings too); the `.chat-code-ln` gutters (highlight.js), `.chat-diff-prefix` (both diff renderers), `.chat-run-arrow`, every spinner (`chat-spinner` ×7 sites, `upload-active-spinner` ×3), the 8 resize handles of every window (window.js) and the `.chat-minimap` strip (one marker div per user turn, uncapped — the one subtree that grew with the conversation's length; the TOC button stays the accessible path to the same turns, a sibling outside the strip) are `aria-hidden` at creation; every generated GLYPH in chat.css / style.css / viewers.css (the ▸/▾/▴ disclosure arrows, the · chip dot, the LRM marks on paths, †, ⫿, the role-indicator icons beside their font-size-0 labels, the menu arrows — 32 rules) is written in the alt-text form `content: '…' / ""` with the plain declaration first as the fallback, so a pseudo-element is no longer a static-text node; a generated sentence never gets the empty alt. Nothing visual or keyboard-reachable changes; no control lost its only name — a census, not a promise (test-ax-paint ②: 7 icon-only buttons, 0 unnamed).
- **The status bar updates in place (a3, src/lib/chat-status-bar.js, design §3 row 8 (b)):** `render()` used to rebuild the whole bar by innerHTML on every context% / cost / turn-state tick — one accessibility subtree remove+insert per chat window per update. The chip set is now a keyed descriptor list (`chip(key, cls, title, html, {style, attrs})`, 26 sites) and `_reconcile` keeps ONE `<span data-chip=…>` per key across renders: class / title / style / data-* patched through setAttribute only when they differ, the inner markup re-written only when its string changed, a node moved only when its position changed, a key that left the set removed. The same node object survives twenty ticks; a chip that appears or disappears (turn state, health, held, workflow, browser…) lands at / leaves its place with the neighbours untouched; a render with nothing changed writes nothing; the click handling stays the one delegated listener (`_onClick` + `closest`); same classes, titles and markup (the bar is a flex row, so the whitespace text nodes the old join(' ') put between chips were never rendered).
- **Measured (scripts/test-ax-budget.mjs, Chrome 153 at 1400×1000, the §1c fixture — 15,691 lines / 199 turns / 36 MB — ONE chat window in the live rendering mode; the same fixture and renderer before (a0) and after (a2/a4, three identical runs):**

  - after four page-ups (50 → 336 rendered cards, sh 767 → 2574 at ch 658): TOTAL 3214 → **2769**, the window 2918 → **2498**. This window is ~4 viewports (the trim's keep zone filling) and sits inside the band whole, so its growth over the 1.2-viewport baseline is the trim's business — printed with its cause, and the band's invariant is asserted where the DOM outgrows the band:

The second slab moves NON-IGNORED **650 → 627** (a1 measured 1,094 → 1,096 before the paint layer; the neutered copy 4,378 → **8,065**), while TOTAL 2158 → **4847** — a hidden card still serialises ≈ 5 ignored `ariaHiddenSubtree` nodes (OQ1, below). The window **4576 TOTAL / 516 NON-IGNORED** (a1's 5,448 / 916 before a2) — under the design's 5,000 per-window ceiling, pinned ×1.25 at 5,700 / 650.
  - the NEGATIVE CONTROL (`_syncAxExposure` neutered at source in the scratch worktree, string-exact marker, bundle rebuilt, the same window / teleport / slabs): TOTAL **14,871** / NON-IGNORED **8,065**, every far card exposed (a1's control before a2: 20,158 / 12,260) — 3.1× / 12.9× the fix.

## 2.369.149 — the account pool no longer moves a conversation whose prompt cache is still warm

- **The warm-cache hold (owner: "如果一个对话最近在活跃（缓存还热）那就尽量不要切，因为无缓启动要消耗大量额度"):** moving a conversation to another member cold-starts it — the prompt cache belongs to the account that wrote it, so the next request re-bills the whole context at uncached prices. The pool's PROACTIVE move (the 'edf' jump toward a member whose weekly quota resets sooner, taken while the current member can still serve) now waits while the conversation is WARM: now − the last instant its CLI produced output (`_lastPtyDataAt`) < its cache TTL — 300 s by default, 3600 s for a `[1m]` request model (read off the pick/spawn model, since a served model never carries the variant). The decision answers `warm-cache` and the pool asks again next cycle; a FORCED move — the member cannot serve (exhausted, or a dead login) — still happens at once: a wall is a wall.
- **Two sites:** the per-session pass holds each warm conversation on its own link while a cold sibling on the same verdict moves; the pool DEFAULT (which moves every conversation without its own link at once) defers its proactive move while ANY of those conversations is warm. A hold is journalled once per (pool, conversation) per 10 min — `[pool] hold <sid>: warm cache (last output <a>s ago < ttl <t>s) — proactive move to <member> deferred` — and never posts a user notice (it is a deferral, not a blocked pool); the pool DEFAULT's hold is ONE deferral, so it speaks once per pool per 10 min whichever follower is warmest that cycle (the line still names it, scoped `(pool default)`). No new setting.
- **A lock is the request model as spelled:** a conversation locked with `/model fable` runs on the 5-minute cache even when it was spawned `[1m]` — the lock is what the server re-asserts at every repin — so a variant-less lock never borrows the spawn model's `[1m]`; only a lock copied verbatim off the served model (the API's base id, which cannot carry the variant) reads the variant back off the pick/spawn model.
- **Gates:** test-pool-auto +19 (the TTL by model, the verdict shapes, forced moves untouched, and a wiring pin over the engine's two proactive call sites and its `warmCache(…_lastPtyDataAt…)` calls); test-fable-cap-pool-storm §17 +27 through the real engine (warm stays / cold sibling moves / the `[1m]` conversation after a variant-less answer / the pool-default hold and its release; the lock shapes — a user lock `fable` over a `[1m]` spawn before and after an answer moves, a served-copied lock and a `fable[1m]` lock hold — and five rotating warm followers speaking exactly once in 10 min and again after the floor; each with a patched-copy pre-fix negative control, plus the `modelsMatch` spelling of the lock rule kept as a control showing why it compares exactly).
