## 2.369.146 — the Communication panel manages ACCOUNTS like the mounts do: N accounts per channel kind, each bound at connect to the OAuth client / tenant app it was minted under — the integration's pick is a DEFAULT for new accounts, never a re-point of an existing token

- **The owner's model (2026-09-22, "为啥不能和mount那种类似，管理的是账号，每个账号添加的时候可以选oauth client？"):** the panel held ONE Gmail account and ONE Lark tenant (`connect(kind)` re-authorized the record whose `id === kind`), and both adapters resolved their application credential through the integration row's CURRENT pick at consent AND at every refresh — so a refresh token minted under client A was refreshed with client B the moment the pick changed (Google answers `invalid_client`), the exact silent swap §14.2 forbids, built into the model. Now, exactly as a Gmail mount stores only the preset KEY it was authorized under: N adapter records per kind (the first keeps `id === kind` so every existing record, conversation, reach entry and filter stays valid untouched; further ones are `<kind>:<8 hex>`), every record carries `credentialKey` (`cluster:<presetKey>` | `own`) stamped at CONNECT from the wizard's choice — validated against what the integration OFFERS right now, refused `400 unknown-credential` by name otherwise, the row's own pick when omitted — and the adapter's consent, refresh, status and Test all resolve THAT key. A preset the env stopped offering answers `preset-gone` naming it and no token call is made for that account at all; the other account keeps refreshing with its own client. NOT built (owner: no over-design): a credentials manager, presets outside the env, any other change to the Integrations window, Task-Group assignment, the outbox, the agents adapter.
- **`src/server/integration-store.js`:** `resolveIntegration(id, {credentialKey})` — `cluster:<k>` indexes the preset list (`clusterPresetsFor`, factored out of `clusterDefaultFor`, never a fallback to another preset), `own` = the user's saved values alone (`own-missing` when absent), an unknown key `unknown-credential`, no key = today's precedence now carrying `credentialKey` (what a NEW account would be stamped with); `offeredCredentials(id)` = the presets as `cluster:<k>` + `own` only while the values are complete and readable, key + label only; `test(id, {credentialKey})`.
- **`src/server/channels-engine.js` / `src/routes/channels.js`:** `connect(kind, {credentialKey, newAccount})` mints only with `newAccount` or on a kind with no record (else the P1a per-kind path re-authorizes the FIRST account), `reauthorize(adapterId)` by id — never by kind — stamping a legacy record's missing key with the row's current pick, a FURTHER account's `disconnect` removes only its own record + live entry + wake windows + index rows (the first's record stays, P1a unchanged), `adapterView` carries `credentialKey` / `credentialLabel` / `credential` (the facts FOR THAT KEY) / `credentials` (the offered list) / `credentialDefault` (the row's CURRENT pick, never this account's key) / `auth.credentialKey`, `available[]` the same; `POST /api/channels/adapters/:kind/connect` takes `{credentialKey?, newAccount?}`, `POST /api/channels/adapters/:id/reauthorize` is new. `src/channels/gmail.js` + `src/channels/lark.js`: every `resolveIntegration` carries the account's key (handed down in the deps AND read live off the record, so the migration's stamp lands on an adapter built before it); `auth.state()` names it.
- **Migration `2026-09-channel-credential-key` (`src/server/migrations.js`):** stamps every adapter record lacking `credentialKey` ONCE with its integration's current key — the honest reading of what minted its token — through the engine's own serialized writer (`stampCredentialKeys()`; server.js hands the registry the engine, adapters.json's ONE writer); a record whose integration resolves to nothing stays unstamped and keeps following the row's pick; without an engine a legacy real record FAILS the run by name so a later boot retries it. Idempotent.
- **The wizard and the panel (`src/lib/channels-panel.js`, `src/lib/integrations-window.js`, `src/lib/channel-words.js`):** every Connect / "Add account…" entry MINTS (`newAccount: true` — this client never issues the P1a re-point of the kind's first record); the wizard reads `credentials` + `credentialDefault` off the digest and draws a CREDENTIAL step ONLY when more than one credential is offered — one radio per preset (its env label) + "Own client", the row's default pre-picked, Cancel mints nothing, Continue posts `{credentialKey, newAccount:true}` and the SAME dialog moves on to the consent step; exactly one offered ⇒ that key rides the body and the step is skipped silently. An existing account re-authorizes ITSELF (the status-line verb and the ⋯ menu post `/api/channels/adapters/:id/reauthorize` by id); "Add account…" on a section (⋯ menu, gated on `connectable`) opens the wizard for another account of that kind. A section is NAMED BY ITS ACCOUNT — the token's user when known, else the kind's label, numbered ("Gmail account 2") only when the kind holds more than one; a credential chip on the head names the credential where it disambiguates and never for a legacy record with no key; every section carries `data-adapter`. The Integrations window's delegating chooser is captioned "Default for new accounts" (nothing else on the card moved); the two new route codes (`unknown-credential`, `no-such-adapter`) are worded by the client; zh + ja for every new string.
- **Verifier r1 (2026-09-22, three findings, each reproduced on the real engine + fake Google before the fix):** ① the migration stamped a legacy record with the row's CURRENT pick although the Gmail token already records the client it was minted under (`clusterKey`, written since P1a) — an org1-minted token was re-bound to the channels client on every instance whose pick had flipped before the upgrade, the exact case the model exists for; `stampCredentialKeys()` now goes through `credentialKeyEvidence(rec, mod)`: the token's own client wins when this instance still offers it (`evidence:'token'`; null = `own`), else the row's pick (`evidence:'row-pick'`, what refreshed it until now — a Lark token names nothing), and the `[migrate]` line names the evidence per record. ② the first account's key was immutable and a supplied key was dropped without a word (the P1a `connect(kind,{credentialKey})` returned `reauthorize()` before looking at it): `reauthorize(id, {credentialKey})` (route body `{credentialKey?}`) now RE-BINDS a TOKEN-LESS account (never authenticated / disconnected — nothing is minted under its key; the live adapter is dropped so it is rebuilt under the new key, measured: the stamp alone left the consent URL on the old client) after validation (`400 unknown-credential`), and refuses `400 credential-bound` BY NAME on an account HOLDING a token bound elsewhere (its stamp, else what the token itself names); the digest carries `auth.tokenHeld`; the panel's Connect on a token-less account runs the wizard's credential step first (its own key pre-picked) and posts the choice to ITS `/reauthorize`, a held token posts `{}`; channel-words words `credential-bound` (zh + ja). ③ three fixture literals in the new suite tripped the pre-push secret scanner — short obviously-fake values now; the working tree scans clean against master. Gates: test-channels-accounts 77 (⑤ bound-vs-token-less + the route legs), test-migrations 82 (the token-evidence legs, incl. a token whose `clusterKey` ≠ the row's pick), test-integrations-ui 105 (⑩(c) rewritten: the token-less Connect path, both directions, the second section's own id), test-integration-registry 208 (the migrations suite's env handle allowlisted with its reason), build gates green (i18n-check 4312/4312, test-architecture 189).
- **Docs:** design-communication-panel §14.5 gains "账号, 像挂载一样" (the decision, the record shape, the migration, what stays out of scope, the gates), §5's `adapters.json` is ONE record per connected ACCOUNT carrying `credentialKey`, §14.2 points there, §17 gains the `test-channels-accounts` row; kb-api's channel route table is complete (`connect {credentialKey?, newAccount?}`, `reauthorize`, a further account's `disconnect`, the digest's credential fields); the kb-file-structure entries for every touched file re-read against the code (channels-engine + routes, channels-panel, integration-store, gmail/lark, channel-words, integration-registry, migrations.js); kb-design-lessons §18's channel row and CLAUDE.md's bugfix index carry the one-line invariant: an account is bound to the credential that minted its token, the row's pick is a DEFAULT for new accounts.
- **Gates (run from the worktree, 2026-09-22, every one green):** build (i18n-check 4311 zh / 4311 ja · test-bundle-globals 6 · test-architecture 189 · test-ws-contract 5 · test-session-schema 5), test-server-globals 2; fast: test-channel-record 37 · test-channel-caps 96 · test-channel-store 124 · test-channels-engine 142 · test-channel-adapter-contract 90 · test-channel-filter 71 · test-channel-outbox 107 · test-channel-acl 38 · test-channels-lark-shape 84 · test-channels-gmail-shape 90 · test-channels-push 70 · test-channels-lane-parity 33 · test-channels-identity 55 · test-channels-egress 22 · test-channels-agent-cli 19 · **test-channels-accounts 59** (new, fast; fake fetch only — incl. a patched engine copy with the hand-down and the record stamp removed that reproduces the silent swap) · test-oauth-loopback 39 · test-secret-box 37 · test-integration-registry 208 (the consumer census accepts the keyed call, its env-name census allowlists the new suite with its reason) · test-migrations 75; chrome, one at a time: test-integrations-ui 93 (⑩ the account model) · test-channels-e2e 132 · test-channels-i18n 27.

## 2.369.145 — the action-trace row said "server unreachable" on every card (a content blocker's rule), "not traced" is now said by name, the Browser profiles window stops stacking its buttons and opens from the rail

- **`/api/browser/trace` → `/api/browser/actions` (owner: "为啥都是没有记录到操作", 4 cards all "轨迹不可用: 无法连接服务器"):** EasyPrivacy carries `/trace?sessionid=` and ad-block filters match case-insensitively, so the client's `/api/browser/trace?sessionId=…` was blocked by every content blocker (uBlock / AdGuard / Brave) — `fetch` threw, `fetchJson` answered null, the row said "server unreachable" while the server never saw the request (the housekeeping window, another path, worked). Renamed on both sides (routes, `frameUrl`, the view, the suite, kb-api). 不变量 = an API path never ends in a tracker-shaped word followed by an id-shaped query.
- **"not traced" is its own state:** when the server has no browser key to match by (`keyFrom: null` — the call drove an agent's own `agent-browser` profile, one of the "unregistered directories", not a browser VibeSpace started), the row now says "not traced — this browser was not started through VibeSpace (Browser profiles)" instead of "no recorded actions", and the expander explains that actions are recorded only for profile browsers. A profile with zero actions still says "no recorded actions".
- **Browser profiles window (owner: "右侧布局需要改进下"):** `.bprof-btn` is `white-space: nowrap; flex-shrink: 0` — a CJK label's min-content is one glyph, so under the grid's `auto` track "收编…" / "搁置" and the bar's "立即清理" stacked vertically.
- **Rail entry (owner: "这个菜单藏太深了，建议放在rail能打开"):** a Browser profiles item on the activity rail (globe) beside System, opening the same singleton window as ⚙ ▸ Tools ▸ Browser profiles… — a window, not a panel, so it carries no active state.

## 2.369.144 — the owner's Windows freeze, solved at the root: Chrome's accessibility tree (a UIA client had the mode on; the page had 50,150 accessible nodes); a lever to keep transcripts out of it

- **The verdict (owner's chrome://tracing, 70 s over a refresh, perfetto):** the browser process's UI thread ran ONE task for **39.5 s** (plus 4.8 s, 0.8 s, 0.6 s) — `HandleAXEvents` from `content/browser/accessibility/render_accessibility_host.cc:77`, Chrome serialising the page's accessibility tree on the browser UI thread. GPU CrGpuMain max 31 ms, renderer main max 91 ms, long tasks ≤ 179 ms: not our JS, not the GPU, and every in-page probe was blind by construction (the renderer was fine while the WHOLE browser was blocked). chrome://accessibility on that box: Web accessibility ON, active AT none, **UIA client `typeless.exe`**, **50,150 accessible nodes** on the VibeSpace tab (9,902 stale). Other sites do not trip it because they do not carry 50k nodes.
- **Settings → Chat → "Expose chat transcripts to assistive technology" (default ON):** off ⇒ every chat message list is `aria-hidden` (existing views live, new views at birth) so the accessibility tree shrinks to the chrome; a desktop-hidden window always carries `aria-hidden` (beside `visibility:hidden` / `content-visibility:hidden`). The default stays honest for screen-reader users; the owner's remedy on the box: chrome://accessibility → "Suppress automatic accessibility enablement from platform API consumers" (= `--disable-platform-accessibility-integration`), or quit the UIA client. test-desktop-resume-paging +2.
- **Gate:** test-window-target's §3 REAL leg still opened the fixture with `open --exec` (the way in before the 2026-09-21 exec-is-human rule) — it now registers the fixture as a keeper registry row and opens it by id, and pins the CLI's own `exec_is_human` refusal (103; the leg SKIPs off this machine). test-desktop-resume-paging's new legs run before the CDP socket closes (a `cdp()` after `ws.close()` never answers — two 20-minute hangs). test-browser-resources owns a chromium by its PROCESS LINEAGE (an ancestor carrying the tagged AGENT_BROWSER_* names or the fixture HOME — the daemon spawns chromium with a clean environ), never by "it appeared after our snapshot" — under the heavy tier's four lanes it claimed another suite's chromium (three user-data-dirs, k=1 = 41 processes, the per-browser slope red twice).

## 2.369.143 — the freeze probe learns the stall the owner actually feels: frames alive but slow

- **The live reproduction (Windows, 07:00Z):** a refresh, then a stall the owner timed at "十几秒" — the telemetry shows a 4 s boot timer landing 29 s late and a batch flush 14 s late, yet neither detector fired: the self-gap needs one tick ≥ 4 s late and the rAF arm needs a frame gap ≥ 2 s, while this stall was timers 1–3 s late per tick and frames every 1–2 s — under both thresholds, main thread idle (long tasks max 179 ms). New PURE `jankStormVerdict`: every frame ≥ 300 ms enters a ring; when the slow frames (≥ 500 ms) of the last 20 s cover ≥ 6 s, that is a `jank-storm` (event + metric + the auto capture, once per storm). The snapshot carries `frameGaps` (last 60) and `tickLags` (every tick ≥ 1.5 s late with visibility facts, last 40). test-freeze-probe +6.
- **Timelines were receipt times:** the client flushes 15 s apart (later under a stall), so the shard's `ts` misplaced an event by up to the stall; every queued event now carries `t` and the server keeps it as `cts` when sane (within 10 min).

## 2.369.142 — huge-session paging (inc-mubvu3a4-x8sb, owner 2026-09-21 on 2.369.136: "没有办法正确翻页，每次都往回跳转很多，往下又直接跳到底部，还有大量空白"): the trims are by HEIGHT and never touch the reader's neighbourhood, pinned means at the live tail, both extends fold first and grow by direction, a wheel notch is never lost — and the whole path leaves evidence

- **The fix (g2, structural):** `_trimEdge(side)` is the ONE trim (`_trimBottom` / `_trimTop` are its spellings) and it removes rendered cards only OUTSIDE THE KEEP ZONE — the viewport plus one viewport above and below (`TRIM_KEEP_VIEWPORTS`); 150 cards (`TRIM_SOFT_CARDS`) is a target a zone may exceed, `FOLD_DOM_CEILING` the only hard bound; a folded card sits at its run header (`_cardPositions`). The 2.369.129 three-viewport gate measured the WHOLE window — including what it was about to remove — and then trimmed by COUNT: on the owner's compact-mode session 150 cards are about one viewport, so every upward page removed the reader's anchor (`trimBottom n:400 removed:250 sh:2851 sh2:972`, `anchorLost {why:removed}`), the delta fallback clamped scrollTop to 0 and the grow loop refilled and trimmed again — 750–1,300 messages per wheel notch. `_extendTop` trims AFTER the anchored landing (a trim that reads the restored scrollTop cannot take the anchor) and grows by the history ABOVE the viewport; `_extendBottom` folds BEFORE its trim (the downward mirror of the .129 order defect) and grows by the content BELOW — one gesture, one landing, each way. PINNED ⇔ AT THE LIVE TAIL: `_atLiveTail` carries `windowEnd ≥ total` (the owner's `repin we:1851 total:3201` handed the reader to the pinned auto-follow, which walked to the tail — "往下又直接跳到底部"); the scroll handler, the run-bar landing and the read-only scroll button read it; the DOM edge pages, never pins. A fresh slab renders once at insert (`_reserveFreshHeights`) so landings and the zone read measured heights, not 80 px placeholders; the viewport anchor never picks the seek sentinel (a huge session's first child — every prepend from the top used to land at scrollTop 0); the gap trim keeps the same zone. THE NOTCH IS NOT LOST: a wheel-up at the top edge / during a load is carried into the landing (≤ one viewport) and a notch eaten by the 300 ms lock re-arms the extend (`_liftLoadLock`) — found by the fixed run's own table, where a 4×700 px fling still parked at the top of the slab with 2,275 messages above.
- **The verifier's round (r1 — five reproduced findings fixed, the low ones taken):** ① the carry captured only a notch that STARTED at the top edge, so a 700 px notch beginning 232 px from it still lost 468 px and a 4×700 px fling parked at scrollTop 43 with 2,178 messages above — the wheel handler now carries the OVERSHOOT (`px − room`, a notch that crosses either edge) through ONE accounting (`_addWheelCarry` / `_applyWheelCarry` at all four landings, both extends AND both gap slabs / `_clearWheelCarry` at every chosen destination), bounded to one viewport per landing, and a notch eaten by the load lock traces `{eaten:1}` before the early return; ② inside a loaded gap slab with content-visibility on, wheels in BOTH directions were absorbed (a 2,800 px fling moved the reader's card under 110 px — native anchoring against the slab's placeholder flips; pre-existing, invisible to a one-sided judge whose plan never left the registered tail) — measured in headless chrome: the slab's visible cards flipped between their 80 px placeholder and their real size on alternate frames (sh 4173 ↔ 18723, 2,205 resize events in six frames, no write of ours) and the reserve did not stop it, content-visibility off did (0 resizes, the wheel delivered exactly), so a tail-mode gap slab now runs with STABLE HEIGHTS from its anchored insert until the top trim drops it (teleport keeps its own regime), the judge gained the DEAD-WHEEL rule (a mid-list gesture must deliver ≥ 50 % of its px) and §4c enters the slab (a minimap jump to message 0, holds up into the gap, mid-list gestures inside it both ways, holds back down); ③ a gap slab survived the walk back to the tail and the next prepend landed the fresh slab ABOVE the ancient cards — `_extendTop` prepends before the first NON-gap card and the top trim drops the slab (sentinel epoch bumped; an in-flight fetch lands `gapUp:stale`) whenever the window leaves message 0: a gap slab lives only directly above message 0; ④ ring reads by index went blind after the 600→400 splice (a false "paged but the ring recorded nothing") — every entry carries a monotonic `seq`, both drivers slice by it; ⑤ a carried notch survived a jump — cleared at `_noteUserNav` / `_resetGapAfterJump` / `_seekTeleport`. The judge's landing band is `st < 100` with history above (window OR gap), not judged while a slab is in flight; the measured-heights claim is worded as the mitigation it is (placeholders resolved once at insert, later drift absorbed by the anchor — §4c prints the max |Δsh| on non-paging gestures); kb-design-lessons §11 and kb-features now describe the height trim; the by-hand driver re-tails after emulating content-visibility (it opened at scrollTop 0 unpinned, a state no live window has) and walks the gap legs.
- **Measured on a copy of the real 976 MB transcript (the final build, cv on, 677 px list, 31 gestures at the owner's cadences):** one notch → `ws 3175→3125` (50 messages, was 750) and `st 0→704` (the notch honored, the reader's card 27 px from where the wheel put it; was 0→8 on the top of the slab); a 4×700 px fling → `ws 2875→2525` landing mid; the 4 s down-hold → `we 1839→3139` unpinned at `st 969` (was `repin we:1851` and a pinned walk to the tail), the scroll button then `we 3225 = total`, pinned; `anchorLost` 0, st-0 landings 0, mid-history repins 0, `foldCeiling` 0, trims 26 bottom / 28 top / 7 zone-skips, 22 carried notches, blank ≤ 9 % at settle (36 px below the content at most, on the button's landing); `RULES: all 31 gestures hold` — the cv-off pass: all 31 hold as well.
- **Gates:** scripts/test-chat-trim-guard.mjs 134 (the zone EXECUTED against injected geometry: the owner's 400 compact cards at st 1400 remove nothing where the count removed 250; the tall window 184/192; the folded far end at no pixel cost; the ceiling's forced 200; `_atLiveTail`; the sentinel-skipping anchor lands at 500, not 0); scripts/test-chat-paging.mjs §1c/§4c/§4d — a synthetic huge compact-mode fixture with the MEASURED shape (48 MB, ≈ 21,000 lines, the kind mix per 1000 lines, tool_result / text / thinking size histograms, fold-run lengths, bookkeeping rows, hook attachments, real PNGs at the largest-record scale), 21 real CDP wheel gestures judged by scripts/paging-gesture-rules.mjs (no jump back > 1.5 viewports · no pin / bottom landing before the window reaches the tail · blank ≤ 25 % · the ring never empty after a page), and the PRE-FIX CONTROL — a scratch copy with the zone and the pin term patched out by exact strings — reproducing the jump and the mid-history pin; scripts/dbg-huge-paging.mjs `repro` prints the same table on a copy of the real transcript and exits 1 on a violation. test-desktop-resume-paging's source-level control now also strips the zone, the measured heights and the sentinel-skipping anchor (the new layer closed its harm — a pinned extend can no longer drop the tail — so the older control had gone green on the fixed build). npm run build (bundle-globals, architecture, ws-contract, session-schema, i18n-check), test-paging-collapse-guard, test-fold-ux, test-minimap-jump, test-chat-frame-guard, test-turn-truth-ui, test-desktop-resume-paging. **r1 gates:** test-chat-trim-guard 178 (the PAGING wheel listener lifted out of the source and executed on the verifier's numbers, the carry consumer, the gap-slab drop with two controls, the ring across the splice, the judge's rows), test-chat-paging ALL PASS (31 checks; §4c 33 gestures incl. the 13 gap legs, every mid-slab gesture delivering exactly; both negative controls red), test-desktop-resume-paging 38, test-fixture-isolation 78 — and the FAST TIER `node scripts/ci.mjs` ALL GREEN (132 suites, 397 s; the branch's first cut was RED there: the §1c generator hand-spelled the synthetic-id family).
- **The ring names the author of every move:** `_traceExpect(by)` stamps every programmatic scrollTop write (anchor restores, both delta fallbacks, the forced-scroll chain, jumps, the run restore, every write in chat-view-seek.js) and the coarse `scroll` sample carries `writeAgo`/`by` beside `wheelAgo`; `trimBottom`/`trimTop` trace `n`, the height the gate read, the height after, `ch`, `st`; `repin` carries `we`/`total`; `wheelTop`/`wheelBottom`/`pageUp`/`pageDown` name the trigger; `anchorLost {why}` says why the anchor restore fell back; the seek mixin — which shipped no evidence at all — traces its sentinel, every slab request/landing/failure, the tail delegation, both trims, teleport, the stable-height toggle and every landing write. Ring 600→400, the recorder ships 300 and, per window, `geom` (scrollTop/height/viewport, cards in view, cards the browser had NOT rendered — the blank strips).
- **Reproduced (scripts/dbg-huge-paging.mjs `measure` + `repro`, on a COPY, never the real ~/.claude):** one 120 px wheel notch walked the window 750 messages back and landed on the top of a slab nobody asked for; a 4 s continuous scroll consumed the whole 3,201-message registered tail; the first down fling re-pinned with 1,350 messages still below the window and a 4 s down-hold chained 14 extendBottoms with the pin held; the blank did not reproduce as pixels (≤ 13 %), only the collapsed one-viewport states behind it. **Causes (evidence only — the fix is the next chunk):** `_trimBottom`'s three-viewport gate measures the whole window INCLUDING the resolved content it removes, then trims by COUNT to 150 cards, so a fold-dominated remainder is one viewport, the anchor goes with the removed bottom, the delta fallback clamps, and the grow loop refills and is trimmed again (the cv-OFF control shows content-visibility is not required — it adds the collapse to exactly one viewport and the st-0 landings); the pin predicate has no `_windowEnd ≥ _total` term, and `_extendBottom` trims before it folds (the 2.369.129 order defect mirrored). The transcript's shape (kind mix, size histograms, fold-run lengths, run-breakers per 200, largest records) is recorded in the kb for the portable §1c fixture.

## 2.369.141 — a tab coming back is not a freeze (the auto capture fired on a tab switch), and the status bar's task chip is short

- **"没有实际卡顿但我切回标签页的时候突然提示抓取卡顿现场":** Chrome throttles a hidden tab's timers to once a minute, so the probe's 1 s tick fires 4–60 s late right after a return with `document.hidden` already false — the 2.340.3 self-gap rule (`gap > 4 s && !hidden`) called that a renderer freeze, and .137's auto capture filed an incident for it. The verdict is now PURE `selfGapIsFreeze`: a gap counts only when the page was visible for the whole of it (the previous tick after the last return, no hide since, not hidden now, not within 3 s of the return); the rAF-stall arm is excused for 3 s after a return too. test-freeze-probe (fast, 9 — the owner's return as the negative control). Caveat for the .137 verdict: some of the month's 54 `renderer-freeze` events were tab returns, not freezes; the `compositor-stall` ones (timers alive) were not.
- **"这个太长的问题还是没解决":** the ⟳ chip in the chat status bar is the harness's BACKGROUND TASK label (the CLI's task description = a Workflow's whole meta.description), not the workflow chip — it now shows `shortWorkflowName(description)`, the tooltip keeps the whole line. test-task-lifecycle +1.

## 2.369.140 — a Workflow card lost its phases on every server restart (owner, inc-muc2fmtt-5jat "还是上面的俩workflow都没展示细节")

- **Why .139 was not enough:** `task_started` / `task_progress` / `task_notification` exist only on the live stream — the transcript never carries them and the wrapper's stdout ring (a few hundred KB) drops them within minutes of a big tool output — so the Update's server restart rebuilt every Workflow card WITHOUT its tree, and the CLI's next `task_progress` (throttled: none at all while one agent runs quietly for 30 min) was the first chance to see it again; a finished run's card never got it back. Now the stdout consumer persists the latest record per task in the server's own session-meta (`taskRecords`: started, the last progress with its tree kept field-wise, the notification; 40 tasks at most, debounced atomic writes; never the wrapper's sidecar), boot-restore carries it into the restored session, and `rebuildHistory` replays it SILENTLY (`MessageManager.replay`, no ops) after the transcript + ring and before the live queue — the card comes back with its phases, agents and outcome. `_taskRecords` / `_taskRecordsTimer` registered in session-schema. test-task-lifecycle +3 (the replay trio, no op emitted, a replayed notification closes).

## 2.369.139 — a Workflow card's live details only appeared after a reload (owner, inc-muc1hfeg-0qn2)

- **The CLI's `system/task_started` names a Workflow `local_workflow` (and a Bash task `local_bash`, an agent `local_agent`), and on the live stream it lands BEFORE the launch ack** — so the card's `taskInfo.type` was the CLI's word, the chat view's live re-render gate compared it with `'workflow'`, and every `task_progress` edit (phases, agent chips, usage) was dropped until a reload rebuilt the card from the server's normalizer. `normalizeTaskType` maps the CLI vocabulary to ours at every read (task_started + background_tasks_changed), the launch ack's own type wins over whatever task_started spelled, the re-render gate also admits any card that carries the tree, and the status bar's level-set rows compare the normalized type. test-task-lifecycle +3 (the normalization, the incident's exact live order, the widened gate pin).

## 2.369.138 — the plan week reads the plan week (inc-mubu23bd-5vxi, owner 2026-09-21 "刚才7d用量红了，刷新之后变成绿的了"): claude 2.1.274's `rate_limit_event` carries `unifiedWindows` — the 5-hour, the weekly and the overage-included weekly, which the binary itself calls a PER-MODEL bucket — and `seven_day_overage_included` is that bucket (measured on 12 live buffers: about twice the plan on every account with a model cap; the owner's 0.43/0.87 against the verified panel's 43 % / Fable 86 %), yet 2.361.2 mapped it to the plan lane and never read the windows, so every event overwrote the plan 7d with the bucket and the taskbar donut flipped red/green against every panel refresh. The lane is decided by what NAMES it: one record yields up to three readings (5h, plan 7d, the model cap), the representative status attaches to the lane its type names, the cap is named through the account's verified window sidecar / an existing cap with the same reset / the request family, else a `model:cap` placeholder that folds into the named cap on the next panel or banner (never the plan, never dropped); the engine names the lane before any signal reads it, hands the window guard every named lane and no longer defers the type (it marks the cap on arrival); the statusline twin writes 2.1.274's `model_scoped[]` (percent, ISO reset) as named scoped buckets and the lift rung restores a model cap the tool measured; a one-shot repair (`2026-09-weekly-lanes-unfold`) re-derives every plan week last written by an event from the newest windowed event in the buffers linked to that slot. The repair is bounded: only a plan limit whose source is the event can still hold the bucket (every other producer states both windows), the evidence is the newest non-rejected windowed event in the buffers linked to that slot (per-session pool link → pool default → own subscription), accepted only on the account's own established window, archived first, written through the one write path with the 5-hour lane left out and a clock that never regresses `fetchedAt`; a key with no evidence is left with its reason. Gates: test-rate-limit-capture 75 (the owner's record verbatim, a no-unifiedWindows control, a seven_day_opus control, a source-listing census over every file that spells the type), test-quota-model 326 (the naming rungs, the one permitted fold, the lift rung, the real statusline tool; the repair named in the writer and reader censuses), test-fable-cap-pool-storm 289 (§2b/§15 rewritten: the cap on arrival, never deferred, never the plan; the PRE-FIX control re-maps the type to the plan and reproduces two demotions for one wall), test-migrations 61 (the repair on the incident fixture: pool links, an older event and a rejection in the same tail, the panel/orphan/foreign/codex controls, the archive, the notice, idempotency, the in-process /api/usage payload), test-restore-smoke (the fixture seeded into a worktree server's own data/ — the first /api/usage of that boot reads 0.43), test-readings-attribution 512, test-auto-resume 227, test-auto-resume-loop 218, test-pool-auto 117, test-account-verdicts 45, test-record-shape 50, test-vendor-whitelist 63, npm run build. **r2 (the adversarial verify, five findings reproduced before the fix):** a weekly window is the same lane by PHASE — a rolled week no longer writes a placeholder beside the stale cap that parked every family until the next panel; the scoped dead mark carries a deadline (the plan lanes' own ladder: stated > stored > the record's weekly > a bounded 24 h); the stream stamps `scopedFetchedAt` with the reading's clock so its cap readings become estimator pairs; the placeholder wall is spelled one way for the signal that records it and the fresh-window edge that opens it (the witness ring refuses that key); a refused repair FAILS the migration and retries next boot instead of being recorded as applied; the fixtures pin the production 60 s panel-vs-API delta; a non-representative window keeps its stored status when its number did not move. Gates: test-quota-model 332 (the roll rungs + fold + parity with reading-lag), test-rate-limit-capture 86 (the dead-mark ladder, the 60 s sidecar, the status-keep rule, ⑨b the estimator pairs), test-migrations 66 (the refused run + the retry), test-fable-cap-pool-storm 293 (§16 the rolled week; the absolute-compare control reproduces the parking), test-pool-auto 119, test-auto-resume 230, test-restore-smoke.

## 2.369.137 — the Windows freeze probe (the month's telemetry says GPU/OS side, not our JS), a WebGL A/B lever, and short workflow names

- **Windows freezes (owner: "越用越卡, 切桌面/跨显示器拖窗口整机卡顿, 想办法解决或者埋点识别"):** this month's telemetry from that client (ANGLE / D3D11 on an RTX 5090) holds 54 `renderer-freeze` events (timer AND rAF stopped, 3–52 s) of which only 7 sit beside a `client-longtask` — the other 47 are GPU / OS side, invisible to the main thread — plus 40 `compositor-stall` (rAF dead, timers alive) — at every page age from 0 to 94 min, so not a leak that needs hours. New instrumentation so the next freeze explains itself: `installScreenWatch` records every DPR change and screen move (the two named triggers) and visibility flips; desktop switches enter the action ring; the incident snapshot carries a FREEZE INVENTORY (canvases + megapixels, live WebGL contexts, DOM nodes, terminals / chat views / rendered messages, windows, desktops, screen geometry + DPR, JS heap, device memory, visibility, the last long tasks, the screen-event ring); every renderer freeze or compositor stall ≥ 5 s CAPTURES ITSELF (one per 10 min, the button's exact bundle, a toast names the incident id). test-gear-menu +4.
- **`terminal.webgl` (Settings → Terminal, default on):** off ⇒ new terminals start on the DOM renderer — the A/B lever for "are the terminals' WebGL contexts what the GPU chokes on"; the inventory prints the live context count.
- **test-desktop-app-keeper on a box with Xvnc:** tigervnc-standalone-server landed here for the vnc-fit work and the keeper took the `x-serves-rfb` recipe, so nine legs that pin the Xvfb+x11vnc recipe went red on the .136 heavy tier; every keeper the suite builds now hands the keeper display FACTS with Xvnc/Xtigervnc hidden (`NO_XVNC`), and the one leg that wants the Xvnc rung asks for the real facts — the leg tests the recipe, not this box's inventory (the .131 lesson).
- **Workflow names (owner: "这个任务名称是不是太长了"):** the chip and the Background-tasks list show a SHORT label from PURE `src/workflow-name.js` (an id-like head before ':' / ' — ' when it has no spaces, else the first clause ≤ 60 chars, else a word-boundary cut with an ellipsis); the whole Summary line rides as `summary` in the chip's tooltip. test-task-lifecycle +1.

## 2.369.136 — the desktop's Paste button gets a way out (userW inc-mubu8xdg-pvwa), a workflow chip shows the run's name, the sidebar's session search hides on the tabs it does not filter, the Channels panel folds its Agents section until something is tracked

- **"desktop 的 paste 用不了" (userW, 2.369.116):** the bundle shows the Paste button pressed three times into a view whose RFB had already closed (code 1006) and keystrokes landing on the button — a silent no-op twice over. `src/lib/vnc-view.js` now: a disconnected view answers "The desktop is not connected — reconnect first"; a clipboard the browser refuses (permission), an empty one, or a page with no async Clipboard API (plain http by hostname) opens a PASTE BOX under the bar — a textarea where Ctrl+V lands through the `paste` event, Send / Cancel, Ctrl+Enter, Esc — and every successful send hands the focus back to the desktop; the unclassified failure keeps the retired window's exact toast AND opens the box. test-vnc-view §5 (60). The launched Chromium on that pod exited with code 0 at once (a hand-off to a running instance or a sandbox refusal — its window said "disconnected" instead of the exit) — recorded for the desktop-apps lane, not fixed here.
- **"这个workflow没有展示正确的名称":** a run launched through `scriptPath` has no `input.name` and the ack is "Workflow launched in background… Summary: <meta.description>" — `parseBackgroundLaunch` now takes the Summary line, then an inline script's `meta.name`, then the script file's basename; the two chat-view launch sites use the same fallbacks; the live `/api/workflow` placeholder "Workflow" never overwrites a name the ack carried; a task_progress `summary` is kept on `taskInfo.summary`. test-task-lifecycle +3 (a verbatim scriptPath ack).

- **"展示一堆agents意义不明":** the Channels panel's built-in Agents section (every live session, the same list as the sidebar) is folded by default until one of its conversations is tracked, with a caption saying what tracking means; an explicit open/close survives repaints (`EXPANDED` beside `COLLAPSED`). The larger question — what the panel's first screen should be (attention across tracked external channels + the outbox, not a session roster) — is B-afa0.

## 2.369.135 — a self-hosted instance can take cluster-style defaults from ~/.config/vibespace/env (the service unit reads it when present)

- `scripts/install-service.sh` writes `EnvironmentFile=-%h/.config/vibespace/env` into the user unit: the same variables the fleet chart injects from its Secret (`VIBESPACE_INTEGRATIONS`, `VIBESPACE_GDRIVE_CLIENTS`, `VIBESPACE_PUBLIC_URL`, …) can be given on one machine without editing the unit; a missing file is ignored; secrets stay in a mode-600 file, never in the unit. First use (owner 2026-09-21): the Lark self-built app as a keyed cluster-style preset for ⚙ → Integrations on this box, in effect after the next Update.

## 2.369.134 — the agent browser, whole (docs/design-agent-browser-v2, B-4609): P0–P4b rebased onto master, then P5 (action trace + live view Actions pane + Browser profiles panel), P6 (hard mediation: the CDP proxy, per-session urls, target scoping, input refused during a takeover), P7 (window binding: two panes on one tab chain), P9 (native windows as targets through the accessibility tree, window leases, the three modes on a window), P10 (tier 3: windows on the user's REAL desktop behind their own consent switch), one adversarial verify (11 findings) and one fix round — squash of feat-browser-v2-whole; `Browser` sits under the Settings tree's Services group

Each chunk below was ONE commit on the lane branch; the sections keep the lane's own words.

- **Merge-time (found by the merged-tree heavy run, not by the lane's own gates): every browser route answered "no such live session".** server.js's mounts-plugins wiring call carried three chunk notes MID-LINE; a chunk had appended `getTelemetry: …` after them (never wired — the wiring's `= null` default hid it) and the r-fix moved `activeSessions,` after them too, so both keys were comment text. test-plugin-loader's `/, activeSessions,$/m` pin was satisfied by the comment; test-window-binding and test-browser-live ③ failed deterministically (also on the lane's own head, cb4edd17 — a control worktree). Now the notes sit on their own line above the code and the two keys are code; test-architecture §48 is the census (no object key after a mid-line `//` in server.js / src/server/*-wiring.js, with the shipped shape as its negative control). Lesson: a pin anchored at `$` proves nothing about a line whose `//` comes first.
- **Settings tree:** `Browser` sits under Services (a category in no group would have landed under a lone "Other" head).

### agent browser: the verifier's round on the whole branch (seven reproduced findings fixed and pinned, the low ones taken, master's 2.369.131 merged in)

- **Sub-agents on rung D** get a generated config of their OWN (`data/browser-env/<key>.<n>.json` = the parent's minus `profile`, fence kept, read back before its path is answered; swept with the parent) — a pinned parent no longer hands its user-data-dir to a second namespace (the SingletonLock shape); without one a profile-naming parent config is unset (`childEnvFor` says `why`). test-browser-handles 120.
- **Desktop-app live pane:** the viewer id is a per-socket secret (128 bits, re-minted per connect; a second socket claiming a live id is refused 409 `viewer id held`), the lease broadcasts an OPAQUE takeover tag and only the taker's own answer carries it — another client can no longer drive or hand back during somebody's takeover. `vnc-view` takes a url FUNCTION. test-window-target 71.
- **`vibespace-window open`** takes registry ids only: `exec`/`args`/`cwd` are refused 403 `exec_is_human` at the engine (the remedy names `list`, which now prints the registry ids); the CLI drops `--exec/--args/--cwd`. test-window-targets 80.
- **Mediation wording:** the sentence, the CLI's `watch` and the manual say what the fence does — input and page-navigation COMMANDS refused while the user drives, script evaluation and reads not (do not navigate by script). test-browser-mediation 130.
- **`new --adopt <dir>`** registers only a directory strictly under `~/.agent-browser/` or `data/browser-profiles/` (`adopt_outside_roots`), never the legacy `default-profile` (`adopt_legacy_refused`) nor somebody else's record (`adopt_registered`).
- **Action trace:** a single-character `press`/`keydown`/`keyup` is «1 key», a `select`'s value/label a length. test-browser-housekeeping 178.
- **Heavy suites on this box:** test-browser-live's real-chromium leg SKIPs with the launch error as evidence; test-browser-tier3-chrome's a11y wait is one 60 s wall and a hung bus SKIPs.
- **Fast tier green again:** browser-live-window imports utils' `COUNTER_ZOOM`; `Browser` sits after `Spending` in SETTINGS_CATEGORIES; the frame census lists `agent-browser`/`app-id`/`per-session`/`vs-key` as prose; server.js keeps `activeSessions,` and `pluginLoader,` at line ends; test-window-target's heavy row names its category; the `spawnOriginHint` line is verbatim again with the browser-profile hint as its own statement.
- **CLAUDE.md size law:** every index line the branch added is a ≤300-char head ending in its ⇒ pointer; the agent-browser routing row's full text lives in kb-design-lessons §18.
- Merged master 2.369.131 (a present-but-unwired xpra rung is passed over) — test-desktop-apps / test-desktop-display / the heavy test-window-target pass on a box with xpra installed.

### agent browser P10: tier 3 — windows on the user's REAL desktop as window targets, behind their own switch (design §7.6 / §7.1's `local-window` row / §4.9 columns 1-2 / §6.6, D27 (b) / D31): measured first (§12.36 / §12.39 / the two capture columns on the user's own session), then the PURE class model, the wired provider row with its named refusals, the engine's second class (consent first, nothing ever injected, the user's pause and the switch always win), the user's pause surface, and the two suites

- **Measured before designed** (src/window-desktop.js `TIER3_MEASUREMENTS`; `scripts/measure-tier3.mjs --sites --no-sandbox | --capture --systemd | --latency --real` reproduces it): §12.36 — the installed agent-browser 0.32.0 on a STOCK headless launch (scratch HOME, the user's AutomationControlled flag not read) reads bot.sannysoft.com 3 passed / 1 failed, nowsecure.nl no Cloudflare challenge, browserscan.net/bot-detection "Robot"; tier 2 = `binary_absent`, tier 3 = `needs_user`, banks = `owner_act` — each a refusal BY NAME. §4.9 columns 1/2 on the user's own GNOME Wayland session: `_NET_CLIENT_LIST` on :1 empty (X11 sees only X11 clients), the Xwayland ROOT grabs all black, an Xwayland client's OWN window is readable through `x11grab -window_id` (151200/151200 bytes), a native Wayland client has NO X window while fully on the a11y bus, the ScreenCast portal answers CreateSession / SelectSources(window) from this shell AND from a `systemd-run --user` unit and `Start` is the user's click, GNOME Introspect / ScreenshotWindow AccessDenied. §12.39 — one `do_action` → a visible PIXEL change: median 1.7 ms on our Xvfb, **3.3 ms on the user's Xwayland** (p95 one 60 Hz frame). The record carries `WIRED` claims and `measurementVerdict` goes red for a rung wired without its ok cell.
- **src/window-desktop.js (PURE, new)**: `window.realDesktopTargets` as the D27 (b) switch (`consentVerdict` admits exactly `true`), the rows = the accessibility bus minus ours marked `origin:'desktop'` + `yourDesktop`, the class's law (`key` / `click --at` refused BY NAME — `desktop_injection_refused` — whatever backend the display has; `watch` `no_live_view`; the tree verbs unchanged), `captureVerdict` (x11grab of an Xwayland client's own pixmap / `capture_needs_portal` for a native Wayland window / `capture_unavailable`), the closed refusal set, `hintAction` (a tier-only hint is a suggestion whose act is `open-window-target`; never `auto`, never a switch).
- **src/browser-profiles.js**: the `local-window` row is WIRED behind `provider_needs_consent`; every row gains `cdp` / `allowedDomains` / `pinTab` / `consent` cells; `capabilityRefusal` gains `cdp` / `allowed-domains` / `pin-tab` / `live-view` (each says what the class has instead) and the local-window `switch` refusal names the act; a tier-3 PROFILE is refused `tier3_is_a_window_target` (§7.6 rule 3: no record, no re-pointing — a window target instead); the keeper's control wrapper feeds the setting on every read and exports `desktopConsent`; **src/routes/browser.js** maps `provider_needs_consent` (403) / `tier3_is_a_window_target` (409) — the boot smoke found both answering 500 — and both providers routes read the switch. **src/browser-switch.js**: the tier-3 blocked sentence says "your act … nothing escalates by itself", never "detected".
- **src/server/window-targets-engine.js + src/routes/window-targets.js**: the second class on the same lease map (persisted with its origin); consent is asked BEFORE existence; `dw-<pid>` resolves through the pids the last `list` saw (alive), a persisted lease trusts its own pid across a restart; `desktopActGate` runs before any backend is probed; `screenshot` = `xdotool search --pid` on the server's own display env + `ffmpeg -f x11grab -window_id`, else refused by name; `watch` = `no_live_view`; `enforceConsent` at every verb, at the tick and at boot drops every desktop lease the instant the switch reads false (audited `by:'consent'`). Routes: the STATUS map covers the class; **the user's side** `GET /api/window/desktop`, `POST /api/window/desktop/:handle/pause|resume` (cookie-authed; the same takeover verdicts as a tab — the agent answers `window_paused`). **src/window-targets.js**: `probeScreenCastPortal` (two property Gets, memoised; raises nothing).
- **Settings + UI**: `window.realDesktopTargets` (Settings → Browser, default OFF, `confirmOn` — the dialog IS the consent; zh+ja); the Desktop apps dialog's "Agents on your real desktop" section (the switch's state, per held window a Pause agent / Resume agent). **data/bin/vibespace-window + docs/agent/window-manual.md**: `list` marks the rows YOUR DESKTOP and prints the switch line + the class's verb law; the refusals are spelled (it is THEIR switch — ask, do not work around it); the manual's "Your real desktop (tier 3)" section; the tools intro's one line.
- **Gate**: test-browser-tier3 (fast, 111 — the PURE model with the record's negative controls, the tier derived from the row + no `tier` on a record, every refusal the local-window row produces with chromium as the control, the site-hint both-at-once control, the engine over a fake keeper + fake helper + routes + the shipped CLI: consent first, the bus minus ours, injection refused BEFORE any helper call with xdotool present, the user's pause, every audit line `origin:desktop`, the lease across a rebuild, the switch off dropping it at the next verb and at boot) + test-browser-tier3-chrome (heavy, 13 — a REAL Google Chrome on an Xvfb with NO `--remote-debugging-*` / `--enable-automation` / `--headless` / disguise flag: listed as a desktop-class row, 235 nodes from the real AT-SPI tree, `click @ref` = do_action on a button through no injection, chord and point refused although xdotool is on PATH, x11grab of its own window, the argv clean before and after — the definition of tier 3 as an assertion; Chrome rewrites its argv area as one space-joined string, so the reader tokenizes both ways).
- Not in this chunk: the ScreenCast/PipeWire live pane for a native Wayland window (P8's transport), injection on the class (D29's portal), any bank reading (the owner's act — D31 "measure first" stands as owed).

### agent browser P9 (second half): window leases + the three modes on a window — the lease persists across a restart (one holder per window, an orphaned lease is free at the next attach), the `window-live` form of the Desktop-app window over the P8-1 vnc-display bridge (Watch / Take over / Hand back shared with tabs — the same lease.input, the same PURE verdicts, the same idle window, the ONE handback announcer), §6.6's two-class marker + audit lines, and a takeover that STOPS INJECTION: every agent verb is `window_paused`, the bridge cuts the viewer's input out of the relay in Watch (design §4.3 / §4.9 / §6.6, D27 (a))

- **src/server/window-targets-engine.js**: `data/window-leases.json` (atomic) — the lease survives a restart like the browser registry's (the keeper adopts the window, the agent's next verb just works; the input side is in memory: a restart is a handback by construction); `attach` takes an ORPHANED lease (holder session gone; `orphanedFrom` audited), `reconcile` drops a gone window at once and a holder-less lease after a 60 s grace at the 15 s tick (at once at `boot()`, after restoreSessions); `takeover` / `handback` / `noteUserInput` / the idle sweep are browser-takeover's own verdicts under `browser.takeoverIdleMs`; `window_paused` for EVERY verb while the user drives (snapshot, click, type, key, --at, screenshot — §6.6: a takeover stops injection of every kind); `inputPolicy(handle, viewerId)` (no lease ⇒ relay, agent ⇒ `watch-mode`, user ⇒ the holder only / `held`), `viewerLeft` ⇒ `viewer-left` handback; `onInput` events with `target:'window'`; `window-leases-updated` broadcast; every audit line `origin:'vibespace'`, takeover/handback lines `by:'user'` with the viewer and the cause.
- **src/server/desktop-stream.js**: `?viewer=<id>` on the upgrade, `create({inputPolicy, onViewerLeft})`, `rfbInputSieve().strip(chunk, allowInput)` on the SAME parser as `feed` — a refused KeyEvent / PointerEvent / ClientCutText / QEMU key is cut OUT of the chunk and the FramebufferUpdateRequest beside it still relays (the picture never freezes on a refused click); complete messages only; an opaque stream is all-or-nothing (the direction that never injects behind a refusal); dropped input never feeds the idle clock; `viewersOf` / `viewerAlive`; the close line names the viewer + the drops.

### agent browser P9 (first half): window targets — a native window as a target through its accessibility tree: the four measurements first (the portal from a background unit, Electron/Chromium coverage, do_action latency, the node-side binding), then SHARED src/window-targets.js with the traversal in a BOUNDED subprocess, the engine's per-verb law, `vibespace-window` + its manual (design §4.9 / §5.1.1 / §6.6, D27 (a) / D28 / D29)

- **Measured before designed** (numbers in kb-file-structure.md under src/window-targets.js; `scripts/measure-window-targets.mjs` reproduces them): the RemoteDesktop portal answers CreateSession / SelectDevices from a `systemd --user` transient unit (the server's own context) and Start raises the consent dialog — the "refused in background contexts" report does not hold here, the user's click is what stands between a service and injection (D29 (a) viable, (c) shipped); Electron exports an `Action` on every node (357/357; buttons 43/43) but only when launched with `--force-renderer-accessibility`, gnome-shell's 74 buttons export none, Qt is not installed here (recorded as unmeasured); `do_action` → tree-visible change median 0.34 ms / p95 0.81 ms on GTK; no maintained node AT-SPI binding exists and a cold walk costs the same order with or without libatspi's cache (0.34–0.51 ms/node raw D-Bus; 2,400–5,400 nodes/s through GI), so the helper is python3 + GObject introspection in a bounded subprocess — the fork tax (62–70 ms) is paid once per traversal, never per node.
- **src/window-targets.js (SHARED)**: `snapshotTarget` → the tree with `@eN` refs + the interface CENSUS every snapshot reports; `runHelper` = the bounded subprocess (wall SIGKILL, `helper_timeout` with the child dead, `python3_missing` naming the packages, a closed `REFUSALS` set); `parseChord` (a closed vocabulary — the string reaches an argv), `pickAction` (Chromium's per-node `showContextMenu` / `clickAncestor` never unnamed), `probeInputBackends` (the runtime ladder xtest / portal / uinput — never a platform name; a display that is not ours gets no injection), `verbVerdicts` (§5.1.1 per verb), `injectKey` / `injectClick` (XTEST on our display), `screenshotDisplay` (the fallback). src/window-targets-helper.py = the only AT-SPI speaker (libatspi per-call timeout + node budget; unreadable subtrees instead of stalls; explicit interface-class calls because PyGObject resolves `acc.get_text` to the deprecated iface getter).
- **src/server/window-targets-engine.js + src/routes/window-targets.js**: the addressable set IS the desktop-app keeper's live records (D27 (a)); one holder per window (`window_leased` names it; in memory this half — re-attach after a restart); refs replaced per snapshot; **a node without `Action` is refused `node_has_no_action` BEFORE any helper call and still with an injection backend present** — never a coordinate click in disguise; `type` through EditableText (the focused node by default); `key` / `click --at` refused `no_injection_backend` WITH the probe rows; the audit line records the node's role + name + action or the point's coordinates, never typed text; `watch` names the Desktop-app window honestly. ### agent browser P7: window binding — one group, two panes side by side: `layout`/`split`/`ratio` on the tab chain, the title-bar half drop zone, the born-in-a-chain `createWindow`, the divider, the ownership badge, layouts persistence + the sync-key fix, mobile tabs-only without write-back (design §4.6 / §3.7, D19 / D24, the §10 P7 row)

- **The model** (src/lib/chain-layout.js, PURE): a chain gains `layout: 'tabs' | 'split'` (a missing field reads as tabs — old records need no migration) and `split: {pair, ratio, dir}`; `tabs` and `active` keep their meanings to the byte. `normalizeChain` is the ONE validation of the pair against `tabs` — a member that left the chain collapses the layout to tabs and drops the split (never a dangling id, never a substitute); the ratio clamps to 0.15–0.85; `chainSyncKey` = tabs + layout + pair order (the ratio applies in place); `displayedPanes` answers wide vs NARROW; `splitReplaceable` is D19 (a).
- **The rendering** (src/lib/tab-group.js): a split is another rendering of the same chain — the host's element becomes a grid (title bar across, pane / divider / pane below) and the pair's contents both show; no re-parenting, the window's external geometry is untouched so move / minimise / maximise / desktop switch keep working on the host. `_normalizeChain` runs at every chain mutation; closing the browser pane, closing the chat (host promotion) and dragging either pane out all collapse to tabs and move nothing else. The divider: a per-drag AbortController, rAF-coalesced, ONE kind of pixel (the host rect + clientX — it lands under the pointer at any UI scale), double-click = 0.5. `bindSplit` / `unbindSplit`; the one new drop zone = the left / right half of another window's title bar (both the title-bar drag and the tab drag); a third tab replaces the non-anchor pane (D19 (a)).
- **The window manager** (src/lib/window.js): `createWindow({intoChain: {hostId, split, side}})` = born in the chain, never painted standalone (no jump, no created-then-merged autosave churn); `setOwnerBadge` draws the per-SESSION ownership badge (the webui id's own counter through the task-colour sequence — never the task-group colour) on the title bar and on the tab; syncHiddenViews derives the narrow-split hider so a pane the phone hides is a suspended view.
- **Persistence + sync** (src/lib/layout.js): layout + split ride layouts.json through the one writeLayouts choke point; the remote-vs-local chain key carries the layout (the pre-fix `tabs.join(',')` read a remote tabs→split flip of the same tabs as "unchanged" — a silent fork); a remote ratio on a structural match is applied in place with no notify; the four §6b anti-ping-pong guards are untouched and pinned.
- **Mobile = tabs only**: ≤768px the stylesheet shows the focused pane and hides the divider; the model keeps the split, so a phone's save carries it verbatim and never flattens the desktop's layout.
- **The live view's side** (src/lib/browser-live-window.js): ONE `toggleBind()` behind three surfaces — the bar's "Snap beside <session>" / "Unbind" button, a title-bar button on the standalone window, and the window menu's `window/browser-bind` row (the title bar's own menu — the tab and the phone's long-press reach it); bind finds the session's own window on this client and calls `wm.bindSplit`, unbind = `wm.unbindSplit`. The OWNERSHIP badge (`wm.setOwnerBadge`) and the switcher strip's per-pane owner dots (§3.7) come from the digest's `leases`, the viewer first, N dots when a profile is shared with the names one per line — never fetched here.
- **Auto-bind** (`browser.autoBindLiveView`, Settings → Browser, default ON): the picker's `_onBrowserProfilesUpdated` hands the previous digest to `onBrowserDigestChanged`; a NEW (profile, session) lease whose session window is open on the desktop you are looking at gets its live view BORN inside that window's chain as a split (`createWindow({intoChain})`), under the deterministic syncId `win-blive-<sessionId>` so two clients open ONE window; the first digest is a snapshot, not an event; never on a phone; an ephemeral browser has no lease and is never auto-opened.
- **Gates**: test-window-binding-model (fast, 65 — the PURE model with the pre-fix dangling-pair shape and the pre-fix sync key as negative controls, two sessions in one task group distinguishable / a session in no group badged at all, the wiring pins incl. §6b's guards); **test-window-binding (heavy chrome, 61 — the §10 P7 row's exit: a desktop page + a 390×844 phone page on a worktree server with a fake claude, a fake agent-browser and a fake stream upstream — auto-bind births the live view inside the chat's chain (one visible window, two measured panes, the deterministic syncId, frames drawn, the ownership badge in the session's own colour), Unbind / Snap beside, the divider under body zoom 1.25 landing within 4 px of the pointer + double-click, a real title-bar drag / minimise / restore / a desktop switch keeping the panes together, closing the browser pane collapsing to tabs with the chat's rect unchanged, D19 (a) on a third tab, closing the CHAT host promoting with no dangling id, layouts.json carrying layout + split, the phone restoring the split in its model while displaying one pane and its own save leaving the split on disk and on the desktop, a remote same-tabs layout flip applied where the pre-fix key would not, a ratio-only change applied in place, a shared profile's two owner dots, a second profile's strip with per-pane dots; the suite kills the fake sessions it created)**; test-contributions (the window-menu parity: the bind row's `when` is false for a window without a type); test-hidden-view-suspend's switchTab pin kept; test-browser-live (the live window's own chrome suite).

### agent browser P6: hard mediation — the CDP-mediating proxy, per-session CDP urls, target scoping, input refusal during a takeover, and `sharing: "instance"` accepted where it exists (design §6.2 / §6.5 / D6, the §10 P6 row)

- **The proxy** (src/server/cdp-mediator.js, ORCH): one lazy loopback server hands every (profile, conversation) lease its OWN `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/m/<token>/devtools/browser` (+ `/json/version` and `/json/list` twins, and page endpoints in scope only). The raw endpoint never leaves the server: the upstream socket is opened there, the client is upgraded only after it is open, nothing is logged with a token or a raw url in it. A grant is minted once per lease for the process's life; `repoint` follows the profile's browser (a restart closes live connections 1012 `browser_restarting` and the SAME url reconnects; a stop answers 503); `revoke` closes 1008 `lease_gone` AND closes the lease's own tabs in the browser (measured: `Browser.close` is refused through a session url, so a mediated `close --all` would leave its tabs behind). An unknown token is 404 on every path.
- **The rules** (src/browser-mediation.js, PURE): `Target.attachToTarget` / `activateTarget` / `closeTarget` / `getTargetInfo` on a tab outside the lease's scope are `target_out_of_scope`; a message on a CDP session the proxy never handed out is `session_out_of_scope`; `Browser.close` / `crash*` / `Target.exposeDevToolsProtocol` / `setRemoteLocations` / `sendMessageToTarget` are `method_refused` always; while the user holds the input side (P3) every `Input.*`, the navigation family, a file upload and the target acts that change what the user sees are `browser_paused` — a CDP error by id on the same session, the typed code as its prefix; `Runtime.evaluate` / `captureScreenshot` are NOT refused while paused (a read is the honest use; the CLI's typed refusal already stops the cooperative path — stated, never sold as a DOM fence). The scope grows from what the browser hands back (a tab the lease created, a tab a scoped page opened, a child auto-attached under an owned session, a target born in an owned context) and shrinks on destroy / detach / dispose; `getTargets` and `getBrowserContexts` are filtered. **Measured on agent-browser 0.32.0 + Chrome 153: Chrome announces `Target.targetCreated` BEFORE it answers `Target.createTarget`**, so the withheld announcement is remembered and REPLAYED before the reply — without it the daemon's target registry never learns its own tab and `open` hangs forever. Also measured: agent-browser connects a `ws://` url directly but DROPS the path of an http one when it rebuilds `/json/version`, so the lease is handed the ws form.
- **`sharing: "instance"`** (src/browser-profiles.js `sharingVerdict`): refused with D6's sentence until a mediating proxy exists in the process, refused BY NAME on a paired-machine profile (the proxy serves this machine), a value otherwise; the legacy "Shared (legacy)" record keeps `instance` for admission but is never mediated (cooperative, labelled legacy). A mediated attachment's env: its session, a PER-SESSION namespace (its own daemon over its own url), the scoped url, an explicit idle, and no profile directory.
- **The wiring** (src/server/browser-keeper.js + mounts-plugins-wiring + routes + the CLI + the panel): the proxy is built beside the keeper and injected (lazy; its shutdown is the keeper's); a mediated attach answers `mediated:true`, the scoped url as the wrapper's `cdpUrl`, the per-session env and a one-line `note` the CLI prints; `start`/`stop` re-point the grants, `detach` and a dropped lease revoke them (the lease's own tabs closed in the browser), a backend switch admits each re-opened tab, the live view and `--confirm-actions` answers go to the session's OWN daemon for a mediated lease; `sharing` is created (`new --sharing instance`, `POST /api/browser/profiles`) and edited (`PATCH`) through the verdict — refused `leased` while sessions hold leases, `pinned` while a conversation pins it, never on the legacy record; **a mediated profile is attached, never pinned** — a pin hands the next launch the profile's DIRECTORY (P0's spawn env) and would launch a second Chromium on the keeper's user-data-dir, so `setPin` refuses `pin_refused`, a Task-Group / instance default naming one is skipped at spawn with its reason in the journal, and the picker does not offer it; the digest carries `mediation:{available, port, grants}` (counts only) and every profile/lease view `mediated`; the panel shows a `shared` chip, the picker `(shared)`; the raw endpoint reaches no answer, view or broadcast. Boot smoke on a worktree server: 200 create / 400 `sharing_refused` with `why` / PATCH both ways / the housekeeping row / zero journal errors / the proxy listening on nothing until the first mediated lease.
- **Gates**: test-browser-mediation (fast, 127 — ④ the real keeper with the proxy injected over the fake agent-browser: instance sharing created here and refused by a proxy-less keeper (the control) and on a paired-machine profile, a mediated attach's env, the raw url in no answer/view/broadcast, scope across two conversations, the keeper's takeover flipping one url to browser_paused, sharing edits, detach ⇒ 1008 + the tab closed, stop ⇒ 1012, a dropped lease ⇒ grant gone, shutdown ends the proxy; ①–③: the verdict matrix, the rules over literal messages incl. the replayed ordering, the real proxy over a fake CDP upstream — two grants on one browser, the second cannot see / attach / activate / close the first's tab, the /json twins re-pointed and filtered, 404 / 403 by name, the paused reader read live, revoke closes the tabs, repoint 1012 / 503) and test-browser-mediation-chrome (heavy: the real chrome — the §6.2 exit). Docs: kb-file-structure (the two new essays + the P6 paragraph on browser-profiles), CLAUDE.md index lines.

### agent browser P5 (client half): the action trace on the tool card, the before/after dialog, the live view's Actions pane, and the Browser profiles panel (design §4.5 / §6.4 / §8 step 3 / D7 / D8 / D35)

- **The tool card** (src/lib/chat-renderers.js `browserTraceHolderHtml` + src/lib/browser-trace-view.js `createCardTraceLoader`): a shell tool call whose command drives the agent browser (`agent-browser …` / `vibespace-browser …` — the PURE `commandDrivesBrowser` over `toolCommandText`, claude's string or codex's argv array, never a tool name) grows a "Browser actions" row on ALL THREE card shapes (pending / error / generic): the after-frame thumbnail of every action is always there (D7 (c)), the summary says `N action(s) · M failed` — or honestly why not (trace off / waiting on a running card / none recorded) — and the button expands the full list (time · command · result · position kind + line · before/after thumbs). ONE loader per ChatView, hooked from `_applyElementMarks` (the one hook every element-making path shares: create / swap / gap), holders batched 150 ms into ONE fetch over the union of their windows; PURE `assignEntriesToWindows` gives each entry to EXACTLY ONE card — the one with the latest ts that was RUNNING when the action happened (500 ms skew; an entry only later cards can hold goes to the earliest of them); a `browser-trace-appended` broadcast for this session or its key re-queues the cards whose window may hold it.
- **A stopped conversation is reviewable** (the point of D35): a view-only window asks `GET /api/browser/trace?conversation=<the CLI's id>` and the route resolves the key through the bindings store (P0 r5/r7's `data/browser-bindings.json`, read per ask — the wiring hands the routes a reader); `browserKey=` may also be given outright (validated); at least one of the three; **nothing to match by ⇒ an honest EMPTY answer** — the suite caught the route answering EVERY entry for an unbound conversation (a filter over nothing filtered nothing). Answers `keyFrom: session|conversation|given|null`.
- **The entry dialog** (`openTraceEntryDialog`): before / after side by side, the click point (a dot) or the element's box (a rectangle) DRAWN on the picture after the image lands — `overlayGeometry` in the drawn picture's px, right at any dialog width — the command, action + position line, result + duration, page, profile, ← / → through the list the click came from, and §6.4's retention sentence (frames of a logged-in page are secrets: 7 d or 200 MB per profile, then the sweep). Every frame through `img.src`, every wire string through textContent, the module never assigns innerHTML (pinned).
- **The live view's Actions pane** (part 2, src/lib/browser-live-window.js): a third side pane — `createTraceTimeline` — shows the trace of the pane you are looking at (the target's profile, or the ephemeral scope): every `hello` re-seeds it (a reconnect fills the gap, ids dedup), the stream's `trace` record grows it live, a pane switch clears it, a row opens the before/after dialog, the button counts `Actions (N)`. The recording indicator is now honest and actionable: it reads the digest only (`recording[profileId]` → "recording" + file + since; `recordingRefused[profileId]` → the reason; else "not recording" + the per-profile opt-in hint) and its click opens the Browser profiles panel.
- **The Browser profiles panel** (part 3 — §6.4 / §8 step 3 / D7 / D8; window type `browser-profiles`, singleton, ⚙ → Tools → Browser profiles… at order 35 gated on the profile digest, `app.openBrowserProfiles({focus})`, also the live view's recording indicator): one row per profile — label + legacy/host chips + the backend chip, the STATE worded from the closed set (not ours / in use / running / recent / stale / kept) with its why, the size ("not measured" for a not-ours row), the trace digest, the recordings with a live mark or the refusal's reason, the per-profile screencast checkbox (= the keeper's `PATCH {record}`, D7; disabled with the reason for not-ours / remote), "Set aside" behind a confirm that says what moves where; the ephemeral row; the UNREGISTERED DIRECTORIES under `~/.agent-browser` with size and last use — "Adopt…" (a label, in place) / "Set aside"; the SET ASIDE ledger where "Delete permanently" (a danger-styled confirm) is THE one permanent deletion and a deleted row says when; the sweep line + "Sweep now". The hint repeats §6.4 and says when the action trace is OFF. Re-rendered from the three broadcasts (1.2 s debounce), the ws handler removed on close, every action through the in-app dialogs (never a native one — pinned). Census rows: test-window-types (type / action / owner / singleton), test-contributions (the fifth external gear-row owner).
- **PURE** (src/browser-trace.js): `HOUSEKEEPING_STATES` (the closed set the panel's phrase table is pinned to), `frameUrl`, `bytesText` ('—' for unmeasured), `toolCommandText`, `traceSummary`, `unionWindow`, `assignEntriesToWindows`, `positionText`.

## 2.369.133 — the phone's settings nav is sectioned, not a flattened row of heads and categories (owner 2026-09-21 "手机上这个配置层级渲染有点问题")

- **2.369.132 dissolved each nav group on phones with `display: contents`, so the group heads sat INLINE among the categories (⌄ 外观与布局 工具栏与布局 窗口 … ⌄ 会话与聊天 会话 聊天 终端 › HARNESS Claude …), still carried the desktop's chevron and fold handler (a tap turned the chevron and folded nothing, and the head stuck in its :hover tint on touch).** Now every group is a full-width row: the head on a line of its own as a plain label (no chevron, `pointer-events: none`), its categories wrapping beneath it; a fold saved on the device is ignored on the phone. Desktop folding is unchanged (test-gear-menu's settings legs). test-mobile-gaps pins the geometry (every head spans the strip, no category shares its row, chevron hidden, no pointer), the ignored-fold negative control, and writes `settings-nav-phone.png` to its shots dir for the human look.

## 2.369.132 — the Settings window is a tree, and a harness section says which rows are global and which are per session (owner 2026-09-21)

- **"所有设置界面也可以做一下设置分级"**: the fourteen flat categories now hang under five group heads — Appearance & layout (Toolbar & Layout / Window / Sidebar / Session Card), Sessions & chat (Session / Chat / Terminal), Harnesses (Claude / Codex / OpenCode + any contributed table), Services (Integration / Channels / Background Work), Spending — with Plugins and Other as the trailing groups by rule. Desktop heads fold (persisted per device in `vibespace.settingsNavFolds`), the scroll-spy opens the group it lands in, a search shows every match regardless of folds, and the phone strip stays flat. `SETTINGS_CATEGORIES` remains the census of what renders (§44); `SETTINGS_GROUPS` only orders and folds it — test-architecture §44c pins that the ordered list is a permutation of the census and that every category has a group.
- **"harness 配置里可以区分一下 global 配置项和 session-level 配置项"**: each Claude / Codex / OpenCode section renders three sub-blocks from the rows' declared `apply.kind` — **Global — written into the CLI config file (~/.claude/settings.json, …)**: applies to every session of the harness on this machine, VibeSpace or not; **Per session — passed to the CLI when a session starts**: new sessions start with them, a resumed conversation keeps its own; **VibeSpace — server-side behaviour**: decided here, nothing written into the CLI. Gate: test-gear-menu's settings block (five groups, the Claude section's block order and row counts, folding + persistence, search).

## 2.369.130 — the Communication panel, designed: the audit, three rendered directions, the i18n census, and the build (a1–a4; owner 2026-09-17 "似乎没太做好 i18n，而且界面也比较缺乏设计" / "界面很乱，没有层次，你需要用前端技能+实际渲染截图好好设计优化一下")

- **a4 — the design, BUILT across all eight surfaces** (docs/kb-features.md "a4 UI design"): the panel is a LIST — bar + Outbox button (glyph · label · accent count), one collapsible `folder-header` section per adapter with a 6 px state dot and EVERY verb in its ⋯ menu (the Sender line a checkable row), a status line only when there is something to say, rows on ONE grid (title + the ONE freshness pill / participants + right-aligned needs-you badges / assignment), badges collapsing to one pill under 180 px; ONE COLOUR PER MEANING (accent needs-you, green live, neutral age, amber warning + `unknown`, red failed) with text tokens that clear AA in both themes; every glyph an SVG (14 new icons; `chan-btn` retired for the house `mounts-btn`); the connect wizard a STEPPER (Credential ✓ → Consent → Track) with the consent page as the one primary + Copy link, the port-busy refusal a named amber line, paste-back a collapsed step; the window bar three tiers (title + ⋯, meta, an assignment chip), day separators and same-author grouping, a 12 px composer with a short placeholder; the card FIVE lines with right-aligned reject · edit · approve; the Outbox window a toolbar with Awaiting | All (grouped by state, a dot per head); the editors on the house form rhythm (two-column grids, rule rows with kind selectors, the estimate as ONE stat + its honesty hint, a bordered reach list named from the roster); Integrations: an undecryptable row as a state chip + one sentence, a one-line verdict, the copy glyph, help as an info affordance; the phone: 36 px targets, one-column grids, no sideways overflow at 375. No behaviour change (freshness honesty, the read-mark rule, frame neutering, escHtml/textContent).
- **Screenshot rounds (a4, scripts/dbg-comm-surfaces.mjs)**: round 1 (zh desktop dark, 66 shots) — the fake fixtures' sections said "not connected" about a control they do not have, the unassigned chip was a sentence, the 172 px bar could not hold the summary and the Outbox word (the a2 mockup assumed 203 px), the reach dialog named a group by id, the Integrations verdict took four lines and the undecryptable row contradicted its own chip; round 2 (zh desktop + mobile dark, en light, 124 shots) — the phone rule row's × on a third line, the phone reach row stacked, the callback URL breaking mid-path at 375, the 200 px rail's pill spilling past the row, no tooltip on a truncated title, an unset secret in monospace; round 3 (the full set at zh/ja/en) — the badge pair was ALREADY collapsed at the default rail because the rows are inline-size containers themselves and the unnamed `@container` query resolved against the 166 px row (fixed with a NAMED `chan-panel` container, pinned at both widths in test-channels-e2e ⑫), ja's 87 px `ポーリングしていません` pill pushed the title to 70 px (the pill now yields only after the title's 60 px floor, then ellipsizes), and the day separator said "Sep 22" between zh messages (the browser's locale, not the device's — `resolveLang()` now picks the tag; the census caught it). The identity warning repeated on every decided card (five amber walls in the Outbox) now appears only while a card still has an Approve, so the Outbox holds ONE. Still owed by design: en pills are wider than zh, so "Announcements" truncates at the 172 px default rail (tooltip); a fresh instance's Outbox button is glyph-only there.
