## 2.369.129 — inc-mub8xwrb-z57x: the ⚙ menu's two "System" entries, paging through a fold-dominated session that jumped to the top of the previous slab and froze Chrome, and the .128 roster regression that crushed every account name to one letter

- **"设置菜单里有俩系统"**: 2.369.125 registered the System… and Ports… rows at the top level one release after 2.369.124 made System a head. Both rows now live INSIDE the System head (after a separator), and the monitor row is named for what it opens: **System monitor…** (系统监控… / システムモニター…). test-mobile-gaps follows the label.
- **"往上翻突然跳到上面一页的最顶部，跳过了中间内容 … chrome卡死"** — the 2.368.29 residual ("a single fold run longer than 600 re-enters the slide regime, acceptable until seen in the field") was seen, on the owner's own window of this session (thousands of consecutive tool calls folded into one run). The trace ring showed it exactly: at the 600 bound every 50-record extend trimmed 50 from the bottom — the only content on screen — the height collapsed to one viewport, scrollTop clamped to 0, fifteen extend/trim cycles in 25 s. THREE fixes in `_extendTop`/the trims: ① the fold now runs BEFORE the trim decision (the 2.368.29 height gate saw the 50 fresh cards still unfolded and tall, so it never held for anyone); ② a window shorter than THREE viewports is never trimmed at all — `FOLD_DOM_CEILING` (3000 hidden cards) is the only bound; ③ one gesture GROWS BY HEIGHT: `_extendTop` keeps loading (doubling the slab, ≤ 8 passes) until the window is two viewports tall, so a wheel notch across a fold lands once on a full viewport instead of fifteen times. Gate: test-chat-paging §4b opens a 1500-pair fold-dominated transcript and asserts per notch — ≥ 2 viewports after the gesture, zero bottom trims while short, never a landing on the very top with history above, one grown landing — the leg reproduced the incident before the fix; test-chat-trim-guard pins the three mechanisms.
- **"你怎么把这界面改的我完全看不到账号名称了"** — .128's identity line gave the NAME the highest shrink weight, so beside a full email every name collapsed to one letter. The ident now ellipsizes FIRST (a huge shrink weight) and the name yields only once the ident is gone; test-roster-reset-eta puts a 70-char ident on a phone row and asserts the name keeps its full text, with a negative control that restores the .128 weights and watches the name vanish.

## 2.369.128 — the last standing mirror red since 2.369.75: the ephemeral-install warning quoted an unbreakable install path

- The Agents modal's "⚠ Installed in a system location (<path>) …" row (shown when the local claude is not a user-local install — every Actions runner, any npm-global container) quotes the install PATH as one unbreakable token; on a 375 px phone the row's min-content (357 px, an 80+ char `/opt/hostedtoolcache/…/cli.js`) pushed the roster section sideways by 20 px. Named by the roster suite's rightmost-element diagnostic on the mirror (r2), reproduced here by injecting the product's own row shape. FIX = `.ob-cli-ephemeral .usage-warn { overflow-wrap: anywhere }` (a path may break anywhere) + the phone modal's backend status row wraps like the rail panel's, so the warning takes the full width instead of a 131 px column beside the buttons.
- **Gate**: test-roster-reset-eta's phone section injects the runner's row shape under both fonts and asserts no sideways overflow, with a NEGATIVE CONTROL (the wrap rule removed → the overflow returns) so the CSS is provably load-bearing.

## 2.369.127 — the CLI's "Stop hook error" notice is hidden by default: a Stop-hook BLOCK is not an error (owner 2026-09-21)

- **Owner: "这个 stop hook error 本质上是预期行为，每次都这样渲染好丑。加个选项可以隐藏".** The CLI's notification queue calls EVERY Stop-hook block an error: each time VibeSpace's bookkeeping nudge blocks a stop, the live stream carries `system/notification {key: stop-hook-error, text: "Stop hook error occurred · ctrl+o to see", priority: immediate}` (never the transcript). Since 2.369.120 that record painted the red Unknown-event fall-back card at every stop; 2.369.126 would have made it a red immediate notice PLUS a toast. The nudge itself is already visible as the "Stop hook feedback" card and the Stop-hook summary card, so the notice adds nothing.
- **The option — Settings → Chat, beside "Show hook cards in chat": `chat.showStopHookErrorNotice`, OFF by default.** Off hides the notice (body class `hide-stop-hook-notice`, live-applied to open chats; the fold/trim machinery treats the hidden card as glue like a hidden hook card); on shows it as the red immediate notice. The card also carries `chat-msg-hook`, so "Show hook cards" off hides it with the rest.
- **No toast for our own nudge:** the server consumer skips the level-2 toast for a stop-hook-error notice when the bookkeeping nudge stamped `_lastStopNudge` within the last two minutes; a stop-hook error with no nudge behind it (another hook failing) still toasts. Gates: test-stdout-registry (+2, the nudged vs stale control) · test-unknown-records (+1, the classes and the three wiring sites).
- Not changed: the nudge itself (`agents.stopNudgeStaleMinutes` / `agents.stopNudgeCooldownMinutes` — this instance runs the explicit-0 every-stop mode; each nudge is a billed mini-turn) — the owner's call, filed in the inbox.

## 2.369.126 — unknown harness records, whole: the schema oracle for KNOWN records (§3), the REPL's own notifications, codex MCP tool cards, every history-only red card routed, and the VCS / PR / background-task signals on the chrome (docs/design-unknown-records.md)

- **Why.** The 2.369.120 fall-back card made an unknown record TYPE visible; the 2026-09-20 census (2,138 telemetry breadcrumbs, 35 live buffers, 38 transcripts, 20 codex rollouts, the 2.1.274 binary's zod union) found that most red cards were the CLI's OWN user-facing notification queue, history rows every old transcript carries, and one codex item (McpToolCall) with no other carrier — and that three fields the product already depends on are not in the SDK schema at all. Owner ruling (b): a KNOWN type carrying undeclared parameters must be recorded and flagged too.
- **§3 the schema oracle + drift module** (`src/record-shape.js`, PURE): every known shape per harness AND carrier — claude stream rows generated verbatim from the installed binary's union, transcript camelCase twins inside the JSONL envelope, codex rollout payloads / events / items; both normalizers judge every record AFTER routing and draw ONE "New fields on a known record: system/init +{…}" card per shape per session (red border, dim head, a second occurrence MERGES by an edit op, the sample through a redactor that masks values under secret-looking keys judged by SEGMENT — api_key / apiKey / access_token / authorization / password…, never the notification's own `key` or `monkey`, folds under the 'unknown' kind — "N unknown events / new fields"), telemetry `harness-shape-drift` once per process per shape with the CLI build in the detail, and a "Harness drift" table in the Diagnostics report. Laws: a field is never deleted from known, only moved to ignored WITH a reason; the three live-seen fields (init.messaging_socket_path, task_started.owned_by_subagent, task_progress.workflow_progress) are declared with a note; user/assistant are judged by content-block type only; enum drift is informational (the handler runs); an unknown TYPE is the fall-back card only, never doubled. `scripts/test-record-shape.mjs` (fast tier): the fixture census, synthetic drift/merge/telemetry-once, enum drift with the handler running, THE BINARY ORACLE (reads the INSTALLED claude's union — every subtype/type on exactly one of HANDLED ∪ KNOWN_IGNORED ∪ DECLARED_UPSTREAM_UNSEEN with a one-line disposition each, every declared shape's fields ⊆ known ∪ ignored, no dead list entry; red the day the CLI updates, SKIP with reason without a binary) and the negative control.
- **`system/notification`** → a dim, priority-coloured notice card (keyed dedupe per turn; stop-hook-error points at the Stop-hook summary); `immediate`/`high` ALSO toast every client through the existing server-notice channel — ONE consumer in src/server/session-brain.js fed by the parse and the device stream.
- **codex `item_completed` McpToolCall** → the MCP tool card ("tool (server)", fold kind mcp, the result as output, failed = error) from the real redacted sample shape; the wrapper's `_stdin_ack` joins SKIPPED_RECORD_TYPES with its reason.
- **History-only rows** (every red card in old transcripts): `local_command` → the /command bubble; `away_summary` → the "Recap — while you were away" card (markdown through DOMPurify); `turn_duration` → the message-meta popup's "Turn: 3m18s · 66 messages [· budget n/limit]" row on the turn's last message; `api_error` → declared card-less (the transcript rows are NOT consumed for side effects — a days-old 401 must not evict today's pool member; the 401/403 consumer is wired on the live feed as forward-compat for a stream record the binary declares but no census has observed, the live twin being api_retry); `microcompact_boundary` → declared card-less with its reason.
- **Chrome signals**: `vcs_state_changed` → a git chip on the session card ("push · fix/x"), the `session-vcs` push (kb-api) that re-lists open File Explorers rooted in that cwd, and a "git push" row in the Session Properties timeline — card-less, restart-safe (session meta `vcs`); `code_change_published` (+ the transcript's `pr-link` row, unified as the same fact) → ONE small "PR #608 pushed" card with an escaped, never-auto-opened link and PR chips on the card (session meta `prLinks[]`, schema rows FIRST); `background_tasks_changed` (a LEVEL signal over BACKGROUND tasks) → the status bar's "N background tasks" chip + the reconcile that SOFT-closes a backgrounded task card the set no longer names (`finished`, outcome not reported — a foreground Bash is never touched; the outcome record that follows overwrites it); `task_updated {patch:{status:failed}}` closes the task card at once (a bonus row from the census).
- **Fixtures** scripts/fixtures/unknown-records/ — redacted, synthetic-valued samples of every routed shape (keys verbatim, values invented). **Gates**: test-record-shape (new, fast) · test-unknown-records 40 (the three lists pinned exactly; a routed name never renders red again) · test-stdout-registry 265 (both feeds reach the same four consumers) · test-codex-history / test-codex-0153 · test-worktree-userchan-ui (the payload key drift guard covers `vcs`/`prLinks`).
- **r3 verifier fixes (2026-09-21, each reproduced first)**: ① the level reconcile closed FOREGROUND tool calls (86 of 107 production task_started were local_bash is_backgrounded:false — a running Bash card read "completed") and pre-empted every task_updated{failed} (the CLI drops membership ~2 records BEFORE the outcome record) — now `taskInfo.backgrounded` gates it, the close is a soft `finished`/closedBy level that task_updated / task_notification (status enum honoured) / the `<task-notification>` twin overwrite, chat-status-bar closes nothing itself and patches its tail when the real outcome lands; ② the opt-in local census leg (VIBESPACE_SHAPE_CENSUS=1) crashed on a 964 MB transcript before printing — files > 256 MB are skipped, named and counted (15,643 files / 830,775 records / 5 skipped on this instance); ③ the api_error 401/403 consumer stated honestly (forward-compat on the live feed, the transcript path deliberately not fed) with a leg that drives the REAL claude classifier (401 attempt 1 refused, attempt 2 / 403 forwarded); ④ the drift-sample redactor judges key SEGMENTS (`key`/`monkey`/`hotkey` visible, credential compounds masked; negative control); ⑤ a codex event_msg line is judged at the envelope level too (a new top-level key on an event line is a drift card like on a response_item line); ⑥ the CLAUDE.md head ≤ 300 chars, the routed-notice CSS drops the literal colour fallback, a url-less code-change row dedupes by repo#identifier and never by a `null#id` key.
- **Deviations from the design, named**: the explorer has no git-status decoration to refresh, so `session-vcs` re-lists the open explorers rooted in that cwd instead; a success `result` creates no normalized message, so `turn_duration` rides the turn's LAST message (the assistant/tool card the result closed) rather than a "result message"; `item/Extension` and `item/SubAgentActivity` carry no `kind` enum in the oracle because an unknown kind is already the fall-back card by name (a drift card on top would double-report — test-codex-history's web.sleep leg proved it).

- **r2 — the heavy tier and the mirror after the squash.** ① `webui_msg_id` on every codex user record was judged as schema drift (the OURS list named five `webui_*` keys; the wrappers write nine) and a red "New fields" card entered every queued send — test-queue-steer (heavy) caught it; `isOurs` now takes EVERY `webui_*` key by prefix, and test-record-shape §2b is a grep-derived census over the tree's writers with a negative control. ② test-roster-reset-eta's phone leg now names the rightmost descendant of the roster section and its wide-font control reaches form controls too (the mirror's last red: the section overflows by 20 px there while every row fits — the next mirror run says which element). ③ The binary oracle names the installed claude build against the pinned one (`SCHEMA_CLI_VERSION` 2.1.274 in record-shape.js): strict on a developer box and whenever the two match; on the Actions mirror — which installs whatever npm serves today (2.1.278) — a newer build's drift is printed and skipped instead of turning the mirror red on every CLI release (`VIBESPACE_ORACLE_PINNED=<v>` drives the mode by hand).

## 2.369.125 — the phone gets what the toolbar and taskbar took with them: the top-10 mobile gaps + the measured defects (docs/design-mobile-gaps.md)

- **Why.** A desktop-vs-phone review of 59 features at 390×844 (2026-09-20) found 9 missing and 16 partial: the For-you inbox (the one surface agents use to ask the user) had NO binding on a phone, the Channels ⚙ row hid itself wherever the rail was not built, plain terminals / Files / Browser / Desktop lost their entry points with `#toolbar`, chat search was Ctrl+F-only, the 21×16 per-message hover buttons sat ON the text (18 of 18), the explorer's Size/Modified columns rendered at x 400–620 and its bookmarks pane ate a third of the width, desktops could not be created/renamed/deleted nor a window moved between them, the status-bar chips were 13–14 px tall, the settings nav was an unhinted 1119 px scroller, and the terminal key row hid paste and every ^C…^\ past the viewport.
- **#1 For-you inbox on the nav bar** (`#mobile-nav-todos`, user-todos-panel.js): the same segmented badge, the same popup opened as the full-width sheet the usage popup uses; the outside-tap closer exempts the button.
- **#2 Channels window fallback** (channels-panel.js): the ⚙ row's `when: _railEl` gate is gone; `focusChannelsPanel` carries openJobsWindow's ladder — rail panel where it exists, else ONE singleton `channels` window hosting the same renderer.
- **#3 "+" long-press sheet** (mobile-nav.js): Agent session / Terminal / Files / Browser, + Desktop when `/api/vnc/status` says available — a real 500 ms press (installLongPressContextMenu), the tap still opens the New Session dialog.
- **#4 Chat search on the status bar** (chat-status-bar.js / chat-view.js): a magnifier chip ≤768px, the touch face of Ctrl+F, wired to the same `open()` — live windows only (a read-only viewer builds no ChatSearch, so it shows no chip either).
- **#5 Message long-press menu** (chat-view.js): Copy text / Open in editor / Fork from here (addForkBtn's gate verbatim) / Message details on any message; the hover buttons are `display:none` ≤768px.
- **#6 Explorer phone layout** (file-explorer.js / -ops.js / viewers.css): one Name column, the bookmarks pane as a folding strip above the list, a wrapping toolbar with 36 px buttons and the path on its own line, and a long-press **Select…** mode — every tap toggles, a batch bar carries All / Copy / Cut / Compress / Delete / Done.
- **#7 Desktop management in the switcher** (mobile-nav.js): the desktop tab bar always renders with a "+" tab; tab long-press → Rename / Delete; window-row long-press → the registered 'window' menu (Move to Desktop included); a Minimized section restores stragglers.
- **#8 Touch-target pass** (style.css, ONE `@media (max-width:768px)` block): nav buttons, sidebar close/filter/manage/sort, the search input, sidebar tabs, status-bar chips and dropdown rows, settings nav items and terminal keys are ≥ 36 px; the ⚙ gear rows are another lane's and untouched.
- **#9 ⚙ System… / Ports…** (sidebar-rail.js, registered by the owning module with explicit orders): the rail panel where the rail exists, else a singleton window hosting the same `_renderSystemPanel` / `_renderPortsPanel` (the System tick + charts disposed with the window).
- **#10 Terminal** (terminal.js / window.js): a **Copy screen** key reads xterm's buffer (visible rows, trailing blanks dropped) and toasts the line count; the key row wraps so every key sits inside the viewport; the paste key is an SVG (no emoji); a layout-synced minimize is TRUTH on the phone too (`isMinimized` kept, hidden locally, another window shown, listed under the switcher's Minimized section — r2 below; r1 refused it and the phone's next save restored the desktop's windows).
- **Measured defects**: the settings nav strip wraps (every category visible, ≥ 36 px rows); the explorer header fits 390 px.
- **Gate**: scripts/test-mobile-gaps.mjs (heavy, ci.mjs) — a worktree server at 390×844 with an iPhone UA, touch emulation and hover:none/pointer:coarse; REAL touch sequences for every long-press; a seeded For-you item; a view-only fixture chat AND a live chat behind a stub `claude` (`CLAUDE_CMD`, the CODEX_CMD precedent) for the magnifier; a real dtach shell for the key row with the clipboard intercepted. Two harness facts recorded in kb-patterns: a fresh instance's first-run wizard covers the nav bar (set `vs-onboarded` first), and `showContextMenu` takes ONE class name.
- **Also**: scripts/test-window-types.mjs pins the three new singleton kinds (channels / system / ports) and their openSpec actions; six SVG icons (search / inbox / copy / globe / monitor / info); 16 zh + 16 ja dictionary entries.
- **r2 — the verifier's findings (two CDP clients, phone 390×844 + desktop 1280×800 on one server; every one reproduced first).** ① MEDIUM `WindowManager.minimize` REFUSED ≤768px (r1's guard), so the phone kept `isMinimized:false` and its next layout save RESTORED every window a desktop client had minimized (cross-client divergence). Now the truth is kept on every client and only the DISPLAY is local: the phone marks it minimized, hides it, shows the most recently used remaining window (closeWindow's rule, now ONE `_focusMostRecent`), lists it under the switcher's Minimized section; a phone save carries min:true; the phone's own restore tap is intent and travels. ② MEDIUM a phone-opened System / Ports / Channels window replayed on a rail-bearing desktop as the RAIL PANEL (its sidebar opened by itself, no window with that syncId existed, the desktop's next save closed the phone's window): every replay closure through a rail-first ladder now passes `forceWindow: true` (system / ports / channels, and jobs / job-interact — the same ladder, the same class) — a layout-sync REPLAY produces the WINDOW it names; the ladder stays for the human ⚙ click. test-window-types carries the census (+4). ③ MEDIUM explorer Select mode: a quick double-tap (Chrome synthesizes dblclick) navigated / opened the file and dropped the mode — both dblclick handlers are gated. ④ LOW the For-you sheet's own controls (tabs 17 px, ✓ ✕ ⤢ 20 px, the session header 18 px), the chat search bar's prev / next / close (17–20 px) and the switcher ✕ (32 px) join the ≥ 36 px pass; the sheet gets an Escape handler of its own (capture phase, deferring to an open popover or a visible dialog — a persistent element cannot carry `[data-popover]`). ⑤ REJECTED: lifting the ⚙ gear rows — they are the gear-menu hierarchy lane's (docs/design-gear-menu-hierarchy.md); design-mobile-gaps #8 now says so by name. test-mobile-gaps: 53 → 72 checks, incl. the two-client legs (desktop minimize → phone truth → phone save leaves it minimized → phone restore travels; phone System… → desktop WINDOW with the same id, rail tab untouched → desktop's next save leaves the phone's windows), the Select-mode double-tap with its outside-the-mode negative control, and the Escape layering control.
- **r3/r4 — the heavy tier on the merged tree.** r3: test-acp-harness pinned the OpenCode settings rows as source text in settings-schema.js, which 2.369.123 derives from the harness table — the pin now reads `HARNESS_SETTINGS.opencode`. r4: the touch pass's 2 px bar padding made a ONE-line phone status bar 41 px (36 px chips + 2+2 + the 1 px border) and tripped test-turn-truth-ui's ≤ 40 px one-line pin; the padding is 1 px (style.css), chips stay 36 px, the bar is 40. r5: test-desktop-app-keeper's process-accounting BOUNDARY leg sampled a kernel RACE (coreutils `timeout`'s group kill vs the intermediate sh's reap — 4 of 6 standalone runs let 70 ticks ride cutime into the loop; red twice with nothing near the keeper changed); the leg now CONSTRUCTS the dead-parent ordering (kb-bugfix-invariants, the keeper's r4 paragraph). r6 (the Actions mirror on cc89d748): test-gear-menu's two Esc-layer legs were red on the runner and green locally with no detail printed — the legs now park the pointer off the menu first (a stationary real mouse over a re-rendered head can re-arm hover intent on a slower machine), print the live state (popover / open flyouts / focus / float count) on every assert, and screenshot each step; the mirror workflow uploads every chrome suite's /tmp/vs-*-shots-* as an artifact on failure. r7 — the r6 artifact answered it: the runner shows the first-run Welcome wizard under the popover (an empty ~/.claude has no sessions, and `_checkOnboarding` skips the wizard on any box WITH sessions — green on every developer machine), so the wizard's own capture-phase Escape ate the first Esc. 40 of 41 chrome suites never pre-set `vs-onboarded`; the flag is now ONE shared `ONBOARDED_SOURCE` (scripts/scratch.mjs) passed to `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` before every navigate, and test-architecture §47 is the census (bare navigate fails, `// onboarding-under-test` exempts). The three suites red on every mirror run since 2.369.75 sat under the same modal: toolbar-resize went green with r7; the other two had a second cause each, both reproduced locally and fixed in r8. **r8** — ① a stored Recent/History host the roster no longer knows was healed only inside the workbench's zone render, and an instance with NO sessions and no hosts (the runner; any fresh install) takes `_renderInner`'s "No sessions" early return first, so the ghost id persisted in localStorage for ever — the heal is now `_wbHealHostSelections()` (sidebar-workbench.js), called ahead of the empty branch; test-ghost-host-heal boots its server under an EMPTY HOME (scratchHome) so the local gate is the runner's condition. ② The roster's identity line wrapped under a wide UI font (the runner resolves `system-ui` to DejaVu Sans, ~10 % wider than Noto/Cantarell): the tail dropped under the name and the "· credits" tag left the identity line at 1200×800 — the line is now `.acct-key-line` (never wraps; the name and the ident ellipsize; the credits tag is its own non-shrinking flex item; `.acct-key-extra` still wraps below) in all four row templates; test-roster-reset-eta prints its geometry on green too, runs the phone section under DejaVu Sans as a control and adds §4 (the desktop roster under the wide font; `VS_ROSTER_FONT=<family>` runs every section under a named font). ③ test-agentd-workers' scratch removal retries ENOTEMPTY (a worker still flushing `agentd/state` at teardown — one flaky red).

## 2.369.124 — the ⚙ menu is a tree: five heads + three direct rows, a left-opening flyout on desktop and a 44 px accordion on phones

- **Owner (docs/design-gear-menu-hierarchy.md, 2026-09-21): the ⚙ popover had grown to ~28 elements.** It is now `Appearance ▸` (the quick per-device prefs — Theme / Font size / Font / UI scale / UI font size / All Settings — as the head's own panel with a live `Dark · 14px · 100%` caption, plus Customize UI… and `Language ▸` whose four choices are real rows with ✓ on the current one) · Manage agents… · `Tools ▸` (Usage, Background Work, Desktop apps, Plugins, plugin windows) · `Communication ▸` (Channels, Outbox, Integrations) · `System ▸` (Report a problem first, Diagnostics, Restore a previous layout, Backup & migrate, Change password) · Update VibeSpace… (direct — its vX → vY label is the update indicator) · `Help ▸` (Welcome tour, All Settings) · Sign out. Eight top-level rows at most.
- **Desktop = a cascading flyout that opens to the LEFT** (the popover is right-anchored): 120 ms hover intent, click / Enter / ArrowLeft open it (a click never toggles it closed), one flyout per level, Esc closes one layer at a time and returns focus to the head, ArrowDown/Up/Home/End over a roving tabindex, `role=menu/menuitem`. **Phones and any hover-less pointer = an inline accordion**: one head open per level, every row ≥ 44 px (the old rows were ~27 px), the Appearance panel inline with 32 px steppers.
- **The registry knows the tree** (`src/lib/contributions.js`): `submenu:true` heads + `parent:'<head id>'` on any item (separators and `expand` included), validated loudly at registration wherever the chain is already known (explicit id + label, no verb on a head, no self-parent, no cross-menu parent, two levels at most checked from above and below, cycles), resolved lazily at `menuItems()` — a parent that is unknown, hidden or not a head warns once + telemetry `menu-unknown-parent` and the row surfaces at the top level, never dropped. Plugins: `api.registerMenuItem({ parent: 'tools' | 'comm' | 'system' | 'help' | 'appearance' })` or a head of their own (`submenu:true, id:'slug'` → `plugin:<id>:slug`); rows without a parent keep the old top-level behaviour (docs/plugins.md). The Channels / Outbox / Integrations / Desktop apps rows are filed by their owning modules (`parent:'comm'` / `'tools'` with distinct orders — the two order-45 twins are gone). New i18n keys Appearance / Communication / Help (zh + ja).
- **r2 — the verifier's four findings (2026-09-21), each with a regression leg in the suite that owns the file.** ① The Appearance head's caption went STALE after a change made inside its own panel (A+ said 15, the head still read `14px` until the popover reopened): the registry now hands a FUNCTION caption through as `captionOf` beside the resolved string and the head re-evaluates it on every click / change / input bubbling out of its members — test-gear-menu pins A+ → the new px → back after A-; test-contributions pins captionOf (function yes, string no) + a WIRING pin on the renderer's refresh. ② Two CLAUDE.md index heads were 394 / 392 chars against the ≤ ~300 size law — trimmed to 289 / 299 (appearance-panel 278). ③ The hover-intent leg slept a fixed 50 / 350 ms from node against the page's 120 ms timer (a starved lane could land the assertion after the timer): it now stamps mouseenter and the `aria-expanded` flip on the PAGE's clock and node polls until-style (≤ 2 s); every hover leg polls. ④ A plugin head registered with `submenu:true` but no `id` slipped past the registry's explicit-id rule through the host's generated `item-N` id — `api.registerMenuItem` refuses it (docs/plugins.md says so; test-contributions pins the refusal ahead of the id generation).
- Gates: test-contributions (182 — tree unit legs + B3 re-based as a TREE fixture over the same 16 states with a flatten census against the legacy flat list: every old row in exactly one place, none twice, none lost, ≤ 9 top-level rows, exactly one danger row, the action→method map over the leaves; the four owners' specs are read off the source), NEW test-gear-menu (heavy, chrome: both modes end to end — headless chrome answers `(hover: none)` by default, so the desktop leg is given a real mouse through blink settings and the phone leg uses CDP touch emulation), test-ui-scale opens Appearance before reading the labels.


## 2.369.123 — harness settings have a home: the Claude / Codex / OpenCode sections are derived from the harness descriptors, every row says where it goes, and the CLI-config rows show which machine they reached (docs/design-harness-settings.zh.md, owner D1–D4)

- **The model (design §2, PURE `src/harness-settings.js`).** Each harness DECLARES its settings as a pure table `{prefix, category, files, rows}` joined to the descriptor by object identity (like `caps`); a row's `apply` is a closed union — `spawn` (consumed by `buildSessionArgs`, `how` is display text, optional `via` field / `live` adapter verb / `mode`), `server` (read by VibeSpace at a decision point), `cli-config` (written INTO the harness's own config file; a value equal to `off` is never written or deleted). `checkTable` validates every rule by name; `coerce` is THE typed read (the 36500 default that lived twice now lives once). Persisted keys are byte-identical (`claude.brief`, `codex.defaultModel`, …) — zero migration, config export/import untouched.
- **The Settings window is the dedicated area (owner D1).** The three harness sections are derived from the tables (`scripts/fixtures/harness-settings-schema-2.369.120.json` pins the 21 rows field-equal); each section opens with one line saying what the values are for and which CLI file the "written into the CLI config" rows land in; every row carries an apply chip — "Applies to new sessions · --brief", "Read by VibeSpace · pool engine", or "Written into the CLI config" with `~/.claude/settings.json → cleanupPeriodDays`, the FRESH local receipt (✓ written 3 min ago / ⚠ is 30 (wanted 36500) — written again at the next start / ? not found — start the CLI once / ⚠ not valid after a hand edit — not touched / leaving the CLI's own value alone) and a human-triggered "Check machines…" that lists every registered host's state. The same chips sit on Manage Agents → Machines under both integration rows (that is where the user looks for WHICH machine; not a second editor). One wording function (`src/lib/cli-config-chips.js`) for all three surfaces. No new tab. `claude.autoResumeOnLimit` is back in the Chat category (generic feature; key unchanged).
- **Receipts are fresh reads (owner D2).** `cliConfigStatus()` re-reads the target file on every probe; the last local write is kept in memory only (never a persisted "applied at" that a hand edit would turn into a lie).
- **No fan-out on change (owner D3).** ONE plan (`{v:1, files:[{rel, format, createIfMissing, hooks?, set:[…]}]}`), ONE env (`VIBESPACE_CLI_CONFIG` = base64 JSON, shell-safe bare), ONE applier: this machine applies it in process at boot and on change (now honouring `hookRegistrationSafe()` — the old retention write let a /tmp worktree server write the real HOME's settings.json); remote hosts get it at the next Install AND at the next ssh spawn (the prelude carries the same env — a host only ever spawned into, never Installed, used to get nothing) AND at the next dial spawn (`dm.runCmd(…, {env})` — the daemon's existing run-cmd env merge, no new op, no capability bit, old daemons work). `hosts.agentToolsStatus` asks the helper's READ-ONLY `--status` only behind a grep gate on the env name (an older helper would treat `--status` as a registration run); ungated it says "not checked — reinstall the agent tools".
- **The codex config.toml writer, built now (owner D4 ≠ the doc's recommendation).** `src/harness-config.js` (SHARED, fs/path/os only) carries the moved CAS JSON writer AND a comment-and-format-PRESERVING minimal TOML setter: set or replace one `key = value` inside a `[section]` — or the dotted top-level `section.key = value` when the file already spells it so — append the section at the end when missing, string/boolean/integer values, byte-identical output when the value is already there, CRLF kept; REFUSES BY NAME a key that lives in an inline table, an array of tables or a multi-line string, an array/float/date value, a duplicate key, and any file its conservative tokenizer cannot read — same CAS + tmp+rename, same "a hand-broken file is never overwritten" rule. The codex descriptor declares `config.toml {format:'toml', writable:true}` and ships ONE real managed row: **`codex.historyPersistence`** (enum, default `save-all` → `[history] persistence`) — the codex analogue of Claude's transcript retention (with `none` codex writes no rollouts and this instance's history is empty; `''` = leave config.toml alone). Evidence, cited in the row comment: the installed codex-cli 0.154.0 binary's embedded resolved-config template `[history]` / `persistence = "save-all"` (5×), the `HistoryPersistence` struct name and the "(Session persistence is disabled; cannot …" branch.
- **The shipped helper embeds the applier as FILE TEXT.** `data/bin/vibespace-hook-register.mjs` (generated, tracked, regenerated) is ESM + `createRequire`; `src/harness-config.js` is evaluated inside a function body with its own `module`/`exports` (never `Function.toString` — a closure reference would be a free identifier, the 2.340.2/2.341.1 lost-binding class); a hooks-only `DEFAULT_PLAN` keeps hook registration working under an older server; `--uninstall` strips only our hook entries and never a managed key; its private hook-event table is gone (the plan's `hooks.events` carries it, and `ensureAgentHooks`/`stripAgentHookEntries` share the same mutators). `VIBESPACE_CLAUDE_KEEP_DAYS` is gone from every code file.
- **The server reads a harness setting through the descriptor, never a spelled id (design §5).** `harnessSetting(session.backend, key)` / `harnessDeclares` / `harnessSpawnSettings` (src/server/harness-config-sync.js) replace the literal `serverSetting('claude.…')`/`'codex.…'` reads (ws-create's instance defaults, the `--brief`/prompt-cache/disableModelFallback trio now one `settings` bag, the pool engine's `limitResetCredit` and `disableModelFallback` off `session.backend`, `claudeKeepDays` gone); the disableModelFallback live loop is generalised by adapter CAPABILITY (`live: 'formatSetFallbackPolicy'` on the row); the client stopped filling `claude.tuiRenderer` itself. A plugin-contributed harness registers its own table (`register()` validates: its own prefix, never a built-in one, ≤50 rows) and gets a derived section through `/api/home` with zero new code.
- **Gates (design §8).** test-harness-contract: table identity pins, `inject.hookFile ∈ configFiles` by identity, every configFiles `rel` the table's own array, and SPAWN CONFORMANCE — every `spawn` row driven into the adapter must change the spawn, a synthetic never-consumed row is the negative control; test-claude-retention kept by NAME and grown (§1 ensureCliConfig, §2 the helper under VIBESPACE_CLI_CONFIG incl. the codex toml row, §3 --status read-only with bytes + mtime pinned, §4 the embed + `node --check`, §5 the three env sites + zero VIBESPACE_CLAUDE_KEEP_DAYS in code); test-architecture: PURE += harness-settings.js, SHARED += harness-config.js, NEW §46 literal-harness-id census over every server-tier file (both spellings, synthetic offenders as controls) + §46b the bare-category-literal pin (the 2.369.120 side finding, with its control) + §46c exactly one hand-written harness-prefixed schema row; NEW scripts/test-harness-settings.mjs (122): checkTable's refusals one fixture each, the derived rows vs the snapshot, coercion, the plan (off ⇒ not written), applyConfigPlan/readConfigPlan on a scratch HOME incl. the TOML fixtures (comments preserved byte-for-byte outside the touched line, existing section, missing section, dotted spelling, CRLF, every refusal by name, idempotence), registerHarnessSettings' prefix rules, the receipt wording, the live-verb fan-out, the helper's DEFAULT_PLAN.
- **r7 — the applier after the verifier (2026-09-21; every finding reproduced on a scratch HOME first).** ① BOTH config writers replaced a SYMLINKED `~/.codex/config.toml` / `~/.claude/settings.json` with a regular file (tmp beside the link, rename onto the link) — the dotfiles pattern silently broken at every boot, remote install, ssh-spawn prelude and dial spawn, receipts ✓ (the JSON half was master's `_patchHookFile`; the TOML half was new and default-on). Now the bytes land on the link's REAL target (tmp beside it, rename onto it): the link survives and the dotfile keeps governing; a dangling link is refused by name, never replaced; an existing-but-unreadable path is refused instead of "created" over; the file's own mode survives the rename (a 0600 config.toml carrying MCP tokens stays 0600 — chmod on the tmp beats the umask). ② An out-of-vocabulary value for a closed enum row (`POST /api/settings {"codex.historyPersistence":"bogus"}` — the Settings window cannot produce one) was written verbatim into config.toml, codex 0.154.0 then refused to load its config (`unknown variant \`bogus\``) on that machine and every receipt said ✓ applied. `coerce` — THE typed read — now closes the vocabulary for every non-combobox enum (the row default rides; combobox rows keep typed values), so neither the plan nor a spawn bag ever carries it, and `syncCliConfig` names the refused value in the log at every sync. ③ The applier re-checks every plan `rel` at apply / read / decode (a `..`, separator or `~` segment ⇒ a `refused` receipt naming it, nothing joined under $HOME; `decodePlan` drops such a plan whole) — a text-identical twin of `checkRel`, pinned. ④ Two more TOML shapes codex refuses as "duplicate key" (both verified on 0.154.0): a root scalar named like the section (`history = 5`) is refused by name instead of appending `[history]`; dotted root keys (`history.max_bytes = 5`, no header) get the new line in THAT spelling; dotted keys AND a header are refused. ⑤ Documented honestly: the JSON writer re-serialises the whole file (2-space JSON, as Claude Code itself does) — "only the touched line" is the TOML writer's promise. Gates: test-harness-settings 122 → 190 (§3/§4 the closed vocabulary incl. a newline-injection value and the PURE builder; §5b symlinked files AND a symlinked CLI dir, 0600/0640 kept, the dangling link, a directory in the file's place, with the old-write CONTROL; §5c the duplicate-key shapes + the REAL codex loading every shape the writer produces + the two broken-shape controls, evidence-SKIP without the binary; §6b ten bad rels at apply/read/decode + the checkRel twin pin; §9 the boot warn), test-claude-retention 33 → 35 (the shipped helper writes through a symlink; a `..` plan never reaches the applier through the env).

## 2.369.122 — the View Workflow window really follows the card now (the run id was never registered on the live stream)

- **Owner, on a .120 instance: "这个还是没同步啊？"** 2.369.119 looked the run's live tree up by `taskInfoById(runId)`, but on the LIVE stream the CLI emits `system/task_started` with a SHORT task_id (a real buffer: `wu93ghxi2`) BEFORE the tool_result that carries the ack ("Run ID: wf_…"); the launch-ack synthesis that registers the wf_ id only runs when no taskInfo exists yet, so it was skipped and the window kept the disk skeleton ("(agent)" rows, the old note). The ack now registers the run id even when task_started came first and remembers it as `taskInfo.runId` (the short id stays `id`, the CLI's key for task_progress/notification). The .119 fixture had put the ack first and used the run id as task_id — a shape the wire never produces (the fixtures-from-real-data rule); it now replays the real order. Gate: test-workflow-live-view §2.

## 2.369.121 — Background Work folds by session and acknowledges in batches

## 2.369.118 — userW's two reports fixed at the root (terminal selection under the UI scale; a Desktop that stays disconnected), live Workflow agent chips, a Notices lane in the inbox, and Claude Code told to keep conversations for 100 years

- **A terminal selection took the wrong lines under the UI scale (userW, inc-mu92zsgw-6c9y: the `claude auth login` terminal "cannot copy text, the lines cross").** Root cause, measured on a standalone xterm page driven by real mouse events: xterm.js maps the pointer by `clientX - rect.left`, which under the body's DPI zoom (`document.body.style.zoom`, the "UI scale" setting) is in ZOOMED px, while the cell size it divides by was measured in layout px — so a drag at row 20 selected row 25 at scale 125 % and row 16 at 80 %. The same class as inc-mtdrm922 (VNC pointer offset). Fix = that incident's rule applied to every xterm container: `.terminal-container` is counter-zoomed (`COUNTER_ZOOM`, now the ONE definition in utils.js, re-exported by vnc-view.js) and the xterm font size is the visual px × the UI scale (`_xtermPx`, every writer of `options.fontSize` goes through it; `rescale()` on a scale change; app.js's font-size row goes through applyOverride). Nothing visible changes (screen size within 3 %), the selection and the link hover land where the pointer is. Gates: `test-terminal-ui-scale` (fast, wiring pins) + `test-terminal-zoom-select` (heavy: headless chrome, the real xterm build, CDP drags — the pre-fix page selects row 20×scale, the fixed page row 20). Forensics: the incident snapshot now records `uiScale` / `dpr` / `bodyZoom` (the report had no way to tell), and the freeze copies the last 64 KB of every open terminal's raw PTY buffer (`frozen/buffers/<id>.tail`) — the login screen itself was swept with the session before anyone looked.
- **"Desktop disconnected" with nothing in any log (userW, inc-mu3lmd4s-dmwf).** The /api/vnc bridge had no keepalive — an RFB stream over a static screen carries no bytes for minutes and a proxy on the way drops a silent WebSocket — and logged neither the open nor the close, so the bundle held zero evidence and the singleton Desktop window sat on "Disconnected" until somebody clicked (only the app windows walked the reconnect ladder). Now: the bridge pings every 20 s (`PING_MS`), terminates a peer silent for two rounds and NAMES it, logs every open and every close (who closed, after how long, bytes each way); the singleton opts into the same bounded reconnect ladder as the desktop-app windows (each retry re-runs the start gate, so a dead VNC server is respawned; the Reconnect button remains for the ladder's end); the incident bundle carries the desktop scene (singleton facts, app sessions, bridge counters). Gate: `test-desktop-stream-keepalive` (real ws client + a TCP stand-in server). The drop's own cause on that instance is not in the evidence — the next occurrence will be.
- **Live Workflow detail (owner: "研究一下 workflow 怎么在运行的时候就展示 subagent 细节").** Claude Code's `system/task_progress` records carry a `workflow_progress` list — phases and agents with label / phaseIndex / state / lastToolName / lastToolSummary / model / attempt — intermittently (heartbeats omit it). The normalizer keeps it FIELD-WISE on `taskInfo.workflow` (a payload without the tree keeps the tree already held; `normalizeWorkflowProgress`, strings bounded, prompt previews dropped) plus `taskInfo.usage` (tokens / tool uses / duration); the Workflow card renders phases with agent chips (label · state dot · last tool · tally · usage) and a workflow's taskInfo edit re-renders its card through the one swap point. Live sessions only (the transcript never carries these records); the post-hoc View Workflow window stays the history surface. Gate: test-task-lifecycle (+10).
- **A Notices lane in the For-you inbox (owner: "spending 这东西不要和其他消息一起挤在 inbox 里").** An item now carries `kind: action | notice` — a PRODUCER's declaration, never inferred (spend-guard's ceiling notices are notices; `vibespace-ask --notice`; older items are actions). Notices leave their session group for their own section under the asks, keep the append-only slots while the popup is open, and never colour the badge: the red/yellow/accent segments count actions only, a grey segment counts notices. Gate: test-user-todos-layout (+11, incl. the producer/route/CLI pins).
- **Claude Code deletes conversations after 30 days — VibeSpace now tells it 100 years (owner: "把默认值配成 100 年，不要让 claude code 乱删对话").** New setting `claude.transcriptRetentionDays` (default 36500, category Claude): the server writes `cleanupPeriodDays` into `~/.claude/settings.json` at boot and on every change through the hook installer's compare-and-swap writer (a hand-broken file is refused by name, never overwritten; 0 = leave the CLI's own value alone); remote hosts receive it through the shipped register helper (`VIBESPACE_CLAUDE_KEEP_DAYS`) at every agent-tools (re)install, never on `--uninstall`. Gate: test-claude-retention (scratch HOME only).
- Tests: every chrome suite now waits for `window.app` INSIDE the page for up to 20 s (an in-page poll) instead of one probe 1.5 s after navigate — the heavy tier went RED on a7ec8ff8 with "no app" in two lanes at once (test-sidebar-rail twice, test-ui-scale once) while both pass alone: a probe timed by a sleep is a bet on load speed under three parallel lanes, and a gate must measure, not bet.
- Housekeeping: `POST /api/agent/user-todo` `add.kind`; the client snapshot's new fields; the desktop scene assembled in incident-wiring (server.js stays under the ratchet).

## 2.369.117 — a stated reset lands a minute late: the pool verdict, the arm and every immediate continue wait one minute after the stated instant

- **Auto-resume fired at the stated reset and got rejected (owner, 2026-09-18: "你每次恢复的时候似乎有时候会抢跑，稍微等一分钟再发自动恢复可能更稳妥一点").** The instants the pool reads come from vendor readings and from the CLI's own /usage panel, whose text names MINUTES ("resets 7:29pm") — a stated reset can be up to ~60 s early and the vendor's clock lags on top. Journal, 09:59:15Z: the pool moved seven conversations onto a member 45 s before its stated 5h reset (`bucketRemaining` read the passed instant as "full again"), fired the continue at once, and the vendor rejected it; 08:59Z: the same shape onto a member whose cache showed an empty window. FIX (PURE, one place): `RESET_GRACE_SEC = 60` in src/account-pool-auto.js — a bucket whose stated reset has passed counts as fresh only a minute later, and `quotaVerdict.blockedUntil` ends a minute after the last stated reset, so the timed arm, a pool switch and a wake all wait for the reset to land; `deadBuckets`/`until` keep the STATED instant so the arm card still names when the reset is and says the continue follows about a minute after it ("已安排在重置约 1 分钟后自动继续"). auto-resume's own 15 s tick margin is unchanged (a prose-stated codex reset is minute-precise on top, so it lands 60–120 s after the stated minute). Gates: test-pool-auto (117, the grace legs), test-auto-resume (227), test-auto-resume-loop (218), test-fable-cap-pool-storm, test-new-member-wake, test-account-verdicts, test-harness-contract, test-account-pool.

## 2.369.114 — a legacy pre-isolation window anchor heals from the isolated panel, the ⟳ falls to the panel when the live reading was archived, and a hot-switched session's spawn-time identity no longer starves the witness ring (inc-mu6djxxt-8166, "5h限额刷新不出来了")

- **The reading the guard archived was reported as a refresh.** The toast "已通过一个活动会话刷新额度——身份未验证: window matches no known account — archived" was the ⟳ route answering `success` for a live `get_usage` reading the window guard had just refused to write — nothing on screen changed, and the isolated panel was never tried. Now a refused control reading is a SKIPPED rung (listed with the guard's reason) and the ⟳ falls to the account's own isolated `/usage` panel, exactly as it does for a session the engine would not ask.
- **The anchor nothing could heal.** One member's `.window-` sidecar was a stamp the PRE-isolation panel left at 00:53Z (source on-demand, no `verifiedBy`) naming a weekly reset the vendor never gave it — B-855a's own artefact. Its API witness ring never filled (every session it hosted had been hot-switched, so the spawn-time OTel identity vetoed every candidate), the standing repair saw "no evidence" and kept the stamp, the isolated panel was "unverified" (nothing to compare against) and so never re-stamped — and every live reading of the member's TRUE window was archived as foreign; the 5h bucket moved only when the auto-cli panel happened to run. FIX: with no API-derived witness, the isolated panel (the creds dir IS the account under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR isolation, measured in 2.369.110) may establish an absent anchor, re-anchor a legacy one that contradicts it (the old stamp archived with a reason, one journal line) or upgrade one that agrees — `verifiedBy: 'isolated-panel', provisional: true`. A verified anchor (an API run, an org/phase-verified panel) is never touched, and an API witness that disagrees still refuses the panel outright. PURE rule: `reading-lag.isolatedPanelAnchorVerdict`.
- **A hot-switched session's OTel identity is spawn-time, not evidence.** `apiWitnessEligibility` vetoed on OTel disagreement unconditionally; for a conversation the pool has re-pointed since its CLI was spawned the disagreement IS the switch (the CLI reports the org it cached at spawn for the life of the process). The veto now applies only to a session the pool never re-pointed since spawn (`switchedSinceSpawn`, memoised per session, no new session field); the lag-shadow / recent re-point / turn-pin legs keep covering the in-flight reading of a fresh switch. Members that only ever host switched sessions can now fill their ring and be verified by the API.

## 2.369.112 — a peer message shows the moment the receiver's turn starts, a window hidden by the phone layout / a tab / minimize no longer pages itself into history, and a compacted "Prompt is too long" card stops offering Compact now

- **A harness-delivered peer message rendered only at turn END (inc-mu6bfv1t-4drq, owner: "the receiver started working on it, but the chat view never showed the message existed").** Another session's `SendMessage` woke the receiver through the CLI's own inbox socket; stdout never carries the user record with the sender's words (the 2.362.2 forensics), so the card was mined from the terminal `result.origin` — four minutes into the turn in the capture. But the CLI does speak at turn START: `command_lifecycle {state:'started', command_uuid}`, and that uuid IS the JSONL uuid of the user record it wrote ~13 ms after enqueue (measured on 2.1.274: `38fa716a…` on both sides). The stream-json consumer now looks that record up in the session's own transcript tail (≤512 KB, async, retries 0/150/600/2000 ms for a write racing the frame) and injects the card immediately through the rebuild-gated `feedPeerCard`, carrying `msgId` so the result rung and a device-fed copy of the same record dedup against it. A typed prompt, a task-notification wake, a body-less server-posted origin (the delivery ladder already drew that card) and a remote-host session are not this carrier's business. `server.js` lists `command_lifecycle` as a handled stream type. Gate: scripts/test-peer-command-card.mjs (24, fast: real consumer + real normalizer over a scratch HOME, the race, every negative control, the wiring pins).
- **Switching conversations on a phone landed in history (inc-mu6bfv1t-4drq, owner: "每次手机上切对话都会滚到对话历史里而不是最新位置").** The 2.369.1 law — a hidden window's geometry is meaningless, decide nothing off it — was physical only for the desktop hider (visibility:hidden → `setSuspended`). Three hiders use display:none, which also ZEROES the scroller's scrollTop, and none suspended: the phone layout's inactive windows (`.window {display:none}` ≤768px), a grouped guest's `.tab-hidden` content, a minimized window. Captured 3/3 windows on every switch: scrollTop → 0 with no touch input, `unpin`, the top sentinel paging 50 older messages in, `trimBottom removed:50`, then `userNav via jumpToBottom` by hand — and at page load `autoFill rendered:50 sh:0 ch:0` on every hidden window. FIX: the ChatView keeps a REASON SET (`setHidden(reason, on)`: mobile / tab / minimized / desktop compose — suspended while any holds, the settle window + pinned re-tail run when the last clears; `setSuspended` is the desktop reason), and `WindowManager.syncHiddenViews()` derives the three from the classes it owns at every site that changes them (focusWindow both branches, switchTab, minimize, every view registration, the breakpoint's matchMedia change). The rule is PURE src/lib/view-visibility.js. Gate: scripts/test-hidden-view-suspend.mjs (42, fast).
- **After a compaction the "Prompt is too long" card still offered Compact now (inc-mu6btbfr-uaxg, owner: "我compact之后还提示compact now，容易误会").** The live `compact_end result:'success'` frame only rewrote the sentence under the button; the button and the red title stayed, and a rebuild / page-in rendered the card on the fallback guidance again. Now a compaction that SUCCEEDED resolves every card older than it: the button goes, the card dims, the hint states the outcome — from the live frame (every card on screen) and from the CLI's own summary user record on a rebuild or page-in (only the cards whose record precedes it in time: a card AFTER a compaction is about the context being full again and keeps its button). The stage line still reaches every card (the round-4 outcome rule, test-turn-truth-ui). PURE rule `ctxFullCardsToResolve` + `isCompactSummaryText` in chat-renderers.js. Gate: scripts/test-compaction-ux.mjs (36).

## 2.369.110 — the /usage probe can no longer report another account (B-855a), the identity anchor is derived from the API and the polluted stores are repaired at boot, a Fable-cap wall marks one lane (B-ccaa), and usage credits are visible before they are spent (B-ad05)

- Owner (2026-09-17, four reports in one day: "所有账号都是 Fable 要用完了根本无法判断", "fable 又都提示 100 了但还在跑", "会不会是 claude -p 有缓存机制", "确保 config dir 和 working directory 都用新的路径"). MEASURED with the CLI's own `--debug` log: `claude -p /usage` fetches with the token it is handed, and when that fetch fails in-band (a 200 with a fieldless body — it tracks probe pressure) it silently seeds the panel from the config dir's machine-wide `cachedUsageUtilization`, the last account any live session fetched. Every probe ran in the shared `$HOME` config, so the busiest members' panels were another account's 15 of 50, 22 of 47 and 14 of 43 times in a day, and each foreign panel re-stamped the account's window sidecar so its own readings were archived as foreign for ever. The roster's "Fable 100 % everywhere", the 02:30 arm card that waited for the wrong member, and the 15:10 pool switch off a fresh member were all this.
- **c1 — the probe may only write the account it proves** (`src/usage-routes.js`): the panel runs under a per-account isolated `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<credsDir>/.probe-config` (seeded with only that account's own oauthAccount) AND `cwd=<credsDir>/.probe-config/cwd` — the only fallback the CLI has left is the account's own previous fetch, a failed first fetch prints nothing; before any write the panel is checked against witnesses it did not produce (the org the CLI reports; the weekly phase of the account's API-derived window) — a mismatch writes nothing, stamps nothing, archives as `panel-identity` naming both identities and lands in the raw probe log as `write-refused`; a phase shared with another member is written UNVERIFIED and never stamps; the ⟳ route skips a session it cannot vouch for and answers `{rung, identityVerified, why}` (Manage Agents shows it).
- **c2 — the identity anchor is derived from the API and the stores are repaired** (`src/server/usage-pool-engine.js`, `src/reading-repair.js`): `.apiwin-<key>` is a ring of eligible slot-verified weekly readings (not in a re-point shadow, turn pin newer than the last re-point, OTel not disagreeing) and the witness is written only when the newest three agree — never from one reading (the verifier reproduced a lagging response poisoning a freshly added member permanently); the same three-run re-anchors a window that genuinely MOVED; `repairSidecarsByApiPhase` runs at boot, hourly and by `POST /api/usage/repair-identity` — contradicted sidecars re-stamped, contradicted caches archived and rebuilt from the newest agreeing anchor (`overage`/`spend` carried through), archived own readings re-admitted; measured on a copy of this instance's data: 3 sidecars re-stamped, 3 caches replaced. **B-ccaa**: `seven_day_overage_included` is deferred like every unscoped weekly rejection so a Fable-cap wall marks one lane.
- **c3 — usage credits are visible before they are spent** (`src/spend-authorizer.js`, `src/account-pool-auto.js`, Manage Agents): `overageState().mode` (allowed needs positive vendor evidence; a status-less `inUse:false` is unknown), a dim credits chip, credits members rank last and are a last resort with ONE parking notice per 6 h, 'Exclude from pool' on the member's own menu; spend-guard unchanged.
- After updating: switch `accounts.onDemandQuotaRefresh` back to `auto-cli` if you set it to `manual` as the stopgap; the boot repair rewrites the polluted caches on the first start.
- Built whole on feat-readings-identity-whole (7 commits + one adversarial verify with 6 findings + one fix pass), squashed here. Gates: test-readings-attribution 495+ (§19 ①–⑩, §20), test-usage-probe-log 32, test-new-member-wake 119, test-pool-auto 110, test-spend-paths 285, test-fable-cap-pool-storm, test-migrations, test-quota-model; fast tier green on the integration tree.

## 2.369.109 — every /usage probe is recorded raw: what was sent, what came back verbatim, what the parser made of it, what the write did

- Owner (2026-09-17): "我建议你以后把最近一段时间的所有的/usage的raw返回结果和对应的parse结果保存起来方便debug". New `src/server/usage-probe-log.js`: the panel rung (`claude -p /usage`, the ⟳ button + the auto-cli loop) and the control rung (a live session's `get_usage`) each append ONE line to `data/usage-probe-log.ndjson` (8 MB × 2 ring) with the account key + creds dir + argv, the machine-wide `~/.claude.json` oauthAccount read before and after the spawn (the org context the panel actually answers for — the B-855a input), the verbatim stdout/stderr or control payload, the parse, and the write verdict (written / write-refused / no-buckets-parsed / spawn-failed / account-removed; control: written / refused-by-window-guard / timeout / unparsed) with the window it was filed under. `GET /api/usage/probe-log?key=&rung=&limit=` reads it back. Zero vendor calls; no secret ever enters it.
- Measured while writing it (the reason it exists): in the last 24 h the panel probe returned ANOTHER member's window for 15 of userP's 50 reads, 22 of Natural Max's 47 and 14 of B-Stack's 43 — the members the pool parks on. userP's own API events put its Fable at 5 % used at 02:08 PDT while the card that morning said 98 % (Fish Max's panel, returned by the probe at 02:23 and carried by the 5h-only events until the wall). The identity gate itself is the readings-identity lane's first chunk (B-855a); this release makes every future foreign panel diagnosable from the log alone.
- Gate: scripts/test-usage-probe-log.mjs (32, fast tier). Also: test-agentd-session's teardown retries the scratch-dir rm (`maxRetries`) — the daemon it had just SIGTERMed was still writing state while the recursive rm walked the tree, and that ENOTEMPTY blocked this release's first push.

## 2.369.108 — the auto-resume arm card says WHOSE reset it waits for, and why the account that rejected you is not it

- Owner (2026-09-17 03:50 PDT): "明明当前hit limit的账号7am就会reset 5h，但你却提示12pm才能等到自动恢复". The wait was computed correctly — a member is usable again only when the LAST of its dead buckets resets, userP's Fable cap sat at 2 % left (under the 5 % floor) so its 7am 5h reset was not a candidate, and the pool's soonest member was Member L whose Fable week rolls at 12pm — but the card said only `已安排在 12pm 重置后自动继续`, naming an instant and nothing about it (and B-Stack's 5h reset hot-switched the conversation 1 h 20 m later anyway).
- Fix: the verdict carries its structure (`quotaVerdict` → `deadBuckets` + `until`; the pool verdict → `soonest` + `rejector`), the engine folds it into an arm `cause` (`armCauseFor`) that the arm persists and a cause-less re-arm inherits, and the card reads `userP 的 5h 将在 07:00 重置，但它的 Fable 仅剩 2%（低于 5% 门槛，视为用尽，9/20 重置）。最早可用的成员是 Member L（Fable 12:00 重置），已安排到时自动继续；任一成员提前可用会立即继续`. The status-bar chip's tooltip says the same in the device's language (zh/ja); the journal's `armed for` line ends `via <member>/<bucket>`. The floor policy itself is unchanged (the owner's call).
- Gates: test-auto-resume-loop 218 (+10: the 02:30:43 shape through the real engine and the real producer, the cause-less control, the single-member and unpooled forms, the wiring pin), test-pool-auto 89 (+6), test-auto-resume 226 (+3).

A bucket that may not name a deadline (an empty window, a passed or missing reset) rendered its donut with NO label under it, so that donut floated above a blank gap while its labelled neighbours read as donut + token — the row heights were equal (the min-height belt) but the donuts were not. ## 2.369.106 — the Communication panel, whole (P0b integrations + P1–P4): shared integration keys, Lark + Gmail read adapters over a loopback OAuth flow, push lanes that demote themselves, assign/filter/wake through spend-guard, an approval outbox, and external send with reconcile

- Owner's design docs/design-communication-panel.zh.md (decisions 1–25 approved 2026-09-13), built whole on one branch (feat-comm-panel-whole, 16 commits + one adversarial verify + one fix pass), squashed here. Every chunk shipped with its own gates; the four verifier findings (a refused wake's stash re-clipped to 400 chars, vendor titles reaching a receipt block un-neutered, a boot-time double delivery, a permanent Gmail pull failure re-armed every minute) are fixed with controls.
- **Integrations & keys (P0b)**: PURE `src/integration-registry.js` rows + `src/server/integration-store.js` (secret-box store, precedence user > cluster > none; an undecryptable ciphertext never falls to the cluster default and says so; the env name is built only in the store) + ⚙ → Integrations window with per-row Test; PURE `src/agent-env.js` is now THE one sanitizer — the daemon was a second holder of the server env and every daemon child inherited the cluster secrets (measured in a real CLI's /proc environ).
- **P1a read adapters**: `src/oauth-loopback.js` dual-mode consent flow (ephemeral port or the FIXED `http://127.0.0.1:17865/lark/cb`, port held only during the flow, EADDRINUSE refused by name, `state` checked at both points); `src/channels/lark.js` + `src/channels/gmail.js` read adapters that take credentials from `resolveIntegration()` only; the Channels panel's connect wizard (three copy paths), re-authorize countdown, tracked picker, options editor; the egress census (`test-channels-egress`, every host literal a claim); Gmail reuses the existing Drive OAuth preset (decision 5).
- **P1b push lanes**: `src/channels/live/{lane,lark,gmail}.js` — the ack is the return after durable persistence, stop() is terminal for an in-flight arm, exclusivity is declared + measured (`push.missRate`) + auto-demoted with a reason, Gmail's Pub/Sub pull is default-off, a permanent pull failure parks `unavailable` instead of reconnecting.
- **P2 assign / filter / wake**: PURE `src/channel-filter.js` (eight rule kinds, honest estimator, `why` as a contract, vendor lines quoted + frames neutered), assignments with `authority:'send'` capped by policy AND capability, the wake through the delivery ladder under new SPEND_REASONS (`channel-message`, `channel-receipt`) charged to the right slot, digest batching, per-assignment pacing, `channels.pushCoalesceSeconds`, pending hits persisted and carried (never dropped), lane parity proven over one day's traffic (`test-channels-lane-parity`).
- **P3 outbox + approval**: PURE `src/channel-policy.js`, the outbox store, inline approval cards + the Outbox window (identity row + marking warning), the For-you pointer with retraction, receipts via `noWake` (delivered only into a running turn, else stashed), the audit log, `data/bin/vibespace-channels` + manual, the AgentReach panel, convCaps re-resolved at approval.
- **P4 external send**: Lark sends as the user (both dotted send scopes required, `uuid` idempotency, a transport failure after the request left is `lost` never a refusal), Gmail sends two-phase (draft = the durable handle, threading headers off the anchor), `reconcile()` is the only way out of `unknown` and is a person's action, the sender-honesty line ships OFF. **The identity proof (§21 item 3) still needs one real Lark send** — owner actions: enable `im:message` + `im:message.send_as_user`, publish the app version, register the fixed loopback redirect URI, re-consent in the panel, approve one message into a test chat; the panel then records the platform's attribution and the declaration flips.
- Integration notes: the branch's long CLAUDE.md index lines are slimmed into kb-file-structure / kb-design-lessons §18 (size law); test-ci-gate §9's production-shape fixture no longer uses REPO (a /tmp/vs-* checkout — an integration worktree or the isolated heavy tier — matched the scratch-root rule); test-integrations-ui's Lark leg now expects the wired runner's named no-credential refusal. Suites (all green on the merged tree): test-channels-engine 142, test-channel-outbox 107, test-integration-registry 195, test-channels-gmail-shape 90, test-channels-lark-shape 84, test-channels-push 70, test-channel-filter 66, test-channels-identity 55, test-channels-e2e 93 (heavy), test-integrations-ui 58 (heavy), test-oauth-loopback 39, test-secret-box 40, test-channels-egress 22, test-channels-lane-parity 33, test-channels-agent-cli 19, test-channel-acl 38, test-spend-paths 275, test-architecture 162, test-ci-gate 224.

## 2.369.105 — the heavy release gate in 14 minutes instead of 75: parallel lanes, an impact-scoped push tier with a 24 h full-run net, abandoned-sha supersession, and a writer-sweep suite that walks only its own pids

- Owner (2026-09-15, "heavy gate太占用时间了吧 不能优化一下"): the last full heavy run before this branch took 4472 s — 40 min WAITING on the machine lock behind a run for a sha that had been amended away, then 108 suites strictly sequential. Measured after (the branch's own full run at 0c5ae5e2): **GREEN in 817 s, 110 of 110 suites** — 4 parallel lanes 564 s + the serial lane 251 s, for 2403 s of summed suite time.
- **Parallel lanes** (`laneCount` = clamp(cpus/8, 2, 4), `VIBESPACE_CI_LANES` overrides): longest-first from the previous marker's per-suite timings (table order the first time); every suite `machineGlobalFixtures` flags plus the explicit `SERIAL` table (test-opencode-s9 alone, measured — the opencode store is one per machine) runs in ONE serial lane after the parallel lanes drain; per-suite output is buffered and printed in completion order tagged `[lane N]`; the marker records `lanes`, `serial`, every timing and the wall. Every lane reaps scratch-dir orphans after each suite through `reapScratchOrphansAsync` (the 2.369.104 sweep with its grace awaited, never `Atomics.wait` on the shared event loop).
- **Supersede an abandoned sha**: `--heavy-launch` now supersedes a lock holder whose sha is neither an ancestor of the launched sha nor reachable from any local branch or ANY remote-tracking ref (a live branch tip still waits; a deleted local branch whose origin/<x> still carries it still lives).
- **Impact-scoped push tier**: the pre-push hook hands `--range=<remote>..<local>` (an existing ref) or `<boundary>..<local>` (a new branch — the merge base with every remote-tracking ref, resolved BEFORE the push, because after the pack transfer `git log <sha> --not --remotes` is empty and the tier would have judged two suites for a push full of code); `affectedSuites` selects the suites whose inputs the range touches — the suite file, its transitive import graph, `require(REPO + '/src/x')` / template concatenations, named literals, `reads:` rows, the boot inputs of suites that boot the product — plus every `always: true` row, computed from the tree AT the pushed sha (never the checked-out working tree); the marker records `scope:'affected'` + `selected`; the launcher runs the FULL tier when the newest QUALIFYING full green (complete, same line of history) is older than 24 h (`fullTierDue`, no cron); `--check-heavy` blocks on an affected red exactly like a full red and an affected green clears only the suites it ran; `npm run ci:status` names the last full green and the next tier; `npm run ci:heavy` stays the full tier; `/api/ci-heavy` + the Diagnostics report carry `scope`/`selected`/`lanes`. test-ci-gate §8 censuses that every heavy row without `always`/`reads:` has at least one product input.
- **test-writer-sweep** narrows its /proc and `lsof +D` walks to the pids it spawned (one literal substituted per run copy; §6 keeps ONE whole-box sweep as the positive control): 414 s under a running tier → 12 s standalone, 239 asserts unchanged.
- Verifier findings all fixed with a control each (the 9 heavy suites loading through `require(REPO + '/src/…')` that the graph missed; the graph read from the working tree; the merge hazard with 2.369.104's reaper; `fullTierDue` accepting an all-absent or off-line full green; the new-branch range race; the abandoned-sha rule ignoring remote-tracking refs). Suites: test-ci-gate 224, test-ci-heavy-launch 109 (real lanes with an orphan stub, a real `--affected` tier from another checkout), test-writer-sweep 239, test-opencode-s9 336, test-incident, test-ghost-host-heal 7, test-worktree-userchan-ui 85. After updating, every checkout re-runs `node scripts/install-git-hooks.mjs` (or `npm install`) to pick up the hook.

## 2.369.104 — the gate reaps the scratch-dir orphans it leaves behind, and the delayed auto-resume arm card says "pool switched" instead of "limit reset"

- **Scratch-orphan reaper** (owner 2026-09-16: the box at 86 GB / load 15, the KVM blank): every worktree server a gate suite boots spawns a DETACHED `vibespace-device` daemon the suite's teardown never sees — 504 of them (34.8 GB), 552 scratch node processes and 2,137 orphaned `dtach -a` clients had accumulated. `scratchOrphans` in scripts/ci.mjs is evidence-based: a known executable rooted (cwd / HOME / device root) under a `/tmp/vs-*` scratch dir, reaped only when that dir is gone or every process rooted there is unowned and older than the 10-min stale floor; never a gate runner, never this process's ancestors, never production. Runs after every suite in both tiers, at every heavy launch, and as `node scripts/ci.mjs --reap`. test-ci-gate §8 drives a fake proc root (173).
- **Auto-resume arm card** (owner: "明明没到也没被中断你却提示到达上限了"): a hot pool switch arms a +45 s near-nudge and its delayed announcement said `用量已达上限。已安排在 <now+45s> 重置后自动继续` — a reset instant that was no reset. PURE `armNoticeFor` words the arm by its cause: a switch says `账号池已切换到 <member>，约 N 秒后自动继续这个任务`; only an arm anchored on a real reset says 重置. test-auto-resume-loop pins both wordings + the wiring (208).

## 2.369.103 — Background Work triage: the red badge counts only what nobody has seen, one-shots fold by owner and family, terminal jobs archive on their own clock, held notifications are visible and the ledger says who spent

- Owner (2026-09-14, with a screenshot): one-shot tasks — including every failed one — piled up flat in the Background Work panel and the red badge never went down. Built whole on one branch (design-background-work.md §13, owner-approved defaults 24 h · 7 d · notified = acknowledged), one adversarial pass, one fix pass:
- **Acknowledgement** (PURE `ackState`/`attentionOf`/`agentReadAcks`/`archiveVerdict` in src/job-model.js): a terminal one-shot is acknowledged by a delivery that REACHED somebody (a drained stash counts, a stash does not), by an owner-lineage `poll`/`show`/`logs` (a job's own jbt_ read never), or by the user opening its row (POST /api/jobs/:id/seen); a new run clears it. `ACK_LANES` covers every lane the delivery ladder answers ok:true on — message / channel / rpc-queue / user-inbox / remote-message — with a census leg that goes red when the ladder grows a lane (the verifier found the codex `rpc-queue` lane missing: every codex-owned failure would have stayed red for ever).
- **Badge + folding** (PURE src/lib/jobs-layout.js, shared by the rail badge and both panel summaries): red = awaiting-user + UNACKNOWLEDGED failures, grey "N seen" for the rest; the Tasks section folds by owner session, then by name family, expanded by default only for running / awaiting / unacknowledged rows; the user's folds persist in user state and are pruned to live groups; a failed row shows its exit code and last log line (`run.lastLine`, computed once at finalize, redacted). Measured on the incident's own shape: badge 36 → "19!" (18 unacked + 1 awaiting), 239 one-shots → 8 groups.
- **Archival**: terminal one-shots leave data/jobs.json for the append-only data/jobs-archive.json (newest 2000) on a sweep at boot and every 5 min — done after `jobs.archiveDoneAfterHours` (24), failed/missed/interrupted after `jobs.archiveFailedAfterDays` (7) SINCE THE ACK, never unacknowledged, never a service / cron parent / live pid / open interaction; GET /api/jobs/:id and the agent CLI read an archived id through (`archived:true`, never a 404), `vibespace-job list --archived`, `rm` deletes for good. **The archive is written BEFORE a record leaves the store** — the verifier reproduced the pre-fix order losing 200 records to one failed archive write (EISDIR standing in for ENOSPC/EACCES); a failed write now keeps every record, logs it verbatim, emits `jobs-archive-write-failed` and retries next tick.
- **Held notifications visible** (5b): every stashed notification is TYPED (`held.kind` spend-cap / rate-floor / not-reachable / off, with the slot and ceiling from the ladder's refusal); the digest rides GET /api/jobs and every `jobs-updated` broadcast; the panel summary, the rail tooltip and the affected conversation's status-bar chip say why in the device's own words and clear on drain. data/spend-budget.json stamps become `{at, reason}` (a bare number still loads and counts as `unknown`), and the refusal + 80 % notice name the window's top producers.
- New settings under a Background Work category (zh+ja); suites: test-job-model 145, test-jobs-triage 78 (fast), test-jobs-panel (heavy chrome, 1200×800 + 375×667), test-spend-paths 273; docs: design-background-work.md §13, the agent manual, kb-api/kb-features/kb-file-structure, settings.md.
