## 2.369.99 — a brand-new account's ONE-percent Fable cap was read as a HUNDRED (inc-mu3giy8t-7k36)

- Owner: "刚才刷新刚刚添加的账号不知道为啥突然提示fable用量100%但实际上不是". Mechanism, reproduced from the anchor stream: `src/harnesses/claude-quota.js`'s OAuth/control parser GUESSED the unit of a named `seven_day_<model>` field (`utilization > 1 ? /100 : as-is`) while every sibling branch of the same payload divides by 100 unconditionally — so the vendor's `utilization: 1` (one percent) became 1.0 = 100 %, the pool called the two-minute-old member exhausted, bounced nine conversations off it, and the next ⟳ panel read (1 %) healed it and bounced them back. Measured: all 139 control-source scoped readings on this instance are exact hundredths, none is 0.01, ten are 1.0. FIX = no guess at either site (the overage `spend.pct` twin used `pct <= 1 ? pct*100 : pct`): the unit is the producer's fact. test-quota-source (d): every integer 0..100 maps to n/100, the incident shape is 0.01, the retired rule is the control, and the overage twin holds at 1 / 45 / 0. No data repair owed — the false mark was overwritten by the next panel read; historical anchor rows stamped 1.0 by this rule stay as history.

## 2.369.98 — the unattended-spend defaults are raised to 30/h · 200/day · 800/instance-day (owner, after a real notification stall)

- Owner (c1206711's session, 2026-09-14): "为啥最近几次 background task 没有自动通知而是等我发消息才通知". Not lost — DEFERRED by design: the P4 spend guard's per-slot hourly ceiling (`spend.unattendedPerIdentityHour`, default 12) is shared by EVERY conversation on the same pool target, so one watcher-heavy session plus a sibling session's auto-resumes filled it twice in a day (journal: `[jobs] notify → stashed for <cid> (spend budget: <slot> has spent 12 unattended turns this hour (cap 12))`), and each Background Work notification was stashed until the owner's next prompt. The owner judged 12 too low; the three defaults become **30/h · 200/day per account · 800/day per instance** (`BUDGET_DEFAULTS` + the settings-schema rows + design-account-hardening D6 revised). The day caps move with the hour cap on purpose — 60/day at 30/h was two hours of headroom. Ceilings stay the same money bound they were (per credential slot, across restarts); only the numbers changed. Making a stash VISIBLE and stamping the REASON on each ledger entry are scoped into the Background Work triage batch that follows.
- CLAUDE.md index line for the ceiling essay records the revision; test-spend-paths §1 pins the new numbers (the old 12/60/200 would now be red).

## 2.369.97 — one card per auto-resume, the status bar keeps its context% through a usage wall, and the Desktop button is back (userW's inc-mu1qa5gj-9qe9)

- Owner: "为啥每次续跑会同时发两个续跑通知" — a delivered continue left the labelled "VibeSpace 自动续跑" prompt card AND a second "来自 VibeSpace 的消息 … 已自动继续这个任务" notice card. Now the cause rides the prompt itself (`sendToSession(id, s, text, {note})` → `originNote` on the record for claude, `webui_origin_note` for codex → the card head reads "VibeSpace 自动续跑 — 账号 X 已恢复可用…"), and `announce()` sends no second notice for a delivered continue; the refusal and far-reset sentences, which have no card of their own, still go out. test-auto-resume 223 · test-auto-resume-loop 205 · test-owner-batch-2369-32 38.
- Owner: "用量限制等待续跑的时候状态栏很多东西会消失，比如 context 信息" — the CLI answers a limit/credit rejection with an assistant record whose model is `<synthetic>` and whose usage is all zeros; the normalizer published those zeros as a usage reading and the context% and cache chips (drawn only for a non-zero last input) vanished for the whole wait. A synthetic record is not a measurement: `syntheticUsage(raw)` drops the op in message-manager, `chatStatus` (the attach payload) skips such records when picking `lastUsage`, and `updateUsage` keeps the last real reading when handed an all-zero one.
- userW (2.369.96, inc-mu1qa5gj-9qe9 "找不到右上角的desktop了，Custom UI 也点不开"): the toolbar Desktop button vanished on every page load on a machine WITH a VNC server. `toolbar.showDesktopButton` had been READ by the chrome applier and by customize mode since 2.111.4 but never DECLARED in the settings schema, so `settings.get` answered undefined and any re-apply of chrome settings after the VNC probe hid the button — latent for ~250 releases (it only bit on customize-mode Done) and triggered on every load by 2.369.96's desktop-apps probe, which re-applies chrome settings when it resolves. Reproduced A/B in headless chrome with an Xvnc on PATH (2.369.95 flex, 2.369.96 none); the key is now a declared, default-true row (so the customize toggle also persists), test-architecture §44b censuses every key the chrome applier reads and every customize `hideKey` against the schema, and test-desktop-app-window states the probe outcome and re-applies (with the user-off control). Cluster users: ⚙ → Update.

- **Two mandatory-gate fixes found by this release's own push.** `test-harness-contract`'s fire-choke-point wiring pin scanned a 400-char window that a new comment in auto-resume.js overran (widened to 1200; the pin still names the one reader). And `src/channels/fake.js` spread its records over ONE UTC day, so for the last `1/(count+1)` of every day (2.4 h for the 9-record room) the fake adapter held no future-dated record and `test-channels-engine` ③/③b went red — measured at 21:44Z. The world now spreads over two spans from the day boundary (still restart-stable), and a standing census samples every 5 minutes of the day with the retired spread as its positive control. Third catch: test-new-member-wake read every continue card from `notify`, and the one-card rule now puts the cause on the prompt — its card readers count the carried note too.

## 2.369.96 — generic desktop-app windows (P8-1): any local desktop application as a browser-rendered X11 window, on the vnc-display rung, through one keeper and one ws bridge — four adversarial rounds

- Owner 2026-09-13: "顺便把通用桌面app支持（浏览器based x11渲染啥的）都支持一下，注意维护良好的代码结构确保后续可维护性，组件合理拆分." Spec: docs/design-desktop-apps.zh.md (DA1–DA5 at their recommendation). The module contract is the deliverable: PURE `src/desktop-apps.js` (registry rows, the `DISPLAY_BACKENDS` capability table, `resolveBackend` ladder `xpra > vnc-display > desktop-singleton` with every fallback reasoned, the session state machine, the shared keeper constants in `src/keeper-limits.js` which opencode-serve now reads too); SHARED `src/desktop-display.js` (binary probes, `-displayfd` display allocation, Xauthority, the RFB banner read-probe, window enumeration for P9, frozen `RECIPES` per rung); ORCH `src/server/desktop-app-keeper.js` (launch / adopt by pid+starttime / count cap / runaway guard over the whole process SESSION / idle stop from real RFB input / stop verified empty, every part stamped `VIBESPACE_DESKTOP_APP=<id>`), `src/server/desktop-stream.js` (the ONE cookie-authed ws bridge `/api/desktop/:id/stream`; the old `/api/vnc` bridge now calls it), `src/routes/desktop-apps.js` (`host` a parameter, non-local refused by name); CLIENT `src/lib/vnc-view.js` (the shared noVNC picture component extracted from desktop-window.js, DPI counter-zoom kept byte-for-byte), `src/lib/desktop-app-window.js` (window type `desktop-app`, status bar naming the rung and its fallback reason, idle countdown, Stop), `src/lib/desktop-app-launcher.js` (⚙ → Desktop apps…, registry list / run a command / recents). A new rung = one table row + one recipe + one relay, proven by a fourth rung driven end to end with the keeper untouched. xpra is probed and recorded (P8-2 wires it); the fleet Dockerfile gains the package.
- Four rounds (18 findings, each reproduced on the real keeper with Xvfb + x11vnc before its fix; the full record is kb-bugfix-invariants): a picture-server spawn failure no longer crashes the server; the picture PORT is a measured fact (x11vnc silently autoports and keeps the number on `[::1]`, so the 127.0.0.1 LISTEN inode must belong to the session); a session is a SET (leaders detached, the env marker inherited, stop = group + every member + a marker census, the guard samples the whole set incl. reaped children and setsid'd escapees); the bridge counts INPUT only for RFB input messages with a stateful sieve whose lengths are DERIVED from noVNC (a wrong fixed length for message 150 silently misaligned it); a stop landing anywhere inside the bring-up captures the in-flight promise first and tears down after it settles; a null starttime is "no evidence", never a licence to signal a recycled pid; the singleton desktop's liveness is re-asked before every verdict. Stated boundary: without a readable /proc a setsid'd member is recorded as ended but left running.
- Measured here: a session = 3 processes / 87 MB (xmessage) to 279 MB (gnome-calculator), ready in ~400–450 ms; marker census 46–51 ms per /proc walk over ~3,800 pids. Gates: test-desktop-apps 123 · test-desktop-display 72 · test-vnc-view 49 (fast); test-desktop-app-keeper 155 · test-desktop-app-window (heavy, real Xvfb/x11vnc/chrome); test-architecture 143; server.js 2082 lines.

## 2.369.94 — Communication panel P0a: the channels CORE (store, capability model, adapter contract, fake adapter, engine skeleton, rail + panel + window) — five adversarial rounds, no real adapter yet

- Owner green-light 2026-09-13 on docs/design-communication-panel.zh.md (every §20 decision at its recommendation). This slice ships the SHARED persistence (`src/channel-store.js`: append-only per-conversation message logs, ONE serialized index owner, date-rolled audit archive, retention with a caller), the PURE record + capability model (`src/channel-record.js`, `src/channel-caps.js`: `laneState`/`scanState`/`freshnessClaim`/`identityWarning`/`authState` as STRUCTURE the client renders in the device's language), the adapter registry + contract with a FAKE adapter covering all three receive modes and both scan sources (`src/channels/`), the ingest engine skeleton (`src/server/channels-engine.js`, wired through `src/server/channels-wiring.js`; the backend-status route stanza moved to `src/server/backend-status-route.js` to keep server.js inside its ratchet: 2099 → 2084 lines), the routes (`src/routes/channels.js`, `host` a parameter on every one), the six rail registrations, the panel list with freshness chips, an empty conversation window, and `RESERVED_CONTRIBUTIONS.channelAdapters`. Nothing talks to a vendor; Lark/Gmail adapters and the §14 integration-credentials layer are P0b/P1.
- Five rounds, every finding reproduced on the shipped bytes before its fix and pinned with a patched-copy control (the full record is in kb-file-structure under `src/channel-store.js` / `src/server/channels-engine.js`): the dedup set remembers a vendorId only after its bytes are durable (r2); paging is the total order `(at, vendorId)` (r2); `adapters.json` has the same single owner as the index (r2); a route may not mint an index row (r2); "read" means the newest record and a derived value never broadcasts a no-op (r2); the server sends structure and the client says the words (r2); the scan lane ingests only through a lane its own resolver resolves (r3); a truncated final line is SEALED before the log grows (r3); history beyond one 2 MiB window seeks backward (r3); tracking broadcasts even over budget (r3); the chip says "not polling" on untracked rows (r3); window titles go through `wm.setTitle` (r3); a FAILED append drops the cached dedup set — the log is the only witness to what a failed write landed (r4); and the dedup REBUILD refuses a log it cannot read — `readTail(…, {strict:true})` at the one reader whose answer writes bytes, so EMFILE/EIO/EACCES fail the pass with the anchor unmoved instead of caching an empty set and writing a replayed page twice for ever (r5).
- Gates (fast tier unless noted): test-channel-record 37 · test-channel-caps 81 · test-channel-store 124 · test-channels-engine 82 · test-channel-adapter-contract 90 · test-channels-e2e 50 (heavy: worktree server + chrome + SIGKILL/reboot) · test-architecture 145 · test-window-types (the `winInfo.setTitle` census). ## 2.369.93 — the Fable-cap pool storm: placement follows the REQUEST model (a safety-classifier fallback never redefines it), a Fable-cap rejection marks the Fable cap and not the plan week, and a healthy member is never "no member can serve it" (inc-mtzcj5sl-lzmw)

- Owner: "账号切换似乎出问题了，明明有账号有 fable 额度但是总是提示没有了" — the owner's locked-to-`fable[1m]` conversation was bounced across four pool members in three minutes (04:58–05:01Z), rejected on each with "You've reached your Fable limit", while Member P — the only member with Fable left — sat unused. Three defects, each reproduced on the real engine + real pool + real credential symlinks + the real stdout consumer over the incident's own caches, then fixed with a patched-copy pre-fix control: **①** at 04:42Z Fable 5.1's safeguards rerouted the conversation to `claude-opus-4-8` (a `fallback` content block, then a `model_refusal_fallback` record); `sessionModelFor` let the newer fallback-served model outrank both the model LOCK and the pick, so the pool projected the OPUS family, dropped the Fable bucket, and EDF moved the session onto Member F (plan 7d 17 % left, Fable 100 % spent). The model ladder is now LOCK > pick > spawn > served-only-if-not-a-fallback; the placement family (`projectionFamilyFor`) is null while a reroute stands — the requested and the substituted model can both refuse, so every bucket counts; the reroute stamp (`_servedViaFallback`) is persisted in session-meta and restored, and it is stamped BEFORE the served-model reader and the target-less lock latch run on the very record that announces it (the CLI's first announcement rides the assistant message whose own model is already the substitute, 51 s before the system record) at both consumers. **②** claude 2.1.267's `rate_limit_event` vocabulary has no `seven_day_fable` (measured: five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_overage_included, seven_day_sonnet, seven_day_opus, seven_day_oauth_apps), so a Fable-cap rejection arrives as an unscoped `seven_day` and only the banner names the model; the wall machine demoted BOTH lanes, marking the PLAN week of Member W (65 %), Member Q (70 %) and Member F (83 %) as 100 % spent for 12–60 h and bouncing the opus conversations along. A rejected unscoped `seven_day` is now provisional for its turn — the banner decides the lane, no banner ⇒ the slot's own evidence (plan clearly alive + the request family's cap ≥ 99 % ⇒ the cap), settled at `result` or at the session's teardown, drops counted. **③** on a HOT pool the proactive scan returned `no-members` beside a healthy current member (no better target), and the engine warned "no member can serve it — out of quota (still available: 5h 84%, 7d 67%, Fable 42%)" every ten minutes — the numbers were the current member's own; that is now `no-better` (silent), and a genuinely blocked pool names the band that blocks it (`spent:` / `nearly spent:` / `still available:`). Data: the three false plan-7d walls healed by themselves on the auto-cli panel reads at 05:35–05:41Z (37–41 min of false exhaustion each); no migration.
- Four adversarial rounds; test-fable-cap-pool-storm (277, fast tier, fixture = the incident's own frozen record with the owner's fields stripped), test-stdout-registry 255, test-session-brain-dark 4, test-pool-auto 83, test-account-verdicts 45, test-readings-attribution 446, test-auto-resume 222/205, test-new-member-wake 119, test-quota-model 299, test-spend-paths 261. Essay: kb-bugfix-invariants "THE FABLE-CAP POOL STORM".

## 2.369.92 — the usage ledger says WHO spent it: main conversation, subagent, or workflow agent (origin on every event; "By project" is the repo an agent worked FOR)

- Owner: "vibespace 和 platform-dev 把 7 个账号全吃完了… 能不能按 session 拆成主会话 / subagent / workflow?" — a request's usage is mined from three kinds of transcript and the ledger event could not say which, because all three attribute to the PARENT session id (2.265.0). Now every walked event carries `origin` (`main` / `subagent` / `workflow` / `unknown` — stamped on EVERY row, never "missing means main", so the backfill can answer `unknown` honestly about a row whose transcript is gone) plus `wf` (workflow run id) and `agent` (agent file stem). An agent event's `cwd` is the PARENT PROJECT's, with the agent's own directory kept as `wcwd` only when it differs: 272 of this instance's 3,155 agent transcripts ran in git worktrees and each was its own "By project" row. A codex rollout is `main` by RULE (the codex store already merges sub-agent rollouts into the parent thread's read). The shipped `data/bin/vibespace-usage-scan` mirrors the walk, parity-pinned.
- The project cwd is VERIFIED, not guessed: a conversation's cwd is not constant (3 of 782 top-level transcripts here state more than one), and one rename filed **$7,828** of the biggest spender's agent cost under `…/claude-code-webui`, a path that no longer exists, in a second row beside its own main spend. `makeProjectCwdReader` matches the project DIRECTORY NAME (the forward encoding of the cwd, kb-design-lessons §5) against the head window → tail window → the conversation's most recent cwd → a sibling transcript; bounded 128 KiB windows, memoized. The same reader drives the backfill, so there is no third copy.
- Usage window: a "By origin" group first in the cost section (stacked bar + a row per origin), "By session" gains main / subagents / workflows columns with a per-row share bar, "By project" hover names the split; `origin` is a panel dimension and a splitBy; the default overview preset ships a cost-by-origin donut + a session × origin panel. "Unattributed" is rendered whenever it has spend. The route's pivot cap moves 6 → 8 (the window now asks for two crosses beside the panel dashboard's own). zh + ja.
- One-shot backfill (migration `2026-09-usage-origin-backfill`, `src/usage-origin-backfill.js` through the shared runner): names every existing row from ONE walk of the transcript tree, archives each shard verbatim under `data/archive/usage-origin-backfill-<day>/` before rewriting it atomically, keeps unparseable lines verbatim, removes nothing, idempotent; `server.js` re-reads the event cache after migrations (the cache only reads appended tails, so a shard rewritten in place was invisible to a warm one). Measured on a COPY of this instance: 12 shards, 506,107 rows in and out; main 360,707 / workflow 78,053 / subagent 14,270 / unknown 53,077 (27,837 remote-host rows carry their own origin from the next harvest; 25,240 local rows' transcripts are rotated away); 34,587 rows re-attributed off an agent's own directory; 8,706 transcripts / 3.88 GB walked in 31.8 s, once, at boot. Last 7 days here: workflow $9,142 (58.9 %) / main $6,282 (40.5 %) / subagent $88.54 (0.6 %) — the top conversation is 72 % agents.
- Gates: test-usage-origin (29, new, fast tier), test-usage-walk-parity 53 (rename + tail-window shapes over both spellings, "first cwd wins" mutation verified red), test-migrations 42, test-fixture-isolation, test-usage-events-push, test-usage-scan-op, test-codex-history. Adversarially verified (ok, three non-blocking notes filed in the backlog: sibling-transcript fallback takes the first match; the window requests both pivots unconditionally, +76 % payload on All time; a transient read failure during the backfill stamps `unknown` yet marks the migration applied).

## 2.369.91 — the reference prices know Fable 5.1 (cache hits $0.25/MTok, not $1) and Sonnet 5 ($2/$10)

- Owner: "完成同样的任务 opus 真的比 fable 便宜吗?" — the first thing the ledger got wrong: `DEFAULT_PRICING` had ONE `fable` tier with the Fable 5 cache-hit rate ($1/MTok), while Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 price cache hits at 0.025× base input = **$0.25/MTok** (official pricing page, 2026-09). On this instance that overstated seven days of Fable by 38 % (the main session is cache-heavy). Now `fable-5-1` and `sonnet-5` ($2/$10, cache hit $0.20 — the launch price became the standard price) are their own tiers; the matcher already prefers the longest key, so `claude-fable-5` stays on the Fable 5 rate; an existing `data/usage-history/pricing.json` gains the new keys on load without clobbering edited rates, and the pricing token changes so memoised costs recompute.
- test-pricing-tiers (10). Measured with the corrected table: opus-agent requests here are 78 % cache-read by cost; the same requests on Fable 5.1 (cache hits half the price, output tokens ~58 % fewer per an independent benchmark) would cost ~19 % less per request before any reduction in request count — the answer to the owner's question is "not for cache-heavy agent work; measure it".

## 2.369.90 — the "For you" inbox keeps every row in its slot while open (inc-mtw02kbq-kj96: "点击对勾后…位置变化…连续点击时造成误点")

- Every ✓ triggered a `user-todos-updated` broadcast, the popup re-rendered from scratch, the resolved row left its group and the rows below slid up under the pointer — four rapid clicks at one screen position resolved four different items. While the popup is OPEN its layout is now append-only (PURE `src/lib/user-todos-layout.js`): a resolved row stays in its slot, dimmed and struck through with ↺, a fully-resolved group keeps its slot, new items append at the end of their group, and the ordinary sorted order is rebuilt on the next open. The group count shows open rows only; the "Recently resolved" tail no longer lists a row still holding its slot above.

## 2.369.89 — a chat file path ends at Chinese punctuation (owner screenshot: `…/designs/（浏览器` became the link)

- The path linkifier stopped only at ASCII punctuation, so a fullwidth "（" (and ，。：；！？“”「」【】《》…—) glued onto the link and the click opened nothing. The rule now lives in ONE PURE module, `src/path-linkify.js` (imports nothing; the renderer delegates `pathRe`/`cleanPath` to it): CJK **punctuation** terminates a path, CJK **letters** and fullwidth digits/letters stay linkable (`/home/u/文档/报告.md` still links), ASCII behaviour (`:line:col`, trailing `)`/`.`) unchanged, and `cleanPath` strips CJK trailing punctuation from URLs too.
- test-path-linkify (14): the owner's exact case, CJK filenames, curly/corner/lenticular brackets, the pre-fix rule as a negative control (it reproduces the swallow), and wiring pins (the renderer carries no local copy; URLs and `/p/<id>` pages are linkified BEFORE paths).

## 2.369.88 — session discovery stops forking a child per session (inc-mtunmv3d-pmd6, fleet userW: "重启筛选之后白屏")

- **The incident.** After "Restart now to apply (Terminate + Resume)" the chat window stayed blank for ~30 s, and on that pod EVERY session create and EVERY kill — chat or plain terminal — was followed by an 11–17 s event-loop freeze of the whole instance (7-day log: 27 of 27). Forensics on the pod: 61 lock files, tmux not installed, server 1.6 GB / 107 threads.
- **The mechanism.** `child_process.spawn()` blocks the parent for fork()'s page-table copy, proportional to the parent's RSS — measured 0.6 ms at 45 MB, 27 ms at 550 MB, **69 ms at 1.55 GB**. Session discovery paid it per SESSION: `tmux list-panes -a` (fails where tmux is absent ⇒ empty map) ⇒ `ps -p <pid> -o ppid=` per lock file ⇒ `pgrep -P` per live session every 15 s, and `refreshWebuiPids()` ran a SYNCHRONOUS `pgrep -P` per session on every create, kill and boot. "Making the exec async" in 2.235 fixed the wait, never the fork.
- **The fix.** Zero spawns per session on Linux: ppid and children come from `/proc/<pid>/stat` / `/proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/children` through the ONE process reader (src/cli-identity.js: `readPpid`, `readChildPids`, `pidsMatchingCmdline`), `ps`/`pgrep` only where /proc is absent and then ONCE per sweep; the tmux map is skipped without a spawn when no tmux binary is on PATH; the kill path's `pgrep -f <socket>` became a /proc cmdline scan. Measured, 61 locks + 61 sessions at 1.55 GB: one sweep **9,160 ms → 1.6 ms**; kill-path lookup latency 155 → 24 ms.
- **The gate.** test-discovery-spawn (65: spawn census per sweep with pre-fix negative controls, the shipped kill-path body run against master's bytes) + test-architecture §45 (a standing per-site spawn census over the sweep facts, keyed on the TOOL name so a promisified alias cannot smuggle the shape back). Three adversarial rounds (r1 found the refreshWebuiPids twin, r2 found the alias-blind census).
- The suite's pre-fix negative controls read a PINNED sha (9516bd8d = 2.369.87), not `master` — the first push of this release went red the moment the fix merged (the 2.369.85 lesson, second strike; `VIBESPACE_DISCOVERY_PREFIX_REF` overrides).
- Follow-ups parked in B-9428 (server RSS as the multiplier; the remaining O(1)-per-sweep spawns; `procArgv`'s `ps` fallback is reachable once per lock on a procfs box when a lock carries no numeric procStart).

## 2.369.87 — the wire probe's positive control skips with evidence on a session-less machine (gate-only)

- test-stdout-registry asserted that discovery "still lists this machine's real sessions" — a claim about the runner's home, not about the reader: the GitHub Actions runner has no claude sessions at all, so the fast mirror job was RED on 2.369.85/.86 for a positive control that could not be measured there. It now asks `~/.claude/projects` for a non-fixture project dir carrying a transcript first: none ⇒ a loud SKIP naming the directory; one or more ⇒ the same assert as before (locally: 4979 sessions listed over 17 real project dirs). The guard legs beside it are unchanged.

## 2.369.86 — quota model v2: an account holds a LIST of limits, ONE write path owns the store, and a rejection is a reading too

- **Typed limits per identity (B-9213).** codex pushes a SEPARATE `rate_limits_updated` per limit — on one conversation here: the plan 32×, GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark 149×, `premium` 27× — and every push was flattened into one `{fiveHour, sevenDay, scopedWeekly[]}` file, last writer wins, so the panel read 0 % on an account at 5 %. Every identity now holds a `LimitSet` keyed by `limitId` (src/quota-model.js, PURE); the old shape is a PROJECTION of it; migration `2026-09-backfill-quota-limits` lifts the existing cache files once (archive-never-destroy).
- **ONE write path** (src/usage-cache-write.js) replaces nine producers with nine merge policies. A producer stamps `source`/`fetchedAt` only on what it MEASURED (one 5-hour event no longer re-labels the Fable cap "via own session, just now"), and only a parse that enumerated the WHOLE set may retire a model cap — stated by the parser, never inferred from a non-empty array.
- **The wall rule runs at every write (inc-mttbrtc0-6049, B-8048).** A rejection is a reading: the window it names decides which member it is filed on, including the per-RECORD rejection write that used to bypass the guard (the incident's foreign 5-hour wall landing on the turn-pinned member, then the pool "escaping" to the member that had just refused). A weekly window's refutation is decisive, a 5-hour one corroborates.
- **Empty and reset-less windows count (B-8b12).** A `usedPercent 0` window's reset slides with the clock (`now + duration`), so it is never the earliest deadline and never arms auto-resume — but its stated 0 % IS headroom; a stated spend WITHOUT a reset is decisive instead of 'unknown' (which dropped the bucket and let the pool keep spending on a refused member).
- **Composition fix (merge verifier, HIGH).** The codex global↔named same-account merge now carries the typed set with the winner — the loser's file would otherwise have held its stale limits beneath the winner's `fetchedAt`, and the freshness guard would then have refused every correction for good.
- Six adversarial rounds + a merge composition verify + a targeted re-verify of the fix. Owning suites: test-quota-model 299 (new) · test-readings-attribution 445 · test-spend-paths 261 · test-auto-resume 222 · test-auto-resume-loop 205 · test-new-member-wake 119 · test-quota-source 112 · test-codex-pool 61 · test-rate-limit-capture 46 · test-migrations 29; fast + heavy tiers green on the merge. Follow-ups parked as B-9f4b.

## 2.369.85 — test fixtures stop being production data (owner: "e2e00000-… 这东西是个啥玩意啊 你浪费我的token干啥呢")

- **The sweep tolerates a run in flight** (round 3): an undeclared fixture dir younger than the staleness threshold — one a concurrent older checkout may still be using, which nothing in the tree is allowed to delete — is spared and NAMED instead of reddening every other worktree's pre-push gate on a box with ~160 checkouts; it becomes litter the moment it goes stale (negative control: the same dir back-dated 15 min ⇒ red with the remedy).

## 2.369.83 — the queue strip tells the truth across a restart (a message that had already run stayed in the strip, red, "no longer queued")

- **After any (re)attach the queue strip's rows come from the WRAPPER, not from the client's memory or a rebuilt normalizer's guess.** A restart rebuilds the server's normalizer from the transcript, which holds no queue events at all, so the attach payload carried an empty queue while the client kept the rows it had; the wrapper had emptied its queue an hour earlier. Now the attach payload says whether the server is GUESSING (`queueKnown:false`), the server asks the running wrapper to republish its queue (an empty answer included — gated on the wrapper's own verb table, so a pre-verb wrapper is never asked), and the client shows no row nobody can act on until the answer lands.
- **The restart payload is judged by when it ARRIVED, not by when the staggered view reset got round to applying it** (round 2): a deferred `_fullViewReset` used to apply the placeholder 0–500 ms late and overwrite the republished answer — a genuinely queued message vanished in a window that stayed open across the restart. Round 3 gave the queue ADVERT the same recency rule as the rows (the last surviving race).
- **A `gone` verdict removes the row** (the wrapper is authoritative about absence) instead of painting it refused; a re-attach never preserves a strip the server no longer knows; a later `queue_changed` outranks any earlier verdict (the race the verifier asked about).
- test-queue-steer 840 (headless chrome: queue → steer → restart the worktree server with the wrapper surviving → re-attach ⇒ empty strip within the round trip; pre-fix controls keep the row) · test-codex-p2-wrapper 401 · test-harness-contract 316. Test hygiene: every patched copy the suite writes beside src/lib/chat-view.js is gitignored and PID-swept (`.chat-view.*prefix-*.js`).

## 2.369.82 — a restored session streams again without anybody typing (the 05:20Z restart: "运行中" for eight minutes until the first keystroke)

- **The boot-time dtach attach OBSERVES the daemon's answer.** attachToDtach's device path resolved as soon as the `open-session` frame was written and never awaited `handle.ready`, so an open the daemon never completed (this restart: the local daemon was self-upgrading 2.369.75→.77 under the restore) was a silently dead pty — no journal line, session still "live", and the only healer was the broken-stdin detector that runs on USER INPUT. Now: `ready` raced against 5 s (measured open→ready 2–11 ms) ⇒ local pty fallback with a journal line naming the session and the reason; a late `ready` kills its handle so two dtach clients never relay one session.
- **Boot ordering:** the daemon path is taken only when the link is ALREADY connected; a restore attaches locally in the same tick (the onExit re-attach ladder still takes the daemon later). Chosen over "connect first" (puts the ~40 s spawn + upgrade in front of every restore) and over "migrate after routing ENABLED" (a second blind window on a bridge that is already relaying).
- **A liveness probe that READS, never writes:** `dtach -a … -r winch` emits its redraw preamble within milliseconds even when the program inside is silent, so a healthy attach always produces a byte (both transports measured). 4 s + a 600 ms confirm stage; device-silent heals (bounded at 2 consecutive, reset by any byte), local-silent only warns. A probe LINE was rejected on measurement: the chat wrapper forwards an unknown line to the CLI = a billed turn, and restored sessions run the previous release's wrapper by construction.
- **ONE healer:** `reattachLocalPty` is the product's only local re-attach (ws-handler's detector lost its private copy); one liveness fact `_lastPtyDataAt` stamped first in setupSessionPty; the daemon shim holds a listener SET (a single slot silently dropped the second registration) and buffers bytes that legally arrive before `ready`.
- scripts/test-restore-liveness.mjs (59, heavy): fault matrix against a REAL daemon (healthy / refuses / never answers / relays nothing) each with a pre-fix control; an end-to-end restart with a real daemon at version 0.0.1 so the self-upgrade + re-exec runs under the restore, the incident's dead-channel fault, a real ws client and ZERO input. Follow-ups B-ae4b (two other single-slot pty ducks, comment wording).

## 2.369.81 — account hardening P4, the spend half: ONE ceiling on every turn nobody typed (owner directive "不正确就是浪费真金白银"; five adversarial rounds + a verified merge)

- **A spend authorizer in front of EVERY unattended-turn producer** — auto-resume continues, Background Work notifications, agent peer messages, the Stop bookkeeping nudge, the codex reset credit (five producers, found by a grep-derived per-SITE census that fails the build on a sixth without a gate above it). PURE `src/spend-authorizer.js` + ORCH `src/server/spend-guard.js`, constructed inside the pool engine so its identity is the engine's own credential-slot answer, never a fifth derivation. Owner-typed turns are never counted (the human ws input path is asserted ungated).
- **Defaults, all settings in a new "Spending" category (zh+ja):** 12 unattended turns per identity per hour, 60 per identity per day, 200 per instance per day, a "For you" notice at 80 %. Measured on this instance's whole corpus (603 Stop-nudge mini-turns over two months, peaks of 93/day and 21 on one conversation in one hour): the ceiling refuses 20–55 of them — a backstop against bursts and loops, not a routine throttle.
- **Overage gating (D3):** while a member's `overage.inUse` is true the authorizer refuses all unattended spend on it (a human turn still runs); both quota panels say "paid overage in use — $x of $y" from the same PURE verdict; a default-OFF setting keeps the pool from choosing such a member voluntarily. Codex's `spendControlReached` now has a reader too (a spent window, refused as `spend-control-reached`, chip on both panels).
- **EDF reserve floor (D2):** `decidePoolSwitch` keeps 15 % of the WEEKLY budget in reserve (never measured on an unknown reading); escapes from a hard-dead member ignore it and say which bar they landed on. **Stop nudge (D8):** cooldown persisted, under the authorizer, plus `agents.stopNudgeMaxUnanswered` = 3.
- **Money gates fail CLOSED at all three layers** (the wiring's, auto-resume's, the delivery ladder's): a thrown or rejected pre-fire gate refuses with a named reason + `spend-gate-error` telemetry; master's trailing `.catch(() => deliver())` used to answer a throw inside deliver() by delivering AGAIN.
- **The turn is charged to the identity it was AUTHORIZED against** (round 4): the delivery ladder re-resolved the slot at charge time, up to 120 s after the authorize on the rpc rung, so a pool re-point in between let the authorized account bypass its cap while a never-asked account was debited. Every producer now carries the verdict's identity; an unhinted charge is counted and journalled.
- **Authorize = reserve** (round 5): a hold (`pendingCounts`, 3-min TTL > the ladder's 120 s settle window) counts against the caps until the charge converts it or the ladder gives it back at ONE `finally`; five concurrent deliveries on one slot at cap 2 used to all pass. The pre-gate probe is the only non-holding call (census). **The persisted ledger is pruned at boot with a retention no configured cap can under-count** (the guard is built before the settings reader; a 500-stamp day under a 500 cap used to come back holding 264).
- **The "Spending" settings category is RENDERED** — `SETTINGS_CATEGORIES` is the settings UI's render loop, so seven new rows plus three OpenCode rows that had been invisible since they shipped never reached the screen; test-architecture §44 now fails the build if any schema row lacks a rendered section.
- **Merged onto the generic auto-resume edge (.78) as ONE fire choke point** — breaker → async pre-fire gate (veto held per wall) → spend authorize (holding, on the identity the gate landed on) → the harness's resume verb → on delivery noteFired + edgeSpent + noteSpend(hold) + one journal line; on a failed send or a missing verb the hold goes back and the arm survives. The merge itself was adversarially verified as a composition (one info note: giveBack legs, B-59b8).
- test-spend-paths 261 · test-auto-resume 221 · test-auto-resume-loop 203 · test-new-member-wake 119 · test-architecture 108 · fast tier ALL GREEN (277 s) on the merged tree. Design record: docs/design-account-hardening.md §1.4 per-field, P8/P9 rewritten, P4 status.

## 2.369.78 — auto-resume after a usage limit is GENERIC over every harness (owner ruling 2026-09-08: "只要支持 hook/注入的 harness 都支持, 形式可以不一样")

- **Two descriptor hooks, one harness-neutral core.** How a LIMIT shows up is the descriptor's `quota.signalFromStream` (claude-quota / codex-quota; null for shell); how a TURN is restarted is the new `descriptor.resume` verb — claude = a user message on the wrapper's chat-input, codex = the wrapper rpc lane's `turn/start` (the same lane conversation-deliver already uses, origin kind 'resume', no second injector), opencode/ACP = the agent's session prompt, shell = null. The capability `backend-caps.autoResume {signal, resume}` is DERIVED from what the descriptor implements — a harness cannot be offered the toggle or armed without both hooks (the codex thread that sat idle 32 h past its weekly reset is the incident: the codex consumer never armed anything). Session Properties / settings / the engine / the module all gate on that row, never on a backend id (source census). Same semantics everywhere: arm at the signal's reset (+ grace), the 90 s false-positive delay, announce, disarm on work, the loop breaker, hourly cap, same-identity quarantine, restart survival; codex's reset-credit rung stays first; a machine login with no pool arms and fires like a pooled session.
- **The FRESH-WINDOW edge (PURE src/auto-resume-signal.js): a reading that says the armed window is open fires NOW** — with three adversarial rounds of money discipline behind it. Round 1's edge re-fired three billed continues per hour for the life of a watch (measured [3,3,3,3] over four simulated hours while the CLI kept refusing); since round 2 a reading may buy ONE turn per wall (`edgeSpent`, stamped at DELIVERY, cleared only by proof of work), `spendControlReached` refuses, and the breaker suites now DRIVE the new producer (removing the caps turns both red). Round 3: the production pre-fire gate is async, so its return value is not an outcome — the journal line about a continue is written where the continue is delivered (1:1 by construction), a gate veto is recorded at the point of knowledge with a BOUNDED 10-min per-wall hold (`edgeHeld`: ~225 gate runs/h → 6 at the incident's own push rate), and the breaker's pruner learned the hold (it deleted it at every hour boundary). Verifier's "resetsAt must have rolled" rule was rejected by measurement (316 distinct weekly resets on this instance's codex stream, one wall spelled two ways).
- Residual by design: a reading-driven continue that the CLI refuted re-opens only on proof of work, the far reset, a user prompt, or a new wall. `credits.hasCredits:false` is deliberately NOT read as spent (this instance's login reports it while serving turns). P4's spend authorizer (still in verify) goes on the ONE fire choke point in `deliver()`.
- test-auto-resume 221 · test-auto-resume-loop 203 · test-harness-contract 306 · test-new-member-wake 119.
- **test-stdout-registry's binary-dump asserts match the SHAPE, not one build's minifier names.** `Oe.status` / `n.onInProgressToolUseIDs?.(e.op)` were 2.1.257's local identifiers; the Actions runner installs the current CLI and its minifier picked other letters, so the fast mirror was red on every push while green here. The property chains are now matched with the identifier as a wildcard (251/251 on 2.1.263).

## 2.369.76 — gate suites stop claiming machine-global names (heavy tier RED on 40ad936d: two runs of test-chat-paging destroyed each other)

- **Every gated suite now uses per-process scratch paths and free ports** (`scripts/scratch.mjs`: `scratch(name)` = `/tmp/vs-<name>-<pid>`, `freePorts(n)` holds every listener until all are chosen). The heavy tier went red on 2.369.75's commit because a verifier agent ran test-chat-paging from its own checkout while the heavy tier ran it too: both claimed `/tmp/vs-chatpage-smoke` + the chrome profile dir + :3990, one run's `git worktree remove --force` deleted the other's tree mid-esbuild, and the retry's `worktree add` hit the path the other had just recreated. The heavy tier's machine lock serialises HEAVY RUNS only — a process that never takes the lock (a verifier, a developer's local run) is not covered by it, so the fix is a name nobody shares. 28 suites rewritten (fixed `/tmp/vs-*` literals, fixed `PORT`/`CDP_PORT`, the `3951 + pid % 20` form = a 1-in-20 collision with two suites sharing a range). 2.369.46 had fixed ONE instance inline (test-chat-e2e :3995); third strike ⇒ shared idiom.
- **The §6 machine-global scan in test-ci-gate covers BOTH tiers** (it scanned fast-tier suites only; the collision was in the heavy tier). A new suite with a fixed port or `/tmp` path fails the fast gate.
- **Live proof**: six heavy suites run concurrently — the same suite twice among them — all green (recorded in the commit message).
- **inc-mttbrtc0-6049 diagnosed, not yet fixed (folded into the quota-model-v2 work, B-8048):** the pool re-pointed a session's credential link twice inside one turn; the CLI's next request used the new member's token and was rejected with THAT member's 5h window ("resets 8:30pm"); `demoteWalledAccount` attributed the rejection to the turn-pinned slot (the member at turn start) and wrote the foreign window into its cache (`source:'wall'`, no window check) — the panel showed the wrong reset until a manual refresh, and a usable member was demoted 3 h on another member's wall. A rejection is a reading and must take the same window-first attribution as values.

## 2.369.75 — a member that becomes usable wakes the pool (owner 2026-09-08 02:18: "添加了个新账号, 似乎没有自动刷新出用量信息, 我手动刷新后也没自动切换+唤醒之前停滞的任务")

- **A member becoming usable is an EVENT, not a state somebody polls.** Login success (relogin-finalize / subscription finalize incl. the auto-merge exit / codex device-auth) reads that member's usage once through the existing rung and re-drives every pool it belongs to; a manual ⟳ refresh that lands a fresh reading does the same; sessions armed on exhaustion fire at once through the existing auto-resume path (breaker, hourly cap and quarantine intact). A member whose credentials do not exist yet is 'not ready' — the auto-cli loop no longer burns its failure backoff on it (the 02:18:40 failure that left "no usage data" for 17 minutes). The cold-restart gate reads the caps-gated verdict, so a codex pool (hot switch impossible) never gets a continue delivered into a CLI that cannot re-read credentials; the finalize route wakes the record that will still exist after an auto-merge; the panel refresher refuses to write a cache or window sidecar for a record removed while its panel ran, and the refresh route stops there instead of spending a sibling's token. Three adversarial rounds. test-new-member-wake 119 (new gate suite), test-auto-resume-loop 191.

Every usage-cache key of an identity is seeded with a `.window-<key>` sidecar and repaired, including the machine login `__global__` (same identity as its subscription); the machine login's SECOND persisted snapshot, `data/usage-cache.json`, is judged too (archived and unlinked when foreign — the product re-seeds it from the repaired directory) and, because `setupUsage()` had already loaded it before migrations run, server.js now calls `reloadRateLimitCache()` right after the runner so the repair reaches the running process. ## 2.369.73 — the 93% misfiling after a pool hot switch (inc-mts8a8mr-ulmm): a reading is evidence about itself

- **Window-fingerprint attribution (PURE `src/reading-lag.js`, four adversarial rounds).** After a pool re-point the sessions' in-flight responses still carry the PREVIOUS member's numbers; on 2026-09-08 one such response filed Member Y's 93% under Member P (13%) and the pool cascaded two false switches in 100 s. Now the weekly window a payload names (its `resetsAt` phase, an org property, ±120 s jitter) outranks our bookkeeping: after a re-point a reading carrying the previous slot's window is the previous slot's (the LAG SHADOW; the first reading matching the new slot ends it), a reading whose weekly window contradicts the target member's own established window is never written to it (re-filed to the one member it matches, else archived with a reason), and the clock bound sits BELOW the window evidence (an unknown re-point age never expires). The five-hour bucket is not identity evidence (47 reset values are shared across identities; measured). Each member's established window lives in a `data/usage-cache/.window-<key>` sidecar, not in the cache object every producer rebuilds. The statusline tool mirrors the rule byte-for-byte, dates the re-point from the credential link's own mtime (the pool mints a new symlink), runs the guard inside its write sentinels and records refusals in `.window-refused.ndjson`. Pool decisions never consume a shadowed or contradicting reading; the incident is replayed against the real engine + pool + symlinks + the shipped tool's bytes with the pre-fix ordering as the negative control. test-readings-attribution 340 (+146).
- **Deferred:** the one-shot repair of the ~475 historically misfiled anchors ships in the next release under a new migration id; its cache half must first cover every key in an identity (`__global__` shares its subscription's identity). The live guard is active now regardless.

## 2.369.72 — the release gate is split: a ~2-minute FAST tier before the push, the HEAVY tier after it (owner: "怎么感觉最近每次更新功能都要特别久")

- **Release gate split (five adversarial rounds).** `npm run ci` = build + the FAST tier (73 pure/unit suites + the ONE real haiku turn, measured 95–125 s here) and writes `.git/ci-green`; the pre-push hook runs it (or accepts a fresh marker for the exact pushed sha), then launches `npm run ci:heavy` DETACHED (97 headless-chrome / real-server / real-CLI suites, ~16 min, one run per MACHINE behind `/tmp/vibespace-ci-heavy-<uid>.lock`, superseded by a newer push, marker `data/ci-heavy/<sha>.{green|red|skipped}`). A RED heavy marker for an ancestor of the refs being pushed BLOCKS the next push with the failing suite names until a newer green exists; `npm run ci:status` and the Diagnostics report show the last verdicts. Exit codes: 0 green · 1 red · 2 refused (dirty tree) · 3 no lock · 4 aborted — only 0/1 are verdicts. Every `scripts/test-*.mjs` is in exactly one tier or EXCLUDED with a reason (census in test-architecture, 193 suites). The hook's "docs-only" arm is a DERIVED set: paths any gated suite reads (CLAUDE.md, docs/kb-*.md, docs/examples/**, docs/agent/** …) are code paths. A pushed ref whose tip is not HEAD is gated in an isolated worktree at that sha; suites absent at an older commit are skipped loudly, never a false RED; one fast subject per push (the rest are covered by the heavy tier). GitHub Actions runs both tiers as separate jobs. Mutation battery scripts/dbg-ci-mutations.mjs: 27 guards, each red when deleted. test-ci-gate 153, test-ci-heavy-launch 93.
- **sysinfo.** The `ps` read bound is 64 MiB and a failure is logged instead of silently reporting no processes (the branch's twin of the .70 fix).

## 2.369.69 — harness batches B3 + B5 and the OpenCode background-service closure (owner rulings 2026-09-07; 32 cherry-picks, four chains, one merge review)

- **Turn truth (B3).** Claude chat sessions spawn with `CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS=1` (the only spawn default that changed): `session_state_changed` drives the streaming state AUTHORITATIVELY, `requires_action` becomes its own status-bar chip, an old CLI keeps today's inference and is never called authoritative; the wrapper-sidecar heal is a backstop that can only end a turn. Compaction is driven by what the CLI really emits (`system/status compacting … compact_result`), which finally covers AUTO-compaction; the "Compact now" card shows the real stage and outcome. Codex `thread_rolled_back` (and claude's tombstone, if it ever arrives) mark the retracted turns in place — live, on reload, and through the huge-transcript gap path. Wire honesty: `set_in_progress_tool_use_ids`, `compact_progress` and `tombstone` never reach our stdout in the production spawn shape (measured on 24 buffers and a controlled probe), so their consumers stay dormant and `caps.inProgressTools` is false; a wire-reachability probe in the gate keeps the caps honest. Session death retires every "right now" claim (chip, compaction stage, in-progress dots).
- **Init frame (B3).** The whole init frame is kept: memory paths classify Read/Write on custom memory dirs (regex is the fallback), terminal-only slash commands leave the picker, MCP servers and plugin errors render as a health strip on the init card, skills and output style are echoed, `commands_changed` replaces the cached command list wholesale (ACP twin shares the path). `review`, `renameWriteback` and `forkAtMessage` are caps rows — no backend-id gates remain on those paths. Status-bar dropdowns share one clamp and stay inside a 375 px viewport.
- **B5.** Per-session "Run in a git worktree" (claude, `--worktree` only, never `--tmux`; badge + Session Properties path; remote spawns carry it; a plain checkout's subdirectory on a remote host no longer reads as an isolated worktree — the probe asks git for absolute paths and answers UNKNOWN when it cannot). SendUserMessage / SendUserFile render as first-class cards (files go through published pages, conversation-scoped, private by default, failures shown); `claude.brief` and the prompt-cache trio are settings, default OFF. A read-only "Permission rules" view (codex `config/read` layers and origins, claude settings hierarchy, opencode v1 store) and click-only local oracles (`claude auth status`, `claude agents`, `codex doctor`) each with a measured zero-network proof in the vendor whitelist. The sidebar's live session facts are ONE table (revived two dead fields on the way).
- **OpenCode background service closure (ten rounds).** The live lane's stop is terminal for every in-flight arm and SSE connect; `adopt()` is the single acquisition point with per-attempt epochs; record clears are owned by the serve they name; a recorded serve that is alive but silent is identified (cmdline/uid; portable `ps` rung when /proc is absent) and stopped before a replacement starts, an unidentifiable one parks with an honest error instead of being orphaned; Disable retires a blocked/runaway park; the ssh script carries the same settlement with a decision-level parity table; process identity collapsed into src/cli-identity.js.
- test-turn-truth-ui 80, test-stdout-registry 251, test-harness-contract 262, test-queue-steer 718, test-opencode-s9 332, test-opencode-remote 55, test-worktree-userchan-ui 85, test-permission-rules; full gate green on the integration branch.

## 2.369.68 — usage readings belong to the credentials that produced them (owner: "为啥不是从根源上解决假数据"); resume keeps the conversation's own effort/model (B-6b6d); re-login clears its own warnings

- **Root cause of the phantom usage.** Every VALUE reading (statusline, rate_limit_event, limit banners, the auto-cli panel, OTel corrections) was keyed by the OTel-observed org — the identity the CLI cached at SPAWN — while the pool's hot switch re-points the credentials a running CLI actually uses. After any switch a session filed its readings under the account it was spawned on; a logged-out member kept "receiving" other accounts' numbers, and the same misattribution happened silently between two live members. Now every reading is keyed by the credential slot in use at that moment (the 2.369.66 wall mechanism extended to values, captured once per turn), the OTel org is corroboration only (`orgVerifiedKey` is gone), link moves are recorded in a slot-transition ledger, and a one-shot migration re-attributes or archives the readings, anchors and ledger rows written under the wrong key (never deletes). Each member's panel names the source of its latest reading; a logged-out member's panel is frozen with "stale since".
- **Resume/fork/restart keep the conversation's own effort and model** (owner ruling): the client sends a value only when you explicitly chose one for this session; otherwise the server resumes with the rollout's own last turn (codex) or the transcript's last served model (claude); the instance default applies to NEW sessions only; Session Properties says which fact it is showing (chosen / conversation / instance / harness); the pool placement still gets the model family hint.
- **Re-login clears the warnings it caused.** The login-expiry watch now resolves the inbox items it filed the moment a member's login session changes (any rung), a successful Manage Agents login sweeps immediately (once per finalize, never per 3-second poll), and a measured short session (this org's logins last ~24 h) is mentioned in the 24 h warning.
- Merge review fixes: the pool-blocked notice again names dead logins (the readings chain's pre-filter had hidden them behind "spent: 5h"), the version-marker gate asks git instead of clearing an already-released number.
- Modules: the readings-by-slot attribution lives in `readingSlotFor` (src/server/usage-pool-engine.js) with src/slot-transitions.js and src/reading-repair.js; the resume rule is the resume-continuity module (src/resume-continuity.js: `resumeSpawnPick` + `spawnOriginHint`).
- test-readings-attribution 194, test-codex-effort-meta 245, test-login-expiry 257.

## 2.369.67 — login sessions expire: say it BEFORE the turn dies (owner: "OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed")

- **The incident.** Two members' Claude login sessions reached their absolute expiry (`claudeAiOauth.refreshTokenExpiresAt`); the CLI blanked their tokens on `invalid_grant`, and the pool only learned it AFTER a conversation's turn died with "Failed to authenticate: OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed" — then moved the conversation to another member, so it "worked again" while nobody was told to re-login, and the pool kept moving other conversations onto the same dead login (four conversations, one dead turn each, on 09-02/09-03).
- **Login-expiry facts, passively.** New PURE `src/login-expiry.js` reads the credential file's own deadline: `ok / expiring (<24 h) / expired / logged-out (the wiped shape) / unknown`; the accounts API and Manage Agents carry it as a chip ("login expires in 17 h" / "login is signed out — re-login") next to the login button; the pooled account summarises its members' worst state. Zero vendor calls (file reads only; test-vendor-whitelist unchanged).
- **The pool avoids dead and dying logins.** A member whose login is expired or signed out can never be "usable"; one within 30 min of expiry is never a switch TARGET; an expiring member ranks below an equal healthy one. The auth-failure and pool-blocked notices now say what the wall IS ("Member F's login is signed out — re-login it in Manage Agents"), never "out of quota", and the quota remedy is not prescribed for a wall no window will heal.
- **Warnings before it happens.** Once per member per rung — 24 h, 1 h, and at expiry — an item lands in your "For you" inbox naming the account and the deadline; persisted so a restart does not repeat it, silenced by a re-login (a fresh deadline in the future clears the ledger); a fresh install never files a stale "expired" item for a member that died a week ago.
- test-login-expiry 185 (pure table incl. the wiped shape, fake-clock rungs, once-only + re-login reset + restart survival, the notice STRINGS, the engine wiring pins).

## 2.369.66 — auto-resume fired 130 times into a wall (owner: "你的切换功能发疯了") — four adversarial rounds

- **The incident.** Two sessions re-fired their "You can continue now" continue 130 and 32 times over 4.5 hours, up to twice a second, each cycle writing a "账号池已切换到 Member Y" card into the conversation. Root cause, confirmed on the frozen journal and reproduced against the real engine and a real pool: the CLI's rejection was attributed to the OTel-observed org (the identity the CLI cached at spawn), never to the member whose credentials it actually used, so that member kept a "usable" verdict; the engine re-armed with "switched to a usable account", the per-session hot switch re-pointed to the same member, and `fireNow` had no memory of the fire that had just failed and skipped the pre-fire gate.
- **Wall verdict by credential slot (owner decision ①④).** A rejection lands on the session's linked member — captured ONCE when the rejection arrives, because the first record of a rejection already re-points the link — and that member is dead-until-reset for verdicts and can never be the per-session switch's target; the OTel-observed org is telemetry only.
- **Loop breaker.** A fire answered by another rejection is a FAILED fire: same-identity quarantine (10 min), immediate-fire backoff (0 / 60 s / 5 min), a hard cap of three immediate fires per session per hour, all persisted so a restart cannot hand the loop a fresh budget; the immediate path runs the same pre-fire gate as the timed one. Only proof of WORK (a completed turn, the user's own prompt) clears the memory — a passive quota reading, twenty times more frequent than a rejection, only disarms the wait.
- **One honest line.** The refusal notice is a pure function of the refusal reason with a per-class budget: backoff and fire-pending are journal-only; "no member can serve — add a member or move the session" requires the pool's own verdict; the success card is once per distinct target per window.
- Mitigation is no longer needed: sessions that had auto-resume switched off can turn it back on.
- New suite scripts/test-auto-resume-loop.mjs (186 asserts: the frozen journal replayed at 2/s through the real engine, the negative-control matrix that re-fires ≥10 times, restart survival, the derived noteRecovered audit table).

## 2.369.65 — codex "Steer all" showed one bubble of 25 (owner 2026-09-07) — seven adversarial rounds + a merge review

- **Every inherited queue submission gets its bubble.** The app-server's queue belongs to the THREAD, so after Terminate+Resume the new wrapper inherits items it never recorded; the only live carrier for a steered submission entering the turn is `item/completed {userMessage, clientId}`, which nothing routed — 25 items steered, one bubble drawn. Now an unrecorded submission entering a turn grows its own bubble, keyed by the codex id (never by content).
- **A pre-existing data loss fixed on the way:** the rollout merge de-duplicated codex's own user records by CONTENT, deleting repeated messages on every reload — 27 of 95 user messages on the owner's rollout, 133 across the local corpus. Identity is the codex id; content matching only pairs OUR copy with codex's copy of the SAME submission, and a copy that codex never committed (a slash command, a failed send, an edited or removed queue item, a Stop sweep) WITHDRAWS its claim by name (`webui_user_retracted`) instead of eating a later genuine message.
- **Three producers, one spelling.** The server preview, the wrapper record and codex's own copy of a typed message now spell attachments identically (text first, `input_image` compared without codex's optional `detail`), so a message with an image collapses to one bubble on reload. Visible change: your own bubble renders the text ABOVE a pasted image, live and after a reload alike.
- **Raw NUL bytes never again in source**: the incident module had two, which made it invisible to grep/rg; test-architecture now runs a NUL census over every tracked file (git-driven, gitignored binaries out of scope, its own git calls in a sanitized environment so a hook's GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE cannot redirect them into a real repository — an earlier draft of that control flipped a checkout's core.bare).
- Merge review caught the one merge-only interaction: an `edit` queue verb (2.369.64) now retracts the pre-edit bubble's claim when the text really changed.
- test-queue-steer 697, test-codex-p2-wrapper 352, test-architecture 80 (+ the hostile git-env build battery).

## 2.369.64 — codex queue verbs + notification steering (owner rulings 2026-09-07; eight adversarial rounds + a merge review)

- **The codex queue is now operable, not just visible.** Drag a queued message to reorder it (relative `afterId`, never an index), edit it in place (every non-text variant — images, local images, skills, mentions, audio — is preserved by exclusion; `text_elements` is cleared), run one item now (refused while a turn is busy, with the reason), or run the whole queue as its own control. Peer messages are never editable. Every verb is gated on the running wrapper's advertised verb table (`queueVerbs`, in-band on every `queue_changed`), never on a backend id; a wrapper that advertises nothing gets the legacy verb set, and a session created before the wrapper answered reports `null` (unknown), never an empty list.
- **Eleven client laws for the queue strip** (docs/kb-file-structure.md, chat-input.js): typed words never live only in a textarea about to be replaced; every writer of the textarea is enumerated; the composer's `_send()` answers with one three-valued contract (the message id that went out, `true` when it took the box without a queueable message such as `/goal` or an edit, `false` when it bailed) so Alt+Enter steer (2.369.61) and the edit flow cannot misread each other; the 2.369.60 auto-collapse never fires under a live drag or an open edit (a collapse mid-drag used to turn the drag into a silent "move to the front"; the merge review reproduced it with trusted CDP input).
- **System notifications STEER into a running codex turn** (owner: "按照 TUI 实现"): a VibeSpace notification arriving while codex is busy goes in as `turn/steer` carrying only itself, the queue untouched; human peer messages keep queueing; our Enter default stays queue. Harnesses without a steer verb (ACP v1 / OpenCode) queue the notification and SAY the steer was unavailable; the notification lane for opencode is the durable stash (`peerDelivery: 'stash-only'`).
- Stop still clears the codex queue (2.369.55) and reports each drop as its own removal; on ACP the dropped-peer count no longer tells the user to re-send a message they never sent (B-7638 rule kept through the merge).
- test-queue-steer 600, test-codex-p2-wrapper 267, test-acp-harness 124, test-harness-contract 132; the merged chain is bisectable (test-queue-steer ⑫ asks git for conflict markers across the branch range).

## 2.369.63 — the two parked review follow-ups, closed (B-7638 seven rounds, B-3185 seven rounds)

- **B-7638 — the remote transcript cache's self-heal, from "seven review residuals" to a heal that pays once and never lies.** Seven adversarial rounds, every finding reproduced before it was fixed: the over-cap adoption scanned only the tail 4 KB (a buried splice passed as verified); the ssh rung could GROW an over-cap slot and never wrote its meta back; two polls appending to one slot at one offset had no single writer (single-flight per slot + positional append that refuses a stale offset); a degradable refusal was not a refusal (the moved-slot verdict is terminal on every rung); a rule written for one corruption condemned the innocent shape wearing its signature (`_prefixIsOurs`, typed SLOT_MOVED verdict); legacy over-stamped metas self-heal through a bounded remote gap probe (byte-for-byte against the host, one stamp of `sizeExact`); and round 7: the whole-file scan is memoized against the bytes it judged (ino:size:mtime, dropped by every writer) instead of running twice per poll and again on every poll, the degrade log throttles per fault CLASS (host + offsets blanked) so a different fault inside the minute still prints, and a slot that shrinks under the probe is the MOVED class — never a memoized "proven foreign" verdict. Plus the plugin-manifest `~/.*` expansion and the three acp-wrapper nudge/Stop residuals from the same review. test-codex-zst 222.
- **B-3185 — the writer sweep identifies a CLI by its executable, and its kill paths probe existence with `kill -0`.** Seven rounds: `*claude*` argv-substring matching used to SIGTERM any process whose argv merely named a transcript (`tail -f ~/.claude/projects/…jsonl`, tests under `.claude/worktrees`); per-process `ls /proc/N/fd` forks blew the 20 s budget at 2000+ processes (batched); identity rules collapsed into ONE module (src/cli-identity.js, JS + shell twins, `(deleted)` mirror); the retired rule survived on the uncounted /api/kill-pid path; busybox `ps` has no `-p` so the pre-kill existence probe was blind on busybox images (`kill -0` first, `/proc` second, `ps` last); and round 7: the STANDING SWEEP that enforces "no `ps -p` existence probe on any kill path" now DERIVES its file set by grep (every file that sends or probes a signal, extension-less agent CLIs by shebang, the built daemon bundle judged against the authored text) instead of a hand-written list that had missed 52 real kill-path files, with the marker alternation naming every spelling a kill takes (`kill -s`, numeric `kill -15`, bare `kill "$pid"`, node `handle.kill()`). test-writer-sweep 237, run from both a plain path and a `.claude`-shaped path.

## 2.369.62 — codex: the effort a turn actually ran at (owner: "调成了 ultra 但 metadata 显示 xhigh")

- **The message-meta popup showed xhigh for a conversation running at ultra.** Root cause, five faults stacked: the wrapper synthesizes the `turn_context` every reader takes a turn's effort from, at `turn/started` — and 0.153.4's TurnStartedNotification carries no effort, so the value came from the wrapper's mutable `effort`, which held the spawn env (the INSTANCE default `codex.defaultEffort` = xhigh, passed because a resume that names no effort falls back to the default); the turn had been started by the app-server itself (auto-continue on resume) so that value never reached codex, whose own record of the same turn says ultra; the `thread/resume` reply carrying `reasoningEffort: 'ultra'` landed AFTER the record and the adoption line is gated on an empty effort; that record was the only turn_context in the whole live buffer, so every message was stamped from it; and on rebuild the merge kept the FIRST twin of a turn id — ours — suppressing codex's authoritative copy forever.
- **Fix:** the synthesized turn_context reports the effort the turn was STARTED with, corrects itself when the resume reply lands late, and publishes `{effort, effortNext}` so a mid-turn attach is honest; set-effort refreshes the live status and the status-bar chip immediately (a live `meta/effort` op) and tells the app-server via `thread/settings/update` (a refused update fakes no codex record); the wrapper's effort reaches session-meta so a `/effort` typed into the chat survives the next resume; the merge never suppresses codex's own turn_context. **Honest label:** ultra renders as "ultra (multi-agent · reasoning xhigh)" using the served model's catalog `multi_agent_reasoning_effort` (codex's own models cache, never a constant) and a plain "ultra" when the catalog names none — gated on the harness META row, never a backend id.
- New suite scripts/test-codex-effort-meta.mjs (108 asserts: the incident replayed against a stub app-server with the REAL wrapper in the measured order, a negative control built from master's record shapes, the two-turn rollout fixture xhigh→ultra, set-effort live refresh, the merge fold, a git-backed version-marker assertion) registered in the gate.
- **Owner gate filed (B-6b6d):** on a resume that names no effort, the instance default still outranks the conversation's own saved effort — the remaining half of this incident; recommendation: the conversation's own value wins, the instance default applies to NEW sessions only.

## 2.369.61 — Alt+Enter steers (owner: "顺便加入一个queue的快捷键，不支持queue的就不显示")

- **A keyboard chord for the other send mode.** While a turn runs, Enter still queues (the web/desktop Codex default); **Alt+Enter sends the composer text as a steer** — it goes out on the ordinary send path and the queued item the harness reports back is converted with the same queue-op frame the strip button and bubble chip use (a steer names a queued item; there is no "steer this text" verb). Tab stays slash completion, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter stays send. The chord is the first core `registerKeybinding` contribution (`chat.steerNow`: the command registered once, the binding per view with the window's signal and a `when` scoped to that window), so plugins can see and rebind it.
- **Shown only where it works.** A one-line hint under the composer ("Enter 排队 · Alt+Enter 立即注入") is decided by the pure `composerSendModes(inputModes)` predicate from the harness caps ∧ the running wrapper's advert: codex shows both segments and takes the chord; OpenCode shows the queue segment only; Claude and shell show nothing (Claude holds a mid-turn message but publishes no queue to act on). Session Properties states the rule.
- **Phones (≤768px):** no chords — a bolt button appears beside Send while a turn runs and steer is supported, hidden otherwise. Measured at 375×667: 36×36 beside Send on the same row, the textarea keeps 3 rows, zero overflow.
- **Rounds 2–3 (adversarial):** the 8 s "could not be injected" notice is silenced only when the turn it was sent into really ended — the turn identity now advances on the normalizers' `turn_complete` meta op, not on the label arm, so an idle wrapper running the message as its own turn stays silent while a permission answer or a reconnect inside the same turn no longer counts as a new turn; Session Properties no longer renders two "Config overrides" headers. test-queue-steer 268, test-contributions 136.

## 2.369.60 — the queue strip is bounded (owner: "堆满了queue，不能翻页，然后看不到任何对话内容和发送框了")

- **A long queue no longer swallows the chat window.** The queued-message rows now live in their own scrollable body capped at 8 rows or 40% of the viewport, whichever is smaller (35% on phones ≤768px), so the message list and the input box stay on screen however many items are queued. Past 8 items the strip starts COLLAPSED to its header ("25 queued — runs after this turn", Steer all) with a chevron to expand; the choice is remembered per view. Measured with the real stylesheet and 30 rows in headless chrome: phone 375×667 → body 183 px, scrollable, textarea inside the viewport, 240 px left for messages; desktop 1280×800 → body capped at 216 px.
- Notification steering (system notifications inject into the running turn instead of queueing as billed turns) follows in a separate release once verified; the official Codex TUI's own semantics were researched today and shape it (Enter = steer, Tab = queue; a steer never carries the queue).

## 2.369.59 — the OpenCode background service is a plugin, default OFF (owner decision 2026-09-07; two adversarial rounds)

- **`opencode serve` is now the third built-in plugin** next to Tailscale and frp (⚙ → Plugins), DEFAULT OFF. The plugin is a control surface only: the keeper, the /proc runaway guard and every store fact stay in the shared serve module; the manager owns user intent (`enabled`/`desiredUp` move in lockstep, `promptedAt`). Disable STOPS the process, including one merely adopted from an earlier run, and nothing respawns it. `install()` names https://opencode.ai instead of offering a dead button (it runs YOUR CLI); config is refused (a free loopback port); boot replay = enabled + desiredUp. `decideAutostart({env, pluginWantsUp})` is THE decision: `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0/1` wins as an ops override (the panel says "forced by the environment" and disables the controls), else the plugin record, default OFF.
- **Setting `agents.opencodeServeAutostart` is removed** (schema, settings UI, docs, every reader; a stored value is ignored). The `VIBESPACE_SKIP_AGENT_HOOKS` serve belt that only existed because the old default was ON is gone with it.
- **First-use offer, once per instance:** creating an OpenCode session (non-blocking — a live session never needs the service), forking, or opening a stopped OpenCode conversation shows ONE dialog (createModalShell): what the service does, Enable & start / Not now. Either answer is remembered instance-wide (data/plugins.json, broadcast) so a second tab or device never re-asks; layout replay never pops it; Enable waits a bounded 25 s and then resumes the pending action (reopening a history window keeps its geometry AND home desktop), a service that never answers toasts its state instead of spinning forever. Persistent surfaces: the ⚙ → Plugins card (state line, Start/Stop, one switch) and a sidebar row "Stopped OpenCode conversations are hidden — its background service is off" with an Enable action, rendered by the workbench on desktop and mobile and gated on the harness descriptor's `store.servicePlugin`, never on a backend id.
- **Round 2 (verifier):** with default OFF, the old store-failure signal (`!ready && autostart === false`) became the normal shipped state and popped a RED error toast on every page load — the availability row now distinguishes "off by choice" from "failed"; `VIBESPACE_OPENCODE_SERVE=0` did not actually keep the daemon off because `locate()` adopted a recorded live serve BEFORE the autostart gate — adoption is now behind the switch too.
- New suite scripts/test-opencode-plugin.mjs (81 asserts: fresh data → OFF and zero spawns from listing/discovery; enable → started + adopted + replay after SIGKILL reboot; disable → stopped, no respawn; env precedence incl. an EMPTY value not being an override; prompt-once flag; removed setting absent; chrome: the dialog appears once and Enable proceeds) registered in the gate.

## 2.369.58 — harness honesty batch: four production defects from the 2026-09-07 survey (owner-approved; two adversarial rounds)

- **codex personality no longer overrides the user's ~/.codex silently.** `personality:'pragmatic'` was hardcoded into thread/start AND turn/start; now the value comes from the same per-session slot claude's output style uses, and UNSET means the key is not sent at all (`none` is a real codex value, so it only arrives from an explicit pick). Accepted values = the schema's enum (none | friendly | pragmatic). A style change applies to the RUNNING codex thread via `thread/settings/update`; claude keeps its spawn-time path — the style chip, menu rows and the "Restart now to apply" row gate on a new caps row `responseStyle {live, closed, values}` (mirrored in the client BACKEND_META, deep-equal pinned), never on a backend id; `closed` is codex-only so claude's user-defined output styles are never rejected. Session Properties names the effective value and its origin; the effective style now survives a server restart (it was a dead field after boot-restore).
- **codex ServerRequest replies dispatched by method.** One method was matched by name and everything else got `{decision: …}` — four of the eleven ServerRequest methods have no such field, so those replies could not deserialize (a hung turn). Every method now has an explicit branch classified at arrival: auto (currentTime/read), unsupported (JSON-RPC -32601 + a visible system line + once-per-method telemetry), or a card. MCP elicitation renders through the AskUserQuestion card family with rows derived once from `requestedSchema`; two silent answer-eaters fell out (the shared UI sends one plain string per question; codex routes by question ID, not text). Round 2: the schema-invalid `acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment` branch (which the new gate had certified) was deleted rather than reshaped — upgrading a session-scoped "always allow" to an execpolicy amendment that outlives the session is a product decision, not a serialization detail.
- **ACP unknown sessionUpdate breadcrumb** (once-per-kind telemetry + one console line) — the installed OpenCode's 11-variant union had exactly one real gap, `session_info_update`, now known and card-less.
- **codex image generation + sleep converge on ONE card.** Three producers (live wrapper, thread-read fallback, rollout parser) now emit codex's own rollout spelling for `image_gen.generation` / `clock.sleep`; generated images render through the 2.369.48 media card (the multi-MB base64 never leaves the wrapper), sleep is a live countdown that freezes to "slept 30s".
- Round 2 also: the "Restart now to apply" row is gated on the running wrapper's advert as well as the harness caps; the origin row no longer mislabels an instance default as "your choice". New gate suite scripts/test-harness-honesty.mjs (190 asserts, fixture-vs-live schema diff where the codex binary exists).

- **Live traffic readout** for codex multi-agent bursts, derived from the collab rows the normalizer already stamps (nothing stored server-side; every client renders the same numbers): the coalesced collab card's head reads "Sub-agent traffic · {n} messages · {m} agents · last {age} ago" and ticks once a second while the turn streams, then freezes to "over {span}"; the run header, footer and floating run bar carry the same count and age; the streaming status line switches to "Sub-agents working — {n} messages, last {age} ago" while the newest record is sub-agent traffic and yields the moment anything else arrives.
